The second witch at Madam Malkin's is one of Madam Malkin's assistants at her robe shop in Diagon Alley. In the summer of 1991 she pinned up the hem of Dracina Malfoy's long black robes. Her name is not recorded.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, Harry Potter came into the shop to be fitted for his first Hogwarts robes. At the back of the shop a girl stood on a footstool while a second witch pinned up her hem. Madam Malkin stood Harry on the stool beside her. The girl was Dracina Malfoy, and that was how the two of them met.

pages.html:
Lucius Malfoy is a pure-blood wizard, the master of Malfoy Manor in Wiltshire, the husband of Narcissa Malfoy and the father of Dracina Malfoy. He is a former governor of Hogwarts with a seat on several Ministry committees. He bears Lord Voldemort's Dark Mark, and in 1992 it was his hand that put Tom Riddle's diary into the world. Against every one of his intentions, he has come to like Harry Potter. John Constantine has been his sworn enemy since their schooldays.

Family and background

The Malfoys came to England from Normandy with William the Conqueror. William himself granted Armand Malfoy the family's land in Wiltshire. Tom Riddle once called the line older even than the Potters'. Lucius keeps the family tree in the drawing room at Malfoy Manor, where it covers an entire wall.

He is tall and pale, with long fair hair. He has the same pointed face and silver eyes as his daughter, though his are as cold as a coin. He wears black gloves and a black travelling cloak, with a silver-topped cane in his hand. The stammer of his boyhood still comes back when he is in a rage.

Hogwarts and John Constantine

Lucius started at Hogwarts in 1964, a thin, pale, white-blond boy with a stammer, smaller than the Muggle-born John Constantine. He introduced himself as being 'of the n-noble and ancient house of M-Malfoy'. He was terrified, because a cousin had told him that first-years had to fight a troll to be sorted. Constantine made him laugh, a startled, unpractised laugh, as though he seldom did. Lucius was sorted into Slytherin straight after John, and hurried over to sit beside him.

For four years the two boys sat together in every lesson. When John was poisoned, Lucius read aloud to him in the hospital wing. In public Lucius still repeated his father's views on blood. In private he told John that he was different, an exception. At fifteen Lucius grew tall and handsome, but the girls passed him over for John. He drifted into a set with old names and cold eyes. Later they would have a master, and a mark burnt into their arms. By the sixth year he had mostly lost his stammer. He watched John with open jealousy.

In March of their seventh year Lucius ambushed Constantine over a Ravenclaw girl. He called him a Mudblood for the first time, and fought him until the caretaker, Pringle, pulled them apart. Lucius swore: 'On my b-blood, Constantine. You'll p-pay for this. Every drop.' Constantine has detested him ever since, as everything that is wrong with pure-bloods.

The first war

After leaving Hogwarts in 1971 Lucius joined Lord Voldemort and took the Dark Mark on his left forearm, the same Mark that Severus Snape carries. Arthur Weasley believes he stood in the inner circle. He married Narcissa Black, six or seven years his junior, after she left school in 1978. Their only child, Dracina, was born in 1980.

When Voldemort fell in 1981, the Malfoys were among the first families to come back to the wizarding side, claiming that they had been bewitched. Lucius escaped Azkaban on that claim, helped along by generous gifts of gold to the right causes. Arthur Weasley never believed a word of it. Lucius keeps a large collection of Dark artefacts, part of it in a hidden room beneath the drawing-room floor at the Manor and part in the cellar. Some of the pieces have not been used in anger for a century.

Influence

Lucius sat on the Board of Governors of Hogwarts until June 1993, and he still sits on several Ministry committees. Cornelius Fudge calls him a very generous man to all sorts of good causes. Even after his removal from the Board, half the governors still go pale when his owl arrives. The office of the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures is frightened of him. The executioner, Walden Macnair, is an old friend. He has spent twenty years learning to manage Cornelius Fudge, with gold, with dinners and with long, patient, flattering letters.

As a father

Lucius has never raised a hand to Dracina, and he spoils her. When she was eight and frightened of the peacocks, he had them moved. That same year he had the lake frozen so that she could skate. He buys her things when she screams. He has also chosen every one of her friends for the use of their fathers. When she made friends at six with the gardener's little girl, he sent the child away.

Dracina believes that she has never once been looked at as something to be proud of. He tells her she is very nearly what a Malfoy should be. Her boggart takes his shape. It sighs over her that she is always second, not a real Malfoy, the first Malfoy in eleven hundred years to come second.

Secrets

Lucius forbids any attachment between Dracina and Harry because of the Dark Mark. He knows that when his master returns, the Mark will compel him to fight Harry on Voldemort's behalf, and that it will break his daughter's heart. He has told her none of this.

In truth Harry has won him over. If it were not for the Mark, he would be content to see Harry marry Dracina. He will never admit it.

When he told Harry that Potters had been kings before they were Potters, he knew exactly what he meant. The Potters descend from King Arthur Pendragon, by a documented line that Lucius, unlike almost everybody else, has taken the trouble to look up. Of Lily Potter's ancestry he knows nothing at all beyond her birth to Muggles.

In the saga: 1991 to 1993

During Dracina's first year Lucius was mostly a voice in her conversation, full of opinions about house teams, Hagrid and Weasleys. Professor Quirrell later revealed that it was Lucius who had arranged the Ministry owl that took Dumbledore to London on the night Quirrell went after the Philosopher's Stone.

In August 1992, fearing raids by the Ministry, he sold poisons and other objects from the Manor to Mr Borgin of Borgin and Burkes. Harry, hidden in a cabinet, overheard him warn Dracina that it was imprudent for a young witch to seem obsessed with a young wizard. Lucius muttered that 'Cissy' had been putting fanciful ideas about the cursed Potter boy into her head. He laid a gentle hand on Dracina's shoulder and said he hoped she would amount to more than a thief. Then he rebuked her for letting a Muggle-born beat her in every exam.

At Flourish and Blotts he sneered at the Weasleys and the Grangers until Arthur Weasley threw the first punch. He took an Encyclopaedia of Toadstools in the eye before Hagrid separated them. In the confusion, on Voldemort's instruction, he slipped Tom Riddle's diary into Ginny Weasley's old Transfiguration book. But Dracina swept up the spilled books, and the diary went home with her. When Dracina became Seeker he bought the whole Slytherin Quidditch team Nimbus Two Thousand and Ones. He had Arthur fined fifty Galleons over the flying car, and demanded his resignation in the Daily Prophet.

Lucius would not tell Dracina about the last opening of the Chamber of Secrets. He hinted that a Muggle-born had died. He told her to keep out of danger and let the Heir get on with it, though she thought his heart was not in it. Then he forced Dumbledore's suspension with the signatures of all twelve governors. Several of them said that he had threatened to curse their families.

At the end of the school year, in Professor McGonagall's office, Lucius learnt that his own daughter had carried the diary and been possessed by it. He went white. Had anybody but Dracina held it, he would have let the attacks go on. Harry handed him the ruined diary wrapped in a sock. Lucius threw the sock away; his house-elf, Dobby, caught it, and was free. Lucius nearly drew on Harry. Then he laughed: 'Fair play, Potter. Fair play. That was well done.'

In private he told Harry that he had been instructed, and that 'One does not decline'. Voldemort, he said, knew magic that was old when the castle was a hill, and was barely a man any more. Harry's mockery of his master made him laugh. He told Harry he would have done well in Slytherin. Almost to himself, he added that he began to see what Dracina saw in him. He visited Dracina's hospital bed to tell her, in his Ministry voice, that she was not to befriend Harry. Being close to him, he said, was a very dangerous place to stand. At the end of the year he was dismissed from the Board of Governors.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

Through the summer of 1993 Lucius forbade Dracina to write to Harry. He was in a peculiar mood, saying 'fair play' at breakfast and looking annoyed with himself. He later admitted that forbidding her had been approximately as effective as forbidding the tide.

In August 1993 he met Harry near Knockturn Alley and walked him back down Diagon Alley. He complained that he had heard the story of the Chamber from Dracina eleven times, with the Basilisk growing to eighty feet; Harry told him it was fifty. He knew about Aunt Marge from the Ministry, and he was coldly furious. Lily Potter had been a Mudblood he never cared for, but she was a witch. Had that woman said such a thing in his house, she would have left in a smaller box, chosen by his wife. 'And this woman is still breathing.' He told Harry that 'Potters have been kings before they were Potters', and that blood was a fact like the colour of one's eyes, not a prejudice. Harry should stop living, he said, as though he were a Muggle. He had never heard of Khan Noonien Singh, Superman or Spider-Man, and he dismissed the Muggle wars as their own business.

When Harry answered that Muggle heroes save people, just as he had gone down the pipe for Dracina, Lucius flared with white anger. All through the conversation his free hand had gone, quite unconsciously, to his own left forearm. Walking away, he muttered that the boy was exceedingly hard to dislike, and that Cissy was not helping. He looked back at Harry with naked fear before his face broke into his daughter's sly, lopsided grin.

After Buckbeak injured Dracina in September 1993, Lucius took his complaint to the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures, and it was upheld. Pansy Parkinson had taken Dracina's angry four-page letter to the Owlery, although Dracina had never meant to send it. Lucius put it before the Committee. He had the hearing brought forward from 20 April to a Friday in March 1994, and wrote to thank his daughter in a letter sealed with green wax. He ignored her plea to drop the case. At the hearing the Committee did as he said. He writes to Dracina every week, and he reads Crabbe's post, though never that of her owl, Juniper.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In the summer of 1994 he asked Dracina at dinner how Harry was, and whether Dumbledore had sent him back to his Muggles, which he called a scandal. Then he told her once again to have nothing to do with him.

Book Four, Chapter Five: the Malfoys camped at the Quidditch World Cup in a towering palace of striped silk, with a row of white peacocks tethered at its entrance. At dusk on 22 August 1994 Harry glimpsed Lucius across the crowd, tall, with his hair so fair it was nearly white and his hand on his silver-topped cane. Lucius turned to look their way. At the next cart John Constantine, who was keeping out of his sight, moved sharply off. Then Lucius was swallowed up by the crowd.

Book Four, Chapter Six: Lucius watched the final from the Top Box as Fudge's guest, having just made a very generous contribution to St Mungo's Hospital. When Harry and Dracina smiled at each other, his lips twitched as though he had only just managed not to smile himself. He asked Arthur Weasley softly what he had sold to afford seats in the Top Box, and his cold grey eyes rested on Hermione with a contempt that needed no words. While Harry flattered Fudge, then unsettled him with talk of mutants, Lucius asked the Minister pointedly about Barty Crouch's Muggle newspapers. He asked, too, what the Ministry's channels were.

Afterwards Lucius took Harry aside behind a gilded pillar at the top of the stairs. Severus Snape had told him about the werewolf in June, and he thanked Harry, as one man to another, for saving Dracina's life again. Harry asked whether Snape sent him minutes. Lucius laughed despite himself, the same startled laugh Harry had heard outside Dumbledore's office in 1993, then admitted that he liked Harry's sense of humour a good deal more than he would wish. He had spent twenty years learning to manage Fudge, he said; Harry had done it in two minutes. He called Harry a man to watch, a clever, cunning one, and said again that he would have done well in Slytherin.

When Harry spoke of Voldemort, Lucius flinched. Without knowing it he rubbed his left forearm, where the Dark Mark lies, which he knows will one day burn to call him to stand against Harry. 'The Dark Lord,' he said quietly, 'is the least of our troubles.' Harry noticed the word our. In Diagon Alley in 1993 Harry had asked him about a Muggle war and a masked man who climbed walls; his blank face that day had shown Harry that wizards knew nothing of the Muggle world's troubles. Since then Lucius had made quiet enquiries, and he had concluded that the Ministry knew far more than it said. Fudge, he told Harry, had been to see the Muggle Prime Minister four times since the spring, and came back from Downing Street grey in the face. For the first time in his life the Minister was frightened of something other than the Daily Prophet.

Before he could say what Fudge knew, Lucius glimpsed a long pale coat on the stairs below. He lunged to the rail in a murderous fury, catching Harry's shin with his cane. He believed he had seen an old enemy, he said, and by his honour he was bound to settle an oath sworn on blood that could be settled only one way. During the match he rose more than once to search the stands, and he sniffed out a drift of cigarette smoke rising from the stand below, where Constantine kept dropping out of sight.

After the Cup had been presented, Constantine stepped backwards onto Winky in the Top Box, and her shriek gave him away. Lucius roared his name with a stammer, his face gone a mottled purple. Constantine remarked that he had lost a bit of weight, though not the stammer. Lucius's first jinx blew the Bulgarian Minister's hat off, then set a gilded pillar alight. He swore on his blood that Constantine would pay, every drop, and demanded satisfaction. Constantine asked whether his wife was not giving him enough, and Lucius howled, weeping with rage. At Narcissa's order to batter him, he chased Constantine down the stairs four at a time, then on through the stands, until the leprechauns took him for a Bulgarian and poured down on him like hail. Constantine got away. Narcissa told the box, with great dignity, that her husband had an old school friend.

That evening Narcissa told Harry that Lucius had liked him, against his will, ever since the business with the Chamber. He called the boy exceedingly hard to dislike, she said, the way other men say they have a cold coming on.

In their own words

We're dignified purebloods. Unlike some wizards.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch5
I was instructed, Potter. Do you understand what that means, from him? One does not decline.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19
And I think that I begin to see what she sees in you.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19
Fair play, Potter. Fair play. That was well done.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19

pages.html:
Narcissa Malfoy, born Narcissa Black, is the wife of Lucius Malfoy and the mother of Dracina Malfoy. She keeps every old pure-blood custom there is. She is also, quietly and against her husband's express wishes, the chief ally of her daughter's attachment to Harry Potter, who is the son of the boy she lost to Lily Evans. She is the twin sister of Bellatrix Lestrange. In August 1994, at the Quidditch World Cup final, she met Harry properly for the first time and pronounced him just right for her daughter.

Early life

Narcissa was born into the House of Black, one of the oldest and proudest of the pure-blood families. Her parents were Cygnus Black and Druella Rosier. Narcissa and her sister Bellatrix were twins. They had the same face and the same proud Black bearing. Only their hair told them apart: Bellatrix was black-haired, Narcissa fair. They were very close, closer than most sisters, in everything but one thing. The two girls started at Hogwarts together in 1971, in the same year as James Potter, Lily Evans and the sisters' cousin Sirius Black. A third sister, Andromeda, was later disowned by the family for marrying the Muggle-born Ted Tonks.

At school both sisters decided that James Potter was theirs. It was the one thing the twins ever truly fought over. Professor Flitwick remembers them feuding across his Charms classroom for years, with hexes and with flowers. Remus Lupin remembers Bellatrix trying to hex her sister's eyebrows off. Once the two of them fought in the entrance hall while James stood between them, looking bewildered. The rivalry caused James great distress, and the other Marauders teased him about it without mercy. It ended only when Lily Evans came along and won him. Flitwick says that neither sister ever quite forgave anybody afterwards.

Marriage and family

After she left Hogwarts in 1978, Narcissa married Lucius Malfoy. Their daughter Dracina was born on 5 June 1980. Narcissa is a tall, fair woman. Dracina has her jaw, her chin, her nose and her smile. Lucius calls his wife Cissy, as her cousin Sirius does. In the east drawing room at Malfoy Manor she keeps a woven hanging of Saint George, and she grows roses in the Manor gardens.

When Dracina was a little girl, Narcissa read her stories of knights protecting princesses. She arranged years of lessons for her at the Manor with a man from Paris. Because Dracina kept falling off her pony, her mother taught her a healing charm. Narcissa describes a boggart as something that wears your fear like a coat, a definition Lupin called sensible. She knows, as Lucius does not, that Dracina learnt to whistle from the gamekeeper.

She is a stickler for the old customs. Gifts of consequence, she says, are not sent by post. It is unlucky, too, to throw away a favour ribbon.

Her reasons

Narcissa encourages her daughter's romance with Harry Potter in secret. She lost James to Lily, so she loves the idea of a Potter marrying a Malfoy at last: her daughter need not lose the son. She finds Harry's chivalry genuinely romantic. At Madam Malkin's, Harry asked Dracina quite seriously whether she was a princess, and Dracina has seen herself as one ever since. Narcissa thinks that charming. She thinks it just as charming that Dracina sees Harry as the knight from the stories her mother used to read her.

She does not know why Lucius forbids it. His reason is the Dark Mark on his arm, of which he has told neither his wife nor his daughter.

In the saga: Narcissa and Harry Potter

In December 1991, during Dracina's first year, Narcissa asked her daughter to invite Harry Potter to Malfoy Manor for Christmas. Dracina told Harry that her mother must have taken leave of her senses. Harry laughed the invitation off as a prank. By the summer of 1992 Lucius was muttering that Cissy had been putting fanciful ideas about the Potter boy into Dracina's head.

In July 1993, with Lucius forbidding all contact, Narcissa helped Dracina write to Harry for his thirteenth birthday. She found out when the birthday was. She sent her own eagle owl, Ganymede, across three counties to Surrey. She insisted that the letter be tied with a green ribbon, the old token of a lady's favour. Harry kept the ribbon, and uses it as his bookmark. Lucius complained that his wife had been 'of no assistance whatever'. That winter she sent a pair of dragon-hide gloves, which Dracina passed on to Harry. She could also have had a Nimbus sent up from London on loan.

Sirius Black, on hearing how matters stood, thought that Cissy would be delighted that James's son had won over a Malfoy.

In the saga: in the background

Until August 1994 Narcissa had never appeared in Harry's company. In 1991 she was up the street seeing about Dracina's wand, while Harry and Dracina were being fitted for robes. In 1992 Dumbledore told Lucius to tell her himself about Dracina's ordeal in the Chamber of Secrets, adding that he would send his own letter anyway. Shortly before the June 1994 examinations Ganymede brought Dracina a long, soft parcel from home. She hid it on her lap, then carried it out of the Great Hall.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In the summer of 1994 Lucius asked after Harry at dinner. Narcissa turned him aside with 'Severus tells me the boy is very well indeed', and was careful not to look at her daughter afterwards. Out of nowhere, she asked Dracina whether Harry still had his father's hair.

Book Four, Chapter Six: on 22 August 1994 Narcissa came into the Top Box at the Quidditch World Cup final with her husband and daughter. Harry saw that Dracina had her mother's jaw, chin, nose and smile; Narcissa was wearing the same smile herself. She looked from Harry to Dracina with a long, slow, knowing smile, as if she had waited a very long time for something and had just seen the first sign of it.

Later Narcissa came down the row to introduce herself. It was absurd, she said, that they had never been properly introduced, considering how often she heard his name at breakfast. Harry kissed her hand. She called him Dracina's knight. When he answered that this made Dracina a princess, she laughed warmly. When he told her that she looked like a queen, she giggled like a schoolgirl. He was as charming and handsome as his father, she said, with James's face exactly, all but the eyes. She and James had been in the same year at Hogwarts.

Narcissa told Harry that Lucius liked him against his will, and that this was the most entertaining thing to happen in their house since Dracina was born. She thanked him for saving Dracina's life three times, from a troll, a diary and a werewolf. Harry said that anyone would have done it. Narcissa said they would not: she had been at school with anyone, and she knew exactly what anyone would have done.

Looking at his hair, she said it was like being fifteen again, waiting in the entrance hall for a boy with hair like his to come down the stairs. Her twin sister, Bellatrix, waited there too: both girls loved James, and they fought over him for years, until Professor Flitwick used to hide behind his desk. Then Lily came along. Narcissa's voice went several degrees colder. Bella never forgave her, she said. Bella tried once to take James back, in the spring of their last year. She had always been a little fragile in her mind, feeling everything far too much. After that spring she was not fragile any more, nor anything at all.

Lily did something to Bellatrix that spring, Narcissa told Harry. When he asked what, she would not say. He should ask his father's old friends, she said, why her cousin Sirius, who was afraid of nothing on God's earth, could not bear to be in the same room as Lily for a month afterwards. Some of the stories of Lily's kindness might even be true. 'Bella went looking for something to fill the space Lily had torn in her. She found the Dark Lord. He did the rest.' Then she seemed to come back to herself. She apologised: it had been unkind, and it had never been Harry's quarrel.

When Dracina came to fetch her mother, Narcissa paused to look Harry over from his hair to his trainers, as if he were a piece of jewellery, then pronounced him just right for her. Dracina was scandalised.

When John Constantine was found in the box and asked Lucius whether his wife was not giving him enough, Narcissa rose to her full height. She was extremely satisfying, she declared, the most satisfying wife in Wiltshire. Then her embarrassment boiled over, and she ordered Lucius to batter him. After the chase she told the box, with great dignity, that her husband had an old school friend. She let Dracina go off with Pansy Parkinson to hunt for a lost earring, saying that Lucius would be some time. When her gaze fell on Ron and Harry, something came into her face that, in a less dignified woman, might have been called a grin.

In their own words

Severus tells me the boy is very well indeed.Narcissa Malfoy · B4 Ch2
Just right for her.Narcissa Malfoy · B4 Ch6
I am extremely satisfying! I am the most satisfying wife in Wiltshire!Narcissa Malfoy · B4 Ch6
Bella went looking for something to fill the space Lily had torn in her. She found the Dark Lord. He did the rest.Narcissa Malfoy · B4 Ch6

pages.html:
Petunia Dursley, born Petunia Evans, is the elder sister of Lily Potter, and the aunt with whom Harry Potter was left in 1981. She refused her mother's faith as well as her sister's magic, and she has resented both all her life. Yet her blood carries the same ancient protection that Lily laid on Harry, and her house is the one place where Lord Voldemort cannot touch him.

Family

Petunia is the daughter of Susan Pevensie, once a crowned Queen of Narnia, who survived the railway accident that killed her brothers and sister. Afterwards Susan came back to Christ. She raised her daughters to be godly. Through her, both girls descend from Aragorn and Arwen.

Lily took her mother's faith seriously from childhood, and she turned out to be a witch. Her magic reconciled Susan to her, because in Lily, Susan at last had somebody who could not dismiss Narnia. Petunia refused both halves. She has neither faith nor magic, and her resentment of Lily is the resentment of a sister shut out of two countries at once. As a girl she wrote to Albus Dumbledore asking to be admitted to Hogwarts, and was refused.

She married Vernon Dursley, and their only son, Dudley, was born in June 1980. She is thin, bony and horse-faced, with a long neck that she uses to look over the garden hedge at the neighbours, because she is very nosy. She hates animals. She buys magazines with horoscopes in them and prefers posh wine. She watches every documentary about serial killers that Channel 4 shows, mouth open, tea going cold. On the rare occasions when she has to say the word 'magic', she wrinkles her nose. The only thing about her that is like Lily is her eyes.

When Lily went to Hogwarts, Susan began to tell her daughters about Narnia. Petunia met it with scorn and derision. It drew Lily closer to their mother, and it left Petunia more resentful than ever.

Harry's childhood

Petunia doted on Dudley. Harry she starved, worked and beat. When he overcooked the eggs, she hit him round the head with a frying pan. She hit him with a rolling pin too, and used it to shoo him away from the television. When he was six and down with flu, the most she did was lay a cold flannel on his forehead, telling him not to be sick on the sheets. The same year she watched from the kitchen window while he weeded the flower beds in the heat.

On his sixth birthday she came to the cupboard door and told him, quite kindly, that there was a parcel for him on the kitchen table. It was a pair of Uncle Vernon's old socks wrapped in newspaper. All three Dursleys watched his face while he opened it. When a dinner lady at St Grogory's slipped Harry an extra bread roll every day for a fortnight, Petunia came in to complain about his jumper, and the dinner lady never looked at him again. Nobody ever said 'there, there' to Harry. Petunia said 'There, there, Diddykins' to Dudley through every thunderstorm.

She once warned the two boys about Uncle Vernon's boss, a man with a big nose and curly hair. Years later Harry recognised the same prejudice when Dracina Malfoy mocked Hermione's looks. The family went to church only twice. The first time was one Christmas when Harry was seven, because the Polkisses had started going and Petunia would not be outdone. The second time was to meet a churchwarden who might buy drills.

In the saga: 1992

On Harry's twelfth birthday, 31 July 1992, Dudley claimed that Harry was doing magic. Petunia knew perfectly well that he was not, but she came out of the back door swinging a soapy frying pan at him all the same. Then she made him clean, mow, weed and paint until evening. For the Masons' dinner she wore a salmon-pink cocktail dress. Her pudding of whipped cream and sugared violets ended up on Mrs Mason's head, dropped there by Dobby. While Harry was locked in his room she pushed food through the cat-flap, a bowl of cold tinned soup among it. On one day the family forgot him altogether.

The protection

When Lily died for Harry in 1981 she laid an old protection on him, the magic of the Elves and of Númenor. It lives in his blood, and it lives in Petunia's too. While Harry can call her house his home, and his mother's blood lives under its roof, Voldemort cannot touch him there. That is why Dumbledore insists that Harry go back to Privet Drive every summer.

At the end of Harry's second year, Dumbledore sat on Petunia's sofa. He told her and Vernon that he would know the moment they harmed the boy: 'Not a hand, not a word.' Petunia stopped locking the fridge. On the third night of the summer of 1993 she twitched, fetched a fourth plate and banged it down in front of the empty chair. Then she told Harry to sit. When Vernon raged, she reminded him what the old man had said: 'He said a word. Not a hand, not a word. He didn't say whose.'

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

During Marge Dursley's visit in 1993, Petunia agreed with Marge's complaints about immigrants. She did not agree when Marge urged extreme force on Harry. When Marge began to inflate, Petunia watched Harry rather than Marge, as if a warning she had long expected had come true. When Harry raised his wand, she whispered to Vernon not to move.

In November 1993 she wrote to Harry for the first time in her life: six lines, to say that the school had contacted them and that he was not to come home for Christmas.

Sirius Black, who watched the house in the summer of 1993, saw her clipping a hedge that did not need it, peering up and down the road. He remembered that Lily used to talk about her.

In the saga: in Harry's dreams

In Harry's revenge dream of November 1993, Petunia stood at the sink and looked at him with his mother's eyes. In the dream of August 1994 she was the matron of an orphanage at number four. She was dressed in black, with keys at her belt, and she wrote in a ledger without ever looking up. Lily had died in her care, after giving birth on the last night of the year.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

On Thursday 18 August 1994 she found the refrigerator full of bleeding rats. She cleaned it out alone, in yellow rubber gloves, crying, 'In my fridge. In my nice, clean fridge...' Afterwards she opened the new one every morning with her eyes shut. That summer she put the whole family on Dudley's diet, making sure that Dudley got more than Harry. On 20 August pond mud came up out of the kitchen plughole and covered her from head to foot. Her hair, which she had put in rollers the night before, was plastered flat to her skull. It was Mrs Weasley's doing.

Book Four, Chapter Four: Petunia spent most of 20 August on her knees, scraping mud out of the kitchen grouting. The woman at number seven was telling the whole of Little Whinging about the Dursleys' drains, and Petunia was so scandalised that she did not set foot outside the front door again. The sink would not let her forget it. Every so often it gave a deep, wet gurgle, most often just as she was opening her mouth to snap at Harry, and she jumped every time. At lunch on Sunday 21 August she ate nothing. Twice she drew breath to lecture Harry. Each time she gave her old twitch, as though a hand had come to rest on the back of her neck, and looked from the new fridge to the sink. Each time the sink gurgled, and she shut her mouth with a tiny squeak.

She spent the afternoon at the net curtains, peeking out every few seconds, and plumped the sofa cushions while looking under each one for anything with whiskers. When the Weasleys burst through the boarded-up fireplace she toppled backwards over the coffee table, then wailed at the dust. When Dudley's tongue swelled from a Ton-Tongue Toffee, she hauled on it by the tip like a woman trying to start a lawnmower, then flung herself on top of him to shield him from Arthur Weasley's wand.

Before he left, Arthur set a house gnome loose under her sideboard. House gnomes live on spite, so a cross, mean household keeps them fat for years. The sink kept on too: that night the Dursleys had to call out a plumber twice, and the second would not set foot in the kitchen. Harry knows nothing of it.

Book Four, Chapter Five: when Hermione said she could not imagine any parent betraying a child, Harry remembered Aunt Petunia's lip curling over the word freak. In Chapter Six, at the World Cup final, Hermione added the veela to a list she keeps, which already had the Dursleys on it.

In their own words

He said a word. Not a hand, not a word. He didn't say whose.Petunia Dursley · B3 Ch2
In my fridge. In my nice, clean fridge...Petunia Dursley · B4 Ch2

pages.html:
Vernon Dursley is a Muggle, the director of a drill-making firm called Grunnings, and the husband of Lily Potter's sister Petunia. For ten years he and his wife kept their orphaned nephew, Harry Potter, in the cupboard under the stairs at Number Four, Privet Drive. He struck the boy until the summer of 1993, when Albus Dumbledore came to sit in his front room.

Background

Vernon is a large man with hardly any neck, small sharp eyes and an enormous moustache, which Petunia makes him groom every morning. He was educated at Smeltings, the school Dudley now attends. He runs Grunnings, which makes drills, and in 1993 he had a new company car. He married Petunia Evans, and their son Dudley was born in June 1980.

On 1 November 1981 the infant Harry Potter was left on the Dursleys' doorstep after the murder of his parents. Vernon took him in, but only, as he later told Molly Weasley, as family 'in a manner of speaking'.

Opinions

Vernon holds firm views on almost everything, and he is wrong about most of them. He shouts at the Irish on the television and goes red with rage at reports of IRA attacks. He is in favour of hanging. By the summer of 1993 he had loathed John Major for about a year, ever since the trouble over the pound and the ERM.

He sneers 'Bloody God-botherers' at vicars on the television. He has been to church perhaps twice: once to keep up with the Polkisses, and once to sell drills to a churchwarden. A picture in his study shows a vast bald man in a white suit between two bodyguards, whom Vernon calls, with deep respect, a very successful American businessman. In July 1993 a British National Party membership card fell out of his wallet. He believes that karate teaches a boy 'dominance'. All through the summer of 1994 he complained about the price of petrol. He judges other men by the size and price of their cars. For years he has raged about cheap foreign drills undercutting Grunnings, taking the bread out of decent men's mouths.

Above all he forbids any mention of magic in his house. He calls it Harry's abnormality. 'This is a respectable house!'

Harry's childhood

Harry spent about ten years in the cupboard under the stairs, with the spiders and a bolt on the outside. Before he could read he had learnt to keep very still in the dark until Uncle Vernon had gone past. The sound of heavy footsteps in a corridor still makes his shoulders creep up round his ears.

Vernon struck him across the back of the head, for burning the bacon among other things. He kept an old slipper with mould on the heel behind the kitchen door, for beating him. For birthdays he gave Harry a coat-hanger, or a pair of his own old socks. The socks came on his sixth birthday, wrapped in newspaper, with all three Dursleys watching his face.

When the Hogwarts letters began to arrive in 1991, Vernon nailed planks across the letter box with his mouth full of nails. He swore when they came down the chimney instead.

In the saga: 1992

In the summer of 1992 Vernon padlocked Harry's school things in the cupboard and Hedwig in her cage. On 31 July he forgot Harry's birthday altogether. Instead he rehearsed the family for a dinner at which he hoped to sell an enormous order of drills to a rich builder, Mr Mason, and then buy a villa in Majorca. Dobby's falling pudding ruined it, along with the Ministry owl that landed on Mrs Mason, who was terrified of birds. Vernon asked Mr Mason whether 'their people' were always nervous of birds, and Mr Mason stormed out.

When he learnt that Harry was not allowed to use magic outside school, Vernon locked him in his bedroom. He paid a man to put bars on the window, whistling as it was done. He fitted a cat-flap in the door himself, to push food through, and swore that Harry would never go back to Hogwarts. He claimed the lock was the kind they fit in prisons. Fred and George Weasley picked it with a piece of wire in under a minute. As Harry climbed out of the window into the Weasleys' flying car, Vernon seized his ankle and left a ring of bruises.

In the saga: 1993

At the end of Harry's second year Albus Dumbledore called on Vernon and Petunia. He sat on their sofa and promised them that he would know the moment they used a hand or a word against Harry. Vernon never laid a finger on him again. Whenever he moved to strike, he twitched and froze. He let Hedwig out at night and gave Harry a plate at every dinner, though he still goes purple when Harry comes into a room. He told Petunia that he would not have 'that man' in his house again, whatever it took. When Ron Weasley telephoned that summer, Vernon answered in his sales voice, then bellowed that there was no Harry Potter there.

On 31 July 1993 he announced that his sister Marge was coming for a week. Harry was to pretend that he attended St Brutus's Secure Centre for Incurably Criminal Boys. Harry blackmailed him with the BNP card into promising to sign his Hogsmeade form. Vernon gagged on his rage. He muttered 'torture', 'psychological damage' and 'said he'd know', then gave in: 'I'll sign the bloody form, you cursed child, just do what I say about Marge!'

All that week he told Marge that James Potter had been unemployed, and poured her more brandy while she abused Harry. On the last evening he looked at Harry pleadingly, begging him with his eyes to go upstairs. When Marge inflated, her dog Ripper bit Vernon's leg. Harry held him off at wandpoint while he backed away with his hands raised. He did not sign the form.

In the saga: June 1994

At King's Cross in June 1994 Vernon stood well back from the Weasleys. He quailed under Molly Weasley's look, trod on a pigeon and told Harry that he had no godfather.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In August 1994 Harry dreamt of Vernon as a filthy wretch in a string vest, living in a shack in a wood that was really the cupboard under the stairs, with a dead boa constrictor nailed to the door. This Vernon hissed at Harry. He wore a gold ring with a black stone and had a wand stuck through the rope at his waist. Harry put him to sleep and took both. The dream was a memory of Lord Voldemort's, with Harry's family put in the places of the people in it.

In August he found the refrigerator full of bleeding rats. He reached for Harry's collar, stopped short and looked out at the garden, as though for a man with a wand. Then he went grey, and left for work an hour early.

Two days later, on 20 August, pond mud erupted from the kitchen plughole, coating Vernon and the kitchen alike. He shouted at the sink. Then he thrust Molly Weasley's heavily stamped invitation to the Quidditch World Cup at Harry, told him to say that he was being looked after, and said that he could go.

Book Four, Chapter Four: at breakfast on Sunday 21 August Vernon read out a newspaper piece about the Americans wanting to build their giant robots again. He looked at Harry over the top of the page. 'Round the lot of them up, I say. Freaks, the whole pack of them.' For the Weasleys' visit he put on his best suit, wanting to look large, solid and important. Every so often he gave the little wobbling chuckle he kept for putting people in their place. He demanded that the Weasleys have the decency to wear normal clothes. When they were late, he muttered a racial slur he had used before about the man who ran the newsagent's and most of the drivers on the M25.

The Weasleys arrived through the boarded-up fireplace, blowing it open and burying the room in dust. When Harry joked that the Dursleys did not want Father Christmas turning up without notice, Vernon protested that he was very fond of Christmas, and had believed in Father Christmas until he was eleven. Deciding that a man who collected plugs was nothing to fear, he stood so close to Arthur Weasley that his stomach nearly touched him, as he did to the men who came to read the gas meter. He was a director at Grunnings, he said, with three hundred men under him. Arthur simply straightened up to his full height, a good head taller, then told him he was standing on his robes. Vernon stepped back very fast. Faced with Arthur's silence, and his wand, he said goodbye to Harry with enormous resentment. When Dudley's tongue swelled from a Ton-Tongue Toffee, Vernon hurled a china shepherdess at Arthur, then a second ornament; Arthur flicked a third out of his fist.

Before leaving, Arthur set a house gnome loose under the Dursleys' sideboard. House gnomes get into the walls, chew the wiring, turn the milk and whisper just out of sight. They live on spite, so a cross, mean household keeps them fat for years, breeding every six weeks or so. Harry glimpsed it, but the Weasleys told him it had been a trick of the Floo smoke. The sink at number four went on gurgling too, though Molly Weasley told Harry its enchantment would have worn off. That night the Dursleys had to call out a plumber twice, and the second would not set foot in the kitchen. Harry knows nothing of any of this.

Book Four, Chapter Five: on 22 August Harry joked to Hermione that Khan had got half of Yugoslavia, more than Uncle Vernon had managed with Grunnings. Vernon would have had a heart attack, Harry told Cedric Diggory, if Harry had flown his Firebolt that summer. Vernon watches spy films every Christmas, and his friends from Grunnings smoke in the garden at his barbecues. About the people coming to Britain, Harry agreed with him, one of the only things they had ever agreed on.

Book Four, Chapter Six: at the World Cup final the referee's moustache rivalled Vernon's, and Lucius Malfoy's rage turned his face the mottled purple Harry had only ever seen on Uncle Vernon. Lucius looked at John Constantine the way Vernon looks at owls. Hermione added the veela to a list she keeps, which already had the Dursleys on it.

In their own words

I'll sign the bloody form, you cursed child, just do what I say about Marge!Vernon Dursley · B3 Ch2
This is a respectable house! I will not have it, do you hear me? I WILL NOT HAVE IT!Vernon Dursley · B4 Ch3
Round the lot of them up, I say. Freaks, the whole pack of them.Vernon Dursley · B4 Ch4
I know a cowboy when I see one, and I know how to deal with him.Vernon Dursley · B4 Ch4

pages.html:
Dudley Dursley is Harry Potter's cousin, the only son of Vernon and Petunia Dursley. He was spoilt to the bone, and for most of their childhood he was Harry's chief tormentor. Since 1993 he has begun, slowly and to his own surprise, to want to be something better. What he wants to be is a Power Ranger.

Childhood

Dudley is blond, pink and very large; by 1992 his bottom drooped over both sides of the kitchen chair. His parents spoilt him completely. Every year he was given nine or ten Easter eggs while Harry got none, and he had Knickerbocker Glories while Harry got the cheapest lemon ice lolly. He kept a second bedroom full of broken things. Christmas at Privet Drive was Dudley's day. He has been able to cry whenever he likes since he was three, usually to get a second pudding. He ran to his parents' room in thunderstorms until he was well past ten.

At St Grogory's Primary School he scribbled on the princesses in the picture books, and kicked the back of Harry's chair in assembly. He made sure that nobody picked Harry for games, or was his friend. Every summer he and his gang, his best friend Piers Polkiss among them, played Harry Hunting behind the shops. Once they hung Harry off the school roof by his ankles while Dudley's friends kicked at his head. Dudley broke Harry's glasses with his fist in the playground, and the teacher let him off because boys would be boys. He liked to tease Harry by holding out sweets at arm's length, then snatching them back. Harry wore his cast-offs.

He owned an Amiga, which he smashed in a Boxing Day tantrum (the pieces are in a box in Harry's wardrobe), and later a Megadrive. He sulked furiously whenever his father refused him a new game. When the family put up a Sky satellite dish he discovered WWF wrestling, and stopped reading altogether. As a small boy he collected superhero annuals. He has never forgiven Spider-Man for retiring. After Superman's death in November 1992 he got a commemorative Superman mug free with something. On Saturday afternoons he watches old Doctor Who episodes on video.

At the zoo in 1991 Harry, who did not yet know that he was a wizard, accidentally set a boa constrictor on him.

Smeltings

Dudley followed his father to Smeltings. The uniform is a maroon tailcoat, orange knickerbockers and a flat straw hat called a boater. Every boy also carries a knobbly stick, for hitting other boys when the masters are not looking, which is supposed to be good training for later life. Harry has mocked Dudley for needing remedial work there.

In July 1992 Dudley rehearsed greeting the Masons. He planned to tell Mr Mason that he had written a school essay about him as his hero. On Harry's twelfth birthday he taunted him for having no cards and no friends. He fled screaming when Harry pretended to be turning the hedge into an Ent.

In the saga: the Power Rangers (1993)

By the summer of 1993 Dudley was thirteen. He had a new television in the kitchen, and he had not hit Harry once all summer. On 31 July he watched, with shining eyes, as the Power Rangers fought a giant creature in Birmingham. Harry saw then, for the first time, that his cousin wanted to be something. Dudley was enthralled by the reports of Khan Noonien Singh as well. During her visit that August, Aunt Marge gave him a twenty-pound note and a video recorder.

Marge had once given him a one-volume The Lord of the Rings for Christmas, which he used to prop up a wobbly table until Harry took it. Harry read it all through his third year at Hogwarts, with Narcissa Malfoy's green ribbon for a bookmark. He finished it in the summer of 1994.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Dudley's Smeltings report for 1994 carried a note from the school nurse: he had grown to the dimensions of a young killer whale. He was put on a strict diet. In August he smashed his Megadrive by throwing it out of the window, after being caught smuggling doughnuts. He is devoted to the Green Ranger, and worries that he is unwell. He has taken up karate at the leisure centre on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. He seems to understand that 'there is no first attack in karate', even if his father does not.

By August 1994 he had not thumped Harry for a long time. On 20 August he made room for Harry on the sofa, and they watched the news together. The bulletin covered the Augment War and crowds protesting against superhumans. Superman was on it too, asking the United Nations to let the Justice League and the Avengers step in. Dudley asked the television: 'Why would anyone be against people saving people's lives?'

Book Four, Chapter Four: by 21 August Dudley seemed smaller somehow, though his diet had not taken an ounce off him, and he ate his cottage cheese with grated celery without complaint. Harry had begun to watch him, the way you might watch a dog that had unexpectedly stopped barking. Dudley watched the Power Rangers with his mouth slightly open. He hardly called Harry names any more, and he had not laid a finger on him all summer. Most evenings he went out into the back garden in his white karate suit, practising the same slow, careful movements by the shed without being told. When his father said the freaks should be rounded up, Dudley put down his spoon and opened his mouth, as he had over the karate leaflet, then shut it again without a word. Harry wondered whether his cousin was growing up, and hardly dared hope it.

Dudley was frightened of wizards, with reason. The first he ever met gave him a pig's tail, which his parents paid a private hospital in London to remove. Then came Dumbledore in the front room, then the Ministry wizards who punctured Aunt Marge. He kept a hand over his bottom, and went from room to room sideways, so as not to offer the enemy the same target twice. When the Weasleys arrived he fled to the kitchen. When Arthur Weasley kindly asked whether he was having a good holiday, he whimpered. Then he ate a Ton-Tongue Toffee that Fred had dropped on purpose, and his tongue grew to four feet long before his parents would let Arthur shrink it. Fred and George called him a great bullying git. Harry agreed, then thought of Dudley making room for him on the sofa, and was no longer sure it was true.

Book Four, Chapter Five: at the Burrow somebody took in the oldest jeans Dudley had ever handed down to Harry, which he had always had to roll up three times at the ankle. Harry had written the Stunning Spell in the back of one of Dudley's old exercise books. In Chapter Six, at the World Cup final, Hermione added the veela to a list she keeps, which already had the Dursleys on it.

In their own words

Why would anyone be against people saving people's lives?Dudley Dursley · B4 Ch3

pages.html:
Ronald Bilius Weasley (born 1 March 1980) is a pure-blood wizard of Gryffindor House, the youngest son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He has been Harry Potter's best friend since 1991. In 1992 he flew his father's car to rescue Harry from a barred window, not long after playing the best game of chess Hogwarts had seen in years. In June 1994 he stood on a broken leg between Harry and Sirius Black. He watches the long war between Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy over Harry with a weary, knowing sigh. In August 1994, with his pen pal Pansy Parkinson, he hatched a secret plan to bring Harry and Dracina together. He hides from everybody that he fancies Hermione himself.

Early life

Ron is the sixth of seven children and the youngest of six sons. He was raised at the Burrow, determined to live up to five older brothers. Almost everything he owned came to him second-hand: Bill's old robes, Charlie's chipped wand with its unicorn hair nearly coming out, and Percy's old rat Scabbers, handed down because the family could not afford an owl.

He has red hair and freckles. He collects Chocolate Frog cards, about five hundred of them, and supports the Chudley Cannons. His bedroom, at the top of the house under the ghoul's attic, is painted a violent orange and covered in Cannons posters, with a plaque on the door that reads Ronald's Room.

His older brothers shaped him. When he was three, Fred turned his teddy bear into a spider for breaking Fred's toy broomstick, and Ron has been terrified of spiders ever since. At seven, Fred gave him an Acid Pop, calling it a Sugar Quill, and it burnt right through his tongue. He plays wizard chess with his grandfather's battered set, whose pieces obey him completely. His uncle Bilius saw a Grim and died the next day.

First year (1991 to 1992)

Ron met Harry on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991. When Dracina Malfoy insulted both their families, he squared up to her. Sorted into Gryffindor, pale green with nerves, he rebuked Dracina for calling Hermione a Mudblood. Yet on Hallowe'en he called Hermione a nightmare within her hearing. That night he levitated the troll's own club and dropped it on its head. The blow saved Harry, Hermione and Dracina. He alone noticed the jealous looks between the two girls afterwards, which puzzled him for years. In the Mirror of Erised he saw himself standing alone, older, Head Boy, Quidditch captain, holding the House Cup and the Quidditch Cup. He warned Harry not to go back to it.

At the Hufflepuff match, provoked by Dracina, he threw himself at her and came off badly. She bit his ear, leaving a small crescent scar, scratched four lines down his cheek and tore out a patch of hair above one temple. He gave her a black eye, which he said she had run into. Norbert bit his hand, which swelled up green. When the school turned on Harry over the lost points, Ron alone walked beside him down every corridor.

Under the trapdoor he directed the black pieces in the giant chess game, and he let the white queen strike him down so that Harry could go on. It won Gryffindor fifty points, for the best-played game of chess the school had seen in many years.

Second year (1992 to 1993)

Ron wrote to Harry about twelve times in the summer of 1992. When none of the letters was answered, he flew his father's enchanted Ford Anglia to Privet Drive with Fred and George. He hauled the bars off Harry's window and pulled him free of Vernon Dursley's grip. Shaken, he told his mother that the Dursleys had been starving Harry. From then on he quietly put extra sausages on Harry's plate at every meal. When the barrier at King's Cross sealed itself, he flew the car north to Hogwarts and crashed it into the Whomping Willow. The crash snapped his wand, but he knocked Harry clear of a falling branch.

His Spellotaped wand misfired all year. It raised a green boil between Flitwick's eyes, and when he tried to curse Dracina it set him belching slugs. It blew purple bubbles, and it whistled like a kettle. In detention he polished the trophy room's silver and was sick over a Special Award for Services to the School, which later let him recognise Tom Riddle's name. Disguised as Crabbe, he nearly gave himself away by correcting Dracina about Percy's name, and he filed away her mention of a hidden room at Malfoy Manor. He followed the spiders into the Forest, where one of them carried him off, and found his father's car living wild.

When Ginny was taken into the Chamber, Lockhart seized Ron's broken wand to cast a Memory Charm. Its backfire brought the tunnel roof down. Ron kicked the unconscious Lockhart, for Ginny and for his wand. Then he cleared a gap in the rubble for Harry's return. He won a Special Award for Services to the School and two hundred points. He glared at Dumbledore for sending Harry back to the Dursleys.

Third year (1993 to 1994)

In the summer of 1993 Ron telephoned Privet Drive, shouting, because he thought telephones had to be yelled into. Then he spent a month in Egypt with Bill, and appeared in the Daily Prophet with Scabbers. His new wand from Ollivander's is willow and unicorn tail-hair, fourteen inches. At school he kept filling Harry's plate, saying 'Eat'. His boggart was a six-foot spider, which he defeated by taking away its legs.

On Hallowe'en night, sleeping in the Great Hall, he lay crossways above Harry and the two girls. He vowed before Merlin and God to look after Harry himself, because the womenfolk were not to be trusted. He threw a crocodile heart into Dracina's face after her dementor imitation. It cost Gryffindor fifty points, and ten more when he said it was worth it. He was outraged that the twins gave the Marauder's Map to Harry: 'I'm their brother.'

He stayed at Hogwarts for Christmas, claiming he wanted to avoid Percy. He told Harry that the Weasleys were his family: too many redheads, but his if he wanted it. When Scabbers vanished, leaving blood on his sheet and ginger hairs on the floor, he blamed Crookshanks. He grieved more than anyone expected. After the Ravenclaw match he woke to find Sirius Black slashing his bed curtains with a knife, and he punched him in the face. The knife grew longer every time he told the story. On the day Buckbeak lost his case, he chose to forgive Hermione first and took over the appeal research. During the exams he carried her bag and made her cocoa, gazing at her with a puzzled frown.

On 6 June 1994 he chased Scabbers across the lawn and was dragged under the Whomping Willow by a black dog, his leg snapping on a root. In the Shrieking Shack he stood in front of Harry and told Black he would knock his head off first. He learnt that the rat his family had kept for twelve years was Peter Pettigrew, and took it as a personal insult. He joined in the Disarming Charm that knocked out Snape. Going pink, he asked Hermione to remind him never to forget her birthday. He chained himself to Pettigrew on the side nearest Harry. Pettigrew struck him down with Lupin's wand, and he lay unconscious through Sirius's rescue. Afterwards he admitted that he had been wondering about God since seeing Harry's Patronus.

On the castle steps at the end of term, Dracina flew at Pansy Parkinson. Ron handed Harry his bag, marched up with his mother's set to his shoulders and told Dracina quietly that no friendship was worth destroying with that kind of anger. He did not notice Pansy gazing at him afterwards. He adopted the tiny owl Sirius sent, after checking with Crookshanks that it was definitely an owl.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In August 1994 Ron wrote that his father had got tickets for the Quidditch World Cup final, Ireland against Bulgaria. The Weasleys would come for Harry at five o'clock on Sunday, he wrote, whatever the Dursleys said. He passed on the news that Percy had started work at the Ministry, and that Hermione was arriving that afternoon. He had sent Harry a birthday cake, and he now claimed to know how to use a 'fellytone'.

Book Four, Chapter Four: On Sunday 21 August 1994 Ron came to Privet Drive by Floo with his father and the twins. He grinned broadly when his father faced Uncle Vernon down, having evidently seen that look before. Harry had seen it too, on Ron himself, white to the lips on a broken leg in the Shrieking Shack, refusing to let Sirius Black past because Harry was his best mate. Ron cheerfully told the Dursleys he would see them, then went home through the green fire with a yell. His attic bedroom at the Burrow still had its whirling Chudley Cannons posters, but four beds were now crammed into it, because the twins had given their room to Bill and Charlie. Pigwidgeon lived there too, since he annoyed Errol and Hermes. Ron called him Pig and grumbled about him, though Harry did not believe a word of it.

Ron mocked Percy's report on cauldron thickness, then was horrified to realise that he had briefly agreed with the least cool of his brothers. Percy was obsessed with his boss, Mr Crouch, he told Harry; the two of them would be announcing their engagement any day, and Crouch even agreed with all the scary things Percy wanted. When Hermione gave Harry her whole attention, a quick, miserable look crossed Ron's face before he chased it away. In the shed that night his ears went pink as she talked about the rats. He looked at her the way he had in the Shrieking Shack, as though he had never seen anybody quite like her.

When Hermione explained the internet to him, Ron admitted that his father had explained it at Easter, and that he had only been teasing. She slapped his arm, which seemed oddly to please him. He had learnt all about the Myst game from her letters that summer, wanted to play it, and admitted that he had been getting into puzzles; Harry told him nobody could beat him at chess. Ron refused to let Harry spend his gold on a computer for the Weasleys, saying he would not use his best mate. His eyes went suspiciously bright when Harry insisted.

Before bed he sent Pig north with a three-page letter to his pen pal. The first page was headed OPERATION GET IT OVER WITH. The second, headed PLAN C (IF THE BOAT ONE DOESN'T WORK EITHER), had Harry's name on it eleven times, Dracina's twelve. The pen pal was Pansy Parkinson, who had recently bought a Chudley Cannons poster that clashed with everything she owned; Ron thought this showed excellent taste. The two of them were scheming to bring Harry and Dracina together. It never once crossed Ron's mind to wonder why she was so very keen to help.

Book Four, Chapter Five: Pansy's reply came back before dawn on 22 August. Ron tried, not at all subtly, to hide it in his back pocket, then read it on his bed under his orange posters. He thought her brilliant, like Hermione, only on his side for once. The boat plan was out of the question, she wrote, since Dracina would not get into a boat, while Plan C was worse. They would do Plan A, properly. Past the big pine with the forked trunk, at the top of the Bulgarian end of the wood, she had found a clearing where a fallen tree lay beside a stream. She had hung it with fairy lanterns, which impressed Ron more than anything. After the match he was to bring Harry, looking presentable, while she brought Dracina on the pretext of a lost earring. Then they would leave the pair alone, finding something to do with themselves for an hour; Ron would have to walk Pansy back to her tent.

She told him to wear the maroon jumper, because it suited him. Ron, who had told his mother the Christmas before that he would sooner be seen dead in maroon, decided it was camouflage for the dark wood. He supposed that Yours was simply how Slytherins signed their letters. He quite forgot her postscript telling him to burn the letter, because Dracina reads everything. Rolled in his spare socks he kept a comb borrowed from Percy without mentioning it, a bottle of Sleekeazy's Hair Potion that had cost two weeks' pocket money and a box of the best Honeydukes chocolates. With them was a list headed THINGS HARRY COULD SAY, crossed out except for one line of Ron's own: Harry could tell Dracina that she looked nice.

Ron's motive was gratitude. Harry had never once made him feel poor, had shared everything from the first day and had snatched Pig out of the air for him on the train. A small voice at the back of his head suggested that if Harry were with Dracina, then Hermione would be free. Ron's ears went hot, and he did not let it finish. When his mother asked about his pen pal, he told her he was entitled to some privacy; she already knew the pen pal was a girl. At the gate, having seen Harry hold back tears, Ron said nothing, but rested a hand on his shoulder for a few steps.

At the campsite he recognised the Malfoys' silk tent at once. He called Viktor Krum a genius, and declared, after seeing old Archie in a nightgown, that a man should not wear women's clothes. When Hermione snarled at Harry's wave to Cho Chang, Ron calmly prised her fingers off Harry's arm one at a time. That afternoon he slipped away for nearly half an hour, claiming to need the loo. Harry saw him under the forked pine with Pansy, who pressed something into his hand; he came back with leaves in his hair, very pleased with himself. He drew a small pencil cross on the campsite map at the top of the wood, asked Harry whether a girl would prefer chocolates or flowers, then insisted that they were not for Pansy. Harry should look smart after the match, Ron told him, just in case. Harry, who had guessed that the pen pal was Pansy, took her for Ron's sweetheart, resolving to help him from a distance.

Ron had saved his pocket money all summer for the World Cup. He bought a hat of dancing shamrocks, a huge green rosette and a tiny figure of Viktor Krum. He has always been sensitive about money, since Harry has a small fortune while Ron has a family of nine. He accepted Harry's gift of Omnioculars on the understanding that he would get nothing for Christmas for ten years.

Book Four, Chapter Six: Ron insisted on bringing his rucksack to the Top Box, clutching it to his chest all evening. Testing his Omnioculars, he found Pansy below the box, a single blaze of Chudley Cannons orange among the Bulgarians. He signalled to her: two taps on the nose, a finger at the back of Harry's head, one finger held up, then an enormous wink. He repeated the signals after every Irish goal, until Hermione asked whether he was all right. After Narcissa Malfoy's talk with Harry he consulted a crumpled sheet of parchment hidden in his programme, muttering that everything was going as planned. He did not know that Pansy had loved him for months; Dracina worked it out that night, following Pansy's gaze through her own Omnioculars.

Entranced by the veela, Ron froze with his arms out, pulling the shamrocks off his hat without noticing, until his father took it away. He gave Harry a handful of leprechaun gold for the Omnioculars, gloating that Harry now had to buy him a Christmas present. He dreaded Krum catching the Snitch during Lynch's time out, then demanded a time out himself when Krum's nose was broken. He called Krum an idiot for ending the match while Ireland led by 160 points. Ireland had won, he decided, because the whole team came from the same country, which he was sure would have impressed Dean Thomas.

When Pansy came up to the box to fetch Dracina, Ron became very interested in the ceiling. Then he exchanged a single solemn nod with Pansy, like a general across a battlefield. He got rid of Hermione by claiming that Ginny felt sick, then told his father that he and Harry were off to watch the Irish dance. At the bottom of the stairs he unrolled his socks, handed Harry the comb and, his ears bright red, begged him to try to do something about his hair. It was important, he said: 'Life or death. Well. Life.' Then he led Harry past the Bulgarian tents towards the pine with the forked trunk, to begin Plan A. Harry supposed that Ron was meeting Pansy, and wanted a friend there for moral support.

Personality

Ron is loyal, funny, quick-tempered and practical. He is the friend who notices when Harry has not eaten, and who makes tea, because that is what his mother does when anyone is upset. He reads people better than Harry does. He saw Dracina's feelings for Harry long before Harry did, and he suspected Hermione of taking Dracina's brooch. He repeats his father's line, 'Women...', with a two-handed shrug he cannot explain. He holds that a gentleman wizard never hits a girl, a rule his mother taught him and he has learnt the hard way.

He shares some of his family's blind spots. His remarks about 'Dean's people' and foreign footballers have strained his friendship with Dean Thomas. He resents Dumbledore, whom his mother condemned for leaving Harry with the Dursleys for eleven years. When Harry praises the headmaster, though, he keeps quiet, letting Harry keep his faith.

Relationships

Harry became his best mate in their first autumn. Ron treats him as a brother, guarding him against the Dursleys, against Sirius Black and, when necessary, against the girls who love him. Hermione is his friend and his sparring partner. By June 1994 she was also something more puzzling. By August 1994 he had come to fancy her, a feeling he hides from everybody, himself included.

Dracina bit him, mocked his family's poverty and called him the Weasel. Yet he sometimes looks sorry for her. Since halfway through their first year he has heaved a particular long-suffering sigh about her and Harry. He and Pansy Parkinson once caught each other sighing in exactly the same way at Dracina's behaviour.

Pansy Parkinson became his pen pal in the summer of 1994, then his partner in Plan A. She has been in love with him for months, though it has never once crossed his mind.

In their own words

My dad always used to say, 'Women...'Ron Weasley · B1 Ch6
She bit me. She's mental, Harry. Properly mental.Ron Weasley · B1 Ch9
I always said he was as mental as a soup sandwich.Ron Weasley · B1 Ch13
Oh, Harry. I missed you, mate.Ron Weasley · B2 Ch3
