pages.html:
Molly Weasley, née Prewett (born 30 October 1949), is a witch, the wife of Arthur Weasley and the mother of seven children. She is a short, warm, formidable woman. In the summer of 1992 she learnt how the Dursleys were treating Harry Potter, and she has treated him as one of her own ever since. She has made her anger about it felt by the Dursleys, by Albus Dumbledore and by anyone else in range. In the summer of 1994 she joined Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy in a secret campaign against the Dursleys, which she hides from Harry. She keeps Dracina's letters in a box under her bed, having privately decided that Dracina would make Harry a wonderful wife.

Family and home

Molly was born a Prewett. Her brothers, Fabian and Gideon, were killed fighting Death Eaters in the first war against Voldemort. She married Arthur Weasley in 1969, so that by 1994 they had been married twenty-five years.

They have seven children. Bill is the eldest, then Charlie, then Percy, then the twins, Fred and George. Ron comes next, and Ginny is the youngest. With five of them still at home in 1991 she had little time to spare, which is why Ron's sandwiches were always corned beef, though he cannot stand it. A second cousin is an accountant, whom the family never mentions. She tells her children that the Weasleys are an old and proper family.

She wears a flowered apron with her wand in the pocket, and she is an excellent cook. The clock on her kitchen wall has one hand and no numbers. It tells the family when it is time to make tea or to feed the chickens. Every Christmas she knits each of her children a jumper. She keeps Gilderoy Lockhart's Guide to Household Pests on the kitchen mantelpiece, because she fancies him. When the family ghoul gets noisy she quietens it by going up with a poker.

As a girl she gave a boy three drops of love potion in his pumpkin juice every morning for a fortnight, over the Easter holidays. Looking at Arthur, she implied that he had chosen to stay without it. She has views on Minerva McGonagall. She calls her a sweetheart, then adds that she knows where McGonagall has been and who she knows.

Harry Potter

Molly sent Harry an emerald-green jumper with a box of home-made fudge for Christmas 1991, though Ron had told her Harry was not expecting anything. At King's Cross in 1992 she sensed more in his thanks than he meant to show. She watched Vernon Dursley's rudeness with thin lips.

That summer her sons brought Harry to the Burrow in the flying car. She confronted them in the yard like a mother bear, but she told Harry that she was not angry with him in the least. She noticed the bruise Vernon had left round his ankle, and gently drew out the truth. She held him while he wept. She told him to stay for as long as he wanted, a promise she repeated all summer. She refused his money for school things, but let him buy her a box of Chocolate Frogs, which nearly made her cry. When Ron wondered how they would explain a lost Harry to the Dursleys, she burst out that Harry was not going back there.

She wrote to Dumbledore stating where Harry would live from now on. She told him, too, what she thought of a headmaster who had let the abuse go on for eleven years. Dumbledore said he had never been shouted at like it. On the night Ginny came back from the Chamber of Secrets, Molly called Harry and Ron the two bravest boys in all the world.

Then she weighed up Dracina Malfoy, as a mother weighs up a son's future wife. She thanked her for healing Ginny. After that she told her sweetly that if she broke Harry's heart, she would kill her slowly. She shouted at Dumbledore for sending Harry back to Surrey. After Ron's telephone call in 1993 she wrote to Dumbledore again, and the owl came back with scorch marks.

On 31 August 1993 she dropped her shopping to hug Harry, then kept filling his plate. She argued that he should not be told Sirius Black was after him, because he was happy not knowing. She packed him the thickest sandwiches for the train, with a card that read 'For the train. Eat ALL of it. M.W.' She wrote to her five children at Hogwarts that Harry had nobody at home to notice if he did something stupid, so they must keep him alive between them.

In June 1994 Hermione and Dracina sent her twenty pages about the Dursleys by one owl. She read them without a word. Then she looked east, towards Surrey, and smiled a smile that sent Arthur straight back out to his shed. At King's Cross she gave Vernon a long, measuring look that made him step back on to a pigeon.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

When the Dursleys' household diet left Harry hungry, Molly fed him by owl. She sent fruitcake, meat pies, home-made biscuits and a plate of Sunday roast with Yorkshire pudding. One parcel held a steak and ale pie, charmed to stay hot. With them came a note saying that he was one of the family, and that he was being looked after in all matters.

She wrote to the Dursleys asking for Harry to come to the Quidditch World Cup, then stay for the rest of the summer. She underlined 'I will be waiting' three times, adding 'P.S. Actions have consequences.' Harry deduced that she was behind the pond mud that erupted from the Dursleys' kitchen plughole on 20 August 1994. She had been sending letters all summer, and would not tell Ron to whom. She spoke of other plans if the Dursleys refused, at which Arthur left the room.

Book Four, Chapter Four: The pond mud had done its work. Harry suspected that Molly's real point was to shame Aunt Petunia before the neighbours, who were soon talking about the Dursleys' drains; Petunia did not set foot outside her front door afterwards. When Harry arrived at the Burrow on 21 August 1994, Molly swept across the kitchen to hug him so hard that it knocked his glasses sideways. She whispered into his hair that he was safe, that he was home. Then she drew a long, slow breath through her nose. When she let him go her eyes went first to Hermione, who gave the smallest of nods. Molly was secretly allied with Hermione and Dracina Malfoy to torment the Dursleys on Harry's behalf. She lied to Harry to keep it from him.

She was in a temper with the twins. Cleaning their room that summer, she had found their order forms for Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, forbidden them to make any more joke goods and burnt the forms. She was angry, too, that they had got fewer O.W.L.s than she expected, since she wanted them to join the Ministry like their father. She had had more owls from Hogwarts about them, she said, than about all her other children together, and feared they would end up before the Improper Use of Magic Office. Cooking in a rage, she made the potatoes burst out of their skins to ping round the kitchen, sent a dustpan after them, set knives chopping and poured a creamy sauce from the tip of her wand. She picked up one of the twins' fake wands, which squeaked and turned into a rubber mouse; later she found another in the bread basket.

When Harry noticed an envelope on the mantelpiece, addressed to her in green ink in a small, neat, spiky hand very like Dracina's, she slipped it into her apron pocket. It was from the school, she told him, about the twins. When he thanked her for the sink, she said that the mud had been only a little nudge, which would have worn off by now. She would never do anything truly unkind to anybody, she said, whatever they had done; that was not how things were done in her house. It was a lie told to protect the alliance. Harry believed her.

Later Harry heard Arthur telling her quietly about the Dursleys, in words that seemed to include bag and skirting board. Then Molly began to cackle, high, cracked and utterly delighted, like the Wicked Witch of the West. Ginny explained that she had been doing it since July, and that their father said it was good for her. At dinner Molly's gaze kept drifting east towards Surrey with nothing kind in it, only fury and a grim, patient relish. She asked Arthur whether he had mended the Dursleys' wall, reminding him drily of his half a life campaigning against the mistreatment of Muggles.

She passed on Muriel's report of a witch in Godalming whose windows had been broken twice. She told, too, of Mrs Fenwick's front door, painted with a great fist above the words HUMANS FIRST. Muggles, she said, always used to be such nice, unobservant people. When Harry spoke of Muggles with powers, she told him kindly that Muggles cannot have powers, because that is what makes them Muggles. She took Bill to task about his fang earring, wishing aloud that he would let her trim his ponytail. He pointed out that she had written him only one letter all summer, about his hair. Her many other letters that summer had gone to her allies.

Over pudding she described house gnomes to Harry, at length and quite placidly. They are thinner cousins of the garden gnome, with sharper teeth, she said. They get into the walls of Muggle houses, chew the wiring, turn the milk, steal one sock of every pair and whisper until the Muggles wonder whether they are going mad. They breed every six weeks or so. They live on spite, so that the nastier a household is, the more gnomes it gets. They were a sort of judgement, she said, which Arthur thought rather fair. Then she assured Harry that house gnomes are terribly rare in towns, so he could not have seen one. She meant to buy everyone's school things in Diagon Alley the next day, in case there was no time after the Cup; the last final had lasted five days.

Book Four, Chapter Five: Before dawn on 22 August Molly woke Harry by tucking his blanket back round him, then smoothing his fringe off his forehead with a warm hand. Harry could not remember anybody ever doing that. In the kitchen she was murmuring to Hermione about something that had happened twice in one night, with a second plumber who would not set foot in the kitchen. When Harry came in she said brightly that she had been talking about her own sink. When Arthur murmured about six weeks being right on time, she silenced him with his name. She gave Harry the biggest bowl of porridge, under a golden spiral of treacle, telling him that he was nothing but elbows.

She Summoned the Ton-Tongue Toffees the twins had hidden about them, threw them in the bin and said it was no wonder they had not got more O.W.L.s. The twins left without a word to her. She asked Hermione what to wear on the Muggle side of the barrier at King's Cross, where she meant to take the children the following week; her hat, George admitted, did hum slightly. When she asked Ron, in the voice that had kept seven children in order for over twenty years, whether his letter was from his pen pal, he told her that he was entitled to some privacy. She knew that his pen pal was a girl, and gave Harry a knowing look across the kitchen.

She had her own reasons for knowing. In a box under her bed she keeps Dracina's letters, written on very good parchment in small, spiky writing in green ink. She has read every one of them twice. She has decided that Miss Malfoy is a delightful young lady who would make Harry a wonderful wife one day, but she has told nobody.

She gave Harry corned beef sandwiches with the crusts cut off, in case Arthur forgot that they all needed feeding. At the gate, in her old coat over her dressing gown, she straightened Harry's collar. Why, she asked, could he not have one nice, quiet year at Hogwarts? When he joked that he loved danger, she held him firmly by both shoulders. 'You deserve some peace, Harry,' she said fiercely. 'You do. More than anybody I know.' Harry nearly cried, then stepped out of her grip with a joke about squashing the sandwiches. When he looked back, she was a small dark shape beside her lantern by the gate, watching them go. Around midday she sent Bill, Charlie and Percy on to the campsite.

Book Four, Chapter Six: At the final, Ron told Hermione that his mother would want her to walk Ginny back to the tents. Fred and George, who had fixed the result to win their bet, meant never to tell their mother how they had done it.

Personality

Molly is loving, practical and fierce. Her children know the face she had on the morning she came back from the Prewetts', the time Bill told them about. It is the face that means somebody's house is getting taken apart. She taught her sons never to hit a girl, and never to go into a girls' bathroom. She forbade the twins to tell Ron the Angelus stories. In Egypt she would not let Ginny see the mummies. She nearly cried when Percy said he wanted to be Minister for Magic so that he could help poor families. Since July 1994 she has taken to cackling like the Wicked Witch of the West, which Arthur thinks is good for her. Her voice has kept seven children in order for over twenty years.

In their own words

You're to stay here, Harry. For as long as you want.Molly Weasley · B2 Ch4
He's not going back there, Ronald!Molly Weasley · B2 Ch5
If you break Harry's heart, I'll kill you slowly.Molly Weasley · B2 Ch19
P.S. Actions have consequences.Molly Weasley · B4 Ch3

pages.html:
Ginevra Molly Weasley, known as Ginny (born 11 August 1981), is a witch of Gryffindor House. She is the youngest of the seven Weasley children, Arthur and Molly's only daughter. Red-haired and brown-eyed, she began Hogwarts in 1992 with a hopeless crush on Harry Potter. She spent her first year shadowing Dracina Malfoy and the diary of Tom Riddle. In the end she was dragged into the Chamber of Secrets, where Riddle began to drain her life.

Early life

Ginny is the seventh Weasley child, and the first girl born into the family for generations. Since she was six she has been creeping into the broom shed to borrow her brothers' broomsticks, and none of them has ever found out.

In September 1991 she ran along Platform Nine and Three-Quarters after the Hogwarts Express until it gathered speed. The following summer, at King's Cross, she squealed, pointed at Harry Potter, and was told that it was rude to point.

She talked about Harry all summer. When he came to stay at the Burrow in 1992 she was so shy that she squeaked and fled. She knocked things over. Once she put both elbows in the butter dish. Ron said that normally she never stopped talking. Many of her school things were second-hand, so Harry gave her the set of Lockhart books he had been given free.

First year (1992 to 1993)

At Flourish and Blotts Ginny stood slightly in front of Harry and told Dracina Malfoy to leave him alone. It was the first thing she had ever said in his presence. When Dracina mocked her second-hand books, Ginny threw Dracina's new books at her head and screamed names at her. Lucius Malfoy had meant to slip Tom Riddle's diary into Ginny's cauldron, but in the struggle it went to Dracina instead. Dracina called her Little Weasel, made her cry and hissed at her like a snake.

Ginny was sorted into Gryffindor on 1 September 1992. On the way to King's Cross that morning the car had to turn back, because she had left her own diary on her bed: a pink one with a lock, from her mother.

She went red whenever Harry was near. She drank Percy's Pepperup Potion in one gulp to impress him, with steam pouring out of her hair. She wished him luck in a rush before the Slytherin match, and at Christmas she gave him a painted card of himself catching the Snitch. On Valentine's Day a dwarf sang him her Valentine, about his raven hair and frog-green eyes. Dracina mocked it until Ginny ran away in tears.

She became friends with Colin Creevey over their shared admiration of Harry. After the attack on Mrs Norris she cried every night, being a great lover of cats. She told Harry and Ron that Dracina had pointed at Hermione on Hallowe'en, then smiled at Ginny as if she were writing her name down somewhere. When Dracina stopped her by the Charms classroom and asked whether she loved him, Ginny ran. When she looked back, Dracina was writing in a little black book.

From then on Ginny watched. She grew pale and thin. Her fingers were stained with ink, and her nightmares woke her dormitory. For weeks she stalked Dracina, hiding behind pillars. Twice she tried to tell Harry what she had seen, the second time three days before the exams, rocking in her seat. Each time Percy interrupted.

Soon afterwards she followed Dracina and the diary into the Chamber of Secrets. There the possessed Dracina struck her with the diary, drawing blood from her temple to write the second message on the wall. Riddle began to take her life force to restore himself.

She woke after the Basilisk's death. Dracina healed the cut on her temple, and Ginny thanked her. When her mother asked what had happened, Ginny shielded Dracina, saying that nasty Tom Riddle had hit her with the diary. By the end of term she was perfectly happy again. On the train home she let slip that she had walked in on Percy kissing Penelope Clearwater, and she asked the others not to tease him.

Second year (1993 to 1994)

In the summer of 1993 Ginny went to Egypt with the family. Her mother would not let her in to see the mummies, and by Ron's count she asked about Harry nine times a day. She was embarrassed whenever she saw him, since he had saved her life. When the dementor boarded the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1993 she shook badly. Afterwards she sobbed.

She wears an HP badge as a member of Colin Creevey's Harry Potter fan club. She and Colin have been best friends since the Basilisk. After Harry's fall in the Hufflepuff match she brought him a lumpy, home-made singing card with a lion on it, then fled. In early 1994 she sat where she could see him, and she went silent whenever Sirius Black was mentioned.

When Scabbers vanished she quietly pushed the toast rack towards Ron. At the victory party after the Ravenclaw match she held the Firebolt, said she would tell Charlie, and admitted that she had watched the whole match through her fingers.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: When Harry arrived at the Burrow on 21 August 1994, Ginny, her red hair tied back, went scarlet as he grinned at her, as she had at every sight of him since his first visit. Hermione turned to watch her with a very calm look that went on a little too long. Harry could see that Ginny was still smitten, but thought her much too young for him, as well as his best friend's sister. Since the Chamber she had been as thick as thieves with Colin Creevey, closer still now with their fan club and its round red badges.

Ginny told Harry that she had named Ron's owl Pigwidgeon, because she thought it sweet. She explained that her mother had been cackling since July, saying that their father thought it good for her. The family, she said, had heard explosions from the twins' room for ages, but thought they just liked the noise. At dinner she told her mother that she liked Bill's long hair, calling her old-fashioned; it was nowhere near as long as Professor Dumbledore's, she added.

Book Four, Chapter Five: The next morning Ginny came down last, pale and bleary, having been looking for her other sock. She asked why they had to be up so early. On Stoatshead Hill she went scarlet when Cedric Diggory shook her hand. At the campsite she asked why Ludo Bagman, as Head of Magical Games and Sports, did not know better than to talk about Bludgers near Muggles.

Book Four, Chapter Six: In the Top Box she leant out over the front, white with horror, at both of Aidan Lynch's crashes; her brother Charlie reassured her that Lynch had only been ploughed. Afterwards she looked rather green, which let Ron claim she was sick, so that Hermione would have to walk her back to the tents. Ginny insisted that she was fine.

Relationships

Ginny's feelings for Harry are unresolved. Harry thinks of her as his best friend's little sister and nothing more. She was quietly saddened to hear him shout that she was not his girlfriend.

Her dealings with Dracina Malfoy began with books thrown in Flourish and Blotts and passed through fear, but after the Chamber she chose to protect Dracina. She is close to Colin Creevey. She is fond of her brothers, despite their teasing, and she keeps Percy's secrets.

In their own words

I'm going to kill you.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch9
It's not funny. It's not funny, Ron.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch10
It was that nasty Tom Riddle. He hit me, Mum! With the diary.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch19
I watched the whole thing through my fingers.Ginny Weasley · B3 Ch13

pages.html:
Fred Weasley (born 1 April 1978), George's twin, is the fourth son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He is a wizard of Gryffindor House, where he plays Beater for the house team, and with his brother he is the school's leading practical joker. In 1992 he drove the flying car that rescued Harry Potter from Privet Drive, and in 1993 he gave Harry the Marauder's Map. With George he invents the joke goods of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, among them Ton-Tongue Toffee. In August 1994 the twins quietly fixed the final of the Quidditch World Cup to win their bet with Ludo Bagman.

Family and character

The twins are tall and broad-shouldered. Their mother knits them Weasley jumpers lettered F and G. As George once pointed out, this is hardly necessary, since they know perfectly well that they are called Gred and Forge.

Some of Fred's mischief has been unkind. When Ron was three, Fred turned his teddy bear into a great spider because Ron had broken his toy broomstick, and Ron has been afraid of spiders ever since. When Ron was seven, Fred gave him an Acid Pop and told him it was a Sugar Quill. It burnt straight through Ron's tongue, and their mother went after Fred with her broom. He also told Ron that the Sorting meant wrestling a troll. His great friend outside the family is Lee Jordan.

Fred is curious about Muggles. He thinks Muggle tricks such as lock-picking are well worth learning, and from the window of the flying car in 1992 he asked Harry who Superman was. He told Harry that the Malfoys had been Dark wizards since the Norman Conquest, and that his father believed Lucius had been in Voldemort's inner circle.

Pranks

In their first week at Hogwarts the twins found a secret passage behind Gregory the Smarmy. Before their first year was out they had taken the Marauder's Map from a drawer in Filch's office marked Confiscated and Highly Dangerous. Filch now keeps a drawer of punishment records for the two of them alone.

In December 1991 they bewitched snowballs to bounce off the back of Quirrell's turban. They made Christmas baubles that burst into live slugs. They pinched Percy's prefect badge, which they later bewitched to read Pinhead, then Bighead Boy.

Fred once fed a Filibuster firework to a Salamander in the common room. He supplied the fireworks for Harry's diversion in Potions. With George he enchanted about twenty suits of armour in the Entrance Hall to dance the can-can, a routine that took twenty-six hours to time. When the school suspected Harry of being the Heir of Slytherin, Fred paraded ahead of him through the corridors crying, 'Heir of Slytherin coming through! Thoroughly evil!'

Quidditch

Fred has been a Beater for Gryffindor since before Harry joined the team. In Harry's first match he drove off a Bludger aimed at Harry and belted it at Marcus Flint. In November 1992 he guarded Harry from the rogue Bludger, then wrestled it back into its box.

He once fell asleep on Alicia Spinnet's shoulder during one of Oliver Wood's tactics talks. At another team meeting Wood whacked him across the knees with a Beater's bat. In the 1994 final he hit Flint on the back of the head with his club after Flint barged Angelina Johnson.

Fred and Harry

In the summer of 1992 Fred drove the Ford Anglia to Privet Drive, though he was still working out how the Muggle machine handled; the twins had already flown it five or six times without being seen. In December 1993 he and George gave Harry the Marauder's Map. They offered to go with him whenever he went after Sirius Black, on condition that he told them first.

Ron once reported Fred's opinion of Harry: 'Fred reckons you're the funniest bloke in this school and nobody's noticed because they're all too busy looking at your forehead.'

Fred is wary of Dracina Malfoy. He checked his toast for poison after she praised his home-made fireworks. He saw her pass a full salt shaker with her supposedly injured arm, and he suspected her of bribing the house-elves with something dead.

After the Ravenclaw match in 1994 he fetched crates of butterbeer, pumpkin fizz and Honeydukes sweets for the party. He gave all the credit to Messrs Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot and Prongs. He taught Ron the swear word that Sirius Black most admired. In June 1994 he scraped through his O.W.L.s with a few passes and celebrated as if he had won the World Cup. He was sixteen that August.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: On Sunday 21 August 1994 Fred came to Privet Drive by Floo with his father, George and Ron. The twins fetched Harry's trunk, hoping for a look at Dudley, about whom they had heard a great deal. Then Fred dropped a bag of Ton-Tongue Toffees on the Dursleys' carpet, quite deliberately, and left one behind. He waved merrily at the Dursleys before Flooing home first. Dudley ate the toffee. At the Burrow Fred explained that the twins had invented Ton-Tongue Toffee, then spent all summer looking for somebody to test it on. When his father shouted at him, Fred said that he had only dropped it; it was Dudley's own fault for eating it.

The twins were in disgrace with their mother. She had found the order forms for Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, their business in fake wands, trick sweets and other joke goods, which they had meant to sell at Hogwarts. She burnt the forms, forbidding them to make any more. She was angry, too, that they had got fewer O.W.L.s than she expected. She wanted them to join the Ministry, but they told her they wanted to open a joke shop. At dinner Fred pointed out that Bulgaria had Viktor Krum. He also whispered to Harry that the twins had sent the dragon dung that Percy insisted was a sample of fertiliser from Norway.

Book Four, Chapter Five: The next morning Fred hid Ton-Tongue Toffees in the turn-ups of his jeans. As his mother Summoned them out to throw them away, he bellowed that they had spent six months developing them; the twins left for the World Cup without a word to her. Fred told Harry that Charlie had failed his first Apparition test. After the Portkey landing he stopped trying to get up, just to listen to Harry swearing. With George he stared daggers at Cedric Diggory's back, never having forgiven Hufflepuff for beating Gryffindor the year before.

At lunch the twins bet Ludo Bagman thirty-seven Galleons, fifteen Sickles and three Knuts, all their savings, that Ireland would win but Viktor Krum would catch the Snitch. Fred threw in a fake wand, which turned into a rubber chicken, to Bagman's delight. When Percy boasted that Mr Crouch spoke over two hundred languages, among them Troll, Fred said that anyone could speak Troll by pointing and grunting. Crouch called Percy Weatherby; later Fred told Percy to shut up, using the same name. That evening the twins came away from the salesmen with no souvenirs, having given Bagman every last bit of their gold.

Book Four, Chapter Six: Fred and George did not merely bet on the final; they fixed it. They had vanished for much of the afternoon, saying they were looking at the pitch, then came back smelling strongly of broom polish, with grass on their knees. When the Irish leprechauns performed, Fred applauded them with unusual enthusiasm, then exchanged a thumbs-up with one of them as it flew past. Later the leprechauns formed a giant hand making a rude sign at the veela, the very sign Fred had made at Percy across the campfire at lunchtime. Throughout the match Fred worked figures on the back of his programme, crossing them out, then writing them again.

When the Bulgarian Keeper, Zograf, kept glaring at the handle of his broom between saves, Harry thought of the broom polish. He looked along the row at the twins; Fred put a finger to his lips, then winked. A fake whistle from George had already cost Bulgaria an open goal. When Ireland reached 160 to 10, Fred jabbed his pencil right through his programme. 'One more,' he mouthed at George, 'and then he can have it.' Krum caught the Snitch with Ireland 160 points ahead, so Ireland won by 170 to 160, exactly as the twins had bet.

The twins collapsed against each other laughing, then collected their winnings in full from Bagman. They cheered John Constantine on as Lucius Malfoy chased him out of the stadium, until their father scolded them. At Narcissa Malfoy's outburst Fred made a strangled noise into his sleeve. The twins meant never to tell a living soul how they had nudged the World Cup, least of all their mother.

In their own words

Stand aside, stand aside! Heir of Slytherin coming through! Thoroughly evil! Mind your ankles!Fred Weasley · B2 Ch14
Nerve damage. Invisible. I'm moved.Fred Weasley · B3 Ch10
Corrupted by a broomstick. Mum'll be heartbroken.Fred Weasley · B3 Ch13
Anyone can speak Troll. All you have to do is point and grunt.Fred Weasley · B4 Ch5

pages.title: George Weasley

Fred Weasley twin brother
Ron Weasley brother, younger brother
Gryffindor, Weasley family, Hogwarts student, Gryffindor Quidditch team, Beater, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
George Weasley (born 1 April 1978), Fred's twin, is the fifth son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He is a wizard of Gryffindor House, a Beater for the house team and his brother's partner in every joke. In 1992 he picked the lock on Harry Potter's door at Privet Drive, and in 1993 he set the Marauder's Map working for him. With Fred he invents the joke goods of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes. In August 1994 the twins quietly fixed the final of the Quidditch World Cup to win their bet with Ludo Bagman.

Character

George shares his twin's looks, his sense of humour and a Weasley jumper lettered with his own initial, a G. With Fred he answers to Gred and Forge.

He has a gentler side. On Christmas Day 1991 he insisted that Percy sit with the family rather than the prefects, because Christmas is a time for family. He congratulated Harry quietly on becoming Seeker. He joked that he could not stand the shame of another Head Boy in the family, and he holds that prefects take all the fun out of life.

Pranks

With Fred, George enchanted the suits of armour in the Entrance Hall to dance the can-can. He said it was worth every hour of the twenty-six it had taken to time. He once leapt out at Ginny from behind the statue of Boris the Bewildered, covered in shaggy orange fur. It was George, too, who gave Ron the dud rhyme for turning Scabbers yellow.

When the school took Harry for the Heir of Slytherin, George jumped back from him in the Great Hall, holding up a huge clove of garlic. Harry, he explained to everybody, was only popping down to the Chamber for a cup of tea and a biscuit with his giant fanged pet. He helped to turn Percy's badge into one that read Bighead Boy.

Quidditch

George has been a Gryffindor Beater since before Harry arrived. In Harry's first match he and Fred tried to pull him off his jinxed broom, then circled beneath him to catch him if he fell.

He fell off his broom in shock on hearing that Snape would referee the Hufflepuff match of 1992. During the match he hit a Bludger at Snape, which gave Hufflepuff a penalty. In November 1992 he guarded Harry from the rogue Bludger. Afterwards he blamed Wood's 'catch the Snitch or die trying' talk for Harry's recklessness. In the 1994 final he elbowed the Slytherin Beater Bole across the nose after Bole clubbed Alicia Spinnet.

George and Harry

During the rescue from Privet Drive in the summer of 1992, the bent wire that opened Harry's prison-grade lock came out of George's pocket. He passed back a hairpin to free Hedwig from her padlock, then found the way home by the car's dashboard compass. He had heard his father call Lucius Malfoy a big supporter of You-Know-Who.

In December 1993 George tapped the Marauder's Map with his wand and spoke the words 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good' to show Harry how it worked.

During the dementors' search of the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1993, Dracina Malfoy gripped George's arm hard enough to leave marks. One night he saw her coming up from the kitchens alone, carrying a parcel. After Ginny was rescued from the Chamber of Secrets he visited her in the hospital wing in his pyjamas. In June 1994 he scraped through his O.W.L.s. He was sixteen that August.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: On Sunday 21 August 1994 George came to Privet Drive by Floo, helped Fred fetch Harry's trunk, then took it back to the Burrow through the green fire. The twins, who match each other freckle for freckle, had invented Ton-Tongue Toffee together, along with the other joke goods of Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes. When their father raged about Dudley's tongue, George asked eagerly how big it had got. They had not given Dudley the toffee because he was a Muggle, George said, but because he was a great bullying git. That August the twins slept in Ron's room, having given their own to Bill and Charlie.

Book Four, Chapter Five: The next morning George told his mother that her hat did hum, a bit. She Summoned Ton-Tongue Toffees from his pocket, then from the lining of his jacket. He reported that Percy had passed his Apparition test two weeks before, and had Apparated downstairs every morning since just to prove he could. For the twins' bet with Ludo Bagman, on an Irish win with Krum catching the Snitch, George turned out every pocket he had. He tucked Bagman's betting slip safely inside his jacket.

Book Four, Chapter Six: To win, the twins needed Ireland to be more than 150 points ahead when Krum caught the Snitch, so they set about nudging the match from several directions at once. When Krum used Lynch's time out to hunt for the Snitch, George went pale, silently begging him not to find it. 'Not yet, Viktor,' he mouthed. 'Not yet, there's a good lad.' Later, as the Bulgarian Chasers bore down on an open goal, a whistle shrilled from the crowd. The Chasers pulled up short, looking for the foul, while Troy stole the Quaffle to score at the other end. George sat with his hands folded on his knees, looking innocent, but Harry saw something small and silver vanish into his pocket.

As Ireland neared the lead the twins needed, George mouthed encouragement at them. The leprechauns, who had been taken into the plan, played their part, as did broom polish on the Bulgarian Keeper's broom. Krum caught the Snitch with Ireland 160 points ahead, so Ireland won by 170 to 160. The twins collapsed laughing, collected their winnings from Bagman, then cheered John Constantine as Lucius Malfoy chased him away. George and Fred meant never to tell a living soul how they had done it, least of all their mother.

In their own words

We know perfectly well we're called Gred and Forge.George Weasley · B1 Ch8
He's popping down to the Chamber of Secrets for a nice cup of tea and a biscuit with his giant fanged pet.George Weasley · B2 Ch14
That sling had a longer run than Lockhart.George Weasley · B3 Ch10
Not yet, Viktor. Not yet, there's a good lad. Not yet.George Weasley · B4 Ch6

Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Lee Jordan is a Gryffindor wizard in the year of Fred and George Weasley. He is their closest friend and their partner in mischief. He is also the school's Quidditch commentator, and he makes no secret of whose side he is on.

Life

Lee wears his hair in dreadlocks. In September 1991 he brought a tarantula the size of a dinner plate on to the Hogwarts Express. That same month he claimed to have found a new secret passage out of the school. In Diagon Alley in 1992 the twins greeted him by chanting his name, and the three of them stocked up on Filibuster fireworks at Gambol and Japes. After the exams of 1992 he tickled the giant squid with the twins.

Commentator

Lee commentates on Quidditch matches under Professor McGonagall's watchful eye. His commentary has been biased towards Gryffindor ever since Harry's first match in November 1991. In 1992 McGonagall rebuked him for open partisanship against Slytherin. She also seized his magical megaphone to stop Dean Thomas's chant. In 1993 he conducted the Gryffindor stand with his wand during the Hufflepuff match. In 1994 he advertised the Firebolt during the Ravenclaw match, then did it again in the final, where he gave up all pretence of impartiality. Afterwards he repeated his commentary three times from a table at the party.

In the saga

Lee hailed Harry and Ron's crash into the Whomping Willow as an inspired entrance. During the attacks of 1993 he pointed out that every Slytherin had escaped, and he urged that they all be expelled. Later he stood on a table proposing that fifty Gryffindors should storm the Slytherin dungeons. On the night in 1992 when Harry went down the trapdoor, Lee was the last Gryffindor to go to bed. Percy Weasley confiscated his Exploding Snap cards during exam revision in 1994.

In their own words

Harry, mate, you've been spending too much time with Ron. Pack it in.Lee Jordan · B1 Ch7
Hasn't one teacher noticed that every single Slytherin is fine?Lee Jordan · B2 Ch16

pages.html:
William Arthur Weasley, always known as Bill (born 29 November 1970), is the eldest child of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was Head Boy at Hogwarts and left with twelve O.W.L.s. He now works for Gringotts Wizarding Bank as a curse-breaker, in the tombs of the pharaohs in Egypt.

Life and career

Bill was sorted into Gryffindor. He was made a prefect, then Head Boy, and he left Hogwarts in 1989 with twelve O.W.L.s, a record only his brother Percy has matched. His old school robes went to Ron.

Gringotts took him on as a curse-breaker and sent him to Egypt, where he breaks the enchantments laid on the tombs of the pharaohs. His mother does not approve of his long hair, or of the fang he wears in one ear. His parents spent Christmas 1992 with him. In the summer of 1993, after Arthur won the Daily Prophet Grand Prize Galleon Draw, the whole family came out to stay with him for a month.

In the saga

Ron thought that Bill might once have told him a story about a secret chamber at Hogwarts. Bill also told the twins about the morning their mother came back from the Prewetts' with a face that meant somebody's house was getting taken apart. They still quote it.

In Egypt in 1993 Bill let the family look through a door at the mummies. The tombs were safe, he told them, provided they touched nothing, though his mother would not let Ginny go in. When the twins pushed Percy into a tomb, its guardian questioned him. Bill explained that it does that to everyone who comes in uninvited. He told Ron that Pocket Sneakoscopes were rubbish sold to tourists. Percy becoming Head Boy, he said, was the worst thing that could have happened.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Bill was still in Egypt in 1994. Harry supposed that a good many of Molly's letters that summer were going to Bill and Charlie.

Book Four, Chapter Four: Harry met Bill for the first time at the Burrow on 21 August 1994, having seen him only once before, as a small figure in a newspaper photograph. Knowing that Bill worked for Gringotts and had once been Head Boy, Harry had pictured an older Percy. Bill, to put it plainly, was cool. He was tall, with his long hair tied back in a ponytail, an earring with what looked very much like a fang on it and boots of dragon hide. That evening he duelled Charlie with flying tables in the garden. He sheared a leg off Charlie's table, mended it with his wand, then conjured tablecloths out of thin air. He and Charlie were sharing the twins' room.

At dinner his mother took him to task about his new earring. Nobody at the bank cared how he dressed, Bill told her, as long as he brought home plenty of treasure; besides, she had written him only one letter all summer, about his hair. Harry, who had supposed that her letters were going to Bill and Charlie, could not imagine whom she had been writing to. Bill also reported that American soldiers had been all over the plateau at Giza since the spring. There had been a Muggle accident down a shaft, he said, and now the goblins would not go anywhere near the place.

Book Four, Chapter Five: Around midday on 22 August Bill Apparated to the World Cup campsite with Charlie and Percy, strolling out of the wood just as the sausages began to spit. Ron mentioned that Bill had once had a pen pal at a wizarding school in Brazil.

Book Four, Chapter Six: Bill watched the final from the Top Box. At Narcissa Malfoy's outburst, then again at Lucius Malfoy's chase after John Constantine, he turned to face the wall, his shoulders heaving with laughter.

Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Charles Weasley, always known as Charlie (born 12 December 1972), is the second son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was a celebrated Seeker for Gryffindor, and captain of the house team. He now works with dragons in Romania. In 1992 he took the Norwegian Ridgeback Norbert off Hagrid's hands. Harry Potter met him for the first time at the Burrow in August 1994.

Hogwarts

Charlie was the outdoor sort, according to Percy, and took Care of Magical Creatures. According to Ron he learnt a Shield Charm in his first year. He was Gryffindor's Seeker when the house won the Quidditch Cup in 1987, and he went on to captain the team. Oliver Wood once said he could have played for England if he had not gone off chasing dragons. In the common room he is still spoken of like a minor saint. Professor McGonagall said that not even Charlie could have matched Harry Potter's first dive.

A Welsh Green once had a go at him. Madam Pomfrey grew him a new ear afterwards, and the new one is slightly bigger than the old. His chipped old wand went to Ron when he left, together with his Shooting Star broom.

Romania

After Hogwarts Charlie went to Romania to study dragons, and to keep them. His arms are covered in burns from the wild ones there. His parents spent Christmas 1991 with him. That year he sent Percy an idol from Romania, which their mother confiscated for having too many tentacles.

In the spring of 1992 Ron wrote to ask whether he would take Norbert, and Charlie agreed. He sent friends of his to collect the dragon from the top of the tallest tower at Hogwarts, at midnight on a Saturday.

In the Daily Prophet's photograph of the family in Egypt in 1993, Charlie was the only Weasley missing. In 1994 Ron joked about going off to keep dragons with him, and quoted him as saying that hippogriffs can fly for days. Ginny promised to tell him all about Harry's Firebolt.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: Harry met Charlie for the first time at the Burrow on 21 August 1994, when he was home with Bill for the World Cup. He is shorter and broader than Ron or Percy, built along the same lines as the twins, with a broad, cheerful face so weathered, so thickly freckled, that it is almost brown. His arms are thick with muscle, one of them bearing a large, shiny burn. His hands are rough with calluses and old blisters. His laugh is the kind Percy might have had if Percy had ever let himself go. That evening he duelled Bill with flying tables in the garden, until Bill's table sheared a leg off his. The two of them were sharing the twins' room.

When Arthur raged at Fred over the toffee, Charlie murmured to Harry, 'Hark at him. Ask Mum what he was like at school some time.' Their mother, he said, reckoned the twins got their mischief from their father. At dinner he reported Muggle aeroplanes over the dragon reserve all summer, low and loud, which had put the Horntails right off their eggs. Refugees from a Muggle war down Serbia way were coming up through the passes, carrying everything they owned. He had never heard of genetic engineering, nor of the Augment War behind it all.

Charlie backed Ireland for the Cup, since they had flattened Peru in the semi-finals, with seven good players to Bulgaria's one. He called England's defeat by Transylvania, 390 to 10, a shocking performance. Some blamed Dracula, but Charlie did not think Dracula had been resurrected again yet.

Book Four, Chapter Five: Fred told Harry that Charlie had failed his first Apparition test by Apparating five miles south of where he meant to, on top of an old woman doing her shopping. He passed the second time. Around midday on 22 August he Apparated to the World Cup campsite with Bill and Percy.

Book Four, Chapter Six: That night Charlie watched the final from the Top Box. When Aidan Lynch was flattened by Krum's feint, he reassured Ginny that Lynch had only been ploughed, which was what Krum had been after. At the end he bellowed along the row for the Snitch.

In their own words

Hark at him. Ask Mum what he was like at school some time. She says the twins get it from him.Charlie Weasley · B4 Ch4

pages.html:
Percy Ignatius Weasley (born 22 August 1976) is a wizard, the third son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was a Gryffindor prefect from 1991 and Head Boy in 1993 to 1994. Pompous, ambitious and devoted to rules, he has meant to become Minister for Magic since he was about six years old. By August 1994 he had joined the Ministry, in the Department of International Magical Cooperation. There he works for Bartemius Crouch, whom he worships, though Crouch calls him Weatherby.

Early life and character

Percy wears glasses and polishes his badges constantly. At school he was always the least popular of six brothers. When he was made a prefect in 1991 his parents bought him a screech owl, Hermes, which he refused to lend to Ron. His old rat, Scabbers, was passed down to Ron at the same time. In 1991 Charlie sent him an idol from Romania, which his mother took off him because it had too many tentacles for her liking. All the following summer he behaved very oddly, shutting himself in his room and sending a great many letters. Like Bill, he gained twelve O.W.L.s, and he hardly gloated about it at all.

His ambition is detailed, and it is written down. In his trunk he keeps a list of plans for when he is Minister. Some of them are kindly meant: help for poor families with books and robes; an end to old families buying their way into Ministry jobs. Others are a good deal less comfortable: identity papers, a register of everyone's blood, curfews and a department of censorship. Taken together, he calls the result a fair and orderly society. His mother nearly cried when he told her he wanted to help poor families. He reads books such as Prefects Who Gained Power.

Prefect (1991 to 1993)

Percy met Harry and Ron at their Sorting in 1991. He told Harry that Dumbledore was brilliant but a little mad, and that Snape wanted Quirrell's job. Then he led the first-years up to Gryffindor Tower with the password Caput Draconis. During the troll alarm he was in his element, leading the whole house to safety. At Christmas 1991 the twins forced him into a jumper with a P on it and pinched his badge. Later they bewitched the badge to read Pinhead, and he never noticed. He docked Ron five points for being outside Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, threatening to write to their mother. He also rebuked the twins furiously for frightening Ginny.

Over Christmas 1992 he stayed at school, saying that it was his duty as a prefect, and was seen coming out of a little side room in the dungeons with his ears pink. Dracina Malfoy humiliated him over his family's poverty and called him Peter. On Valentine's Day 1993 he plucked Tom Riddle's diary out of her hands on a staircase and gave it back to Harry, with no idea of what it was. When she made Ginny cry, he threatened to march her to her lesson by the ear.

Twice he interrupted Ginny just as she was trying to tell Harry what she had seen. When his secret girlfriend, Penelope Clearwater, was Petrified, he was stunned into silence. When Ginny was taken into the Chamber he owled his parents, then shut himself in his dormitory. Afterwards he kept touching her hair, as if to make sure she was still there.

Head Boy (1993 to 1994)

Percy was made Head Boy in 1993. The letter came on the day the family left for Egypt. There the twins pushed him into a tomb, where its bandaged guardian sat up on its slab and asked whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. Percy answered it for about ten minutes, with examples, until it lay back down. At the Leaky Cauldron the twins relettered his badge to read Bighead Boy. On the night the Fat Lady was slashed he sent for Dumbledore, then ran the Great Hall like a junior Fudge.

Mrs Weasley wrote to her five children at Hogwarts, asking them to keep Harry safe. Percy took it to heart. He shadowed Harry round the castle at a distance of four paces, and he drew up a timetable of Harry's unaccounted hours. He bet Penelope ten Galleons, which he did not have, on the Ravenclaw match, and won. On the night of Sirius Black's break-in he put his badge on over his pyjamas and told the house that Ron had had a nightmare.

Before his N.E.W.T.s he enforced silence in the common room after seven o'clock. He gave a second-year a week's detention for laughing. He also confiscated three of Seamus Finnigan's Chocolate Frogs, one of which he ate.

He left Hogwarts in 1994 with the highest N.E.W.T. grades there are. At breakfast after Sirius Black's escape he held forth about it to the only person who would listen, Penelope. If he managed to get into the Ministry, he told her, he would have a lot of proposals to make about Magical Law Enforcement. She nodded patiently and went on eating her toast. By August 1994 he had started work in the Department of International Magical Cooperation. Ron warned Harry not to mention anything about Abroad at the Burrow, unless he wanted the pants bored off him.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: In August 1994 Percy kept a room at the Burrow to himself, because he had to work. He was writing a report for the Department of International Magical Cooperation on standardising cauldron thickness. Leakages, he said, had been rising by almost three per cent a year, while some foreign makers were absolute chancers. Somebody had evidently told him that the Department could not be too harsh on foreign makers who might not know any better, which annoyed him. He wanted an international law to keep flimsy, shallow-bottomed cauldrons off the market. When his brothers' furniture duel disturbed him, he screamed from his window that he hated Indians and their shoddy cauldrons. Harry, who had listened to Uncle Vernon raging about cheap foreign drills for years, thought Percy had a point, and that he might be very useful one day.

Percy is devoted to his boss, Mr Crouch, whom he quotes constantly; he had promised him the report by Tuesday 23 August. According to Ron, Crouch agreed with all the scary things Percy wanted. At dinner Percy complained that the Department of Magical Games and Sports gave too little support over the World Cup. He wondered how Ludo Bagman had ever become head of a department, criticising him for not searching for the missing Bertha Jorkins, as Mr Crouch surely would. He kept hinting at a top secret event his department was organising for straight after the World Cup, in the hope that somebody would ask. He approved of Crouch's answer to the Bulgarians, that Muggle disturbances were a matter for the Muggle Liaison Office. When Harry mentioned the United Nations Security Council, Percy dismissed it. 'A Muggle committee, Father,' he said. 'Of no consequence.' He drank elderflower wine, shuddered at the thought of his in-tray after five days away and insisted that the dragon dung once put in it had been a sample of fertiliser from Norway. Fred and George had sent it.

Book Four, Chapter Five: Percy had passed his Apparition test about two weeks before, and had Apparated downstairs every morning since just to prove he could. Around midday on 22 August he arrived at the campsite with Bill and Charlie, announcing loudly that he had just Apparated. Though he disapproved of how Ludo Bagman ran his department, he rushed forward to impress him. When Bagman said that Mr Crouch spoke about 150 languages, Percy corrected him: over two hundred, including Mermish, Gobbledegook and Troll. He worships Crouch because Crouch follows rules to the letter. When Crouch arrived, Percy bowed himself into a hunch to offer him tea. Crouch thanked him, calling him Weatherby, to the twins' delight, then later handed the cup back untouched.

Crouch warned that the Muggles were organised against people born with powers, and that he would not have the Statute put at risk on British soil. Percy, who had called the Security Council a Muggle committee of no consequence only the night before, nodded so hard that his glasses nearly fell into the fire. When Ludo Bagman almost let slip that something was happening at Hogwarts, Percy called it classified information, saying that Mr Crouch was right not to disclose it. Fred took to calling him Weatherby.

Book Four, Chapter Six: In the Top Box Percy kept springing out of his seat for important wizards. He bowed so deeply to Cornelius Fudge that his glasses fell off and smashed. Scarlet to the ears, he mended them with his wand, then spent the rest of the evening throwing jealous looks at Harry, whom Fudge had greeted like an old friend. After Lucius Malfoy's jinxes he helped Fudge out from behind the World Cup, apologising over and over. The comb Ron gave Harry that night, borrowed without mentioning it, looked very much like Percy's.

In their own words

I am a Prefect. It's my job to roam.Percy Weasley · B2 Ch14
He told you to give it back, Ms Malfoy.Percy Weasley · B2 Ch15
I happen to be patrolling. Head Boy duties. The route is confidential.Percy Weasley · B3 Ch9
It feels like twice.Percy Weasley · B3 Ch12

pages.html:
Arthur Weasley (born 6 February 1950) runs the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office at the Ministry of Magic. He is Molly Weasley's husband and the father of seven children. Tall, thin, balding, red-haired and bespectacled, he is fascinated by Muggles, above all by their machines. Yet he knows almost nothing of their troubles: in 1994 he had never heard of mutants or of Khan, and took Superman for a Muggle story like Father Christmas. He enchanted the Ford Anglia in which his sons rescued Harry Potter in 1992. In August 1994 he secretly planted a house gnome in the Dursleys' house. He is also the old enemy of Lucius Malfoy.

Family

Arthur is the son of Septimus Weasley and Cedrella Black. He married Molly Prewett in 1969, so that by 1994 they had been married for twenty-five years. Their children are Bill, Charlie, Percy, Fred, George, Ron and Ginny. He bought Percy an owl for being made a prefect. He and Molly spent Christmas 1991 in Romania with Charlie, then Christmas 1992 in Egypt with Bill. In the summer of 1993, at forty-three, he won the Daily Prophet Grand Prize Galleon Draw of seven hundred Galleons, and took the whole family to Egypt for a month.

Ministry career

Arthur works in the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office, a job the rest of the Ministry laughs at. He has one colleague, an old warlock called Perkins. Cornelius Fudge is his superior, and Arthur says 'the Minister' the way other people say 'the drains'. His raids turn up shrinking door keys and biting kettles. After one night of nine raids he reported that Mundungus Fletcher had tried to hex him. He deals with cursed and bewitched books as well. One sang lullabies until the reader never woke; another ate a man's fingers. The worst, he says, are the ones you like. He wrote the Muggle Protection Act. He once visited Azkaban on Ministry business, and came home grey in the face, unable to eat. He maintains an embargo on flying carpets, which the Registry of Proscribed Charmable Objects defines as a Muggle Artefact, to the annoyance of the carpet trader Ali Bashir.

In September 1992 Ron and Harry were seen flying his car to Hogwarts. Arthur faced an inquiry at work, was fined fifty Galleons and had to listen to Lucius Malfoy demanding that he step down. In 1993 he and his colleagues were taken off their usual work to hunt for Sirius Black. He learnt that Fudge had heard Black say 'He's at Hogwarts' in his sleep. For the final of the 1994 Quidditch World Cup he got prime tickets through friends in the Department of Magical Games and Sports.

Muggles and the flying car

Arthur fills his shed with Muggle objects, which he takes apart, enchants and puts back together. He keeps a picture of a jump jet out there, and he is mad on Muggle football. He questioned Harry eagerly about plugs, the post, telephones and escalators. In the summer of 1992 Harry taught him how to use a telephone. He has been pestering McGonagall about hers for fifteen years. Molly sighs whenever he starts on electricity. He is dead keen on the internet, which he explained to Ron at Easter 1994. His shed holds hundreds upon hundreds of batteries, with an old transistor radio beneath them and a car battery labelled EXHIBIT ONE in pride of place.

His Ford Anglia was enchanted to fly. It had cushioned seats, puncture-proof tyres, an engine that ran on vegetable oil and a charm to hide all this from Muggles. It also had a stretched boot and a faulty Invisibility Booster. It was legal because Arthur had written a loophole into the law himself: a car may be enchanted, provided its owner never intends to fly it. After it crashed into the Whomping Willow it went to live wild in the Forbidden Forest.

Harry Potter

In 1992 Arthur told Harry that Dumbledore knew where he was, and that since hearing from Molly, Dumbledore 'really knew now'. At Flourish and Blotts, when Lucius Malfoy sneered at his family and at the Grangers, Arthur threw the first punch. He came away with a cut lip. He would have chinned Lucius, he said, if Hagrid had not pulled them apart. He mended Harry's glasses with a tap of his wand, then took the Grangers for a drink. After the Chamber of Secrets he warned the children never to trust anything that can think for itself if you cannot see where it keeps its brain.

On 31 August 1993 he looked Harry over in the light, as though he were inspecting a plug. Then he asked him privately whether the Dursleys or Marge had laid a finger on him. He argued that Harry had a right to know Black was after him. He arranged Ministry cars to take them to King's Cross, putting Harry on the list under 'Weasley'. He also made Harry promise not to go looking for Black. In June 1994, seeing the smile on Molly's face over the letters from Hermione and Dracina, he fled back to his shed with a toaster under his arm.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: On Sunday 21 August 1994 Arthur had the Dursleys' fireplace connected to the Floo Network for one afternoon, through a useful contact at the Floo Regulation Panel, though Muggle fireplaces are not supposed to be connected. Finding it boarded up, he blasted the boards out in a shower of plaster. Then he grinned at Harry with a wink: he had made as much mess as he possibly could on purpose, and was in no hurry to put it right with a spell. Taking Harry's joke about Father Christmas quite literally, he told him gently, as though breaking hard news to a small child, that Father Christmas is not real. He told Uncle Vernon about his collection of plugs and batteries, which his wife thinks mad.

When Vernon pressed his stomach close to him, Arthur stopped stooping. He stood a good head taller than Vernon, the mildness gone from his face. 'I'd step back, if I were you, Mr Dursley,' he said quietly. 'You're standing on my robes.' Vernon was not, but stepped back very fast. Arthur's ears had gone red at the tips exactly like Ron's. He relit the ruined fireplace with Incendio, turning the flames green with Floo powder from a little drawstring bag in which something wriggled. Then he kept his hand on Harry's shoulder, waiting in silence, wand in hand, until Vernon said goodbye to his nephew.

When Dudley ate one of Fred's Ton-Tongue Toffees, Arthur tried to help. He dodged a china shepherdess hurled by Vernon, then a second ornament, flicking a third clean out of Vernon's fist. While the Dursleys were busy with Dudley, he took a house gnome out of the bag, then set it down on their carpet as casually as if he were tying a shoelace. Planting it was his own idea. He shrank Dudley's tongue once it was four feet long.

He Apparated into the Burrow kitchen angrier than Harry had ever seen him, shouting at Fred that such behaviour seriously undermined wizard-Muggle relations, when he spent half his life campaigning against the mistreatment of Muggles. Charlie murmured to Harry that their mother said the twins got their mischief from him. Harry thought Arthur was the twins' father quite as much as Ron's. At dinner Molly asked whether he had mended the Dursleys' wall. It had gone clean out of his head, he claimed; reminded of his campaigning, he said quietly that this was quite different, because they had it coming. When Molly described house gnomes to Harry, Arthur coughed into his napkin. He told Harry that what he had seen in the bag was only Floo powder shifting about, or one of Fred's toffees.

He told the table that he liked Ludo Bagman, who had got him good tickets for the World Cup after Arthur smoothed over trouble involving Ludo's brother Otto and a lawnmower with unnatural powers. He had asked Ludo about the missing Bertha Jorkins, saying he would be worried if it were somebody in his own department. He also told of Wilfred Thimble, a retired wizard dragged off his ladder by young Muggles in Stockport, the third such attack that month, then asked Harry what 'mutie' meant. Harry found that Arthur, for all his love of Muggles, had never heard of mutants, of Khan or of the Augment War. He asked whether the Augments were a Muggle machine. He blamed the Muggles' new hostility on the heat, or on their television. He took Superman for a Muggle story like Father Christmas, having once seen a comic about him at the office. If Mr Weasley did not know, Harry thought, then nobody did.

Book Four, Chapter Five: For the World Cup on 22 August Arthur dressed as a Muggle, in a golfing jumper patterned with yellow diamonds over jeans gone white at the knees, with a belt buckled over the top of the lot. Hermione kindly told him that Muggles wear belts underneath. Over his tickets he murmured to Molly that six weeks was right on time, a remark about the house gnomes breeding at the Dursleys'; she silenced him with his name, while he went pink trying not to laugh. At breakfast he explained the Apparition test, splinching and the fines imposed by the Department of Magical Transportation. The Muggles' screaming at splinched body parts honestly baffled him. He blamed the Muggle unrest on Britain letting in all sorts of people who did not get on, then said it was mostly the Germans, who like their rules too much, and the French, who smell of garlic. He had missed the point entirely.

On the walk to Stoatshead Hill he explained the arrangements for the Cup: about a hundred thousand wizards, a deserted moor, staggered arrivals, a wood as the Apparition point and two hundred Portkeys round Britain. He believed, wrongly, that some wizards were travelling by Apache helicopter or flying rucksack. At the campsite he could not tell Muggle banknotes apart, so Harry had to help him pay the site manager, Mr Roberts. He walked past the Malfoys' silk tent on the far side of the path, chin up, without once looking at it. He had borrowed a tent from his colleague Perkins. He glowed at the prospect of cooking on an open fire like real Muggles, though he hindered more than he helped with the tents, enjoying himself enormously breaking matches until Hermione showed him how to strike one.

Through lunch he named every Ministry official who passed, mainly for Harry and Hermione. He bet Ludo Bagman a Galleon on Ireland to win, but only feebly tried to stop the twins betting all their savings. When Mr Crouch passed on a complaint from Ali Bashir about the carpet embargo, Arthur sighed that he had written to Bashir only the week before. When Crouch warned that the Muggles were organised against people born with powers, Arthur told him kindly that it was all a misunderstanding, since Muggles can be very excitable.

Book Four, Chapter Six: That night Arthur led his party through the wood to the stadium. It seated a hundred thousand, he explained, had taken a Ministry task force of five hundred all year to build and had Muggle-Repelling Charms on every inch. He spoke fondly of the Muggles who kept remembering urgent appointments whenever they came near it. The ticket witch greeted him by name. In the Top Box Lucius Malfoy asked him what he had sold to afford such seats; Arthur's smile at the news of Lucius's gift to St Mungo's looked painful. They had last met when they came to blows in Flourish and Blotts.

Arthur recognised the veela, polishing his glasses hurriedly, then told everyone to put their fingers in their ears. He called Lynch a fool for following Krum's feint. When Lucius chased John Constantine out of the stadium, Arthur laughed into his handkerchief until his face went purple. Then he scolded the twins for cheering, put out the burning pillar and helped the Bulgarian Minister look for the brim of his hat. He told Ron and Harry to go straight back to the tents afterwards, without wandering off.

Sayings

Ron quotes his father often. Arthur's only remark on the subject of women is 'Women...', with a shrug of both hands. He holds that night adds about forty per cent to any trouble. By midnight, he says, a man who wants to kill somebody has worked out how. Having suffered Mundungus Fletcher's tricks in his youth, he believes that you should never sneak up on a sleeping man. He thinks Squibs come from the same five families marrying one another for three hundred years. He never believed the Malfoys' claim that Voldemort had bewitched them, and he is practically certain that Lucius served him. Being in the same grounds as dementors, he once said, was like living downwind of something.

In their own words

Yeah, and I would've chinned him if Hagrid didn't stop us.Arthur Weasley · B2 Ch5
Never trust anything that can think for itself if you can't see where it keeps its brain.Arthur Weasley · B2 Ch19
I'd step back, if I were you, Mr Dursley. You're standing on my robes.Arthur Weasley · B4 Ch4
That's quite different. Quite different, Molly. They had it coming.Arthur Weasley · B4 Ch4

pages.title: Molly Weasley's second cousin
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Apparently none: a Squib, or a Muggle
pages.html:
Molly Weasley's second cousin is an accountant, and the one relation the Weasley family never mentions. As far as Ron Weasley knew, he was the only person in the family who was not a witch or wizard.

A family silence

Ron did not say so outright, but the way he spoke suggested that the cousin had no magic. He is either a Squib, one of the rare people born into a wizarding family without any magic of their own, or a Muggle. Squibs are often a source of embarrassment in the old wizarding families, which may be why nobody mentions him.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, Harry Potter asked Ron whether everyone in his family was a wizard. 'Er, yeah, I think so,' said Ron. 'Mum's got a second cousin who's an accountant, but nobody mentions him.'

pages.title: Scabbers
infobox:
Ron Weasley owner
Peter Pettigrew true identity
Pet, Rat, Weasley family, rat, pet, Ron's pet, Animagus form
Tattered left ear; a toe missing from a front paw
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Scabbers was the Weasley family's fat grey rat, passed down from Percy Weasley to Ron as the last word in hand-me-downs. In June 1994 he was unmasked as the Animagus form of Peter Pettigrew, who had hidden in the family for twelve years after betraying Harry Potter's parents.

As a pet

Scabbers was a small, fat, grey, second-hand rat who almost never woke up. He had a tattered left ear and a toe missing from one front paw. He belonged to Percy until 1991, when Percy became a prefect and was given an owl. Then he went to Ron, because the family could not afford a second owl.

On the Hogwarts Express in 1991 he bit Goyle's knuckle when Goyle grabbed at the Chocolate Frogs, leaving a scar. He was flung against the window and went straight back to sleep. On his first night at school he tried to eat Ron's sheets. Later he chewed through the sheet that became the Potter for President banner. He was fond of Fudge Flies. In the summer of 1993 he appeared on Ron's shoulder in the Daily Prophet photograph of the Weasleys in Egypt.

Decline and disappearance

After Egypt Scabbers grew thin and droopy. The witch at the Magical Menagerie told Ron that an ordinary rat lives about three years, and sold him a rat tonic. Crookshanks attacked him in the shop. By Christmas 1993 he was gaunt, breathing fast and losing his fur. He had been losing weight ever since Sirius Black's escape.

In early March 1994 he vanished, leaving blood on Ron's sheet and ginger hairs on the floor. Ron grieved for him more than anybody expected, and he blamed Crookshanks.

Unmasking

On 6 June 1994 Hermione found Scabbers hiding in a milk jug in Hagrid's cabin, thin and patchy with bald spots. He fought frantically to get out of Ron's pocket. He bit Ron, and fled from Crookshanks across the lawn. In the Shrieking Shack Remus Lupin and Sirius Black forced him back into human form as Peter Pettigrew. He had been with the Weasley family for twelve years. Ron took it as a personal insult.

When Lupin transformed under the full moon, Pettigrew escaped again as a rat. Sirius later gave Ron a tiny owl, since it was his fault that Ron no longer had a rat.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Four, when Harry Potter came to the Burrow in August 1994, Scabbers was gone from Ron's attic bedroom. In his place was Pigwidgeon, the tiny owl Harry had caught out of the train window in June. Ron had grumbled about Scabbers for years, yet Harry remembered how terribly upset he had been when it looked as though Crookshanks had eaten him.

pages.title: The trolley witch
aliases: the witch with the food trolley
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Sells food from a trolley on the Hogwarts Express
Sweets, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, ice-cold pumpkin juice
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The trolley witch is the plump, smiling witch who pushes the food trolley along the Hogwarts Express. The train is usually kept for students. Until September 1993 she was the only grown-up Harry Potter and his friends had ever seen aboard it.

The trolley

Her trolley carries Bertie Bott's Every-Flavour Beans, Drooble's Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes and Liquorice Wands, along with a great many other things. There are no Mars Bars on it. She also sells ice-cold pumpkin juice. She comes clanking along the corridor at lunchtime, pulling back each compartment door in turn.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, at about half past twelve on 1 September 1991, something came clanking along the corridor, and she pulled back the door of the compartment Harry Potter was sharing with Ron Weasley. "Fancy anything from the trolley, my loves?" The Dursleys had never given Harry money for sweets. He had meant to buy every Mars Bar on the trolley, but there were none, so he bought some of each instead, for eleven silver Sickles and seven bronze Knuts.

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, Harry and Ron were flying north in Mr Weasley's car with nothing to drink. Harry thought longingly of the train somewhere far below them, where ice-cold pumpkin juice could be had from a plump, smiling witch with a trolley.

In Book Three, Chapter Five, on 1 September 1993, she reached their compartment at one o'clock and handed Harry a large stack of Cauldron Cakes. Professor Lupin was asleep by the window. "Don't worry, dear," she said. "If he's hungry when he wakes, I'll be up front with the driver."

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-Two, on the journey home in June 1994, Harry bought an enormous lunch from her trolley. He did not buy anything with chocolate in it.
