Harry Potter first walked down it with Rubeus Hagrid in the summer of 1991, and in August 1993 he lived there for three weeks.

The street

The way in is through the little back yard of the Leaky Cauldron. Tapping the third brick from the left above the dustbin opens an archway in the wall. Beyond it are shops selling cauldrons, robes, books, wands, owls, broomsticks and potion ingredients. Gringotts, the snow-white goblin bank, towers over the little shops. At the top end the street bends round towards Knockturn Alley, where the crowds thin out and the trade turns to the Dark Arts.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, Hagrid took Harry to Diagon Alley to buy his school things in the summer of 1991. In Madam Malkin's robe shop Harry met Dracina Malfoy for the first time.

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Harry shopped there with the Weasleys and the Grangers. They went to Gringotts, Quality Quidditch Supplies, Gambol and Japes, a junk shop, a second-hand robe shop and Flourish and Blotts. In Chapter Eleven, faced with the list for the Polyjuice Potion, Harry asked sarcastically whether there was a Bicorn shop in Diagon Alley next to the ice-cream place. In Chapter Fifteen Hermione Granger showed him the Revealer she had bought there.

In Book Three, Chapter Three, Cornelius Fudge told Harry to keep to Diagon Alley for the rest of the holidays, and to be back at the Leaky Cauldron before dark each night. In Chapter Four Harry spent three weeks there, in August 1993. He did his homework outside Florean Fortescue's and read on the steps of Eeylops. He sat on the wall by Gringotts, watching the goblins come and go. Almost every day he went back to look at the Firebolt in the window of Quality Quidditch Supplies, priced on request. One afternoon, at the top end of the Alley where it bends towards Knockturn Alley, Lucius Malfoy spoke to him from the shade of a doorway. On the last day of the holidays Harry found Ron Weasley and Hermione waiting outside Florean's.

In Chapter Ten, reading Which Broomstick by the common-room fire, Harry came to a picture of the Firebolt he had stood in front of day after day through that shop window. In Chapter Thirteen the look on Ginny Weasley's face as she touched his new Firebolt reminded him of his own, pressed against a shop window in Diagon Alley. In Chapter Sixteen Ron reminded Harry that he had first told him about Percy's ambition to be Minister for Magic in Diagon Alley. In the Book Three Interlude Harry, travelling under the name of Neville, asked the Knight Bus to take him to Diagon Alley.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Three, Harry remembered Lucius walking beside him down Diagon Alley the summer before, his cane ticking on the cobbles.

In Chapter Four, at the Burrow, Molly Weasley offered to buy Harry's school things in Diagon Alley the next day, along with everybody else's, since there might be no time after the World Cup. When none of the Weasleys had heard of the Augment War, Harry recalled what he had learnt in Diagon Alley the summer before, from Lucius Malfoy's blank face: wizards did not know.

In Chapter Five Arthur explained that places such as Diagon Alley were protected from Muggles, but could never hold the hundred thousand wizards of the World Cup.

In Chapter Six Lucius admitted to Harry that he had thought the boy had been out in the sun too long. In Diagon Alley the summer before, Harry had asked him about a Muggle war, and about a masked man who climbed walls. Lucius had since made enquiries, very quietly. Harry, for his part, remembered that Lucius had muttered there about somebody called Cissy.

pages.title: Gringotts
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Far below London, reached by carts on miniature railway tracks
Dragons, it is said, at the deepest vaults
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Gringotts Wizarding Bank is the wizarding bank of Britain, a snow-white building that towers over the little shops of Diagon Alley. It is run by goblins. Its vaults lie in a maze of tunnels far below London, reached by carts that hurtle along miniature railway tracks, and dragons are said to guard the deepest of them.

The bank

The bank takes its name from its goblin founder, Gringott. Its halls are lit by torches. Goblins keep the accounts and drive the carts. Every wizarding family of any standing keeps its gold there. Robbing it is supposed to be impossible.

Before it went to Hogwarts in 1991, the Philosopher's Stone was kept in vault seven hundred and thirteen. Gringotts also employs curse-breakers, to get gold out of the old tombs and treasure houses of the world. Bill Weasley, the eldest of the Weasley children, does this work for it in the tombs of Egypt.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, in the summer of 1991, Hagrid took Harry Potter down to the vaults to draw gold for his school things. The cart ride turned Hagrid a delicate shade of green. That day Hagrid also emptied vault seven hundred and thirteen. In Chapter Three torches burned along the walls of the castle's Entrance Hall as they had at Gringotts. In Chapter Twelve, going down the sloping passage beneath the trapdoor, Harry remembered the dragons that were said to guard the deepest vaults. In Chapter Thirteen it came out that Quirrell had tried and failed to steal the Philosopher's Stone from Gringotts on Voldemort's orders. It seems he made the attempt on the very day Hagrid emptied the vault.

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, with Bill away working for the bank in Egypt, Harry went down to the vaults with the Weasleys. When their vault swung open, it held only a very small pile of Sickles and one gold Galleon. Harry felt dreadful. He felt worse still at his own vault, in front of a heap of gold he had done nothing to earn. In Chapter Eleven Oliver Wood mocked Dracina Malfoy as a Seeker with nothing going for her but a father with a fat Gringotts vault.

In Book Three, Chapter Four, in August 1993, Harry refilled his money bag from his vault. Bill was still breaking curses for Gringotts in Egypt. In Chapter Twenty-Two Sirius Black wrote to tell Harry that the gold for his Firebolt had come out of his own Gringotts vault: 'Please consider it as thirteen birthdays' worth of presents from your godfather.'

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: at the Burrow on 21 August 1994 Bill Weasley told his mother that nobody at the bank cared how he dressed as long as he brought home plenty of treasure. In Mr Weasley's shed that evening Harry offered to buy the Weasleys a computer, since he had loads of gold at Gringotts just sitting there.

pages.title: The Leaky Cauldron
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Diagon Alley, through the back yard
Harry Potter in number eleven, August 1993; Ron and Percy Weasley in number twelve
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
The Leaky Cauldron is a small, grubby wizarding pub on Charing Cross Road in London, which most Londoners have never noticed. It lets rooms upstairs, and through its back yard lies Diagon Alley.

The pub

Inside, it is dark and shabby. The barman is called Tom. There is a fireplace on the Floo Network, a private parlour and rooms upstairs for guests. Out at the back is a small walled yard with a dustbin in it. Tapping the third brick from the left above the bin opens an archway in the wall, with Diagon Alley on the other side.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, Hagrid went off to the Leaky Cauldron for a quick pick-me-up after the cart ride through Gringotts. It was in the pub that Harry first met Professor Quirrell, the jittery young man he saw again at the staff table in Chapter Three. In Chapter Nine Harry remembered strangers queueing there to shake his hand. In Chapter Thirteen it came back to him that Quirrell had shaken it too, nervously, on the very day Hagrid emptied vault seven hundred and thirteen.

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Mr Weasley took the Grangers there for a drink. That evening the Weasleys went home to the Burrow by Floo powder from its fireside, while the Grangers left through the pub into the Muggle street.

In Book Three, Chapter Three, the Knight Bus set Harry down outside the pub just before dawn in the summer of 1993, and Cornelius Fudge, the Minister for Magic, was waiting for him at the door. The Interlude tells the same arrival from inside the bus. In Chapter Sixteen Harry remembered how polite he had been to Fudge in the pub, saying 'Minister' and 'with respect' in all the right places.

In Chapter Four Harry lived in room eleven for three weeks. Nobody shouted at him there, and nobody rang any bells. He had given Fudge his word not to go out through the front door into the Muggle world, and with the whole of Diagon Alley at the back he never felt the least wish to. Ron and Percy Weasley had room twelve when the Weasleys came to stay.

In Chapter Nine, lying awake in the Great Hall on the night the Fat Lady was slashed, Harry heard again a voice through a bedroom wall at the Leaky Cauldron: he's at Hogwarts, he's at Hogwarts. Percy's bustle that night had put him irresistibly in mind of Fudge in the same pub. In Chapter Eighteen he remembered exactly what he had overheard outside the parlour door, in Mr Weasley's worried voice: The guards say he's been talking in his sleep... always the same words... 'He's at Hogwarts.'

In Book Four, Chapter One, in a dream in the summer of 1994, Harry found the Leaky Cauldron halfway up a hill, its sign showing a man hanging by his neck from the branch of a tree. In Chapter Three, on 20 August 1994, a nurse on the Muggle news described the great blackout of the August before. Harry had spent most of that month at the Leaky Cauldron, where everything ran on candles and magic. He had slept straight through it.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, meeting Cornelius Fudge again in the Top Box on 22 August 1994, Harry Potter remembered their morning in the Leaky Cauldron in 1993 very well: the crumpets, the warm fire and the feeling afterwards of having been handled. Later that night he learnt the name of the dodgy bloke who had sworn all the way to the Leaky Cauldron on the Knight Bus: John Constantine.

pages.title: Number Four, Privet Drive
infobox: Privet Drive; The cupboard under the stairs
Little Whinging, Dursley family, Surrey, Number Four, Privet Drive
A blood ward laid by Lily Potter's sacrifice
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Number Four, Privet Drive is the Dursleys' spotless house in Little Whinging, Surrey. Harry Potter was left on its doorstep as a baby in November 1981, and he grew up in the cupboard under the stairs. Lily Potter's blood lives under its roof in her sister Petunia, so it is the one place where Lord Voldemort cannot touch Harry. Harry must go back there every summer.

The house

Number Four is a neat suburban house, with a clipped lawn, net curtains and a garden hedge kept at exactly the right height for watching the neighbours. Magnolia Crescent is close by. There St Michael's Church stands behind a lych-gate, with a bench beside it. Mrs Figg lives in the same neighbourhood with her cats. In 1993 the Dursleys put a new television in the kitchen.

The living-room fireplace was boarded up years ago, with an electric fire of imitation coals plugged in on the hearth in front of it. Since August 1994 it has been a ragged hole. A new fridge hums in the corner of the kitchen, and house gnomes have been breeding in the walls.

When the Hogwarts Express pulled out of King's Cross in September 1991, Harry had no idea what was waiting for him at the other end of the line. He was quite certain, all the same, that it could not be worse than Privet Drive.

The cupboard and the bedroom

On 1 November 1981 Albus Dumbledore left the orphaned Harry on the doorstep. For about ten years Harry slept in the cupboard under the stairs, among the spiders, with a bolt on the outside of the door. If he was caught watching television he was sent back to it. He learnt to keep still in the dark until Uncle Vernon had gone by. In 1991, once the Hogwarts letters began to arrive, he was moved into Dudley's second bedroom, which was full of Dudley's broken things.

In the summer of 1992 his school things were padlocked in the cupboard. After the ruin of the Masons' dinner Vernon put bars on his bedroom window and a prison-grade lock on the door. He had a cat-flap cut in it as well, through which a bowl of cold tinned soup came each day. Ron, Fred and George Weasley rescued him, tearing the bars out of the wall with their father's flying car. When Dumbledore learnt of the cupboard, the bars and the cat-flap, he was angry.

Harry's bedroom has a loose floorboard under the bed, where he hides presents, letters and food. It also has a wardrobe with a mirror. Its window is lit orange by the streetlamp.

The blood ward

When Lily Potter died for her son she laid on him a very old protection, the magic of Elves and of Númenor. It lives in his blood, as it does in her sister's. While Harry can call Number Four his home, the dark creature that is hunting him cannot touch him there, so long as his mother's blood lives under its roof. When Gandalf told Dumbledore so, he added: 'Not Tom. Not Tom's true master.'

So Dumbledore requires Harry to live there every summer, in spite of Molly Weasley's protests. It is also why Harry could not accept his godfather Sirius Black's offer of a home in June 1994. Cornelius Fudge told Harry in 1993 that his aunt's house was the safest place for him, because of the ward.

At the end of Harry's second year Dumbledore came to the house himself. He sat in the front room and warned the Dursleys that he would know the moment they harmed Harry. They have not struck him since.

Events

On 31 July 1992 Dobby appeared in Harry's bedroom, then wrecked the Dursleys' dinner party. On the last evening of Marge Dursley's visit in August 1993 Harry inflated her in the dining room. Then he walked out of the house with his trunk.

On Thursday 18 August 1994 the Dursleys' refrigerator was found full of bleeding rats. Two days later pond mud erupted from the kitchen plughole, coating the room and the family. Harry put the mud down to Molly Weasley.

In Harry's dream

In Harry's dream of August 1994 Privet Drive lay sunk at the bottom of a valley. Number four was an orphanage, kept by Aunt Petunia, with soot-black bricks and bars on every window. His mother had died there after giving birth to him.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Four, on Sunday 21 August 1994, Harry packed his trunk, clearing the last of the food from under his loose floorboard. Nobody at number four said a civil word all day. The kitchen sink gurgled whenever Aunt Petunia drew breath to snap at him. She had not set foot outside since the woman at number seven began telling all Little Whinging about the drains. At breakfast Uncle Vernon read out a piece about the Americans wanting their giant robots back, and approved. Dudley, who had grown quiet over the summer, said nothing. That afternoon Harry saw somebody standing in shimmering air by the lamp post outside number five, looking up at his window. It was Yeesha, watching over him for Sirius Black. Mr Prentice had just put a HUMANS FIRST sticker in his car.

The Weasleys came by Floo after half past five, only to find the fireplace boarded up. Arthur Weasley blew the boards out, burying the usually spotless living room in dust, plaster and broken brick, far more than one small fireplace could hold. While the twins fetched Harry's trunk from the bedroom they had once pulled him out of, Arthur faced Uncle Vernon down. He made the Dursleys say goodbye. Dudley ate one of Fred's Ton-Tongue Toffees, and his tongue grew four feet long. In the uproar Vernon threw a china shepherdess, which smashed in the ruined fireplace, while Arthur quietly set a house gnome loose under the sideboard. House gnomes, Molly explained at dinner, feed on spite. When she asked Arthur whether he had mended the wall, he said it had gone clean out of his head. 'They had it coming,' he added quietly.

In Chapter Five Molly told Hermione at breakfast that the Dursleys' sink had struck twice in one night. The second plumber would not set foot in the kitchen. Arthur murmured that the gnomes were breeding right on time. All of it was the work of Molly and her allies, among them Hermione, who kept a long list in a red notebook under the heading Privet Drive. Twice that day Harry remembered the cupboard under the stairs, the bars on his window and the cat flap in his door.

pages.title: Hogwarts Express
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Platform nine and three-quarters, King's Cross, London
The trolley witch, with her trolley of sweets
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
The Hogwarts Express is the scarlet steam train that carries the pupils of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry north from London at the start of every school year, and brings them back at the end of each term. It leaves platform nine and three-quarters at King's Cross on 1 September.

The train

The journey takes all day, and the train reaches Hogsmeade station after dark. Pupils' trunks are left on board to be brought up to the school separately. A witch comes along the corridor with a trolley of sweets. The train is kept for pupils as a rule, so that apart from the trolley witch an adult passenger is a rare sight.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, on Harry's first journey in September 1991, he bought sweets from the trolley for eleven silver Sickles and seven bronze Knuts. In Chapter Thirteen, at the end of that year, the pupils crossed back over the lake in the little boats. The train took them home to platform nine and three-quarters.

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, the train left King's Cross without Harry and Ron. They followed it due north from the air in Mr Weasley's flying car, with the scarlet engine streaking along below them like a snake. In Chapter Eleven Dobby asked Harry why he had not gone home when the train went without him. In Chapter Fourteen, after the attack on Justin Finch-Fletchley and Nearly Headless Nick, there was very nearly a stampede to book seats home for Christmas.

In Chapter Eighteen, when Ginny Weasley was taken into the Chamber of Secrets, Professor McGonagall told the Heads of House to let their pupils know that the Hogwarts Express would take them home first thing the next morning. In Chapter Nineteen, with Ginny safe, it turned out that the train would not be leaving in the morning after all.

In Book Three, Chapter Five, on 1 September 1993, Harry, Ron and Hermione found Professor Lupin asleep in the last compartment. The train was usually kept for pupils, and he was the first adult they had ever seen on it apart from the witch with the food trolley. That evening the train stopped in the dark and the rain short of Hogsmeade. All its lamps went out. Dementors came aboard to search it for Sirius Black. When one of them came into the compartment, Harry collapsed.

In Chapter Eleven the train took most of the school home on the last morning of term in December 1993, while Harry stayed behind at the castle. In Chapter Twenty-Two, on the way home in June 1994, Harry, Ron and Hermione played Exploding Snap until they all had singed eyebrows. Dracina Malfoy looked in to sneer at them and set the whole pack off with one fingernail. In the cloud of smoke she pushed a tightly folded note into Harry's hand. As the sun was getting low, a tiny owl, the one Ron now calls Pig, brought Harry a letter from Sirius.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Four, at the Burrow on 21 August 1994, Hermione Granger closed her fingers round Harry's wrist and found that he was thinner than he had been on the train in June. Dracina had thought him thin on that journey too. On the same journey Harry had caught Pigwidgeon out of the train window, and the tiny owl now lived in Ron's room.

pages.title: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Highlands of Scotland, on a crag above a lake
Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff, Rowena Ravenclaw, Salazar Slytherin
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry is the school of magic for the young witches and wizards of Britain. It is a vast castle of a hundred towers, on a crag above a lake in the Scottish Highlands. It was founded in 990 by four young witches and wizards from four rival peoples of the island. It took the Istar Gandalf eleven years of argument to bring them together. Hogwarts was the first place where Britain's quarrelling magical communities were made to sit down in one room. From 1991 it has been home to Harry Potter and Dracina Malfoy for most of each year.

Before the school

The magic taught at Hogwarts is older than the school by many thousands of years. When the ice withdrew from the northern mountains, the great meltwater flood drowned the old world. Gandalf was sent to the frightened families who survived on the new shores. He sat by their fires and taught them the first words of light magic: how to call a flame, how to ask the rain to wait, how to heal a cut. He taught them, too, how to know that a voice in the dark offering power is never the voice of a friend.

Over the following ages men carried that inheritance off in a hundred directions. They quarrelled over it, forgot half of it and invented the rest.

By the tenth century Britain held several magical cultures, all of which despised one another. In the south were the sorcerers of London and the old Roman towns. They worked as the Greeks and Romans had. Their incantations were in Latin or Greek, with a great deal of geometry besides. The druids, Brythonic, Cymric or Cornish, held the Midlands, Wales and the North. They worked with song, stone and the seasons. In the North-East lived Viking families who had stayed on after the Saxons took Jorvik, and had simply stopped calling themselves Norse. The Picts of Scotland had a magic that ran to knots and tattoos. Each of them thought itself the only true kind of wizard.

The founding

Gandalf, travelling as he always had under many names, gathered the four most quarrelsome young people he could find. They were a tall, proud girl from the glens, a red-headed firebrand from the moors, a round, sensible farm girl from the valleys, and a dark, watchful young man from the fens. He stood them in the mud on a crag above a lake. It took him eleven years to get them to sit at one table, and he broke two staffs banging on it for order.

The four were Rowena Ravenclaw, Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff and Salazar Slytherin. The school they built together was raised in 990, in a wild place far from common eyes, at a time when magic was feared and its practitioners hunted. It was another two hundred years before the four peoples would marry one another. Wand magic did not take its modern form until the eighteenth century.

In its first years Hogwarts was a half-built hall of grey stone, with half a roof and no gate. There was no Forbidden Forest, because the forest had not yet been forbidden to anybody. Villagers came up to stare at a school of magic on a crag in all that weather. Many of them gave it ten years. The founders went out into the country to find children who showed the signs, and brought them back to be taught. Helga Hufflepuff taught there herself.

Once, in the early days, a very tall old man in a grey hat walked up out of the valley in the snow. He sat half the night by the kitchen fire with the first-years, and told them that magic was a gift held in trust, given long ago by Somebody who had never given up on them.

Hogwarts is one of the eleven long-established wizarding schools of the world. Its American counterpart, Ilvermorny, was founded about 1627 on Mount Greylock in Massachusetts by Isolt Sayre. Isolt was a descendant of Salazar Slytherin who had been forbidden Hogwarts as a girl, and she modelled her school on the one she never saw.

The quarrel and the Chamber

For a time the four worked in concert. Salazar Slytherin mistrusted the children of non-magical parents, and would have had magic taught only to those of magical families. In the end he quarrelled bitterly with Godric Gryffindor and left the school, which broke Helga Hufflepuff's heart.

The break came over the Basilisk. When Muggles came against Hogwarts, Salazar set the great serpent on them to defend the castle. Godric would not have a school that defended itself in that way against the people it had to live beside, and the two of them fell out past mending.

Legend held that before Salazar went he built a hidden Chamber within the castle. It was sealed so that only his true heir could open it, and loose the horror inside to purge the school of the unworthy. The legend has his purpose wrong: he had kept the serpent to defend the school, and he left it beneath the school to defend it still. The most learned witches and wizards searched the castle for the Chamber many times without success. Professor Binns taught that it did not exist. It did. It was opened in 1943, and again in 1992.

About a thousand years ago the castle also saw to it that none of the old midnight roads, which run from one crossroads to the next across the world, came within twenty miles of it.

The castle and grounds

Hogwarts is a vast castle bristling with turrets and towers. It has a thousand windows, and stands on a cliff above a black lake with mountains behind it. First-years cross the lake by boat on their first night, and enter through an ivy-hidden tunnel to an underground harbour. Older students ride up from Hogsmeade station in carriages; at least a hundred of them met the train in 1993.

The gates are flanked by pillars topped with winged boars. From them a drive winds up through the trees to the oak front doors and the Entrance Hall. In the hall, great hourglasses filled with jewels keep the running total of each house's points. Ambrose Greyhame took the hourglasses for Rowena Ravenclaw's idea.

The castle has a hundred and forty-two staircases, many of which move or have vanishing steps. Some doors open only if asked politely, or tickled in the right place. Hundreds of living portraits visit one another's frames, and the suits of armour are said to walk at night. One corridor has a wall-hanging of trolls in tutus. A stone gargoyle guards the stair to the Headmaster's office, whose password in the summer of 1993 was Acid Pop.

The Great Hall holds four long house tables and a staff table. It is lit by thousands of floating candles, under a ceiling enchanted to show the sky outside. Gryffindor Tower stands on the seventh floor. Professor McGonagall's study is on the first floor, as is the hospital wing. The trophy room is on the third floor, and the Slytherin common room lies in the dungeons under the lake. The kitchens are below the Great Hall, reached by a corridor that hardly anybody but the house-elves uses.

In winter the castle smells of woodsmoke, roast potatoes and wet wool. At Hallowe'en 1991 a thousand live bats hung from the walls, and a thousand more swooped over the tables. At Christmas twelve trees stand in the Great Hall, and the suits of armour hum carols.

The Marauder's Map showed seven secret passages out of the castle in 1993. One of them, behind the mirror on the fourth floor, had fallen in the winter before. Another runs from the hump of the one-eyed witch on the third floor to the cellar of Honeydukes in Hogsmeade.

The grounds hold the lake, the greenhouses, the Quidditch pitch, the Owlery, Hagrid's hut and the edge of the Forbidden Forest. There is also the Whomping Willow, planted over the tunnel to the Shrieking Shack when Remus Lupin was admitted as a boy. A giant squid lives in the lake, and on warm days it basks in the shallows.

Protections

Hogwarts is Unplottable. To Muggle eyes it looks like a mouldering ruin, with signs warning of danger. Enchantments prevent anyone from Apparating into the grounds or Disapparating out of them. Others guard against entry by stealth.

The gates are locked by a great many enchantments. In December 1992 they opened at once for Ambrose Greyhame, rather the way a dog rolls over for someone it knows. In the summer of 1993 they swung open without a sound for John Constantine. Dumbledore has said that it is very rare for anybody to cross the castle without his noticing.

In the school year 1993 to 1994 Dementors from Azkaban guarded every entrance to the grounds, in the hunt for Sirius Black. After Black's first break-in, Professor Flitwick taught the oak front doors to recognise his face from a poster. On the night Black escaped from Flitwick's office, not one Dementor got inside the castle. Flitwick said the thousand-year-old protections had held.

School life

Students are sorted into four houses by the Sorting Hat on their first night. All year they win and lose points for their house in the contest for the House Cup. Teaching runs over seven years, with Ordinary Wizarding Level examinations in the fifth year and Nastily Exhausting Wizarding Tests in the seventh. Third-years and above may visit Hogsmeade on certain weekends with a form signed by a parent or guardian. Each house fields a Quidditch team, and the four play for the Quidditch Cup.

Some twenty ghosts live in the castle, among them the four house ghosts and Professor Binns, who teaches History of Magic. There is also the poltergeist, Peeves.

Hogwarts has no chapel, and nobody says grace at its tables. The Fat Friar, who was a boy there when it was new, believes it is God's own joke that wizards keep Christmas every year without knowing whose feast it is. Remus Lupin found the castle magnificent, but steeped as much in dark magic as in light, which made it very hard for a Garou to bear. He said he could smell the Wyrm everywhere in it.

The Defence Against the Dark Arts post became so hard to fill that people thought it jinxed. Quirinus Quirrell held it in 1991 to 1992, Gilderoy Lockhart in 1992 to 1993 and Lupin in 1993 to 1994.

The Board of Governors oversees the school; Lucius Malfoy sat on it in 1992 and 1993. Albus Dumbledore has been Headmaster throughout these years, with Minerva McGonagall as his deputy. The rest of the staff include Severus Snape for Potions, Filius Flitwick for Charms, Pomona Sprout for Herbology and Sybill Trelawney for Divination. Rubeus Hagrid is Keeper of Keys and Grounds. From 1993 he has also taught Care of Magical Creatures. Madam Hooch teaches flying, Madam Pomfrey runs the hospital wing and Madam Pince keeps the library. Argus Filch is the caretaker.

In the saga

In the 1991 to 1992 year Harry Potter arrived by boat across the lake on 1 September 1991. He was sorted into Gryffindor, and Dracina Malfoy into Slytherin. Dumbledore closed the right-hand corridor on the third floor, where a three-headed dog stood over a trapdoor, guarding the Philosopher's Stone. In the course of the year a troll was let into the dungeons at Hallowe'en, and a unicorn was killed in the Forest. Quirrell, carrying Lord Voldemort on the back of his head, went down through the trapdoor after the Stone, and was stopped by Harry. Gryffindor took the House Cup at the end-of-year feast.

Before the 1992 to 1993 year began, the house-elf Dobby warned Harry of a plot to make terrible things happen at Hogwarts. On Hallowe'en a message on a second-floor wall announced that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened. Over the following months a cat, three students, a ghost and a prefect were Petrified. In December Ambrose Greyhame walked up from Hogsmeade in the first snow. He left a long package with Dumbledore, which Dumbledore hid in the Sorting Hat.

In the spring the governors suspended Dumbledore, Hagrid was taken to Azkaban and the school came close to closing. Students were escorted everywhere and confined to their common rooms after six. Quidditch was suspended. After Harry killed the Basilisk and closed the Chamber, the plan to send everybody home was cancelled. A feast in pyjamas went on all night.

In the summer of 1993 Hogwarts stood nearly empty when John Constantine came up the lane from Hogsmeade at Dumbledore's summons, with a D'ni linking book in a carrier bag. Riddle had once called Hogwarts the only place that had ever felt like home. Harry, waiting out the summer at Privet Drive four hundred miles away, felt the same.

Throughout the 1993 to 1994 year Dementors stood at the winged-boar gates. Sirius Black slashed the Fat Lady's portrait at Hallowe'en. In March he reached a Gryffindor dormitory with a knife, after which the castle was locked down so tightly that no student could go out after dark. Lupin taught Harry the Patronus in the History of Magic classroom. Buckbeak escaped his execution at sunset, and Black escaped from Flitwick's office through a D'ni linking book. At the end of term the Great Hall was hung with scarlet and gold, as Gryffindor won the House Championship for the third year running.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

By late August 1994 the new school year had not yet begun.

In Book Four, Chapter Four, Harry took down the chart on which he crossed off the days until 1 September, with eleven squares left. At the Burrow he saw an envelope in green ink propped on the kitchen mantelpiece. Hogwarts letters always come in green ink, so he took it for a letter from the school about Fred and George, as Molly said it was. She had had more owls from Hogwarts about the twins than about all her other children together. The letter was really from Dracina Malfoy. At dinner Percy hinted at a top secret event that his department was organising for after the World Cup.

In Chapter Five Hermione explained why she never spoke of the Muggle world's troubles. Hogwarts was the one place they could not get in, and she did not want to be the one who let them in. At the gate of the Burrow Molly asked why Harry could not have one nice, quiet year at Hogwarts. Harry joked that his favourite part of every year was the Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher trying to kill him. On the campsite he saw teenagers from schools abroad, and wondered for the first time about schools besides Hogwarts. At lunch Ludo Bagman let slip that something already agreed and signed was going to happen at Hogwarts. Barty Crouch cut him off, while Percy called it classified. Harry prayed for one quiet year.

In Chapter Six Narcissa Malfoy thanked Harry for saving her daughter's life once in every year Dracina had been at Hogwarts: from a troll, a diary and a werewolf. She remembered standing in the school's entrance hall at fifteen, waiting for James Potter to come down the stairs, while her twin sister Bellatrix waited there too. The sisters had fought over him so fiercely that Professor Flitwick used to hide behind his desk.

pages.title: Great Hall
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Hogwarts Castle, off the entrance hall
Four long house tables, with the High Table across the top
Bewitched to look like the sky outside
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The Great Hall is the dining hall of Hogwarts, where the whole school eats, the first-years are sorted and the feasts are held. It is lit by thousands of candles floating in the air above four long house tables, with the High Table for the staff across the top. Its ceiling is bewitched to look like the sky outside, so that anyone looking up sees stars, or storm clouds, or the blue of a summer morning.

The Hall

The Hall is dressed for every feast. There are bats and pumpkins at Hallowe'en. At Christmas there are trees and holly. The house tables can be cleared away when the room is wanted for something else. Exams are sat there under wards against cheating, with Anti-Cheating Charms on the quills.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Harry Potter first saw the Hall on 1 September 1991, when he was sorted into Gryffindor under its floating candles.

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, at Hallowe'en 1992, it was hung with live bats. Hagrid's monstrous pumpkins had been carved into lanterns big enough for three men to sit in. In Chapter Twelve the long tables vanished for the Duelling Club, and a golden stage stood in their place under the starry ceiling. In Chapter Fourteen, at Christmas, the Hall held a dozen frosted trees under streamers of holly and mistletoe. Warm, dry, enchanted snow fell from the ceiling.

In Chapter Fifteen, on Boxing Day morning, Dracina Malfoy came into the Hall at breakfast in her nightdress and bare feet, searching wildly for the diary. Harry had taken it from the Slytherin common room on Christmas night. She flew at him with her fists, sobbing, until Dumbledore came down the Hall and laid a hand very gently on top of her head. He told the school that she had an uncommon complaint called Morrigan's Fever. On Valentine's Day 1993 Gilderoy Lockhart covered the walls of the Hall with enormous pink flowers, while heart-shaped confetti drifted down from the ceiling.

In Book Three, Chapter Five, the enchanted ceiling was black and cloudy for the start-of-term feast on 1 September 1993. In Chapter Nine, on Hallowe'en night 1993, after Sirius Black had slashed the Fat Lady's portrait, Percy Weasley sent the house tables drifting to the walls with a wave of his wand. The whole school slept in the Hall in purple sleeping bags. In Chapter Fifteen Harry looked up at the hundreds of candles under the ceiling and wondered who had lit the very first one.

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine and Lucius Malfoy were sorted in the Hall in 1964, a few minutes apart, both into Slytherin. Later John sat his exams there and found the gaps in the wards the way water finds the gaps in a roof. He was never once caught.

pages.title: The Entrance Hall
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Hogwarts, inside the great oak front doors
The Great Hall; the marble staircase; the dungeons
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
The Entrance Hall is the vast, echoing hall just inside the front doors of Hogwarts. Flaming torches in brackets light its stone walls, the ceiling is too high to make out, and a magnificent marble staircase faces the doors, leading to the upper floors. It is so big that the Dursleys' whole house would fit inside it.

The hall

Doors off it open into the Great Hall, while a flight of stone steps runs down to the dungeons. Suits of armour stand round the walls. The great hourglasses that keep the score for the House Cup stand there too, one for each house, filled with rubies, sapphires, yellow diamonds or emeralds. There is a noticeboard for school notices.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, on 1 September 1991, Harry Potter saw it for the first time. It could have swallowed the Dursleys' house whole.

In Book Two, Chapter Eight, on 5 September 1992, Professor McGonagall met Harry and Ron Weasley there to set their detentions for flying the car to school. In Chapter Fifteen, on Boxing Day 1992, about twenty suits of armour came down off their plinths, linked arms and danced the can-can, singing in deep metal voices a song Harry was fairly sure was not a carol. Peeves conducted them from the chandelier with a stick of celery. Fred and George had enchanted them.

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty, after Hermione Granger turned back time, she and Harry came out into the empty Entrance Hall in golden evening sunlight. They hid in a broom cupboard while their earlier selves passed through.

The Interlude of Book Three tells how John Constantine, as a Slytherin student in the 1960s, paid back a sixth-year who had read his father's letter out at breakfast. On Valentine's Day he pinned the boy's own love letter, a dreadful thing full of poetry, to the noticeboard in the Entrance Hall, with the girl's name in the margin. The girl laughed for a week. The boy never forgave him.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, on 22 August 1994, Narcissa Malfoy told Harry Potter that meeting him was like being fifteen again, standing in 'that dreadful entrance hall' waiting for a boy with hair like his to come down the stairs. Her twin sister, Bellatrix, used to wait there for James Potter too.

pages.title: The Black Lake
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
The grounds of Hogwarts, below the castle
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The Black Lake is the great dark lake below Hogwarts, stretching away from the foot of the castle's cliff to the edge of the Forbidden Forest. New students cross it by boat on their first night, four to a boat. Beneath its water live the giant squid, the merpeople and the grindylows. Somewhere under it, through solid rock, lies the Slytherin common room.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, on 1 September 1991, Harry Potter crossed the lake in the little boats with the other first-years, four to a boat. In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, at Christmas 1992, the lake froze over. Fred and George Weasley built a snow fort beside it.

In Book Three, Chapter Twelve, in the second week of January 1994, the lake froze hard right out to the middle. Harry found Dracina Malfoy alone at the edge, throwing small stones that went skittering away over the ice, singing. 'It's the best noise in Britain,' she said. For about four minutes the two of them skimmed stones without a word, which was the longest Harry had ever been comfortable in anybody's company. Then a Hufflepuff second-year who had walked thirty feet out on the ice looked down, saw the black depths under his feet and went through. A sixth-year hauled him out.

In Chapter Sixteen, in the hot weather before the June exams, the giant squid drifted on the lake like an old dog asleep in a bath. In Chapter Nineteen, on the night of the full moon, a hundred dementors or more came sweeping round the shore in a single black swarm. In Chapter Twenty Harry, who had gone back three hours in time, stood on the opposite bank and drove them off with a Patronus. It galloped across the water as though the lake were a floor, and it was a stag. The memory he held on to as he cast it was of skimming stones with Dracina across the singing ice in January.

The Interlude of Book Three tells how, in John Constantine's third year at Hogwarts, a gang of fifth years dangled him by his ankles out of a tower window over the lake. They held him there so long that the giant squid came up to have a look at him.

pages.title: Forbidden Forest
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
The edge of the Hogwarts grounds
Out of bounds to all pupils
Centaurs, unicorns, Acromantulas, thestrals and other creatures
Firenze, Bane, Aragog; a wild Ford Anglia
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
The Forbidden Forest is the ancient wood on the edge of the Hogwarts grounds. It is out of bounds to all pupils and known to be full of dangerous creatures, although when the castle was founded it was simply the forest. In Harry Potter's first three years it sheltered the dying Voldemort, the Acromantula colony of Aragog, the Weasleys' runaway car, the fugitive Sirius Black and the escaped hippogriff Buckbeak.

Description

The Forest runs from the edge of the lawns beyond Hagrid's hut deep into the mountains, a dark mass of old trees cut by streams and clearings. Every year, at the start-of-term feast, Dumbledore reminds the school that it is forbidden to all pupils. It was not always so. When Gandalf, now Ambrose Greyhame, first stood on the crag above the lake, with four young founders shouting at one another in the mud, there was no gate, no drive and no Forbidden Forest either, because the forest had not yet been forbidden to anybody. It was simply the forest.

A herd of centaurs lives there under its own laws. Among them are Bane, Ronan and the gentler Firenze, all of them readers of the stars. There are unicorns, whose blood will keep alive a creature close to death, at the price of a cursed half-life. There are thestrals. Deep in the trees, in a hollow of its own, lives the colony of giant spiders founded by Hagrid's Acromantula, Aragog.

Hagrid is the Forest's keeper. Harry told Ron in 1993 that the centaurs and unicorns were all right. Remus Lupin smelt of the Forest at night.

In the saga

In early 1992 Harry followed Snape on his broom to a shadowy clearing in the Forest. From a beech tree he overheard Snape pressing Quirrell about Fluffy and the Philosopher's Stone.

Later that spring Quirrell led four first-years into the Forest on a detention: Harry, Hermione, Neville and Dracina Malfoy. They were supposedly collecting mushrooms along a trail of silver. Quirrell then ran off screaming with the light, using the children as bait for a unicorn that would not come near him. Left alone with Harry and the only lamp, Dracina demanded that he escort her. She held his hand, overjoyed that her knight was protecting her. A unicorn came to her and let her touch it. Then a hooded figure killed it with green light and drank its blood. Harry's scar blazed, Dracina fled, and the centaur Firenze, defying Bane, carried Harry to safety. Firenze told him that Voldemort was drinking unicorn blood while he waited for the Stone.

On 1 September 1992 the Weasleys' Ford Anglia crashed into the Whomping Willow with Harry and Ron inside it. The wrecked car threw out their luggage, then roared off into the Forest, where it lived wild for months. In May 1993 Harry and Ron followed a line of spiders into the Forest with Fang. It was Ron's first time inside it. They met the feral car, and then they were carried off to Aragog's hollow. The blind old spider told them he had never been the monster of the Chamber, then gave them to his children as food. The car crashed into the hollow and rescued them.

In the winter of 1993 the Forest lay white with snow at Christmas, and Sirius Black, escaped from Azkaban, was living in it as a great black dog. At sunset on the day Buckbeak was to be executed, in June 1994, the hippogriff broke loose and flew into the Forest with a hooded rider on his back. It was Dracina Malfoy, who had lured him with a dead ferret and hid him there. That night Dementors drifted through the trees, leaving frost and rags of cloak on the branches. Lupin, who had missed his potion, roamed the Forest in his Garou war form.

In a clearing by a stream Dracina dived to Harry's rescue on Buckbeak. Harry knelt in the water in front of her while she sobbed into his back, and cast a Shield Charm that turned white as the moon came out. It swept through the creature, restoring Lupin to his human shape. Harry lifted Dracina out of the stream and forgave her.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Four, in August 1994, the Weasleys' old Ford Anglia was still living wild among the trees of the Forest. Harry Potter supposed that it was still frightening the centaurs.

pages.title: The third-floor corridor
aliases: the third-floor corridor on the right-hand side
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Fluffy, the three-headed dog, standing on a trapdoor
pages.html:
The third-floor corridor on the right-hand side at Hogwarts was closed to students for the school year of 1991 to 1992. Behind a locked door in it, Hagrid's three-headed dog Fluffy stood on a trapdoor. Under the trapdoor lay the protections round the Philosopher's Stone.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the start-of-term feast in 1991, Dumbledore gave the school its notices: 'And lastly, I must tell you that this year the third-floor corridor on the right-hand side is out of bounds to all who do not wish to die a most painful death.' He did not say why. In Chapter Five, running from Filch on the night of the midnight duel that never was, Harry, Ron, Hermione and Neville came up against a locked door. Hermione opened it with Alohomora, and they tumbled through, only to find themselves face to face with a monstrous three-headed dog standing on a trapdoor.

In Chapter Ten, in the weeks that followed, Harry, Ron and Hermione crept up to the door whenever they passed it, pressing their ears to the wood to make sure Fluffy was still growling on the other side. In Chapter Twelve, on the night they went after the Stone themselves, they found it already open a crack.

In Book Two, Chapter Five, Harry remembered how Professor McGonagall had come up behind him and Ron outside the third-floor corridor during their first year, without a sound. He put it away in the drawer in his head marked later, with Kosovo, Kandahar and a place called Zanzibar Land.

pages.title: Gryffindor Tower
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Hogwarts Castle; the entrance is on the seventh floor
The portrait of the Fat Lady
The Fat Lady; Sir Cadogan, from November 1993 to the spring of 1994
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Gryffindor Tower is the home of Gryffindor house at Hogwarts. Its entrance is the portrait of a fat lady in a pink silk dress on the seventh floor, and nobody gets past her without the password. Behind her lies a snug, circular common room crowded with squashy armchairs, with the dormitories up spiral staircases beyond it.

The tower

The boys' dormitories are round rooms at the top of a spiral staircase, each with five four-poster beds hung with deep red velvet curtains. The password changes often, and in theory only Gryffindors know it.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Harry Potter first climbed to the tower on 1 September 1991. Percy Weasley gave the Fat Lady the password, Caput Draconis, and Harry found his four-poster waiting for him in the first-year boys' dormitory. In Chapter Five he learnt that the Fat Lady's portrait was on the seventh floor.

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, the whole house waited up in the common room to cheer Harry and Ron Weasley's arrival. In Chapter Fourteen Harry, Hermione Granger and the Weasleys had the tower almost to themselves over Christmas 1992. They played Exploding Snap. With the furniture pushed back, they practised duelling. In Chapter Sixteen, on the evening before the Hufflepuff match, Harry's dormitory was ransacked. Hermione pointed out that only Gryffindors knew the password. Harry was not so sure. At the end of the year before, on the night they went down through the trapdoor, Dracina Malfoy had been standing in that very common room. Neville Longbottom had confessed afterwards that he had told her the password, because she had been nice to him.

In Book Three, Chapter Five, Harry was back in the circular dormitory with its five four-posters. In Chapter Nine, after Sirius Black slashed the Fat Lady's portrait at Hallowe'en 1993, Sir Cadogan took over the entrance, since nobody else would take the job. He changed the password at least twice a day, and one of them was Oddsbodikins. In Chapter Thirteen, in March 1994, Black got into the boys' dormitory with a written list of passwords. He had a knife.

In Chapter Fourteen Sir Cadogan was sacked, and the Fat Lady came back to the entrance with a gang of security trolls to guard her. Neville was not to be told the password. Harry told him anyway. 'Password's Victis, Neville,' he said, in a low voice, so that the trolls would not hear. In Chapters Fifteen and Sixteen it was Flibbertigibbet. In Chapter Eighteen it came out that Crookshanks had stolen the passwords for Black.

pages.title: Gryffindor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Gryffindor Tower, seventh floor, behind the portrait of the Fat Lady
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Gryffindor is one of the four houses of Hogwarts, founded by Godric Gryffindor for the bold, the daring and the true. Its colours are scarlet and gold. Its emblem is a lion. Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger were sorted into it in 1991. With them it ended Slytherin's long hold on the House Cup. It won the House Championship three years running, from 1992 to 1994, as well as the Quidditch Cup in 1994.

Founder and history

The house takes its name from Godric Gryffindor, the red-headed young firebrand from the moors. He was one of the four founders whom Gandalf gathered on the crag above the lake, and who opened the school in 990. Gryffindor thought any quarrel a sword could not end was not worth having. He carried the ancient blade that was later miscalled the Sword of Gryffindor.

He welcomed children of non-magical parents. His bitter quarrel with Salazar Slytherin was over Slytherin's use of the Basilisk against the Muggles who attacked the castle, and it ended with Slytherin leaving the school. The rivalry between the two houses has outlasted both men by a thousand years.

Gryffindor has produced a long line of the wizarding world's champions. Albus Dumbledore is said to have been a Gryffindor. Rubeus Hagrid was one until his expulsion in 1943. In the 1970s the house held James Potter, Sirius Black, Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew. They called themselves the Marauders, and they made the Marauder's Map. Lily Evans was in the house with them. Minerva McGonagall played on the house Quidditch team in her own schooldays.

By 1991 the house had fallen on lean years. Slytherin had won the House Cup six years running, and Nearly Headless Nick told the new first-years that Gryffindor had never gone so long without it. The house had not won the Quidditch Cup since about 1987, when Charlie Weasley was its Seeker. Every Weasley has been sorted into Gryffindor.

Traits

The Sorting Hat sends to Gryffindor 'the bold, the daring and the true'. The house prizes courage, nerve and chivalry. Its members are expected to stand up for others, whatever it costs them.

When the Hat sorted Harry it noted 'a good deal of courage' among other things. Dumbledore told him in 1993 that it is choices, far more than abilities, that show what a person truly is. He also told Harry that the sword which came to him in the Chamber can only be wielded by a true Gryffindor.

The Hat has warned, too, that Gryffindor's courage, like every house's virtue, can be turned to evil in the wrong hands. Not everybody admires it. The eleven-year-old John Constantine decided that Gryffindor was for brave people too thick to know any better.

Colours and emblem

Gryffindor's colours are scarlet and gold. Its emblem is a rampant lion, its element is fire, and its hourglass in the Entrance Hall is filled with rubies. The house-point hourglasses were Rowena Ravenclaw's idea.

When Dumbledore awarded Gryffindor the House Cup in June 1992 he clapped his hands. The green hangings of the Great Hall turned scarlet, the silver turned gold, and a towering Gryffindor lion took the place of the Slytherin serpent. On 2 September 1993 Dracina Malfoy's hair ribbons were found to have turned scarlet and gold, by Hermione Granger's doing.

Head of house

Minerva McGonagall, Transfiguration teacher and Deputy Headmistress, is Head of Gryffindor. She is very strict. She is no fairer to her own house than to any other. In 1992 she took fifty points each from Harry, Hermione and Neville Longbottom. She took twenty more when Dean Thomas led a second chant at the Slytherin match.

She is also quietly loyal. She took no points for the flying car, because term had not yet begun. She privately covered for Harry over the dragon, as she had once covered for his father. In 1994, when the house won the Quidditch Cup, she wept harder than Oliver Wood into a Gryffindor flag the size of a bedsheet.

House ghost

The ghost of Gryffindor Tower is Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, known as Nearly Headless Nick. He died on 31 October 1492. In December 1992 he was Petrified by the Basilisk. He is a cheerful, rather touchy figure in a ruff and tights, who greets each year's new Gryffindors at the start-of-term feast.

Common room

The Gryffindor common room is at the top of Gryffindor Tower. It is reached through a round hole behind the portrait of the Fat Lady, a large woman in a pink silk dress on the seventh floor, who swings forward when given the password. It is a snug, round room, crowded with squashy armchairs and lopsided tables. A fire burns in the grate, and there is a notice board by the portrait hole.

Spiral staircases lead to separate dormitories for the boys and girls; in 1993 the third-year boys' dormitory held five four-poster beds hung with red velvet. Entering another house's common room without permission from a member of staff is an expellable offence.

The passwords change regularly. In the first fortnight of the autumn term of 1991 the password changed from Caput Draconis to Pig snout. In September 1993 it was Fortuna Major. After Sirius Black slashed the Fat Lady at Hallowe'en 1993, the mad knight Sir Cadogan took her place. He changed the password constantly, through 'Scurvy braggart', 'Oddsbodikins' and 'Scurvy cur'.

In March 1994 Black got in using a list of the week's passwords that Neville Longbottom had written down and lost. Sir Cadogan was sacked. The mended Fat Lady came back under the guard of security trolls, with whom she flirted. The password that month was 'Victis'.

Notable members in the saga

Harry Potter, sorted in 1991, has been the house Seeker since his first year, the youngest house player in about a century. Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger are his closest friends. The rest of their year are Neville Longbottom, Seamus Finnigan, Dean Thomas, Lavender Brown and Parvati Patil.

Of the Weasleys, Bill was a Gryffindor before Harry's time. Charlie was the Seeker in the house's last Cup-winning side before 1994. Percy was a prefect, then Head Boy, and left in 1994 with the highest N.E.W.T. grades there were. The twins, Fred and George, are the house Beaters. Ginny was sorted on 1 September 1992.

Oliver Wood was Keeper and captain until he left in 1994. The Chasers are Angelina Johnson, Alicia Spinnet and Katie Bell. Lee Jordan commentates on the matches. Colin Creevey was sorted in 1992, and Petrified that November.

Of earlier generations, the house can claim Lily Potter, Rubeus Hagrid and Minerva McGonagall. James Potter, Sirius Black, Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew, the four Marauders, were Gryffindors too.

House Cup and Quidditch Cup by year

1985 to 1991: Slytherin held the House Cup six years running. Gryffindor's last Quidditch Cup was won about 1987, with Charlie Weasley as Seeker.

1991 to 1992: Gryffindor beat Slytherin 170 to 60 in November, with Harry catching the Snitch in his mouth. Then it beat Hufflepuff, when Harry caught the Snitch in about five minutes under Snape's refereeing. That put the house top of the House Championship for the first time in nearly seven years. The loss of a hundred and fifty points in one night, over Norbert the dragon, sent it to last place. Without Harry, who was in the hospital wing, it was steamrollered by Ravenclaw in its last match, so it did not win the Quidditch Cup. At the end-of-year feast the House Cup stood at Gryffindor 312, Hufflepuff 352, Ravenclaw 426 and Slytherin 472. Then Dumbledore awarded fifty points to Ron, fifty to Hermione and sixty to Harry, which levelled Gryffindor with Slytherin at 472. Finally he took a hundred points from Slytherin for Dracina Malfoy's trespass in the Gryffindor common room. Gryffindor won the Cup for the first time in seven years.

1992 to 1993: Gryffindor lost twenty points for Harry's remark about Filch's parentage, ten in Potions, five to Percy and twenty for Dean's chant. It went top of the House Cup all the same, with fifty points for Harry's catch against Slytherin in November, which he made with a broken arm. The Hufflepuff match was cancelled in the spring, when Hermione and Penelope Clearwater were Petrified. No Quidditch Cup was played for that year. The two hundred points each awarded to Harry and Ron for Services to the School won Gryffindor the House Cup for the second year running. The feast went on until half past three in the morning.

1993 to 1994: Slytherin pulled out of the opening fixture. Gryffindor lost to Hufflepuff by a hundred points in a November storm, when Dementors invaded the pitch and Harry fell. The house lost sixty points in a single Potions lesson after Ron threw a crocodile heart at Dracina. In early March, on the new Firebolt, Harry called a time-out, turned a 40 to 10 deficit round and beat Ravenclaw 230 to 70. Slytherin went into the final two hundred points clear, so Gryffindor had to win by more than two hundred. It led 80 to 20 when Harry caught the Snitch, winning 230 to 20 to take the Quidditch Cup for the first time in seven years. Mostly thanks to the final, Gryffindor won the House Championship for the third year running.

1994 to 1995: the new school year had not yet begun in late August 1994.

In the saga

Harry's Sorting in 1991 was a near thing. The Sorting Hat told him he could be great in Slytherin, and placed him in Gryffindor only because he begged it not to send him there. The house took him to its heart after the Hufflepuff match. It turned on him when he lost it a hundred and fifty points. When he and Ron crashed the flying car into the Whomping Willow in 1992, it greeted them as heroes. Dean Thomas, a West Ham supporter, led the Gryffindor stand in football chants against Hufflepuff and Slytherin, which the other houses took up.

In 1992 to 1993 Lee Jordan pointed out that the Basilisk's victims were two Gryffindors, a Gryffindor ghost, a Ravenclaw, a Hufflepuff, and not a single Slytherin. Ginny Weasley was taken into the Chamber. In 1993 to 1994 the house sat up all night in its pyjamas after Black's second break-in. When Wood put the Quidditch Cup into Harry's hands, the Gryffindors poured over the barriers in their hundreds and carried the team off on their shoulders. Harry later realised that Dracina Malfoy had let him win the final, as her way of saying sorry.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, at the World Cup final on 22 August 1994, Harry Potter remembered the day in the spring when he had thrown mud at Dracina Malfoy near the Shrieking Shack. Snape never seemed to care about anything except docking points from Gryffindor. That day, though, he had cared very coldly about the state in which Dracina arrived at his door.

Members

Every witch and wizard in the saga sorted into Gryffindor, principal characters first.

  • Albus Dumbledore
  • Ginny Weasley
  • Harry Potter
  • Hermione Granger
  • Minerva McGonagall
  • Ron Weasley
  • Sirius Black
  • Charlie Weasley
  • Colin Creevey
  • Dean Thomas
  • Fred Weasley
  • George Weasley
  • Nearly Headless Nick
  • Neville Longbottom
  • Oliver Wood
  • Percy Weasley
  • Peter Pettigrew
  • Alicia Spinnet
  • Angelina Johnson
  • Katie Bell
  • Lavender Brown
  • Lee Jordan
  • Parvati Patil
  • Seamus Finnigan
  • The Fat Lady
  • The Gryffindor fifth-year
  • The leek-eared duellists
  • Godric Gryffindor
  • James Potter
  • Lily Potter

pages.title: Hufflepuff
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Kindness, loyalty, hard work, patience, fair play
In the basement, near the kitchens
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Hufflepuff is one of the four houses of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, founded by Helga Hufflepuff for 'the fair of heart who see a hard task through'. Its colours are yellow and black, with the badger for its emblem. It has a name for kindness, loyalty and making everybody welcome. Its ghost, the Fat Friar, was taught by Helga herself when the school was new. In November 1993 its captain, Cedric Diggory, gave Gryffindor its only defeat of the season.

Founder and history

The house takes its name from Helga Hufflepuff, the round, sensible, warm-hearted farm girl from the valleys of Wales who fed the other founders and made them sit down. Gandalf privately thought her the cleverest of the four. She taught at Hogwarts in its first years, when it was a hall on a crag with half a roof, and she once boxed the ears of the boy who became the Fat Friar for turning the porridge into frogspawn. Each of her colleagues chose students for a single quality. Helga undertook to teach all the rest and to treat every one of them the same. Her house has kept that welcome ever since. Salazar Slytherin's departure broke her heart.

Hufflepuff has always been the most underrated of the houses. Dean Thomas's chant of 1992 asked what a Hufflepuff was good for and answered 'guarding the coal'. On her first day in Diagon Alley, Dracina Malfoy announced that if she were put in Hufflepuff she would go straight home. The magizoologist Newt Scamander was a Hufflepuff.

What the house values

The Sorting Hat sends to Hufflepuff 'the fair of heart who see a hard task through'. The house prizes kindness, loyalty, hard work, patience and fair play. In 1993 the Fat Friar told Harry Potter that he would have made a decent Hufflepuff, being loyal to a fault and working like a dog. John Constantine decided at eleven that it was the house for the nice ones.

The Hat has also warned that even Hufflepuff's kindness, its loyalty and its welcome can be bent by somebody who has convinced herself that she is working for the greater good. In 1994 two first-year Hufflepuffs were found arguing in the library over whether to trust a healed wound. Harry explained them simply as Hufflepuffs. Dracina said they were like a sort of weather.

Colours and emblem

Hufflepuff's colours are yellow and black. Its emblem is the badger, its element is earth, and its hourglass in the Entrance Hall is filled with yellow diamonds. The Hufflepuff team wore canary yellow for the match that was called off in the spring of 1993. At the November 1993 match the Hufflepuff end of the stadium was one great mass of yellow and black, five hundred voices strong.

Head of house

Pomona Sprout, who teaches Herbology, is Head of Hufflepuff. In 1992 the second-year Gryffindors shared Herbology with the Hufflepuffs, and she taught them to repot Mandrakes. The Mandrakes she raised that year cured the Basilisk's victims. In March 1993 several of them threw a loud party in Greenhouse Three that kept half of Hufflepuff awake, which made her very happy indeed.

House ghost

The Hufflepuff ghost is the Fat Friar, a plump, round, bald Benedictine monk with a rope girdle, who always seems to be pleased about something. He was a Hufflepuff himself. He waves to every new Hufflepuff at the Sorting, and in 1991 he argued that Peeves deserved one more chance. He haunts the tall window at the far end of the ground-floor corridor that leads down to the kitchens, close to his own house.

Common room

The Hufflepuff common room is in the basement, on the same corridor as the kitchens. The way in lies behind a stack of large barrels in a shadowy nook on the right-hand side of the passage. Tapping the barrel two from the bottom, in the middle of the second row, in the rhythm of 'Helga Hufflepuff' opens its lid on to a passage. Tapping the wrong barrel, or tapping in the wrong rhythm, drenches the intruder in vinegar.

The room itself is round, earthy and low-ceilinged. Round windows at ground level look out on grass and dandelions. There is honey-coloured wood everywhere, with copper fittings and a great many plants, some of which talk or dance. Round doors lead off to the dormitories, where the beds have patchwork quilts and copper warming pans. Over the wooden mantelpiece hangs a portrait of Helga Hufflepuff, raising a small golden cup.

Notable Hufflepuffs

Cedric Diggory, big, steady and decent, was captain as well as Seeker in 1993 to 1994. After he won the November match against Gryffindor he tried to have it replayed, because he had not known that Harry had fallen. Justin Finch-Fletchley was Petrified in December 1992 and apologised to Harry about fifteen times at the end-of-year feast. Ernie Macmillan accused Harry of being the Heir of Slytherin in the library in 1992, then apologised in Herbology the following spring. Hannah Abbott and Susan Bones were the first two pupils to be sorted in 1991.

The house can also claim the Fat Friar, who was Helga Hufflepuff's own pupil; the big, worried prefect whom Dracina scratched in the Great Hall on Boxing Day 1992; and the enormous sixth-year who hauled a second-year Hufflepuff out of the frozen lake in January 1994.

The Cups, year by year

1991 to 1992: Hufflepuff lost to Gryffindor when Harry caught the Snitch after about five minutes. Snape refereed, awarding Hufflepuff penalties for nothing at all, while the Gryffindor stand sang at the bewildered Hufflepuffs. At the end-of-year feast Hufflepuff stood third for the House Cup with 352 points. After Dumbledore's last-minute awards it finished fourth, behind Gryffindor (472), Ravenclaw (426) and Slytherin (372).

1992 to 1993: the Hufflepuffs joined Dean Thomas's chant against Slytherin in November. Their own match against Gryffindor was called off on the morning it was due to be played, when Hermione Granger and Penelope Clearwater were found Petrified. No Quidditch Cup was played for that year.

1993 to 1994: under its new captain, Cedric Diggory, Hufflepuff beat Gryffindor by a hundred points in a November hurricane. Cedric caught the Snitch as more than a hundred dementors flooded on to the pitch and Harry fell fifty feet. Hufflepuff was gracious in victory, almost unbearably decent about it, as Hufflepuffs are. Ravenclaw flattened it at the end of November, and Gryffindor took both Cups.

In the saga

In 1992 a group of Hufflepuffs who ought to have been in Herbology sat in the library deciding that Harry must be the Heir of Slytherin. When he stepped out from behind the shelves, they looked as though they had been Petrified on the spot. During the scare of spring 1993 some Hufflepuffs took to walking along the corridors with their backs to the wall, so that nothing could come at them from behind.

At the November 1993 match Dean Thomas led a football chant from the Gryffindor end. From the Hufflepuff end, from the house that was supposed to apologise when you trod on it, came the answer to the same tune, deeper, louder and in better time. Fred and George bowed to the Hufflepuff stand. The whole stadium laughed together. At the 1994 final the Hufflepuffs booed the Slytherins. When John Constantine was fifteen, the Hufflepuff girls were the first in the school to go after him.

pages.title: Ravenclaw
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Ravenclaw Tower, on the west side of the castle
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Ravenclaw is one of the four houses of Hogwarts, founded by Rowena Ravenclaw for 'the quick of wit'. Its colours are blue and bronze; its emblem is the eagle. Through the early 1990s it was the strongest of the houses standing between Slytherin and Gryffindor. In 1992 it finished second for the House Cup, and it beat Gryffindor at Quidditch that year.

Founder and history

The house is named after Rowena Ravenclaw, the tall, proud girl from the glens of Scotland who thought nothing worth knowing that could not be written down in a book. She was one of the four founders whom Gandalf brought together in the mud on the crag above the lake in 990. She once argued with him all night and lost. It was the only time, she said, that any man had won an argument with her.

When Ambrose Greyhame came up to the castle in December 1992, he saw the jewelled hourglasses that keep the house points in the Entrance Hall and laughed out loud. That, he said at once, would have been Rowena's idea: 'Make a competition of it, and then make sure everybody wins something.'

Her daughter Helena, the Grey Lady, haunts the castle as the Ravenclaw ghost. Rowena owned a diadem that was said to enhance the wisdom of its wearer. It passed out of the knowledge of the wizarding world after Helena stole it and fled to Albania. Moaning Myrtle, who died in the second-floor bathroom in 1943 when the Chamber of Secrets was opened, was a Ravenclaw.

In 1971 John Constantine, a Slytherin, was going out with a Ravenclaw girl whose laugh carried right across the Great Hall. Lucius Malfoy had wanted her for a year. The quarrel ended the two boys' friendship, with a duel and then a fistfight in a fourth-floor corridor.

Traits

The Sorting Hat's song promises that 'in Ravenclaw the quick of wit will find their kindred kind'. The house prizes intelligence, learning, wisdom and wit. Its pupils are known for their love of books, and for their originality of mind. The words carved in its common room are 'Wit beyond measure is man's greatest treasure'. In 1992 the Hat warned that Ravenclaw's cleverness, like every house's virtue, can be turned to evil in the wrong hands.

John Constantine, at eleven, took Ravenclaw to be the house for the clever ones, and fully expected to be sorted into it. Hermione Granger, before her own Sorting, thought Ravenclaw would be all right too.

Colours and emblem

Ravenclaw's colours are blue and bronze. Its emblem is an eagle, and its element is air. Its hourglass in the Entrance Hall is filled with sapphires. At the March 1994 match against Gryffindor, the Ravenclaw team stood in the middle of the pitch, a block of blue against the grass.

Head of house

Filius Flitwick, the tiny Charms master, is Head of Ravenclaw. In 1991 he knew of the special circumstances behind Harry's broomstick. In 1994, after Sirius Black's second break-in, he spent a morning on a stool in the Entrance Hall, holding up a poster of Black until the oak front doors had learnt the face. He kept the captured Black in his office, and Black escaped from it through a D'ni linking book.

He secretly paid a pupil's nine-Galleon debt in 1994, then shamed the boy, Hobday, over two Sickles. He remembers the long feud between Bellatrix and Narcissa Black in his Charms classes in the 1970s.

House ghost

The Ravenclaw ghost is the Grey Lady: tall, pale and beautiful, in a high-collared gown. She rarely speaks to anyone. Her favourite window is on a landing near the top of a tower. There, in December 1992, she recognised Ambrose Greyhame as the man who had come to her mother when she was very small.

Common room

The Ravenclaw common room is at the top of Ravenclaw Tower, on the west side of the castle, up a spiral staircase. Its door has no handle and no keyhole. There is only a bronze knocker in the shape of an eagle, which asks a riddle of anyone who wants to come in. A sensible answer opens the door, so that nobody gets in without thinking.

The room is wide and circular. Silks of blue and bronze hang on its walls. Arched windows look out over the grounds to the mountains. The domed ceiling is painted with stars, and the carpet matches it. In a niche opposite the door stands a tall statue of Rowena Ravenclaw in white marble, wearing her diadem.

Notable members in the saga

Penelope Clearwater is the curly-haired prefect whom Harry and Ron met by mistake in the Entrance Hall at Christmas 1992. She was Petrified near the library in 1993, and she was secretly going out with Percy Weasley. In 1994 she bet him ten Galleons on the Ravenclaw against Gryffindor match, and lost.

Cho Chang, the house's small, quick Seeker, stuck to Harry like glue in 1994. Roger Davies, the captain in 1993 to 1994, was a big fifth-year built like a rower. Terry Boot, Mandy Brocklehurst and Lisa Turpin were sorted into Ravenclaw in Harry's year, in 1991, along with Padma Patil. Among earlier generations the house counts Moaning Myrtle and the Grey Lady herself.

House Cup and Quidditch Cup by year

1991 to 1992: Ravenclaw finished second for the House Cup with 426 points. Gryffindor won with 472; Slytherin had 372, and Hufflepuff 352. At Quidditch, Ravenclaw ended the season by steamrollering Gryffindor, whose Seeker was in the hospital wing.

1992 to 1993: Ravenclaw cheered against Slytherin at the November match and joined in Dean Thomas's chant from the Gryffindor stand. Quidditch was suspended in the spring, and no Cup was played for. Gryffindor won the House Cup.

1993 to 1994: Ravenclaw flattened Hufflepuff at the end of November, Cho Chang taking the Snitch from Cedric Diggory like a thrown dart. In January it lost narrowly to Slytherin, having led for an hour; Dracina Malfoy took the Snitch at the Ravenclaw end with about four inches to spare. In March it led Gryffindor 30 to 10, and later it closed the gap to 80 to 70. Then Harry caught the Snitch, and Gryffindor won 230 to 70. Gryffindor took both cups.

In the saga

At the House Cup feast in 1992 the Ravenclaws enjoyed Slytherin's defeat as much as everybody else. Earlier that year, like the rest of the school, they had turned on Harry when he lost Gryffindor a hundred and fifty points, since everyone had wanted to see Slytherin lose the Cup for once.

In 1992 a big Ravenclaw sixth-year leaned over the barrier to tell Dean Thomas that football was a game in which nobody scored, and nearly came to blows with him. During the scare of spring 1993, a Ravenclaw first-year burst into tears in the Charms corridor because somebody had dropped a book behind her.

On Hallowe'en night 1993, when the school slept in the Great Hall after Black's first break-in, the Ravenclaws came down clutching books they had no intention of reading. Early in 1994 Harry found a Ravenclaw sixth-year lying flat on the gravel with a lantern, testing a fleece twice over. The Ravenclaws applauded good play even against their own side. At the 1994 final the house, which usually stayed out of things, stood up to shout at the Slytherins.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, at the World Cup final on 22 August 1994, Dracina Malfoy trained her Omnioculars on 'that Chang girl from Ravenclaw', who sat with her family in the stands opposite. Cho Chang had her own Omnioculars trained quite openly on the Top Box, and Dracina was sure she meant to bewitch Harry away from her.
