The Slytherin stand went berserk. A whole row of them surged towards the steps, and Crabbe's older cousin took his jacket off. Then Professor McGonagall seized Lee Jordan's megaphone. Her last order was for the boy in the Slytherin stand in the green scarf, who was to put his jacket back on that instant.

pages.title: The Slytherin sixth-year on the rail
infobox: Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary, Chapter Eleven
pages.html:
The Slytherin sixth-year on the rail climbed on to the rail of the Slytherin stand during the match against Gryffindor in November 1992 to shake both fists at the Gryffindors.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, the Gryffindor stand greeted the start of the match with a song Dean Thomas had written, to a tune from the terraces at West Ham. It was a very rude song about Slytherins, and by the third chorus most of the stadium had joined in. Harry Potter, swooping low over the Slytherin stand, saw a sixth-year climb on to the rail to shake both fists at the singers. A whole row of Slytherins surged towards the steps. Then Professor McGonagall seized Lee Jordan's megaphone and ordered every one of them to sit down.

pages.title: The Ravenclaw sixth-year who mocked football
infobox: Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary, Chapter 11
pages.html:
The Ravenclaw sixth-year who mocked football was a big Ravenclaw whose cousin had once taken him to a match. At the Slytherin match of November 1992 he announced that he had had more excitement watching Flobberworms breed, and very nearly came to blows with Dean Thomas over it.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, Dean stood on his seat in the Gryffindor stand, holding up a red card at Dracina Malfoy. Seamus Finnigan explained that it came from football. The big Ravenclaw in the row behind leaned over the barrier to sneer at the game. 'My cousin took me once. I've had more excitement watching Flobberworms breed.'

Dean, a West Ham supporter, went red. He told the Ravenclaw to come down to Upton Park on a Saturday and say that to the Chicken Run. Both of them began to climb over the seats. Ron Weasley shoved himself in between them, talking very fast. 'Twenty-two of them, and only one ball, it's dead clever when you think about it.' Dean sat down, muttering. After a moment the Ravenclaw did too.

pages.title: The Ravenclaw girl with long curly hair
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
The Ravenclaw girl with long curly hair came up out of the dungeons on Christmas night 1992, straight into two boys who looked exactly like Crabbe and Goyle. She was Penelope Clearwater, the Ravenclaw prefect.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, Harry and Ron, transformed by Polyjuice Potion, were waiting in the empty Entrance Hall for a Slytherin to follow down to the Slytherin common room. The words were hardly out of Ron's mouth when a girl with long curly hair came out of the entrance to the dungeons. Ron hurried up to her and said they had forgotten how to get back to their common room.

'Your common room?' she said stiffly. 'I'm in Ravenclaw.' She walked off, looking back over her shoulder at them suspiciously.

In Chapter Sixteen Harry found her Petrified in the hospital wing, and knew her at once for the Ravenclaw they had stopped by mistake.

pages.title: The girl singing a lullaby
infobox: High, sweet and a little cracked
December 1992, in a dark corridor at Hogwarts
pages.html:
The girl singing a lullaby is the unknown owner of a voice that Harry Potter heard in a dark corridor at Hogwarts in December 1992, moments before he found Justin Finch-Fletchley and Nearly Headless Nick Petrified. Nobody knows who she was.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, Harry was walking down a corridor whose torches had been blown out by an icy draught. Somewhere ahead a girl was singing a slow, old-fashioned lullaby, the kind of song you sing to a baby to get it to sleep. Her voice was high, sweet and a little cracked. Harry could not make out the words. All the same, it made the hairs rise on the back of his neck, as the voice in the walls had done on the night of the Deathday Party.

When he called out "Hello?" the singing stopped. Quick, light footsteps went away round the far corner. Probably Myrtle, Harry told himself; she had sounded a bit like Myrtle. Halfway down the passage he tripped over Justin, lying rigid on the flagstones. Beside him floated Nick, gone black and smoky.

pages.title: Fawkes
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
A golden perch by the door of the Headmaster's office
pages.html:
Fawkes is Albus Dumbledore's phoenix, a scarlet and gold bird who lives on a golden perch in the Headmaster's office. In June 1993 he came to Harry Potter in the Chamber of Secrets, and carried him out of it.

Nature

As Dumbledore told Harry, a phoenix can lift enormous weights, and its tears will heal almost any wound. There is no more faithful friend in the world. Its song is said to put courage into the pure of heart, and fear into the impure. Phoenixes are among the very last remnants of an age long gone. They are very hard to tame, and few wizards have ever had one.

At the end of each life a phoenix bursts into flame on its Burning Day, and rises again from the ashes as a newborn chick. Two of Fawkes's tail feathers lie at the cores of two wands, Harry's and Lord Voldemort's. Fizzing Whizbees give him hiccups.

He was not in the Headmaster's office in 1943, when Dumbledore was still a teacher. When Harry saw that office in the memory kept in Tom Riddle's diary, there was no golden perch, and no phoenix.

In the saga

In December 1992 he looked like a half-plucked turkey. Ambrose Greyhame, who waited in the office overnight, told him that he would soon feel better. Shortly afterwards he burst into flame in front of Harry, and a newborn chick rose from the ashes.

In the Chamber of Secrets, in the dark, a voice told Harry: 'Your work is not yet done, my child.' Then Fawkes came, with a single long note like a trumpet and a bell at once. He stooped down the whole height of the Chamber, and dropped the Sorting Hat into Harry's hands. When the diary was destroyed he sang very softly on a broken pillar. Afterwards he flew Harry, Ron, Ginny Weasley, Dracina Malfoy and the memoryless Gilderoy Lockhart up the pipe, with Harry holding on to his strangely hot tail feathers.

Dumbledore told Harry what had brought the bird to him: 'You must have shown me real loyalty, down there in the Chamber. Nothing else could have brought Fawkes to you.' That night Fawkes carried Dumbledore's letter to Azkaban. At half past three in the morning he came back riding on Hagrid's shoulder.

In the summer of 1993 he dozed on his perch while Dumbledore received John Constantine, and lifted his head when the Headmaster grew angry.

pages.title: The man from Paris
infobox: For years, at Malfoy Manor; by every sign, dancing
pages.html:
The man from Paris taught Dracina Malfoy for years at Malfoy Manor, because her mother insisted on it. By every sign his lessons were in dancing. She learnt enough from him to find fault with the way Harry Potter turned on a broomstick.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, in the autumn of 1992, Harry flew the best he ever had in the Quidditch match against Slytherin, diving and pulling up again in the rain. Dracina, sitting sidesaddle on her broom, asked whether he had taken up ballet. Then, in a smaller, softer voice, she offered to teach him. She had had lessons for years, she said. Mother had made her, at the Manor. There had been a man from Paris. Harry dropped his shoulder when he turned, which was why he wobbled. She could show him, if he would only ask. ‘I'm not asking you for anything,’ said Harry.

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, in June 1994, Dracina spoke of him again as she listed the luxuries of her life for Hermione Granger: he was the man who came by Floo all the way from Paris to teach her to dance.

pages.title: Cornelius Fudge
infobox: Cornelius; Fudge; Minister; Minister for Magic; Minister of Magic

Arthur Weasley employee
Lucius Malfoy benefactor, host of, generous friend
Ministry of Magic head
Walden Macnair Ministry employee
Severus Snape withdrew his Order of Merlin
Bartemius Crouch subordinate he relies on
The Bulgarian Minister for Magic counterpart
Ministry of Magic, Minister for Magic
Junior Minister, Department of Magical Catastrophes
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Cornelius Fudge is the Minister for Magic, a portly, anxious, amiable man. In Albus Dumbledore's words, he means well, loudly and often, without the faintest idea what to do about anything. Since 1993 the escape of Sirius Black has been the great crisis of his time in office. By the summer of 1994 he was frightened by what he knew of the troubles in the Muggle world, and had been to see the Muggle Prime Minister four times since the spring.

Career and character

In 1981 Fudge was Junior Minister in the Department of Magical Catastrophes. He was one of the first on the scene after a street full of Muggles was blown apart and Peter Pettigrew was believed killed. He became Minister for Magic in 1990, in succession to Millicent Bagnold. At first he leant heavily on Dumbledore for advice. By 1994 he had been dealing with dementors for twenty years.

He is a short, stout man with untidy grey hair and a worried face. In 1993 he wore a striped Muggle suit and a scarlet tie under a long black cloak. He had on pointed purple boots, and he carried a lime-green bowler hat. He also owns a long pinstriped cloak. His hand is soft and damp. He drinks redcurrant rum. Harry thinks him rather like an older Percy Weasley, or like a Muggle politician such as John Major.

Flattery shows on Fudge at once: he glows, and turns pink. He boasts that he never trusts a report he has not read twice. Lucius Malfoy says that he has an exceedingly loud voice when he believes himself to be whispering. Fudge, for his part, calls Lucius a very generous man to all sorts of good causes.

In the saga: the Chamber of Secrets

In December 1992 Fudge summoned Dumbledore to the Ministry overnight over the attacks at Hogwarts. In the spring of 1993, after Hermione Granger and Penelope Clearwater were Petrified, he came down to Hagrid's hut. He took Hagrid off to Azkaban without a hearing, as a precaution: 'Four Muggle-borns attacked now. Four. It's gone far enough. The Ministry's got to step in.' Harry watched it all from under the Invisibility Cloak. When Lucius Malfoy arrived with the governors' Order of Suspension, Fudge objected that if Dumbledore could not stop the attacks, nobody could.

In the saga: Sirius Black

When Sirius Black escaped from Azkaban in July 1993, Fudge went to the prison that same night. There he was told that Black had been talking about Hogwarts in his sleep. Fudge kept that out of the papers. He told the Daily Prophet that every resource of the Ministry was turned to finding Black. He also briefed the Muggle Prime Minister, a step without precedent in peacetime, for which the International Confederation of Wizards criticised him. It was Fudge who, on an earlier inspection, had handed Black the newspaper with the Weasleys' photograph in it. He remembered Black as strangely normal. Black had asked him whether he had finished with the paper, because he missed the crossword.

At dawn after Harry fled Privet Drive in August 1993, Fudge was waiting for him outside the Leaky Cauldron, cold and exhausted. He steered Harry into a private parlour. He laughed off Harry's claim to be Barry Trotter. Instead of punishing him, he gave him tea and crumpets. The Accidental Magic Reversal Squad, he said, had punctured Aunt Marge and modified her memory. Harry would not be punished. The Dursleys would take him back next summer, provided he stayed at Hogwarts for Christmas and Easter. Fudge shivered at the thought of Dumbledore having 'another word' with the Dursleys, for he had seen for himself how little love they had for Harry.

He gave Harry room eleven, on condition that he stayed in Diagon Alley and came back before dark. He told Harry that his aunt's house was the safest place for him, because of the blood ward. Glowing under Harry's flattery, he still refused to sign his Hogsmeade form: rules were rules. Afterwards Harry realised that he had been expertly handled.

Before Christmas 1993 Fudge came to Hogsmeade to discuss Black, and dined with Dumbledore. In the Three Broomsticks he went over the story of the Potters' betrayal with Professor McGonagall, Professor Flitwick, Hagrid and Madam Rosmerta. Harry listened to all of it, hidden behind a Christmas tree. Fudge said the dementors were furious at being kept out of the grounds. He remarked that 'those parasite creatures and those Nephilim' would not be bothering them again. McGonagall's reply, about her file, made his legs shudder. Early in 1994 the Ministry authorised the Kiss on Black.

In the saga: June 1994

Fudge came to Hogwarts on the day of Buckbeak's appeal to witness the execution for the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures. He insisted that the Committee was independent. When the hippogriff vanished, he flapped about helplessly while the executioner, Walden Macnair, raged.

That night, after Snape brought in Black, Fudge praised Snape and talked of an Order of Merlin. He admitted that Black had never been properly tried. All the same, the Kiss had been authorised and signed: 'My hands are tied, I'm afraid. Quite tied.' Harry flattered him in the hospital wing, then mocked him to his face.

When Black vanished from Flitwick's locked office, Fudge blamed 'dementor hysterics', the worst frenzy he had seen in twenty years. He hinted that Dumbledore might have had a hand in it. Then he accepted Snape's account, and dropped the matter. Because Black was loose again, he withdrew Snape's Order of Merlin, patting him on the shoulder: 'Next time, perhaps!' Dumbledore later convinced him that Lupin had been trying to save the children's lives.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Six: Fudge watched the Quidditch World Cup final on 22 August 1994 from the Top Box, in a green bowler hat. He greeted Harry as an old friend, and Harry flattered him on purpose, eyes wide, with a shy smile borrowed from Hermione. Fudge credited the Portkeys to Barty Crouch's Department of International Magical Co-operation, calling Crouch a splendid fellow. He was enchanted when Harry suggested that nobody ever thanked him for the paperwork. He had been miming to the Bulgarian Minister all day, believing that the man spoke no English; he admitted that he was no great shakes at languages, and needed Crouch for that sort of thing. Introducing the Malfoys, he told Harry that Lucius was fond of him, then mangled the Bulgarian's name as Oblansk or Obalonsk.

Then Harry pressed him about the Muggle at the campsite, about mutants, Khan's Augments and the giant American robots built to hunt mutants down. Fudge waved Mr Roberts away, laughing at the idea of mutants. All the same his hand went to the brim of his hat, turning it round, then round again. Muggle matters, he insisted, went through the proper office, by the proper channels. There were arrangements. He began to mention the Prime Minister, then stopped himself. When Lucius Malfoy asked what the channels were, Fudge answered sharply: 'Confidential, Lucius. Quite confidential.' Harry said he would tell the next lot with the torches that there were channels. Fudge hooted with laughter, then hurried off to deal with the Bulgarians' demand for twelve more chairs, with a sheen of sweat on the back of his neck.

Lucius told Harry afterwards that Fudge had been to see the Muggle Prime Minister four times since the spring, and came back from Downing Street grey in the face. For the first time in his life, Lucius said, Fudge was frightened of something other than the Daily Prophet. He predicted that Fudge would go home to tell his wife what a charming boy Harry was.

When the final was over, Fudge was outraged to learn that the Bulgarian Minister spoke English after all. He received the World Cup in the Top Box. When a jinx of Lucius's, aimed at John Constantine, set a gilded pillar alight, he dived behind the Cup with a squeal. From behind it he said faintly that he would want a word with Lucius's old school friend.

In their own words

Four Muggle-borns attacked now. Four. It's gone far enough. The Ministry's got to step in.Cornelius Fudge · B2 Ch16
I had no choice, and I'd do it again.Cornelius Fudge · B3 Ch3
And frankly, who would believe him?Cornelius Fudge · B3 Ch3
At least we know those parasite creatures and those Nephilim won't be bothering us again.Cornelius Fudge · B3 Ch10

pages.title: Mad-Eye Moody
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
A magical eye; a wooden leg; part of his nose missing
The Order of the Phoenix, in the first war
pages.html:
Mad-Eye Moody is Alastor Moody, the most famous Auror of his day, now retired. He walks with a long staff as well as carrying a wand. Albus Dumbledore once named him as perhaps the only other wizard alive who could match the staff-magic that Ambrose Greyhame had taught Dumbledore.

The Auror

Moody fought through the first war against Lord Voldemort in the Order of the Phoenix, and he filled half the cells in Azkaban. Nearly every Dark wizard he caught left a mark on him. His face is badly scarred, a chunk of his nose is missing, and he has a wooden leg. In place of one eye he wears a magical one, which swivels in every direction and sees through solid things. He trusts nobody.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Dumbledore told Ambrose that there were not five wizards living who could do what Ambrose had taught him with a staff. 'Maybe old Mad Eye,' he said. Not even the Unspeakables could do it any more. They had all forgotten. They thought it a quaint old country thing, like Morris dancing, and they used nothing but wands.

pages.title: Godric Gryffindor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The moors of the West Country
Co-founding Hogwarts (990); founding Gryffindor house; the Sorting Hat
Gandalf (Ambrose Greyhame), who gathered and taught the four founders as young adults
Andúril, which the goblins later renamed the Sword of Gryffindor
Through the Pevensies and Lily Potter, an ancestor of Harry Potter on his mother's side
pages.html:
Godric Gryffindor was one of the four founders of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, which opened in 990, and the founder of Gryffindor house. He was a red-headed firebrand from the moors. With the other three founders he was gathered as a young man by Gandalf, who mentored the four of them while they built the school. He came of the line of Aragorn and Arwen. Aragorn's sword, Andúril, was his by right of blood, and through that same line he is an ancestor of Harry Potter on his mother's side. His quarrel with Salazar Slytherin over Slytherin's use of the Basilisk against Muggles broke the four apart.

Birth and blood

Gryffindor came from the wild moors of the West Country, where the village of Godric's Hollow still bears his name. He was of the line of Aragorn, the King of the West, and of Arwen Evenstar. Their blood had come down through the Flood and the forgotten ages, unrecognised among men. It carried the old magic of the Elves and of Númenor.

Nobody needed to tell Godric that he was a king's heir for him to behave like one. Gandalf remembered him as a young man who thought any quarrel a sword could not end was not worth having. He became the finest duellist of his age.

Gandalf and the four

Gandalf had been sent to the peoples of the isle after the Flood to teach them light magic. For thousands of years he watched them go off in a hundred different directions with what he gave them, quarrel about it, forget half of it and make up the rest. In the tenth century he set out to give that magic a home.

He sought out four gifted young witches and wizards, every one of them from a different people, with a different tradition of magic. There was Godric Gryffindor, the red-headed firebrand from the moors; Rowena Ravenclaw, the tall proud girl from the glens; Helga Hufflepuff, the sensible farm girl from the valleys; and Salazar Slytherin, the watchful young man from the fens.

He stood the four of them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake and set them to build a school together. When they began there was no gate, no drive, no Forbidden Forest: only a half-built hall of grey stone on the crag, a great deal of mud and four young people shouting at one another. For years afterwards he mentored them. He taught them, argued with them, held them to the work and kept them from one another's throats. It took him eleven years to get them to sit down at the same table, and he broke two staffs on it.

Hogwarts opened in 990. Long afterwards, walking the road to the castle alone in the snow, Gandalf said to nobody in particular: "You did well, all of you. Better than I ever told you."

The founding

With his colleagues Godric went out into the country to find children who showed the signs of magic, whoever their parents were. He would turn none of them away. His house, he said, would take the brave: those of courage, daring, nerve and chivalry.

He is credited with the hat that became the Sorting Hat. The four founders put something of their own minds into it so that it could choose their students after them. It still speaks of all four as people it knew.

The sword

Gryffindor wielded a long sword with a blade bright as water, running with strange letters, which was not his by origin. It was Andúril, the sword of Elendil reforged for Aragorn. Gandalf placed it in Godric's hands when he gathered the four founders, because it was his by right of blood: he was one of Aragorn's descendants, of the ancient and noble line to which the sword belongs. Dumbledore described it as having passed through a series of brave men, Godric among them. It can be wielded, he said, only by men of Godric's calibre.

Millennia of history had worn the blade down by the time it came to him. Godric took it to the goblins, the finest smiths of the isle, and the goblin smith Ragnuk the First repaired it.

That repair was how the goblins came to claim the sword. After Godric died they put about the name "the Sword of Gryffindor", and they claimed that they had forged it for him. The claim was a trick, laid down as the grounds on which they meant to take the sword for themselves. It had just enough truth in it to be believed. Before they could take it, Gandalf stole it back and kept it hidden, holding it for the day when another of Aragorn's heirs would need it. The histories record only that the sword of Gryffindor vanished.

It slept for a very long while. In December 1992 Gandalf, as Ambrose Greyhame, brought it back to Hogwarts, and it came to Harry Potter out of the Sorting Hat in the Chamber of Secrets. Dumbledore called the name by which it had been known a trick of the goblins.

The quarrel with Salazar

In the first years Godric and Salazar Slytherin were close friends. Their quarrel became the most famous in the history of the school. Salazar mistrusted Muggles and the children of Muggle families, with good reason, given what had been done to people like him before the four came together. Godric would take any child who had magic.

The break came over the Basilisk. When Muggles came against Hogwarts, Salazar set the great serpent he kept on them to defend the castle. Godric would not abide a school that defended itself by such means against the very people it had to live beside. The two of them fell out past mending.

Salazar left Hogwarts, which also ended his love affair with Helga Hufflepuff. The story told in later centuries, that he left because he wished to purge the school of the unworthy, is only a legend. The rivalry between the two houses has outlasted both men by a thousand years.

Descendants

Godric's line, the line of Aragorn and Arwen, went on quietly among the families of the isle for a thousand years. In the twentieth century it ran through the four Pevensie children, Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy, who were crowned in Narnia. It ran on through Susan, the only one of them to survive the railway crash that killed the others, to her daughter Lily, then to Lily's son, Harry Potter.

Godric is therefore Harry's ancestor on his mother's side. The sword came back to the line it belonged to when Harry drew it from the Sorting Hat in the Chamber of Secrets. Besides Gandalf himself, exactly two people living know of that descent: Albus Dumbledore and Lord Voldemort. Harry's descent through his father, from King Arthur, is a separate line.

Legacy

His house, Gryffindor, prizes courage, daring, nerve and chivalry. Its colours are scarlet and gold. Its emblem is the lion. His hat still sorts every new pupil who comes to the castle, a thousand years after he wore it.

In the saga

In December 1992 Ambrose Greyhame handed Dumbledore a long package wrapped in oilcloth. It had slept a long time since Godric used it, he said, and it had earned its rest. Dumbledore laid it inside the brim of the Sorting Hat. Later that day, when Harry asked the Hat whether it had placed him rightly, it told him that Godric would have been very proud of him.

In the Chamber of Secrets in 1993 Harry drew the sword from the Hat, killed the Basilisk with it and pierced Riddle's diary. Riddle called it a borrowed sword from a long-forgotten ancestor.

pages.title: Helga Hufflepuff
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Co-founding Hogwarts (990); founding Hufflepuff house; bringing the house-elves to the Hogwarts kitchens
Gandalf (Ambrose Greyhame), who gathered and taught the four founders as young adults
Salazar Slytherin, until he left Hogwarts
pages.html:
Helga Hufflepuff was one of the four founders of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, which opened in 990, and the founder of Hufflepuff house. She was a young woman, a warm-hearted, sensible farm girl from the Welsh valleys, when Gandalf gathered her with the other three to build the school. He mentored the four of them for years. In his private opinion she was the cleverest of them all. She held the quarrelsome founders together and welcomed every kind of student. She and Salazar Slytherin were lovers until his falling out with Godric Gryffindor took him away from Hogwarts. It broke her heart.

The farm girl from the valleys

Helga came from the broad valleys of Wales. Gandalf remembered her as a round, sensible, warm-hearted farm girl who fed them all and made them sit down. He privately thought her the cleverest of the four.

She was famous for her charms, above all her charms to do with food. Many of the dishes still served at the Hogwarts feasts began as her recipes.

Gandalf and the four

Gandalf had been sent to the peoples of the isle after the Flood to teach them light magic. For thousands of years he had watched them go off in a hundred different directions with what he gave them. They quarrelled about it, forgot half of it and made up the rest.

In the tenth century he set out to give that magic a home. He went looking for four gifted young magicians, each from a different people with its own tradition of magic: Godric Gryffindor, the red-headed firebrand from the moors; Rowena Ravenclaw, the tall, proud girl from the glens; Helga Hufflepuff, the sensible farm girl from the valleys; and Salazar Slytherin, the watchful young man from the fens.

He stood the four of them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake and set them to build a school together. For years afterwards he mentored them. He taught them, argued with them, held them to the work and kept them from one another's throats. It took him eleven years to get them to sit down at the same table, and he broke two staffs on it.

Hogwarts opened in 990, with no gate on the drive and no forest yet forbidden to anybody. Long afterwards, walking the road to the castle alone in the snow, Gandalf said to nobody: "You did well, all of you. Better than I ever told you."

Hufflepuff house

Each of her colleagues chose students for a single quality. Helga said she would take the rest, teach them all and treat them just the same. Her house has kept that welcome ever since.

She is credited with bringing the house-elves into the castle kitchens, where they could work in safety and be treated well.

She taught at Hogwarts when it was new. The Fat Friar, then a boy in his first week, had his ears boxed by her for turning the porridge into frogspawn. She caught him with his hand in the honey crock more times than he could count. He remembers her as a great woman and a terrible cook, which he insists is no contradiction.

Helga and Salazar

Of the four, Helga was the one who saw past Salazar Slytherin's suspicion and his sharp tongue. The two of them became lovers. For some years the warmest of the founders and the most guarded were together.

It ended when Salazar left. His quarrel with Godric Gryffindor over his use of the Basilisk to defend Hogwarts from Muggles could not be mended. He went away from the school and from her. His going broke her heart.

The cup

Helga owned a small golden cup with two fine handles, engraved with a badger. It was a family heirloom, said to have magical properties, and it came down through her descendants. Her portrait in the Hufflepuff common room shows her raising it in welcome.

Legacy

Her house prizes kindness, loyalty, hard work, patience and fair play. Its emblem is the badger; its colours are yellow and black. Its ghost is the Fat Friar, who was her pupil.

In the saga

In 1992 the Sorting Hat warned Harry Potter that her virtues could be turned like any other: 'Even Hufflepuff's kindness, even its loyalty and its welcome, can be bent, Harry, by somebody who's convinced herself she's working for the greater good.'

In 1994 the Fat Friar told Harry about his schooldays under Helga Hufflepuff. Hogwarts was a new thing on a crag then, and half the villagers who came up to stare at it gave it ten years.

pages.title: Rowena Ravenclaw
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Co-founding Hogwarts (990); founding Ravenclaw house; naming the school; the house-point hourglasses
Gandalf (Ambrose Greyhame), who gathered and taught the four founders as young adults
Wit beyond measure is man's greatest treasure
pages.html:
Rowena Ravenclaw was one of the four founders of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, which opened in 990, and she founded Ravenclaw house. She came from the Scottish glens, a tall, proud girl who grew into the most brilliant witch of her day. Gandalf gathered her as a young woman with the other three founders, set the four of them to build the school and mentored them while they did it. It was Rowena who gave Hogwarts its name, and Rowena who thought of the hourglasses that keep the house points. Her daughter Helena is the Grey Lady, the Ravenclaw ghost.

The girl from the glens

Rowena came from the glens of Scotland. Gandalf remembered her as a tall, proud girl who thought that anything which could not be written down in a book was not worth knowing. She was also the most brilliant witch of her day.

Gandalf and the four

Gandalf had been sent to the peoples of the isle after the Flood to teach them light magic. For thousands of years he watched them go off in a hundred different directions with what he had given them. They quarrelled about it, forgot half of it and made up the rest. In the tenth century he set out to give that magic a home of its own. He sought out four gifted young people, each from a different people of the isle, with its own way of doing magic: Godric Gryffindor, the red-headed firebrand from the moors; Rowena Ravenclaw, the tall, proud girl from the glens; Helga Hufflepuff, the sensible farm girl from the valleys; and Salazar Slytherin, the watchful young man from the fens.

He stood the four of them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake and set them to build a school together. For years afterwards he mentored them. He taught them, argued with them, held them to the work and kept them from one another's throats. It took him eleven years to get them to sit down at the same table, and he broke two staffs on it, banging for order. Hogwarts opened in 990, with no gate on the drive and no forest yet forbidden to anybody. Long afterwards, walking the road to the castle alone in the snow, Gandalf said to nobody: "You did well, all of you. Better than I ever told you."

The name and the hourglasses

It is said that Rowena dreamed of the place before Gandalf ever brought her there. In the dream a warty hog led her to a cliff above a lake. When at last she stood on the crag she knew it at once, and it was she who named the school Hogwarts, after the dream.

At Hogwarts she favoured pupils of ready intelligence. Her house still prizes wit, learning and wisdom. A thousand years later, when Gandalf saw the jewel-filled hourglasses in the Entrance Hall, he guessed at once that the house points had been her idea. It was exactly the sort of thing she would have done: make a competition of it, and then make sure everybody wins something.

Rowena and Gandalf

Of the four, she argued with Gandalf the most, and the best. Years after the founding, when her daughter was very small, he came to her house and the two of them argued by the fire all night. In the morning Rowena said he was the only man in the world who had ever won an argument with her. Her daughter still remembered him a thousand years later.

The breaking of the four

Rowena watched Godric Gryffindor's friendship with Salazar Slytherin turn to enmity over Salazar's use of the Basilisk to defend the castle from Muggles. She could not mend it. When Salazar left, the school went on with three founders. Ever after, her house and Helga's stood between the two rivals.

The diadem and her daughter

Rowena owned a diadem that was said to enhance the wisdom of its wearer. Her daughter Helena, jealous of her mother's fame, stole it and ran away to Albania. When Rowena fell mortally ill, she sent the Baron, a man who loved Helena, to bring her home. Helena refused to come. He killed her in a forest, and then he killed himself.

Rowena died without seeing her daughter again. Helena had hidden the diadem in a hollow tree in the Albanian forest, where it passed out of the knowledge of the wizarding world. She came back to Hogwarts as the Grey Lady, and the Baron as the Bloody Baron.

In the saga

In December 1992 the Grey Lady recognised Ambrose Greyhame on a moonlit tower landing and nearly wept. She remembered him as the man who had argued all night with her mother, and won. He put a finger to his lips. She bowed her head and stepped back into the shadows.

pages.title: Salazar Slytherin
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Co-founding Hogwarts (990); founding Slytherin house; the Chamber of Secrets
Gandalf (Ambrose Greyhame), who gathered and taught the four founders as young adults
After falling out with Godric Gryffindor over the Basilisk
pages.html:
Salazar Slytherin was one of the four founders of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, which opened in 990, and he founded Slytherin house. He was a Parselmouth from the fens, called Serpent-tongue. Gandalf gathered and mentored him as a young man, with the other three founders, to build the school. He and Helga Hufflepuff were lovers. When Muggles came against Hogwarts, he defended it with a Basilisk. Over that he fell out with Godric Gryffindor past mending, and he left the school, leaving Helga behind. The Sorting Hat insists that he was never evil. His last living descendant is Lord Voldemort.

The boy from the fens

Salazar came from the fens. Gandalf remembered him as a dark, clever, watchful young man who spoke to the adders in the reed-beds and trusted nobody, with good reason. He was famous for talking to snakes, which is why the emblem of his house is a serpent. People called him Serpent-tongue.

The Sorting Hat, which knew him, insists that he was never evil. He was difficult, proud and suspicious, with good reason, given what had been done to people like him before the four of them came together. He would never have stood for evil in himself, nor in his house. He mistrusted Muggles, as well as children whose parents were not magical, holding them unreliable and a danger. He wished the school to be more particular about whom it took.

Gandalf and the four

Gandalf had been sent to the peoples of the isle after the Flood to teach them light magic. For thousands of years he watched them go off in a hundred different directions with what he had given them. They quarrelled about it, forgot half of it and made up the rest. In the tenth century he set out to give that magic a home of its own. He sought out four gifted young people, each from a different people of the isle, with its own way of doing magic: Godric Gryffindor, the red-headed firebrand from the moors; Rowena Ravenclaw, the tall, proud girl from the glens; Helga Hufflepuff, the sensible farm girl from the valleys; and Salazar Slytherin, the watchful young man from the fens.

He stood the four of them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake and set them to build a school together. For years afterwards he mentored them. He taught them, argued with them, held them to the work and kept them from one another's throats. It took him eleven years to get them to sit down at the same table, and he broke two staffs on it, banging for order. Hogwarts opened in 990, with no gate on the drive and no forest yet forbidden to anybody. Long afterwards, walking the road to the castle alone in the snow, Gandalf said to nobody: "You did well, all of you. Better than I ever told you."

Helga

Helga Hufflepuff was the one of the four who saw past his suspicion, and the two of them became lovers. For some years the most guarded of the founders and the warmest were together. It ended only when he left Hogwarts, and his going broke her heart.

The Basilisk and the quarrel

Salazar kept a Basilisk, the king of serpents, whose gaze kills and which only a Parselmouth can command. When Muggles came against Hogwarts, he set it on them to defend the castle.

Godric Gryffindor had once been his close friend. He would not abide a school that defended itself by such means against the very people it had to live beside, and over that the two of them fell out past mending. It was the last of a great many quarrels between them, and the worst. For years they had argued about whom the school should take and what it owed the Muggle world. Salazar left Hogwarts, and he left Helga behind.

The Chamber of Secrets

Before he left, Slytherin built a hidden chamber deep beneath the castle, without the other founders' knowledge. He left the Basilisk sleeping in it, sealed so that only his true heir could open the Chamber and command the serpent. The legend, as Professor Binns tells it, holds that he meant his heir to use it to purge the school of everybody he thought unworthy to study magic. The Sorting Hat, which knew him, denies it. He had kept the serpent to defend the school, and he left it beneath the school to defend it still.

The entrance lies behind a sink in a second-floor bathroom. It is marked with a tiny snake, and it opens only to Parseltongue. At the far end of the Chamber stands a colossal statue of Slytherin himself, ancient and monkeyish, with a long, thin stone beard. The Basilisk came out of its mouth. For centuries the learned denied that the Chamber existed at all. Tom Riddle opened it in 1943 and turned the Basilisk on the school's own pupils. It was opened again, through Riddle's diary, in 1992 to 1993.

Descendants and legacy

Slytherin's line came down through the Gaunt family to Tom Marvolo Riddle, his last living descendant. Riddle called him the greatest of the Hogwarts Four. As Lord Voldemort, Riddle passed to Harry Potter, among other things, the power to speak Parseltongue. Among Slytherin's heirlooms was a heavy gold locket.

His house prizes ambition and cunning. Dumbledore listed the qualities Slytherin valued in his students as Parseltongue, resourcefulness, determination and a certain disregard for rules. The Hat told Harry that of all the minds it had ever sat on, Harry's reminded it most of Slytherin's.

One branch of his line crossed the Atlantic. His own wand came down through the Gaunts to Gormlaith Gaunt, whose niece Isolt Sayre stole it and carried it to America in 1620. Isolt founded Ilvermorny, the wizarding school of North America. After Gormlaith followed her there and was killed, Isolt buried Slytherin's wand in the school grounds, where a snakewood tree grew from it.

In the saga

Professor Binns told the legend of the Chamber to Harry's History of Magic class in November 1992, and dismissed it as nonsense. A few weeks later the Sorting Hat defended Slytherin to Harry at length. Harry, walking the dungeons disguised as Goyle, wondered who had designed a dungeon with so many corridors that went nowhere, and hoped Slytherin had enjoyed himself. In the Chamber Harry faced the Basilisk beneath Slytherin's statue and killed it.

pages.title: King Arthur Pendragon
aliases: the young king in the West Country
infobox: Excalibur, forged by the Elves of the Grey Havens
The Lady of the Lake, the Elf-lady Roma
Avalon, which was the Grey Havens, now the hidden Otherworld, where he sleeps
The Peverell brother who received the Cloak of Invisibility
The Potters, among them James and Harry Potter; the Braddocks, through a Squib branch
pages.html:
Arthur Pendragon was the young king in the West Country, a boy with a sword, a round table and a great deal more courage than sense. Gandalf advised him for years under the name of Merlin. His sword, Excalibur, was forged for him by the Elves of the Grey Havens, and the Lady of the Lake, who was one of them, gave it to him. When he lay dying after Camlann, he was carried to the Havens, which legend remembers as Avalon. Arthur descended from the Peverells, and his descendants took the name Potter before the Norman Conquest, to hide from his ancient enemies. Harry Potter is his direct descendant through his father.

Birth

Arthur was the son of Uther Pendragon, King of the Britons, by Igraine of Cornwall. He was conceived at Tintagel through Merlin's art, about the year 480, then raised in secret, well away from the court. Sir Ector brought him up as his own son, beside Ector's son Kay, and Arthur had no idea who he was.

The sword in the stone

When Uther died there was no clear heir, and the kingdom began to fall apart. About 495 a sword appeared in a stone in a London churchyard, with words in gold saying that whoever drew it out was the rightful king of all Britain. Every knight in the land tried and failed. Arthur, who had gone to fetch a sword for Kay, drew it out without knowing what it was. So he proved his right to the throne.

Excalibur

The sword from the stone did not last. It broke in Arthur's hand in a fight with King Pellinore, and Merlin took him to a lake to find a better one. There an arm clothed in white samite rose out of the water, holding a sword. It was Excalibur.

The Lady of the Lake was an Elf, one of the last of her people in these lands. The Elves of the Grey Havens had forged Excalibur for Arthur, and she gave it to him. Its scabbard was worth even more than the blade: so long as he wore it, he could lose no blood, however badly he was wounded.

Legend has given her several names, among them Nimue and Viviane. It also tells stories about her and Merlin that Gandalf has never troubled to correct.

Her name is Roma. Gandalf had fostered her, and in the 1990s she rules the hidden Havens as Roma of Otherworld.

Camelot and the Round Table

From Camelot he gathered the knights of the Round Table, at which no seat stood higher than another. Among them were Lancelot, Gawain, Percival, Bors and Galahad. He married Guinevere, defeated the Saxons and sent his knights on the quest for the Holy Grail, which only Galahad achieved.

The fall

His reign was broken by Lancelot's love for Guinevere, then by the treachery of Mordred. About 525 Morgana stole the scabbard of Excalibur and threw it into a lake. At the battle of Camlann, about 537, Arthur killed Mordred, but without the scabbard he was mortally wounded himself.

As he lay dying he sent Sir Bedivere to throw Excalibur back into the lake. Twice Bedivere could not bring himself to do it. The third time he threw it. An arm rose out of the water, caught it, brandished it three times and drew it under.

Legend says that three queens carried him away in a barge, and that Morgana was one of them. Whoever was in the barge, it was bound for the Grey Havens.

Avalon

Avalon was the Grey Havens, the old harbour of the Elves, from which their ships sail into the West. Círdan the Shipwright, who founded the Havens at the start of the Second Age, had said that he would stay there until the last ship sailed. In Arthur's day he was still there, with the last of the Elves who had not yet gone.

When the time came for the last ship, the Elves who meant to stay did not let the Havens fade. They took them out of the circles of the world, as Aman had been taken long before, and the Havens became the hidden country that Britain's folk tales call the Otherworld. It lies alongside Britain still, reached through mists, standing stones and old roads. Its Majestrix is the Elf-lady Roma, who was the Lady of the Lake.

Legend, which remembers the Havens as an isle in the West called Avalon, made Morgana its mistress. She never was. No mortal sorceress was ever mistress of the Grey Havens.

Arthur lies there still, asleep. It was said in Britain that he would come again in its need, which is why he is called the Once and Future King. Nobody has woken him. In 1980 servants of the Netherworld stole him from his resting place, hiding him on an island far out at sea. Captain Britain found him and broke the giants who guarded him, but the king did not wake.

Merlin

For the whole of that long, strange stretch of years his adviser was Gandalf. The name Gandalf bore at Arthur's court, Merlin, stuck to him so firmly that it is printed on Chocolate Frog cards to this day.

Gandalf remembers Arthur as 'a boy with a sword and a round table', with 'a great deal more courage than sense'.

Half-history

Like the other great ages before this one, Arthur's comes down to the present only as half-history: legend that is truer than the people who tell it suppose.

Lucius Malfoy, who has looked into it, told Harry Potter in Diagon Alley in August 1993: 'The Potters go back a very long way. Further than you have been told. Potters have been kings before they were Potters. When there was a king worth the name, and that was not an accident either.' The king worth the name was Arthur.

The Potter line

The Pendragons descend directly from the Peverell brother who received the Cloak of Invisibility. After Arthur's time his ancient enemies, dark wizards aligned with Morgana among them, went on attacking his descendants. Before the Norman Conquest the family changed its name to Potter to escape them. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what the name was hiding.

The Cloak came down the line intact, Peverell to Pendragon to Potter. It passed to James Potter, then, by way of Dumbledore, to Harry.

Harry's descent through his mother is a secret that only Dumbledore and Voldemort know. His descent from Arthur is nothing of the kind. It is documented, so that anyone who pulls the genealogies in the right archive can trace it straight back without special access. It is unknown only because almost nobody bothers to look.

Lucius Malfoy, who keeps the family tree on his drawing-room wall, is exactly the sort of man who does look, and he knows. Hermione Granger could establish the whole of it in an afternoon in the library. Harry does not know.

The Potters are not the only heirs of Arthur. In the generations after him, before his house took the name Potter, a Squib child of the house was sent out to live among Muggles. That branch became the Braddocks, a Muggle family of Essex. Brian Braddock, Captain Britain, is one of them, a very distant kinsman of Harry's. Neither of them knows it.

pages.title: Aragorn
aliases: the ranger with a broken sword
the tall, weather-stained man at the inn
infobox: Ambrose's old friend; Strider; Elessar; Estel; Isildur's Heir

Arwen wife
Harry Potter descendant
Gandalf friend
Man of the Dúnedain, of the line of Númenor
King Elessar of Gondor and Arnor
Harry Potter, through Lily Potter and Susan Pevensie
pages.html:
Aragorn son of Arathorn, the ranger called Strider, was the heir of Isildur. He bore Andúril in the War of the Ring, and Gandalf crowned him King Elessar before Minas Tirith. He married Arwen. Through their line, by way of the Pevensies, Harry Potter descends from him on his mother's side.

Early life

Aragorn was born in the year 2931 of the Third Age, the last of the line of Isildur, whose forefathers had come out of drowned Númenor. His father was killed when he was two. He was raised in Rivendell by Elrond under the name Estel, which means Hope. There he met Elrond's daughter Arwen, and loved her. Elrond would not give her to him until he was king of both Gondor and Arnor.

For many years he was a Ranger of the North, guarding the lands of Eriador without thanks. He also served Rohan and Gondor in disguise. To the folk of Bree he was Strider, a weather-stained man who looked like nobody much.

The War of the Ring

In the year 3018 he met Frodo Baggins at the Prancing Pony, and guided the Ring-bearer to Rivendell. There the shards of Narsil were reforged for him as Andúril. He went south with the Fellowship.

For a long time he was unsure of himself. At last he looked into the palantír of Orthanc, and wrestled with Sauron himself through it. Then he took the Paths of the Dead, which everybody had told him led only to death. He came out at the other end. He came up the Anduin on the black ships, with a star on his brow and Andúril drawn, to turn the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. In the Houses of Healing he laid his hands on the wounded and they woke. The old woman Ioreth said that the hands of the king are the hands of a healer.

King Elessar

After the Ring was destroyed, Gandalf set the crown on his head before the city, and at Midsummer he married Arwen. He reigned as King Elessar for a hundred and twenty years. Their son Eldarion was king after him.

He died in the Fourth Age at the age of two hundred and ten. When he knew that his time had come, he lay down in the House of the Kings and gave up his life of his own will, as the kings of old Númenor once could. Arwen did not long outlive him.

Descent

Harry descends from Aragorn and Arwen through his mother. Aragorn gave the line Númenor, Arwen the Elves. That is what Dumbledore meant when he called Lily Potter's protection 'the magic of Elves, Harry. And of Númenor'. Godric Gryffindor was of the line, long ago. So were all four Pevensies. Through Susan Pevensie it came down to Lily, and so to Harry.

Tom Riddle, sneering at him in the Chamber of Secrets, called Harry's sword 'a borrowed sword from a long forgotten ancestor'.

In the saga

Gandalf remembers Aragorn sitting in a dark corner of a crowded inn in the rain, his boots up on a stool, his hood pulled low, watching everybody and saying nothing. He looked for all the world like a vagabond nobody would trust with a farthing, until he pushed back his hood. When Gandalf first saw Harry Potter, in December 1992, the boy was twelve, small and battered, duelling in the Great Hall. He was quite obviously frightened, and quite obviously not going to give an inch. Gandalf saw that old face in the set of Harry's jaw, in the way he stood. 'You'd be proud of him, old friend.' He is the one man alive who could make the comparison.

Harry read of Aragorn in Dudley's copy of The Lord of the Rings. He took it up in July 1993, looking for the drowned kingdom, the sword and the king. He finished it in July 1994. In early 1994 he compared himself to the ranger with a broken sword and no kingdom, who doubted himself in the dark.

On the night of the lake in June 1994 he stood at Professor Flitwick's window, resolved that the wizarding world must change. A single white star shone out low in the west, brighter than any star had a right to be. Its light was warm on his face, like the hand of somebody proud of him. Without knowing why, he thought of Aragorn looking into the palantír and deciding at last to be a king. Lying awake afterwards, he badly wanted to know whether Aragorn came out of the Paths of the Dead. He had a feeling it was important. Aragorn did.

pages.title: Legolas
aliases: a prince of the forest folk
the prince of the forest folk
infobox: Elf, of the Woodland Realm of Mirkwood
One of the Nine Walkers, 3018 to 3019 of the Third Age
pages.html:
Legolas was an Elf of Mirkwood, the son of Thranduil, the Elvenking of the Woodland Realm. He was the Elves' member of the Fellowship of the Ring, the nine companions who set out from Rivendell with the Ring-bearer at the end of the Third Age. He was a lightfoot archer, with an infuriating habit of keeping score. Gandalf, who knew him well, still remembered his face many thousands of years later.

The War of the Ring

Legolas came to Rivendell in 3018 of the Third Age with the news that Gollum had escaped from his father's guards. At the Council of Elrond he was chosen as one of the Nine Walkers. He went with the Fellowship through Moria and Lothlórien, where the Lady Galadriel gave him a bow of the Galadhrim. With it he shot down a winged steed of the Nazgûl over the Great River in the dark.

When the Fellowship broke, he followed the captured hobbits across Rohan with Aragorn and Gimli the Dwarf. He fought beside them at Helm's Deep, where he and Gimli kept count of the orcs they killed. Gimli won, forty-two to forty-one. The two of them became the closest friends an Elf and a Dwarf have ever been.

Afterwards

He rode with Aragorn by the Paths of the Dead. At Pelargir he heard the gulls, and the longing for the Sea woke in him. After the war he brought Elves of his father's realm to Ithilien. When Aragorn died, Legolas built a grey ship and sailed over the Sea into the West, taking Gimli with him.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame was at Hogwarts. He looked hard at Dracina Malfoy, who had been duelling Harry Potter. Her hair was so pale it was almost silver. Her silver eyes, when the candlelight caught them, were the clear, bright grey of starlight on still water. He had known a face like that once: a prince of the forest folk, a lightfoot archer with a bow, a quiver and an infuriating habit of keeping score. The old man found that he was smiling. Then he felt something cold about her, a pull he had known long ago, and stopped.

pages.title: The Stygian
infobox: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (12 March 2001), as Herpo the Foul
pages.html:
The Stygian was a dark wizard of Stygia, the serpent-worshipping kingdom of the Hyborian Age, who lived on into the world after the Flood. His were among the dark hands that carried the knowledge of putting a piece of someone into a vessel through thousands of years and several forgotten ages. Out of the ruins of that knowledge he made the modern Horcrux. History remembers him as Herpo the Foul and takes him for a Greek. Gandalf, who knows better, thinks of him as that damn Stygian.

Stygia and the old craft

Before the ice, Stygia kept the dark craft of Morgoth, the being men also know as Satan and Lucifer. The greatest thing ever made by that craft was the One Ring, into which Sauron, Morgoth's lieutenant, put a great part of his own native power. Only a Maia could make such a thing, and Gandalf made sure the knowledge of it was lost. Some of it survived all the same. The Stygian survived the Flood. He gathered up what was left of the art, which was ancient, corrupted and full of holes, then filled in the blanks by guesswork.

The modern Horcrux

What he produced is the Horcrux as wizards know it. It needs no Maia's power, but it costs the maker a torn soul. It is the Ring worked out backwards by guesswork, and the guesswork is why it costs what it costs. The histories that call him Herpo the Foul make him a Greek Dark wizard and a Parselmouth, who also bred the first Basilisk by hatching a chicken's egg beneath a toad. Greece, however, is merely where the written record happens to pick up his trail. Wizarding scholarship has never questioned the label. The only two beings who could put the textbooks right are Gandalf and the enemy.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Gandalf, who was living as Ambrose Greyhame, slipped into the Great Hall at Hogwarts and watched Harry Potter duelling Dracina Malfoy. About the girl he felt a coldness he had known once before, long ago, from a heavy gold thing that whispered and wanted. He had made sure the knowledge of making such a thing was lost. Yet he knew it remained, half forgotten, 'carried forward by dark hands like that damn Stygian's', over thousands of years and several forgotten ages.

What hung about Dracina had not been made by the same hands, the same craft or for the same purpose. It had been made in the same way: a piece of someone poured into a vessel, so that it could wait, whisper and be carried. It was Tom Riddle's diary.

pages.title: Lucifer
aliases: the master of all that darkness
infobox: Morgoth; Satan; Tom's true master; Melkor; Mephisto; Mephistopheles

Lord Voldemort servant
John Constantine adversary
Sauron lieutenant
Lilith servant
God rebelled against
Satan, the Devil, the old serpent
Melkor; Morgoth, the Black Foe of the World
Lilith; the Chaos Gods; Lord Voldemort, among many
Dark magic; the dementors; vampirism, through Lilith's trap
Morgoth (the elder days); Satan (Scripture); the Wyrm (to the Garou); the First of the Fallen (to the lords of Hell); Mephisto (in the age of heroes)
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Lucifer is the Devil: the first of the angels to rebel, who sang out of tune before the world was made. He is one being under many names. He was Morgoth in the elder days. Scripture calls him Satan, and the Garou call him the Wyrm. To the lords of Hell he is the First of the Fallen, and in the age of heroes he has walked the world as Mephisto, the buyer of souls. Dark magic began with him. Every vampire is his property, and he is the singer out of tune behind every dark lord the world has known, Voldemort included.

Names

Lucifer means the light-bearer: 'How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!' Satan means the adversary. Scripture also calls him the Devil, the old serpent and the great dragon.

In the elder days he was Melkor, 'he who arises in might', the mightiest of the Ainur, until Fëanor named him Morgoth, the Black Foe of the World. The Garou call him the Wyrm. John Constantine, who has met him, reckons he has worn a good many names since the day he first sang out of tune.

The elder days

When Ilúvatar set the great Music before the Ainur, Melkor tried to bring into being things of his own. He wove his own thoughts into the Music, and the discord spread. He came down into the world to master it, and marred everything the others made. In the north he raised the fortresses of Utumno and Angband.

He stole the Silmarils and slew Fëanor's father. With Ungoliant he destroyed the Two Trees of Valinor. He bred dragons and Orcs. For the whole of the First Age he made war on Elves and Men from his iron hells. At the end of that age he was overthrown in the War of Wrath, and thrust out of the world through the Door of Night. But the malice he had poured into the very substance of the world remained, and the lies he had sown went on bearing fruit.

Dark magic is his craft, taught by him and by his servants. It is as old as his rebellion. His lieutenant Sauron put a great part of his own native power into the One Ring, the first Horcrux. Through the Hyborian Age Stygia kept, collected and practised his craft at scale. The Flood scattered it, so that what reaches a modern wizard is a corrupted copy of a copy. In Gandalf's words he has been 'the serpent in the hot lands', 'the dragon in the north' and 'the dark lord of a dozen ages'.

In Scripture

In Eden he came to Eve as the serpent. In the book of Job he stands among the sons of God as the adversary, and asks leave to test a righteous man. He tempted Christ for forty days in the wilderness, and was refused. Christ said, 'I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.'

The Revelation tells of war in heaven. Michael led his angels against the dragon, 'that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan'. The dragon was cast out. The vicar of St Michael's in Little Whinging teaches that the pride which goes before a fall is the Devil's own sin, and the oldest there is.

Servants and works

Lilith is his immortal servant. After the Flood she told Cain that she was Adam's first wife. She taught him the blood magic by which he empowered himself and spread his curse, so that vampires began. The bargain put Cain under Morgoth's power and will. Every vampire descended from Cain is under it too. The dementors are his making as well.

One tribe of the Garou went over to him, every man, woman and whelp of it. 'There were fourteen tribes,' Snape told his third-years in 1993. 'One went over. Whole.'

Tom Riddle, Lord Voldemort, is in Gandalf's telling only a leaf on a very old tree that Lucifer planted. In December 1992 Gandalf told Dumbledore: 'Tom's only a symptom. The sickness is older, and it's growing.' The power behind it had grown, he said: first gradually, now more quickly. While Harry Potter calls his aunt's house home, the dark creature hunting him cannot touch him there: 'Not Tom. Not Tom's true master.'

Dumbledore had already told Harry that things a good deal older and worse than Voldemort had begun to take an interest in him. The Sorting Hat, talking to Harry in Dumbledore's office the same morning, spoke of 'the master of all that darkness', who gets his hooks into well-meaning wizards and pulls. When Harry asked his name, the Hat choked and fell silent.

To guard men against him, God sent Gandalf after the Flood to teach light magic. The first lesson was how to tell that a voice out of the dark offering power is never the voice of a friend.

Among the Maiar cast out with him were the Ori. They fled to the Alteran galaxy, where they set themselves up as gods, with a religion made in time to mock God and Jesus Christ.

Long ago Rita Repulsa, mad with grief for her son, Kai, sold him her soul for the power to take vengeance on the dinosaurs; she called him the Great Satan, and Zordon's light broke his hold on her in 1998.

In Japan demons called the Horrors come up out of the Makai, a dark country of their own, through objects steeped in human malice. Their mother, Messiah, is a great demon of his following, whatever her name pretends. The Makai Knights, who have hunted the Horrors for longer than anybody has counted, have never heard his name.

Among the lesser spirits that fell with him is the thing worshipped by the Order of Silent Hill, the cult of a small town in Maine. Its faithful take it for the maker of paradise. It was born into flesh at Silent Hill on 13 September 1983, then again on 17 September 2000. Each time it was killed within minutes: first by a writer, Harry Mason, then by his seventeen-year-old daughter.

The Great Old Ones and the Outer Gods are not among his servants. They are God's creatures, as he is, but they did not fall with him, and he does not command them. Some cults mistake one for the other. From time to time his servants have worked the same ruin as theirs without caring who else was at it.

The four Chaos Gods serve him, among them Slaanesh, whose hunger brought down the Eldar.

The First of the Fallen

In Hell he is the First of the Fallen, the eldest and greatest of its lords. The Second and the Third of the Fallen rule beneath him.

In 1990 he made a show of abandoning Hell. He emptied it of its demons and its damned. He locked its gates, handed the key to Dream of the Endless, and walked out into the world, saying he was tired of it. It was the oldest of his tricks, to be thought gone. By 1991 he was back on Hell's throne under his oldest title there, the First of the Fallen, with the Second and the Third beneath him again. That is where John Constantine found him.

In 1991 John, the Liverpool occultist, crossed him. John was dying of lung cancer. He sold his soul separately to two other lords of Hell, the Second and the Third of the Fallen. Then he waited for the First to come for him. When the First arrived to collect, the other two came to claim what they had bought. Rather than fight a war in Hell over one soul, the First was forced to cure John's cancer and leave him alive. John made an obscene gesture at his back as he went.

John says that he has sat across a table from the Devil himself, come as close as any man alive to tricking him, and walked away with his soul still in his own pocket, more or less. He thinks the Devil far worse than God. Beside the Devil, to John's mind, Voldemort is only a scally with a flick knife and a fancy name. Lucius Malfoy, he reckons, stands about as much chance of getting one over on Voldemort as Voldemort does of getting one over on Lucifer. The First of the Fallen has not forgiven any of it.

As Mephisto

In the age of heroes the Devil has gone among men as Mephisto, a red-skinned lord of Hell who trades in souls. His bargains run through the century. Cynthia von Doom gave him her soul in exchange for power. Her son, Victor von Doom, spent years trying to win it back. In 1989, with Doctor Stephen Strange beside him, Doom at last went down into Hell and freed her.

In 1972 the motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze sold Mephisto his soul to save his foster father. He was bound to the demon Zarathos, and became the Ghost Rider. Mephisto tempted the Silver Surfer time after time once the Surfer was exiled to Earth. He could not break him. The twin sons of the Vision and the Scarlet Witch were made in part from shards of his own essence. In 1989 he took those shards back, and the children were unmade.

Wise heads among the heroes have long suspected that Mephisto was no mere demon who called himself Satan for the grandeur of it. He was the thing itself, wearing one more mask.

The Wyrm

The Garou are whelped into a war against him on Gaia's behalf. They can smell his work in a place, an object or a man. In their telling creation stands between the Weaver, the Wyld and the Wyrm. The Wyrm is the Corrupter.

Snape described the war to his third-years in 1993 without naming the enemy: 'a corruption that eats at the world from underneath, that wears a thousand shapes and has servants everywhere'. To the Garou everything in creation is either sound timber or rot. They have a name for the rot.

Remus Lupin growls at the scent of him. The dementor on the train, Snape's Dark Mark, Voldemort's name, a boggart in the shape of a dementor and Harry's account of Cain are all one smell to him, the oldest there is. In June 1994 he told Harry that he could smell the Wyrm everywhere at Hogwarts. Most wizards, he said, do not realise how mixed up light and dark magic are in their teaching. That might well be the purpose of the one from whom all dark magic comes.

Among Muggles and wizards

Muggles now draw him in picture books with horns, a tail and a pitchfork. They laugh at him, which, Gandalf says, he likes: 'It means nobody's watching.'

Some Muggles who call themselves witches say Satan is 'an alright lad really'. It galls John Constantine, a real wizard, who has been lied to by the Devil himself. Medieval Muggles believed that magic was the Devil's work, and in time the Church came to agree. That is why the wizarding world hid from it in 1692.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, John Constantine had once been in a pub with the Devil himself, and had walked out with his soul still more or less in his own pocket. On 22 August 1994, ducking Lucius Malfoy's jinxes in the Top Box at the World Cup, he called back that the Devil had bought him a pint since they last met. The Devil, he said, would laugh himself sick at Lucius.

pages.title: Julius Belmont
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
Dracula, in the Demon Castle War of 1999; Celia Fortner's cult (2036)
pages.html:
Julius Belmont is the head of the Belmont family in the late twentieth century, a man of about thirty who is actively hunting vampires. In 1993 and 1994 he holds the Vampire Killer. He is an old friend of Professor McGonagall's, and he spent some years in Transylvania. In the Demon Castle War of 1999 he and Alucard destroyed Dracula for good, at the cost of his memory. In 2035 and 2036 he came back to the fight as the nameless hunter called J.

Birth and family

Julius was born in about 1964. He is the heir of the line that runs from Leon Belmont through Trevor Belmont, Sypha Belnades, Christopher, Simon, Juste and Richter. He was born into a family that had not long had its whip back. For much of the nineteenth century the Belmonts had been missing. In their absence the Vampire Killer passed to their distant kin, the Morris family, who carried it in 1917 and 1944: first John Morris, who died of the strain of wielding it without Belmont blood, then his son Jonathan. Afterwards the whip came back to the Belmonts from their Morris kin, and Julius inherited it.

He was raised as every Belmont has been raised since Leon swore his oath in 1094, trained from childhood to the whip, the cross and holy water. He was taught that Dracula always comes back, and that when he does, one of the family must go up the mountain. He is the head of the family in his generation.

The hunter

In 1993 and 1994 Julius is actively hunting vampires. He always carries the whip. Dracula himself lies between returns, last destroyed in 1944, but the Belmonts have never sat idle waiting for him. Between his risings they hunt the night as Leon swore they would. Their quarry is the Kindred who prey openly on the living, and the creatures his castle leaves behind it. They hunt, too, the cults that worship Dracula and work for his return.

He fights as his family has always fought, with the Vampire Killer, holy water and the cross. Like the best of the Belmonts before him, he has what the Kindred call True Faith, a faith strong enough to burn the undead or drive them back. To the Kindred, who have feared the Belmonts above all other mortal hunters for nine hundred years, he is the Belmont of his generation. In 1994 he is a man of about thirty.

The Kindred he hunts are not the Kindred Leon fought. Since 1435 most of them have hidden behind the Masquerade, and the Camarilla, which keeps it, has had an agreement with the wizarding world since 1900. The Sabbat keeps no such bargains, and Dracula, nominally of the Sabbat, has never troubled to keep the Masquerade at all. It is among the Sabbat, and among Dracula's worshippers, that a Belmont finds most of his work.

Transylvania and McGonagall

Julius spent some years in Transylvania, Dracula's own country, where the Tzimisce ruled in the Middle Ages. He is an old friend of Professor Minerva McGonagall of Hogwarts, who speaks of him as 'dear Julius'. How the two of them met is not recorded.

Transylvania is also the country of Dracula's worshippers. In 1992 Gilderoy Lockhart claimed to have put down a cult of them there, all in red, led by a Tzimisce Methuselah of the fourth generation. The claim was false, but the ground was real. McGonagall's answer showed that she and Julius both knew that ground. So few Tzimisce are of the fourth generation that whoever truly faced such a cult met either Dracula himself or one of very few others. Who it was, and what happened there, is not recorded.

The Demon Castle War

In 1994 the Demon Castle War has not yet been fought, but it is coming. Dracula has risen roughly once a century, or sooner whenever his followers have managed it. By 1994 a new rising is brewing.

In 1999, when Dracula's castle rose for the last time, Julius fought the Demon Castle War with Alucard beside him. Alucard, Dracula's dhampir son, had fought his father in 1476 and destroyed him in 1797. Together they destroyed Dracula for good, so completely that, for the first time in nine hundred years, he could not come back. The castle was sealed inside a solar eclipse, out of the world. Dracula's power did not die with him. It waited for the man in whom it would be reborn.

Julius was the last of his family to face Dracula himself, and the one who ended the war Leon had begun nine centuries before. The battle cost him his memory. He came out of the war knowing nothing of who he was, except that his name began with J.

As J

For more than thirty years he lived as a man without a past, known by that letter alone. In 2035, during the first eclipse of the century, he was drawn into the sealed castle. There he met Soma Cruz, the young man in whom Dracula had been reborn, and Genya Arikado, who was Alucard. In the castle his memory came back to him, quickened by the dark power he sensed in Soma. He knew himself again as Julius Belmont, the hunter who had ended Dracula in 1999. He stood ready to destroy Soma if Dracula woke in him, but Soma mastered the darkness himself.

In 2036 he joined the witch Yoko Belnades, of Sypha's blood, in the Church's work against Celia Fortner's cult, which was trying to wake the Dark Lord in Soma. He was past seventy by then, and he still carried the Vampire Killer. With Yoko and Arikado he saw Soma refuse his inheritance a second time.

In the cult's stronghold he spent all his strength to break the barrier that guarded the way down to the Abyss. It left him too weak to go further, so the last fight was Soma's alone.

In the saga

On Halloween 1992 Gilderoy Lockhart claimed to have foiled a cult of red-robed Dracula worshippers in Transylvania. Professor McGonagall said pleasantly that in that case he must know 'dear Julius', an old friend of hers who had been in Transylvania for some years and always carried a whip. Lockhart said that he knew 'old Julius Carrow' very well. McGonagall sighed, and Harry Potter understood from her look that whoever Julius was, he was not a Carrow. Harry resolved to ask her about Julius one day.

pages.title: The Master
aliases: the founder of the Aurelian line
infobox: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Welcome to the Hellmouth' (10 March 1997)
Claimed: the Antediluvian of Clan Ventrue
The devout: those who pray and mean it
pages.html:
The Master is an ancient vampire, a Ventrue of the fourth generation so old that he has forgotten his own name. He founded the Aurelian line, and he is the grandsire of Angelus. Since 1937 he has been sealed beneath a town in California, after a ritual went wrong.

Origins

The Master claims to have been sired by the Antediluvian of Clan Ventrue, the clan's founder, who was of the third generation. He will never say that founder's name. If the claim is true, he is among the oldest vampires walking.

He is too powerful to be bound to either the Camarilla or the Sabbat, and he has never tried to belong to either. He follows his own purposes. He has never paid the Masquerade the least regard.

Age has worn the human features from his face. What is left looks more like a bat than a man.

The Order of Aurelius

He gathered about him a following of vampires who served him as a priesthood, the Order of Aurelius. From his blood came the line that bears its name.

In 1609, in the Virginia colony, he sired his favourite childe, Darla. Through her came Angelus, Drusilla and William the Bloody.

One kind of blood

Like every Ventrue, the Master can feed from only one kind of mortal, and he would starve sooner than drink from anybody else. His is the devout: people of real faith, who pray and mean it.

That is why he came to Darla's deathbed in a priest's clothes, when she was praying for salvation. It is why his followers serve him as a priesthood. It is also why he worked his great ritual of 1937 from a church.

Imprisonment

In 1937 he tried to open the Hellmouth beneath a small town in California, a mouth of the pit over which the town had been built. The ritual went wrong. An earthquake swallowed the church in which he was working it, and he was sealed beneath the town in a mystical prison from which he could not get out.

His followers waited on him there. They waited, too, on a prophecy that he would rise when the Slayer died.

Destruction

In 1997 the town, Sunnydale, received a new Slayer, Buffy Summers. That spring the Master fed on her and left her face down in a pool to drown. Her death, brief as it was, set him free.

She was revived the same night. She came after him and destroyed him, leaving only his bones. His followers later tried to raise him from them, so the Slayer ground the bones to powder.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1992 Gilderoy Lockhart re-enacted for his class an adventure with a fourth-generation Tzimisce. He claimed that the Tzimisce had been in league with an elder of Clan Ventrue: 'A creature so old he'd forgotten his own name, and called himself only... the Master.' This Master, Lockhart said, was the grandsire of the infamous Angelus. Lockhart claimed to have defeated both of them, bare-knuckled, in Eastern Europe.

Hermione Granger said, apologetically, that she had read three books on the Aurelian line. All three said the Master had been trapped under a town in California since 1937, so Lockhart could not have fought him. Lockhart called it a psychic projection.

The Master was the first subject on which Hermione meant to explain, from her hospital bed in early 1993, exactly how Lockhart had lied. Lockhart was right only that the Master is Angelus's grandsire.

pages.title: Captain America
infobox: Steve Rogers; Steven Grant Rogers; Cap
Seventy-four by the calendar; looks no more than thirty
pages.html:
Captain America is Steve Rogers, the American super-soldier who fought through the Second World War and then spent nearly twenty years frozen in the ice. Since he was found in 1964 he has led the Avengers on and off. He was the one clear success of the Weapon programme, Weapon I. By 1994 he is the only one of the famous early Avengers still in active service: seventy-four years old by the calendar, and looking no older than thirty.

Weapon I

Steve Rogers was born on the Lower East Side of Manhattan on 4 July 1920, to poor Irish immigrants. He grew up thin, sickly and determined. In 1940, with war already raging in Europe, he tried to enlist and was turned down as unfit for service. An army officer who had watched him try chose him instead for Project Rebirth, the American super-soldier experiment run by the refugee scientist Dr Abraham Erskine.

Rogers was given Erskine's serum and bombarded with Vita-Rays. He came out of the chamber at the very peak of human strength, speed and endurance. Minutes later a Nazi agent who had wormed his way into the project shot Erskine dead. Erskine had kept most of the formula in his head, and it died with him.
