The project was the first of a long, secret, numbered series, the Weapon programme, and Rogers was Weapon I. He remains its one unambiguous success. Almost everything the programme attempted afterwards was an effort to make another man like him.

The war

Captain America first came to public notice in December 1940, a year before Pearl Harbor, in a costume of stars and stripes. He was given a teenage partner, James Buchanan 'Bucky' Barnes. Together they spent the war fighting the Axis and its agents. His great enemy was the Red Skull, Johann Shmidt, the Nazi terror chief. With Bucky he fought beside Sergeant Nick Fury's Howling Commandos as well.

In the wartime team called the Invaders he fought beside the Sub-Mariner and the Human Torch. Among their enemies was the witch Greta Grindelwald, whose followers they fought in occupied Europe more than once, and whom they came close to taking.

His first shield was a triangular badge of steel. It was soon replaced by the round shield he has carried ever since, made of an alloy of vibranium and steel that nobody has ever managed to repeat. It is nearly indestructible, balanced so well that it can be thrown and will come back.

In 1945, in the last weeks of the war in Europe, Rogers and Bucky tried to stop an explosive-laden drone aircraft launched by Baron Heinrich Zemo. The plane blew up in the air, and Bucky was lost. Rogers fell into the freezing waters of the North Atlantic, where the serum kept him alive in suspended animation inside a block of ice.

The man out of his time

He lay in the ice for nineteen years. In 1964 the young Avengers found the block in which he was frozen, adrift in the sea, and Rogers woke into a world that had moved on without him. He joined the team almost at once, and soon led it. In 1965, when most of the founding members left, he held the Avengers together with three former outlaws: Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch. He has been the team's conscience ever since.

He was among the heroes carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars of 1984, where he led the heroes' side. In 1987 he gave up the name and the costume rather than serve as the agent of a government commission on superhuman activities. Another man wore the uniform for a time. Rogers came back to it in 1989.

Captain America does not age. It is common knowledge that he was given something that stops him growing older, and in 1994 he looks no more than thirty, though he first fought the Nazis more than half a century earlier. He does not chair the team, an office the Black Widow has held since 1992. In 1994 he serves under her, beside Thunderstrike and War Machine.

In 1965 he took Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch down to the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the armies of the two kingdoms that call themselves Atlantis were facing each other over some ruins. With Superman he stood between them for three days until both kings went home.

He faced Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, three times. In January 1965, while the founders were still with the team, he went to Japan with Iron Man, Thor, Giant-Man and the Wasp, beside the whole Justice League. Three monsters were loose there at once. He ran the evacuation on the ground with Batman. On 19 December 1965 he went back with Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch, when the Xiliens of Planet X loosed the same three. He was the one Avenger who had been there both times, so he told the others what to expect. In the summer of 1979 he met Godzilla once more, in New York.

Early in 1977 an errand for S.H.I.E.L.D. took him to England, where he fought Captain Britain over a misunderstanding before the two of them turned on the Red Skull. The Skull meant to found a Fourth Reich in Britain. The two Captains freed James Callaghan, then Prime Minister, from the Skull's men, then found the germ bomb he had hidden at Big Ben.

Onslaught, 1996 to 1997

In the summer of 1996, when Onslaught's Sentinels sealed off Manhattan, Captain America led the Avengers down into the dead subway to bring out the people trapped there. When two of Onslaught's servants came after them, he tricked them into fighting each other. That August, at seventy-six by the calendar, he was among the Avengers who went into Onslaught in Central Park to give him a body the X-Men could strike.

In 1945 the public had never been told that he was gone. In 1996 it was told, and it mourned him. He was alive all the same. Franklin Richards had carried the fallen into a world of his own making, and he brought them home late in 1997, exactly as old as they had been when they fell. Rogers looked no more than thirty, as before.

Abilities

Rogers has no powers in the ordinary sense. Weapon I made him as strong, fast, agile and enduring as a human being can be. He heals far faster than other men, and recovers from exhaustion just as quickly. He is a master of hand-to-hand combat, a gifted tactician and a natural leader. His shield is his only weapon, and he uses it to defend as much as to attack.

In the saga

Book Two: talking with Ambrose Greyhame, Albus Dumbledore compares Harry's complete trust in him to the way the Americans trust 'old Superman or Captain America' to save them. Unlike most of the wizarding world, Dumbledore knows who they are.

Book Four, Chapter Three: on the Muggle news of Saturday 20 August 1994, Harry sees Captain America at the United Nations. He stands with the Avengers, a little apart from the Justice League, behind Superman as he appeals to the Security Council for leave to act against Khan's forces in the Balkans. He wears his blue mask with the white A. On his back is the round shield of red and white rings round a white star. Of all the Avengers on Dudley's old lunchbox, he is the only one who looks the same as ever.

pages.title: Zordon
aliases: The blue man in golden armour
the blue man in golden armour
infobox: The blue man in golden armour; Zordon of Eltar

Albus Dumbledore friend
Gandalf fellow Istar
Rita Repulsa enemy
Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Day of the Dumpster' (28 August 1993)
Maia; one of the five Istari
The Istari; one of the two Blue Wizards
Alatar or Pallando, Morinehtar or Rómestámo; nobody now knows which
Zophram, the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar
Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd, Master Vile, Dark Specter
Held in a time warp, without a body
The Command Center, outside Angel Grove
pages.html:
Zordon of Eltar is one of the two Blue Wizards of the Istari, a Maia and Gandalf's equal, who was sent off the world altogether to shepherd Eltar against evil. There he wore the likeness of an Eltarian, and in time he became Supreme Guardian of Eltar. Some ten thousand years ago he fought Rita Repulsa on Earth, and her curse shut him in a tube outside time, with no body to return to. In the summer of 1994 he keeps watch over Earth from the Command Center near Angel Grove, where he chooses who carries the Power Coins. The only surviving likeness of his face hangs in Albus Dumbledore's office. In 1998 he gave up the form he wore, and his light went out across the universe.

One of the Istari

About the year 1000 of the Third Age five of the Maiar were sent out on commission, to unite all who would resist Sauron and the darkness behind him. These were the Istari, the wizards of Gandalf's order. Gandalf was sent to Earth. Zordon was sent to Eltar, a world far out among the stars, to shepherd it against evil as Gandalf shepherded the free peoples of the West. They are colleagues in the same commission, of the same order and the same rank. Zordon is Gandalf's equal, not some lesser being who happens to be blue.

Two of the five were the Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, who went into the far East with Saruman and never came back. In the West they were remembered as Alatar and Pallando. Other records call them Morinehtar and Rómestámo. The names mean the Darkness-slayer and the East-helper. Nobody now knows which of those names was Zordon's.

The old records of Middle-earth go vague about the two Blue Wizards and never settle what became of them. They were the two sent furthest from the centre. One of them went further than anybody was keeping records of: off the world altogether. Nothing was written down, because nobody who could have written it ever saw him again.

The Guardians of Eltar

On Eltar Zordon took the likeness of an Eltarian, as Gandalf on Earth took that of an old man. He did not come as a lord but as a young soldier of the line, the First Spearman of the Bronze Company. Gandalf, too, had come last of the five and seemed the least of them.

Eltar is kept by the Guardians of Eltar, who answer to its Elders. The first of them in those days was Zophram, the Gold Guardian, a mortal Eltarian. At his request the Elders took the young spearman into the Guardians, as the Bronze Guardian, beside Zartus, the Silver. Zophram taught them both, never knowing what his pupil was. When the Guardians drove back an attack on the planet Artavias, the Elders made Zophram the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar. His first act was to ask that Eltar's forces should reach beyond their own galaxy, to protect young worlds against Dark Specter. He meant Zordon, not Zartus, to come after him.

Zophram and Lord Zedd

On the moon of a young world far from Eltar, the Guardians fought a scouting party of Hartunians in Dark Specter's service. There they found a palace of the Bandorian monks, who guarded the Zeo Crystal, a thing of enormous power. Eltar took it under its protection. In secret, Zartus had one of the monks lay a spell on it, the Fire of Truth, so that whoever touched it would die, or worse.

Then an assassin of Dark Specter's poisoned Zordon, who lived far longer than the poison should have allowed; the healers of Eltar could not say why. Zophram struck the assassin down, but it had already got into his head, telling him that the Elders were a dead end. When they would not let him use the Crystal, he went to take it himself, to end the war at a stroke.

The Fire of Truth flayed the skin from his body. It killed everything on that moon but the palace, a few soldiers, Zartus and the dying Zophram. Zartus killed the soldiers, carried Zophram away and told him lies: that he had been born again, stronger; that Eltar thought him dead as a hero; that the Elders had called Zordon home to take his place as Supreme Guardian.

Zophram came to believe that Zordon had known what the Crystal would do, and had betrayed him. Zophram of Eltar died, and Lord Zedd was born, sworn to the ruin of Eltar. Eltar held Zophram's funeral, and Zordon became Supreme Guardian to honour him. Without the Elders' leave he set up a watch post on the young world whose moon held the Crystal. It was Earth. For long ages Zordon fought the man who had taught him, on Eltar and among the worlds around it. Eltar did not fall.

The war on Earth

Zordon had known Rita Repulsa since the day she was born. Her mother, Lady Fienna, was his ally. Fienna had fled her husband, Master Vile, while she was carrying his child, and on the planet Iutus she gave birth to Rita with Zordon beside her. He gave the baby a rattle. He meant to keep them both safe from Vile. When Rita was six, her father's Tenga Warriors took her back, and Fienna was mortally wounded.

Zordon was at war with Master Vile in those years. King Lexian of Edenoi comforted him, and the people of Edenoi built him a robot helper, the first Alpha. Rita grew up in her father's cruel ways. In time Lord Zedd turned her from Vile and made her the commander of his armies. She conquered world after world in his name.

Some ten thousand years ago Rita came to Earth. She made her home in a palace on the Moon and invaded the world below. Zordon stopped her. For years the war went on, on Earth and on Eltar. Battles were won and lost on both sides. At last Rita seemed to admit that she was beaten, and she asked to talk terms.

It was a trap. At the meeting she caught Zordon in a time warp. He had been ready for treachery: he called up a space dumpster, sealed her in it with her servants and cast it out into space. It came to rest on the Moon.

Her curse, in return, put him in a tube outside time, with no body to return to. For a while Alpha 5 let the universe believe that Zordon was dead. Then he appeared again, in a column of light, held there by a temporal beacon that Alpha had set up during the battle. The body he had worn on Eltar was lost to him: from her prison Rita sent a thief, Loriyan, to carry it off to the planet Bizerk. A Maia cannot be killed, but he can lose the form he wears, as Gandalf lost his on the peak of Zirakzigil. The time warp, Zordon said afterwards, had shown him his true purpose.

The Command Center

Zordon's Command Center stands in the desert outside Angel Grove, in California, out of the city's sight. He built it with his robot, Alpha 5, who comes from Edenoi and keeps the machines running. He appears there as a vast, calm face within a column of light. He cannot leave it.

Zordon chooses who carries the Power Coins, which Ninjor made in his Temple of Power. Through them the Rangers draw on the Power, a great current of energy running through creation, which they call the Morphin Grid. He sends them out with the words 'May the Power protect you'.

One coin never came to him. From her dumpster Rita had the thief Loriyan steal the Dragon Coin, the Green Power Coin, from Ninjor. It lay for a long time afterwards in the Temple of Repulsa, on the planet Breel.

The Rangers of 1969

With the Power Coins Zordon raised a first team of Rangers in the 1960s. It never came to public notice, and it was a disaster.

In July 1969, while the whole world was watching the Americans land on the Moon, Dark Specter sent a creature called Psycho Green to the same place, to break Rita out of her dumpster. Zordon chose five Rangers in a hurry: grown men and women of different nations, who had never fought together. Grace Sterling, who ran the typing pool at NASA, was the Red Ranger, and she led them. Nikolai Chukarin, an agent of the Soviet KGB, was the Blue. Jamie Gilmore, a British singer, was the Black. Terona Washington, back from the war in Vietnam, was the Yellow. Daniel O'Halloran, a student, was the Pink.

They fought Psycho Green on the Moon, on their first and only mission. They had never trained together, and it showed. Psycho Green crushed Jamie Gilmore under a thrown rock, killing her. He broke the visor of Daniel O'Halloran's helmet, and Daniel suffocated. When the creature swelled into a monstrous shape and swallowed Nikolai Chukarin whole, Nikolai fired one of Zordon's cannons from inside it, destroying them both. Rita stayed in her dumpster.

Only two came home, Grace Sterling and Terona Washington. Terona, for his part, told Zordon that it had been irresponsible to send untrained strangers to fight. Zordon blamed himself, but he took back their powers all the same, and the two of them left him in anger. Grace kept a souvenir of the Moon: Psycho Green's dagger. She left NASA afterwards, and with Terona she founded a company of their own, Promethea.

The Mighty Morphin Power Rangers

In 1993 two astronauts landed on the Moon and opened the dumpster, not knowing what was inside it. Rita was free. She went back to her palace and turned on Earth once more. Zordon tried again. He chose five young people of Angel Grove, pupils at Angel Grove High School: Jason Lee Scott, the Red Ranger; Billy Cranston, the Blue; Zack Taylor, the Black; Trini Kwan, the Yellow; and Kimberly Hart, the Pink. That team, the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, worked.

Each of them carries a Power Coin in a morpher, and each coin calls up a Zord, a giant fighting machine. The five Zords join together into the Megazord, a robot the size of a cathedral. On 30 July 1993 the Rangers came to public notice for the first time, when five of them fought a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham. They have been on the news ever since.

Later in 1993 Rita gave the stolen Green Power Coin to Tommy Oliver, a martial artist new to Angel Grove, and bound him with a spell to destroy the Rangers. When Jason broke the spell, Tommy joined Zordon's team as the sixth Ranger, the Green.

Within weeks Lord Drakkon, the Tommy Oliver of another world, sent a war machine into this one, the Black Dragon. It wrecked the Command Center, cutting Zordon adrift between the two worlds. He would have faded there if the other world's Saba, a sabre that talks, had not kept him tethered until the Command Center was rebuilt, a few weeks later.

Before the year was out Rita had drained Tommy's powers with a cursed green candle. What Zordon could give back to him was not permanent. By the summer of 1994 there are six Rangers on the news nearly every morning, and the Green Ranger's powers keep running out.

In the spring of 1994 Rita Repulsa carried the Green Ranger off to Japan with a stolen gem, the Multiversal Focus. Zordon traced him there, then sent the other Rangers after him. They came home having fought first against Godzilla, the great beast of that country, then beside him. Afterwards Zordon could find no trace of Rita, though he did not expect her to stay away.

Lord Zedd on the Moon

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon. He was Rita's master, and he had lost patience with her. He shrank her, sealed her in a dumpster and threw her out into space, then took up her war himself. His monsters outclassed Finster's, so Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords.

Zedd went after Tommy Oliver first. With a green crystal he stripped away what was left of the Green Ranger's powers. Zordon and Alpha 5 worked in secret on a new power for him. The way to it was shown them by the Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, as the price of a bargain with Jason that Zordon knew nothing of. In October 1994 Tommy came back as the White Ranger, with the White Tigerzord and Saba, a sabre that talks. He took Jason's place as leader.

In November 1994 Jason, Zack and Trini were chosen to go to a peace conference in Geneva. Zordon agreed that they must go, believing that they meant to. Before they went, they brought back the Sword of Light from a far planet, though Zedd's great machine Serpentera laid most of that world waste. With the Sword, Zordon passed their powers to three friends from Stone Canyon. Rocky DeSantos became the Red Ranger, Adam Park the Black and Aisha Campbell the Yellow. The three never went near Geneva. They went into space as the Omega Rangers, sworn to keep it from Zordon above all.

Late in November the Omega Rangers, strangers to Zordon behind their helmets, carried Lord Zedd off from the Moon. That angered him: Zedd was an enemy he could manage. Early in December the three came to the Command Center with their faces bare, Jason badly hurt, and Zordon forgave them at once.

In December he locked the fallen Lord Drakkon in a cell under the Command Center, and he barred Billy Cranston from the place for helping Grace Sterling to mend the Dragon Coin behind his back. When the Omega Rangers took Drakkon from his cell in January 1995, Zordon called it a complete betrayal and disowned them.

The Eltarian War

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus, his old comrade, now Supreme Guardian of Eltar, asked him to come home. Zordon chose Earth, so Zartus smashed his tube. Zartus never knew what Zordon was. A Maia cannot be killed, but he can lose the form he wears. What the tube had held was caught by a second vessel that Billy had built in secret, and Zordon went to war in a body of metal, on his own feet for the first time in ten thousand years.

On the Moon he laid down his weapon before Lord Zedd, who saw at last that the Fire of Truth had been Zartus's doing. Together they turned on Zartus, and Zordon killed him with a piece of the Zeo Crystal. Afterwards Grace Sterling gave him a new tube. He made his peace with her, and with Billy too.

The darkest hour

In February 1995 Rita came back as Mistress Vile, with the Vessel, the body Zordon had worn on Eltar before the time warp. It came into his mind, offering to make the two of them one again, and he refused. When the Rangers of both teams gathered round his tube and morphed as one, Zordon was at the heart of the pulse that cleansed the Grid. It destroyed the Vessel and threw Dark Specter back into the dark, much reduced. The world was mended a second time, and Zordon was among the few who remembered. Afterwards he put the Zeo Crystal back in the caves beneath the Moon Palace, under the ward that no evil hand can pass. That is where Master Vile found it in November 1995.

Rita, Rito and Master Vile

Soon afterwards Rita came back to the Moon, and in February 1995 she married Zedd, whom she had dosed with a love potion. In September 1995 her brother, Rito Revolto, arrived and destroyed the Thunderzords. Zordon sent the Rangers to Ninjor, who gave them new powers, the Ninja coins.

That autumn Katherine Hillard, a girl Rita had used as a spy until she broke free, took Kimberly Hart's place as the Pink Ranger. In November 1995 Master Vile came looking for the Zeo Crystal. With his Orb of Doom he turned back time until the Rangers, and everyone else on Earth, were children again. Zordon called in the Alien Rangers of Aquitar to defend Earth in their place.

In February 1996 Rita and Zedd destroyed the Power Coins. Rito and Goldar stole the Zeo Crystal, leaving a bomb behind them. It blew the Command Center to pieces. The Rangers had been sent to safety first.

Zeo, Turbo and the fall of Eltar

Zordon and Alpha 5 had not been destroyed with it. In April 1996 the Zeo Crystal, still whole, led the Rangers to them in the Power Chamber beneath the ruins. With its power Zordon made them the Zeo Rangers, to fight the Machine Empire of King Mondo, which had come to conquer Earth. Rita and Zedd fled from it to Master Vile in the M51 Galaxy.

In April 1997 Zordon went back to Eltar, taking Alpha 5 with him. He left the Rangers in the care of a mentor called Dimitria, with a new robot, Alpha 6. By then they had Turbo powers, to fight a space pirate called Divatox.

Before the year was out Eltar had fallen to evil, and Dark Specter had taken Zordon prisoner. He set about draining Zordon's power. In November 1997 Divatox destroyed the Power Chamber.

In October 1996 the Zeo Rangers fought in the town of Charterville beside the Beetleborgs, three children whose armour had come from a wish granted by a phasm. Billy Cranston could make no sense of their powers. Zordon knew a spirit's work when he saw it, as he told Billy. He had never met the phasm, whose name was Flabber.

The breaking of the tube

The Rangers, with no powers left, went into space after him in a shuttle. They found Andros, the Red Ranger of the planet KO-35, and in 1998 they took up new powers as the Space Rangers. Dark Specter had gathered every villain of any consequence in the universe into one alliance: Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd, Divatox, the Machine Empire and others. He kept Zordon on the Dark Fortress, the base of his pupil Astronema.

In November 1998 Dark Specter sent the alliance against the whole universe at once. He did not see the end of it. He and Darkonda, one of his own allies, destroyed each other. Astronema led the attack in his place, and her armies came down on Angel Grove.

Andros found Zordon at last. Zordon asked him to break the tube that held him, knowing what would follow. In the end Andros did. Zordon gave up the form he had worn for ten thousand years, and his light went out across the whole of the universe in a single wave. Where it passed, the alliance's monsters crumbled into sand. Rita, Zedd and Divatox were made human, with the evil gone out of them. Astronema became Karone again, Andros's lost sister.

A Maia cannot be killed. What became of Zordon afterwards, nobody on Earth knows. Gandalf may; if so, he has not said. In 2022 Billy Cranston, once the Blue Ranger, tried to bring him back by gathering what was left of the wave. What came back instead was the evil that the wave had driven out of Rita Repulsa.

The painting

A plain Muggle oil painting of Zordon, made before Rita cursed him, hangs in the Headmaster's office at Hogwarts, between two bookcases and a little apart from the portraits of the old heads. It is the only surviving likeness of his face, and it does not move. It shows a bald man with skin of a deep, calm, even blue, like the sky just after the sun has gone down. He wears a high-collared golden breastplate covered in curling designs. His expression is very patient, very wise and very, very kind. A brass plate on the frame reads: 'For Albus. From your friend who keeps watch. May the Power protect you.'

The painting was not in the office in 1943, so Dumbledore acquired it himself. It hangs there, and nowhere else in Britain, because of whose colleague Zordon is. Gandalf, who as Ambrose Greyhame calls it 'the office', has known the room since before the drive had a gate on it. He is Zordon's colleague, and one Istar's portrait simply hangs where the other visits. Dumbledore himself is not one of the Istari.

In the saga

Book Two, Chapter Fourteen: alone in Dumbledore's office, Harry found his eyes going back to the still Muggle painting of the blue man in gold armour. He had the oddest feeling, though he could not have said why, that the man was somebody important. He was right.

Book Two, Chapter Fifteen: inside Tom Riddle's memory of the office fifty years earlier, Harry noticed that there was no blue man in golden armour between the bookcases.

Book Three, Chapter Two: the Rangers Zordon raised appeared on the Dursleys' television fighting a starfish in Birmingham. Dudley wanted to be one of them.

Book Four, Chapter Three: by August 1994 there were six Rangers on the news nearly every morning. The newest was green, with a gold shield across his chest, and Dudley adored him.

pages.title: The Auror who wept at a Garou
infobox: A very brave man and a war hero
pages.html:
The Auror who wept at a Garou was a very brave wizard and a war hero, whom Minerva McGonagall once watched lose his nerve entirely. A Garou came round the corner of a barn. He dropped his wand and stood there weeping like a child.

The Delirium

It was not cowardice. The sight of a Garou in its war shape, the Crinos, which stands nine feet tall, does something to the mind. It is called the Delirium. Muggles who see one forget it, or go mad, or both. Most wizards are not much better off. The Auror's name is not recorded.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, in the autumn of 1992, Gilderoy Lockhart made Harry Potter play the Wagga Wagga werewolf in class. That evening Professor McGonagall took Harry aside into a window alcove to put him right about werewolves, and she told him about the Auror. If Harry ever met a Garou, she said, and it was angry, he was not to fight it or try to Stun it. He was to run.

pages.title: The Honeydukes witch
infobox: Behind the counter at Honeydukes, Hogsmeade
Dropping a jar of Pepper Imps
pages.html:
The Honeydukes witch serves behind the counter at Honeydukes, the sweetshop in Hogsmeade. In December 1992 an old man laughed so loudly at a Chocolate Frog card in her shop that she dropped a jar of Pepper Imps, the tiny black sweets that make you breathe fire.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame came up the road from Hogsmeade to Hogwarts on foot, with the first of the snow. Long ago, as adviser to a young king in the West Country, he had borne a name that is still printed on the cards in Chocolate Frogs. On his way through the village he bought one at Honeydukes, out of curiosity, and looked at the picture for some time. He thought the nose was quite wrong. The beard was far too tidy. Then he laughed so loudly that the witch behind the counter dropped a jar of Pepper Imps.

pages.title: Boris the Bewildered
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
By a staircase on the fifth floor, Hogwarts
The prefects' bathroom, the fourth door to its left
pages.html:
Boris the Bewildered is a statue at Hogwarts of a puzzled-looking wizard who wears his gloves on the wrong hands. It stands by a staircase on the fifth floor. The prefects' bathroom is the fourth door to the left of it.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, in November 1992, a few days after Colin Creevey was Petrified, Fred and George Weasley were trying to cheer their sister Ginny up. On the Tuesday, Harry Potter was coming down the staircase to breakfast when George leapt out from behind the statue, covered from head to foot in shaggy orange fur. Ginny screamed so loudly that a portrait of a sleeping monk fell off its nail. "Got you!" said George happily.

pages.title: Portrait of a sleeping monk
infobox: By a staircase at Hogwarts, near the statue of Boris the Bewildered
pages.html:
The portrait of a sleeping monk hangs by a staircase at Hogwarts, not far from the statue of Boris the Bewildered. It is best known for falling off its nail.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, in November 1992, the news that Colin Creevey had been Petrified had spread right through the school by Monday morning. Fred and George Weasley were trying to cheer their sister Ginny up, but they were going about it all wrong. On the Tuesday, Harry Potter was coming down the staircase to breakfast when George leapt out from behind the statue of Boris the Bewildered, covered from head to foot in shaggy orange fur. Ginny screamed so loudly that the portrait of the sleeping monk fell off its nail.

pages.title: Portrait of a fat friar eating a pie
infobox: A fat friar eating a pie
An upper corridor of Hogwarts castle
pages.html:
The portrait of a fat friar eating a pie hangs in one of the corridors of Hogwarts castle, a few flights above the Entrance Hall. The friar in it once put down his pie to bow to Ambrose Greyhame.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, on the snowy evening in December 1992 when Ambrose Greyhame came up to the castle, the old man climbed the stairs in no hurry at all. He stood for a whole minute in front of a hanging of trolls in tutus, with his head on one side, then went on, chuckling into his beard. Next he passed the portrait of the friar. The friar looked up with his mouth full, his eyes popping. He lowered the pie very slowly, and bowed.

pages.title: Portrait of a knight on a fat grey pony
infobox: A knight on a fat grey pony
An upper corridor of Hogwarts castle
pages.html:
The portrait of a knight on a fat grey pony hangs in an upper corridor of Hogwarts castle. Its knight challenges passers-by to single combat. In this he is very like Sir Cadogan, who also rides a fat grey pony and also falls off it.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame passed the painting on his way up through the castle. The knight drew his sword and challenged him to single combat. The old man drew himself up and challenged him back, very gravely. Then he said he was afraid it would have to wait for another day, as he was expected elsewhere. The knight was so pleased that he fell off his pony.

pages.title: Portraits in Dumbledore's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Former headmasters and headmistresses of Hogwarts
pages.html:
The portraits in Dumbledore's office are the likenesses of the old headmasters and headmistresses of Hogwarts. They cover the walls of the round room at the top of the gargoyle staircase. Most of the time they snooze in their frames, or pretend to.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame sat up all night by the fire in Dumbledore's office while the portraits of old headmasters snored in their frames. Now and then a smoke ring from his pipe changed shape on its way to the ceiling. Once it became a tiny dragon, which flew twice round the room and settled on the head of a sleeping portrait. The portrait sneezed.

When Ambrose said that Harry must go back to the Dursleys, Dumbledore was angry for a moment. The air in the office went heavy and still. The fire sank low and blue. The portraits, who had all been pretending to sleep, opened their eyes.

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, Harry Potter waited alone in the office and looked round at them, snoozing gently on the walls. Among them was a very fat old wizard with a pipe and a parrot. There was a thin-lipped witch too, whose hair was scraped back so tightly that she looked astonished even asleep.

pages.title: The snake conjured at the Duelling Club
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
The snake conjured at the Duelling Club was a long black snake that Dracina Malfoy produced from her wand with the spell Serpensortia in 1992. When Harry Potter spoke to it, the school learnt that he was a Parselmouth.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, at the end of her duel with Harry, an exhausted Dracina cried 'Serpensortia!' A long black snake shot from her wand, fell heavily to the floor between them and reared up to strike. Lockhart insisted on dealing with it. With a loud bang he flung it ten feet into the air. It came down furious and went straight for Justin Finch-Fletchley.

Harry found himself shouting at it, in Parseltongue, to leave Justin alone. The snake slumped to the floor, as limp as a coil of wet rope, and looked at Harry as if waiting to be told what to do next. Then Snape waved his wand, and it vanished in a puff of black smoke.

pages.title: The boa constrictor at the zoo
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
The reptile house of a Muggle zoo
Harry Potter, by accident, in June 1991
pages.html:
The boa constrictor at the zoo was the first snake Harry Potter ever spoke to. On Dudley Dursley's birthday in June 1991 it told Harry that it had never been to Brazil, and Harry, without meaning to, set it loose on Dudley.

The zoo

The sign on the boa's tank said that its kind came from Brazil, but it had been bred in the zoo. When Harry looked at it, it winked. Moments later the glass of the tank had vanished. The boa slid out across the floor and away. As it went past Harry it thanked him, and called him amigo.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, after the Duelling Club, Ron and Hermione were dismayed to find that Harry was a Parselmouth. Harry told them it was only the second time he had ever done it. The first time he had set a boa constrictor on his cousin Dudley at the zoo, by accident, before he even knew he was a wizard. The snake had been telling him it had never been to Brazil.

In Book Three, Chapter Eleven, in December 1993, Harry lay awake in the dark hating Sirius Black. Until then, the place in him where such things were kept had held nothing but the small change of revenge: blown-up aunts, 'a ticket to Brazil for a snake'.

pages.title: The student with badger-striped hair
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
The student with badger-striped hair was one of Professor McGonagall's Transfiguration pupils in December 1992. On the day of the blizzard when Justin Finch-Fletchley was Petrified, a boy in her class turned his friend into a badger. When the class came running out after her, one of them still had black-and-white striped hair.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, Harry Potter walked past McGonagall's classroom on his way to the library. Inside she was shouting at somebody who, by the sound of it, had turned his friend into a badger. Not long afterwards Peeves found Harry standing over the Petrified Justin and screamed the news down the corridor. Doors flew open all along it. McGonagall came running, followed by her own class, one of whom still had black-and-white striped hair.

pages.title: The crying Hufflepuff first-year
pages.html:
The crying Hufflepuff first-year was one of the students watching at the Duelling Club in the Great Hall in December 1992, standing near the doors. When the duel between Harry Potter and Dracina Malfoy turned frightening, the first-year began to cry.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, Snape paired Harry with Dracina. The two of them went on circling each other and firing long after the teachers tried to separate them, shouting insults across the gap. When Harry shouted that at least Hermione was not mental, Dracina flinched as if he had hit her, and for a second her eyes went completely black. The watching students fell into the other kind of quiet, the frightened kind. A first-year Hufflepuff near the doors started to cry, while two Ravenclaw girls held on to each other. Nobody left. A moment later Dracina cast Serpensortia.

pages.title: Moaning Myrtle's bathroom
aliases: the girls' bathroom on the second floor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Moaning Myrtle, who died there in 1943
The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets
pages.html:
Moaning Myrtle's bathroom is a dismal girls' bathroom at Hogwarts, out of order because its ghost keeps having tantrums and flooding it. Myrtle died there in 1943. One of its sinks hides the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets.

Description

An OUT OF ORDER sign hangs on the door. Inside are a big cracked mirror, a row of chipped stone basins and a damp floor. The cubicle doors are scratched, with one of them hanging off its hinges. Nobody in their right mind ever goes there, which gives the place its uses.

The door stands beside the stretch of corridor where Mrs Norris was found Petrified, and where the messages of the Heir were written on the wall. The entrance to the Chamber is a sink whose copper tap has a tiny snake scratched on its side. The tap has never worked. Spoken to in Parseltongue, it lights up and turns. Then the whole sink drops out of sight, leaving a wide pipe gaping where it stood.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Ten, on the night Mrs Norris was attacked at Hallowe'en 1992, water from the bathroom had spread across the corridor outside its door.

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger brewed the Polyjuice Potion in one of its cubicles, judging that nobody in their right mind ever went there. In Chapter Fourteen Dracina Malfoy said that she had once found herself there alone in the dark, with the taps running and her shoes wet. She could not remember how she had got there.

In Book Two, Chapter Fifteen, water was seeping out under the door again, past its Out of Order sign, on to the spot where Mrs Norris had been attacked and the messages written. Inside, Myrtle complained that a posh girl with long, straight, shiny hair had stood at the sinks, running her hands over the taps and asking where 'it' was. Then the girl had thrown her bag at Myrtle and run off crying, leaving the taps running.

In Chapter Eighteen Myrtle told Harry and Ron that she had died there in 1943, after seeing a pair of great big yellow eyes. Harry found the tiny snake on the tap and spoke to it in Parseltongue. The bathroom where Hermione had brewed the Polyjuice Potion had held the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets all along.

pages.title: The corridor of the Hallowe'en attack
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
THE CHAMBER OF SECRETS HAS BEEN OPENED. ENEMIES OF THE HEIR, BEWARE.
pages.html:
The corridor of the Hallowe'en attack is the passage on the second floor of Hogwarts where Argus Filch's cat, Mrs Norris, was found Petrified on Hallowe'en night in 1992. Above the spot, between two tall windows, somebody had daubed a message across the wall in letters a foot high, glimmering red in the torchlight. It announced that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened.

The corridor

The message read: THE CHAMBER OF SECRETS HAS BEEN OPENED. ENEMIES OF THE HEIR, BEWARE. On the night of the attack a great puddle of water lay on the floor beneath it, and Mrs Norris hung stiff above the puddle by her tail from a torch bracket. The water had come from Moaning Myrtle's toilet, whose door opens off the same corridor. Filch afterwards kept guard there from a chair set against the wall under the message.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, on Hallowe'en 1992, Harry Potter heard a voice in the walls. He ran up past the first floor to the deserted second floor, with Ron and Hermione behind him. There they found the message, the puddle and the Petrified cat.

In Chapter Ten they came back to look. The corridor was just as it had been, except that there was no stiff cat, and an empty chair now stood against the wall where Filch had been keeping guard. Harry crawled along the flagstones and found scorch marks. Hermione noticed twenty or so spiders at the topmost pane of the window beside the message, scuttling out through a small crack in the glass. Ron would not go into the girls' toilet next to the spot where the water had been. 'That's a girls' toilet. Mum was always very clear about that.'

pages.title: Slytherin common room
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The dungeons of Hogwarts, under the black lake
A hidden stone door in a bare, damp wall
pages.html:
The Slytherin common room is the long, low room under the black lake where the students of Slytherin house spend their evenings. It lies behind a stretch of bare, damp dungeon wall, in which a hidden stone door slides open at the password. At Christmas 1992 the password was 'Pureblood'.

The room

It was dug out of the bedrock under the castle, and somewhere overhead, through all that rock, lies the black lake. The walls are rough, bare stone beaded with damp, and the ceiling is low. Lamps of thick green glass swing from it on long iron links, so that everything is lit with a green, underwater gloom. A fire burns in a vast stone hearth under a mantelpiece carved with a row of grinning skulls, with serpents winding in and out of their eye sockets.

A hanging on the far wall shows a long-dead witch in green doing something extremely unpleasant to a dragon. Every chair is black, every cushion green, and every candlestick a silver snake. Professor Snape, the Head of Slytherin, calls the place a warren.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, at Christmas 1992, Harry Potter and Ron Weasley got in by Polyjuice Potion, wearing the shapes of Dracina Malfoy's two cronies. Dracina gave the password with relish. Harry thought the room looked like every evil wizard's lair in every story he had ever read.

In Chapter Fifteen, on Boxing Day 1992, the day after Harry took the diary, Dracina turned the common room upside down looking for it. She pulled the cushions off the chairs, the books off the shelves and the rugs off the floor, then threw a candlestick at a prefect.

In Chapter Eighteen, after Ginny Weasley was taken into the Chamber, Snape told the other teachers in the staffroom that one of his own Slytherins had not answered the register either. 'The Slytherin common room is a warren, and I have not yet searched the whole of it.'

In Book Three, Chapter Sixteen, in the last round of the 1994 feud between Gryffindor and Slytherin, somebody let off a crate of Dungbombs outside it. Somebody else filled every sock drawer in Gryffindor Tower with frogspawn.

The Interlude of Book Three tells how, in the 1960s, the other boys in the Slytherin dungeon dormitory made it clear to the Muggle-born John Constantine that they would not put up with him. They started on his first night. His bed had been charmed to tip him out on to the stone floor every hour, on the hour, until dawn.

pages.title: Headmaster's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Hogwarts, at the top of a moving spiral staircase
A stone gargoyle, which moves aside for the password
Polished oak, with a brass griffin knocker
The Sorting Hat; Fawkes's golden perch; a Muggle painting of Zordon
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
The Headmaster's office is the round room high in Hogwarts where the head of the school works. It lies at the top of a moving spiral staircase, behind a stone gargoyle that steps aside only for the password. In Albus Dumbledore's time it is a large, beautiful room full of light, with silver instruments whirring on spindle-legged tables and the portraits of former heads asleep round the walls.

The way up

The gargoyle is large and extremely ugly. Given the right password, which under Dumbledore is nearly always the name of a sweet, it springs to life and hops aside. The wall behind it splits in two. Beyond it a spiral stone staircase moves smoothly upwards, like an escalator, and visitors rise on it in circles until they reach a polished oak door with a brass knocker in the shape of a griffin.

The room

The office is full of funny little noises. Silver instruments whirr and puff on spindle-legged tables. The portraits of old headmasters and headmistresses snooze in their frames all round the walls. There is an enormous claw-footed desk, a chintz armchair by the fire and, on a shelf behind the desk, the Sorting Hat. Fawkes, Dumbledore's phoenix, dozes on a golden perch beside the door.

Between two bookcases hangs a perfectly ordinary Muggle oil painting, which never moves. It shows Zordon of Eltar, a bald, blue-skinned man in a high-collared golden breastplate. The brass plate on the frame reads: 'For Albus. From your friend who keeps watch. May the Power protect you.'

History

In 1943, under Armando Dippet, the office had the same dozing portraits, but no golden perch, no phoenix, no silver instruments and no blue man in golden armour. Those all came with Dumbledore.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, in December 1992, Harry Potter found Justin Finch-Fletchley and Nearly Headless Nick lying Petrified. Professor McGonagall marched him to the gargoyle and gave the password, 'Sherbet lemon!' They rose on the moving staircase to the oak door.

In Chapter Thirteen, on a dark night, with the first of the snow, Ambrose Greyhame walked up from Hogsmeade to see Dumbledore. He sat in the chintz armchair by the fire, with a long package across his knees, and took out a pipe. When Dumbledore next turned round, the armchair was empty. There was only a faint, sweet smell of pipe smoke, and a single smoke ring drifting up towards the ceiling. As Dumbledore watched, it became a little ship with a grey sail, which sailed away through the west window into the snow.

In Chapter Fourteen Dumbledore went off to see the Petrified pair and left Harry alone in the office to wait. Harry had been in trouble in plenty of offices, but never in this one, where hardly anybody was ever sent. He stared for a long time at the blue man between the bookcases, then lifted the Sorting Hat off its shelf and put it on.

In Chapter Fifteen Harry saw the office again through Tom Riddle's diary, as it had been under Dippet in 1943. Before Christmas he had told Dumbledore, in this same room, that everything was being handled.

In the Book Three Interlude, in August 1993, John Constantine came back to the gargoyle for the first time in twenty-two years. It was always a sweet with the old man, he remembered. 'Sherbet lemon' did nothing; 'Acid Pop' worked. He walked in without knocking and found Dumbledore behind the desk, filling in a form. 'Ah, John,' he said pleasantly. 'I have been expecting you.'

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, in the Top Box on 22 August 1994, Harry Potter made Lucius Malfoy laugh in spite of himself. It was the same dry, startled laugh that Harry had heard at the top of the stairs outside Dumbledore's office, at the end of his second year.

pages.title: Hogsmeade
infobox: Below Hogwarts, in the Scottish Highlands
Honeydukes, Zonko's, Dervish and Banges, the Three Broomsticks, the Hog's Head, the post office, the Shrieking Shack
Hogsmeade station (Hogwarts Express); the Knight Bus
Third-years and above, on certain weekends, with a signed form
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Hogsmeade is the only all-wizard village in Britain: a single street of thatched cottages and shops at the foot of the road up to Hogwarts. Its station is the end of the line for the Hogwarts Express. From the third year onwards, Hogwarts students may visit the village on certain weekends with a signed permission form.

The village

Hogsmeade lies below the castle in the Scottish Highlands. Tradition says it was founded by Hengist of Woodcroft, a wizard driven out of his home by Muggle persecution. Sites of Historical Sorcery records that one of its inns was the headquarters of the goblin rebellion of 1612. The same book calls the Shrieking Shack, on the slope above the village, the most severely haunted building in Britain.

The Shack's reputation was in fact made by the young Remus Lupin. While he was at school he was taken there every month for his transformations, through a tunnel from the Whomping Willow. His friends roamed the village by night in animal form.

Shops and inns

Honeydukes is the sweetshop. Ambrose Greyhame bought a Chocolate Frog there on his walk up to the castle in December 1992, and laughed so loudly at the picture on the card that the witch behind the counter dropped a jar of Pepper Imps.

Zonko's is the joke shop, which Percy Weasley called frankly a menace. Dervish and Banges sells magical instruments, mends them and deals in second-hand brooms. There is also a quill shop, which Dracina Malfoy meant to show Harry Potter in 1993. The post office keeps two hundred owls, colour-coded by speed, with little Scops owls for local deliveries only. At Christmas the trees along the street are hung with enchanted candles.

Students drink Butterbeer at the Three Broomsticks, which is kept by Madam Rosmerta. The Hog's Head is the village's other pub, a rougher one; as Hagrid said, 'Yeh get all sorts in the Hog's Head.' It was there that he won Norbert's egg at cards in 1992, from a stranger who never once put his hood down and kept buying him drinks. Before the night was out the stranger had learnt how to get past Fluffy.

In the back room of the Hog's Head, in 1985, John Constantine tried to apologise to Albus Dumbledore for stealing his Deluminator. A goat looked in at the window while Dumbledore let him get about three words out, then shouted him down.

Getting there

The Hogwarts Express runs from King's Cross to Hogsmeade station. From there the first-years go down to the lake for the boats, while the older students take the carriages up to the castle. The Knight Bus also calls.

Ambrose Greyhame, who has always liked to walk the last mile to anywhere, came up the road from Hogsmeade to Hogwarts on foot in December 1992. In the summer of 1993 John Constantine took the Knight Bus to the village and walked up the lane to the castle gates.

In the saga

Harry Potter had no signed form for his third year. He had extracted a promise from Uncle Vernon to sign it, by blackmail over a British National Party membership card, but the promise came to nothing after Harry inflated Aunt Marge. Cornelius Fudge would not sign it either.

Before the last Hogsmeade weekend of 1993, Fred and George Weasley gave him the Marauder's Map. He went through the one-eyed witch's passage into the cellar of Honeydukes. In the Three Broomsticks, hidden behind a Christmas tree, he heard McGonagall, Flitwick, Hagrid, Fudge and Madam Rosmerta tell the story of Sirius Black. As they told it, Black, his father's best friend and his own godfather, had betrayed his parents.

Dementors searched the village twice for Black, and patrolled it at night from December 1993. In 1994 they guarded every road out of it. On the next Hogsmeade Saturday Harry went under the Invisibility Cloak. Near the Shrieking Shack he pelted Dracina, Crabbe and Goyle with mud until the Cloak slipped.

On the night of Buckbeak's execution in June 1994 a huge black dog dragged Ron under the Whomping Willow. Harry went after him with Hermione, down the tunnel to the Shrieking Shack. There Sirius Black, Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew met again for the first time in twelve years.

After Black's escape there was a Hogsmeade trip after all, and nearly the whole school went, to get away from the grounds. On the train home a tiny owl brought Harry a letter from Sirius, with signed permission to visit Hogsmeade at weekends.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, before the World Cup final on 22 August 1994, the gigantic blackboard in the stadium carried an advertisement for Gladrags Wizardwear, with shops in London, Paris and Hogsmeade.

pages.title: Azkaban
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
A fortress on a rock far out in the North Sea
Ekrizdis, a dark sorcerer of the fifteenth century
One: Sirius Black, in the summer of 1993
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Azkaban is the prison of the British wizarding world, a fortress on a rock far out in the sea. Its guards are the Dementors, who are allowed to feed on the prisoners, guilty and innocent alike. Remus Lupin says that most of the inmates are mad inside a month. Until Sirius Black slipped out of it in the summer of 1993, nobody had ever escaped.

The fortress

The fortress was built in the fifteenth century by Ekrizdis, a dark sorcerer who lured Muggle sailors there to their deaths. After he died, the Ministry found the island swarming with Dementors. In time the wizarding authorities decided that the Dementors would make perfectly good gaolers, and Azkaban became their prison.

The Dementors

'Nobody in Azkaban needs a wall,' Lupin once said. The Dementors drain every happy thought from the people near them, leaving each prisoner shut up inside his own skull with the worst of himself. Arthur Weasley went out there once on Ministry business, years ago, and came home grey. He said it was like being somewhere all the light had been sucked out of.

Prisoners

Many of Lord Voldemort's followers were sent to Azkaban after his fall in 1981. Sirius Black went with them, without a trial. He spent twelve years there in the cell next to his cousin Bellatrix Lestrange's. In the summer of 1993 he slipped out through the bars in the shape of a dog, the first prisoner ever to escape.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, Dracina Malfoy told Harry Potter, who was disguised as Goyle, that whoever had opened the Chamber of Secrets fifty years before would be rotting in Azkaban, if they were still alive. When Harry repeated the word before he could stop himself, she was scornful: 'Azkaban, Goyle. The wizards' prison? On the island? With the Dementors?' In Chapter Sixteen, in the spring of 1993, Cornelius Fudge took Rubeus Hagrid there as a precaution. Lucius Malfoy had a word of advice for him: 'If I were you, I should take care not to raise your voice like that to the guards at Azkaban. I'm told they don't care for it.' Hagrid was held there until the night of 29 to 30 May. In Chapter Nineteen, once the Chamber had been closed, Dumbledore wrote to Azkaban that same night. Hagrid turned up at the feast at half past three in the morning, with Fawkes on his shoulder and the sea still on his coat.

In Book Three, Chapter Three, Stan Shunpike told Harry on the Knight Bus that nobody had ever broken out of Azkaban before Black. Harry remembered Hagrid being taken there the year before, without a hearing or a trial. In Chapter Six George Weasley told him about his father's visit to the prison, and in Chapter Ten Lupin said that most of the prisoners were mad inside a month.

In Chapter Eighteen Sirius told Harry about his twelve years there without a trial, with Bella in the next cell, and how he had slipped out through the bars as a dog. In Chapter Twenty-One Harry thought about the people who had chosen the Dementors as prison guards. The wizarding world had let them feed on whole prisonfuls of people, year after year, guilty and innocent alike.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, at the World Cup final on 22 August 1994, Harry Potter worked out who 'Bella', the prisoner in the cell next to Sirius Black's, had been: Bellatrix, the twin sister of Narcissa Malfoy. He remembered too that Sirius had kept himself alive in Azkaban on the things Lily used to say.

pages.title: Transylvania
infobox: Inside the curve of the Carpathian Mountains
pages.html:
Transylvania is the high, wooded country inside the curve of the Carpathian Mountains, now part of Romania. It is Dracula's own country. In the Middle Ages the Tzimisce voivodes held it, and the Tremere fought them for its mountains for generations. It was the old home of the Belmonts, the family of vampire hunters, whose dead lie buried there.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Ten, on Hallowe'en 1992, Gilderoy Lockhart claimed to have foiled a cult of Dracula worshippers in Transylvania, all in red, who kept a cat like Mrs Norris on their altar. Professor McGonagall said pleasantly that he must know dear Julius, an old friend of hers who had been in Transylvania for some years and always carried a whip. Lockhart said he knew old Julius Carrow very well, and that Julius had helped him foil the cult. Its leader, by his account, was a Tzimisce Methuselah of the fourth generation, who came at him in the shape of a great wolf made out of men. Harry could tell from McGonagall's small sigh that whoever Julius was, he was not a Carrow. He was Julius Belmont.

pages.title: Wagga Wagga
pages.html:
Wagga Wagga is a city in New South Wales, Australia, on the Murrumbidgee River, in the middle of sheep country. Gilderoy Lockhart claimed it as the scene of one of his greatest triumphs.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, Lockhart made Harry play the beast while he acted out his cure of the Wagga Wagga werewolf: a moonlit pasture outside the town, the sheep scattering like dandelion clocks, and the Homorphus Charm performed with the very last of his strength. As he told it, the fur fell away before his very eyes, and there knelt a man, weeping, in the moonlight. 'And to this very day,' said Lockhart, with a catch in his voice, 'the mothers of that little village tell my name to their children at bedtime.' He set the class an ode on his triumph at Wagga Wagga for Thursday, twelve lines at the very least.

pages.title: Sunnydale
aliases: the Californian town above the Master
infobox: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Welcome to the Hellmouth' (10 March 1997)
The Hellmouth; the prison of the Master, 1937 to 1997
pages.html:
Sunnydale is the small town in California beneath which the vampire called the Master has been sealed since 1937, after a ritual went wrong. The town stands over a Hellmouth. From 1997 it was home to the Slayer, Buffy Summers.

The Hellmouth

Sunnydale was built over a Hellmouth, a place where the barrier between this world and the demon worlds runs thin. It has always drawn more than its share of vampires and demons.

Its residents put it all down to gang violence, or to accidents. They have had a good deal of practice. The town has a great many cemeteries for a place of its size, and nobody there seems to think this odd.

The Master's prison

In 1937 the Master tried to open the Hellmouth from a church in the town. An earthquake swallowed the church, and the ritual failed. He was trapped beneath the town in a mystical prison, where his followers attended him for sixty years.

The Slayer's town

In 1997 Buffy Summers came to live in Sunnydale, and that spring she destroyed the Master. The Hellmouth remained. Sunnydale went on drawing the dangerous and the damned until 2003. That year the whole town collapsed into the ground and was destroyed.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1992 Hermione Granger told Gilderoy Lockhart's class about the town without naming it: 'Because I've read three books on the Aurelian line, and all three of them say the Master's been trapped since nineteen thirty-seven. Under a town in California.' He had been sealed in, she said, when something went wrong with a ritual. He could not get out.

pages.title: Paris
infobox: The French Ministry of Magic keeps its offices there
Dracina Malfoy's dancing master came from there
pages.html:
Paris is the capital of France, for Muggles and wizards alike, since the French Ministry of Magic keeps its offices there too. For the Malfoys of Wiltshire it is where the finest things come from, teachers included.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, in the autumn of 1992, Dracina Malfoy jeered at Harry Potter's flying in the middle of a Quidditch match. Then, in a smaller and much softer voice, she offered to teach him. 'I had lessons for years. Mother made me, at the Manor. There was a man from Paris.' Harry dropped his shoulder when he turned, she told him, and that was why he wobbled.

In Chapter Fourteen, at Christmas 1992, she wore a new blouse to dinner: dark green silk, with little silver buttons all the way down, very obviously expensive. Harry did not so much as look at it. Afterwards she complained bitterly to the two people she took for Crabbe and Goyle. 'I had it sent from Paris. Paris.'

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, on the dock at Myst Island, Hermione Granger called her spoilt. Dracina agreed, very loudly, and went on to describe her lovely, spoilt little life. 'I have a pony, a music room and a man who comes by Floo all the way from Paris to teach me to dance.'

pages.title: The West Country
infobox: King Arthur's realm; Albus Dumbledore's boyhood; Godric's Hollow
pages.html:
The West Country is the south-west of England: Cornwall, Devon, Somerset and Dorset, with parts of the counties beside them. It is old ground for wizards. Merlin advised King Arthur there, and Albus Dumbledore grew up there, by a river at the bottom of a lane.

History

Arthur Pendragon was conceived at Tintagel on the Cornish coast, and ruled from Camelot. His adviser through those years was the old man in grey who was Gandalf in the elder days, and who is now Ambrose Greyhame, the vicar of St Michael's, Little Whinging. The name he went by at Arthur's court, Merlin, stuck to him so firmly that it is printed on Chocolate Frog cards to this day.

In the summer of 1892, when Albus Dumbledore was eleven, the same old man found him skimming stones in the river at the bottom of the lane. Albus had been sent out of the house for setting fire to the curtains. Godric's Hollow, where James and Lily Potter died in 1981, is a West Country village too.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, walking up from Hogsmeade to Hogwarts with the first snow of December 1992, the old man remembered his long, strange stretch of years as adviser to a young king in the West Country: a boy with a sword, a round table and a great deal more courage than sense. When the two of them met that night, Dumbledore's whole face changed. For a moment he was eleven again, standing in a meadow by a river in the West Country, while an old man in grey made a dandelion clock explode into a thousand floating stars.

pages.title: The drowned serpent temples
aliases: the black towers by the warm seas
infobox: Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary, Chapter 13
By the warm seas of the south
Drowned in the meltwater flood at the end of the Ice Age
pages.html:
The drowned serpent temples were the temples by the warm seas, before the Flood, where men worshipped a great serpent and fed it. Black towers stood beside them. Sorcerers learnt their magic from the thing that lived in those temples, and paid dearly for it. All of it went under the water when the ice went back at the end of the Ice Age.

History

They belonged to Stygia, the serpent-worshipping kingdom of the Hyborian Age, which kept the dark craft of Morgoth and practised it on a grand scale. Its people called their god Set, the Old Serpent. Scripture calls the Devil himself that old serpent.

The meltwater flood, which was the Flood of Noah, came down out of the north for a hundred years and drowned whole countries. The black towers went under, the temples with them, and the sorcerers too. Only scraps of what they knew survived, carried forward by dark hands.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame, who is Gandalf, walked up to Hogwarts through the snow and thought of how far back it all went. He thought of the ice going back, and of what had been drowned with the countries. 'The black towers by the warm seas, the temples where men had worshipped a great serpent and fed it.' Then he thought of the few frightened families on the cold new shores afterwards, by whose small fires he had once sat.

pages.title: Hogwarts Board of Governors
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Oversight of the school; suspension of the Headmaster
pages.html:
The Hogwarts Board of Governors is the body of twelve witches and wizards that oversees Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. It has the power to suspend the Headmaster. Lucius Malfoy sat on it until June 1993, and its members are frightened of him still.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, Dracina Malfoy reminded people again and again of her father's seat on the Board. 'He's a governor of Hogwarts, you know,' she told Percy Weasley. In Chapter Sixteen, in the spring of 1993, Lucius came to Hagrid's hut with an Order of Suspension for Dumbledore. 'You will find all twelve of our signatures on it.' He had forced the other governors to sign.

In Chapter Nineteen, Dumbledore came back. The other eleven governors had written to him that day, he told Lucius, having heard that Arthur Weasley's daughter had been killed. 'Rather like being caught in a hailstorm of owls, if I'm honest.' Several of them believed Lucius had threatened to curse their families if they did not suspend him. Lucius was sacked from the Board in June 1993. Even afterwards, half the governors still went pale at the sight of one of his owls.

In Book Three, Chapter Six, the governors knew of Dracina's injury by the evening of 2 September 1993. Hagrid told Harry Potter miserably: 'They're sayin' I went in too big. Shoulda started small.'

In Book Three, Chapter Nine, Lucius no longer sat on the Board, but its members still feared him. Dracina silenced the Slytherin team by asking Marcus Flint to tell them what had happened to the last governors who crossed her father over Dumbledore. In Chapter Eleven the governors wrote to Hagrid. They accepted Dumbledore's assurances and cleared him of blame, but they upheld Lucius Malfoy's complaint against the hippogriff. Lucius's name was not in the neat column of governors at the foot of the letter. Harry looked at it a moment longer than he needed to, thinking that a man did not have to sit on a thing to lean on it.

pages.title: Wizengamot
infobox: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (21 June 2003)
pages.html:
The Wizengamot is the high court of wizarding Britain. Its name comes from the witenagemot, the council of wise men that advised the Anglo-Saxon kings. In 1994 its Chief Warlock is Albus Dumbledore.

The court

Its members sit in plum-coloured robes to try the gravest cases under wizarding law. Henry Potter, Harry's great-grandfather, was one of them. Not everybody sent to Azkaban comes before it: Sirius Black went there in 1981 without a trial.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fourteen, Hagrid offered to swear to Harry's innocence in front of the whole Wizengamot if he had to. In Book Three, Chapter Four, Lucius Malfoy assured Harry that if a wall-climbing man such as Spider-Man existed, the Wizengamot would have heard of him.

pages.title: Unspeakables
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
pages.html:
The Unspeakables are the witches and wizards who work in the Department of Mysteries at the Ministry of Magic. They may not speak of what they do there to anyone, which is how they got their name.

The work

The Department lies on the lowest floors of the Ministry. It studies the deepest things there are, among them time, thought, love and death.

Minerva McGonagall has been an Unspeakable since before she came to teach at Hogwarts, about 1970. She has never entirely left. Through the 1980s she took sabbaticals from the school to do the Department's work, and in 1994 she is an Unspeakable still, though semi-retired. Her work has set her against vampires, Garou, the Nephilim and worse.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Thirteen, Dumbledore told his old teacher, Ambrose Greyhame, that there were not five wizards living who could do what Ambrose had taught him with a staff, old Mad-Eye perhaps excepted. Not even the Unspeakables could: 'They think it's a quaint old country thing, like Morris dancing.'

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Five, at the World Cup campsite on 22 August 1994, Arthur Weasley pointed out Bode and Croaker as Unspeakables. He had no idea what they got up to in their top-secret department.

pages.title: Aurors
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
The Department of Magical Law Enforcement, Ministry of Magic
Dawlish; Williamson; Frank and Alice Longbottom
pages.html:
The Aurors are the Dark wizard catchers of the Ministry of Magic, an elite force of highly trained witches and wizards. They bore the brunt of the first war against Lord Voldemort. Even an Auror, though, can be undone by the sight of a Garou.

History

An Auror's training lasts three years, and few of those who apply are taken on. In the first war the Aurors fought Voldemort's Death Eaters across Britain, and many of them died. After Voldemort's fall, four of his Death Eaters, Bellatrix Lestrange among them, tortured two of the best Aurors with the Cruciatus Curse. They wanted to know where their master had gone. The Aurors were Frank and Alice Longbottom.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eleven, Professor McGonagall warned Harry Potter about the Garou. She had once watched a very brave man, an Auror and a war hero, see one come round the corner of a barn. He dropped his wand and stood there weeping like a child.

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty, on the night of 6 June 1994, Ministry Aurors, Dawlish among them, came up to Professor Flitwick's office on the seventh floor. They were to take Sirius Black down to the dementors. By the time they opened the door, the room was empty. In Chapter Twenty-One Severus Snape named them to Cornelius Fudge as Dawlish and Williamson.

pages.title: Duelling Club
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
The Duelling Club was set up at Hogwarts by Gilderoy Lockhart in December 1992, with Professor Dumbledore's permission, to teach the pupils to defend themselves. Professor Snape was his assistant. Its first meeting ended with a snake in the Great Hall, and with the discovery that Harry Potter could speak to it.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, a notice about the club went up in the Entrance Hall. That evening Lockhart addressed the crowd in the Great Hall: 'Professor Dumbledore has been gracious enough to let me set up this little Duelling Club, so that I may train you all to protect yourselves, as I myself have had to do on more occasions than I could possibly count.'

To demonstrate, Snape cast the Disarming Charm at Lockhart, which blasted him clean off the end of the stage. Then the pupils paired off, and Harry duelled Dracina Malfoy. At the end of it, white-faced and swaying, she lifted her wand one last time. 'Fine,' she whispered. 'Fine. If you won't see... I'll show you.' She cried Serpensortia! A long black snake shot out of her wand. When it reared at Justin Finch-Fletchley, Harry spoke to it. It slumped to the floor, as limp as a coil of wet rope. He had spoken Parseltongue in front of everybody in the Great Hall.

In Book Two, Chapter Fifteen, Ernie Macmillan was still convinced that Harry had given himself away as the heir of Slytherin at the Duelling Club, and he told anyone who would listen. Harry had learnt something more useful there. In Chapter Eighteen he turned Snape's Disarming Charm on Lockhart himself, and blasted him backwards over his own trunk. 'Watched Snape do that one in the Duelling Club,' he said, through his teeth.

pages.title: Clan Tzimisce
infobox: The Eldest (Antediluvian); claimed destroyed by Lugoj Blood-Cursed, about 1413
Must rest with two handfuls of the earth of their homeland
None of note; the Old Clan keeps apart from every sect
The Eldest; the Dracon; Lugoj Blood-Cursed; Dracula; Vukodlak
pages.html:
The Tzimisce are the vampire clan of the Carpathians: the old lords of Transylvania, who shape living flesh and bone as though it were wax. The name has three syllables, not four. They are scholars and monsters both. An old law of hospitality binds them, as does the earth of their homelands. With the Lasombra they founded the Sabbat, which they lead still. Dracula is one of them.

The Eldest

The clan's founder, whom the Tzimisce call the Eldest, was one of the thirteen Antediluvians. He was Embraced in the First City about 9300 BC. After Cain departed into Nod he ruled in the Second City with the other founders, and when that city fell he went into the east. The Tzimisce say he held the lands about the Carpathians from the first nights of their history. He was a scholar, and what he studied above all was himself: he meant to remake his own body into something more than Cain's blood had left it.

In the Anarch Revolt, about 1413, the anarch Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed to have drunk the Eldest's blood and soul. Many Tzimisce doubt that he did. Some whisper that the Eldest still sleeps beneath the Carpathians, with his flesh grown out through the roots of the mountains. Others say the clan's gift for shaping flesh never came from Cain at all, but from Kupala, a demon said to lie bound beneath those same mountains.

Gift and curse

Vicissitude, the clan's own Discipline, lets a Tzimisce reshape flesh and bone, its own or anybody else's, as a sculptor works clay. With it a Tzimisce can make itself beautiful or monstrous. It can turn a servant into a living weapon, grow its own bones into blades or put on a great war-form. It can even divide itself into several bodies, so that when it is struck it does not fall down, but comes apart and walks off in several directions.

The clan has Animalism and Auspex as well. Its old sorcerers, the koldun, call on the spirits of earth, wind and water in the lands the clan holds. Other Kindred call the Tzimisce the Fiends, and do not mean it kindly.

Their curse ties them to the soil. A Tzimisce must rest each day with two handfuls of the earth of its homeland, or of the place where it was Embraced, or it loses its strength. Those who travel carry their native soil with them.

Voivodes and revenants

In their homelands the Tzimisce ruled as voivodes, lords of the land and of the people on it. Each held its domain as a mortal prince holds a kingdom. They Embrace scholars, nobles, priests of the old faiths and anybody else whose mind they think worth keeping. They test their childer hard.

Over the centuries they have bred whole families of born ghouls, the revenants, who serve them from birth; the Bratovich, the Grimaldi and the Obertus are among them. Their war-ghouls, the szlachta, are shaped for battle. Their greatest war-beast, the vozhd, is many bodies fused into a single enormous creature.

For all their cruelty they keep a strict code of hospitality. A guest under a Tzimisce's roof is safe there, whatever the host may privately think of him, and the clan holds that law sacred.

From the Second City to the Dark Ages

After the Second City fell, the Eldest's childer spread through the forests, mountains and plains of eastern Europe. In time they ruled the Slavic lands from the Carpathians northwards. In Constantinople the Dracon, a Tzimisce of the fourth generation, was one of the three who ruled the Kindred of that city, with the Toreador Michael and the Ventrue Antonius.

In the Middle Ages the Tzimisce voivodes held Transylvania and the lands around it. The Shadow Lords, a tribe of the Garou, fought them in those mountains for centuries. From the eleventh century the clan's great enemy was the Tremere, whose first vampiric blood had come from captured Tzimisce. From their fortress of Ceoris the Tremere fought the clan for Transylvania for generations, and they made gargoyles out of the Tzimisce they took.

The Revolt and the Sabbat

In the Anarch Revolt the clan's young rose against their voivodes more savagely than in any other clan, and Lugoj's claim against the Eldest came out of that rising. When the Convention of Thorns made peace in 1493, the Tzimisce anarchs refused it. They withdrew to the east and founded the Sabbat with the Lasombra.

Ever since, the Tzimisce have been the Sabbat's scholars, priests and shapers. They shape its war-ghouls and its monsters. They keep much of its ritual, and they stand beside the Lasombra at its head.

Some elders of the clan refused the Sabbat as firmly as they had refused the Camarilla. These are the Old Clan. They keep to their ancestral lands in the east, hold to the old ways and answer to no sect.

Dracula and the fourth generation

Vampires of the fourth and fifth generations are called Methuselahs. Very few Tzimisce are of the fourth, and Dracula is one of them. He was born Mathias Cronqvist. In 1094, through the Crimson Stone, he took the blood and soul of Walter Bernhard, who was Tzimisce. Mathias had been mortal, with no clan of his own, so he took Walter's. The Stone set him at the fourth generation, although Walter was no Antediluvian.

As Dracula, and in Wallachia as Vlad Tepes, he has risen from destruction roughly once a century ever since. His followers have worked time after time to bring him back, and the Belmont family has hunted him with the whip called the Vampire Killer. He has the clan's gifts and its curse. He rests, like any other Tzimisce, in the earth of his homeland. He is nominally allied with the Sabbat, but his deaths, his absences, his resurrections and his own designs make the alliance largely meaningless.

So few Kindred are of that blood that whoever really put down the cult of three hundred Dracula worshippers in red, which Gilderoy Lockhart claimed in 1992 to have defeated, met either Dracula himself or one of very few others. Minerva McGonagall's view was that one of the fourth generation is not killed with a wand at all, if one has any sense.

Later nights

Dracula's last return came in 1999. In the Demon Castle War Julius Belmont destroyed him for good, with Alucard beside him, and his castle was sealed inside a solar eclipse.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1992 Gilderoy Lockhart claimed to have defeated three hundred Dracula worshippers in red. Their leader, he said, was a Methuselah of the fourth generation, 'Clan Tzi-mi-see', a shapeshifter with bone and flesh like wax in his hands. He had come at Lockhart in the shape of a great wolf made out of men. Minerva McGonagall, standing near Harry Potter, murmured that it was Tzimisce, three syllables, not four. One did not kill one of the fourth generation with a wand held so, she said: 'Not with a wand at all, if one has any sense.'

Later that autumn Lockhart made Harry stand at the front of the class with his arms up, pretending to be one. Afterwards, in a window alcove, McGonagall told Harry that if he was asked to play a vampire again, he might tell Lockhart from her that a Tzimisce does not fall down when you hit it, but comes apart and walks off in several directions. Harry tried hard not to think about that. The knowing look she gave him then was one he saw on her face perhaps three times in two years.

pages.title: The Aurelian line
infobox: Darla (fifth), Angelus (sixth), Drusilla (seventh), William the Bloody (eighth)
pages.html:
