In Chapter Fourteen, in March 1994, Ron came out of Greenhouse Three grumbling about a Puffapod that had gone off in his face.

pages.title: Darla
aliases: The pale lady from the colonies
the pale lady from the colonies
infobox: The pale lady from the colonies
Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Welcome to the Hellmouth' (10 March 1997)
1609, in the Virginia colony, by the Master; sired again in 2000 by Drusilla
Fifth (unchanged by her second siring in 2000)
Young men with fair skin and dark hair, of confidence and drive
1997, by Angel; died again in 2001, giving birth to Connor
pages.html:
Darla is a vampire of the Aurelian line, a Ventrue of the fifth generation, sired by the Master in the Virginia colony in 1609. She was the pale lady from the colonies who sired Angelus in a Galway alley in 1753. For a century and a half the two of them were the terror of Europe. She was destroyed in 1997 and raised as a mortal woman in 2000, then sired again by Drusilla. In 2001, by a direct act of God, she bore Angel a living son, Connor. She died to give him life.

The colony, 1609

Her name before she was sired is not recorded. In 1609 she was a woman of the young English colony in Virginia, earning her living as a prostitute. She was dying of syphilis when the Master came to her deathbed in the guise of a priest. She asked him for salvation, and he gave her the only kind he had. She took the name Darla, and she has used no other since.

By the standards of her clan the choice was a scandal. The Ventrue sire their childer from among the powerful and the successful: princes, bankers, men of affairs. The Master sired his favourite from a dying prostitute in a colonial stockade. He never cared what the rest of the Ventrue thought of it. After him, neither did she.

The blood of the fifth generation

Every step away from Cain thins the blood. Darla stood only five steps from him, closer than all but a handful of the vampires walking the world in her century.

The blood of the fifth generation is the blood of the great elders. It mends what would destroy a younger vampire, and it holds more power than lesser blood can carry. No vampire of a later generation can bend her mind, though she can bend theirs.

Of the gifts of her clan she used Presence most. Men followed her into alleys without asking why. Vampires older in years than her childe stepped aside for her in the street. She had the Ventrue command of other minds, as well as the Ventrue endurance. In four centuries she seldom needed either for long.

One kind of blood

Like every Ventrue, Darla can feed from only one kind of mortal, and she would starve sooner than drink from anybody else. Hers is young men with fair skin and dark hair. They must be men of confidence and drive.

It is a very close description of Angelus. Her blood was bound to that kind from the night of her siring in 1609, more than a century before Liam of Galway was born. When she saw him outside a tavern in 1753, fair-skinned, dark-haired and sure of himself, she saw exactly what her blood had always wanted. She did not let him go.

The Order of Aurelius

For a century and a half she was the jewel of the Master's court, the priesthood of vampires called the Order of Aurelius. She hunted for him in the colonies as well as in the Old World.

In 1753, in Galway, she saw a handsome, drunken linen merchant's son outside a tavern. She beckoned him into an alley and sired him. He became Angelus.

In 1760 she brought him to London to be presented to the Master in his lair beneath the city. Angelus laughed at a lord of the night who lived in the sewers and called it piety. When he walked out, Darla went with him. The Master never forgave either of them.

The Scourge of Europe

For decades afterwards the two of them cut a path across Europe, he at the front and she beside him. In May 1764 they came to the house of the hunter Daniel Holtz in York while he was away. They killed his wife and infant son, then turned his daughter. Holtz pursued them across Europe for nine years. He never caught them.

Like the Master and Angelus, Darla was unaligned. She paid no attention to the Masquerade. Her line did more to endanger it than any other of its age. That is why the Camarilla, the sect her own clan leads, quietly paid for the hunters who chased her.

Angelus's childe Drusilla joined them about 1860, and Drusilla's childe William the Bloody in 1880. For some years the four of them were the most feared company of vampires in Europe.

The gift and the curse

In 1898, in Romania, Darla gave Angelus a girl of the Kalderash as a present. She was the clan's favourite daughter. For that the elders cursed him with a new soul.

When Darla found what he had become, she cast him out. Then she went to the clan's camp. She offered an elder the lives of his wife and daughters if the curse were taken back. It was not. While she argued, Drusilla and William went through the camp, killing everyone they found.

In 1900, in Beijing during the Boxer Rising, Angel found her again and asked to come back. She tested him with a baby taken from a missionary family. He could not kill it. He fled with it through a window, and she knew that Angelus was gone. She did not look for him again.

Sunnydale

In the twentieth century she returned to the Master, sealed since 1937 beneath Sunnydale in California, and served him while he waited to rise.

In 1997 a new Slayer, Buffy Summers, came to the town. Darla meant to kill her, and to wound Angel in doing it. Angel staked her in the Slayer's own house.

A second life

In 2000 the Los Angeles law firm Wolfram and Hart raised her from the dust as a mortal woman, meaning to use her against Angel. She came back with her old disease. Within weeks she was dying of it again.

When Drusilla sired her again in December 2000, Darla should by every rule of the blood have risen as Drusilla's childe. She would then have been of the eighth generation, three steps further from Cain than before. Because of the particular manner of her siring, she did not. Her blood came back to her as the Master had given it, of the fifth generation, and with it came the same hunger.

That winter the two of them went through Los Angeles together. Early in 2001 Angel set them both alight and left them to burn. They lived.

Connor

Early in 2001 Angel and Darla lay together, on a night of despair, not of happiness, so that the curse held. Months later she found that she was carrying his child.

By every law of the blood it could not be. Of all the Kindred, only the thin-blooded of the last generations can father or bear children. What they bear are dhampirs, half one thing and half the other. Angel was of the sixth generation and Darla of the fifth. Their blood was far too strong ever to bring forth a child.

It was an act of God: a direct intervention, a miracle, done for a purpose of His own. The child grew in her as a living human boy, not a dhampir, with a soul of his own. While she carried him his soul shone through her, so that Darla felt remorse for the first time since 1609.

A vampire's body could not deliver a living child. On a rainy night in November 2001, in an alley in Los Angeles, she staked herself. As she crumbled to dust the child was born alive. Angel named him Connor.

In the saga

Darla is the pale lady from the colonies in the account Hermione Granger read to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages in the autumn of 1993. She was the woman who beckoned Angelus into an alley in 1753, so that he was never alive again. Afterwards she went with him across Europe, through the years Hermione summed up in three words: 'Decades of blood.' The book does not name her.

pages.title: Kathy
infobox: Liam (Angelus), her brother; their father, a linen merchant
pages.html:
Kathy was the little sister of Liam of Galway, who became the vampire Angelus. In 1753 she saw her dead brother standing in the moonlight at the window, believed he had come back to her as an angel and let him in. He killed her with the rest of the household. It was from her mistake that he took his name.

The girl at the window

Kathy was the younger child of a Galway linen merchant. She adored her brother Liam, whatever their father thought of him. When Liam died in 1753, sired in an alley by Darla, she believed him safe in Heaven.

He came back to the house that same night and stood at the window in the moonlight. A vampire cannot cross the threshold of a home unless someone inside invites him in. Kathy, who thought her brother had returned to her as an angel, opened the door to him.

Her death

He killed the whole household, servants included, and Kathy with them. Their father he saved for last. No one was left alive to bury them.

The name Angelus comes from the angel she thought she saw.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1993 Hermione Granger told Harry Potter and Ron Weasley the story from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages. Her voice faltered when she came to the little sister who let him in, but she pressed on: 'She opened the door to an angel.' Her book does not give the girl's name.

pages.title: Angelus's father
pages.html:
Angelus's father was a linen merchant of Galway, a stern man who had long ago given up hoping for anything from his idle, drunken son, Liam. In 1753, on the night Liam was sired, the son came home and killed the whole household. He left his father until last.

The merchant of Galway

He did well out of linen. He kept a comfortable house in Galway with his wife, his son and a younger daughter, Kathy. He was a strict, God-fearing man, and he had always expected his son to follow him into the trade.

Liam had no intention of following anybody. He was handsome, idle and nearly always in drink. His father made no secret of what a disappointment he was. On a night in 1753 the two of them quarrelled for the last time, and the father turned his son out of the house. That same night, in an alley not far away, Darla sired him.

The last night

Liam's first act as a vampire was to go home. He killed the servants, his mother and his little sister. His father he kept for the end, so that the old man would have seen all the rest first. Nobody was left alive to bury them.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1993, on a stormy night in the Gryffindor common room, Hermione Granger told the story to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley, reading from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages. She whispered the worst of it: 'His father he saved for last, so he'd have seen all the rest.'

pages.title: Drusilla
infobox: The devout London witch; The devout witch of London

Angelus sire
William the Bloody childe
The Sight, which she had as a living witch
The frightened: only those truly afraid of her
pages.html:
Drusilla is a vampire of the Aurelian line, a Ventrue of the seventh generation. She was a devout, gentle London witch with a little of the Sight when Angelus destroyed her for sport, about 1860. He turned her on the day she took her holy orders, so that she would be mad for ever. She sired William the Bloody in 1880. In 1998 she killed a Slayer, and in 2000 she sired Darla, who had been her grandsire.

The London witch

Drusilla was a young woman of London in the middle of the nineteenth century, very devout and very gentle. She was a witch, with a little of the Sight. She took her visions for a curse, and she prayed to be rid of them.

When Angelus learned of her gift, he decided that killing her would be a waste. Instead he took everyone else. He killed her family one by one, slowly, in order, and he let her find them. Every door she ran to, he had been through first.

In the end she fled to a convent. On the day she took her holy orders he came through the chapel like a wolf through a fold. When there was nothing left of her mind but pieces, he turned her. The account of it ends with the words 'he did not make her mad. He made her mad eternal.'

The blood of the seventh generation

Drusilla's madness is not the curse of the Malkavians, whose blood drives every one of them out of their wits. Angelus put it into her while she still lived, and the blood fixed it there for ever.

Her Sight came through the turning with it. The blood of a vampire carries no gift of prophecy of its own. Hers was a witch's gift, and it survived her death.

Of the Ventrue gifts she uses Dominate above all. She has only to catch a mortal's eye and murmur. They stand still for her. She has used it to hold a Slayer motionless while she killed her.

Her power stops at older blood. The seventh generation cannot bend the minds of the sixth or the fifth, so Angelus and Darla were always beyond her reach.

One kind of blood

Like every Ventrue, Drusilla can feed from only one kind of mortal, and she would starve sooner than drink from anybody else. Hers is the frightened. She can drink only from someone who is truly afraid of her when she bites.

Angelus sired her out of terror, family by family, door by door, and her blood keeps the shape he gave it. She has never minded. She is very good at frightening people, and she takes her time about it.

The Sight

She speaks in riddles. She talks to the stars and to her dolls, of which the dearest is Miss Edith. She sees what is coming with uncomfortable accuracy.

She hears the stars sing, and they tell her things. What she foresees is true more often than not, though she seldom says it in a way anybody else can use.

William

In 1880, in London, she found a young man weeping in an alley. The woman he loved had scorned him at a party. He was William, a would-be poet. She saw what was in him and sired him. He became William the Bloody, called Spike, and for more than a century he was her devoted consort.

For some years the four of them travelled together: Darla, Angelus, Drusilla and William. In 1898 the Kalderash cursed Angelus with a soul. While Darla argued with an elder, Drusilla and William went through the clan's camp, killing everyone they found. In 1900 they were in Beijing during the Boxer Rising, where William killed his first Slayer.

Sunnydale

Shortly before 1997 a mob in Prague nearly destroyed her. William brought her, weakened, to Sunnydale in California. In November 1997 she was restored there with the blood of her own sire, Angel. The Ventrue restriction governs only the blood of mortals. The blood of another vampire lies outside it, and the blood of her sire was the strongest medicine her line could give her.

Early in 1998 she and William gathered the pieces of the Judge, a demon who burns the humanity out of the living. When Angel lost his soul that January, she welcomed Angelus home.

In May 1998 she caught the Slayer Kendra Young with her gaze. She held her still and cut her throat. She worked on the mind of the Watcher Rupert Giles until he saw the dead Jenny Calendar before him. Then he told her what Angelus wanted to know.

When Angelus was stopped, William took her away to Brazil. There, that autumn, she left him for a chaos demon.

Los Angeles

In December 2000, in Los Angeles, she sired Darla again. Darla had been her grandsire. By every rule of the blood Darla should have risen as Drusilla's childe, of the eighth generation. Because of the particular manner of her siring, her blood and her generation came back to her unchanged, of the fifth.

The two of them went through the city together that winter. Early in 2001 Angel set them both alight and left them to burn. They survived it. Drusilla left the city.

In the saga

In September 1992 Hermione Granger told Harry Potter of the things Angelus had done in London, including at a convent. In the autumn of 1993 she read the full account to Harry and Ron Weasley from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages. At the end of it she supposed that the girl was still a vampire: 'She's still... I mean, presumably she's still...' Then she shut the book on her finger, as though it had grown too hot. Her book does not name her.

In October 1993 Hermione sent away for a book on the convent, which arrived wrapped in brown paper with a Ministry stamp. She dreamed about convents all night after telling the story.

pages.title: The Romani clan's favourite daughter
aliases: the favourite daughter of the Kalderash
pages.html:
The favourite daughter of the Kalderash, an old and learned Romani clan of the Carpathians, was killed by Angelus in Romania in 1898. Her death led her clan's elders to curse him with a soul. That curse ended his career as the Scourge of Europe.

Her death

She was a young woman of the Kalderash, the girl her clan loved best. Darla brought her to Angelus in 1898 as a present, and he killed her.

By then he had a hundred and forty-five years of horrors behind him. She was one girl among his thousands of victims. She was also one girl too many.

The curse

Her elders did not hunt Angelus. They sat down around a fire and cursed him. The curse gave him a new soul.

Her name is not recorded in any of the accounts that have reached the wizarding world.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1993 Hermione Granger read her story to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages. The book calls her the clan's favourite daughter, and it records that the curse which followed caused Angelus to vanish from public life overnight. 'Just one girl,' Hermione said.

pages.title: Alucard
infobox: Dracula's son; Adrian Fahrenheit Tepes; Adrian; Genya Arikado
Adrian, in his father's castle in Wallachia, before 1450
None: he was born, not Embraced
Trevor Belmont, by the account of the Belmont chronicles
Sonia Belmont, Trevor Belmont, Sypha Belnades, Grant DaNasty, Richter Belmont, Maria Renard, Julius Belmont
pages.html:
Alucard, born Adrian, is the son of Dracula and the witch Lisa. He is a dhampir, half his father's kind and half not, who has spent more than five hundred years hunting his own father. By the laws of the blood no vampire of the fourth generation can father a child, and Kindred scholars count him an impossibility. He was born with a soul of his own, and he has never been Embraced. He loved Sonia Belmont in 1450, fought beside Trevor Belmont in 1476 and destroyed Dracula himself in 1797. In the Demon Castle War of 1999 he was at Julius Belmont's side.

Birth and name

Alucard was born Adrian, the son of Dracula and his second wife, Lisa. Lisa was a witch who had studied medicine, and she healed the sick of the villages below the castle. From his father the boy took long life, great strength and the powers of the night. From his mother he took a witch's gift for magic, and a conscience.

The Wallachian villagers who came to her for healing took her for a witch in the worst sense of the word, and they put her to death. Her last wish for her son was that he should not hate mankind for it. If he could not live among them, he was at least to do them no harm, because their lot was hard enough already. Dracula answered her death with war on the human race. His son took the other side. The name he chose, Alucard, is his father's name spelt backwards.

The impossible dhampir

The Kindred do not bring new life into the world. Among them only the thin-blooded, of the fifteenth generation and later, keep enough of the living body to father or bear a child. Their children are dhampirs: born alive, mortal in the end, with something of the vampire in them. By that rule Dracula could never have had a son. He is of the fourth generation, as far from the thin-blooded as any vampire walking. His blood came to him in 1094 through the Crimson Stone, which set him at the fourth generation against every ordinary rule of diablerie. Nothing about that blood has ever obeyed the rules, and Alucard is the proof of it.

He is a dhampir all the same, and he shows every mark of one. He was born, not Embraced, so he has no generation, no Beast and no clan. He has a soul of his own, which no vampire has. He needs no blood to live, and he will not drink it from the living. The sun does not destroy him. He knows the Kindred when he sees them, and they know him.

In everything else his father's blood makes him far more than an ordinary dhampir, whose span is a mortal's. He has lived more than five hundred years without growing old, with the strength and speed of the elders. He can take the shapes his father takes: a bat, a wolf, a drift of mist. He works a range of dark magic, and he is a master swordsman. The same blood is the reason he fears himself. Twice he has chosen to sleep for centuries rather than let what he inherited loose on the world.

Sonia

In 1450 Alucard met the young hunter Sonia Belmont, the first of her family to face his father as Dracula. The two came to love each other. Alucard meant to destroy his father himself, and he tried to keep her out of the fight. When they met in Dracula's castle he tested her with his sword, and she beat him. He left the fight to her, sealed away his own power and withdrew to rest. They parted in sorrow. The Belmont chronicles hold that her son Trevor was his.

If the chronicles are right, every Belmont since Trevor descends from Alucard, and so from Dracula. The family has spent five centuries hunting its own forefather with a whip. Trevor and his line are mortal. Whatever came down to them from Alucard has never shown.

The war of 1476

In 1476, when Dracula loosed his armies on Wallachia, Alucard woke. He joined Trevor Belmont, the sorceress Sypha Belnades and the pirate Grant DaNasty. He tested Trevor in combat first. Then he fought beside him through the castle to Dracula's throne, and the four of them destroyed Dracula together.

Afterwards Alucard chose to sleep. He sealed himself away so that his father's blood in him could do the world no harm.

The castle of 1797

He woke in 1797, when Dracula's castle reappeared a year after Richter Belmont had vanished. Inside, he found Richter installed as lord of the castle, under the control of the dark priest Shaft. With the help of Maria Renard he freed Richter and destroyed Shaft. Last of all he faced his father in the inverted castle that had risen above the first. Before Dracula fell, Alucard told him that Lisa had loved him, and that she forgave him. Then he went back into the dark to sleep again.

Dracula's servant Death had met him at the castle gate, warned him to turn back, then stripped him of the arms he carried. He went on without them. Maria Renard was wary of him at first. By the end she had come to love him, so when he walked away to his sleep she went after him. What passed between them is not recorded.

The Demon Castle War and after

In 1999 he fought again, beside Julius Belmont, in the Demon Castle War. Dracula was destroyed for good, and his castle was sealed inside a solar eclipse.

In 2035 and 2036 he went by the name Genya Arikado, in the service of the Japanese government. In that guise he watched over Soma Cruz, the young man in whom Dracula's power had been reborn. Soma refused his inheritance twice. Alucard, who had refused his own for nearly six hundred years, was there both times.

In the saga

In December 1993 Hermione Granger was planning her Christmas shopping for the Hogsmeade visit. She told Harry Potter and Ron Weasley that she meant to buy a book on Dracula's son Alucard at Tomes and Scrolls. The Hogwarts library's copy had pages missing, and somebody had cut the illustrations out. She explained that he was a dhampir, and that he had hunted his own father. Her feeling for Alucard, Harry noticed, was not quite the feeling she had for Angelus or for William the Bloody, but it was feeling enough.

pages.title: The Camarilla
infobox: 1435; confirmed at the Convention of Thorns, 1493
Elders including the Ventrue Hardestadt and the Toreador Rafael de Corazón
Brujah, Gangrel, Malkavian, Nosferatu, Toreador, Tremere, Ventrue; Caitiff tolerated
The Six Traditions, the first of them the Masquerade
The Inner Circle, meeting in Venice every thirteen years
Justicars and their Archons; in each city a Prince, primogen, sheriff, scourge, harpies and the keeper of Elysium
1900, with the Ministry of Magic and the other wizarding governments
pages.html:
The Camarilla, called by its enemies the Ivory Tower, is the closest thing vampires have to a government. It is a society of Kindred, founded in the fifteenth century to keep the Masquerade. It claims authority over every vampire in the world, and it rules most of the cities of the West through its Princes. Seven clans founded it. Most of the Kindred belong to it, or say they do. Since 1900 it has had an agreement with the wizarding governments of the world, the Ministry of Magic among them.

Founding

The Camarilla grew out of the convocation of elders of 1435. It was called while the Inquisition burned vampires across Europe, and while the young Kindred, whom their elders had so often left to the fires, rose against their sires in the Anarch Revolt. The Ventrue Hardestadt and the Toreador Rafael de Corazón were among its founders. The elders agreed that the Kindred must vanish from mortal sight. The Masquerade became the first law of the new society.

In 1493 the Convention of Thorns, at Thornbury in England, ended the revolt. Most of the anarchs accepted the Camarilla's terms and came into it. The Assamites, who had fought for the anarchs, were bound by a curse laid by the Tremere. Those who refused any peace with their elders went on to form the Sabbat.

Seven clans founded the Camarilla, and they remain its pillars. They are the Brujah, Gangrel, Malkavians, Nosferatu, Toreador, Tremere and Ventrue. The Ventrue have led it from the start. More of its cities have Ventrue Princes than Princes of any other clan. It accepts any vampire who keeps its laws, the clanless Caitiff among them, though it does not treat them as equals.

The Six Traditions

The Camarilla lives by six laws. In substance they are older than the sect itself, but it set them down as its own. The Masquerade forbids any vampire to reveal its nature to those not of the Blood. The Domain makes each Prince master of his city, and each elder master of what the Prince grants him. The Progeny forbids any vampire to sire a childe without the leave of the Prince. The Accounting makes a sire answerable for a childe until the childe is released. Hospitality obliges any vampire coming into a city to present itself to the Prince. Destruction reserves to the Prince alone, or to the Prince's elders, the right to destroy another of the Kindred.

A Prince may punish a breach as he pleases, from a public humbling to the blood hunt. Under a blood hunt any vampire in the city may destroy the offender, or drink its blood and soul. The Camarilla holds itself the heir of an older law of judgement among the Kindred, the Lextalionis.

Government

At the top of the Camarilla sits its Inner Circle, the eldest of each founding clan. It meets every thirteen years in Venice, and few Kindred could name its members. It appoints the Justicars, one from each clan, who judge breaches of the Traditions too great for any single Prince. A Justicar may summon a Conclave, a great gathering of all the Kindred who will come, to judge a Prince himself. Each Justicar commands Archons, who go where the Justicar cannot.

Each city is ruled by its Prince, who claims the city as his domain. Beside him stand the primogen, the eldest of each clan in the city, who advise him and sometimes depose him. A seneschal rules when he is away. A sheriff keeps order. A scourge hunts the thin-blooded and the unsanctioned. The harpies keep the city's gossip, and its reckoning of favours. Elysium is the neutral ground of a city, an opera house or a gallery or a museum. Violence is forbidden there, and the Kindred meet in peace.

The Camarilla's true currency is the boon, the favour owed. A boon may be trivial, minor or major. The greatest are the blood boon and the life boon, which can bind a vampire for centuries. Boons are bought, sold, called in and traded. The harpies record every one. A Kindred who will not pay what it owes soon finds that nobody will deal with it.

What the Camarilla believes

The Camarilla officially holds that Cain and the Antediluvians are legends. It holds that the Jyhad, the ancient war of the elders fought through their descendants, is a story told to frighten the young. Gehenna, the night when the Antediluvians are to rise and devour their children, will never come, it says. Many of its own elders know better. Cain was perfectly real. So is everything that came of his curse.

Angelus and the hunters

The Aurelian line answered to no sect. It flouted the Masquerade through the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The Camarilla often secretly supported or manipulated mortal vampire-hunters to bring Angelus down. Among them were the Society of Leopold and Leopold hunters such as Daniel Holtz. None of the hunters knew whose money it was. All of this came before the Camarilla's agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world.

The Sabbat and the anarchs

The Sabbat is the Camarilla's great enemy. It holds the Masquerade to be cowardice, and the elders, with the Antediluvians behind them, to be the true foe. The two sects have fought across the world for five centuries, in cities taken and lost. By the twentieth century the Sabbat held much of the eastern seaboard of the Americas, with Mexico. The Camarilla held most of Europe and the rest of North America.

Within the Camarilla itself, the anarchs are a standing argument. In 1944 the anarchs of Los Angeles, led by the Brujah, threw down the Toreador Prince Don Sebastian. They founded the Anarch Free States of California, which the Camarilla has never taken back.

The agreement of 1900

In 1900 the Camarilla came to terms with the wizarding governments of the world, meeting through the International Confederation of Wizards. The British Ministry of Magic was one of the parties. The wizards would lend the Camarilla their own concealment magic, to help it keep the Masquerade. This is the magic of their Statute of Secrecy: wards, Muggle-Repelling Charms and the like. It keeps Diagon Alley, Hogwarts and every wizarding house out of Muggle sight. In return no vampire who answers to the Camarilla would ever hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Ventrue elders very occasionally sit across a table from somebody at the Ministry, being polite about it. The agreement is old, and it is fragile. It has held, more or less, for most of the century, because both sides have more to lose than to gain by breaking it. The Sabbat, which never signed, has tried to break it more than once.

Later nights

Towards the end of the twentieth century the Camarilla began to lose its own. The Gangrel had never cared for its courts. In the late 1990s they withdrew from it, after their Justicar, Xaviar, came back from a meeting with an Antediluvian that the Inner Circle would not believe.

In the saga

Remus Lupin described the Camarilla and its agreement to Harry Potter's class in October 1993. 'About ninety years ago, give or take,' he told them, the Ministry and the Camarilla had come to an arrangement. When Parvati Patil asked whether that made them allies, he answered with something close to a growl. The Camarilla, he said, is on its own side. For the moment its side and the wizarding world happen to want the same thing, which is not the same as friendship.

A Camarilla vampire, he said, will very probably leave a witch or wizard alone, because it has promised to. A Sabbat vampire will not. Nobody can tell which is which until it is far too late to ask.

pages.title: Sabbat
infobox: From the anarchs who refused the Convention of Thorns, 1493
pages.html:
The Sabbat is the society of vampires that rejects the Camarilla, the Masquerade and the rule of the elders. It calls itself the Sword of Caine. It thinks the Masquerade cowardice and the Camarilla's agreement with the wizarding world worse. More than once in the twentieth century it has tried to break that agreement.

Origins

The Sabbat was born of the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century, when the young Lasombra and Tzimisce struck down the elders of their own clans. When the Convention of Thorns made peace in 1493, those among them who would not accept it withdrew to Spain and the east. There they became the Sabbat.

Its customs were set down later in the Code of Milan, in 1520. The Lasombra and the Tzimisce lead it still. It has members of most other clans as well: the antitribu, who have turned against their own clans' sects.

Beliefs

The Sabbat hold that the Kindred, whom they call Cainites, are above mortals and ought not to hide from them. They honour Cain as the Dark Father. They believe the Antediluvians still exist, and that they will rise at Gehenna to devour their descendants. The elders of the Camarilla, in the Sabbat's view, are the ancients' unwitting pawns. The Sabbat means to fight the Antediluvians when they come.

Instead of clinging to Humanity, many of its members follow Paths of Enlightenment, codes that accept the Beast.

Practice

The Sabbat is organised in packs, bound together by the Vaulderie. In this rite the packmates mix their blood in a chalice and drink it. It breaks every other blood bond, and binds them to one another instead. The sect is ruled by a Regent, with cardinals, archbishops and bishops beneath. Its military arm is the Black Hand.

In war the Sabbat sires vampires by the score. It digs the newly sired out of shallow graves and throws them at the enemy. Its strongholds are Mexico City, Montreal and the eastern seaboard of America, where it has fought the Camarilla for decades.

The end of the century

By the end of the century one faction of the Sabbat served the Tzimisce Methuselah Vukodlak, and meant to raise him. In 1999 his followers carried him to New York and hid him beneath the Cathedral of Flesh. Others of the sect fought them. Ecaterina the Wise, a Brujah elder who had become a Sabbat archbishop in New York, was one of them.

In the saga

Remus Lupin warned Harry Potter's class in October 1993 that the Sabbat never signed anything, and does not care who gets hurt while it tries to break the agreement. 'A Camarilla vampire will very probably leave you alone, because it has promised to,' he said. 'A Sabbat vampire will not. And you won't know which is which until it's far too late to ask.'

Dracula, a fourth-generation Tzimisce, is nominally allied with the Sabbat. His constant deaths, absences and resurrections make it a fairly empty distinction; so do his own purposes.

pages.title: Clan Malkavian
infobox: Auspex, Obfuscate, and Dominate or Dementation
pages.html:
The Malkavians are the clan of madness. Every Malkavian is mad, because the blood makes them so. The madness spreads, too: anyone who talks with one for long enough may come to see what the Malkavian sees. Seers and jesters, they are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla. In Remus Lupin's judgement they are also the clan most likely to catch a wizard out.

Malkav

The clan's founder, Malkav, was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, Embraced about 9300 BC in Enoch, the First City. He is remembered as the wisest of them, a prophet whose visions broke his mind. With the rest of the Third he rose against the Second Generation and slew it about 8990 BC. When Cain cursed the clans for it, about 8980 BC, he laid madness on Malkav and on every vampire of his line.

His childer hold that the madness is a gift as well as a curse. Through it, they say, their founder saw, and still sees, what is hidden from everybody else. What became of Malkav is not known. Many Malkavians insist that he is not gone at all, but sleeps somewhere and dreams through them. Some of them say that the voices they hear are his.

Gifts and curse

Malkavians see more than other Kindred. Auspex gives them heightened senses and second sight. Their insight often runs ahead of any sense at all: a Malkavian may know what a stranger dreamed last night, or what will happen at the end of the week. With Obfuscate they pass unnoticed through a crowd. They bend other minds too, some with Dominate and some with Dementation. Dementation is the clan's own power to unhinge others, waking buried fears and rages until the victim sees what the Malkavian sees.

Every Malkavian carries at least one madness that can never be cured. The Embrace either creates it or drags it up from wherever it was hiding. Some are mad the way a poltergeist is mad, and some the way a very clever man is mad who has seen something he should not. Nobody can tell which is which by looking. The other clans call them Lunatics, and treat even their jokes with care.

The madness spreads

The madness does not stay inside one head. The minds of the clan touch one another in a shared current of thought and dream, which the Malkavians call the Cobweb. Ideas, visions and delusions pass along it across great distances. A Malkavian may wake knowing something that a clanmate learnt on another continent.

The same current carries the madness out of the clan. If somebody talks with a Malkavian for long enough, really talks, and lets the Malkavian into their head, they start to see what the Malkavian sees. People have come out of a conversation with one and never been quite right again. The trouble is that a Malkavian seldom looks dangerous. The one to fear is likely to be a beautiful, charming, slightly odd person at a party, who seems to know things about others that nobody could possibly know.

Whom they Embrace

Malkavian sires choose their childer for reasons only they understand. Some choose the gifted and the visionary: poets, mystics, scientists, detectives. Some choose those already on the edge, the haunted and the inmates of asylums. Some choose people who seem entirely ordinary, and who stop being ordinary in the first nights after the Embrace. The clan has no hierarchy worth the name. Its members find one another, help one another and play elaborate jokes on everybody else. Some of those jokes have run for centuries.

Within the Camarilla they serve as seers and advisers. A prince who ignores a Malkavian's warning sometimes regrets it. They are tolerated because they are useful, and because nobody is quite sure what they would do if they were not.

History

After Cain departed into Nod, Malkav and his childer lived among the founders in the Second City as its prophets. When it fell they went out among mortals, as oracles and soothsayers in the ancient world. In the Middle Ages they were holy fools, prophets, wandering preachers and hermits. The Inquisition found them hard to tell from mortal lunatics, and easy to burn. Anatole, a Malkavian mystic of those centuries, preached his visions of God and the damned to any Kindred who would listen. In those nights the whole clan used Dementation.

Young Malkavians joined the Anarch Revolt, though nobody could ever be sure on whose side. At the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the clan became one of the founders of the Camarilla. It has stayed there since, valued for its insight and feared for its jokes. After the Convention the Malkavians of the Camarilla began to use Dominate where their forebears had used Dementation. The change has never been explained to anybody's satisfaction. Those of the clan who went over to the Sabbat kept Dementation. These Malkavian antitribu are, if anything, madder, and the Sabbat sets them loose on its enemies more readily than it trusts them.

Malkavians and wizards

Under the Camarilla's agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world, no Malkavian who answers to the Camarilla may hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard. The agreement says nothing about conversation. A Malkavian needs neither fangs nor the blood bond to ruin a mind. It needs only to be listened to. Wizards who know the Kindred are taught that the best defence against the clan is to make their excuses, early.

The madness of the clan is not the only madness among vampires. Drusilla of the Aurelian line, the most famously mad vampire of the last two centuries, is a Ventrue. Angelus drove her mad while she still lived. Her Sight was a witch's gift, and it survived her turning. At least one wizarding family has had cause to study the Malkavians closely: Neville Longbottom learnt a good deal about them for what he called a family matter.

Count Fangula

Not every Malkavian is dangerous. Count Fangula, an old vampire of the clan, lives at Hillhurst Mansion, outside the American town of Charterville. His madness long ago turned harmless: he believes himself a vampire of the stage sort, cape and all. The Camarilla leaves him where he is, because nobody who meets him comes away believing in vampires. In November 1996 two boys spent an evening in his company. They came away believing that they were vampires themselves, which wore off.

Later nights

In the last years of the century Dementation returned to the Malkavians of the Camarilla. It spread through the Cobweb from one mind to the next. Before long few of the clan's Camarilla members used Dominate at all, and the clan's Disciplines were once again what they had been in the Dark Ages.

In the saga

In October 1993 Remus Lupin told Harry Potter's class to remember this clan above all: 'Every Malkavian is mad. All of them. The blood makes them so.' People had come out of a conversation with one, he said, and never been quite right again. Anyone who met a beautiful, charming, slightly odd person at a party who seemed to know things they could not possibly know should make their excuses, early. Neville Longbottom pointed out that Professor Trelawney said the same of herself, to general laughter, and Lupin assured him that Professor Trelawney had a perfectly good pulse.

Neville knows a good deal about the Malkavians. In the spring of 1994, when Harry mentioned an essay on 'the mad ones', Neville supplied the name at once and offered to help, explaining that he had studied them a while before for what he called a family matter.

pages.title: Garou tribes
infobox: Older than Hogwarts and older than wands
pages.html:
The Garou run in packs, and the packs hold to tribes, of which there are thirteen. The tribes are older than Hogwarts and older than wands. Each has its own totem spirit, its own Kinfolk, its own homelands and its own ways. Together they keep the Litany, and they bow to no Ministry. A fourteenth tribe went over whole to the Wyrm.

History

The Garou say they were once a single people. The tribes grew apart in the ages after the ice, each following its own totem and its own Kinfolk across the world. When the Impergium ended at the Concord, the tribes agreed to the Litany as their common law. They have quarrelled ever since over leadership, over territory and over the right way to fight the Wyrm. Some old wrongs are not forgotten, such as the Viking raids that set the Get of Fenris against the Fianna, or the coming of the European Garou to the lands of the Wendigo and the Uktena. Together the tribes are called the Garou Nation, though they seldom act as one.

There were fourteen tribes once. One went over, every man, woman and whelp of it, down into the dark. It serves the very thing the other thirteen were whelped to fight. Its members are the Black Spiral Dancers.

The thirteen

The Black Furies, under Pegasus, are a tribe of women from Greece and the lands about the Black Sea. They avenge wronged women and guard the wild places. The Bone Gnawers, under Rat, are the tribe of the streets, the poor and the outcast. The Children of Gaia, under Unicorn, are healers and peacemakers who led the call to end the Impergium. The Fianna, under Stag, are the tribe of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, bards as much as warriors. The Get of Fenris, under the great wolf Fenris, are the fierce warriors of Scandinavia and the German lands.

The Glass Walkers, under Cockroach, are the tribe of cities, machines and commerce. The Red Talons, under Griffin, are born only to wolves, and would sooner see mankind culled again. The Shadow Lords, under Grandfather Thunder, are the ambitious tribe of the Carpathians and the Balkans. The Silent Striders, under Owl, are wanderers and messengers, exiled long ago from their homeland in Egypt. The Silver Fangs, under Falcon, are the royal tribe, the traditional leaders of the Garou. The Stargazers, under Chimera, are the philosophers of the Garou, mystics of the Himalayas and the East. The Uktena, under the great horned serpent Uktena, and the Wendigo, under the spirit of the cold north wind, are the Pure Ones, the native tribes of North America.

In the saga

Severus Snape told the Hogwarts third years in November 1993 that there are thirteen tribes and that they keep their own law. A fourteenth, he said, went over whole, and dances a spiral. In June 1994 Remus Lupin told Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger that the pack he had joined in the hills of mid-Wales was mostly Fianna, one of the thirteen tribes.

pages.title: Black Spiral Dancers
infobox: The White Howlers of Scotland, under Lion
Hives, the corrupted caerns of the Wyrm
Black fur; the dance of the spiral
pages.html:
The Black Spiral Dancers are the fourteenth tribe of the Garou, the one that went over. Every man, woman and whelp of it went down into the dark. It now serves the very thing the other thirteen were whelped to fight: the Wyrm, whom Scripture calls Satan and the elder days called Morgoth.

The fall

Before their fall they were the White Howlers, the Garou of Scotland. Their Kinfolk were the Picts, and their totem was Lion. They were a proud, fierce tribe. In the days when the Picts held the north, they went down into the caverns beneath their own land to carry the war to the Wyrm in its lair. There they found the Black Spiral, a labyrinth of the Wyrm's making, and danced it. It turned their minds inside out. What came back up out of the earth was no longer a tribe of Gaia, but a tribe of the Wyrm.

They did not go over to an idea. The thing they serve is the oldest enemy there is, the one whose rebellion began dark magic, and they have been in his service ever since.

Ways

The Dancers take their name from the rite at the heart of the tribe. Every one of them must dance the Black Spiral, a winding path through the Wyrm's realm that teaches a new lesson of corruption at every turn. Each of them comes out of it mad, and bound to him. Their totem is Whippoorwill, a spirit that guided their ancestors through the labyrinth. They are often black of fur, and they are given to dancing.

They make their homes in Hives, caerns they have poisoned and given to the Wyrm. These often lie beneath polluted ground, old mines or waste.

The Litany means nothing to them. They breed metis freely, and many of them are twisted in body as well as in mind. They also make others by the bite, which the other tribes forbid, and they are extremely particular in their choosing. Among them the biteborn, so rare in the thirteen tribes, are common. Their get are still abroad. They hunt for the lost cubs of the other tribes, hoping to find them before their own people do.

Place in the world

Every other Garou is sworn to kill a Black Spiral Dancer on sight, and the Dancers return the hatred in full. They are found wherever the Wyrm is strong, in every land where Garou live. To wizards and Muggles alike they are the worst of all werewolves, though few who meet one remember it.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1992 Minerva McGonagall warned Harry Potter that if a Garou has black fur and is dancing, he should run faster, because some of them have gone over to the other side, like people.

In November 1993 Severus Snape told the Hogwarts third years that there had been fourteen tribes. One had gone over whole into the dark. Its members dance a spiral, he said. 'Their get are still abroad, still making others by the bite, still extremely particular in their choosing.'

pages.title: Kalderash clan
aliases: The Romani clan of the Carpathians
the Romani clan of the Carpathians
infobox: Romani clan of the Carpathians; The Romani clan of the Carpathians
pages.html:
The Kalderash are a very old Romani clan, learned in curse-work, who travelled the Carpathians. In 1898 Angelus killed their favourite daughter. Their elders cursed him with a new soul, by a binding the Ministry of Magic has never reconstructed.

The curse of 1898

The clan's elders knew bindings beyond the reach of wizarding scholarship. In 1898, in Romania, Angelus killed a girl of theirs, the favourite daughter of the clan. He had a century and a half of horrors behind him by then.

The elders did not hunt him. They did not stake him. They sat down around a fire and cursed him.

The curse gave him a soul. It was not his old soul, which vampirism had destroyed, but a new one. The magic that gave it came from the same root as the working by which the monks guarding the Key later made it into a living girl, Dawn Summers. The Beast remained in him.

The clan meant the soul as vengeance, so that he would suffer for every crime he had committed. The curse carried a condition as well: one moment of true happiness would take the soul from him and bring Angelus back. He vanished overnight. The most feared creature in Europe was never seen again in the old way.

The curse was Romani witchcraft: wizarding magic as the tribes teach it, by word of mouth and never in writing. That is why the Ministry of Magic has never been able to reconstruct it.

The price

The clan paid for its vengeance. When Darla learned what had become of Angelus, she came to the Kalderash camp to demand that the curse be taken back. It was not. While she argued with an elder, Drusilla and William the Bloody went through the camp, killing everyone they found.

Later history

The clan did not forget him. In 1997 a young woman of the Kalderash, Janna, was living in Sunnydale, California, as the computer teacher Jenny Calendar. The clan's elders had sent her to watch him. Her uncle, Enyos, came to hold her to the task.

When the curse broke in January 1998, Angelus killed them both. Jenny's translation of the ritual survived her. The witch Willow Rosenberg used it that spring to restore the curse.

In the saga

In the autumn of 1993 Hermione Granger read the story to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages. The book describes the clan respectfully, as Hermione pointed out, and it admits that no one knows what the curse was. Ron's verdict was 'Good for them.'

pages.title: Messrs Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot and Prongs
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
Purveyors of Aids to Magical Mischief-Makers
pages.html:
Messrs Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot and Prongs is the style in which the four makers of the Marauder's Map signed their work. They called themselves Purveyors of Aids to Magical Mischief-Makers. Behind the nicknames were four Gryffindors of the 1970s: Remus Lupin, Peter Pettigrew, Sirius Black and James Potter.

The signature

When a wand touches the blank parchment and the oath is spoken, 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good', the four names bloom across the top in great curling green letters. Beneath them the four are proud to present the Marauder's Map. Anybody who tries to make the map give itself up without the oath gets insults instead, each one signed by one of its makers.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Ten, Fred and George Weasley gave Harry Potter the map. They had taken it in their first year from a drawer in Filch's filing cabinet marked Confiscated and Highly Dangerous. George woke it with the oath, and the four names came up across the top.

In Chapter Fourteen Professor Snape tried to force the map to give up its secrets. It answered him with four insults instead, signed in turn by Mr Moony, Mr Prongs, Mr Padfoot and Mr Wormtail, the last of whom advised him to wash his hair.

pages.title: Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
The Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures
pages.html:
The Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures is the body of the Ministry of Magic that decides whether a dangerous beast is to be destroyed. It keeps offices in London, with its own executioner, Walden Macnair. In 1994 it condemned the hippogriff Buckbeak to death, because its members were frightened of Lucius Malfoy.

The Committee

A creature referred to the Committee is given a hearing, at which its keeper must appear with it. If the creature is condemned there may be an appeal. A member of the Committee then goes with the executioner to see the sentence carried out. Its old cases include a manticore of 1296 that was cleared of savaging a woodcutter, but only because the Committee could not find anybody willing to fetch it in.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eleven, the school governors cleared Hagrid of blame for the hippogriff's attack on Dracina Malfoy. They upheld Lucius Malfoy's complaint against the creature all the same, and referred it to the Committee. A hearing was set for 20 April 1994 at the Committee's offices in London. Hagrid had no hope at all: 'Them Disposal devils, the lot of 'em, they're all in Lucius Malfoy's pocket!'

Lucius had the hearing brought forward from 20 April to the Friday after the Ravenclaw match. In Book Three, Chapter Fifteen, he stood up before a roomful of doddery old wizards to say his bit, after which the Committee did just as he told them. Hermione Granger said it plainly: 'They're a bunch of doddery old fools, and they were scared.' Hagrid agreed: 'That Committee's in Lucius Malfoy's pocket.'

In Book Three, Chapter Sixteen, the Committee came to Hogwarts for the appeal on 6 June 1994, and brought its executioner. On the castle steps Cornelius Fudge, the Minister for Magic, told Harry Potter: 'The Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures required a witness to the execution of a mad hippogriff.' Two more wizards came out behind him. One was so old that he seemed to be shrivelling as Harry watched. The other was Macnair, running his thumb along the edge of his axe. The appeal was lost that afternoon.

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty, Fudge read out the sentence inside Hagrid's cabin. The hippogriff Buckbeak, 'hereafter called the condemned', was to be beheaded on the sixth of June at sundown, by the Committee's appointed executioner, Walden Macnair. Out in the pumpkin patch Macnair's axe came whistling down through the space where Buckbeak's neck had been a second before, and buried itself in a tree. A hooded rider swung up on to the hippogriff's back, and Buckbeak was away into the red evening sky. The rider was Dracina Malfoy. The old Committee member sat down rather suddenly on an upturned bucket and fanned himself with his hat.

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-Two, Harry learnt why the Committee had come down on Hagrid like a ton of bricks. It had acted on the strength of the four pages Dracina had written to her father about Buckbeak in the autumn, and never sent. Pansy Parkinson had found the letter and sent it herself, to be helpful.

pages.title: Magical Law Enforcement Squad
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
The Department of Magical Law Enforcement
pages.html:
The Magical Law Enforcement Squad is the wizarding police force of the Ministry of Magic, whose trained fighters are called Hit Wizards. In November 1981 twenty of its members took Sirius Black.

The Squad

The Squad deals with lawbreaking witches and wizards in general, while the Aurors hunt the Dark wizards. Its Hit Wizards are trained to face a cornered wizard and to win.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Ten, on the last weekend of term before Christmas 1993, Cornelius Fudge sat in the Three Broomsticks with Hagrid and Madam Rosmerta, talking about Sirius Black. Hagrid growled that he would have ripped Black limb from limb. Fudge cut him short: 'No one but a trained Hit Wizard from the Magical Law Enforcement Squad would have lasted a minute against Black once he was cornered.' Black, he said, had been taken off by twenty members of the Squad. Harry Potter heard every word from under the table.

pages.title: Colin Creevey's fan club
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Eight or nine younger pupils, among them Ginny Weasley
Round and red, with HP in gold letters
pages.html:
Colin Creevey's fan club is a band of Harry Potter's admirers among the younger Gryffindors. In 1993 it had eight or nine members, Ginny Weasley among them, and every one of them wore a round red badge with HP on it in gold letters.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eight, on Hallowe'en 1993, Harry stayed behind in the castle while the rest of the third years went to Hogsmeade. Colin found him in the common room. Behind him by the fire sat eight or nine younger Gryffindors, every one of them wearing a red HP badge. Ginny had gone scarlet, trying to hide hers behind her hand.

Colin asked Harry to come and sit with them. Harry pleaded homework in the library. The truth was that he was not in the mood for nine people staring at the scar on his forehead all afternoon. When Colin's face fell, Harry told him that he could never have sorted out the Basilisk without him, and that Ginny could tell him all about it. He left the whole fan club turning round as one to stare at Ginny.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Four: by August 1994 Harry had heard that Colin and Ginny Weasley were closer than ever, thanks to the fan club with its round red badges. Ginny still went scarlet whenever Harry grinned at her.

pages.title: The Masquerade
infobox: The Camarilla, as the first of its Six Traditions
Princes, sheriffs and scourges; the Justicars and their Archons
Final Death, often by blood hunt
The Sabbat, which keeps a secrecy of its own all the same
The International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy, by the agreement of 1900
pages.html:
The Masquerade is the vampires' law of secrecy, and the first of the Six Traditions of the Camarilla. No vampire may reveal its true nature to those who are not of the Blood; any who does forfeits every claim the Blood gives it. The law has been in force since 1435. It has made the Kindred a legend, a story that mortals tell and do not believe. A vampire who breaks it is hunted down by its own kind and destroyed. As Remus Lupin put it, they are far less gentle about it than the Obliviators. Some wizards say the Statute of Secrecy was inspired by it, and since 1900 the wizarding world has helped to keep it.

The law

The First Tradition says, in substance, that no Kindred shall reveal its true nature to those not of the Blood, and that whoever does so renounces its claims of the Blood. It is the first of six. The others are the Domain, the Progeny, the Accounting, Hospitality and Destruction. Every Camarilla vampire learns that the Masquerade comes first for a reason. The other five govern how the Kindred live with one another, but the Masquerade is what lets them live at all.

The Burning Times

For most of their history the Kindred ruled more or less in the open, as the princes of the night in the cities of the ancient and medieval world. That ended with the Inquisition. From the thirteenth century the Church's hunters burned witches and heretics across Europe. They burned vampires too, by the hundred. The elders who had ruled in the open learnt how quickly faith and fire can bring down a creature of the night. In the same years the young Kindred rose against their sires in the Anarch Revolt, for their elders had often left them to burn in their place.

In 1435 elders of several clans met in convocation, among them the Ventrue Hardestadt and the Toreador Rafael de Corazón. They agreed that the Kindred must vanish from mortal sight and become a legend. From that agreement grew the Camarilla, and the Masquerade became its first law. In 1493, at the Convention of Thorns in England, most of the anarchs accepted the Camarilla's terms, and the Masquerade with them. Those who would not went on to form the Sabbat.

Enforcement

In each city the Prince enforces the Masquerade, with a sheriff to keep order. A scourge destroys the thin-blooded and the unsanctioned who endanger it. A Kindred whose breach is grave enough is declared outlaw in a blood hunt. Any vampire in the city may then destroy it, or drink its blood and soul.

Above the Princes stand the Justicars, appointed by the Camarilla's Inner Circle. They judge the worst breaches and summon Conclaves. Their Archons carry out their orders across the world.

Mortals who see too much are not usually killed, since a death draws attention of its own. They are made to forget.

Keeping it

Under the Masquerade a vampire does not look like a vampire. It looks like a lawyer, or a nurse, or a pleasant young man at a party who is very interested in where you live. It feeds without killing where it can. The Kiss of a vampire's bite brings the victim a pleasure that clouds the memory, and a lick of the tongue closes the wound.

Its powers serve the secret as much as the hunt. Dominate can take a night out of a mortal's memory and put another in its place. Obfuscate can make a vampire unseen in a crowded room. Ghouls, mortals kept on vampire blood, carry on its business by day.

Every clan plays its part. The Ventrue manage the money and the influence that buy silence. The Toreador move through mortal society without a hair out of place. The Nosferatu, who could never pass for human, keep to the sewers and trade in everybody's secrets. The Tremere guard their chantries with wards.

The Kindred have even learnt to use mortal fiction, since the more stories mortals tell about vampires, the less they believe in them. When an Irish novelist put Dracula into a book in 1897, the most famous vampire in the world became, for nearly everybody, a character in a novel.

The sects

The Sabbat calls the Masquerade cowardice, and thinks it a disgrace that the Kindred should hide from the cattle. All the same it keeps a secrecy of its own, out of necessity rather than law, because the fires that burned the Camarilla's elders would burn the Sabbat's just as well. The independent clans, the Assamites, the Followers of Set, the Giovanni and the Ravnos, keep the Masquerade for the same reason, though they owe the Camarilla nothing.

Breaches

The Aurelian line answered to no sect, and it ignored the Masquerade openly throughout its reign of terror. Angelus cut crosses into his victims' cheeks, and it was in all the broadsheets of the day. The Camarilla answered by secretly backing mortal hunters against him. Among them were the Society of Leopold, the heir of the Inquisition, and Leopold hunters such as Daniel Holtz. None of them knew whose money they were spending.

Dracula broke the Masquerade at every one of his returns, roughly once a century, with armies, castles and open war on the villages of Wallachia. The Camarilla has been content to leave him to the Belmonts.

The modern nights

The twentieth century has made the Masquerade harder to keep and, in one way, easier. Cameras, film and computers can catch what no witness would be believed about. The Society of Leopold has never stopped looking, and neither have the other hunters. Since the coming of the costumed heroes in 1938, however, mortals who see something impossible have a ready explanation: a metahuman, a mutant, a stunt. In a world where men fly, a stranger with fangs is easily taken for one more freak.

In Sunnydale, California, the town built over the Hellmouth, the Masquerade has been kept for decades less by the vampires than by the townspeople. They have become expert at not seeing what is in front of them.

The wizarding world

Some wizards say that the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy, recognised in 1692, was inspired by the Masquerade. In 1900 the wizarding governments of the world, meeting through the International Confederation of Wizards, came to terms with the Camarilla. The British Ministry of Magic was one of the parties.

The wizards agreed to lend the Camarilla their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade. These are the enchantments that hide Diagon Alley, Hogwarts and every wizarding house. In return, no vampire who answers to the Camarilla would hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard. The arrangement has held, more or less, for most of the century, mainly because both sides have more to lose than to gain by breaking it. The Sabbat never signed it, and has tried more than once to break it.

In the saga

Remus Lupin taught the Masquerade to Harry Potter's class in the second week of October 1993, as the first thing to understand about vampires: that they hide, just as wizards do. The danger, he told them, lies not in the thing in the cellar but in the nice young man.

pages.title: The Beast
infobox: Hunger, frenzy, the red fear of fire and sunlight
pages.html:
The Beast is the endless wanting that fills a vampire in place of the soul that was destroyed when it was sired. Whatever a vampire was before, however good or kind, it spends every night of its existence holding the Beast down. Most vampires lose, in the end.

Nature

When vampirism destroys a soul, something has to fill the place where it was. What fills it is the Beast, a hunger that never stops wanting. It drives a vampire to feed, to kill and to rage. Three things wake it most readily: hunger, anger and fear. When it breaks loose in a frenzy, the vampire acts as an animal would, careless of the Masquerade and of everybody it loves. Fire and sunlight wake its terror, which the Kindred call the Rötschreck, the red fear.

Most Kindred hold it back by clinging to what remains of their Humanity, the habits and scruples of the living. Every cruelty wears a little of it away. A vampire that loses the last of its Humanity becomes the Beast entirely, and the Kindred call that final frenzy the Wassail.

Many of the Sabbat follow Paths of Enlightenment instead, codes that accept the Beast and try to master it. Old tales tell of Golconda, a state in which a vampire is at peace with its Beast. Few are said to have reached it, and many doubt that it exists at all.

The Dementor's Kiss

The same vacancy can come about by another road. A soul taken by a Dementor's Kiss is gone for good. Its place in the living body has to be filled by something, and what fills it is never the victim's own: a beast of the sort a vampire carries, or one or two other things.

In the saga

Remus Lupin named the Beast to Harry Potter's class in October 1993, when Hermione Granger asked whether a vampire could be good. 'Vampirism destroys the soul,' he said, and he told them what fills it. Early in 1994, during their Patronus lessons, he told Harry that the Kiss leaves the same kind of vacancy. Angelus, given a new soul by the Kalderash in 1898, still carries his Beast. If he ever knows a moment of true happiness, the soul will go, and Angelus will be back.

pages.title: Blood bond
infobox: Drinking one vampire's blood three times
pages.html:
The blood bond is the hold a vampire gains over anybody who drinks its blood. Anyone who drinks a few drops from the same vampire three times will love it for the rest of their life, whether they want to or not, and will never know the difference.

How it works

The three drinks must be taken on three separate nights. After the first, the drinker feels drawn to the vampire. After the second, the pull is hard to resist. After the third, the bond is complete: the drinker is a thrall, and the vampire is the regnant. Vampires bind their ghouls, their servants and one another with it.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eight, at the end of a lesson on vampires in 1993, Remus Lupin warned his third-years about it. ‘They call it the blood bond. It’s the cruellest thing they do.’

pages.title: Garou moon signs
pages.html:
The moon is not the Garou's cage but their birth sign. The phase under which a Garou is whelped, its auspice, fixes its role for the whole of its life. The Garou hold to it as gravely as Hogwarts holds to its Houses.

The five auspices

Ragabash, born under the new moon, are tricksters and questioners. They lie, steal and mock their own chieftains. They are permitted to, because a people at war needs somebody to test its leaders and its customs.

Theurges, born under the crescent, deal with spirits. They are the seers and mystics of the Garou. They walk in the spirit world, bind spirits and learn their secrets. They go where others cannot follow.

Philodox, born under the half moon, are judges. Balanced between the dark and the full, they keep the Litany. They settle disputes, hear challenges and weigh the guilt of those who break the law.

Galliards, born under the gibbous moon, keep every history their people have, and they keep it in song. They commit nothing to paper that a Ministry might one day read. They are the storytellers of the Garou, their howlers and the keepers of their lore.

Ahroun, born under the full moon, are warriors and nothing else. They carry more rage than any other Garou. They are the ones a traveller had better pray never to meet on a lane after dark.

The moon and the tide

The moon makes a wolf of nobody. What it does is raise the tide of rage, so that on the nights about the full every Garou is harder to hold, whatever its birth sign. That is the whole grain of truth in what wizards believe about werewolves at the full moon, and the Ministry has built a Registry upon it. The Garou honour the moon as Luna, Gaia's companion. They mark their signs with simple glyphs of its phases.

A Garou's auspice is quite separate from its tribe. A child may be born under any moon in any tribe, so that every tribe has its tricksters, its judges and its warriors.

In the saga

Severus Snape set out the five signs for the Hogwarts third years in November 1993. He warned Dean Thomas that the moon is a birth sign, not a cage. Remus Lupin's battered case carries a birth-sign mark, scratched into the leather long ago with the point of a knife: a crescent lying on its back, with three short strokes beneath it. The crescent is the sign of those who deal with spirits. Harry Potter saw the mark on the Hogwarts Express in September 1993, without knowing what it meant.

pages.title: Garou rage
infobox: On the nights about the full moon, and in the full-moon born
pages.html:
Every Garou carries a rage from birth. It is not a temper but a substance, like the fire in a lamp. A Garou's whole life is the keeping of that lamp, and when it spills, what is left standing afterwards is a matter of chance.

Nature

Rage is what drives a Garou to change and to fight. It rises at the scent of the Wyrm. It is harder to hold on the nights about the full moon, when the tide rises in every Garou, and the Ahroun, born under the full moon, carry the most of it. When rage overwhelms a Garou, the result is frenzy. Frenzy takes one of two forms: a blind killing fury, or a headlong flight like a hunted animal's. A Garou in frenzy may strike its friends as readily as its foes.

People and animals sense a Garou's rage without knowing what it is they sense. They grow uneasy, keep their distance and distrust it for no reason they can name. Many Garou grow up lonely because of it, even before their First Change.

Keeping the lamp

Garou keep their rage by discipline, by the company of their pack and by the Litany. Remus Lupin keeps his by faith: it is how he bears being Garou. The Wolfsbane Potion that Severus Snape brewed for him at Hogwarts held back his war form, though only just. Even with the potion, the compulsion never truly goes away.

Lupin's rage shows in small things. A sound like the bottom note of a church organ comes from his chest. Lamp flames shrink to blue beads. His nails lengthen, and wood creaks or splinters under his hands. It is worst when the Wyrm comes near the conversation: a dementor, Snape's left arm, the name of Lord Voldemort, or Cain.

In the saga

Snape described the rage to the third years in November 1993. Harry Potter heard Lupin's growl many times in his third year: on the Hogwarts Express when a dementor came to the door, over Snape's smoking goblet, over the word Garou, and whenever dark things were discussed. In Snape's office in early 1994 Lupin splintered a chair when Snape mocked him. In June 1994 he spent an hour chained to Peter Pettigrew, who reeked of the Wyrm, with no potion in him. Under the full moon his rage broke.

pages.title: Secret-Keeper
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
Peter Pettigrew, in place of Sirius Black
pages.html:
A Secret-Keeper is the person who holds a secret hidden by the Fidelius Charm. The charm hides the secret inside a single living soul, and nobody can find what it conceals unless the Secret-Keeper chooses to tell them.

The Potters' Secret-Keeper

In 1981, with Lord Voldemort hunting them, James and Lily Potter hid their house at Godric's Hollow under the Fidelius Charm. Everybody believed they had made Sirius Black their Secret-Keeper. At the last moment, as a bluff, they changed to Peter Pettigrew instead. Pettigrew betrayed them to Voldemort, who killed them on Hallowe'en. Black was blamed, and spent twelve years in Azkaban without a trial.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Ten, in the Three Broomsticks shortly before Christmas 1993, Harry Potter overheard Professor Flitwick explain the Fidelius Charm and its Secret-Keeper to Madam Rosmerta. He learnt that Dumbledore had offered to be the Potters' Secret-Keeper himself, and that everybody believed they had chosen Sirius Black. In Book Three, Chapter Twelve, he still carried what he had overheard, though he had told nobody but Ron and Hermione.

In Book Three, Chapter Eighteen, in the Shrieking Shack, Black told him that he had persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter Pettigrew at the last moment. Then he turned on Pettigrew: ‘I thought it was the perfect plan... a bluff...’

pages.title: Gamp's Law
infobox: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (21 July 2007)
Five, of which food is the first
pages.html:
Gamp's Law of Elemental Transfiguration sets out what Transfiguration cannot do. Its five principal exceptions are things that cannot be conjured out of nothing, and the first of them is food.

Food

A witch can summon food if she knows where it is, she can transform it, and she can make more of what she already has. She cannot produce a meal out of thin air.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eight, in the autumn of 1993, Professor McGonagall set her third-years to read about it in their Transfiguration lesson: ‘Page forty-three. Exceptions to Gamp’s Law. Quietly, please.’

pages.title: Staffroom
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Old armchairs, none of them matching
pages.html:
The staffroom is the long, panelled room at Hogwarts where the teachers gather between lessons. It is full of old armchairs, none of which match. In the autumn of 1993 a boggart lived in the wardrobe where the staff keep their spare robes, until Professor Lupin's third years dealt with it.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eighteen, Harry Potter hid with Ron Weasley in the staffroom wardrobe. From there they heard Professor McGonagall tell the staff that Ginny Weasley had been taken into the Chamber. Ron slid silently down the inside of the wardrobe until he was sitting on the floor among the shoes.

In Book Three, Chapter Seven, in September 1993, Lupin brought his class there to face the boggart. Snape was the only teacher in the room, sitting in a low chair by the window. 'No... leave it open, Lupin. I'd rather not be here for this,' he said, and went. The boggart became Snape for Neville Longbottom, who put it into his grandmother's long green dress and vulture hat. For Dracina Malfoy it became her father, telling her she was not a real Malfoy. She wept in the middle of the staffroom. Then she turned him into a tramp in odd wellingtons and laughed it away.

pages.title: Fourth-floor disused corridor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Chapter Nine
The fourth floor of Hogwarts Castle
The castle's attic, by Fred Weasley
Old, unwanted paintings, among them the painting of the two brothers
pages.html:
The disused corridor on the fourth floor of Hogwarts is where the castle hangs the paintings nobody wants. They are old, brown and unpopular. Fred Weasley calls the corridor the castle's attic. Its suits of armour were taken away for cleaning and never brought back. Among the paintings hangs the cracked canvas of the two brothers at their altars, Cain and Abel.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Nine, in November 1993, Harry Potter went to Transfiguration the long way, alone, through the disused corridor. He was angry at being watched over, and the quiet was wonderful. He had come that way perhaps twice in three years and had never once looked at the paintings. This time one of them caught his eye, because it had a fire in it, and the fire was moving.

It was the big, dark canvas of the two brothers, cracked all over like a dry riverbed. The man with the fists talked to Harry about the thing that had lain at his door-sill ever since his smoke first went wrong. 'You're angry, boy,' he told Harry. 'I can always tell. It's a smell in your blood, like rain coming. Mind the door-sill.' Harry was eight minutes late for Transfiguration.

In Chapter Ten the same man stood watching Harry, without a word, all through a dream in the hospital wing. Harry told Professor Lupin about it afterwards, and about the big old brown painting in the corridor where the armour had been taken away. Lupin went the colour of the wall. In Chapter Fifteen, trying to empty his mind over a crystal ball in Divination, Harry found the painting on the fourth floor bobbing up in it again.

pages.title: Lupin's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
A grindylow in a tank; a kettle
pages.html:
Lupin's office is the office Remus Lupin used while he taught Defence Against the Dark Arts at Hogwarts, in the school year of 1993 to 1994. He kept a grindylow there in a big tank in the corner, and a kettle for tea.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eight, on Hallowe'en 1993, the other third-years went to Hogsmeade without Harry Potter, who had no signed form. Lupin saw him in the corridor and called him into his office. A grindylow had just been delivered for the next lesson: a sickly green water demon with little pointed horns, pressed against the glass of the tank. Lupin tapped the kettle with his wand and made tea with teabags, in a chipped mug. While they were talking about the boggart, Snape came in with a smoking goblet and told Lupin to drink it at once.

pages.title: McGonagall's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
A stuffed Goa'uld symbiote in a lit glass case
pages.html:
McGonagall's office is the room where Professor McGonagall, the Deputy Headmistress, sees her pupils, generally when they are in trouble. Over its fire hangs a long glass case, lit from inside, holding a dead spinal parasite: a stuffed Goa'uld symbiote.

The case

The creature is grey-white and segmented, about as long as a boy's forearm. It has fins down its back, with a mouth that opens four ways at once. McGonagall met it a long time ago, a very long way from Hogwarts, living in a human host. No Transfiguration would part them; in the end it took a knife, a steady hand and a good deal of help from Big Boss. The host died, and so did the creature. She keeps it as a reminder that there are some problems one cannot solve with a wand.

In the saga
