Susan Pevensie, the last of the four, joined the others in Aslan's country in October 1981, when Lord Voldemort killed her.

pages.title: Arwen
infobox: Half-elven, of the Elves by choice until her marriage
On Cerin Amroth in Lórien, early in the Fourth Age
Harry Potter, through Lily Potter and Susan Pevensie
pages.html:
Arwen Undómiel, the Evenstar of her people, was the daughter of Elrond of Rivendell. She gave up the long life of the Elves to marry Aragorn, which made her queen of Gondor and Arnor. Through her line the blood of the Elves came down the ages to Godric Gryffindor, to the Pevensies, to Lily Potter and at last to Harry.

The Evenstar

Arwen was the daughter of Elrond Half-elven and Celebrían. Through her mother she was a granddaughter of Galadriel, the Lady of the Golden Wood. She lived for long years in Rivendell, with stays among her mother's kin in Lothlórien, and it was said that the likeness of Lúthien, fairest of all the Elves of old, had come back into the world in her. Her name, Undómiel, means Evenstar. The evening star in the west is the star of Eärendil, who was her father's father.

She met Aragorn in the woods of Rivendell when he was twenty years old. Many years later she plighted her troth to him on the green hill of Cerin Amroth. Elrond would not let them marry until Aragorn was king of both Gondor and Arnor, which was a great deal to ask of a ranger with no kingdom. During the War of the Ring she wove for him the standard that he unfurled on the black ships.

The choice

As one of Elrond's children, Arwen was free to choose which kindred she would belong to. She chose Men, and with them death. She married Aragorn at Midsummer in the year the Ring was destroyed. She bore him a son, Eldarion, and daughters besides.

When Aragorn died in the Fourth Age, she went alone to Lórien, which by then stood empty. There, late in the year, as the leaves of the mallorn trees were falling, she lay down on Cerin Amroth and died. Her grave lay on that hill until the world was changed, and the men who came after forgot her altogether.

Descent

Harry Potter descends from Aragorn and Arwen through his mother. Arwen gives the line the Elves, as Aragorn gives it Númenor. Between them they are what Dumbledore meant in June 1993, when he told Harry that Lily's protection was 'the magic of Elves, Harry. And of Númenor'. They are also what he meant when he told Harry that his mother had come down from Elves.

Godric Gryffindor was one of the heirs of that line, and so were all four Pevensies. Through Susan, the only one of the four to survive, it came to Lily and so to Harry. Reading of Rivendell in August 1993, Harry felt a light come off the Elves like pages left in the sun. He could not see anything of it in the boy in the mirror.

pages.title: Elendil
infobox: End of the Second Age, on the slopes of Orodruin
pages.html:
Elendil the Tall was the leader of the Faithful of Númenor. When the island was drowned he escaped with his sons to Middle-earth, where he founded the realms of Arnor and Gondor. At the end of the Second Age he fell fighting Sauron on the slopes of Orodruin, and his sword Narsil broke beneath him.

His heirs

With the hilt-shard of Narsil his son Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand. Elendil's heirs kept the shards for three thousand years, until the Elves of Rivendell reforged them for Aragorn as Andúril. Through Aragorn, Elendil is a forefather of Godric Gryffindor, and so of Harry Potter, who does not know it.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, on the night of 6 June 1994, Harry stood at the window of Flitwick's office with Dracina Malfoy's hand in his. He felt his anger change into something steadier. He thought of Narsil, the sword of Elendil, which had lain broken for three thousand years until the Elves of Rivendell made it new for Aragorn as Andúril. Nobody at Hogwarts could have guessed how well Harry knew that sword. He had held it in his own two hands.

pages.title: Ioreth
infobox: Remembering the old saying about the king's hands
pages.html:
Ioreth was an old woman of Minas Tirith who served in the Houses of Healing at the end of the Third Age. She remembered an old saying about the hands of the king. When Aragorn laid his hands on the wounded after the Battle of the Pelennor Fields and they woke, that was how the city knew its king had come back.

The Houses of Healing

Ioreth was the eldest of the women who served there, and a great talker. When Aragorn asked for athelas she had never heard of it by that name. She knew it only as kingsfoil, a weed of the woods with a strange name. It was she who spread the old saying through the city, and with it the news that the king had come back.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-Two, in the summer of 1994, Harry Potter finished The Lord of the Rings in bed at Privet Drive, by the light of the streetlamp, long after the Dursleys had gone to sleep. In the Houses of Healing Aragorn laid his hands on the wounded, and they woke. Old Ioreth said that the hands of the king are the hands of a healer, and that was how they knew him.

pages.title: Sauron
infobox: The Hobbit (21 September 1937), as the Necromancer; named in The Fellowship of the Ring (29 July 1954)
The One Ring, the first Horcrux
End of the Second Age; destroyed with the Ring at the end of the Third
pages.html:
Sauron was Morgoth's lieutenant. After his master's fall he became the Dark Lord of the Second and Third Ages. He put a great part of his own native power into the One Ring, so that he could not be wholly ended while it lasted. In doing so he made the first Horcrux.

History

Sauron was a Maia, a spirit of the same order as Gandalf. He served Aulë the smith until Melkor, the rebel later called Morgoth, seduced him. In the First Age he was Morgoth's chief servant. He was the master of werewolves and of the isle of Tol-in-Gaurhoth.

After Morgoth was overthrown he hid. About the year 1000 of the Second Age he chose Mordor for his stronghold and began to build Barad-dûr. About 1200 he came among the Elven-smiths of Eregion in a fair form, calling himself Annatar, the Lord of Gifts. He taught them, and under his teaching they forged the Rings of Power. About 1600, in secret, in the fire of Orodruin, he forged the One Ring to rule the rest. The Elves were aware of him the moment he put it on, and they took off their rings. He made war on them for the rings and laid Eregion waste in 1697. He gave the Nine to kings of Men, who became his Ringwraiths, while the Seven went to the lords of the Dwarves.

In 3262 the King of Númenor carried him off a prisoner, and on the island he corrupted the King. He brought about the drowning of Númenor in 3319. His fair body perished with it, but his spirit fled back to Mordor to take up the Ring again. At the end of the Second Age the Last Alliance of Elves and Men overthrew him, when Isildur cut the Ring from his hand with the shard of Narsil.

Because the Ring endured, he could not be ended. Through the Third Age he took shape again, first as the Necromancer of Dol Guldur and then in the Dark Tower of Barad-dûr. He sought the Ring until Frodo Baggins destroyed it in Orodruin, and with it his power ended for ever.

The first Horcrux

What Sauron did with the Ring is what wizards now call making a Horcrux: he put a great part of his own native power into a made thing, so that he could not be ended while it lasted. His was the first, and everything since is imitation. The modern technique was invented after the Flood by the Stygian whom history calls Herpo the Foul. It is the Ring reverse-engineered by guesswork, from what survived of Sauron's craft.

Aragorn and the palantír

In the War of the Ring, Aragorn looked into the palantír of Orthanc and wrestled with Sauron himself through it. From then on he stopped doubting that he would be king. Harry Potter read of it in Dudley's copy of The Lord of the Rings, and thought of that moment at Professor Flitwick's window in June 1994.

pages.title: Horcrux
infobox: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (16 July 2005)
The One Ring, made by Sauron
Invented after the Flood by a Stygian, recorded as Herpo the Foul
The tearing of the maker's own soul
pages.html:
A Horcrux is a made thing into which a dark wizard has put part of himself, so that he cannot be ended while it lasts. The first was the One Ring. Every Horcrux since has been an imitation of it, made by a cruder technique that a Stygian, whom history calls Herpo the Foul, invented after the Flood from the ruins of Sauron's craft.

The Ring

Sauron, Morgoth's lieutenant, put a great part of his own native power into the One Ring, so that he could not be ended while it lasted. That was the first Horcrux. It cannot be made again in quite the same way. Its maker was a Maia, a spirit older than the world, and no mortal wizard has such power to give. What is missing is not knowledge but the nature of the maker.

Gandalf made sure that the knowledge of making such a thing was lost. Some of it survived all the same, carried forward through forgotten ages by dark hands.

The Stygian's craft

After the Flood a Stygian who had lived through it gathered up what was left of the old craft. It was corrupted and full of holes, so he filled in the blanks himself. The result is the modern technique. A mortal wizard has no native power of that kind to give, so he pays with his own soul instead, tearing it on purpose. It is the Ring worked out backwards by guesswork, which is why it costs what it costs.

The soul is torn by murder, the supreme act of evil, and the torn piece is sealed into an object. It is the extreme case of a general rule: dark magic takes something out of the caster's soul and does not give it back. Once made, a Horcrux is very hard to destroy. It takes something so destructive that the vessel cannot mend itself.

Wizarding history calls the inventor Herpo the Foul and makes him a Greek. Every textbook on the subject is confidently wrong about its own origin.

Voldemort

In June 1992 Dumbledore told Harry Potter that Voldemort was still out there somewhere: 'Not being properly alive, he can't be killed. The things keeping him anchored to this mortal plane will not let him die.' He was describing a working on the pattern of the Ring, badly made, in the plural.

Voldemort's Horcruxes are the work of a man rebuilding a lost art from a damaged manual without knowing that is what he is doing. He believes he is at the summit of the discipline. He is standing in its ruins.

The diary

Tom Riddle's diary was a Horcrux. In December 1992 Gandalf felt on Dracina Malfoy, who was carrying it, the coldness he had felt long ago from the Ring. It was a piece of someone poured into a vessel, so that it could wait, whisper and be carried. Whoever carried it would come to love it, then to need it, holding it tighter and tighter until they could not let go.

The diary possessed Dracina through the spring of 1993. It drew her down into the Chamber of Secrets, and Ginny Weasley, who had followed her, was taken too. There Riddle's memory began to take solid form. In June 1993 Harry drove the point of Andúril through the diary. Ink burst out of it like blood. Riddle screamed, frayed at the edges like smoke and was gone.

The one he never meant to make

On 31 October 1981 Voldemort's Killing Curse rebounded from the infant Harry Potter. It tore loose a fragment of his already broken soul, which lodged in the only living thing in the room. Harry is a Horcrux that Voldemort never meant to make.

The fragment is the root of Harry's Parseltongue, and of the pain in his scar when Voldemort is near or stirring. Under the full moon in June 1994 the war form of Remus Lupin, a Garou, breathed him in as though it had found two smells on him. Then it made a grinding sound that was very nearly a word: 'Wyyyrrrm'. Harry does not know what he carries.

pages.title: Herpo the Foul
infobox: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (12 March 2001)
Inventing the modern Horcrux; breeding the first basilisk
pages.html:
Herpo the Foul was a dark wizard whom history places in Ancient Greece. Wizarding scholarship credits him with the first Horcrux and the first basilisk. In truth he was a Stygian who survived the Flood. He gathered up the remnants of Morgoth's broken craft, filled the gaps by guesswork and so invented the modern Horcrux.

As history records him

Wizarding history knows Herpo the Foul as a dark wizard of Ancient Greece and a Parselmouth. He is said to have bred the first basilisk by hatching a chicken's egg beneath a toad, and to have been the first wizard ever to make a Horcrux. Every textbook on the subject says so. Wizarding scholarship has never once thought to question it.

The breeding of basilisks has been against wizarding law since the Middle Ages, though the practice is easily hidden: a breeder need only take the chicken's egg out from under the toad when the Ministry comes to call.

The Stygian

History is wrong on two counts. Herpo was not a Greek at all. He was a Stygian of the Hyborian Age, from the serpent-worshipping kingdom that kept Morgoth's dark craft, and he lived on into the world after the Flood.

There he gathered up what was left of the old art. It was ancient, half forgotten, corrupted and full of holes. He filled the blanks himself. What he produced was the modern Horcrux, the version a mortal wizard can make without a Maia's native power, at the price of tearing his own soul. It is the One Ring worked out backwards by guesswork, which is why it costs what it costs. Greece is merely where the record happens to pick him up.

Long ago Gandalf made sure that the knowledge of making a thing like the Ring was lost. He knows that some of it survived all the same, 'carried forward by dark hands like that damn Stygian's'. In December 1992 he recognised the same making in Tom Riddle's diary. The only two beings who could put the textbooks right are Gandalf and the enemy. Neither of them has offered.

pages.title: Stygia
infobox: Drowned in the Flood at the end of the Ice Age
pages.html:
Stygia was the serpent-worshipping kingdom of the south in the Hyborian Age, beyond the River Styx. It did not invent dark magic, but it collected it, preserved it and practised it on a grand scale, until it became the library of dark magic for the whole of the old world. Most of the dark spells still in use come, at least in part, from what Stygia held.

The kingdom

Stygia lay south of the pastures of Shem, along its great river. Its people worshipped Set, the Old Serpent, in black temples. Its sorcerers learnt their art from the thing that lived in those temples, and paid dearly for it. The craft they kept was Morgoth's, come down from the Elder Days. The sorcerers of the Black Ring, Thoth-Amon greatest among them, made Stygia feared in every kingdom of the west. Conan the Cimmerian crossed swords with its sorcerers many times, and once followed the stolen Heart of Ahriman as far as the black city of Khemi.

The Flood

The Flood that ended the Ice Age drowned Stygia along with nearly everything else. Its black towers by the warm seas went under, with the temples where men had fed the serpent. The written record of its craft drowned with it.

One Stygian lived on into the world after the Flood: the man history calls Herpo the Foul, wrongly making him a Greek. He gathered up the broken remnants of the craft, patched the gaps by guesswork and so made the modern Horcrux.

The inheritance

Egypt was Stygia's heir. From Egypt the dark inheritance passed to Greece, then to Rome, then to England and the rest of Europe. A wizard who goes looking for the beginnings of his own craft finds Egypt, then Stygia, then nothing at all, because that is where the record drowns. So the wizarding world assumes that its oldest magic is morally neutral and merely old.

pages.title: Hyborian Age
infobox: The Ice Age and the Flood
Aquilonia, Nemedia, Cimmeria, Stygia, Zingara, Koth, Shem, Turan, Hyrkania, Vendhya, Khitai
Conan the Cimmerian, King of Aquilonia
pages.html:
The Hyborian Age was the age of the world that followed the ages of Middle-earth. It ended with the Ice Age and the Flood. Conan the Cimmerian is a man of its real history. Stygia, the serpent-worshipping kingdom of the south, kept Morgoth's dark craft and practised it on a grand scale, until it became the library of dark magic.

The age

The Hyborian Age was a time of kingdoms, sorcerers and barbarians across the west of the world. The Hyborian nations held the middle lands: Aquilonia, Nemedia, Ophir, Koth and the rest. To the north lay Cimmeria and the Nordheim. To the east were Turan, Hyrkania, Vendhya and far Khitai. Zingara faced the western sea. The pastures of Shem ran down to the border of Stygia, which stood to the south, beyond the River Styx.

The most famous man of the age was Conan, a barbarian of Cimmeria. He was a thief, a reaver, a pirate and a mercenary before he took the throne of Aquilonia with his own hand. The age ended in barbarian invasion and cataclysm. The Picts, the Hyrkanians and the peoples of the north overran the Hyborian kingdoms. Then the ice came down.

Stygia

Stygia did not invent dark magic. It was where Morgoth's craft was kept, collected, systematised and practised on a grand scale. Most dark spells still in use come at least in part from what Stygia held. Its people worshipped Set, the Old Serpent, in black temples. Its sorcerers learnt their art from the thing that lived in those temples, and paid dearly for it. Gandalf remembers what the Flood drowned at the end of the age: 'The black towers by the warm seas, the temples where men had worshipped a great serpent and fed it.'

The dark inheritance survived the water. One Stygian lived on into the world after the Flood. He gathered the broken remnants of the craft and invented the modern Horcrux. History calls him Herpo the Foul, and wrongly makes him a Greek. Ancient Egypt was Stygia's descendant and heir. Everything that the wizards of Europe call ancient and dark came first through Egypt, then Greece, then Rome, before it reached Britain.

Memory

Like Middle-earth before it, the Hyborian Age reaches the present only as story. Conan survives as a legend in the tales Muggles tell. The wizarding world assumes that its oldest magic is merely old. It has no idea that the written record of its dark arts drowned with Stygia. Conan himself outlived the age. Born of the ritual sacrifice of elder sorcerers, he found after laying down the crown of Aquilonia that he could not die. He walks in the world still.

The kingdom of the Sub-Mariner claims to be the heir of the Atlantis that sank in the Cataclysm. Its people found the drowned island about 8000 BC and built their first city in its ruins. Aquaman's kingdom, which claims the name for itself, holds that the island of Kull's day was a land of barbarians of no account. In this, if in nothing else, it is right.

pages.title: Conan the Cimmerian
infobox: Conan of Cimmeria; Conan the Barbarian; King Conan; Amra
Cimmeria, about 10,090 BC, of the sacrifice of a circle of elder sorcerers
Amra, the Lion (as a pirate); King Conan of Aquilonia; a great many more since
King of Aquilonia, from about 10,050 BC until he laid down the crown
He cannot die; a sorcery that has grown with every age
The Emperor of Mankind, worshipped as the God-Emperor
pages.html:
Conan of Cimmeria was a barbarian of the Hyborian Age who had been a thief, a reaver, a pirate and a mercenary before he took the throne of Aquilonia with his own hand. He was born of a ritual sacrifice: a circle of sorcerers of the elder world gave up their lives so that their power would live again in a single child. Only after he had laid down his crown did he come to understand that he could not die. He has walked in and out of history ever since under many names. His own sorcery has grown with every age, above all since the Ice Age ended. Long afterwards, at the end of the Age of Strife, he rose as the Emperor of Mankind, and he was worshipped as the God-Emperor.

Birth

In the last ages before the ice came down, a circle of the elder world's sorcerers foresaw the long dark that lay ahead of mankind. They resolved that mankind should have a champion. In a single ritual they gave up their lives, so that their power and everything they knew would not die with them, but would be born again together in one child.

The child was born about 10,090 BC in Cimmeria, among the dark hills of the north, of a people descended from the Atlanteans. The Cimmerians said that he had been born on a battlefield, and in a sense he was. His father was a blacksmith. Conan grew up a Cimmerian like any other, grim, black-haired and blue-eyed, with no notion of what had gone into his making. He had, too, a deep distrust of sorcery, which he kept for most of his life.

The adventurer

At fifteen he was among the warriors who stormed and burned Venarium, the Aquilonian fort on Cimmeria's southern border. He fought beside the Æsir in the snows of Nordheim. In Zamora, as a young thief, he climbed the Tower of the Elephant and freed the enslaved being from the stars who lived at the top of it.

He sailed the Black Coast with the pirate queen Bêlit, whose corsairs named him Amra, the Lion. When she died he sent her burning out to sea. In the years after that he was a general in Khoraja, then a captain of the guard in Khauran who survived crucifixion in the desert. He led the Afghuli hillmen as their chief and broke the Black Seers of Mount Yimsha. He was a scout on the Pictish frontier of Aquilonia. Sorcerers crossed his path all his life, Stygians above all, who served the serpent and the dark craft that Stygia kept. He killed most of them.

King of Aquilonia

About 10,050 BC, as general of Aquilonia's armies on the western frontier, Conan led a rebellion against the mad king Numedides and strangled him on his own throne. As king he survived the conspiracy of Ascalante, after the shade of the sage Epemitreus warned him in a dream. He survived, too, the treachery of the kings of Koth and Ophir, who threw him into the dungeons of the Scarlet Citadel.

In the Hour of the Dragon the sorcerer Xaltotun, raised from three thousand years' sleep, took his kingdom from him. Conan followed the stolen Heart of Ahriman into Stygia, as far as the black city of Khemi, and won it back. He destroyed Xaltotun, regained his throne and made Zenobia his queen. Their son, Conn, was his heir.

The crown laid down

When he had reigned long enough, Conan gave the crown of Aquilonia to Conn and sailed west into the unknown lands beyond the ocean. It was in the years after he laid down the crown that he understood at last what he was. He was not growing old. His wounds closed as they always had, and the decades passed over him without leaving a mark. He outlived his son, and then his son's sons. He could not die.

He watched the Hyborian kingdoms fall to the Picts, the Hyrkanians and the peoples of the north. He watched the ice come down. Then he came through the Flood that ended the Ice Age, which drowned Stygia along with nearly everything else he had ever known.

The sorcerer

Conan had distrusted sorcery all his life. Once he knew what he was, he set himself to master it, and the power that the sorcerers of the elder world had poured into him at his birth began to wake. When the Flood went down, the Ice Age was over. A new magic of light came into the world, sent by God and taught to men by Gandalf. Beside it was the old dark craft that had survived the water. Conan studied both.

His power has grown in every age since. By the twentieth century there was very probably no sorcerer alive to match him, although almost nobody knows that he exists.

Many names

He has walked in and out of history ever since, under many names, in many guises: a soldier in one century, a counsellor of kings in another, a wanderer who turns up in the margins of the chronicles, then is gone again. Amra was the first of his other names. There have been a great many since. He keeps no record of them, and nobody has ever put them together.

To the world he is a legend of a lost age, told in tales and pictures. The wizarding world, which assumes that its oldest magic is merely old, has no idea that he still walks among it.

The Emperor of Mankind

Many thousands of years later, in the Age of Strife, mankind's worlds among the stars fell into darkness, while Earth itself fell into war. At the end of that age Conan stepped out of history for the last time. Coming among the warring peoples of Terra first under the name Revelation, he united the world under his rule as the Emperor of Mankind and founded the Imperium of Man.

He made the Primarchs, his twenty sons, and the Space Marines. He led the Great Crusade to bring mankind's scattered worlds back together. In the thirty-first millennium his favoured son Horus turned on him, and in the Siege of Terra the Emperor cast Horus down. He was wounded past healing. He was set upon the Golden Throne, where he sat for ten thousand years and more, unable to die, while the Imperium he had founded worshipped him as the God-Emperor of Mankind, against everything he had ever taught.

pages.title: The Flood
aliases: the end of the Ice Age
infobox: The end of the Ice Age
Noah and his household, in the ark; Cain, who could not die; one Stygian sorcerer, later called Herpo the Foul
The Hyborian world, Stygia's towers and temples, the Nephilim
Nearly all knowledge of the elder days was lost
pages.html:
The Flood, Noah's Flood, the story of the ark in Genesis, was the end of the Ice Age. When the ice that had lain a mile thick on the mountains melted, its waters became God's judgement on the old world. At God's command Noah built the ark. He brought his household and the beasts through in it, while the Nephilim drowned with all the kingdoms of the Hyborian Age. Nearly all knowledge of the elder days went under with them, so that Middle-earth, the Hyborian Age and much else reach the present only as story.

The Flood of Noah

God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and resolved to destroy all flesh. But Noah found grace in His eyes.

At God's command Noah built an ark of gopher wood. He took into it his wife, his three sons and their wives, with the beasts of the earth two by two. The sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

The fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. It rained for forty days and forty nights. The waters prevailed upon the earth, and Scripture records that every living thing outside the ark perished. That was very nearly true.

When the waters went down, the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat. Noah sent out a raven, then a dove. The dove came back the second time with an olive leaf. God set His bow in the cloud as the token of His covenant. Never again would the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.

The end of the Ice Age

The Flood came when the ice that had lain a mile thick on the mountains of the north went back at last, groaning and cracking. Gandalf remembers the meltwater coming down out of the north in a flood that went on for a hundred years. It drowned whole countries. The black towers by the warm seas went under. So did the temples where men had worshipped a great serpent and fed it, with the sorcerers who had learnt their magic from the thing in those temples.

So ended the Hyborian Age, and Stygia with it. Afterwards a few frightened families huddled round small fires on the cold new shores, with nothing at all. It was to them that God sent Gandalf to teach light magic.

What it took, and what it spared

The Nephilim of Genesis 6 were under no sentence of immortality, and the Flood took them. It could not take Cain. God had already cursed him: deathless, soulless, burned by the sun and condemned to wander. God does not revoke His own sentences. Cain went into the water a cursed man, and he came out of it a cursed man. Only afterwards did he meet Lilith, who led him into the blood magic by which he became the first vampire.

Nor did the Flood take the dark craft entirely. Morgoth's art, which Stygia had kept and practised at scale, was scattered rather than drowned. A Stygian survived. He gathered up what was left, and invented the modern Horcrux; history calls him Herpo the Foul. What reaches a modern wizard of the old dark magic is a corrupted copy of a copy. A wizard who digs for the origins of his craft finds Egypt, then Stygia, then nothing, because that is where the written record drowns.

Nothing of the elder days came through whole. The Lord of the Rings survives as a novel, and Conan as a legend; even Arthur, who lived long after the water, is only half-history. The true account of the first gift of light magic survives only as the shape of things: why the oldest spells are dark, and why the Patronus is different.

The Flood took R'lyeh too, the city of Cthulhu in the southern ocean, and put it under the sea with him inside. It did not kill him. God's judgement fell on him as on the rest of the old world, and he outlasted it, dead but dreaming in his drowned house. It is the first great instance on record of what the Great Old Ones can do against God, though none of them is His equal.

pages.title: Noah
pages.html:
Noah was the righteous man whom God spared through the Flood that ended the Ice Age. He came through it in the ark, with his household and the beasts. Nearly everyone born since the Flood descends from him.

Before the Flood

Noah was the son of Lamech, the grandson of Methuselah and, through them, a descendant of Seth, the son Adam had after Abel's death. His father named him in hope: 'This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands.' Noah was a just man, perfect in his generations. He walked with God.

When God saw the wickedness of man, He resolved to destroy the earth. He told Noah to build an ark of gopher wood, three hundred cubits long, fifty broad and thirty high. It was to be pitched inside and out. It had a window, a door in its side and three decks. Into it Noah was to take his family, with two of every living thing, male and female. Of the clean beasts he was to take seven.

Noah did all that God commanded. He was six hundred years old when the Flood came.

After the Flood

When the waters went down, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sent out a raven, then a dove. The dove came back the second time with an olive leaf in its beak. The third time it did not come back at all.

Noah left the ark, built an altar and offered sacrifice. God made His covenant with Noah and his sons. He set the rainbow in the cloud as its sign: never again would the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh. He gave them every moving thing for meat, though not with its blood still in it. Whoever shed man's blood, He said, by man should his blood be shed.

Noah planted a vineyard. He drank of its wine and lay uncovered in his tent. Ham saw his father's nakedness, and went out to tell his brothers. Shem and Japheth laid a garment on their shoulders. They walked in backwards, with their faces turned away, to cover him. When Noah woke he cursed Canaan, Ham's son. He blessed Shem and Japheth.

He lived three hundred and fifty years after the Flood. All the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years. From his three sons came the nations of the earth, which spread out over the whole world after the water.

The world after the water

The Flood that Noah came through was the end of the Ice Age. It drowned the Hyborian world, and nearly all knowledge of the elder days with it. The frightened families on the cold new shores, by whose fires Gandalf sat to teach the first words of light magic, were the children of the world that Noah's ark had carried through.

Not everything that survived was human, or righteous. Cain, who could not die, came through the water too. Shortly afterwards Lilith found him, and the first vampire was the result. One Stygian sorcerer also survived, with the dark craft he carried. History remembers him as Herpo the Foul.

pages.title: The Istari
infobox: The Return of the King (20 October 1955), appendices
Maiar in the likeness of old men
To contest the power of Sauron and, later, of Morgoth's inheritance
Saruman, Gandalf, Radagast and the two Blue Wizards
Gandalf on Earth; Zordon on Eltar
pages.html:
The Istari are the five wizards sent out on commission in the elder days: Saruman the White, Gandalf the Grey, Radagast the Brown and the two Blue Wizards. Gandalf was sent to Earth, where he remains. Zordon, one of the Blue Wizards, was sent off the world altogether, to Eltar.

The commission

The Istari were Maiar, spirits of the same order as Sauron. They came into Middle-earth from over the Sea about a thousand years into the Third Age, clothed as old men, to unite and stir up all who would resist him. They were forbidden to match his power with power, or to dominate the minds of those they came to help.

Saruman, the chief of the order, came first and was given the white. Gandalf came last, and seemed the least of them. Radagast, the friend of birds and beasts, wandered the borders of Mirkwood. Saruman fell, coveting the Ring for himself, and was killed at the end of the War of the Ring. Gandalf fell in Moria and was sent back as Gandalf the White.

The Blue Wizards

The two Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, went into the far East with Saruman and never came back. The record of them goes vague and never settles what became of them. They were the two sent furthest from the centre, and one of them went further than anybody was keeping records of: off the world entirely, to Eltar.

He is Zordon of Eltar, Gandalf's equal and his colleague in the same commission. In ancient times he fought Rita Repulsa, both on Earth and on Eltar. Her curse put him into a tube outside time, with no body to go back to. Later he raised the Power Rangers, who came to public notice in the summer of 1993, with the Power Coins that Ninjor made. Nothing was written of his going, because nobody who could have written it down ever saw him again.

A Muggle oil painting of Zordon hangs a little apart from the portraits of the headmasters in the headmaster's office at Hogwarts. It was made before Rita Repulsa cursed him, and it is the only likeness of his face that survives. It shows a bald man with skin of a deep, calm blue, like the sky just after sunset, in a high-collared golden breastplate. His expression is very patient, very wise and very kind. It hangs there, and nowhere else in Britain, because the office is one that Gandalf has known since before the drive had a gate.

On Eltar Zordon took the likeness of an Eltarian, as Gandalf took that of an old man; nobody now knows whether he was Alatar or Pallando. In November 1998 he gave up the form he wore, and his light went out across the universe.

Gandalf's second sending

At the end of the Third Age Gandalf sailed into the West. Long afterwards, when the Ice Age ended in the Flood and the old world went under the water, God sent him to Earth again. He was to teach light magic to the families of men who had survived, as a counterweight to Morgoth.

He has stayed ever since, under many names. He was Merlin to King Arthur, guide to the founders of Hogwarts and teacher of Albus Dumbledore. In the 1990s he is Ambrose Greyhame, vicar of St Michael's, Little Whinging.

pages.title: Light magic
pages.html:
Light magic is the younger of the two great inheritances of magic. God gave it to men after the Ice Age, through Gandalf, to counteract Morgoth. That is why it is cleaner, simpler and newer than dark magic, which is as old as Morgoth's rebellion.

The gift

Light magic did not exist in its present form in the elder days, in the ages of Middle-earth or in the Hyborian Age. There was power then, with craft and the Secret Fire, but no body of light magic that ordinary men could use. After the Flood, God sent Gandalf to the first men of the new age, to sit by their small fires and teach them. It was given as a defence, at a time when the enemy had worked on mankind unopposed for ages.

How it spread

From those fires the light inheritance spread, was quarrelled over and was half forgotten. In the end it was gathered into four schools on a crag in Scotland, which became Hogwarts. The Patronus Charm was among the first spells Gandalf taught. There is no dark version of it, and there cannot be.

Light and dark

Dark magic is the elder art. It began with Morgoth and was kept by Stygia. It reached the modern world through Egypt, Greece and Rome, as a corrupted copy of a copy. So most of the really old spells are dark, while the light ones are younger than the ice. Animagus magic is light magic too, though not as close to God as the Patronus.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twelve, Harry Potter asked whether the Patronus was dark magic, since Snape said all the really old spells were. ‘Professor Snape,’ said Lupin, with a very faint stress on the first word, ‘is correct that most of them are. This one is the exception, and it is the exception so completely that it is nearly the proof of the rule.’ In Book Three, Chapter Eighteen, Lupin told Harry that Animagus magic was not Wyrm-touched at all, but light magic.

pages.title: Dark magic
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Stygia, Egypt, Greece, Rome, England and Europe
Light magic, given by God through Gandalf
pages.html:
Dark magic is the craft of Morgoth. It is as old as his rebellion, and he taught it to his servants, who taught it in their turn. Stygia preserved it and the Flood broke it apart. What reaches a modern wizard is a corrupted copy of a copy: imprecise, costly and badly understood by those who cast it. It is the elder art. Light magic is the younger gift.

Origin and descent

Dark magic did not begin with men. It began with Morgoth in the Elder Days, and his lieutenant Sauron brought it to its height in the One Ring. Stygia did not invent it. Through the Hyborian Age the Stygians kept it, collected it, set it in order and practised it on a great scale. Most of the dark spells still in use come, at least in part, from what Stygia held.

The Flood washed the old world away and broke the craft into pieces. A Stygian who survived it, whom history calls Herpo the Foul, gathered up the remnants and patched the gaps by guesswork. From Egypt, Stygia's heir, the inheritance passed to Greece, then to Rome, then to England and the rest of Europe. Hermione Granger has called Druidic magic 'practically all blood, oaths and bindings'. Her account of it, like her account of the Celtic and Norse blood rites, describes fragments that came downstream from the same source.

The Weasleys spent the summer of 1993 in Egypt, where Bill Weasley breaks curses in the tombs of the pharaohs for Gringotts. There are things in there, Molly was warned, that would turn your hair white. A wizard who goes looking for the beginnings of his own craft finds Egypt, then Stygia, then nothing at all, because that is where the written record drowns. So the wizarding world assumes that magic is merely old, and neither good nor evil in itself.

Dark and light

Light magic did not exist in its present form in the Elder Days. It was given after the Ice Age, when God sent Gandalf to teach men, as a counterweight to an enemy who had been working on them unopposed for ages. That is why light magic is cleaner, simpler and newer. It is also why the oldest spells to survive are nearly all dark. Severus Snape holds that all the really old spells are dark; Remus Lupin will only grant that most of them are. The Patronus Charm, which has no dark version, is the exception that nearly proves the rule.

The first thing Gandalf taught, after how to call up a flame and how to heal a cut, was how to tell that a voice out of the dark offering power is never the voice of a friend. The Church of the Fat Friar's day condemned the same thing: calling up spirits, and bargaining with things in the dark for power, which the Friar calls idolatry.

In June 1994 Lupin told Harry Potter that most wizards do not realise how mixed up light and dark magic are in what they are taught. He could smell the Wyrm everywhere at Hogwarts, he said. That might well be the purpose of the one from whom all dark magic comes.

Magic of the soul

As Lupin put it: 'Most magic draws on what a wizard can do. A very small number of spells draw on what he is. Those are the dangerous ones, in both directions.' The three Unforgivable Curses, the Killing Curse, the Cruciatus Curse and the Imperius Curse, cannot be cast merely by learning them. Everybody knows the words, but said without the whole heart behind them they do nothing at all, which Lupin calls 'the single most merciful fact in our entire body of law'. The Ministry of Magic classed the three curses as Unforgivable in 1717. To use any of them on another human being earns a life sentence in Azkaban.

Dark magic of that order asks the caster for something out of his soul. It takes it, and it does not give it back. The Horcrux, in which the soul is torn on purpose, is the extreme case. The Patronus runs on something that comes from God meeting the caster's soul, and it leaves the soul whole.

To a Garou the dark arts have a smell. Lupin smells the Wyrm on a dementor, on Voldemort's name, on Peter Pettigrew and on the Dark Mark on Snape's left arm. In March 1994 he told Snape so: 'As you well know, I know when something reeks of Dark Magic, Severus.' Vampirism, which Cain learnt as blood magic from Morgoth's servant Lilith, belongs to the same inheritance.

pages.title: Adam
infobox: God, from the dust of the ground
Cain, Abel and Seth, with other sons and daughters
pages.html:
Adam was the first man, whom God formed from the dust of the ground. He was the father of Cain, who murdered his brother Abel and was cursed by God with a deathless, sunless, wandering life.

The garden

God formed Adam of the dust of the ground. He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living soul. God planted a garden eastward in Eden. He put Adam in it to tend it and to keep it. Adam gave names to every beast of the field and every fowl of the air, but among them all there was no helper fit for him. So God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, took one of his ribs, and made from it a woman. Adam called her Eve, because she was the mother of all living.

The fall

God had forbidden them to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The serpent tempted Eve to eat of it all the same. She gave the fruit to Adam, and he ate. God drove them out of the garden. At the east of Eden He set cherubim, with a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way to the tree of life.

Outside the garden Adam was to eat his bread in the sweat of his face, until he went back to the ground he had been taken from. Dust he was, and to dust he would return.

His sons

Eve bore him Cain, then Abel. After Abel's death came Seth, from whom Noah descended. Adam was a hundred and thirty years old when Seth was born. He had other sons and daughters besides. He lived nine hundred and thirty years. Then he died.

Cain

Adam's elder son Cain was a tiller of the ground. Abel was a keeper of sheep. God had respect to Abel's offering but not to Cain's. He told Cain that sin lay at the door, that its desire was for him, and that he should rule over it. Cain murdered his brother.

God cursed him with immortality, with burning in sunlight and with wandering for ever. What the curse meant underneath was soullessness. Cain walked through every age that followed, and the Flood did not take him. Afterwards he became the first vampire through Lilith, a servant of Morgoth, who lied to him that she had been Adam's first wife. She had never been anything of the kind.

In the saga

A cracked painting hangs in the disused corridor on the fourth floor at Hogwarts, where the suits of armour were taken away for cleaning and never brought back. It shows the two brothers at their altars on a bare hillside. Abel's smoke goes up in a straight white feather, while Cain's crawls sideways along the ground.

In November 1993 the painted Cain complained to Harry Potter that nobody would tell him why. Then he warned him: 'You're angry, boy. I can always tell... Mind the door-sill.' The brother at the accepted altar has no face.

pages.title: Lilith
infobox: Isaiah 34:14; as Adam's first wife, The Alphabet of Ben Sira
The Bahari, as the Dark Mother
pages.html:
Lilith is the immortal who taught Cain blood magic after the Flood, and so made vampires possible. She told him she was Adam's first wife. In truth she was a powerful servant of Morgoth. The craft she gave Cain bound him to Morgoth's will, and every vampire after him.

The lie

The story Lilith told Cain is the one Jewish tradition tells of her. She said she had been made from the earth as Adam was, and that she had refused to be ruled by him. She had spoken the Name of God, flown out of Eden and refused ever to go back. Cain, cursed, deathless and alone, met her shortly after the Flood. He believed her. It was the most consequential lie ever told to a man.

She showed him that his cursed blood held power, and how to wake it. With her blood magic he strengthened himself and passed his curse on to others. From that moment vampires existed as a kind, and not merely as one wretched man. Cain thought he was being given relief from his sentence. He was being recruited. Her master, the being called Morgoth in the elder days, Satan in Scripture and the Wyrm by the Garou, had gained every vampire that would ever be sired.

What she made

Every vampire since stands under Morgoth's will, whether it knows it or not. Each carries Cain's sentence as well. The soul is gone, the sun burns, and in the soul's place there is something the Kindred call the Beast.

The blood magic she taught belongs to the elder, dark inheritance of magic that began with Morgoth: the same inheritance as the old spells of Stygia and the Horcrux. It owes nothing to any separate supernatural order.

Remembrance

Kindred tradition remembers Lilith as the one who woke the gifts in Cain's blood that the clans now call Disciplines. The Camarilla counts her a legend, as it counts Cain himself.

A few vampires and mortals, the Bahari, revere her as the Dark Mother. They seek wisdom through pain in her name, and hold that Cain repaid her teaching badly. None of them knows whose servant she was.

pages.title: Society of Leopold
infobox: The Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome
The Camarilla, in the hunt for Angelus
pages.html:
The Society of Leopold is the Inquisition as it survives in the modern age: a secret Catholic order sworn to destroy vampires and other creatures of the dark. In the eighteenth century its hunters pursued Angelus across Europe, never knowing that the Camarilla was paying for the chase.

The order

It takes its name from Leopold of Murnau, an inquisitor of the early thirteenth century. The Church does not openly acknowledge it, but it keeps the inquisitors' old traditions alive. It believes that the end of the world is near, and that the creatures it hunts serve the Antichrist. Its house is the Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome.

The hunt for Angelus

Angelus and his line flouted the Masquerade so openly that the Camarilla feared for every vampire in Europe. Rather than act against him itself, it quietly supported the hunters on his trail. Daniel Holtz of York, who took up the chase in 1764, never knew whose money he was spending.

pages.title: Daniel Holtz
pages.html:
Daniel Holtz was an English hunter of vampires in the eighteenth century, one of the Society of Leopold. After Angelus and Darla destroyed his family in 1764, he pursued them across Europe for nine years. Like the other men who hunted Angelus, he never knew that some of the money behind the hunt came from the Camarilla.

York, 1764

Holtz came from York. He was one of the most capable hunters of his age, and he is said to have destroyed several hundred vampires.

In May 1764 Angelus and Darla came to his house while he was away. They killed his wife, Caroline, and their baby son. His daughter, Sarah, they turned. When Holtz came home he had to destroy his own daughter, which he did by putting her out into the sunlight.

The hunt

From then on he hunted the pair of them across Europe as a hunter of the Society of Leopold. He had help he never knew about. The Camarilla was anxious about a vampire who flouted the Masquerade as openly as Angelus did, so it secretly supported or manipulated the organisations that hunted him. None of the hunters knew whose money they were spending.

In nine years of hunting he came close to his quarry more than once, but he never caught them.

Sahjhan

In 1773 a demon named Sahjhan offered him a way to outlive them, and Holtz accepted. He slept, untouched by the years, for more than two centuries. He woke in Los Angeles in 2001 to find that Angelus had become Angel, and he meant to have his revenge all the same.

Sahjhan believed he had woken Holtz for his own ends. The hand behind it was Jasmine's, working against God's purpose for Angel's son.

Steven

In February 2002 Holtz took the infant Connor and leapt with him into the hell dimension Quor-toth. There he raised the boy as his own son, Steven, to hate his father.

In May 2002, back in Los Angeles, Holtz arranged his own death so that Connor would believe Angel had killed him. At his request his young follower Justine Cooper killed him, leaving wounds in his neck like a vampire's bite.

pages.title: Dawn Summers
infobox: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Buffy vs. Dracula' (26 September 2000)
The Key, made into a living girl
pages.html:
Dawn Summers was the Key, an ancient energy that opens the walls between worlds, made into a living girl in 2000 by the monks who guarded it. The magic they used comes from the same root as the curse with which the Kalderash gave Angelus a new soul. In 1994 there was no Dawn Summers, although everyone who knew her afterwards would have sworn there was.

The Key

For ages the Key was kept by an order of monks. In 2000 the hell-god Glory came hunting for it. The last of the monks hid it by making it into a real person: a girl of about fourteen, sent to the Slayer, Buffy Summers, as her younger sister, for protection.

The monks shaped her out of Buffy herself, so that the two sisters truly shared one blood. Then they altered the memories of everyone around her. Her family and friends remembered Dawn as if she had always been there, born years before. She was not.

The same root

The monks' working is closely related to the curse with which the Kalderash clan bound Angelus in 1898. In both cases magic made something that had not existed before. In Dawn's case it was a whole person. In Angel's it was a new soul, in place of the one vampirism had destroyed.

Later life

Early in 2001 Joyce Summers died suddenly at home, and Buffy was left to bring her sister up. Later that year Glory used Dawn's blood to open the way between worlds. Buffy, who shared her blood, closed it by dying in her place.

Dawn grew up in Sunnydale. She remained with her sister after the town was destroyed in 2003.

pages.title: Buffy Summers
infobox: Joyce Summers (mother); Hank Summers (father); Dawn Summers (sister, from 2000)
pages.html:
Buffy Summers is a Los Angeles schoolgirl, born in January 1981, who was called in 1996 as the Slayer, the one girl of her generation chosen to fight vampires. In the early 1990s she was not yet the Slayer. In the summer of 1994 she is thirteen years old, and she has no idea of what is coming. Her years in Sunnydale, California, began in 1997.

Los Angeles

Buffy was born on 19 January 1981 to Joyce and Hank Summers. She grew up in Los Angeles, a popular, cheerful girl at Hemery High School with no interest whatever in the supernatural.

In 1996, aged fifteen, she was called as the Slayer. A Watcher named Merrick came to find her and train her. Merrick was killed. Buffy then burned down her school gymnasium, full of vampires at the time, and her parents' marriage broke up soon afterwards. In 1997 her mother moved with her to Sunnydale.

Sunnydale

Sunnydale stands over a Hellmouth. Her new Watcher, Rupert Giles, worked there as the librarian of her school. She found two friends there who stayed beside her through everything, Willow Rosenberg and Xander Harris.

In the spring of 1997 she destroyed the Master, the founder of the Aurelian line. He had fed on her first and left her to drown. She was dead for a short time before Xander revived her. Her brief death was enough to call the next Slayer, Kendra Young, so that for a while there were two.

She came to love Angel, the vampire with a soul. In 1998 she was forced to send him into a hell dimension to save the world.

Later years

In 2001 she died to save the world, and her sister Dawn with it. Later that year her friends brought her back.

In 2003 she led the fight in which Sunnydale was destroyed.

In the saga

From 1991 to 1995 Buffy was a girl in Los Angeles who knew nothing of what she would become. The Slayer whom Gilderoy Lockhart claimed in 1992 to have trained with was not Buffy. His claim was untrue in any case.

pages.title: Walter Bernhard
infobox: A castle in the Forest of Eternal Night
pages.html:
Walter Bernhard was a Tzimisce vampire of the eleventh century, lord of a castle in a forest of eternal night. In 1094, as Leon Belmont destroyed him, Mathias Cronqvist took his blood and soul with the Crimson Stone. Through that diablerie Mathias rose as the vampire who became Dracula.

Lord of the Forest of Eternal Night

Walter held the Ebony Stone, an alchemical stone that makes darkness. With it he kept his castle, and the forest around it, in endless night. It also made him all but invulnerable. He treated the hunting of mortals as a game. Challengers were allowed to come to his castle, so that he could play with them as a cat plays with mice.

He had killed the daughter of the alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi, who lived at the edge of the forest, to goad the old man into a duel. Rinaldo knew his limits and refused. Walter let him live, since an alchemist selling help to hunters only made the sport more amusing. Five guardians stood between any challenger and Walter's throne. One of them, the vampire Joachim Armster, was there as Walter's prisoner.

In 1094 Walter carried off Sara Trantoul, the betrothed of the knight Leon Belmont, and made her his prey. Leon came after her with a whip that Rinaldo had given him, which Sara's sacrifice turned into the Vampire Killer. With it he destroyed Walter. As Walter fell, the demon Death carried his soul to Mathias Cronqvist, Leon's friend, who had set the whole affair in motion. Mathias took Walter's blood and soul into the Crimson Stone.

Clan and generation

Walter was a Tzimisce. Mathias had been mortal and had no clan of his own, so he took Walter's. Walter was not of the third generation, and he was no Antediluvian. The Crimson Stone set Mathias at the fourth generation all the same, an exception to the ordinary rules of diablerie that nobody has ever explained. The Kindred have not forgotten that a mortal knight destroyed Walter, or what his blood became.

pages.title: The Crimson Stone
infobox: Turns the soul of a vampire into power for its holder
pages.html:
The Crimson Stone is the alchemical stone through which Mathias Cronqvist took the blood and soul of the vampire Walter Bernhard in 1094. With them he rose as the vampire who became Dracula. The Stone broke the ordinary rules of diablerie. Whatever Walter's own generation had been, it set Mathias at the fourth.

The two Stones

The Crimson Stone and its counterpart, the Ebony Stone, are works of alchemy. The Ebony Stone, which Walter Bernhard held, makes darkness. With it he kept his castle and the forest round it in eternal night. The Crimson Stone does something stranger: it turns the soul of a vampire into power for whoever holds it.

The alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi, who kept a cottage at the edge of Walter's forest, knew of both Stones and told Leon Belmont about them. He knew, too, that the Cronqvist family had been alchemists of note.

The night of Walter's destruction

Mathias Cronqvist arranged for his friend Leon Belmont to destroy Walter. As Walter fell, the demon Death carried his soul to Mathias, who was waiting in the throne room with the Stone. Through it Mathias took Walter's blood and soul into himself.

The act was diablerie, but not of any ordinary kind. A mortal cannot normally commit diablerie at all, and a vampire who does gains a single step in generation at most. Walter was not of the third generation. Yet the Stone set Mathias at the fourth, and gave him Walter's clan, the Tzimisce. How it did so has never been explained. No other such case is known.

The Stone's blood

The Stone went on breaking rules long after that night. By the laws of the blood only the thin-blooded, of the fifteenth generation or later, can father a child, and Dracula is of the fourth. All the same, the witch Lisa bore him a son, Alucard. Nothing about the blood the Crimson Stone gave has ever obeyed the rules, and Alucard is the proof of it.

pages.title: The Vampire Killer
infobox: Holy relic, bearing the soul of Sara Trantoul
Rinaldo Gandolfi; completed by the soul of Sara Trantoul
Answers freely only to Belmont blood
pages.html:
The Vampire Killer is the whip with which the Belmont family has hunted Dracula since 1094. About nine hundred years old, it passed through the hands of the Morris family in 1917 and 1944 before it came back to the Belmonts. In 1993 and 1994 it belonged to Julius Belmont. It is a holy relic, finished with the soul of Sara Trantoul, and its full power answers freely only to Belmont blood. Anyone else who calls on that power without first mastering the whip pays for it with his life.

How the whip was made

The whip began as the Whip of Alchemy, the work of the alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi. He gave it to Leon Belmont in 1094, when Leon went into the Forest of Eternal Night after his betrothed, Sara Trantoul. By the time Leon reached her, Sara had been bitten by the vampire Walter Bernhard and was already turning. Rinaldo told them that the whip could be made strong enough only if Sara died by Leon's hand. Rather than become one of Walter's kind, she chose death gladly. At her wish Leon struck her down. Her soul went into the whip and made it the Vampire Killer. Its first victim was Walter.

She had not yet been turned, so her soul was still hers to give. She gave it freely, so that Leon could destroy the creature that had taken her.

What it is

The Vampire Killer is a holy relic: a work of alchemy, finished by a soul freely given and made for the destruction of the undead. It does not merely cut the Kindred, as a blade would. It burns them, as holy things burn them, because the curse they carry was pronounced by God. In the hands of a Belmont with what the Kindred call True Faith, it is among the most dangerous weapons any mortal has ever carried against them. It has destroyed Dracula more often than anything else has.

Its power answers freely only to Belmont blood. To a Belmont it is a birthright, handed from parent to child along with the training that goes with it. The whip also holds a spirit of its own, the memory of the last true Belmont to have used it, and it tests anyone else who would take up its full power.

The cost to others

Anyone without Belmont blood who calls on the whip's full power, without first passing that test, pays for it with his life. The Morris family, the Belmonts' distant kin, learnt this when the whip came to them during the Belmonts' long absence in the nineteenth century. John Morris carried it in 1917. Wielding it without Belmont blood wore his life away, and he died of it some years after his victory.

His son Jonathan carried it in 1944, and he had to win its full power by facing the memory held in the whip itself. It met him in the shape of Richter Belmont, the last true Belmont to have used it before it left the family. Jonathan overcame it. The whip's power became his by right, and he was spared the price his father had paid.

Those who have carried it

The whip has passed from parent to child through every generation of the Belmonts. Each time Dracula returned, a Belmont carried it up the mountain to his castle. Leon Belmont carried it first, in 1094. The Belmonts of the next three and a half centuries carried it after him against the night. Few of their names are recorded. From 1450 the names are known. Sonia Belmont carried it that year, and her son Trevor from 1476 to 1479. Christopher fought with it in 1576 and 1591. Simon used it in 1691 and again in 1698. Juste, Simon's grandson, took it up in 1748. Richter carried it in 1792 and 1797.

When the Belmonts went missing for much of the nineteenth century, the whip came to the Morris family, their distant kin: John Morris carried it in 1917, and his son Jonathan in 1944. Afterwards it returned to the Belmonts. Julius Belmont held it in 1993 and 1994. He carried it in the Demon Castle War of 1999. In 2035 and 2036 he still had it. By then he had lost his memory, and went only by the name J.

In the saga

In September 1992 Hermione Granger told Harry Potter, with some emphasis, that the family who hunted Dracula had a whip. On Halloween that year Professor McGonagall mentioned her friend Julius, who had been in Transylvania for some years and always carried one.

pages.title: Demon Castle War
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
Julius Belmont and Alucard against Dracula
Dracula destroyed for good; his castle sealed inside a solar eclipse
Julius Belmont lost his memory; Dracula reborn as Soma Cruz, 2035
By priests of the Hakuba shrine, in the eclipse of 11 August 1999
pages.html:
The Demon Castle War of 1999 was the last of Dracula's returns. Julius Belmont, with Alucard beside him, destroyed Dracula for good, and the castle was sealed inside a solar eclipse. In the summer of 1994 the war is still five years off, though it is already brewing.

The war

Dracula had risen roughly once a century since 1094, and sooner whenever his followers could manage it. In 1999 his castle rose again. Julius Belmont, who held the Vampire Killer, went against it with Alucard, Dracula's dhampir son, who had fought his father in 1476 and 1797. Together they destroyed Dracula so completely that, for the first time in nine hundred years, he could not come back. His castle was then sealed away inside a solar eclipse, out of the world.

It was the end of the hunt that Leon Belmont had sworn in 1094. It cost Julius dearly. He came out of the war with no memory of who he was, except that his name began with J.

The war was fought in a year when the world was looking elsewhere. In 1999 the Kilaaks, an alien people, turned Godzilla loose on New York, with other monsters on Moscow, Beijing, London, Paris, then Tokyo. With six great cities burning, very few people noticed that a castle had risen.

The sealing was the work of priests from the Hakuba shrine in Japan. They shut the castle inside the eclipse of the sun that crossed Europe on 11 August 1999. The castle had always been the seat of Dracula's power, the reason he could return. Cut off from it, he could be destroyed like any other vampire. Julius did not go in alone: other hunters fought beside him, though few of their names are recorded.

Three children born on the day of Dracula's destruction grew up to claim his inheritance: Graham Jones, Dario Bossi and Dmitrii Blinov. A prophecy held that the true heir would come to the castle in 2035.

Aftermath

Dracula's power outlived him. At the first solar eclipse of the twenty-first century, in 2035, Soma Cruz, the young man in whom that power had been reborn, was drawn into the sealed castle. There he met Julius, still without his memory, and Alucard, under the name Genya Arikado. Julius knew himself again in the castle. Soma refused to become the Dark Lord, then and again in 2036.

In the saga

During the years 1991 to 1995 the war lay ahead. Julius Belmont held the Vampire Killer in 1993 and 1994. Professor McGonagall spoke of him as an old friend in October 1992.

pages.title: Leon Belmont
infobox: Walter Bernhard, Mathias Cronqvist (Dracula), the reaper Death
pages.html:
Leon Belmont was the first Belmont, a knight and baron of the late eleventh century. In 1094 he destroyed the vampire Walter Bernhard with the newly finished Vampire Killer. When his friend Mathias Cronqvist took Walter's soul and rose as the vampire who became Dracula, Leon swore the oath his family has kept ever since.

Knight and baron

Leon was a baron and a knight. In the Church's wars against heretics and heathens he was known as a man who feared nothing, whose skill at arms nobody in his company could match. His closest friend was the strategist Mathias Cronqvist, a man of rare learning, and the company the two of them led had never lost a battle. Leon was betrothed to Sara Trantoul.

In 1093, while Mathias was away on campaign, his wife Elisabetha fell ill and died. Mathias took to his sickbed, and for a year Leon kept the company together alone.

Sara Trantoul

In 1094 monsters began to appear in Leon's lands. The Church, intent on its war against the heathens, refused him leave to fight them. Then the vampire Walter Bernhard carried Sara off to his castle in the Forest of Eternal Night. Mathias rose from his sickbed to tell Leon who had taken her, and where. The Church would not release Leon from his duties to rescue her. He gave up his title instead, surrendering his sword with it, and went after her alone.

Rinaldo Gandolfi and Walter's castle

Past the barrier at the edge of the forest he met the alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi, an old man who kept a cottage there and sold help to the hunters who came. Walter had killed Rinaldo's daughter to goad him into a duel. Rinaldo, knowing his limits, had refused, and Walter let him live because supplying the hunters made his own sport more amusing. Rinaldo gave Leon a whip of alchemy in place of his surrendered sword. He enchanted Leon's gauntlet so that it could draw in the magic of his enemies, and he told him that the Cronqvists had been alchemists of note.

Walter played with hunters as a cat plays with mice. The Ebony Stone, an alchemical stone that makes darkness, kept his castle and forest in endless night. To reach his throne Leon had to defeat five guardians: a golem, the Medusa, a succubus, an undead parasite and the vampire Joachim Armster, whom Walter kept imprisoned. Rinaldo told him too of the Ebony Stone's counterpart, the Crimson Stone, which turns a vampire's soul into power for whoever holds it.

The Vampire Killer

Leon fought through Walter's castle and found Sara. He brought her back to Rinaldo's cottage, but she had already been bitten and was turning. Worse, his whip could not harm Walter. Rinaldo told him that it could be made strong enough only if Sara died by Leon's hand, so that her soul, which now held something of Walter in it, could join its power. Sara accepted, saying she would gladly become one with the whip if others might live. At her wish Leon struck her down, and she gave her soul to the whip, which became the Vampire Killer. With it Leon went back to the throne room and destroyed Walter.

Mathias and the oath

As Walter fell, the reaper Death carried his soul to Mathias, who stood in the throne room with the Crimson Stone. Mathias revealed that he had planned it all: he had set Leon against Walter to obtain Walter's soul. Now he took it with the Stone, and rose as a vampire to curse God for the death of his wife. He offered Leon eternity at his side, to curse God with him for Sara's loss. Leon refused: he had destroyed Walter so that others might live. Mathias left him to Death, which now served Mathias, and departed in the shape of a bat.

Death drew Leon into a realm of chaos. Leon beat it with the Vampire Killer, which can harm vampires and the things bound to them. Before it fled, he gave it a message for its master: Mathias had turned himself into a cursed being, and Leon would never forgive him. Then Leon swore that he and his descendants would hunt the night for ever. Every Belmont since has inherited that oath, and his whip with it.

Afterwards

Leon escaped the collapsing castle with a quiet resolve and an empty heart. When sunlight came through his windows, Rinaldo knew that Walter was gone. What became of Leon after 1094 is not recorded. Nor is the name of the wife through whom the family descends. The whip passed from him down the generations. In 1450 Sonia Belmont became the first of his descendants to face Mathias under the name Dracula. After her came Trevor, Christopher, Simon, Juste, Richter and, in the twentieth century, Julius.

Among the Kindred

Walter Bernhard was a Tzimisce, of the clan whose elders ruled lands in the East as lords. The Kindred remembered that a mortal knight had destroyed one of them. Leon had what the Kindred call True Faith, a faith strong enough to burn and repel the undead. He kept it even when his friend chose to curse God. Mathias, through the Crimson Stone, rose at the fourth generation against every rule of diablerie, and nobody has explained how. Sara had been bitten but not yet sired, so her soul was still hers to give. The whip has carried it ever since.

pages.title: Sonia Belmont
infobox: Dracula; Alucard, in a trial of her strength
A sense for spirits and unseen beings
pages.html:
Sonia Belmont was the first of the Belmont family to face Dracula under that name. She destroyed him at his castle in Transylvania in 1450, in her seventeenth year. She loved Dracula's son, Alucard, and not long afterwards she bore a son, Trevor, whom the Belmont chronicles hold to have been Alucard's child.

Birth and gift

Sonia was born into the Belmont family in the fifteenth century, more than three hundred years after Leon Belmont swore his oath. The Belmonts of those centuries kept the oath, and the whip with it, hunting the night as Leon had sworn they would. Little of their history is recorded, and none of them is known to have faced Mathias Cronqvist himself.

She was born with a gift: she could sense spirits, and the presence of beings that others could not see. In her seventeenth year the power in her grew, and she was told that it had been given to her for a purpose. Her grandfather raised her. He trained her with his whip, the Vampire Killer that had come down from Leon, and taught her to use her gift as a hunter.

Alucard

On her seventeenth birthday Sonia met Alucard, the dhampir son of Dracula and his wife Lisa, a witch. He had turned against his father after Lisa's death, and he was watching Dracula's preparations for war. The two grew close and became lovers. Alucard meant to destroy his father himself, even if it cost him his own life, and so stop the war that Dracula was readying against mankind. He tried to keep Sonia out of it. She would not be kept out.

The hunt of 1450

In 1450 Dracula's castle rose in Transylvania, and his monsters attacked the house where Sonia had grown up. Her grandfather was mortally wounded. Sonia took up his whip and went to the castle. On her way through it she recovered holy weapons her ancestors had left hidden there, among them an axe, a dagger, holy water and a cross. Her gift let her do something no Belmont before her is recorded to have done: she could take the spirit of each great creature she destroyed and turn its power against its master.

Alucard met her on the way and challenged her, to test whether she was strong enough for what lay ahead. She beat him. He accepted that the fight was hers to finish, sealed away his own power and withdrew to rest. The two of them parted in sorrow.

Sonia went on to Dracula and destroyed him on his throne. As he fell he swore that he would rise again for as long as evil remained in the world. She answered that there would always be someone ready to take up the fight against him. It was the first true defeat any Belmont had dealt him.

The birth of Trevor

Not long afterwards Sonia gave birth to a son, Trevor. The Belmont chronicles hold that his father was Alucard. Whatever his father's blood, Trevor was a mortal man who aged, bled and could be killed like any other, as every Belmont after him has been. What Sonia passed to him was the family's own inheritance: the whip, the training and the faith. Trevor destroyed Dracula in 1476, fighting at Alucard's side.

Exile

The family's strength had always unsettled its neighbours, and after 1450 it frightened them. The people of Wallachia were afraid of what the Belmonts could do, and of what might happen if their power were ever turned to ill. They drove the family out, and Trevor grew up in exile. When and where Sonia died is not recorded. The people who drove the Belmonts out called them back in 1476, when Dracula rose again and nobody else could stand against him.

Among the Kindred

Sonia fought fifteen years after the founding of the Camarilla, the sect that bound most of the Kindred of Europe to the Masquerade. Dracula ignored the Masquerade then, as he did at every return. The young sect had no wish to fight him itself, and was content to leave him to the Belmonts. To the Kindred Sonia was the kind of hunter they fear most: a mortal with a holy relic and a sight that found them wherever they hid. She had what they call True Faith as well, a faith strong enough to burn the undead or drive them back.

pages.title: Trevor Belmont
pages.html:
Trevor Belmont was the hunter who destroyed Dracula in 1476, when the vampire loosed his armies on Wallachia. He did not do it alone. Beside him were the sorceress Sypha Belnades, the pirate Grant DaNasty and Dracula's own son, Alucard, who by the Belmont chronicles was also Trevor's father. Trevor afterwards married Sypha, and every Belmont since descends from them both.

Birth and exile

Trevor was born soon after 1450 to Sonia Belmont, who that year had become the first of her family to face Dracula under that name. The Belmont chronicles hold that his father was Alucard, Dracula's dhampir son, whom Sonia loved. If so, nothing of it showed. Trevor was a mortal man in every respect, as all his descendants have been. He was brought up to the whip and to Leon Belmont's oath like every Belmont before him.

Before 1476 the Belmonts were driven out of Wallachia. The townsfolk of Warakiya, and of the country round about, were afraid of what the family could do. They feared still more what might happen if that strength were ever misused. So they asked the Belmonts to leave and never come back. The family went, resentful, and lived apart.

The war of 1476

In 1476 Dracula raised his armies of the dead and set out to destroy the land. Towns burned, and the undead walked across Wallachia. The Church found out that Dracula was behind it and sent its own forces against him. They failed. Then the Church called on Trevor, the only one left who could stand against him. He set out from Warakiya, the very town that had driven his family away.

On the road to the castle he met the three who would go with him. The first was Grant DaNasty, a pirate whose family Dracula had killed. Dracula's magic had turned him into a beast to guard the clock tower outside Warakiya. Trevor's whip broke the spell and gave Grant back his mind. In a graveyard Trevor found Sypha Belnades, a sorceress of the Church, whom a cyclops had ambushed and sealed in stone; he set her free. In the catacombs Alucard was waiting. He had sensed that his father was not finished, and he had sensed Trevor's power too. He tested Trevor in combat to see whether he could be trusted, and then joined him.

The four travelled on by land and by sea. They went through caverns, marshes and a sunken city, then up through the castle's clock tower to its keep. Dracula's servant Death met them on the way. At the top they found Dracula himself. He fought them first in his own shape, then in monstrous ones, and the four destroyed him together. In Wallachia Dracula was known as Vlad Tepes, the Impaler. The prince was reported dead at the end of that same year.

Afterwards

Trevor went home with his friends. The people who had once driven his family out now honoured it instead. Grant stayed on as Trevor's close friend and helped to rebuild Warakiya. Alucard spent a little time with them, then sealed himself away in sleep so that his father's blood in him could do the world no harm. Trevor married Sypha afterwards.

In 1479 he was still in the field. That was the year Dracula's lingering curse was broken by Hector, who had once been one of Dracula's Devil Forgemasters. Hector had come to the abandoned castle on the trail of his rival, Isaac. Trevor took him at first for a meddler, and fought him to test him. Then he believed Hector's account, and helped him break through a magically sealed passage to reach Isaac. When and how Trevor died is not recorded.

His descendants

From Trevor the Belmont line went on to Christopher, Simon, Juste, Richter and, in the twentieth century, Julius. His marriage to Sypha joined the Belnades gift for magic to the Belmont blood. Sypha's own family, the Belnades, went on producing witches who fought beside the Belmonts. A century after Trevor's war, his descendant Christopher Belmont faced Dracula in 1576.

The Church and the Kindred

The Church called on Trevor in 1476; it did not command him, and it has never commanded the family. The Society of Leopold, the Church's own hunters, honours the Belmonts and has never claimed authority over them. The Kindred saw the war differently. Dracula had broken the Masquerade in front of a whole country, and the Camarilla, which had no wish to fight him itself, was content to let the Belmonts deal with him. In Trevor they saw the kind of hunter they fear most: a mortal who carried a holy relic and had what they call True Faith. Faith of that kind is strong enough to burn and repel the undead.

pages.title: Sypha Belnades
pages.html:
Sypha Belnades was a sorceress who fought Dracula beside Trevor Belmont in 1476, and later became his wife. Her family, the Belnades, went on producing witches who fought beside the Belmonts for centuries after her.

The war of 1476

Sypha was a young sorceress in the service of the Church. She fought Dracula's creatures in Wallachia, hooded and robed. In 1476 a cyclops ambushed her in a graveyard and sealed her in stone. Trevor Belmont freed her on his way to the castle. She joined him, as did the pirate Grant DaNasty and Alucard.

Her spells were of fire, ice and lightning. It was her magic, together with Trevor's whip, that carried the four of them through the castle to Dracula, whom they destroyed together.

Marriage and descendants

She married Trevor after the war, joining the Belnades gift for magic to the Belmont line. Through the two of them that line went on. Every Belmont since has carried her blood, and in Juste Belmont, in 1748, it ran stronger than in any of the others.

Her own family went on too, as the Belnades. Among her kin are Carrie Fernandez, who fought Dracula in 1852, and the witch Yoko Belnades, who worked with Julius Belmont in the twenty-first century.

pages.title: Grant
pages.html:
Grant DaNasty was the pirate who fought Dracula alongside Trevor Belmont in 1476, with the sorceress Sypha Belnades and Dracula's own son, Alucard.

1476
