Dracula's armies had killed Grant's family, and he had taken them on alone. When Trevor found him he was under one of Dracula's spells. Trevor's whip broke it and gave him back his mind. Grant was nimble enough to climb walls like a spider, and he threw daggers with deadly aim. That year the Church had called the Belmonts back to the Wallachia that had driven them out, and the four of them destroyed Dracula together. Afterwards Grant stayed on as Trevor's friend and helped to rebuild Warakiya.

The spell had turned Grant into a beast, set to guard the clock tower outside Warakiya. He was the first of the three companions Trevor found. Sypha Belnades came next, freed from the stone in which a cyclops had sealed her, then Alucard, who was waiting in the catacombs.

pages.title: Hector
infobox: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness (PlayStation 2 and Xbox, November 2005)
pages.html:
Hector was a Devil Forgemaster, one of the men who forged demonic servants for Dracula. He turned against his master before the war of 1476. In 1479 Death and the rival Forgemaster Isaac tried to raise Dracula again. Hector destroyed what they raised, and broke the curse that had hung over the land since Dracula's defeat.

Forgemaster

A Devil Forgemaster is a mortal man who has mastered the dark art of forging Innocent Devils: demonic familiars that grow and change as they fight beside their master. Dracula had two Devil Forgemasters among the generals of his army, Hector and Isaac. Hector's Innocent Devils fought in its ranks.

In time he sickened of what his master did to mankind. Before the war of 1476 he left Dracula's service, gave up his powers and lived quietly among mortals. Dracula's defeat by Trevor Belmont that year left a curse behind it that spread across Europe, bringing plague, war and fear.

Rosaly

Living among mortals, Hector came to love a woman named Rosaly. Isaac had stayed loyal to Dracula, and he never forgave Hector for leaving. After the war, by Isaac's scheming, Rosaly was burned as a witch.

In 1479 Hector took up his forging again and went after Isaac. On his way he was helped by Julia Laforeze, a witch who lived in hiding from the witch-hunters. She looked startlingly like Rosaly.

The year 1479

Hector found that the demon Death, in the guise of a man named Zead, meant to raise Dracula through a living vessel. Death had wanted Hector for that vessel before it settled on Isaac. Trevor Belmont crossed Hector's path that year, and tested him.

In Dracula's own castle Hector brought Isaac down at last. Death then killed Isaac, and called Dracula into Isaac's body. Hector cut down what rose, and with a last forging he destroyed the essence of the curse itself. What became of him afterwards is not recorded.

Julia Laforeze was Isaac's sister. She helped Hector all the same, because she believed that Dracula's curse had hold of her brother. She warned Hector that it would take him too if he fought in anger. A stranger called Saint Germain, who could step through time, tried more than once to turn Hector from the chase. He warned him against Zead.

Trevor Belmont opened the sealed corridor beneath the abandoned castle for Hector, using his own blood. Isaac stabbed Trevor from behind for it. Julia's healing saved the Belmont's life. Hector's battle in the corridor fed a spell of Isaac's, which raised Dracula's castle anew. When Hector had Isaac beaten in its throne room he remembered Julia's warning, so he held his hand. Zead then showed himself as Death. The two Forgemasters had been meant to fight to the death, so that the winner, mad with blood, could serve as Dracula's vessel. Hector had refused the part, which left Isaac. When the curse was broken, Julia brought Hector out of the falling castle.

pages.title: Christopher Belmont
infobox: Dracula (1576 and 1591); his son Soleiyu, possessed by Dracula (1591)
pages.html:
Christopher Belmont destroyed Dracula twice. The first time, in 1576, the vampire cheated death by turning himself to mist. The second time, in 1591, Dracula had possessed Christopher's son, Soleiyu, and Christopher had to free his own son before he could destroy his family's old enemy again.

Family

Christopher descended from Trevor Belmont and Sypha Belnades. He was born into the family about a century after Trevor's war of 1476. By his time the Belmonts were exiles no longer: the people who had once driven them out of Wallachia had honoured them ever since Trevor's victory. Like every Belmont, Christopher was raised to the Vampire Killer, the family's holy weapons and Leon Belmont's oath. Little else of his early life is recorded.

1576

In 1576, a hundred years after Trevor's war, Dracula came back to make war on mankind again. Christopher took up the Vampire Killer to defend Transylvania, as his ancestors had done. He fought his way across the countryside into Dracula's castle, and at its summit he had the better of him. Just before the last blow, Dracula spent the last of his strength turning himself into mist. He left behind him every appearance of a vampire utterly destroyed.

Believing him gone, Christopher escaped from the collapsing castle. As was the family's custom, he watched it fall from a nearby clifftop. Once he had gone, Dracula took the shape of a bat and slipped away from the ruins.

The years between

Dracula came out of 1576 weaker than he had ever been. For fifteen years he stayed mostly in the form of mist, with no body of his own, until he had won back the power to possess one. Christopher, meanwhile, raised his son Soleiyu to be the next hunter. By 1591 Soleiyu had come of age. Christopher was ready to hand on to him the Vampire Killer, with the family's holy weapons, and the whole town prepared to celebrate.

1591

On the night before the ceremony Dracula came into Soleiyu's room as mist while he slept, and possessed him. Soleiyu's Belmont blood made him a powerful vessel. Through him Dracula took back a human form. With a gesture of his ring finger he conjured four castles to hold off the father who would come for his son: the Plant Castle, the Cloud Castle, the Rock Castle and the Crystal Castle.

Christopher was no longer young, but he went through all four and destroyed the guardian of each. He did not know that he was serving Dracula's plan. Dracula took the life of each fallen guardian, and with it he raised his own castle from the depths. Christopher climbed that castle too. At its height he found Soleiyu waiting in a hall hung with chandeliers. His son refused his embrace and challenged him to a fight to the death. Christopher fought him, holding back his blows, until he had beaten the last of Dracula out of him and Soleiyu came back to himself.

Christopher went on alone into the last part of the castle. Dracula was waiting there, restored to his true form, and Christopher destroyed him once more.

Afterwards

What became of Christopher after 1591 is not recorded. Nor is it known whether the ceremony at which Soleiyu was to receive the whip was ever held. The line went on. A century later, in 1691, Dracula's castle rose again, and Simon Belmont carried the Vampire Killer into it.

Among the Kindred

Dracula ignored the Masquerade at every return, and never more openly than in 1591, when four castles stood in plain sight across the land. The Camarilla had no wish to fight him itself. As in 1450 and 1476, it did nothing that is recorded, leaving him to the Belmonts. To the Kindred Christopher was the kind of hunter they fear most: a mortal with a holy relic and what they call True Faith, a faith strong enough to burn the undead or drive them back. In 1591 he showed something rarer still: the restraint to fight his own possessed son, driving the vampire out of him without killing him.

pages.title: Simon Belmont
infobox: Dracula (1691 and 1698); the reaper Death; the vampire Camilla
Destroying Dracula twice and breaking his curse
pages.html:
Simon Belmont faced Dracula twice. In 1691 he fought through the castle alone and destroyed him. In 1698 he gathered Dracula's scattered remains to break the curse he had taken in that first battle. He was the grandfather of Juste Belmont, who carried the Vampire Killer after him.

Family

Simon was born into the Belmont family in the second half of the seventeenth century. He descended from Leon Belmont, who swore the family's oath in 1094, through Trevor Belmont and the sorceress Sypha Belnades. He descended too from Christopher Belmont, who had destroyed Dracula in 1576 and again in 1591. Like every Belmont he was raised to Leon's oath, trained from boyhood to the whip and the family's other weapons. The Vampire Killer came down to him as the heir of his generation.

In his time the family lived in Transylvania, and its dead lay buried there. For a hundred years after Christopher's victory of 1591, Dracula did not come back.

1691

In 1691 the village was keeping the Easter festival when evil men gathered in a monastery at its edge to hold a black mass. Dracula rose again, and his castle with him. Simon took up the Vampire Killer and went in alone. He carried holy water as well, with crosses, axes and daggers. He fought through the castle's halls, galleries, catacombs and dungeons against the creatures that served it. There was a great vampire bat in the first of its halls, then a gorgon, then a pair of mummies. After them came a giant made of dead men's parts, with a hunchbacked servant at its side. Last of all came the reaper Death, Dracula's own servant.

He destroyed Dracula at the top of the castle. When the vampire's first shape fell, he rose again in a monstrous second one, and Simon destroyed that too. In the battle Dracula laid a curse on him: a wound that would not heal, and that was slowly killing him. The castle fell to ruin as Simon left it.

1698

Seven years later Simon had not long to live. The curse was spreading, and the country round the castle ruins was sliding into fear. Dracula's evil had outlived him in the land. By night the dead walked and overran the villages, whose people kept behind their doors until morning.

Simon went to visit his family's grave. At the cemetery a young woman came to him and told him what he must do. After his fall Dracula's body had been divided into five parts: his rib, heart, eye, nail and ring. They had been hidden in mansions across Transylvania, and only by gathering them could the curse be broken. Simon must bring them to the ruins of the castle, raise Dracula there and destroy him again. She warned him that even this might not be Dracula's end.

Simon went from town to town, through Jova, Veros, Aljiba, Alba, Ondol, Doina and Yomi. From the merchants he bought holy water, garlic, laurels and, where they could be had, finer whips. He learnt, too, that the townspeople's advice was often false. He found the five mansions: Berkeley, Rover, Brahm, Bodley and Laruba. From each he took the relic it held. In Brahm's mansion he destroyed the reaper Death and took Dracula's eye, which showed him what had been hidden. In Laruba's he destroyed the vampire Camilla and took the ring. Each relic served him once it was his. The rib, for one, turned aside the missiles thrown at him.

With all five parts in hand, together with a holy cross he had found on the way, he passed the barrier before the ruins of the castle and burned the remains there. Dracula rose from the fire. Simon destroyed him again, and with that he was freed of the curse.

Afterwards

Simon survived the curse, and Dracula himself did not rise again for almost a century, until 1792. The Vampire Killer passed down Simon's line to his grandson, Juste Belmont. In 1748 Juste faced a revenant raised from the relics of Dracula's body, the same remains that Simon had gathered half a century before.

Among the Kindred

Simon's two victories show why the Kindred have always feared the Belmonts above other mortal hunters: the family has a relic made for the work, and its best members have what the Kindred call True Faith, a faith strong enough to burn the undead or drive them back. The victories show, too, what Dracula's blood is. Every vampire's curse comes down from Cain, and Dracula, of the fourth generation, stands near its source. The wound he gave Simon worked on him for seven years like a slow poison. The parts of his body kept enough of his power after his destruction to raise him in 1698, and to trouble Simon's grandson fifty years later.

pages.title: Juste Belmont
infobox: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance (Game Boy Advance, June 2002)
Spells joined to his sacred weapons, from his Belnades blood
The reaper Death; the possessed Maxim; a revenant of Dracula raised from his relics
pages.html:
Juste Belmont, the grandson of Simon Belmont, carried the Vampire Killer in 1748. That year his friend Maxim Kischine came home wounded, with no memory of where he had been, and their childhood friend Lydie Erlanger was carried off. Juste went into a castle that the relics of Dracula's body had raised. There he saved them both, and destroyed a revenant of Dracula.

Birth and family

Juste was born in the early eighteenth century, the grandson of Simon Belmont, who had destroyed Dracula in 1691 and 1698. He was raised to Leon Belmont's oath, as every Belmont has been since 1094, and he received the Vampire Killer at sixteen. By his time the people of the villages looked on the Belmonts as heroes, and Juste grew up among them.

Every Belmont since Trevor has carried the blood of Sypha Belnades, the sorceress Trevor married after the war of 1476. In Juste it ran stronger than in any of them. He had the Belnades gift for magic as well as the Belmont strength. He learnt spells from books of magic, and he could join them to the axe, the cross, holy water or any of the family's other sacred weapons, so that each struck with the spell's force as well as its own.

He grew up with two close friends. Maxim Kischine trained beside him, and was his rival as well as his friend. Lydie Erlanger had been the friend of both since they were children.

Maxim

Maxim was not a Belmont, and he could not wholly bear to stand second to one. Two years before 1748 he set out on his own to prove himself. He went looking for the relics of Dracula's body, meaning to find them and destroy them as Simon had done. He gathered all six pieces, and after that he remembered nothing. The relics woke an evil spirit in him, born of their power and of a jealousy of Juste that Maxim had kept hidden even from himself. From then on two spirits shared his body.

The castle of 1748

In 1748 Maxim came back, badly hurt and unable to remember where he had been. He told Juste that Lydie had been taken. The two of them went to the castle that had appeared, which the relics had raised. It stood in two layers on the same ground, each the mirror of the other, so as to hold the two spirits in Maxim's body. Juste crossed between them as he searched. Maxim came and went within it, sometimes Juste's friend, sometimes something else that turned on him. In time he confessed that it was he who had carried Lydie off.

The reaper Death, Dracula's servant, held Lydie in the castle. It meant to use her blood to make the two castles one, destroying Maxim's own spirit so that the evil one would have his body to itself. Juste fought his way through both castles and destroyed Death. But Lydie was carried off again. He searched on for her and for Maxim, gathering the scattered relics of Dracula's body as he went.

Maxim and the revenant

He found them at last. Maxim was wholly in the grip of the evil spirit, and Juste had to fight his friend. Juste was wearing Maxim's bracelet. When Maxim saw it, the sight helped him resist the possession and come back to himself. What had held him was not destroyed, however. From the relics rose a revenant of Dracula, a weakened shape of the vampire himself, and Juste destroyed it with the Vampire Killer. He escaped the castle with Maxim and Lydie. The bite marks on Lydie faded, and the three of them went home together.

Afterwards

Dracula himself did not rise again until 1792, when Richter Belmont faced him.

Among the Kindred the affair of 1748 is a lesson in what the remains of an elder can do. Maxim never drank Dracula's blood, and he was neither vampire nor ghoul. Yet the relics alone mastered him, and raised a castle about him. Juste's answer to them was the one his family has always given: the Vampire Killer, the faith that goes with it, and the blood that lets a Belmont use them both.

pages.title: Richter Belmont
infobox: Akumajō Dracula X: Chi no Rondo (Rondo of Blood, PC Engine CD, 29 October 1993)
Dracula; the priest Shaft; the reaper Death
pages.html:
Richter Belmont destroyed Dracula in 1792, when the dark priest Shaft revived him and carried off Richter's beloved, Annette. Four years later Richter himself vanished. In 1797 he was found enthroned in Dracula's castle as its puppet lord, and it was Alucard who set him free.

Birth and family

Richter was born in about 1773, the Belmont of his generation and heir to the Vampire Killer. He was raised to Leon Belmont's oath, as all his family were. He grew into one of the most gifted hunters the Belmonts have ever had: quick, acrobatic, and able to loose the whole holy power of a sacred weapon in a single great blow. He loved Annette, a girl of seventeen from the country near Dracula's castle.

1792

For a century Dracula's worshippers had gathered in secret. In 1792 a cult led by the priest Shaft raised him, and his servants took a number of young women from the villages near the castle. Among them were Annette, whom Richter loved; a girl of twelve named Maria Renard, a distant relative of the Belmonts; Tera, a nun of the village church; and Iris, the doctor's daughter.

Richter, then nineteen, went into the castle with the Vampire Killer. He met the reaper Death on the road through the woods, and fought on through the ruins of a burning village, where a wyvern attacked him, to the entrance of the castle. Inside, he fought his way through the chapel, where a minotaur waited, then the inner corridors, the clock tower and the halls of Dracula's guardians. He rescued the captives one by one, Maria among them. Child as she was, Maria was a fierce fighter, and once freed she joined him. Richter faced Shaft, then Dracula himself at the top of the castle, and destroyed him. Shaft's body perished, but his spirit did not. Afterwards Richter married Annette.

1797

In 1796 Richter disappeared. When the castle rose again the next year, it was found to have a new lord: Richter, held under Shaft's control and made to serve Dracula's return. Maria Renard, now grown, came to the castle in search of him. Alucard, woken from his long sleep by the castle's rising, came to it as well.

Alucard and Maria fought their way to him. Maria gave Alucard a pair of holy spectacles that let him see past illusions. Through them he saw the green orb hanging over Richter, in which Shaft's spirit held him. Alucard broke Shaft's hold by destroying the orb rather than the man. With Richter freed, a second castle appeared above the first, inverted in the sky. In it Alucard went on to destroy Shaft, and then Dracula. Richter left the castle a free man.

Afterwards

Richter was the last Belmont to carry the Vampire Killer before the family went missing for much of the nineteenth century. Others fought Dracula in those years: Nathan Graves, Shanoa of the Order of Ecclesia, Cornell, Reinhardt Schneider and Carrie Fernandez. The whip passed to the Morris family, the Belmonts' distant kin. When Jonathan Morris won its full power in 1944, he had to overcome the spirit held in the whip. It met him in the shape of Richter, the last true Belmont to have used it. The whip came back to the Belmonts in the twentieth century, and Julius Belmont carried it in the Demon Castle War of 1999.

Among the Kindred

Shaft was no vampire. He was a mortal priest who had given himself to Dracula, and through Dracula to the Devil, whose property every vampire is. The Kindred call such servants infernalists. His spirit served on after his body died. The years 1792 and 1797 showed that Dracula's worshippers could be as dangerous to the Belmonts as Dracula himself. In five years Shaft raised him twice, and the second time he turned the Belmont of the day into his tool.

pages.title: Nathan Graves
pages.html:
Nathan Graves was the young vampire hunter who faced Dracula in 1830, when Dracula's servant Camilla raised him in a castle in Austria. Nathan destroyed him, and he rescued his own teacher, Morris Baldwin, whom Dracula had meant to use to restore his strength.

1830

Morris had trained Nathan alongside his own son, Hugh. When he chose Nathan, not Hugh, to carry the Hunter Whip, Hugh could not forgive it. In the castle Dracula turned that jealousy against Nathan, who brought Hugh back to himself. The Belmonts were missing in those years, and Nathan fought in their place.

About ten years earlier Morris Baldwin had fought Dracula beside Nathan's parents. Dracula was sealed away, but Nathan's parents died in the fight. Baldwin brought the boy up as his own, training him beside Hugh for the day the seal should fail.

It failed in 1830. In an old castle on the edge of the Austrian Empire the vampire Camilla held the rite that woke Dracula. Baldwin arrived with his two pupils as it ended. Dracula knew the man who had sealed him. He broke open the floor under the two young men, who fell into the catacombs. Baldwin he kept, meaning to spend the hunter's life at the next full moon to make himself whole.

Hugh went off alone to save his father, telling Nathan to keep out of his way. Nathan climbed through the castle by himself. He destroyed Camilla in the waterway beneath it. Near the top Hugh attacked him, his old jealousy swollen by Dracula into hatred, so Nathan had to beat his friend to free him. Hugh came to himself. He admitted that he had doubted his own worth ever since his father's choice, then asked Nathan to save Baldwin.

Nathan fought Dracula in the ceremonial room while Hugh got his father away. Then he followed the vampire into the dark to destroy him at his full strength. The castle fell. Baldwin told Nathan that he was a master hunter now, while Hugh went back to his training.

pages.title: Shanoa
pages.html:
Shanoa was a sorceress of the Order of Ecclesia, one of several bodies founded in the nineteenth century to stand against Dracula while the Belmonts were missing. In the end she destroyed him herself, after she learnt that her own Order meant to bring him back.

Dominus

Ecclesia's leader, Barlowe, had made a weapon out of Dracula's own power, the glyph called Dominus, and he chose Shanoa to bear it. Her fellow acolyte Albus stole it before the rite could be finished. When the rite was broken off she lost her memory, along with every feeling she had. She learnt at last that Barlowe meant to sacrifice her to raise Dracula, not to destroy him. She destroyed Dracula herself, and her feelings came back to her.

Barlowe sent her after Albus to bring Dominus back. The trail led to the village of Wygol, which she found empty. Albus had carried off its people, shutting them away in hiding places across the country. Shanoa freed them one by one. They told her that he had been taking their blood.

Dominus was in three parts: Anger, Hatred and Agony. Twice Albus let Shanoa catch him, each time handing her one of them. The third he kept too long. It mastered him, so she had to kill him. As he died his spirit passed into her with the glyph, where it told her the truth. Dominus takes the life of whoever uses it, which was why Albus had stolen it from her. The villagers of Wygol were descendants of the Belmonts. He had hoped that their blood would let him master the glyph in her place.

Shanoa went back to Barlowe, who dropped the pretence. Ecclesia guarded the vessel that held Dracula's soul. Dominus was the key to its seal, with Shanoa the sacrifice that would turn it. She defeated him. He gave his own life to break the seal instead, so Dracula's castle rose.

She climbed it, then destroyed Dracula with all three parts of Dominus joined. It should have killed her. The glyph asks only one life, however, so Albus's spirit gave itself in her place. He asked her to smile for him before he went. She found that she could. Nothing more is recorded of the Order of Ecclesia.

pages.title: Cornell
pages.html:
Cornell was a man-beast, able to take the shape of a wolf, who fought Dracula's servants in 1844. That year they were working to raise their master again. They burnt Cornell's village and carried off his sister, Ada.

1844

Cornell went after her into Dracula's castle and brought her out alive. The Belmonts were missing in those years, and others fought Dracula in their place.

Cornell was one of a clan of man-beasts. In 1844 he came home from a long spell of training to find his village burnt. Three of Dracula's servants were behind it: the demon Death, the witch Actrise and the vampire Gilles de Rais, who needed a sacrifice to raise their master.

The one who had set the fire was Ortega, a man-beast like himself, once his friend. Ortega had lost to Cornell in a contest of strength, then gone over to Dracula for the power to win the next one. On the way to the castle Cornell came to the villa of the Oldrey family, whose master Gilles de Rais had sired. Mary Oldrey begged him to save her small son, Henry, which he did.

At the top of the castle Ortega fought him in the shape of a chimera, with Dracula's strength behind him, yet lost again. Cornell beat Dracula too. As Dracula fell he dragged Ada down with him, shut in a crystal. Cornell tore his own wolf-shape out of himself, hurling it at the crystal to break it. He came out of the castle with Ada in his arms, an ordinary man for the rest of his life.

That had been the plan from the start. It was Cornell's power the three had wanted for their sacrifice, never Ada. With it they brought Dracula to birth again in a human child. Henry Oldrey grew up to be a knight of the Church. In 1852 he went back to the castle to bring out the children whom Dracula's servants had stolen.

pages.title: Reinhardt Schneider
infobox: The Schneiders, distant kin of the Belmonts
A whip and a short sword
Dracula, reborn in the boy Malus, 1852
pages.html:
Reinhardt Schneider was a vampire hunter of the Schneider family, distant kin of the Belmonts. In 1852 he fought Dracula with the young sorceress Carrie Fernandez, and the two of them destroyed him in the body of the boy Malus, in whom he had been reborn.

1852

The Belmonts themselves were missing for much of the nineteenth century, so others had to take their place. Reinhardt fought as his Belmont kinsmen did, with a whip, though he carried a short sword as well. In 1852 Dracula had been reborn in the body of a boy, Malus. Reinhardt and Carrie saw through him. Together they destroyed him.

At the villa below the castle Reinhardt met an old hunter named Charlie Vincent, who meant to destroy Dracula himself. He met a boy called Malus, who said that Dracula's creatures had killed his family. In the villa's rose garden he met Rosa, a young woman who had been bitten against her will. She would not come near him for fear of what she was becoming.

Deeper in the castle Rosa tried to end her life by walking into the sun. Reinhardt stopped her. Dracula's servant Death then set her on him, so he had to fight her. At the top of the clock tower, when Death swung at Reinhardt's back, Rosa stepped into the blow. Reinhardt put a cross in her hand, telling her that God forgives everything. Then he destroyed Death.

The vampire he found in the keep was only a servant playing Dracula's part. The real one was Malus, who showed himself on the tower as a grown man. When Reinhardt had beaten him he became a frightened child again, with no memory of any of it. Charlie Vincent arrived at that moment to throw holy water over the boy, which burnt him. Malus carried Reinhardt off to a desert place outside the world. There he fought in his true shape, a dragon, until Reinhardt destroyed him.

Afterwards Rosa was given back to Reinhardt alive, free of the bite.

pages.title: Carrie Fernandez
infobox: The Belnades line of Sypha Belnades
Dracula, reborn in the boy Malus, 1852
pages.html:
Carrie Fernandez was a girl of the Belnades blood, the line of the sorceress Sypha Belnades. In 1852, at the age of twelve, she fought Dracula beside the vampire hunter Reinhardt Schneider.

1852

The Belmonts were missing for much of the nineteenth century, and others fought Dracula in their place. In 1852 he had been reborn in the body of a boy, Malus, who first appeared to his hunters as a lost child in need of rescue. Carrie and Reinhardt saw through him. Together they destroyed him. She fought with sorcery, as Sypha had done nearly four hundred years before.

In the castle the witch Actrise, who had sacrificed children to bring Dracula back, tried to win Carrie to her master's side. Carrie refused. Actrise then set a vampire on her who had once been a warrior of the Fernandez family, Carrie's own kin, whom Carrie had to destroy. Later, at the top of one of the castle's towers, she destroyed Actrise as well.

Like Reinhardt, she was deceived for a while by the boy Malus, until the old hunter Charlie Vincent unmasked him with holy water. When it was over Carrie laid flowers on her stepmother's grave.

pages.title: John Morris
infobox: The Morris family, distant kin of the Belmonts
pages.html:
John Morris was an American vampire hunter of the Morris family, distant kin of the Belmonts. He carried the Vampire Killer in 1917. That year, with Eric Lecarde beside him, he hunted down Dracula's niece, who was raising her uncle through the slaughter of the Great War, and destroyed them both.

The hunt of 1917

John's father, Quincy Morris, died destroying Dracula in 1897. The Belmonts were missing for much of the nineteenth century, so the whip passed to the Morrises. In 1917 Elizabeth Bartley, Dracula's niece, set about raising him again through the bloodshed of the war that was tearing Europe apart. John took up the whip. Eric Lecarde fought beside him with a spear, and together they hunted her across Europe, from the ruins of Dracula's castle in Romania to Castle Proserpina in England. They destroyed Elizabeth, and Dracula with her.

John was born in Texas on 12 December 1895, so he was not yet two when his father died. Elizabeth Bartley had been put to death as a vampire long before. A witch named Drolta Tzuentes brought her back, by a spell she barely understood. A strange woman was seen in the shadows of the plot at Sarajevo in June 1914, when the Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot. The hunters believed that it was Elizabeth, who wanted the war for the sake of its dead.

The hunt began in the ruins of Dracula's castle in Romania. It went on through Greece to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, a munitions factory in Germany and the palace of Versailles, all in the middle of the war. It ended at Castle Proserpina in England, where Elizabeth had finished her rite before the hunters reached her. They destroyed her, then Dracula as he rose.

The cost

The full power of the Vampire Killer answers freely only to Belmont blood. John had not first mastered the whip, so wielding it wore his life away. He died of it some years after his victory. His son Jonathan carried the whip in 1944.

pages.title: Eric Lecarde
pages.html:
Eric Lecarde was a young Spaniard from Segovia who fought Dracula in 1917 beside John Morris, the son of Quincy Morris. He fought with a spear, the Alucard Spear.

1917

That year Dracula's niece, Elizabeth Bartley, tried to raise him through the slaughter of the Great War. The hunt for her ran across Europe, from the ruins of Castle Dracula through Greece, Italy, Germany and France to a castle in England. There John Morris, carrying the Vampire Killer, destroyed Dracula with Eric beside him.

Eric was born at Segovia on 3 May 1892. His quarrel with Elizabeth Bartley was his own: she had sired Gwendolyn, the woman he loved.

Death and daughters

Eric lived to see the next war. In 1944 Dracula's castle rose again, so he went to find out who had raised it. The vampire painter Brauner killed him there. Before he died Eric cast a spell that kept his spirit in the castle, free of its master's control.

His twin daughters, Stella and Loretta, came looking for him. Brauner bound them to himself with his blood, keeping them as daughters of his own. When Jonathan Morris came to the castle with Charlotte Aulin, Eric met them at the gate as a ghost who gave his name as Wind. He taught them what he knew. In time he told them who he was, though he asked that his daughters should not be told he lingered.

Charlotte's spell freed the twins, who then worked the rite that called up the memory in the Vampire Killer for Jonathan to face. When Dracula had fallen Eric showed himself to his daughters once, to say goodbye. Then he went to his rest.

pages.title: Jonathan Morris
infobox: The Morris family, distant kin of the Belmonts
pages.html:
Jonathan Morris was the son of John Morris, and a vampire hunter of the Morris family, distant kin of the Belmonts. He carried the Vampire Killer in 1944, in the middle of the Second World War. With the young sorceress Charlotte Aulin beside him, he fought his way through Dracula's castle, which the vampire painter Brauner had seized.

1944

That year Dracula's castle rose again, but its master was Brauner, who meant to draw strength from the slaughter of the war. He hated humankind, and he worked through painted worlds of his own making. Death, Dracula's servant, meanwhile worked to bring its own master back. Jonathan and Charlotte went into the castle together. Among Brauner's servants they found Stella and Loretta, the twin daughters of Eric Lecarde. Brauner had bitten them both, then bound them to himself with his blood to keep as his own. Jonathan and Charlotte set the two girls free. Brauner fell. At the last they faced Dracula himself, with Death at his side, and overcame them both. Dracula was destroyed once more.

The castle stood in lands the Axis held. The Spear of Destiny kept the mightiest heroes of the Allies out of such country. The Invaders were fighting in the west that year. The Church, which sent Jonathan, told nobody else. He was eighteen.

At the gate a ghost who called himself Wind offered to teach the two of them. He was Eric Lecarde, John Morris's old companion, whom Brauner had killed. From him Jonathan learnt why his father had never trained him to the whip. A man without Belmont blood who draws on its full power pays for it with his life, as John had.

Brauner did not want Dracula back. He had sealed the throne room with his paintings so that the castle's power would be his alone. Death, which wanted its master, cut Brauner down as soon as the two hunters had beaten him. That broke the seal. Dracula then took Death's power into his own, which did not save either of them.

The whip

Jonathan was not a Belmont, and his father had never taught him the secret of the whip. To win its full power without paying for it with his life, Jonathan had to pass the test of the memory held inside it. It met him in the shape of Richter Belmont, the last true Belmont to have used it. Jonathan beat him, and the whip was his. Afterwards the Vampire Killer came back to the Belmonts.

pages.title: Charlotte Aulin
pages.html:
Charlotte Aulin was a young sorceress who fought Dracula in 1944, in the middle of the Second World War, beside her childhood friend Jonathan Morris.

1944

That year the vampire painter Brauner had seized Dracula's castle, while Dracula's servant Death worked to raise his master again. Charlotte fought with spells, Jonathan with the Vampire Killer. Together they went through the painted worlds Brauner had made inside the castle. In the end they destroyed Death and Dracula together. She was quick, clever and sharp-tongued. She bickered with Jonathan the whole way.

Charlotte's part was the one that could not have been done with a whip. Stella and Loretta Lecarde, the daughters of Eric Lecarde, were in Brauner's keeping, bound to him by his blood, believing him their father. Charlotte searched the castle until she found a spell of sanctuary, which lifts curses. With it she broke his hold on both of them. She used the same spell on Vincent Dorin, the priest who had come with the two hunters, when a vampire bit him.

pages.title: Soma Cruz
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
Dominance: taking the souls and powers of monsters
Mina Hakuba, Genya Arikado (Alucard), Julius Belmont, Yoko Belnades
Graham Jones; Celia Fortner, Dario Bossi and Dmitrii Blinov
pages.html:
Soma Cruz is the young man in whom Dracula's power was reborn after the vampire's final destruction in the Demon Castle War of 1999. In 2035 and 2036 he twice refused to become the Dark Lord.

2035

Soma was born long after Dracula's fall, and he grew up knowing nothing of what he carried. In 2035 he was an eighteen-year-old exchange student in Japan. On the day of the first solar eclipse of the century he was visiting a shrine with his friend Mina Hakuba, the shrine-keeper's daughter. The two of them were drawn into Dracula's castle, which had been sealed inside the eclipse since 1999.

There Soma found that he could take the souls of the monsters he destroyed, and use their powers. He met Genya Arikado, who was Alucard, and a man with no memory called J, who was Julius Belmont. Others had come to the castle for reasons of their own. Graham Jones, a missionary, believed that he himself was Dracula reborn, since he had been born on the day of Dracula's destruction. Yoko Belnades, a witch of the Church, had come to stop him. A soldier called Hammer set up shop inside the castle walls and sold Soma what he needed.

Soma learned that it was he, not Graham, who was Dracula reborn, and that the power of dominance was his inheritance. When Graham tried to take that power for himself, Soma destroyed him. Then he refused his inheritance, and went instead into the heart of the castle, where he destroyed the chaos from which Dracula's power had always come.

2036

In 2036 a cult led by Celia Fortner tried to force the Dark Lord awake in him. Celia had two candidates of her own for Dracula's throne, Dmitrii Blinov and Dario Bossi. To break Soma's will, she had a false Mina, a doppelganger, killed in front of him. A talisman the real Mina had given him helped him see through the trick. He refused a second time, with help from Arikado, Julius and Yoko Belnades. In the depths of the castle he destroyed Menace, the monster that Dmitrii had become.

Dario Bossi's command of fire came from Aguni, a demon bound to his soul. Soma passed through a mirror to destroy the demon, which left Dario powerless. Dmitrii Blinov was more dangerous, for he could copy any power he had met, Soma's included. At the bottom of the castle he sacrificed Celia herself to seal Arikado's strength, but the souls he had taken were more than he could hold. They tore out of him, becoming Menace. Julius Belmont had spent the last of his strength breaking the barrier that guarded the way down, so Soma faced it alone.

pages.title: Amenti
infobox: Ma'at, the order of truth and justice
Weighing the hearts of intruders in the tombs
pages.html:
An Amenti is one of the risen dead of Egypt, a servant of Ma'at, the order of truth and justice that the old Egyptians held sacred. Amenti keep watch in the tombs. To any intruder they administer the weighing of the heart against the feather of Ma'at.

The weighing

In the old Egyptian judgement of the dead, the heart was laid in the scales against a single feather of Ma'at. The Amenti carry that judgement on in the tombs, for everyone who goes in uninvited. They ask whether the intruder has lived with a true heart, what he has done with the years given him, and whether he is ready to have his heart weighed. The lucky ones are only asked questions.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Four, at the Leaky Cauldron on 31 August 1993, George Weasley told Harry Potter that the twins had tried to shut Percy in a pyramid that summer in Egypt. 'Very nearly worked, too,' said Fred. 'Got him through the door and everything.' There had been a thing in there, all bandages. It sat up on its slab and asked Percy whether he had lived with a true heart. 'And Percy answered,' said George. 'For about ten minutes. With examples.' 'It lay back down,' said Fred. 'I think it'd rather have had the eternal dark.' Bill had told them afterwards that it did that to everyone who went in uninvited. They were lucky, he said, that it had only asked questions, because most people came out of there a lot quieter than they went in. Then Mrs Weasley had arrived.

pages.title: The mummy who questioned Percy
infobox: Amenti, a risen servant of Ma'at
Percy Weasley, in the summer of 1993
pages.html:
The mummy who questioned Percy is the bandaged guardian of a pyramid in Egypt. In the summer of 1993 it sat up on its slab to ask Percy Weasley whether he had lived with a true heart, and whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. Percy answered it for about ten minutes. Then it lay back down.

An Amenti

It is no ordinary cursed corpse. It is an Amenti, one of the risen dead who serve Ma'at, the old Egyptian law of truth and right order. In questioning Percy it was simply doing its job.

Its questions are those of the weighing of the heart, the judgement of the dead, in which a heart is set in the scales against the feather of Ma'at. Bill Weasley, who breaks curses in the Egyptian tombs for Gringotts, knows that it puts them to everybody who goes in uninvited. He does not know why.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Four, at the Leaky Cauldron in August 1993, Fred and George told Harry how they had tried to shut Percy in a pyramid. They had got him through the door, but there was something inside, all bandages. It sat up on its slab. Then it asked Percy whether he had lived with a true heart, what he had done with the years given him and whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. ‘And Percy answered,’ said George. ‘For about ten minutes. With examples.’ ‘It lay back down,’ said Fred. ‘I think it’d rather have had the eternal dark.’

Bill had told them that they were lucky it had only asked questions. Most people, he said, came out of there a good deal quieter than they went in. Then Mrs Weasley had arrived.

pages.title: Giza
infobox: West bank of the Nile, near Cairo, Egypt
Dr Daniel Jackson, August 1994 (a cover story)
pages.html:
Giza is the plateau on the west bank of the Nile, near Cairo, where the Great Pyramid stands. The Stargate was dug up there in 1928. In August 1994 the Egyptologist Daniel Jackson was declared dead after a shaft beneath the plateau was said to have collapsed.

History

The plateau holds the three great pyramids, the Sphinx and the tombs about them. Egypt was the old seat of Ra, the Goa'uld who ruled the country as its sun god. The Great Pyramid was built in the likeness of the landing places of his ships. When his slaves rose against him at last, they buried his Stargate at Giza.

Thor, the son of Odin, had fought beside the Egyptians in the rising that buried it.

In 1928 an expedition under Professor Paul Langford uncovered the gate beneath the plateau. With it lay its carved cover stones and an amulet bearing the Eye of Ra, which Langford's daughter Catherine kept. The gate was shipped to the United States in 1939, out of reach of Germany.

Egypt is the oldest country in the world, and the least safe. Giza is no exception. As the heir of Stygia, Egypt passed every dark art on to Europe. The dead are weighed there against the feather of Ma'at, and it was out of Egypt's sand that the gate came.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: on 20 August 1994 the Muggle news reported that the American Egyptologist Dr Daniel Jackson, aged twenty-nine, had been declared dead after an accident at an excavation near Giza. Egyptian officials said that he had been working in a shaft beneath the plateau when it collapsed. His body was not recovered. The same report recalled the lecture he had given earlier that year, arguing that the Great Pyramid was not built by the pharaohs of the Fourth Dynasty at all.

Book Four, Chapter Four: at the Burrow the next day Bill Weasley said that American soldiers had been all over the plateau since the spring. Since the Muggle accident down a shaft, he added, the goblins would not go anywhere near the place.

The accident is a cover story. Jackson went through the Stargate to Abydos that year, and he stayed there.

pages.title: The Goa'uld symbiote in McGonagall's office
aliases: the thing in the glass case
infobox: Minerva McGonagall killed and kept it
A lit glass case over the fire in her office, Hogwarts
pages.html:
A stuffed Goa'uld symbiote hangs in a lit glass case over the fire in Minerva McGonagall's office at Hogwarts. She killed it with the help of Big Boss, and she kept it as a reminder that some problems cannot be solved with a wand.

Description

The case is long and lit from inside. It hangs on a bracket, where another teacher might have hung a painting or a clock. The creature in it is about the length of a boy's forearm, grey-white and segmented, like a very large worm or a very thin eel. A fringe of fins or fronds runs down its back. At one end its body opens into a mouth that goes four ways at once, four hinged flaps lined with needle teeth, held wide as if the thing had been caught screaming. It has no eyes that can be seen. It has been dead a long time, and whoever stuffed it took great care.

History

McGonagall met it a long time ago and a very long way from here, living in a human host. She tried to separate the two by Transfiguration, and found that nothing would do it. In the end the only thing that answered was a knife, a steady hand and a good deal of help from Big Boss, who was considerably better with the knife than she was. The host died. So did the creature.

Jack O'Neill, her other Muggle friend from those years, was not there and knows nothing of it. The Ministry of Magic keeps a file on that part of her work. Cornelius Fudge has read it, and he is confident that 'those parasite creatures' will not be bothering anybody again.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Five: Harry noticed the case properly for the first time. He had last been in the office on the night of the Chamber, with no attention to spare for the furniture. He judged it the most horrible object he had ever seen in a teacher's office, Gilderoy Lockhart's portraits included.

Book Three, Chapter Eight: in a lesson on the limits of Transfiguration, McGonagall described a creature that wraps itself round its host's spine, and the knife that had finally parted them. Harry realised then what was in the case. Ron had been in the same office on the night of the Chamber, but he had never noticed it. Harry spent the rest of the lesson wondering where 'a very long way from here' had been, and who the man with the knife was.

pages.title: The Stargate
infobox: Destroyed in space during the Third World War, unknown to anyone
pages.html:
The Stargate is a great ring of alien metal, dug out of the sand at Giza in 1928, which opens a passage across space to other worlds. In 1994 an American military expedition went through it to Abydos and destroyed Ra. In 1997 the Goa'uld came back, and the people who fought them through the gate were Muggles.

Description

The gate is a ring of naquadah some twenty-two feet across, set upright on a base. Around its inner track run thirty-nine symbols, each standing for a constellation. Nine chevrons are spaced round its outer edge. Six symbols fix a destination in space. A seventh, the point of origin, marks the gate that is doing the dialling. When the seventh chevron locks, the gate throws out a violent surge of energy that destroys whatever stands in front of it. Then it settles into a still, rippling pool that leads to the gate at the other end.

Travel runs one way only, from the dialling gate to the receiving one. A traveller crosses the distance in a moment, arriving cold and shaken. The gates were built by the Ancients, a race long gone, and they form a network across the galaxy. The Goa'uld did not make them. They found them, then used them to move their armies and their slaves from world to world. The Goa'uld word for the gate is Chappa'ai.

The Ancients were human beings of a far older age. Those of them who ascended became Maiar, spirits of the same order as Gandalf, in the service of God.

Discovery at Giza

In 1928 an expedition at Giza under Professor Paul Langford uncovered the gate, buried beneath the plateau. With it were two great cover stones carved with hieroglyphs, and a gold amulet bearing the Eye of Ra. His young daughter, Catherine Langford, was at the dig and kept the amulet. The cover stones described the gate as Ra's, sealed and buried for all time.

The gate and its stones were shipped to the United States in 1939, out of reach of Germany. In 1945 a team including Langford and Ernest Littlefield, Catherine's fiancé, managed to open it by hand while studying it as a possible weapon. Littlefield went through and did not come back. The programme was shut down and its records were buried. Catherine was told that he had died in a laboratory explosion.

The Abydos mission

The United States Air Force revived the project in 1994, at a mountain installation in Colorado. Catherine Langford recruited Daniel Jackson, a young Egyptologist whose career had just collapsed, to read the cover stones. He saw that the symbols on the gate were constellations, and he identified the missing seventh symbol. The gate opened on to Abydos, a desert world where Ra still ruled a people taken from Egypt thousands of years before.

A team under Colonel Jack O'Neill went through, with orders to destroy the gate with a nuclear device if they found a threat. Ra was killed when the bomb was sent up to his ship. Jackson stayed on Abydos with the wife he had married there. On Earth he was declared dead after what was announced as an accident in a shaft near Giza.

Later history

The gate did not stay quiet for long. In 1997 the Goa'uld came back through it, and the programme was reopened, this time with teams sent out to other worlds. The best known of them was SG-1. From then on Earth's struggle with the Goa'uld was fought by Muggle soldiers and scholars, through a gate found in Egypt.

It was Apophis who came. He had been taking over Ra's domains since Ra's death, he knew that Earth had killed Ra, and he had heard that Thor was busy elsewhere. His Jaffa killed the soldiers guarding the gate and carried one of them off.

In 1939 Ba'al, come back from 2008, tried to keep the gate from reaching America; Cameron Mitchell shot him aboard the ship that carried it, the Achilles.

Early in the Third World War the programme sent the gate into space aboard one of its BC-304s, to keep it out of the war. The ship was destroyed in space with the gate aboard. Nobody who knew of it lived through the war, and nobody on Earth ever learnt what had become of the gate. The programme had been secret, and by 2053 it was forgotten.

Earth's starships

From 2002 Earth's Stargate programme also built starships of its own, the Prometheus and the BC-304 battlecruisers, from captured Goa'uld engines. They were crude, costly prototypes that never travelled far without Asgard's help. None of them outlasted the Third World War.

In the saga

The gate has not been named in the saga. The Muggle news of 20 August 1994 (Book Four, Chapter Three) reported Daniel Jackson's death beneath the Giza plateau and said nothing more. The wizarding world knows nothing of the gate. The Ministry of Magic believes that 'those parasite creatures' will not be bothering it again (Book Three, Chapter Ten). It did not notice when they came back.

pages.title: Ra
infobox: The Abydos expedition of Jack O'Neill and Daniel Jackson
pages.html:
Ra was the greatest of the Goa'uld, the Supreme System Lord, who ruled Egypt as its sun god thousands of years ago. His slaves rose against him and drove him off Earth, but he kept his hold on Abydos. In 1994 he was destroyed above Abydos by the first American expedition through the Stargate.

Ruler of Egypt

Ra came to Earth in the remote past and took a human host, a young boy, whose body he kept youthful for thousands of years in the sarcophagus. Egypt was his seat. He ruled it as a god, with guards in the masks of Horus and Anubis. He came and went in a great pyramid-shaped ship. The pyramids were built in the likeness of its landing places. Through the gate at Giza he took Egyptians to other worlds as slaves.

The people of Egypt rose against him at last, and Ra fled. They buried his Stargate under the sand, with cover stones declaring it sealed and buried for all time. There it lay until Professor Paul Langford's expedition dug it up in 1928.

When the people of Egypt rose against him, Thor, the son of Odin, came down in a storm to fight beside them. He broke Ra's guards and struck Ra's ship with lightning as it rose from the desert. Ra never forgave the Egyptians or Thor, and he could not bear to have it spoken of. He forbade any Goa'uld to mention Earth again, and the System Lords have kept the ban.

Lord of the System Lords

Away from Earth Ra remained the foremost of the System Lords, the ruling council of the Goa'uld, and the others feared him. Hathor was his queen, and Heru'ur was their son. On Abydos his slaves mined naquadah for him. They were forbidden to read or write, so that they would not remember where they had come from.

Death

In 1994 an expedition from Earth came through the gate to Abydos under Colonel Jack O'Neill, with Daniel Jackson to read the inscriptions. Ra seized their nuclear device. He meant to send it back to Earth through the gate, with its power magnified by naquadah. The Abydonians rose against his guards. O'Neill and Jackson sent the armed bomb up to his ship through the transport rings. Ra tried to escape into orbit and was destroyed with his ship.

His death left a gap at the head of the System Lords, and others hurried to fill it.

Apophis was the quickest. With Ra gone there was nobody left to enforce his ban on Earth, and in 1997 Apophis came through the gate to Earth himself.

In the saga

Ra has not appeared or been named in the saga. The Abydos mission against him took place in 1994, the year in which Book Four begins. Egypt, where the Weasleys spent the summer of 1993, was his old seat. It is one of several reasons why Egypt has never been quite as innocent a place for a holiday as it looks.

pages.title: Jack O'Neill
infobox: Blackjack; Jack Blackjack O'Neill; Jack 'Blackjack' O'Neill; Colonel Jonathan O'Neill
United States Air Force, special operations
pages.html:
Colonel Jack 'Blackjack' O'Neill is a United States Air Force special-operations officer. Minerva McGonagall mentored him in the 1980s, and he has been her close friend ever since. He has never known that she is a witch. In 1994 he led the expedition through the Stargate to Abydos, and learnt the hard way that the Goa'uld exist.

Career

O'Neill made his name in covert special operations for the Air Force, the kind of work that is never reported, and he earned the nickname Blackjack. He is dry, impatient with officialdom and quicker than he lets anyone see. He is fiercely loyal to the men under him.

He married Sara, and they had a son, Charlie. Shortly before the Abydos mission Charlie shot himself by accident with his father's pistol. O'Neill blamed himself. His marriage broke under it. He had retired from the service, with no wish to go on living, when the Air Force called him back.

McGonagall

On one of her sabbaticals from Hogwarts in the 1980s, Minerva McGonagall's work as an Unspeakable put her alongside O'Neill, and she mentored him. Whatever she taught him, she taught in Muggle terms. He never knew that she was a witch, or that a magical world exists.

They are still close friends, and they still write to each other. Neither can tell the other anything about their work, or in practice about their lives. Theirs is a friendship conducted round two large silences. He knows that she cannot talk. He has no idea how much. He is one of the 'great many friends in the Muggle world' that Molly Weasley meant when she said that she knew where McGonagall had been and who she knew.

O'Neill was not with McGonagall when she confronted a Goa'uld symbiote and its host. That was Big Boss. O'Neill knew nothing of the Goa'uld until 1994. By then McGonagall had killed one and kept it over her fire. She could not tell him.

Abydos

In 1994 O'Neill was given command of the first team through the Stargate. Daniel Jackson went with them to read the symbols, and O'Neill carried secret orders to destroy the gate with a nuclear device if they met a threat. On Abydos he found Ra and his Jaffa guards. He also found Skaara, a boy of the Abydonians, who attached himself to O'Neill. Without either of them quite intending it, Skaara taught him to want to live again.

With Jackson he sent the armed bomb up to Ra's ship, and the Goa'uld died in orbit. O'Neill brought the survivors home and left Jackson on Abydos. In his report he said that Jackson was dead and that the gate on Abydos had been destroyed. Neither was true.

Later years

In 1997 the Goa'uld came back through the gate. O'Neill was recalled to command SG-1, the team that carried the war to them across the galaxy.

It was Apophis, who had been taking Ra's place among the System Lords since O'Neill killed Ra. On Abydos he took Skaara, the boy who had taught O'Neill to want to live again, as a host for his son.

In 2002 Ba'al tortured him to death many times over, reviving him each time in the sarcophagus.

The free Jaffa remembered SG-1 long after Earth had forgotten it. Their children were told of O'Neill's team for generations. When Captain Kirk's Enterprise found the Jaffa worlds about 2268, it was from the Jaffa that Earth learnt of him again.

Thor

O'Neill came to know Thor well. In 1999 the Asgard took the knowledge of the Ancients out of his head on Othala, in the Pegasus galaxy. That summer Thor brought him aboard his ship to warn him that the System Lords meant to destroy Earth, then offered Earth a place in the Protected Planets Treaty. In 2000 Asgard named its newest warship the O'Neill. In 2004 Thor woke him from the frozen sleep in which he had lain in the Antarctic since saving Earth from Anubis, and O'Neill built the weapon that cleared Orilla of the Replicators. He was made a general that year, and given command of the base.

In the saga

O'Neill has not appeared or been named in the saga. McGonagall's letters to him run on through the years of Harry's schooling. So in 1994 she is writing to a man in mourning for his son, about none of the things that matter to either of them.

pages.title: James Bond
infobox: Bond; John Mason; John Patrick Mason; 007
Casino Royale (novel, 13 April 1953); on screen in Dr. No (5 October 1962); as John Mason in The Rock (7 June 1996)
MI6, agent 007; former SAS captain as Mason
Wolfburg Penitentiary, in isolation, without trial
1996, to lead a team back into Alcatraz
pages.html:
James Bond is a Scottish agent of MI6, codenamed 007. From 1960 to 1962 he had a romance with Minerva McGonagall, which ended when she found out how much he had lied to her. Under the name of John Patrick Mason he is also the only man ever to escape from Alcatraz. He has been held in isolation at Wolfburg Penitentiary, without trial, since the mid-1980s, which covers all of Harry's years at Hogwarts so far. He was not brought out until 1996.

McGonagall

From 1960 to 1962, before she began teaching, Minerva McGonagall worked alongside Bond and had a romance with him. Once he needed a great deal of gold to go missing in a hurry, and she turned a vault's worth of it into beetles for him. He had a way of asking, she said, that one found hard to refuse. She ended the affair when she discovered that he had lied to her about a great many things. She has never forgotten the lying.

They kept in touch after the break until late in 1962, when he went undercover as John Mason and was locked up on Alcatraz. Her contact with him ended there.

John Mason and Alcatraz

In late 1962, as John Mason, a former SAS captain trained by MI6, Bond stole the microfilm on which J. Edgar Hoover kept the secrets of the American establishment. He was caught. He refused to say where he had hidden it, and he was sent to Alcatraz without trial. Early in 1963, before the prison closed on 21 March, he escaped from it, the only man ever to do so. The United States government has claimed him ever since.

Active service

His missions as 007 fall on these dates. On Crab Key, off Jamaica, he destroyed Dr Julius No, an agent of SPECTRE who had been toppling American rockets (5 October 1962). He brought the Soviet cipher clerk Tatiana Romanova and the Lektor decoding machine out of Istanbul on the Orient Express, past SPECTRE's assassins (10 October 1963). He stopped Auric Goldfinger's attempt to irradiate the gold at Fort Knox (17 September 1964). Off Nassau he recovered two atomic bombs that SPECTRE's Emilio Largo had stolen from a NATO bomber (9 December 1965). In Japan he found the base inside a volcano from which Ernst Stavro Blofeld's SPECTRE had been stealing American and Soviet spacecraft (12 June 1967). He followed a diamond-smuggling ring through Las Vegas to Blofeld, and to the laser satellite the diamonds had been gathered to build (17 December 1971).

After December 1971 he was recaptured as Mason and sent to San Quentin, from which he escaped in February 1976. In 1983, older and long thought past it, he was called back to recover two cruise missiles stolen by SPECTRE (7 October 1983).

Wolfburg

After 1983 he was recaptured once more. He has been held ever since in isolation at Wolfburg Penitentiary, without trial, the government's prisoner on and off for more than thirty years.

In 1996 renegade Marines under General Francis Hummel seized Alcatraz, threatening San Francisco with rockets of VX gas. Bond was brought out of Wolfburg to take a team back in, as the only man who had ever found a way off the island.

In the saga

Book Two, Chapter Seven: while Harry was trying to turn a beetle into a button, McGonagall told the class that she had once turned a vault's worth of gold into beetles, a very long time ago. When Seamus Finnigan asked why, she said it had been for a gentleman she was working alongside: 'A Muggle. Scottish. He had a desk at a very dull-sounding office near the river, though he was seldom at it.' She had not heard from him in a good many years. She expected, she said, that he had retired somewhere warm and was lying about it. Something like fondness crossed her face.

Book Two, Chapter Fifteen: when Gilderoy Lockhart took the credit for shutting the Chamber, McGonagall said nothing whatever. Her nostrils went very thin as she thought about what she had done to 'that charming MI6 agent who so brazenly lied to her face for the last and very final time'.

Through all of Harry's years at Hogwarts so far, Bond has been a prisoner at Wolfburg, a long way from anywhere warm.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

Book Four, Chapter Five: on 22 August 1994 Cedric Diggory introduced himself to Harry Potter as 'Diggory, Cedric Diggory', in the manner of James Bond. He said it like somebody out of the spy films Vernon Dursley watched every Christmas, with a charm a secret agent would have been proud of.

pages.title: Alcatraz
pages.html:
Alcatraz is a rocky island in San Francisco Bay, which from 1934 to 1963 held the most secure federal prison in the United States. Only one man ever escaped from it: John Mason, early in 1963.

The Rock

The island lies more than a mile from the shore, in cold water with fierce currents. It held the most troublesome men in the federal system, Al Capone among them. It was costly to run, and the prison closed on 21 March 1963.

John Mason

Mason, a former SAS captain trained by MI6, was in truth James Bond. In late 1962 he stole the microfilm on which J. Edgar Hoover kept the secrets of the American establishment. He would not say where he had hidden it, so he was sent to Alcatraz without trial. Early in 1963, weeks before the prison closed, he escaped.

In 1996 renegade Marines under General Francis Hummel seized the island, threatening San Francisco with rockets of VX gas. Mason, as the only man who had ever found a way off it, was brought out of prison to take a team back in.

pages.title: San Quentin
infobox: Point San Quentin, Marin County, California
pages.html:
San Quentin is the oldest prison in California, on Point San Quentin at the edge of San Francisco Bay, north of the city. James Bond, the British agent, was held there under the name of John Mason in the 1970s, until he broke out in February 1976.

John Mason

The prison opened in 1852 and keeps the state's condemned men. The Americans had wanted Mason back ever since 1963, when he became the only man ever to escape from Alcatraz. After December 1971 they caught him again and sent him to San Quentin. In February 1976 he escaped from there too.

pages.title: Wolfburg Penitentiary
infobox: John Patrick Mason (James Bond), in isolation since the mid-1980s
pages.html:
Wolfburg Penitentiary is an American federal prison. Since the mid-1980s it has held John Patrick Mason in isolation, without trial. Mason is the only man ever to escape from Alcatraz, and he is in truth James Bond of MI6.

Its prisoner

Mason was first locked up without trial on Alcatraz in 1962, for stealing the microfilm of J. Edgar Hoover's secret files, and escaped from it in 1963. In the 1970s he was recaptured and sent to San Quentin. He broke out in February 1976. After 1983 he was taken once more, and this time he was sent to Wolfburg. By 1994 the American government had held him, or hunted him, for more than thirty years without once bringing him to trial.

He came out in 1996, when renegade Marines seized Alcatraz. The government needed the only man who had ever found a way off the island.

pages.title: Saint Peter
infobox: Peter; Simon Peter; Simon son of Jonah; Cephas
Fisherman, of the lake of Galilee
Crucified at Rome under Nero, by tradition
pages.html:
Saint Peter was a fisherman of Galilee who became the chief of Christ's apostles. In June 1994 the Fat Friar told Harry Potter the story of Peter's walk on the water. It is the key to how Harry's Patronus killed dementors: Peter walked on the water until he looked down.

Life

Simon, son of Jonah, was fishing on the lake of Galilee with his brother Andrew when Jesus called the two of them to follow him. He would make them, he said, fishers of men. Christ named Simon Cephas: Peter, the rock. Upon that rock, he said, he would build his church. He gave Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

One night in a storm the disciples saw Christ walking towards their boat on the water. Peter asked to come to him. He climbed out of the boat. He walked on the water towards Christ until he saw the wind and the waves. Then he was afraid. He began to sink, and Christ caught him by the hand: 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?'

It was Peter who first confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God. It was Peter, too, who asked how often he must forgive his brother, to be told 'until seventy times seven'.

On the night of the betrayal he denied Christ three times before the cock crowed, and wept bitterly. After the resurrection Christ asked him three times whether he loved him. Each time Peter said yes, and Christ told him to feed his sheep. Peter led the apostles after Pentecost. By tradition he was crucified at Rome under Nero, head downwards, at his own request.

In the saga

In January 1994, standing by the frozen lake with Dracina Malfoy, Harry watched a small Hufflepuff walk far out across the ice as though it were a floor. Then he looked down, and went straight through. The boy who hauled him out said, 'You were fine till you looked down.'

In March Lupin told Harry the seventy-times-seven story without naming either party. He said he would very much like Harry to go looking for where it was written down.

In June 1994 Harry's stag Patronus crossed the lake as though the lake were a floor. The next day the Fat Friar told him the story of Peter on the water. Harry, the Friar said, had stopped looking down. When Harry asked whether the Hufflepuff on the ice had been a sign meant for him, the Friar laughed: God does not often speak so clearly. Then he told Harry that wondering whether he was too thick to hear it was the very doubt that made Peter sink.

pages.title: Dark Mark
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
Death Eaters, Severus Snape and Lucius Malfoy among them
pages.html:
The Dark Mark is the sign of Lord Voldemort, burnt into the left forearm of each of his Death Eaters. It is horrific dark magic. It links whoever bears it directly to Voldemort himself.

The bearers

Severus Snape bears the Mark, and so does Lucius Malfoy. To Remus Lupin, who is a Garou, it reeks of the Wyrm. Every instinct he has tells him to take his war form and tear Snape apart. Only the Wolfsbane Potion lets him stand in the same room.

Lucius knows that his own Mark will compel him to fight Harry Potter on his master’s behalf, and that this will hurt his daughter. It is the real reason he stands against anything between Dracina and Harry, though the boy has grown on him more than he will ever admit. Dracina believes that her father simply disapproves of Harry.

The sign in the sky

During Voldemort's first rise his followers sent the same sign into the sky, a skull with a serpent coming out of its mouth, over every house where they had killed.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Four, in Diagon Alley in August 1993, Lucius Malfoy told Harry that he had forbidden Dracina to write to him. As they walked on, his free hand went to his own left forearm, gripped it hard through the sleeve and let go, as if it had remembered something.

In Chapter Eight, when Snape came into Lupin’s office with a smoking goblet, every hair on Lupin’s forearms stood on end and his lip came up off his teeth. It lasted no more than a moment.

In Chapter Fourteen Dracina told Snape why she had joined in her teammates’ trick with the dementors at the Ravenclaw match. As she talked, Snape’s right hand moved, without his seeming to notice it, to grip his own left forearm through the sleeve.

In the saga: 1994 to 1995

In Book Four, Chapter Six, in the Top Box at the World Cup final on 22 August 1994, Harry Potter told Lucius Malfoy drily that he would have to get past Voldemort first. Lucius flinched at the name, then rubbed his left forearm through his sleeve, the way a man rubs an old wound that aches in the cold. Harry did not know what was under the sleeve, but Lucius knew that the Mark would one day burn, calling him to stand against Harry.

pages.title: J. R. R. Tolkien
infobox: Professor at Oxford; scholar of Old English
The Hobbit (1937); The Lord of the Rings (1954 to 1955)
pages.html:
J. R. R. Tolkien was an English scholar of old languages who wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Most people take his books for stories. They are in fact history, the history of the elder days of the world: of the Elves, of Númenor and of the War of the Ring.

Life

Tolkien was born in South Africa in 1892. He was brought up in Birmingham by his mother, a convert to the Catholic Church, until she died when he was twelve. He fought on the Somme in 1916, and most of his close friends were killed in the war. For more than thirty years he taught at Oxford, where his friends included C. S. Lewis.

The Hobbit came out in 1937. The Lord of the Rings, which took him twelve years to write, followed in three parts in 1954 and 1955. He died at Bournemouth in 1973.

His record

Tolkien's record of the elder days has its gaps. It is vague about the two Blue Wizards and never settles what became of them. The reason is simple. Five Istari were sent out, and one of the Blue Wizards, Zordon, was sent off the world entirely, to Eltar. Nobody who could have written it down ever saw him again.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter One, in the summer of 1993, Harry Potter found an enormous copy of The Lord of the Rings, all three parts bound into one, among Dudley Dursley's unwanted Christmas presents. Dudley had been using it to prop up a wobbly table. Harry read it all through his third year.

In Chapter Twenty-One, on Myst Island in June 1994, the empty grey sea made him think of Tolkien's drowned kingdom of Númenor, lying somewhere under a grey sea in the West. Later that night he thought of it again. Dumbledore had once told him that the magic of Elves and of Númenor lived in his blood. Harry knew Númenor from Tolkien by now, as the kingdom across the sea where Aragorn's family had come from. What it had to do with him, he had no idea. He finished the book in Chapter Twenty-Two, in July 1994.

pages.title: Francisco Vásquez de Coronado
infobox: Governor of New Galicia, in New Spain
1540 to 1542, in search of the Seven Cities of Cíbola
pages.html:
Francisco Vásquez de Coronado was a Spanish Muggle explorer who led an army north out of New Spain in search of the Seven Cities of Cíbola, which were said to be made of solid gold. They did not exist. In 1541 his army was in New Mexico, and a few wizards in its ranks became the first wizards ever to meet the D'ni.

The expedition

Coronado was the young governor of New Galicia when he marched north in 1540. The first of the golden cities turned out to be a Zuni village of stone and mud. His men searched the deserts of the north for two years. He came home in 1542 with nothing, and died in Mexico City in 1554.

The wizards in his army

Coronado never knew that a few of his men were wizards. In New Mexico they slipped away to try long-distance Apparition across the desert. One night they Apparated somewhere they had not meant to go, and found themselves in the D'ni cavern.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, on Myst Island in June 1994, Hermione Granger told Harry Potter and Dracina Malfoy the story. 'The first wizards who ever met them were Spanish. It was in 1541. They were with Coronado.'

pages.title: Hugh Everett
pages.html:
Hugh Everett was an American Muggle physicist. In 1957 he proposed that the universe branches into every possibility, with each branch as real as the rest, an idea later called the Many Worlds interpretation.

Life

Everett set the idea out in his doctoral thesis at Princeton in 1957, and hardly anybody took it seriously. He left physics to work for the Pentagon, calculating what a nuclear war would do. His theory found an audience only in the 1970s. He died of a heart attack in 1982, at the age of fifty-one.

The D'ni teaching

His theory comes very close to what the D'ni priests taught: that every world that could possibly be already exists, and a Writer creates nothing. He only describes a world so exactly that his book finds one to match.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, on Myst Island in June 1994, Hermione Granger explained Everett's theory to Harry Potter and Dracina Malfoy. 'There was an American physicist called Hugh Everett, in 1957. He said that whenever something tiny could happen more than one way, it actually happened every way at once.'

pages.title: Erwin Schrödinger
infobox: The Schrödinger equation; the cat in the box
pages.html:
Erwin Schrödinger was an Austrian Muggle physicist, one of the founders of quantum physics, who shared the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1933.

Life

Schrödinger was born in Vienna in 1887. He left Germany in disgust when the Nazis came to power, worked for many years in Dublin and died in Vienna in 1961.

The cat

In 1935 he asked his colleagues to imagine a cat shut in a box with a flask of poison and a little radioactive material. If a single atom decays, the flask breaks and the cat dies. By the rules of quantum physics the cat is both alive and dead until somebody opens the box. Schrödinger meant it to show how absurd those rules looked when applied to cats.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-One, on Myst Island in June 1994, Hermione Granger mentioned a book of her father's, In Search of Schrödinger's Cat, and began to explain. 'Schrödinger's cat is a sort of thought experiment, you see, with a cat in a box, a bottle of poison and a little bit of radioactive…' Dracina Malfoy, who was freezing, stopped her there.

pages.title: Ludwig van Beethoven
infobox: Nine symphonies, many of them written as his hearing failed
pages.html:
Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer who spent most of his working life in Vienna. Much of his greatest music was written after he had gone deaf. Mr Granger, Hermione's father, plays him on compact disc.

Life

Beethoven was born in Bonn in December 1770 and moved to Vienna at twenty-one. He began to lose his hearing before he was thirty. By the time his Ninth Symphony was first played, in 1824, he could not hear the applause, and one of the singers had to turn him round to see it. He died in Vienna in 1827.

In the saga

In Book Four, Chapter Two, Hermione Granger wrote to Harry Potter in August 1994 about the new computer her father had bought, and the CD-ROMs that came with it. 'They're like the compact discs Dad plays his Beethoven on, only they hold pictures as well as sound.' One of them was Myst.

pages.title: Ronald Reagan
infobox: President of the United States, 1981 to 1989
Grounding every costumed hero in America, 1986
pages.html:
Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States, from 1981 to 1989. In 1986 he grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter.

President

Reagan was Governor of California before he won the White House in 1980. Two months into his first term he survived an assassination attempt. Since leaving office in January 1989 he has lived in retirement in California.

The grounding

In 1986 Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, set out to turn America against its heroes through his agent Glorious Godfrey, who went before the cameras as the preacher G. Gordon Godfrey. Coming so soon after the Crisis, the campaign found a frightened audience. Reagan issued an executive order forbidding every costumed hero in America to act. Early in 1987 Godfrey was faced down at a great march on Washington, and the order was lifted.

In the saga

In Book Four, Chapter Three, on 20 August 1994, the news on the Dursleys' television recalled earlier attempts to rein in superhumans. 'In 1986 President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter.'

pages.title: Manfred Wörner
infobox: West German Minister of Defence, 1982 to 1988
pages.html:
Manfred Wörner was a German statesman and the Secretary-General of Nato from 1988 until his death on 13 August 1994. He died a week before British television reported Augment forces within forty miles of Belgrade.

Life

Wörner was a Christian Democrat from Stuttgart and a jet pilot in the air force reserve. He was Helmut Kohl's Minister of Defence from 1982 to 1988, then the first German to lead Nato, through the end of the Cold War. In his last years, ill with cancer, he went on working while the alliance argued over how hard to bomb the Bosnian Serbs. His deputy, Sergio Balanzino, took over as acting Secretary-General.

In the saga
