In Book Three, Chapter Four, in Diagon Alley in August 1993, the memory of the jumper came back to Harry with his anger. In Chapter Ten, lying in the hospital wing, he dreamt of paying back everyone who had hurt him. The teachers from the primary school came, and Dracina Malfoy, at his shoulder, told him to go on.

pages.title: Abydos
pages.html:
Abydos is a desert world at the far end of the Stargate found at Giza. Ra kept a people taken from ancient Egypt there as his slaves, to mine naquadah for him. In 1994 the first expedition from Earth reached it, Ra was destroyed in the sky above it, and Daniel Jackson stayed behind.

World and people

Abydos is a world of sand and wind under a hard sun. Its gate stands inside a great pyramid in the open desert, a long walk from Nagada, the walled town where the Abydonians live. They are descended from Egyptians whom Ra carried through the gate thousands of years ago, and they still speak a form of the ancient Egyptian tongue. Their beasts of burden are mastadges, big shaggy animals that haul loads across the dunes. They mined naquadah for Ra, whom they worshipped as their god.

Ra forbade them to read or write, so that they would forget where they had come from. Their history survived only in hidden chambers, whose inscriptions told of Ra's coming, of the rising on Earth that drove him out and of the gate that had been buried behind him. The elder of Nagada is Kasuf. His daughter Sha'uri and his son Skaara are among the young people who rose against Ra.

One of the inscriptions shows a storm over the desert, with a giant in it holding a hammer. The Abydonians do not know who he was.

The 1994 expedition

In 1994 a United States Air Force team under Colonel Jack O'Neill came through the gate, with Daniel Jackson to read its symbols. When the Abydonians saw the Eye of Ra on the amulet Jackson carried, they bowed down before the strangers. The people of Nagada took them in, and Kasuf gave Sha'uri to Jackson as his wife.

When Ra arrived in his ship, the Abydonians took up arms against his guards for the first time in their history. O'Neill and Jackson sent the expedition's bomb up to Ra's ship. He was destroyed in the sky above them.

Jackson chose to stay with Sha'uri and her people. O'Neill told his superiors that the gate on Abydos had been destroyed, so that the Abydonians would be left alone.

Apophis

In 1997 Apophis, who had been taking over Ra's domains since Ra's death, came to Abydos. He took Sha'uri as a host for his queen, Amaunet, and Skaara as one for his son, Klorel.

In 2003 Anubis destroyed Abydos. Oma Desala had already raised its people beyond his reach, Skaara among them.

In the saga

Abydos has not been named in the saga. The only trace of it is the reported death of Daniel Jackson beneath the Giza plateau, on the Muggle news of 20 August 1994 (Book Four, Chapter Three). The death was a cover story for his going there.

pages.title: Adam of Ventara
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Advent Master Returns' (14 November 2009)
Letting Xaviax into the base of the Kamen Riders, about 2007
pages.html:
Adam of Ventara is the first Dragon Knight, the youngest of the twelve Kamen Riders, a friend of Len. In the summer of 1994 he is still one of Ventara's guardians. About 2007 he led a stranger to the place where the others slept, which cost Ventara everything. In 2009 Xaviax made use of him a second time. He told the truth at the last moment, fought in the battle that destroyed Xaviax, then gave up his deck to his mirror twin, Kit Taylor of Earth.

The youngest Rider

Adam was chosen with eleven others to wear the armour that Eubulon made. His deck was Dragon Knight, contracted to the red dragon Dragreder. He was the youngest of the twelve. Len, the Wing Knight, was his friend.

A Rider's life is a strange one. He sleeps in suspended animation for years at a time. He wakes to stand guard for one year in twelve. Adam fell in love with a Ventaran woman, Sarah, then found that he no longer wanted any of it.

Paragon

About 2007 a man came to him who said that his name was Paragon. He was from Karsh, he said, but he was a friend of Eubulon, the lost master of the order. He knew how to release the lock that bound a Rider to his Advent Deck. Adam could be free of his.

Adam took him to the base where the others slept. Paragon was Xaviax. He vented the sleeping Riders, took every deck, Adam's included, then carried the people of Ventara away to Karsh.

Adam had not meant any of it, but he had opened the door. Xaviax kept his side of the bargain after a fashion. He shut Adam up with Sarah in a false Ventara, made for the purpose, where the two of them lived quietly while the real one stood empty.

The spy

On Earth, the Dragon Knight's deck went to a boy with Adam's face, Kit Taylor. Kit was vented in November 2009, so the deck came back into Xaviax's hands. Xaviax went to the false Ventara. He told Adam to put the armour on again. If he refused, Sarah would suffer for it.

Adam was to win back the trust of his old comrades, who were returning from the Advent Void, then betray them once more. He came to Len's help in a fight on 14 November. A week later he fought Len in earnest, but he found that he could not vent his friend. The Rider Hunt would have nothing to do with him.

On 28 November he met his twin. Kit, in the black armour of Onyx, beat him. He would have vented him if Eubulon had not stopped the fight. Eubulon let Adam explain himself. In December Adam told them all about Paragon. Xaviax helped the lie along by shutting down a transmitter for show.

Adam began to waver. Xaviax came to him wearing Eubulon's face, to scold him, then to fight him.

The confession

On 18 December 2009 Adam went with Len to Australia, to the last of the transmitters. His orders were to let Len disarm it, then to vent him. He attacked. He told Len that Xaviax could not be beaten. He said that he would not give up Sarah. He had Len at his mercy, but he could not strike.

When Kit arrived with Kase, Adam asked them to vent him. They refused. Then he told them what he knew: the transmitters had never really been shut down. Len took his deck away.

There was no time to punish him. Eubulon needed every Rider. Adam was given the Dragon Knight's armour once more, to fight in Xaviax's stronghold beside his twin. The two of them struck the first blow together.

Afterwards

When Xaviax was dead, Adam laid down his deck for good. It passed to Kit Taylor. Adam went home to the real Ventara, which had its people again, to live there with Sarah.

pages.title: Agatha Harkness
infobox: The Massachusetts Bay Colony, in the seventeenth century
Whisper Hill, in the Adirondacks of New York
New Salem, Colorado, which she once led
Franklin Richards, as his governess, from 1969; the Scarlet Witch, from 1974
A ghost for some years; alive again from 2017
pages.html:
Agatha Harkness is an American witch of very great age, who came through the Salem trials of 1692 and has been alive ever since by means she has never explained. She once led New Salem, a hidden town of witches in Colorado, until her own son turned it against her. In 1969 she became governess to Franklin Richards, the son of Reed and Sue Richards of the Fantastic Four. In 1974 she took the Scarlet Witch as her pupil, and taught her the witchcraft that her mutant power had hidden.

Salem

Agatha was born in the Massachusetts Bay Colony in the seventeenth century. She has never said exactly when, and nobody has managed to find out. She was schooled at Ilvermorny in its first century, when it was still more household than castle.

In 1692 the Puritans of Salem began hanging witches, with the help of the Scourers. Most of those they hanged were No-Majs. Agatha was one of the real ones, and she came through it alive. She is older than MACUSA, which was founded the next year to break the Scourers.

New Salem

In time a band of Salem's witches went west, far beyond the settlements, to make a town of their own in the mountains of what is now Colorado. They called it New Salem. It hides from No-Majs as thoroughly as any wizarding place in America. It is governed by its own elders, under its own old laws, and MACUSA, glad of a town of witches that keeps itself out of sight, has always let it manage its own affairs.

Agatha led it for a long time. Her son, Nicholas Scratch, grew up there, and so did his seven children, who are called Salem's Seven. By the twentieth century she had left it for Whisper Hill, a rambling old house in the Adirondacks, where she taught gifted children to master their powers.

The Fantastic Four, 1969 to 1977

In the autumn of 1969 Reed and Sue Richards brought their son, Franklin, to Whisper Hill, looking for a governess. Four years earlier, under Rappaport's Law, she could not have taken the post. That night the Frightful Four attacked the house, though Agatha warned them that her cat's hackles were up. She dealt with them herself, without letting the Fantastic Four see how, and she became Franklin's governess. The family found out what she was in 1971, when she helped them against Annihilus.

In 1974 she brought the sleeping Franklin to Quicksilver's wedding to Crystal. Ultron's beams woke the boy there, and his power destroyed the robot.

The Scarlet Witch

In 1974 Agatha took Wanda Maximoff, the Scarlet Witch, as her pupil. She had seen at once what the Avengers had not: that Wanda was a witch as well as a mutant, with her Romani mother's magic in her, half taught and never finished. Agatha taught her true witchcraft. She has said that Wanda's two gifts are so tangled together that even she cannot always tell which is at work.

New Salem's judgement, 1977 to 1990

In 1977 Nicholas Scratch carried Agatha and Franklin off to New Salem. There she was tried for leaving the town and putting its secret in danger. She was sentenced to be burnt. The Fantastic Four broke free in time to stop it. The town turned against Scratch, who had killed one of his own followers before its eyes. Its witches banished him to another plane, then took New Salem out of the world after him. Only then did Agatha tell the Fantastic Four that Scratch was her son.

In 1979 Scratch came back with Salem's Seven, and Agatha beat them again. In 1985 the Seven took New Salem for themselves. They burnt Agatha at the stake, but her spirit stayed close enough to guide the Scarlet Witch, whom they had taken prisoner. In 1989 she came back alive, without a word of explanation to anybody.

That year she took away Wanda's memory of her lost sons, to save her reason. In 1990, when Immortus had used the loss against her, Agatha gave the memory back.

Agatha and the wizarding world

Agatha is a witch of the wizarding world, Ilvermorny-schooled, and she keeps the Statute of Secrecy as carefully as anybody in America. The Fantastic Four know what she is. The public knows her, if at all, as an old lady who looks after children. In the summer of 1994 she is as old as ever, and quite as sharp.

pages.title: Alessa Gillespie
infobox: Midwich Elementary School, Silent Hill; never at Ilvermorny
1976 to 1983, in the basement of Alchemilla Hospital
13 September 1983, as the child Harry Mason raised
pages.html:
Alessa Gillespie was a witch of Silent Hill, born with magic to a No-Maj mother who was a priestess of the town's cult. Her classmates called her a witch, and they were right, though nobody in the town knew what the word really meant. In the summer of 1976, when she was seven, her mother burnt her in a rite that was meant to make her the mother of the Order's god. She lived for seven more years in a hospital basement, with her soul torn in two. Her pain made the Otherworld. In September 1983 she was made whole again, bore the thing her mother wanted and saw it killed. Then she died, leaving a newborn child in the arms of Harry Mason.

A witch in Silent Hill

Alessa was born about 1969, the daughter of Dahlia Gillespie. Dahlia had no magic of her own, only the rites of the Order of Silent Hill, in which she was a priestess. Alessa was different from birth. Things moved around her that she had not touched.

In a wizarding family the signs would have been understood at once. In Silent Hill they made her an outcast. The other children at Midwich Elementary School called her a witch and tormented her for it. She kept to herself, with her picture books and her collection of pinned insects. Her one friend was Claudia Wolf, a girl two years younger, whose family belonged to the same faith. Each had a parent to be afraid of.

Her mother drew her own conclusions. The Order had tried for years to get its god on a human mother, without success. Dahlia looked at her daughter's power and decided that the Holy Mother had been living in her house all along.

The burning, 1976

In the summer of 1976, when Alessa was seven, Dahlia performed the rite of birth on her in the cellar of the Gillespie house. The rite needed fire. The fire got away, and it destroyed six homes before it was put out. The newspapers reported that the charred body of Alessa Gillespie, aged seven, had been found in the ruins. The blame was put on an old boiler.

The body in the report was not hers. The director of Alchemilla Hospital, Dr Michael Kaufmann, did business with the Order, and he signed whatever papers were needed. Alessa was carried into the hospital's basement alive.

The rite had half worked. The seed of the god was in her, which meant that she could not die, however badly she was burnt. Her soul had refused it all the same, and in refusing had split in two. One half stayed in the burnt body. The other fled the town altogether. It was found that same day as a newborn baby at the side of the highway. A writer named Harry Mason and his wife took the child home, where they called her Cheryl.

With half the soul gone, the god could not be born. Dahlia settled down to get it back.

Why nobody came for her

No witch or wizard ever learnt that Alessa existed. Ilvermorny takes every magical child in North America, whatever the family, but it writes to them at eleven. Alessa was burnt at seven. By the time she turned eleven she had been on record as dead for four years, and she was lying in a hospital basement that hardly anybody was allowed to enter.

Nor did her magic give her away to MACUSA. It was done in a town where strange things were put down to the Order, by a child whose own mother wanted them kept quiet.

Nor did the two secret bodies that watched Silent Hill in those years, Delta Green and the SCP Foundation. Delta Green never heard her name. The Foundation's file lists her among the dead of the fire of 1976, on the newspapers' word.

Seven years in the basement

From 1976 to 1983 Alessa lay in a locked room under Alchemilla Hospital. Her burns never healed. A nurse, Lisa Garland, changed the dressings on a child whose skin went on seeping blood week after week, long after she ought to have been dead. Dahlia came to work a spell over her, year in and year out, calling the lost half of her soul home.

Alessa could not move, but her magic could. It was strong, and it was all she had. It went out through the hospital into the town, carrying her fear and her hatred with it. Lisa Garland wrote in her diary of insects swarming in her room, and of a tap that ran with blood. That was the beginning of the Otherworld as later visitors met it. A witch with a whole soul might have mastered such power. Alessa had half a soul, and she was in agony.

1983

After seven years the spell worked. Cheryl Mason, aged seven, asked her father to take her to Silent Hill for a holiday. On the night of 12 September 1983, on the road into the town, Alessa's image stepped out in front of the car. When Harry woke after the crash, Cheryl was gone.

Having Cheryl near gave Alessa back the use of her power. She could not stop the two halves joining, so she set out to stop the birth. She went from place to place in the Otherworld, marking each with the Seal of Metatron: the school, the hospital, an antique shop, the lighthouse and the amusement park. The finished seal would have held the god back. It might well have destroyed Alessa with it. She was content with that.

Dahlia could no longer get near her, so she used Harry. She told him that the marks were the Mark of Samael, the work of a demon, and that the girl who made them would be the death of his daughter. She gave him a charm called the Flauros. At the amusement park Harry met Alessa face to face, and the Flauros broke her power.

Dahlia joined the two halves of the soul, and the god was born. Dr Kaufmann, who felt cheated, threw a flask of aglaophotis over it. Harry killed what came out. With her last strength the girl who had been both Alessa and Cheryl put a newborn baby into his arms. She showed him the way out, and died as that whole burning place came down. It was the night of 13 September 1983. She was fourteen.

Afterwards

The baby was Alessa herself, whole at last and beginning again. Harry raised her. For seventeen years she knew nothing of her first life. When she went back to Silent Hill in September 2000 she began to remember it. On the carousel at the amusement park she met the memory of the burnt girl, who had wanted to die sooner than bear the god. She had to fight her.

The Order made Alessa one of its three saints. Claudia Wolf, who had loved her, called the reborn girl by her old name.

Alessa's magic did not go with her into her new life. She had poured it into Silent Hill for seven years. It is there still.

pages.title: Alpha 1
infobox: On Edenoi, by order of King Lexian, more than ten thousand years ago
pages.html:
Alpha 1 was the first of Zordon's robot helpers, built for him on Edenoi more than ten thousand years ago. He was lost for centuries. In September 1993 he found his way to Earth, where he helped the Power Rangers in secret, then turned on Zordon for fighting his war with too much mercy. Dark Specter destroyed him in February 1995.

Edenoi

Long ago, when Zordon was at war with Master Vile, King Lexian of Edenoi comforted him. The people of Edenoi built him a robot helper by the king's order, the first Alpha. Alpha 5, who keeps the Command Center running today, came from the same world long afterwards.

Alpha 1 was lost in a trap on Prillon 12, a far-off moon. He drifted for centuries, then searched for Zordon for a great deal longer.

Earth, 1993

He found Zordon at last in September 1993, while Rita Repulsa was hunting for a way to wake the Dragon Coin. For a while he helped the Rangers from the shadows. When Jason Lee Scott and Trini Kwan were dragged off to the planet Breel after Rita, it was Alpha 1 who covered for them at home. He saved people at a museum. Then he came to the Command Center, where he met Alpha 5.

He built a suit of blue armour with Billy Cranston, the Tricera Armour. Zordon wanted more tests before it was used. Trini never trusted the old robot. He took a good deal of trouble over Zack Taylor, who already felt that Zordon had passed him over.

His creed was to kill without mercy. When Goldar wrecked the Youth Center, hunting for somebody worthy of the Dragon Coin, Alpha 1 shot him in the back. He told the Rangers to finish Goldar off. They refused, so he shut them in a force field. Zordon, he said, had dragged the war out with his mercy.

Goldar, of all people, set the Rangers free. Alpha 1 had built himself a body the size of a Megazord, which they fought outside the Command Center, with Alpha 5 wearing Billy's armour. When it was broken he would not be mended. He blew himself up, promising to come back. Afterwards Zordon promised to stop treating his Rangers as his children.

Dark Specter

He kept his promise. By early 1995 he was in the service of Master Vile, who offered him to Dark Specter as a body to wear in the world. Dark Specter scorned him. Alpha 1 went with Rita, as Mistress Vile, to fetch the Vessel, Zordon's old body, from the planet Bizerk.

Once Dark Specter had come through the Arch in February 1995, he destroyed Alpha 1.

pages.title: Amanda Sefton
infobox: Kurt Wagner, who has also been her lover
The Winding Way, taught at home by her mother
The Excalibur team, as Daytripper (1994 to 1997)
pages.html:
Amanda Sefton is the name that Jimaine Szardos, a Romani witch, has gone by since the 1970s. She is the daughter of Margali Szardos and the foster sister of Kurt Wagner, with whom she grew up in a Bavarian circus. She was his girlfriend for years before he knew who she was. Early in 1994 she took the name Daytripper and joined the Excalibur team on Muir Island, the only witch who has ever served with it.

The circus

Jimaine was born about 1955, the younger child of Margali Szardos, and grew up in the Jahrmarkt, the travelling circus in Bavaria where her mother told fortunes. She trained on the trapeze. Her mother took in a baby with indigo fur that same year. Jimaine grew up beside Kurt Wagner, half his sister and, before long, in love with him.

Her mother taught her at home, as the women of the family have always been taught, for Jimaine had the Szardos magic in her blood. Margali told her that she would walk the Winding Way and one day carry the Soulsword. Jimaine did not care much for any of it. When she meant to leave the circus with Kurt, a performer who had taken her place in the act was killed, by a creature that looked like the demon Belasco. Jimaine believed that she had been the one meant to die. She stayed, and she learnt the Way. She did not know for many years that the creature had been her mother.

Amanda Sefton, 1975 to 1986

After her brother Stefan died, Kurt was blamed, and he left for America with Charles Xavier. Jimaine never believed that he had murdered anybody. She went to America too, changed her name to Amanda Sefton and became an air stewardess. A spell of her own kept Kurt from knowing her face. At his first Christmas with the X-Men, in December 1975, they met, and they fell in love.

In 1980 Margali drew Kurt into her Inferno to avenge Stefan. Amanda showed the X-Men the way down to her mother, and when it was over she told Kurt who she was. She went on fighting beside the X-Men for some years. In 1983 she asked Doctor Strange to take her as his pupil, and he refused.

Early in 1986, after the X-Men's meeting with the Beyonder, Kurt accused her of using spells to make him love her. She walked out, and was sorry almost at once.

Muir Island, 1989 to 1991

In 1989 she went looking for Kurt at the lighthouse where the Excalibur team lived, and found only Brigadier Alysande Stuart. The two of them went on to Muir Island just as the Reavers attacked it. Amanda turned herself into a mermaid to dive after the drowning Banshee, then carried him by magic to Moira MacTaggert's laboratory. Her spells only half worked on the Reavers themselves, since there was too much iron in their machine bodies. In 1991 she fell under the Shadow King's control with the rest of the island, and when he was beaten she left to put her life back together.

Daytripper, 1994 to 1997

Early in 1994 Kurt asked for her help. She came to Muir Island under a new name, Daytripper, chosen with a nod to his own. With Meggan and Rachel Summers she searched the stream of time for the lost Brian Braddock. When they found him, the two had to change places: Brian came home, while Rachel went into the stream. In February Amanda and Kurt freed her mother from the demon D'Spayre at Cottbus.

In the summer of 1994 she comes and goes from the island. To any Muggle who has seen her at work she is one more of Muir Island's mutants, and her spells pass for a mutant's powers. She has never said otherwise.

That autumn she killed the sorcerer Gravemoss with the Soulsword, then talked Kitty Pryde into letting her keep it. She gave it to her mother, which was the worst thing she ever did: Margali used it to murder every witch and wizard ahead of her on the Winding Way. In 1996, when Margali loosed the demon beneath London, Amanda was the one who bound it again. Early in 1997 she left the team, saying goodbye to nobody but Piotr Rasputin. In fact it was not Amanda at all, but her mother, hiding from Belasco in her daughter's body.

Limbo

In 1998 mother and daughter changed back in Limbo. With Kurt's help they beat Belasco. With Belasco gone, Amanda was the only one able to rule Limbo, and if nobody held it, its demons could use its stepping discs to reach the Earth. So she stayed. In 2000 she took the name Magik, so that her enemies would take her for Illyana Rasputina, who had ruled Limbo before her. Belasco drove her out of it in the end, and she lost the Soulsword.

pages.title: Amaterasu
infobox: Amaterasu, the sun goddess of Japan
pages.html:
Amaterasu is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in Japan as the goddess of the sun. In 2004 she came to Earth with Lord Yu and Camulus to ask for help against Ba'al. She went home without it. By early 2005 she and Yu were gathering their armies for a last stand. What became of her is not known.

The sun goddess

Amaterasu came quietly to Japan, against Ra's ban. On islands at the far eastern edge of Asia she was a very long way from the North, which suited her.

The Japanese worshipped her as the goddess of the sun. They told how she once shut herself away in a cave, in anger at her brother, until the other gods lured her out. The emperors of Japan claimed descent from her.

The embassy to Earth

Earth's defeat of Anubis in 2004 left the System Lords in disarray. To avoid open war among themselves, they agreed to divide his territories and his armies evenly. Ba'al learnt where Anubis had been making his Kull warriors, and he took the place for himself.

That summer Camulus asked Earth for talks. The System Lords sent him to Stargate Command with Amaterasu and Lord Yu, to ask for Earth's help against Ba'al. Amaterasu said what the others had been thinking. Asgard, she pointed out, had not come to Earth's aid when Anubis attacked it, and nobody had heard from Asgard for a long time. Ba'al was convinced that Asgard could no longer exercise its power in the galaxy, and he meant to take the protected planets for himself.

After a thousand years of keeping the treaty for fear of Asgard, the System Lords were beginning to wonder whether there was anything left to fear. Daniel Jackson, who knew perfectly well where Asgard's strength had gone, told her that Earth talked to Asgard all the time. Earth was now keeping up Asgard's bluff for it.

The System Lords offered Earth the means to build a fleet of ships as good as their own motherships. Elizabeth Weir, who led Earth's side, declined. Amaterasu then wondered aloud what Ba'al would think if he heard that Earth's great Ancient weapon was temporarily out of commission. He would come to take Earth for himself, Camulus observed. Earth would have to destroy him, and the System Lords would have to give Earth nothing at all.

When the talks broke down, the System Lords secretly sent a ship to test Earth's defences. Earth held the delegates prisoner. The ship never came, because Ba'al destroyed it on its way. Weir then let them go, judging them more use fighting Ba'al than sitting in a cell. Camulus stayed behind to ask for asylum. As she left, Amaterasu asked Weir to 'make sure Camulus knows he will forever be branded a traitor and a coward'.

The last stand

By early 2005 Ba'al had killed or broken one System Lord after another. The Tok'ra reported that Amaterasu and Lord Yu were rallying their armies for what would probably be their last stand. The free Jaffa were moving against her as well. Bra'tac said that they had allies within the ranks of Amaterasu's own Jaffa, ready to help when they struck.

Then the Replicators began a full-scale invasion of the galaxy. By then the System Lords knew exactly what had kept Asgard so busy. The Ancient weapon on Dakara destroyed every Replicator in the galaxy. Yu was dead by then. Ba'al fled from the free Jaffa at Dakara, and the rule of the Goa'uld collapsed.

What became of Amaterasu in all this was never recorded.

pages.title: Amuro Ray
infobox: The Imperial Entanglement, at fifteen; the Intergalactic War
pages.html:
Amuro Ray was the pilot of the RX-78-2 Gundam. He was the fifteen-year-old son of its designer, Tem Ray, when he first took it into battle against the Galactic Empire at Side 7 in 2293.

Side 7

Amuro Ray grew up on Starbase Side 7, where his father was building the Gundam. On 17 May 2293 the Galactic Empire attacked the starbase. Its small fighters swarmed around a Starfleet that had none of its own. Amuro, who had read his father's manuals, climbed into the Gundam. He destroyed fighter after fighter with it, though he had never flown a mobile suit before.

The war

He flew the Gundam again in the Intergalactic War, by then a grown man. At the Battle of Earth in March 2300 he fought beside Char of Aznable, the Klingons' Red Comet, against the Imperial fighters.

In the saga

Amuro Ray has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: The Ancient One
infobox: Wizard, of a hidden village of wizards
Wong, whom he sent to Strange
pages.html:
The Ancient One was a wizard of Kamar-Taj, in the Himalayas, who lived for five centuries and was Sorcerer Supreme for most of them. He made Kamar-Taj a school of wizards. In the early 1960s he took as his last pupil a broken American surgeon called Stephen Strange. He died in 1973, and Strange succeeded him.

Kamar-Taj

He was born in the fifteenth century in Kamar-Taj, a hidden village of wizards high in the Himalayas, and he worked its fields as a young man. His friend Kaluu was the first of the two to reach for the deeper arts, and they learnt them together. Between them they made the valley a paradise where nobody grew ill or old.

Kaluu wanted more. He made the people of Kamar-Taj his slaves and named himself their king. The young wizard fought him and won, but the village was destroyed in the fighting, with its people. He banished Kaluu from the world, and it cost him most of his power. He kept the slow ageing that the valley had given him, and with it he lived for five hundred years.

Five centuries

On the ruins he made a school. He gathered pupils to it: grown witches and wizards who had found their way through the snow to its gate. In time he became Sorcerer Supreme, the chief guardian of the Earth against attack by magic, and he held the office for most of five centuries. His first chosen successor turned to the dark arts, and he sent him away.

In the twentieth century his most gifted pupil was Baron Mordo, a Transylvanian nobleman, who meant to have the old man's power before he was ready to give it.

Stephen Strange

In about 1962 a New York surgeon whose hands had been ruined in a car crash came to Kamar-Taj and demanded to be cured. He was Stephen Strange, a No-Maj-born wizard who had turned his back on the wizarding world thirteen years before. The gate let him through, so the Ancient One knew what he was. He would not heal him. He offered to teach him instead, which Strange did not want.

Strange changed his mind when he found Mordo's plot against his master's life, and foiled it. The Ancient One taught him magic without a wand, to a height no school could reach, and humility along with it. He sent Wong, a wizard of a family that had served him for generations, to look after him in New York.

Death

In 1973 the creature called Shuma-Gorath, a power from outside the world, came at the Ancient One through his own mind. At his wish Strange shut his master's mind for good, trapping the creature inside it. The Ancient One's body crumbled to dust, and his spirit passed out of the world. Strange became Sorcerer Supreme in his place.

pages.title: Ancients
infobox: Human beings raised to the order of the Maiar
The Stargates; outposts across the galaxy
A city that could sail between the stars
Not to meddle in the affairs of the living
pages.html:
The Ancients are the builders of the Stargates, a people of human beings who long ago rose to a higher plane of existence and became Maiar, spirits of the same order as Gandalf, in the service of God. Nobody knows when they were mortal. They left the Stargates behind them, with outposts and weapons scattered across the galaxy. They also left the memory of a city that could sail between the stars, which myth has confused with Atlantis.

The builders

The Ancients built the Stargates, the great rings that open a passage from one world to another, and set them in a network across the galaxy. The Goa'uld did not make a single one. They found the gates, as they found most things. Then they used them to carry their slaves and armies from world to world.

The Ancients also left outposts, machines and stores of knowledge on many worlds. Their language survives in inscriptions, and it looks a little like Latin, which has misled more than one scholar. In 1999 one of their repositories forced its knowledge into the head of Jack O'Neill, who could neither use it nor bear it for long. Asgard took it out again.

Ascension

At some time nobody can now fix, the Ancients ceased to be mortal. They rose to a higher plane of existence and became Maiar, spirits of the same order as Gandalf, in the service of God. They are the only mortals known to have been raised to that order, apart from the few whom Oma Desala has helped to follow them.

As Maiar they keep one rule above all: they do not meddle in the affairs of the living. They are hard on those of their number who break it. Oma Desala, who helps those she judges worthy to rise, has been in trouble with the rest of them more than once.

The worst of it was Anubis. The Devil gave him the power to deceive Oma, and she began to help him rise before she saw what he was. A being as wicked as a Goa'uld could never finish that journey. He was left halfway, in torment, and the Ancients would not admit him.

In 2002 Oma raised Daniel Jackson, who was dying. For a year he was one of them, until he tried to interfere and was sent back, without his memories. In 2003 she raised the people of Abydos beyond Anubis's reach before his weapon fell on their world.

Before they came to this galaxy, the Ancients lived in another, which takes its name from them: the Alteran galaxy. Their story there cannot have begun before the Third Age, for in the First Age there was hardly any life beyond the Earth. There the Ori, Maiar who had followed Melkor and been cast out with him, set themselves up as gods. The Ancients who would not worship them left.

The city

The Ancients once had a city that could sail between the stars. It could rest on the sea, or sink beneath it and rise again. More than one story of a shining city lost under the waves began with it.

Long ago, at a time nobody can now fix, it stood on Earth, where the Antarctic ice now lies. Then it rose and went out among the stars. It is believed to lie now in another galaxy.

Atlantis

Myth has mixed the city up with Atlantis, and so have nearly all the people who think they know where Atlantis was. Two kingdoms under the sea claim the name. The Sub-Mariner's people, under the Antarctic sea, say that they are the true Atlantis, the heirs of the island that went down in the Cataclysm in the days of Kull. Aquaman's Atlantis, the kingdom of his mother's people, says the same of itself. Each disputes the other's claim, loudly.

Neither is right. The Atlantis of the old story, the great island kingdom of the West that grew proud, made war on the powers of the West and was swallowed by the sea, was Númenor. The Elves called it Atalantë, the Downfallen. Both undersea kingdoms are real, and both are old, but neither is the place the story remembers. Albus Dumbledore, the only man alive who knows the whole truth, has tried to tell both kings more than once. Neither believes him.

No living man or woman knows the whole truth of it except Albus Dumbledore.

Dumbledore suspects that the Ancients were somehow related to Númenor. He has never been able to work out exactly how. Nor, if he is right, can he see how they left Earth to build an empire among the stars and make the Stargates.

On Earth

The Ancients left an outpost on Earth itself, under the Antarctic ice. In 2004 Anubis came for it, believing that Earth held the secrets of the Ancients, and he was right. Jack O'Neill, carrying their knowledge in his head for the second time, reached the outpost first. From its chair he sent out the drone weapons that destroyed Anubis's fleet.

They also left a weapon on Dakara that could wipe out every living thing in the galaxy. In 2005 Earth turned it on the Replicators instead.

pages.title: Anezka
infobox: Vampire (Kindred); for eight centuries a ghoul
pages.html:
Anezka is a Bohemian nun of Prague who nursed the wounded crusader Christof Romuald in 1141, and loved him. The Tzimisce took her and made her the ghoul of the Methuselah Vukodlak. She seemed to turn against Christof, and spent more than eight hundred years at her master's side. All that time she worked in secret against his waking, and prayed for Christof to come back. When Christof destroyed Vukodlak in New York in 1999, he Embraced her so that she would not die. She became his childe.

The nun of Prague

Anezka was a young nun in Prague in 1141. When the French knight Christof Romuald was wounded in battle there, she nursed him back to health in a church. The two of them fell in love, though neither said so. Their vows stood between them, and she kept hers.

That same year Christof was Embraced into Clan Brujah, and the faith he had shared with her broke. Anezka's did not.

Vukodlak's ghoul

In the war between the Tremere and the Tzimisce, the Tzimisce took her. At Vyšehrad, their castle above Prague, she was made the ghoul of the Methuselah Vukodlak. He was an elder of the clan who lay sleeping beneath the castle, and he meant to rise above the ancestors of every clan. His blood kept her from growing old. With it came the bond that such blood brings.

When Christof came to Vyšehrad for her, she turned from him and went to wake her master. Before she could, mortal forces stormed the castle and brought it down. The elders of the Tzimisce bound Vukodlak in a sleep of their own. Anezka stayed at his side.

Eight hundred years

For more than eight centuries she lived on Vukodlak's blood. She served his followers, who counted her one of his creatures. She was nothing of the kind. All that time she worked in secret against his waking, undoing what she could of the work of those who meant to raise him. Every night she prayed for Christof to come back.

In 1999 Vukodlak's followers carried him to New York and hid him beneath the Cathedral of Flesh. Anezka went with him. By then she lived only by the Methuselah's blood. When Christof found them, Vukodlak offered her to him, if Christof would serve him. Christof refused. Thrown into the tunnels beneath the Cathedral, he found the Wall of Memories. In it he saw what she had done for eight hundred years.

The Embrace

Christof went back up into the Cathedral and destroyed Vukodlak. With her master gone, Anezka had no blood left to keep her. Without it the centuries she had been spared would have taken her at once. Christof was reconciled with her. He Embraced her so that she would not die, and she rose of Clan Brujah, of the tenth generation: his childe.

In later years Kindred who saw a beautiful, quiet woman at Christof's side often took her for a Tzimisce. Eight centuries of a Tzimisce Methuselah's blood leave their mark. She never troubled to correct them.

pages.title: Angela Orosco
infobox: Thomas Orosco, a lumberjack, whom she killed
On a burning staircase in the Lakeview Hotel
pages.html:
Angela Orosco was a girl of nineteen who came to Silent Hill in September 1994, at the same time as James Sunderland. She said she was looking for her mother. She had been abused by her father since she was a child, and she had killed him. The town showed her fire. She walked into it.

Before Silent Hill

Angela was born about 1975. Her father, Thomas Orosco, was a lumberjack. He abused her from childhood. Her mother knew, and told her that she had deserved it.

When Angela left school she ran away from home. Her father found her and brought her back. Some time after that, Thomas Orosco, aged thirty-nine, was found stabbed to death in his room. He had died late at night. The newspaper said that the police thought it a crime of passion, as nothing had been stolen. Angela was already gone.

The town

James Sunderland met her first in the graveyard on the edge of Silent Hill. She was looking for her mother, she said. She advised him to keep out of the town.

He met her again in an empty flat, lying on the floor in front of a mirror with a kitchen knife in her hand. He talked her into giving it up. She handed it to him, then shrank away when he reached for it, as though he had meant to use it on her.

Under Toluca Prison he heard her screaming. The thing that had her in a corner was the size of a bed. It was made like two bodies under one skin, one pressing the other down. James killed it. Angela kicked it again and again, then threw a television set on top of it. It had been her father, as she saw him. She turned on James afterwards. He was the same as the rest of them, she said. He had probably wanted his sick wife out of the way.

The staircase

The last time James saw her was in the Lakeview Hotel, on a staircase with the walls on fire. She took him for her mother at first. She asked for her knife back. He would not give it to her. He remarked on the heat. For her, she told him, it was always like that.

She thanked him for saving her in the prison, though she wished he had not. Then she turned round, climbed the stairs into the fire and was not seen again.

The town calls people who have done something they cannot live with. James Sunderland found things there that wanted to punish him. Angela found her father waiting, with flames wherever she looked. James saw the fire only when he stood beside her.

pages.title: Anguirus
infobox: A giant armoured reptile, from the age of the great reptiles
Killed by Godzilla at Osaka Castle, January 1955
Godzilla's ally, on Monster Island by 1972
pages.html:
Anguirus is a four-legged monster with a shell of spikes, a creature of the age of the great reptiles that the bomb tests woke as they woke Godzilla. The first Anguirus was Godzilla's first enemy, killed in Osaka in 1955. A second became his most loyal friend.

Osaka, 1955

In January 1955 two pilots of an Osaka fishing company found Godzilla fighting another monster on Iwato Island. Scientists in Osaka put a name to it: Anguirus, a quick, savage, armoured reptile known until then only from its bones. Both monsters fell into the sea.

They came ashore again at Osaka, where a fire in the docks had drawn Godzilla. The fight wrecked the city. It ended at Osaka Castle, where Godzilla bit through Anguirus's throat, then burnt the body.

Godzilla's friend

By 1972 a second Anguirus was living on Monster Island beside Godzilla. When the hunters of Nebula M began to call monsters down on Tokyo, Godzilla sent Anguirus ahead to Japan to see what was happening. The Self-Defence Forces, not unreasonably, drove him back into the sea. He returned with Godzilla. The two of them fought Gigan, with King Ghidorah, until both invaders fled.

In 1973 an earthquake set off by a bomb test split Monster Island, so that Anguirus fell into the crack. He survived it.

In 1974 a Godzilla came out of Mount Fuji, to all appearances the real one. Anguirus knew better. He attacked it at once. It was Mechagodzilla in a false skin, which broke his jaw for his trouble.

Later years

In 1999 he was among the monsters that the Kilaaks took from Monsterland. At Mount Fuji, once free, he sank his teeth into one of King Ghidorah's necks. He did not let go.

pages.title: Anubis
infobox: The jackal-headed god of the Egyptian dead
Stranded halfway between ordinary life and a higher plane, in endless torment
The power to deceive Oma Desala
Lord Yu, SG-1, the Tok'ra, Asgard
Held by Oma Desala in a struggle without end, from 2005
pages.html:
Anubis is a Goa'uld whom the other System Lords banished long ago, for crimes so terrible that even they could not stomach them. They believe him dead. He is not. The Devil gave him the means to deceive Oma Desala, one of the Ancients, into helping him rise to a higher plane of existence. No being as wicked as a Goa'uld could ever finish that journey, and the Devil knew it: Anubis was left halfway, in a state of endless torment. From 2001 he made war on the System Lords, the Tok'ra and Earth with what he had brought back. In 2005 Oma Desala, the Ancient who had helped him, took him out of the world, and he was not seen again.

Banishment

Anubis took his name from the jackal-headed god of the Egyptian dead, whose mask Ra's own guards wore. Whatever it is that keeps watch over the weighing of the dead in Egypt, it has never been him.

What he did to earn his banishment the Goa'uld prefer not to say. The Tok'ra say only that his crimes were unspeakable, even by the standards of the Goa'uld, which are not high.

The System Lords cast him out of their council, swore that he should never return and then tried to kill him. They believed they had succeeded. It was all so long ago that by 2002 only Yu, the oldest of them, was left of the System Lords who had done it.

Between the planes

While the System Lords believed him dead, Anubis set out to raise himself to a higher plane of existence, as the Ancients had done long before. The Ancients were human beings of a far older age, the builders of the Stargates. Those of them who ascended became Maiar, spirits of the same order as Gandalf, in the service of God.

No Goa'uld could make that journey, and Anubis knew it. He went to the Devil for help, and the Devil gave it gladly. The gift was a single power: the power to deceive Oma Desala, one of the Ancients, who helps those she judges worthy to rise. With it Anubis made her believe that he was worthy, and she began to help him.

The gift was a trick, and meant to be one. Anubis had believed that he could rise to stand near God, and near the Devil himself. The Devil does not forgive that sort of presumption in a parasite. He knew that a being as wicked and corrupt as a Goa'uld could never make the journey properly, however far it was helped along.

By the time Oma saw what Anubis was, it was too late for her to stop him on her own. He rose halfway and no further. He was left between ordinary life and the higher plane, neither one thing nor the other. It is a state of horror and endless torment. It was exactly what the Devil had intended.

The Ancients would not admit him, and they never quite forgave Oma for having helped him on his way.

He kept some of the knowledge he had gained. That knowledge, much of it the Ancients' own, made him the most dangerous Goa'uld there has ever been.

The return

Anubis came back after the deaths of Apophis and Cronus. At first he worked through underlords, among them Osiris, Zipacna and Tanith. In 2001 Tanith forced the Tollan, a people far more advanced than Earth, to build weapons for destroying Earth through the Stargate. The Tollan Narim blew the weapons up, and Tanith's ships laid Tollana waste.

In 2002 Osiris came before the System Lords in council on his behalf. Anubis, Osiris said, would destroy Earth as his gift to them if they took him back. Since he was not a System Lord, the Protected Planets Treaty did not bind him. They voted to take him back by six votes to one, with only Yu against. At the same time his underlord Zipacna fell on the Tok'ra base on Revanna, and very few of the Tok'ra there survived.

That year Anubis did a thing no other Goa'uld would have dared. Over Adara II, one of the protected worlds, the weapons of an Asgard ship made no impression on his shields, and Thor himself, who had come to drive him off, was taken prisoner. Anubis put a device into Thor's head that joined his mind to the ship's computers, meaning to read everything he knew.

Thor turned the link against him. Through it he let Jack O'Neill and Teal'c out of their cell. He guided them through the ship, which they crippled, and SG-1 got him away. Anubis withdrew when more Asgard ships arrived. He had learnt enough from Thor's mind by then to copy the way Asgard beams people from place to place, as well as its holograms.

Later in 2002 he used a weapon of the Ancients to hold open a wormhole to Earth's Stargate, pouring energy into it until it would explode with force enough to destroy the planet. O'Neill carried the gate away into space on Earth's new fighter, where it exploded harmlessly, while Teal'c, Bra'tac and Rya'c destroyed the weapon itself.

Abydos

Anubis built a great new ship with a weapon powered by the six Eyes of the Goa'uld. By 2003 he had five of them. The sixth, the Eye of Ra, was hidden on Abydos.

SG-1 found the Eye first. Yu had at last persuaded the other System Lords to act together, and their fleet came to face him. Daniel Jackson, whom Oma Desala had raised to a higher plane the year before, offered Anubis the Eye if he would leave Abydos alone for ever. Anubis agreed.

Once he had the Eye he destroyed most of the System Lords' fleet with his new weapon. Then he turned it on Abydos anyway. When Jackson struck at him, Oma Desala held Jackson back. The weapon fell on Abydos, but its people were already gone. Oma had raised them beyond his reach before it struck, Skaara among them.

Langara and the Kull

Later in 2003 SG-1 destroyed the weapon aboard Anubis's ship. Yu, whose mind was going, called off the attack that should have finished it.

Anubis took Jonas Quinn prisoner and read his mind. It led him to Langara, Jonas's home, and to its naquadria. He seized Kelowna while his Jaffa stripped the planet of the mineral. There Ba'al, now at the head of the System Lords' fleet, caught him and destroyed his ship. Anubis escaped in a pod.

He devised a new kind of soldier, the Kull warriors, armoured, nearly impossible to kill and utterly loyal to him. He made them on Tartarus, with a healing device of the Ancients and symbiotes without memories, born of a queen who served him. Later that year SG-1 got into Tartarus with Jacob Carter's help. They killed the queen, along with his servant Thoth, which slowed the making of more.

Earth

In 2004 Anubis came for Earth itself. He believed it held secrets of the Ancients, and he was right: there was an outpost of theirs under the ice of Antarctica.

He sank American warships from orbit, then appeared as a hologram in the White House to demand that Earth surrender to its god. The President of the United States offered to discuss the terms of Anubis's surrender instead.

Then the whole of his fleet came. Jack O'Neill, who carried the knowledge of the Ancients in his head at the time, reached the outpost first. From its chair he sent out its drone weapons, which destroyed Anubis's fleet, flagship and all.

Anubis did not die with it. Later that year what was left of him reached Earth aboard the International Space Station and passed from one body to another inside Stargate Command, trying to get to the gate. He went through at last in the body of a Russian officer, Colonel Alexei Vaselov, who had offered himself to spare the others. Samantha Carter had changed the address, so the gate sent him to a frozen world.

Dakara

Anubis got away from the frozen world. In secret he took back his forces from Ba'al, who from then on ruled the Goa'uld in his name.

He wanted the weapon that the Ancients had left on Dakara, which could destroy every living thing in the galaxy. Being what he was, he would survive it. Earth turned the weapon on the Replicators first, with Ba'al's help. In 2005 Anubis took Dakara back from the free Jaffa all the same, and he dialled every Stargate in the galaxy.

Oma Desala stopped him. Taking responsibility at last for the harm she had let loose, she rose against him and drew him away from the world into a struggle that neither of them can win. She cannot defeat him. But so long as she fights him he must fight back, and he can harm nobody else.

The weapon on Dakara fell silent. His Kull warriors stopped fighting and stood about, quite lost, as though nobody were telling them what to do any more.

Character

Anubis killed servants who failed him, as a lesson to the rest. He broke his word whenever it suited him, as Abydos found out. After his return he called himself a true god, in speeches grand even by the standards of the Goa'uld.

The other System Lords are cruel because cruelty is useful to them. Anubis was cruel in a way that frightened even them, and in the end he meant to kill every living thing in the galaxy except himself.

pages.title: Apocalypse
infobox: About 3000 BC, at Akkaba in Egypt
Command of every cell of his body
Unknown since early 1993, when he was left for dead on the Moon
pages.html:
Apocalypse is the first of the mutants. He was born in Egypt some five thousand years ago, in the years after the rising against Ra, and he has lived ever since by a single law: only the strong deserve to survive. He has added to his powers with the machines of the Celestials. He has slept away most of the centuries since his birth in hidden chambers, and each time he wakes he sets out to test the world, with four Horsemen to help him. Earth's heroes first met him in 1986. Nobody has known where he is since the beginning of 1993, when he was left for dead on the Moon.

Akkaba

En Sabah Nur was born about five thousand years ago at Akkaba, a settlement in Egypt, in the years just after the rising against Ra. Ra, the greatest of the Goa'uld, had ruled Egypt as its sun god until his slaves rose against him. Thor, the son of Odin, had come down in a storm to fight at their side, and Ra had fled. The Egypt the child was born into was a country getting used to the absence of its god.

He was born with grey skin and blue lips. The people of Akkaba took one look at him and left him in the desert to die.

He was found by Baal, the chief of the Sandstormers, a tribe of raiders who lived off the desert and whatever crossed it. This Baal was a mortal man, no kin to the Goa'uld System Lord Ba'al. The name means ‘lord’, and a great many men have borne it. Baal saw strength in the child. He raised him as his own son and named him En Sabah Nur, which means ‘the First One’.

The Sandstormers lived by one law, which Baal taught the boy before anything else: the strong survive, while the weak do not. En Sabah Nur grew up among them in the ruins of a god's rule. He drew his own lesson from Ra's fall, and he has never changed it. Ra had not been driven out because he was a tyrant. He had been driven out because he was not strong enough.

The First One

Baal died while En Sabah Nur was still young. The Sandstormers were attacked by the soldiers of a general called Ozymandias, and Baal, badly wounded, took refuge with the boy in a cave. Before he died he showed him what lay hidden there: machines left on Earth by the Celestials, the space gods who visited it before history began.

En Sabah Nur went into the royal city as a slave. There Ozymandias's sister, Nephri, took a liking to him, until she saw his true face and turned from him in disgust. His rage woke his powers to their full height. He gave himself a new name, Apocalypse, and from then on he did not grow any older.

He turned Ozymandias into a creature of living stone, blind, but able to see what is to come. Ozymandias has served him ever since. Then Apocalypse withdrew into the desert, vowing to return one day to test the strong and weed out the weak.

Powers and the machines of the Celestials

Apocalypse commands every cell of his body. He can make himself as tall as a house, grow his hands into blades or cannon, put out wings or close up any wound he is given. He is enormously strong, very hard to hurt and harder still to kill, since he can put himself back together after injuries that would kill anyone else.

The Celestials' experiments on the first human beings produced three new peoples: the Eternals, the Deviants and the mutants. Apocalypse has spent five thousand years studying the machines they left behind. He thinks of himself as tending what they planted, which in his view mostly means weeding it.

Like the Goa'uld, he rules by machines he did not make. Unlike the Goa'uld, he has taken the trouble to understand his.

The long sleeps

Apocalypse does not stay long in the world. He wakes, tests it and sleeps again, sometimes for centuries, while his body renews itself in one of the sanctuaries he keeps hidden about the world. Between sleeps he has gone about the earth in the guise of one god or another. He has set nation after nation at war, which he holds to be good for them.

His children, and their children after them, became Clan Akkaba, named after the village that left him to die. The clan has worshipped him as a living god for thousands of years. It watches over him while he sleeps, and wakes him when it must.

For his wars he chooses four servants at a time, named after the riders in the Revelation: War, Famine, Pestilence and Death. He calls them his Horsemen. He gives each of them new powers, which they pay for by belonging to him.

In 1859 he woke in London. There he gave a scientist called Nathaniel Essex the powers that made him Mister Sinister. Essex repaid him with a plague made to kill nobody but Apocalypse, who was obliged to go back to sleep to recover. Apocalypse forgave him with a warning, which is more than most people get.

The Goa'uld

After Ra's fall most of the Goa'uld kept away from Earth, since Ra had forbidden any of them to speak of it. At least one did not. Coming quietly to Earth in the centuries after Ra, it tried to take Apocalypse as its host, and it went in at the back of his neck, as the Goa'uld do.

Apocalypse, who can reshape every cell of his body at will, simply closed round it. The Goa'uld never learnt what had become of it. Apocalypse has never said, although it is a fair guess that he did not think it strong enough.

X-Factor

Apocalypse came to notice in 1986. That year the five original X-Men came together again as X-Factor, passing themselves off at first as hunters of mutants for hire. Early on they fought a band called the Alliance of Evil over Michael Nowlan, a mutant who could strengthen the powers of others. The master of the Alliance was Apocalypse.

He invited X-Factor aboard his ship, which hung unseen above Manhattan. He told them that their dream of peace did nothing to make mutants grow strong. They turned him down.

He chose four new Horsemen. Pestilence was Plague, one of the Morlocks, the mutants who live in the tunnels under New York. War was Abraham Kieros, a paralysed former soldier. Famine was Autumn Rolfson, an angry girl who wanted power over other people. The place of Death he kept for a man who had lost everything.

That man was Warren Worthington, the Angel, one of X-Factor's own founders. Late in 1986 killers working for Mister Sinister massacred the Morlocks, and Warren's wings were ruined in the fighting. In the spring of 1987 they had to be cut off. Soon afterwards the private plane he was flying blew up, and the world believed he was dead.

Apocalypse had taken him out of the plane at the last moment. He offered Warren new wings, but the price was Warren himself. By the end of 1987 Warren was the fourth Horseman, Death, with blue skin and wings of razor-edged metal.

At the start of 1988 the Horsemen fell on New York. Death fought his old friends until Bobby Drake, Iceman, tricked him into believing that he had killed him, and Warren turned on his master. With his help X-Factor beat the Horsemen. They took Apocalypse's ship for their headquarters.

Warren kept the blue skin and the metal wings. In 1989 he took a new name, Archangel. Few of Apocalypse's enemies hate him as Warren does.

Nathan

In 1991 Apocalypse's servants, the Riders of the Storm, carried off Nathan, the small son of Scott Summers, X-Factor's Cyclops. Apocalypse took the child to his stronghold on the Moon. There he infected him with a techno-organic virus, a sickness that turns living flesh into machinery.

X-Factor followed him to the Moon. They beat his Riders, wrecked his machines and seemed to have killed Apocalypse himself. Nathan was dying all the same.

A woman called Askani came out of the future, saying she had been sent to save the boy. Scott gave her his son. She took him away with her, nearly two thousand years ahead, where he might be cured.

His stronghold on the Moon was the Inhumans' city, whose people he had enslaved, and the Royal Family fought beside X-Factor.

Cable and Stryfe

Nathan grew up in the age that Askani came from, nearly two thousand years from now, in which Apocalypse rules the Earth. He spent his life fighting him. He came back to the twentieth century in 1990 as a grown man, with a metal arm where the virus had taken hold, under the name Cable. He took charge of a band of young mutants, the New Mutants, who became X-Force in 1991.

In case Nathan died of the virus, Askani's followers had made a clone of him while he was still a baby. Apocalypse's servants stole the clone. Apocalypse raised him as his heir, meaning one day to move into his body. The clone grew up believing that he was the real Nathan, abandoned by his parents. He called himself Stryfe.

When the time came, Apocalypse tried to pass into Stryfe's body. Nathan broke the bond between them, and Apocalypse's old body, with nowhere to go, withered away. That is the end of Apocalypse, nearly two thousand years from now.

Scott Summers saw it. In 1994, soon after he married Jean Grey, the two of them were drawn into that future in spirit. They spent twelve years there raising Nathan under other names, before they were returned to their own bodies.

The Moon

Stryfe followed Cable into the past. At the end of 1992 he shot Professor Xavier with a bullet carrying the virus, wearing Cable's face to do it. Then he had Scott Summers and Jean Grey carried off to Apocalypse's old base on the Moon.

Apocalypse had never fully recovered from his defeat of 1991, and his servants had woken him before he was ready. Stryfe caught him unawares and stabbed him in the chest. Apocalypse went to the X-Men for sanctuary. As the price of it he cured Xavier of the virus.

On the Moon his own servants, the Dark Riders, who had gone over to Stryfe, beat him almost to death. Archangel found him there. Apocalypse asked him to finish it. Warren refused, and left him to die.

Cable dragged Stryfe into a whirlpool of time, and the two of them vanished. Cable came back. Stryfe did not.

Nobody has seen Apocalypse since early in 1993. Nobody who knows him believes that he is dead.

Stryfe left something worse behind him. He had taken a plague that Apocalypse designed in the far future to kill the last people who were not mutants, turned it against mutants, and left it with Mister Sinister. It got loose at the end of 1992 as the Legacy Virus.

Later years

Apocalypse came back early in 1995. Five years later he very nearly found himself a new body. He meant to take the body of a young mutant of enormous power, but Scott Summers gave himself up in the boy's place, and for months the two of them shared one body.

Early in 2001 Jean Grey tore Apocalypse out of her husband, and Cable destroyed what was left of him. He came back from that too, as he has come back from every death anyone has ever given him.

The end of Apocalypse

Apocalypse had come back from every death anyone gave him, but there was no coming back from the end of his kind. He was not among those who outlived the Third World War, and by its end Wolverine was the last mutant alive.

So the future from which Cable and Stryfe had come, in which Apocalypse ruled the Earth two thousand years on, was never this world's. Like the world of Rachel Summers, it belonged to another history.

pages.title: Apophis
infobox: Apophis, the serpent of Egypt, enemy of the sun
Bra'tac; then Teal'c, who turned against him in 1997
2001, when his ship fell on Delmak
pages.html:
Apophis is one of the Goa'uld System Lords, the serpent god whose Jaffa wear the helmets of snakes. For thousands of years he was the rival of Ra, and when Ra died above Abydos in 1994 he moved faster than any of the others to take Ra's worlds. In 1997 he broke Ra's old ban on Earth and came through the Stargate, which began SG-1's long war with the Goa'uld. He lost two fleets in that war, as well as his queen, his son and his freedom. Every time, he came back stronger, until the Replicators finished him in 2001.

Ra's rival

Apophis takes his name from Apep, the great serpent of Egyptian story, who was the enemy of the sun. His host is an Egyptian scribe, whom he took thousands of years ago and has kept young in the sarcophagus ever since. The man is still in there, as every host is, although it was a very long time before anybody heard from him.

The priests of Egypt told how the serpent lay in wait every night for the boat that carried Ra through the underworld, and how every night he was beaten back. The story was a tidier version of the truth. For thousands of years Apophis was Ra's rival among the System Lords. Neither of them ever quite managed to destroy the other, and neither ever stopped trying.

They could still make common cause when it suited them. Long ago both of them joined the alliance that brought down Sokar, once among the mightiest of the System Lords. When the Egyptians rose against Ra, with Thor fighting beside them, Ra fled Earth and forbade any Goa'uld to speak of it again. Apophis kept the ban with the rest. He had no more wish to meet Thor than they had.

Chulak and the First Primes

Apophis rules from Chulak, the home world of the Jaffa. His personal guard, the Serpent Guard, wear helmets shaped like the heads of snakes. Every Jaffa in his service bears the mark of the serpent on his forehead, and for his First Prime it is set in gold.

For many years his First Prime was Bra'tac, the old master of the Jaffa of Chulak. Bra'tac served him faithfully, and believed privately that he was no god at all. He kept the belief to himself. In 1984 he was one of those whom the Beyonder carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars, so that a servant of Apophis stood for a while among the heroes of Earth.

Bra'tac's successor was his best pupil, Teal'c. Teal'c's father, Ronac, had been First Prime to the System Lord Cronus, who killed him for losing a battle that could not have been won. The boy was sent with his mother to Chulak in disgrace. There he grew up under Bra'tac's teaching to serve Apophis, and he rose to be the highest of his warriors. As First Prime he led the raids by which Apophis took hosts and slaves from worlds such as Cartago. He also came to share his old master's doubt.

Thor

Towards the end of the tenth century Apophis did something the System Lords seldom do: he made common cause with his rivals. With Heru'ur, Ra's own son, and with Ba'al, he brought his fleet against the worlds of Asgard, on the reckoning that Thor could not be everywhere at once.

Thor met the three fleets above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space, which the Jaffa still will not name. Apophis saw what was happening to the other two. He turned his own round before the end, and his was the only one of the three to survive. It was the worst defeat the Goa'uld had ever suffered. The Protected Planets Treaty followed soon afterwards.

Apophis does not speak of it. Every Goa'uld is born with the memories of its ancestors, so every Goa'uld remembers Thor. Apophis remembers him twice over.

After Ra

In 1994 the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, destroyed Ra above Abydos. For the first time in thousands of years the System Lords had no Supreme System Lord, and Ra's worlds had no master. Apophis was quickest. He took more of Ra's domains than any of the others, and he took them first.

He had also learnt that it was the Tau'ri who had killed Ra. Earth was a nuisance again, and Ra was no longer there to forbid its name. As for Thor, Apophis had heard only what all the System Lords had heard: that the Thunderer seemed to be busy somewhere else. He did not know where, or why. Asgard had taken great care that he should not.

The rumour was stale by the time he acted on it. In August 1996 Thor, home from the war in the Pegasus galaxy, had fallen in New York in the battle with Onslaught. When Apophis came through the Stargate in 1997, the Thunderer was not merely busy but gone. Asgard had told the Goa'uld nothing. Apophis never knew how good his timing had been.

Earth

In 1997 Apophis came through the Stargate to Earth himself, the first System Lord to come openly in more than a thousand years. The gate stood in an American military base deep inside a mountain in Colorado. Five airmen were playing cards in front of it when it opened. His Jaffa seized one of them, Airman Carol Weterings, and Apophis looked her over. Then he had the other four shot. By the time the base's soldiers reached the gate room, he was going back through the gate with her.

The attack brought Colonel Jack O'Neill back into the service. It also sent him back to Abydos, whose gate he had reported destroyed in 1994. While his team was there, Apophis's Jaffa came through that gate as well. They seized Sha'uri, the wife of Daniel Jackson, and her brother Skaara, the boy who had taught O'Neill to want to live again. On Chulak, Apophis gave Sha'uri to his queen, Amaunet, as her host, and Skaara to his son, Klorel.

O'Neill's team followed them to Chulak and was taken prisoner there. Apophis's First Prime, Teal'c, was ordered to kill the prisoners. He turned on his master instead, escaped with them through the gate to Earth and joined O'Neill's new team, SG-1. From then on he was shol'va, the traitor, to every Goa'uld. Bra'tac became one of Earth's closest allies.

Apophis had come for hosts. What he had actually done was to remind Earth that the Goa'uld existed, and to show the Goa'uld that Earth would fight. From then on the System Lords took a close interest in Earth, and Earth, through SG-1, took a close interest in them.

The motherships

Early in 1998 Apophis came back in force. He and Klorel brought two motherships against Earth, the great pyramid-shaped ships of the Goa'uld, with an army aboard. SG-1 had already got on to his ship before it left. So had Bra'tac, who was still in Apophis's service. The old master threw in his lot with them, and together they planted explosives in both ships.

Both ships blew up above Earth. SG-1 escaped in death gliders and was picked up by an American space shuttle. Apophis and Klorel got away through the Stargate on board. Everything else was lost: the ships, the army and most of Apophis's standing among the System Lords. Hardly anybody on Earth ever knew how close it had come.

Apophis spent the rest of the year trying to make up for it. He kidnapped Teal'c's son, Rya'c, turned the boy's mind to his own service and hid in him a sickness meant to kill every living thing on Earth. SG-1 found the boy in time and broke the hold on his mind.

That summer Sha'uri bore Apophis a son. Amaunet had lain quiet inside her while she carried him, so that the child would live. A child of two Goa'uld hosts is called a Harcesis. It is born with all the knowledge of the Goa'uld in its head, and Goa'uld law forbids it. Sha'uri's father, Kasuf, hid the boy on Abydos, and Apophis was led to believe that Heru'ur had stolen him.

Sokar and Netu

Without his fleet Apophis was easy prey. Sokar, the old enemy whom he had once helped to bring down, caught him, tortured him to death, then revived him in the sarcophagus and began again.

Early in 1999 Apophis escaped in a death glider and crashed on a distant world, where SG-1 found him dying. He begged them for sanctuary, and they took him to Earth. Sokar fired a beam through the wormhole at the iris that guards Earth's gate, and he showed his face on it to demand Apophis back. Apophis died in the infirmary. Before the end his host, the Egyptian scribe, was able to speak for himself for the first time in thousands of years. When he died, Daniel Jackson said the rites of the dead over him. Then the body was sent through the gate to Sokar, who put it back in the sarcophagus.

In the summer of 1999 SG-1 found a world where Apophis had been training humans in the uniforms of Earth's teams to slip into the base in Colorado. They were still drilling for him months after his death on Earth, until SG-1 showed them a recording of his death and they gave him up. That autumn Amaunet tried to kill Daniel Jackson with her hand device, and Teal'c killed her to save him.

Sokar had sent Apophis down to Netu, the prison moon of Delmak, which he had made over in the likeness of Hell. Apophis did not stay a prisoner. He passed himself off as the First Prime of Bynarr, the underlord who kept the moon for Sokar, then killed Bynarr and began to raise the prisoners against their master.

A few weeks after Amaunet's death SG-1 came to Netu to rescue Jacob Carter, the host of the Tok'ra Selmak, whom Sokar had caught. Apophis captured them and tortured them for anything they knew that might help him against Sokar. The Tok'ra settled the matter with a bomb. It destroyed Netu, together with Sokar's ship in orbit above it, and Sokar died with his ship. SG-1 escaped with Jacob Carter. So did Apophis, who took Sokar's leaderless forces on Delmak for his own. He had come back from the dead with a larger army than he had ever had.

Heru'ur

Apophis's chief rival was now Heru'ur, Ra's son, who had once stood beside him against Asgard. While Apophis was still rebuilding, Heru'ur went after his son. Early in 2000 two of Heru'ur's motherships chased Klorel to Tollana, where the Tollans' guns destroyed them both. Klorel came down there in a death glider. The Tollans put him on trial, and their judges ruled that Skaara had the better right to his own body. The Tok'ra took Klorel out of him, and Klorel was sent away to a Goa'uld world.

That summer SG-1 destroyed a new kind of mothership that Apophis was building on a distant world. By the autumn of 2000 he and Heru'ur commanded the two largest armies the Goa'uld had. Together they could have overthrown every other System Lord. At war, they would have ruined each other. They agreed to meet alone in the Tobin minefield, a belt of floating mines left by a people long extinct, to talk of an alliance.

Heru'ur brought a gift to seal the bargain. It was Teal'c, who had been betrayed on Chulak by a Jaffa named Rak'nor and handed over to be broken by Heru'ur's torturer, Terok. Teal'c would not break. Rak'nor watched him hold out, and changed his mind. He struck Terok down, set Teal'c free and sent the senseless Terok across to Apophis in Teal'c's place.

Apophis had not come alone either. A whole fleet of his lay hidden close by under cloak. When he found that he had been cheated of Teal'c, he brought it out and destroyed Heru'ur's ship, with Heru'ur aboard. He took Heru'ur's fleet and Jaffa for his own. With them, and with Sokar's, he now led the largest army of any Goa'uld alive.

The Replicators

Early in 2001 Apophis brought his fleet to Vorash, the world where the Tok'ra had their base. SG-1 and the Tok'ra met him there with the mothership SG-1 had lately taken from Cronus. They dropped a Stargate into Vorash's sun with its wormhole open to a black hole, and the sun exploded. The blast destroyed Apophis's fleet. It threw his own ship, and SG-1's with it, into another galaxy. Teal'c, whom Apophis had taken prisoner in the battle, went with him.

Far from home, the Replicators found him. A strange ship attacked his. The Replicators came aboard from it, killing his Jaffa as they went. Apophis escaped in a cargo ship with Teal'c, whom he had revived in the sarcophagus and persuaded that he was once again his loyal First Prime. With Teal'c's help he took SG-1's ship and set a course for Delmak, his new home. He had brought the Replicators with him.

They took that ship too, and drove it towards home far faster than it had ever been built to go. SG-1 wrecked its sublight engines, so that it could not slow down when it came out of hyperspace, then got away with Teal'c in the cargo ship. The mothership fell on Delmak out of the sky. Apophis was still aboard, shut in his command chamber while the Replicators swarmed over him. He did not get out.

That was the end of Apophis, who had escaped Thor, Earth and Sokar in turn. The ship that killed him had once been Cronus's. His death also gave the System Lords their first sight of the Replicators, and the first hint they had of the war that had kept Thor so busy for so long.

pages.title: Aquaman
aliases: the King of the Seven Seas
infobox: Tom Curry, a lighthouse keeper; Atlanna, an exile of Atlantis
The All-Star Squadron; the Justice League (a founder, 1960 to 1985)
pages.html:
Aquaman is Arthur Curry, King of Atlantis, the son of a lighthouse keeper and a woman of the sea. He came out of the water in 1941, helped to found the Justice League at the turn of 1960, then was crowned in Poseidonis in 1964. For more than half a century he has also been the Sub-Mariner's bitterest rival, because each of them claims to rule the true Atlantis. Neither of them does.

Birth

Arthur Curry was born about 1920 in a lighthouse on the New England coast. His father, Tom Curry, kept the light. His mother, Atlanna, had come out of the sea. She was a woman of Atlantis who had been cast out of Poseidonis for loving the world above, washed ashore in a storm, then nursed back to health by the keeper she married.

She taught her son what she could. He learnt from her to breathe water, to swim faster than any fish and to call the creatures of the sea with his mind. She died while he was still a boy, so he grew up knowing her city only from her stories. He did not go down to it until he was a grown man.

His hair was the colour of sand. In Poseidonis that would once have counted against him. Atlantis has an old dread of fair-haired children, who are said to carry the mark of Kordax, an outlaw king of the ancient city who could command the beasts of the deep. Arthur had that gift as well, which did not help. The Sub-Mariner has never let him forget it.

Powers

Aquaman breathes air or water with equal ease. The pressure of the deep has made him far stronger and tougher than a man of the surface. He can swim at a hundred miles an hour. His mind can reach any creature of the sea, from a shark to a whale, and call it to his side. Most will come.

He has one great weakness. Out of the water his strength drains away, and after about an hour without it he begins to die. His mother's blood ages him slowly. In 1994, past seventy, he looks a man of forty. He cannot fly, which is another thing the Sub-Mariner has never let him forget.

The war

Arthur Curry came to public notice in 1941, when the U-boats were sinking ships off the American coast. He sank a good many of them himself. Sailors began to talk about the man in the orange shirt who could talk to fish.

After Pearl Harbor he served in the All-Star Squadron, Roosevelt's wartime gathering of every mystery man in the country. He fought the war at sea, as the Squadron's strongest members did, since the Spear of Destiny kept heroes of great power out of the lands the Axis held. In 1942, off Iceland, he met the Sub-Mariner for the first time. They have been quarrelling ever since.

Aqualad and Mera
