In 1960 he took in a boy called Garth, an Atlantean child born with purple eyes. The superstitious people of Poseidonis had taken those eyes for a curse and left him to die. As Aqualad, Garth became Aquaman's partner, then one of the founders of the Teen Titans.

In 1963 Mera came to him out of another sea entirely. She was the queen of Xebel, a kingdom of water folk in a dimension of its own, and she could shape water into anything she pleased. She had fled a usurper. She stayed for Arthur.

King of Atlantis

In 1964, after Aquaman had saved Poseidonis more than once, its council asked him to be king. He accepted. He married Mera that year in the city, and in 1965 their son, Arthur Curry junior, was born. The child breathed water from the first, as his father did.

He gained two lasting enemies in the next years. In 1966 his half-brother Orm, Tom Curry's son by a second wife, turned up as the pirate called Ocean Master. Orm had always hated Arthur for the gifts their father's other son had never had. In 1967 the treasure hunter Black Manta appeared, with a grudge against Aquaman that nobody has ever fully explained.

In 1977 Black Manta took the boy. He shut Arthur junior in a bubble of air, which for a child of the sea meant death, then made his father choose between him and Aqualad. The prince of Atlantis died at twelve years old. Mera never forgave Arthur for what she saw as his failure to save their son. Their marriage did not recover for many years.

Aquaman has given up the crown and taken it back more than once since. The scientist Vulko has been his counsellor through all of it. The king's rule over Poseidonis has always been uneasy, partly because he was chosen rather than born to it, and partly because he spends so much time with surface folk.

The history of his kingdom, from the drowning of the island to his own reign, is told on the page Aquaman's Atlantis.

The Justice League

At the turn of 1960 Aquaman was one of the seven founders of the Justice League, beside Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, the Flash, Green Lantern and the Martian Manhunter. He served in it for twenty-five years, longer than he has ever managed to keep the throne of Atlantis without a break.

By 1984 he was the League's chairman. That year an alien attack left the satellite unusable. He was angry that so few members had answered the alarm, so he dissolved the League, then re-formed it in Detroit with those willing to give it their whole time. He left the Detroit League himself in 1985. The same year, the Sub-Mariner joined the Avengers, which Aquaman took personally.

Twice in 1965 he went to Japan with the League, when Godzilla was loose there with two other monsters. In January he pulled the survivors out of a liner that Godzilla had sunk off Yokohama. On 19 December the battle was fought inland. Aquaman watched the coast, which nothing came near.

The quarrel over Atlantis

Aquaman holds that his mother's people are the true Atlantis. By their own chronicles they descend from the islanders of the drowned city, so he regards them as the only people with any right to the name. The Sub-Mariner's people, he says, are a blue race of the deep who moved into some ruins and took the name off the door. The Sub-Mariner says much the same of him, at greater length and at the top of his voice.

Their quarrel began in 1942. It has drawn in the Justice League and the Avengers time after time. Albus Dumbledore has tried several times to tell both kings that neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story, which was Númenor. Aquaman has never believed him. He has always suspected that the Sub-Mariner put Dumbledore up to it.

In the autumn of 1979 Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, walked home from New York to the Pacific along the floor of the Atlantic. Aquaman knew what had happened to Superman in 1954. He did not try to stop him. He called every whale within reach to swim on either side of Godzilla, steering him clear of the domes of Poseidonis, then kept him company as far as the Antarctic sea. The Sub-Mariner accused him of driving a monster into his waters. Aquaman said that he had merely seen a traveller to the border.

pages.title: Aquaman's Atlantis
infobox: Undersea kingdom of a water-breathing people descended from islanders of the surface
About 8000 BC, by its own chronicles
pages.html:
Aquaman's Atlantis is the undersea kingdom of Poseidonis, deep in the Atlantic, and of its sister city of Tritonis. By its own chronicles it is the island city of Atlantis itself, which went down about 8000 BC and lived on under the sea. Aquaman, the son of one of its exiles, has been its king since 1964. The Sub-Mariner's people deny its claim to the name, and it denies theirs. Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story, which was Númenor.

The island

The royal chroniclers of Poseidonis kept the history of their city for ten thousand years. In their account Atlantis was an island in the Atlantic, a city of scholars and sorcerers that had grown very rich. Then a star fell into the sea nearby. Its fire gave the island's wise men power beyond anything they had known, and they quarrelled over it.

About 8000 BC, by the chroniclers' reckoning, the island broke apart and went down. Its king, Orin, had seen what was coming. His scientists raised great domes over the cities of Poseidonis and Tritonis, so that when the sea closed over them, their people lived. The rest of the island died.

Learning the sea

Life under the domes could not last for ever, so the drowned cities changed their people. In Poseidonis the change came by science, over many generations. Its people learnt to breathe water, and most of them lost the power to breathe air for long. In Tritonis, which Orin's brother Shalako ruled, it came by sorcery. Its people grew the tails of fishes and became the merfolk.

The Atlanteans of Poseidonis look like the men and women of the surface, only paler, since they have lived so long in the dark. The deep has made them strong. They can bear its weight and its cold. A few minutes out of the water does them no harm. Much longer than that, and they begin to fail.

Kordax and the old fears

In the ancient city there was an outlaw king called Kordax. He could command the beasts of the sea with his mind, and he used them to make war on his own people. His hair was fair. Since his day Atlantis has dreaded fair-haired children, above all those born with his gift, and in darker ages it left them on the rocks to die.

It has other fears of the same kind. Children born with purple eyes were once thought cursed as well, which is why the boy Garth was abandoned before Aquaman took him in. Aquaman himself has both the fair hair and the gift. His people have learnt to live with it. The Sub-Mariner calls him the heir of Kordax whenever he wants to start a fight, which is often.

The crown

Atlantis has been a kingdom since before it sank, but its kings have not always been born to the throne. In hard times its council has chosen them. Aquaman's mother, Atlanna, was a woman of the city who loved the surface and was cast out for it. She married a lighthouse keeper of New England, and her son came out of the sea in 1941.

In 1964, after he had saved Poseidonis more than once, the council asked Aquaman to be king. He married Mera, the exiled queen of Xebel, in the city the same year. Their son, Arthur Curry junior, was born in 1965 and killed by Black Manta in 1977. The scientist Vulko has served the crown as counsellor through all of it.

The kingdom's enemies are many. Xebel, Mera's own kingdom in a sea of another dimension, has made war on it. Aquaman's half-brother Orm, the pirate called Ocean Master, has tried to take the throne. Black Manta has attacked the city itself. Aquaman has given up the crown and taken it back more than once. The council has sometimes ruled without him.

Poseidon and the trident

The people of Poseidonis revere Poseidon, the god of the sea, and their city is named for him. Among the treasures of its kings is a trident that their chronicles call the trident of Poseidon himself, which they say Orin carried down into the deep.

The Sub-Mariner's people say that the true trident of the sea god is the Trident of Neptune, which Namor won in 1966. Neptune is the Romans' name for Poseidon. Scholars of the surface have pointed out that the two kingdoms cannot both hold the sea god's own trident. Neither kingdom has thanked them for it.

Atlantis and the Sub-Mariner

Poseidonis has three answers to the Sub-Mariner's claim, and it gives all three at once. The first is the name: Aquaman's kingdom lies in the ocean that is named for Atlantis, while the Sub-Mariner's lies at the bottom of the world. The second is blood. The people of Poseidonis are the islanders' own descendants, by their chronicles, while the blue folk of Namor's empire are a different race of the deep, who found a drowned island and moved into it. The third is the island itself. The one the blue folk found sank in the Cataclysm, in Kull's day, and Poseidonis has always held that it was a land of barbarians of no account.

The Sub-Mariner answers that his people's Atlantis is ten thousand years older, and that a city which needed sorcery to breathe was never a people of the sea. Poseidonis also has a story that he does not care for. It says that the blue men came up out of the deep while the island of Orin was going under, then carried off whatever they could reach. The empire calls this a slander.

The whole history of the quarrel is told on the page The feud of Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner.

The truth of it

Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story. The island of Orin was real, and so are its drowned cities, but the great kingdom the Greeks remembered was older than either of the undersea Atlantises. It was proud, mighty and swallowed by the sea for making war on the powers of the West. That was Númenor, which the Elves called Atalantë, the Downfallen. Myth has also mixed into the story the memory of the star-faring city of the Ancients.

No living man or woman knows the whole truth of it except Albus Dumbledore. He has tried to tell Aquaman more than once, first in 1945. Aquaman does not believe him, and suspects the Sub-Mariner of putting him up to it.

pages.title: Arcade the assassin
infobox: Assassin, at a million dollars a time
Murderworld, built anew for each job
1988, at Strangeways in Manchester, with the Crazy Gang
pages.html:
Arcade is an American assassin who kills people for a million dollars a time, in a hidden funfair of his own building called Murderworld. He dresses like a music-hall comedian and talks like one. He has tried to kill Spider-Man, Captain Britain, the X-Men and the Excalibur team, among a good many others. He has never quite succeeded, and it is not clear that he minds.

Murderworld

Arcade says that he was born rich, in Texas or in Beverly Hills depending on the telling. He says, too, that he killed his father when his allowance was cut off, at eighteen or at twenty-one. Nobody knows his real name.

He found he had a gift for machines. With two assistants, Miss Locke and Mr Chambers, he built his first Murderworld, an underground funfair of brightly painted death traps. He builds each one to the weaknesses of the people he means to kill. He always leaves them a small chance of escape, since it is the game he enjoys rather than the killing. If they find it, he lets them go without a fuss.

The first contracts

Arcade first came to public notice in the autumn of 1977, when he tried to kill Spider-Man and Captain Britain, who was visiting New York. They got out. He went on to try the X-Men, more than once.

The Crazy Gang, 1988

In the autumn of 1988 Arcade brought Murderworld to England, in a disused factory at Strangeways, in Manchester. With the Crazy Gang, a band of thieves dressed as figures from Alice in Wonderland, he took Courtney Ross as bait for Captain Britain. The Crazy Gang changed bodies with most of the Excalibur team.

Kitty Pryde and Lockheed, the only ones not caught, dragged Arcade into his own game. Kitty beat it with a program she had written with Doug Ramsey. Courtney put everyone back in their own bodies, and Commander Dai Thomas took Arcade away. Miss Locke and Mr Chambers slipped off, with a little help from Lockheed.

Later years

Arcade has gone on taking contracts. In later years he murdered Miss Locke in a temper and replaced her with robot copies. In 2012 he carried off sixteen young heroes to an island Murderworld and set them to fight to the death.

pages.title: Art Fortunes
infobox: The Beetleborgs; the Magnavores; the Astralborgs
The White Blaster armour; the Thunder Stinger; the Metallix armour; the Battle Station
pages.html:
Art Fortunes is an American comic-book artist, the creator of the Beetleborgs. In 1996 a wish made three of his characters real in the town of Charterville, with their enemies after them. Art became the real Beetleborgs' armourer, because whatever he drew, Flabber the phasm could bring to life. His elder brother, Les, drew the monsters on the other side.

The comic

Art draws the adventures of the Beetleborgs, three armoured heroes in the likeness of beetles, who fight Vexor's Magnavores. He lives in Urbana City, where he has his office. As a boy he made a comic at home with his elder brother, Les. Art drew its heroes, the Astralborgs, while Les drew its villains. It was buried afterwards, then forgotten.

The two brothers did not stay friends. Les became the black sheep of the family, ending up in Charterville Prison.

The convention

On 7 September 1996 three children of Charterville wished to be the Beetleborgs, a wish that Flabber granted. Art knew nothing about it. In October he came to a comic convention, where Vexor tried to have him kidnapped. Three Beetleborgs in real armour fought the monsters off in front of him. Art had invented them, so the sight was too much for his nerves.

The White Blaster

He recovered. In November 1996 Shadowborg took the three Beetleborgs' powers, so the children went to Art for help. He drew a fourth Beetleborg, the White Blaster, whose armour Flabber brought off the page for a boy named Josh Baldwin. He drew a new weapon for the Blue Stinger too, the Thunder Stinger. With those, Shadowborg was destroyed.

In May 1997 the Magnavores stole a drawing of a monster from his office. Art told the children that it was none of his. The monster was Nukus. That September Art told them whose work it was: his brother's.

The Metallix armour

On 8 September 1997 Nukus destroyed everything the Beetleborgs had. The next day the Crustaceans broke Les out of Charterville Prison. Art was there, shut in a cell with the three children. He begged his brother to make peace with him. Les refused.

Art drew the Metallix armour that day. The Crustaceans carried him off, treating him roughly, until the children got him back. Then he drew them a Battle Station with three Battle Vehicles. From that time he was at Hillhurst Mansion as often as the Beetleborgs were.

The Lost Comic

In November 1997 Les led the Crustaceans to the place where the brothers' boyhood comic lay buried. Art took the Beetleborgs after them. Out of its pages came the Astral Sword, the Astral Coins, his own Astralborgs, his brother's Mantrons and, in the end, the giant Roboborg.

On 2 March 1998 Les went back to prison of his own accord. Art had not won his brother back. He had at least stopped having to draw against him.

pages.title: Asgard
infobox: The Protected Planets Treaty, with the Goa'uld System Lords
The Replicators, in the Pegasus galaxy (until 2005)
Hala, Othala and Orilla, in the Pegasus galaxy
pages.html:
Asgard is the realm of the Aesir, the long-lived people whom the Norse worshipped as gods. It is ruled by Odin All-Father, and Thor is his son. Asgard is also a power among the stars, one that the Goa'uld System Lords fear. It holds the Protected Planets Treaty with them and is at war with the Replicators, which is why Thor is absent from Earth in 1994.

The Realm Eternal

Asgard is one of the Nine Worlds held in the branches of the World Tree, Yggdrasil. It is joined to Earth, which its people call Midgard, by Bifrost, the Rainbow Bridge, which the watchman Heimdall guards. Its golden city is ruled by Odin, with his wife Frigga beside him. Among its people are Thor; his adopted brother Loki, a scheming sorcerer; Balder the Brave; the warrior Sif and the Warriors Three.

The Aesir are far stronger and longer-lived than humans, though they are not immortal. They keep their youth by eating the golden apples of Idunn. The Norsemen knew them as gods. The old stories of Thor, Odin and Loki are memories of them. Asgard came to the notice of the modern world in 1962, soon after Thor did, and the Avengers have fought there more than once since.

The Protected Planets Treaty

The Asgard High Council holds a treaty with the Goa'uld System Lords, the parasites who rule much of the galaxy. Under it the Goa'uld must leave alone the worlds it names. Its terms bind Asgard as well. Asgard may not use its own technology to advance the peoples it protects, and a serious breach on one world could free the Goa'uld to attack all of them.

One protected world, Cimmeria, is home to a people descended from Norsemen. There Thor left a device known as Thor's Hammer, which seizes any Goa'uld who comes through the stargate. Earth is not one of the protected worlds.

The treaty came out of Thor's wars with the Goa'uld. He fought beside the Egyptians when they drove Ra off Earth some five thousand years ago, and for thousands of years afterwards he hunted the Goa'uld wherever they came near the North. He ended the war by destroying the combined fleets of Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al. The System Lords fear Asgard, but Thor they fear in particular. It is said in Asgard that their first demand was that he should not be present at the signing.

The Replicator war

The Replicators are machines built of small identical blocks, which join together into larger forms like insects. They feed on metal and technology. They copy whatever they take in, multiplying without end, and the more advanced the technology they take, the more dangerous they become. They adapt to Asgard's weapons as fast as Asgard can design new ones.

The war is fought in the Pegasus galaxy, far beyond this one. Asgard's worlds among the stars lie there: Hala, the first that the Aesir settled, Othala, the chief of them, and others besides. They are not the Realm Eternal, which is held in the branches of the World Tree, beyond the reach of any ship. The Replicators have already taken some of them.

The Aesir live for many centuries, but they are slow to have children, and a child is born among them only seldom. That has never mattered much before. It matters now. Every Asgardian the Replicators kill is a loss that will take generations to make good, and the Aesir are dying in this war far faster than children are born to replace them.

Asgard's fleet fights them under Thor's command. The war has become Asgard's first concern, and it has left Asgard less able to enforce its treaty with the Goa'uld. It also keeps Thor away from Earth. In his absence Eric Masterson, who once served as Thor himself, carries Odin's gift, the mace Thunderstrike, among the Avengers.

The Goa'uld have never been told of the war, and Asgard means to keep it that way. It goes on showing its ships over the protected worlds as though its fleet had nothing else to do. The System Lords, who do not know the truth, still believe Asgard could crush any of them that broke the treaty, and it is that belief, more than Asgard's ships, which keeps the protected worlds safe.

Losing the war

In 1996 Thor came home to fight Onslaught. He fell in that battle, and for more than a year Asgard believed him dead. The fleet fought on in the Pegasus galaxy without him. It lost a great deal of ground: ships, worlds and Aesir that Asgard could not replace. It told the Goa'uld nothing. When Thor came back to the fleet late in 1997, Asgard was losing the war.

Asgard and the Tau'ri

From 1998 Asgard dealt often with the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, through the team from Earth's Stargate known as SG-1. Thor answered Cimmeria's call for help himself that year. In 1999 Asgard took the knowledge of the Ancients out of Jack O'Neill's head on Othala, and Thor brought Earth under the Protected Planets Treaty.

Asgard's own minds had come to the end of what they could think of against the Replicators. The Tau'ri, whose science was simpler, kept finding answers that Asgard had missed. In 2000 Samantha Carter's plan destroyed a great swarm, at the cost of Asgard's newest warship. In 2003 SG-1 set right the trap on Hala. In 2004 O'Neill built the weapon that cleared Orilla, the world where the Aesir had made their new home after the Replicators overran Othala in 2002. In 2005 the Tau'ri turned the weapon of the Ancients on Dakara against the last of them.

Asgard repaid them with its trust. Thor spoke for SG-1 before the envoys of the great powers in 2003. Asgard lent Earth its engineers, and it fitted Earth's warships with some of its own technology.

The withdrawal from the stars

Asgard won the Replicator war in 2005, with a great deal of help from the Tau'ri. It had spent its people to do it. Afterwards it drew back from this galaxy. In 2006 a single Asgard ship stood with the fleet of Earth and the free Jaffa at the Ori's great gate. The Ori destroyed it.

In 2007 the High Council gave up Asgard's worlds among the stars, since the Aesir left there were too few to hold them. To the Tau'ri, the fifth race that Thor had once said they would become, Asgard gave the lore of the Aesir: what Odin's people know of the Nine Worlds, of the branches of Yggdrasil that join them, of the runes and of the Rainbow Bridge. It gave them none of its machines, for the Aesir teach younger peoples and do not arm them. When the Ori's warships came, Asgard destroyed Orilla rather than leave its lore for them. The last of the Aesir among the stars went home to the Realm Eternal, where children might be born to them in peace, however slowly.

That lore was kept, and kept classified. It came through the Third World War, and in 2063 Zefram Cochrane drew on what it told of the Rainbow Bridge to build the Phoenix, Earth's first warp ship. Only what touched warp flight was ever made public. Section 31 kept the rest classified.

pages.title: Ashley Williams
infobox: Gunnery Chief Williams; Ashley Madeline Williams
The garrison of Starbase Side 7, to 2293; the armoury of the USS Enterprise-B
The Imperial Entanglement; the Intergalactic War
pages.html:
Ashley Williams was a gunnery chief of the Starfleet Marines and the wife of John Shepard. She met him on Starbase Side 7 during the Imperial Entanglement of 2293, as the last survivor of her unit. She went on to run the armoury of the USS Enterprise-B.

Side 7

In 2293 Gunnery Chief Williams was serving with the Marine garrison of Starbase Side 7. When the Galactic Empire's stormtroopers boarded the starbase on 17 May, her unit was wiped out around her. Commander John Shepard's detachment from the USS Enterprise-A found her still fighting. She fought beside him for the rest of the battle.

The Enterprise-B

Shepard took her with him to the USS Enterprise-B, where she was put in charge of the armoury. She held xenophobic beliefs of her own, which she kept, on a ship whose crew came from many peoples. After several adventures together she fell in love with her captain. They married, and they had several children. After the Enterprise-B was lost at Tomed in 2311, the two of them retired from Starfleet to raise them.

In the saga

Ashley Williams has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Atlantis
infobox: A name claimed by two undersea kingdoms; the island of an old story
The island of Kull's day; the star-faring city of the Ancients
pages.html:
Atlantis is the great island kingdom of the old story, which grew proud, made war on the powers of the West and was swallowed by the sea. Two kingdoms under the sea claim its name: the Sub-Mariner's, under the Antarctic sea, and Aquaman's, in the deeps of the Atlantic. Neither of them is the Atlantis of the story. The closest thing to it that ever existed was Númenor.

The story

The Greek philosopher Plato told the story of Atlantis about 360 BC. In his account it was an island empire beyond the Pillars of Hercules, mighty, rich and proud. It made war on the peoples of the Mediterranean, failed, then sank into the sea in a single day and night. He said the story had come to Greece from the priests of Egypt.

Most of the people who think they know where Atlantis was are wrong, and so are most of those who think it never existed. Three real places lie under the story, and only one of them fits it.

What lies under the story

The first and truest is Númenor, the island kingdom of Men in the western sea, which the Elves called Atalantë, the Downfallen. It was founded at the beginning of the Second Age and grew greater than any kingdom of Men before or since. Its kings grew proud, made war on the powers of the West, then were drowned with their island late in that age. Elendil escaped with his sons, and from him came Aragorn. That is the story Plato heard, worn down by long ages of telling.

The second is the island of Kull's day, in the Thurian Age, which sank in the Cataclysm about 18,000 BC with Lemuria. It was real, and its people's blood ran on in the Cimmerians, but it was a land of barbarian tribes. Nothing in it resembled the empire of the story, apart from its fate.

The third is the star-faring city of the Ancients, which once stood on Earth where the Antarctic ice now lies. Myth has mixed its memory into the story as well. Nobody knows when the Ancients were mortal, or when the city left.

The two kingdoms

Two living kingdoms under the sea call themselves Atlantis, and each says that it is the only one with the right.

The Sub-Mariner's Atlantis is the empire of a blue-skinned people of the deep, under the Antarctic sea. Its people found the drowned island of Kull's day about 8000 BC and built their first city in its ruins. They hold that the drowned islanders were their own forefathers. Namor, the Sub-Mariner, is their king.

Aquaman's Atlantis is the kingdom of Poseidonis and Tritonis, in the deeps of the Atlantic. By its own chronicles it is the island city itself, which sank about 8000 BC, its people surviving under domes until they learnt to breathe water. Aquaman, Arthur Curry, is its king.

Each kingdom has spent most of the century calling the other a fraud. The quarrel between their kings began in 1942. It has drawn in the Justice League and the Avengers more times than either team would like. It is told on the page The feud of Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner.

Who knows

No living man or woman knows the whole truth of it except Albus Dumbledore, who has read more of the old histories than anyone alive. Gandalf knows it too.

Dumbledore has tried to tell both kings, in 1945, in 1964, on Rockall in 1979 and in letters in 1992. Neither believes him. Each is privately sure that the other put him up to it.

pages.title: Azathoth
infobox: The Daemon Sultan; the blind idiot god; the nuclear chaos
In a chaos beyond the world
The lesser Outer Gods, who dance about it
pages.html:
Azathoth is the greatest of the Outer Gods, the Daemon Sultan, who lies in a chaos beyond the world. It is blind and mindless. About it the lesser Outer Gods dance for ever to the thin piping of flutes. Its messenger, Nyarlathotep, goes out into the worlds to do what it cannot.

Beyond angled space

The books place Azathoth beyond angled space, in a chaos that no traveller has ever come back from. It is not a place a man could reach by ship or by star, nor quite a place at all. The Necronomicon, which says as little of it as it can, gives that chaos the name of Azathoth.

There Azathoth gnaws hungrily in a darkness without light, amid the beating of drums and the whine of flutes. The other Outer Gods dance about it without stopping.

It has no mind that any sage has ever found. It does not plan, or hate, or want. The books call it the centre of all things, and that is what makes it the most terrible of them to those who read of it. They are wrong about the centre of all things, which belongs to God. They are right that Azathoth cannot be reasoned with, or bargained with, because there is nobody there to bargain.

Spoiling at second hand

Azathoth spoils nothing on purpose, for it has no purposes. What it spoils, it spoils through others. Nyarlathotep is its messenger. It is through him that whatever Azathoth is reaches the world of men.

Cults that worship it are few, short-lived and mad. Sorcerers who try to call on it seldom survive the attempt, and the luckiest of them are those who fail.

Delta Green

What Delta Green knows of Azathoth comes almost entirely from the books, and the books are not to be trusted. It has never knowingly met it, and hopes never to.

pages.title: Ba'al
infobox: Baal, the storm god of Canaan
The coasts of the North, about 1000 BC
Thor, Lord Yu, SG-1, the Tok'ra
Shot dead by Cameron Mitchell in 1939, having travelled there from 2008
Taken from its host by the Tok'ra, 2008
pages.html:
Ba'al is a Goa'uld System Lord, and the cleverest of them by some distance. The Canaanites worshipped him as Baal. About 1000 BC he raided the coasts of the North in defiance of Ra's ban on Earth, and Thor followed him home. He has kept the ban ever since. From 2002 he was one of SG-1's most persistent enemies: he tortured Jack O'Neill to death many times over, led the System Lords against Anubis and outlived every one of them. He died in 1939, shot through the head by Cameron Mitchell, having gone back there from 2008 to change history.

Baal of Canaan

Ba'al took his name from Baal, the lord of storms whom the Canaanites worshipped, as did the Phoenicians. He came to them quietly, in defiance of Ra's ban, as a few of the bolder Goa'uld did, and he kept well away from the North.

His worship spread along the eastern shores of the Mediterranean. It lasted for centuries after he had stopped coming, and the prophets of Israel spent a good deal of their time denouncing it.

The raid on the North

About 1000 BC Ba'al grew bolder. He thought Ra's ban one of Ra's vanities, so he sent his ships to the coasts of what is now Norway to carry off people as slaves and hosts.

Thor met them on the shore. He killed every Jaffa who set foot on the beach, and he brought one of the ships down into the sea with his lightning. Then he followed the rest of them home. On the world where Ba'al kept his palace he freed the captives, broke the palace open and killed every Goa'uld he could find in it. Ba'al himself escaped.

Some time afterwards Thor sent him a jar. In it was the symbiote of one of his underlords.

Ba'al has kept Ra's ban ever since. He is not a Goa'uld who needs to be told anything twice. He had learnt to keep away from Earth. He had not yet learnt to keep away from Thor.

The war of the 990s

In the 990s Ba'al joined Apophis and Heru'ur in one of the very few alliances the System Lords have ever managed. The three of them brought their fleets together to strike at the worlds of Asgard, reasoning that Thor could not be everywhere at once.

Thor met them above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space. Ba'al's fleet was one of the two he destroyed, and Thor went down after its survivors to finish them on the ground. Apophis saved his own fleet only by running. Ba'al lived, as he generally does.

About the year 1000 the System Lords asked Asgard for terms, and the Protected Planets Treaty was the result. Asgard says, and the System Lords deny, that their first demand was that Thor should not be present at the signing. Earth was left off the list.

The summit and Jack O'Neill

By 2002 Apophis and Cronus were both dead. The other System Lords had spent months fighting over their worlds, and when they met in council to make peace, it was Ba'al who presided. Osiris came before them as the envoy of Anubis, whom they had banished long before and believed dead. Ba'al put Anubis's return to the vote. It passed by six votes to one, with only Yu against.

Ba'al's own lo'taur, his favoured human slave, warned Yu that Yu's slave was not to be trusted. He was quite right: the slave was Daniel Jackson in disguise.

Later that year Ba'al's Jaffa caught Jack O'Neill as he ran for the Stargate on the world of Ba'al's secret fortress. O'Neill was carrying a Tok'ra, Kanan, who had been blended with him to save his life. Kanan had once spied in Ba'al's household, where he had fallen for Ba'al's lo'taur, Shallan. He had used O'Neill's body to go back for her. When they were caught, Kanan abandoned O'Neill's body, leaving O'Neill to answer for him.

Ba'al wanted to know what Kanan knew. At the fortress he had been studying gravity in secret, and he pinned O'Neill to a wall with one of his gravity fields. Then he dropped knives into the field until O'Neill died. He revived him in the sarcophagus and began again. The next time he used acid. O'Neill was killed and brought back many times.

Earth had no ship that could reach the fortress. Instead it sent its plans to Yu, who had every reason to want the place destroyed, asking him to strike at its power first. Yu's ships bombarded it from orbit, the power failed and O'Neill escaped with Shallan.

The war against Anubis

In 2003 the System Lords put their fleets together against Anubis under Lord Yu, who was by then too far gone to lead them. Teal'c and Oshu, Yu's First Prime, persuaded Ba'al to take command. His fleet caught Anubis's great ship above Langara and destroyed it, although Anubis escaped in a pod.

Ba'al used the ships he had been given against Anubis to make himself greater than any of the others, which surprised nobody who knew him. On Erebus, a world he had lately taken, Jaffa who would not change masters mined naquadah for his new motherships until the fumes killed them. Bra'tac was among them, with Teal'c's son Rya'c, until SG-1 got them out.

Later that year he got hold of a computer virus that Earth had made to disable Stargates. He altered it, spread it through the whole network of gates and attacked his rivals while their gates were dead. He had the largest fleet of any System Lord, so he gained more from it than anybody.

Supreme Commander

Anubis's fleet was destroyed over Earth in 2004. To keep the peace, the System Lords divided his worlds among themselves. Ba'al, however, found Tartarus, where Anubis had made his Kull warriors, and took them for himself.

Yu, Camulus and Amaterasu went to Earth to ask for help against him. While they talked, Ba'al destroyed the ship they had come in. Camulus begged Earth for asylum. Ba'al got him all the same, by pretending to hold SG-1 prisoner and offering to trade them for him. Camulus was not seen again. When Moloc was killed later that year, Ba'al took his domain as well.

By 2005 he had conquered or cowed most of the other System Lords, and he called himself the Supreme Commander of the Goa'uld. In truth he was a servant. Anubis had returned in secret and taken back his forces. From then on Ba'al ruled in his name, which he disliked very much.

That year the Replicators came into the galaxy. The Goa'uld found out at last what had been keeping Asgard so busy, and it was not good news. The machines tore through the fleets of the System Lords. Yu was killed by one of them at the very meeting where Ba'al's envoy, Selkhet, had come to offer the last of the High Council terms.

Ba'al was losing too, so he came to Earth by hologram to ask for help. He told Earth of the weapon the Ancients had left on Dakara, which could wipe out every living thing in the galaxy, and warned that Anubis meant to use it. With his help Samantha Carter and her father, Jacob, turned the weapon on the Replicators instead. Ba'al gave them a means of dialling every Stargate in the galaxy at once, so that it struck everywhere together.

It was the end of the Goa'uld empire all the same. When Ba'al moved to take back Dakara, rebel Jaffa stormed his ship, and he saved himself by beaming away. Jaffa all over the galaxy saw one of their gods run, and stopped believing. Anubis kept Ba'al alive so that he could watch the end of everything. Then Oma Desala took Anubis out of the world, and Ba'al was left as the last of the System Lords.

The clones

With his armies gone, Ba'al went to Earth, the world whose ban he had kept for three thousand years. There was nothing left to keep. He set himself up as a businessman, bought companies and took over the Trust, a secret society of rogue intelligence agents that the Goa'uld had already got into. He also made copies of himself, each of whom claimed to be the real one.

In 2005 he warned Earth that he would destroy one of its cities if anybody tried to take him. SG-1 tried anyway. The bomb turned out to be a whole new skyscraper in Seattle, built with naquadah through its frame, and at the call of Earth's ship Prometheus an Asgard beam carried it into space before it went off. Gerak, a Jaffa leader, caught a Ba'al and put him to death on Dakara in front of Teal'c. It was one of the clones.

The clones went on scheming for years. In 2006 one of them set about brainwashing the new Jaffa High Council until Teal'c killed him. Others stole Stargates. Later that year a Ba'al crashed a ship on Earth and gave himself up, saying that his clones had turned on him. SG-1 rounded up twenty of them before they all escaped together, taking with them a list of the gate addresses of the Ancients.

In 2007 a Ba'al seized Adria, who led the armies of the Ori. He gathered the other clones in one place and killed them with poison, then put one more into Adria to take her as a host. SG-1 killed the Ba'al behind the plot. The Tok'ra took the one in Adria out of her, but as they did it he poisoned her with the last of his strength.

The last Ba'al

In 2008 the Tok'ra took the last of the clones from its host on their own homeworld, after reading aloud the list of Ba'al's crimes, which took three hours. The clone told SG-1 that they had made a terrible mistake. The real Ba'al was still at large, and he had planned for this.

He had. The real Ba'al had gone back through time, by way of an outpost for watching the sun on the world of Praxyon, to 1939. That year the Stargate was crossing the Atlantic to America in the hold of a freighter, the Achilles. Ba'al came through it with his Jaffa, killed the crew and left a bomb to sink the ship.

For a little while he succeeded. History ran differently: the gate lay frozen in the Arctic, there was no Stargate programme, and Ba'al, who knew what was coming, made himself master of the Goa'uld. He took Qetesh as his queen and Teal'c as his First Prime. He chose to deceive the people of Earth rather than slaughter them, having been impressed by them the first time round. Qetesh grew suspicious of how much he knew and killed him with a sword.

Cameron Mitchell was one of three members of SG-1 who had slipped through the change. He went back to 1929, the nearest year he could reach, and waited ten years. When the gate on the Achilles opened in 1939 he was waiting in the hold with a Thompson gun beside the ship's bosun. They shot the Jaffa as they came through. Then Mitchell shot Ba'al through the head.

History went back to its proper course. On the Tok'ra homeworld the extraction went ahead without a hitch, and nobody there ever knew what had happened. So the last of the System Lords died in the hold of a freighter in the Atlantic, at the hands of a man who had waited ten years for him.

Character

Ba'al does not believe that he is a god. Among those who already know the truth he does not trouble to pretend, and he suspects that most other Goa'uld do not believe it either. He is dry, patient and quick. He keeps a short, neat beard, and he dresses well.

He prefers a trick to a battle. Unlike most of his kind he likes to do his own work. He experimented with gravity himself, and he knows the workings of the Stargate network better than any other Goa'uld.

He is entirely selfish but never stupid. When something threatens the whole galaxy, Ba'al is usually the first Goa'uld to notice, if only because he lives in it too.

pages.title: Bahro
infobox: The cavern of D'ni and its Ages
When the Tablet was given to them
pages.html:
The Bahro are a hidden race of beings, not human, who lived in the cavern of D'ni before the D'ni came. The D'ni took the cavern from them and made them slaves. Yeesha, the daughter of Atrus, calls them the Least, and she has worked for their freedom.

The name

Bahro is a D'ni word, and an insulting one, usually rendered as beast people. The D'ni and their Ronay ancestors used it for peoples who were not human. In Terahnee, the lost sister realm of D'ni, it was the word for slaves.

Bondage

The beings who bear the name lived in the great cavern under New Mexico before the D'ni arrived, nearly ten thousand years ago. The D'ni took the cavern from them and enslaved them. There are signs that they were once hunted for sport.

The D'ni bound the Bahro with a stone Tablet whose holder could command them. The Bahro move between places, and even between worlds, without books. They answer to symbols drawn on slates. Long after the Fall of D'ni, when the city stood empty, they stayed on in its shadows. Screams in the dark of the cavern have been put down to them.

The Grower

A prophecy among them spoke of a Grower who would restore D'ni. Yeesha came to believe that she was the one. She unlocked the Tablet, chose wrongly with it and lost the power to use it. In the end the Tablet was given to the Bahro themselves, and their bondage was over.

In the saga

The Bahro have not appeared in the saga. They belong to the hidden life of the cavern, which the small group of Muggles digging under New Mexico in the 1990s have only begun to uncover.

pages.title: Barago
infobox: Kiba, the black armour of the knight of darkness
Karune Ryuzaki, a counsellor; Shiroku, a man in a white mask
To devour a thousand Horrors, then Messiah herself
The three priestesses of the Eastern Watchdog; the Makai Guide Elda
Taiga Saejima; Douji; Shizuka; the knight Bado
pages.html:
Barago is a fallen Makai Knight, once the pupil of Taiga Saejima, the Golden Knight, whom he murdered in about 1990. He wears Kiba, a black armour given to him by Messiah, the mother of the Horrors. He does not fight Horrors. He eats them, meaning to eat a thousand before he swallows Messiah herself. In the summer of 1994 he is at large somewhere in Japan with a cross-shaped scar on his face, still counting.

The boy

Barago was the son of a Makai Knight by a Makai Priestess. It was a happy house until his mother fell ill. As a small boy he trained hard so that he could protect her. A Horror took her all the same. His father cut her down in front of him.

Barago left home to find a better teacher. When word came that his father had died fighting Horrors he felt nothing. He had decided that his father died because he was weak. By then he hated Makai Knights rather more than he hated Horrors.

Taiga's pupil

He went to the strongest knight there was, Taiga Saejima, hoping to be Garo after him. Taiga taught him. He would not make him his heir, since Barago wanted strength for its own sake.

In a forbidden place Barago found a book of the dark arts. Messiah spoke to him out of it. She offered him the armour of Kiba, the knight of darkness of the old legends, in exchange for his service. He took it. He stayed in the armour past its limit, was devoured by it, and tore himself free by swallowing a Horror whole. After that he swallowed every Horror he defeated. He took what each one could do, losing a little more of himself each time.

Taiga fought him. He left a cross cut into Barago's face, a mark meant to kill within days, but the Horrors inside Barago kept him alive. In about 1990 Barago killed Taiga in front of Taiga's young son, Kouga.

The thousand

For years he ate his way towards a thousand Horrors. He made gates of his own, by pouring his darkness into objects, to bring more of them through. He ate Makai Knights when they found him. One of them, Bado the Storm Knight, fought him many times. In losing the last fight Bado left a spark of light buried in him, which Barago did not notice.

Messiah needed a living woman as her door. In about 1988 Barago chose her: Kaoru Mitsuki, six years old, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. He marked her. He watched her grow up.

To come near her he needed another face. A potion that would give him one was kept by the old knight Douji. Douji refused him. Barago killed him, with the girl Shizuka, in armour that Douji's foster son mistook for Garo's. With the potion he became Karune Ryuzaki, a gentle counsellor. Kaoru was his patient.

Messiah

By 2005 he had allies. The three priestesses who kept the Eastern Watchdog gave him the Horrors that Kouga Saejima brought them to be sent home. A woman named Elda, a Makai Guide whom he had saved from death for his own purposes, read the cards for him. In February 2006 the priest Amon was found murdered, almost certainly by Barago. That month twelve sealed Horrors broke loose as a single giant, too strong for Garo with Zero beside him. Barago swallowed it.

In March he threw off Ryuzaki's face, carried Kaoru away, and told her his whole history while he waited. Messiah, speaking through the girl, had shown him the light that Bado left in him. He went down into his own mind to put it out. It had the shape of the Golden Knight. The last of it had the shape of his mother, whom he cut down himself.

Then Messiah came through Kaoru, with no more use for him. She ate him. Kouga defeated her. The armour of Kiba got up without its wearer to fight on, until Kouga destroyed it in single combat.

Shiroku

The malice that had soaked into the armour did not die with either of them. It drifted, taking dead bodies to walk in, from about the time Kouga's son was born. In 2045 it wore a white mask under the name of Shiroku. It seized Mayuri, the young woman Raiga Saejima loved, to draw him aboard a black train bound for the Makai. It meant to join itself to the armour of Ouga, a knight of legend. For a while it did.

It took three Golden Knights to end it: Raiga, his father Kouga, with the spirit of his grandfather Taiga, whom Barago had murdered half a century before. Their blows split Kiba from the stolen armour. Raiga destroyed it.

pages.title: Barbara Gordon
infobox: James Gordon, for many years Gotham's police commissioner
Shot by the Joker in 1988; walked again in 1990 with cybernetics from Stark Enterprises
Head of the Gotham Public Library; member of Congress from 1972; Commissioner of the Gotham police by 1991
pages.html:
Barbara Gordon is the daughter of James Gordon, the honest police commissioner who worked with the first Batman. From 1967 to 1988 she fought crime in Gotham as Batgirl, while the city knew her as the head of its public library and later as a member of Congress. In 1988 the Joker shot her and left her unable to walk. From a wheelchair she became Oracle, who supplied the heroes with what they needed to know, until cybernetics from Stark Enterprises let her walk again in 1990. She married Dick Grayson, the second Batman. By 1991 she held her father's old post as Commissioner of the Gotham police.

Early life

Barbara Gordon grew up in Gotham, the daughter of James Gordon, who was for many years the one honest man at the top of the city's police. She was quick, clever and athletic. She trained herself in judo. She took a doctorate in library science. As a young woman she became head of the Gotham Public Library, where she was thought a quiet, bookish sort of person.

Batgirl

In January 1967 Barbara made herself a costume for a fancy-dress party, a woman's version of Batman's own. On the way there she came upon the villain Killer Moth trying to kidnap Bruce Wayne, and she stopped him. That brought her to Batman's notice. He did not want a woman in his line of work, and he told her so.

She carried on all the same as Batgirl, and in time Batman came round to her. Through the late 1960s she fought Gotham's criminals beside Batman and Robin. Nobody guessed that the girl in the cape was the commissioner's daughter from the library.

Congress

In 1972 Barbara Gordon was elected to Congress. She moved to Washington meaning to give up Batgirl for good, but she could not keep away from the work for long. In the middle of the 1970s she told her father who she was. He had known for years.

The Dynamite Duo

From 1975 she often worked beside Dick Grayson, the first Robin, who had grown up at Batman's side. The newspapers called the pair the Dynamite Duo. Over the years they fell in love.

Retirement

Barbara kept up the cape and cowl into the 1980s. In 1988 she gave up being Batgirl for good. Her identity was never made public.

The Joker

Later in 1988 the Joker escaped from Arkham Asylum. He came to her father's house, and when Barbara opened the door he shot her through the spine. He photographed her as she lay wounded, to torment her father, whom he carried off to an empty fairground to drive him mad.

Batman, who was then Dick Grayson, found them in time. James Gordon came through it with his mind whole, and he made Batman bring the Joker in by the book. The bullet left Barbara unable to walk.

Oracle

Barbara would not be beaten. From her wheelchair she made herself one of the best-informed people in the world, under the name Oracle. She found what the heroes needed to know and passed it to them, from government secrets to the hiding places of criminals. For a long while even they did not know who Oracle was.

Walking again

Early in 1990 Barbara Gordon walked again. Tony Stark had been shot through the spine himself in 1989, and an implant built by his own engineers had let him walk again. For Barbara, Stark Enterprises went further, with advanced cybernetics that took over the work of the nerves the bullet had cut. Nothing else could have done it.

Dick Grayson

Barbara Gordon married Dick Grayson. She knew that he had been the second Batman since 1980, and that it was he who had brought the Joker in after the shooting. His secret was safe with her. A Lazarus Pit had kept him young, and he could have worn the cowl for years more. In the summer of 1990 he put it away of his own choice, to make a life with her.

Commissioner

By 1991 Barbara Gordon was Commissioner of the Gotham police, the post her father had held for so long. Gotham had changed around her into a city of towers, neon and flying traffic, with gangs of Jokerz in its streets.

In the summer of 1991 a new Batman appeared, in a black suit with a red bat across the chest. Barbara wanted him off her streets at first, since she knew better than anyone what the cowl cost the people who wore it. In time she came to work with him, though she never quite liked it.

pages.title: Barry Allen
pages.html:
Barry Allen was the second Flash, the red-suited speedster of Central City. He came to public notice in 1956, helped to found the Justice League and died in 1985 in the Crisis, in a battle nobody has ever properly explained. Wally West, his nephew by marriage, has carried the name ever since.

The police scientist

Barry Allen was a police scientist in Central City, a careful and famously unhurried man. One night in 1956 a bolt of lightning smashed through his laboratory window and drenched him in a rack of chemicals. Afterwards the most unhurried man in the Central City police found that he could move faster than sound.

He made himself a red costume with a lightning flash on the chest, which folded away into a ring. He took the name of the Flash from Jay Garrick, the Justice Society hero he had admired as a boy. In 1961 he met Jay in person, and helped to bring him back into action with several of his old team.

At the turn of 1960 Barry was among the founders of the Justice League. He married the reporter Iris West, whose young nephew Wally had been given the same powers by the same freak accident in 1959, and he trained the boy as Kid Flash. He fought a long line of enemies, among them Captain Cold, Gorilla Grodd and, worst of all, Professor Zoom, who murdered Iris in 1979. In 1983 Barry killed Zoom to stop him from murdering again, and he stood trial for it.

In April 1964 Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, came ashore near Nagoya. Barry ran across the Pacific when he heard. He knew from Superman what Godzilla's breath could do, so he never crossed in front of it. He spent the day carrying people out of the streets in Godzilla's path, two at a time, several thousand times over. In January 1965 he did the same for the towns round Mount Fuji, when the Justice League went to Japan against three monsters at once. On 19 December 1965 he did it a third time, round Tokyo.

Death

Barry Allen died in 1985, during the Crisis. Those who were there say that he was captured and escaped. Then he ran faster than he had ever run, to destroy a weapon aimed at the world, and he went on running until there was nothing left of him but his costume. Like everything about the Crisis, the details are uncertain. The world knew only that the Flash was gone, and soon afterwards that the boy who had run beside him had taken up his name.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994, watching the news at the Dursleys', Harry Potter reflected that the Flash of Dudley's old annuals had died in 1985, in a battle nobody had ever properly explained. The Flash now standing behind Superman was the boy who used to run beside him.

pages.title: Bastet
infobox: Bastet, the cat goddess of Egypt
Killed in Ba'al's war on the System Lords, by early 2005
pages.html:
Bastet is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in Egypt, long ago, as a goddess with the head of a cat. Among the Goa'uld she is known for treachery, which in that company is saying a good deal. In 2002 she sat at the council of the System Lords that took Anubis back among them. She was killed in Ba'al's war on the other System Lords, and was dead by early 2005.

The cat goddess

Bastet was one of the Goa'uld who ruled in Egypt in Ra's day. The Egyptians knew her as a goddess with a cat's head, the protector of the home, of women in childbirth and of secrets. She left Earth with the rest of them when the Egyptians rose against Ra, about 3000 BC. Afterwards she kept Ra's ban on speaking of Earth, as all the System Lords did, and she is not known ever to have gone back.

The Egyptians went on worshipping her for thousands of years without her. Her chief city was Bubastis, in the Nile delta, where her temple stood and the cats sacred to her were buried by the thousand.

Sobek

Bastet's best-known treachery was carried out with Kali the Destroyer. The two of them made a treaty with Sobek, a Goa'uld who had taken the name of the crocodile god of Egypt. Then they turned on him at the feast held to celebrate it, when he had let his guard down. It is said that his head still decorates Bastet's palace.

Lord Yu, the oldest of the System Lords, knew the story perfectly well. In 2002 he still reckoned Bastet and Kali his likeliest allies.

The council at Hasara

In 2002 the System Lords met under truce on a space station in the Hasara system, which they counted as neutral ground. For months an enemy none of them could name had been attacking their worlds. He struck only with his ships, never with troops on the ground, and none of them knew who he was.

Bastet brought the nearest thing to evidence. When her outpost on Zeldor was attacked, her First Prime had disabled one of the enemy's ships and boarded it. Its Jaffa fought to the death. Most of them had been in the service of Cronus or Sokar, she told the council, but one bore the mark of Olokun. Olokun, who was sitting with the rest of them, took it very badly.

The enemy turned out to be Anubis, whom the System Lords had cast out long before. He sent Osiris to the council to ask for his old place among them. Bastet had lost two motherships to him, and she said so. She voted to take him back all the same. Only Yu voted against.

Ba'al's war

By 2003 Yu was failing, and the combined fleet he led against Anubis was failing with him. Teal'c of SG-1 and Oshu, Yu's First Prime, went looking for another System Lord to take the command. Ba'al refused it with contempt. Teal'c wondered aloud whether they should ask Bastet instead. Ba'al promptly changed his mind. It was probably the most useful thing Bastet ever did for anybody, and she was not even there.

After Earth defeated Anubis in 2004, Ba'al took Anubis's Kull warriors for himself and turned them on the other System Lords. Their Jaffa were no match for the Kull. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that Bastet was dead.

pages.title: The Beetleborgs
infobox: Drew McCormick, Jo McCormick and Roland Williams; for a few days in November 1996, Josh Baldwin
Blue Stinger, Green Hunter and Red Striker, 1996 to 1997; the Metallix armour, from September 1997; Mega Spectra, from February 1998
Vexor and the Magnavores, 1996 to 1997; Nukus and the Crustaceans, from 1997
Art Fortunes; the Astralborgs; Roboborg; the Power Rangers
pages.html:
The Beetleborgs are three children of Charterville who fought as armoured heroes, in the likeness of beetles, from 1996 to 1998. Their powers came from a wish granted by Flabber, a phasm whom they let out of the pipe organ at Hillhurst Mansion on 7 September 1996. The same wish let their enemies out of the pages of a comic book. In the summer of 1994 none of it has happened yet.

The wish

On 7 September 1996 two rich brothers of Charterville, Trip and Van, dared three other children to go into Hillhurst Mansion, the old house outside the town that everybody said was haunted. The three were Drew McCormick, his younger sister, Jo, and their friend Roland Williams. They were about ten to twelve years old, and they went in.

Everybody was right about the house. A vampire, a mummy and a creature built from spare parts chased them through it. In the chase they knocked against the pipe organ, which let out Flabber, a phasm who had been shut inside. He offered them a wish. All three wished to be the Beetleborgs, the heroes of their favourite comic book.

Flabber granted it, armour, weapons and all. His magic can make drawn things real, but it did rather more than he had meant, for it opened the comic book in both directions. The Beetleborgs' enemies in the story, Vexor and his Magnavores, climbed out of the pages into Charterville.

Armour and powers

Each of the three carried a Beetle Bonder. At the cry of 'Beetle Blast!' it put its owner into armour of a grown person's size, so that nobody watching would have guessed there was a child inside. Drew became the Blue Stinger Beetleborg, the leader, with a triangular sword. Roland became the Green Hunter, with the Hunter Claw. Jo became the Red Striker, with the Striker Blaster. The comic supplied machines too: three Attack Vehicles, the great carrier Gargantis and a base.

The wish left each of them a gift out of armour as well. Drew could move things without touching them, Roland could outrun anything, and Jo was far stronger than any grown man. All of it was Flabber's magic, which failed whenever he was ill.

In Charterville the Beetleborgs were public heroes, though who they were stayed a secret. No larger company of heroes ever came to help. The Magnavores were a small-town menace, usually beaten before anybody farther off had cause to notice. The Power Rangers were the exception, because their own enemies came to Charterville first.

The Magnavores

From September 1996 to May 1997 the enemy was Vexor. He kept his court in a crypt in the Charterville cemetery, from which he called one monster after another out of the comics. The Beetleborgs sent them back.

In October 1996 the three met Art Fortunes, the man who had first drawn them. Whatever Art drew, Flabber could bring to life, so Art became their armourer.

On 11 November 1996 Vexor made a Beetleborg of his own, Shadowborg, who beat all three and took their powers. Art drew a fourth Beetleborg to fight him, the White Blaster, whose armour a new boy in town, Josh Baldwin, agreed to wear. Josh won the stolen powers back. On 16 November Drew destroyed Shadowborg in the new Mega Blue armour. The White Blaster's powers had been made only for that fight, so they went out with Shadowborg.

In May 1997 the Magnavores brought to life a monster that Art had not drawn. It was Nukus, the work of Art's brother, Les. Nukus built the giant Borgslayer, which destroyed Gargantis, the Attack Vehicles and the base. On 21 May the three brought it down with their lasers fired together. The blast swept Vexor and the Magnavores back into the comics for good, as Nukus had intended.

The Metallix armour

Nukus meant to have Charterville for himself. On 8 September 1997 he destroyed the Beetleborgs' armour, weapons and powers in a single fight, then turned Flabber to ice. He broke Les Fortunes out of Charterville Prison to draw him an army, with Horribelle and Vilor as its captains.

The children thawed Flabber out, while Art sat down to draw. On 9 September the three had the Metallix armour. Drew was now the Chromium Gold Beetleborg, Roland was Titanium Silver and Jo was Platinum Purple. Art drew them a Battle Station with three Battle Vehicles. All that autumn Les drew monsters, Nukus brought them off the page, and the Beetleborgs destroyed them.

The Lost Comic

As boys, the Fortunes brothers had made a comic of their own, which Les had buried. In it were the Astral Sword, eight Astral Coins, four heroes called the Astralborgs and four villains called the Mantrons. In November 1997 both sides dug for it. On 26 November Drew brought the Sword together with all eight coins, which summoned Roboborg, a giant in beetle armour. Roboborg sent the Mantrons back into the Lost Comic.

In February 1998 Roboborg joined the Beetleborgs' old powers to the new, which gave them the winged Mega Spectra armour. Les drew the Astral Axe, and with it a giant to match Roboborg: Boron, who obeyed whoever held the Axe.

The end came on 2 March 1998, when Nukus made his worst monster, Repgillian. Roland got the Astral Axe away from the Crustaceans, so that Boron changed sides. The two giants destroyed Repgillian with the Beetleborgs. Les Fortunes walked back into Charterville Prison of his own accord, which left Nukus with nobody to draw for him. Nukus, Horribelle and Vilor were still at large. The Beetleborgs had both giants, however, and Charterville was quieter than it had been for eighteen months.

The Zeo Rangers, October 1996

The first Power Rangers the Beetleborgs met were the Zeo Rangers. In October 1996 King Mondo of the Machine Empire had just been broken in battle, and his small son, Prince Sprocket, wanted a victory of his own. On Saturday 19 October he sent Klank to Charterville with Orbus and a company of Cogs, to strike a bargain with Vexor. Vexor would call a monster out of the comics. Klank would make it grow, a trick the Magnavores had not learnt.

The monster, Scrapjaw, stood as tall as a ten-storey building when Klank had finished, far too big for Gargantis. Billy Cranston had tracked the Cogs from the Power Chamber. Jason Lee Scott, the Gold Ranger, reached Charterville first, with Tommy Oliver close behind him in the Zeo Megazord.

Vexor chose that moment to cheat: Jara tried to carry off Orbus, so that the Magnavores could make giants of their own. While she fought the Cogs for him, the Megazord destroyed Scrapjaw. Klank fled to the Moon.

Nobody took off a helmet. Tommy shook hands with the Blue Stinger Beetleborg without knowing that there was a boy of twelve inside.

Divatox's wish, May 1997

In the spring of 1997 the space pirate Divatox heard that a spirit in Charterville granted wishes. On Saturday 3 May she sent her nephew, Elgar, to Hillhurst Mansion with a crew of Piranhatrons to fetch it. Vexor, glad to see Flabber taken away, drew the Beetleborgs off to the far side of town.

The Turbo Rangers, led by Tommy Oliver, had followed the Piranhatrons from Angel Grove. Elgar got away from them with Flabber in a sack. Rangers and Beetleborgs together caught up with him at the cemetery gates, where Divatox was waiting.

She wished for more treasure than she could carry. Flabber obliged. A pirate's chest came up out of the nearest comic book, followed by the monster that guarded it in the story, Davy Bones. Flabber's magic has never brought out the good without the bad. Divatox's torpedoes made the monster grow. The Turbo Megazord destroyed it, whereupon the chest turned back into paper.

At Hillhurst that evening, with nobody present who could be called the public, the Blue Ranger took off his helmet. He was Justin Stewart, twelve years old, who knew every number of the Beetleborgs' comic by heart. The three took off theirs. Justin wrote to them from then on.

The changelings, September 1997

By September 1997 both teams were new. The Beetleborgs had worn the Metallix armour for eleven days. Four of the five Turbo Rangers had held their powers for nine: T.J. Johnson, Cassie Chan, Ashley Hammond and Carlos Vallerte. Only Justin was left of the Rangers the Beetleborgs knew.

Divatox and Nukus chose that moment to work together. Between them they made a band of changelings. On Saturday 20 September some of these wrecked the park at Angel Grove in the likeness of the Beetleborgs, while the rest, as Power Rangers, turned over the middle of Charterville.

The two teams met outside Charterville, in a fight that was short but in earnest. Justin stopped it by standing between the sides until T.J. would listen.

Found out, the changelings took new shapes, half Ranger and half Beetleborg. Divatox's torpedoes made them grow. To meet them the Rangers joined their Turbozords to the Beetleborgs' new Battle Vehicles in a single machine. It was the only time that was ever done, and it was enough. Divatox and Nukus each blamed the other.

The stolen artist, October 1997

Divatox had envied Nukus one thing: his monsters cost him nothing, because Les Fortunes drew them. On Saturday 25 October 1997 her Piranhatrons carried Les off to her submarine at Angel Grove. He drew her a swordfish in sea boots, which he called Cutlass. Nothing happened. It was Nukus's power that lifted Les's drawings off the page, a point Les had not thought it wise to mention.

Nukus came to Angel Grove for his artist, with Horribelle, Vilor and a squad of Dregs. Divatox sent Elgar ashore to meet him, with Les under guard. The Beetleborgs came after Nukus: Justin had telephoned Zoom Comics, and Flabber sent the three of them across country in a blink.

In the fight Elgar dropped the drawing. Nukus brought Cutlass to life himself, Divatox made it grow, and the Rangers destroyed it with the Rescue Megazord. Jo threw Vilor into the lake. Les settled the rest by walking back to Nukus, having decided that he preferred the employer he knew.

The Astral Axe, February 1998

On 16 February 1998 Roboborg and Boron fought on the Moon, where Astronema could hardly help noticing. A giant that obeyed whoever held an axe was exactly what she wanted for her master, Dark Specter. On Saturday 21 February she sent Ecliptor to Charterville with her Quantrons, to take the Astral Axe from Nukus.

The Space Rangers followed him. Four were old friends in new colours, the Turbo Rangers of the autumn. The fifth was their leader, Andros of KO-35. Justin had stayed in Angel Grove with his father when the others went into space.

Ecliptor cut his way to the Axe. For some minutes Boron was Astronema's, and it took Roboborg with the Astro Megazord to hold him. Andros could move things with his mind. So could Drew McCormick. Between them they pulled the Axe out of Ecliptor's hand. It flew rather too far, to Horribelle, so Boron went back to Nukus. Ecliptor went home with nothing.

Andros thought it a poor result. T.J. told him that in Charterville it counted as a good day. Nine days later the Axe was in Roland's hands.

pages.title: Biliskner
infobox: Thor, Supreme Commander of the Asgard fleet
The Pegasus galaxy; the protected worlds
2000, to the Replicators, over the Pacific
The O'Neill (lost in 2000); the Daniel Jackson
pages.html:
The Biliskner is Thor's own ship, the warship from which he commands Asgard's fleet against the Replicators. It was in the Biliskner that he came to Cimmeria in 1998, when the team from Earth called SG-1 met him for the first time. In 2000 the Replicators took it, and it fell burning into the Pacific.

Thor's ship

The Biliskner is one of the great warships of Asgard. It takes its name from Bilskirnir, Thor's hall in Thrudheim, in the Realm Eternal. Thor commands the fleet from it in the Pegasus galaxy, far beyond this one, where Asgard's war with the Replicators is fought.

Like the other ships of Asgard, it can lie unseen in orbit above a world. It can also carry people up to it, or down from it, in a beam of light. Thor uses this freely, and has never been in the habit of asking first.

Cimmeria

In 1998 Heru'ur came back to Cimmeria, the world where Thor had left the Northmen eleven centuries before. The Cimmerians called on Asgard from the Hall of Thor's Might, and the Biliskner answered. It cleared Heru'ur's army off the planet, while Heru'ur ran for the gate. Aboard it, Thor met SG-1 for the first time.

In 1999 Thor brought Jack O'Neill up to the ship without warning. He had come to tell him that the System Lords meant to destroy Earth, and that Asgard would offer it a place in the Protected Planets Treaty instead.

The Replicators

Early in 2000 the Replicators came aboard the Biliskner in battle. They fed on the ship's own metal to make more of themselves until it was theirs. It reached Earth with the Replicators swarming through it and Thor badly hurt aboard. They meant to land, and to devour whatever they found.

Thor brought O'Neill up to the ship, and the rest of SG-1 came after him. They could not take it back. Instead they wired its engines so that it could not slow down as it fell, then beamed a Stargate aboard and escaped through it at the last moment. The Biliskner broke up as it came down, and what was left of it fell into the Pacific off California. One Replicator lived through the fall.

After the Biliskner

Thor lived. That summer Asgard's newest warship, the first built for the Replicator war alone, was named the O'Neill, after Thor's friend. It was not yet finished when it was destroyed, blown up on purpose with a great swarm of Replicators inside it.

Thor's later ship was the Daniel Jackson. The Replicators boarded that one too, in 2005. He took it away from Earth with them still aboard, and it came through when the weapon of the Ancients on Dakara destroyed every Replicator in the galaxy.

pages.title: Billy Cranston
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Day of the Dumpster' (28 August 1993)
The Triceratops Dinozord; the Unicorn Thunderzord, from the autumn of 1994; the Wolf Ninjazord, from 1995
The Power Lance, which splits in two
The Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 1993 to 1996; technical adviser to the Zeo Rangers, 1996
The Blue Ninja Ranger, 1995 to 1996; the Blue Ranger again, 2022 to 2023
The Rangers' wrist communicators; molecular decoders
pages.html:
Billy Cranston is the Blue Ranger of the Power Rangers, whose Power Coin draws on the Triceratops. He is the brains of the team, who builds the gadgets the others need. His talk is so technical that Trini Kwan often has to put it into plain English. He was the only one of the five whom Zordon chose in 1993 to stay on into 1996, as a Ranger and then as the team's technical adviser. In November 1996 he left Earth for the planet Aquitar. Years later he came home and founded a company of his own. In 2022 his attempt to bring Zordon back brought back the evil of Rita Repulsa instead, and Trini died saving his life.

Angel Grove

Billy was born about 1977 and grew up in Angel Grove, California, where he is a pupil at Angel Grove High School. He is the brains of the team. In 1993 he was learning karate in Jason Lee Scott's class at the Youth Center.

Something that happened to him as a small child left him frightened of fish. When Rita Repulsa used that fear against him, he got over it.

The Blue Ranger

Zordon chose Billy with four friends in 1993. He became the Blue Ranger. His Power Coin calls up the Triceratops Dinozord, and his weapon is the Power Lance, which splits into two.

Billy builds what the team needs when Zordon has not foreseen it. He made the wrist communicators the Rangers wear, and a link that lets them use the Command Center's teleporter from afar.

On 30 July 1993 the Rangers came to public notice for the first time, when they fought a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham.

In August 1993 Promethea, the technology company of Grace Sterling, offered Billy an internship. His father thought it very important. Coming late to a fight from his interview, Billy was saved from Goldar by Matt Cook, or by what looked like Matt. He proposed to the others that Matt should take his place as the Blue Ranger. Jason Lee Scott told him that Zordon had chosen Billy for a reason. The Matt who had saved him was Rita's spy, the Putty Infiltrator. Once it had been unmasked, in September, Billy turned Promethea down.

That month he built a suit of blue armour, the Tricera Armour, with Alpha 1, the first robot Zordon ever had, who had come back after centuries lost. When Alpha 1 turned on the Rangers, Alpha 5 wore the armour against him.

Late that year Tommy Oliver, as Rita's Green Ranger, shut Jason up in the Dark Dimension. Billy rescued him, with Trini and Alpha 5.

At the end of October the Black Dragon, a Zord steered from another world, wrecked the Command Center. It carried Billy off, then used his Power Coin to strip the other Rangers of their powers. He was held in Goldar's Dark Dimension, where Goldar himself was in disgrace. Billy talked him into letting him go. He had noticed a hatch on the Black Dragon, which told him that it was a machine. With Tommy he went inside to wreck it. It blew up, throwing the two of them into Lord Drakkon's world.

That world was further on in time, darker, harder. Its own Billy was dead; his photograph hung on the wall of the Coinless, the old Rangers who had lost their coins. Billy rigged the Blue coin of that world with its Trini, so that its burst struck the power from Drakkon with every Sentry he had. That world's Zordon had died when Drakkon broke his tube. Once he was home, Billy built a second vessel for this world's Zordon in secret, against the same thing happening here.

In November 1993 Billy's molecular decoders took the Rangers into the Dark Dimension again, when Jason went after the green candle that was draining Tommy's powers.

In the spring of 1994 the team followed Tommy Oliver to Japan, where the Megazord fought Godzilla. Billy was the first of them to say that Godzilla seemed to understand that they had the same enemies.

Promethea

Early in 1994 Grace Sterling told the Rangers that she had been Zordon's first Red Ranger, in 1969. After that they worked with Promethea, though its methods wore on them. Talking to Andrea, one of its scientists, Billy came to suspect that it was hiding something.

At the end of August 1994 he noticed that one of Promethea's buildings was drawing only half its power. He teleported in to see why. In a secret cell underneath he found Lord Drakkon, who had been Grace's prisoner since the autumn before. Jason ended the alliance with Promethea that day.

The Thunderzords

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon. Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords. Billy's became the Unicorn Thunderzord.

Early in October, when Brainiac shrank Angel Grove into a bottle, Billy wrote the virus that freed the Rangers' Zords from Brainiac's hold. He wrote it over the radio with a voice from Gotham that talked in Batman's ear, whose owner he never met.

Later that month Zordon shut himself away to make Tommy the White Ranger. Billy found the plans of the hidden room with Grace Sterling's help.

In November Jason, Zack and Trini left for a peace conference in Geneva. Billy stayed.

That month Lord Zedd sent a monster to dig into Promethea for Psycho Green's dagger. Grace blew the dagger to pieces before Goldar could carry it off. Billy saw that it had been an illusion. He told her that he knew she had kept it, and that he would say nothing if she helped him with an experiment of his own. The experiment was the Dragon Coin, which Rita's green candle and Lord Zedd's crystal had drained.

The second Green Ranger

Billy and Grace woke the coin together with the dagger's energy. Billy meant to tell Zordon. Grace persuaded him to let Promethea choose who should carry it, though Billy wanted somebody the team could trust. In the middle of December 1994, with the Rangers losing to Lord Zedd's Dark Rangers, he told Grace to start the Green Protocol. Her Green Ranger was Matt Cook.

Billy coached Matt in the field, in secret. When a Chaos Putty knocked Matt senseless at a music festival, Billy ran to him in front of everybody. Aisha Campbell saw it, so he told her the truth. Zordon learnt the rest when Matt asked Billy's advice within his hearing. Late in December Zordon barred Billy from the Command Center. The bond between them, he said, could not be mended. The others took Billy's side. Aisha talked him into apologising.

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus of Eltar smashed Zordon's tube. Eltarian soldiers shot Billy in the back, then took him prisoner with Alpha 5. His second vessel had caught what the tube held. Zordon's mind had gone deep into its own memories. Billy went in after him, guided by an image of the Blue Emissary left in the Grid, then brought him out. In the fighting that followed he beat Zero-Zero of Sentry Force Four with the help of Squatt. When it was over Zordon made his peace with him.

In February 1995 a recording left by Grace Sterling, set to play at her death, told Billy what the Arch was. Afterwards an image of her, left in the Grid, told him of the Power Eggs. With them he shielded the Earth while Dark Specter's corruption was in the Grid.

Ninja powers

In September 1995 Rita's brother, Rito Revolto, destroyed the Thunderzords. Ninjor gave the Rangers new powers, the Ninja coins, and Billy became the Blue Ninja Ranger, with the Wolf Ninjazord. In November 1995 Katherine Hillard took Kimberly Hart's place as the Pink Ranger. Billy was now the last of the five whom Zordon had chosen in 1993.

The Alien Rangers

In November 1995 Rita's father, Master Vile, turned back time on Earth with his Orb of Doom, until the Rangers were children again. Zordon called in the Alien Rangers of Aquitar to defend Earth in their place.

Billy built a machine, powered by the Ninja coins, to give the Rangers back their proper age. He was the only one it had restored when Rita's servants stole it. After that he worked beside the Aquitians, as their adviser and their go-between with Earth.

In February 1996 Rita and Zedd destroyed the Power Coins. A bomb left by Rito and Goldar blew the Command Center to pieces. Billy's own days as a fighting Ranger were over.

Zeo
