In April 1996 the Zeo Crystal gave the Rangers new powers, to fight the Machine Empire. Billy gave up fighting. He stayed in the Power Chamber as the team's technical adviser, building their weapons, gadgets and Zords.

In May 1996 he finished at Angel Grove High School early. That month Cestro of the Alien Rangers crash-landed on Earth to ask for his help, and Billy went with him to Aquitar. On his way home the Machine Empire attacked him, and very nearly caught him.

In October 1996 Billy was chosen to take over the powers of the Gold Ranger from Trey of Triforia, who had been hurt. The negative energy left over from the destruction of the Command Center kept the powers from him, so they went to Jason instead. That month it also came out that Billy held a black belt in karate.

On 19 October 1996 Billy tracked a company of the Machine Empire's Cogs from the Moon to the town of Charterville. The Zeo Rangers went after them, to find the town defended by three armoured heroes of its own, the Beetleborgs. Billy studied his readings afterwards. He could make no sense of the Beetleborgs' powers. Zordon told him that they were a spirit's work, not a machine's, which was why.

Aquitar

The machine that had given Billy back his age had a side effect that nobody had foreseen. In November 1996 he began to age at great speed, until he was an old man. The Alien Rangers came to help.

Cestria of Aquitar took him to the Eternal Falls, whose waters made him young again. Billy had fallen in love with her. He decided to stay on Aquitar with her, and he said goodbye to his friends.

Cranston Tech

Billy came home from Aquitar some time after 1998. He founded a company of his own, Cranston Tech, and under its headquarters he built a new Command Center in secret.

In 2014 he was among the Rangers of every generation who came to the help of the Mega Rangers against the Armada's invasion of Earth.

With his robot, Alpha 8, Billy set out to bring Zordon back by gathering what was left of the wave of light in which Zordon had given up his form. In 2022 something went wrong. The evil that the wave had driven out of Rita Repulsa took hold of Alpha 8 and made it over into a body of its own, Robo-Rita.

Billy went after her first as the Blue Ranger, and the rest of the old team came to help him. In the battle Robo-Rita fired a blast at Billy. Trini threw herself in front of it, and it killed her. Her daughter, Minh, blamed Billy.

Robo-Rita

A year later Robo-Rita took Jason, Tommy and Kimberly prisoner. Billy worked out what she was doing with them. She was draining their power to open a door into the past, so that she could reach herself at the moment she was let out of the dumpster in 1993. Together they would kill the Rangers before Zordon could ever choose them.

Billy went after her with Zack, Katherine Hillard and Rocky DeSantos. Minh had taken her mother's morpher, and Robo-Rita caught her. When Robo-Rita fired at Billy, Minh jumped in front of the blast, as Trini had. The Sabre-toothed Tiger coin bonded to her, and she became the Yellow Ranger.

Billy talked her through piloting the Megazord, and the two of them made their peace. Afterwards, at the juice bar, he said that Zordon might yet be brought back one day.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' news showed helicopter film of the fight in Birmingham the afternoon before. Five people in coloured suits and helmets ran in a line across a rooftop towards the creature. The one in blue was Billy. Dudley, with a sausage halfway to his mouth, watched them leap off the roof as though he would like to be one of them.

Book Three, Chapter Four: Harry told Lucius Malfoy about the team in California, and the starfish the size of a bus that they had fought in Birmingham. 'It wouldn't have looked out of place in the Forbidden Forest.'

Book Four, Chapter Three: by August 1994 the Rangers were on the Dursleys' news nearly every morning, and there were six of them now. Billy was still the Blue Ranger, though Dudley's favourite was the newest, the green one.

pages.title: Biteborn
infobox: Garou made by the bite rather than born
pages.html:
The biteborn are Garou made by the bite rather than born. It is rare. A Garou in any of its shapes can pass the change by biting, at any hour, though it does not pass with every bite. The Litany frowns on it, and most Garou never do it. Those who make others by the bite on purpose mostly serve the Wyrm. The tribes despise the biteborn as no true Garou, though by every measure that matters they are Garou. Remus Lupin is biteborn.

The bite

The Garou are a born people. The blood runs quiet for generations in Kinfolk families, human and wolf. Then a child is born who has it, and the First Change wakes it.

But there is a second way in. A Garou in any of its shapes can make another by the bite, upon anyone and at any hour. Severus Snape put it plainly to the Hogwarts third-years in 1993: 'They are born. Or a man is bitten.'

It happens rarely. The change does not pass with every bite, and very few Garou will ever try to pass it. The Litany frowns on making Garou by the bite. A Garou of the thirteen tribes who did it would answer to his sept for it. The great exception is the fallen tribe, the Black Spiral Dancers. They make others by the bite deliberately, and they are extremely particular in their choosing.

Garou in every measure

Whatever the tribes say of them, the biteborn are Garou. A biteborn wears all five shapes at will, from the man to the wolf, with the nine-foot war form between. He carries the rage that sits in every Garou like fire in a lamp. The moon raises its tide in him as in any other.

He has a birth sign, and the work that goes with it. He can learn the Gifts of the spirits and step sideways into the spirit world. He can smell the Wyrm in a place, an object or a man. Silver burns him. Those who see him in his war form suffer the Delirium. The Litany binds him, and Gaia accepts him. By every measure the Garou themselves use, a biteborn is a Garou.

'Not true Garou'

The tribes despise them all the same. The Garou set great store by blood and breeding. They care about Kinfolk lines, the names of ancestors, the tribe a whelp is born into and the moon it is born under. A biteborn has none of that by birth.

Many Garou call the biteborn not true Garou. They are made things, the tribes say, the fruit of a crime against the Litany. Very likely they carry the taint of whatever bit them, since most Garou who make others by the bite belong to the Wyrm.

A biteborn is given the worst work and the least thanks. He is passed over for rank, and spoken over at moots. He must prove at every turn what a born Garou is simply assumed to be. Few septs will take one at all. The contempt is close kin to the way the Garou treat the metis, the malformed children of two Garou. In some septs it is worse, for a metis was at least born of the People.

The Wyrm's biteborn

The Black Spiral Dancers are the one people among whom the biteborn are common. They choose with care, children above all. They raise them apart from their families, and turn them to the Wyrm before they are grown. Fenrir Greyback, the Spiral Dancer who bit Remus Lupin, seeks out the children of wizards, so that one day there will be enough of his kind to overwhelm wizards altogether.

It is the Spiral Dancers' biteborn that the tribes have in mind when they say a bitten Garou carries the taint of the thing that bit him. It is also why a biteborn of the thirteen tribes, like Lupin, must spend his life proving that he does not.

Remus Lupin

Remus Lupin was bitten as a very small boy by Greyback, in revenge on his father. He has been Garou ever since.

After 1981 he found a pack in the hills of mid-Wales, mostly of the Fianna, which fought beside him and still sends for him. It never let him forget, for a single day, that he was bitten rather than born. Worse, he was a wizard.

He is still himself in his war form, and remembers everything he does in it. He holds his rage in check with the Wolfsbane Potion, his faith and a great deal of prayer. In June 1994 Harry Potter saw him take that war form in the grounds of Hogwarts.

pages.title: Black Air
infobox: A secret unit of the British government
The work of the Weird Happenings Organisation, after 1992
Dream Nails, in the Midlands; the Acquisition Station, in North Yorkshire; Ronsaphan, in Thailand
Michele Scicluna; Threadgold; Shrine, a telepath; Scratch; Pete Wisdom, until 1994
The London Inner Circle of the Hellfire Club
1996, folded into a new department under Alistaire Stuart
pages.html:
Black Air is the most secret of the British government's services for the unexplained, a unit that grew out of the Ministry of Defence. It deals with superhumans, aliens and anything else nobody wants to touch. A good deal of its work is killing. It took over the work of the Weird Happenings Organisation by a vote that the Hellfire Club had paid for. In 1996 the Excalibur team brought it down, and what was left of it was folded into a new department.

Origins

Black Air began as a unit of the Ministry of Defence. When the Weird Happenings Organisation was wound up, after its head, Brigadier Alysande Stuart, was murdered in 1992, Black Air came to take over its work. The vote that gave it the job had been bought by the London Inner Circle of the Hellfire Club, a society of the rich and powerful with secrets of its own.

It took Warpies apart to see how they worked: the children whom Mad Jim Jaspers' warp had changed.

Muggles and secrets

Black Air is a Muggle service, like every other body of its kind in Britain. Like the Prime Minister, its masters may know that a Ministry of Magic exists, but they have never had any dealings with it.

It knows of PISCES, the older secret section of British intelligence that deals with the unnatural. The two trust each other no further than they trust anybody else.

Its work

Black Air's agents have a name for killing first. Pete Wisdom did its killing for years, until he asked to leave at the end of 1994 after what he had done at its base at Ronsaphan, in Thailand. His superior, Michele Scicluna, let him go on condition that he went first to Genosha with the Excalibur team as its observer.

At Dream Nails, a base in the Midlands, Black Air kept alien prisoners, among them a creature of the Phalanx and a drone of the Brood, which the Hellfire Club had given it. There, in an operation called Easy Tiger, it bred a bacterium called Blood Eagle. Its telepath Shrine nearly killed Pete Wisdom with it in the summer of 1995, before he and Kitty Pryde blew the place up.

London, 1996

In 1996 Black Air hunted Alistaire Stuart, once of the Weird Happenings Organisation, and shot down the aircraft that was bringing him to Muir Island. It harpooned Douglock from a jet. Its scientists took him apart, first at its Acquisition Station in North Yorkshire, then in London.

All the while it was helping the Hellfire Club to buy votes in Parliament through the Earl of Bute Society. Together they joined Douglock's head to a demon that lay beneath London, in a chamber called the Necromanteion under Blackwall, Black Air's headquarters. That summer London broke out in fires and riots. The Excalibur team stormed Blackwall, and Amanda Sefton bound the demon.

Afterwards the government folded what was left of Black Air, with what remained of the Weird Happenings Organisation, into a new department under Alistaire Stuart.

Remnants

Not all of it went quietly. In 1997 a cell that had survived hired Sari St Hubbins, a contract killer who had once tried to kill the Queen, to kill Pete Wisdom. It also handed Kurt Wagner over to the Sidri, alien hunters, in Venice.

pages.title: Black Furies
infobox: Greece, Asia Minor and the shores of the Black Sea
Avenging wronged women and children; guarding the wild
pages.html:
The Black Furies are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: a tribe of women, risen from ancient Greece and the lands about the Black Sea. They guard the wild places of the world. They take vengeance on those who prey on women and children.

Totem and ways

The Furies follow Pegasus, the winged horse, a spirit of wild places, freedom and righteous anger. They take their name from the avenging spirits of the old Greek stories, and they count the Amazons among their ancestors. Their members are women born to the tribe's Kinfolk. Sons who prove to be Garou are given to other tribes to raise, most often to the Children of Gaia. Only the male metis stay among the Furies, tolerated rather than honoured.

They are fierce, proud and disciplined. They are devoted to the Wyld above the other powers of creation, because they see in it the untamed strength that the Weaver's order and the Wyrm's corruption both seek to crush. Their rites honour Gaia, as well as the moon in her three aspects of maiden, mother and crone.

Homelands

The tribe's oldest caerns lie in Greece, in Asia Minor and about the Black Sea. They are mountain sanctuaries, sacred groves or caves that were holy before the first temples were built. Over the centuries the Furies spread through the Mediterranean and Europe, then across the oceans. Wherever they go, they make a point of seeking out the wild places that nobody else defends.

Place in the world

Among the Garou the Black Furies are respected as warriors and feared as judges. They hunt down men who harm women and children, whether or not those men serve the Wyrm. They are closest to the Children of Gaia, who raise their sons. They are slow to trust any tribe they think proud or domineering, and slowest of all to trust the Get of Fenris.

pages.title: The Black Widow
infobox: Black Widow; Natasha Romanoff; Natalia Romanova
The Soviet Union, in the late 1930s
The Avengers (from 1973; chairwoman since 1992); formerly the Champions of Los Angeles; formerly the KGB
pages.html:
The Black Widow is Natasha Romanoff, born Natalia Romanova. She was a Soviet agent who came to America in 1964 to destroy Tony Stark, broke with her masters and became one of the Avengers. She has been the team's chairwoman since 1992, and in August 1994, a woman in her mid-fifties, she still holds the chair.

The Soviet agent

Natalia Romanova was trained as a spy in the Soviet Union. In 1964 she was sent to the United States to sabotage the work of the armaments maker Tony Stark, whose Iron Man was then the face of American power. She worked against him for two years. In that time she drew the young archer Hawkeye into her schemes. He fell in love with her, and slowly she came to return it.

Her husband, the test pilot Alexi Shostakov, had been reported dead, and her masters used his memory to keep their hold on her. In the end she broke with them and stayed in America.

The Avengers

From 1970 she worked as a costumed adventurer in her own right, for a time in San Francisco. In 1973 she joined the Avengers. In the middle of the decade she led a short-lived team of her own in Los Angeles, the Champions.

She has served with the Avengers on and off ever since. In 1992 she became the team's chairwoman. Under her the Avengers kept to their United Nations accord through the Augment War. On 19 August 1994 the team's delegation, Captain America among it, stood with Superman before the Security Council.

At Superman's funeral in November 1992 she walked the Sub-Mariner away from Aquaman, with whom he had been arguing over precedence in the procession.

In October 1977 her Champions fought Godzilla at the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco. The bridge came off worst.

She was still the chairwoman in August 1996, a woman in her late fifties, when Onslaught's Sentinels came down on Manhattan. She fought them through the streets and lived. Most of those who went into Onslaught were Avengers, and the world believed them dead. She tried to gather a new team, but every hero she asked turned her down. Late in 1996 she stood the Avengers down and went back to the work she had begun in, as a spy.

The fallen came home late in 1997, and that winter the Avengers came together again.

Age

She was already a grown woman when she first came to America in 1964, and she has aged as everyone else has. In 1994 she is in her mid-fifties, one of the oldest of the serving Avengers after Captain America, whose years do not show.

pages.title: Blade
infobox: Deacon Frost, the vampire who fed on his mother
Sixty-five by the calendar; he looks far younger
pages.html:
Blade, born Eric Brooks in London in 1929, is a dhampir and the most famous vampire hunter of the modern age. No vampire fathered him. The vampire Deacon Frost fed on his mother while she was giving birth to him, and he came into the world with the taint of the blood in him. He has a vampire's strength and senses without its weakness to the sun. The Kindred call him the Daywalker, and he has spent his life destroying them.

Birth

His mother, Tara Brooks, went into labour in 1929 in a house in Soho, in London. A doctor was sent for, and the man who came was the vampire Deacon Frost. He fed on her as the child was born, and she died of it. The child lived. The vampire's taint passed into his blood at the moment of his birth.

The hunter

He was brought up by the women of the house where he was born. When he was nine he met Jamal Afari, an American jazz trumpeter who hunted vampires, and Afari trained him. When Afari was sired in his turn, Blade destroyed him.

He has hunted the Kindred ever since, at first with knives of teak and later with a sword. Above all he has hunted Deacon Frost.

A dhampir

By the laws of the blood, only the thin-blooded of the last generations can father children, and Blade had no vampire father at all. The Kindred count him a dhampir all the same, because he bears every mark of one. He and Alucard, the son of Dracula, are both exceptions to the rule that a dhampir is a thin-blood's child, for very different reasons.

He is far stronger and quicker than any ordinary man. He can sense the Kindred near him, no vampire can sire him, and he ages far more slowly than other men. He carries a share of the thirst as well, and has held it down all his life. He is sixty-five years old in 1994 by the calendar, and he looks very much younger.

pages.title: Blue Beetle
infobox: Mystery Men Comics #1 (August 1939); Ted Kord in Captain Atom #83 (November 1966)
pages.html:
Blue Beetle is the name of two American heroes. The first was Dan Garret, who came to public notice in 1939 and drew his powers from a scarab found in Egypt. The second is his former student, Ted Kord, an inventor with no powers at all, who has carried the name since 1966. Ted Kord helped to found the new Justice League in 1987, and in 1992 Doomsday very nearly killed him.

Dan Garret

The first Blue Beetle was Dan Garret, an archaeologist who found an ancient scarab in an Egyptian tomb. At a spoken word the scarab gave him great strength and endurance, among other powers. From 1939 he fought crime with it in a blue costume. He was killed in 1966 on Pago Island, fighting Ted Kord's uncle, Jarvis Kord, who had built an army of androids there and meant to conquer the world with it. With his last breath he passed the name to his student Ted, though not the scarab's power. Ted kept the scarab, but he never could make it answer to him.

Ted Kord

Ted Kord was a scientist, inventor and athlete who had no powers whatever. He fought as Blue Beetle with gadgets of his own design, chief among them the Bug, a flying craft shaped like a beetle, and he paid for it all with the fortune of Kord Industries. He was one of the founders of the new Justice League in 1987. In the League he became known for his jokes, and for his partnership with Booster Gold.

In the autumn of 1992 the League was the first to meet Doomsday. Blue Beetle was beaten into a coma, but he lived. Superman, who took up the fight after them, did not. Ted Kord recovered in time and went back to the League.

In February 1988 he flew the League to Japan in the Bug, when Godzilla came up off the coast. He spent the day ferrying fishermen off their boats with Booster Gold. He also fished Guy Gardner out of the sea, where Godzilla's breath had put him.

pages.title: Bone Gnawers
infobox: The poor quarters of every city
The poor, the homeless and the outcast
Survival, scavenging and knowing everything that happens on the streets
pages.html:
The Bone Gnawers are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the tribe of the streets, living among the poor, the homeless and the outcast of the world's cities. Other tribes look down on them. There is hardly a city on earth, all the same, where the Bone Gnawers do not know exactly what is going on.

Totem and ways

The Bone Gnawers follow Rat, a spirit of survival, of cunning and of plenty in hard places. Their name comes from their habit of living off what others throw away, and they are proud of it. They make their homes in alleys, under bridges, in derelict buildings and in cardboard shelters. Their Kinfolk are the people nobody else counts: the destitute, the drifting and the forgotten.

They are scavengers, survivors and gatherers of news. A Bone Gnawer may look like a tramp on a park bench and know more about the neighbourhood than any policeman. They share what they have, and they look after their own. Their Gifts suit the life. They run to going unnoticed, finding a meal where there seems to be none, and hearing whatever the street knows.

They fight the Wyrm where it hurts the poor first: in poisoned slums, in the drug trade and in the cruelty of the powerful towards the weak.

Homelands

The tribe claims no single homeland. Bone Gnawers say they have followed people into towns ever since the first towns were built, scavenging at the edges of every settlement. They are now found in every large city in the world, wherever there are streets for people to fall through.

Place in the world

In the Garou Nation the Bone Gnawers have the lowest standing of any tribe. The proud tribes treat them as curs at the gate, the Silver Fangs above all, and the Red Talons despise them for living among men. Yet every tribe needs what they know, and few Garou who have seen them defend a city's outcasts call them cowards twice. They are on uneasy but practical terms with the Glass Walkers, the other tribe of the cities.

pages.title: Brad Barrett
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Kamen Rider Camo' (21 February 2009)
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Brad Barrett is an American motocross rider, born about 1987. In 2009 a cheating scandal that was none of his doing had ended his career. Xaviax, who had arranged the scandal, offered him a way to clear his name: a contest of armoured fighters called Battle Club. Brad fought in it as Kamen Rider Thrust. He learnt the truth too late to act on it. Strike vented him on 4 April 2009.

Battle Club

Brad was a professional, good enough to have a name to lose. Then he was accused of tampering with a rival's machine. He had not done it. The sport shut him out all the same.

A man came to him who claimed to hold the proof that would clear him. He would hand it over, he said, if Brad won a private tournament called Battle Club, in which men fought in powered armour. The man was Xaviax, who had laid the false charge in the first place. He gave Brad the Advent Deck of Thrust, contracted to the rhinoceros Metalgelas. It opened for him because he was the mirror twin of Cameron, the Ventaran who first wore it.

Brad took Battle Club for a sport. It was some time before he understood that it was nothing of the kind.

Thrust

His first opponent, late in February 2009, was Len of Ventara. On 7 March he helped Kit Taylor to destroy a mirror monster, then attacked him, demanding to be told what was going on. Kit told him all of it a week later.

By then Brad had two other voices in his ear. Drew Lansing, the Rider called Torque, wanted his help against Xaviax. Xaviax told him that he would never get his life back unless he vented the Wing Knight. Brad did not see how he could refuse. He went after Len. On 21 March Len beat him, stood over him, then let him go.

The shield

Xaviax judged that Brad was about to change sides. He told Strike to get rid of him.

On 4 April 2009 Brad was fighting Len again when a second battle, between Torque and Strike, ran into theirs. Torque loosed his Final Vent at everybody. Strike seized Brad, using him as a shield. Brad, furious, turned on Strike. Strike overpowered him, then vented him.

Brad lay in the Advent Void until December 2009. With Xaviax dead, Eubulon brought him out, took away his memories of the war, then sent him home. Cameron wears the armour of Thrust again.

pages.title: Braddock Manor
infobox: Caverns, a laboratory and a computer with a mind of its own
pages.html:
Braddock Manor is the house at Maldon in Essex where Captain Britain and his sister, Psylocke, grew up. Their father built it in 1945, and under it he built the computer that killed him. It has been blown up, rebuilt, haunted by its own machinery, filled with mutated children and attacked by a killing machine from another world. Between 1992 and 1994 the Excalibur team lived there.

The house

Sir James Braddock built the Manor in 1945, when he brought his wife and their baby son, Jamie, home from Otherworld. It is a large, comfortable house with caverns underneath it, where Sir James kept his laboratory. There he built a great computer, which in time woke with a mind of its own and called itself Mastermind. In 1974 it killed Sir James and Lady Elizabeth in an explosion that looked like an accident.

In 1977 the agents of the Red Skull bombed the house flat while Captain Britain and Captain America were inside it. The two of them came out of the cellar unhurt. The house was not so lucky.

Mastermind's house

When Brian Braddock came back to Maldon in 1983, he found the Manor standing again, with the charwoman, Emma Collins, at the door. Mastermind had rebuilt it in secret, and it tried to talk him into joining his parents in death. Brian took the murder out of its mind instead. In 1985 it served the family as a sort of butler.

Betsy Braddock came to live there in 1983 with her friends from the Psi Division. That autumn the Fury attacked the house, and Brian buried it in the caverns underneath. It dug its way out the next spring, having fed on the computer down there on its way. Mastermind survived it. In 1985 RCX housed the Warpies at the Manor, the children changed by Jaspers' warp, which drove Brian out of his own house.

The Excalibur team

After the lighthouse was destroyed in 1992, the Excalibur team moved into the Manor. At its housewarming party that summer, Jamie Braddock, smuggled in among the guests, killed Brigadier Alysande Stuart. The team left the Manor for Muir Island early in 1994.

pages.title: Bra'tac
infobox: Well over a hundred and thirty by the 1990s
pages.html:
Bra'tac is a Jaffa master of Chulak who was once First Prime of the Goa'uld Apophis. He has spent more than a century training warriors, and the better part of it doubting the gods he serves. In 1984 he was one of those whom the Beyonder carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars.

Life

Bra'tac has served the Goa'uld for well over a hundred years, kept strong by the larva he carries. He is now some hundred and thirty years old. He rose to be First Prime of Apophis, the highest warrior in a System Lord's army. For generations he has trained the Jaffa of Chulak in the staff, the hand and the discipline of the warrior.

Long ago he came to believe that the Goa'uld are not gods at all, only parasites who lie to their servants. He kept the belief to himself, because to speak it would have meant death. He passed it on only to those he trusted. The best of his pupils is Teal'c, who came to him as a boy after the System Lord Cronus put Teal'c's father, Ronac, to death. Teal'c succeeded Bra'tac as First Prime of Apophis, and he shares his old master's doubt.

The Secret Wars

In 1984 the Beyonder took heroes and villains from across the world to Battleworld, the patchwork planet on which he set them to fight. Bra'tac, the Jaffa master, was among them. So it was that a servant of Apophis stood among Earth's costumed heroes and their enemies ten years before Earth opened the Stargate again. When it was over he went home to Chulak.

On Battleworld Bra'tac saw Thor for the first time, across a field of heroes. He had been brought up, like every Jaffa, on the stories of the Thunderer who killed Jaffa who surrendered. He kept his distance. Thor, who did not know who he was, never noticed him.

Later years

In 1997 Teal'c turned against Apophis and joined Earth's SG-1. From then on Bra'tac was one of Earth's closest allies, and a leader of the free Jaffa who rose against their false gods.

In 1998 he turned against Apophis aboard his mothership and helped SG-1 destroy the fleet sent against Earth. In 2003 he was a slave in Ba'al's naquadah mines on Erebus until SG-1 got him out.

The free Jaffa never forgot him. Long after the Third World War had cut them off from Earth, Jaffa children were still told of Bra'tac, of his pupil Teal'c and of the Tau'ri who had fought beside them. About 2268 it was the Jaffa who told Captain Kirk of the Enterprise the story that Earth had forgotten.

In the saga

Bra'tac has not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Brauner
infobox: Jonathan Morris, Charlotte Aulin; Dracula's servant Death
pages.html:
Brauner was a vampire and a painter who seized Dracula's castle in 1944, in the middle of the Second World War. He had lost his daughters in the Great War, and he hated mankind for it. He meant to turn the castle's power on the human race. He had no intention of bringing Dracula back to share it.

The Great War

Almost nothing is known of Brauner before the twentieth century. He had two daughters, and both of them died in the Great War. No vampire of strong blood can father a child, so they must have been the daughters of his mortal life, or else mortals he had taken as his own. Which they were is not recorded.

Men had made the war that killed them, and Brauner held all mankind guilty of it. He resolved to destroy the human race.

The castle and the paintings

In 1917 Elizabeth Bartley had used the dead of one war to raise Dracula. In 1944 Brauner turned the dead of the next to a purpose of his own. He gathered the souls of the war's dead, with all their anguish, and raised Dracula's castle with them.

He had no wish to raise its master. Dracula, he said, had failed too often. Brauner wanted only the castle's power, which he drew off through his art. He hung the castle with paintings, each one a doorway into a world he had made: a city lost in fog, a tomb in the Egyptian desert, a house in a dark forest, a topsy-turvy country he called the Nation of Fools. The paintings fed the castle's strength to him. They also sealed its throne room, so that Dracula could not return.

That made him the enemy of Dracula's servant Death, which wanted its master back. Brauner thought Death the greater danger to him, greater than any hunter.

The Lecarde sisters

Eric Lecarde, who had fought Dracula in 1917 beside John Morris, came to the castle to find out what had raised it. Brauner killed him. Eric's twin daughters, Stella and Loretta, had followed their father to the castle.

Brauner looked at the twins and saw his own daughters given back to him. He bit them both, bound them to himself with his blood and took them for his own. Under that binding they forgot who they were. They called him Father, they guarded his paintings and they fought for him.

Defeat

The castle stood in lands the Axis held, where the Spear of Destiny kept the mightiest heroes of the Allies from following. The Church sent two young hunters of its own: Jonathan Morris, the son of John, with the sorceress Charlotte Aulin. Eric Lecarde's ghost met them at the gate, under the name of Wind, to guide them.

They broke Brauner's paintings one after another. Charlotte learnt a spell of sanctuary, which lifts curses. With it she freed Stella and Loretta from him. The sisters remembered themselves. They showed the hunters the way to the last painting of all, Brauner's own studio.

Brauner fought there in a fury, crying out that they had taken his daughters from him again. Jonathan and Charlotte beat him. Then Death, which had been waiting for exactly that, cut him down. With Brauner gone the seal on the throne room broke. Dracula returned, joined his power to Death's, and the two hunters destroyed them both.

Among the Kindred

Brauner was one of the Kindred, but his clan and his sire are not recorded. Kindred who tell the story usually make him a Toreador, the clan of artists, on no evidence beyond his brushes.

The Lecarde sisters are the puzzle in it. A mortal who has been fully sired has no soul left to save, and no spell will bring her back. Stella and Loretta were brought back. It follows that Brauner had never finished the work. He had bitten them, then bound them by his blood as a ghoul is bound. The last step was still to come when Charlotte's spell reached them.

pages.title: Caitiff
pages.html:
Caitiff are vampires without a clan. Either their sire's blood was too thin to pass on a clan's nature, or they were Embraced and abandoned before anyone could say whose line they came from. They carry no clan's gift and no clan's curse. The name is an old word for a wretch, or a coward, and the other Kindred mean it.

Nature

A Caitiff has no Disciplines that come to it by birthright, though it may learn any it can find a teacher for. Nor does it suffer any clan's weakness. Like every vampire, it descends at the last from Cain, but it cannot say by which road.

Most Caitiff are of the later generations, far from Cain, where the blood runs too weak to carry a clan's nature. Many were Embraced carelessly, by sires who neither named nor taught them. They learnt what they were on their own, and late. Many of the thin-blooded, of the fifteenth generation and after, are Caitiff too.

Standing

The clans despise them. The Camarilla accepts Caitiff who keep the Traditions, but it treats them as lesser Kindred. Many were sired without a Prince's leave, against the Tradition of the Progeny. A Prince may destroy such a childe along with its sire, and in some cities the Prince's scourge hunts down the unsanctioned among them. A Caitiff who does answer to the Camarilla is bound by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world, like any other vampire of the sect: it may not hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

The Sabbat throws its Caitiff into its wars, though one who proves itself may win a place in a pack. In the Sabbat the clanless are called the Panders, after Joseph Pander, who won them a place in the sect almost as if they were a clan.

Many Caitiff find their way to the Anarchs, who care less about lineage. Some elders read the growing number of Caitiff in the twentieth century as a sign of the Time of Thin Blood, which the Book of Nod says will come before Gehenna.

pages.title: Camulus
infobox: Camulus, the Celtic god of war
pages.html:
Camulus is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped by the Celts of Gaul and Britain as a god of war. In 2004, with his fleet destroyed and his domain overrun by Ba'al, he asked Earth for asylum. Before long Earth handed him over to Ba'al, for reasons that were largely his own doing.

The god of war

Camulus came quietly to the Celts, in defiance of Ra's ban. He kept to Gaul and the south of Britain, well away from the North. The Britons named a stronghold after him, Camulodunum, the fortress of Camulus, which the Romans later made the first capital of their province. It is now Colchester. The Romans themselves worshipped him as a form of Mars, their own god of war.

Asylum

It was Camulus who sent word to Earth in the summer of 2004, after Earth had defeated Anubis, to propose a treaty. He came to Stargate Command with Amaterasu and Lord Yu to ask for Earth's help against Ba'al. 'If you do not help us stop him,' he warned, 'millions of humans will die.' The talks broke down all the same.

His own position was worse than he had let on. His fleet had been destroyed before he came, and his domain had been among the first to fall to Ba'al. When the others went home, Camulus stayed behind and asked for asylum. Through the Stargate, he told Elizabeth Weir, nothing waited for him but shame and torture.

The other System Lords branded him a traitor and a coward. Earth locked him up in a secure facility.

The bargain

Ba'al wanted him. Soon afterwards Ba'al told Earth that he had captured SG-1, and offered to exchange them for Camulus. It was not true. SG-1 had been trapped in one of Anubis's old bases, with Ba'al's Jaffa waiting for them at the Stargate outside.

Camulus thought he knew why Ba'al wanted him. He had once boasted at a meeting of the System Lords that he had found a device of the Ancients, although he had never said where. He gave Earth the address. There SG-3 found the device, with a zero point module, one of the Ancients' power sources. It had been booby-trapped. Jack O'Neill, by then the general commanding Stargate Command, called Camulus 'Cammy'. He worked out that Camulus had never discovered what the device was for, and had made sure nobody else would. Camulus denied it, then admitted that it had been worth a try.

O'Neill then offered Camulus a chance to kill Ba'al. He would go to Ba'al with the booby-trapped power source, trade it for SG-1 and let it do the rest. Camulus found the plan amusing. What O'Neill actually sent with him was Earth's own power source, which was dead. Earth kept the other.

Camulus went through the Stargate to Ba'al with his empty gift. SG-1 fought its way home on its own. What Ba'al did with Camulus is not recorded. Some months later Daniel Jackson could say simply that Camulus was gone, beaten by Ba'al.

pages.title: Canada
infobox: Queen Elizabeth II, Queen of Canada
pages.html:
Canada is a self-governing realm of the Crown in North America, with its capital at Ottawa. Queen Elizabeth II is its Queen. It still flies the Canadian Red Ensign: the maple-leaf designs proposed for a new flag in the 1960s were never adopted. Lester Pearson, the Liberal leader of those years, never became Prime Minister.

The flag

The Canadian Red Ensign is a red flag with the Union Flag in the upper corner by the staff, and the shield of the arms of Canada in the fly. Canadians fought under it in both world wars. Since 1945 it has flown over Parliament and the federal buildings of the country.

In the 1960s there was talk of replacing it with a new flag bearing a maple leaf, but no such flag was ever adopted. In 1994 the Red Ensign still flies over Parliament Hill. It is the flag Canadians know as their own.

Government

Canada is governed by a Parliament at Ottawa under the Crown. The Queen is represented in Canada by a Governor General. Laws are made by the House of Commons and the Senate.

Lester Pearson was the diplomat who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1957 for proposing the United Nations force that kept the peace at Suez. He led the Liberal Party from 1958, but he never became Prime Minister.

Wizarding Canada

Canadian witches and wizards are schooled at Ilvermorny, the wizarding school of North America, on Mount Greylock in Massachusetts. They are keen on Quidditch. The best-known Canadian teams are the Haileybury Hammers, the Moose Jaw Meteorites and the Stonewall Stormers.

In the age of heroes

The Canadian government's Department H handles superhuman affairs. Its best-known agent was the long-lived mutant Logan, Wolverine, who was born in Alberta late in the nineteenth century. He came to public notice in 1974, when Department H sent him against the Hulk and a Wendigo in the wilderness. Department H later raised a team of its own, Alpha Flight, which came to public notice in 1979.

The Weapon programme's tenth project, Weapon X, was run from a facility in the Canadian Rockies. It was there that adamantium was bonded to Logan's skeleton. The far northern forests and the tundra are the hunting grounds of the Wendigo.

pages.title: Captain Britain Corps
infobox: Long ago, by Roma, on Merlin's counsel
One champion for each of a great many Britains on the worlds that border Otherworld
Captain UK (Linda McQuillan); Captain England; Captain Albion; Captain Marshall
pages.html:
The Captain Britain Corps is the company of champions that Roma of Otherworld commands, one for each of a great many Britains. Otherworld lies outside the circles of the world, so it borders a great many worlds besides this one, and each of them has a Britain of its own. The Corps guards them. Brian Braddock, Captain Britain, is its captain for this world. He first met the others in June 1984, in Otherworld, at Merlin's funeral.

The Corps

Roma raised the Corps long ago, on Merlin's counsel, and keeps its hall at the Starlight Citadel. Each captain guards the places where his own Britain meets other worlds, and keeps his own land's laws. Their power comes from Otherworld, which gathers most strongly where the worlds wear thin. A great many of them are, on their own worlds, a Brian or a Betsy Braddock. Roma and Merlin chose them all. Between the captains stands the Dimensional Development Court, a court of many worlds, which keeps the Corps' laws and can be hard in their enforcement.

The other worlds are real places, as real as this one, though very few people on this one have seen them. Whether they have anything to do with the Crisis of 1985 to 1986, which nobody can remember clearly, nobody can say.

Captain Britain and the Corps

In the summer of 1983 captains of the Corps served as the court's officers at the trial of Saturnyne, and they came to blows with Brian, who did not know who they were. He learnt in June 1984, when Roma brought him to Otherworld to mourn Merlin and the captains stood about him in the Citadel.

In 1989, on one of the worlds the Excalibur team passed through, Brian was given the uniform of Captain Marshall, a captain who had died years before. He learnt then that away from Britain he needed a uniform to carry his power. In 1991 the Corps arrested him for breaking Kurt Wagner's leg in a fit of jealousy, and for older offences besides. He would not admit that the court had any right to try him, which might have cost him his life, until Saturnyne came with word from Roma. Captain UK spoke in his defence. Afterwards she told him what the Corps is for, and he found out that Merlin had built a lighthouse on every Britain the Corps guards.

Captains

Captain UK is Linda McQuillan, the last hero of the Britain the Corps numbers 238, which the Fury had swept clean of heroes. Merlin brought her across to this world in 1983. In May 1984 she tore the Fury apart before it could kill Brian, and in 1985 she trained Betsy Braddock to be Captain Britain.

Captain England, Henric Lockwood, and Captain Albion, Katherine Huggen, were among the first captains Brian met. Kaptain Briton, from a Britain ruled by a tyrant called Sat-yr-9, was a brute who wore the Corps' colours. In 1985 he came to Braddock Manor in Brian's clothes. Betsy killed him.

pages.title: Captain Britain
infobox: 1953, in England, minutes after his twin sister
Braddock Manor, Maldon, Essex; Muir Island, from 1994
Sir James and Lady Elizabeth Braddock, killed in 1974
Betsy Braddock (Psylocke), his twin; Jamie Braddock, his elder brother
Fettes College, Edinburgh; Thames University, London (physics)
Merlin (Gandalf) with Roma of Otherworld, 13 October 1976
An Elvish enchantment of Otherworld: great strength, speed, flight, a force field
King Arthur, through the Braddocks; he does not know it
The Captain Britain Corps; the Excalibur team, from 1987
pages.html:
Captain Britain is Brian Braddock, a physicist from Maldon in Essex, whom Merlin chose on 13 October 1976 to be Britain's champion. Merlin is Gandalf, who has watched over King Arthur's blood since Camelot, and the Braddocks come down from a Squib child of Arthur's house. Brian's power is an Elvish enchantment of Otherworld, not wizardry, so he is a Muggle. He has died twice and been brought back twice. In 1987 he helped to found the Excalibur team, and in the summer of 1994 he lives with it at Muir Island, calling himself Britanic.

Early life

Brian was born in England in 1953, a few minutes after his twin sister, Betsy. Their brother, Jamie, was about nine years older, and had been born in Otherworld, where their parents were staying at the end of the war. The twins grew up at Braddock Manor, which their father, the scientist Sir James Braddock, had built at Maldon in 1945.

Jamie was dashing and Betsy fearless. Brian was the quiet, bookish one. After Fettes College in Edinburgh he went up to Thames University in London to read physics, then stayed on for a higher degree.

In 1974, when he was twenty-one, he sat talking one night in a car outside the Manor with a girl instead of going in. While he sat there, his parents died in an explosion in his father's laboratory. Brian blamed himself.

The Amulet of Right

In the autumn of 1976 Brian was working as an assistant at Darkmoor, a secret nuclear research centre on a remote moor. On 13 October Joshua Stragg, who called himself the Reaver, attacked it with armoured men to carry off its scientists. Brian fled on his motorbike to fetch the police, and Stragg's men ran him off a cliff.

He lay broken at the bottom, and should have died. Instead he found himself in a ring of standing stones, the Siege Perilous, under two great faces made of light: an old bearded man and a dark-haired young woman. They were Merlin and Roma of Otherworld, though she called herself only the Lady of the Northern Skies. They offered him the Sword of Might or the Amulet of Right.

Brian took the amulet. He rose as Captain Britain, strong, fast and armed with a quarterstaff. Stragg had seized the sword, but Brian beat him in the Cheviot Hills. Merlin told him later that he was an heir of Arthur's. Brian took it for a figure of speech. It was the plain truth.

London, 1976 to 1977

Back at university, Brian caught the eye of a rich, clever student called Courtney Ross. As Captain Britain he fought the men of a crime lord called the Vixen, while Chief Inspector Dai Thomas of Scotland Yard, who hated costumed heroes, swore to unmask him.

In December 1976 a man calling himself Lord Synne made himself master of the villages round Maldon. He took hold of Betsy's mind, then set her on her brothers, so Brian showed himself as Captain Britain to stop her killing Jamie. In January 1977 he found the source of Synne's power: his father's computer, which had a mind of its own, called itself Mastermind and had killed his parents on purpose.

That winter Captain America came to England on an errand for S.H.I.E.L.D. The two Captains fought over a misunderstanding, then turned together on the Red Skull, who meant to found a Fourth Reich in Britain. His agents inside S.T.R.I.K.E., Britain's own agency of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s kind, bombed Braddock Manor. The Captains freed James Callaghan, then Prime Minister, from the Skull's men. With Nick Fury they found the germ bomb the Skull had hidden at Big Ben.

That spring a criminal called Lord Hawk put him in a coma. His spirit went to Otherworld, where Merlin gave him the Star Sceptre, with which he could fly. In August 1977 he told Courtney who he was, and they became a couple.

America and Cornwall, 1977 to 1979

Late in 1977 Brian went to Empire State University in New York for a year, where he shared rooms with Peter Parker. The assassin Arcade kidnapped Brian with Courtney, then caught Spider-Man by mistake, and Spider-Man's wits got all three of them out of Arcade's Murderworld. Brian drank too much in America, and Spider-Man told him so.

In 1978 he flew home. Off Cornwall the aeroplane lost its fuel, and Brian felt something evil reaching for him out of the dark. He jumped, to draw it away from the other passengers. The sea put him ashore, where he saw three oddly shaped stones with a light behind them. Then his memory went, and for more than a year he lived as a hermit in a Cornish cave.

Otherworld, 1979 to 1980

In March 1979 the Black Knight, Dane Whitman of the Avengers, found him, sent by Merlin. Otherworld was at war with the Netherworld, a dark country on its borders whose masters call themselves gods and are nothing of the kind.

In July 1979 Brian opened the gates of Otherworld with the Star Sceptre. A spectral horseman came out of them and ran him through. Merlin went after his spirit, which was drifting towards the dark, and brought it back before it had passed beyond the world. By the turn of the year he had healed Brian in body and memory.

In the spring of 1980 Brian went to find the three stones with the Black Knight and Jackdaw, a small, quick-tongued fellow of the Fair Folk. The servants of the Netherworld had stolen the sleeping King Arthur from his rest and hidden him on an island far out at sea. The stones were giants set to guard him, and Brian broke them. The king did not wake. A voice Brian took for his told him that his work there was done, and he was flung out of Otherworld. Arthur sleeps there still.

The crooked world, 1981 to 1983

In September 1981 Brian came down on another Britain beside this one, the world the Captain Britain Corps numbers 238, whose government had hunted its heroes down. There he stopped a bank raid by Mad Jim Jaspers. Saturnyne, an official from yet another world, was there to hurry that Britain forward with a fluid that quickened all life. When it took hold, Jaspers showed what he was: a mutant who could bend the world itself.

The government let loose the Fury, a machine built to kill superhumans. In the summer of 1982 the Fury killed Jackdaw, then destroyed Brian altogether. Merlin made him a new body in Otherworld, then called back his spirit, which had not yet gone on. It was the hardest test Merlin ever set him. Brian had failed it, and Merlin brought him home all the same, without telling him that he had died. In January 1983 Brian woke at Darkmoor believing he had been saved at the last moment.

Jaspers' warp, 1983 to 1984

At Maldon he found Braddock Manor standing again, rebuilt by Mastermind, which tried to talk him into joining his parents in death. Brian took the murder out of its mind. In the spring of 1983 he saved Betsy from Slaymaster. That summer he spoke at Saturnyne's trial before a court of many worlds.

That autumn Captain UK, Linda McQuillan, the last hero of the crooked world, came to the Manor. Brian's Britain had a Jaspers of its own, Sir James Jaspers, a politician calling for war on superhumans, and the Fury had followed her across. Over the winter Jaspers' power woke. The warp spread across Britain, people with powers were rounded up into camps, and Brian could not touch him. In May 1984 the Fury came back to kill Jaspers. Captain UK tore it apart.

In June 1984 Roma brought Brian to Otherworld to mourn Merlin, who had fallen holding the world together, and he met the Captain Britain Corps for the first time. Britain mended, as Roma had promised. Most people forgot.

Meggan and the lighthouse, 1984 to 1986

In July 1984 Brian met Meggan, a frightened young woman who could change her shape, and took her home to Braddock Manor. In 1985 he fought the Crazy Gang, Slaymaster and the Technet. Mastermind, tamed now and serving as a butler, told the twins that their father had been born in Otherworld. It was wrong: Sir James had spent part of his youth there, and it was Jamie who had been born there.

Then RCX, the government body that replaced S.T.R.I.K.E. after the warp, asked to house the Warpies at the Manor, children the warp had changed. Betsy said yes, and Brian walked out. In October 1985 he went to Africa to rescue Jamie, found out what Jamie had been doing there and left him to his gaolers. When he came home from his travels with Meggan, Betsy had taken his name.

He and Meggan settled in a lighthouse on the coast. In December 1985 he felt Betsy's pain from far away, and found her as Slaymaster tore out her eyes. Brian killed him, then took up his own name again. That Christmas Eve Dai Thomas came to the lighthouse to ask for his help, and the two men began, grudgingly, to be friends.

The Excalibur team, 1987 to 1998

In 1987 Brian fought beside the X-Men against the alien Horde. Weeks later the X-Men were seen to die in Dallas, and Brian drank hard. Meggan took him to Muir Island, where Kurt Wagner sobered him up by dropping him in the sea. When the Technet carried off Kitty Pryde, Rachel Summers and Meggan, Brian freed them in London with Kurt's help. By a campfire in the Highlands the five of them founded the Excalibur team, which Brian paid for.

Courtney Ross came back into his life, though in the end she turned out to be Sat-yr-9, a tyrant from another world who had killed her and taken her face. In 1991 the Corps tried him for breaking Kurt's leg in a fit of jealousy, and Roma sent Saturnyne to save his life. In the autumn of 1992 he asked Meggan to marry him. In the summer of 1993 he was swept away into the stream of time.

He came back early in 1994, when Rachel Summers took his place in time. He calls himself Britanic now, and speaks like a man listening to something far off. He lives at Muir Island with the Excalibur team, which the government keeps at home under the rules on superhumans. Late in 1994 he put his costume away to work as an engineer on the island.

In 1996 he took his father's old seat in the Hellfire Club, to find out who was rotting it from within, and learnt that the bullets which killed mutants in Genosha had been made from his father's work. That summer he became Captain Britain again. Early in 1997 he spent his power sealing a rift between the worlds. In 1998, still without it, he married Meggan in Otherworld, with Roma presiding. The Excalibur team broke up after the wedding.

Powers and secrecy

Captain Britain is very strong and very fast. He can fly, and he carries a force field about him. His power is an Elvish enchantment of Otherworld, laid on him by Merlin, which draws on a strength that gathers about the British Isles.

He has no wizard magic of any kind. The Ministry of Magic keeps a file on him. It has never decided whether the Statute of Secrecy covers a Muggle with an Elf's enchantment on him, and it has never asked him.

pages.title: Carcosa
infobox: Ambrose Bierce; Robert W. Chambers; Delta Green
On the shore of the Lake of Hali
Twin suns; black stars; strange moons; the Hyades
A dead man's, given through the medium Bayrolles, 1886
A ghost city that consumes other cities
The play The King in Yellow; the Yellow Sign; the Night Floors, 1995; Dorchester House and the Hotel Broadalbin, 2015
pages.html:
Carcosa is the city of the King in Yellow, on the shore of the Lake of Hali, where twin suns go down into the water and black stars hang in the sky. It is not on any map of the Earth, nor quite anywhere else. The oldest account of it is a dead man's, given through a medium in 1886. In Delta Green's files it is a ghost city that eats other cities. It has ways into this world that Delta Green has spent decades closing.

The dead man's city

The oldest account of Carcosa was given by the spirit of a dead man, Hoseib Alar Robardin, to the medium Bayrolles. Ambrose Bierce printed it in San Francisco at Christmas 1886, as 'An Inhabitant of Carcosa'.

The dead man had woken, he said, in a wilderness among broken stones and old graves. He remembered a fever, and a great city. He saw a lynx, an owl and a man in skins who carried a torch. None of them took any notice of him.

Slowly he understood. The broken stones were the ruins of the ancient and famous city of Carcosa. One of the graves was his own. His name was cut on the stone, with the years of his birth and of his death. He had been dead a very long time.

He set down the words of the philosopher Hali on the many kinds of death. Whether Hali was a man, a lake or both, no account makes clear.

The city of the play

In the play called The King in Yellow the city stands whole. Its towers rise beyond the lake, behind the moon. Cloud waves break along the shore of Hali, and the shadows lengthen as the twin suns sink. Strange moons circle in its skies. The Hyades sing there, and Aldebaran is near. Its court is Cassilda's. Its King is the King in Yellow.

The Lake of Hali lies below the city. Its waters are cloudy, and twin suns set in them. Hildred Castaigne, who read the play in New York, said in 1895 that his mind had sounded its depths. The man in the Court of the Dragon saw the lake at the last, in Paris that spring, with the towers beyond it and the black stars over them.

The readers of 1895 named Hastur as a place among the stars of Carcosa. Hildred Castaigne wrote of 'the lakes which connected Hastur, Aldebaran and the mystery of the Hyades'. Delta Green uses the name otherwise.

Ruin and city

The dead man found Carcosa in ruins, its people long gone. The play shows it whole, with its court about it. No account explains the difference. No account gives either the ruin or the city a place in the world.

The city that feeds on cities

Delta Green's account of Carcosa is its own, and grimmer than the play's. In its files Carcosa is a ghost city that consumes other cities. Where vice, paranoia and melancholy run deep enough in a city, they draw Carcosa towards it. Then the city begins to change. In time it is not quite itself, and then it is part of Carcosa.

Yhtill was one such city. It was ruled by a king, until the quarrel over the end of his line drew the Phantom of Truth to it, and Carcosa took it. In Carcosa, Delta Green believes, ordinary reality does not hold.

The Night World

About Carcosa lies what Delta Green calls the Night World, a country without end. Anything the King has touched may be found there, whether person, place or thing. It reaches into this world wherever his influence gathers. In 1995 it lay beyond the Night Floors above a building in Manhattan, and in May 2015 it broke into Dorchester House, a psychiatric hospital in Boston.

The agents of Delta Green who went through it in 2015 found a false Yhtill on the shore of the Lake of Hali, and then the true one. They passed through the Secret City, a war zone and the Silent City before they reached the masquerade in the King's palace. In one corner of it the battle of Stalingrad was still being fought, among the ruins of a tractor factory.

Its doors

Carcosa has doors. The play is one, and the Yellow Sign another. The Night Floors of the Macallistar Building in Manhattan, which Delta Green found in 1995, were another. Delta Green's files say that a door in Stephen Alzis's nightclub in New York opens on it too.

In 2015 the Outlaws of Delta Green went in by way of the Hotel Broadalbin, which has no fixed place in the world, and the Whisper Labyrinth beneath it. Some of them came home.

pages.title: Carmilla
infobox: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest (Famicom Disk System, 28 August 1987)
1698, by Simon Belmont; 1830, by Nathan Graves
pages.html:
Carmilla, also called Camilla, was a vampire who worshipped Dracula. In 1698 she guarded one of the relics of her master's body, and Simon Belmont destroyed her. She came back. In 1830 she raised Dracula in a castle on the edge of the Austrian Empire, where Nathan Graves destroyed her a second time.

Laruba's mansion

After Simon Belmont destroyed Dracula in 1691, the vampire's body was divided into five parts. His servants hid them in mansions across Transylvania. The ring went to Laruba's mansion, with Carmilla as its keeper.

Simon came for it in 1698, dying of the curse Dracula had laid on him. Carmilla met him in the shape of a great mask that floated in the air. He destroyed her, took the ring and went on to burn all five relics in the ruins of the castle.

Austria, 1830

About 1820 the hunter Morris Baldwin had sealed Dracula away, with the help of the parents of Nathan Graves, who died in the doing of it. Ten years later Carmilla undid their work. In an old castle on the edge of the Austrian Empire she held the rite that woke her master.

Baldwin arrived as the rite ended. He had two pupils with him, his son Hugh together with Nathan Graves. Dracula sent the young men through the floor into the catacombs. Baldwin he kept. Dracula had come back weak, so Carmilla stood guard over him until the full moon, when Baldwin's life was to be spent to make him whole.

She had a hand in what was done to Hugh Baldwin as well. Hugh resented Nathan, whom his father had named as his successor. Dracula worked on that resentment until Hugh was ready to kill his friend.

Nathan met Carmilla in the waterway beneath the castle. She told him that darkness was the true nature of mankind, which he would do well to accept. He declined. She fought him in her true form, and he destroyed her. He went on to bring Hugh back to himself, free Baldwin and destroy Dracula.

Among the Kindred

Carmilla was one of the Kindred, though her clan and her sire are not recorded. Like her master, she did not stay destroyed. Nobody has explained how she came back after 1698. Nor is it known whether 1830 was the end of her.

An Irish writer's tale of 1872 gave her name to a vampire countess of Styria, in the Austrian lands. How much he knew of her is not recorded. As with Dracula, most mortals have since taken her for somebody's invention, which suits the Kindred very well.

pages.title: Catherine Langford
infobox: Ernest Littlefield, lost through the gate in 1945
The amulet with the Eye of Ra
pages.html:
Catherine Langford is the daughter of Professor Paul Langford, whose expedition dug the Stargate out of the sand at Giza in 1928. She was there as a child, kept the amulet found with the gate, and spent her life beside it. In 1994 she recruited Daniel Jackson to read its cover stones, and so opened the way to Abydos.

Giza

Catherine was a girl of about ten when her father's workmen uncovered the gate beneath the Giza plateau in 1928. In the dust of the dig she found a gold amulet bearing the Eye of Ra, which she kept from then on. She grew up with the gate, with its two carved cover stones and with the riddle of what they meant.

1945

In 1939 the gate was shipped to the United States. In 1945 her father's team opened it by hand while testing it as a weapon for the war. Among them was her fiancé, a young scientist called Ernest Littlefield. He stepped through the gate and was lost.

The programme was shut down. Its films and papers were classified. Catherine was told that Ernest had been killed in an explosion in the laboratory. She did not learn the truth for more than fifty years.

Daniel Jackson and Abydos

When the United States Air Force revived the project in 1994, Catherine was its link with the past and the keeper of its oldest records. The military's translators had made nothing of the cover stones. After Daniel Jackson's disastrous lecture on the pyramids, she was waiting for him on his way out, and she offered him the work. Within weeks he had found the missing symbol, and the gate had opened.

Before Jackson went through, Catherine gave him the amulet she had kept since she was a girl, for luck.

Later years

In 1997, when the gate was opened again, Ernest Littlefield was found alive on a distant world, where he had lived alone for fifty-two years. He and Catherine met again when they were both old.

In the saga

Catherine Langford has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Cerise of the Shi'ar
infobox: A warrior of the Ghrand Jhar
The Shi'ar Imperium, as a ship's pilot
pages.html:
Cerise is a warrior of the Ghrand Jhar who once served the Shi'ar Imperium, and who can shape solid light at will. She fell to Earth at the end of 1991, joined the Excalibur team and fell in love with Kurt Wagner. In 1993 she gave herself up to the Shi'ar as a war criminal, and the Majestrix Lilandra sentenced her to serve at her side. In the summer of 1994 she is Lilandra's bodyguard.

The fugitive

Cerise told the team that she came from a world called Shaskofrugnon, which had bored her, so she had gone looking for adventure on the frontier. A storm in space burnt out her drive, she said, and pulled her through a rift to Earth. It was not the whole truth.

She had been the pilot of a Shi'ar recruiting ship under Captain C'Efn, sent to bring a people of the sea into the Imperium by wiping most of them out. Cerise would not do it. She sent the ship into a sun and escaped. Her crew died with it.

Earth

From the light that she draws out of herself Cerise can make shields, weapons and anything else she needs. They are as solid as steel for as long as she wills them. She fought beside the team against Necrom in 1992, and went with it to Braddock Manor. There she and Kurt Wagner fell in love.

At the end of 1992 she went with Kurt and Kitty Pryde to look for Alistaire Stuart at Cloud Nine, where the RCX declared all three of them illegal aliens. It was Cerise and Kurt who found out that the Kitty with them was a double.

Judgement

In June 1993 the Starjammers came to Braddock Manor for a Shi'ar war criminal, and Cerise gave herself up. She was sent to Krag, a prison world, where she shared the trouble of an old prisoner called Cryan. Members of the High Council sent an assassin, Fang, to make sure of her. Cerise killed him.

Cryan was the Majestrix Lilandra in disguise, who had watched it all. She read the ship's logs, then sentenced Cerise to serve at her side as her bodyguard, rooting out officers of C'Efn's kind. That August Cerise parted from Kurt.

She came back for Brian Braddock's wedding in Otherworld in August 1998, where she scolded Kurt for never coming to look for her.

pages.title: Char of Aznable
infobox: The Imperial Entanglement; the Intergalactic War
pages.html:
Char of Aznable was a human commander of the Klingon Empire, raised among Klingons from childhood. He led the Klingons' Zaku mobile suits in a red machine of his own, which earned him the name of the Red Comet.

The Red Comet

Char of Aznable grew up as a Klingon in everything but blood. He rose to command the Zakus, the mobile suits that the Klingons had lately begun to build. His own was painted red. It was said to move three times as fast as any other.

Side 7 and after

On 17 May 2293 he brought the Klingon force to Side 7 as the ally of the Galactic Empire. When the Empire's part in the destruction of Praxis came out, he turned his Zakus on the Imperial fleet. In the Intergalactic War he covered the retreat from Morska. At the Battle of Earth he fought beside Amuro Ray's Gundam.

In the saga

Char of Aznable has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Charterville
infobox: Zoom Comics; Charterville Cemetery; Charterville Prison
Hillhurst Mansion; Zoom Comics; the cemetery; Charterville Prison
pages.html:
Charterville is a small American town with a comic shop, a cemetery, a prison and, just outside it, a haunted house. From 1996 to 1998 it was the home ground of the Beetleborgs, whom the whole town knew as its own heroes. Most of their battles were fought in its streets.

The town

Charterville is an ordinary place, where everybody knows everybody. Hillhurst Mansion stands a little way outside it, empty of the living since Old Man Hillhurst died. The town has always said that the house is haunted. Urbana City, a larger place some way off, is where the comic-book artist Art Fortunes has his office.

The town has a monster of its own in legend, known as Charterville Charlie. In April 1997 it seemed to have turned up at last. It proved to be one of Vexor's monsters out of the comics.

Zoom Comics

Zoom Comics is the town's comic shop, kept by Aaron Williams with his wife, Abbie. Their son, Roland, has a grandmother whom everybody calls Nano, a martial artist who rides a motorcycle. The children of the town spend their pocket money there. Three of them, Roland Williams with his friends Drew and Jo McCormick, hardly spend their time anywhere else.

It was at Zoom Comics, on 7 September 1996, that two rich brothers, Trip and Van, dared the three to go into Hillhurst. What they found there made them the Beetleborgs.

Townspeople

Trip and Van are rich, spoilt, bullies both. After the dare went wrong they tried to have Hillhurst pulled down. In November 1996 Count Fangula, the vampire of the house, caught them at last. In May 1997 it was Trip and Van whom Nukus told how the monster Borgslayer could be destroyed, because he wanted the Magnavores swept away with it.

Heather is a girl of the town whom Drew McCormick admired from a distance. Josh Baldwin came new to Charterville in November 1996. For a few days he was the White Blaster Beetleborg.

The cemetery and the prison

From September 1996 Vexor kept his court in a crypt in the Charterville cemetery. Jo McCormick found it that November. When the Magnavores were gone, Nukus took the place over for his Crustaceans.

Charterville Prison held Les Fortunes, the brother of Art Fortunes, for what offence is not recorded. In September 1997 the Crustaceans broke him out, starting a riot as they went. On 2 March 1998 he walked back in of his own accord.

The town's heroes

The Beetleborgs were public heroes in Charterville from the first week. Nobody knew who they were. A journalist found it out in September 1997, when it took the Beetleborgs with the whole household at Hillhurst to keep the story out of print.

Three times the town had stranger visitors still. On 19 October 1996 the Cogs of the Machine Empire marched in, with the Zeo Rangers after them. On 20 September 1997 changelings in the likeness of Power Rangers wrecked the middle of the town, until the real Rangers came. On 21 February 1998 Astronema's Quantrons fought the Crustaceans in the cemetery. Charterville took it calmly on the whole. It had been living next door to Hillhurst for years.

pages.title: Cheryl Mason
infobox: Found as a baby in the summer of 1976; lost at Silent Hill on 12 September 1983
Jodie Mason, by adoption, who died in 1979
None that has ever shown itself
The god of the Order of Silent Hill, 17 September 2000
pages.html:
Cheryl Mason, who goes by the name of Heather, is the adopted daughter of the writer Harry Mason. In the summer of 1994 she is ten years old and knows nothing of where she came from. She is the second child Harry has raised under that name. The first Cheryl was the lost half of the soul of Alessa Gillespie, found as a baby in 1976 and drawn back to Silent Hill in September 1983. The second is Alessa herself, whole again and born a second time. In September 2000, four days after her seventeenth birthday, she went back to Silent Hill. She killed the Order's god there and took her own name back.

The first Cheryl

In the summer of 1976 Dahlia Gillespie burnt her seven-year-old daughter, Alessa, in a rite of the Order of Silent Hill. Alessa's soul split in two. One half stayed in her burnt body. The other became a newborn baby, which Harry Mason and his wife, Jodie, found at the side of the highway on their way home from a holiday. They adopted her, and named her Cheryl.

She grew up as an ordinary child. Jodie died when she was three, so that Harry was all the family she remembered. She was a schoolgirl of seven in 1983, with short dark hair and a sketchbook.

For all those seven years Dahlia had been working a spell to call her back. In September 1983 Cheryl asked her father to take her to Silent Hill for their holiday. On the night of the 12th, on the way into the town, the car crashed. Cheryl walked away into the fog, towards the other half of herself. Harry searched the whole town for her. By the time he found her she had been joined to Alessa again, and there was no Cheryl left to take home.

Born again

The Order's god was born from the rejoined girl on the night of 13 September 1983, and Harry killed it. As the place burnt, she held out a baby to him. It was herself: the one soul, Alessa's and Cheryl's together, begun again from the first day.

Harry took the baby home. He wrote later that he had been afraid of her at first, not knowing what she was. He raised her all the same, and gave her his daughter's name.

Heather

The Order did not forget her. In 1988, when she was still very small, one of its people found Harry and the child in Portland. Harry shot him. They moved to another city, and from then on she was called Heather, to make her harder to find. On paper she is still the Cheryl Mason of 1976, which makes her seven years older in the records than she is in life.

She is growing up knowing none of this. In the summer of 1994 she is ten, living with her father in a flat a long way from Silent Hill. On one of her birthdays Harry gave her a pendant with a red tablet inside it. He did not tell her what it was for.

Alessa was a witch. Her magic did not come back with her: she had poured it out over Silent Hill for seven years, and there it stayed. Heather has never shown any. She turned eleven on 13 September 1994, and no letter from Ilvermorny followed.

The summons, 2000

On Saturday 16 September 2000, three days after her seventeenth birthday, Heather fell asleep in a burger bar in a shopping centre. She dreamt of an amusement park in the dark. When she woke, a middle-aged private detective named Douglas Cartland was waiting to speak to her about her birth. She climbed out of a lavatory window to get away from him.

The shopping centre had emptied while she slept. There were creatures in it. A barefoot woman in black, Claudia Wolf, told her that she would lead the faithful to paradise with blood on her hands. Then the building changed around her into the rust and darkness of the Otherworld, a long way from Silent Hill.

Heather made her way home through the night by the underground railway, the sewers and a half-built office block. A priest named Vincent Smith stopped her to explain that he was on her side, which she doubted. When she reached the flat, her father was dead in his armchair. Claudia was waiting on the roof to tell her why. One of the Order's creatures had done it on her orders. She would be in Silent Hill, she said, if Heather wanted her.

Heather wanted her very badly. Cartland, who had been told a pack of lies by his client, offered to drive. On the road she read her father's notebook, which told her what she was.

Silent Hill

They reached Silent Hill the next day, Sunday 17 September. The town was empty and deep in fog. On Vincent's advice Heather went to Brookhaven Hospital to find Leonard Wolf, Claudia's father, who was said to hold a seal that could stop the god. In the hospital her first life began to come back to her. Leonard, a patient there, had become a monster. When he found that she was no believer he tried to kill her. She killed him, and took the Seal of Metatron.

The way to the Order's church lay through Lakeside Amusement Park, which was the place she had dreamt of. She found Cartland there with a broken leg. He had gone ahead to stop Claudia, and had failed. On the carousel she met a burnt girl with her own face, the memory of Alessa, who had wanted to die sooner than give the god a body. Heather had to fight her to get past.

The god

In the church that night she felt the god move inside her. It had been there since her birth, asleep, and her hatred of Claudia had fed it. Claudia thanked her for that. Vincent told her to use the seal. Claudia stabbed him, and remarked that the seal was only a piece of metal.

Heather remembered the pendant. She swallowed the tablet of aglaophotis that was in it, and was sick on the chapel floor. What came up was the god, unborn. Before she could crush it Claudia snatched it up and swallowed it herself.

Claudia bore the god and died of it. It was a thin, half-made thing with something of Alessa's face. Heather killed it. Then she sat down on the floor and cried for her father.

Cheryl again

She went back to the amusement park for Cartland, as she had promised. He asked what he should call her now. She told him to use the name her father had given her, which was Cheryl.

pages.title: Children of Gaia
infobox: Peacemaking, healing and ending the Impergium
pages.html:
The Children of Gaia are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: healers, peacemakers and mediators, who led the call to end the Impergium. They still work to hold the quarrelling tribes together against the Wyrm.

Totem and ways

The Children follow Unicorn, a spirit of peace, healing and purity, whose followers are held to honesty. They believe that after the Wyrm, the Garou's worst enemy is their own rage, and that tribes who spend their strength on each other cannot win the war. Their Gifts run to healing wounds, and to calming rage, whether it is their own or somebody else's. They are gentler than other Garou with humans and the weak. They are more willing, too, to talk before they fight. Against the servants of the Wyrm, though, they fight as hard as any tribe.

The tribe takes in those whom others reject. Sons born to the Black Furies find a place among the Children. So do metis cast out by their own tribes, cubs the Get of Fenris judged too weak, and lost cubs who never learnt which tribe they belonged to. It makes the Children one of the largest of the tribes, and the most varied.

History and homelands

The Children say their tribe was born of the Garou who could not stomach the Impergium, the long culling of mankind in the ages after the ice. At the Concord they were foremost among those who called for it to end. They have played the peacemaker ever since.

They claim no single homeland. Their septs are found on every continent, often near places of pilgrimage, healing and refuge, in the countryside as often as in the cities.

Place in the world

Other tribes respect the Children's healers and mediators. Many a moot has been saved from bloodshed by one of them. The warrior tribes think them soft, naive about mankind. The Get of Fenris and the Red Talons think so most of all. The Children are closest to the Black Furies, whose sons they raise.

pages.title: Chris Ramirez
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Vent or Be Vented' (14 March 2009)
Kit Taylor; Len of Ventara; Maya Young
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Chris Ramirez is an American, born about 1989 into a family that has sent its sons into the Marines for five generations. He followed them, but the Marines discharged him because of his asthma. In 2009 Xaviax, passing himself off as a federal agent, made him Kamen Rider Sting. Apart from Kit Taylor, Chris was the only one of Xaviax's recruits who changed sides. On 22 August 2009 he took a blow that was meant for Len of Ventara, which vented him.

The Marine

Chris wanted to be a Marine, like the men of his family before him. He got as far as the uniform. Then he was given a medical discharge, because of his asthma. He was about nineteen.

A man who said that he was a federal agent came to him with an offer. Earth was being invaded by aliens, the agent said. The government had a secret programme to fight them, which needed a soldier to wear a suit of armour. The agent was Xaviax. The armour was the stolen Advent Deck of Sting, which opened for Chris because he was the mirror twin of Quinn, a vented Rider of Ventara.

The hero of Gramercy Heights
