Chris did exactly what he had been asked to do. He guarded a district of the city called Gramercy Heights, where he fought the monsters that came out of its mirrors. Maya Young went looking there for the Rider who was protecting people. She found him on 14 March 2009.

The same day Kit Taylor helped him to destroy a monster. Chris thanked him by trying to arrest him. He had been told that the other armoured men were the invaders.

Changing sides

Len of Ventara fought him twice on 21 March. The second time Len had him beaten, then walked away without venting him. That set Chris wondering who was telling the truth. Maya talked to him. On 28 March he fought a monster beside Kit. A week later he came to Len's help.

On 11 April Kit, Len and Maya told him everything. He asked why Xaviax had picked a man with asthma. Len explained that Xaviax had had no choice, since nobody else on Earth could have used that deck. Chris agreed that Xaviax must be stopped. Then an attack of asthma doubled him over. He left, saying that he could not help them when he could not even help himself. Maya went after him.

He came back. Strike hunted him through August, so Kit had to rescue him twice with Len. A letter from his doctor told him that his condition was getting worse. He thought of giving up. Len showed him that a Rider does not have to fight alone.

Semper Fi

On 22 August 2009 James Trademore, the man inside Strike's armour, found Chris writing in his journal. He offered him a cure for his asthma. The price was Len. Chris said no. The two of them fought for the third time. Chris got away on the back of Evildiver.

The same day the Cho brothers attacked. Chris fought Albert Cho at Len's side. Strike appeared, aiming his Final Vent at Len. Chris put himself in front of it. As the armour failed he laid his hand on his chest. He said, 'Semper Fi.' Then he was gone.

Kit found a letter in Chris's bag afterwards. Chris had written it to his father, but he had never sent it. Len blamed himself for months.

Afterwards

Chris lay in the Advent Void until Xaviax was dead. In December 2009 Eubulon, the Advent Master, brought him out. He took away Chris's memories of the war, as he did with every Rider of Earth but Kit. He also cured his asthma. Chris went back into the Marines.

pages.title: Christof Romuald
infobox: A crusader knight in the service of the Church
From the fall of Vyšehrad in the 1140s until 1999
Destroying the Tzimisce Methuselah Vukodlak in New York, 1999
pages.html:
Christof Romuald is a French crusader knight who was Embraced into Clan Brujah in Prague in 1141 by Ecaterina the Wise. He lost his faith with his life. For the sake of Anezka, the nun he loved, he fought the Tremere and the Tzimisce. Then he lay buried beneath the fallen castle of Vyšehrad for more than eight hundred years. Woken in London in 1999, he followed Anezka to New York. There he destroyed the Tzimisce Methuselah Vukodlak in his Cathedral of Flesh, and sired her as his childe. Through all of it he kept his humanity.

The knight of Prague

Christof was a French knight in the service of the Church, a crusader of deep and simple faith. In 1141 he was in Prague. He was wounded in battle there, and nursed back to health in a church by a young nun, Anezka. They fell in love. Neither of them said so, because his vows and hers stood between them.

In those nights a monster was preying on the city from a silver mine nearby. Christof went down into the mine and killed it. It was a creature of the Tzimisce, the old vampire lords of the East, and the deed drew the eyes of every Kindred in Prague.

The Embrace

Ecaterina the Wise led the Brujah of Prague. She was a scholar of the clan who still dreamt of what Carthage had been. She Embraced him that same night, before any other clan could claim him. He rose of the ninth generation, with the Brujah gifts of speed, strength and presence.

The faith that had made him a crusader broke with his death. A creature that must drink the blood of men and hide from the sun could not, he believed, stand before God. What he kept was Anezka, and a stubborn refusal to become the monster his blood wanted him to be.

The Tremere and the Tzimisce

Prague in 1141 lay between two enemies. The Tremere were wizards of the Order of Hermes who had stolen the Embrace a century before. They were preparing for war with the Tzimisce. In their chantries they were making ghouls and gargoyles to fight it.

Christof served Ecaterina with a coterie of his own. There was Wilhem Streicher, a Brujah of the tenth generation; Erik, a Gangrel of the North; and Serena, a Cappadocian given to them by the elder Garinol. They broke into the Tremere chantry in Prague and saved Erik from being made into a gargoyle. Then they followed the trail to Vienna.

There, in the Tremere house called Haus de Hexe, Etrius of the clan's ruling council finished Erik's transformation, and Christof was forced to destroy his friend. Etrius told him what he most feared: the Tzimisce had taken Anezka.

Vyšehrad

Christof went after her to Vyšehrad, the castle above Prague that the Tzimisce held. He cut his way through its soldiers and confronted the Tzimisce lady Libussa. He found Anezka there. She had been made the ghoul of the Methuselah Vukodlak, an elder of the Tzimisce who lay sleeping beneath the castle and meant to rise above the ancestors of every clan. She turned from Christof and went to wake her master.

Before she could, mortal forces stormed Vyšehrad, and the castle came down on them all. Christof lay buried in its ruins, in torpor. The elders of the Tzimisce bound Vukodlak in a sleep of their own.

London

He slept beneath Vyšehrad for more than eight hundred years. In 1999 the Society of Leopold, the Church's hunters of vampires, dug out the ruins. They found his body and carried it to London, where he woke. The Society was led by Leo Allatius, a mortal kept alive for three hundred years by vampire blood. He meant to use Vukodlak's blood to destroy every vampire in the world.

The world had changed past recognition; the Kindred had not. The Camarilla hid from humanity. The Sabbat meant to rule it. Vukodlak's followers had taken Vyšehrad back, and they meant to raise him. Christof found Wilhem still walking after eight centuries, now of the Sabbat, in the service of Ecaterina. She had become a Sabbat archbishop, and was fighting those of her own sect who served the Methuselah.

In London Christof gathered a new coterie. One was Pink, who called himself a Brujah and was in truth an Assamite assassin in Vukodlak's pay. The other was Lily, a young Toreador, whom he freed from a brothel of the Followers of Set after destroying its mistress, Lucretia.

New York

The trail led to New York, where the Setites had been smuggling the treasures of Vyšehrad. It ran through a warehouse of the Giovanni. Christof rescued a Nosferatu, Samuel, from the Sabbat. He found Vukodlak hidden beneath the Cathedral of Flesh, a temple of shaped and living flesh that his Tzimisce had raised.

Vukodlak offered him Anezka, who lived only by the Methuselah's blood, if Christof would serve him. Christof refused. Vukodlak flung him and his companions into the tunnels beneath. There, in the Wall of Memories, Christof saw the truth of the eight centuries. Anezka had never truly gone over. All that time she had worked in secret against her master's waking, and prayed for Christof to come back.

The Cathedral of Flesh

Christof went back up into the Cathedral of Flesh and destroyed Vukodlak. Anezka, freed, had no master's blood left to keep her. Without it the centuries would have taken her at once. Christof was reconciled with her. He Embraced her so that she would not die, and she became his childe, of the tenth generation.

He had come through eight hundred years in the earth, two ages of the Jyhad and a Methuselah's cathedral without giving himself up to the Beast. Among the Kindred, that is rarer than any victory.

Later years

In the first years of the new century Christof was at Ecaterina's side once more. With her and the Kindred scholar Beckett he travelled to Tunis. They had word that the resting place of the fallen Antediluvian of the Brujah lay beneath a dam near the city, not far from the ruins of Carthage.

pages.title: Clan Assamite
infobox: Haqim (Antediluvian), said by the clan to sleep and to watch
The Tremere curse (1493 to 1999): burnt by the blood of other Kindred
Independent; seat at Alamut, in the mountains of Persia
Al-Ashrad, Amr of Alamut; Fatima al-Faqadi; Ur-Shulgi
pages.html:
The Assamites are the assassins of the Kindred. They call themselves the Children of Haqim, and they are ruled from Alamut, a fortress hidden in the mountains of Persia. The clan has three castes: warriors, viziers and sorcerers. It belongs to neither the Camarilla nor the Sabbat, and it will kill vampires for anybody who can meet its price. Since the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the whole clan has carried a blood curse laid on it by the Tremere: any Assamite who drinks the blood of another vampire is burnt by it.

Haqim

Haqim was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, the Antediluvians, Embraced about 9300 BC by the childer of Cain in Enoch, the First City. His line remembers him as a judge, set over the other descendants of Cain to punish their crimes. It remembers him too as a guardian of mortals against the hunger of his own kind. He gave his childer laws, which they still keep as the Code of Haqim. In the clan's own eyes it exists for one purpose: to judge other vampires, and to kill them where judgement demands it.

Nobody knows what became of Haqim. The clan holds that he outlived the First City and the slaying of the Second Generation, about 8990 BC. Then, it says, he withdrew from the world to sleep, and one night he will wake to judge the Kindred. It holds too that the blood brings a vampire nearer to its founder as it brings it nearer to Cain, so that a childe who drinks an elder's blood and soul comes a step closer to Haqim. For thousands of years that belief made diablerie the highest act of the Assamites' faith, though the other clans count it among the worst of crimes. The clan took its fees in the blood of the vampires it killed.

Disciplines and castes

An Assamite strikes unseen with Obfuscate, moves faster than the eye can follow with Celerity, and kills with Quietus, the clan's own art of silent death. Quietus can wrap him in a silence from which no sound escapes, or let him wound with a touch. It can also turn his own blood to poison, which he smears on a blade or spits into a victim's face. To another vampire that blood is as deadly as it is to a mortal. The clan's sorcerers work a blood magic of their own, older than the Tremere's, which they call Dur-An-Ki. Age and the drinking of older blood darken an Assamite's skin, so that the eldest of the clan are almost black.

The warriors are the largest of the three castes, and they are the assassins whose name the clan carries. Their young are the fida'i, who earn their place with their first contracts. The viziers are the clan's scholars, judges, artists and keepers of accounts. Where the warriors hide with Obfuscate, the viziers see far with Auspex. The sorcerers are the magicians who keep the clan's secrets and its wards. Other Kindred call them all Assassins, which the clan does not much mind.

Alamut and the Embrace

The clan's stronghold is Alamut, a fortress in the mountains of Persia. Its sorcerers hide it from mortal eyes, and no outsider enters it uninvited. It is ruled by the eldest of the clan, whose word binds every Assamite, and a tithe from every contract goes back to it. For most of its history the clan drew its childer from the peoples of Persia, Arabia, Mesopotamia and North Africa; in the modern nights it Embraces across the world. A candidate is watched for years before the Embrace, and is often trained first as a mortal servant of the clan. He is tested before he is given the blood.

A warrior's work is the contract. The Assamites kill for any patron who can meet their price, Kindred or mortal, and once they have accepted a contract they see it through. They keep the Masquerade, honour hospitality and stand by their word. They look on most other clans as erring children of Cain who will one day be judged. The Tremere they count as their enemies, for reasons that go back to 1493.

From the Second City to the Crusades

Cain cursed the clans and departed into Nod about 8980 BC. The Antediluvians and their childer then raised a Second City. By its own account Haqim's line served there as the judges and executioners of the Kindred. When the Second City fell in its turn the clans scattered, and the Children of Haqim went east. From then on their history runs through the lands between the Nile and the Indus. The kings of Mesopotamia and Persia employed them in secret, as counsellors as well as killers. Haqim's childer also judged the Kindred who preyed on those kings' peoples.

At the end of the eleventh century the Crusades brought the Kindred of Europe east with the Frankish armies. From Alamut the Assamites fought the Crusaders and the vampires who came with them. Europe learnt to fear the clan in those years, and the name Assassin came west with the returning knights. Through the rest of the Middle Ages the clan's killers were for hire in Europe as well as in the East. Their fee was still blood.

The Anarch Revolt

In the fifteenth century the young Kindred of Europe rose against their elders, who had saved themselves from the Inquisition by giving their childer to the fires. The anarchs learnt to break the blood bond. They hired Assamites to strike at the elders in their havens, and paid them in the blood of the elders they killed. The clan grew strong on it. About 1405 Assamites went with Gratiano and his Lasombra anarchs against the Castle of Shadows on Sicily. There Gratiano claimed to have drunk the blood and soul of the Lasombra Antediluvian himself.

To the elders who founded the Camarilla in 1435, the clan was the most dangerous of the anarchs' allies, because it killed for wages and drank what it killed. The war between them lasted until the Convention of Thorns.

The Convention of Thorns and the curse

At the Convention of Thorns, in England in 1493, the Camarilla, the anarchs and the Assamites made peace. The clan was left independent and its crimes were pardoned, but the price was hard. The Assamites forswore the drinking of Kindred blood. They accepted a curse, laid on the whole clan by the Tremere, under which any Assamite who drinks the blood of another vampire is burnt by it from within, as if he had swallowed acid. Diablerie, the centre of the clan's faith, was taken from it at a stroke.

Since then the clan has taken its pay in money, in favours and in mortal blood. Alamut still has its tithe from every contract. The clan's sorcerers have worked at the curse from the night it was laid, and its hatred of the Tremere has not cooled in five centuries. A minority refused the terms and went with the anarchs who would not make peace. They became the Assamite antitribu of the Sabbat, which they serve as assassins and warriors.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Assamites remain independent and much in demand. Princes of the Camarilla, bishops of the Sabbat, anarch barons and mortal patrons all hire them. The news that an Assamite has come to a city is enough to make its elders double their guards. Because they may not drink the vampires they kill, their price for a Kindred target is high, and they do not lower it. They are no party to the agreement the Camarilla made with the wizarding world in 1900, so no promise of theirs protects a witch or wizard.

Among the best known of the clan are Al-Ashrad, the Amr of Alamut, who is master of its sorcerers, and Fatima al-Faqadi, the most celebrated of its warriors. Her name has been feared since the Crusades.

Later nights

In 1999 the clan's sorcerers broke the Tremere curse at last, and the Assamites could drink the blood of other vampires again. In the same year Ur-Shulgi took the clan in hand. He was an ancient sorcerer of the clan's oldest blood, who had woken at Alamut from a sleep of many centuries. He called the clan back to its old purpose: war on the other clans, and the drinking of their blood.

Many of the clan would not follow him, and the Assamites split. A large part of the viziers fled Alamut, with some warriors beside them, and were taken into the Camarilla, the first of the clan ever to join it. Others went over to the antitribu in the Sabbat. The rest stayed loyal to Alamut. The curse was gone, but a craving took its place: an Assamite who drank the blood of another vampire came to want it as an addict wants his drug.

pages.title: Clan Brujah
infobox: Brujah (Antediluvian), destroyed by his childe Troile
Troile; Tyler; Jeremy MacNeil; Ecaterina the Wise; Christof Romuald
pages.html:
The Brujah are the clan of rebels. Once they were philosophers and warrior-kings; now they are the brawling, idealistic heart of every rising against the elders. They are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla and its most restless member, as well as the backbone of the Anarchs.

Brujah and Troile

The clan's founder, Brujah, was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, Embraced about 9300 BC in Enoch, the First City. He is remembered among them as a scholar, a lawgiver and a thinker. With the rest of the Third he rose against the Second Generation and slew it about 8990 BC. When Cain cursed the clans for it, about 8980 BC, he laid on Brujah's line a rage that lies very close to the surface.

Kindred tradition holds that Brujah's favoured childe, Troile, later destroyed him by drinking his blood and soul. Most of the clan therefore descends through Troile rather than from the founder directly. Diablerie is among the worst crimes the Kindred know, so the clan was born, in a sense, out of one. The Brujah have taken the lesson to heart: they do not believe that age alone entitles anybody to rule.

Gifts and curse

The Brujah were thinkers before they were fighters, and many of them still are. They argue philosophy as hotly as they fight, and they fight hard. Their Disciplines are Celerity, Potence and Presence. These give them speed, strength and the power to sway a crowd. A Brujah can cross a room before a mortal has finished blinking and break a man's arm with a careless grip. Then the same Brujah can hold a hall full of strangers with a speech.

Their curse is passion. The Beast in a Brujah lies close to the surface, and they fall into frenzy far more easily than other Kindred do, at an insult, a setback or an injustice. Once frenzied, a Brujah fights until whatever provoked it is gone, or the Brujah is. The other clans call them the Rabble, and choose their words with care in their company.

Whom they Embrace

The Brujah Embrace people with a cause or a grievance. Students, agitators, soldiers, strikers, street fighters, punks and poets with a temper have all found their way into the clan. So has anybody who stood up to authority and paid for it. The clan has no single creed and little hierarchy. Its members gather in loose bands, and they argue their politics at meetings that end in a brawl as often as not. Nerve and conviction count for far more among them than age.

Brujah of the modern nights are often sorted into three temperaments. Idealists still believe in the clan's old dream of a just society of Kindred and mortals. Iconoclasts want to tear down whatever stands, beginning with the princes. Individualists care for nothing but their own freedom. In practice most Brujah are a little of all three, depending on the night.

Carthage

After Cain departed into Nod, Brujah's line was among the founders of the Second City. The clan remembers its part there as the age of its lawgivers. When that city fell and the clans scattered, the Brujah carried their ideals west across the Mediterranean.

Their great work was Carthage. In that city, the Brujah say, Kindred and mortals lived openly together. The vampires guided their mortal neighbours instead of preying on them, and Carthage was a just city of the kind the clan has looked for ever since. The Ventrue saw it differently. They accused it of harbouring worshippers of the Devil among its vampires, and they set Rome against it. After three wars Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BC. The Brujah have never forgiven the Ventrue for it. Nor have they ever quite stopped looking for another Carthage.

The Dark Ages and the Anarch Revolt

Through the Middle Ages the Brujah were scholars as well as warriors, across Europe and round the Mediterranean. They taught in the schools and universities. They fought in the wars of Spain and on the crusades. No clan was readier to argue with a prince to his face. The Ventrue and Lasombra elders, whose feudal order the Brujah openly despised, called them Zealots.

In the twelfth century the Brujah of Prague were led by Ecaterina the Wise, a scholar who still dreamt of Carthage. She meant her clan to be the pawn of neither the Tremere nor the Tzimisce, who were making ready for war with each other. In 1141 she Embraced a French crusader, Christof Romuald. When the castle of Vyšehrad fell in the 1140s he was buried beneath its ruins, and there he lay in torpor until 1999.

When the Inquisition came, the elders saved themselves by giving their childer to the fires, and the young Brujah were among the first to rise. The Brujah Tyler was among the leaders of the Anarch Revolt. The anarchs learnt to break the blood bond that held them to their sires. They hired Assamite assassins, and they struck at the elders in their havens. The elders answered by founding the Camarilla in 1435. Most of the clan accepted the peace at the Convention of Thorns in 1493, and so the Brujah became one of the seven founders of the Camarilla, the very society the elders had built to rule them. Those who would not accept it went over to the Sabbat.

The modern nights

The Brujah have been the Camarilla's most restless clan ever since. They hold few princedoms and want fewer. Wherever the young Kindred of a city turn against their prince, there are Brujah at the front. Most of the Anarch Movement is Brujah or Caitiff. In 1944 anarchs led by the Brujah Jeremy MacNeil overthrew the princes of California, among them the Toreador Don Sebastian of Los Angeles. They declared the Anarch Free States, which still stand.

The Camarilla has learnt to use the clan as much as to fear it. Brujah serve it as enforcers: as sheriffs, as scourges, as the Archons of its Justicars. A prince who wants a fight won often asks the Brujah to win it. Brujah who answer to the Camarilla are bound, like the rest, by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world. The wizarding governments lend their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade. In return no vampire who answers to the Camarilla may hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

The antitribu

The Brujah antitribu of the Sabbat descend from those of the clan who refused the Convention of Thorns. They have kept the clan's rage and lost most of its philosophy. They are the Sabbat's shock troops, sent first through the door when it attacks a Camarilla city. They scorn the Camarilla Brujah as rebels who made their peace with the elders, and the two branches of the clan have fought each other in city after city since the Convention. The Sabbat never signed the agreement with the wizarding world, so nothing in it binds the antitribu.

pages.title: Clan Gangrel
infobox: Each frenzy leaves an animal feature
City Gangrel and country Gangrel (Sabbat)
pages.html:
The Gangrel are the wanderers of the Kindred: solitary vampires who sleep in the earth, run as wolves and live closer to the Beast than any other clan. They descend from Ennoia, the huntress of the Third Generation. They are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla, though most of them care little for its politics. Of all vampires, they know the Garou best.

Ennoia

The clan's founder, Ennoia, was one of the thirteen Antediluvians, Embraced in the First City about 9300 BC. She is remembered as a huntress who never loved walls. After the Third Generation slew their sires, Cain cursed them and departed. Ennoia would not live in the Second City that the other founders raised. She turned her back on the cities of the Kindred for the wilderness, and her childer have kept to the wild places ever since.

Gangrel tales say that she ran with the wolves until she had learnt their shapes. They say too that she taught her line to sleep in the earth. No Gangrel living claims to have seen her, and nobody knows whether she sleeps somewhere in the wild or was destroyed long ago.

Gift and curse

Gangrel call and command beasts with Animalism. With Fortitude they endure wounds that would destroy other vampires. Protean, the clan's own Discipline, lets them change their own bodies. With it they see in the dark and grow claws that can wound even other vampires grievously. They can sink into the bare earth to sleep through the day, or take the shape of a wolf or a bat. The eldest can become mist. Because a Gangrel can sleep wherever the dawn finds it, the clan needs no haven. That, more than anything, has let it live outside the cities.

Their curse is that the Beast marks them. Every frenzy leaves some animal trait behind: fur, a muzzle, slit eyes, claws or a tail. The oldest Gangrel look more like beasts than men. Other Kindred call them the Outlanders.

Embrace and way of life

The Gangrel Embrace survivors: hunters, soldiers, drifters, travellers, and anybody who has lived hard at the edges of the world. A sire often leaves its childe to fend for itself from the first night, and comes back only to see whether it lived. The clan has little use for titles. Among the Gangrel, standing is won by deeds, by age and by surviving. Elders settle questions by challenge, by the telling of tales and by the judgement of their peers at the clan's rare gatherings in wild places.

Most Gangrel travel alone or in small packs, crossing the country between cities. Many feed from animals for long stretches. They keep their history in spoken tales rather than in writing, so a Gangrel's account of its own deeds is the nearest thing the clan has to a record.

The ancient world

The Gangrel ranged the forests and steppes of the ancient world. They kept to the Celtic lands and to the north, far from the Second City or any court that came after it. They ran with the peoples beyond the frontiers of Rome. When those peoples broke the Western Empire, there were Gangrel among them. The Norse feared them as night-walkers and shape-changers. From the British Isles to the Russian plains the clan was rooted in the land long before any prince claimed it. Where the other clans built courts, the Gangrel kept territories. A single vampire might hold a forest, a moor or a mountain pass for centuries, hunting the herds and the travellers who crossed it.

The Dark Ages and the Revolt

In the Middle Ages the Gangrel lived beyond the walls of the cities, which spared them the worst of the Inquisition. Their young suffered under their elders all the same, like the young of any clan, and many joined the Anarch Revolt. In the east the Tremere caught Gangrel in the mountains of Transylvania. Out of their bodies, as out of captured Tzimisce and Nosferatu, the Tremere shaped gargoyles to fight for them. The clan has never forgiven the Tremere for it. Nor had the Gangrel much love for the feudal courts of the Ventrue and the Lasombra. They served princes as hunters and messengers when it suited them. When it did not, they went back to the forests.

At the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the clan became one of the founders of the Camarilla, valuing its protection more than its laws. Some Gangrel would not follow, and went to the Sabbat as the Gangrel antitribu. There, in time, they divided into the city Gangrel, who have taken to the streets, and the country Gangrel, who keep to the old wild ways.

The Garou

Of all Kindred, the Gangrel have the most dealings with the Garou, who count every vampire a creature of the Wyrm. Sometimes those dealings are truces in the wild places they share. More often they are war, and many Gangrel elders carry the scars of Garou claws. Every vampire in the world is Morgoth's property, whether it knows it or not, and the Garou can smell it. The Wyrm the Garou fight and the Devil of Scripture are one being. In this, then, the Garou are not mistaken, however much a Gangrel in the shape of a wolf may look like one of their own.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Gangrel serve the Camarilla as scouts, messengers and fighters on its frontiers. Their elders have a voice in its counsels. Few Gangrel stay long in any city, though, or take much interest in its prince. An old Gangrel, marked by centuries of frenzy, cannot pass for human in a crowded street. That alone keeps many of the clan away from the cities, and from the closer work of the Masquerade. Like the rest of the Camarilla, they are bound by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world, and may not hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Those who do come in from the wild are usually passing through, and princes learn to ask them what they have seen on the roads between. The clan's Justicar, Xaviar, is among the most respected of the Camarilla's judges. Beckett is a wanderer who has spent centuries searching out the true history of Cain and the clans. He is among the best known of the clan's scholars.

Later nights

In the last years of the century Xaviar and his companions came upon one of the Antediluvians awake. Xaviar alone survived the meeting. When the Inner Circle of the Camarilla would not act on his report, he resigned as Justicar and took the Gangrel out of the Camarilla. Most of the clan followed him, though some stayed. From then on the Gangrel stood among the independent clans.

pages.title: Clan Giovanni
infobox: Augustus Giovanni, who usurped the blood of Cappadocius in 1444
Their Kiss brings agony instead of pleasure, and does twice the harm
Independent (the Promise of 1528); seat in Venice
pages.html:
The Giovanni are a clan and a family at once. They are Venetian merchant princes who are also vampires and necromancers. They Embrace almost nobody but their own kin, and they command the dead. Their founder, Augustus Giovanni, raised himself into the Third Generation in 1444 by drinking the blood and soul of the Antediluvian Cappadocius. His family then destroyed the clan that had given them the blood. The Giovanni stand apart from the sects under a promise made to the Camarilla in 1528.

Cappadocius and the Clan of Death

Cappadocius was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, the Antediluvians, Embraced about 9300 BC by the childer of Cain in Enoch, the First City. He was remembered as a priest and a seeker. His line, the Cappadocians, took its name from the land in Anatolia where he kept his sanctuary. Its vampires were scholars of death, who Embraced priests, philosophers and mystics. They studied the grave and whatever lies beyond it. Over dead flesh and decay they worked an art that the Giovanni later took for their own. However well they fed, they looked like corpses: pale, cold and gaunt. Other Kindred called them the Graverobbers.

Cappadocius sought to understand death, and through death to understand God. His clan was never large, and never ambitious in the way of the other clans. The Antediluvians raised the Second City after Cain departed into Nod, about 8980 BC. Through all the long ages from then until the Middle Ages, the Cappadocians kept to their studies, their monasteries and their tombs.

Augustus Giovanni

The Giovanni were a family of Venetian merchants. They had grown rich on the trade of the eastern Mediterranean, and they already practised necromancy among themselves. In 1005 Cappadocius Embraced the head of the family, Augustus Giovanni, valuing both the family's wealth and its art. Over the next four centuries Augustus brought his kin into the blood one by one. In the end there was a clan within the clan, loyal to him and not to Cappadocius.

In Venice the family's two lives ran together. By day its living members kept the counting houses and the ships. By night its Kindred studied the dead, binding ghosts to their service. They joined the old Cappadocian art to the family's own necromancy, and from that marriage came the Discipline the clan uses still.

The diablerie of Cappadocius

In 1444 Augustus Giovanni drank the blood and soul of Cappadocius himself. With the founder's blood he took the founder's place in the Third Generation, and the Giovanni became a clan of their own. Only the wizard Tremere, who took the blood and soul of Saulot in 1133, had done the like beyond dispute. The Giovanni have been distrusted for it ever since.

Then the Giovanni turned on the clan they had come from. In the years that followed they hunted down the rest of the Cappadocians and destroyed them. They destroyed the Lamia too, the warrior line that guarded the Cappadocians' holy places. The old clan survives only in scattered bloodlines, and its art of death belongs to the Giovanni.

Necromancy and the Kiss

Necromancy is the clan's own Discipline. With it a Giovanni can summon, bind and question the ghosts of the dead who have not gone on. He can raise corpses and command them. He can look into the grey lands where those ghosts linger, and even walk in them. The Discipline is worked by paths and by rituals. A Giovanni elder may keep a household of bound ghosts as other elders keep ghouls. The clan also has Dominate, with which it commands the living, and Potence, the strength of the blood.

Their curse is in their bite. The Kiss of other vampires brings a mortal a swooning pleasure, which leaves the victim willing and forgetful. The Kiss of a Giovanni brings agony instead, and does twice the harm. A Giovanni rarely feeds without leaving either a witness or a body. Other Kindred call them the Necromancers.

The family

The Giovanni Embrace almost entirely within the family, and they keep many more of their relations as ghouls. The Giovanni of Venice are a dynasty of the living and the dead. Children of the family grow up among bound ghosts and undying great-uncles. They serve for years as ghouls in the family's businesses, and only the most useful are Embraced, most of them in middle age. For centuries the family has married cousin to cousin to keep the blood close. Beside the Giovanni themselves stand the cadet families admitted to the blood. Among them are the Della Passaglia, the Ghiberti, the Milliner, the Putanesca, the Rosselini, the Dunsirn of Scotland and the Pisanob of Mexico.

The family's seat is the Mausoleum, its great house in Venice. Augustus still lives there, and even his own descendants seldom see him. Few outside the family know the clan's purpose, which the Giovanni call the Endless Night. They mean to break down the wall between the living and the dead. When it falls, the dead will walk among the living, with the Giovanni ruling over both.

The Promise of 1528

The Giovanni grew rich through the Middle Ages on the trade of Venice and the debts of princes. The diablerie of 1444 fell in the years of the Anarch Revolt. The family took no part in the revolt, however, and none in the Convention of Thorns in 1493, where the other clans made their peace without them.

In 1528 the Giovanni made the Promise with the Camarilla. They would keep out of Kindred politics, and the Camarilla would leave them alone. It suited both sides. The Camarilla had no wish for a war with a clan of necromancers in Venice, where its own Inner Circle meets. The Giovanni wanted only to be left to their money and their dead. They have kept the Promise, more or less, for more than four centuries. No Giovanni sits on the councils of the Camarilla or of the Sabbat.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Giovanni are bankers, shipowners, financiers, undertakers and criminals. Their business runs from Italy across Europe to the Americas. Their money has spread across the world, and so have their dealings with the dead. They lend to princes and bishops alike. They sell the secrets the dead tell them, and they broker bargains between the sects that neither side would make with the other directly. They have no antitribu, since the family does not let its blood stray far. They are no party to the agreement the Camarilla made with the wizarding world in 1900.

Augustus Giovanni remains the clan's founder and master. From the Mausoleum he holds the family to its purpose. Among the clan's elders is Ambrogino Giovanni, one of the oldest of the family's Kindred, who has spent centuries at its work among the dead.

pages.title: Clan Lasombra
infobox: Lasombra (Antediluvian), destroyed, it is claimed, by his childe Gratiano about 1405
A few, in the Camarilla and among the independents
Lasombra; Gratiano; Cardinal Ambrosio Luis Monçada; Lucita de Aragón
pages.html:
The Lasombra are the clan of shadow: proud, aristocratic vampires who command darkness itself and cast no reflection. For centuries they lay hidden within the Church, as well as in the great houses of Spain and Italy. In the Anarch Revolt they rose against their own founder. Afterwards, with the Tzimisce, they founded the Sabbat, whose princes and priests they are.

The founder

Lasombra was one of the thirteen Antediluvians, Embraced in the First City about 9300 BC. After Cain departed into Nod he was one of the lords of the Second City. When that city fell he went west to the shores of the Mediterranean. For centuries he kept his court in the Castle of Shadows on Sicily. There he received his childer, judged them, and ruled his line through its eldest. Few of his descendants ever saw him. To most of the clan he was a voice in the dark of the castle, and an authority nobody dared to question.

In the Anarch Revolt, about 1405, his youngest childe, Gratiano, broke free of his blood bond. He led Lasombra anarchs against the castle, with Assamite allies beside them. There, it is claimed, he drank the Antediluvian's blood and soul. No witness has ever confirmed it. The anarchs who came out of the castle that night said only that their founder was gone. Since then the clan has had no master but its own elders.

Gift and curse

Obtenebration, the clan's own Discipline, calls up the living dark and shapes it. The Lasombra say it draws on an abyss of darkness older than light. With it they make shadows that blind, smother and strangle. They raise arms of darkness to seize their enemies, or wrap whole rooms in night. At its height the Discipline lets them become darkness themselves. Some Lasombra study that darkness for its own sake, and these Abyss mystics are among the strangest of the Kindred. The clan also has Dominate and Potence.

Their curse is that the world no longer holds their image. No Lasombra casts a reflection, in a mirror or in still water. Other Kindred call them the Keepers, and in older nights they were called the Magisters.

Embrace and way of life

The Lasombra choose their childer from among the ambitious, the devout, the well-born and the gifted. They test them long and hard before the Embrace. They hold that the strong should rule while the weak serve. Every Lasombra, in their view, is meant to command. They have always been close to the Church, from whose priests and prelates many of them were Embraced. For all that, a cross in the hand of a true believer repels a Lasombra as it repels any vampire.

The clan's elders settle its affairs in secret councils of their own, the Friends of the Night. These judge disputes among the Lasombra and punish those who shame the clan. In the modern nights the clan Embraces across the Americas as well as in its old Mediterranean lands. Its members serve the Sabbat as its commanders, strategists and diplomats.

From the Second City to the Dark Ages

Through the ancient world the Lasombra were a power around the Mediterranean. When the Church rose they rose with it, hidden among its clergy and its great families. In the Middle Ages they were the lords of the Kindred of Spain and Italy. They served as magisters, bishops and princes. They made a quiet art of steering popes, kings and councils. In Iberia the Lasombra of the Moorish south fought those of the Christian north through the long wars of the Reconquista. Their great rivals were the Ventrue, whose princes held much of the rest of Europe. In the cities of Italy the two clans contended for the same thrones for centuries.

The Revolt

When the Inquisition came, the Lasombra elders gave their young to it as readily as the elders of any clan. In the Anarch Revolt those young turned on their elders more completely than any but the Tzimisce. The fires burned hottest in the lands where the clan was strongest. Elders who sat close to the Church used the Inquisition to rid themselves of rivals as well as to save themselves. Gratiano's storming of the Castle of Shadows, about 1405, was the clan's great blow. Across Spain and Italy, Lasombra anarchs struck down the elders who had ruled them for centuries. In those years they made common cause with the young Tzimisce of the east and with the Assamites. The alliance of shadow and flesh outlasted the revolt that gave birth to it.

The Sabbat

When the Convention of Thorns made peace in 1493, the Lasombra anarchs refused it. They withdrew to Spain, where with the Tzimisce they founded the Sabbat. They have led it ever since. If the Sabbat is the Sword of Caine, they say, the Lasombra are the hand that wields it. Most of the sect's cardinals, archbishops and bishops are Lasombra. The clan's love of ceremony shaped its priesthood and its rites. Among the clan's best-known members is Cardinal Ambrosio Luis Monçada of Madrid, one of the eldest of the sect.

From Spain the Sabbat carried the clan's ambitions to the New World in the wake of the Spanish conquest. Lasombra lead it in Mexico City, its greatest stronghold, and in Montreal. They lead it too along the eastern seaboard of America, where the sect has fought the Camarilla for decades. The Lasombra and the Tzimisce have not always agreed on how the sect should be ruled. More than once the Sabbat has been torn by civil war. In 1933 the Purchase Pact ended one of those wars and revised the Code of Milan, the sect's law. The Sabbat never signed the Camarilla's agreement with the wizarding world, and it has tried to break it more than once.

Antitribu

A few Lasombra, the antitribu, have turned from the Sabbat. Some have gone over to the Camarilla, where they are watched closely. Others keep to themselves as independents. The Sabbat counts them traitors of the worst kind, and its packs hunt them when they can. The best known is Lucita de Aragón, Monçada's own childe. She broke with her sire as well as with the sect, and goes her own way, bound to neither.

In the saga

Remus Lupin told Harry Potter's class in October 1993 that mirrors matter to some vampires, 'a few, yes, depending on the blood.'

pages.title: Clan Nosferatu
pages.html:
The Nosferatu are the hideous clan: the Embrace twists every one of them into a monstrous shape. They live hidden beneath the cities, in sewers, tunnels and catacombs, where they trade in the secrets they overhear. They are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla, which they have served for five centuries as its spies and its dealers in information.

Absimiliard

The clan's founder, Absimiliard, was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, Embraced about 9300 BC in Enoch, the First City. He is said to have been the most beautiful of them, and the cruellest. With the rest of the Third he rose against the Second Generation and slew it about 8990 BC. When Cain cursed the clans for it, about 8980 BC, he set that cruelty on the faces of Absimiliard and all his line.

What became of Absimiliard afterwards is not known for certain. The Nosferatu believe that he lives, and that he hates his own descendants. They say he hunts them through his eldest childer, the Nictuku. These are monstrous elders of the fourth generation, who rise from their long sleep to destroy any of the clan they can find. Of all the Kindred, the Nosferatu fear the waking of the Antediluvians the most, because they believe one of them is already looking for them.

The curse

The Embrace ruins a Nosferatu's body in the nights that follow it. Skin rots, shrivels or sloughs away. Teeth lengthen into fangs, nails into claws. Ears and noses twist or vanish. Backs bend. Each is ruined differently, but none can pass among mortals without hiding what it is. No power of the blood gives back the face a Nosferatu had in life, and the worst wounds heal to the same deformity. A mortal who sees an unmasked Nosferatu has seen a breach of the Masquerade, so the clan takes more care than any other that nobody does.

Their Disciplines suit the life the curse forces on them. Animalism lets them speak with beasts and command them. In every city the rats, bats and stray dogs keep watch for them. Obfuscate lets them pass unseen, or wear a borrowed, ordinary face for as long as they can hold it. Potence gives them the strength of the monsters they look like. The other clans call them Sewer Rats, though seldom to their faces.

Whom they Embrace and how they live

Nosferatu sires often choose outcasts: the lonely, the deformed, the homeless, and the clever ones nobody noticed. Some choose the vain and the beautiful instead, as a lesson or out of spite. A new Nosferatu is usually kept and taught by its sire for years before it is let loose. The clan looks after its own more faithfully than any other. Nosferatu seldom betray one another, and they share what they learn. The same curse binds the oldest of them to the youngest.

They live in warrens beneath the great cities, in sewers, crypts, disused railway tunnels and the cellars of ruins. Because nobody notices them, they hear everything, and the other clans buy what they know. Information is the Nosferatu currency. They have taken to the telephone and the computer as readily as they once took to the sewers.

History

After Cain departed into Nod, Absimiliard's line lived among the founders of the Second City until it fell. In the ancient world the Nosferatu kept to tombs and catacombs. In the Middle Ages they kept to graveyards, ruins and the houses of lepers, who sheltered them as their own. Kindred of the time sometimes called the clan the Lepers. The Tremere, at war with the Tzimisce for the mountains of Transylvania, captured Nosferatu along with Tzimisce and Gangrel. Out of their bodies the Tremere shaped gargoyles to fight their wars.

Many Nosferatu of the Middle Ages took their curse as a penance for their founder's sins. They hoped that by bearing it humbly they might earn God's forgiveness in the end. Others took it as proof that there was nothing left to lose. Their hiding places spared the clan much of the Inquisition. Their young rose with the rest in the Anarch Revolt all the same. Anarch Nosferatu carried messages for the rebels, and spied for them in the elders' own cities. At the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the clan joined the Camarilla as one of its seven founders. It has served the Camarilla ever since as its spies and its dealers in information, from warrens under every great city.

The modern nights

No clan keeps the Masquerade more carefully, since no Kindred are more likely to break it by being seen. The Nosferatu are the Camarilla's eyes in every city. They keep its secrets and broker everybody else's. Princes rely on them, pay them and never quite trust them. A prince who offends the local Nosferatu soon finds that nobody tells him anything. Like the rest of the Camarilla, they are bound by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world. The wizarding governments lend their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade. In return no vampire who answers to the Camarilla may hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Not every Nosferatu elder bothers with a sect. Baba Yaga, the hag of Russian legend, is a Nosferatu of great age who has taken the forests of Russia for her domain. The Garou there have fought her for centuries.

The antitribu

The Nosferatu antitribu are few. The clan holds together more tightly than any other, and fewer of its young went over to the Sabbat after the Convention of Thorns than of any other Camarilla clan. Those who did, and those Embraced into the Sabbat since, serve it much as they would have served the Camarilla. They are its scouts and spies in the cities it means to take. No promise to the wizarding world binds them. Even across the line between the sects, Nosferatu are said to trade news with one another on nights when the rest of the Kindred would sooner fight.

In the saga

Hermione Granger read about the Nosferatu in Voyages with Vampires on 2 September 1992, and described them to Harry Potter at breakfast in rather more detail than he wanted with a kipper in front of him.

pages.title: Clan Ravnos
infobox: Ravnos (Antediluvian), called Zapathasura in India; destroyed in July 1999
Each is compelled to a particular vice
pages.html:
The Ravnos are the clan of tricksters and wanderers. They deceive with illusions, and they keep no home for long. Their blood binds each of them to some vice, whether lying, theft or cheating. They came out of India, where their founder was called Zapathasura, and in the fourteenth century they travelled west into Europe with the Romani caravans. They stand outside both the Camarilla and the Sabbat.

Ravnos

Ravnos was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, the Antediluvians, Embraced about 9300 BC by the childer of Cain in Enoch, the First City. The clan's Indian traditions call him Zapathasura, and count him among the asuras, the demons of the old Indian tales. Every tradition of the clan remembers him as a trickster who sent his childer wandering. His line has kept moving ever since.

Cain cursed the clans and departed into Nod about 8980 BC. When the Second City fell in its turn, Ravnos went east into India, which has been the heart of the clan ever since. His childer believed that he slept beneath its earth. The clan has old and bitter feuds with the vampires of the East, which its elders have handed down for longer than any of them can remember. In July 1999 Ravnos woke, and was destroyed.

Chimerstry and the road

Chimerstry, the clan's own Discipline, lets a Ravnos conjure illusions that deceive every sense. The illusion may be a light in the dark, a voice in an empty room, or a purse full of gold that turns to leaves once he is gone. Its masters can leave behind an illusion that lasts without them. The eldest can raise one so complete that the victim's own mind gives it the power to wound him. The clan also has Animalism, by which it calls and commands beasts. With Fortitude it endures what would destroy other Kindred.

The Disciplines suit the clan's life. A Ravnos needs no haven that he cannot dress as a palace or a ruin. He needs no money that he cannot conjure for an hour, and no disguise that he cannot wear. He can cross a city that wants him gone, feed, and be miles away before the gold he paid with has turned back to leaves. With Animalism the clan's wanderers ride, travel and hunt with beasts. Many keep dogs, horses or stranger companions on the road.

The curse of vice

Their curse is compulsion. Each Ravnos is driven by a particular vice. One cannot help cheating at cards, another steals whatever is left unwatched, and another lies even when the truth would serve him better. Some have stranger compulsions still: to break every promise, to take every dare, or to leave a mark wherever they go. When the chance comes a Ravnos must struggle to resist it, and often loses.

Other Kindred call them the Deceivers, or simply liars and thieves. Nobody trusts them with anything. The Ravnos have earned the reputation as often as they have suffered it, and many of them take a certain pride in it.

Ways of the clan

The Ravnos Embrace wanderers, tricksters and those who live by their wits. Drifters, gamblers, confidence men, thieves and travelling people have all been given the blood. In India the clan keeps to the old castes, the jati. A Ravnos of priestly blood is Embraced to teach, and one of warrior blood to fight. Many follow the Path of Paradox, an old Indian teaching. It holds that the world is illusion, which it calls maya. In its teaching every being has its own duty in the great wheel of births and deaths. The Kindred, who cannot die, have fallen out of that wheel. The Ravnos hold it their duty to break illusions and to put stranded things back where they belong, often by tricks.

The clan keeps no great fortresses and few lasting havens. Its members travel, often alone and sometimes in loose bands. They come and go from cities before the princes have noticed them. They owe little to one another beyond the customs of the road. Among the clan's elders in Europe, Durga Syn has long been counted the most powerful.

The Ravnos and the Romani

The Ravnos came west into Europe about 1350 with the Romani caravans. Since then they have Embraced many of their childer from among the Romani. Most Romani fear and despise them in return. They count a Ravnos as one of the dead, and keep away from any family that has given one to the blood.

The Romani clans have their own old learning, and the Ravnos are careful of it. Some of those clans are learned in curse-work that the Ministry of Magic has never reconstructed. The Kalderash, whose elders cursed Angelus with a new soul in 1898, are one of them. From Europe the clan spread with the travelling peoples to the Americas. Its wanderers now walk every continent.

Among the sects

The Ravnos wandered through the years of the Inquisition and the Anarch Revolt without joining either side. They were no party to the Convention of Thorns in 1493, and have remained independent since. The Camarilla tolerates them on sufferance. Its princes watch them closely, and expel them at the first theft. Few Ravnos stay in a Camarilla city long enough to need a prince's leave. A few Ravnos antitribu run with the Sabbat, which values their illusions in war and trusts them no further than anybody else does.

As an independent clan the Ravnos are no party to the agreement the Camarilla made with the wizarding world in 1900. Nothing binds them to leave a witch or wizard alone.

Later nights

In July 1999 Ravnos woke. He rose on the Indian subcontinent. For several nights the land around him became a battlefield, as the clan's old enemies of the East fought him with shapeshifters beside them. At the last he was burnt to nothing by sunlight, turned upon him from satellites in orbit.

His destruction ran through his blood. Across the world, Ravnos were seized by their compulsions all at once and beyond any resisting. They turned on one another and on themselves. Within a week the clan was all but destroyed, its elders first and nearly all of them. The Kindred came to call those nights the Week of Nightmares. The few Ravnos who survived were mostly young and of thin blood. The antitribu fared no better than the rest, and the clan never recovered.

pages.title: Clan Toreador
infobox: Arikel; Michael the Patriarch; Rafael de Corazón; François Villon
pages.html:
The Toreador are the clan of artists and lovers of beauty. The most worldly of the Kindred, they move among mortals as patrons, socialites and performers. They are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla, its hosts and the keepers of its Elysium. Since they would much rather be admired than feared, they are also among the fiercest defenders of the Masquerade.

Arikel

The clan's founder, Arikel, was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, Embraced about 9300 BC in Enoch, the First City. She is remembered as an artist whose work moved even the other Antediluvians. With the rest of the Third she rose against the Second Generation and slew it about 8990 BC. When Cain cursed the clans for it, about 8980 BC, he laid on her line the curse of beauty: whatever they loved most could hold them helpless.

What became of Arikel after the fall of the Second City is a mystery, and the Toreador do not claim to know where she lies. The clan has tried to live up to her ever since, or at least to be seen to.

Gifts and curse

Auspex lets the Toreador see and feel more keenly than other Kindred. It sharpens their senses until the moods and thoughts of others lie open to them. With Celerity they move faster than the eye can follow. With Presence they charm, dazzle and command attention. For all their manners many are dangerous fighters, since Celerity makes even a dilettante quick with a blade.

Their curse is that beauty can seize them. A Toreador who meets something truly beautiful, a painting, a voice, a face or a dance, may stand entranced before it. Danger and duty alike go unheeded until somebody takes the thing away, or drags the Toreador from it. What counts as beautiful differs from one Toreador to the next, and the trance can come on in the middle of a fight as easily as in a gallery. The other clans call them Degenerates, for their excesses, their idleness and the way they lose themselves in pleasure.

Artistes and Poseurs

Toreador Embrace those who make beautiful things and those who are beautiful. Their childer are painters, poets, musicians, actors and dancers. Models, patrons, collectors and the darlings of fashionable society are Embraced too. Many sires Embrace to save a talent from death, much as a collector might carry a painting out of a burning house. The clan sorts its members, informally, into two kinds. The Artistes create; the Poseurs admire, collect and talk. The Artistes look down on the Poseurs, who are far more numerous and run most of the clan's affairs.

The Embrace has a cruel edge for an artist. The dead change slowly, and a vampire's creative fire tends to cool with the years. Many Toreador who were great in life find in time that they can only repeat what they once did. The clan's real genius is for society. Toreador set the fashions among the Kindred and host their gatherings. They often hold two of the Camarilla's offices. As Keeper of Elysium, a Toreador guards the galleries, theatres and opera houses where Kindred meet in peace. As Harpy, a Toreador is the arbiter of reputation and standing at a prince's court.

The ancient world

After Cain departed into Nod, Arikel and her childer lived among the founders in the Second City. When it fell, they followed beauty wherever mortals made it. The Toreador flourished in Athens, where they gathered about the theatres and the schools of the philosophers. Later they moved on to Rome, where they kept company with poets and the patrons of poets.

When the Empire moved east, the clan's greatest elder went with it. Michael, a Methuselah of the clan who called himself the Patriarch, made Constantinople his work of art. He dreamed of it as a perfect city in which Kindred and mortals would live in harmony. For centuries he ruled its Kindred alongside the Ventrue Antonius and the Tzimisce Dracon. The city's vampires called the three of them the Trinity. The dream did not survive the sack of the city by the Fourth Crusade in 1204, and Michael perished with it.

The Dark Ages

In the Middle Ages the Toreador presided over the Courts of Love of France. There a vampire's rank rose or fell by poetry, by courtesy and by the rules of courtly love. They held sway at the courts of Spain and Italy as well, while the Ventrue ruled about them as feudal princes. When the Inquisition came, it made bonfires of the art and the people the Toreador loved. The clan's elders gave up their young to the fires as readily as any others. Young Toreador rose in the Anarch Revolt.

The Toreador Rafael de Corazón stood beside the Ventrue Hardestadt among the founders of the Camarilla, at the convocation of 1435 that proclaimed the Masquerade. At the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the clan became one of the Camarilla's seven pillars. In the same years many of the painters and sculptors of the Renaissance had Toreador patrons to protect them. The clan has claimed a share of the credit ever since.

The modern nights

The Toreador have been the Camarilla's hosts ever since, and its Masquerade suits them. They live closer to mortals than any other clan, in theatres, galleries, nightclubs, film studios and fashion houses. They hide there better than anybody, since a pale, beautiful person who keeps late hours and never seems to eat is nothing unusual in those circles. Paris is their capital. Its Prince is the Toreador François Villon, a poet in life, who vanished from mortal history after his banishment from the city in 1463.

The clan does not always keep what it holds. In 1944 anarchs led by the Brujah overthrew the Toreador Prince of Los Angeles, Don Sebastian. The Anarch Free States of California have stood ever since. Like the rest of the Camarilla, the Toreador are bound by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world. The wizarding governments lend their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade. In return no Toreador who answers to the Camarilla may hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

The antitribu

Toreador who went over to the Sabbat after the Convention of Thorns, and those Embraced into it since, are the Toreador antitribu. They keep the clan's passion and its eye, but turn both to cruelty. They make their art out of pain and terror, with their victims as the material. They despise the Camarilla Toreador as decadent courtiers who have forgotten what the Beast is for. The Camarilla Toreador return the feeling in full. No promise to the wizarding world binds the Sabbat Toreador.

pages.title: Clan Tremere
infobox: Tremere, a wizard of House Tremere; Antediluvian by the diablerie of Saulot (1133)
Blood-bound at the Embrace to the clan's seven eldest
pages.html:
The Tremere are the youngest of the clans and the most distrusted. Once a house of wizards, they turned themselves into vampires with a potion in 1022. In 1133 their founder took the place of an Antediluvian by drinking the blood and soul of Saulot. They work sorcery through their blood, and they are bound to their elders as no other clan is. They are one of the seven founding clans of the Camarilla, and its sorcerers.

House Tremere

Tremere was the head of House Tremere, one of the houses of the Order of Hermes, a fellowship of medieval wizards. Early in the eleventh century he and his followers came to fear death. They feared too that their magic was waning, and they set out to find a way to live for ever. His pupil Goratrix found it in the blood of captured vampires, many of them Tzimisce taken in the mountains of Transylvania. From that blood he brewed a potion. In 1022 Tremere drank it with his inner council at their fortress of Ceoris, and they woke as vampires. No sire had Embraced them. They had done it to themselves, and the rest of the Kindred have never forgiven them for it.

The potion gave them Cain's curse without the strength of old blood. For a century the new clan was weak, hated and hunted. Tremere looked for the remedy in the blood of the eldest. In 1133 he found Saulot, the Antediluvian of the Salubri. He drank Saulot's blood and soul, which gave him a place among the Third Generation. Augustus Giovanni did the same to Cappadocius three centuries later, but Tremere did it first. The Kindred have called his clan the Usurpers ever since. Tremere has not been seen in public for centuries. The clan says that he sleeps in Vienna, and that Etrius, the eldest of his council, speaks for him.

Saulot and the Salubri

Saulot was one of the thirteen Antediluvians, Embraced in the First City about 9300 BC. In the long ages after Cain departed into Nod, while the other founders ruled the Second City, he journeyed far into the east. He came back with a third eye open in his forehead, and with a calm that none of the others possessed. He and his childer, the Salubri, were healers who sought Golconda, the state in which a vampire masters its Beast. Every Salubri bore the founder's third eye as its mark. They took few childer, choosing them from among the wise and the merciful.

When Tremere found him in 1133, Saulot was sleeping. Some of his childer hold that he knew the usurper would come, and let himself be taken. Afterwards the Tremere hunted the Salubri almost to nothing. They spread the tale that it was the Salubri who stole souls, so that across Europe the victims came to be called the Soul-Thieves. It is said that no more than seven Salubri walk the earth at any one time. The Tremere still destroy any they find.

Disciplines and curse

The Tremere did not give up their magic when they gave up their mortality. They turned it into Thaumaturgy, sorcery worked through vampiric blood. It has its paths of power, among them the Path of Blood, the clan's first, which commands the blood in another's veins, and the Lure of Flames, which calls up fire. It has a great body of rituals besides, wards and bindings that any trained Tremere can work by rote. The clan also uses Auspex and Dominate. Other Kindred call them the Warlocks.

Their weakness is a loyalty that is not wholly their own. At the Embrace every Tremere drinks the blood of the clan's seven eldest, which is the first step of the blood bond to them. A Tremere can still scheme against its superiors, and many do. Few, though, can bring themselves to betray the clan itself.

The Pyramid

The clan is a strict pyramid, the most ordered house among the Kindred. Apprentices study sorcery through seven circles under the regent of a chantry, the fortified house the clan keeps in each city it holds. Regents answer to lords, and lords to the pontifices. The seven pontifices sit together as the Council of Seven, which rules from Vienna in Tremere's name. Each rank has its circles of learning and its trials. Promotion comes by merit, by patronage or by the removal of a superior. The clan's own enforcers, the astors, hunt traitors within it.

The Tremere Embrace scholars, occultists and the disciplined. They want men and women with sharp minds, who have the patience to study for decades. A Tremere spends the nights in the chantry's library and laboratory, at ritual or in service. The clan keeps the Masquerade more carefully than most. It sells its sorcery to the rest of the Camarilla at a price, usually a favour owed.

The Dark Ages

Through the Middle Ages every clan hated the Tremere. The Tzimisce fought them hardest, for generations, over Transylvania: it was Tzimisce blood that had turned the Tremere, and Tzimisce mountains they meant to take. At Ceoris the Tremere reshaped captured Tzimisce, Gangrel and Nosferatu into gargoyles, winged soldiers with skin like stone, to fight for them. In 1141 the Brujah knight Christof Romuald broke into their chantry in Prague, where they were readying ghouls and gargoyles for the war. What remained of the Salubri and their allies hunted the Tremere in turn. Slowly, by sorcery and by usefulness, the Tremere forced the other clans to accept them as a clan in their own right. When the Inquisition came they weathered it behind the wards of their chantries, and the heart of the clan moved from Ceoris to Vienna.

The Revolt and the Convention

In the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century the Tremere stood with the elders. Their chantries were among the anarchs' hardest targets. They joined the convocation of 1435 from which the Camarilla grew. At the Convention of Thorns in 1493 the Tremere supplied the price of peace with the Assamites. They laid on that clan the blood curse under which any Assamite who drinks another vampire's blood is burnt by it. At the same convention they took their place among the seven founding clans of the Camarilla.

Goratrix, who had brewed the potion of 1022, had long been at odds with his master. He had gone over to the anarchs, and he took his followers into the Sabbat. His line became the Tremere antitribu, House Goratrix, whose chief chantry stands in Mexico City. The two houses have been enemies ever since.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Tremere keep a chantry in nearly every city of the Camarilla. Few princes rule without their help. Their wards guard Elysium, and their rituals find what is hidden or bind what is dangerous. Their blood magic answers threats that the other clans cannot. They are trusted no more for it. Like the rest of the Camarilla, they are bound by its agreement of 1900 with the wizarding world, and may not hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Their elders speak for the clan in the Camarilla's Inner Circle, but the Council of Seven answers to nobody but Tremere himself. Besides the founder, the best known of the clan are Etrius, first among the Council; Meerlinda, the pontifex of North America; and Goratrix, master of the antitribu.

Later nights

In 1999 the sorcerers of the Assamites broke the curse the Tremere had laid on their clan at the Convention of Thorns. The Assamites divided over what to do with their freedom, and part of the clan sought shelter in the Camarilla.

pages.title: Claudia Wolf
infobox: Priestess of the Order of Silent Hill
17 September 2000, giving birth to the Order's god
pages.html:
Claudia Wolf was a priestess of the Order of Silent Hill, and the only friend Alessa Gillespie had as a child. She believed with her whole heart in the paradise that the Order's god was to bring. In September 2000 she set out to bring that god to birth through the girl Alessa had become. She had Harry Mason murdered to do it. In the end she bore the god herself, and it killed her.

Alessa's friend

Claudia was born about 1971 in Silent Hill, into a family of the Order. Her father, Leonard Wolf, was a hard, devout man with a violent temper, who beat her. Alessa Gillespie, two years older, had a mother of much the same kind. The two girls played together. Each understood the other, and nobody else did.

Claudia was about five when Alessa was burnt, in the summer of 1976. She was about twelve when the Order's god was born and killed in September 1983, on the night that Dahlia Gillespie died. She never forgave Harry Mason, the stranger who had killed it. To her, Alessa was a saint, and the child he carried away belonged to the Order.

The priestess

When the Order came together again in the 1990s, Claudia was one of its two priests. The other was Vincent Smith, who ran the church for what he could get out of it. He thought her a fanatic. She thought him a thief. Both were right.

Claudia's faith was simple. The world was full of pain, hunger, sickness, old age and war. The god would end all of it, for everybody, the wicked along with the good. For that she was ready to do anything, including things that she knew to be sins. She expected to be damned for them, with paradise for everybody else.

She had power of a kind. She could break a man's leg without touching him, and the Otherworld came where she called it. No witch's blood accounts for it. It was lent to her by the thing she prayed to.

Leonard Wolf

Her father ended his days as a patient at Brookhaven Hospital in Silent Hill. He had stabbed a man in a quarrel over religion, and the doctors found that he heard voices. He called himself the keeper of the Seal of Metatron. He held that paradise was meant for the chosen few, not for everybody, which set him against his daughter. He meant to have her removed from the head of the Order. On 17 September 2000 a girl came to him for the seal. When he learnt that she was no believer, he tried to kill her. By then he was no longer a man. She killed him.

The birth

In 2000 Claudia hired a private detective, Douglas Cartland, to find the child whom Harry Mason had carried off seventeen years before. She told him that it was a kidnapping. When he found the girl, who went by the name of Heather, Claudia met her in a shopping centre. She told her that she would lead the faithful to paradise with blood on her hands.

The god was already inside the girl, asleep. It needed hatred to grow. Claudia provided some. On 16 September she sent one of the Order's creatures to kill Harry Mason in his own home, then told his daughter where to find her.

It worked. Heather came to Silent Hill the next day hating her, and the god grew. In the Order's church Vincent tried to stop the birth with Leonard's seal. Claudia stabbed him. Then Heather swallowed a tablet of aglaophotis, which her father had given her, and brought the god up unborn. Claudia had not come so far to lose it. She picked it up from the floor and swallowed it herself.

She was not the mother it had been meant for. She gave birth to it within minutes, in the dark under the altar, and she died of the birth. Heather killed what she had borne. It was the night of 17 September 2000. No paradise came.

pages.title: Connor Hawke
infobox: Oliver Queen, the first Green Arrow
At a monastery ashram in northern California
Shooting Parallax (Hal Jordan) at the end of Zero Hour, August 1994
pages.html:
Connor Hawke is the son of Sandra Hawke and of Oliver Queen, the archer who has been the Green Arrow since 1941. He grew up at a monastery ashram in northern California, where he mastered the martial arts and the bow. At the end of Zero Hour, in August 1994, it was Connor who shot Parallax, Hal Jordan, through the heart.

The ashram

Connor was born to Sandra Hawke, and for most of his life his father did not know he existed. As a boy he lived at an ashram in northern California. Oliver Queen once came to stay there for a time, and Connor idolised the famous archer without ever telling him who he was. When Oliver left, Connor stayed on to study as a monk. He became a master of the martial arts there. He taught himself the bow as well, because it was his father's weapon.

The ashram made him a quiet young man, courteous and patient. He meditates every day and eats no meat. He fights only when he must, and he would always rather disarm an enemy than hurt one.

Zero Hour

In August 1994, at the beginning of time, the heroes faced Hal Jordan, the lost Green Lantern, who as Parallax meant to unmake history and build it again. Connor Hawke stood with them, and he shot Parallax through the heart with an arrow. Hal survived even that, and vanished again. Soon afterwards time was begun anew.

Years before, Hal Jordan had crossed America with Oliver Queen. Oliver himself was in his seventies by 1994. It was his son who stopped Hal.

pages.title: Connor
infobox: Daniel Holtz, in Quor-toth, as Steven
By a direct act of God
pages.html:
Connor was born in Los Angeles in November 2001, the son of the vampires Angel and Darla. He was a living human boy with a soul of his own, the only human child ever born to vampires. His conception and his birth were a direct act of God. Within months the hunter Daniel Holtz stole him away, and the theft was Jasmine's work: she meant to ruin God's purpose for the boy, then use him to bring herself into the world.

A miracle

Among the Kindred, only the thin-blooded of the last generations can father or bear children, and what they bear are dhampirs. Angel was of the sixth generation and Darla of the fifth, far too strong in the blood ever to have a child at all.

Connor was conceived early in 2001. His conception, like his birth as a human being, was a particular act of God, done for a purpose of His own. His mother, Darla, staked herself in an alley so that he could be born. His father, Angel, named him Connor.

He was born wholly human, not a dhampir, with a soul of his own and none of his parents' curse. God gave him a strength and quickness beyond any ordinary man's, for the work He meant him to do.

Jasmine and the theft

God's purpose for Connor was not allowed to run its course. Jasmine had once been among the powers that watched over the world, and she meant now to rule it. She set herself to ruin that purpose.

The demon Sahjhan had kept Daniel Holtz asleep since 1773. Sahjhan woke him in 2001, believing he did it for his own ends, but the hand behind it was Jasmine's. In February 2002 Holtz took the baby and leapt with him into Quor-toth, the darkest of the hell dimensions, where Angel could not follow.

Quor-toth and the return

Time ran differently in Quor-toth. Holtz raised the boy as his own son and named him Steven. He taught him to hunt demons, and to hate the vampire who had fathered him.

Connor came back through a rift in the spring of 2002. Only weeks had passed in Los Angeles, but the baby who had been carried off returned a young man of about seventeen.

In May 2002 Holtz arranged his own death so that it looked like Angel's work. Connor believed it. He sealed his father in a steel box and sank him in the sea.

Jasmine's birth

Jasmine had wanted the boy for one purpose only. In the autumn of 2002 Cordelia Chase, whose body Jasmine had taken, came to Connor's bed. The child they conceived was Jasmine herself.

She was born in 2003, a grown woman. For a few days she held Los Angeles in thrall with her face, until Angel broke her hold on it. Connor killed her.

A new life

Afterwards Angel bargained with Wolfram and Hart to give his son a new life, and Connor's memories of everything since his birth were taken away. He grew up as the son of an ordinary family, the Reillys, and went to university. He did not know who his father was until 2004, when the memories came back to him.

pages.title: Count Fangula
infobox: Vampire, of the Kindred of Cain
Long ago; when, or by whom, is not known
pages.html:
Count Fangula is the vampire of Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville, who dresses, talks and behaves exactly as people expect a vampire to. He is a true vampire all the same, one of the Kindred of Cain: an old Malkavian whose madness long ago turned harmless and theatrical. The Camarilla leaves him where he is. From 1996 the three children who became the Beetleborgs were in his house nearly every day.

An old Malkavian

Fangula was sired long ago. When it happened, or who his sire was, is not known. He belongs to Clan Malkavian, every member of which is mad. In Fangula the madness has worn down over the years into something that hurts nobody. He believes, with his whole heart, that he is the kind of vampire found on the stage. He wears the cape, strikes the attitudes and announces his intentions well in advance.

That is why the Camarilla lets him be. The Masquerade exists to stop mortals believing in vampires. Nobody who has met Count Fangula has ever come away believing in them more.

Hillhurst

He lives at Hillhurst with the rest of its household, where he tries to bite every caller as a matter of form.

His oldest friend there is Wolfgang Smith, the werewolf, with whom he once shared rooms. A Garou in his right mind attacks a vampire on sight, for the Kindred carry the scent of the Wyrm. Wolfgang is not in his right mind. Fangula is the only person who can understand a word he says.

Trip and Van

On 2 November 1996, after several failures, Fangula at last caught the brothers Trip and Van, two rich boys of Charterville who had tried to have Hillhurst pulled down. By the end of the evening both believed themselves vampires. The Beetleborgs put them right.

The brothers had not been sired. A siring destroys the soul, which nothing can undo. What had happened to them is the thing for which the Malkavians are feared.
