The madness of the clan is catching, so that a mortal who spends long enough with one of them begins to see what the Malkavian sees. Trip and Van had spent an evening with a vampire who thinks he is a stage vampire. For a while they thought the same of themselves.

Vlad and the vampire hunter

In April 1997 a caller who styled himself Vlad, Commissioner of Vampires, came to reproach Fangula for adding nobody to the ranks. He threatened to send him back where he had come from. The Kindred have no such office. The Camarilla, besides, forbids any vampire to sire without a Prince's leave. The likeliest explanation is that Vlad was another Malkavian, since the clan's jokes have been known to run for centuries. A monster of the Magnavores carried him off before the matter was settled.

In May 1997 a boy named Norman Nussbaum, who came of a long line of vampire hunters, tracked Fangula to Hillhurst. He did not get him.

Later years

In September 1997 the ghost of an actress of the silent pictures called on him at Hillhurst, because he had always admired her. That October a cursed ring turned him into a monstrous bat, which the Crustaceans tried to recruit.

In November 1997 he swallowed one of the eight Astral Coins, which made him ill. Horribelle came to his bedside dressed as a nurse, hoping to get it. The Beetleborgs got it first. With it they called up Ladyborg, the last of the Astralborgs.

In February 1998 Flabber lent him the powers of a costumed hero for a while. He used them to help the Beetleborgs, to everybody's surprise, his own included.

pages.title: Courtney Ross
infobox: Banker in the City of London, known there as the Ice Queen
pages.html:
Courtney Ross was Brian Braddock's first love, a rich, clever student he met at Thames University in 1976, who grew up to be one of the sharpest bankers in the City of London. She was the first person Brian ever told that he was Captain Britain. Late in 1988 Sat-yr-9, a tyrant from another world who looked exactly like her, murdered her and took her place. For nearly four years nobody knew.

Brian Braddock

Courtney came of a wealthy family. In the autumn of 1976 she was a student at Thames University, a sharp girl with auburn hair who took an interest in the quiet young physicist Brian Braddock, much to the annoyance of his classmate Jacko Tanner. She did not know that Brian had become Captain Britain. In August 1977, after he saved her from a kidnapper, he told her. They became lovers.

Late in 1977, while she was visiting him in New York, Arcade, an assassin hired by the Maggia, kidnapped them both and set them loose with Spider-Man in his Murderworld. They got out alive. Over the next years Brian vanished from her life, into a Cornish cave, into Otherworld and off the face of the earth. They drifted apart.

The Ice Queen

By 1988 Courtney was a vice-president of Fraser's Bank, known in the City as the Ice Queen. She had stopped dyeing her hair, and it turned out to be the palest blonde, which made her the image of Saturnyne. Brian met her again when he went to the bank to open accounts for the Excalibur team, and for a while they took up where they had left off.

Late in 1988 Arcade carried her off to a new Murderworld to get at Brian. She kept him amused with comedy she made up on the spot until the Excalibur team came for her.

Sat-yr-9

She survived Arcade only to be murdered soon afterwards by Sat-yr-9, the tyrant of Kaptain Briton's Britain, who was Saturnyne's double on that world. Sat-yr-9 took Courtney's name, her face and her place at the bank. She won Courtney's colleague Nigel Frobisher at cards in the Hellfire Club, and he served her after that. She went on seeing Brian for years.

In the summer of 1992 she told him what she had done, drugged him and kept him as her prisoner until the Excalibur team broke him free. Sat-yr-9 escaped. Courtney Ross has been dead since 1988, and in the summer of 1994 her murderer is still at large.

pages.title: Crisis on Infinite Earths
infobox: Supergirl (Kara Zor-El); the Flash (Barry Allen)
pages.html:
The Crisis on Infinite Earths was the catastrophe of 1985 to 1986, in which the skies of the world turned red. The heroes of every nation were drawn into a battle that few of them could afterwards describe. Two of them were killed: Supergirl and the Flash, Barry Allen. It certainly happened. Nobody can remember exactly what happened, however, and the world came out of it unsure of what it had lived through.

What is remembered

Through 1985 the skies over the whole world turned red, sometimes for days at a time. Strange storms came and went, with spells of darkness between them. For a time whole regions seemed to be overlaid by places that did not belong there. People reported seeing figures from other eras in the streets. Heroes and villains alike were drawn into the struggle. Many of them were seen fighting side by side.

Two deaths are certain. Supergirl, Superman's cousin Kara Zor-El, died in 1985 fighting the being held responsible for the catastrophe. Later the same year the Flash, Barry Allen, died destroying a weapon aimed at the world, and was never seen again. When the red skies faded at the turn of 1986, the world was still there, which not everybody had expected.

What is not

Almost everything else about the Crisis is disputed. Those who took part speak of a being called the Monitor who gathered them, of his enemy the Anti-Monitor, and of many worlds that ran into one; most people dismiss all this. Witnesses who stood side by side remember different things. Histories written before 1985 and after it do not quite agree about the lives of some well-known people. Often the people themselves cannot say which version is true.

Afterwards the world was left with an unease it never quite lost. The name Supergirl, in particular, became curiously hard for people to place, as though she had been known for twenty-five years and yet not quite remembered. Within a year Darkseid's agents were turning public fear of costumed heroes into a campaign against them. In 1986 President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994 Harry Potter recalled that the Flash of Dudley's annuals had died in 1985, ‘in a battle nobody had ever properly explained’.

pages.title: Cronus
infobox: Ronac, whom he put to death
Sokar, from the council of the System Lords
A machine made in the likeness of Teal'c
pages.html:
Cronus is one of the Goa'uld System Lords, a hard, cold lord of the old kind, who takes his name from the father of the Titans. He is among the most influential of the System Lords. He banished Sokar from their council, and he put his own First Prime, Ronac, to death, which made Ronac's son Teal'c his enemy for life. In 1999 he came to Earth for the talks that put it under the Protected Planets Treaty, and very nearly died there. In 2001 he was killed on the world of Juna, shot in the back by a machine made in Teal'c's likeness.

Father of the Titans

Cronus takes his name from the Titan whom the Greeks remembered as the father of Zeus, Hera, Poseidon and Hades, the old king who ruled before the gods.

He has been a mortal enemy of Apophis for as long as either of them can remember. He does not forgive failure, as his own First Prime found.

Ronac

Teal'c's father, Ronac, was Cronus's First Prime when Teal'c was a boy. Ronac lost a battle that nobody could have won. Cronus killed him for it, slowly, with his own hands.

Ronac's widow and son were sent away to Chulak in disgrace. There the boy grew up under Bra'tac's teaching to serve Apophis instead, and in time he rose to be Apophis's First Prime. He never forgot who had killed his father.

Sokar

Long ago Cronus joined Ra, Apophis and the other System Lords to bring down Sokar, who had grown too great for their liking. When it was done, it was Cronus who banished Sokar from their council. Sokar survived on his own world, Delmak, and in time he built up his strength again.

The talks on Earth

In 1999 the System Lords resolved to attack Earth, which had been killing Goa'uld since 1997. Asgard warned Earth, and offered to bring the two sides together. The talks were held on Earth, in the base that houses its Stargate. Three System Lords came to them: Cronus, Nirrti and Lord Yu.

Thor himself opened the talks. It is said in Asgard that the System Lords' first demand, a thousand years before, had been that he should not be present. This time they sat at the same table with him, and managed not to mention it. He was soon called away, and the rest was left to the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth.

The System Lords' price for peace was that Earth should give up its Stargate. Before the matter was settled, Cronus was found badly beaten, and so was Teal'c. Since Cronus had killed Teal'c's father, Teal'c was blamed. Yu and Nirrti swore to attack Earth in revenge.

It had been Nirrti. She had made herself invisible with a device for shifting out of phase with the world, and she meant the talks to fail so that she could seize power in the confusion. She said she had tried to heal Cronus with her hand device and failed. Samantha Carter of SG-1 used the device on him herself, and saved his life.

When Nirrti's part came out, Cronus and Yu turned on her. They took her away with them as their prisoner. Earth was put under the treaty after all. The System Lords left with a warning: the Tau'ri were safe on Earth, but anywhere beyond it they were fair game.

Juna

By early 2001 Cronus had taken Juna, a world that had lately been freed from Heru'ur's rule. There he captured three of the machines that a being called Harlan had made in the likeness of SG-1, on the world of Altair. They thought and remembered exactly as the real team did. For some time they had been travelling through the gate on missions of their own.

Cronus had the machine Daniel Jackson beheaded in front of his court, which showed the Goa'uld what they were. He meant to kill the machine Teal'c slowly, as he had killed Ronac. The real SG-1 came to Juna to help, and the machines fought beside them. The machine Teal'c shot Cronus in the back with a staff weapon, and he died.

None of the machines survived the battle. SG-1 freed Juna once more and took Cronus's mothership.

The ship

Cronus's ship did not outlive him long. SG-1 took it to Vorash, where the Tok'ra had their base. There, to destroy Apophis's fleet, SG-1 made Vorash's sun explode, and the blast flung the ship into another galaxy. Apophis took it from SG-1 there. It fell out of the sky on to Delmak, Sokar's old world, with Apophis aboard and the Replicators swarming through it.

pages.title: Crossworld City
infobox: Cross World City; Crossworld City, California; Crossworld
pages.html:
Crossworld City is a town on the west coast of the United States, in California. It is the home of the VR Troopers, as well as of the man they fought without knowing it, the industrialist Karl Ziktor. The way into the world called virtual reality was found here.

The town

Crossworld City is an ordinary Californian town with a university, a power station, a dam and an amusement park. There are woods round it, with a stretch of old forest. Beyond those lie hills, with a quarry among them.

Its mayor is Abner Rooney, a weak man who is ruled at home by his wife. At the town hall he is ruled by Karl Ziktor. Its newspaper is the Underground Voice Daily, edited by Woody Stocker. Its karate school is Tao's Dojo.

Ziktor's town

In the middle of Crossworld City stands the building of Ziktor Industries. Karl Ziktor, who owns the company, is a billionaire, by a long way the richest man in the town. When he wants a forest felled, the mayor seldom finds the courage to refuse him. Nobody in the town knows that he is also Grimlord, the master of virtual reality.

The laboratory

In the hills outside the town is a hidden laboratory. Two scientists of Crossworld City, Tyler Steele and Professor Horatio Hart, built it for their work on virtual reality, which they had found to be a real world lying beside this one. Since about 1984 Professor Hart has lived on there as a mind in its machines. A vault at Crossworld University still holds the two men's early plans.

The Troopers' war, 1994 to 1996

From September 1994 Grimlord's creatures came through the reality barrier into Crossworld City again and again. Three young people of the town met them in armour: Ryan Steele, Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese, the VR Troopers. The town knew the Troopers by sight. It never knew their names.

Grimlord's schemes fell on the town's ordinary life. He tried to blow up the dam. His general, Ivar, tried to freeze its electricity supply. He loosed a sludge from virtual reality in its streets, which Ryan Steele had to find a rare plant to cure. In September 1995 Colonel Icebot set a great electromagnet beside the power station, with a second at the North Pole, in order to warp the barrier between them.

Most of the fighting, though, happened where the town could not see it: on the far side of the barrier, or out in the hills. There was seldom anything left afterwards for a camera to record.

That is one reason why the wider world heard so little of it. California had another city under attack by monsters in the same years, Angel Grove, whose Power Rangers were on the news nearly every morning. The great matter of the day lay further off still, in the Augment War, which was being fought in Asia as well as the Balkans. Crossworld City followed that on the news like everywhere else.

pages.title: Cthulhu
infobox: A vast thing with an octopus's head, a scaly body, claws and narrow wings
The cult of Cthulhu; the Deep Ones; the Cult of Transcendence works for his return
March 1925, when R'lyeh rose for a month
By his cult and his dreamers; never seen
pages.html:
Cthulhu is the greatest of the Great Old Ones who sleep on the Earth. He lies in his house in R'lyeh, a drowned city of the southern ocean, dead but dreaming, as he has lain since the Flood put it under the sea. His dreams reach the sensitive, the artists and the mad. His cult has waited in every age for the stars to come right. In the spring of 1925 R'lyeh rose for a few weeks, and he walked.

Before the Flood

Cthulhu came to the Earth from the stars, or so his worshippers say, with the spawn that served him. It was in the Third Age of the world, not long after the Elder Things had come. The two peoples fought, and in the end made a peace, by which the spawn kept the lands that rose out of the Pacific. His spawn built R'lyeh in the southern ocean, a city of vast green stone whose angles are wrong. There he lay down to sleep, as his kind sleep when the stars are not right for them.

His worshippers say that he was there before men, and that men first heard of him in dreams. The cult that grew from those dreams is older than any record of it. Its priests carved small idols of him in stone: a thing with an octopus's head, a scaly, rubbery body, long claws and narrow wings.

Dead but dreaming

The Flood took R'lyeh, as it took the rest of the old world. The city went down under the southern ocean, and Cthulhu with it. The water did not kill him. It holds him, in the words his cult repeats: 'In his house at R'lyeh dead Cthulhu waits dreaming.'

It was God's judgement that put him there, and it did not finish him. That is the first great instance on record of what the Great Old Ones can do against God: the judgement fell, and one of them outlasted it. Whether God meant the water to end him or only to bind him, no account says. It binds him still.

He is not idle in his sleep. His dreams go out from R'lyeh into the minds of men, most strongly into those who are sensitive to such things: painters, poets, sculptors, the half-mad. Some of the dreamers make things they do not understand. Some go mad. Some find the cult, or the cult finds them.

More than one man who believed that Heaven was calling him has been hearing Cthulhu instead. That is how he spoils God's work from the bottom of the sea: not by force, but by sending a voice that sounds, to the right ear, like a call.

The cult

The cult of Cthulhu has never been one body. It has lived among sailors and outcasts, in swamps, on islands, in far mountains, wherever men were lonely enough to listen to their dreams.

On 1 November 1907 the police of New Orleans raided a gathering of the cult in the swamps south of the city. Squatters had been vanishing from the settlements nearby. The police found a ring of naked worshippers dancing round a bonfire, about a monolith on which stood a small stone idol, with the bodies of the missing hung about it. Five cultists were killed and forty-seven taken. Inspector John Raymond Legrasse carried the idol away.

Under questioning an old prisoner called Castro told him what the cult believed. The Great Old Ones, he said, had come from the stars and ruled the Earth before men. They were not dead. They lay in their houses in R'lyeh, kept by the spells of mighty Cthulhu, and when the stars came right the cult would set them free. He said the cult's chief priests lived in the mountains of China, and that the Arab Abdul Alhazred had written of these things in the Necronomicon.

Legrasse took the idol to a meeting of scholars at St Louis in 1908. Professor William Channing Webb of Princeton recognised its shape. He had met the same worship, many years before, in the far north of Greenland.

The spring of 1925

At the end of February 1925 an earthquake shook the floor of the southern Pacific, and part of R'lyeh rose above the sea. For a month the dreams came thick and fast. In Providence, Rhode Island, a young sculptor called Henry Anthony Wilcox began making things out of what he dreamt. On 1 March he brought the first of them, a clay tablet carved with Cthulhu's likeness, to Professor George Gammell Angell of Brown University.

All over the world artists and poets dreamt of a city of slimy green stone. An architect went mad on 23 March. In Britain the psychics of a small section of military intelligence, the section that became PISCES, broke down that spring, one after another.

On 23 March the crew of the Emma, a schooner out of Auckland, came ashore on R'lyeh. The day before they had beaten off an attack by the Alert, a yacht crewed by men of the cult, and taken her, losing their own ship in the fight. Six of them died on the island. A great carved door opened, and Cthulhu came out.

Gustaf Johansen, the Norwegian second mate, got back to the Alert with one other man and put to sea. Cthulhu came after them through the water. Johansen turned the yacht and drove her straight at him. The bows burst through the thing's head like a bladder, and it began, slowly, to come together again behind them.

On 2 April a storm came up, and R'lyeh went down again. Whether the stars had been wrong after all, or something else had a hand in it, the accounts do not say. On the same day the dreamers woke. Wilcox's fever broke that afternoon, and he remembered nothing of it.

The freighter Vigilant found the Alert drifting on 12 April, with Johansen alive and one dead man aboard. Johansen went home to Oslo with his hair turned white. He died not long afterwards, when a bundle of papers fell from an attic window and struck him. He had written down what happened. Professor Angell, who had been gathering the pieces, died in the winter of 1926 to 1927, after a fall in a Providence street. His great-nephew finished the work, and wished he had not.

There were no costumed heroes in 1925 to ask about any of it. The newspapers printed a storm, a derelict and a few odd cases of madness. Nobody connected them.

Cthulhu and the heroes

Long before the Flood, Cthulhu set down his spells on leaves of parchment, the book that sorcerers call the Darkhold. It is the oldest book of dark magic in the world. It has passed from hand to hand ever since, and it ruins almost everyone who reads it. Witches and wizards who know of it rank it with the Necronomicon among the books that ought never to be opened.

Not all of Cthulhu's reach runs from R'lyeh. Under Wundagore Mountain in the small country of Transia lies one of the old bindings laid on him, and there his dreaming mind can come nearest to the waking world. Sorcerers have served him there, among them the one called Modred the Mystic.

In 1946 the Scarlet Witch, Wanda Maximoff, was born on Wundagore, and the witch's blood in her caught his eye. In 1979 he took her body on the mountain, until her brother Pietro and the Avengers drove him out of her into a wooden doll, which she buried under an avalanche. The heroes who fought him took him for a demon. He was something older, and he has not forgotten her.

Delta Green and Cthulhu

Delta Green came too late to the spring of 1925 to do anything about it. It has studied what came of it since.

By 1994, in Delta Green's reckoning, the old cult of Cthulhu, the cult of sailors, swamps and outcasts, is all but gone. What has taken its place troubles Delta Green more: a quieter following among the powerful, the cream of society, commerce and politics, who have heard the call in their own way. The Cult of Transcendence, which serves Nyarlathotep, has worked for Cthulhu's return for most of the century. The Deep Ones worship him too.

Nobody in Delta Green has ever seen him, and nobody wishes to. It watches the cult. It watches the dreamers.

pages.title: Cybil Bennett
infobox: Brahms, the next town to Silent Hill
pages.html:
Cybil Bennett was the police officer from Brahms who rode into Silent Hill on the night of 12 September 1983 to find out why the town had stopped answering. She was twenty-eight. She was the only person from outside who came to look that night. She is one of the very few who have seen the Otherworld and left it alive. She walked out with Harry Mason and a newborn child.

The road from Brahms

Brahms is the next town along the highway from Silent Hill. On 12 September 1983 every line between the two towns went dead at once. Cybil Bennett was sent over on her motorcycle to see what had happened. On the road she overtook a car with a man and a small girl in it. A little further on, her motorcycle came off the road.

She found Silent Hill deep in fog, with snow coming down out of season and not a soul in the streets. The telephones did not work. Nor did her radio. The man from the car was called Harry Mason, and his daughter was missing. Cybil gave him a pistol, on the understanding that he would be careful where he pointed it. Then she set off to fetch help. She found that the roads out of the town had gone.

The amusement park

Cybil did not believe at first in the other world that Harry described. She thought that the old woman who kept telling him about demons, Dahlia Gillespie, was probably on drugs. She changed her mind in an antique shop, where the two of them found a hidden altar. Harry vanished from the room in front of her.

By nightfall on the 13th she had seen the dark side of the town for herself. The two of them agreed to split up: Harry would go to the lighthouse, Cybil to the amusement park. Something caught her there. A parasite got into her body, and it used her. When Harry reached the carousel, she walked towards him with her eyes red and her gun raised. She fired at him.

He had a bottle of red liquid from the hospital in his pocket. It was aglaophotis, though he did not know the name. He threw it over her. The parasite came out of her back, and Harry crushed it. When Cybil could speak again, she asked him why anybody would want his daughter. He told her then that Cheryl was not his own child. He had found her at the side of the road, seven years before.

The way out

Cybil was there at the end, when Dahlia Gillespie brought the Order's god to birth. She saw Harry kill it. When the place began to burn, she ran with him along the path that Alessa Gillespie opened for them, with the baby in his arms.

Nothing in the record says what she reported in Brahms. No report of hers has ever brought anybody else to Silent Hill.

A listening post of the SCP Foundation stood on the Brahms road. It logged a police motorcycle going towards Silent Hill that night, and nothing coming back.

pages.title: Dagon
infobox: The Bible; H. P. Lovecraft; Delta Green
One of the Great Old Ones; perhaps the eldest of the Deep Ones
The Philistines; the Deep Ones; the Esoteric Order of Dagon
The Ark of the Lord, at Ashdod, about 1050 BC
House at Gaza pulled down by
Jonathan, brother of Judas Maccabeus, about 147 BC
pages.html:
Dagon is one of the Great Old Ones, a vast being of the sea whom the Deep Ones call Father Dagon. The Philistines worshipped him as their god in the days of the Judges. At Ashdod his image fell on its face before the Ark of the Lord, and was found next morning broken on the threshold, which is the plainest proof on record that none of his kind is God's equal. He has never stopped trying to lead men away from God all the same.

The god of the Philistines

The Philistines came to the coast of Canaan from over the sea. They built five cities there: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron. Their god was Dagon. His great houses stood at Gaza and at Ashdod. His images were made in the likeness of a man above and a fish below, or so the later tradition says.

Whether the Philistines knew what they worshipped is doubtful. They thought him a god of the harvest, and of the sea. What answered their prayers was older than their cities, and lived in the deeps.

Samson

About 1070 BC the lords of the Philistines took Samson, the judge of Israel, put out his eyes and set him to grind in the prison house at Gaza. They gathered in the house of Dagon for a great sacrifice, saying that their god had delivered their enemy into their hands. They sent for Samson to make sport for them.

He asked the Lord for his strength one last time, set his hands on the two middle pillars of the house, and bowed himself with all his might. The house fell on the lords and on all the people in it. Scripture says the dead he slew at his death were more than those he slew in his life.

Before the Ark

About 1050 BC the Philistines beat Israel in battle near Ebenezer and took the Ark of the Lord. They carried it in triumph to Ashdod, into the house of Dagon, and set it by his image as a trophy.

In the morning Dagon had fallen on his face before the Ark. The priests stood him up again. The next morning he had fallen again. This time his head lay cut off upon the threshold, with both the palms of his hands. Only the stump of Dagon was left to him. From that day, the First Book of Samuel records, neither the priests of Dagon nor anyone who came into his house would tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod.

Then the hand of the Lord lay heavy on Ashdod. The people were struck with a plague of emerods, and the mice marred the land. They sent the Ark to Gath, then to Ekron, and the plague went with it. After seven months the Philistines sent it home to Israel on a new cart, with golden images of the emerods and the mice as a trespass offering.

It is the plainest defeat any of the Great Old Ones has suffered on record. Dagon could not stand in the presence of the Ark. He was not set up a third time.

Spite

Dagon did not stop. The Philistines went on worshipping him, and their enmity with Israel lasted for generations. About 147 BC Jonathan, the brother of Judas Maccabeus, beat the army of Apollonius near Azotus, which is Ashdod. The beaten men fled into the house of Dagon. Jonathan burnt it over their heads, as the First Book of the Maccabees records. After that his worship faded from the coast. It did not fade from the sea.

What he wanted of the Philistines, or of anybody, nobody knows. What he did with them is plain enough. A people who might have turned to the God of Israel, whose Ark had broken their idol before their eyes, turned back to Dagon instead.

Father Dagon

In the deeps of the sea the Deep Ones worship him still, with Mother Hydra, his consort. Their oaths name them both. Nobody in Delta Green can say whether Dagon is truly a power of his own kind or only the eldest of the Deep Ones, grown vast beyond measure with the centuries.

Some in Delta Green believe that such elders exist, twenty feet tall or more, and all but undying. They plan over spans of time no man could keep in his head. Off the coast of Alaska there is said to be a third, which the people of Black Cod Island call He-Who-Swims-With-Corpses.

Innsmouth

In the nineteenth century his worship came ashore in New England. Obed Marsh, a sea captain of Innsmouth in Massachusetts, learnt it in the South Seas, and brought it home with the gold the Deep Ones paid for it. The Esoteric Order of Dagon took the town's old Masonic Hall for its temple. One by one the churches of Innsmouth lost their congregations, until the Order was the only faith the town had left.

A Christian town of New England had been led out of its churches, into the sea. The government's raid on Innsmouth in 1928 is where Delta Green's long war began.

The castaway

Early in the Great War a German sea-raider took a cargo ship in the loneliest part of the Pacific. One of her officers escaped in a boat and drifted south until he ran aground on a stretch of sea-bed that had heaved itself up out of the water. On it stood a white monolith carved with figures of fish-men. As he watched, something huge rose out of the water beside it and threw its arms about the stone.

He fled, was picked up by an American ship and woke in a hospital in San Francisco. He knew the old Philistine legend, and he took the thing for Dagon. He spent the rest of his short life on morphine. The last thing he wrote was about a hand at his window.

pages.title: Dahlia Gillespie
infobox: Priestess of the Order of Silent Hill
None of her own: a No-Maj working the rites of the Order
13 September 1983, killed by the god she had brought to birth
pages.html:
Dahlia Gillespie was a priestess of the Order of Silent Hill and the mother of Alessa Gillespie. In the summer of 1976 she burnt her seven-year-old daughter in a rite meant to bring the Order's god into the world. When it failed she kept the child alive, in agony, for seven years, until she could try again. In September 1983 she succeeded. The god was born, and its first act was to kill her.

The priestess

Dahlia was born about 1937. She was a medium, devoted to the occult, who rose to lead the Order's ceremonies. She was no witch. What she could do, she did by ritual, with the Order's books open in front of her, like every priest of the Order before her. It worked because the Order's god answered.

Her daughter was another matter. Alessa was born about 1969 with real magic, the kind a witch is born with, though Dahlia had no name for it. She saw a child who could do without effort what the Order's priests laboured over. The Order had been trying for years to find a mother for its god. Dahlia decided that she had given birth to one.

The burning

In the summer of 1976 she performed the rite of birth on Alessa in the cellar of her own house. The fire that went with it burnt down six homes. Alessa was reported dead. In fact Dahlia had her taken to Alchemilla Hospital, whose director, Dr Michael Kaufmann, had long done business with the Order.

The rite had put the god into the child, but it could not be born. Half of Alessa's soul had got away. Dahlia understood what had happened, though she did not know where the missing half had gone. She began a spell to call it home. She kept the spell up for seven years, while her daughter lay burnt in a locked room.

Seven years

The arrangement with Kaufmann held throughout. The Order supplied him with White Claudia for the drug he sold to the summer visitors. He supplied a hidden room, a nurse and false papers. When the mayor of Silent Hill set out to stamp out the drug, he died. A narcotics officer who took up the case died of a failed heart, with no history of illness. Kaufmann drew his own conclusions about what Dahlia could do.

She found time for the Order's other business. On 16 October 1976 she visited Wish House, its orphanage. The next day she told a six-year-old boy there that his mother lay asleep in Ashfield. He could wake her, she said, if he learnt his scripture. The boy was Walter Sullivan.

1983

On 12 September 1983 the missing half of the soul came back, in the shape of a seven-year-old girl called Cheryl Mason. Its coming gave Alessa back her power. She used it against her mother, going through the town from place to place to set a seal on it that would stop the birth. Dahlia could not get near her.

The child's father could. Harry Mason was searching the town for his daughter, and Dahlia met him in a church. She gave him the Flauros, a charm that would break Alessa's power. She told him that the seal was the mark of a demon, which was a lie, and that the girl who drew it meant his daughter harm. He caught Alessa for her at the amusement park.

On the night of 13 September Dahlia joined the two halves of the soul and finished the rite she had begun seven years before. She had the satisfaction of telling Harry Mason all about it. Then Kaufmann, whom she had cheated, threw aglaophotis over the newborn god. It came out in its true shape, and it killed her where she stood.

pages.title: Dai Thomas
infobox: Police officer, Scotland Yard: chief inspector in 1976, commander by 1990
Before 1976, when his wife was killed in a fight between costumed strangers in America
Hating Captain Britain, then grudgingly befriending him
pages.html:
Dai Thomas is a Welsh policeman of Scotland Yard who swore in 1976 to unmask Captain Britain. His wife had been killed in America as a bystander in a fight between costumed strangers, and he meant to see that nothing of the kind happened in Britain. On Christmas Eve 1985 he swallowed his pride and asked Captain Britain for help. They have been friends of a sort ever since.

The policeman

In 1976 Dai Thomas was a chief inspector at Scotland Yard. When Captain Britain appeared that autumn, Thomas saw in him the first sign of the plague of costumed heroes that had killed his wife, and he set out to have him unmasked. For a year Captain Britain spent more time running from Thomas's men than from criminals. In 1977 the two of them worked several cases together, without either liking the other any better for it.

Thomas came to suspect that Captain Britain was Brian Braddock, but he was ordered not to act on it.

Christmas Eve, 1985

On Christmas Eve 1985 Thomas came to the lighthouse where Brian was living with Meggan. He was stuck on a string of murders that made no sense, and he asked for help. Together they found that the killer was one of the Warpies, a child whom Jaspers' warp had given powers. The case was the start of a friendship, of a sort, between two men who still did not much like each other.

By 1990 Thomas had risen to commander. He has worked with Captain Britain ever since, more willingly than he lets anybody see.

pages.title: Daisuke Serizawa
infobox: Lost his right eye in the war
November 1954, in Tokyo Bay, by his own hand
pages.html:
Dr Daisuke Serizawa was the Japanese chemist who killed the first Godzilla. He invented the Oxygen Destroyer, the only weapon that has ever killed one of Godzilla's kind. He used it once, in Tokyo Bay in November 1954, then died with it so that nobody could ever build another.

The chemist

Serizawa was a young colleague of the palaeontologist Dr Kyohei Yamane, whose daughter, Emiko, had long been promised to him in marriage. He had lost his right eye in the war. Afterwards he shut himself up in his laboratory in Tokyo, where he saw almost nobody.

Emiko, meanwhile, had fallen in love with a salvage officer, Hideto Ogata. She had not found the courage to tell Serizawa so.

The Oxygen Destroyer

Serizawa was studying oxygen. He came by chance on a reaction that horrified him. A pellet of his compound, dropped into water, destroyed all the oxygen in it. Every living thing in the water suffocated at once. Then its flesh dissolved, leaving bare bones.

He saw immediately what he had made: a weapon as terrible as the hydrogen bomb. He resolved to tell nobody until he had found some good use for it. He showed it, once, to Emiko, in a tank of fish. She swore to keep the secret.

Tokyo Bay

On the night of 3 November 1954 Godzilla burnt Tokyo. Nothing had stopped him. Superman, the one hero who came, had been struck out of the sky by Godzilla's breath; he lay recovering for days.

In a hall full of the wounded Emiko told Ogata what she had seen. The two of them went to Serizawa, who refused them. If he used the thing even once, he said, the statesmen of the world would never rest until they had it. Then a broadcast from the ruined city carried the voices of its schoolgirls, singing a prayer for peace. He gave way. He burnt every page of his notes while Emiko watched.

Two days after the raid a coastguard ship, the Shikine, took him out into the bay. He went down in a diving suit with Ogata, found Godzilla resting on the sea bed, then set the device working. He sent Ogata up. Over the telephone line he wished him happiness with Emiko. Then he cut his own air hose.

The water boiled. Godzilla rose once, roared, sank, then came apart until nothing was left of him, not even bones. On the deck Dr Yamane said that he could not believe this Godzilla had been the last of its kind. He was right within three months.

The secret

Nobody has made an Oxygen Destroyer since. Serizawa left no notes, no pupils, no second sample. That is why the second Godzilla has never been killed.

pages.title: Dark Specter
infobox: Power Rangers in Space, 'From Out of Nowhere, Part 1' (6 February 1998)
Psycho Green to the Moon, July 1969
Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd, Divatox, the Machine Empire and others
pages.html:
Dark Specter is the Grand Monarch of Evil, an old enemy of Eltar and its Guardians. In 1969 he sent Psycho Green to the Moon to set Rita Repulsa free. In February 1995 Rita, as his general Mistress Vile, opened a gate for him into the world, and the Rangers threw him out again, much reduced. In November 1997 he took Zordon prisoner. In November 1998 he died at the hands of Darkonda, one of his own allies.

Eltar's enemy

Nobody on Earth knows what Dark Specter is or where he came from. He is not the Devil, for all the grandeur of his title. He was at war with Eltar before Zophram ever became its Supreme Guardian.

When the Elders made Zophram the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar, his first act was to ask that Eltar's forces should go beyond their own galaxy, to protect young worlds against Dark Specter. It was a party of Hartunians in Dark Specter's service that the Guardians were fighting on Earth's Moon when they found the Zeo Crystal there.

Then an assassin of his poisoned Zordon. Zophram struck the creature down, but not before it had got into his head. What it told him led him to the Crystal, whose curse flayed him, so that Lord Zedd was born.

Psycho Green

In July 1969, on the day the Americans landed on the Moon, Dark Specter sent Psycho Green to the same place to break Rita Repulsa out of her dumpster. Psycho Green had once been a Ranger himself, on another world. Zordon raised five strangers against him in a single evening. Three of them died, but Psycho Green was destroyed, while Rita stayed where she was. One of the survivors, Grace Sterling, kept his dagger.

Mistress Vile

Rita Repulsa's father, Master Vile, had offered Dark Specter a body to wear in the world: Alpha 1, the old robot of Edenoi. Dark Specter scorned it. Early in 1995 Rita overthrew her father. She promised Dark Specter a better body, with the Zeo Crystal besides, so he raised her up as his general, Mistress Vile.

The better body was the Vessel: the Eltarian body that Zordon had worn before Rita's curse took it from him, which she fetched from the frozen planet Bizerk. She corrupted it so that it could hold Dark Specter. It went to Zordon's mind, offering to be one with him again. Zordon refused.

In February 1995 Mistress Vile took the Zeo Crystal. With it she opened the Arch, an old gate into the Morphin Grid in the Bermuda Triangle. Grace Sterling was killed there. The Rangers had to choose between saving Matt Cook, whom Mistress Vile held under a spell, and shutting the gate. They saved Matt. Dark Specter came through, then took the Vessel for his own.

The darkest hour

His corruption got into the Grid itself. Any Ranger who morphed was turned to his side, and whole teams of the Rangers of years not yet come fell to him one after another. Safehaven, the home of the Omega Rangers, became his prison. In the World of the Coinless, Lord Drakkon's own world, creatures of lava in his service, which had once been people, were overrunning what was left.

He destroyed Alpha 1. He turned on Mistress Vile, his own general, and would have killed her if Lord Zedd had not saved her. Two coins were proof against him, Tommy Oliver's White coin and Lord Drakkon's. Joined together, they let the Rangers morph in safety.

Thrown back

Dark Specter was not killed. When the Rangers cleansed the Grid, the cleansing burnt his corruption out of it and destroyed the Vessel. Dark Specter himself was thrown back into the dark he had come from, much reduced. It was nearly three years before he moved openly again.

The mended world kept no memory of his coming.

The capture of Zordon

In 1997 Zordon went home to Eltar. In November that year Eltar fell to evil, and Dark Specter took Zordon prisoner. He set about draining Zordon's power, slowly, through the whole of the next year.

He gathered into one alliance every villain of any consequence in the universe: Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd, Divatox, the Machine Empire and others. They met at his council on the Cimmerian Planet, to celebrate the conquest of Eltar and the capture of Zordon. He kept Zordon on the Dark Fortress, the base of his pupil Astronema.

His end

In November 1998 Dark Specter sent his alliance against the whole universe at once. He did not see the end of it. Darkonda, one of his own allies, struck him down with an experimental laser fired from a stolen fighter. Dying, Dark Specter swallowed Darkonda whole, then exploded, which destroyed them both.

Astronema led the attack in his place. Soon afterwards Zordon's light went out across the universe, which ended the war.

pages.title: Darkseid
infobox: King Yuga Khan and Queen Heggra
Kalibak, by Suli; Orion, by Tigra
Granny Goodness, DeSaad, Kalibak, Glorious Godfrey, the Parademons
Highfather of New Genesis, Orion, Mister Miracle, Superman
pages.html:
Darkseid is the Lord of Apokolips, a world of fire pits and slaves on the far side of the universe. He is one of the beings who call themselves the New Gods, and he wants only one thing: the Anti-Life Equation, which would give him command of every living mind. He believes it is hidden somewhere in the minds of human beings, which is why he takes such an interest in Earth. Very few people on Earth have ever heard of him, and he prefers it that way.

Uxas

Darkseid was born Uxas, the second son of King Yuga Khan and Queen Heggra of Apokolips. His elder brother, Drax, was the heir. When Drax set out to claim the Omega Force, a power that lay waiting for whoever could master it, Uxas killed him and took it for himself.

The Omega Force turned his body to something very like grey stone, and he took a new name to go with it. From then on he was Darkseid.

Suli, Tigra and Heggra

As a young man Darkseid loved a woman called Suli, the only person he is ever known to have loved, and she gave him a son, Kalibak. Heggra thought Suli made him weak. She had her poisoned by DeSaad, the court's chief torturer, who was not particular about whom he poisoned.

Darkseid married Tigra afterwards, and she gave him a second son, Orion. He never forgave his mother. In time DeSaad poisoned Heggra too, this time on Darkseid's orders, and Darkseid took the throne of Apokolips.

The war with New Genesis

Apokolips has a twin world, New Genesis, a green and peaceful place ruled by Izaya, who is called Highfather. The two worlds have hated each other for as long as either has existed. Their last great war began when Darkseid's uncle Steppenwolf, at Darkseid's bidding, murdered Izaya's wife, Avia.

The war went on until both sides were close to ruin. It ended with the Pact, by which the two rulers exchanged their sons. Darkseid's son Orion was sent to grow up on New Genesis, and Izaya's son Scott Free was handed over to Apokolips.

Neither exchange turned out as Darkseid intended. Orion grew up to be the fiercest warrior New Genesis has, and he has spent his life fighting his father. Scott Free was raised in one of Granny Goodness's orphanages, where the children of Apokolips are trained into soldiers, and in time he escaped to Earth with Big Barda, one of Granny's own Female Furies.

On Earth Scott became Mister Miracle, the escape artist, and Barda became his wife. In 1987 he was one of the founders of the new Justice League. His escape broke the Pact, which gave Darkseid the excuse he had been waiting for.

Metron, the restless seeker of New Genesis, gave Darkseid the secret of the Boom Tube in exchange for the X-Element.

Apokolips

Apokolips is a world of fire pits, factories and slums, on which nothing grows. Its people, the Lowlies, toil in their millions in the shadow of Darkseid's towers, and they have long since been taught to cheer him. Above them fly the Parademons, his winged soldiers. Those who can no longer work are left to rot in the slums of Armagetto. It is not Hell, although very few of the Lowlies would know the difference.

His court is made up of the people who are useful to him. Granny Goodness runs the orphanages. DeSaad is his torturer, as well as the inventor of most of the machines for it. Kalibak, his elder son, is strong, brutal and desperate for a word of praise from his father, which he has never had. Glorious Godfrey has a voice that can turn a crowd.

The Omega Effect

Darkseid's power is the Omega Effect. It comes out of his eyes as the Omega Beams, which will chase whatever he aims them at round corners and through walls until they find it. They can burn a living thing out of existence or send it somewhere else entirely, and he can bring back what they have taken if he chooses. He rarely does.

He is enormously strong, very old and almost impossible to hurt. He seldom needs to prove it. He prefers to send other people, and to wait.

The Anti-Life Equation

What Darkseid wants above everything is the Anti-Life Equation. It is a proof that hope and free will are worthless, so complete that whoever knows it can command the mind of any living thing.

He has searched for it across the universe. He has come to believe that its pieces lie scattered in the minds of human beings, and that is why Earth matters to him.

He once looked for it among the Goa'uld, the parasites who rule much of Earth's galaxy, since each of them is born with the memories of all its ancestors. DeSaad took the whole court of a lesser System Lord apart, one mind at a time. He found nothing but vanity and a great many memories of Thor.

Earth

Darkseid first came to notice on Earth in late 1970, when Superman found that Intergang, the crime syndicate of Metropolis, was armed with weapons from Apokolips. Darkseid had been behind it from the start. It was the first of many such discoveries.

In 1986 he set out to break the heroes of Earth by turning their own people against them. He did not come himself. His instrument was Glorious Godfrey, who went before the television cameras as the preacher G. Gordon Godfrey and told America night after night that its heroes were dangerous. Darkseid's creatures staged disasters to prove him right.

That winter President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America. Godfrey was exposed early in 1987, at a great march on Washington, and the order was lifted. A new Justice League came out of the struggle.

In the spring of 1994 Doomsday, the creature that had killed Superman, rose again far from Earth and fought its way across Apokolips. At the same time Hank Henshaw, the Cyborg Superman, surfaced there. Darkseid compressed what remained of his life force into a small sphere, and kept it. Nobody knows what he means to do with it.

Thanos

Darkseid's bitterest enemy outside his own family is Thanos, the Mad Titan. Their feud began in 1973, when Darkseid tried to take the Cosmic Cube from him. It has drawn the Avengers and the Justice League into one war after another.

In 1977 Darkseid helped the heroes bring Thanos down, so that he could steal the Soul Gems from the wreck. In 1991 Thanos, wearing the Infinity Gauntlet, turned him into a statue of glass for a day that almost nobody remembers. Darkseid does.

Character

Darkseid is patient in a way that only something very old can be. He does not lose his temper, he does not hurry and he does not forgive. He has no use for love, which he tried once, or for loyalty, which he expects but never returns. His servants fear him far more than they love him, which he considers the proper arrangement.

The end of Apokolips

About 2037 Darkseid made his last war on New Genesis, the war the twin worlds had been threatening each other with since the Pact broke. Neither world survived it. Darkseid died with Apokolips, and he never found the Anti-Life Equation.

Nobody on Earth knew of it until 2155, when the Enterprise NX-01 found the empty Mobius Chair of Metron in deep space, its memory full of two worlds burning.

In the saga

Book 4: on 20 August 1994 the newsreader on the Dursleys' television recalls that in 1986 President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter. Nobody on the news mentions Darkseid, whose campaign it was.

pages.title: Darth Vader
aliases: the Dark Lord of the Sith
infobox: The Emperor of the Galactic Empire
A tall man in black armour, with a black helmet that breathes for him
A sword with a blade of red light
The Imperial fleet at Side 7, 2293; the invasion of the Milky Way, 2299 to 2300
James T. Kirk and John Shepard, 2293; John Shepard, 2300
pages.html:
Darth Vader was the Emperor's right hand in the Galactic Empire, a Dark Lord of the Sith in black armour. He led the Empire's fleet against the Federation in the Imperial Entanglement of 2293. He came back as commander of its invasion in the Intergalactic War.

The Dark Lord

Vader was human under the armour. He had once been a Jedi knight called Anakin Skywalker, who turned to the dark side of the power his people called the Force. Terrible burns left him unable to live outside the armour, whose helmet breathed for him. He fought with a sword of red light, which no weapon of the Federation's could turn. He could choke a man from across a room without touching him.

Against the Federation

On 17 May 2293 Vader brought an Imperial fleet across the bridge to Starbase Side 7, to punish the theft of the Empire's technology. He boarded the starbase himself. James T. Kirk and John Shepard fought him together. They beat him. He withdrew, promising to return in greater numbers.

He returned in 2299 at the head of the invasion. He took Thessia from the Asari in person that December. At the Battle of Earth, in March 2300, Shepard fought him for the second time aboard his own flagship. When the Barrier was lit, that flagship was thrown back to the Empire's galaxy with Vader aboard. Nothing that he did afterwards in his own galaxy was changed by the war.

In the saga

Darth Vader has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Death (servant of Dracula)
infobox: A powerful demonic creature in the shape of a reaper
pages.html:
Death is a powerful demon that has served Dracula since 1094. It takes the shape of a robed skeleton with a great scythe, and it has stood at its master's right hand at almost every one of his returns. Despite its name it is simply a demon in Dracula's service. It is not Death of the Endless, the being who meets every living thing at the end of its life, and it has nothing to do with her.

Nature

Death is a demon of great power that wears the shape of a reaper: a skeleton in a dark hooded robe, carrying a great scythe. It can fill the air with flying sickles, and pass at will through the dark places of its master's castle. The name is a borrowed one, and so is the fear that goes with it. It does not lead the dead anywhere. Its only power over death is the power to kill.

Like every demon, it belongs in the end to the Devil, whose property Dracula and every vampire also are. Its loyalty, though, is to Dracula. It has served him for nine centuries, working again and again to bring him back whenever he has been destroyed. It has been destroyed itself more than once, and it has always come back, as its master does.

In Dracula's service

In 1094, as Leon Belmont destroyed the vampire Walter Bernhard, Death carried Walter's soul to Mathias Cronqvist. Mathias took it into the Crimson Stone and rose as the vampire who became Dracula. From that night Death served Mathias, and it fought Leon while its new master withdrew.

It was in the castle in 1476, when Trevor Belmont fought his way up through the clock tower. In 1479 it took the guise of a man called Zead and schemed to raise Dracula again through a living vessel. It killed the Devil Forgemaster Isaac to do it, and Hector thwarted it. Simon Belmont met it in the castle in 1691, and destroyed it in Brahm's mansion in 1698. Juste Belmont destroyed it in 1748, after it had held Lydie Erlanger prisoner. Richter Belmont met it on the road through the woods in 1792.

In 1797, when Alucard entered his father's risen castle, Death met him at the gate and stripped him of the arms he carried. In 1944, while the vampire painter Brauner held the castle, Death worked to restore its master. In 2035, after Dracula's final destruction, it tried to wake his power in Soma Cruz.

It was one of three servants who set out to raise Dracula in 1844. The others were the witch Actrise and the vampire Gilles de Rais. In 1852 it killed Rosa, who had stepped in front of its scythe to save Reinhardt Schneider, who then destroyed it. In 1917 it guarded Castle Proserpina for Elizabeth Bartley. In 1944 it cut down the painter Brauner the moment the hunters had beaten him, since Brauner's paintings were all that kept Dracula from his throne. Dracula took Death's power into himself that year, yet both were destroyed.

Not Death of the Endless

Death of the Endless, the second of the Endless, is death itself: the being who comes to every living thing at the end of its life. Dracula's servant is no such being. It is a demon in a reaper's shape, under a borrowed name, and it serves one master.

pages.title: Douglas Cartland
infobox: A widower; one son, shot dead robbing a bank
Cheryl Mason, then living as Heather
pages.html:
Douglas Cartland was the private detective whom the Order of Silent Hill hired in 2000 to find a missing girl. He found her. Within a day her father was dead because of it. Cartland spent the rest of the affair trying to put right what he had done, which is how a middle-aged man in a raincoat came to be lying in an amusement park in Silent Hill with a broken leg.

The job

Cartland was a widower in late middle age, working alone. He had had a son, who was shot dead while robbing a bank.

In 2000 a woman called Claudia Wolf came to him with a story. Seventeen years before, she said, a man named Harry Mason had kidnapped a baby girl from Silent Hill. She wanted the child found. Cartland's notebook shows how he did it. He turned up an old newspaper report of a girl of seven, Alessa Gillespie, dead in a fire. He traced Mason to Portland, where the man had shot somebody in 1988, been cleared, then moved away. He found a girl who used the name Heather. The records made her twenty-four. She looked seventeen.

He told his client where the girl was. Then, on Saturday 16 September, he went to speak to her himself, in a shopping centre. She took him for a man who followed girls about, and climbed out of a window.

The road to Silent Hill

By the time he caught up with Heather again, her father had been murdered. Cartland had not known what his client wanted the girl for. He knew now what he had done. He helped her to carry the body to the bedroom. He covered it with a sheet. Then he offered to drive her to Silent Hill, since she meant to go whether he drove her or not.

It was a long drive. He gave her a notebook of her father's that had been left for her, with a map from the priest Vincent Smith. On the road she told him what she remembered of being somebody else.

The amusement park

At Silent Hill the next day the two of them took rooms at a motel and separated. Cartland went to look at Leonard Wolf's house, then set off round the lake to find Claudia himself. He caught up with her at the amusement park. He told her what he thought of a paradise in which nothing was ever lost. She told him that she was sorry for him. He drew his gun. She broke his leg without laying a finger on him.

Heather found him there afterwards, unable to walk. He told her about his son. He admitted, too, that he had thought of shooting her, to make sure that the Order's god was never born. He could not do it. She went on alone, promising to come back for him.

She kept the promise. When the god was dead she walked back to the amusement park, where Cartland was still sitting with his leg stretched out in front of him. He asked her whether it was over. She frightened him badly first, by pretending that the god had won. Then she told him that she would like to be called Cheryl again.

pages.title: Douglock
infobox: A being of living metal, made by the Phalanx; in truth Warlock, as he learnt in 1999
The face and memories of Doug Ramsey
Changes his shape; Doug Ramsey's gift for every language, spoken, written or made by machines
The Excalibur team, from July 1994 to 1998
pages.html:
Douglock is a being of living metal, a creature of the Phalanx made in the likeness of Doug Ramsey, the dead New Mutant, with Doug's face and Doug's memories. He broke away from the Phalanx in the spring of 1994, and that July Kitty Pryde asked him to stay with the Excalibur team. In the summer of 1994 he is its newest member, living on Muir Island and still unsure who he is. In 1999 he found out: he was Warlock, Doug's alien friend, come back with a copy of Doug in his memory.

Doug Ramsey and Warlock

Doug Ramsey was one of the New Mutants at Xavier's school, a boy who could understand any language at all. His closest friend was Warlock, a young Technarch, one of an alien race of shape-changing living machines. Warlock had fled his father, the Magus, rather than fight him to the death, as Technarch children are expected to do. The two boys could merge into a single fighter.

At the end of 1987 Doug stepped in front of a bullet meant for Rahne Sinclair, and died. In 1990, on Genosha, Cameron Hodge drained Warlock to ash. At Rahne's asking the ashes were scattered over Doug's grave.

Out of the Phalanx

From Warlock's remains came the transmode virus that made the Phalanx, men who hated mutants and made themselves into living machines. In the spring of 1994 Zero, a teleporting machine that had once served Stryfe, found one of them in the woods of Maine, wearing Doug's face, and cut it loose from the rest. It called itself Douglock.

Zero brought him to Captain Britain, Meggan and Kitty Pryde. Early in the summer, in a hidden base of Stryfe's beneath the Pentagon, Zero gave his life to save them all. Before he died he put the secrets of the Legacy Virus that he carried into Douglock, who could not read them.

The Excalibur team

Kitty had loved Doug, and at first she could hardly bear to look at the thing that wore his face. She called him names and phased her hand into him to make a point. In July 1994, over a drink in a pub in Aberdeen, she asked him to stay with the team, so that they could learn about each other.

In the summer of 1994 he lives on Muir Island, a stranger among people who remember somebody he is not. He does not know whether he is Doug.

In August 1994 the Phalanx built a tower in the Alps, the Babel Spire, out of the people of the villages it had swallowed. From its top it meant to call down the Technarchy, Warlock's people, who would have eaten the world. Douglock climbed it with Rahne Sinclair and Sam Guthrie. He knocked Rahne down and gave himself to the Phalanx, which built him into the tower. Then he scrambled its beacon from within, and the Phalanx there fell to pieces. He rose out of the ground afterwards, and said that he wanted to belong to a team.

Muir Island, 1995 to 1998

In 1996 Black Air harpooned him from a jet. Its scientists took him apart in London, and found the files on the Legacy Virus inside him. The Hellfire Club joined what was left of him to a demon that lay beneath the city. The team got him back from Blackwall, Black Air's headquarters, and he mended.

That autumn Kitty phased into Doug's grave at Salem Center and found his bones still in it. Douglock was not Doug come back, whatever else he was. She said goodbye to her old friend, then introduced herself to Douglock properly.

He fell in love with Rahne Sinclair. She kissed him in the summer of 1997, then kept him at arm's length. In Venice that winter the Sidri, alien hunters, tried to swallow him into themselves; his Phalanx parts healed them instead, and he declared himself his own person at last. In March 1998 he broke into Moira MacTaggert's quarantine to set Rahne free, which she did not forgive him for until the wedding of Brian Braddock and Meggan that August.

Warlock

After the Excalibur team broke up he stayed on Muir Island with Rahne and Moira. In 1999 the Red Skull made him his slave to spread the transmode virus, and in the struggle he learnt the truth. He had been Warlock all along, carrying a copy of Doug's memories and believing himself someone new. He took back his own name.

pages.title: Drew Lansing
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'A Rider's Challenge' (24 January 2009)
Magnugiga, a horned giant like an ox
Xaviax, whom he meant to betray
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Drew Lansing is an American, born about 1986, who made his living as a confidence trickster. In 2009 he was Kamen Rider Torque, one of the men whom Xaviax armed on Earth. Unlike most of them he knew what Xaviax intended. He had been promised a share of the spoils. He talked Kit Taylor into fighting against his own teacher, vented one of his fellow Riders, then plotted against Xaviax too. Strike vented him on 4 April 2009.

The bargain

Drew lived by telling people what they wanted to hear. Xaviax had a use for that. He told Drew the real plan, which was to carry off the whole human race, then offered him a share in ruling the Earth afterwards. Drew took the Advent Deck of Torque. It opened for him because he was the mirror twin of Chance, the Ventaran who first wore it.

His task was to set Rider against Rider.

The lie

He was first seen on 24 January 2009, the day Len of Ventara vented Richie Preston. A week later he watched Kit Taylor fight. In February he made himself known. He did not attack. He told Kit that Len was the true traitor of Ventara, the man who had stolen the decks. Xaviax put in an appearance to help the story along.

Then Kit's father was found, drained, in a hospital. Drew went to the bedside with Kit. He said that Xaviax had done it. He added that there was a cure. Len said that there was not, so Kit believed Drew. Drew fought Len soon afterwards. His Final Vent left Len barely alive.

For some weeks Kit fought at his side. It ended on 28 February. Maya Young rang Kit to tell him whom Drew really served. That day Drew fought another of Xaviax's Riders, Grant Staley, the Rider called Camo, whom Kit had nearly persuaded to give up. Drew vented him. He tried to vent Kit as well, but Len got there first.

The plot

Drew did not mean to serve Xaviax for ever. In March he went to Brad Barrett, the Rider called Thrust, with a proposal. They should vent the Wing Knight, then Xaviax himself, after which the two of them could have their lives back. Xaviax found out. He sent Strike after him.

Drew slipped away from Strike once. He asked Kit for help. Kit refused, so the two of them fought, until Kit drove him off.

On 4 April 2009 Strike caught up with him. Their fight ran into another, between Len and Thrust, with Kit close behind. Drew saw his chance to be rid of every Rider at once. He loosed his Final Vent at the whole field, which very nearly worked. Then he left. Before the day was over Strike had found him again. This time Strike vented him.

Afterwards

Drew lay in the Advent Void until Xaviax was dead. In December 2009 Eubulon, the Advent Master, brought him out with the other men of Earth. His memories of being a Rider were taken away. The armour of Torque went back to Chance, who had fought in it against Xaviax at the end.

pages.title: Drew McCormick
infobox: Blue Stinger, 1996 to 1997; Mega Blue, from November 1996; Chromium Gold, from September 1997; Mega Spectra, from February 1998
A triangular sword; the Thunder Stinger; the Metallix Lancer; the Astral Sword
pages.html:
Drew McCormick is a boy of Charterville, about ten years old in the summer of 1994, whose favourite reading is a comic book about armoured heroes called the Beetleborgs. In September 1996 a wish made him one of them: the Blue Stinger Beetleborg, the leader of the three. He destroyed Shadowborg that November in the Mega Blue armour. In 1997 he became the Chromium Gold Beetleborg, the one who summoned the giant Roboborg.

Charterville

Drew was born about 1984. He is growing up in Charterville, where his younger sister, Jo, goes everywhere that he does. His best friend is Roland Williams, whose family keeps Zoom Comics, where the three of them spend most of their spare time. Drew is the eldest of the three. He was about twelve when the wish was made, which settled who was leader without anybody having to discuss it.

He admires Heather, a girl of the town, a good deal more than he has ever managed to tell her.

The Blue Stinger Beetleborg

On 7 September 1996 two boys of the town dared Drew, Jo and Roland to go into Hillhurst Mansion. Inside, the three let Flabber out of the pipe organ, for which he granted them a wish. They wished to be the Beetleborgs.

Drew became the Blue Stinger Beetleborg, whose armour was modelled on the rhinoceros beetle. His weapon was a triangular sword, with a Sonic Laser at his side. The wish left him a gift out of armour too. He pointed at a thing, nodded, and it moved.

The wish also let the Beetleborgs' enemies out of the comic. From that day Drew led his sister and his best friend against Vexor's Magnavores, mostly after school.

Into the comic book

In September 1996 Drew saw an amulet in a comic book that he wanted as a present for Heather. Flabber took him into the comic to fetch it from its owner, Queen Magna. The Magnavores shut the pair of them inside, then sent their jet fighters against Jo and Roland.

Drew came back out with more than he had gone in for. He brought Gargantis, the Beetleborgs' great carrier, in time to save the other two.

Shadowborg

On 11 November 1996 Vexor made Shadowborg, a black Beetleborg of his own, out of a piece of Drew's armour. Shadowborg beat all three of them, then took their powers.

The same week a new boy came to Charterville, Josh Baldwin, whom Heather liked at once. Art Fortunes drew the White Blaster Beetleborg, and Josh was asked to wear its armour. Drew found that he had a rival at school besides the one in black.

Josh won back the stolen powers. Art drew Drew a new weapon, the Thunder Stinger, which only the Blue Stinger could use. Its first trial failed against a whole company of old enemies. On 15 November Drew and Josh broke into Vexor's crypt in the cemetery to steal the source of Shadowborg's strength, Vexor's energy Axis. Drew turned the Axis on himself, which made him the Mega Blue Beetleborg.

The next day, with the Thunder Stinger in his hand, he destroyed Shadowborg. Josh's powers went out in the same moment, since they had been made only for that fight. Drew kept the Mega Blue armour.

Chromium Gold

On 21 May 1997 the Beetleborgs sent Vexor back into the comics. On 8 September Nukus destroyed their armour, weapons and powers. Art Fortunes drew new ones, which Flabber brought to life the next day. Drew became the Chromium Gold Beetleborg, with the Metallix Lancer, a staff bladed at both ends.

In November 1997 both sides hunted for the Astral Coins. The first Astralborg the three called up, Dragonborg, gave Drew a weapon of his own, the Astral Laser. On 26 November Drew held the Astral Sword with all eight coins in it. It summoned Roboborg, a giant in beetle armour.

In February 1998 Roboborg gave the three the Mega Spectra armour. On 2 March Drew led them, with both giants, against Repgillian, the last of Nukus's monsters.

The Power Rangers

Drew met the Zeo Rangers on 19 October 1996, when the Machine Empire's Cogs came to Charterville. Afterwards Tommy Oliver, the Red Ranger, shook his hand. Neither of them took off his helmet, so Tommy did not know that he was congratulating a boy of twelve.

He found out on 3 May 1997, the day Divatox tried to steal Flabber for a wish. That evening at Hillhurst the Blue Turbo Ranger, Justin Stewart, showed his face, with the three Beetleborgs following suit. Justin was twelve, a reader of the same comic, who became a friend of all three.

On 21 February 1998 Ecliptor seized the Astral Axe in the Charterville cemetery. The Red Space Ranger, Andros of KO-35, could move things with his mind, as Drew could. The two of them pulled the Axe out of Ecliptor's hand between them. Andros had not expected to find his own gift in a schoolboy from a small town, which he was honest enough to say.

pages.title: Earth's first starships
infobox: 2002 to 2007, in secret, under the Nevada desert
The Prometheus (2002), then the Daedalus, the Odyssey, the Korolev, the Apollo and the Sun Tzu
Hyperdrives copied from captured Goa'uld engines
Between nearby stars; never far without Asgard's help
pages.html:
Earth's first starships were the warships that its Stargate programme built in secret between 2002 and 2007: the Prometheus, then the larger ships of the BC-304 class, among them the Daedalus with the Odyssey. They were crude, enormously expensive prototypes, put together from captured Goa'uld engines and Earth's own engineering. Their drives filled much of their hulls, failed often and never carried them far without Asgard's help. None of them outlasted the Third World War. The true beginning of Earth's travel among the stars was Zefram Cochrane's Phoenix in 2063.

Borrowed engines

By 2002 the Stargate programme had captured enough Goa'uld machinery to try building ships of its own. Earth did not understand most of what it had taken. It copied what it could, round power plants fed with naquadah, then built hulls around the engines that were as large as a building.

Asgard gave it none of its machines. The Aesir teach younger peoples and leave them to build for themselves, as Thor told the Tau'ri more than once. What Earth flew, it had made, and it showed.

The ships

The first was the Prometheus, launched in 2002. Its drive was so unreliable that its crew were glad to reach a neighbouring star on schedule. When Thor needed SG-1 on Hala in the Pegasus galaxy early in 2003, an Asgard ship carried the Prometheus there, since its own engines could never have reached so far. It was destroyed in 2005.

From 2005 came the ships of the BC-304 class, longer, better armed, a little more dependable: the Daedalus, the Odyssey, the Russian Korolev, then the Apollo and the Chinese Sun Tzu. The Korolev was lost in 2006 at the Ori's great gate. The Odyssey was the ship aboard which Thor set down the lore of the Aesir for the Tau'ri at Orilla in 2007. It reached Orilla only because Asgard had called it there and opened the way.

Crude and costly

Each ship cost as much as a small country's navy, and Earth could afford only a handful. Their drives and power plants took up so much room that the crews lived in what was left. They broke down far from home more often than anybody outside the programme was told. Without Asgard's help, no Tau'ri ship ever crossed from one galaxy to another.

They were kept secret, like the Stargate itself. When the Third World War broke out in 2026 the programme was lost with much else. Neither the ships nor the yards in Nevada survived the war. One of the BC-304s was destroyed in space with the Stargate itself aboard, and nobody on Earth ever knew.

The Phoenix

In 2063 Zefram Cochrane flew the Phoenix at warp speed from a missile complex near Bozeman, Montana. His engine worked on a principle of his own, learnt from what the lore of the Aesir told of the Rainbow Bridge, which carries a traveller from world to world without crossing the space between. It was small enough to fit inside the body of an old missile. The rest of the lore of the Aesir stayed classified, and in later years Section 31 kept it.

What the Odyssey and its sister battlecruisers had needed a hull the length of a warship to do, badly, at ruinous cost, the Phoenix did with an engine a few men could carry. That is why its flight, not theirs, is counted the true beginning of Earth's travel among the stars.

The Vulcans, who had watched Earth for many years, saw it the same way. They made themselves known only to a people who had built a warp engine of their own, and ships flying on captured Goa'uld engines did not count.

pages.title: Ecaterina the Wise
infobox: The Prometheans, the idealists of her clan
The Camarilla from its founding; later, in secret, the Sabbat
A Sabbat archbishop in New York, under the name Catherine Weiss
pages.html:
Ecaterina the Wise is a Brujah elder: a scholar, and an idealist of the faction called the Prometheans. In the twelfth century she led the Brujah of Prague, and in 1141 she Embraced the crusader Christof Romuald. She later went over in secret from the Camarilla to the Sabbat. By 1999 she was a Sabbat archbishop in New York, fighting those of her own sect who served the Methuselah Vukodlak.

The Brujah of Prague

In the twelfth century Ecaterina led the Brujah of Prague. She was a scholar before she was anything else. She belonged to the Prometheans, the Brujah who still believe that the Kindred can be better than their Beast, and who still dream of what Carthage was before Rome destroyed it. To a Promethean, Carthage is the proof that Kindred and mortals could once live side by side.

Her right hand was her childe Cosmas. His own childe, Wilhem Streicher, was among her most loyal followers.

Prague in those nights lay between the Tremere and the Tzimisce, who were making ready for war with one another. Ecaterina meant the Brujah to be neither side's pawns, which in Prague in those years was a great deal easier to mean than to manage.

Christof

In 1141 a French crusader, Christof Romuald, went down alone into a silver mine near Prague and killed the Tzimisce monster that had been preying on the city. Ecaterina saw what he was worth. She Embraced him that same night, before any other clan could claim him, and he became her childe, of the ninth generation.

She set Christof's coterie against both the Tremere and the Tzimisce. She watched him lose his faith but keep his humanity. She lost him in the 1140s, when Vyšehrad fell and buried him beneath its ruins.

Camarilla and Sabbat

When the Camarilla was founded in the fifteenth century, Ecaterina belonged to it. In time she came to think that it had turned the Kindred into jailers and courtiers. She had hoped to see them free, and better than they were. She and Wilhem went over to the Sabbat in secret.

The Sabbat disappointed her too. The sect that had promised revolution became, in her eyes, one more vehicle for the old politics of the clans.

New York, 1999

By 1999 Ecaterina was a Sabbat archbishop in New York, going by the name Catherine Weiss. Within her own sect she fought the faction that served the Methuselah Vukodlak and meant to raise him. When the Society of Leopold woke Christof in London, Wilhem found him and brought him back into her cause. Christof went on to destroy Vukodlak in the Cathedral of Flesh.

Later years

In the first years of the new century Christof was at her side once more. With him and the Kindred scholar Beckett she travelled to Tunis. Word had come that the resting place of the fallen Antediluvian of the Brujah, destroyed long ago by his own childe Troile, lay beneath a dam near the city, not far from the ruins of Carthage.

pages.title: Eddie Dombrowski
infobox: Part-time attendant at a petrol station
September 1994, killed by James Sunderland under Toluca Prison
pages.html:
Eddie Dombrowski was a young man of twenty-three who turned up in Silent Hill in September 1994, on the run. He had been laughed at for his weight all his life. Shortly before he came to the town he had shot a dog dead and wounded its owner. In Silent Hill he went on to kill people, and James Sunderland killed him.

Before Silent Hill

Eddie was born about 1971. He worked part-time at a petrol station. He was very fat, and for as long as he could remember people had called him names for it. For the most part he took it quietly.

One day he stopped taking it. He shot a dog that belonged to a footballer who had tormented him. Then he shot the footballer in the knee, so that the man would never play again. He ran before the police came, and ended in Silent Hill.

The town

James Sunderland found him in a block of flats, on his knees in a lavatory, being sick. There was a dead man in the refrigerator in the kitchen. Eddie said at once that he had not done it. He had not done anything, he said. James had not asked.

They met again in a bowling alley, where Eddie was eating pizza. A small girl called Laura was keeping him company. She was rude to him, which he did not seem to mind. He let her run off alone into the town. When James was angry about it, Eddie could not see what the fuss was about.

By the time James reached the old prison, Eddie had a revolver. There was a body at his feet. He was tired of being laughed at, he explained. It did not matter whether a person was clever, stupid, ugly or handsome: everybody was the same once they were dead. When James asked whether he really thought he could kill people for that, Eddie laughed. He had only been joking, he said.

The cold store

They met for the last time in a cold store under the prison, hung with sides of meat. Eddie had worked it out by then. The town had called James as well, he said, so James was no better than he was. Then he started shooting.

James killed him. He stood over the body afterwards, appalled, for he had never knowingly killed a human being before. It was some hours before he learnt how wrong he was about that.

pages.title: Eileen Galvin
infobox: The twentieth sacrament, the Mother Reborn
pages.html:
Eileen Galvin was the young woman who lived in Room 303 of South Ashfield Heights, next door to Henry Townshend. As a very small girl she had once given her doll to a ragged stranger. He was Walter Sullivan. In June 2004 he chose her to be the twentieth of his twenty-one sacraments, the Mother Reborn. She was the first of his chosen victims to be attacked by him and live.

The doll
