When Eileen was a small girl she met a ragged young man, a stranger, and gave him her doll. He was Walter Sullivan, who came every week in those years to stand outside the door of Room 302.

She forgot all about it. Walter Sullivan did not. Ten years after his own death he still had the doll. He handed it to Henry Townshend as a present, remarking that Miss Galvin had given it to him a long time ago.

Room 303

By June 2004 Eileen was living on her own in Room 303. She noticed that the man in 302 had not been seen for days. She spoke about it to the superintendent, Frank Sunderland, whose key would not open the door.

The journalist Joseph Schreiber, who had lived in 302 before Henry, had worried about her in his turn. Her name was in his diary. He had worked out who the twentieth sacrament was to be.

The twentieth sacrament

Walter Sullivan came for her in her own flat on the evening of 21 June 2004. He beat her with his fists until she could not stand. He did not finish. A small boy came into the room and stood between them. He was Walter too, the child that Walter had once been, who remembered the doll. Eileen was taken to St Jerome's Hospital alive.

Henry Townshend found her in the dark copy of that hospital which lay on the far side of Room 302. Her arm was broken. She could not go back to the waking world through the holes that Henry used, so she went on with him.

She was useful. She could read writing on the walls that meant nothing to Henry, and she hit the things that came at them with her handbag, for want of anything better. All the while Walter's hold on her was growing. Towards the end she was not always herself. She left Henry to follow the small boy, who wanted his mother.

Afterwards

In the last place of all, Eileen walked like a sleeper towards a wheel of turning blades, a step at a time, while Henry fought Walter Sullivan beside it. When Walter died, on 22 June, she stopped.

She woke properly in a bed at St Jerome's. Henry came to visit her with a bunch of flowers. She told him that she would have to find a new place to live.

pages.title: Eubulon
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Advent Master Returns' (14 November 2009)
The Advent Decks; the Advent Void; the teleport that works through reflections
From 1947 to 14 November 2009, in the keeping of the No-Men
pages.html:
Eubulon is the Advent Master, the scientist of Karsh who made the Advent Decks and founded the Kamen Riders of Ventara. He was once the servant of Xaviax. In 1947 Xaviax struck him down, and the blow threw him to Earth. In the summer of 1994 he lies in a frozen sleep in the keeping of the No-Men, a secret office of the American government, as he has for more than forty years. Len of Ventara woke him in November 2009. Within five weeks the vented Riders were free and Xaviax was dead.

The scientist of Karsh

Eubulon comes from Karsh, where Xaviax was the leader. He was Xaviax's chief scientist. When the wars of Karsh had left the planet in ruins, Xaviax ordered him to find other worlds whose people could be taken as slaves to rebuild it. Eubulon built a teleport that worked through reflections. It brought him to Ventara.

There he fell gravely ill. The Ventarans took him in. They nursed him until he was well. He found afterwards that he could not go through with it.

The Advent Master

He changed sides. He warned Ventara that Xaviax was coming, then set about arming it. For twelve chosen Ventarans he made the Advent Decks, each locked to its owner's body, each contracted to a beast of the mirror world. He called the twelve Kamen Riders. He led them as the Advent Master, in armour of his own.

He also made the Advent Void, a refuge between the worlds. A Rider beaten in battle would be carried there, to lie safe in a frozen sleep until Eubulon could fetch him out. Nobody but the Advent Master can open it.

So that his Riders might outlast a long war, he arranged for them to sleep in suspended animation. Each woke to stand guard for one year in twelve.

The fall to Earth

In 1947 Eubulon met Xaviax in battle on Ventara. Xaviax beat him. The blow that should have sent him into the Void threw him across to Earth instead. He came down, senseless, near Roswell in the desert of New Mexico.

The Americans who found him could not heal him, so he was kept in a frozen sleep, sealed in a capsule. The secret office that guarded him came to be called the No-Men.

The American government has never been frank about what came down near Roswell that year. More than one thing did, and he was only one of them. It was Eubulon. He slept for sixty-two years.

Without him the Void became a prison. Every Rider vented after he was lost stayed vented, with nobody to bring him back.

The waking

On 14 November 2009 Len of Ventara, by then the last Rider on either world, held up his Advent Deck to the sleeper at the headquarters of the No-Men. Eubulon woke.

He went to work at once. He altered the lock on Kase's deck so that Maya Young, a woman of Earth, could fight as Siren. He opened the Void. First he brought out three Ventaran Riders: Chance, Price and Hunt. Kit Taylor came next, with Kase. For Kit he made a new deck, Onyx. He wrote a virus to kill the transmitters with which Xaviax meant to carry off the people of Earth.

He was a patient master. When Kit was about to vent the traitor Adam of Ventara, Eubulon stopped him, then let the traitor speak. He sparred with Len to teach him to rule his anger. He told Kit and Maya Young the truth about himself, that he had built the teleport for Xaviax before he ever built a deck against him. Xaviax once took Eubulon's face in order to frighten his spy.

The end of Xaviax

On 18 December 2009 Eubulon laid the plan for the last attack. He fought Xaviax himself in the control room of Xaviax's stronghold. He held him there until thirteen Riders arrived to finish it with the Link Vent.

Afterwards he emptied the Void. The men of Earth whom Xaviax had armed were sent home with their memories of the war removed. He cured Chris Ramirez of his asthma as well. He offered Kit Taylor the choice of the two dragon decks, to keep, which made Kit a Kamen Rider for good.

pages.title: Excalibur (team)
infobox: Excalibur Special Edition: The Sword Is Drawn (on sale 1 December 1987)
December 1987, in London and the Scottish Highlands
Captain Britain, Meggan, Kitty Pryde, Kurt Wagner and Rachel Summers, with Lockheed the dragon
The Braddock Lighthouse (1988 to 1992); Braddock Manor (1992 to 1993); Muir Island (from 1993)
Captain Britain at first; Kurt Wagner for most of the 1990s
Kurt Wagner, Kitty Pryde, Lockheed the dragon, Meggan, Brian Braddock (as Britanic), Moira MacTaggert and Douglock

Widget the robot (1988); Kylun (1991); Cerise of the Shi'ar (1991); Feron (1992); Micromax (1993); Moira MacTaggert (1993); Amanda Sefton (1994); Douglock (1994); Pete Wisdom (1995); Rahne Sinclair (1995); Piotr Rasputin (1995)
The Weird Happenings Organisation; later Black Air
August 1998, after the wedding of Brian Braddock and Meggan
pages.html:
The Excalibur team is a band of British heroes, founded at the end of 1987 by two X-Men who believed themselves the last of their team, a third who had come out of a future that will now never happen, Captain Britain and Meggan. They took their name from King Arthur's sword, as a sign that Charles Xavier's dream would not die with his students. They spent their first years in a lighthouse on the west coast of England where a great many worlds meet. In the summer of 1994 they live on Muir Island, off the north-west coast of Scotland. The team broke up in 1998, after Captain Britain's wedding.

The fall of the X-Men, 1987

In the autumn of 1987 the X-Men died in Dallas, or seemed to, in front of the television cameras of the world. They had given their lives to bind a demon called the Adversary. The cameras did not see Roma of Otherworld draw their souls back before they had passed beyond the world, then restore them to their bodies. She hid them from every camera on Earth. The X-Men let the world go on believing them dead, to keep the people they loved out of harm's way.

Kitty Pryde and Kurt Wagner, badly hurt in the massacre of the Morlocks the year before, were recovering at Moira MacTaggert's research station on Muir Island. Kitty watched the X-Men die on television there. Brian Braddock, Captain Britain, learnt that his twin sister, Psylocke, had died with them. He shut himself up with a bottle in the lighthouse he shared with Meggan, and he would not come out.

The founding, December 1987

At the start of December 1987 Rachel Summers came to Britain on the run from Mojo, a slaver of another world who had kept her for his entertainments. His Warwolves were on her trail, creatures that wear the skins of the people they kill. So were the Technet, bounty hunters from other worlds whom Saturnyne had hired. They raided Muir Island and carried off Kitty, with Meggan, who had gone there for Kitty's advice.

Kurt got away, sobered Brian up by dropping him in the sea and went with him to London. There they freed Kitty, Meggan and Rachel, then turned the Warwolves on the Technet. Both bands went home beaten.

Afterwards the five of them sat round a campfire in the Scottish Highlands, talking about the friends they had lost. Rachel would not let Xavier's dream die with his students, and she proposed a new team named for King Arthur's sword, Britain's old sign of hope. None of them knew how near the mark Rachel had come: Brian is of Arthur's blood, though he does not know it.

The meeting was no accident, as Brian learnt years later. Roma had set the Technet on Rachel's trail through Saturnyne, so that the five would come together.

London and the lighthouse, 1988 to 1989

In the summer of 1988 the team caught the Warwolves in London, and they were put on show at London Zoo. That autumn it moved into the Braddock Lighthouse, whose cellar opened more than once on other worlds.

With the Crazy Gang, Arcade the assassin took Courtney Ross, Brian's old love, as bait. He trapped the team in a Murderworld at Strangeways, in Manchester. Kitty and Lockheed got them out. Days later Opul Lun Sat-yr-9, a tyrant from another Britain who wears Saturnyne's face, killed Courtney and took her place. Nobody noticed for years.

Over the winter Rachel dreamt that demons threatened her baby brother, Nathan, and flew to a Manhattan overrun by demons out of Limbo. The demons made Meggan their Goblin Princess for a while, until Kitty called up the Soulsword of her friend Illyana Rasputin to set Meggan and Brian free.

In the spring of 1989 Brigadier Alysande Stuart of the Weird Happenings Organisation called the team in. Moira MacTaggert and Callisto had been swept off to a world where the Nazis had won the war. Nazi doubles of the team, the Lightning Squad, came through from that world to attack the Tower of London. At the exchange of prisoners at the old Fenborough station a small atomic bomb came through the closing gate. Rachel held the blast. The backlash swept the whole team away, with Professor Alistaire Stuart and a train from the Nazis' world.

Across the worlds, 1989 to 1990

From the summer of 1989 to the spring of 1990 the team wandered from world to world aboard the train, with a little robot called Widget opening the gates. The journey came to be called the Cross-Time Caper. They saw a Britain of knights, a world that Galactus destroyed for being too silly to exist and a London where Meggan had become Captain Britain. At the end of it Saturnyne mended Widget and sent them home.

The train came up beneath the lighthouse in the spring of 1990, and Galactus was waiting there. He had come to destroy Rachel's body, with the Phoenix Force inside it. Rachel made up her mind to give herself up for the Earth's sake, and in the end Galactus let her be.

At home, 1990 to 1991

In the autumn Kitty took a post at St Searle's School for Young Ladies, then helped to save it from closure.

In the spring of 1991 an old man who called himself Myrd helped the team free Meggan at Braddock Manor from the restless wraith of the Changeling, a mutant who had died in Xavier's service long before. Nobody guessed who he was. He was Gandalf, whom Brian knew as Merlin and had mourned as dead, sent back. He showed himself openly only the next year.

Soon afterwards Victor von Doom asked Kitty to draw Illyana's Soulsword for him, from the stone outside the lighthouse where it had stood since 1989. He meant to turn the demon realm of Limbo into promethium, a new source of power, and make the world buy it from Latveria. The team stopped him in Limbo with the West Coast Avengers, whom the Lady of the Lake, Roma of Otherworld, had called to help.

In the summer of 1991 the Warwolves got loose and came to the team in the shapes of the X-Men. When they had been dealt with, the team, who knew by then that the X-Men were alive, sent word to them. Cable answered.

New friends and the end of the lighthouse, 1991 to 1993

In the summer of 1991 Saturnyne called off her warrant on Rachel. She exiled the Technet to Earth, and Kurt, over Brian's objections, let them live at the lighthouse. Over the next year the team took in Kylun, a Scottish boy grown into a warrior in another world, Cerise of the Shi'ar, a fugitive from her own people, and Feron, a young mystic with a claim of his own on the Phoenix Force.

In the spring of 1992 Necrom, a sorcerer from the world where Kylun grew up, came to the lighthouse for the Phoenix Force and for the web of power that binds the worlds together. Gandalf had let his enemies go on thinking him dead, so that Necrom would show himself. Rachel let Necrom take the Phoenix's whole power, which destroyed him. It left her all but dead, and the lighthouse in ruins.

The team moved to Braddock Manor. That summer the Phoenix Force carried Rachel away to the stars to heal her. In the autumn Brian asked Meggan to marry him, and she said yes. Rachel came home early in 1993.

In 1993 Rachel took the team into the future she had been born in, where she and Kate Pryde, Kitty's older self, set the Sentinels that ruled it to protecting all life. On the way home Brian was lost in the stream of time. Cerise went back to the Shi'ar to face trial, and Kylun went to look for his parents.

Muir Island, 1993 to 1994

In September 1993 Piotr Rasputin, Kitty's old love, left the X-Men for Magneto's Acolytes. Kitty lured him down to Muir Island, but he went back to the Acolytes all the same. Afterwards the team stayed on the island to help Moira MacTaggert with her research, and Muir Island has been its home ever since.

Early in 1994 Brian came back out of the stream of time. Rachel went into it in his place, with Meggan and Amanda Sefton, an old friend of Kurt's, beside her. Brian came home cold and distant, under a new name, Britanic. That year the team also took in Douglock, a being of living metal who carries the memories of Kitty's dead friend Doug Ramsey.

The team in 1994

In the summer of 1994 the Excalibur team lives at Moira MacTaggert's research station on Muir Island. Kurt Wagner leads it. With him are Kitty Pryde, Lockheed the dragon, Meggan, Brian Braddock, Moira MacTaggert and Douglock. Amanda Sefton comes and goes.

The team has not gone to war with Khan Noonien Singh. Britain's government has kept it at home through the Augment War, under the Security Council's rules on superhumans. It keeps an eye instead on the Friends of Humanity, who have been holding meetings in British church halls under the slogan KEEP BRITAIN HUMAN, since a good many of the island's people are mutants.

The only witch who has ever served with the team is Amanda Sefton, a Romani witch taught by her own tribe, who joined it as Daytripper early in 1994. Muggles take her magic for a mutant power. Captain Britain's power is an Elvish enchantment of Otherworld, not wizardry. The Ministry of Magic, which keeps a file on him, has never had any dealings with the team. The government bodies the team works with, the Weird Happenings Organisation and RCX among them, are Muggle services, which may know that a Ministry of Magic exists but have nothing to do with it.

Later years, 1994 to 1998

From late in 1994 Black Air took over the Weird Happenings Organisation's dealings with the team. In 1995 Pete Wisdom, a Black Air agent, left the service to join the team. Kitty fell in love with him, and Lockheed took against him at once. Rahne Sinclair and Piotr Rasputin came to the island that year.

In 1995 Kurt found out that Moira had the Legacy Virus, the plague that was killing mutants. In the summer of 1996, while the X-Men were fighting for their lives in New York, Kurt's foster mother, Margali Szardos, loosed a demon bound beneath London. Kurt led the team into Black Air's headquarters, where they freed Douglock, through whom she had worked, then bound the demon again. That year Brian took back the name of Captain Britain.

In 1997 Brian went away for a time. While he was gone, Meggan and Piotr were drawn to each other. Early in 1998 Pete left the island, after he and Kitty had come to the end of things.

Brian and Meggan were married in Otherworld on 19 August 1998, with Roma of Otherworld presiding. The guests included the Captain Britain Corps, the Technet, the Crazy Gang and the Lightning Squad. Afterwards Kitty, Kurt and Piotr went back to the X-Men. That was the end of the team. Roma and Gandalf agreed that the sword might yet be drawn again, when the time was right.

pages.title: Fenrir Greyback
infobox: The Wyrm; Lord Voldemort's followers in the First Wizarding War
Biting children; the bite that made Remus Lupin
pages.html:
Fenrir Greyback is a Garou who makes others of his kind by the bite, deliberately, and who prefers to choose children. He is the werewolf who bit Remus Lupin when Lupin was a very small boy.

Life

Greyback is a big, grey-haired man with long yellowish nails and pointed teeth. He smells of dirt, sweat and blood. He has never put his name on the Ministry's Werewolf Registry, and he has never kept any wizarding law.

In the 1960s he was brought before the Ministry of Magic's Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures over the deaths of two Muggle children. He passed himself off as a Muggle vagrant, and was let go, because nobody on the committee knew what he was. The wizard who questioned him, Lyall Lupin, an authority on Boggarts, poltergeists and other non-human spirits, told the hearing that werewolves were soulless, evil things, fit for nothing but death. Greyback took his revenge on Lyall's son. He found the boy, Remus, asleep in his bed, and bit him.

In the First Wizarding War he ran with Lord Voldemort's supporters, who promised him prey in return for his help. He spread terror by threatening to set his teeth in the children of those who stood against them.

Greyback and the Garou

Most Garou are born, not made, and their law frowns on making new Garou by the bite. Those who do it all the same serve the Wyrm. Severus Snape once told a class that the fallen tribe's 'get are still abroad, still making others by the bite, still extremely particular in their choosing'. That marks Greyback as one of the tribe that went over, the Black Spiral Dancers. He seeks out the young, above all the children of wizards, so that he can raise them apart from their families to hate wizardkind. He means one day to make enough of his kind to overwhelm the wizards altogether.

Remus Lupin, whom he made, grew up to be his opposite: a Garou who fights the Wyrm. Lupin has said only that he was a very small boy when he was bitten, and that his parents tried everything to cure him.

Garou made by the bite are called the biteborn. Among the thirteen tribes they are rare, and despised as no true Garou, even though they are Garou by every measure. Among the Black Spiral Dancers they are common, and Greyback has made more of them than most. Lupin is his biteborn. The tribes suspect that a bitten Garou carries the taint of whatever bit him, and Lupin has had to live that suspicion down all his life.

pages.title: Feron
infobox: A monastery in County Sligo, Ireland
The last of a line of sentinels said to be a thousand generations long, going back to the days of the Flood
The mystic power of his line; floats in the air
That the Phoenix Force was meant for him
The Executioner of the Crazy Gang
pages.html:
Feron is a pale, elfin young mystic from County Sligo, the last of a line of sentinels that the monks who raised him say goes back to the days of the Flood. He was brought up to receive the Phoenix Force, and he never forgave Rachel Summers for having it instead. He served with the Excalibur team from 1992 until the summer of 1993, when he fell into a sleep while trying to wake Meggan, and was lost. His magic is the inheritance of his line, not a wizard's, and the wizarding world has never heard of him.

The monastery

Feron was brought up by monks in a monastery in County Sligo. From his birth they kept his feet from touching the ground, binding them in the skin of a black boar of the old stories, because the power of his line would come into him when his bare feet touched the earth. When the team first saw him he was floating in the air, reading Yeats.

His line had kept watch for the Phoenix Force for a thousand generations. The first Feron had called on it long ago, and had stood against Necrom, a sorcerer of another world who wanted it for himself.

In January 1992 Alistaire Stuart's survey of a prehistoric site nearby uncovered a crypt, deep underground, where a dark power lay: the Anti-Phoenix. Feron's magic helped to stop it. Then he found that the Phoenix Force had chosen Rachel Summers, and he was outraged: she was not worthy of it, he said. Brother Francis, his teacher, scolded him, then asked the team to take him with them.

The Excalibur team

He fought Necrom beside the team in the spring of 1992, and went with it to Braddock Manor, where he proved unable to cook. In the summer of 1993, with Captain Britain lost in time and Meggan sunk in a grief from which nobody could wake her, Feron put on Brian's likeness to bring her back. He fell into the same sleep himself.

Nobody knew what became of him after that. In August 1998, on the eve of Brian Braddock's wedding, he attacked Braddock Manor as the new Executioner of the Crazy Gang. He said that he had been lost ever since Meggan's long sleep.

pages.title: Flabber
infobox: In the pipe organ at Hillhurst, until 7 September 1996
The wish that made the Beetleborgs
Drew McCormick, Jo McCormick, Roland Williams
pages.html:
Flabber is a phasm: a wish-granting spirit with a pale blue face, a great quiff of black hair, a very large chin and a suit that glitters. In the summer of 1994 he is shut inside the pipe organ at Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville. On 7 September 1996 three children let him out. The wish he granted them in thanks made them the Beetleborgs, as he had intended. It also let their enemies out of a comic book, which he had not.

A phasm

A phasm is a spirit of its own kind, nearer to a genie or a poltergeist than to a ghost. Flabber is not one of the restless dead, the wraiths, any more than Peeves of Hogwarts is. Like a genie he can be shut up inside a thing, and like a genie he grants wishes. The poltergeist in him shows in everything else. He cannot be serious for two minutes together.

He looks a good deal like Elvis Presley, with something of Liberace thrown in. Three singing spirits called the Pipettes live in the organ. They sing behind him whenever he performs, which is often.

The pipe organ

How Flabber came to be shut in the organ at Hillhurst is not recorded. In the summer of 1994 he is still inside it, with the house falling slowly to pieces round him.

On 7 September 1996 three children of Charterville came into the house on a dare: Drew McCormick, his sister, Jo, and their friend Roland Williams. The household chased them. In the chase they knocked against the organ, which let Flabber out. He was so pleased that he offered them a wish.

The wish

The three wished to be the Beetleborgs, the heroes of their favourite comic book. Flabber's magic can make drawn things real. It gave them the armour, the weapons, the machines and a gift apiece besides.

It did not stop there. The comic book had villains in it too, Vexor with his Magnavores, who came out of the pages by the same door. Flabber's magic has a way of bringing out more than was asked for.

The Beetleborgs' powers remained his magic for as long as they had them. When he was ill, they failed. He made himself the three children's friend, counsellor and host, with Hillhurst as their meeting place. He also saw to it that the rest of the household did not eat them.

Magic

Flabber works from a spellbook, which other people ought not to touch. In September 1996 it turned Jo invisible. In April 1997 Wolfgang Smith got hold of it, with the result that Jo's face was changed for good. All Flabber could do was to lay a second spell over the first, so that the town went on seeing the girl it knew.

He can go into a comic book or fetch things out of one. In September 1996 he took Drew into a comic after an amulet. In October he called two heroes, Karato and Silver Ray, out of other comics to help the Beetleborgs at a convention. That November he fetched the pirate Blackbeard out of the past to help the children with their history homework, which went about as well as might be expected.

Whatever Art Fortunes drew, Flabber could bring to life. That was how the White Blaster Beetleborg was made in November 1996. It was how the three came by the Metallix armour in September 1997. The Sector Cycles, their three motorcycles, were his own idea.

In December 1996 the children helped him to keep Christmas, which he had never done before. The Magnavores tried to steal it. They did not succeed.

Enemies

Anybody who wanted the Beetleborgs beaten went for Flabber first. In September 1996 the brothers Trip and Van, who did not know what the children had become, hired a phasm hunter to clear the house. In May 1997 Flabber was shut back into the organ for a time, while Nukus built the monster Borgslayer. On 8 September 1997 Nukus turned him to ice.

In October 1997 Horribelle left a portrait of him on the porch. It drained the life out of him as he admired it, so that he grew old before his time. He would not hear of destroying it, because he looked so handsome in it.

In November the Mantrons poisoned him, which stopped the Beetleborgs' powers altogether until he was cured. Later that month the Crustaceans carried him off. They demanded the Astral Sword, with all eight Astral Coins, as his ransom. The bargain fell through, but he was rescued.

The Power Rangers

Zordon of Eltar never met Flabber. In October 1996, after the Zeo Rangers had fought beside the Beetleborgs in Charterville, Billy Cranston admitted that he could make no sense of the Beetleborgs' powers. Zordon told him that they were a spirit's work, not a machine's, which was why.

On 3 May 1997 the space pirate Divatox sent her nephew, Elgar, to Hillhurst with a crew of Piranhatrons, to fetch her the spirit that granted wishes. The household defended him with enthusiasm. Elgar got him away in a sack regardless. At the cemetery gates Divatox wished for more treasure than she could carry, which Flabber, who would do a good deal to be let out of a sack, duly granted.

A pirate's chest came up out of the nearest comic book. Behind it came Davy Bones, the monster that guarded it in the story. When the Turbo Rangers destroyed the monster, the chest turned back into paper. Divatox never asked him for anything again.

That evening Flabber had the Turbo Rangers to supper at Hillhurst, where the youngest of them took off his helmet. He was Justin Stewart, twelve years old. On 25 October 1997, when Justin telephoned for help, Flabber sent the three Beetleborgs to Angel Grove in a blink. His aim was a little off, since he had never seen the place. They landed in the lake.

pages.title: Frank Taylor
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
A city in the United States
pages.html:
Frank Taylor is the father of Kit Taylor. In the summer of 1994 he lives in an American city, where his son is three years old. About December 2007 he vanished. Xaviax had drained the life out of him, then left him lying in a hospital, in a sleep that nothing could break. For the next two years Xaviax used him as a lever against his son. He woke when Xaviax was destroyed.

The disappearance

Frank brought Kit up in a flat in the city. About a year before Kit's eighteenth birthday he disappeared. It was the time when Xaviax's mirror monsters had begun to take people, and Frank was put down as one more of the missing. Kit went into foster care.

Xaviax had picked Frank out for a reason. Kit was the mirror twin of the first Dragon Knight, so the Dragon Knight's deck would open for him. Xaviax wanted the boy as his own Rider. In December 2008 he sent Kit visions of his father in mirrors, which led him to the deck.

The hospital

On 7 February 2009 Maya Young and Trent Moseley found Frank in a hospital. Kit was at his bedside a week later. Frank was alive, but he knew nobody.

Drew Lansing, one of Xaviax's Riders, told Kit that there was a cure. Len of Ventara told him that there was none. Kit visited him often.

The hostage

In August 2009 Strike, another of Xaviax's Riders, took Frank out of the hospital. On 4 September he offered to hand him back in return for Len's Advent Deck. Kit refused. While the fight went on, Maya Young got Frank away. He went back to the hospital.

On 19 September Xaviax came to the hospital himself. He woke Frank for a few moments. He would do it for good, he told Kit, once Kit had vented the Wing Knight. Kit did not do it. On 3 October the No-Men seized Kit as he was leaving his father's room.

The waking

Xaviax was destroyed on 18 December 2009. Frank recovered. He had his son back, two years older than he had left him, a Kamen Rider.

pages.title: Frankenbeans
infobox: None; a younger creature of the same maker, Little Frankie
pages.html:
Frankenbeans, called Frankie, is the creature of Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville. Dr Baron von Frankenbeans built him out of parts. That makes him the one member of the household who is nobody's kin, for he was never born, sired or bitten. He is very large, very strong and not at all clever.

The doctor's work

Frankenbeans owes his existence to a scientist, Dr Baron von Frankenbeans, who has never been quite satisfied with him. In October 1996 the doctor came to Hillhurst to put right what he saw as his creature's faults. In March 1997 an operation made Frankenbeans clever for a time. It also made him an unbearable snob, so nobody was sorry when it wore off.

The doctor went on building. In October 1997 he sent a smaller creature, Little Frankie, to live at Hillhurst with his big brother. In February 1998 he brought his newest work, a plant called Monster Mother. The Crustaceans tried to steal it, only to find that they could not control it.

In March 1998 the household learnt why Frankenbeans had never been clever. There was no brain in his head at all.

Hillhurst

Frankenbeans was one of the three who chased Drew McCormick, his sister, Jo, and Roland Williams through the house on 7 September 1996. On Hallowe'en that year he got out into Charterville by himself. The children went after him, with one of Vexor's monsters close behind.

In April 1997 he was to be married. The bride turned out to be after money. One of Vexor's monsters broke up the wedding in any case. On 3 May 1997 Elgar, the nephew of the space pirate Divatox, broke into Hillhurst with a crew of Piranhatrons to carry off Flabber. Frankenbeans met them in the hall. When the Turbo Rangers arrived he had a Piranhatron under each arm.

pages.title: Franklin Richards
infobox: Reed Richards and Sue Richards, of the Fantastic Four
Dr Franklin Storm, his mother's father
Power over what is real; telepathy and other powers of the mind
About twenty-six; keeps out of the public eye
Catching the fallen of Onslaught, August 1996, and bringing them home late in 1997
pages.html:
Franklin Richards is the son of Reed and Sue Richards of the Fantastic Four. He was born in 1968, so he is a man of about twenty-six in the summer of 1994. He was born a mutant with power over what is real, one of the most powerful ever known, and he has spent most of his life keeping it in check. In 1996 Onslaught carried him off to use that power against the world. When his parents and their friends gave themselves up to destroy Onslaught that August, Franklin caught them as they fell, then carried them into a world of his own making. He did not know that he had done it until the Celestials came to him late in 1997, and then he brought them home.

Birth, 1968

Franklin was born in New York in 1968, three years after his parents married. His birth very nearly killed his mother and himself with her. The cosmic rays that had changed the family in 1961 were in Sue's blood, and the baby could not be born safely.

Reed went into the Negative Zone, a dark universe that lies alongside our own, with Ben Grimm and Johnny Storm. There they took a device from Annihilus, the insect lord who rules it. With it Reed brought mother and son safely through. The boy was named after Sue's father, Dr Franklin Storm, who had died some years before.

The sleeping power, 1973 to 1974

Franklin's power woke when he was about five. It drew Annihilus out of the Negative Zone to feed on it. It went on building in the boy until Reed feared that it would destroy all life on Earth. To stop it, he turned a machine on his own son and shut down his mind.

Sue was so angry that he had done it without asking her that she left him, and the Fantastic Four, for a time. Franklin lay for months in a sleep like death.

In 1974 the robot Ultron came uninvited to Quicksilver's wedding to Crystal, where the Fantastic Four, the Avengers and the Inhumans were gathered. His governess, Agatha Harkness, brought the sleeping boy there. Ultron's beams woke Franklin, whose power struck back through them and destroyed him. Afterwards the power seemed to have burnt itself out. It had only gone to ground.

Growing up

Franklin grew up among heroes. The Thing was the nearest thing he had to an uncle, and the Human Torch was his uncle in fact. His father built machines to hold his power in check, and as he grew older he learnt to hold it himself. He was nineteen when the family moved into Four Freedoms Plaza in 1987.

In the summer of 1994 Franklin is about twenty-six. He keeps out of the newspapers, which in his family takes some doing, and he has never worn a costume or taken a name. He uses his power as little as he can, since he has known since he was five what it can do.

Onslaught, 1996

For months before Onslaught showed himself, Franklin dreamt of a friend who called himself Charlie. The voice in his dreams was kind, and it seemed to understand what it was like to be afraid of one's own power. Franklin told nobody about it.

In the summer of 1996 Charles Xavier came to Four Freedoms Plaza and asked for Franklin to come to his school, to learn to govern his power. Reed and Sue refused. So did Franklin, who was old enough to answer for himself. Xavier was Onslaught by then. He struck them all down, with the Avengers who came to help, and carried Franklin away.

Inside Onslaught, Franklin's power was turned against the world, and with it Onslaught raised a black fortress in Central Park. Franklin tried to reach his parents by sending images of himself out into the city. Onslaught twisted them into the family's oldest enemies, but they told Reed and Sue that their son was alive.

His mother reached him at last, travelling in mind with Cable. With them came Apocalypse, who had offered to help, since he would let nobody but himself destroy the world. When they found Franklin, Apocalypse moved to kill him as a danger for the future. Sue stopped him. She told her son not to give up hope, before Onslaught threw them all out.

The catch

In August 1996, in Central Park, Franklin's parents gave themselves up to Onslaught with his uncle, Ben Grimm, most of the Avengers, Bruce Banner and Doctor Doom. Their bodies gave Onslaught a substance the X-Men could strike, and the X-Men destroyed him. Charles Xavier and Cable had gone into the heart of Onslaught to bring Franklin out, with Nate Grey. The two young men fell free as Onslaught broke apart.

In that moment, without knowing that he did it, Franklin caught the others as they fell. Everything in him that could not bear to lose them reached out at once, and it carried them into a world of his own making. The story of that world is told on the page Franklin's world.

The year of mourning, 1996 to 1997

Franklin believed what everyone else believed, that his parents were dead. He mourned them with the world. He could not bear to stay at Four Freedoms Plaza, so he left it empty, and the city later gave it to the Thunderbolts. Alicia Masters, who had loved Ben Grimm, saw him through the worst of it.

All that year he kept a small blue ball by him without knowing why. It held the world he had made.

Ashema and the return, 1997

Late in 1997 the weather went wrong all over the Earth. A woman who called herself Ashema came to Franklin. She was a Celestial, the Listener, one of the vast armoured beings who came to Earth before history began, wearing a shape that a man could bear to look at. She told him what the blue ball was. His parents were alive inside it.

The Celestials had noticed what he had done. They had not thought a man could make a world, and they did not like two Earths standing where there ought to be one. They told Franklin to choose which should go on. He could not choose. Ashema took him into his world instead, to his parents.

There the fallen learnt the truth about themselves. Reed Richards, Tony Stark and Victor von Doom built a ship to carry them home through the Negative Zone. On the way Doom tried to seize Franklin, to take his power for himself. Reed and Thor stopped him. The Celestials let Franklin's world go on, on condition that everyone who belonged to Earth left it and never came back.

Franklin brought them all home, apart from Doom, each of them exactly as old as on the day they fell. He went home with his parents.

The Third World War

Franklin was fifty-eight when the Third World War broke out in 2026. He had used his power as little as he could all his life. In the war he used all of it once, to hold a dying city together long enough for its people to be got out, and it was the death of him.

Powers

Franklin is one of the most powerful mutants ever born. He can reshape what is real, from the stuff of a single room to, as it turned out, a whole world. He has telepathy too, with other powers of the mind, and he can send images of himself far from where he is. The Celestials themselves thought his power a match for their own. He has always used it as little as he can.

pages.title: Franklin's world
aliases: the world in the blue ball
infobox: A small blue ball, which Franklin kept by him
The fallen of Onslaught, from August 1996 until late in 1997
In the keeping of Ashema the Listener
pages.html:
Franklin's world is the world that Franklin Richards made in August 1996, in the moment his parents and their friends were lost destroying Onslaught. He caught them as they fell and carried them into it, without knowing that he had done so. They lived there for more than a year, in new lives, with no memory of who they had been, while the Earth mourned them. Late in 1997 the Celestials found it, and Franklin brought the fallen home.

The making

When the Fantastic Four, nine Avengers, Bruce Banner and Victor von Doom gave themselves to Onslaught in Central Park, Franklin Richards was falling free of Onslaught himself. Everything in him that could not bear to lose his parents reached out at once. It caught them all, and it carried them somewhere Onslaught's end could not follow.

Only God makes out of nothing. Franklin made his world out of his own power and his memories, which is why so much of it looked like home. He did not know that he had made it. For a year he kept a small blue ball by him without knowing why, and the world was inside it.

The world

It was a whole Earth, with its own sun, its own cities and millions of people. Many of them were shaped from Franklin's memories of people he had known or heard of. The fallen lived among them as if they had been born there, since they no longer knew that they had not.

Each of them had a new life, much like the old one, as though it had all begun within living memory. Ben Grimm had flown in the Gulf War. Captain America had a Falcon and a girl Bucky as his partners. The Avengers there had a Swordsman and a Hellcat, both made from Franklin's memory. Tony Stark joined them only later. The Fantastic Four met Doom all over again, with the Sub-Mariner, then made friends with the Black Panther and Crystal.

Bruce Banner became a Hulk of his own in that world, while the Hulk he had been torn from raged on Earth without him. The two halves were never meant to live apart. The longer they were parted, the less steady both worlds became.

Ashema and the Celestials

Late in 1997 the weather went wrong all over the Earth, and the Celestials came to look. The Celestials are the vast armoured beings who came to Earth before history began. They have been called the space gods. They are not God, nor anything like Him, only very old, very large and very curious.

What had caught their eye was a man who had made a world, which they had not thought a man could do, and two Earths standing where there ought to be one. One of them, Ashema the Listener, came to Franklin in the shape of a woman. She told him what the blue ball held. The Celestials wanted him to choose which world should go on. He could not choose, so Ashema took him into his own world, to his parents.

The way home

With Franklin among them, the fallen learnt who they really were. The two Hulks were caught and held. Reed Richards, Tony Stark and Victor von Doom built a great ship to carry everyone home through the Negative Zone.

The Celestials relented, on condition that everyone who belonged to Earth left Franklin's world and never came back. On the way Doom tried to seize Franklin, to take his power for himself. Reed and Thor stopped him, then Thor put him off the ship before it crossed.

As the ship crossed the border between the worlds, the fallen remembered who they had been. The year behind them faded like a dream on waking, so that they kept only scraps of it. The Hulk and Banner were made one again. Franklin brought them all home exactly as old as they had been on the day they fell.

Afterwards

Franklin's world went on without them. The Celestials put it in Ashema's keeping, and she gave up her place among them to look after it herself. Doom alone of Earth's people was left behind in it.

pages.title: Galactus
infobox: The life energy of whole planets
pages.html:
Galactus is a vast cosmic being who keeps himself alive by draining the life energy of whole planets. Just before Christmas 1965 he came to devour the Earth, and the sky over Manhattan seemed to catch fire. The Fantastic Four were said to have talked him out of it. He has come back more than once since, and each time he has been turned away.

Nature

Galactus was once a mortal man, Galan of the world Taa, in the universe that existed before this one. When that universe ended he survived its death, and was reborn in the new one as Galactus. He is now so vast that he must consume the energy of living worlds to go on living. He travels the universe in a great ship and sends heralds ahead of him to find planets that will suit him. The first and most famous of them is the Silver Surfer, once Norrin Radd of Zenn-La, who gave himself to Galactus to spare his own world.

Galactus once ate a world that belonged to one of the Goa'uld System Lords, together with the System Lord. It is the only time the Goa'uld are known to have prayed.

Earth, 1965

In December 1965 the Watcher, an alien observer pledged never to interfere, tried to hide the Earth from the Surfer by setting the sky above New York ablaze. The Surfer found the Earth all the same. Galactus arrived above Manhattan and began to build the engine that would drain it. The Fantastic Four could not stop him by force.

The blind sculptor Alicia Masters turned the Surfer against his master. Johnny Storm was sent into Galactus's ship to fetch the Ultimate Nullifier, the one weapon Galactus feared. Holding it, Reed Richards persuaded Galactus to go. Galactus spared the Earth, and he punished the Surfer by imprisoning him on it.

Days before Galactus came, Maximus had sealed the Inhumans' Great Refuge behind a barrier of negative energy.

Later visits

He came back to Earth in 1972, and again in 1982. On the second occasion the Avengers and the Fantastic Four together drove him to the brink of starvation. Reed Richards saved his life, a mercy for which the Shi'ar Empire later put Richards on trial.

In 1984 Galactus was among those the Beyonder brought to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. There he tried to devour that world too, and Victor von Doom stole his power for a time.

In 1983 he ate the Skrull Throneworld, Tarnax IV, with billions of Skrulls on it.

In the spring of 1990 Galactus came to the Braddock Lighthouse, on the west coast of England, for Rachel Summers of the Excalibur team. He meant to destroy her body and the Phoenix Force inside it. When she resolved to give herself up for the Earth's sake, he let her be.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: an old man at the protest outside the United Nations in August 1994 recalls that just before Christmas in 1965 the sky caught fire over Manhattan, because something had come to eat the world. The Fantastic Four were said to have talked it out of it. His wife had a heart attack on the second day.

pages.title: Garo
infobox: A title, with the golden armour that goes with it
Soul Metal, in the likeness of a golden wolf
Taiga Saejima, to about 1990; Kouga Saejima, from the early 2000s; Raiga Saejima, by 2040
Unclaimed: the sword stands where Taiga Saejima fell
pages.html:
Garo is the Golden Knight, the first in honour among the Makai Knights, who hunt the demons called Horrors in Japan. It is a title, and it is also the suit of golden wolf armour that the title's holder calls down to fight in. For generations it has passed from father to son in the Saejima family. In the summer of 1994 nobody holds it. Taiga Saejima, the last Garo, has been dead for about four years, and his son Kouga is a boy of fourteen who cannot yet lift his father's sword.

The name

Garo means 'hope' in the old tongue of the Makai. The name has nothing to do with the Garou, although the armour is made in the likeness of a wolf. The two words merely sound alike.

The title carries no rank. The Golden Knight takes his orders from a Watchdog like any other knight, and he is given nothing extra for the honour. What the title carries is respect. When the knights of the Order quarrel among themselves, they will still fall quiet for Garo.

The armour

The armour is made of Soul Metal, gold from helm to heel, with the head of a snarling wolf. Its holder summons it by cutting a circle of light in the air above his head with his sword, the Garoken. Soul Metal answers to the heart of the man who holds it. To a knight who has trained for it the sword weighs almost nothing. An untrained man cannot lift it off the ground.

In the world of men a knight may wear his armour for 99.9 seconds at a time. If he keeps it on any longer it begins to devour him, until he is a beast in golden plate that knows neither friend nor enemy. The knights call this the Lost Soul Beast. Kouga Saejima fell into it once, in March 2006, when rage kept him fighting past the limit. Rei Suzumura brought him out of it.

A Golden Knight who has cut down a hundred Horrors is put to a trial. If he passes it he wins Gouten, a Madou Horse of golden metal, whose hoofbeats can strike his sword out to twice its size. At each new moon the Madou Ring Zaruba, the Golden Knight's adviser, takes one day of his life as the price of its help.

The dead Golden Knights are honoured in the Tower of Heroic Spirits. A new holder must go there to be accepted by the spirits of those who went before him.

The Saejima line

Nobody now alive can say when the first Garo took up the sword. The Order tells stories of Golden Knights who fought before there were Madou Rings to advise them. For as long as its records run, the title has belonged to the Saejima family, who live in a large house in the eastern district with one butler. Gonza Kurahashi has kept that house for three Golden Knights.

Taiga Saejima was Garo until about 1990, when his own pupil Barago killed him. Barago had wanted the title for himself. Taiga had judged him unfit for it, since what he wanted was strength for its own sake. Barago went to Messiah, the mother of the Horrors, for another armour instead: the black armour of Kiba.

Taiga's sword stayed where it fell, upright in the ground. In the summer of 1994 it is still there. His son, Kouga Saejima, trains every day in the hope of drawing it.

Kouga Saejima

It took Kouga more than ten years to draw the sword. He was Garo by 2005, when he was twenty-five. In October of that year he spared Kaoru Mitsuki, a painter stained with a Horror's blood, whom the law of the Order told him to kill. In March 2006 he defeated Messiah herself, wearing wings that Kaoru's painting had given the armour. Then he destroyed the armour of Kiba, his father's murderer, in single combat.

He held the title for some thirty years. He destroyed the ancient Horror Legules at Kantai in 2006, the Apostle Horror Karma in 2010 and Gyanon in 2012. The Senate made him one of its own knights in 2011. In about 2020 his wife, Kaoru, was dragged into a rift in time. He went in after her, still the holder of the armour.

Raiga Saejima

Kouga's son, Raiga Saejima, grew up believing both his parents dead. When he went to the Tower of Heroic Spirits to claim the armour, the spirits refused him, because his father was alive in another place with the title still his. Kouga gave it up to his son of his own will.

Raiga was Garo by 2040, when he destroyed the ancient Horror Eyrith. In 2045 Kiba came back. Raiga fought it beside his father, with the spirit of his grandfather Taiga standing with them.

Zaji

Every Horror the Golden Knights have slain leaves a trace of its malice on the title. Over the generations these traces have gathered into a thing called Zaji, which exists only to kill whoever is Garo. It can bend time around a fight.

Kouga destroyed it in December 2011 at the tower where the old Golden Knights are laid to rest, with the spirits of his ancestors standing behind him. It promised that its kind would come for him again, then for his heirs. It kept its word in 2040, when it attacked Raiga in his own house.

Other worlds

The Makai lies beneath more worlds than this one, and the golden armour is known in at least two of the others.

In one of them the armour had gone black. The story told there was that it had spent all its light in a great battle long before, to save the people of that world. It stood dark in that world's Tower of Heroic Spirits until a young knight named Ryuga Dougai, who was no Saejima, took it up. In 2013 he won back its gold. Rekka, a Makai Priestess of this world, once met a priestess of his in a rift between the two. Kouga Saejima heard of the other Garo from her.

In another, a Golden Knight had died saving his world from a disaster that comes round every five hundred years. He left no son. A school called the Shidoin tried to find his successor among a hundred picked candidates, which came to nothing. Twenty years later, in the spring of 2020, one of those candidates, Shosetsu Hagiri, gathered a hundred young men for a contest called Versus Road. It was offered to them as a computer game, played through a headset. It was played in the Makai, with real Horrors, where the players killed one another for the promise that the last of them would be Garo.

Hagiri wanted the darkness that their killing made. Out of it he forged a black armour of his own, which he called Veil. His partner was Azami Kado, a priestess, the dead Golden Knight's own daughter. The last player standing was a student named Sena Kuon, who had refused all through to kill for the prize. The spirits of that world's Golden Knights lent him the armour, in which he beat Hagiri. Azami killed Hagiri herself, took Veil, then vanished. Sena Kuon handed back the sword. He went home.

pages.title: Garrus Vakarian
infobox: An investigator of the Turian Hierarchy's police
Chief of security and weapons officer of the USS Enterprise-B
pages.html:
Garrus Vakarian was a Turian, the chief of security and weapons officer of the USS Enterprise-B under Captain John Shepard. He was the finest shot aboard her. He became the closest friend that Shepard, who had distrusted every people but his own, ever had among them.

Palaven

Garrus Vakarian was born on Palaven, the son of a senior police officer of the Turian Hierarchy. He followed his father into the service as an investigator. He was good at the work, but he chafed at its rules, since he cared more about stopping a criminal than about how it was done. In the end he left it for Starfleet.

The Enterprise-B

Shepard took him aboard the Enterprise-B as chief of security. He made him weapons officer as well. Garrus was a sniper by training, with a patience to match. When he was not on the bridge he could usually be found adjusting the ship's phaser banks, which he never believed were quite right.

The two of them were alike in more than they admitted. Each had a hard view of justice. Each had been told more than once that he went too far. Shepard had come aboard with a hatred of everything that was not human. Garrus was the first of his crew to wear it down.

The war

In the Intergalactic War the Galactic Empire laid siege to Palaven for nine months, with Garrus's father and sister on the planet. He stayed at his post aboard the Enterprise-B throughout. He fought her guns at Vega, Cestus III, Romulus, Thessia and Earth.

In the saga

Garrus Vakarian has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Genya Arikado
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
Agent of a secret agency of the Japanese government
Soma Cruz, Mina Hakuba, Yoko Belnades, Julius Belmont
pages.html:
Genya Arikado was the name under which Alucard, the dhampir son of Dracula, worked in Japan in 2035 and 2036. To those who met him he was an agent of the Japanese government, a silent young man in a black suit. His task was to see that his father's power did not fall into the wrong hands.

The name

Dracula was destroyed for good in the Demon Castle War of 1999, in which Alucard fought beside Julius Belmont. His castle was sealed inside an eclipse of the sun, but his power was not destroyed with him. Alucard did not go back to his sleep. He stayed awake to watch for whoever might try to claim it.

By 2035 he was in Japan, attached to an agency of the government that dealt in secrets of state. Arikado is his own name, Alucard, in a Japanese shape. He kept the older name to himself. Yoko Belnades, the Church's witch, had worked with him before.

The eclipse of 2035

A prophecy held that in 2035 a new master would come to Dracula's castle to inherit all his power. The way in lay through the Hakuba shrine in Japan, whose priests had worked the sealing of 1999.

On the day of the eclipse two eighteen-year-olds climbed to the shrine: Soma Cruz with his friend Mina Hakuba, the shrine-keeper's daughter. They were drawn into the castle, where Arikado was waiting. When monsters attacked, Soma destroyed one, then took its soul into himself. Arikado had seen that power before. He told Soma to make for the castle's throne room. He raised a barrier at the castle gate to keep Mina safe.

He was busy elsewhere in the castle after that. The missionary Graham Jones had come to claim Dracula's inheritance, and when Graham stabbed Yoko Belnades it was Arikado who kept her alive. After Graham's fall Soma understood that he himself was Dracula reborn. Arikado told him that the power flowed from the chaos at the castle's heart, then how to cut it off. Soma did so.

The cult of 2036

A year later Arikado was investigating a cult called With Light, whose priestess, Celia Fortner, meant to make a new lord of darkness by destroying Soma. He arrived as she set her monsters on Soma in the street, in time to throw him a weapon. Afterwards he told Soma that his power had only been sleeping. He also told him to stay out of the matter, which Soma did not do.

In the cult's stronghold Arikado brought Soma a talisman from Mina. It was needed. Celia had a double of Mina killed in front of Soma to drive him into the dark. The talisman slowed the change, long enough for Arikado to shout that the girl was not Mina.

At the bottom of the castle Dmitrii Blinov, the last of Celia's candidates, sacrificed Celia herself to seal Arikado's power. It was left to Soma to destroy the monster that Dmitrii became. Arikado got out of the falling castle with him. Soma asked whether he was fated to become the Dark Lord. Arikado, who had spent nearly six hundred years refusing his own inheritance, told him that nobody's fate was fixed.

pages.title: Get of Fenris
infobox: Scandinavia, Iceland and the German lands
War, endurance and contempt for weakness
pages.html:
The Get of Fenris are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou. They are the warriors of Scandinavia and the German lands, followers of the great wolf Fenris. They believe that only the strong will survive the last battle against the Wyrm.

Totem and ways

The Get take their name from their totem, Fenris, the monstrous wolf of the Norse stories, a spirit of strength, ferocity and survival. Their ways are hard. Cubs are tested without mercy, and weakness is despised. Those who fail are driven out, and it is often the Children of Gaia who take them in. The Get honour courage, endurance, loyalty to the pack and a good death. Many of them see the coming end of the war, which other Garou call the Apocalypse, as their own Ragnarok: the battle for which they were bred.

Their rites are bloody and their sagas long. Their Galliards keep the sagas in the old northern manner, as verse to be chanted. A Get of Fenris rarely backs away from a fight, and seldom forgets who started one.

Homelands

Their oldest caerns lie in Scandinavia, Iceland and the mountain forests of Germany. Their Kinfolk are the Norse and Germanic peoples. The Get went wherever those peoples went. They crossed the North Sea with the raiders, settling in Britain and Ireland. They went east into Russia, and later across the Atlantic.

Place in the world

The other tribes value the Get as the fist of the Garou Nation and fear their temper. Their feud with the Fianna dates from the Viking raids on Ireland, and both sides still sing of it. They have little patience with the Children of Gaia, whom they think soft. Nor have they much time for the Bone Gnawers and the Glass Walkers, who in their view have forgotten what they are.

pages.title: Ghouls (vampiric)
infobox: Drinking a vampire's blood, without the Embrace
pages.html:
A ghoul, in the vampires' sense of the word, is a living mortal or animal kept on draughts of vampire blood without being Embraced. It does not age while it is fed, and it is stronger than an ordinary mortal. It is nearly always blood-bound to the vampire it serves. It has nothing to do with the creature wizards call a ghoul, such as the one that lives in the Weasleys' attic and bangs on the pipes.

Nature

Vampire blood keeps a ghoul alive and unchanging for as long as the supply lasts. It heals the ghoul's wounds and lends it some of the strength of the Kindred. With practice a ghoul can learn a little of its master's Disciplines. A ghoul still lives, all the same. It walks in daylight, eats ordinary food and keeps its soul.

It also craves the blood. A ghoul needs a fresh draught about once a month, and if the supply stops, its years catch up with it. One that has been kept for centuries does not simply grow old; the centuries take it at once.

A ghoul who drinks from the same vampire three times is bound to it by the blood bond, and will love it whether it wants to or not.

Service

Vampires keep ghouls as servants who can act by day: watchmen, drivers, lawyers and bodyguards. The vampire who keeps a ghoul is called its domitor. Animals are made ghouls to serve as guards.

Over the centuries the Tzimisce have bred whole families of born ghouls, the revenants, who serve them from birth. They have shaped others into monsters for war. Their greatest war-beast, the vozhd, is built of many bodies fused into one. Some ghouls escape their masters and live as independents, always hunting for more blood.

Notable ghouls

Anezka, a nun of Prague, was the ghoul of the Tzimisce Methuselah Vukodlak from the 1140s until 1999. All that time she worked in secret against his waking. When Christof Romuald destroyed Vukodlak, she had no master's blood left to keep her, and the centuries would have taken her at once. Christof Embraced her instead.

Leo Allatius, who led the Society of Leopold in 1999, was a mortal kept alive for three hundred years by vampire blood. He meant to use Vukodlak's blood to destroy every vampire in the world.

In the saga

Remus Lupin warned Harry Potter's class about the blood bond in October 1993. With some vampires, he said, a mortal need only drink from them three times, a few drops, to love them for the rest of their life without ever knowing the difference. He called it the cruellest thing vampires do.

pages.title: Gigan
infobox: A monster from space, part creature, part machine
Hooked claws; a buzz saw in its belly
pages.html:
Gigan is a monster from space, part living creature, part machine. It has a beak, a single red eye, hooks in place of hands, with a buzz saw set in its belly. The hunters of Nebula M brought it to Earth in 1972, since when other invaders have borrowed it.

The hunters of Nebula M

In 1972 a company in Tokyo was building an amusement park called World Children's Land. Its centrepiece was a hollow tower in the shape of Godzilla, as tall as the real one. The company's chairman, Fumio Sudo, was seventeen. Its manager, Kubota, talked a great deal about peace. Both had died in a climbing accident the year before.

What wore their likenesses were creatures from a world in the M Space Hunter Nebula: cockroaches the size of men. Their planet had been ruined by the filth of the people who had lived on it before them. They wanted a clean one. They meant to have the Earth before its own people spoilt it.

A cartoonist whom the park had hired, Gengo Odaka, found them out. By then they had called Gigan down from space with signals played on tape from the tower, bringing King Ghidorah with it. Godzilla heard the signals on Monster Island. He came with Anguirus.

The Justice League's satellite saw the two monsters coming. Superman met them above the Earth with Green Lantern, but the signal from the tower pulled them on.

Gigan's saw cut both of them badly, while a ray in the mouth of the tower burnt Godzilla. Then Odaka's friends sent a lift full of explosives up the tower. With the tower gone the two monsters had no orders, so they fled.

Later

In 1973 the hunters lent Gigan to Seatopia, to help its monster Megalon against Tokyo. Godzilla beat it again, with Jet Jaguar.

In the spring of 1994 the Xiliens of Planet X called it down on Japan, where Godzilla fought it beside the Megazord of the Power Rangers. It fled that time too.

pages.title: Glass Walkers
infobox: City dwellers, from financiers to crime families
Machines, money and the spirits of the city
pages.html:
The Glass Walkers are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the tribe of the cities. They are at home among machines, money and glass towers. They hold that the city belongs to Gaia as much as the forest does, and that it must be fought for. Other Garou suspect them of having gone too far over to the Weaver.

Totem and ways

The Glass Walkers follow Cockroach, a spirit that went with mankind into its towns and thrived there, as they have. They are the most modern of the tribes. Where other Garou shun human works, Glass Walkers use telephones, computers, cars and guns. They run businesses, hold office and keep accounts. Their Theurges deal with the spirits of the city, of electricity and of machines, which are the Weaver's creatures. They bargain with those spirits where other tribes would only fight.

Their Kinfolk are city people of every kind, from bankers and engineers to the old crime families of the Mediterranean ports. Glass Walkers fight the Wyrm with the city's own weapons: money, information and influence. They turn them against the companies and cartels that poison the world for profit.

History

In the earliest towns the tribe was called the Warders of Men: the Garou who lived among humans and watched over them. As the cities grew, the tribe grew with them. In the age of steam and the railway they were known as the Iron Riders. They took the name Glass Walkers as the modern cities rose. They have no wild homeland. Their caerns lie in strange places: old cellars, office towers and the hearts of great cities.

Place in the world

The other tribes depend on the Glass Walkers' money and contacts. They distrust them for the same reasons. The Red Talons and the Get of Fenris think them traitors to Gaia. Many Garou believe that the Weaver's madness is as great a danger as the Wyrm, which keeps the Glass Walkers under constant suspicion. They share the cities, uneasily, with the Bone Gnawers.

pages.title: Godzilla
infobox: A giant reptile of the deep sea, from the age of the great reptiles
The hydrogen bomb tests in the Pacific
Killed in Tokyo Bay by the Oxygen Destroyer, November 1954
First seen in January 1955; never killed
Mothra, Rodan, Anguirus, Jet Jaguar, King Caesar
King Ghidorah, Gigan, Hedorah, Megalon, Mechagodzilla; the Xiliens; the Kilaaks
Alive, in the seas round Japan
pages.html:
Godzilla is a giant reptile of the deep sea, a survivor of the age of the great reptiles, whom the hydrogen bomb tests in the Pacific woke and burnt. The first of his kind destroyed Tokyo in 1954, then died in Tokyo Bay, killed by Dr Daisuke Serizawa's Oxygen Destroyer. A second appeared within months, and nobody has ever killed him. He has laid waste Osaka, Nagoya, Las Vegas and a good part of New York, yet he has saved the Earth from one invader after another, which is why the Japanese have never quite decided what to think of him.

The beast of Odo Island

The fishermen of Odo Island, far out in the Pacific to the south of Japan, had an old name for something that lived in the sea beyond their reefs. They called it Gojira. In bad years, when the nets came up empty, their forefathers had sent girls out to it on rafts.

The creature was real. It was a reptile of the deep sea, about fifty metres tall, left over from the age of the great reptiles. Its kind had lived on in the trenches of the ocean floor long after their cousins vanished from the land. In the early 1950s hydrogen bombs were tested in the Pacific. The tests drove it out of its home, burning it as they did so. What came up to the surface carried the fire of the bomb inside it.

Dr Kyohei Yamane, the palaeontologist who first studied it, gave it the islanders' name, which in English became Godzilla. He never believed that there was only one.

Tokyo, 1954

On the evening of 13 August 1954 the freighter Eiko-maru went down with all hands off Odo Island, in a flash of white light that came up out of the sea. The Bingo-maru, sent to look for her, was lost in the same way. A few nights later, in a storm, something came ashore on Odo Island itself, where it crushed houses with the families still inside them.

The navy's depth charges did nothing. On the night of 3 November Godzilla came up out of Tokyo Bay. He walked through a line of electrified pylons that the army had built to stop him, then burnt the centre of Tokyo from end to end. Thousands died.

No hero stood in his way. The Justice Society had disbanded three years before, and the heroes of the 1960s had not yet appeared. Superman did come. He reached Tokyo Bay that night, and Godzilla's breath, which is the fire of the bomb, struck him out of the sky. He was days recovering.

Japan's wizards kept to the Statute of Secrecy. Mahoutokoro, their school, stands on Minami Iwo Jima, some thirty miles from the place where the Eiko-maru sank. Its teachers strengthened the charms that hide the island and left a beast woken by a Muggle bomb to the Muggles.

That left Dr Daisuke Serizawa, a young chemist who had lost an eye in the war. He had found by accident a way to destroy the oxygen in water, which he called the Oxygen Destroyer. It frightened him so badly that he kept it secret until Tokyo burnt. Then he burnt his notes. Two days after the raid he took the only one in existence down into Tokyo Bay in a diving suit. It reduced Godzilla to bones, then to nothing. Serizawa cut his own air line, to be sure that the secret died with him.

The second Godzilla, 1955 to 1964

Yamane had been right. In January 1955 two pilots, Shoichi Tsukioka and Koji Kobayashi, found a second Godzilla on Iwato Island, fighting a spiked, four-legged monster called Anguirus. The fight moved to Osaka. Godzilla killed Anguirus against the walls of Osaka Castle, by which time not much of the city was left.

Before the winter was out the Self-Defence Forces caught him on Kamiko Island, in the far north. Their rockets brought an ice cliff down on top of him.

The ice held him for seven years. In June 1962 the submarine Seahawk ran into a glowing iceberg in the Arctic. Godzilla broke out of it, sank the submarine, then came south to Japan. That summer a drug company had brought King Kong, the giant ape of Faro Island, to Japan for the sake of the publicity. The two met on the slopes of Mount Fuji. They fought their way down to the sea at Atami, then fell into the water together. Only Kong came up.

Godzilla had not drowned. In April 1964 he rose out of reclaimed land on the coast near Nagoya, where a typhoon had buried him, then destroyed a good part of the city. The same typhoon had washed a giant egg ashore from Infant Island. It was Mothra's. Old as she was, she came to defend it, and she died of her burns with one wing spread over it. The egg hatched two larvae, which wrapped Godzilla in silk until he toppled into the sea.

Through all of this Japan fought him with its own Self-Defence Forces, as it has always preferred to. The heroes of the West came seldom. When they did come, it was to get people out of his way.

Defender of the Earth, 1965 to 1975

In January 1965 a golden dragon with three heads, King Ghidorah, hatched out of a meteorite in the Kurobe valley. Godzilla was busy at the time, fighting Rodan at the foot of Mount Fuji. The surviving Mothra larva crawled between them to ask for their help. They refused. Men had never done anything for them, they said, besides which each wanted the other to apologise first. She went against King Ghidorah by herself, which shamed them into following. The three of them drove it back into space.

After 1964 he fought for the Earth more often than against it. In December 1965 the Xiliens of Planet X carried him off with Rodan, promising a cure for cancer in return. They sent both monsters back under their control, together with King Ghidorah, to conquer the Earth. When the control was broken, Godzilla and Rodan threw King Ghidorah out again.

In 1966 he destroyed the island base of the Red Bamboo, a terrorist army, tearing the claws off Ebirah, the giant lobster that guarded it. In 1967 an egg on Sollgel Island hatched a small Godzilla, Minilla, whom he took for his son.

In 1971 a creature of living sludge called Hedorah grew fat on the filth of Suruga Bay. Its mist killed thousands. It all but blinded Godzilla before he dried it to dust between two giant electrodes on the slopes of Mount Fuji.

In 1972 the hunters of Nebula M, giant cockroaches wearing dead men's faces, called King Ghidorah back with a new monster, Gigan. Godzilla drove them off beside a second Anguirus. In 1973 the undersea kingdom of Seatopia, its cities shaken by bomb tests, sent its guardian, the giant beetle Megalon, against Tokyo, with Gigan to help. Godzilla beat them both beside Jet Jaguar, a robot that had learnt to think for itself. Seatopia has never called itself Atlantis, which is the one quarrel in which it has no part.

In 1974 the ape-like people of the Third Planet of the Black Hole sent a steel copy of him, Mechagodzilla, to Japan under a false skin. Godzilla tore its head off on Okinawa, with the help of King Caesar, the old guardian of the island. In 1975 they rebuilt it. He destroyed it again, burnt their ships, then swam out to sea.

For the most part the heroes of the West left him to Japan in those years. He was plainly doing more good than harm, and Japan had grown used to him.

America, 1977 to 1979

In August 1977 he broke out of an iceberg off the coast of Alaska. Nobody knows how he came to be frozen into it, though it had happened to him before. He wrecked a stretch of the oil pipeline, then turned south.

Nick Fury gave the task of stopping him to Dum Dum Dugan of S.H.I.E.L.D. Dugan's Godzilla Squad included Gabe Jones and Jimmy Woo. With them came Dr Yuriko Takiguchi of Japan, with his twelve-year-old grandson, Rob.

Godzilla pulled down the Golden Gate Bridge, where the Champions fought him: the Black Widow, Hercules, the Angel and Iceman. Hercules threw a piece of the bridge, which hit S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Helicarrier, sinking it. On an island in the Aleutians Godzilla killed four giant beasts that a geneticist called Dr Demonicus had bred.

S.H.I.E.L.D. built a bigger Helicarrier for the hunt, the Behemoth. Stark International built a giant samurai robot, which Rob stole before anybody could use it. He named it Red Ronin. Rob liked Godzilla, so he used the robot to drive him away from San Diego without letting S.H.I.E.L.D. kill him.

In 1978 Godzilla broke the Hoover Dam, drowning the Las Vegas Strip. Near Salt Lake City he killed three monsters sent by the Megans, an alien people. At the end of the year Dugan had him sprayed with Henry Pym's shrinking gas, which left him the size of a rat. He escaped into the sewers of New York as the gas began to wear off.

By the time he was twenty feet tall the Fantastic Four had cornered him in the American Museum of Natural History. Reed Richards sent him back to the age of the great reptiles on Doctor Doom's time machine. There he fought beside Devil Dinosaur until the machine brought him back.

He arrived in Times Square at his full size, early in the summer of 1979. S.H.I.E.L.D., the Fantastic Four and the Avengers fought him through Manhattan. Six of the seven Avengers had met him in Japan in 1965, so they knew what to expect. Thor wrestled him on the side of the Empire State Building until the building began to crack. Captain America, Iron Man, the Vision, the Scarlet Witch, Yellowjacket and the Wasp did what they could. None of it stopped him.

In the end Rob Takiguchi called to him from the Behemoth. Godzilla took the boy gently in his hand, let himself be guided to the harbour, then went under the water. Spider-Man took a photograph. The best that the greatest heroes in America had been able to do was to turn him towards the sea.

The heroes, 1962 to 1988

What happened to Superman in 1954 was not forgotten. The heroes who met Godzilla afterwards kept out of his breath, got people out of his way, then left the rest to Japan. Not one of them ever beat him. Most did not try.

In June 1962, swimming south from the Arctic, he came on a Japanese crab fleet in the Bering Sea. Hal Jordan, the Green Lantern, lifted the boats clear behind a wall of green light. His ring stood up to the breath, which Superman had not, but it drained so fast that he let Godzilla go on to Japan. In April 1964 the Flash, Barry Allen, ran across the Pacific to Nagoya. He never crossed in front of Godzilla. He spent the day carrying people out of the streets ahead of him, two at a time.

The first great meeting came in January 1965. Godzilla was fighting Rodan at the foot of Mount Fuji when King Ghidorah hatched in the Kurobe valley. With three monsters loose at once, one of them from the stars, Japan asked for help for the first time. The Justice League came: Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, the Flash, Green Lantern, Aquaman, the Martian Manhunter, Green Arrow, the Atom and Hawkman. So did the Avengers: Captain America, Iron Man, Thor, the Wasp and Henry Pym, who was then calling himself Giant-Man. The Fantastic Four had the Frightful Four on their hands.

Superman remembered Tokyo Bay, so he sent nobody into Godzilla's breath. He went for King Ghidorah himself, with Wonder Woman, Iron Man and Thor. Thor met the dragon's lightning with his own, which was the first thing that had made it give ground. Green Lantern's ring was useless against a creature the colour of gold; he tried to wall Godzilla off from Rodan instead, which neither of them noticed. The Martian Manhunter reported that Godzilla was thinking of nothing but Rodan. Giant-Man held a broken bridge together while the Flash took a town across it. Batman ran the ground with Captain America.

It was the Wasp, too small for any monster to notice, who saw the Mothra larva crawl out between the two fighters. She told Superman that the three of them seemed to be talking. He called everybody back. From the slopes the heroes watched Godzilla drive King Ghidorah off the Earth, with Rodan beside him. Neither team had ever before stood aside to let a monster finish its work.

They did it again on 19 December 1965, when the Xiliens loosed all three monsters on Japan under their own control. The League was the same ten. The Avengers were not: the founders had stepped down, leaving Captain America with Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch, whom he told what to expect. Superman, who had hoped for Thor, was introduced to an archer.

Nobody tried to win this time. The Martian Manhunter looked into Godzilla's mind, where he found only the Xiliens' machines, so the League knew that the monsters were not their own masters. Green Lantern did not try his ring on the dragon twice; he caged Rodan for most of an hour. The Scarlet Witch's hexes tripped Godzilla twice, which was more than anybody had managed in January. Together they kept the three out of Tokyo for one night. When the sound that the Xiliens could not bear went out over the wireless, the heroes drew back, knowingly this time, to let Godzilla finish it.

In December 1966 Nick Fury brought S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Helicarrier to Letchi Island, on the trail of the Red Bamboo's heavy water, in time to see the island blow up. Godzilla swam away beneath him. Fury had just watched the creature do his work for him, so he let it go. In July 1971 the Sub-Mariner came into Suruga Bay, where the sea was dying.
