He fought Hedorah under water for a night, was burnt, then left it to Godzilla. His own kingdom had been wrecked by bomb tests. He has counted Godzilla a fellow sufferer ever since.

In March 1972 the Atom, on watch in the Justice League's satellite, saw Gigan coming in from beyond the Moon with King Ghidorah. Superman went out to meet them with Green Lantern, whose ring was no more use against the golden dragon than before. Neither monster could be turned, for the hunters' signal kept pulling them on. The League followed them down, found Godzilla already fighting, then kept the crowds clear while he finished it.

In April 1975 Interpol asked Tony Stark to examine the wreck of Mechagodzilla. Iron Man, who had not seen Godzilla since Mount Fuji, was cutting samples from it when Godzilla came back up the valley for a last look. Iron Man shut off his weapons, then stood still. Godzilla studied the man of metal on the heap of metal for a long minute before he went back to the sea.

In August 1976 a freighter went aground on Monster Island with Bruce Banner among its crew. By morning the Hulk was loose there. He fought Godzilla for a day. The fire that had felled Superman did the Hulk no harm, since he was a child of the bomb himself; it only made him angrier. Neither could put the other down. It ended when Minilla wandered between them: the Hulk looked at the little monster, lowered his fists, then sat down.

In the autumn of 1979 Godzilla walked home from New York to the Pacific along the floor of the Atlantic. Aquaman's whales steered him past Poseidonis. At the edge of the Antarctic sea the Sub-Mariner declared him a guest of his own Atlantis, then accused Aquaman of driving a monster into his waters. Godzilla did not notice either king.

In September 1983 he came up off the coast of Japan while the X-Men were in the country. Storm did not strike him. She raised a thunderstorm out at sea, then walked it away from the land, so that he turned from the lightning as he had once turned from the army's wires. In February 1988 Japan asked the United Nations for the Justice League. Guy Gardner attacked, only to be knocked into the sea. Then Doctor Light, Kimiyo Hoshi, hung a light like a second sun over the water. She moved it slowly out to sea, where he followed it, as he had followed the flares at Osaka in 1955.

The Power Rangers, 1994

In the spring of 1994 Rita Repulsa seized a gem called the Multiversal Focus from an old temple. It can carry its holder anywhere. Rita asked it for a land with no Power Rangers in it, so it took her to Japan. Tommy Oliver, the Green Ranger, was swept along with her.

The Xiliens were back, with a saucer over the Japanese coast, where Godzilla was killing Megalon in the ruins of a seaside city. Rita made an alliance with their Supreme Controller. She tried to take hold of Godzilla's mind, which did not work.

Tommy took him for one of Rita's monsters. He called up the Dragonzord, which Godzilla knocked flat, then burnt. Zordon sent the other five Rangers after him. Their Megazord fought Godzilla until both went down.

The Rangers soon saw that they had been fighting on the wrong side. Godzilla fought beside the Megazord against Gigan, Kumonga, Kamacuras, with a good many monsters of Rita's, though nobody could tell him that they were allies. Then Rita had King Ghidorah called down. It drained Godzilla's strength, dropped the Megazord in the sea, then turned on the Xiliens' own saucer. Tommy woke the wrecked Dragonzord. Joined to the Megazord as the Mega Dragonzord, it added its fire to Godzilla's, which brought King Ghidorah out of the sky.

Godzilla burnt the saucer, then the Supreme Controller with the last of his people. Rita fled through the gem, which had cracked. Godzilla turned at once on the Mega Dragonzord, so the Rangers went home.

The Kilaaks, 1999

By the end of the century the United Nations had gathered Godzilla, with the other monsters of the Pacific, on Monsterland, an island in the Ogasawara chain. In 1999 the Kilaaks, an alien people with a base on the Moon, gassed the island, then put the monsters under their control. Godzilla attacked New York. Rodan went to Moscow, Mothra to Beijing, the sea-dragon Manda to London, while Gorosaurus came up through the streets of Paris. Then four of them destroyed Tokyo.

Dracula's castle rose for the last time in 1999, while in Central Asia Zanzibar Land was seizing nuclear weapons. With six great cities burning, neither war was much noticed at the time. The heroes of those cities could do no more against the monsters than the Avengers had done in 1979.

Captain Katsuo Yamabe took the moon-ship Moonlight SY-3 to the Kilaaks' base, where his crew broke their control. The freed monsters went of their own accord to the Kilaak stronghold at the foot of Mount Fuji. King Ghidorah was called to defend it. Ten monsters were waiting for him, so this time he did not get away. Godzilla broke the stronghold open, letting in the cold, which the Kilaaks could not bear.

Nature

Godzilla walks upright. He has a long tail, a hide like charred bark, with three rows of jagged plates down his back. The plates glow just before he breathes. His breath is a blue-white beam of atomic fire that melts steel. He swims better than he walks, and he can sleep for years at a time on the sea bed or in the ice.

Shells, rockets, a million volts of electricity and the weapons of several alien peoples have all failed to do him lasting harm. Only the Oxygen Destroyer has ever killed one of his kind, and its secret died with its maker. Nobody has ever killed the second Godzilla.

He is not a tame creature, nor a friendly one. He will fight whatever threatens the sea he lives in, which has several times meant fighting on mankind's side. Children seem to be the only people he will listen to: he let Rob Takiguchi talk him out of New York.

The Garou of Japan say that the bomb's fire is on him but the Wyrm's scent is not. They have never hunted him.

pages.title: Gonza Kurahashi
infobox: Taiga Saejima; Kouga Saejima; Raiga Saejima
Bringing up the orphaned Kouga Saejima
pages.html:
Gonza Kurahashi is the butler of the Saejima family, the house of the Golden Knight. In time he served three generations of it. He has no training in the Makai arts whatever. He cooks, cleans, reads the old Makai script and brings up orphaned heirs. In the summer of 1994 he is about fifty-six, with the whole care of the fourteen-year-old Kouga Saejima.

Taiga's butler

Gonza was born about 1938. He served Taiga Saejima first. By 2005 he had lived beside the business of the Makai Order for more than fifty years without ever being counted part of it.

When Taiga's wife, Rin, died, Gonza helped to bring up their small son. When Barago killed Taiga in about 1990 there was nobody else left to do it. He was father, elder brother and cook to the boy. He also saw to Kouga's training, as far as a man who cannot lift Soul Metal is able.

Kouga and Kaoru

In 2005 Kouga brought home Kaoru Mitsuki, a young painter with nowhere to live. Gonza took to her at once. He did what he could to push his silent master in her direction.

In March 2006, while Kouga fought Messiah, Rei Suzumura was losing to Gulm, the creature that had ruled the Eastern Watchdog. Gonza walked into the fight carrying a weapon of Soul Metal, which he should not have been able to lift. It gave Rei his opening.

In March 2012 Sigma Fudou tore the Saejima house out of the ground. It was rebuilt.

Raiga

In about 2020 Kouga went after Kaoru into a rift in time, leaving a son of six. Gonza, who was past eighty, brought up a second orphaned Saejima. He baked the boy a cake every birthday. When Raiga was ten, Rei Suzumura came to train him.

Gonza was still the butler in 2040, when Raiga was Garo. He was past a hundred by then, kept on his feet by the longevity medicine of the age. When the Senate sent Mayuri, a young woman it regarded as a tool, to live in the house, Gonza treated her as a guest from the first day. He lived to see Kouga's face once more.

pages.title: Grace Sterling
infobox: Red, on the night of 20 July 1969
The Rangers of 1969, as their leader
Head of the secretarial pool at NASA
Lord Drakkon, from November 1993 to September 1994
Matt Cook, as the second Green Ranger, December 1994
In the summer of 1994, the head of Promethea
February 1995, at the Arch in the Bermuda Triangle
pages.html:
Grace Sterling is the founder and head of Promethea, one of the great technology companies of California. In 1969 she was a secretary at NASA who had been refused a place among its astronauts. On the night of the Moon landing Zordon made her the Red Ranger, the leader of his first team, which lost three of its five on the Moon. She has never forgiven him for taking the powers back. In the summer of 1994 she is the Rangers' most useful ally, though she is keeping a prisoner they know nothing about. In December 1994 she made Matt Cook the second Green Ranger. She was killed in February 1995.

NASA

Grace Sterling went to work for NASA in the 1960s as a secretary. She rose to run its secretarial pool. What she wanted was to go into space. She sat the tests that had been set for the first American astronauts, the men of the Mercury programme, coming out at the top of her class. When she applied for the Moon mission of 1969 she was turned down, for no better reason than that she was a woman.

The night of the Moon landing

On the night of 20 July 1969 she was on the roof at NASA with a colleague, Marcus, while the first men walked on the Moon. That same night Dark Specter had sent a creature called Psycho Green there, to break Rita Repulsa out of her dumpster. Zordon had no Rangers. He had Alpha 5 fetch five grown strangers to the Command Center, Grace among them. He gave her the Red Ranger's coin, with the command of the rest.

The other four were Nikolai Chukarin of the Soviet KGB, the British singer Jamie Gilmore, a soldier named Terona Washington, who was home from Vietnam, and a student, Daniel O'Halloran.

They came down in the Aitken crater, on the far side of the Moon. Grace wept for joy when she touched the ground. Psycho Green kicked Nikolai so hard that he would have flown off into space if Grace had not caught him. He crushed Jamie Gilmore under a boulder. He broke Daniel's visor, so that Daniel suffocated.

The three who were left put their weapons together into a single blaster. Its fire only fed the creature, which grew into a giant. They fell back on Rita's empty palace, where one of Zordon's old cannons still stood. Nikolai took the cannon. 'We will save the earth today, Grace,' he said. 'Make sure it's worth saving.' Then he let Psycho Green swallow him. He fired from inside it, which destroyed them both.

The quarrel with Zordon

Two came home, Grace with Terona Washington. Terona told Zordon that it had been irresponsible to send untrained strangers to fight. Zordon blamed himself, as it happened, but he asked for the powers back now that the danger was over. Grace wanted to keep them. With such power, she said, they could end the war in Vietnam, perhaps the Cold War itself. Zordon answered that it was not a Ranger's place to meddle in mankind's own affairs. He took the coins. The two of them left him in anger. He never told his later Rangers that they had existed.

Grace did not leave empty-handed. She had picked up Psycho Green's dagger on the Moon, which she kept.

Promethea

She resigned from NASA. With Terona she founded a company, Promethea, to keep the promise that Nikolai had asked of her. It grew into one of the great firms of Silicon Valley, with an island of its own in San Francisco Bay. Its business is new sources of energy, among other things. It has made Grace a billionaire, who gives a great deal of the money away.

Promethea's machines are beyond what such a firm ought to be able to build, because the energy of the dagger is behind them. Its headquarters is also a ship. It has soldiers of its own. It has the Mechazord, a fighting giant like the Rangers' Megazord which draws nothing from the Morphin Grid; Grace pilots it herself. It also has relief crews, who go into cities after a monster has been through them.

In August 1993 Promethea offered a place to a clever schoolboy from Angel Grove, Billy Cranston. He turned it down.

Lord Drakkon in the cell

Early in November 1993 Lord Drakkon, the Tommy Oliver of another world, was dragged into this one without his powers. Promethea's soldiers found him in the mountains. Grace shut him in a cell under one of her buildings, in restraints of pure energy, with armed guards outside. She told nobody. He was there for ten months, during which he liked to tell her about the Rangers he had killed.

Those were the weeks after Rita had turned the Rangers' own Zords on the cities of the world. A great many people were afraid of the Rangers now. Grace sent Promethea's relief crews to the cities that had been hit. Then she went on television to defend the Rangers, at a time when few others would.

The Rangers' ally

She met them that winter, at the scene of a disaster in Dubai. A Promethea aeroplane had vanished a month before over a village in the Carpathians that was on no map, hidden in purple fog. Her photographs showed Finster there. The Rangers found a village of Putties in human shape, with a castle above it. Finster had learnt from the two captured pilots how to make monsters that could pass for people. He surrendered. The Rangers brought the pilots out. Grace offered them everything Promethea had; Jason Lee Scott, the Red Ranger, said no.

Then it came out that more of Finster's creatures were loose in the world, living as men, some of them not knowing what they were. Grace walked up to the door of the Command Center to ask for Zordon. There she told his Rangers what she had been in 1969. They watched the whole of that night on the viewing globe. Zordon's reasons for his silence did not satisfy them.

After that Jason agreed to work with her. Promethea tracked the hidden monsters by the energy they gave off, then the Rangers dealt with them. She fought beside them in the Mechazord. She talked to Jason, one leader to another, about what it is to lose people. Zordon warned them that her machines were more than human.

Her methods wore on them. She kept a captured Putty in a cage at Promethea. In the summer of 1994 she traced a monster to four streets of Vancouver, so she had her soldiers arrest everybody in them. At the end of that August Billy Cranston, puzzled that one of Promethea's buildings was drawing only half its power, found the hidden cell with Drakkon in it. Jason was furious that she had never told him. He ended the alliance on the spot.

The lost ship

Days later Drakkon escaped. He murdered Tommy Oliver, then set about taking the powers of every Ranger there had ever been or would be. Jason sent for Grace, who came. She hardened the Rangers' morphers against him. Her headquarters flew. Aboard it she took a company of Rangers to the Moon of Drakkon's world, where they freed the Rangers he held. She gave shelter to the Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of his world, who had turned against him.

When Drakkon unmade the world, Grace used the dagger to armour the ship. It was thrown clear of everything, into a dark place where there was no Morphin Grid at all. Her crew were aboard, with Terona Washington, the Ranger Slayer and a handful of Rangers whose powers were guttering out. They were there for more than forty days. With a scavenger called Ellarien, the Solar Ranger, they brought down the Praetor, the tyrant who had starved that place of the Power, which opened the way home.

The world they came home to had been mended. Tommy Oliver was alive. Nobody on Earth remembered the war. By October 1994 Grace was back at her desk, with the Ranger Slayer in her service, patrolling space in the Gravezord. Early that December she sent the Slayer out to help the Rangers against the Anointed, in which fight the Gravezord saved Adam Park's life.

The Dragon Coin

In October 1994, when Zordon shut himself away to make the White Ranger, it was Grace who helped Billy Cranston to find the plans of the hidden room. The next month Lord Zedd sent a monster to dig into Promethea for the dagger. Grace fought it in the Mechazord. Goldar took her prisoner; she got free, then blew the dagger to pieces before he could carry it off. It was a trick. She had destroyed an illusion, so the real dagger never left her keeping.

Billy saw through it. He offered her a bargain: his silence about the dagger, in return for her help with an experiment of his own. The experiment was the dead Dragon Coin. Together they woke it with the dagger's energy. Billy meant to tell Zordon. Grace persuaded him to let Promethea choose who should carry it.

Her first thought was Lord Drakkon, who had fallen to Earth again that December. He was locked in a cell under the Command Center. She went to that cell to make him an offer. The Green Ranger who appeared the same day was somebody else: Matt Cook, a schoolboy she had plucked from under a falling wall. She trained him at Promethea. She had lost three Rangers on the Moon, so she did not mean to lose another.

When Zordon found out, the two of them quarrelled bitterly over the coin.

The dome

Late in December 1994 Zedd shut Angel Grove under a dome of green energy. Matt showed the city his face. Then the pair of them seemed to go over to Zedd, who was offering the city peace. Grace let it be thought that an old grudge had decided her: Zedd, she said, had helped Angel Grove in ways that Zordon never had. She had not changed sides. She told Zedd so herself, on the day Matt brought the dome down.

The Eltarian War

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus of Eltar smashed Zordon's tube. Zordon was thought dead. Grace told the Rangers that she was in command now. Then the Empyreals, the three giants that served Zartus, destroyed Promethea's headquarters with Grace inside. Matt Cook dug her out of the wreck, with her scientists.

Zartus ruled the Empyreals through a crystal. Grace broke it with Psycho Green's dagger, which ended his hold on them. The freed Empyreals at once set about burning the Earth, so that the Rangers had to destroy them one by one.

Zordon came through the war in a body of metal that was failing. Grace had a hidden workshop with everything needed to make him a new tube. There the two of them made their peace, twenty-five years late. While a new Command Center was fetched from space, Zordon's tube stood at a Promethea base. Her soldiers guarded the Power Chamber beside Matt.

The Arch

There is an old gate into the Morphin Grid on Safehaven, the Master Arch. Earth had one too, a ruin in the Bermuda Triangle, which Grace had found. She had rebuilt it in secret. Early in February 1995 she told the Rangers that it existed.

By then Rita Repulsa had come back as Mistress Vile, Dark Specter's general, with the Zeo Crystal in her hands. She had captured Matt, whom she bound to her with the Sword of Darkness. Grace blamed herself for ever having given him the coin. When the two women met, Grace told Mistress Vile that she was 'a scared little girl with daddy issues'. Mistress Vile raided Promethea. The Vessel, the creature that served her, carried Grace off alive.

She was taken to the Arch. Mistress Vile opened it with the Zeo Crystal, to bring Dark Specter through. There Matt Cook, with the sword's spell on him, killed Grace Sterling.

She had prepared for it. A recording, set to play at her death, told Billy Cranston what the Arch was. Later an image of her, left in the Grid, told him of the Power Eggs, with which he shielded the Earth while the Grid was foul.

What the world remembers

When the Rangers cleansed the Grid the world was mended, for the second time in six months. Everything broken since Zedd's dome stood whole again. The world kept no memory of those weeks. The dead of that war stayed dead all the same, Grace among them. The mended world remembered her death as the loss of a Promethea research ship in the Bermuda Triangle. The Rangers knew what had really happened. So did Terona Washington. So did Matt Cook, who had to live with it.

Terona Washington and Terra Venture

Promethea passed to Terona Washington, her co-founder, the last of the Rangers of 1969. He closed its secret work. He kept its ships. He gave the rest of his life to the promise that Nikolai Chukarin had asked of them on the Moon.

Promethea's headquarters had always been a ship. From its designs came the colony ship built with the Global Space Alliance. It left Earth in 1999 as Terra Venture, the space colony that the Galaxy Rangers defended.

pages.title: Graham Jones
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
1999, on the day of Dracula's destruction
Yoko Belnades, Genya Arikado, Soma Cruz
pages.html:
Graham Jones was a missionary, the founder of a sect of his own, who believed that he was Dracula reborn. He had been born in 1999 on the very day of Dracula's destruction. In 2035 he entered the sealed castle to claim the vampire's power. Soma Cruz, who was the true heir, destroyed him there.

Birth and belief

Graham was born on the day in 1999 when Julius Belmont destroyed Dracula for good. He was not the only child born that day who grew up with strange gifts. Dario Bossi could command fire, and Dmitrii Blinov could copy the powers of others. Graham's gifts were real too. What he made of them was a religion.

He became a missionary, then the head of a sect, which grew quickly. He preached that the world would end in 2035. A prophecy said that in that year a new master would come to Dracula's castle, to inherit everything that Dracula had been. Graham had no doubt who was meant. He had been born as Dracula died, so Dracula's power, he reasoned, was his by right.

The sealed castle

The castle had been shut inside an eclipse since 1999. In 2035, when he was thirty-six, Graham reached it through the Hakuba shrine in Japan, on the day of that year's eclipse. The Church had sent a witch, Yoko Belnades, after him.

At first he was friendly to Soma Cruz, the eighteen-year-old he found wandering the halls. He told the boy the story of 1999 with the prophecy that went with it. He was a good deal less friendly once Soma mentioned that he had found a power of his own, a power to rule. Graham left in a hurry for the throne room.

When Yoko Belnades called him a fraud, he stabbed her. By then he had begun to draw the power of the castle into himself. He took the throne room, declared himself the Dark Lord and waited.

The throne room

Soma came. Graham accused him of stealing the souls of the castle's monsters, which belonged, he said, to its master. He fought as Dracula had always fought in that room, which did him no good. Soma destroyed him.

The power Graham had gathered did not die with him. It went into Soma. That was how Soma learnt which of them had been Dracula reborn.

The other candidates

Graham's mistake was repeated the next year. Celia Fortner, the priestess of a cult called With Light, put forward Dario Bossi and Dmitrii Blinov as candidates for the lordship of darkness, on the same ground: the day of their birth. Neither fared any better than Graham had.

pages.title: Grant Staley
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Kamen Rider Camo' (21 February 2009)
Fighter in unlicensed martial arts bouts
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Grant Staley is an American, born about 1988, a martial artist who fought in unlicensed bouts. In February 2009 Xaviax made him Kamen Rider Camo. He was a Rider for barely a week. Kit Taylor was close to talking him out of it when another of Xaviax's Riders vented him, on 28 February 2009.

The strongest man on two worlds

Grant fought for a living, in the kind of match that is not advertised. What he wanted was to be the best there was. Xaviax came to him as an officer of a private army, hiring fighters. He gave him the Advent Deck of Camo, contracted to the chameleon Biogreeza. It opened for Grant because he was the mirror twin of Van, the Ventaran who first wore it.

Grant believed that he was a hired soldier. His orders were to deal with the Wing Knight. He meant to beat every other Rider as well, to prove that he was the strongest man on two worlds.

Camo

On 21 February 2009 Grant watched Len of Ventara rescue Maya Young from a mirror monster. The same day he fought Kit Taylor, who was then keeping company with Drew Lansing, the Rider called Torque. Camo fought the pair of them, then got away. Drew Lansing blamed Kit for letting him go.

A week later he met them again. Kit could see that Xaviax had lied to Grant, as he had lied to everyone. He tried to tell him so. Grant was beginning to listen. Then the two Riders of Xaviax fought. Drew Lansing wounded Grant with a blow that he did not see coming, then vented him.

Afterwards

Seeing it done showed Kit which side Drew Lansing was really on. Grant lay in the Advent Void until December 2009. With Xaviax dead, Eubulon brought him out, took away his memories of the war, then sent him home. Van wears the armour of Camo again.

pages.title: Gray Fox
infobox: Frank Jaeger; Frank Hunter; Null; Deepthroat
Zanzibar Land, 24 December 1999; again at Shadow Moses, 2005
pages.html:
Gray Fox, whose name is Frank Jaeger, is the best soldier in FOXHOUND, the holder of its highest rank of Fox. He has been a fighter since he was a small boy in Mozambique. He was Solid Snake's senior comrade and friend, then his enemy at Zanzibar Land in 1999. He died there. He was brought back as something half machine, then died a second time at Shadow Moses in 2005.

The hunter

Nobody knows where he was born, nor what he was first called. In 1966, when Mozambique was fighting for its independence, there was a boy among the guerrillas who had killed dozens of government soldiers with nothing but a knife. They let him come close because he was a child. He spoke a few words of German, so they called him Frank Jaeger, the frank hunter.

The Philosophers took him. They made him into an experiment called the Perfect Soldier, under the codename Null. After every mission he was shut in a tank of fluid, cut off from all sensation, until he had forgotten everything.

In 1970 Null was one of the FOX soldiers who rebelled on the San Hieronymo Peninsula. Big Boss fought him there, then set him free. He never forgot it.

FOXHOUND

He followed Big Boss into FOXHOUND, where he earned the codename Gray Fox. In the civil war in Rhodesia, under the name Frank Hunter, he killed a man with his wife. Their small daughter was left alone. In 1979 he took her away with him, out of remorse. Big Boss helped the two of them to settle in America, where they lived as brother and sister. The girl grew up to be Dr Naomi Hunter. She did not learn who had killed her parents until 2005.

In February 1988, at the Winter Olympics in Calgary, he fell in love with a Czech figure skater, Gustava Heffner. Her attempt to claim asylum failed, costing her the right to compete. He came away with a grudge against his own superiors.

Outer Heaven

In 1995 FOXHOUND sent him into Outer Heaven ahead of anyone else. He was captured. His last message was two words: 'Metal Gear'. The rookie Solid Snake got him out of his cell, learning from him what Metal Gear was.

Afterwards Gray Fox vanished. He had gone to Big Boss.

Zanzibar Land

On Christmas Eve 1999 Snake found him again in Zanzibar Land, at the controls of the new Metal Gear D. A missile from it killed Gustava Heffner, who was there as bodyguard to the kidnapped Dr Marv. All through that night an unnamed voice on the radio had been helping Snake. That was Gray Fox too.

When Snake had wrecked the machine, the two of them fought with their bare hands in a minefield, as friends. Gray Fox lost.

The ninja

He was not allowed to stay dead. Dr Clark of the Patriots, who had once been Para-Medic, kept the body alive as a subject for her experiments in gene therapy. She shut him in an armoured skeleton, with drugs to keep him quiet. In 2003 he killed her, then escaped.

In 2005 he appeared at Shadow Moses, invisible when he chose, armed with a sword. Hardly anything was left of his mind except the wish to fight Snake once more. He cut off Revolver Ocelot's right hand. He also gave Snake advice by radio under the name Deepthroat. Before the end he told Snake the truth about Naomi's parents.

At the last he threw himself at Metal Gear REX to give Snake a chance. He broke its radar housing before Liquid Snake crushed him under the machine's foot.

pages.title: Greg Adams
pages.html:
Greg Adams was the chief engineer of the USS Enterprise-B under Captain John Shepard. The young Quarian Tali'Zorah nar Rayya served under him as an adviser.

The engineer

Adams had the Enterprise-B from her fitting out. He took her out of spacedock on 14 October 2293 with half her systems missing, on the voyage that lost James T. Kirk. Among his charges was the cloaking device hidden in her hull, which very few engineers in the Federation had ever been allowed to see.

When Shepard gave a Quarian girl on her Pilgrimage the run of his engine room, Adams expected little of it. He changed his mind within days. Tali'Zorah knew more about keeping an old engine alive than anyone he had met. He was soon asking her advice as a matter of course. After the war he said that his proudest work was the part his engineers had played, beside the Quarians and the Geth, in building the Barrier.

In the saga

Greg Adams has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Grimlord
infobox: An orb on Ziktor's desk; a prism, from September 1995
The Virtual Dungeon, to September 1995; the Virtual Dark Fortress
General Ivar, Colonel Icebot, Decimator; later Despera, Doom Master, Oraclon
The VR Troopers; Professor Horatio Hart
pages.html:
Grimlord is the master of virtual reality, a world lying beside this one, which he rules from a throne among his creatures. He is also Karl Ziktor, the billionaire owner of Ziktor Industries, the richest man in Crossworld City, California. An orb on Ziktor's desk turns the one into the other. About 1984 he seized the scientist Tyler Steele. From September 1994 he was at war with the VR Troopers, who stood between his armies and the Earth. Outside his own service nobody knows that Ziktor is Grimlord. When the record stops, in February 1996, nobody had found out.

Karl Ziktor

To Crossworld City Karl Ziktor is its great man: a billionaire, the owner of Ziktor Industries, with an office in the company's building in the middle of the town. He deals in oil, timber and a good many other things. The mayor, Abner Rooney, does what Ziktor tells him. Beside Lex Luthor or Tony Stark he is a small figure, a rich man of one Californian city.

His secretaries are Skugs, soldiers of Grimlord's wearing human faces, as is his inventor, Strickland. The one living thing he is fond of is his pet iguana, Juliet. He once drew back from using her in an experiment, which is more than he has ever done for a human being.

The orb

On Ziktor's desk stands an orb. When he is alone he speaks to it. 'Forces of darkness, empower me!' he says. 'Take me back to my virtual reality!' The blinds close over the windows, and the next moment he is sitting on a throne on the far side of the reality barrier, in the shape of Grimlord.

What the forces of darkness are that answer him, the record does not say. Nor does it say where the orb came from. His power dates from the years when Tyler Steele and Professor Hart were first opening the way between the worlds. Ziktor had once worked with both men.

Tyler Steele and Professor Hart

About 1984 Grimlord struck at the two scientists. He left Professor Hart dying. He carried Tyler Steele off into virtual reality, wiped his memory, and remade him as the cyborg Dark Heart, one of the fiercest of his own warriors.

He kept his prisoner for more than ten years, drawing all the while on what Tyler Steele knew. Ziktor used his notes to grow a copy of Ryan Steele in February 1995. Colonel Icebot used them to build the Red Python. In September 1995 Grimlord drained what was left into a prism.

The Virtual Dungeon, 1994 to 1995

Grimlord's first stronghold was the Virtual Dungeon, where he sat enthroned before a hall full of his creatures. The Troopers call them mutants. They are no kin to the mutants born among mankind: Grimlord's are robots, cyborgs or beasts, made in virtual reality. His commanders were General Ivar, the scientist Colonel Icebot and the swordsman Decimator. His foot soldiers were the Skugs.

He wants one thing, which is to break down the reality barrier so that his armies can pour through into the Earth. Small parties can cross already. The whole army cannot. On 3 September 1994 he learnt that Professor Hart had armed three young people against him, and he attacked them that day.

For the next year he tried one scheme after another, some as Grimlord, some as Ziktor. As Ziktor he went after a collection of books on solar power, the plans for a clean engine that threatened his trade in oil, a stretch of old forest. As Grimlord he sent creatures against the Troopers almost daily. He has no patience with failure. Three times he blew up a stronghold of his own in the hope of killing the Troopers inside it.

His servants do not all love him. In October 1994 General Ivar plotted to act on his own account. In September 1995 a creature called Amphibidor tried to raise a mutiny, which Grimlord turned into one more attack on the Troopers.

The prism and the Virtual Dark Fortress

In September 1995 Ryan Steele took Tyler Steele out of Grimlord's hands. Grimlord had already taken what he wanted. The prism that held Tyler Steele's knowledge made him stronger than the orb had ever done. The orb was destroyed, with the prism set in its place.

As Grimlord he changed. He now wore a cape, had grown a long tail, and could pass from place to place in an instant. He abandoned the dungeon for the Virtual Dark Fortress, a stronghold in the shape of a great ship. There he made himself new commanders: Despera, the swordsman Doom Master, and Oraclon, an oracle built into the fortress wall. His Skugs became Ultra Skugs.

The secret

In November 1995 the archaeologist Nebraska Smith opened an ancient doorway inside a pyramid, behind which lay the secret of Grimlord's true name. Grimlord sent Despera with Doom Master to guard it. He tried to shut Ryan Steele up in another world altogether sooner than be known. Ryan came within reach of the answer, then turned back to save his friends. Oraclon sealed the door.

Ziktor's own name suffered a little all the same. In February 1996 he announced that he would flatten a forest for a research station. The three Troopers, as their ordinary selves, pressed him into a camping trip there, with Kaitlin Star's camera for company. The photographs did his public standing no good.

Knighttime

Late in 1995 Grimlord called in an old friend, Knighttime, a prince from a savage part of virtual reality, who had power over dreams as well as over time. In November Knighttime sent two of the Troopers into the far past. Later he put all three to sleep, showing them a world in which Grimlord had won.

On 20 February 1996 Knighttime betrayed him. He stopped time over the whole Earth for purposes of his own. Nobody else in the world knew that it had happened. Grimlord, for the only time on record, fought on the same side as Ryan Steele, until the machine was destroyed. Afterwards he kept Knighttime as a prisoner.

Where the record stops

On 21 February 1996 the Troopers raided the Virtual Dark Fortress to fetch back a stolen robot. They overloaded Oraclon, leaving Grimlord's chamber in flames. The fortress was crippled, though it was not destroyed.

There the record ends. Grimlord had not been beaten. Karl Ziktor had not been found out. Nothing is recorded of either after February 1996.

pages.title: Grimlord's army
infobox: General Ivar; Colonel Icebot; Doom Master; Ultra Skugs; Skugs; Decimator; Despera; Oraclon
Despera, Doom Master, Oraclon; General Ivar; Colonel Icebot
Dark Heart, who was Tyler Steele
pages.html:
Grimlord's army is the host of robots, cyborgs and armoured beasts with which Grimlord rules virtual reality. He means to lead it through the reality barrier into the Earth. Its commanders in the summer of 1994 are General Ivar, Colonel Icebot and the swordsman Decimator, with the Skugs for its foot soldiers. From September 1994 the VR Troopers of Crossworld City stood in its way.

The Skugs

The Skugs are Grimlord's common soldiers. In their own shape they have golden heads, black bodies and capes. On this side of the barrier they usually go about in twos or threes, looking like ordinary men or women. Karl Ziktor's secretaries are Skugs, as is his inventor, Strickland.

They have one great weakness. If two Skugs are knocked against each other, both vanish. The Troopers learnt early to throw one into the next.

In September 1995 Grimlord remade them with knowledge drained from Tyler Steele. The Ultra Skugs wore blue, had the faces of monsters, and could take a blow that would have finished a Skug. Knocking them together still worked.

The first commanders

General Ivar is a robot who commands Grimlord's forces on the ground as well as in the air. He can turn himself into a rocket. In October 1994, tired of taking orders, he hatched a scheme of his own to freeze the electricity supply of Crossworld City. J.B. Reese destroyed him. Grimlord had him rebuilt, so he served on into 1996.

Colonel Icebot is Grimlord's scientist, who designs his aircraft as well as most of his other devices. There is no ice about him, whatever the name suggests. He seldom fights. In February 1995 he built the Red Python, an armoured warrior modelled on the Troopers, out of knowledge stolen from Tyler Steele.

Decimator is a swordsman. On 3 September 1994, the first day of the war, he all but killed Ryan Steele. He fought Ryan again many times over the following year. It was his sword that wounded Dark Heart in November 1994. He is not heard of after Grimlord destroyed the Virtual Dungeon in September 1995.

Others stood beside them in that first year. Zelton was a robot who could take the shape of other robots. Toxoid was a green beast, more cowardly than the rest. Blue Boar led the gun-robots. None of the three is heard of after the dungeon fell. Renegade was a marksman, the one who shot Dark Heart. In the air Grimlord had Air Stryker, a robot shaped like a helicopter, with the jet-shaped Fighterbot for company.

Dark Heart

The fiercest of the first commanders was the cyborg Dark Heart. He was not a creature of virtual reality at all. He was Tyler Steele, the scientist Grimlord had carried off about 1984, with his memory wiped. His own son, Ryan, fought him in November 1994 before either knew the other.

The Virtual Dark Fortress

When Grimlord moved to the Virtual Dark Fortress in September 1995, he made new commanders to go with it. Despera was the first, a warrior in a white robe with a horned head-dress, who fights with a staff. She is Grimlord's chief adviser. She has a fierce temper, though she is devoted to him. In February 1996 she brought in her sister, Desponda, to command Grimlord's Air Castle. J.B. Reese beat Desponda there. The castle was destroyed, though she seems to have survived it.

Oraclon is an oracle: a huge round face with three eyes, built into the wall of the fortress. He knows whatever can be known about virtual reality, besides being able to turn out new creatures on demand. Ryan Steele destroyed him in November 1995 by striking between the eyes. Grimlord rebuilt him at once. In February 1996 the Troopers overloaded his circuits, which left the fortress crippled.

Doom Master is a swordsman in black armour, proud to a fault. He leads the Vixens, five women warriors in five colours, with the Ultra Skugs under him as well. He quarrels with Despera constantly. He once destroyed one of Grimlord's own creatures sooner than see it beat Ryan Steele before he could.

Knighttime

Knighttime was never quite one of them. He is a robed prince from a savage part of virtual reality, an old friend of Grimlord's, with power over dreams besides power over time. He joined the war in November 1995. For a while Grimlord left him in command. In February 1996 he stopped time over the whole Earth on his own account. Grimlord joined Ryan Steele to destroy the machine, then kept Knighttime as his prisoner.

pages.title: GRU SV-8
infobox: After soldiers of the Red Army came upon cults of ghouls
Delta Green and Majestic 12, against the Karotechia, 2001
pages.html:
GRU SV-8 is the section of Russian military intelligence, the GRU, that deals with the unnatural. It was founded in Soviet days, after soldiers of the Red Army came upon cults of ghouls, and it outlasted a long rivalry with Smersh. In 2001 it joined Delta Green and Majestic 12 in the operation that broke the Karotechia, the only time the three are known to have worked together.

The Soviet years

SV-8 grew up inside the GRU, the intelligence arm of the Red Army. Its first work was against the cults of ghouls that Red Army soldiers had come upon. Through the Second World War it was at odds with Smersh, the Soviet counter-intelligence service. In the end SV-8 moved against Smersh and won.

Russia

When the Soviet Union fell in 1991, SV-8 went on in the service of Russia. In 2001 it worked with Delta Green and Majestic 12 against the Karotechia. After 2010 the Russian government gave it a large budget and turned it to the service of the Kremlin's ambitions abroad.

pages.title: Hal Emmerich
infobox: Princeton; the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
pages.html:
Hal Emmerich is an American boy of fourteen in the summer of 1994, the son of two weapons scientists. He grew up to design the walking tank Metal Gear REX without understanding what it was for. He spent the rest of his life helping Solid Snake to destroy such machines. His friends call him Otacon.

A family of bomb-makers

Hal's grandfather worked on the Manhattan Project, which built the first atomic bombs. His father, Huey Emmerich, was born on 6 August 1945, the day the bomb fell on Hiroshima. Huey was born with a damaged spine. He could not walk, so he became an engineer of machines that could.

In 1974, in Costa Rica, Huey helped to build the nuclear weapon Peace Walker for a rogue station chief of the CIA. Then he changed sides to join Big Boss. The mind of the machine was the work of an Englishwoman, Dr Strangelove, who became Huey's wife. Hal, their son, was born in 1980.

Huey

Hal was very small when his mother died. Huey had wanted to put the child inside a new machine as its test pilot. Strangelove would not have it, so he shut her in one of her own machines, where she suffocated. In 1984 the soldiers of Diamond Dogs held him guilty of that, as of much else. They put him to sea in a lifeboat.

Huey married again. His second wife, Julie Danziger, had a small daughter, Emma, who adored her new brother. In 1997 Huey drowned himself in the family swimming pool. He very nearly took Emma down with him, for she was six years old. Hal was not there to help, which Emma held against him for years.

REX

After his father's death Hal left home. He gave up school, taught himself over the internet, then went on to Princeton and to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where he took his doctorate young. The FBI employed him until it caught him reading its own files.

He loved Japanese cartoons about giant robots. His nickname, Otacon, came from a yearly gathering of their admirers. When the arms company ArmsTech hired him, he set out to build a robot of his own. The result was Metal Gear REX, which he had been told was a shield against missiles. He also invented a suit that made its wearer invisible.

In 2005, on Shadow Moses Island, Solid Snake found him hiding in a locker. Snake told him what REX was: a launcher for a nuclear warhead that no radar could see. Hal was the third generation of his family to build such a thing. He helped Snake to destroy it. During the incident he fell in love with one of the renegades, the sniper called Sniper Wolf, whom Snake killed.

Philanthropy

Afterwards Revolver Ocelot sold REX's design, so that every country with nuclear weapons soon had a Metal Gear of its own. Hal held himself to blame. With Snake he founded Philanthropy, a small body recognised by the United Nations, whose work was to find such machines so as to expose them. Mei Ling and Nastasha Romanenko, who had both helped Snake at Shadow Moses, joined them.

On 8 August 2007 a message that seemed to come from Emma sent Snake aboard a tanker on the Hudson to photograph the new Metal Gear RAY. It was a trap. Ocelot sank the tanker, then the blame was laid on Snake. For two years Hal kept up the pretence that Snake had drowned.

Emma had grown up to be a brilliant programmer. The Patriots had hired her to build their computer GW. On 29 April 2009 Hal found her among the hostages on the Big Shell, where she had written a virus to destroy her own creation. Before she could finish, she was stabbed by Vamp, a Romanian knife-fighter. Vamp was no vampire of Cain's blood. He was a living man with a liking for blood, kept from dying by machines in his veins. Emma died with Hal beside her.

Sunny

In 2011 Raiden brought Hal a small girl, Sunny, the daughter of the mercenary Olga Gurlukovich. The Patriots had held her since her birth. Hal brought her up. He taught her to program, at which she was soon very good.

In 2014 he guided the ageing Snake through his last mission from an aircraft, with a small robot that he had built with Sunny to scout ahead. That year he grew close to Dr Naomi Hunter, who died before it was over. Afterwards he stayed with Snake to the end. Later he adopted Sunny, who went on to design spacecraft.

pages.title: Hal Jordan
infobox: Green Lantern Corps; Justice League (founding member)
Vanished again, August 1994, after Zero Hour
pages.html:
Hal Jordan was Green Lantern for thirty-four years: the test pilot of Coast City who received his ring in 1959 and helped to found the Justice League. When Coast City was destroyed in 1993, he fell. At the turn of 1994 he destroyed the Green Lantern Corps and its masters, then vanished. His ring's last successor, Kyle Rayner, took his place. In July 1994 he came back as Parallax, the power behind Zero Hour, meaning to remake history so that Coast City had never fallen. The heroes stopped him at the beginning of time, and he vanished again.

The man without fear

Hal Jordan was a test pilot for Ferris Aircraft in Coast City, a man said to be entirely without fear. In 1959 the dying alien Abin Sur crash-landed in the California desert, and his power ring went looking for the one man fit to replace him. It found Hal. The Guardians of the Universe accepted him into the Green Lantern Corps as guardian of Earth's sector.

At the turn of 1960 he was among the founders of the Justice League. Over the next three decades his greatest enemy was Sinestro, a renegade Green Lantern. He also had to fight Carol Ferris, his employer and the love of his life, when she was possessed as Star Sapphire. In the early 1970s he travelled across America with Green Arrow, Oliver Queen, seeing the country's poverty and prejudice at first hand. He left the Corps and returned to it more than once.

He met Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, four times. In June 1962 he found him in the Bering Sea, bearing down on a Japanese crab fleet. Hal lifted the boats clear behind a wall of green light. His ring held against Godzilla's breath, which is the fire of the bomb, but it drained faster than he had ever known. In January 1965, in Japan with the Justice League, he found the ring useless against King Ghidorah, a dragon the colour of gold. He tried to wall Godzilla off from the flying monster Rodan instead, which neither of them noticed. On 19 December 1965, when the League went back, he did not try the dragon twice: he caged Rodan for most of an hour. In March 1972 he met the golden dragon again above the Earth, with no better luck.

Coast City and the fall

In the summer of 1993 Hal came home to find Coast City gone, destroyed by Mongul and the Cyborg Superman, with Engine City standing in its crater. He fought his way in, beat Mongul unconscious and stood with Superman at the end. Afterwards, alone in the ruins, he used his ring to raise a ghost of the city and the people he had known. The Guardians ordered him to stop and summoned him to Oa.

He went, but not as they expected. On the way he defeated every Lantern sent against him, and took their rings. He killed Sinestro, and his old friend Kilowog. Then he drained the Central Power Battery into himself. The Guardians died and the Corps fell. Hal Jordan vanished from public view, and all the public has known since is that the old Green Lantern is gone.

Parallax and Zero Hour

In July 1994 time began to fail across the world in the catastrophe called Zero Hour. Its visible face was the time-mad Extant, but the power behind it was Hal Jordan, now calling himself Parallax. With the power of the Central Power Battery inside him, he meant to unmake history and build it again. In the new history Coast City would never have been destroyed, and nothing else he could not forgive would have happened either.

The heroes would not let him. At the beginning of time they stood against him, Kyle Rayner among them. Connor Hawke, the young son of Hal's old companion of the road, Oliver Queen, shot him through the heart. Hal survived even that, and vanished again when time was begun anew early in August. Of all this the public knows very little. To most of the world the old Green Lantern simply vanished at the turn of the year.

In the saga

In August 1994 Harry Potter noticed that the young Green Lantern standing behind Superman had turned up out of nowhere in January, after the old one vanished.

pages.title: Hank Shepard
infobox: Starfleet; security officer aboard the USS Einstein; resigned 2252
21 August 2268, on Mindoir, killed by the Orion Syndicate
pages.html:
Hank Shepard was the father of John Shepard. He had been a Starfleet security officer aboard the USS Einstein before he left the service to farm on Mindoir. Slavers of the Orion Syndicate killed him there in 2268.

Life

Hank Shepard married Hannah, a fellow officer, while both were in Starfleet. They resigned together in 2252 to raise a family on Mindoir. He taught his son, John, to shoot, to farm, to mend what was broken.

On 21 August 2268 the Orion Syndicate raided the colony. Hank held the farmhouse with his wife for most of the night. When it fell, the slavers tortured him to death, with Hannah and their daughter, Jane, while John was made to watch.

In the saga

Hank Shepard has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Hannah Shepard
infobox: Starfleet; lieutenant commander aboard the USS Kilimanjaro; resigned 2252
21 August 2268, on Mindoir, killed by the Orion Syndicate
pages.html:
Hannah Shepard was the mother of John Shepard. She had been a Starfleet officer, a lieutenant commander aboard the USS Kilimanjaro, before she resigned her commission to raise a family on Mindoir. Slavers of the Orion Syndicate killed her there in 2268.

Life

Hannah Shepard met her husband, Hank, in Starfleet. In 2252 the two of them resigned their commissions together to settle on the farming colony of Mindoir. Their son, John, was born there in 2253, with their daughter, Jane, following in 2258.

When the Orion Syndicate raided Mindoir on 21 August 2268, she fought the slavers beside her husband from their farmhouse through most of the night. The slavers tortured her to death afterwards, with Hank and Jane, in front of her son.

In the saga

Hannah Shepard has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Harry Mason
infobox: Cheryl Mason, found in the summer of 1976; raised a second time from September 1983, as Heather
Portland, to 1988; afterwards under another name elsewhere
The god of the Order of Silent Hill, 13 September 1983
16 September 2000, murdered on the orders of Claudia Wolf
pages.html:
Harry Mason is an American writer, a widower who lives quietly with his daughter under a name that is not quite their own. In September 1983 he went into Silent Hill after his missing seven-year-old, Cheryl. He came out with a newborn baby, having killed the thing the town's cult called its god. He has no magic, no training and no powers of any kind. He raised the child as his own for seventeen years. In September 2000 the Order of Silent Hill found them, and Harry was murdered in his own armchair.

The child on the highway

Harry was born about 1951. He married his school sweetheart, Jodie, and made his living by writing. They wanted children. An illness had left Jodie unable to have any.

In the summer of 1976 the two of them were driving home from a holiday when they found a baby girl lying at the side of the highway, not far from Silent Hill. Nobody claimed her. They adopted her, and called her Cheryl. Jodie died three years later, in 1979, after which Harry brought Cheryl up alone. He did not know that she was half of another child's soul.

Silent Hill, 1983

In September 1983, when Cheryl was seven, she asked to be taken to Silent Hill for a holiday. On Monday 12 September they were still on the road after dark. A police motorcycle overtook them. Then a girl stepped out into the headlights. Harry swerved, and the car went off the road.

He woke at the wheel in daylight, in thick fog, with snow falling out of season. Cheryl was gone. He followed a small figure into an alley, where the daylight failed and the walls turned to rusted wire. Something with knives came at him out of the dark.

He woke again in a café, unhurt. A police officer from Brahms, Cybil Bennett, was sitting opposite him. She had found the town empty, with the telephones dead. She gave him a pistol and went to look for help. Harry went to look for his daughter.

The search took him through the whole of the town. At Midwich Elementary School he first saw the dark side of the place, which changed around him at the sound of a siren. At a church an old woman, Dahlia Gillespie, pressed a charm called the Flauros into his hand. She told him to hurry to the hospital. At Alchemilla Hospital he met its director, Dr Michael Kaufmann, who seemed as lost as he was. He also met a frightened nurse, Lisa Garland, who was the only person in Silent Hill to show him any kindness.

Dahlia told him that the town was being swallowed by darkness. A demon was marking it with its sign, she said, and the girl he had seen in the road was at the bottom of it. Unless she was stopped, Cheryl would die. Harry believed her. He had no reason not to.

The lake shore

By the time Harry reached the resort district on the lake, the dark world had covered the whole town. In a bar he shot a creature that had Kaufmann on the floor. At a motel Harry found a flask of red liquid hidden in the fuel tank of a motorcycle. Kaufmann snatched it from him and left.

At the amusement park Cybil turned her gun on him. A parasite had got into her, and she no longer knew him. Harry had picked up a bottle of the same red liquid at the hospital without knowing what it was. He threw it over her, and the parasite came out. It was aglaophotis, which drives out demons.

Then the girl from the road was there in front of him. The Flauros in his pocket woke, and her power went out like a lamp. Dahlia stepped forward to collect her. It was her own daughter, Alessa Gillespie, she explained. Harry had been the only person who could get close enough.

Harry went after them into the place underneath the town. There he met Lisa Garland for the last time. She had worked out that she was dead, as dead as the nurses who walked the dark hospital, and she begged him to help her. He could not. He fled, shutting the door between them, and read her diary afterwards.

The god

At the bottom of it all, on the night of 13 September, he found Dahlia, with a burnt girl in a wheelchair and the girl from the road kneeling beside it. Dahlia told him the truth at last. Seven years before, she had burnt her daughter to bring the Order's god to birth. The child's soul had split, and the half that escaped had been Cheryl. Now the halves were one again. There was no Cheryl to give back.

The god began to come. Kaufmann walked in, furious at having been used, and threw his flask of aglaophotis at it. What tore itself free was a winged thing with the head of a goat. It killed Dahlia where she stood. Harry killed it. It had only just been born into flesh, and flesh can be shot.

As the place burnt around them, the girl held out a newborn baby. Harry took it. She showed him a way out and stayed behind. Kaufmann tried to follow, but Lisa Garland rose up at his feet, took hold of him and dragged him down. Harry left Silent Hill with Cybil Bennett beside him and the child in his arms.

Heather

He wrote afterwards, in a notebook meant for the child, that he had not known what to do with her. He had thought of leaving her somewhere. Once or twice he had thought of worse. She was what his daughter had become, though, and in the end he could not do anything but love her. He gave her Cheryl's name.

He told nobody what had happened. A man who says that he shot a god in the fog does not keep his daughter for long.

The two of them lived in Portland until 1988. That year a man from the Order found them, and Harry shot him. The police ruled that he had acted in self-defence. Harry moved away with the girl, and from then on she went by the name Heather. In the summer of 1994 they are living quietly in another city. She is ten.

He gave her a pendant for one of her birthdays. Inside it was a tablet of aglaophotis.

Death

In 2000 Claudia Wolf, a priestess of the Order, traced Heather through a private detective, Douglas Cartland. On Saturday 16 September, while Heather was out, Claudia sent one of the Order's creatures to their flat. Heather came home to find her father dead in his chair.

Claudia told her that it was payment for 1983. It was also meant to make the girl hate, since hatred was what the god inside her fed on. Cartland helped Heather lay her father on his bed. He gave her the notebook, in which Harry had written down the whole story for her.

Heather went to Silent Hill the next day. She killed the god her father had killed before her, and wept for him when it was done.

pages.title: Hastur
infobox: Ambrose Bierce; Robert W. Chambers; Delta Green
A force, not a being, in Delta Green's reckoning
The old name for the force now called entropy
The Yellow Sign; the play The King in Yellow
The name of a place, beside Aldebaran and the Hyades
pages.html:
Hastur is the name that Delta Green gives to the force behind the King in Yellow. Its files are plain that Hastur is not a being. It is not one of the Great Old Ones, it has no mind or personality, and it is the old name for the force that men now call entropy, by which all made things run down. The King in Yellow, who rules in Carcosa, is its avatar.

The name in 1895

The readers of the play in 1895 used the name for a place. Hildred Castaigne wrote of 'Carcosa, the Hyades, Hastur, and Aldebaran'. He called himself king by right in Hastur. Mr Wilde told him of the lakes which connected Hastur, Aldebaran and the Hyades. In Paris Alec named Hastur among the stars, with Aldebaran, the Hyades and Alar. On the night Tessie Reardon died in New York, she had talked with the painter Scott of Hastur and of Cassilda.

None of them spoke of Hastur as a being. Delta Green's files use the name for something else. This page follows them for what Hastur is, and the readers of 1895 for what was said then.

Delta Green's reckoning

In Delta Green's files Hastur is the old name for the force that men now call entropy. It is not one of the Great Old Ones. It has no sentience and no personality. It wears down whole civilisations by infecting the minds of their people with ideas, until they come apart.

The King in Yellow is its avatar, worshipped as a god by those who serve him, and the ruler of Carcosa. He never speaks, so that little else is known of him. The play that bears his name, the Yellow Sign and Carcosa itself are all Hastur at work, in Delta Green's reckoning. Under its influence reality as men know it breaks down.

Delta Green's later files are a little less certain. They call Hastur more a force of nature than a being in its own right. The King in Yellow, they say, is believed to be one of its manifestations.

Hastur and God

A force without a mind is no rival to God. It has no will to set against His. Whatever will is at work in Carcosa is the King's, and the King is God's creature, not His equal.

Delta Green and Hastur

Delta Green does not hunt Hastur, since nobody can hunt a force. It hunts what Hastur carries: the play, the Sign and the people who have taken them in. Since 1 September 1955 its rule for them has been the STATIC Protocol. Under it everything they have touched is destroyed, Delta Green's own agents included.

In 1995 Delta Green's agents followed the play into the Night Floors above a building in Manhattan. In 2015 the Outlaws followed it into Carcosa. The King in Yellow, the play, the Yellow Sign and Carcosa each have a page of their own.

pages.title: Hedorah
infobox: A creature of living sludge, from space
pages.html:
Hedorah was a monster of living sludge that fed on pollution. It came to Earth from space, then grew enormous on the filth of Suruga Bay in 1971. Its poisonous mist killed thousands. It died on the slopes of Mount Fuji, dried to dust by Godzilla.

Suruga Bay

Hedorah arrived as a spore from somewhere among the stars. It fell into the sea off Fuji City, an industrial town whose factories emptied their waste into Suruga Bay. There it began to feed.

At first it looked like a tadpole. A fisherman brought one to the marine biologist Dr Toru Yano, who dived to look for more. The one he met was a good deal larger. It burnt half his face.

His small son, Ken, gave the creature its name, from the Japanese word for sludge. It fed on oil tankers, then came ashore to breathe at factory chimneys. With every meal it changed its shape. Soon it could fly. Wherever it passed, its mist of acid killed the people in the streets below, leaving bones behind.

It had one other enemy in the bay. The Sub-Mariner, who rules a kingdom under the sea, came to find out what was killing the fish. He fought Hedorah under water for a night. It burnt him as it had burnt Dr Yano, so he left it to Godzilla.

Mount Fuji

Dr Yano worked out that sludge can be dried. The Self-Defence Forces built two giant electrodes on the slopes of Mount Fuji to do it. Godzilla, who had fought Hedorah before, met it there. Its acid closed one of his eyes in the struggle. When the power to the electrodes failed, Godzilla fired them himself with his breath.

Hedorah's dried husk split, then a last piece of it flew off. Godzilla flew after it, driving himself backwards through the air with his own fire, which he has not been seen to do before or since. He brought the piece back to the electrodes to finish it.

Dr Yano warned that as long as the filth remained, another Hedorah might grow in it.

pages.title: Henry Townshend
infobox: Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, summer 2002 to June 2004
The twenty-first sacrament, the Receiver of Wisdom
pages.html:
Henry Townshend was a quiet young photographer who took a flat in South Ashfield in the summer of 2002. It was the wrong flat. Room 302 was the centre of a rite that the murderer Walter Sullivan had been working for ten years, from beyond his own death. Henry was meant to be its twenty-first victim, the last. On 12 June 2004 he was sealed inside the flat. He came out of it having put an end to Walter Sullivan.

Room 302

Henry was born in the mid-1970s. He was a man who kept to himself, with a camera for company. As a boy he had been taken to Silent Hill, like any other tourist, and he had photographs of the town on his wall.

In the summer of 2002 he moved into Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, a block of flats half a day's drive from Silent Hill. The tenant before him, a journalist, had disappeared six months earlier. That spring the flat had been measured twice by men who found nothing wrong with it. For two years Henry lived there happily enough. His neighbour in Room 303 was Eileen Galvin.

The hole

On 12 June 2004 Henry woke from a nightmare to find his front door chained shut from the inside, with a warning not to go out painted on it. The nightmare came back every night. The windows would not open. The telephone was dead. He shouted, he hammered on the walls, and nobody heard him, though he could see his neighbours through the spyhole going about their day.

On 17 June, after five days, a hole opened in the wall of his bathroom. Henry crawled into it, having nowhere else to go. It let him out in a railway station under the city, empty but for a frightened woman called Cynthia Velasquez, who thought that she was dreaming. She was stabbed to death there. Henry woke in his own bed, with the door still chained. The radio was reporting that Cynthia Velasquez had been found dead.

It happened three times more, on the three days that followed. The hole took him to the woods outside Silent Hill, where a stammering young man named Jasper Gein burnt to death at an orphanage. It took him to a round prison standing in water, where a fat, terrified guard, Andrew DeSalvo, was drowned. It took him to a rooftop world of shops and flats, where his neighbour Richard Braintree was electrocuted. Each of the bodies had numbers cut into it.

Eileen

Pages of a diary kept turning up in the flat, pushed under his door. They had been written by Joseph Schreiber, the journalist who had lived there before him. From them Henry learnt the name of Walter Sullivan. He learnt about the 21 Sacraments, the numbers on the bodies and how far the count had gone. Nineteen were dead.

The twentieth was to be Eileen Galvin. Henry could see into her flat through a hole in his wall. He could not warn her. On the evening of 21 June he found his way at last into a copy of his own building, in time to see the man in the coat go into her flat. When Henry got through the door she was lying in her own blood. A small boy was standing beside her. An ambulance came for her in the waking world, and Henry woke to hear its siren.

He found her again in the dark side of St Jerome's Hospital, bandaged, on her feet, with her arm in a plaster cast. She could not go back through the holes as he could. So the two of them went on down together, through each of the places he had already seen, with the dead of those places walking in them.

The end of Walter Sullivan

At the bottom of the stair they came to Room 302 as it had been years before. Joseph Schreiber's ghost was waiting there, with his head hanging down through the ceiling. He told them everything. Walter Sullivan had made that whole world by a rite worked in the flat. Eileen was to be the Mother Reborn. Henry was the Receiver of Wisdom. There was one way out, which was to kill a man who was already dead.

Henry went back up to his flat and took a pickaxe to the wall of the store room. Walter Sullivan's body was hanging behind it, as it had hung there for ten years. In the superintendent's rooms Henry found the cord that had joined the infant Walter to his mother. Frank Sunderland had kept it in a box since 1970.

The last place was a pit beyond the flat, with a great wheel of blades turning in it. Eileen, who was no longer herself, was walking slowly towards the blades. Henry used the cord on the creature that sat at the centre of the place. He drove eight spears into it, one after another. Walter Sullivan became a mortal man again, and Henry killed him. It was 22 June 2004.

Eileen stopped at the edge of the wheel. Henry went to see her in hospital afterwards, with flowers. She said that she supposed she would have to find somewhere else to live.

pages.title: Heru'ur
infobox: Horus the Elder, the falcon god of Egypt
Killed by Thor on Cimmeria, about 870
2000, in the Tobin minefield, killed by Apophis
pages.html:
Heru'ur is one of the Goa'uld System Lords, the son of Ra and his queen, Hathor. He goes by the name of Horus the Elder, the falcon god of Egypt. He is a conqueror, much feared among the Goa'uld, but twice he was driven off the same cold world by Asgard: by Thor himself about the year 870, and by an Asgard ship in 1998. In 2000 he went to meet his father's old rival Apophis to talk of an alliance, and Apophis killed him.

Son of Ra

Heru'ur is the son of Ra, the last Supreme System Lord, by Ra's queen, Hathor. He takes his name from Horus the Elder, the falcon-headed god of Egypt, and his Jaffa wear the falcon as their mark. His own guards are the Horus Guards, in helmets made in the likeness of a falcon's head. They are the same helmets that Ra's guards wore in Egypt.

He is a conqueror by nature. For most of his long life he has been at war with one or another of them. His bitterest enemies are Apophis, his father's old rival, and Sokar.

Cimmeria

About the year 870, in the days of the Vikings, Heru'ur defied his father's ban on Earth. He carried off the people of several Norse settlements to a cold world far away, to be his slaves. He was Ra's own son, and of all the Goa'uld he ought to have known better.

Thor followed him. He came down on that world in a storm that lasted three days. He killed Heru'ur's First Prime in front of the army, then killed the army. He tore Heru'ur's ship out of the sky and broke it on the mountains. Heru'ur got away in a cargo ship with a handful of guards, leaving everyone else behind.

Thor did not bring the Northmen home. He judged them safer where they were, under his own protection, than they would be if the Goa'uld were shown the way back to Earth. Their world is now called Cimmeria. Thor left a device there, known as Thor's Hammer, which seizes any Goa'uld who comes through the gate. The Jaffa still tell the story to their recruits, to frighten them.

Against Asgard

Heru'ur went to the other System Lords. Towards the end of the tenth century he, Apophis and Ba'al brought their fleets together to strike at the worlds of Asgard. Thor met them above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space. He destroyed two of the three fleets, Heru'ur's among them, then went down after the survivors and finished them on the ground. Heru'ur himself escaped, as he had a way of doing. Apophis saved his own fleet by running.

The System Lords asked for terms soon afterwards, and the Protected Planets Treaty followed. Cimmeria was on its list.

After Ra

In 1994 the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, destroyed Ra above Abydos. Heru'ur lost his father, but he did not get his father's place. It was Apophis, his father's old rival, who moved fastest to take Ra's worlds.

Cimmeria again

In 1997 a team from Earth came through the gate to Cimmeria. Thor's Hammer seized one of them, the Jaffa Teal'c, for the larva he carried. To free him, his friends destroyed it.

Heru'ur heard of it. In 1998 he came back to Cimmeria with his Jaffa, for the first time since Thor had driven him off, to take it at last. The Cimmerians called on Asgard through the hall that Thor had left them, and Asgard answered. A ship came out of the sky over Cimmeria. Many of Heru'ur's Jaffa were destroyed, and the rest were taken off the planet. Heru'ur escaped through the Stargate. It was the second time he had left an army behind on that world.

The ship was Thor's own, the Biliskner, and Thor was aboard it. He had been back at the head of Asgard's fleet in the Pegasus galaxy for less than a year, after more than a year in which Asgard had believed him dead. It was the first time that SG-1, the team from Earth, had met him.

The Harcesis

Later that year Heru'ur came to Abydos with his Horus Guards. He had learnt that Sha'uri, the host of Apophis's queen, Amaunet, had borne Apophis a son. A child of two Goa'uld hosts is called a Harcesis. Goa'uld law forbids it, because it is born with all the knowledge of the Goa'uld. Heru'ur meant to have both mother and child.

Two of SG-1, Daniel Jackson and Teal'c, were on Abydos before him. They met him in the pyramid that holds the gate. After a fight he went back up to his ship by the rings, without the child or its mother. The boy stayed hidden. Apophis came to believe that Heru'ur had stolen him, which did nothing to mend matters between them.

The war with Apophis

Earth destroyed Apophis's motherships in 1998, and Heru'ur made the most of his rival's weakness. Early in 2000 two of Heru'ur's motherships chased Apophis's son, Klorel, to Tollana, the world of the Tollans. The Tollans' guns destroyed them both.

By the autumn of 2000 Heru'ur and Apophis commanded the two largest armies the Goa'uld had. Together they could have overthrown every other System Lord; at war, they would have ruined each other. They agreed to meet alone in the Tobin minefield, a belt of floating mines left by a people long extinct, to talk of an alliance.

Heru'ur brought a gift to seal the bargain: Teal'c, who had been betrayed on Chulak and given to Heru'ur's torturer, Terok, to be broken. Teal'c would not break. Rak'nor, the Jaffa who had betrayed him, watched him hold out and changed his mind. He struck Terok down, freed Teal'c and sent the senseless Terok across to Apophis in Teal'c's place.

Apophis had not come alone after all. A whole fleet of his lay hidden close by under cloak. When he found that Heru'ur had not given him Teal'c, he brought it out and destroyed Heru'ur's ship, with Heru'ur aboard. Heru'ur's fleet and Jaffa passed to Apophis, who now led the largest army of any Goa'uld alive.

Heru'ur had twice run from Thor. He did not see Apophis coming.

pages.title: Hildred Castaigne
infobox: 'The Repairer of Reputations', The King in Yellow (1895)
While recovering from a fall from his horse
Dr John Archer, who kept him for a time in his private asylum
Mr Wilde, the repairer of reputations, of Bleecker Street
Heir to an imperial throne of America that never existed
1895, in the Asylum for Criminal Insane
pages.html:
Hildred Castaigne was a New Yorker who read The King in Yellow after a fall from his horse, and never came back from it. He came to believe that he was the heir of an imperial house of America that had never existed, and that a little crippled man of Bleecker Street, Mr Wilde, was helping him to its throne. In 1895 Mr Wilde was found dead with his throat torn open, and Castaigne was taken away by the police. He died in the Asylum for Criminal Insane.

The fall and the play

Castaigne was thrown from his horse. For a long time afterwards he suffered pains in the back of his head and neck. While he was recovering he bought a copy of The King in Yellow. He threw it into the fire at the end of the first act. It fell open on the hearth, and he caught sight of the opening words of the second. He snatched it from the coals. He read it over many times, weeping, laughing and trembling.

Dr John Archer pronounced his brain affected, and kept him in his private asylum. At last Archer decided that he was well. Castaigne never forgave him.

Mr Wilde

Mr Wilde lived at the top of a shabby house on Bleecker Street, where Hawberk the armourer kept his shop. He was a very small man, no taller than a boy of ten, with a yellow face and pale eyes. He had no ears of his own, and wore false ones of wax, painted pink. His left hand had no fingers. He called himself a repairer of reputations. He kept ledgers of his clients, and claimed to have hundreds of men at his command.

He kept a cat, a savage creature that he tormented, and that flew at him whenever it could. He also kept a manuscript, which he showed to Castaigne. It set out a royal line running from Carcosa, by way of names from the play, Uoht, Thale, Naotalba and the Phantom of Truth, to Aldones. It ended with Hildred Castaigne himself, the last heir of the Imperial Dynasty of America.

The world that was not

Castaigne wrote his story down as though it were the spring of 1920, a quarter of a century on. In the New York he describes, the government has built a Lethal Chamber on Washington Square where anybody who wishes may die painlessly, and an empire is waiting for its king. None of it existed. It was the world he lived in after he read the play, and nobody else lived in it.

His own account gives him away. He describes a crown of heavy beaten gold; his cousin Louis called it a brass crown. The steel safe in which he kept it was, to Louis, a biscuit box.

1895

In 1895 Castaigne went to his cousin Louis with three demands. Louis was to give up his place in the succession, accept exile and never marry. Louis humoured him until Hildred forbade him to marry Constance Hawberk, the armourer's daughter, whom he loved. Then Hildred told him that he had murdered Dr Archer, and that Constance had been put out of the way.

He ran back to Mr Wilde's rooms. In the dark of the doorway the cat sprang at him, and his knife flew. When the light came Mr Wilde lay on the floor with his throat torn open, his eyes rolling back. The police came and dragged Castaigne away, while Constance, very much alive, wept.

Whether he had really killed Dr Archer, his account does not make plain. Who or what had torn Mr Wilde's throat, it does not say. Castaigne died in the Asylum for Criminal Insane.

Where the accounts disagree

Castaigne's account, the only one there is of these things, makes Mr Wilde a man, if a very strange one, and this page follows it for the 1890s. Delta Green's files of 2015 hold that Mr Wilde was something other than a man.

pages.title: Hillhurst Mansion
infobox: Flabber, Count Fangula, Mums, Frankenbeans, Ghoulum and the Pipettes; Wolfgang Smith, from 1996; Little Ghoul, from 1997
pages.html:
Hillhurst Mansion is a big old house outside Charterville, which has stood in disrepair since its last owner, Old Man Hillhurst, died. The town says that it is haunted. This understates the case: a vampire, a mummy and a creature built by a mad doctor live in it, with a phasm shut in the pipe organ. From September 1996 it was the meeting place of the Beetleborgs.

The house

Nobody among the living has kept Hillhurst up since Old Man Hillhurst died. The children of Charterville dare one another to go in. The household regards a trespasser as a meal that has been good enough to deliver itself, so it chases each one through the house with that in mind.

The pipe organ is the heart of the place. In the summer of 1994 Flabber, a phasm, is shut inside it, together with three singing spirits called the Pipettes.

The household

Count Fangula is a true vampire, one of the Kindred of Cain. He is an old Malkavian whose madness long ago turned harmless and theatrical, which is why the Camarilla leaves him where he is.

Mums is a mummy, one of the undying of old Egypt, who was a prince there some five thousand years ago. Frankenbeans was built by Dr Baron von Frankenbeans, which makes him nobody's kin. Ghoulum is a stone statue that happens to be alive, though he seldom troubles to move.
