Two more came later. Wolfgang Smith arrived in September 1996. He is a Garou whose mind is gone, more dog than wolf, whom the others keep as a pet. Little Ghoul moved into the basement in September 1997. She is called a ghoul without being one in the Kindred's sense, a servant bound by blood.

Flabber is the head of the house. Once he was out of the organ, it was he who decided who might come in without being eaten.

The Beetleborgs

On 7 September 1996 the brothers Trip and Van dared three other children to go into Hillhurst. Drew McCormick, his sister, Jo, and their friend Roland Williams went in. They ran from the household, knocked against the organ and let Flabber out. He granted them the wish that made them the Beetleborgs.

From then on the three came to Hillhurst nearly every day. It was the one place in Charterville where they could talk freely, since everybody in it knew who they were. Art Fortunes, who drew their armour, became a regular caller too. In May 1997, with Flabber shut back in his organ for a time, the household was making ready to eat him when the children arrived.

Callers

Trip and Van never forgave the house for frightening them. In September 1996 they hired a demolition company to pull it down, then a phasm hunter to clear it. Neither did the work. The same month some bank robbers chose Hillhurst as a hiding place, which no sensible robber would have done.

In April 1997 Old Man Hillhurst came back. A Magnavore monster had been playing the trumpet badly over his grave. He rose as a wraith, one of the restless dead, held to the world by the house he could not let go. He did his best to drive the household out of it.

In September 1997 the household tried to raise money by opening Hillhurst as a hotel for monsters. On Hallowe'en that year Mums lured a party of local children up to the house. The Beetleborgs spent the evening seeing to it that every one of them went home again.

Under attack

Hillhurst was attacked more than once, because Flabber lived there. On 3 May 1997 Elgar, the nephew of the space pirate Divatox, broke in with a crew of Piranhatrons to carry Flabber off. The household took it badly. Frankenbeans was seen with a Piranhatron under each arm, and Wolfgang bit Elgar. The Turbo Rangers arrived in the middle of it. They had supper there afterwards.

Later that month Nukus bombed the house while his monster Borgslayer was loose. On 8 September 1997 he came back to turn Flabber to ice.

In November 1997 both sides hunted for the eight Astral Coins, several of which turned up at Hillhurst. Mums had one, Wolfgang had another, and Count Fangula swallowed a third. For a while the rest were locked in Little Ghoul's safe.

pages.title: Hollis Tibbetts
infobox: Special agent of the Drug Enforcement Administration
From 1979; Agent Homer of H Cell from 1994; one of the Outlaws from 2001
22 June 1994, in the Silent Hill morgue incident
pages.html:
Hollis Tibbetts is an American narcotics agent and a member of Delta Green, in which he goes by the name of Agent Homer. No agent of Delta Green has given more years to Silent Hill, in Maine. He went there first in September 1983, a few days too late. He went back in June 1994 for the body of the murderer Walter Sullivan. He came away with a bullet in his hip and nothing else. In the summer of 1994 he is forty-seven, and walking with a stick.

The Bureau

Hollis Tibbetts was born about 1947 in Bangor, Maine. He joined the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs in 1970. It became the Drug Enforcement Administration in 1973, and he went with it. In 1979, after a case in the north woods that he could not explain to his superiors, an older agent took him for a drink and told him what Delta Green was.

He was married, with a daughter. His wife left him in 1985, taking the girl with her. She said afterwards that she had never known where he was or what he was doing, and that he came home from it a stranger.

Silent Hill, 1983

In 1983 a narcotics officer of Silent Hill had been sending samples of a drug called PTV to the Boston office of the DEA, with what he knew of the men who sold it. Tibbetts had the file. That summer the mayor of Silent Hill, who had campaigned against the drug, died suddenly. Not long afterwards the narcotics officer died too, of a failed heart, with no history of heart trouble. Tibbetts did not think it a coincidence.

He reached Silent Hill a few days after 13 September 1983. Something had happened there; everybody could tell him that much. The telephones had been dead for a night and a day. The director of Alchemilla Hospital, whom the narcotics officer had suspected above anybody, had disappeared. Nobody would say anything more. Tibbetts took the hospital's ledgers of the trade, read them in his motel room and burnt them.

In October he came back with a can of petrol and burnt the beds of White Claudia in the marsh, the plant from which the drug was made. They grew back the next summer. The SCP Foundation, which had been watching the town for years, took seed from the new growth. Its file records that the beds had been burnt 'by persons unknown'.

Agent Homer

In 1994, after the murder of General Reginald Fairfield, Delta Green was rebuilt as a conspiracy of cells. Tibbetts became Agent Homer of H Cell. Another agent of the cell was an FBI agent known in it as Hazel.

In June 1994 Walter Sullivan killed ten people in Silent Hill, Pleasant River and Ashfield. He cut out their hearts and carved numbers into the bodies. The first two to die were priests at Wish House, the orphanage by the lake that belonged to the Order of Silent Hill. Tibbetts knew the name. Hazel had herself attached to the case. Sullivan was arrested on 18 June, and they arranged to question him on the 22nd.

He killed himself in his cell early that morning. That night Tibbetts and Hazel went to the morgue to claim the body, with a friendly from the FBI waiting outside in the car. They found the SCP Foundation there before them, with papers as good as their own. Tibbetts took its people for the enforcers of Majestic 12, who had killed Fairfield four months before. In a minute of darkness somebody fired. When the lights came back a Foundation officer was dead, Tibbetts had a bullet in his hip and the body had gone from its drawer. He has never known who fired the shot that hit him.

Alphonse ruled that the men at the morgue had been the Foundation, not Majestic, and closed Delta Green's file on Silent Hill. He forbade any agent to go back. In the summer of 1994 Tibbetts is on sick leave from the DEA, with a story about a fall on a boat.

Afterwards

He went back all the same, on his own time. In the summer of 1997 a schoolboy, Peter Walls, was found dead in South Ashfield with 12121 cut into him. The police called it the work of an imitator. Tibbetts read the number as a count, twelve of twenty-one. He spent two years trying to work out who the other nine were to be, and he never did.

He read what the journalist Joseph Schreiber wrote about Wish House in the magazine Concord, and decided to leave Schreiber alone. A small magazine that nobody believed was, in his view, as good a silence as any. When Schreiber vanished in 2001, Tibbetts went looking for him. He did not think to look in Schreiber's own flat.

After the attacks of 11 September 2001 he would not join the Program, and he became one of the Outlaws. In 2003 the Program sent for White Claudia from Silent Hill to study. Tibbetts burnt the beds a week before its people came. They came back the following summer and took what they wanted.

In June 2004 Walter Sullivan's body was found at last, in a hidden room of the very flat from which Schreiber had vanished. Tibbetts heard of it from a friendly in the FBI and drove to South Ashfield. The Foundation had taken the body two days before.

pages.title: Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
infobox: 'Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry' (28 June 2016)
Isolt Sayre and James Steward, with Chadwick and Webster Boot
The summit of Mount Greylock, Massachusetts, hidden from No-Maj eyes
The Sayre family cottage at Coomloughra, County Kerry, Ireland
Blue and cranberry robes fastened with a gold Gordian knot
Chadwick and Webster Boot; Tina and Queenie Goldstein; Agatha Harkness; Zatara; Zatanna Zatara; Stephen Strange
pages.html:
Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry is the wizarding school of North America. It stands hidden on the summit of Mount Greylock in Massachusetts, and it is one of the eleven long-established wizarding schools of the world. It was founded in the 1620s by Isolt Sayre and her No-Maj husband, James Steward. Isolt was an Irish witch of Salazar Slytherin's blood who had fled to America on the Mayflower. It is often called the most democratic of the great wizarding schools, and the least elitist. Its four houses are Horned Serpent, Wampus, Thunderbird and Pukwudgie.

Isolt Sayre

Isolt Sayre was born about 1603 at Ilvermorny, her family's cottage at Coomloughra in County Kerry. When she was five, her aunt Gormlaith Gaunt, a fanatical pure-blood of Salazar Slytherin's line, murdered her parents, burned the cottage and carried Isolt off to raise. Gormlaith kept the child shut away from the Muggle neighbours, whom she cursed, animals and all. She would not hear of Isolt going to Hogwarts.

In 1620, at about seventeen, Isolt stole her aunt's wand, which had once been Salazar Slytherin's own. She fled to the New World on the Mayflower, disguised as a Muggle boy called Elias Story, and took with her a brooch of her mother's in the shape of a Gordian knot.

The founding

In the forests of the new country Isolt met creatures she had never heard of: Hidebehinds, Hodags, Snallygasters, Wampus kittens and, in a river, a Horned Serpent whose speech she could understand, being of Slytherin's blood. She rescued a Pukwudgie, a small grey-faced cousin of the goblins, from a Hidebehind. She named him William, after her dead father. He became her companion and, in time, her friend.

With William she came upon two young wizards in the forest, the brothers Chadwick and Webster Boot. A Hidebehind had killed their parents, and the boys were wounded. Isolt took them in. When she went back to bury their parents, she met a No-Maj called James Steward and married him. Isolt had always spoken wistfully of the school she had never been allowed to attend. So the four of them set out to make one of their own, in their house on the summit of Mount Greylock, hidden from No-Maj eyes by enchantment. The Boot brothers were its first pupils. They brought to it something of the magic of the peoples who had lived in that land long before the colonists came.

Isolt named the school Ilvermorny, after the cottage where she was born. Accounts of the founding give dates anywhere from the early 1620s to 1634, because it became a school by degrees: it was a household that took in pupils long before it was a castle. It is usually dated to about 1627.

Gormlaith's attack

Gormlaith Gaunt followed her niece across the ocean, meaning to destroy Ilvermorny as she had destroyed the cottage in Kerry. Speaking in Parseltongue, she put Slytherin's wand to sleep in Isolt's hand. All the same, Isolt, James, the Boot brothers and William fought her off together. William shot Gormlaith through the heart with an arrow, and she shattered into pieces.

Afterwards Isolt buried Slytherin's wand in the grounds. A snakewood tree grew where it lay. Its leaves are said to have healing powers.

Houses and the Sorting

Each of the four first members of the household named a house after the creature of the new land that they most admired. Isolt chose the Horned Serpent, which favours scholars and the mind. Webster Boot chose the Wampus, which favours warriors and the body. Chadwick Boot chose the Thunderbird, which favours adventurers and the soul. James Steward named the last house after William the Pukwudgie; it favours healers and the heart.

New pupils are sorted in the round entrance hall, not in a great hall. Each stands in turn on the Gordian knot set into the stone floor, while the staff and the older pupils look down from the balcony. Then the four great wooden carvings of the houses give their answer. The crystal in the Horned Serpent's forehead lights up, the Wampus roars, the Thunderbird beats its wings, the Pukwudgie raises its arrow. If more than one carving answers, the pupil chooses.

The school

Ilvermorny's pupils wear robes of blue and cranberry, fastened with a gold Gordian knot in memory of Isolt's mother's brooch. Isolt and James both lived past a hundred. Isolt served as the school's headmistress, James as its headmaster. Their twin daughters were Martha, a Squib, who married a No-Maj, and Rionach, who taught Defence Against the Dark Arts at the school. By the nineteenth century Ilvermorny was renowned throughout the wizarding world. Statues of its founders stand beside the castle doors.

The school takes any child in North America who shows magic, whatever their family, and it has always been proud of doing so. Chadwick Boot's books of charms became standard texts, known simply as Chadwick's Charms.

Under MACUSA and Rappaport's Law

After the Salem witch trials of 1692 and 1693, American wizardry came under the Magical Congress of the United States of America, MACUSA. From 1790 Rappaport's Law, named after MACUSA's President Emily Rappaport, forbade witches and wizards to befriend or marry No-Majs. For 175 years Ilvermorny's pupils grew up in a wizarding America more closed off from its neighbours than any other in the world. The school went on admitting No-Maj-born children all the same. The law was repealed in 1965.

Pupils and staff

Among Ilvermorny's pupils in the early twentieth century were the Goldstein sisters of New York, Porpentina and Queenie. Eulalie Hicks taught Charms there in the 1930s. The stage magician Zatara was a pupil in the 1920s. His half-blood daughter, Zatanna Zatara, was there from 1955 to 1962 as a Thunderbird, before she made her name as a stage magician and, from 1978, as a member of the Justice League.

Agatha Harkness, who came through the Salem trials of 1692, was a pupil in the school's first century, when it was still more household than castle. Stephen Strange, a No-Maj-born boy from Philadelphia, was there from 1942 to 1949 as a Pukwudgie. The school treated him fairly. The old pure-blood families of wizarding America did not, and when he left at the top of his year he left the wizarding world with it.

A witch the school never found

Ilvermorny has never claimed to find every magical child in North America. Alessa Gillespie was born about 1969 at Silent Hill, in Maine, to a No-Maj mother who belonged to the town's cult. She was burnt at seven, in the summer of 1976, four years before a letter would have gone to her. The newspapers reported her dead. She lived until 1983 in a hospital basement, and no witch or wizard ever knew that she had existed.

Ilvermorny and its neighbours

Ilvermorny is one of the eleven long-established wizarding schools of the world; Hogwarts, Beauxbatons and Durmstrang are among the others. It should not be confused with the Salem Witches' Institute, which is not a school at all but a society of American witches named after the town of the trials.

pages.title: Inhumans
infobox: An offshoot of mankind, changed by the Kree
Some thousands of years after the Flood
An island in the North Atlantic; a hidden valley in the Himalayas; the Blue Area of the Moon (since 1982)
Black Bolt, Medusa, Karnak, Gorgon, Triton, Crystal, Lockjaw
Maximus the Mad, Black Bolt's brother
About a hundred and fifty years
Extinct by the end of the Third World War
pages.html:
The Inhumans are a hidden people descended from a tribe of men on whom the Kree once experimented. Their powers come from the Terrigen Mists, which change every Inhuman who breathes them, and not always for the better. For thousands of years they have kept apart in their city of Attilan, which has stood on an island in the North Atlantic, in a hidden valley of the Himalayas and, since 1982, on the Moon. They came to the notice of the outside world in 1965, through the Fantastic Four, who have been their friends ever since. They are ruled by Black Bolt, a king who never speaks, because the faintest whisper from him can shake a building.

The Kree's experiment

The Inhumans began as ordinary men. In the thousands of years after the Flood, while most men still lived by hunting, the Kree came to Earth. They were at war with the Skrulls, as they have been for longer than anyone can remember. From a station on Uranus they had noticed that the people of Earth carried a strange capacity for change in their blood, which the Kree, who had none left of their own, wanted to understand. They took a tribe of hunters and set to work on them, hoping to make soldiers for the war.

Then they lost interest and went away. They left behind a people stronger, quicker and longer-lived than other men. In their blood the capacity for change had been woken, though not yet used. The Kree also left them weaker against sickness than other men, which is why the dirt and diseases of the outside world have troubled the Inhumans ever since.

The Inhumans do not count themselves men, and most of them would be offended to be taken for one. An Inhuman lives about a hundred and fifty years.

Attilan

About seven thousand years ago the Inhumans built a city on an island far out in the North Atlantic, and called it Attilan. They kept to themselves, and the outside world forgot them, if it had ever known of them at all.

Attilan stayed on its island until the twentieth century, when the ships and aeroplanes of the outside world began to come too close. Early in his reign Black Bolt moved it. The Inhumans lifted the whole city from its foundations and carried it to a hidden valley high in the Himalayas, with help from the Eternals, the immortal people to whom Sersi of the Avengers belongs. There it became known as the Great Refuge.

The Terrigen Mists

In the early days of Attilan its king, Randac, found the Terrigen Mists in the caverns beneath the island. They rise from crystals that have never been found anywhere else. Randac breathed them on purpose, to see what they would do, and came out of them with great powers of the mind.

The Mists woke what the Kree had left in Inhuman blood. Every Inhuman who goes into them comes out changed, and no two are changed alike. Some gain great powers. Others are twisted out of shape, or come out of the Mists little better than animals.

So the Inhumans ration them. Their Genetic Council decides who may go into the Mists, and who may marry whom, so that the gift is neither wasted nor spoilt. An Inhuman's place in Attilan is fixed by what the Mists make of him, and it cannot be changed afterwards.

The heavy work of Attilan is done by the Alpha Primitives, a race of strong, slow-witted labourers whom the Inhumans made for the purpose. They cannot have children. When more are needed, more are made.

The Royal Family

Attilan is ruled by its Royal Family, the most remarkable Inhumans of all. At its head is Black Bolt, the king.

Medusa, his cousin and since 1984 his queen, can move every strand of her long red hair as other people move their fingers. It is strong enough to lift a car. Because Black Bolt does not speak, Medusa speaks for him.

Crystal, her younger sister, commands the elements: earth, air, fire and water.

Karnak, another cousin, was never put into the Mists at all. He was trained by monks instead, from boyhood, to see the flaw in anything, a wall or a man or an argument, and to break it there with a single blow.

His brother Triton was made for the sea. He has green scales, breathes water and cannot stay long out of it without help. Gorgon, yet another cousin, has the legs and hooves of a bull. When he stamps, the ground splits.

Lockjaw is the family's dog, an enormous bulldog with a forked antenna growing out of his forehead. He can take anybody who holds on to him across the world, or to the Moon, in a single step.

Black Bolt and Maximus

Black Bolt is the elder son of Agon, who was king of Attilan, and of his queen, Rynda. They put him into the Mists before he was born, and he came into the world with a voice that could wreck a city. His first cry shook Attilan.

He was brought up alone in a chamber that no sound could leave, and taught there to master his power. He learnt to keep perfectly silent. He was nineteen before he was let out.

His younger brother Maximus was waiting for him. Maximus had come out of the Mists with no great strength, only a talent for working on other people's minds, and he had been jealous of his brother from the start. Soon after Black Bolt came out, he overheard Maximus making a bargain with Kree agents: Maximus was offering them the Inhumans as soldiers. As the Kree tried to escape, Black Bolt spoke aloud, and brought their ship down out of the sky.

The ship crashed in the heart of the city. It killed his parents and several members of the Genetic Council. The sound of his voice broke something in Maximus's mind, which has never mended. Black Bolt became king, and he has never forgiven himself.

Maximus, who is called the Mad, has wanted his brother's throne ever since, and he has taken it more than once. The first time, some years before 1965, he did it with the Trikon, a creature he made by putting three Alpha Primitives into the Mists.

Coming to notice, 1965

The Royal Family was driven out of Attilan and scattered. Medusa lost her memory in the struggle, and early in 1965 she fought the Fantastic Four as one of the Frightful Four, a gang of criminals led by the Wizard. The others had gone into hiding among men in New York.

In the autumn of 1965 Gorgon came looking for her, and the Fantastic Four found themselves in the middle of a family quarrel they did not understand. Johnny Storm, the Human Torch, met Crystal in an alley in Manhattan and fell in love with her almost at once. She took him home to meet her family, which did not go well.

Black Bolt led his family back to the Great Refuge, with the Fantastic Four close behind. There he scattered Maximus's Alpha Primitives, and Maximus gave up the crown without a fight.

Maximus had not given up anything else. He had built the Atmo-Gun, a weapon meant to wipe out every human being on Earth and leave the Inhumans untouched. When he fired it, the mountains shook, and nothing else happened. Then he turned it round. It threw up a barrier of negative energy over the whole of the Great Refuge, and sealed it off from the world.

The Fantastic Four only just got out. Crystal's family pulled her back at the last moment, and the Thing carried Johnny out over his shoulder as the barrier closed. Within days, just before Christmas 1965, Galactus came to eat the world.

For most of a year the Inhumans were shut in. Late in 1966 Black Bolt sent his people down into the deepest shelters under the city, and spoke aloud. The barrier broke, and so did most of Attilan. While the city was rebuilt, the Royal Family went out to see the world.

The Fantastic Four

The Inhumans have been friends of the Fantastic Four ever since, although the friendship has had its strains. In 1968, the year Sue Richards had her son, Crystal took her place in the team. She stayed until 1970, when the air of New York made her so ill that she had to go home to Attilan. In 1973, when Sue had left the team for a time, Medusa served in it instead.

In Attilan Crystal had rescued Quicksilver, Pietro Maximoff of the Avengers, when he was badly hurt, and nursed him back to health. In 1974 she married him. It was the first marriage ever made between an Inhuman and an outsider. Johnny Storm took it hard.

It has been a troubled marriage. In the middle of the 1980s it came close to breaking, after Crystal fell in love with a neighbour. It came out afterwards that Maximus had been working on both their minds.

Reed Richards has been Attilan's friend at every turn. It was he who found the Inhumans their home on the Moon.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 Black Bolt, who had left Attilan again, lost his memory and was found wandering in California. Maximus seized the throne in his absence. This time he went further. The Kree were at war with the Skrulls over Earth, and Maximus made a pact with them, pledging the Inhumans to Ronan the Accuser as soldiers.

Triton swam to New York for help. He could not find the Fantastic Four, so he went to the Avengers. Captain America went with him to San Francisco, where the sight of Triton gave Black Bolt his memory back.

Maximus had shut Attilan behind another barrier. Black Bolt broke it with a whisper. The Avengers drove the Kree off, though not before the Kree had carried away Rick Jones, and Maximus collapsed into a stupor. Black Bolt, ashamed that his own brother had sold his people, left Attilan again for a time.

The Blue Area of the Moon

By the early 1980s the poisoned air of the outside world had reached even the Himalayas, and the Inhumans had begun to die of it. Reed Richards would not keep them alive on drugs. Instead he proposed the Blue Area of the Moon, a pocket of breathable air round a great city that the Kree had built there long ago, and left empty. It was not the first time Attilan had moved, as Medusa pointed out.

At the turn of 1982 the Inhumans lifted the city out of its valley and flew it to the Moon. Reed and Black Bolt fitted the engines between them. Black Bolt broke the mountain round the city with his voice, so that it could rise. He persuaded the Alpha Primitives to come too.

The Watcher, the alien observer who lives in the Blue Area, watched the city come down, and said nothing. The Phoenix had died in the Blue Area two years before. Within hours of the landing Crystal gave birth to a daughter, Luna. To everyone's surprise she was an ordinary human child, without a trace of power.

Black Bolt married Medusa in 1984. A Kree soldier and a Skrull, still fighting their own war, broke in on the wedding.

In 1988 Medusa bore Black Bolt a son, Ahura. The Genetic Council had forbidden the birth, for fear of what Black Bolt's son might be, so she went to Earth to have him. Afterwards she and Black Bolt gave him into the Council's keeping.

In 1991 Apocalypse, the first of the mutants, took the Inhumans' home on the Moon for his stronghold and made its people his slaves. The Royal Family won it back, fighting beside X-Factor, which had followed him there to rescue Cyclops's small son, Nathan.

1994 and after

Crystal joined the Avengers in 1991, and in the summer of 1994 she is still among them. In 1992 she was with them through Operation Galactic Storm, when the Kree, the people who had made her own, went to war with the Shi'ar. She lives at Avengers Mansion with Luna. She has grown fond of the Black Knight, Dane Whitman, and he of her.

Attilan still stands in the Blue Area of the Moon. Black Bolt still rules it in silence, Medusa still speaks for him, and Maximus is still his brother. Since July 1994 they have had neighbours of a kind, for the Justice League now works from the Watchtower, a half-built station elsewhere on the Moon.

In 2009 the Inhumans took over the Kree Empire, the people who had made them, and Black Bolt led it to war with the Shi'ar.

In August 1996 Crystal fought Onslaught in Central Park beside the Avengers. When her husband, Quicksilver, tried to follow the others into Onslaught, she blew him back with a gust of wind, then went in herself. The world believed her dead, and Luna was left without her mother for more than a year. Crystal came home late in 1997 with the rest of the fallen.

The end of the Inhumans

The Inhumans' rule over the Kree did not last. It was long over by 2020, when the Kree and the Skrulls joined their empires. The Royal Family was back in Attilan, in the Blue Area of the Moon.

In 2028 the old war between the Kree and the Skrulls began again. It was the worst of all. The Kree, who had never found a way out of their evolutionary dead end, came to Attilan for the one people they had ever managed to change, to take them as the soldiers they had first made them to be.

The Royal Family would not give their people up. Black Bolt, Medusa, Karnak, Gorgon and Triton held Attilan against the Kree while Lockjaw carried as many Inhumans as he could to Earth. Black Bolt broke his silence a last time against the Kree ships. None of the Royal Family survived the fight, and the Inhumans the Kree carried off died with the last Kree worlds by about 2041.

Crystal, who had served with the Avengers, fell on Earth in the war, fighting the fires of a burning city. The other Inhumans on Earth, where the air had always made them ill, did not outlive the war. The Alpha Primitives, who could have no children, died out with their makers. Attilan was left empty on the Moon, and the Terrigen Mists were never breathed again.

pages.title: Innsmouth
infobox: The Shadow over Innsmouth (Visionary Publishing Company, April 1936)
Massachusetts, at the mouth of the Manuxet River
Devil Reef, with Y'ha-nthlei beneath it
pages.html:
Innsmouth is a decayed fishing port on the coast of Massachusetts, at the mouth of the Manuxet River, between Newburyport and Arkham. For eighty years its people traded with the Deep Ones, who live beneath Devil Reef offshore, and married into them. In February 1928 the federal government raided it, burnt its waterfront and carried off a great part of its people. It has been half empty ever since.

The port

Innsmouth was founded in 1643. Before the Revolution it was known for its shipbuilding. In the early years of the nineteenth century it was a rich port, its captains trading as far as the East Indies and the South Seas. The war of 1812 cost it many of its ships and men. After that it went slowly down in the world.

Obed Marsh

Captain Obed Marsh was the town's great man. On an island of the Carolines, near Ponape, he found a people who gave sacrifices to the Deep Ones in return for fish and gold. When the islanders of the neighbouring islands wiped that people out, he brought the bargain home.

He set up the Esoteric Order of Dagon, and in time it became the town's religion. The townspeople gave sacrifices at Devil Reef. Gold came up from the sea, and the Marsh refinery on the falls of the Manuxet turned it into bars.

1846

In 1846 the neighbouring towns grew suspicious, and Obed Marsh was jailed with several of his crew. That night the Deep Ones came up from Devil Reef. More than half the people of Innsmouth died. Outside the town it was put down to a plague.

Those who were left took the oaths of the Order, or kept their mouths shut, and the Deep Ones came to live among them. Obed Marsh took a second wife from the sea. He lived until 1878.

The Innsmouth look

For the next eighty years the town bred hybrids. Its people had a look of their own, which the towns round about called the Innsmouth look: narrow heads, flat noses and wide, staring eyes that never seemed to blink. As they aged, the look grew on them, until at last they went down into the sea for good.

The Marshes kept the refinery. In 1927 Obed's grandson Barnabas Marsh, who was very far gone in the change, still ran it, although he no longer showed himself in the street. Strangers who came to Innsmouth stayed at the Gilman House, the one hotel, and seldom stayed long. Old Zadok Allen, born in 1831, was one of the last people in the town with no taint of the sea in him.

1928 and after

In July 1927 Robert Olmstead, a young man from Ohio, spent a night at the Gilman House and barely got away with his life. What he told the federal authorities led to the raid of February 1928, in which the waterfront was burnt and a great many of the townspeople were taken away. That story is told on the page The raid on Innsmouth.

Afterwards the town was almost empty. It has been slow to fill again, and in 1963 Delta Green had cause to look at it once more.

pages.title: Invasion! (1988)
infobox: The Alien Alliance, led by the Dominators
The word metahuman; the gene bomb; leftover alien weapons
pages.html:
The alien invasion of 1988 was the attack on Earth by an alliance of alien powers led by the Dominators, who feared the hidden potential for superhuman powers in the human race. Earth's heroes and armies beat it off. It left three things behind: the word metahuman; a gene bomb that struck down almost every superhuman on Earth; and alien weapons that would be turned on Metropolis in 1994.

The Alliance

Late in 1988 a coalition of alien races, the Alien Alliance, demanded Earth's surrender. The Dominators led it. With them came the warlike Khunds, the shape-changing Durlans, the Thanagarians and others. Among their forces were the Daxamites, a people related to the Kryptonians. The Dominators' real fear was the metagene: the hidden factor in some human beings that lets powers emerge, which they believed would one day make humanity the most dangerous race in the galaxy.

The Dominators also invited the Goa'uld System Lords to join. They refused without giving a reason; the Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of Earth for five thousand years, and they had no intention of going there.

Earth's heroes, the Justice League and Superman among them, fought the Alliance alongside the world's armies. Under Earth's yellow sun the Daxamites gained powers like Superman's, and they turned on their allies. The Alliance broke apart and withdrew.

The gene bomb

As they left, the Dominators set off a gene bomb that attacked the metagene itself. For a time nearly every superhuman on Earth whose powers came from it lost control of them or fell gravely ill, until a remedy was found. The episode made the metagene, and the word metahuman, part of ordinary speech.

What they left behind

The invaders left a great deal of their technology behind. Lex Luthor had sonic torpedoes reverse-engineered from it and hidden beneath Metropolis. In May 1994 his aide, Sydney Happersen, fired them, and flattened the city's downtown.

The fate of the Alliance

None of the Alliance's peoples outlived the Third World War on Earth. About 2033 the Dominators had their revenge on the Daxamites, filling the air of Daxam with the lead to which every Daxamite was fatally weak. A few years later they tried to give the metagene they had feared in human beings to their own highest caste. The change ran wild in their blood, and by about 2039 it had killed them all.

The Khunds plundered the dying Dominion, as Khunds would, and carried the plague home. The Durlans, few since the ancient atomic war that made them shape-changers, were gone by the 2040s. The Thanagarians died with Rann about 2038, when it fell into the star Polaris.

In 2155 Dr Phlox of the Enterprise NX-01 found the Dominators' plague in the dead crew of a drifting Khund warship. Its records told the rest.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994 the news spoke of metahumans as ‘a word few people had heard before the alien invasion of 1988’. A protester in New York complained that in May ‘some lunatic in a lab coat flattened downtown with torpedoes left over from the alien invasion’.

pages.title: Iron Man
infobox: Tony Stark; Anthony Edward Stark; Shellhead
Stark Industries, later Stark International and Stark Enterprises
Retired; the armour worn by James Rhodes as War Machine
pages.html:
Iron Man was the armoured hero in red and gold, one of the founders of the Avengers. The American industrialist Tony Stark built the armour and wore it himself. After more than thirty years in it Stark has retired, and by 1994 his friend James Rhodes has taken his place among the Avengers in the heavier armour called War Machine.

Stark and the armour

Tony Stark was a brilliant engineer and the heir to a great American arms business. While he was demonstrating his weapons in Vietnam, a booby trap left a fragment of shrapnel lodged near his heart. He was taken prisoner by a local warlord, who ordered him to build weapons. With a fellow captive, the physicist Ho Yinsen, he built instead a suit of armour that kept his heart beating and let him fight his way free. Yinsen died covering his escape. On the way out Stark met James Rhodes, a Marine helicopter pilot, who became his closest friend.

Iron Man came to public notice at the end of 1962. His first armour was grey and bulky. Early in 1963 it turned gold. Before the year was out it had become the sleek red and gold suit that the world came to know. For years Stark's company presented Iron Man to the public as Stark's bodyguard. He helped to found the Avengers in 1963, and gave them his family's mansion on Fifth Avenue for a headquarters.

He met Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, three times. In January 1965 the Avengers went to Japan beside the Justice League, when Godzilla was loose there with two other monsters. Iron Man drew the lightning of the dragon King Ghidorah away from a crowded town until his armour ran dry. In April 1975 Interpol asked Stark to examine the wreck of Mechagodzilla, a fighting machine that alien invaders had twice sent against Japan, which Godzilla had twice destroyed. Iron Man was standing on the wreck, cutting samples of its metal, when Godzilla came back up the valley for a last look at it. He shut off every weapon in the armour, then stood still. Godzilla looked at him for a long minute before he went back to the sea. What Stark learnt from the wreck went into Red Ronin, the giant robot that his company built for S.H.I.E.L.D. in 1978. In the summer of 1979 he was one of the Avengers who failed to move Godzilla from New York.

Later career

Stark fought a long battle with drink. In 1983 he relapsed and lost his company to the corporate raider Obadiah Stane. He gave up the armour, which Rhodes wore in his place until 1985. That year Stark recovered and took it back. In 1987 and 1988 he waged a private war against everyone who had stolen his armour designs to use them.

In 1992, with his nervous system failing, he faked his own death and left Rhodes a new suit, War Machine. He came back early in 1993, but he has since retired from the armour. Rhodes has gone on wearing War Machine among the Avengers.

The last flight, 1996 to 1997

In the summer of 1996 Onslaught's Sentinels came down on Manhattan, and the Avengers called on everyone who had ever served. Tony Stark, retired since 1993, put on the armour one last time. Onslaught's pulse killed it around him, so he built another, with armour for the others too. He made it from Xavier's own plans, with vibranium from Wakanda and whatever his old company could spare. It kept a wearer's mind safe from Onslaught for a while.

In Central Park that August he went into Onslaught carrying Victor von Doom, who had not meant to go at all. It was the last flight of the red and gold.

The world believed him dead. Franklin Richards brought him home late in 1997, exactly as old as he had been when he fell. Stark took the armour off again and went back to his retirement. James Rhodes kept War Machine.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: watching the Avengers at the United Nations on the news of 20 August 1994, Harry sees that the red and gold armour from Dudley's old lunchbox has been replaced by a heavier gunmetal suit bristling with guns, with a different man inside it.

pages.title: Isaac the Devil Forgemaster
infobox: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness (PlayStation 2 and Xbox, November 2005)
1479, as the vessel of Dracula's return
pages.html:
Isaac was one of Dracula's two Devil Forgemasters, and the one who stayed loyal. He blamed his fellow Forgemaster, Hector, for their master's defeat in 1476. He had Hector's beloved, Rosaly, burnt as a witch. In 1479 he led Hector on a chase across Wallachia that was meant to end in Dracula's return, and it did, in Isaac's own body.

Forgemaster

A Devil Forgemaster is a mortal man who has mastered the dark art of forging Innocent Devils, demonic familiars that grow as they fight beside their master. Dracula kept two Forgemasters among the generals of his army, Isaac and Hector. They had been friends.

Isaac had a sister, Julia Laforeze, a witch who lived in hiding from the witch-hunters.

Before the war of 1476 Hector sickened of what Dracula did to mankind. He left the castle, gave up his powers and went to live among mortals. Isaac stayed. When Trevor Belmont destroyed Dracula that year, Isaac held Hector's desertion to blame for it.

Rosaly

Dracula's dying curse lay over Europe for three years, spreading plague, fear and the violence of mobs. Isaac turned it to his own use. Hector had come to love a woman named Rosaly. About 1478 Isaac saw to it that she was tried for witchcraft, which she had never practised, and burnt.

It was done to bring Hector back. A Forgemaster who had laid down his powers was no use to Isaac's purpose. A Forgemaster mad for revenge was.

The chase of 1479

In 1479 Hector found Isaac waiting for him in Dracula's abandoned castle. Isaac mocked him, dared him to take up the forge again and fled. Hector did as he was dared, and followed.

They met in the town of Cordova, where they fought. Julia came between them. She told Hector that her brother was in the grip of Dracula's curse, and that he must not strike in anger. Isaac got away. In the Aiolon Ruins he fought Trevor Belmont, whose victory over Dracula he called a fluke, and fled again when Hector arrived.

His real ground was a hidden chamber beneath the abandoned castle, at the end of a sealed corridor. Trevor opened the seal for Hector with his own blood. Isaac came up behind Trevor, stabbed him and left him for dead. Julia's healing saved Trevor's life. Hector's battle with the guardian of the corridor fed a spell that Isaac had laid there. It raised Dracula's castle anew.

The vessel

In the throne room of the risen castle Hector fought Isaac for the last time and beat him. He had his rival at his mercy when he remembered Julia's warning, and held his hand.

The priest Zead, who had been guiding Hector to Isaac all year, now showed himself as Dracula's servant Death. The two Forgemasters had been meant to fight to the death, so that the winner, soaked in blood and rage, could serve as the vessel for Dracula. Since Hector had refused the part, Death took Isaac for it. Dracula rose in Isaac's body, and Hector destroyed him.

Nothing was left of Isaac afterwards but the body his master had used. Julia mourned him. She held that the curse, not her brother, had done what Isaac did.

Among the Kindred

Isaac was never a vampire. He was a living man who had given himself wholly to Dracula, as the priest Shaft did three centuries later. The Kindred call such servants infernalists, since the things a Forgemaster forges are demons, whatever name he gives them.

pages.title: Jabi
infobox: A girl in her teens, Amon's pupil
pages.html:
Jabi is a Makai Priestess, the childhood friend of Kouga Saejima, an orphan brought up by the priest Amon. In February 2006 she was struck down by a servant of the Eastern Watchdog, with only her brush left behind. She was not dead. Kouga cut her out of a Makai Tree that December. In the summer of 1994 she is in her teens, a little older than Kouga, still learning her art.

Amon's pupil

Jabi had no parents that anybody knew of. Amon took her in, taught her the priest's art and brought her up. As children she trained beside Kouga Saejima, the son of Amon's friend Taiga. They went their separate ways in their teens.

The twelve blades

In February 2006 Amon was murdered. The three priestesses of the Eastern Watchdog put it about that Jabi had done it. She already suspected them. A knight's sword is supposed to be emptied of its Horrors at the Watchdog, so that they can be sent back to the Makai. The priestesses had been keeping them. Jabi broke in, took twelve of the sealed blades, and set out to send them home herself.

Kouga caught her, heard her, believed her. She hid Kaoru Mitsuki from the Watchdog's servants. While she was working the rite of return with Kouga beside her, the priestesses' man Kodama, whom she had outwitted once already, struck her from behind. Nothing was left of her but her brush. The blades ran together into one enormous Horror.

The Makai Tree

Her body had been taken into the Makai Forest, where a Makai Tree held it. She lay inside the tree, neither alive nor dead. Only somebody with a strong bond to her could wake her. In December 2006 the spirit of Amon sent a girl called Rin Yamagatana to fetch Kouga. He went into the tree, fought the shapes it made out of his own memories, and cut Jabi free.

She came back to Kantai, a village that had no welcome for a woman returned from the dead. Its knight, Tsubasa Yamagatana, called her an abomination. She made him feel her heart beating. Days later his sister, Rin, was splashed with Horror's blood. Jabi drew the poison out of the child by a rite that hurt them both badly. Tsubasa apologised.

She fought the Horror Legules beside Kouga. Afterwards she stayed at Kantai to teach Rin.

Later years

In January 2012 Kouga asked her to carry the ailing Zaruba to the Life-Circulating Waterfall. Sigma Fudou attacked her on the road with one of his machines to take the ring. She drove him off by calling up Kouga's horse, Gouten, with a Barchess piece that Kouga had lent her. She warned Kouga that his partner, Leo, was hiding something.

That March she went into Sigma's engine with Rekka to bring Kouga out, killing Sigma's creature Gigi on the way. In the last battle the two priestesses held the Horrors back at the mouth of the true Makai.

By 2016 she was hunting Horrors in company with Tsubasa Yamagatana, the knight who had once called her a monster. They were a couple.

pages.title: Jaffa
infobox: Soldiers, and carriers of Goa'uld larvae
Their god's emblem on the forehead
Up to about two hundred years
Lived on as men and women, free of larvae
Found by Captain Kirk about 2268; joined the United Federation of Planets about 2270, as the Free Jaffa Nation
pages.html:
The Jaffa are humans whom the Goa'uld altered long ago to serve as their soldiers and to carry their young. Each Jaffa holds a Goa'uld larva in a pouch in the belly. It keeps him strong and long-lived, but it also makes him wholly dependent on his masters. Their greatest teacher is Bra'tac.

Nature

Long ago the Goa'uld took human slaves and changed them, giving each an abdominal pouch in which a larval Goa'uld can mature. The larva in turn gives its carrier strength, healing and a lifespan of up to two hundred years. It also takes the place of the Jaffa's own immune system. A Jaffa child receives a first larva at about the age of ten, in the ceremony of the Prim'ta, and is never without one again. A Jaffa whose larva is taken from him dies within hours unless another is put in its place. It is the most perfect chain the Goa'uld ever forged.

A Jaffa bears his master's emblem on his forehead. For a First Prime, the highest-ranking warrior in a Goa'uld's army, it is set in gold. Instead of sleeping, Jaffa enter a deep meditation called kel'no'reem, through which the larva heals them. They fight with the staff weapon and serve in great numbers on the worlds of every System Lord. Ra's guards, who wore the helmets of Horus and Anubis, were Jaffa.

Faith and doubt

Jaffa are raised from childhood to believe that their masters are gods, and that to serve them is the whole of honour. Some have come to doubt it all the same, although a Jaffa who turns against his god is called shol'va, a traitor, and is hunted down. Bra'tac, the old master of Chulak and once First Prime of Apophis, has privately believed for many years that the Goa'uld are false gods. He has trained his best pupil, Teal'c, to think as he does. Their doubt is the first seed of a Jaffa rebellion.

Every Jaffa recruit is told about Thor. Nobody tells them about Earth, which Ra forbade the Goa'uld to mention after Thor helped the Egyptians drive him out. In the old wars before the Protected Planets Treaty Thor killed Jaffa who had thrown down their weapons, and he laughed while he did it. The stories are meant to make young warriors brave. Mostly they make them careful never to be sent anywhere near the North.

Contact with Earth

Before the Stargate was opened again, one Jaffa had already met Earth's heroes. In 1984 the Beyonder carried Bra'tac, the Jaffa master, to Battleworld with heroes and villains from across the world, in the affair called the Secret Wars. In 1994 Ra's Jaffa guards fought the Abydos expedition. From 1997 the Jaffa of the System Lords met Earth's teams through the gate.

The first of them were Apophis's, led by his First Prime, Teal'c, who turned against him that same year.

After the Goa'uld

From 2003 a drug made on Earth, tretonin, could take the place of a larva, and after the fall of the System Lords in 2005 the free Jaffa lived on it rather than serve the Goa'uld. They would carry no more young for their old masters, which did as much as anything to finish them. By about 2045 the Goa'uld were extinct.

The Jaffa lived on. Their children were never given a larva, so they grew up as other children do, with their own bodies to defend them. Within two generations the Jaffa were simply men and women, of a proud warrior people, on the worlds where their grandfathers had served false gods.

In 2152 the Enterprise NX-01 found a Goa'uld mothership adrift, with the log of the free Jaffa who had taken it from the last of its lords.

The Free Jaffa Nation

After the fall of the System Lords in 2005 the free Jaffa governed themselves as the Free Jaffa Nation, with a High Council that met at Dakara. They were allies of Earth, whose warriors they called the Tau'ri. Then in 2026 the Third World War broke out on Earth, and the Stargate programme was lost. No word came from Earth through the gate again, for Earth's own gate was destroyed in space during the war without anyone knowing.

Earth forgot them. The Stargate programme had always been secret, and by the end of the war in 2053 nobody alive remembered it. Starfleet knew the Goa'uld only from the log of a drifting mothership found in 2152, which said nothing of Earth.

The Jaffa did not forget the Tau'ri. Their forefathers had fought beside them against the false gods, and the stories of those years were told to every Jaffa child. They passed from generation to generation. Children on every Jaffa world learnt of Teal'c, who first turned against Apophis, of his old master Bra'tac, and of SG-1, the warriors of Earth who had come through the gate to help set the Jaffa free.

About 2268 the USS Enterprise, under Captain James T. Kirk, came upon the Jaffa worlds. When the Jaffa learnt that much of her crew came from Earth, they greeted them as Tau'ri. Kirk knew nothing of the Stargate, the rule of the Goa'uld or SG-1, so the Jaffa had to tell him everything. About 2270 the Free Jaffa Nation joined the United Federation of Planets. It did so out of respect and thanks for the Tau'ri who had helped to free their forefathers.

In the saga

The Jaffa have not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: James Sunderland
infobox: Frank Sunderland, superintendent of South Ashfield Heights
Maria of Silent Hill; Angela Orosco; Eddie Dombrowski; Laura, a child of eight
pages.html:
James Sunderland was a clerk of twenty-nine who came to Silent Hill on 25 September 1994 because of a letter from his wife, who was dead. He believed that she had died of her illness three years before. In truth he had smothered her himself, and had hidden the memory where he could not find it. The town found it for him. He was one of three guilty people it called that year, and the only one who left it alive.

His wife

James was born about 1965, the son of Frank Sunderland, who looks after a block of flats in South Ashfield. He worked as a clerk. He married Mary Shepherd, who took both their names.

They spent a holiday at Silent Hill, in room 312 of the Lakeview Hotel, looking out over Toluca Lake. She loved the place. James recorded her there with a video camera. They left the tape behind at the hotel by mistake.

Then his wife fell ill. The doctors could not cure the disease, and they gave her three years at the most. It spoilt her looks, and for a time it spoilt her temper. She said terrible things to James, then wept and begged him not to leave her. He nursed her whenever the hospital let her come home. He loved her. He also came to hate the illness, the waiting and, on the worst days, the woman in the bed.

One day he put a pillow over her face. His mind would not keep what he had done. He remembered instead that the disease had killed her, long ago.

The letter

In September 1994 James had a letter in his wife's handwriting. It said that she was waiting for him at Silent Hill, in their special place. He knew that a dead woman could not write. He drove to Silent Hill all the same, on Sunday 25 September.

The road into the town was closed, so he left the car at a lookout above the lake and walked down through the fog. In the graveyard he met a nervous young woman, Angela Orosco, who was looking for her mother. She told him there was something wrong with the town.

The town

The streets were empty of people. They were not empty of other things: shapes that walked like bodies sewn into their own skins, and shop dummies made of two pairs of legs. In a block of flats he came upon a fat young man, Eddie Dombrowski, being sick beside a corpse he swore he had not killed. A small girl called Laura kicked a key out of James's reach and ran off laughing.

It was in the same building that he first saw the Red Pyramid Thing, a man's figure in a butcher's smock with a great iron pyramid for a head. It stood behind a set of bars and watched him.

In the park by the lake a woman was waiting, though not the one he had come for. She called herself Maria. She had his wife's face and his wife's voice, but she was dressed like a dancer from a nightclub. She said she had never heard of any Mary Sunderland. She did not want to be left alone, so James took her with him.

They followed Laura to Brookhaven Hospital. The child said that she had been in hospital with his wife only the year before, which James knew to be impossible. She locked him in a room with something that hung from the ceiling. When he got out, the hospital had turned into its dark self. In a basement corridor the Red Pyramid Thing ran Maria through, as the lift doors closed between her and James.

The prison and the lake

A key led James to the Silent Hill Historical Society. A hole in its floor took him down into the old Toluca Prison, then into a maze below that. In a cell he found Maria alive, with no memory of having died. She talked about the tape left behind at the hotel, which only his wife could have known about. When he had found a way round to her door, she was dead on the bed.

In the same maze he heard Angela screaming. A thing like two figures stretched over a bedframe had her cornered. James killed it. She kicked it where it lay, for it had the shape of her father. Then she turned on James. He had probably wanted his sick wife out of the way, she said.

Eddie was down there too, with a revolver and several fresh corpses. He had decided that everybody was laughing at him, James included. He opened fire. In a cold store hung with carcasses James killed him. It was the first time, as far as he knew, that he had taken a human life.

He came up at a jetty, and rowed across Toluca Lake to the hotel.

Room 312

Laura was at the Lakeview Hotel before him. She showed him a letter that his wife had written to her for her eighth birthday. She had hoped to adopt the child. The letter was real, and it was not three years old.

In room 312 James played the tape. It showed his wife by the window, coughing, asking him to bring her back to Silent Hill one day. Then it showed him what he had done to her. When Laura came in to ask where her friend was, he told the child the truth. She screamed at him, and ran.

The letter in his pocket had gone blank. There had never been any writing on it.

The hotel he walked out into was burnt and flooded. Angela stood on a staircase that was on fire. For her, she said, it was always like that. She climbed on up into the flames. In the lobby two Red Pyramid Things were waiting with spears, with Maria hung between them. They killed her a third time. James understood then why they had followed him. He had wanted somebody to punish him. He told them he no longer needed them, and they turned their spears on themselves.

Leaving

At the top of the hotel Maria was waiting once more, in his wife's clothes. She offered to take his wife's place. He refused her. She changed into something monstrous, and he killed it.

Afterwards he found himself at his wife's bedside, or at a memory of it. He told her why he had done it: partly to end her pain, partly because he had wanted his own life back. She had known. She gave him the letter she had really written. It told him that he had made her happy. It told him, too, to go on living.

On the morning of 26 September James walked out of Silent Hill through the graveyard with Laura beside him. Where the two of them went is not recorded. The SCP Foundation was still watching the roads that autumn, and Delta Green had forbidden its agents the town. Neither noticed him come or go. In 2004 his father still believed that his son and daughter-in-law had vanished at Silent Hill years before, having heard nothing from either.

The town called three people that year with something on their conscience. It showed each of them what they had brought, and it let one go.

pages.title: James T. Kirk
infobox: Captain Kirk; James Kirk; Admiral Kirk; James Tiberius Kirk
George Samuel Kirk, killed on Deneva in 2267
David Marcus (2261 to 2285), by Carol Marcus
The USS Republic, as an ensign; the USS Farragut, as a lieutenant
The USS Enterprise, from 2265; the USS Enterprise-A, 2286 to 2293
14 October 2293, in the Nexus, aboard the USS Enterprise-B
Captain; admiral from 2270; captain again from 2286

The Palm Leaf of the Axanar Peace Mission; the Grankite Order of Tactics; the Prantares Ribbon of Commendation; the Medal of Honor; the Silver Palm with Cluster; the Starfleet Citation for Conspicuous Gallantry; the Karagite Order of Heroism
pages.html:
James T. Kirk was the most famous starship captain of the twenty-third century. He commanded the USS Enterprise on her five-year mission from 2265 to 2270, and later her successor, the Enterprise-A. As a boy he lived through Kodos's massacre on Tarsus IV. As a man he saved Earth more than once and lost his son to the Klingons. Bold and inventive, he was the only cadet ever to beat the Kobayashi Maru. In 2293 he fought Darth Vader beside his protégé John Shepard in the Imperial Entanglement, then saw Shepard given command of the new Enterprise-B. He was lost in the Nexus on her maiden voyage.

Family and early life

James Tiberius Kirk was born on 22 March 2233 in Riverside, Iowa, the younger son of George and Winona Kirk. His father was a Starfleet officer. He was named for his two grandfathers, James and Tiberius. His elder brother, George Samuel Kirk, known as Sam, became a research biologist.

Sam married a woman called Aurelan, and they had three sons, Peter among them. In 2267 Sam and Aurelan died on the colony world of Deneva, killed by the parasites that had overrun it. Kirk came too late to save them, though Peter lived.

Tarsus IV

In 2246, when Kirk was thirteen, he was living in the Earth colony on Tarsus IV. A fungus destroyed most of its food. Its governor, Kodos, declared martial law and put four thousand of its eight thousand colonists to death, so that the rest might live until help came. Help came sooner than he had reckoned. A burnt body was taken for his, and Kodos the Executioner was never brought to trial.

Kirk was one of the few who had seen Kodos and lived. In 2266 he found him alive, acting under the name Anton Karidian with a travelling company of players. Someone had been killing the last witnesses who could identify him, one by one. It was his own daughter, Lenore. She meant her last shot for Kirk, and Kodos stepped in front of it.

Starfleet Academy

Kirk entered Starfleet Academy in 2250. Not long after he arrived he went to Axanar with the Axanar Peace Mission, which failed, and he was given the Palm Leaf of the Axanar Peace Mission for his part in it. He studied the victories of Garth of Izar, as every cadet did. His favourite teacher was the historian John Gill.

He worked hard enough to be called a stack of books with legs, and he took a good deal of teasing from an upperclassman, Finnegan. He became the only cadet ever to beat the Kobayashi Maru, the test that no one was meant to pass, by reprogramming the simulation. He was given a commendation for original thinking.

After he graduated in 2254 he stayed on for a time as an instructor. One of his students, Gary Mitchell, became his closest friend, and on Dimorus took the poisoned darts meant for Kirk.

Early career

As an ensign aboard the USS Republic Kirk logged a mistake by his friend Ben Finney, who had left a circuit open to the ship's atomic matter piles. Finney's career never recovered, and he never forgave Kirk.

In 2257, as a lieutenant aboard the USS Farragut, Kirk met a gaseous creature at Tycho IV that fed on red blood cells. He hesitated at his phaser for a moment, and it killed two hundred of the crew, Captain Garrovick among them. For eleven years he blamed himself.

About 2261 Kirk and the scientist Carol Marcus had a son, David. Carol wanted the boy to grow up in her world, not chasing through the universe after his father, and Kirk kept away. He came to regret it bitterly.

The Enterprise

In 2265 Kirk took command of the USS Enterprise from Christopher Pike, who had commanded her after her first captain, Robert April. He was thirty-two. Spock was his science officer and first officer. Montgomery Scott ran her engines, Hikaru Sulu flew her and Nyota Uhura kept her communications. From 2266 Dr Leonard McCoy was her doctor, and from 2267 Pavel Chekov plotted her course. Kirk, Spock and McCoy became the closest of friends.

The mission had hardly begun when the Enterprise tried to cross the barrier at the edge of the galaxy. Gary Mitchell came back from it with powers growing past anything human, and with a contempt for those who had none. On Delta Vega Kirk killed his oldest friend before Mitchell could set himself up as a god.

2266

In 2266 Kirk bluffed the vast ship of Balok, of the First Federation, with the threat of a substance that did not exist, which he called corbomite. A faulty transporter once split him in two, into a savage man and a gentle one. He learnt from it that a captain needs both halves.

That year he crippled the Romulan ship that had crossed the Neutral Zone, in the first battle between Earth's people and the Romulans since the war of 2156. He also found Kodos, alive after twenty years.

2267

In 2267 Kirk was court-martialled for the death of Ben Finney, whose pod he was said to have jettisoned too soon. Areel Shaw, who had once loved him, prosecuted. His lawyer, Samuel T. Cogley, and Spock proved that Finney was still alive, hiding aboard to take his revenge.

That year the Gorn destroyed the outpost on Cestus III. The Metrons set Kirk and the Gorn captain to fight it out alone on a desert world. Kirk won by making a cannon from what he found there, and he spared the Gorn's life.

He talked the computer Landru, which ruled Beta III, into destroying itself, as he later did the probe Nomad. On Janus VI he made peace between the miners and the Horta, a mother defending her eggs. At Organia he saw the Organians impose peace on the Klingons and the Federation. He stood with Spock on Vulcan when the pon farr came, and he fought him there as T'Pring's choice of champion.

That year an ion storm caught the transporter as Kirk, McCoy, Scott and Uhura were beaming up. It carried them across into a mirror universe, where a cruel Terran Empire stood in the Federation's place, with their counterparts aboard a savage Enterprise. Kirk got them home. Starfleet studied the accident for years afterwards, since it had opened a door that nobody had known was there.

On Gamma Canaris N that year Kirk found Zefram Cochrane, the man who had made Earth's first warp flight, alive. A being of energy that Cochrane called the Companion had kept him young for a hundred and fifty years. Kirk promised to keep his secret, so Earth never heard of Cochrane again.

That year McCoy, maddened by an accidental overdose, leapt through the Guardian of Forever into New York in 1930. Kirk and Spock followed him there. Kirk fell in love with Edith Keeler, who ran a mission for the poor. McCoy would have saved her life, and with it changed history for the worse, so Kirk had to let her die. She was killed by a lorry crossing the street, and Kirk held McCoy back.

He found the wreck of the USS Constellation, whose commodore, Matt Decker, had lost his crew to a planet-killer, a vast machine that ate worlds. Kirk destroyed it by flying the Constellation down its throat. On the way to the Babel conference an Orion agent stabbed him. Spock took the Enterprise to Talos IV with Christopher Pike, who was crippled and could not speak, then stood trial for it. Kirk sat in judgment, and in the end he let Pike stay on Talos IV to live as he pleased among the illusions of the Talosians.

On Deneva that year Kirk lost his brother Sam.

2268

In 2268 Kirk found the cloud creature of Tycho IV again and destroyed it, with the son of his old captain, Ensign Garrovick, beside him. He forgave himself at last for the hesitation of 2257.

At Space Station K-7 that year the Klingon agent Arne Darvin poisoned the grain meant for Sherman's Planet, and the station's tribbles gave him away. On Neural Kirk armed the hill people with flintlocks, since the Klingons had armed the villagers, to keep the balance between them. In the Romulan Neutral Zone he and Spock stole a cloaking device from a Romulan flagship. Aboard the Enterprise a creature that fed on hatred set Kang's Klingons and Kirk's crew at each other's throats, until both sides laughed it off the ship.

He found Garth of Izar, whose victories he had studied as a cadet, mad in the asylum on Elba II. He came upon the worlds of the Free Jaffa Nation, whose people had to tell him everything that Earth had forgotten about the Stargate. He tested the M-5, Dr Richard Daystrom's computer, which destroyed the USS Excalibur with all hands before Kirk talked it into shutting itself down.

On a world of Native American people, carried there long ago from Earth, Kirk lost his memory. He lived among them for weeks as Kirok, married the priestess Miramanee and was happy. She died of the stones thrown by her own people, carrying his child.

Caught between universes aboard the derelict USS Defiant, Kirk was believed dead for a time. He had left Spock and McCoy his last orders, which were to stop quarrelling.

That year, too, the Enterprise answered a distress call from Mindoir, a colony that slavers of the Orion Syndicate were raiding. Kirk's people reached fifteen-year-old John Shepard just in time, after his family and friends had been killed in front of him. Kirk took pity on the boy, remembering Tarsus IV and the son he had stayed away from. The two of them wrote to each other for years, and Shepard came to look on Kirk as a father.

The end of the five-year mission

In 2269 Orion pirates hijacked the drug that Spock needed to live, when he had fallen ill with choriocytosis. Kirk ran them down and got it back in time.

In 2270 he carried Commodore Robert April, the first captain of the Enterprise, to his retirement. On the way a universe where time ran backwards made April young again for a while, and he took command of his old ship one last time.

The five-year mission ended in 2270, and Kirk was promoted to admiral, as Chief of Starfleet Operations.

Admiral

Kirk spent the next years behind a desk on Earth, and he hated it. In 2273 a vast cloud came towards Earth, destroying three Klingon cruisers and the station Epsilon IX on its way. Kirk took back the newly refitted Enterprise from her captain, Willard Decker, the son of Matt Decker. At the heart of the cloud was V'Ger, the old Earth probe Voyager 6, grown into a living machine that wanted to join with its creator. Decker joined with it, and it left the universe.

By 2285 Kirk was teaching at Starfleet Academy again, and feeling his age. On his birthday McCoy gave him a pair of reading glasses, and Spock gave him an old copy of A Tale of Two Cities.

That year an old enemy seized the USS Reliant and the Genesis Device, which could remake a dead world. Kirk took the Enterprise, crewed by cadets under Spock, to stop him, and he beat him in the Mutara Nebula. The dying enemy set off the Genesis Device. Spock died restoring the ship's engines so that she could escape the blast, after placing his katra in McCoy's mind.

In the same days Kirk met his son David, now a grown man working on the Genesis project, and the two of them were reconciled. A new planet formed from the nebula where Genesis had gone off.

Spock's father, Sarek, told Kirk that Spock's katra had to be brought home to Vulcan with his body. Starfleet forbade it. Kirk stole the Enterprise with McCoy, Scott, Sulu, Chekov and Uhura. On the Genesis planet the Klingon commander Kruge's men killed David. Kirk destroyed the Enterprise rather than let Kruge take her, killed Kruge on the dying planet and took his Bird-of-Prey to Vulcan, where Spock was made whole again.

In 2286 a probe came to Earth, calling for humpback whales that no longer lived there, and began to destroy the planet. Kirk took his crew back to San Francisco in 1986 in the captured Klingon ship. With the help of Dr Gillian Taylor, a marine biologist, they brought two whales, George and Gracie, home to answer it. Taylor came with them.

For saving Earth the Federation Council dropped all charges but one against him. He was reduced to captain, which was what he wanted, and given the new USS Enterprise-A.

The Enterprise-A

In 2287, on shore leave in Yosemite with Spock and McCoy, Kirk fell while climbing El Capitan. Spock caught him in rocket boots. Soon afterwards the half-finished Enterprise-A was sent to Nimbus III, where Sybok, Spock's half-brother, had seized the envoys of three powers. Sybok took the ship to the centre of the galaxy in search of Sha Ka Ree.

The being they found there was not God, and it wanted the Enterprise for itself. Kirk was the one who asked why God would need a starship. Sybok gave his life to save the others. The Klingon captain Klaa, who had come hunting Kirk for the glory of it, ended by saving him.

The Enterprise-A and Shepard

In March 2293 Commander John Shepard of the Starfleet Marines came aboard the Enterprise-A, with Lieutenant Kaidan Alenko and Corporal Richard Jenkins, as a detachment to lead away missions. Kirk was his captain now as well as his mentor.

On 12 February that year the Klingon moon Praxis had exploded, which brought the Federation and the Klingons close to war. Kirk was sent to Starbase Side 7 to collect the RX-78-2 Gundam, a mobile suit built to answer the Klingon Zaku. His ship was chosen as a symbol of the long years in which the Enterprise had foiled the Klingons.

He reached Side 7 on 17 May, the day a fleet of the Galactic Empire under Darth Vader attacked it. The affair is known as the Imperial Entanglement. Kirk sent Shepard aboard the starbase to secure the Gundam and save its civilians, then fought the Imperial fleet with the Enterprise-A. Before the end he went aboard himself. He fought Darth Vader beside Shepard, and the two of them beat him.

The Enterprise-A was decommissioned on 30 June 2293. Kirk recommended Shepard for promotion himself. Shepard was made captain and given the new USS Enterprise-B. Kirk had passed the torch.

The Nexus

On 14 October 2293 Kirk was a guest of honour aboard the Enterprise-B on her maiden voyage, under Captain Shepard. The ship answered a distress call from two transports caught in the Nexus, a ribbon of energy of the kind a later age would call a warp storm. Kirk went below to alter the deflector so that the ship could break free. The ribbon tore open the hull where he was working. When Shepard's people reached the place, he was gone. Starfleet listed him as killed.

Loves

Kirk loved many women and married only one. At the Academy there was Ruth. Later came the lawyer Areel Shaw, who prosecuted him at his court martial, and Dr Janet Wallace, who found the cure for the radiation that aged him in 2267. Carol Marcus was the mother of his son.

He never forgot Edith Keeler, whom he let die in 1930 to save history. Miramanee, the priestess he married in 2268 while he had lost his memory, died carrying his child.

Character and honours

Kirk was bold, quick to act and unwilling to believe that any situation was hopeless. He beat the Kobayashi Maru because he did not believe in a no-win scenario. For most of his career he cheated death rather than faced it, until Spock died. He loved old books, and he had a gift for talking computers into destroying themselves.

By 2267 his decorations included the Palm Leaf of the Axanar Peace Mission and the Grankite Order of Tactics, Class of Excellence. He held the Prantares Ribbon of Commendation, First and Second Class. He also held the Medal of Honor, the Silver Palm with Cluster, the Starfleet Citation for Conspicuous Gallantry and the Karagite Order of Heroism.

In the saga

Kirk has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: James Trademore
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Kamen Rider Torque' (7 February 2009)
Computer hacker; writer on strange happenings
7 November 2009, by Len of Ventara; freed December 2009
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
James Trademore is an American, born about 1985, who became a computer hacker known by the letters JTC. In 2009 he was Kamen Rider Strike, the most dangerous of the men whom Xaviax armed on Earth. Most of the others were tricked into it. He knew exactly whom he was serving. He vented five Riders, more than anybody else in the war, before Len of Ventara vented him on 7 November 2009.

JTC

As JTC, James Trademore was a name among people who followed strange happenings on the internet. He was also a hacker, good enough to be wanted by the FBI. Xaviax got him out of the FBI's hands. He gave him the Advent Deck of Strike, which would open for him because he was the mirror twin of Price, the Ventaran who first wore it.

Most of Xaviax's recruits were told lies. JTC was told the truth, or enough of it. He joined Xaviax because he thought that Xaviax was going to win.

The source

Early in 2009 a reporter, Maya Young, began to get tips from a source who signed himself JTC. In February one of them led her to the hospital where Kit Taylor's father lay. In March JTC came to her aunt's bookshop to meet her. To Kit and Len of Ventara he was a mystery who knew far too much.

In August they went looking for him at a warehouse, where a robot attacked them. A week later they watched him being carried off, as it seemed, by the enemy. He had been Strike all along.

Xaviax's right hand

Strike did the work that Xaviax's other Riders would not. On 4 April 2009 Brad Barrett, who wore the armour of Thrust, was about to change sides. Strike used him as a shield against another Rider's Final Vent, then vented him. The same day he vented Drew Lansing, the Rider called Torque, who had been plotting against Xaviax.

In August he hunted Chris Ramirez, the Rider called Sting, who had gone over to Len. He offered him a cure for his asthma as the price of betraying Len. Chris Ramirez refused. On 22 August Strike aimed a Final Vent at Len. Chris Ramirez stepped into it.

That month he took Frank Taylor from the hospital. On 4 September he offered him to Kit in return for Len's Advent Deck, which Kit would not give. On 26 September he vented Danny Cho, the Rider called Axe, whom Xaviax no longer trusted. He had already let him off once.

The last weeks

In October Strike fought beside Xaviax himself, who had put on the armour of Wrath. Together they held Trent Moseley hostage with Lacey Sheridan in the bookshop. Later they wounded Kit Taylor.

On 31 October he ambushed Len, taking from him the decks of Thrust and Sting. He had found a way to take other Riders' beasts for his own use. He joined them with Venosnaker into a single monster. The same day he vented Kase of Ventara, the Rider called Siren.

Len came after him. On 7 November 2009 Len rose into Survive Mode, then struck Strike down with a Final Vent.

Afterwards

James Trademore lay in the Advent Void until Xaviax was dead. In December 2009 Eubulon, the Advent Master, brought him out with the other men of Earth. His memories of being a Rider were taken away, then he was sent home. The armour of Strike went back to Price.

pages.title: Jamie Braddock
infobox: Sir James and Lady Elizabeth Braddock
Brian Braddock (Captain Britain) and Betsy Braddock (Psylocke), twins, about nine years younger
He can bend reality, which he sees as strings
In a coma at Muir Island
pages.html:
Jamie Braddock is the elder brother of Captain Britain and Psylocke. He was a racing driver of great charm with no conscience at all, and the only one of the three to be born in Otherworld. He gambled, dealt in slaves, robbed relief supplies and killed for money in Africa. His brother found him there in a dictator's prison in 1985, then left him to it. His mutant power to bend reality woke later, and drove him mad. In the summer of 1994 he lies in a coma at Muir Island.

Childhood

Jamie was born about 1944 in Otherworld, the hidden country of the Elves, where his parents were staying at the end of the war. They came home with him to Essex, then built Braddock Manor at Maldon in 1945. The twins, when they came, were born in England. Like them, Jamie comes down from King Arthur through a Squib branch of his house, and like them he has no idea of it.

He was about nine when the twins were born. He resented being left in charge of them, bullied them both, and was jealous of how close they were. In time he grew fond of Betsy, who shared his taste for danger. Brian, the bookworm, he never understood.

The racing driver

By the 1970s Jamie was a famous racing driver with a flat in Chelsea, a string of companies and a gift for being liked. In December 1976 a car he was testing blew up under him. Lord Synne had arranged it, and when Synne turned Betsy against him at the Manor, Brian had to show himself as Captain Britain to save his life. Early in 1977 agents of the Red Skull held Jamie hostage with Betsy until the two Captains, Britain and America, set them free.

He liked to gamble, and he liked to win more. Once he took the Maggia's money to throw a race, then won it and kept the money. To pay for the way he lived he turned to crime in Africa, where he poached, dealt in slaves, robbed the Red Cross and murdered. He felt nothing about any of it.

Doctor Crocodile

In 1985 Doctor Crocodile, the ruler of a small African state, caught him and made him call Brian for help. Brian came, saw what Jamie had done and left him to be punished. Doctor Crocodile sentenced him to a slow death. Before it was finished, the Technet carried him off for Sat-yr-9, a tyrant from another world who had guessed what slept in him. She meant to wake his mutant power, then use him as a weapon.

The power
