She woke it. Jamie found that he could see the world as a web of strings, and pull them to change what was real. The power took his reason with it. In 1989, on a world of his own making where life was a grand prix, a version of himself beat Captain Britain badly. In 1992 he came to Braddock Manor at Sat-yr-9's side, hidden among the guests at a party, and killed Brigadier Alysande Stuart of the Weird Happenings Organisation. He escaped with her.

Not long afterwards the Excalibur team found him in a coma. It took him to Moira MacTaggert's research station on Muir Island, where he has lain ever since.

In 1994

In the summer of 1994 Jamie lies asleep at Muir Island, with no sign of waking. That year Brian and Betsy went into his mind together, looking for whatever had made him what he was. They found a childhood memory that had fed his hatred, and they mended it. Afterwards he looked happier in his sleep. He did not wake.

pages.title: Jane Shepard
infobox: 21 August 2268, on Mindoir, aged ten, killed by the Orion Syndicate
pages.html:
Jane Shepard was the younger sister of John Shepard, five years his junior. She was ten when slavers of the Orion Syndicate killed her on Mindoir, with her parents, in 2268.

Life

Jane Shepard was born on Mindoir in 2258, the second child of Hannah and Hank Shepard. She grew up on the family's farm with her brother. On 21 August 2268 the slavers who raided the colony tortured her to death with her parents, in front of John. James T. Kirk found him kneeling beside her. Her death, above all, was what her brother never forgave.

In the saga

Jane Shepard has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Jasmine
infobox: A being who had once been among the powers that watched over the world
2003, Los Angeles, as a grown woman
Connor and Cordelia Chase, whose body she had taken
pages.html:
Jasmine was a being who had once been among the powers that watched over the world, and who meant to rule it. She set herself against God's purpose for Connor, the miraculous son of Angel and Darla. She had him stolen into a hell dimension, then used him to bring herself into the world. Born in 2003, she held Los Angeles in thrall for a few days before Connor killed her.

Against God's purpose

Connor was conceived and born by a direct act of God, for a purpose of His own. Jasmine would not let that purpose run. She worked through every hand she could reach.

One of them was the demon Sahjhan, who woke the hunter Daniel Holtz in 2001 believing he did it for himself. In February 2002 Holtz took the baby into Quor-toth.

Her coming

She wanted Connor for one purpose. She took the body of Cordelia Chase, and in the autumn of 2002 Connor fathered a child on her. The child was Jasmine herself.

In the months of her coming a beast of her making blotted out the sun over Los Angeles. The city went dark at noon.

Her reign

She was born in 2003, a grown woman, and Cordelia's body was left in a coma. Everyone who looked on her face loved her and obeyed her. Within days Los Angeles was hers.

Those who had her blood in them saw what the others could not: her true face, rotting under the beautiful one. Angel broke her hold on the city. Connor, her father, killed her.

pages.title: Jason Lee Scott
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Day of the Dumpster' (28 August 1993)
The Tyrannosaurus Dinozord; the Red Dragon Thunderzord, from the autumn of 1994
The Power Sword; the Omega Katana, as an Omega Ranger
The Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 1993 to 1994; the Omega Rangers, 1994 to 1995, as their leader
Rocky DeSantos, as the Red Ranger; Trini Kwan, as the Red Omega Ranger
The Red Omega Ranger, 1994 to 1995; the Gold Zeo Ranger, 1996; the Red Ranger again, from 2002
Zack Taylor, his best friend; Tommy Oliver
January 1995, breaking the Death Ranger's hold on him
pages.html:
Jason Lee Scott is the Red Ranger, the first leader of the Power Rangers, whose Power Coin draws on the Tyrannosaurus. He is a martial artist of Angel Grove, about seventeen in the summer of 1994, who teaches karate at the Youth Center. It was Jason who broke Rita Repulsa's spell on Tommy Oliver. Since then the two of them have been the best of friends and rivals. In October 1994 Zordon made Tommy the leader in his place. In November Jason passed his powers to Rocky DeSantos, saying that he was going to a peace conference in Geneva. In truth he went into space as the Red Omega Ranger, until the Death Ranger cost him his link to the Power in January 1995. Only then did he go to Geneva. He came home in 1996 to carry the Gold Ranger's powers for a while, and in 2002 he was one of the ten Red Rangers who fought the last of the Machine Empire on the Moon.

Angel Grove

Jason was born about 1977 and grew up in Angel Grove, California, where he is a pupil at Angel Grove High School. At ten he was a bully, much like Bulk and Skull. After one bad day at summer camp his mother took him to the dojo of Sensei Kazu, who taught him to master his temper. Jason promised himself that he would change, and he has kept the promise.

A year or so later Ernie opened the Youth Center, where the city's teenagers spend their afternoons. Zack Taylor met Jason there on the day it opened. Jason is a martial artist of real skill, who teaches a karate class at the Youth Center. Billy Cranston is one of his pupils, and his best friend, Zack, often trains with him.

The Red Ranger

In 1993 Rita Repulsa was set free on the Moon. Zordon had his robot, Alpha 5, bring five teenagers of Angel Grove to the Command Center: Jason, Billy, Zack, Trini Kwan and Kimberly Hart. Only Jason believed what Zordon told them at first. The others came round when Rita's Putty Patrollers attacked.

Jason became the Red Ranger. His Power Coin calls up the Tyrannosaurus Dinozord, and his weapon is the Power Sword. Zordon made him the leader of the team.

Zordon once told Zack why he had chosen Jason to lead. There had been a time, he said, when Jason used his strength to take whatever he wanted, as Rita does. He had changed, and he had been trying to make up for it ever since. Jason, said Zordon, 'would die before he would allow another Ranger to go down that path'.

On 30 July 1993 the Rangers came to public notice for the first time, when they fought a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham. Rita's warrior Goldar is Jason's particular enemy.

In September 1993 a Putty dragged Jason and Trini Kwan through one of Rita's portals to the planet Breel. There their minds were linked for a while, and the two of them began a short, secret romance. They ended it by agreement, since an enemy could have used it against them.

Tommy Oliver

Late in 1993 a new boy came to Angel Grove, Tommy Oliver, a martial artist as good as Jason. The two of them met at the Angel Grove Karate Tournament, and neither could beat the other: the bout was declared a draw.

Rita had been watching. She gave Tommy the stolen Green Power Coin and bound him with a spell to destroy the Rangers. As the Green Ranger he captured Jason, took his morpher and shut him up in Rita's Dark Dimension. Billy, Trini and Alpha 5 got him out seconds before Tommy would have killed him.

In the end it came down to the two of them. Jason beat Tommy in a duel with swords, then destroyed the Sword of Darkness with his blaster, for it was the Sword that held Rita's spell together. Tommy came to himself. 'What have I done?' he said, and Jason was the first at his side. Jason and the others talked him into joining the team.

Weeks later the Black Dragon, a war machine steered from another world by Tommy's other self, Lord Drakkon, wrecked the Command Center, cut Zordon adrift and took the powers of every Ranger but Tommy. Jason went with Tommy to the Moon in the Dragonzord with no powers at all. Once Tommy had shared out his own, Jason fought on in green, with the Dragon Shield across his chest.

Rita never forgave Tommy. In November 1993 she lit a green candle that would drain his powers when it burnt down. Jason went into the Dark Dimension to fetch it, and he fought Goldar there. He had to choose between saving Tommy's powers and saving his own life. The candle burnt out before he could bring it back.

When his powers were all but gone, Tommy gave Jason the Green Power Coin, so that Rita could never have it back. For a while Jason carried the Dragon Shield and the Dragon Dagger as well as his own powers. With the dagger he could call up the Dragonzord. Early in 1994 Zordon put new power into the coin, and it went back to Tommy.

In the spring of 1994 Rita carried Tommy off to Japan with a stolen gem. Jason led the others after him. Their Megazord fought Godzilla, the great beast of that country, then fought beside him against King Ghidorah.

Shattered Grid

In the summer of 1994 Jason works with Grace Sterling, the head of Promethea, who was Zordon's first Red Ranger in 1969. At the end of that August Billy found the prisoner she had kept for ten months in a secret cell: Lord Drakkon. Jason, furious that she had never told him, ended the partnership on the spot.

Days later Drakkon escaped and murdered Tommy, on the night of Tommy's first proper date with Kimberly Hart. Jason took up the Dragon Shield and the Dragon Dagger. In the war that followed he gave them to Kimberly for the last assault on Drakkon's tower, where he led the fight on the ground until Serpentera seemed to destroy him. Then Drakkon unmade the world. Tommy's spirit undid him, and the Rangers mended it with Tommy alive. Nobody on Earth remembered, but Jason was the one chosen to be given the memory back.

Lord Zedd

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon and took over Rita's war. His monsters outclassed Finster's, so Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords. Jason's became the Red Dragon Thunderzord, which can rise up as a warrior and beat a monster on its own.

Zedd stripped away what was left of Tommy's powers. Jason blamed himself, because he had not brought back the green candle in time. When he won a martial arts trophy that autumn, he dedicated it to Tommy.

Late one night that October the Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, came to Jason as he took out his anger on a punchbag. The mended world was leaking Power into people all over the galaxy, and somebody had to find them. A touch on the forehead gave him back his memory of Drakkon's war. He was to tell nobody, Zordon least of all, because the telling would endanger the mended world.

Jason would not leave while Tommy was lost, so his price was the White Light: at his wish the Emissary showed Zordon the way to it. Then Zack and Trini walked in on Jason with the Emissary, their blasters drawn. Given back their own memories, they told him that he was not alone.

In October 1994 Tommy came back as the White Ranger, and Zordon made him the leader of the team. Jason became his second-in-command.

The lie about Geneva

In November 1994 Jason, Zack and Trini were chosen as delegates to the World Peace Conference in Geneva. The conference was real, as were Angel Grove's three places for young delegates, which is what made the lie easy. The three of them never meant to go. Lying was nothing new to them by then. Their first trip into space had been passed off as a scuba-diving holiday, and Jason had told his friends that his communicator was broken.

They told Zordon, who agreed that they must go, then set Alpha 5 to finding three new Rangers. He gave the team the news himself, believing every word. Jason told the same story to Tommy, Kimberly and Billy. He told it to his parents, his teachers, Ernie and anybody in Angel Grove who asked. His father, not knowing what he was agreeing to, told him to do whatever he had to do to make him proud.

It meant leaving Angel Grove. It also meant giving up their powers. First the Rangers fetched the Sword of Light from a far planet. With it the powers of the three passed to three friends from Stone Canyon, who took them in good faith. Jason's went to Rocky DeSantos, the new Red Ranger.

Tommy called him a coward for leaving when the team needed him most. Jason could not answer him. Then the three left Earth. They never went near Geneva.

The Red Omega Ranger

On Safehaven, a world a very long way from Earth, the three took up the Omega powers, handed down from some of the earliest Rangers in the universe. Jason became the Red Omega Ranger, whose power is fire, with the Omega Katana, and he led the team.

Late in November 1994 they took Dayne, the bounty hunter Lord Zedd had hired, then stormed the Moon, where Jason brought the Red Omegazord down on the giant Zedd. Zedd was carried off to a cell on Safehaven. Afterwards Jason, with his helmet on, had a short, tense talk with Tommy outside the Command Center.

Early in December Kiya Kyatyl, the fourth of the team, turned on them and struck Jason down before he could morph. Xi, their robot, got the three to the Command Center so that he could be treated. They arrived with their faces bare. Jason woke with Alpha 5, Billy, Kimberly and Tommy standing over him. Tommy was livid.

Zordon forgave the three at once. Tommy did not, and when Jason was on his feet the two of them had it out, sparring. Jason's only answer was that he had had no choice. Then he said that he was going back to Safehaven to protect its people, even if it killed him. He and Tommy fought the Anointed side by side, joining their Zords to beat Garrison Vox. By the end they were friends again.

Drakkon and the Empyreals

In the middle of December Drakkon fell to Earth, and Zordon locked him in a cell under the Command Center. Early in January 1995 the Omega Rangers asked for him as a guide against the Empyreals, giants that burnt whole worlds clean. Zordon refused. That night they took him anyway. Jason stayed behind long enough to say that they were sorry. Zordon called it a complete betrayal, then disowned them.

Drakkon sold them to the Empyreals in the end. Fetched out in time for the Eltarian War, Jason went aboard Zartus's ship with Trini, beside Zordon in a body of metal, to free the Guardian Zelya.

The Death Ranger

Late in January 1995 a visitor to Safehaven took the Gold Omega morpher out of its vault, hoping to wake a friend who lay beyond help. What woke was Spa'ark, the Death Ranger, who struck Jason down and wore his body.

Jason was held inside the Power. There he was shown his mother, alive. She had just died at home, of an illness, while he was away under a lie. He refused the vision, then broke the Gold morpher from within, which ended the Death Ranger's hold. He lived, but the breaking tore out his own link to the Power. He could not be the Red Omega Ranger again, nor carry a Power Coin. Trini sent him home to his father, then took the Red Omega powers herself.

Geneva in earnest

He was at home when Rita came back as Mistress Vile, early in February. Matt Cook, under her spell, wounded him at the Youth Center. When the Rangers cleansed the Grid, Jason held the Arch in the Bermuda Triangle with Tommy, who had given up his own coin. That is why Jason remembered those weeks when hardly anybody else did.

He could not stay in Angel Grove without undoing the story for all three. After his mother's funeral, later that February, he took up his place at the peace conference in earnest, months late, so that the lie became the truth for him. He stayed in Switzerland until the autumn of 1996.

The Gold Ranger

Jason came home from Switzerland in the autumn of 1996. He had been without powers since January 1995. By then the Rangers drew their powers from the Zeo Crystal. Their ally Trey of Triforia, the Gold Ranger, had been badly hurt by the Varox, a band of bounty hunters, and he could no longer hold his powers.

The powers were meant for Billy Cranston. The negative energy left over from the destruction of the Command Center kept them from him, so in October 1996 Tommy brought Jason to the Power Chamber instead. The Gold powers were Triforia's, held in a staff, so they did not need the link to the Power that Jason had lost. He became the Gold Ranger.

The powers had not been made for a human body. They wore him down, sapping first his strength and then his life, until Zordon warned that they would kill him. In November 1996 they went back to Trey. Jason was none the worse for it, and he went off with Emily, the girl he had been seeing.

On 19 October 1996, while he held the Gold powers, Jason was the first Ranger to reach the town of Charterville. The Machine Empire's Cogs had marched in there with a monster grown to giant size. He fought on the ground beside the Beetleborgs, the three armoured heroes of the town, while Tommy's Zeo Megazord dealt with the giant. He did not know that the three were children, the eldest of them twelve.

Divatox

In the spring of 1997 Jason and Kimberly Hart were out diving together when Divatox, a space pirate, took them both prisoner. She meant them as sacrifices to Maligore, and she used them to put pressure on the Rangers.

Maligore's evil got into them, and they turned on their old friends. 'Now I'm the one with the muscles and the power!' Jason told Tommy. Lerigot and his wife, Yara, undid what had been done to them.

Afterwards Jason took the injured Rocky DeSantos's place in a martial arts tournament. He won it with Tommy and Adam Park.

Later years

In 2002 the last generals of the Machine Empire set about digging Serpentera, Lord Zedd's old war machine, out of the Moon. Tommy gathered the Red Rangers, ten of them in all, to stop them. By then the link to the Power that he had torn out in 1995 had grown back. Jason fought among them with his old powers, and they won.

In 2014 Rangers of every generation came to the help of the Mega Rangers against the Armada's invasion of Earth. Jason fought among them, though he never took off his helmet. In 2020 Devon Daniels, the Red Ranger of the Grid Battleforce, sent a call for help through the Morphin Grid, and Jason answered it.

In 2022 Billy Cranston tried to bring Zordon back. What came back instead was the evil that Zordon's light had driven out of Rita Repulsa, in a body of its own, Robo-Rita. Jason fought her beside the rest of the old team, in the battle in which Trini Kwan was killed.

A year later Robo-Rita's creatures took Jason prisoner, with Tommy and Kimberly. She drained their power to open a door into the past. When her machine was broken they were set free. Adam Park and Aisha Campbell took them to Aquitar to be healed.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' news showed helicopter film of the fight in Birmingham the afternoon before. Five people in coloured suits and helmets ran in a line across a rooftop towards the creature. The one in red was Jason. Dudley, with a sausage halfway to his mouth, watched them leap off the roof as though he would like to be one of them.

Book Three, Chapter Four: Harry told Lucius Malfoy about the team in California, who had no magic at all and fought monsters anyway. 'They save people. That's all.'

Book Four, Chapter Three: by August 1994 the Rangers were on the Dursleys' news nearly every morning, and there were six of them now. Jason was still the Red Ranger, though Dudley's favourite was the newest, the green one.

pages.title: Jay Garrick
infobox: Retired; the Justice Society disbanded after Zero Hour
pages.html:
Jay Garrick was the first Flash, a college student who came to public notice at the end of 1939 in a winged helmet, and one of the founders of the Justice Society. He retired with the Society in 1951 and was drawn back into the work in the 1960s. For decades he stayed vigorous far beyond his years, until Zero Hour, in July 1994, aged him in moments to his true age of about seventy-four.

The first Flash

Jay Garrick was a student at Midwestern University when he breathed in the fumes of an experiment with hard water and found that he could move at superhuman speed. He came to public notice at the end of 1939 as the Flash, in a red shirt with a lightning bolt, blue trousers and his father's winged steel helmet. He worked chiefly in Keystone City. In 1940 he was one of the founders of the Justice Society, and for a time its chairman. He married Joan Williams.

When the Society disbanded in 1951 rather than unmask before a committee of Congress, Jay retired. In 1961 Barry Allen, the new Flash, who had taken the name in his honour, came looking for him. The meeting drew Jay back into action, with several of his old colleagues. He has worked on and off ever since, often beside the Justice League.

Borrowed years

During the war the members of the Justice Society were caught in the strange temporal energies of the sorcerer Ian Karkull, which slowed their ageing. Jay stayed fast and fit into his seventies. In 1986 the Society left this world to fight an endless battle in another realm, holding off Ragnarok. It came back in 1992, and Jay with it.

In July 1994, during Zero Hour, the time-mad Extant took those stolen years back. Three of Jay's oldest friends died of it: the Atom (Al Pratt), Hourman (Rex Tyler) and Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider). Jay himself was aged in moments to his true age, about seventy-four. He kept his speed, and he lives on in Keystone City with Joan, but the Society he had helped to found disbanded soon afterwards.

pages.title: J.B. Reese
infobox: A laser pistol; a laser sabre that becomes a lance; the Techno-Bazooka
The Skybase, a battle cruiser, a flying cycle
pages.html:
J.B. Reese is a young karate instructor of Crossworld City, California, who knows more about computers than anybody else at Tao's Dojo. In September 1994 he became one of the three VR Troopers, the one in black armour, who flew most of their machines. In the summer of 1994 he is eighteen. Nobody has ever said what the initials stand for.

Crossworld City

J.B. was born about 1976. He teaches karate to children at Tao's Dojo beside his friend Ryan Steele, holding a black belt of his own. His other gift is for machines: he can make a computer do almost anything. His father is alive. Nothing is recorded of his mother.

He, Ryan and the reporter Kaitlin Star have been friends since before any of them had heard of virtual reality.

A Trooper

On 3 September 1994 J.B. went with his two friends to Professor Hart's laboratory, where each of them was given a Virtualizer. His armour was black. He carried a laser pistol, with a laser sabre for close work. To finish a fight he opened a second blade from the sabre's hilt, making a lance of it, which he drove through his enemy.

When a fight in this world grew too dangerous for the people round it, he had another resource. A control at his belt, the Vortex Command, pulled him through the reality barrier into virtual reality, taking his enemy with him.

The Troopers' machines were mostly his to fly. He piloted the Skybase, the flying fortress the three shared, as well as a battle cruiser. Against Grimlord's air force he used the Techno-Bazooka, a weapon so large that he fired it by throwing a giant image of himself into the sky.

At the laboratory he was the Professor's second pair of hands. When Grimlord's aircraft bombed the place in November 1994, it was J.B. who fed the Troopers' commands back into the machines.

Dr Poindexter

In September 1994 an inventor called Dr Ulysses T. Poindexter designed an engine that made no pollution. Karl Ziktor, who sells oil, wanted the plans. The Troopers kept them out of his hands, and with Poindexter's work J.B. gained a flying cycle of his own.

In February 1995 a rigged arcade game damaged all three Virtualizers. Poindexter mended them, which meant that he learnt who the Troopers were. J.B. took that memory away from him afterwards. Poindexter went on helping the Troopers all the same.

Captured and changed

On 21 September 1994 J.B. was dragged through a computer screen into Grimlord's dungeon, where chains of lightning drained his strength until Ryan came for him. That autumn he destroyed General Ivar, the commander of Grimlord's armies, whom Grimlord had to have rebuilt. In February 1995 a weapon made by Ziktor's inventor Strickland turned J.B. into one of Grimlord's creatures. Ryan saved him. He got his own shape back in time to sit a scholarship examination.

The Red Python

When the Red Python nearly killed Kaitlin on 27 February 1995, J.B. swore to bring it down. He fought it the next day. Its powers failed in the middle of the fight. By then he knew that there was a girl inside it, Kaitlin's friend Amy, so he reasoned with her instead. The Troopers got her out before the armour destroyed itself.

1995 to 1996

In September 1995 the Ultra Skugs caught J.B. with Kaitlin in the cavern where Grimlord was holding Tyler Steele. Ryan freed all three at the cost of his own armour. In October Grimlord trapped J.B. with Kaitlin between the worlds as ghosts, whom nobody could see but Ryan's dog, Jeb. They found the buried machine that was doing it, so that Ryan could break it. The same month the bite of a spider from virtual reality aged them both before their time, until that too was put right.

In November Knighttime, an ally of Grimlord's, sent the pair of them back into the far past. Ryan fetched them home.

On 7 February 1996 J.B. was a prisoner aboard Grimlord's Air Castle. Freed by Ryan, he beat its commander, Desponda, with his lance, a blow that brought the whole castle down. On 20 February he fought Grimlord's Fanbot beside Kaitlin, while Ryan dealt with the machine that had stopped time.

That month the Troopers built Galileo, a robot whose memory held everything the laboratory's computers knew. Grimlord's Skugs stole it on 21 February. In the raid that followed, J.B. overloaded Oraclon's circuits with Kaitlin's help, crippling the Virtual Dark Fortress. Galileo came home with its memory wiped clean. Nothing is recorded of J.B. Reese after that.

pages.title: Jeb the dog
pages.html:
Jeb is Ryan Steele's dog, a Redbone Coonhound who has been with him since Ryan was a small boy. In September 1994 a surge of power in Professor Hart's laboratory left him able to talk. He had opinions ready. From then on he was the fourth member of the household of the VR Troopers, as well as the least respectful.

Ryan's dog

Jeb has been Ryan's dog since Ryan was small, so by the summer of 1994 he is no longer young. He is an ordinary hound: fond of his master, fonder of food. He will eat anything he finds.

How Jeb came to talk

In September 1994 Ryan became one of the VR Troopers, which meant that Jeb began coming to Professor Hart's laboratory. In the first week a surge of power from the machines caught him. When it had passed, he spoke. He had a dry way of talking, like a dog who had been keeping his remarks to himself for years.

Ryan made him promise never to speak in front of anybody outside the secret. Jeb kept the promise, more or less. His one indulgence was Percy Rooney, a reporter on the Underground Voice Daily, who is allergic to dogs. Jeb could not resist making a sly remark to him now and then, or setting him sneezing.

At the laboratory

Jeb turned out to be useful. He had a knack with the Professor's machines, with a good head for a problem. On 15 September 1994 Ryan lost his memory in a collision with one of Grimlord's flying robots. It came back when Jeb greeted him.

Scrapes

Grimlord's servants went after Jeb more than once. On 28 September 1994 Karl Ziktor, disguising his voice, got Jeb hired for a dog food advertisement. The stuff turned pets into raging monsters, with Jeb the first of them. Professor Hart turned him back. In October the Skugs kidnapped him as bait. That same month Jeb fell for a dog called Princess, whose puppies were stolen. The Troopers got them back.

Later in October 1994 Skugs made him invisible. The Professor's first cure brought back only his front half, which he bore with what dignity he could. In February 1995 a stolen machine exchanged his mind with Ryan's. For one day Jeb wore the armour, fighting as a Trooper.

He could be brave when it was wanted. In September 1995 he volunteered to go into Grimlord's dungeon as a spy, to look for Tyler Steele. Grimlord blew the dungeon up with Jeb inside it, though he came out alive with Ryan. In October Grimlord turned Kaitlin Star into a ghost, along with J.B. Reese. Nobody but Jeb could see them, so it was Jeb who led them back.

Nothing is recorded of him after February 1996.

pages.title: Jeff Moreau
infobox: Joker; Jeff 'Joker' Moreau; Flight Lieutenant Moreau
pages.html:
Jeff Moreau, known to everyone as Joker, was the helmsman of the USS Enterprise-B under Captain John Shepard. He was the best pilot in Starfleet, as he was the first to say.

The pilot

Moreau was born with a disease that left his bones as brittle as glass. Federation medicine eased it, though it could not cure it. He walked with difficulty all his life. At Starfleet Academy his instructors took him for a charity case, so he set out to beat every record they had. He beat all of them. They called him Joker there because he never smiled.

He made up for that afterwards. At the helm of the Enterprise-B he kept up a stream of remarks that few captains would have put up with. Shepard put up with them, since nobody else could fly the ship as he did. It was Joker who brought her out of Vega with a third of her crew dead, then out of Thessia with the Empire's fighters all round her.

In the saga

Jeff Moreau has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Jet Jaguar
infobox: A robot that once thought for itself
That of a man; that of Godzilla, when it chooses
In Goro Ibuki's keeping, in Japan
pages.html:
Jet Jaguar is a man-sized robot built in 1973 by the Japanese inventor Goro Ibuki. In the middle of a battle it began to think for itself. Then it grew to the size of Godzilla, which its maker had certainly not designed it to do.

Seatopia, 1973

Goro Ibuki built Jet Jaguar at his home in Japan, with his small brother Rokuro for company. It was a robot the size of a man, with a pointed silver face, that could fly. In 1973 agents of Seatopia broke in to steal it.

Seatopia is a kingdom under the bed of the sea, ruled in 1973 by an Emperor called Antonio. Underground bomb tests had been shaking its cities to pieces, the latest of them on Asuka Island in the Aleutians. Antonio meant to answer by sending his people's guardian, the giant beetle Megalon, to destroy Tokyo. Megalon needed a guide on the surface, for which the Seatopians wanted Jet Jaguar.

Neither of the kingdoms that call themselves Atlantis has ever claimed Seatopia as kin. Seatopia, for its part, has never claimed them.

Goro got control of his robot back, then sent it to Monster Island to fetch Godzilla. When it returned it no longer answered him. It had begun to think for itself. To hold Megalon until Godzilla arrived, it grew, from the height of a man to the height of a monster.

The hunters of Nebula M sent Gigan to Megalon's aid. For a while Jet Jaguar fought the pair by itself. Then Godzilla came. Megalon went home underground, Gigan fled into space, then Godzilla shook hands with Jet Jaguar before he left. The robot shrank again to go home with the Ibuki brothers. Seatopia closed its tunnels to the surface.

Since that day it has done only what it is told. Goro Ibuki thinks that its will might wake again if it were ever needed.

Megalon, 1994

Megalon came to the surface again in the spring of 1994, at the call of the Xiliens of Planet X. Godzilla killed it on the coast of Japan.

pages.title: Jinga
pages.html:
Jinga was a Makai Knight of another world who became a Horror, the worst enemy of that world's Golden Knight, Ryuga Dougai. His wife, Amily, a Makai Priestess, fell with him. Ryuga destroyed him in 2015. Other Horrors brought him back in 2018, when he was beaten a second time. Then he was destroyed by Messiah herself, whom he had the nerve to challenge.

The village

Jinga was a knight of real gifts, known as the fang of the gods. He travelled with Amily, hunting Horrors, with their small son, Yuto, beside them. They came to a village in trouble. The villagers did not believe a word the strangers said. They gave the boy to a Horror as a sacrifice.

Jinga and Amily slaughtered the village. By the time they had finished they were Horrors themselves, of a rare kind that feeds on other Horrors. Moyuru, a Makai Priest, died saving two of the village children, Gald with his sister Haruna. They grew up to be priests with no love for knights.

Radan

In 2015 the pair came to Line City, which Ryuga Dougai guarded with the priestess Rian. They wanted Radan, a Horror in the form of a flying castle, sealed long before between the worlds by the priests of Gald's village. Radan obeys whoever sits on its throne. It needs a second Horror to be its moon, the source of its power. Jinga meant to sit there, with Amily for his moon, to play with human lives as his own had been played with.

They tricked a priest into drawing the sword that held the seal. Amily shut Ryuga inside a mirror. Rian called him back out of it in a darker form of the golden armour, a match for Jinga at last. Radan rose all the same.

On 18 September 2015 Jinga seized Rian to be the castle's moon in Amily's place. She blew herself up sooner than serve. Ryuga beat Jinga with his fists, then ran him through. Jinga never admitted that he had lost. He had already killed Amily, who was of no more use to him, with his own hand. Gald sealed Radan. Rian, as it turned out, lived.

The ark

In January 2018 a Horror named Rinza fooled a priestess into raising a dead knight with stolen armours. The knight who rose was Jinga, without his memory. Rinza wanted him to wake an ark, called Kami no Kiba, that would carry the Horrors to the Moon. From there a gate could be opened for Messiah. Jinga, once he remembered himself, killed Rinza. He kept the ark, which climbed to the edge of the sky. Ryuga beat him there a second time.

He fell into the true Makai. There he met Messiah, the mother of the Horrors, the same who had been beaten in March 2006 by Kouga Saejima, the Garo of this world. He challenged her. She destroyed him.

He was born again afterwards as a man, a knight named Jinga Mikage, in whom the old Jinga woke in the end.

pages.title: Jo McCormick
infobox: Red Striker, 1996 to 1997; Platinum Purple, from September 1997; Mega Spectra, from February 1998
The Striker Blaster; the Metallix Baton; the Astral Pulsar
pages.html:
Jo McCormick is the younger sister of Drew McCormick, a girl of Charterville who wears her baseball cap back to front. In the summer of 1994 she is about eight years old. In September 1996 a wish made her the Red Striker Beetleborg, the youngest of the Beetleborgs, with the strength of several grown men besides. In 1997 she became the Platinum Purple Beetleborg. From April 1997 she also had a different face, though hardly anybody knew it.

Charterville

Jo was born about 1986. She is growing up in Charterville beside her elder brother, Drew, whom she follows everywhere without ever doing as he says. Their best friend is Roland Williams, whose family keeps Zoom Comics. She is the youngest of the three by a year or two, which has never stopped her from saying what she thinks.

In September 1996 her small cousin, Oliver, came to stay. He photographed everything in sight, dressed up as a Beetleborg. Noxic of the Magnavores took the costume for the real thing, so he carried Oliver off, whereupon the real Beetleborgs had to fetch him back.

The Red Striker Beetleborg

On 7 September 1996 Jo went into Hillhurst Mansion with Drew and Roland, on a dare. The three let Flabber out of the pipe organ, for which he granted them a wish. They wished to be the Beetleborgs, the heroes of their favourite comic book.

Jo became the Red Striker Beetleborg. Her weapon was the Striker Blaster, four barrels that fired together. In armour she stood as tall as a grown woman, so nobody in Charterville ever supposed that the Red Striker was a small girl.

The wish left her a gift out of armour too. Once she had cracked her knuckles, she was stronger than any man in the town.

Mishaps with magic

Hillhurst is full of magic, a good deal of which went off in Jo's direction. In September 1996, while Drew was trying to learn magic, Flabber's spellbook turned Jo invisible by accident. A week later she was changed for a while into a snarling monster, in the manner of Dr Jekyll's Mr Hyde.

She came through both. It was Jo who found the Magnavores' hiding place in November 1996, a crypt in the Charterville cemetery. That discovery let Drew steal the source of Shadowborg's strength. In March 1997 a figure called the Phantom tried to carry her off from Hillhurst, without success.

A new face

On 10 April 1997 Wolfgang Smith, the werewolf of Hillhurst, got hold of Flabber's spellbook. The spell he set off changed Jo's face, with her voice, for good.

It could not be undone. What Flabber could do was to cast a second spell over it, so that everybody else would go on seeing the Jo they had always known. Only those who were in the room when it happened saw her as she had become. Charterville never noticed any difference.

Platinum Purple

On 8 September 1997 Nukus destroyed the Beetleborgs' armour, weapons and powers. The next day the Crustaceans broke Les Fortunes out of Charterville Prison. In the riot they shut the three children in a cell with Art Fortunes. The gifts of the wish had not gone with the armour. Jo cracked her knuckles, which got them out.

That day Art drew the Metallix armour, which Flabber brought to life. Jo became the Platinum Purple Beetleborg, in the likeness of a ladybird, with the Metallix Baton.

In November 1997 both sides hunted for the Astral Coins. One of them, the Firebug coin, turned up in the keeping of Mums at Hillhurst. Jo used it to call up Fireborg, the second of the Astralborgs. He gave her the Astral Pulsar, which mended damaged armour.

In February 1998 Roboborg gave the three the Mega Spectra armour. Jo wore it on 2 March, when the Beetleborgs destroyed Repgillian with both giants.

The Power Rangers

Jo fought beside the Zeo Rangers in Charterville on 19 October 1996, with her helmet on. She had supposed that all Power Rangers were grown up. On 3 May 1997 the Blue Turbo Ranger took off his helmet at Hillhurst, where he turned out to be Justin Stewart, twelve years old. Jo, who was younger still, told him that the Beetleborgs had started earlier.

On 25 October 1997 Flabber sent the three to Angel Grove, where Nukus had gone to fetch Les Fortunes back from Divatox. Flabber's aim was a little off. They arrived in the lake. Later in the same fight Jo picked up Vilor, the fish-headed captain of the Crustaceans, to throw him in after them. Justin said afterwards that it was the best thing he had seen all year.

She met the Space Rangers in the Charterville cemetery on 21 February 1998. Four of them were the friends she had made in the autumn, Cassie Chan and Ashley Hammond among them.

pages.title: John Shepard
infobox: Commander Shepard; Captain Shepard; Captain John Shepard
Hannah and Hank Shepard, former Starfleet officers
Tortured and killed by slavers of the Orion Syndicate on Mindoir, 21 August 2268
James T. Kirk and the USS Enterprise, 2268
The Skyllian Blitz, 2277; Akuze, 2278; Torfan, 2279; the Imperial Entanglement, 2293; the Intergalactic War, 2299 to 2300
The Star of Terra, for the Skyllian Blitz
The USS Enterprise-A, 2293, as commander of her Marine detachment
After the Tomed Incident of 2311, with Ashley Williams, to raise their children
The Orion Syndicate; Darth Vader and the Galactic Empire
Ashley Williams, gunnery chief of the Enterprise-B
pages.html:
John Shepard was a Starfleet officer, the captain of the USS Enterprise-B, and the man the Federation came to call the next Kirk. He was born on the farming colony of Mindoir, where slavers of the Orion Syndicate tortured his parents and his sister to death in front of him when he was fifteen. James T. Kirk saved him, and Kirk became the nearest thing to a father that he had left. Shepard rose through the Starfleet Marines by way of the Skyllian Blitz, Akuze and Torfan. In 2293 he fought beside Kirk against Darth Vader in the Imperial Entanglement, then took the Enterprise-B from Kirk's own hands. Six years later he led the alliance of old enemies that drove the Galactic Empire out of the Milky Way in the Intergalactic War. When the Enterprise-B was destroyed at Tomed in 2311 he brought every one of her crew off alive, then retired to raise his children.

Family

John Shepard was born on 11 April 2253 on Mindoir, a farming colony on the Federation's frontier, not far from the edge of Orion space. His mother, Hannah Shepard, and his father, Hank Shepard, had both been Starfleet officers. Hannah had served aboard the USS Kilimanjaro, where she rose to lieutenant commander. Hank had been a security officer aboard the USS Einstein. They met in the service, married in it, then resigned their commissions together in 2252 to raise a family somewhere quiet.

Their daughter, Jane Shepard, was born in 2258, five years after John. The two children grew up on the family's farm outside the main settlement. Their parents taught them to shoot, to mend an engine, to read a star chart. Hank had the boy up before dawn for the harvest. Hannah told him stories of the Kilimanjaro at night. Shepard later said that everything good in him had been put there before he was fifteen.

The raid on Mindoir

On 21 August 2268 the Orion Syndicate raided Mindoir for slaves. Its ships came in under the colony's sensors at dusk, with Batarian slavers leading the landing parties. Most of the colonists were taken in the first hour. The Shepards were not. Hank and Hannah had been Starfleet officers, so they fought. They held the farmhouse for most of the night, and they killed a number of the raiders before it fell.

The slavers made an example of them. They tortured Hank, Hannah and ten-year-old Jane to death, slowly, over several hours. They made John watch all of it. Friends and neighbours of the family died in the same yard. When it was over, the slavers turned to the boy.

The USS Enterprise had picked up Mindoir's distress call. Captain James T. Kirk beamed down with a landing party just as a slaver put a blade to John Shepard's throat. Kirk shot the man himself. The raiders who could still run fled to their ships, with the Enterprise after them. Of the Shepard family only John was left alive.

Kirk found him kneeling beside his sister. The boy stood up, looked the captain in the face and swore that he would make the Orion Syndicate pay, every last one of them, if it took him the rest of his life. He was fifteen. Kirk did not tell him that he was wrong.

The raid left Shepard with a rage that never really went away. What he had seen that night made him deeply xenophobic, out of fury, trauma and grief. It was an uneasy thing to carry into a Federation of many peoples. He carried it all the same.

Kirk

Kirk took pity on the boy. He had been thirteen on Tarsus IV when its governor, Kodos, put half the colonists to death, so he knew what it was to watch people die and to live on afterwards. He had also kept away from his own son, David Marcus, at the wish of the boy's mother. He regretted it more with every year.

He kept Shepard aboard the Enterprise until a place could be found for him, then saw him settled with a foster family on Earth. After that the two of them wrote to each other for years, messages going back and forth across the Federation. Kirk answered every one. Shepard came to look on him as a father. When David Marcus was killed by Klingons in 2285, Shepard was among the first to write to Kirk.

Starfleet Academy

Shepard entered Starfleet Academy in 2271, at eighteen, to become an officer of the Starfleet Marines. He did exceptionally well there, near the top of his class in tactics, small arms and survival. He made no secret of whose example he was following. He was commissioned in June 2275, then posted to the Marine detachment of the USS Hastings, which patrolled the Orion frontier.

The Skyllian Blitz: the war hero

On 14 June 2277 the Orion Syndicate struck at Elysium, a rich Federation colony in the Skyllian Verge. It was the largest raid the Syndicate had ever mounted, with a fleet of slave ships, Batarian slavers by the thousand and Krogan mercenaries to break the defences. Shepard was on Elysium on shore leave. He had no command there, no orders, nothing but a sidearm.

He took charge anyway. He rallied the colony's militia and its civilians, armed them from a constable's store, then set them to hold the streets around the landing fields. When the Krogan broke through the last barricade, he held the gap almost alone for hours, until the USS Agincourt arrived with reinforcements. The colony was saved, with all its people.

Shepard was awarded the Star of Terra, the highest honour the Starfleet Marines give for valour. He was twenty-four. The newsfeeds called him the Hero of Elysium. Some of them had already begun to compare him with Kirk.

Akuze: the sole survivor

In March 2278 the pioneer colony on Akuze fell silent. Shepard, now a lieutenant, was sent with a unit of fifty Marines to find out why. They found the settlement standing empty, without a body in it. They made camp beside it.

On the night of 9 March thresher maws, the great burrowing beasts that hunt by the shaking of the ground, came up out of the earth beneath the camp. They killed forty-nine of the fifty Marines. Shepard fought his way out, then walked alone for two days across open country to the landing site, where a shuttle from orbit found him.

He was the sole survivor of Akuze. Starfleet's doctors expected the ordeal to break him. It did not. He asked to go back on duty within the month.

Torfan: the Butcher

Starfleet's answer to the Blitz came on 27 October 2279, on Torfan. The Syndicate kept its largest slaving base there, in tunnels dug deep under the surface of an airless moon. Shepard had waited eleven years for it. When his commanding officer hesitated at the cost, Shepard took over the assault himself.

He drove his Marines down through the tunnels without a pause, level after level. Three quarters of them died doing it. When the last of the slavers threw down their weapons, he had them shot. No slaver left Torfan alive, though several hundred slaves did.

The Federation did not know what to make of it. A board of inquiry cleared him, since the base had been taken, the slaves freed and the Syndicate's power in the Verge broken for a generation. Some in Starfleet called him a hero. Others called him the Butcher of Torfan, a name that followed him for the rest of his career. Kirk did not excuse what he had done, but he did not turn his back on him either.

N7 and command

In 2280 Shepard was accepted into the Starfleet Marines' Interplanetary Combatives Training at Vila Militar, in Rio de Janeiro. Its grades run from N1 to N7, each harder than the last. Most candidates fail the first. Shepard passed all seven, earning the N7 badge in 2281, which very few officers have ever worn.

For the next twelve years he fought the Orion Syndicate wherever Starfleet would send him. He led raids on its slave markets, its convoys and its paymasters, in operations that freed thousands of people. He was promoted to lieutenant commander in 2284, then to commander in 2289.

By then he was the most famous Marine in the Federation. He was an orphan of the frontier, the Hero of Elysium, the man who had walked out of Akuze. He was also the Butcher of Torfan, with a temper to match. Admirals who had known Kirk at the same age said openly that he was the next Kirk. Kirk, when he was asked, said only that he hoped Shepard would do better.

The Enterprise-A

In March 2293 Commander Shepard was posted to the USS Enterprise-A, which was soon to be decommissioned, with Lieutenant Kaidan Alenko and Corporal Richard Jenkins. They were her Marine detachment. Starfleet had decided that Marines, not the commanding officers of starships, ought to lead away missions, and the three of them were the trial of it. Her captain was James T. Kirk. For the first time Shepard's mentor was also his commanding officer.

The Imperial Entanglement

On 12 February 2293 the Klingon moon Praxis exploded. The Klingons suspected the Federation, the two powers moved towards war, and Starfleet sent the Enterprise-A to Starbase Side 7. Her task was to collect a new weapon, the RX-78-2 Gundam, a mobile suit built to answer the Klingon Zaku. The ship was chosen as a symbol. No ship had foiled the Klingons more often than the Enterprise, nor any captain more than Kirk.

The Enterprise-A reached Side 7 on 17 May, as the engineer Tem Ray was finishing the suit. That same hour a fleet of Star Destroyers appeared out of nothing around the starbase. It belonged to the Galactic Empire, a power from a distant galaxy, under the command of Darth Vader. The Gundam had been built with technology stolen from the Empire, so the Empire had come to make war on the thieves. A few people in Starfleet, holding to the idea called Section 31, had taken it in secret across a transporter bridge.

Kirk ordered Shepard to beam aboard Side 7, secure the Gundam and save every civilian he could. Shepard knew nothing of the Empire until its soldiers were in front of him. Corporal Jenkins charged ahead of the others and was killed by Imperial stormtroopers in the first minutes. Among the starbase's garrison Shepard found Gunnery Chief Ashley Williams, the last of her unit, who fought beside him from then on. When they pulled the helmet off a dead stormtrooper they found a human face under it. For all its strange machines, the Empire was human.

Outside, Tem Ray's fifteen-year-old son, Amuro Ray, had climbed into the Gundam. Starfleet had nothing to match the Empire's swarms of small fighters except its mobile suits, so the boy fought them alone. Then the Klingons arrived, with a force of Zakus led by Char of Aznable in his red machine. They had struck a secret alliance with the Empire after Praxis. In the middle of the battle it came out that the Empire itself had destroyed Praxis. The Klingons turned on their allies at once.

Darth Vader came aboard Side 7 himself. Shepard and Kirk fought him together, the old captain beside the Marine he had saved as a boy. Between them they beat him. The Empire withdrew the way it had come. Vader promised that it would return in greater numbers to take its revenge.

Captain of the Enterprise-B

The Enterprise-A was decommissioned on 30 June 2293. On Kirk's personal recommendation Shepard was promoted to captain. He was given the new USS Enterprise-B, an Excelsior-class starship then fitting out in spacedock. Kirk had passed the torch. The Klingons, who had fought beside the Federation at Side 7, signed the Khitomer Accords with it that August.

The Enterprise-B left spacedock on her maiden voyage on 14 October 2293, with Kirk aboard as a guest of honour. She was not ready. Half her systems had not been fitted, nor had half her crew arrived. Within the hour she answered a distress call from two transport ships that had been caught in the Nexus, a ribbon of energy crossing the sector. It was the kind of thing that a later age would call a warp storm. Shepard saved forty-seven of the refugees aboard. Kirk went below to alter the deflector, the ribbon tore open the hull where he stood, and he was gone.

Starfleet listed James T. Kirk as killed. Shepard had lost a second father, on his own bridge, in his first hour of command. A good many people in the Federation said that the next Kirk had lost the first one. He carried that disgrace into everything that followed.

The cloak

The Enterprise-B was not quite like the other ships of her class. The swellings along her hull housed a cloaking device, built from the Romulan one that Kirk had stolen in 2268. Very few people in the Federation knew of it. Shepard used it often, since he knew the Empire would come back. Before the war, during it and after it, the Enterprise-B went quietly into places where a Federation starship was not supposed to be.

The crew

Shepard gathered his crew over the years that followed, a good many of them from peoples he had been raised to distrust. Garrus Vakarian, a Turian, was his chief of security and weapons officer. Tali'Zorah nar Rayya, a young Quarian on her Pilgrimage, served in engineering as an adviser to the chief engineer, Greg Adams. Urdnot Wrex, a Krogan, came aboard as a paid mercenary. Liara T'Soni, an Asari archaeologist, was taken aboard while she was studying the ruins of the Eldar.

Kaidan Alenko came with him from the Enterprise-A. Jeff Moreau, called Joker, was at the helm, with Dr Karin Chakwas as the ship's doctor. Gunnery Chief Ashley Williams, whom he had met on Side 7, was put in charge of the ship's armoury. She kept her own xenophobic beliefs.

The years aboard the Enterprise-B changed him, though not entirely. The man who had hated everything that was not human learned to trust a Turian with his ship, then a Krogan with his life. He never forgave the Orion Syndicate.

The Intergalactic War

The Empire came back on 21 March 2299. This time it came to conquer. Its fleets appeared without warning over world after world, carried across the gulf between galaxies in an instant. Its weapons, shields and fighters were unlike anything in the Milky Way. In the first weeks nothing could stand against it. Shepard's Enterprise-B was driven from Vega, badly damaged, in the first great defeat of the war.

No one power could win it. Shepard saw that sooner than most, so he spent the year that followed making allies of enemies. The Enterprise-B fought beside the Gorn at Cestus III and beside the Tholians above Tholia. She stood beside the Romulans over Romulus itself. At Rannoch Shepard stopped the Empire from seizing control of the Geth, then stopped the Quarians' Migrant Fleet from destroying them. The two peoples made peace, which let the Quarians go home at last.

There were defeats as well. Shepard could not save Thessia, the homeworld of the Asari, which fell to Darth Vader in December 2299. But the alliance held. Federation, Klingon, Romulan, Gorn, Tholian, Geth and Quarian ships fought as one fleet at the Battle of Earth in March 2300. There the Empire was thrown back across the gulf for good.

It was the boy from Mindoir who had brought them together. The man who had once hated every people but his own had pleaded the cause of Klingons, Romulans, Gorn and Geth. After the war nobody in the Federation called him the next Kirk any longer. They simply called him Shepard.

Ashley Williams

After several adventures together aboard the Enterprise-B, Shepard and Ashley Williams fell in love. They married, and they had several children together.

Tomed

Shepard commanded the Enterprise-B for eighteen years. She was destroyed in the Tomed Incident of 2311, a clash with the Romulans that cost thousands of Federation lives. The Romulans had never forgiven the Federation for her cloak.

None of the dead were hers. Shepard kept the dying ship together long enough for every member of her crew to get away. He was the last man aboard. Starfleet picked up all of them, their captain included. In the Treaty of Algeron, which followed, the Federation gave up the use of cloaking devices altogether.

Shepard did not take another ship. He retired from Starfleet with Ashley Williams to raise their children.

Legacy

The peace Shepard made at Rannoch lasted. In 2350, fifty years after the war, the Quarians and the Geth of Rannoch joined the United Federation of Planets together. Many Quarians entered Starfleet, where their engineers had a hand in the great ships of the next age. The friendship between the Federation and the Klingons, begun at Side 7, sealed at Khitomer, outlived everyone who had fought there.

In the saga

Shepard has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Josh Baldwin
infobox: Big Bad Beetleborgs, 'Curse of the Shadowborg' (11 November 1996)
pages.html:
Josh Baldwin is a boy who came new to Charterville in November 1996. For a few days that month he was the White Blaster Beetleborg, the fourth of the Beetleborgs. His powers had been made for a single purpose, the destruction of Shadowborg. When Shadowborg was destroyed, they ended.

The new boy

Josh arrived in Charterville in the week that Vexor made Shadowborg. Heather, the girl whom Drew admired, liked the new boy at once. When she sprained her ankle during one of Shadowborg's attacks, it was Josh who took her to hospital. Drew did not warm to him.

The White Blaster Beetleborg

Shadowborg had taken the powers of all three Beetleborgs. Art Fortunes drew a fourth to fight him, the White Blaster, in the likeness of a Hercules beetle. The three asked Josh to wear the armour, which Flabber brought to life for him on 13 November 1996. Like the others, he had a gift out of armour. By dusting his hands together he could make himself invisible.

He fought Shadowborg, winning back the stolen powers. Then he gave the whole thing up. He doubted that he was fit for it, a doubt in which Flabber's clowning did not help. He came back when the others needed him. On 15 November he broke into Vexor's crypt with Drew to steal the energy Axis, the source of Shadowborg's strength.

The end of his powers

On 16 November 1996 Drew destroyed Shadowborg. The White Blaster's powers were bound to the enemy they had been made to fight, so they went out in the same moment. Josh was an ordinary boy again, after less than a week. Nothing more is recorded of him among the Beetleborgs.

pages.title: Kahless the Unforgettable
infobox: Killing the tyrant Molor; uniting the Klingons; founding the Klingon Empire
The first Emperor of the Klingons
The Sword of Kahless, the first bat'leth
pages.html:
Kahless the Unforgettable was the warrior who killed the tyrant Molor, united the Klingons and founded their Empire, in the ninth century. He made the first bat'leth with his own hands, and he gave his people the laws of honour by which they have lived ever since. Before he left them he promised that one day he would return.

The sword

Kahless lived in the ninth century, when the Klingons were ruled by a tyrant called Molor. He rose against him.

The story of how he armed himself was known only to the high clerics. Kahless went up to the volcano of Kri'stak, cut a lock of his own hair and thrust it into the molten rock. He cooled the burning lock in the Lake of Lusor, then twisted it into a blade: the first bat'leth. With it he killed Molor. He named it the Sword of Honour, though the Klingons have called it the Sword of Kahless ever since.

The Unforgettable

Kahless united the Klingon people under one Empire, with himself as its first Emperor, then gave them his code of honour. A great many stories are told of him. He fought his brother Morath for twelve days and twelve nights, because Morath had lied, which brought shame on their family.

Once, after he was Emperor, five hundred warriors stormed the great hall at Qam-Chee, and its garrison fled. Only Kahless stood his ground, with the Lady Lukara beside him. The two of them fought the attackers side by side. Lukara became his mate, and the Klingons have told their story ever since.

The promise

When Kahless left his people, he pointed to a star in the sky over Qo'noS. One day, he promised, he would return there. Klingons later settled Boreth, a world that circles that star, where clerics built a monastery to wait for him. The Klingons believe that Kahless himself waits in Sto-vo-kor for the honoured dead.

The sword he left behind was kept for centuries, until the Hur'q plundered Qo'noS in the fourteenth century and carried it off.

pages.title: Kaidan Alenko
infobox: The Imperial Entanglement; the Intergalactic War
pages.html:
Kaidan Alenko was an officer of the Starfleet Marines who served under John Shepard aboard the USS Enterprise-A, then aboard the Enterprise-B.

Service

In March 2293 Lieutenant Alenko was posted to the USS Enterprise-A with Commander John Shepard and Corporal Richard Jenkins, as her Marine detachment for away missions. He fought through Starbase Side 7 beside Shepard in the Imperial Entanglement. When Shepard was given the Enterprise-B, Alenko went with him.

In the saga

Kaidan Alenko has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Kaitlin Star
infobox: Reporter and photographer on the Underground Voice Daily
A laser pistol; sometimes a hatchet
Can become two Troopers at once, from October 1995
pages.html:
Kaitlin Star is a young reporter and photographer on the Underground Voice Daily, the newspaper of Crossworld City, California. In September 1994 she became one of the three VR Troopers, who fought Grimlord's armies on both sides of the reality barrier. In the summer of 1994 she is about eighteen. Her closest friends are two karate instructors, Ryan Steele and J.B. Reese. From October 1995 she could do something neither of them could, which was to become two Troopers at once.

The paper

Kaitlin was born about 1976. Nothing is recorded of her parents. She works for the Underground Voice Daily, where she writes her own stories as well as taking the photographs for them. Her editor is Woody Stocker, a cheerful man who wears a different hat every day. Her rival is Percy Rooney, the mayor's nephew, who is always trying to beat her to a story.

She trains at Tao's Dojo, where her friends Ryan Steele and J.B. Reese are instructors. She drives a small hatchback. She has never liked heights.

A Trooper

On 3 September 1994 Kaitlin went with her two friends to Professor Hart's laboratory in the hills outside the city. She came away with a Virtualizer of her own. A week later, out with her camera, she was the one who saw Grimlord's army moving into position for its first great assault.

Her armour was red. She carried a laser pistol, sometimes a hatchet as well. She usually fought beside J.B., the two of them firing together to stun one of Grimlord's creatures while Ryan fought elsewhere. Twice she gave up part of her own power to heal another Trooper who had been hurt. Professor Hart altered her car so that it could fly.

Grimlord's spies learnt in the first week that she was afraid of heights. He made what use of it he could.

Stories and traps

Her work kept leading her into Grimlord's traps. On 30 September 1994 she photographed a prisoner in an abandoned building in the woods, who proved to be Ryan's lost father. On 5 October a tip for a front-page story turned out to be bait. The Skugs strapped her to a bomb, from which the other two freed her in time.

At the end of that October a creature called the Dreammaster filled her sleep with nightmares. She had to master her own fear before she could save the others. In November someone sent her flowers. They were Grimlord's, with poison in them, so J.B. had to make the antidote.

The paper could be a weapon too. In November 1994 Grimlord tried to seize an animal sanctuary. The Troopers saved the animals. It was Kaitlin's story in the Underground Voice Daily that kept the land protected afterwards.

The Red Python

In February 1995 Kaitlin's friend Amy, who worked at an animal shelter, was seized by Skugs. Grimlord took over her mind, shutting her up inside the Red Python, an armoured warrior that Colonel Icebot had built in imitation of the Troopers. In their first fight, on 27 February, the Red Python hurt Kaitlin very badly. It was a machine of Dr Poindexter's, an inventor who had helped the Troopers before, that put her right.

The Red Python's armour then began to tear itself apart. Amy was brought out of it alive. She never knew that it was her friend she had nearly killed.

Two Kaitlins

On 3 October 1995 one of Grimlord's machines, a kind of mirror, split Kaitlin in two. The second Kaitlin was her opposite in everything, with Grimlord for a master. Professor Hart warned that if the two were not joined again within a day, both would vanish.

In the end the double was talked round. She turned on Grimlord, stole the mirror machine and brought it back to Earth. With it the Professor made the two into one. Something of the accident stayed with her, all the same. From then on Kaitlin could split herself into two Troopers whenever she chose, which Grimlord had not intended at all.

Later

Later that October she was offered a career in Hollywood, which would have meant leaving the Troopers. She stayed. In November 1995 a love potion of Grimlord's, hidden in a box of chocolates, set her on the way to marrying Percy Rooney. It was stopped in time.

In February 1996 Karl Ziktor announced that he would flatten a forest to build a research station. The Troopers pressed him into coming on a camping trip there, which Kaitlin covered for the paper. Her photographs of the great man in the woods did his reputation no good at all.

On 7 February both Kaitlins were caught, with J.B., aboard Grimlord's Air Castle, until Ryan got them out. On 21 February, in the raid on the Virtual Dark Fortress, it was Kaitlin who overloaded Oraclon's circuits with J.B. beside her. That is the last thing recorded of her.

pages.title: Kali
infobox: Kali, the Hindu goddess of destruction
pages.html:
Kali, called the Destroyer, is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in India as the goddess of death and destruction. She is best remembered among the Goa'uld for a single act of treachery, which she shared with Bastet. In 2002 she sat at the council of the System Lords that took Anubis back among them. What became of her afterwards is not known.

Kali the Destroyer

Kali came to India long after Ra's fall. Ra had forbidden the Goa'uld even to speak of Earth, so she did not speak of it; she simply went, quietly. She kept to the south of Asia, a very long way from the North. Every Goa'uld is born remembering what Thor does to those who go there.

Her name means the Black One. Her worshippers made images of her black-skinned, with her tongue out and a garland of severed heads about her neck.

Sobek

Kali and Bastet once made a treaty with Sobek, a Goa'uld who called himself the crocodile god of Egypt. They moved against him during the feast that celebrated it, once he had let his guard down. Rumour has it that his head still decorates Bastet's palace. What Kali took as her share is not recorded.

Lord Yu, who knew all this, still counted the pair of them among his likeliest allies in 2002. Among the System Lords a talent for treachery is not held against anyone for long.

The council at Hasara

By 2002 an unseen enemy had been attacking the worlds of the System Lords for months, and Kali had suffered with the rest. That year the System Lords met under truce in the Hasara system to decide what to do about it. Seven of them came, each with a single slave.

None of them knew that the Tok'ra had sent a man among them to poison them all. He was Daniel Jackson of SG-1, in the guise of one of Lord Yu's slaves. In the end he did not use the poison. The enemy turned out to be Anubis, whom the System Lords had cast out long before, and killing them all would only have left the galaxy to him.

When Osiris asked the council to take Anubis back, Kali nodded with the rest. Only Yu voted against. Afterwards the System Lords ate live symbiotes from a vat in a ritual of their own. Kali was the third to help herself, after Ba'al and Osiris.

Afterwards

In the wars that followed, first against Anubis and then against Ba'al, one System Lord after another was killed or forced to submit. Kali's name is not among those recorded. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that some of the surviving System Lords were scouting worlds they had abandoned long ago, as places to hide. Whether Kali was one of them is not known.

pages.title: Kamar-Taj
infobox: A hidden valley high in the Himalayas
As a school, in the fifteenth century, on the ruins of an older Kamar-Taj
pages.html:
Kamar-Taj is a school of wizards hidden in a valley high in the Himalayas. It takes no children, and it sends no letters. Its pupils are grown witches and wizards who have found their own way to its gate, since nobody else can pass it. For five centuries its master was the Ancient One, Sorcerer Supreme, who taught Stephen Strange there in the early 1960s.

The gate

Kamar-Taj is hidden as Hogwarts is hidden, only more thoroughly. A No-Maj climber who comes up its valley finds only rock and snow, then turns back without knowing why. Only a witch or wizard can walk through its gate. Even a witch or wizard has to find it first, which can take years.

When Stephen Strange came looking for the Ancient One in about 1962, he had not used a wand since 1949. The gate let him through at once, which told the Ancient One what Strange had not troubled to mention.

Kaluu and the old Kamar-Taj

The Ancient One was born in Kamar-Taj in the fifteenth century, when it was a hidden village of wizards. He and his friend Kaluu learnt the deeper arts together. Between them they made the valley a paradise where nobody grew ill or old.

Then Kaluu made its people his slaves, with himself as their king. The Ancient One overthrew him in a duel of magic, but the old Kamar-Taj was destroyed in the fighting, with its people. He banished Kaluu from the world. It cost him most of his own power, though he kept the slow ageing that the valley had given him.

The school

On the ruins he made the school. Kamar-Taj is not one of the eleven great wizarding schools of the world, and it does not try to be. It teaches what they do not: magic without wands, worked by the will alone, joined to the old occult learning of invocations, amulets and the spirit sent out of the body. A wizard who has learnt at Kamar-Taj can do things for which no Ministry of Magic has a name.

Its masters and pupils live there as an order. Its servants are wizards too, among them the family of Wong, who have served the Ancient One for generations. Wong was born there, and the Ancient One sent him to America to serve Strange.

The Sorcerer Supreme

The Sorcerer Supreme is the chief guardian of the Earth against attack by magic. Only a witch or wizard can hold the office, and at Kamar-Taj it has passed from master to chosen pupil. The Ancient One held it for most of five centuries.

His first chosen pupil turned to the dark arts, and he sent him away. Baron Mordo, a Transylvanian nobleman and one of his best pupils, plotted to murder him for his power. The newcomer Stephen Strange foiled him in about 1962. When the Ancient One died in 1973, Strange became Sorcerer Supreme.

Kamar-Taj and the wizarding world

Kamar-Taj is older than the Statute of Secrecy, and it keeps the secret better than most places that signed it. It answers to no Ministry. The wizarding governments know that it is there, and they leave it alone, as they leave the Sorcerer Supreme alone.

It should not be confused with the monastery in Tibet where Victor von Doom studied, whose monks forged his armour.

pages.title: Kaoru Mitsuki
infobox: Yuji Mitsuki, author of picture books
The White Spirit Beast and the Mysterious Forest (2012)
Carried off through a rift in time, about 2020
pages.html:
Kaoru Mitsuki is a painter, the daughter of the picture-book author Yuji Mitsuki. She became the wife of Kouga Saejima, the Golden Knight, and the mother of his heir, Raiga. In the summer of 1994 she is a girl of twelve who likes to draw. She does not know that a fallen knight marked her at the age of six as the gate through which Messiah, the mother of the Horrors, is to enter the world.

Childhood

Kaoru was born on 6 June, in about 1982. Her mother, Karin, died of an illness while she was small. Her father, Yuji, was so deep in his work that he did not visit his wife's sickbed, which Kaoru held against him for years.

As a boy Yuji had been saved from a Horror by the Golden Knight. He put the knight into a picture book, The Black Flame and the Golden Wind, whose last page he left blank. Kaoru grew up dreaming of a golden knight without knowing why. Both her parents were dead by the time she was grown.

When she was six a stranger took notice of her. He was Barago, the knight Kiba, who needed a girl of exactly that age, born on the sixth day of the sixth month, for Messiah to come through. He marked her without her knowing. He watched her from then on.

The hundred days

By 2005 Kaoru was twenty-three, an unknown painter living on odd jobs, behind with her rent. On 7 October she went to a gallery about her first exhibition. The owner turned into a monster in front of her. A young man in a white coat killed it, wearing golden armour out of her father's book. Some of its blood fell on her.

The young man, Kouga Saejima, neither killed her, as his law required, nor told her that she had a hundred days to live. He gave her a ring to wear. Horrors came at her wherever she worked, whether she was selling bread, carrying parcels or restoring a mural, with Kouga always close behind them. After her landlord turned her out she moved into his house, where the butler, Gonza Kurahashi, made much of her.

All this while she was seeing a counsellor, a kind, soft-spoken man named Karune Ryuzaki. She drew Kouga's hands until he complained. She cooked so badly that she made her best friend ill. In February 2006 she learnt that Kouga had been using her as bait from the first day. She took off his ring. Then she ran. He went into the Makai for the fruit that cured her all the same, so she forgave him.

The gate

Ryuzaki was Barago. In March 2006 he carried her off, told her the story of his life, and gave her to Messiah. Messiah came into the world through her body. Inside her own mind Kaoru met her dead parents, who told her to finish her painting. She painted Kouga with wings. The wings appeared on the golden armour, with which he struck Messiah down.

Afterwards she drew the blank last page of her father's book. She gave it to Kouga before she left for Italy to study painting. Nobody else ever saw what she drew there. It made him cry.

The picture book

She was back by the end of 2006. Over the next years she was often at the Saejima house. She painted a great wall. She began a picture book of her own. In 2011 the priest Leo Fudou took her to see a spirit beast of the Makai, then gave her a blessed brush.

In March 2012 Sigma Fudou sealed Kouga inside his engine, Idea. Kaoru went into it with the priestesses Jabi and Rekka. She called him back to himself with the last page of her father's book. Her brush finished the Horror Gyanon. At the end Sigma took her hostage in the Saejima house, where Kouga killed him.

Her book, The White Spirit Beast and the Mysterious Forest, was published in 2012, while Kouga was away in the Promised Ground. He came back to her early in 2013.

Wife and mother

Kaoru married Kouga. Their son, Raiga, was born about 2014. She told him stories of the Golden Knights of old. In about 2020, when the boy was six, a rift in time opened in front of the three of them. It dragged her in. It was the work of the Horror Eyrith. Kouga went after her.

She was lost for more than twenty years, as the world counts them. Kouga found her at last in the Promised Ground. In 2045, when Kiba came back for their son, her thought reached Mayuri, the young woman at Raiga's side. Between them the two women sent him the golden armour, made clean again by what his parents felt for him.

pages.title: Karin Chakwas
infobox: Chief medical officer of the USS Enterprise-B
pages.html:
Dr Karin Chakwas was the chief medical officer of the USS Enterprise-B under Captain John Shepard. She had been a Starfleet doctor since before most of the crew were born.

The doctor

Karin Chakwas joined Starfleet as a young doctor in search of adventure. She found that she liked the service too well to leave it. By the time she came to the Enterprise-B she had spent decades in the sickbays of starships, patching up soldiers. She could have had a hospital on any world in the Federation. She said that she would be bored there within a week.

She was older than her captain, of whom she was not in the least afraid. She treated his Marines, his helmsman's brittle bones and a crew drawn from half a dozen peoples. In the Intergalactic War her sickbay took the wounded of Vega, then of Thessia.

In the saga

Karin Chakwas has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Kase of Ventara
pages.html:
Kase is a Kamen Rider of Ventara, the Rider called Siren, whose white armour is contracted to the swan Blancwing. She is a healer as well as a fighter. In the summer of 1994 she is on Ventara with the other Riders, keeping the long watch. When Xaviax took Ventara, about 2007, he believed that he had destroyed her. She reached Earth in September 2009, fought beside Len of Ventara for two months, was vented, then came back from the Advent Void to see Xaviax destroyed.

A Rider of Ventara

Kase was one of the twelve Ventarans whom Eubulon armed against Xaviax. Of the twelve she was closest to Len, the Wing Knight. Like the rest she gave up an ordinary life to sleep in suspended animation, waking only for her turns on watch.

About 2007 the Dragon Knight, Adam of Ventara, led Xaviax to the sleeping Riders. Nearly all of them were vented. Xaviax believed that he had destroyed Kase. Len, who had escaped to Earth, thought the same.

The return

At the beginning of September 2009 a Rider in white appeared, who cut down a band of Xaviax's foot soldiers. On 5 September she drove off Danny Cho, who had Kit Taylor at his mercy. Then she turned on Kit. He was wearing the traitor's armour, so she took him for one of Xaviax's Riders. Len arrived in time to stop her.

She did not warm to Kit quickly. She fought him to see whether he had the makings of a real Rider. She won. It was October before she said that she was sorry. By then she knew that he had refused to buy his father's life with Len's.

That month she fought Strike, broke into the headquarters of the No-Men with Len to fetch Kit out, then healed the wound that Xaviax had given him.

Swan song

Kase kept the Survive cards, which lift a Rider into a stronger armour. On 31 October she gave one to Len, with another for Kit. The same day she broke away from Xaviax, who was fighting in the armour of Wrath, to go to their help. In the fight that followed Strike vented her.

Len picked up her deck. A week later he vented Strike.

Out of the Void

While Kase lay in the Advent Void, Eubulon altered her deck so that Maya Young of Earth could wear the armour of Siren. On 21 November he brought Kase out, with Kit Taylor. She found Len again a week later. On 5 December Maya gave the deck back. Kase was not sure at first that she deserved it.

On 18 December she went to Australia with Kit, where the traitor begged the two of them to vent him. They would not. The same day she fought in Xaviax's stronghold, one of the thirteen Riders whose Link Vent destroyed him.

She is still Siren. With Len and Kit she guards both worlds.

pages.title: Kazuhira Miller
infobox: Master Miller; McDonell Miller; Kaz Miller
Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake (MSX2, 20 July 1990), as Master Miller
An American officer; a Japanese mother
Left leg and right arm lost by 1984
pages.html:
Kazuhira Miller is FOXHOUND's survival instructor, known to its soldiers as Master Miller. He is the son of an American officer by a Japanese mother. Twenty years before the summer of 1994 he was Big Boss's partner, the man who turned a band of mercenaries into a business.
