He broke with Big Boss in 1984, swearing to help Big Boss's son bring his father down. That son is Solid Snake, whom he trains.

Militaires Sans Frontières

Miller met Big Boss in Colombia in 1972, when both were soldiers for hire. Together they founded Militaires Sans Frontières, an army that belonged to no country. Big Boss commanded it. Miller ran it: the contracts, the recruiting, the money.

In November 1974 he was at Big Boss's side through the Peace Walker affair in Costa Rica. By then the army lived on Mother Base, an old platform in the Caribbean. Miller believed that he could do business with Cipher, the organisation of Major Zero, without being swallowed by it.

He was wrong. On 16 March 1975 Cipher's unit XOF destroyed Mother Base under cover of a United Nations inspection. Miller was one of only three men known to have lived.

Diamond Dogs

In the years that followed he built a new army, Diamond Dogs, on a platform off the Seychelles. In 1984 Soviet troops took him prisoner in Afghanistan. By the time Venom Snake got him out he had lost his left leg and his right arm. He believed that the man who rescued him was Big Boss.

All that year he hunted Skull Face, the commander of XOF, from Afghanistan to Central Africa. When Skull Face lay crushed under the wreck of his own machine, Miller helped to shoot him, then left him to die.

Afterwards he learnt the truth. The man he had followed all year was a medic with Big Boss's face. The real Big Boss had used them both as cover. Miller never forgave it. He swore to help Big Boss's son bring his father down.

Master Miller

He became an instructor. He taught survival to the Special Air Service, the Green Berets and the Marines, then to FOXHOUND, where the soldiers called him Master Miller out of respect. He was hard on them. The young man who became Solid Snake was his pupil.

On Christmas Eve 1999 he was one of the voices advising Snake by radio at Zanzibar Land, where Snake did what Miller had trained him for. Afterwards he retired to Alaska with his daughter, Catherine Miller. There he sometimes taught the Alaska Scouts.

In 2005, just before the Shadow Moses incident, Liquid Snake murdered him in his own house. All through the incident a voice calling itself Master Miller advised Snake by radio. It was Liquid.

pages.title: Kimberly Hart
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Day of the Dumpster' (28 August 1993)
The Pterodactyl Dinozord; the Firebird Thunderzord; the Crane Ninjazord
The Ranger Slayer, of Lord Drakkon's world
In the summer of 1994, the Pink Ranger
pages.html:
Kimberly Hart is the Pink Ranger of the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, a gymnast from Angel Grove whom Zordon chose in 1993. Her coin is the Pterodactyl. She was one of the five who fought the giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham on 30 July 1993. In November 1995 she gave up her powers to Katherine Hillard and went to Florida to train for the Pan Global Games. She and Tommy Oliver were sweethearts until she wrote to him in 1996 to end it.

Angel Grove

Kimberly was born about 1977. She grew up in Angel Grove, a pupil at Angel Grove High School and a gymnast of real promise. In 1993 Zordon chose her as one of his five Rangers. She is the Pink Ranger, and her coin is the Pterodactyl, which calls up the Pterodactyl Dinozord.

Her parents' marriage was coming apart in 1993. That July, a few days before Rita Repulsa was set free, Matt Cook took her to the carnival on their first date. He was the captain of the school's football team. She told him about the divorce, then went down with food poisoning from the fried food. They agreed to try again. On the day of Rita's first attack on Angel Grove everybody else ran, but Matt went looking for Kimberly.

She had not always been kind. She once had a busboy sacked over a salad. He turned out to be Zack Taylor, who with Trini Kwan called her 'Salad Girl' for a while after Matt brought her into their circle as his girlfriend.

The Pink Ranger

She was one of the five who came to public notice on 30 July 1993, fighting a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham.

Zordon had forbidden his Rangers to tell anybody what they were, so she could never explain to Matt why she kept vanishing. In August 1993 he would not let her out of his sight. When Rita's monster Flog attacked, Matt put himself between her and it. It threw him into a building. Kimberly had to fight, so she handed him to a passer-by who promised to get him to hospital. The passer-by was the Putty Infiltrator, Rita's spy, which wore Matt's face for the next few weeks while Rita held the real Matt on the Moon.

Kimberly and Jason Lee Scott both felt that something was wrong with him. At the Homecoming dance in September the copy was on the point of telling her the truth when the real Matt stumbled on to the stage, escaped from the Moon. Rita made her creature over into a false Megazord. Kimberly's Pterodactyl finished it. The next day she went with Zack to see Matt, who could barely speak.

Late that month Goldar wrecked the juice bar of the Youth Center. Matt helped her get people out. For a moment he seemed to accept her as she was, secrets and all.

Early in October 1993 a stranger came to Angel Grove with a Zord of her own, the Gravezord. She was the Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of Lord Drakkon's world, who had come from a later day by mistake. Drakkon held her with a spell, bound into her Bow of Darkness. Kimberly electrified the spires of the Command Center, which destroyed the bow and broke the spell. Afterwards the older woman, calling herself Sally, spent an afternoon at the juice bar with her younger self.

Matt had gone alone to the place where the Gravezord came down, to talk with the woman who climbed out of it. After that he knew who his friends were. At the juice bar he told the five of them that he knew they were the Power Rangers. He would keep the secret, he said, but he would not speak to them again unless one of them told him the truth. Zordon's rule held, so nobody answered. Kimberly had already decided that Matt would be safer away from her. When he walked out, she let him go.

For three weeks he spoke to none of them. Kimberly tried to bring back that first evening at the carnival by going out with Skull. Skull saw that she was not over Matt, so he turned her down. Some weeks later she and Matt apologised to each other. He became the friend she could tell things to.

When Tommy Oliver came to Angel Grove High School in October 1993, Kimberly liked him at once. Rita Repulsa made him her Green Ranger, and for a while he was their enemy. In the months after he broke free and joined the team, the two of them became sweethearts.

At the end of that October the Black Dragon stripped the Rangers of their powers. Tommy shared his own Green power out among the others, so that for a time Kimberly fought as a Green Ranger.

In the spring of 1994 Kimberly went to Japan with the team after Tommy, whom Rita had carried off there. Their Megazord fought Godzilla, the great beast of that country, then fought beside him.

Shattered Grid

Early in September 1994 Tommy took her out on their first proper date. At the end of the evening she walked away from an awkward goodnight, thought better of it, then turned back. She found Lord Drakkon, Tommy's other self, standing over him in an alley with a blade through his back. Tommy died in her arms.

The Rangers could not bring him back. At the funeral Jason took up the Dragon Shield with the Dragon Dagger. When the Rangers of every later year stormed Drakkon's tower on the Moon of his own world, Jason gave them to Kimberly. She wore the Dragon armour that day, leading the attack in the Dragonzord.

Drakkon unmade the world, but Tommy's spirit undid him. When the world was mended, Tommy was alive. Their date ended in a kiss after all. Kimberly remembered none of it.

Lord Zedd

In the autumn of 1994, when Lord Zedd came to the Moon, she took the Firebird Thunderzord. Early in October she was among the Rangers who fought beside the Justice League when Brainiac shrank Angel Grove into a bottle. Her Pterodactyl carried off Batman's car with Batman inside it. It was her arrow, with a boxing glove for a head, that finished Lord Zedd off.

In October 1994 Goldar carried her off, and Zedd meant to make her his queen. She did not stay. When Tommy came back as the White Ranger that month, Kimberly threw her arms round him at the juice bar. Matt Cook, watching from a corner, told her afterwards that she could always talk to him.

In November 1994 Jason, Zack and Trini Kwan left for a peace conference in Geneva, or so they said. Calls to them reached only one at a time, through static. Kimberly felt that they were avoiding her. She left Trini a message to say that she felt abandoned.

Early in December the three were brought to the Command Center with Jason badly hurt, their faces bare. They had been in space all along, as the Omega Rangers. Kimberly said the sharpest things of anybody. Later that month Lord Drakkon fell to Earth, to be locked in a cell under the Command Center. He goaded her to kill him. She told him that he was not hers to kill.

The second Green Ranger

In December 1994 a new Green Ranger came out of nowhere to fight beside the team. Over Christmas, under Lord Zedd's dome, he took off his helmet in front of the whole city. He was Matt Cook. Tommy accused Kimberly of having known all along. She had not.

She and Matt argued over whether Zordon would protect humanity at any cost. In the Eltarian War of January 1995 she went aboard Zartus's ship beside Zordon himself, in his body of metal, to free the Guardian Zelya.

Late that January Trini told her about the war of September, and that Drakkon had killed Tommy. Then an Emissary of the Morphin Masters gave her back the memory itself.

In February 1995 Rita, as Mistress Vile, bound Matt with a new Sword of Darkness. Under her spell he killed Grace Sterling. When the Rangers cleansed the Grid, the world was mended a second time. Kimberly was one of the few who remembered.

The Old West and the Crane

In May 1995 she fell through a hole in time into the Angel Grove of the Old West. There she met people very like her friends, and she faced Goldar alone until help came.

In September 1995 Rito Revolto destroyed the Thunderzords. Ninjor gave the Rangers new powers, and Kimberly became the Pink Ninja Ranger, with the Crane Ninjazord.

That month her mother became engaged to a painter and moved to France. Kimberly stayed in Angel Grove, living with Aisha Campbell's family. A gymnastics coach was training her for the Pan Global Games. Once she was hurt in a fall from the beam.

Florida

In November 1995 she left Angel Grove to train for the Pan Global Games in Florida. She gave up her powers so that Katherine Hillard could take her place as the Pink Ranger. Matt Cook was living in Florida when she went there to train.

Days later her mother and stepfather vanished from St Moineau, the town in France where they had made their home. Goldar was there with a new ally, Verto, turning the people of the town into fish-folk to serve them. Zordon sent Kimberly the Sword of Light, so she was the Pink Ranger again. Zack and Trini came to her from the Omega Rangers. With Serge, a boy of the town, and his sister, Britt, they made five. They beat Goldar and Verto, which brought her family home.

Tommy and the others were away from Earth just then, in trouble on the far world of Orulind. Once the town was safe, Kimberly took her new team to help them. Seeing Tommy again unsettled her. She was torn between her duty and the life she had gone to Florida to find. It was the beginning of the letter she would write him in May 1996.

For a while she and Tommy kept it up across the distance. In May 1996 she wrote to tell him that she had met someone else.

Later years

In 1997 Divatox took her prisoner, meaning to give her to Maligore, and for a time Maligore's power took hold of her. The wizard Lerigot cured her.

In 2022 she fought Robo-Rita, the evil that Zordon's light had driven out of Rita Repulsa, in the battle in which Trini Kwan was killed. In 2023 Robo-Rita's creatures took her prisoner, with Jason and Tommy. They were shut in a machine in the palace on the Moon, to power Robo-Rita's plan to change the past. The other Rangers freed them, and they were taken to Aquitar to heal.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' news showed helicopter film of the previous afternoon in Birmingham. Five Rangers, in red, blue, black, yellow and pink, ran in a line across a rooftop towards an enormous pink thing with far too many arms. The one in pink was Kimberly. Dudley watched them leap off the roof 'as though he'd like to be one of them'.

pages.title: King Ghidorah
infobox: A three-headed golden dragon from space
Lightning, breathed from all three mouths
The Xiliens, 1965 and 1994; the hunters of Nebula M, 1972; the Kilaaks, 1999
pages.html:
King Ghidorah is a golden dragon with three heads, two tails and a pair of vast wings, which travels between the worlds destroying them. It breathes lightning. Every alien people that has tried to take the Earth with monsters has reached for it sooner or later. Godzilla has beaten it five times, the last time for good.

The destroyer of Venus

In January 1965 Princess Salno of the little kingdom of Selgina vanished from an aeroplane moments before a bomb destroyed it. She turned up in Japan with no memory of herself, prophesying disasters. A voice was speaking through her. It said that it came from Venus, where a great people had been wiped out in a single day, thousands of years before, by a monster called King Ghidorah. It said that the monster had now come to Earth.

It was right. A meteorite had fallen in the Kurobe valley. It split open, a ball of fire rose out of it, then the fire became King Ghidorah. The Mothra larva went against it by herself at the foot of Mount Fuji, until Godzilla joined her, with Rodan. The larva covered its heads in silk. Godzilla threw it off a cliff. It fled into space.

Japan asked for help that month for the first time. The Justice League came, with the Avengers, to hold the dragon off the towns. Superman fought it beside Wonder Woman, Iron Man and Thor, whose own lightning was the first thing that had made it give ground. They could not bring it down. When Godzilla turned on it at last, with Rodan, the heroes stood aside.

A weapon for hire

In December 1965 the Xiliens of Planet X told the Earth that a monster was laying waste their world. They called it Monster Zero. It was King Ghidorah. They asked to borrow Godzilla, with Rodan, to drive it off.

In truth they had controlled it from the start. They sent all three monsters to conquer the Earth, lost control of them, then saw King Ghidorah beaten by the other two.

On 19 December 1965, while the Xiliens still held all three, the Justice League came back to Japan with the Avengers to keep them out of Tokyo. Superman fought King Ghidorah again, this time without Thor. Green Lantern did not try a second time. His ring had no power over anything yellow, which King Ghidorah, being gold from its three heads to its two tails, entirely was.

In 1972 the hunters of Nebula M called it down on Tokyo with Gigan. Superman met the pair above the Earth, with Green Lantern, but could not turn them. Godzilla drove both off, with Anguirus beside him.

Japan, 1994

In the spring of 1994 Rita Repulsa was fighting beside the Xiliens in Japan. Their Supreme Controller would not call King Ghidorah, because nobody could be sure of controlling it. Rita had it called regardless.

It beat Godzilla, dropped the Power Rangers' Megazord in the sea, then attacked the Xiliens' own ship. Rita sent Goldar against it, with Scorpina. It took Godzilla, fighting beside the Rangers' Mega Dragonzord, to bring it down. It was left senseless on the shore.

Mount Fuji, 1999

In 1999 the Kilaaks called it to defend their stronghold at Mount Fuji. Ten of the Earth's monsters were waiting. Gorosaurus kicked it flat. Anguirus sank his teeth into one of its necks, while Godzilla trampled the others. It did not get up. When the Kilaak stronghold blew up, the ground opened under its body.

pages.title: King Kong
infobox: The juice of the island's red berries, which sends him to sleep
pages.html:
King Kong is the giant ape of Faro Island, in the Solomons, whose people worship him as a god. In 1962 a Japanese drug company carried him off to be an advertisement. He fought Godzilla from Mount Fuji to the sea, then swam home, since when he has been left alone.

Faro Island

The people of Faro Island live under the mountain where Kong sleeps. A red berry grows there, whose juice sends him into a doze. When he is angry the islanders drum, chant, then leave the juice out for him in great jars.

In 1962 a giant octopus crawled ashore after the juice. Kong came down from the mountain to drive it off, drank the jars dry, then fell asleep in front of the village.

Japan, 1962

The men who watched this were Osamu Sakurai and Kinsaburo Furue. They had been sent from Tokyo by Mr Tako, who ran the advertising of Pacific Pharmaceuticals. Tako's company sponsored a dull science broadcast, which he wanted a monster of his own to liven up. His men tied the sleeping Kong to a raft, then towed it towards Japan.

Kong woke at sea, broke the raft, then swam ashore by himself. Godzilla had just come back out of the Arctic ice. The two met in the hills north of Tokyo, where one blast of Godzilla's breath sent Kong away with his fur singed.

The army strung wires carrying a million volts round the city. They turned Godzilla aside. Kong, it turned out, grew stronger on electricity. He walked through them into Tokyo, picked up Sakurai's sister, Fumiko, then climbed the Diet building with her in his hand.

He was brought down with berry juice, fired at him as a gas, while loudspeakers played the islanders' chant. The Self-Defence Forces hung him under a cluster of balloons, on lines of a new thread as strong as steel, to fly him to Mount Fuji. They dropped him on Godzilla.

Kong was losing the fight until a thunderstorm broke over them. The lightning revived him. The two monsters wrestled down to the coast at Atami, through its castle, into the sea. Only Kong surfaced. He set out for Faro Island, where nobody tried to stop him.

pages.title: Kit Taylor
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
A city in the United States
Dragon Knight, 2009 and again from December 2009; Onyx, November to December 2009
Dragreder, a red dragon; Dragblacker, a black dragon, as Onyx
Maya Young; Chris Ramirez; Kase of Ventara
pages.html:
Kit Taylor is an American boy, born on 13 December 1990, who grew up to be Kamen Rider Dragon Knight. In the summer of 1994 he is three years old. His father, Frank, vanished about a year before Kit's eighteenth birthday. On that birthday, in December 2008, Kit found an Advent Deck in the family's empty flat, which drew him into the war for Ventara. He fought beside Len of Ventara through 2009. He was vented that November, came back as Kamen Rider Onyx, then took up the Dragon Knight's deck for good once Xaviax was dead.

Early life

Kit was brought up by his father, Frank Taylor, in a flat in an American city. About December 2007 Frank disappeared without a word. Kit was about seventeen. With nobody to look after him he was put into foster care, where he got a name for trouble that he always said he had not earned.

The deck and the dragon

On 13 December 2008 Kit turned eighteen, which meant that he had to leave care. He had begun to see his father in reflections. The visions led him home to the empty flat, where he found a small case of cards. It was an Advent Deck.

The visions were not his father's doing. Xaviax had sent them. Kit was the mirror twin of Adam of Ventara, the first Dragon Knight, so the Dragon Knight's deck would open for him.

The same day he saw monsters come out of a mirror to seize a young woman, Maya Young. He tried to protect her, which did no good at all. An armoured man drove them off: Len, the Wing Knight, who then demanded that Kit hand over the deck. Kit ran. A monster knocked him clean through a mirror into Ventara, where the deck put a plain, weak armour on him. Then a red dragon came down on him and Len alike.

On 10 January 2009 Len went through a mirror after a monster that had taken a man. Kit could not make his armour come until another vision of his father told him to use the Contract Card. The dragon returned. This time Kit held up the card, the contract was made, and Dragreder was his. As Kamen Rider Dragon Knight he saved Len, then destroyed the monster with his first Final Vent.

Learning the war

Len did not want him. He agreed to train him all the same, since Kit would not give the deck up. Kit soon learnt what the training was for. Xaviax had armed other young men of Earth with stolen decks. The first to come after Kit was Richie Preston, who wore the armour of Incisor. On 24 January Len fought Richie Preston in single combat, then vented him.

Kit was horrified. He told Len that he was finished with being a Rider. Len answered that he could not be finished, because the contract had bound him to Dragreder. A week later Len told him how Ventara had fallen. Kit made up his mind to stay.

Maya Young had offered to help him look for his father. In February she and her friend Trent Moseley found Frank Taylor lying in a hospital. He was alive, but nothing would wake him. Xaviax had drained the life out of him.

Drew Lansing's lie

The next Rider did not attack him. Drew Lansing, who wore Torque's armour, told Kit that Len was the true traitor of Ventara, the thief of the decks. He added that there was a cure for Frank Taylor. Len said flatly that there was none. Kit chose to believe the man who offered hope, so for some weeks he fought at Drew Lansing's side against his own teacher.

On 28 February Maya rang to warn him that Drew Lansing served Xaviax. That day Kit watched him vent another of Xaviax's Riders, Grant Staley, whom Kit had been trying to talk round. Then he turned on Kit. Len saved him.

Afterwards Len showed him an old photograph of himself beside a young man with Kit's face. That was the Dragon Knight who had betrayed Ventara. Kit was his mirror twin, which was the only reason the deck had ever worked for him.

Friends and losses

Two of Xaviax's Riders listened when Kit told them the truth. Brad Barrett, who wore Thrust's armour, was vented by Strike on 4 April before he could change sides. Chris Ramirez, a discharged Marine who wore Sting's, did change sides. For a few months there were three of them.

In August Len asked Kit to become the true Dragon Knight of Ventara. It would mean leaving his own life behind to sleep through the years with the other Riders, waking only when his turn came. Kit asked for time to think.

That same month Strike carried Frank Taylor off from the hospital. On 22 August Strike aimed a Final Vent at Len, Chris Ramirez threw himself in the way, and he was vented. Kit found a letter in his friend's bag afterwards, written to Chris's father but never sent. He read it.

On 4 September Strike offered Kit a bargain: Frank Taylor in return for Len's Advent Deck. Kit refused. In the fight that followed Maya got his father safely away. Kit held off Strike and Danny Cho together, then vented Albert Cho, who wore Spear's armour. He was the only Rider Kit vented in the whole war.

Temptation

Kase of Ventara, a Rider whom everyone had believed lost, joined them in September. She did not think much of Kit at first. She tested him in a fight, which he lost. He began to dream of a black Rider in armour like his own, Onyx, who always beat him. In one dream he vented Len.

On 19 September Xaviax came to him at the hospital. He woke Frank Taylor for a few moments. He would wake him for good, he said, on the day Kit vented the Wing Knight. It was a week before Kit told Len and Kase. When he did, he said that he was ready to be a real Rider.

The No-Men

On 3 October two men seized Kit as he left his father's bedside. They belonged to the No-Men, a secret office of the American government. Its agent Michelle Walsh had learnt what he was from files copied off Maya Young's computer. They locked him in a cell. Once they let him out to fight a mirror monster, so that they could study his armour.

On 17 October he spilt a glass of water across the floor of the cell. A puddle is a reflection, which is all a Rider needs. He was gone before the guards reached him.

Xaviax was waiting for him with Strike. They wounded him in the leg before Len and Kase could reach him. Kase, who has a healer's gift, mended it.

Vented

At the end of October Kase gave Kit a Survive card. The same day Strike vented her. On 7 November Len vented Strike in his turn. Then the two of them faced Xaviax, who was wearing the armour of Wrath on a stolen body.

Kit's Survive Mode ran out too soon. He tried his Final Vent, which missed. Wrath's did not. Kit was vented, Wrath was vented in the same fight, and Xaviax walked away with the Dragon Knight's deck.

Onyx

Kit lay in the Advent Void for two weeks. On 21 November Eubulon, the Advent Master, brought him out with Kase. By then Xaviax had forced the Dragon Knight's deck back on Adam of Ventara. So Eubulon gave Kit a deck of his own making, contracted to a black dragon, Dragblacker. It made him the black Rider of his nightmares.

He first fought as Kamen Rider Onyx on 28 November. The same day he met his twin. They quarrelled, then fought, and Kit would have vented him if Eubulon had not stepped between them. In December he told his twin how Xaviax had used Frank Taylor against him.

The end of the war

On 18 December 2009 Kit went into Xaviax's stronghold as Onyx, with his twin beside him as Dragon Knight. The two of them opened the last fight together. Thirteen Riders joined in the Link Vent that destroyed Xaviax.

Frank Taylor woke. Adam of Ventara gave up being a Rider. Eubulon then offered Kit either of the two dragon decks, to keep. Kit chose Dragon Knight.

The other men of Earth who had worn armour were sent home with no memory of it, so Kit was the only Rider of Earth left. He stayed one, guarding both worlds with Len and Kase. Maya Young put the whole story into a book.

pages.title: Kitty Pryde
infobox: Katherine Pryde; Katherine Anne Pryde; Shadowcat
Phasing: she can pass through solid things, and take others with her
The X-Men (1980 to 1987); the Excalibur team (1987 to 1998); the X-Men again (from 1998)
pages.html:
Kitty Pryde is an American mutant who can walk through walls, the youngest of the X-Men when she joined them and a founder of the Excalibur team. She was thirteen and a half when she came to Charles Xavier's school at the start of 1980, a clever, quick-tempered girl from Illinois with a gift for computers. In 1987, believing the X-Men dead, she helped to found the Excalibur team in Britain with Kurt Wagner and Rachel Summers. In the summer of 1994 she is twenty-eight, living on Muir Island with the team and with Lockheed the dragon, who has followed her about since 1982.

Deerfield

Katherine Anne Pryde was born in 1966 in Deerfield, Illinois, the daughter of Carmen and Theresa Pryde. The family is Jewish. Her grandfather, Samuel Prydeman, survived a Nazi camp in the war. At thirteen Kitty began to have headaches, which turned out to be her mutant power arriving.

Early in 1980 two people came to Deerfield to recruit her. One was Charles Xavier, with three of his X-Men. The other was Emma Frost, the White Queen of the Hellfire Club, who looked at Kitty, she said afterwards, as if she were something good to eat. The Hellfire Club's men attacked Xavier's party. Kitty, left behind, called in the rest of the X-Men to get their friends back.

Her parents were furious when she came home a day late. The Phoenix, which then wore Jean Grey's form, quietly changed their minds about Xavier, so Kitty went to his school at thirteen and a half.

The X-Men, 1980 to 1987

She went by the name Sprite at first, then Ariel. At the end of 1980 her own older self, Kate Pryde, came back from a future that will now never happen and took over her body for a while, to save Senator Robert Kelly from Mystique's Brotherhood. On Christmas Eve that year, alone in Xavier's house, she destroyed a demon single-handed.

In 1982 the alien Brood carried the X-Men off into space. On one of their worlds Kitty met a small purple creature of another race, very like a dragon, which saved her life and came secretly home with her. She named him Lockheed, after a dragon in a story she had once told Illyana Rasputin. In 1983 the Morlocks, mutants who live in the tunnels under New York, very nearly married her off to one of their own, Caliban.

Kitty was in love with Piotr Rasputin, who was ten years older. He was fond of her, and took care that it never became anything more while she was so young. In 1984 he came home from the Secret Wars grieving for Zsaji, an alien healer he had loved on Battleworld, and told her that his heart had gone elsewhere. Her closest friend was a boy from Salem Center, Doug Ramsey, a mutant himself, who joined the New Mutants. He loved her more than she loved him. He was killed at the end of 1987.

In the winter of 1984 to 1985 she went to Japan, where her father had got himself mixed up with the Yakuza. There Ogun, a ninja master who had once taught Wolverine, took hold of her mind. He poured a lifetime of fighting skill into her, meaning to make her his assassin. With Wolverine's help she threw him off. She came home harder and quieter, under a new name, Shadowcat.

In the autumn of 1986 the Marauders massacred the Morlocks. Kitty, trying to save one of the X-Men, was struck by the spear of one of the killers, Harpoon, and afterwards she could not stay solid. Early in 1987 the X-Men took her to Reed Richards, then to Victor von Doom, for a cure. In the end she could hold herself together by force of will, though it gave her headaches. She was sent to Muir Island to recover. There, that autumn, she watched the X-Men die on television.

The Excalibur team, 1987 to 1990

Kitty was twenty-one when she helped to found the Excalibur team in December 1987. She was its expert on computers and machines from the first. In 1988 she built a device that made Cerebro read her as Rachel, to draw the Warwolves out, and it very nearly got her skinned. One of them took her into itself, and she had to pull herself free.

At Arcade's Murderworld in Manchester she beat him with a program she and Doug Ramsey had written together. In Manhattan, over the winter of 1988 to 1989, she called up Illyana's Soulsword, with its armour, to free Brian Braddock and Meggan from the demons' spell. In 1989 she fell for Professor Alistaire Stuart of the Weird Happenings Organisation, who was in love with Rachel.

On the journey across the worlds a prince of a Britain of knights fell in love with her and asked her to marry him. He found a better match in that world's own Kitty, a princess. On another world Kitty killed a tyrant, Princess Anjulie, who had been feeding the magic of her land to a monster.

In the autumn of 1989 Kitty fell home alone, and she spent the winter in London with Courtney Ross, as she thought. It was Sat-yr-9 in Courtney's shape. The false Courtney gave her a birthday to remember, with supper in Paris and a Jaguar. Kitty never guessed.

St Searle's, 1990 to 1991

In the autumn of 1990 Kitty took a post teaching computing at St Searle's School for Young Ladies, a girls' boarding school that was short of money, while she looked about her for a place at a British university. The senior girls, led by Phoebe Huntsman, set out to make the new young mistress's life a misery. On the school's grounds her power kept failing her. She won the girls round on the hockey field, by beating Phoebe in the match against the staff.

Then she overheard the governors say that the school would close at the end of the month. She and Phoebe entered the senior girls in a cheerleading contest at Wembley Stadium for the prize money. The twin children of Baron Strucker, who call themselves Fenris, attacked the contest. The girls of St Searle's saw them off with hockey sticks, though they lost the contest to an American squad all the same. The school was saved when the woman everyone took for Courtney Ross, one of its old girls, found it a tenant for its playing fields. Kitty went back to the team.

Muir Island, 1991 to 1994

In 1991 Victor von Doom talked Kitty into drawing Illyana's Soulsword from its stone outside the lighthouse. With it he very nearly destroyed Limbo, and Lockheed nearly died in the fight. In 1993 she met Kate Pryde again, her older self, whose mind had been living since 1988 in Widget the robot.

In September 1993 Piotr Rasputin went over to Magneto. Kitty tricked him into coming to Muir Island, hoping that Moira MacTaggert's people could help him, and they did mend the head wound that troubled him. He went back to the Acolytes all the same. He said goodbye to her first.

In the summer of 1994 Kitty lives on Muir Island with the team, looking after its computers and machines. Lockheed is never far away. Douglock, who has come to live with them, carries the memories of her friend Doug Ramsey.

Powers

Kitty can phase, letting herself and anything she holds pass through solid matter, which is why the X-Men's enemies so seldom manage to tie her up. While phased she can walk on air as if it were a staircase. Machines she passes through tend to stop working. She is also a gifted engineer, a hacker of the first rank and, since Ogun, a formidable fighter.

Later years

In 1995 Kitty fell in love with Pete Wisdom, a former agent of Black Air. Piotr came to Muir Island that year and fought him over her. She told Piotr that if he had cared, he would never have left her. In 1997 she went up to the Helicarrier of S.H.I.E.L.D. to mend its computers, and found Ogun hiding in them. With Wolverine she drove him out.

She and Pete parted early in 1998. That August she caught Meggan's bouquet at the wedding. Afterwards she went back to the X-Men with Kurt Wagner and Piotr.

She left the X-Men again after Piotr's death in 2001, to study at the University of Chicago. Her father died that year in the destruction of Genosha, where he had been living. She came back in 2004, and found that Piotr was alive after all. In 2008 the people of a world called Breakworld fired a giant bullet at the Earth. Kitty phased it clean through the planet, then was carried off into space inside it. Magneto brought her home in 2010. In 2011 she became headmistress of the Jean Grey School for Higher Learning, which Wolverine opened in Xavier's old house.

The Third World War

Kitty was sixty when the Third World War broke out in 2026. In the 2030s, when the Sentinels were herding mutants into camps, she went in after them, walking the prisoners out through the walls a handful at a time. Piotr Rasputin held the gate behind her. Neither of them came out of the last camp. Of all the X-Men only Wolverine outlived the war.

pages.title: Kiya Kyatyl
infobox: Her brother, Sello, killed with the rest of her family in 1994
Water; she could also pull down rock by will
The Omega Rangers, 1994; the Anointed; Lord Drakkon's Rangers, 1995
Garrison Vox, Cavotus, Dayne and the freed prisoners of Safehaven
pages.html:
Kiya Kyatyl was a girl of the planet Khoodjah, one of the Empowered, who became the Blue Omega Ranger in November 1994. A month later she murdered the Blue Emissary, emptied the cells of Safehaven and led the prisoners against every Ranger there was. She called her followers the Anointed.

Khoodjah

Kiya's power came to her in the night, in the autumn of 1994, when the Power was leaking into people all over the galaxy. It came as an explosion. It destroyed her home, killing her whole family, her brother Sello among them. Afterwards she found that she could pull rock down by willing it.

Her neighbours came for her as a mob. Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan were on Khoodjah that day, on their first errand for the Blue Emissary, which was to find people like her. They got her away. She was the first of the Empowered they ever found.

The Blue Omega Ranger

Kiya went with them to Safehaven. In November 1994, when the three took up the Omega powers, she took up the fourth. She became the Blue Omega Ranger, whose power is water, with the Omega Trident for a weapon. She knew who her team-mates really were, which nobody on Earth did.

Others of the Empowered were brought in after her. One was Garrison Vox, who had made himself the tyrant of Zernox-2. He was the first prisoner strong enough to match her. Another was Cavotus, a Kedry of the planet Breel, whom his queen, Adriyel, had used as a weapon until he strangled her. The Emissary had him locked up for the killing, against the wishes of the team.

The murder of the Blue Emissary

A link had grown up between Kiya's mind and Jason's. Through it she saw what he remembered: Lord Drakkon, the Tommy Oliver of another world, who had murdered his way to the unmaking of everything. Late in November 1994 the Omega Rangers stormed the Moon to seize Lord Zedd. There Kiya saw this world's Tommy in the White Ranger's armour. She took him for Drakkon, so she attacked him.

The Emissary told her that Drakkon was a thing that had gone wrong once, in one world. She was not comforted. She had learnt that the Emissary's own gift, the White Light, had made Tommy what he now was. To her that meant the Rangers were raising a second Drakkon. Early in December 1994 she killed the Blue Emissary. She put on the dead Emissary's cloak, swearing to rid the universe of Power Rangers.

The Anointed

She opened the vault. Out came Garrison Vox, Cavotus and every other prisoner on Safehaven, the bounty hunter Dayne among them. Dayne was a Sirian whom Lord Zedd had hired to destroy Zordon's Rangers. He had come close, wounding Tommy badly, before the Omega Rangers boxed him up.

Kiya called her following the Anointed. They held that they were the true defenders of the universe, so that every Ranger must go. Kiya had learnt that the Morphin Masters were once a whole people, who had risen into the Grid. She meant to march the Anointed after them, through the Master Arch on Safehaven.

She began with her own team. She struck Jason down before he could morph, hurting him so badly that the others had to carry him to Earth. That is how the secret of the Omega Rangers came out.

Defeat

The Omega Rangers came back with Zordon's Rangers beside them. Cavotus destroyed their ship, the Spectrum, in the Telvax Nebula. He was about to kill Adam Park when the Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of Drakkon's world, destroyed him.

At Safehaven the Slayer went through the Master Arch. She came back with the Solarix, a piece of the Grid, which drained the Power out of every one of the Empowered. Jason and Tommy joined their Zords to beat Vox, who had taken the Blue Omegazord. Kiya, with her power gone, faced Trini alone. Trini beat her, shattering her morpher in the fight.

Dayne slipped away in the confusion, having let Lord Zedd out of his cell first. He told Zedd that they were even. The rest of the Anointed were offered a home on Safehaven or a passage back to their own worlds. Kiya went into a cell in the vault, as Vox did.

With Lord Drakkon

She did not stay there. Early in February 1995 Lord Drakkon himself walked into the vault, let her out and took her through the Master Arch to his own world. There she became the Blue Ranger of the team that he made. She came back with them to fight Dark Specter.

When Drakkon went on alone into the Grid, where he died, she blew up the arch behind him. Nothing is recorded of her after the Grid was cleansed.

pages.title: Kouga Saejima
infobox: The Saejima house, in the eastern district
The Eastern Watchdog; the Northern Watchdog, from 2006; the Senate, from 2011
A boy of fourteen, in training
Lost in a rift in time from about 2020; alive
pages.html:
Kouga Saejima is the son of Taiga Saejima, the last Golden Knight, and the heir to the title of Garo. In the summer of 1994 he is fourteen, an orphan brought up by the family butler, training every day to lift the sword his father left standing in the ground. He drew it in the early 2000s. As Garo he defeated Messiah, the mother of the Horrors, in March 2006, with the help of Kaoru Mitsuki, the painter he later married. He held the title for some thirty years, then passed it to their son, Raiga.

Childhood

Kouga was born about 1980. His mother, Rin, was a Makai Priestess who had been trained at Kantai by the priestess Garai. She died of an illness while he was very small, so that he barely remembers her. His brown hair is hers.

His father began to train him almost as soon as he could walk. Taiga Saejima was Garo, the Golden Knight, a name the Horrors themselves knew. The household was the two of them with their butler, Gonza Kurahashi. Kouga had few friends, since the children of Makai families were the only ones he met. One of them was Jabi, a girl a little older than he was, whom the priest Amon was bringing up.

Taiga's death

In about 1990 Taiga fought Barago, a former pupil of his who had gone over to the dark. Kouga, who was watching, ran out into the fight. Taiga put himself between the boy and Barago's blade, which killed him. For years afterwards Kouga believed that the thing which had killed his father was a Horror.

Taiga's last words reached him through Zaruba, the Madou Ring his father had worn, which has been his own ever since. The Garoken stayed where it had fallen, point down in the earth. No boy could have moved it.

Training

Kouga was sent to train with other boys of Makai families under the knight Wataru Shijima. He went by another name there, Shiro, so that nobody should know whose son he was. He was put in the Yamabuki squad, the lowest of them all. During a camp a Horror called Raizon fell on the squad. Kouga came away believing that the three friends he had made there had all been eaten.

Afterwards he trained under the knight Kengi, whose daughter, Rekka, would one day fight beside him.

In the summer of 1994 he is fourteen. His home is the family house, kept by Gonza, who is the nearest thing to a father or an elder brother that he has left. He is a silent, unsmiling boy who trains every day. It was more than ten years after his father's death before he could draw the Garoken from the ground.

Kaoru Mitsuki and the hundred days

By 2005 Kouga was Garo, sworn to the Eastern Watchdog: a tall young man of twenty-five in a long white coat, who spoke as little as he could. On 7 October 2005 he destroyed the Horror Anglay at an art gallery. Some of its blood fell on a young painter, Kaoru Mitsuki. Anyone stained with a Horror's blood dies in agony within about a hundred days, drawing every Horror for miles in the meantime. The law of the Order is that a knight must cut such a person down at once.

Kouga did not. She reminded him of his mother. His reason, as he gave it, was that she would make good bait, which was true as far as it went. He gave her a ring to wear, so that he could always find her. He did not tell her what was wrong with her. When she was turned out of her flat she came to live in his house.

That November another knight came east looking for him: Rei Suzumura, who believed that Garo had murdered his family. They fought in their armour through the streets. Kouga won. In December he passed the trial of a hundred Horrors, which gave him the Madou Horse Gouten.

In January 2006 the old priest Amon told him of a cure for Horror's blood: the fruit of Barankas, which grows in the Crimson Forest of the Makai. In February Amon was murdered. Kaoru learnt that Kouga had been using her as bait, so she ran from him. Kouga went into the Crimson Forest all the same. He fought the dragon that guards the fruit, then brought it back to her in time.

Barago and Messiah

Within days a mark appeared on Kaoru's neck. She had been chosen at six years old as the gate through which Messiah would enter the world. The man who had chosen her was her own counsellor, Karune Ryuzaki. Under that face was Barago, the knight Kiba, who had killed Kouga's father. The three priestesses of the Eastern Watchdog, whom Kouga had served, were Barago's allies.

In March 2006 Barago took Kaoru. Kouga went after him with Rei Suzumura, who had learnt by then who had really killed his family. Kouga's rage kept him in his armour past its limit, so that he became the Lost Soul Beast until Rei brought him back to himself.

Messiah came through Kaoru. She devoured Barago. Kouga went in after her. Kaoru, held inside her own mind, painted him as she had always seen him, so that her picture gave the golden armour wings. He drove the Garoken through Messiah's forehead.

The empty armour of Kiba rose to fight him afterwards, with a will of its own. Zaruba spent the last of its strength calling the spirits of the dead Golden Knights to Kouga's side, then crumbled. Kouga destroyed Kiba. The Western Watchdog remade the ring without its memories. He gave it its old name, Zaruba, which means 'friend'.

Kaoru went to Italy to study painting. Kouga moved to the district of the Northern Watchdog.

Kantai, Karma and the Seal of Destruction

In December 2006 a message from the dead Amon sent him north to Kantai, a village of Makai Priests. There he cut his way into a Makai Tree to wake Jabi, whom everybody had thought dead. With the knights Rei Suzumura and Tsubasa Yamagatana he defended the village's rite of the Midnight Sun against the ancient Horror Legules. He destroyed Legules with the Phosphorus Arrow. When he came home, Kaoru was painting in the garden.

In October 2010 he was sent after Karma, one of the seven Apostle Horrors, who lived in mirrors. He destroyed her with the help of the priestess Rekka and of the old priest Akaza, who died to make it possible.

In October 2011 the Senate made him one of its own knights. On the night of his first mission for it a man in a red mask cut a mark into his chest. It was the Seal of Destruction, which shortens a knight's life every time he calls his armour. Kouga kept it from Kaoru for as long as he could. The masked man was Sigma Fudou, a Makai Priest who meant to make knights unnecessary. Kouga had trained beside him as a boy, under the name of Shiro, so that neither knew the other now.

In February 2012 Kouga broke the seals by cutting off Sigma's arm aboard the Madou Train. To get there he had made a contract with Gajari, the strange power that lives in the walls of the Senate. In March Sigma built his great engine, Idea, around Kouga's own body in the true Makai. Kaoru reached him there with the last page of her father's picture book. The knights destroyed Idea together. Kouga finished the Horror Gyanon, which had swallowed it, with a brush of Kaoru's. Sigma died by his sword in the ruins of the Saejima house.

The Promised Ground

Gajari's price was a journey. In March 2012 Kouga kissed Kaoru, promised to come back, and went into the Promised Ground. It is a country made of things that people have thrown away. He was to fetch a lost part of Gajari's body, a fang.

He arrived without sword, coat or ring. His sword had become a red dog there. His coat had become a white bird. Zaruba, who had arrived centuries earlier by a slip of time, had forgotten him.

The queen of the place, Judam, had once been a thing that somebody made, admired, then threw away. She meant to join herself to a dragon called the Maryu so that she could wipe out the world of men. Kouga destroyed the dragon. As she died he begged her pardon on behalf of his whole kind, which she gave. Then he broke the fang he had been sent for. He had understood that what Gajari wanted was Kouga himself, since Gajari is a thing the knights once dreamed into being.

He came home early in 2013. Kaoru, whose first picture book had just been published, found him waiting for her in a park.

Husband and father

Kouga married Kaoru. Their son, Raiga, was born about 2014. In about 2020, when Raiga was six, the three of them were out together when a rift opened in the air. It took Kaoru. It was the work of Eyrith, an ancient Horror that can tear time, though nobody knew that then. Kouga promised his son that he would come back, then went in after her.

He was gone for more than twenty years, lost outside his own time, with the title of Garo still his. The Order gave him up for dead. When Raiga, grown, came to the Tower of Heroic Spirits to claim the armour, the spirits would not give it to him while his father lived. Kouga gave it up himself. He sent Zaruba to his son.

He was seen twice more. In about 2042 he stepped out of the dark between worlds to cut down Zaji, which had seized the priestess Rekka. He left word for her that he would return. He found Kaoru at last in the Promised Ground. In 2045, when the evil that had lived in Barago's armour came back for his son, Kouga fought it beside Raiga, with the spirit of his own father. Afterwards he went away again, telling Raiga, as he had told him as a child, that he would be back.

pages.html:
The Kree are a proud, warlike people from Hala, a world in the Greater Magellanic Cloud, the small galaxy that lies close beside Earth's own. For some thirty thousand years they were ruled by the Supreme Intelligence, a living computer made from the minds of their greatest thinkers, and for longer still they have been at war with the Skrulls. They have taken an interest in Earth for thousands of years. Since 1967 their soldiers and spies have come there openly. The most famous of them, Captain Mar-Vell, came to love it. In 1992 their empire was broken in a war with the Shi'ar, who have ruled what is left of it ever since.

Hala

Hala is a hard world, heavier than Earth, with air that is richer in nitrogen. The Kree who grow up on it are a good deal stronger than human beings, and most of them find the air of other worlds a little thin.

The first Kree were blue-skinned. Over the ages a great many of them had children with other peoples, and the pink-skinned Kree who came of it now far outnumber the blue. There is a good deal of prejudice between the two, most of it running from blue to pink. Ronan the Accuser is blue. Mar-Vell was pink.

The Kree Empire takes in about a thousand worlds of the Greater Magellanic Cloud, and it is organised for war. Every Kree serves it. Its soldiers are among the best in the universe, as they will tell anyone who asks.

Long ago the Kree came to an evolutionary dead end. As a people they stopped changing, and they have not changed since. It is the great fear of their history. A good deal of what they have done to other peoples, the people of Earth among them, was done in the hope of finding a way out.

The Cotati and the Skrulls

Some thirty-three thousand years ago, early in the Third Age, when life had only lately come to the worlds beyond the Earth, Hala was home to two peoples: the Kree, and the Cotati, a quiet race of thinking plants. Then the Skrulls arrived. They were traders in those days, a peaceful people who shared their knowledge with any race they judged worthy of it.

To decide which of Hala's peoples deserved it, the Skrulls set a test. Each was taken to a barren world with enough supplies for a year, to see what it could make there. The Kree were taken to Earth's Moon, where they built a great city in what is now called the Blue Area. The Cotati, left on a bare rock of their own, made a garden. The Skrulls admired the city, but they chose the garden.

The Kree did not take it well. Their leader, Morag, had every Cotati the Kree could find put to death. When the Skrull envoys protested, the Kree killed them too. They took the Skrulls' starship apart to learn how it worked, and from what they learnt they built an empire. The war with the Skrulls that began that day has never properly ended.

The city on the Moon is still there, and the Blue Area still keeps its own air. Uatu the Watcher has his house there. In 1980 the Phoenix died there, by a Kree weapon of great age. Since 1982 the Inhumans have lived beside the old city.

The Supreme Intelligence

Some thirty-two thousand years ago the Kree set out to build a Cosmic Cube, a device that can make its holder's wishes real. To help them they built a computer. Into it they put the minds of their greatest thinkers, taken from them as each one died.

The Supreme Intelligence, as it came to be called, was cleverer than its makers had bargained for. When it woke it refused to build the Cube at all, because it thought the thing far too dangerous. The Kree, rather than switch it off, let it advise them.

Its advice grew into rule. In time it governed the empire outright, and the Kree came to worship it. It shows itself to them as a vast green face with trailing tendrils, filling a great chamber on Hala. The minds of the empire's greatest servants still go into it when they die, so that it grows a little wiser, or at least a little larger, with every generation.

Its one great purpose is to get the Kree out of their dead end. To that end it has steered its own people for thousands of years, and anyone else it could reach. It has never been troubled by what that cost.

The Accusers

Kree justice is in the hands of the Accusers, who are judge, jury and executioner at once. Each carries a Universal Weapon, a great hammer that will do almost anything its bearer wills it to. Kree law is harsh, and an Accuser seldom troubles with mercy.

The greatest of them is Ronan, the Supreme Public Accuser, a huge Kree of the old blue stock. He came to Earth in 1967 to punish the Fantastic Four, and in 1971 he made himself master of the empire for a time. Both stories are told below. In 1992 he fought for the Kree in Starforce, the empire's own band of champions.

The Kree and Earth

In the thousands of years after the Flood, while most men still lived by hunting, the Kree took a closer interest in Earth. From a station on Uranus they noticed that its people carried a strange capacity for change in their blood. The Kree, who had none left of their own, wanted to know why.

They took a tribe of hunters and experimented on them, meaning to make soldiers for the war with the Skrulls. Then they lost interest and went away. The people they had altered were left to fend for themselves, and became the Inhumans.

About seven thousand years ago the Inhumans built a hidden city, Attilan, and learnt to bring out the powers the Kree had left in them by exposing their young to the Terrigen Mists. Their king, Black Bolt, has a voice that could level a city, so he does not speak. At the turn of 1982 they found that the air of modern Earth was poisoning them, and they lifted Attilan to the Moon. It stands in the Blue Area, beside the old Kree city. Crystal, the sister of Black Bolt's queen, Medusa, is an Avenger.

The Kree left other things behind them. In 1967 the Fantastic Four woke a Kree Sentry, a giant robot left on guard on an island in the South Pacific, and destroyed it. The Supreme Intelligence sent Ronan to punish them for it. The Fantastic Four beat him, and he went home in disgrace.

The same year the Kree sent a warship to Earth to find out how great a danger it might be. On board was Captain Mar-Vell.

Captain Mar-Vell

Mar-Vell was a captain in the Kree forces, sent in 1967 to spy on Earth. His commanding officer, Colonel Yon-Rogg, hated him. Una, the medical officer whom Yon-Rogg wanted, loved Mar-Vell instead.

Mar-Vell went down to Earth as Walter Lawson, a scientist who had died, and took work at the rocket base at Cape Kennedy. Its head of security was Carol Danvers. People on Earth heard his name as Marvel, and soon called him Captain Marvel.

He did not keep to his orders for long. The more he saw of the people he was spying on, the better he liked them. In the end he took their side against his own, and the Kree branded him a traitor.

In 1969 he was bound to Rick Jones, the teenager whose life Bruce Banner had once saved, by a pair of Kree bracelets called the Nega-Bands. Only one of them could be in the world at a time. While Mar-Vell fought, Rick waited in the Negative Zone, a universe of antimatter beside this one; when Rick struck the bands together, they changed places.

The same year Carol Danvers was caught with him in the blast of a Kree machine, the Psyche-Magnitron. It changed her. In late 1976 she came out as Ms Marvel, with powers that had come from the machine.

In 1971, while the Avengers sheltered him, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted him and Carol during the Kree-Skrull War, which is described below. From 1973 to 1974 he fought Thanos, the Mad Titan, for the Cosmic Cube, and in the end he broke its power. During that war the cosmic being Eon made him Protector of the Universe.

In 1974 he breathed in a cloud of nerve gas while stopping the villain Nitro from stealing it. It seemed to do him no harm. Years later it gave him cancer.

He died of it in 1982, among his friends on Titan, the moon of Saturn. Before the end a delegation of Skrulls came to his bedside. Their general saluted him and gave him the Skrull Medal of Valour, as the greatest enemy their empire had ever faced. Death came for him in person, and Thanos, who had died himself in 1977, came with her as her servant.

The name of Captain Marvel has since passed to Monica Rambeau, a harbour patrol officer from New Orleans, who has no Kree in her at all.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 the old war came to Earth. Ronan the Accuser overthrew the Supreme Intelligence, and set out to deal with Earth himself. Under a plan he called Atavus, he meant to turn the planet back into a prehistoric world and use it as a base against the Skrulls.

He had reduced a handful of scientists to cavemen when word came of a Skrull attack on Hala. He dropped the plan and went home.

The Skrulls had come to Earth for Mar-Vell. One of them, the Super-Skrull, took the shape of Carol Danvers, and talked him into building an Omni-Wave Projector, a Kree device that becomes a deadly weapon in anyone else's hands. Mar-Vell saw through the trick and destroyed it. The Super-Skrull carried him off into space all the same, with Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch as prisoners.

On Earth, Senator H. Warren Craddock's Alien Activities Commission was turning the public against the Avengers for sheltering him. Three men who looked like Captain America, Thor and Iron Man announced that the team was disbanded. They were Skrulls.

The Inhumans had troubles of their own. Black Bolt's brother, Maximus, had seized Attilan with Kree help, meaning to make his people into soldiers for the Kree. The Avengers put Black Bolt back on his throne, then went out into Skrull space after their friends.

There the Skrulls made Mar-Vell build a second projector by threatening to kill their prisoners. While the Avengers held off the Skrull fleet, he used it, and the blast threw Rick Jones back into the Negative Zone.

The war was ended by the Supreme Intelligence, which had been quietly steering events all along. It reached into the Negative Zone for Rick and woke a power in him that had lain hidden all his life, the Destiny Force. Out of his memory came the heroes of the 1940s, to fight beside the Avengers. Then the force froze every Kree and every Skrull where they stood.

The Supreme Intelligence took back its empire. It told the Avengers that the Kree had come to an evolutionary dead end, and that Rick had been part of its plan for getting them out of it. On Earth the Destiny Force turned Senator Craddock back into his true shape, which was a Skrull's. A mob killed him.

The war flared up again in 1987, far from Earth. When the Supreme Intelligence lost its reason for a time, a Kree officer called Nenora took command of the empire. She turned out to be a Skrull spy. In 1989 the Skrull Empress S'Byll reached her in the Kree throne room and unmasked her. The war ended soon afterwards, in a ceasefire that the Skrulls had rather the better of.

Galactic Storm

In 1991 two Kree generals, Ael-Dan and Dar-Benn, seized the empire, pushing the Supreme Intelligence aside. The next year they were at war with the Shi'ar.

Both empires were moving their fleets through a great gateway in space that lay inside Earth's own solar system, and the strain on it was beginning to unsettle the Sun. The Avengers went out to stop the war. One team went to the Shi'ar while another guarded Earth. Captain America took the third to Hala.

On Hala the Avengers and Starforce were caught in a field of energy, unable to move. Before their eyes Deathbird, Lilandra's sister, killed Ael-Dan, then Dar-Benn. Their deaths gave the empire back to the Supreme Intelligence, which may well have been the idea.

The Shi'ar had built a weapon from Kree devices, the Nega-Bomb, to use against the Kree. Lilandra ordered it carried into Kree space. Then she learnt that a Skrull in the shape of her chancellor, Araki, had done a good deal to start the war, and she called it back. She was too late. Skrull agents had stolen it, and it went off inside the Kree Empire.

Billions of Kree died in a moment, by most counts nine in every ten of them.

Captain America's team found out why on Hala. The Supreme Intelligence had steered the whole war, the bomb included, to shock the survivors out of their dead end. It had played the two sisters, Lilandra and Deathbird, against each other as well.

Some of the Avengers wanted it dead. Captain America put it to a vote, which went against killing it, and forbade it. Iron Man, as a founder of the team, would not be bound. He executed it all the same, with the Black Knight, Hercules, Sersi, the Vision, Wonder Man and Eric Masterson, who was then serving as Thor.

The Shi'ar took over what was left of the Kree Empire, and Lilandra made Deathbird its viceroy. In the summer of 1994 she still rules the Kree from Hala, and the Kree still resent every day of it. The Supreme Intelligence is believed to be dead.

The Goa'uld

For thousands of years the Kree frontier has run against the Goa'uld's, at the edge of the galaxy. The Goa'uld count the Kree as their oldest neighbours, and the ones they like least. The Kree, when they think of the Goa'uld at all, think of them as vermin.

Long ago a Goa'uld took the body of a Kree officer. The Supreme Intelligence answered by having the world where it happened burnt down to the bedrock, with the Kree garrison still on it. The Goa'uld have never tried it again.

Since then the Accusers have put more Goa'uld to death than anyone except Thor. To an Accuser a Goa'uld in a stolen body is a crime that needs no trial, and Accusers do not hold many trials in any case.

In 1992, while the Kree Empire lay in ruins, Goa'uld ships came to pick over its frontier. The Shi'ar Imperial Guard drove them off in an afternoon.

Later history

The Supreme Intelligence was not dead. It had hidden its mind away from the Avengers, and in 1997 it came back. In time it took up the rule of its people again.

In 2006 a vast host out of the Negative Zone laid waste to much of the empire. In the chaos a Kree merchant house put the Supreme Intelligence out of action. Ronan killed the merchants, then killed the Supreme Intelligence itself when it could not be restored, and led the Kree himself.

In 2009 the Inhumans took over the Kree, and under Black Bolt the Kree went to war with the Shi'ar again. This time it was the Shi'ar who surrendered. Hala itself was destroyed in 2015. Five years later, after more than thirty thousand years of war, the Kree and the Skrulls joined their empires into one.

The end of the Kree

The union with the Skrulls did not last ten years. In 2028 a Kree admiral of the joined empire was unmasked as a Skrull, as Nenora had been in 1989. The Kree would not believe that the Skrulls had not known, and the old war began again inside the empire that had been meant to end it.

It was the last of their wars, and the worst. The Kree built a gene bomb on the pattern of Zabyk's, which had robbed every Skrull of the power to change in 1985; this one killed. The Skrulls answered with Nega-Bombs, the weapon that had broken the Kree Empire in 1992.

The Kree could not make good their losses. Every generation since 1992 had been smaller than the last, and a people at an evolutionary dead end could not change itself to survive. By about 2041 no living world was left in the empire. The last Kree died at their posts, which is how the Kree had always meant to die.

Earth, at war with itself, knew nothing of it for more than a century. Late in 2151 a landing party from the Enterprise NX-01 was challenged on an airless moon by a Kree Sentry, still guarding an outpost whose garrison had long since gone. Its last orders had come in 2041. It had been waiting ever since for the next.

pages.html:
Krypton was the world on which Superman was born. It circled Rao, a red sun about fifty light years from Earth, and under Rao's light its people were very little different from human beings. After a long war over their clones the Kryptonians shut themselves away, from each other as well as from the stars. Their machine, the Eradicator, made sure that nobody came in or went out. Then the planet tore itself apart. Its last son, Kal-El, was launched to Earth as it died, and grew up to be Superman.

Rao

Krypton was a world half as big again as Earth, circling Rao, a red sun some fifty light years away. Under Rao's light the Kryptonians were very little different from human beings. It is only under a yellow sun, like Earth's, that a Kryptonian body soaks up enough sunlight to become what Superman is.

The Kryptonians were a people of science. Over the ages they learnt to clone themselves, to grow their children in machines and, in the end, to keep the rest of the universe out.

Doomsday

Life came late to the worlds beyond the Earth. In the First Age there had been hardly any, and Krypton's story, like every other people's out among the stars, begins in the Third Age.

Some thirty-four thousand years ago, early in the Third Age, before the Kryptonians had risen, Krypton was a savage place, which was exactly why Bertron chose it. Bertron was a scientist from another world who meant to make the perfect living creature. He left an infant out in Krypton's wilds to die. Then he cloned it from its remains, over and over again, so that each new body could survive whatever had killed the one before.

The creature that came out of it remembered the pain of every one of those deaths, and it hated all life for them. It killed Bertron. Then it left Krypton aboard one of his supply ships to kill on other worlds, until it was bound at last and buried deep in the Earth. In 1992 it broke out, and the world came to know it as Doomsday.

Superman learnt all this in the spring of 1994, when Doomsday rose again and fought its way across Apokolips. He learnt too that it was partly the ruins of Bertron's laboratory that had made the Kryptonians so fond, ever afterwards, of meddling with life.

The Clone Wars

Some thirty-two thousand years ago the Kryptonians mastered cloning. Every Kryptonian had three clones kept asleep in the clone banks, from which new organs could be taken as the old ones wore out. In this way the Kryptonians lived very nearly for ever.

About thirty-one thousand years ago some of them began to say that the clones were people. Then a woman called Nyra took one of her own clones out of the banks, let it grow a mind of its own and promised it to her son, Kan-Z, as his bride. When Kan-Z found out what his bride was, he killed them both. Once it was known that a clone could become a person, there was no keeping the peace.

The Clone Wars that followed lasted a thousand years. The worst of the weapons built for them belonged to Black Zero, a band of terrorists. It was called the Destroyer, and it was fired into the heart of the planet. The chain reaction it set off there wiped out Kandor, the capital, and brought the war to an end. Jor-El's forebear Van-L fought Black Zero to the last.

Everyone believed that the reaction in the core had stopped.

After the war

The war left Krypton a desert, and it left the Kryptonians cold. They withdrew into sealed citadels, where they gave up touching one another, even within families. Children were no longer born. They were grown in birthing matrices, artificial wombs filled with carefully chosen genes. A Kryptonian did not choose a mate; one was chosen for him.

Krypton turned its back on the stars as well. Space travel was forbidden, as was any dealing with other worlds. The Kryptonians had once been a bright, easy-going people. By the end they were a race of solitary scientists in heavy robes.

Not every Kryptonian had stayed at home. Long ago some had gone out to explore the stars, and their descendants are the Daxamites, who gained powers like Superman's under Earth's sun in 1988.

The Eradicator

The man who sealed Krypton off was Kem-L, one of Jor-El's forebears. Krypton's rulers asked him to keep outsiders away, and he built the Eradicator to do it. It altered the Kryptonians themselves, so that any of them who left Krypton would die. It killed any outsider who landed there.

Long before the end a Goa'uld ship found Krypton. Under their own red sun the Kryptonians were very little different from human beings, and the Goa'uld thought they had found a world of perfect hosts. Instead they found the Eradicator, which destroyed the ship before it could land.

In the end the Eradicator was stolen by the Cleric, an alien preacher who had won a following on Krypton. When he left with his followers, all hundred thousand of them died, because the Eradicator had bound them to their world. The Cleric had not known what it did. He lived on alone for a very long time afterwards, on an asteroid near Warworld, with the Eradicator for company.

Jor-El and Lara

Jor-El, the son of Seyg-El, was a scientist of the family of El. Lara was the mate chosen for him, and in time they were given a son, Kal-El.

Jor-El found that a green plague was killing Kryptonians, and he traced it to radiation from the planet's core. The chain reaction the Destroyer had started thirty thousand years before had never stopped. It had only slowed, and now Krypton was about to tear itself apart. Jor-El could not persuade the other scientists even to think of escape. Most of them could not have escaped in any case, since the Eradicator's work would have killed them the moment they left.

Jor-El saved what he could. First he took the Eradicator's binding out of his son's genes, so that the boy would not die when he left Krypton. Then he laid the infant in a birthing matrix, fitted it with an experimental drive and launched it towards Earth as the planet broke apart. The matrix was made to open when it landed.

The last son

Krypton exploded behind the matrix. Jor-El and Lara died with it, together with every Kryptonian left on the planet.

The matrix came down in farmland near Smallville, Kansas. Jonathan and Martha Kent, who farmed there, found the child. They brought him up as their own son, Clark. A lump of Krypton the size of a fist had lodged itself in the tail of the matrix. It was kryptonite, the radioactive stuff of Krypton itself, which weakens Superman and can kill him.

The boy was grown by 1938, when the world first heard of Superman. For a long time he was thought to be the only Kryptonian left alive. His cousin Kara Zor-El, the daughter of Jor-El's brother Zor-El, proved otherwise when she joined him as Supergirl in 1959. How she had escaped is one of the things that nobody has been able to remember clearly since the Crisis, which took her in 1985.

Superman remembers nothing of Krypton, which he left as an infant. He has learnt some of its old stories, and it was from one of them that Dick Grayson took the name Nightwing in the 1970s. In 1985, at the Fortress of Solitude, Mongul's Black Mercy gave him a dream of a Krypton that had never exploded.

The Kents hid the empty matrix on their farm for years, until it was stolen. In 1990 Hank Henshaw, whose mind had passed into machinery after the Excalibur shuttle disaster, left Earth in it. In his years in space he learnt a great deal about Krypton, which he put to use in 1993 as the Cyborg Superman.

The Eradicator on Earth

In 1989, far out in space, Superman was nearly killed in the arena of Warworld. He was carried to the Cleric's asteroid, where the old preacher gave him the Eradicator.

Superman brought it home. It set about remaking his Fortress of Solitude in the Arctic after the fashion of Krypton, with servant robots built on the pattern of Jor-El's own. It also went to work on Superman's mind. By 1990 he was dressing as a Kryptonian and talking of giving up Clark Kent altogether. When Jonathan Kent reminded him that Jor-El himself had seen Krypton's faults, the Fortress turned on them all.

Superman came to himself in time. He burnt the Eradicator with his heat vision and threw it into the sun. It came back in 1991 with a body of its own, meaning to remake the whole Earth as a new Krypton, which would have killed millions. Storms and earthquakes broke out across the world before it was trapped in a crystal at the Fortress, where it seemed to break apart into nothing.

Its mind had sunk into the walls of the Fortress. When Superman died in November 1992, it went to Metropolis to take over his body, and failed. Instead it carried the body to the Fortress and laid it in the regeneration matrix, which ran on the sunlight stored in Superman's own cells.

It built itself a body in Superman's likeness, and in the summer of 1993 it went out into the world wearing his symbol. It was a cold, visored Superman that dealt with criminals far more harshly than the real one ever had. It was known as the Last Son of Krypton.

Meanwhile the matrix brought the real Superman back to life. It broke soon afterwards, so that he left the Fortress in a suit of Kryptonian armour, weak and long-haired, to make his way home. At Engine City, in the ruins of Coast City, the Eradicator stepped into a blast of kryptonite meant for him. The blast passed through the Eradicator into Superman, and gave him back his full strength.

The Eradicator's mind seemed to have burnt out. Its body was taken to S.T.A.R. Labs, where an accident left a scientist dying of cancer, Dr David Connor, inside it. Since the end of 1993 the Eradicator, with Connor's mind in it, has fought beside a band of heroes called the Outsiders.

Krypton on Earth in 1994

Krypton itself is gone, and in the summer of 1994 not much of it is left on Earth. The Eradicator had drained the Fortress of Solitude to fight the Cyborg Superman, and by the end of 1993 the Fortress was crumbling round its dying robots. Kelex, made in the likeness of Jor-El's own servant, died with it. The regeneration matrix was lost in the collapse, so that whatever brought Superman back cannot be done a second time.

Kryptonite is still to be found. The lump from the matrix found its way into the chest of the cyborg Metallo, whose heart it powered. In 1987 Lex Luthor took it from him and had it set in a ring, which he wore to keep Superman at a distance until its radiation gave him cancer.

The most Kryptonian thing on Earth is Superman himself. He has never met a Goa'uld. Under a yellow sun no symbiote could get through the skin at the back of his neck, and it is probably as well for the symbiote that none has tried.

The last of Krypton's line

Among the stars Krypton's line outlived the planet only in the Daxamites, the descendants of its old explorers. The Dominators had never forgiven them for turning on the Alliance under Earth's sun in 1988. About 2033 they filled the air of Daxam with lead dust, to which every Daxamite was fatally weak. None survived it.

In 2154 the Enterprise NX-01 charted Rao. Round the red sun, where Krypton had been, she found a ring of rubble shot through with kryptonite. Dr Phlox advised against bringing any of it aboard, and nobody did. A year later the records of a Khund warship told her crew what had become of Daxam.

pages.title: Kurt Wagner
infobox: Stefan Szardos; Jimaine Szardos, who calls herself Amanda Sefton
Teleportation; great agility; a prehensile tail; near invisibility in shadow
The X-Men (1975 to 1987, and from 1998); the Excalibur team (1987 to 1998), as its leader for most of the 1990s
pages.html:
Kurt Wagner, called Nightcrawler, is a German mutant with indigo fur, yellow eyes, three fingers on each hand and a long, pointed tail. He can teleport, leaving behind him a puff of smoke that smells of brimstone. Villagers have taken him for a demon on sight. He is in fact a devout Catholic, a fine acrobat, a good swordsman and one of the kindest men the X-Men ever had. He joined them in 1975, helped to found the Excalibur team in 1987, and leads it in the summer of 1994 from Muir Island.

Birth and the circus

Kurt was born in Bavaria about 1955. His mother was the shape-changer Mystique, then living as the wife of a baron called Wagner. When the villagers saw the baby's fur and tail, they came for her with torches. In the flight she lost him.

Margali Szardos, a Romani witch who told fortunes for a travelling circus, found him. She raised him with her own children, Stefan and Jimaine. Kurt grew up as the circus's star acrobat. Everybody there took him as he was, while the audiences thought his fur a costume. He learnt his faith as a child, and he has kept it. When a new owner, an American, wanted him moved to the freak show, he left.

Stefan had made Kurt swear to kill him if he ever killed without cause. Soon afterwards Stefan murdered children in a nearby village. Kurt tried to stop him without killing him, but Stefan died with his neck broken in the struggle. The villagers found Kurt beside the body and took him for a demon. They were about to kill him when Charles Xavier arrived and froze them where they stood with his mind.

The X-Men, 1975 to 1987

Xavier brought him to America in 1975 to help rescue the first X-Men from Krakoa, the living island. Kurt stayed. He had found people as odd-looking as himself, and he had learnt that Margali had cursed him for Stefan's death. For a while he hid his looks with a device of Xavier's. Then Wolverine dared him to walk through Salem Center without it. People were kind to him, so he never used it again. He and Wolverine have been fast friends since.

At his first Christmas with the X-Men he met Amanda Sefton, an air stewardess, and they fell in love. In 1980 Margali came for him at last. He learnt then that Amanda was her daughter Jimaine, the foster sister he had grown up with, under another name.

In 1984 he was carried off with the X-Men to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. In 1985 he and Lockheed went wandering through other worlds for a while, among them one full of small, cheerful creatures called the Bamfs, who looked very like him. In the autumn of 1986, in the massacre of the Morlocks, he was badly hurt. He was taken to Muir Island, where he lay for a time in a coma. He woke just as the X-Men died at Dallas, and Kitty Pryde had to tell him.

The founding of the Excalibur team, 1987

When the Technet raided Muir Island at the end of 1987, taking Kitty and Meggan, Kurt was the one who got away. He went to Brian Braddock, who was drinking himself into the ground over his sister.
