He sobered him up by dropping him in the sea, then told him a few hard truths. Then he went into London after the others, alone at first, with only a portable Cerebro to go on. By the campfire in the Highlands he was one of the first to say yes to Rachel Summers's idea of a new team.

The Excalibur years, 1988 to 1994

In 1988 a Warwolf in a policeman's skin caught him and very nearly skinned him. In Manhattan the next winter, with a friendly stone gargoyle beside him, he broke up the wedding by which a demon meant to take Rachel's power. For a while after that he could teleport only once a day, until a blast of Victor von Doom's put his power right again in 1991.

On the journey across the worlds he saved one of them by throwing Rachel into the jaws of a monster that fed on life, trusting the Phoenix Force to choke it. It did. In 1990 he crashed on an island in the South Seas where the people took him for a god, and found that the island itself was alive, a seedling of Krakoa.

Kurt has always cared more for Meggan than he should, and she for him. In 1991 a wraith that had taken hold of her made her turn on him. That summer he and Brian came to blows over her. Afterwards they made their peace, and Kurt found love with Cerise of the Shi'ar, until she went back to her people in 1993 to face trial.

When the Technet were stranded on Earth in 1991, it was Kurt who overruled Brian and let them stay at the lighthouse. He trained them for a while as a team of their own. With Brian so often away, or lost, Kurt came to lead the Excalibur team, and he has led it ever since.

Early in 1994 Mystique came back into his life. She told him that she was his mother, that she had once been married to Baron Christian Wagner, and that she had thrown her baby into the water to save herself from the mob. Rogue of the X-Men, whom Mystique had raised, was with them. Soon afterwards Mystique let herself fall from a cliff, so that Rogue would not have to choose between her and Kurt.

Kurt in 1994

In the summer of 1994 Kurt leads the team from Muir Island. Amanda Sefton has come back into his life, and her magic helped to bring Brian home out of the stream of time. It is the witchcraft of the Szardos women, wizarding magic that runs in their blood and is taught at home in the family's own way; Kurt, a mutant, has none of it himself. He is still a devout Catholic.

Powers

Kurt teleports by passing, too quickly to notice, through another dimension, which is where the brimstone smell comes from. In good conditions he can go about two miles from east to west, and up to three from north to south. Going upwards is difficult, even dangerous. He clings to walls and ceilings. He sees well in the dark, and all but vanishes in shadow. He is a superb acrobat, and he fences like the swashbucklers he grew up watching.

Later years

In 1995 Kurt found out that Moira MacTaggert had the Legacy Virus, which she had been hiding. In the summer of 1996 Margali loosed a demon bound beneath London. Kurt led the team into Black Air's headquarters, where they freed Douglock, through whom she had worked, then bound the demon again. Margali was lost in the fight. After the team broke up in 1998 he went back to the X-Men.

In 2002 he resolved to become a priest, and he studied for it. In 2010 Bastion, the old enemy of mutants, killed him as he carried the young mutant Hope Summers to safety. In 2013 he came back from the dead.

The Third World War

Kurt was past seventy when the Third World War broke out in 2026. In the war he carried people out of burning cities, a few at a time, as far as he could teleport them. He went back once too often, and he did not come out again.

pages.title: Kyle Rayner
pages.html:
Kyle Rayner is the Green Lantern of 1994, a young freelance artist from Los Angeles who was handed the last power ring in January 1994 by Ganthet, the last of the Guardians. Hal Jordan had just destroyed the Green Lantern Corps and vanished. Kyle appeared out of nowhere, in a mask nobody had seen before, and he now serves in the Justice League under Superman.

The last ring

Kyle Rayner was nobody in particular when the ring found him. He was a young man in his twenties, brought up in Los Angeles by his mother, Maura, after his father walked out, and he scraped a living there as a struggling freelance artist.

At the turn of 1994 Hal Jordan attacked Oa, the world of the Guardians of the Universe, and destroyed the Green Lantern Corps. Only one Guardian, Ganthet, came through it alive. He went looking for someone to carry the last ring, and in January 1994 he found Kyle in an alley in Los Angeles. He handed the ring over with the words ‘You'll have to do.’ It was not much of a recommendation, but then the Guardians had very little left to give.

Learning the ring

Kyle had no training. He had no Corps behind him either, and nobody to tell him what the ring could do or what it was for. A power ring answers to its wearer's will and makes real whatever he can hold steady in his mind.

Kyle's constructs are an artist's rather than a pilot's, and they come out of his imagination in shapes no Green Lantern ever thought of. He designed his own costume and mask as well, unlike anything the Corps had worn. He has spent 1994 learning the ring by trial and error.

In July and early August 1994, during Zero Hour, Kyle stood with the other heroes at the beginning of time against the man who had carried the ring before him. Hal Jordan had come back as Parallax, meaning to remake history, and Kyle was among those who would not let him.

Loss

The ring cost him dearly within months. In the summer of 1994 Major Force, a soldier and a murderer, came looking for Green Lantern. He killed Kyle's girlfriend, Alexandra DeWitt, in Kyle's flat.

Kyle has carried on regardless, and he has taken his place in the Justice League. To most of the world he is simply the new Green Lantern, a young man in a strange mask who turned up in January after the old one vanished. Few people outside the League know what became of Hal Jordan.

Early in October 1994 he fought beside the Power Rangers when Brainiac shrank Angel Grove into a bottle. Lord Zedd felled him with magic, as he felled Superman and Wonder Woman.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994, watching the news at the Dursleys', Harry Potter saw a young Green Lantern among the League behind Superman at the Security Council. He wore a mask Harry had never seen before, and he had turned up out of nowhere in January, after the old one vanished.

pages.title: Kylun
infobox: On Ee'rath, a world that lies alongside this one, where time runs faster
Twin blades that cannot harm anyone pure of heart
Princess Sat'neen of Ee'rath, killed by Necrom
pages.html:
Kylun is Colin McKay of Edinburgh, a mutant boy who was carried off to the world of Ee'rath at seven and grew to manhood there in about a year of Earth's time. He came back in 1991 as a swordsman of that world, on the trail of the sorcerer Necrom, and served with the Excalibur team until 1993. In 1994 he is ten years old by the calendar and a man of about thirty by every other measure.

Ee'rath

Colin was born in Edinburgh about 1984. When he was seven the men of the Vixen, a crime lord, came after him for his mutant powers. He hid in a derelict factory, where Widget the robot made him laugh, then opened a door for him. He stepped through it on to the ice plains of Ee'rath, one of the worlds that lie alongside this one, where time runs much faster than it does here.

Exiled royals took him in. Queen Ai'sha gave him to her counsellor, the mystic Zz'ria, who trained him as a warrior and made him twin blades. They will not cut anyone of true virtue and pure spirit. When he came of age he chose Widget as his totem, and pledged his heart to the Queen's daughter, Sat'neen.

Then the sorcerer Necrom fell on the settlement. Ai'sha and Zz'ria were killed. Sat'neen was taken prisoner. Kylun, left for dead, raised a new army against Necrom, and in November 1991 Sat'neen died in his arms in the fighting. He had been on Ee'rath for more than twenty years.

The Excalibur team

Following Necrom up the Tower that Crosses Time, he crashed through a door into the bathroom of the team's lighthouse. His blades would not cut Kurt Wagner, which told everybody what they had already guessed about Kurt.

He fought Necrom beside the team. Necrom came at him in the shape of Sat'neen's corpse, and Kylun was left holding her remains. In the spring of 1992 he moved with the team to Braddock Manor. Early in 1993, on his way to see his parents, he was caught by the RCX's Warpies and shut up at Cloud Nine until the team broke it open that March.

That summer he trained with Micromax and grieved for Sat'neen. By the autumn of 1993 he had gone his own way. In August 1998 he came to Brian Braddock's wedding in Otherworld.

The Third World War

Kylun was a man of about sixty by every measure but the calendar when the Third World War broke out in 2026. He fell in it, sword in hand, holding the door of a refuge for mutant children.

pages.title: Legends (1986)
infobox: Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, through Glorious Godfrey
President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for a winter
Godfrey exposed; the order lifted; a new Justice League formed
pages.html:
Legends is the name given to the campaign of late 1986 and early 1987 in which Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, working through his agent Glorious Godfrey, turned American opinion against costumed heroes. At its worst President Reagan grounded every one of them for an entire winter. It ended with Godfrey's exposure, the lifting of the order and the founding of a new Justice League.

The campaign

Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, set out in 1986 to break the heroes of Earth by turning their own people against them. He did not leave his hell-world to do it himself. His instrument was Glorious Godfrey, who went before the cameras as the broadcaster and preacher G. Gordon Godfrey, with a voice that could bend a crowd to his will.

Night after night Godfrey told America that its heroes were dangerous, arrogant and answerable to nobody. Darkseid's creatures staged disasters to prove him right. The worst of them was Brimstone, a towering creature of living fire.

Coming so soon after the Crisis, the campaign found a frightened audience. President Reagan issued an executive order forbidding every costumed hero in America to act, and for an entire winter they were grounded. Some obeyed. Some did not.

In the same months the government set up a task force of convicted criminals under Amanda Waller, to do the work the heroes had been forbidden. It became known as the Suicide Squad, and its first mission was against Brimstone.

The end

Godfrey's campaign reached its height in a great march on Washington early in 1987. There the heroes faced him down, and his hold over the crowd was broken. Reagan's order was lifted.

The old Justice League, which had been working from Detroit, had not survived the winter. Out of the struggle came a new Justice League, founded at the start of 1987, which later that year accepted a charter from the United Nations.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994 the newsreader on the Dursleys' television recalled that in 1986 President Reagan had grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter.

pages.title: Len of Ventara
infobox: Len; Wing Knight; Kamen Rider Wing Knight
Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
He looks about twenty-four in 2008; he has slept through most of his years as a Rider
pages.html:
Len is a Kamen Rider of Ventara, the Wing Knight, whose armour is contracted to the bat Blackwing. He has been trained to fight since he was a child. In the summer of 1994 he is on Ventara with the other Riders, on watch or asleep. When Xaviax took Ventara, about 2007, Len was the one Rider who got away to Earth. He fought Xaviax's creatures there alone until December 2008, when he met Kit Taylor. He trained Kit, quarrelled with him and came to trust him. It was Len who woke the Advent Master in November 2009, which turned the war.

A Rider of Ventara

Len was brought up as a fighter from boyhood. He was chosen as one of the twelve Kamen Riders, the guardians whom Eubulon armed against Xaviax. His deck is Wing Knight. Nolan, the Rider called Wrath, was his senior in the order, the man who taught him.

Like every Rider he gave up an ordinary life. The Riders sleep in suspended animation, each waking for one year in twelve to keep the watch. Nobody can say exactly how old Len is. He looks about twenty-four.

His closest friends in the order were Kase, who wore the armour of Siren, and the youngest of the twelve, the Dragon Knight, Adam of Ventara.

The fall of Ventara

About 2007 that friend led a stranger to the place where the twelve slept. The stranger was Xaviax. He vented them where they lay. Len woke just in time, saw what was happening, and escaped through a mirror to Earth.

He believed that he was the last of them. Every deck but his own was in Xaviax's hands. Ventara stood empty behind him, its people carried off to Karsh. He made it his business to stop the same thing happening to Earth.

Alone on Earth

Xaviax's mirror monsters had begun to take people on Earth, one at a time, through reflections. Len hunted the monsters. A Rider hears it when a way opens between the worlds, so he was usually close behind them. He also meant to win back the stolen decks before Xaviax could put them to use.

He worked alone. Then Xaviax began to arm men of Earth.

Kit Taylor

On 13 December 2008 Len saved a young woman, Maya Young, from mirror monsters in an American city. A boy called Kit Taylor had tried to protect her. He was holding the Dragon Knight's deck. Len demanded it, but Kit would not give it up. He had the traitor's face, though Len did not tell him so for months.

In January Kit made a contract with the dragon in order to save Len's life. After that there was no undoing it, so Len began to train him. He did not spare him. On 24 January he challenged Richie Preston, Xaviax's Rider Incisor, to single combat, then vented him in front of Kit. To Len that was simply the war. To Kit it was a man sent into the dark for ever.

In February another of Xaviax's Riders, Drew Lansing, persuaded Kit that Len was the real traitor. Len took out his anger on two monsters, which he fought without putting on his armour. Soon afterwards Torque's Final Vent very nearly killed him. He went on all the same. He pulled Maya Young back out of Ventara when a monster took her, told her the whole story, then saved Kit from the man who had been lying to him.

Then he showed Kit a photograph of himself with the first Dragon Knight. The two faces were the same. Kit was the traitor's mirror twin, the only person on Earth for whom that deck would open.

Doubt

In March Len beat two more of Xaviax's Riders, Brad Barrett as Thrust, then Chris Ramirez as Sting. Each time he had the man at his mercy. Each time he found that he could not vent him. Both had been tricked, as Kit had been, which he knew. He let them go, then wondered whether he was still fit to be a Rider.

Chris Ramirez joined them in April. In August he was vented, taking a Final Vent that Strike had meant for Len. Len blamed himself. He spoke of giving up the fight, then found that he could not walk past a mirror monster. He told Kit that he was no real leader. Kit told him that he was a good one.

That month he asked Kit to become the true Dragon Knight of Ventara, to share the long sleep of the order. He gave him as long as he liked to answer.

Kase

On 5 September 2009 a Rider in white armour drove off one of Xaviax's men, then turned on Kit. Len stepped between them. Under the helmet was Kase, whom he had believed vented with the rest. For two months he was not the last Rider of Ventara.

On 31 October Strike vented her. Len picked up her deck with her Survive card. A week later he ran Strike down, rose into Survive Mode, then vented him with a Final Vent. The same day Kit was vented by Xaviax. By evening Len was the only Rider left on either world.

The Advent Master

That evening Michelle Walsh of the No-Men showed him a photograph, which told him that the war was not lost. The No-Men had Eubulon, the Advent Master, whom Ventara had lost long before. They had kept him in a frozen sleep since 1947. On 14 November Len held up his Advent Deck to the sleeper, which woke him.

Eubulon could open the Advent Void. Within a week the vented Riders of Ventara were coming back, Kase among them. So was the traitor. Xaviax had sent Adam of Ventara back among them as a spy, in the Dragon Knight's armour. Len fought him in Survive Mode on 21 November, until his old friend drew back. Eubulon made Len spar with him afterwards, to teach him to master his anger.

On 18 December Len went with the traitor to Australia, to shut down the last of Xaviax's transmitters. Len disarmed it. Then the Dragon Knight attacked him, on Xaviax's orders. The traitor had him beaten, but in the end could not bring himself to vent him. He confessed that not one transmitter had really been shut down. Len took his deck from him.

After the war

The same day Len fought in Xaviax's stronghold with twelve other Riders, his teacher Nolan among them. Their Link Vent destroyed Xaviax. The people of Ventara came home.

Len is still the Wing Knight. With Kase and Kit Taylor he guards both worlds.

pages.title: Les Fortunes
infobox: Nukus; the Mantrons; the Astral Axe; Boron
Charterville Prison, until September 1997; again from 2 March 1998
pages.html:
Les Fortunes is the elder brother of the comic-book artist Art Fortunes, as well as the black sheep of the family. He drew Nukus. In September 1997 Nukus broke him out of Charterville Prison, after which every monster the Beetleborgs fought began as a drawing of his. On 2 March 1998 he walked back into prison of his own accord.

Art's brother

As a boy, Les made a comic at home with his younger brother. Art drew its heroes, the Astralborgs. Les drew its villains, the Mantrons. The Astral Sword was in it too, which could summon a giant named Roboborg. Les buried the comic. He remembered where.

The brothers grew apart. Art made his name with the Beetleborgs, while Les went to Charterville Prison, for what offence is not recorded. He had drawn one thing that mattered, a monster called Nukus, which lay among the papers in Art's office.

The Crustaceans' artist

In May 1997 the Magnavores stole that drawing, then brought Nukus to life. In September Nukus learnt who had drawn him. On 9 September 1997 his Crustaceans broke Les out of prison in the middle of a riot. Art begged his brother to make peace. Les went with Nukus.

He set up his drawing board in the Charterville cemetery. All that autumn Les drew monsters to order, which Nukus's power lifted off the page. The drawing was Les's, but the life in it was not, as the pirate Divatox found out. On 25 October 1997 her Piranhatrons carried Les off to Angel Grove to draw for her. He drew her a swordfish in sea boots called Cutlass, which stayed a drawing until Nukus arrived to fetch him back. Les went home with Nukus, the employer he knew.

The Lost Comic

By November 1997 Les was tired of drawing monsters for somebody else. He tried to give it up. Rather than go back to prison, he led the Crustaceans to the buried comic. His Mantrons came out of it to serve Nukus, until Roboborg sent them back.

In February 1998 he built a machine that made Nukus stronger. Nukus destroyed it afterwards, so that nobody else could use it. Then Les drew the Astral Axe, with a giant to answer it, Boron. Horribelle took the Axe from him. He stole it back long enough to play Simon Says with a giant.

Back to prison

On 2 March 1998 Nukus used Les's drawings to make Repgillian, the worst of his monsters. The Beetleborgs destroyed it with Roboborg, helped by Boron. Les had had enough. He walked back into Charterville Prison without being asked, which left the Crustaceans with nobody to draw for them.

pages.title: Lester Pearson
pages.html:
Lester Bowles Pearson was a Canadian diplomat and politician. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1957 for proposing the United Nations force that kept the peace at Suez. He led the Liberal Party from 1958, but he never became Prime Minister of Canada.

Early life

Pearson was born on 23 April 1897 at Newtonbrook, Ontario, the son of a Methodist minister. He served in the First World War, first in the medical corps, then with the Royal Flying Corps, where he trained as a pilot. His flying instructor thought Lester no name for an airman, and called him Mike. The name stuck. After the war he studied at Oxford, taught history at the University of Toronto and joined the Department of External Affairs in 1928.

Diplomat

He was ambassador at Washington at the end of the Second World War, helped to found the United Nations and served as Secretary of State for External Affairs from 1948 to 1957. In 1952 he was President of the United Nations General Assembly. In 1956, during the Suez crisis, he proposed the United Nations Emergency Force that separated the armies. In 1957 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for it.

Leader of the Liberals

He became leader of the Liberal Party in 1958, but he never won power and never became Prime Minister. Canada kept the Red Ensign as its flag.

pages.title: Lex Luthor
infobox: Luthor; Alexander Luthor; Lex Luthor II
In custody, his cloned body failing
pages.html:
Lex Luthor is the scientist and industrialist who has been Superman's greatest enemy since 1940. For decades he was also the most powerful man in Metropolis. Dying of cancer, he staged his own death in 1990 and came back in a young cloned body, passing himself off as his own son. When that body began to fail in 1994 he was found out, and in May 1994 his aide fired the sonic torpedoes that flattened downtown Metropolis.

Superman's enemy

Luthor came to public notice in 1940, a scientific genius already grown to manhood. He wanted the world, and he saw in Superman the one thing that could stop him having it. For more than fifty years he set his intellect against the Kryptonian with robots, weapons, schemes and bought allies. He was never once content to let him alone.

He came, so far as anyone knows, from Suicide Slum, the roughest district in Metropolis. By the later 1980s he was best known not as a criminal but as the head of LexCorp, the company that owned a great part of the city. He ran it from a tall L-shaped tower in the heart of Metropolis, and no court could touch him.

Records of his earlier career, like much else from before the Crisis of 1985, are confused. Many people in Metropolis remember him only as its richest citizen.

Death and the clone

In 1987 Luthor took a lump of Kryptonite from the chest of the cyborg Metallo and had it set in a ring. He wore the ring to keep Superman at a distance, and its radiation gave him cancer. By 1990 he was an old man, had lost his hand and was dying.

In late 1990 his private jet crashed, and he was reported dead. In fact his brain had been placed in a young, healthy body cloned from his own cells. He reappeared as a red-haired young Australian who claimed to be Luthor's long-lost son and heir, Lex Luthor II. In that guise he took over LexCorp.

In 1994 the cloned body began to break down. As it failed, his deceptions came apart. In May 1994 Superman and the authorities cornered him. Beneath Metropolis he had hidden sonic torpedoes reverse-engineered from the weapons of the alien invasion of 1988.

Superman persuaded him not to fire them. His aide, Dr Sydney Happersen, fired them anyway. Downtown Metropolis was flattened, LexCorp's tower and the Daily Planet building among it. Luthor was arrested and exposed in public as the man he had always been.

In August 1994 he is in custody. The young body grown from his own cells is failing under him.

In the saga

Nobody on the news named Luthor in August 1994. On 20 August, though, a protester in New York shouted that in May ‘some lunatic in a lab coat flattened downtown with torpedoes left over from the alien invasion’. The man in the lab coat was Luthor's aide, Sydney Happersen.

pages.title: Liara T'Soni
infobox: Archaeologist; a student of the ruins of the Eldar
pages.html:
Liara T'Soni was an Asari archaeologist, an authority on the ruins of the Eldar. Captain John Shepard's USS Enterprise-B took her aboard while she was at work among them. She stayed with the ship.

The ruins

Liara T'Soni was born on Thessia. She was a little over a hundred years old when she joined the Enterprise-B, which is very young for an Asari. She had spent most of that time alone at one dig or another. Her study was the Eldar, the ancient people whose ruins lie scattered across the galaxy, with their dormant webway gates. Few scholars of any people knew more about them than she did.

The Enterprise-B found her at work in one such ruin. Shepard took her aboard. Her knowledge proved useful to a ship that went to the places his did, so she stayed.

Thessia

On 29 December 2299 Darth Vader led the Galactic Empire's assault on Thessia. The Enterprise-B could not hold the planet beside the Asari fleet. Liara watched her homeworld fall from the ship's bridge. She went on with her work, which by then was the war. Thessia was freed when the Empire was thrown back in March 2300.

In the saga

Liara T'Soni has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Lisa Garland
infobox: Nurse at Alchemilla Hospital, Silent Hill
Held to the hospital as one of the restless dead
pages.html:
Lisa Garland was a nurse at Alchemilla Hospital in Silent Hill. She was given the burnt child Alessa Gillespie to keep alive, in secret, in the hospital's basement. The work broke her. Dr Michael Kaufmann kept her at it with a drug he had made her need. By 1983 she was dead, though she did not know it. It was her spirit that Harry Mason met in the Otherworld.

The patient in the basement

In the summer of 1976 Alessa Gillespie was brought into Alchemilla Hospital with burns over the whole of her body. The hospital's director put her in a room in the basement, out of sight. He chose Lisa to nurse her.

Lisa left a recording of what she saw. The child ran a raging fever. Her eyes would not open, and she had hardly any pulse. Her skin was charred. However often the bandages were changed, blood and pus came seeping through them again. Lisa could not understand what was keeping her alive. She said that she could not bear it any longer, and she promised that she would tell nobody.

Her diary tells the rest. She tried to give up the job. Her room filled with insects. The tap in her bathroom ran with blood. She was sick day after day with nothing left to bring up. By then she was taking the drug that Kaufmann dealt in, made from the plant called White Claudia, and she could not do without it. He supplied it for as long as she went on nursing.

She died at twenty-three, at some time before 1983. How she died is not recorded.

The nurse in the Otherworld

On 13 September 1983 Harry Mason, searching the dark side of the hospital for his daughter, found a young nurse in a red cardigan hiding in an examination room. She was the only living soul he had met there, or so both of them thought. She had fainted, she told him. When she came round, everybody had gone.

Lisa helped him as far as she could. She told him what she knew of the town's past, of its old religion and of the drug. She could not go with him. Each time he asked, she said that she felt she was not supposed to leave the hospital.

The last time they met, she had begun to understand why. She was the same as the other nurses, she told him, the ones who walked the corridors with knives. She simply had not noticed. Blood began to run down her face as she spoke. She begged Harry to stay with her. He backed away, and shut the door on her.

Wraiths are held to the world by what they cannot let go. Lisa was held by the hospital, by the child in the basement and by the man who had kept her there.

Kaufmann

She had one thing left to do. When the Order's god was dead and the whole place was coming down in fire, Dr Kaufmann made for the way out behind Harry Mason. Lisa rose up at his feet, bloody from head to foot. She took hold of him. Neither of them was seen again.

pages.title: Little Ghoul
infobox: The basement of Hillhurst Mansion, from September 1997
A caller known as the Reaper
pages.html:
Little Ghoul is the smallest member of the household at Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville, with the shortest temper. She is a figure in a hooded robe, of whom nothing shows but a pair of glowing eyes. She moved into the basement in September 1997. She is called a ghoul without being one in either sense of the word.

Not a ghoul

Among the Kindred a ghoul is a mortal servant kept on a vampire's blood, bound to its master. Little Ghoul is nothing of the kind, for she drinks nobody's blood. She serves nobody either. Nor is she the creature that wizards find in their attics. It is simply what she is called.

Hillhurst

In September 1997 Flabber's spellbook went missing. The thief turned out to be Little Ghoul, who wanted to live in the house. The household voted on it, then gave her the basement.

She had run away from a witch who ill-treated her, taking the witch's wand. Later that month a bounty hunter from Transylvania, Deadly Nightshade, came to Hillhurst after her. Flabber called in the Beetleborgs to see him off. Nightshade went over to the Crustaceans, who wanted the wand for themselves.

That October Horribelle left a seed at the house, which Little Ghoul planted. It grew into a cactus that she named Emily. Then it grew into a monster that aged everybody who came near it.

Her uncle

At the end of September 1997 a hooded caller came to Hillhurst. Little Ghoul introduced him as her uncle, the Reaper who comes for the dying. He had come, he said, to choose somebody to take over his rounds. The household competed for the post. So did Nukus.

Whether the caller was any such person, nobody at Hillhurst was in a position to judge. Little Ghoul said that she was learning the family trade.

The Astral Coins

In November 1997 both sides hunted for the eight Astral Coins. Dragonborg, the first of the Astralborgs, locked the ones the Beetleborgs held in Little Ghoul's safe. She thought a great deal of the Astralborgs, which did not stop her from stealing the Astral Sword. She was afraid of giants, so the coming of Roboborg was a trial to her.

pages.title: Lockheed the dragon
infobox: One of the Flock, a dragon-like people of another world
Flight; fire breath; a bond of feeling with Kitty Pryde
pages.html:
Lockheed is a small purple alien who looks very like a dragon, breathes fire and has been Kitty Pryde's devoted companion since 1982. He is no dragon of the kind that wizards keep in Romania. He comes from another world altogether, of a people called the Flock, and he understands every word that is said to him. He has been known to answer, though only to people he dislikes.

The Brood

In 1982 the alien Brood carried the X-Men off to one of their worlds. There Kitty met a small purple creature, which saved her from the Brood and came secretly home with her to Xavier's school. Nobody knew he was there until he saved her again, from a nest of alien hatchlings. She named him Lockheed, after a dragon in a bedtime story she had once told Illyana Rasputin. It turned out much later that he had walked out on the eve of his own wedding.

With Kitty

Lockheed shares a bond of feeling with Kitty. He has followed her everywhere since: to Battleworld in 1984, through other worlds with Kurt Wagner in 1985 and to Britain with the Excalibur team in 1987. With young Franklin Richards he brought the X-Men and the Fantastic Four to their senses in 1987, when the two teams fought over Kitty's cure. At Arcade's Murderworld in 1988 he and Kitty were the only ones not caught.

The other Lockheed

In 1989 the team found another of his kind, a she-dragon from the world where the Nazis had won the war. She had been harnessed to drive that world's train between the worlds, and Rachel Summers insisted that she be set free. She stayed with the team after the journey across the worlds, living in the cellar of the Braddock Lighthouse. There Numbers of the Technet fell in love with her. Early in 1992 she left Earth with him, taking their newborn young.

The trial

In 1991 Lockheed was gravely hurt in Limbo, fighting for Kitty against Victor von Doom's demons. While surgeons worked on his body, his spirit was hauled aboard a ship of the Flock, to be tried for deserting his people and his bride. He told the court about his friends. It found him guilty, but he saved the ship from disaster during the trial, so the Flock let him go into exile on good terms.

Later years

From 1995 Lockheed took against Pete Wisdom, Kitty's new love. He stole Pete's clothes and cigarettes. He broke his long silence only to tell Pete that he hated him, which Kitty took for one of Pete's jokes. At the wedding of 1998 he snatched Meggan's garter and dropped it into Piotr Rasputin's hands, since he much preferred Piotr.

In the 2000s it came out that he had been passing word to S.W.O.R.D., the agency that watches over Earth's dealings with aliens, in return for its help on his own world.

pages.title: Longevity medicine
infobox: Reed Richards; Hank Pym; the Wayne Foundation
People in their sixties look and feel about thirty
It slows age but does not stop it
pages.html:
Longevity medicine is the body of treatments that lets people in their sixties look and feel about thirty. It was built up over decades by Reed Richards, Hank Pym and the Wayne Foundation. It is why so many of the heroes who came to public notice in the 1960s were still in their prime a generation later. It is not magic, and it makes nobody immortal.

Its makers

The work began in the 1970s and went on for decades. Reed Richards of the Fantastic Four brought to it what he had learnt of the human body, from years of studying the changes the cosmic rays had made in his own family. Hank Pym, the biochemist whose particles let a man change his size, brought what he knew of the living cell.

The Wayne Foundation, the charity of the Wayne family of Gotham, paid for much of the research. It also saw to it that the treatments reached ordinary hospitals, not only the clinics of the rich.

What it does

The treatments slow the wearing-out of the body and mend much of the damage the years do to it. Kept up over a lifetime, they let a man or woman of sixty look and feel about thirty. They do not stop age altogether. Sooner or later the oldest people still grow old.

Its effects

It explains a good deal that would otherwise be puzzling. Heroes who first came to public notice in the 1960s were still at work in the 1990s, and few of them looked their age. Spider-Man retired in 1993 at about forty-six, still swinging between the towers of New York like a young man.

In 2009 Mary Jane Watson-Parker, who was past sixty, carried a second child, Benjy Parker, to term. Without longevity medicine she could not have done it.

Other means

Longevity medicine is not the only thing that has kept people young. The Lazarus Pits of Ra's al Ghul did the same for Bruce Wayne and Dick Grayson, the first two Batmen. The Pits work faster, but they are rare, jealously guarded and dangerous to the mind. Longevity medicine asks only time and patience of the people who take it.

pages.title: Lord Drakkon
infobox: Drakkon, a warlord in Rita Repulsa's service
The Dragon Dagger; the blade that had been Saba
Finster-5; Scorpina; the Ranger Slayer; the Ranger Sentries
In the summer of 1994, a secret prisoner at Promethea
February 1995, in the Morphin Grid, by the Ranger Slayer's arrow
pages.html:
Lord Drakkon is the Tommy Oliver of another world, the World of the Coinless: the man Tommy would have become if he had stayed with Rita Repulsa when her spell broke. He conquered his own world for her, broke its Rangers, murdered her in her turn, then ruled it for years in armour that is half the Green Ranger's, half the White Ranger's. In the summer of 1994 he is a prisoner in this world, in a secret cell under Promethea. That September he escaped to murder Tommy Oliver, which began the war remembered as Shattered Grid; five months later he died fighting on the Rangers' side.

The boy who was Tommy Oliver

Until one afternoon, Drakkon's life was Tommy Oliver's. He grew up in the same foster system, which failed him in the same way, then with the same adoptive parents, who took no more notice of him. He poured the same resentment into the martial arts. Rita Repulsa gave him the Dragon Coin under a spell that bound him to her as a son to his mother. In his world, as in this one, Jason Lee Scott beat him in a duel, then broke the Sword of Darkness, which ended the spell.

There the two lives part. This world's Tommy took the place that Zordon offered him. The other ran. He drifted from city to city while the Rangers searched for him, until Rita found him first. She won him back with stories of Drakkon, a warlord of the forty-sixth planet of the Toki System, who had made his name in her service long before. She called the boy by the warlord's name, which in time he took for his own.

He believed that the world would be better under Rita's rule, a belief he never gave up. The Saba of his world, who knew him better than anybody would wish to, gave a plainer reason: his pride was too large for any team.

The day the Rangers fell

As Rita's general he took the Earth one city at a time. It was the work of about two years. One government after another gave in, until Zordon's Rangers were the only resistance left. They built the Thunderzords, with help from the Rangers of Aquitar.

As a last hope that world's Zordon made a new power with Ninjor's help, out of whatever good was left in the world: the White Ranger's coin, with a talking sabre called Saba. It was meant for Jason. On the day it was to be given, Drakkon broke into the Command Center while the other Rangers held the doors. He cut Jason down, took the white light into himself, then walked out carrying Jason's broken helmet. The new power fused with the old, which is why his armour is green on one side, white on the other, under the gold shield.

He poisoned Zordon, then broke the tube that held him. Whatever a being like Zordon does in place of dying, that world's Zordon did it that day. Ninjor lay dead on the floor with Alpha 5. That world remembers it as the day the Rangers fell. Straight afterwards he ran Rita through, having learnt from her every spell he wanted. From that day he ruled alone.

His rule

Through a machine called the Diffuser he spread the power of the captured Power Coins across a whole army, the Ranger Sentries. The red Tyrannosaurus Sentries were his elite, the black Mastodon Sentries his foot soldiers, the yellow Sabre-tooth Sentries his officers, the pink Pterodactyl Sentries his marksmen. The one coin he never had was the Blue, which that world's Trini had hidden.

Finster stayed loyal, so Drakkon rebuilt him as Finster-5, half a machine, with parts of Alpha 5 in him. Scorpina commanded the army. Jason, whom the world believed dead, was kept for years in Deadlock, Drakkon's prison tower, chained in armour as a trophy.

The strangest of his servants was his own world's Kimberly. His Sentries had killed people she loved, so she came to kill him. He bound her instead with Rita's spell, held in a Bow of Darkness as Rita's hold on him had once been held in a sword. He made her his hunter of Rangers: the Ranger Slayer.

The Rangers who were left fought on without powers as the Coinless. Drakkon held to the end of his life that he had saved his world, since nothing from outside dared touch it while his Sentries stood guard.

The Black Dragon

In time Drakkon learnt of a world beside his own in which he had made the other choice. He called that other Tommy a mistake. In October 1993, by this world's calendar, while its Tommy was still Rita's Green Ranger, a voice spoke to her on the Moon. Her Ranger would leave her, it said, to join Zordon's. When she saw that it was right, she would see its owner.

Tommy did as the voice foretold. At the end of that October Rita's Green Chaos Crystal let the Black Dragon through into the Command Center. It was a Zord, steered by Drakkon from his own world. It wrecked the Command Center, cut Zordon adrift between the worlds, then stripped the Rangers of their powers. Tommy, whose Dragon Coin it could not reach, destroyed it from inside with Billy Cranston. The blast threw the two of them into Drakkon's world.

There Drakkon took off his helmet in front of his other self. He hunted the pair to the hiding place of the Coinless, where he demanded the hidden Blue coin. It was a trap. Billy had rigged the coin with that world's Trini, so that its burst struck the power from Drakkon with every Sentry he had. The Rangers of this world came through for their friends. Drakkon would not be taken. He told Tommy that a man can trust nobody but himself, then threw himself into a chasm.

Grace Sterling's prisoner

He did not die. The pull of the Rangers' road home dragged him after them into this world, where soldiers of Promethea found him. Grace Sterling had him locked in a cell under one of her buildings, without a word to Zordon or to the Rangers. In the summer of 1994 he is still there. He passes the time by telling her about the Rangers he has killed.

At the end of that summer Billy Cranston found the cell. Early in September 1994 the Saba of his own world, who had been living at the Command Center, stole in to put an end to him. Drakkon got loose in the struggle. He struck off Saba's head, worked what was left into one of Rita's incantations to open a way out, then took the blade with him.

The murder of Tommy Oliver

His link to the Power was still broken. He went to the Temple of Power, passed Ninjor's trials, kept his purpose to himself, then had his powers mended by a Ninjor who took him for a Ranger in need. He repaid Ninjor by carrying him off in a jar.

Then he went looking for Tommy Oliver. That evening Tommy had taken Kimberly Hart out on their first proper date. She had walked away from an awkward goodnight, thought better of it, then turned back. She found Drakkon standing over Tommy in an alley, with the blade that had been Saba through his back. Tommy died in her arms.

The murder tore something in the Power itself. It left the Rangers of every later year cut off from one another, each team in a time of its own. Drakkon went home to his army, then set out to rob them one team after another. He wanted power enough to break into the Morphin Grid. The Rangers of all those years stormed his tower on the Moon of his own world. Rita herself burnt a green candle against him there. Finster-5 got him away from it. Drakkon broke his servant's neck, then took every stolen power into himself at once.

The world he made

With all that power he broke into the Grid. He beat the Emissaries Three, who speak for the Morphin Masters, then took from them the heart of a Morphin Master. With it he unmade everything: this world, his own, every other. In their place he made one world to his own liking. In it he was young, a hero whom everybody loved. Zordon was his father there, Rita his mother. The Rangers were ordinary people.

He had reckoned without an arrow. A year earlier his Ranger Slayer, set free from his spell, had shot the young Tommy Oliver with a splinter of the Chaos Crystal. It held Tommy's spirit between the worlds when he died. Now that spirit walked into Drakkon's new world, woke Tommy's friends, then fought him on equal terms. Tommy won.

He told Drakkon why he had lost. Of all the Tommy Olivers in all the worlds there are, Drakkon was the only one who had gone wrong, which he had never been able to bear. Tommy offered to take him out of the made world before it fell to pieces. Drakkon refused. The Rangers mended everything without him.

The wreck

He was left by himself in the ruin of the world he had made. By this world's calendar he was there three months. He said afterwards that it had been longer than anybody could imagine. He built a town of dummies out of sports equipment, to have somebody to talk to. He talked to a Saba who was not there.

The Red Emissary came into the ruin to look for him. An Empyreal, one of the three world-burning giants that served Zartus of Eltar, tore the Emissary to pieces. Then the Empyreals offered a bargain: his freedom, with his powers to follow, if he brought them to the Yellow Emissary, who was in hiding. He accepted.

In the middle of December 1994 he fell out of the sky beside the Command Center, inside what looked like a meteor. He was grey, scarred, half out of his wits with terror. Tommy, by then the White Ranger, knocked him senseless. Zordon had him locked in a cell under the Command Center. He remembered the whole of the war, which nobody at the Command Center could, so he used it to taunt his gaolers. He goaded Kimberly to kill him. She told him that he was not hers to kill. Tommy would not go down to speak to him at all.

The Omega Rangers

Early in January 1995 the Omega Rangers came to Zordon about the Empyreals. Jason, Zack and Trini wanted Drakkon for a guide. Zordon refused. They took him anyway, with a collar on him.

When the Horrid, a swarm of ghostly parasites that feed on life, crippled the Omega Rangers' ship, he offered to sell his keepers to the Horrid King, then stabbed the King in the back. Trini came nearer to trusting him than anybody had in years. She told him that it was not too late. He asked whether he had 'Idiot' stamped on his forehead. She laughed, then told him that he need not be the man he had been.

He was the Empyreals' man throughout. He led the Omega Rangers to the hiding place of the Yellow Emissary, whom the Empyreals killed. He slipped his collar, took back his coin, put out the eye of the Omega Rangers' robot, Xi, then flew off in their ship. The Empyreals burnt that world behind him, with the three still on it.

He had not quite left them to die: he put Xi's body where Safehaven would find it, with the means of fetching them home. In the middle of January, in the last hours of the Eltarian War, he came back at the head of the Horrid, whose master he now was. The last Empyreal refused his offer of a partnership, so he turned the Horrid loose to drain it, which let the Blue Emissary finish it.

The Drakkon Rangers

At the beginning of February 1995 he walked into the vault on Safehaven. He let out Kiya Kyatyl, the Omega Ranger who had turned on her own team, then took her through the great Arch there to his own world.

It was not his any longer. The Ranger Slayer had ruled in his place, pulled down Deadlock, freed Jason. The Sentries were gone, their coins burnt out. Creatures of lava that served Dark Specter were overrunning what was left. His own Kimberly took him prisoner on arrival.

He proposed that they should all become Rangers, though he would not give up the Dragon Coin. Finster-5 made the suits. The Drakkon Rangers were Drakkon in green, Bulk in red, Trini in yellow, Scorpina in black, Kiya in blue and Kimberly in pink. When the horde broke into their stronghold, Kimberly held the hatch so that the others could get away. They thought her lost. Drakkon swore to carry the fight to Dark Specter.

Death in the Grid

The Drakkon Rangers came into this world in the first days of February 1995, just as Dark Specter did. Dark Specter's corruption was turning every Ranger who morphed. It could not turn Drakkon, because the white half of his power came from the same light as Tommy's.

He went into the Grid alone. Inside he found an image of his own world, with the Ranger Slayer waiting in it: alive, corrupted, Dark Specter's creature. He threw the Dragon Dagger at her with his White Tiger coin set in it. Its light burnt the corruption out of her. Her arrow, already loosed, went through his heart.

Dying, he gave her the coin. His last order to her was to find the Morphin Masters, then save the universe. Joined with Tommy Oliver's own, that coin let the Rangers morph in safety, which is how the Grid came to be cleansed. When the world was mended for the second time, Lord Drakkon was among the dead who stayed dead.

pages.title: Lord Zedd
infobox: Zedd; Zophram; Zophram of Eltar; Vintra
Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'The Mutiny, Part 1' (21 July 1994)
Gold Guardian, then the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar
The emperor of all that is evil
Goldar, Finster, Squatt, Baboo, the Z Putty Patrollers
Of the Omega Rangers, on Safehaven, late in 1994
pages.html:
Lord Zedd is the warlord who was once Zophram, the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar and the mentor of Zordon. The Zeo Crystal flayed the skin from his body, and the lies of a rival turned him against everything he had served. He swore his new life to the ruin of Eltar. He is Rita Repulsa's master, and in the summer of 1994 he has not yet come to Earth's Moon. He came that autumn, banished Rita and took up her war against the Rangers himself. In 1995 he married her. In 1998 Zordon's light took the evil out of both of them.

Zophram

Zophram was a mortal Eltarian, one of the Guardians who keep Eltar under its Elders. He was the Gold Guardian, the first among them. He taught two younger Guardians, Zartus the Silver and Zordon the Bronze. Zordon had come into the Guardians from the ranks, a young spearman whom Zophram had asked for himself.

Zophram never knew that his pupil was one of the Istari, a Maia sent to keep Eltar against evil. To him Zordon was a promising young soldier, and his friend.

When the Guardians drove off an attack on the planet Artavias, the Elders made Zophram the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar. His first act was to ask that Eltar's forces should go beyond their own galaxy, to protect young worlds against Dark Specter. He meant Zordon, not Zartus, to succeed him.

The Zeo Crystal

On the moon of a young world, the Guardians fought a scouting party of Hartunians in Dark Specter's service. There they found a palace where the Bandorian monks guarded the Zeo Crystal, a thing of enormous power. Eltar took it under its protection. The young world was Earth.

Zartus had a monk lay a spell on the Crystal in secret, the Fire of Truth, so that whoever touched it would die, or worse. He did not warn Zophram.

Then an assassin of Dark Specter's poisoned Zordon. Zophram flew into a rage and struck the assassin down, but the creature had got into his head first, telling him that the Elders were a dead end. Zordon lived far longer than the poison should have allowed, and the healers of Eltar could not say why. Zophram asked the Elders to let him use the Crystal against their enemies. They refused. They were protectors, they said, not conquerors, and Zordon had known the risks.

With his friend dying, Zophram went to the moon to take the Crystal himself and end the war. When he touched it, the Fire of Truth flayed the skin from his body. It killed everything on the moon except the palace, a few soldiers, Zartus and Zophram himself, who was dying. Zartus killed the soldiers who were left, then carried Zophram off to his ship.

Lord Zedd is born

Zartus kept him alive with tubes and a mask. He told Zophram that he had been born again, stronger than before. He told him, too, that Eltar believed he had died a hero, and that the Elders had called Zordon home to be Supreme Guardian in his place. Zophram came to believe that Zordon had known what the Crystal would do to him, and had wanted him to suffer.

Zophram of Eltar died, and Lord Zedd was born. He swore his new life to the destruction of Eltar, which pleased Zartus very much. Eltar held Zophram's funeral, and Zordon became Supreme Guardian to honour him.

His skin never grew back. What can be seen of his body is raw red flesh, held together with silver metal. A silver helmet hides his face. He carries a staff with a great Z at its head.

Vintra

Zedd learnt his magic by stealth. On the planet Ilvayx a stranger calling himself Vintra was taken in by the Holy Master as a groundskeeper. He watched the priests at their forbidden spells until he knew them. Then he killed the Holy Teacher, and every priest after him, each with the priest's own spells. He left one alive, Vronin, to tell of it.

The empire

Zedd made himself an emperor, and he called himself the emperor of all that is evil. His monsters are stronger than any that Finster can make from clay. His own Putty Patrollers, the Z Putties, wear a Z on the chest; a blow there breaks them to pieces. His great war machine is Serpentera, a monstrous thing shaped like a dragon, so huge that it can lay a world waste and so hungry for power that it is always running dry.

Goldar's brother, Silverback, once plotted to overthrow him. Zedd, cloaked to hide his flayed body, struck Silverback down and made Goldar finish him. Then he sent Goldar to serve Rita Repulsa.

Rita was the daughter of Master Vile, an old enemy of Zordon's. On the planet Spearo V Zedd turned her from her father. She became the field commander of his armies, conquering world after world in his name, and his regent when he was away.

War on Eltar

For long ages Zedd made war on Eltar, as he had sworn to. Zordon, now its Supreme Guardian, stood against him, on Eltar and among the worlds around it. Eltar did not fall to him.

It was as Zedd's commander that Rita made war on Earth, some ten thousand years ago. That war ended with Rita sealed in a dumpster on the Moon, and Zordon shut in a time warp, with no body to return to. Where Zedd was for the ten thousand years that followed, nobody on Earth knows.

The Moon, 1994

In the autumn of 1994 Zedd came to Rita's palace on the Moon, angry at her long failure against the Rangers. He shrank her, sealed her in a dumpster and threw her out into space. Then he took her palace, her servants and her war for himself.

His monsters outclassed Finster's, so Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords. Zedd went after the Green Ranger first, the boy Rita had once looked on as something like the son she had lost. With a green crystal he stripped away what was left of Tommy Oliver's powers, using it to power Dark Rangers of his own until Tommy smashed it. He lost Tommy all the same. In October 1994 Tommy came back as the White Ranger, the leader of the team.

Serpentera overpowered the Thunderzords, but it burnt power so fast that it could never finish them off. When the Rangers went to a far planet for the Sword of Light, it laid most of that world waste before its power ran out. With the Sword, in November 1994, Zordon gave three new Rangers the powers of Jason, Zack and Trini, who were leaving for a peace conference in Geneva.

Zedd had cause for his anger. In the spring of 1994 Rita had gone to war in Japan beside other invaders, the Xiliens of Planet X. Godzilla had ended by fighting on the Rangers' side, so that she lost.

The Omega Rangers

Late in November 1994 Zedd hired Dayne, a Sirian bounty hunter, to destroy Zordon's Rangers. Dayne wounded Tommy Oliver badly and ran the Thunder Megazord through. Then a team of strangers, the Omega Rangers, boxed him up and took him away. Next they stormed the Moon Palace. Zedd beat their red leader on foot and grew to giant size, whereupon the Red Omegazord came down on top of him.

He woke on Safehaven, a world very far from the Moon, shut in a great dumpster in a chamber lined with copper. Goldar kept the broken Z Staff, hiding on Earth with Squatt, Baboo and Finster in an empty petrol station. There he used it to turn a school bus into a monster. Zordon was not pleased to see Zedd go: he was an enemy Zordon could manage.

Early in December Kiya Kyatyl, one of the Omega Rangers, turned on her team and emptied the cells of Safehaven. In the confusion Dayne let Zedd out. They were even now, Dayne told him, then went his way. Zedd took back his staff and swore to rebuild.

The Dark Rangers and the dome

In the middle of December Zedd sent down the Psychoslug, a monster that let the Rangers hit it with their Power Blaster on purpose. Its shell carried the charge home to the Moon, into a new Green Chaos Crystal. With it Zedd made Dark Rangers again, this time out of his own household: Squatt, Baboo, Goldar and Finster, with a Rita whom Finster had made out of clay as their red. Their Terrorzords joined into a giant that began to tear Angel Grove apart. Then a Green Ranger whom nobody knew, Matt Cook, came down on Zedd in the street and smashed the crystal. The Dark Rangers lost their powers. The crystal burst in Zedd's face, which left him stronger than ever.

Over Christmas he shut the whole of Angel Grove under a dome of green Chaos energy. Inside it his Putties mended the streets while his monsters kept order, so that a good many people seemed content. Grace Sterling of Promethea, with Matt beside her, appeared to come to terms with him. Then Grace told him to his face that she had never changed sides, and Matt brought the dome down. Zedd said that he had only meant to show the city what life would be like without Rangers.

He went home to the Moon with a prisoner, Zelya, a Guardian of Eltar who had been living in Angel Grove as a schoolgirl called Candice Clark. He told her that he had once been Zophram. He told her, too, that Zartus had raised the Empyreals, the giants that were burning worlds. She carried it to Zordon. When Zordon called him, Zedd said that he had told her so that Zordon would know how alone he was.

Zartus

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus smashed Zordon's tube, then claimed the Earth for Eltar. He warned Zedd to keep out of it. Zedd sent his generals to make sure that Zordon did not come back. Then the Empyreals destroyed the Moon Palace with Zedd inside it, as everybody supposed. Goldar, Squatt, Baboo and Finster, believing him dead, threw in their lot with the Rangers.

He was alive in the ruins. Zordon found him there, come in a body of metal for the Zeo Crystal in the caves beneath the palace. The two of them fought. Then Zordon laid down his weapon, telling Zedd to strike. Zedd did not. In that moment he understood that Zordon had never betrayed him, and that the Fire of Truth on the Crystal had been Zartus's work from the first.

When Zartus came to the caves, the two old Guardians turned on him together. Zartus was about to kill Zedd when Zordon drove a piece of the Zeo Crystal into his chest. Zedd stood over Zordon, who was spent, then let Alpha 5 carry him away. Afterwards Zedd gathered his court in the ruins and hid the palace from sight.

Mistress Vile

Early in February Rita came back as Mistress Vile, Dark Specter's general. On the Moon she beat Zedd with an army of Thralls. He sent out a call for help, so the Rangers came. Matt Cook held her off while they got Zedd's people away in Serpentera, and she took the Zeo Crystal. Zedd himself was brought in hurt, to be held at Promethea. He broke out, took up powers of his own as a Ranger, then fought Dark Specter as one.

Dark Specter cast Rita off and very nearly killed her. Zedd saved her. Then he shut her in a small dumpster. Within days it came back to the Moon, where Finster let her out.

When the Rangers cleansed the Grid the world was mended for the second time in six months. Zedd kept no memory of anything since the dome: not Zelya, not Zartus, not the moment on the Moon, not what he had done to Rita. Rita kept none either. That is why neither of them ever spoke of it afterwards. He never again knew what Zartus had done to him.

Rita, Rito and Master Vile

Early in 1995 Rita came back. While Zedd lay in the chamber where, once a century, he renews his evil, she gave him a love potion that Finster had made. He fell in love with her, and in February 1995 they were married.

The potion never took away his will. He tried to master her, and he wanted heirs. When at last the potion was undone, he found that he loved her anyway. They quarrelled for the rest of their wicked days.

In September 1995 Rita's brother, Rito Revolto, came to live with them. Zedd thought him a fool, and it made him furious when Rito called him 'Ed'. In November 1995 Rita's father, Master Vile, came to the Moon, angry about the marriage, and he had nothing but scorn for his son-in-law.

Master Vile turned back time on Earth with his Orb of Doom until the Rangers were children, then went home. Zedd and Rita stayed. In February 1996 they destroyed the Power Coins. Rito and Goldar stole the Zeo Crystal, leaving a bomb that destroyed the Command Center.

The Machine Empire and Dark Specter

In April 1996 the Machine Empire of King Mondo came to conquer Earth. Zedd and Rita fled to Master Vile in the M51 Galaxy. In October 1996 they came back to the Moon in a motorhome, meaning to take back their empire. In November they sent Mondo's family a present, as a peace offering. It exploded when Prince Sprocket opened it, crippling the Empire's leaders, and Mondo swore revenge.

In 1998 Zedd and Rita joined Dark Specter's alliance. At his council on the Cimmerian Planet, Zedd drank to the capture of Zordon. He was caught spying on Andros, the Red Space Ranger. When the alliance struck at the whole universe in November 1998, he and Rita invaded the Vica Galaxy. They took the Gold Ranger prisoner.

The wave

Then Zordon's light went out across the universe in a single wave. It did not destroy Zedd. It made him human, with the evil gone out of him, and he danced with Rita.

Serpentera outlasted its master's wickedness. In 2002 the last generals of the Machine Empire dug it out of the Moon, meaning to destroy Earth with it. Tommy Oliver gathered the Red Rangers, ten in all, to stop them, and they did.

In 2007 Thrax, a son of Zedd and Rita whom nobody had known of, set out to restore his parents' old empire. The Sentinel Knight defeated him.

In the saga

Lord Zedd has not appeared or been named in the saga. He came to the Moon in the autumn of 1994, a few weeks after the Dursleys' news of 20 August showed the Green Ranger swaying on a car-park roof in Angel Grove, his powers running out.

pages.title: M-EPIC
infobox: Delta Green: Targets of Opportunity (Arc Dream Publishing, 2010)
Canada's secret section for the unnatural
Using sorcery far more freely than Delta Green
pages.html:
M-EPIC is Canada's secret section for the unnatural, the nearest thing the country has to Delta Green. It hides behind the name of a dull government body, the Environmental Policy Impact Commission. It began in 1903 as Detachment M and was made over in 1946. It is far readier than Delta Green to use sorcery against what it hunts.

Detachment M

Detachment M was set up in 1903, and it watched over Canada's dealings with the unnatural for more than forty years. In 1946 it was made over. In time it took the name M-EPIC, with the cover of a commission on environmental policy.

Its methods

Delta Green treats sorcery as a last resort, because of what it does to those who use it. M-EPIC uses it far more freely.

Beside PISCES in Britain and GRU SV-8 in Russia, M-EPIC is one of the few bodies outside the United States that know anything at all of the unnatural. None of the heroes of Canada is known to have had any dealings with it.

pages.title: Mad Jim Jaspers
infobox: He could bend reality to his will
The warp of 1983 to 1984, which most of Britain has forgotten
pages.html:
Mad Jim Jaspers was a bank robber on the crooked Britain beside this one, the world the Captain Britain Corps numbers 238, who was secretly a politician and a mutant who could bend reality. This world's Jaspers, Sir James Jaspers, could do the same, and he bent Britain nearly to breaking in the winter of 1983 to 1984. Captain Britain could not lay a finger on either of them. The Fury, a killing machine from the crooked world, killed this world's Jaspers in May 1984. Most people in Britain have since forgotten that any of it happened.

The crooked world

On the crooked world James Jaspers was a politician who sent the Fury and the Status Crew, a force of armed police, to hunt down that Britain's heroes. For his own amusement he robbed banks dressed rather like the Mad Hatter, with a gang of followers got up as characters from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Captain Britain stopped one of his raids in September 1981.

Jaspers was a mutant of terrible power. When Saturnyne's fluid took hold of that world, early in 1982, he let it out. His Britain began to bend and run like wet paint. The court of many worlds that Saturnyne served destroyed the crooked world in 1983 rather than let the warp spread.

The warp

In 1983 this world's Sir James Jaspers was a politician who wanted Britain rid of its superhumans. His speeches sounded very like the ones that had begun the purge on the crooked world, which frightened Captain UK, who had heard them before. Over the winter of 1983 to 1984 his own power woke.

The warp spread across Britain. Streets changed overnight, while the laws of nature began to fail. Jaspers rose on a promise to rid the country of superhumans. S.T.R.I.K.E., already rotten from within, did his bidding, and people with powers were rounded up into camps. Within the warp he came to rule Britain from Downing Street. When the Vixen tried to have him killed, he turned her into a docile animal for the rest of the warp. His men killed Tom Lennox of the Psi Division. Captain Britain, who went to face him alone, could do nothing against a man who could change the ground under his feet.

In May 1984 the Fury found him. The two of them fought through shape after shape, and the world strained at the seams around them. Merlin fell in that fight, holding the world together. At last the Fury carried Jaspers out of the world altogether, where there was no reality for him to bend, and killed him there.

Britain mended, as Roma had promised it would. Most people forgot. The records of those months do not agree with what the few who remember will say, and it is hard to find anybody now who will admit to having been ruled by him. The children whom the warp had changed were left. They are called the Warpies.

The Fury

The Fury was a machine built on the crooked world to kill superhumans, a thing of metal and living tissue that learnt from every fight. It changed itself to win the next one. Jaspers claimed it as his own work. It killed nearly every hero on that world, then Jackdaw of the Fair Folk, then Captain Britain, in the summer of 1982.

It survived its world's destruction and followed Captain UK across. In the autumn of 1983 it attacked her at Braddock Manor. Two of the Special Executive died fighting it before Brian could bury it in the caverns under the house. It dug its way out, stronger than before, for it had fed on the great computer that lay beneath the Manor. It killed Jaspers, then nearly killed Brian, until Captain UK tore it apart.

A trace of it lived on in a tramp called Sid, whom it had touched on its way through. In 1985 it turned him into a monster in its likeness, and Brian killed him without knowing who he had been.

The Crazy Gang

During the warp Jaspers made himself a new gang of friends, since he had none. They were the Jester, the Knave, Tweedledope, the Red Queen and her Executioner, a silent machine in a hooded robe who carries an axe. They outlived him. They are all of them quite remarkably stupid.

In 1985 they advertised in the personal columns for a criminal mastermind, and the assassin Slaymaster used their advertisement to trap Captain Britain. In 1988 Tweedledope's machine changed minds between the gang and the Excalibur team in Arcade's Murderworld. In 1992 the gang made a small Wonderland of its own in Britain, where some old people had gone missing, and Captain Britain met nothing there but violence.

pages.title: Magda Eisenhardt
infobox: Witchcraft, taught at home by her tribe
Anya, who died in a fire; the twins Pietro and Wanda, born 1946
pages.html:
Magda Eisenhardt was a Romani witch who survived the Nazi camps and married Max Eisenhardt, the man who became Magneto. She fled from him after the death of their daughter, Anya. In 1946 she gave birth to his twins, Pietro and Wanda, on Wundagore Mountain in Transia. Then she walked out into the snow, and she was never seen again. Some accounts call her Magda Lehnsherr, after the name her husband took later.

Life

Magda was born into a Romani tribe that taught her its witchcraft at home, as the tribes teach all their own. The Nazis sent her people to the camps, where a great many Romani were murdered. She survived. After the war she married Max Eisenhardt, a Jewish survivor of Auschwitz, and they had a daughter, Anya.

Whether she ever told her husband that she was a witch, nobody knows. He has no magic of any kind. When Anya died in a fire while a mob held her father back, his power broke loose and killed the mob. Magda fled from him in horror. She did not tell him that she was carrying his children.

Wundagore

In 1946 she came to the Citadel of Science of the High Evolutionary, on Wundagore Mountain, asking for shelter from a husband of terrible power. Bova, the cow-woman who nursed the High Evolutionary's creatures, delivered her of twins. A few days later Magda left a note saying that her husband must never learn where the children were. Then she walked out into the snow. It is generally believed that she died on the mountain.

The twins were raised by Django and Marya Maximoff, of a Romani band in the foothills. Magda's magic passed to her daughter and not to her son: Wanda, the Scarlet Witch, is a witch, while Pietro is a Squib. Magneto did not learn that the twins were his until 1982, when Bova told him.

pages.title: Major Zero
infobox: The Special Air Service; the CIA's FOX unit
pages.html:
Major Zero, whose name is David Oh, is the Englishman who founded the Patriots. He was Big Boss's commanding officer in 1964, then his friend, then his enemy for forty years. In the summer of 1994 he is in his middle eighties, a sick man hidden away, while the system he built runs America's secrets without him. Hardly anybody knows that he exists.

Soldier and spy

He was born in Exeter in 1909. He served in the Special Air Service, where he came to know The Boss. Afterwards he went to work for the Americans.

He put a new idea to the CIA: a unit small enough to send one man alone into enemy country, with a handful of specialists guiding him by radio. The CIA let him try it. The unit was called FOX. Unusually for its day, it had women at its centre, for Zero chose people by their talents.

In 1962 he brought the Soviet rocket scientist Sokolov out through Berlin. That October Sokolov was handed back, as a secret part of the bargain that ended the Cuban missile crisis.

1964

FOX's first real mission was the Virtuous Mission of 24 August 1964, which was meant to fetch Sokolov out again. Zero ran it from an aircraft over Soviet territory under the name Major Tom. His man on the ground was Naked Snake. It failed when The Boss went over to the other side.

Six days later he sent Snake back on Operation Snake Eater, to kill her. FOX's survival depended on it, as did a good deal else. Snake did what he was sent to do, for which the President named him Big Boss.

The Patriots

In 1970 FOX itself rebelled, on the San Hieronymo Peninsula in Colombia. The Pentagon arrested Zero for treason, then had to let him go. That year Revolver Ocelot killed the Director of Central Intelligence. He brought Zero the records of the Philosophers' Legacy, with the names of the Philosophers themselves.

With the money Zero founded the Patriots. The others were the people who had been through 1964 with him: Big Boss, Ocelot, EVA, Para-Medic and Sigint. He meant to carry out what he took to be The Boss's will, a world made one under a single unseen authority. Big Boss was to be its hero, the face that men would follow.

The break with Big Boss

Big Boss did not care to be an emblem. Fearing to lose him, Zero had him copied. In 1972, on Zero's orders, Para-Medic cloned Big Boss without his knowledge, in the project called Les Enfants Terribles. When Big Boss found out, he walked out.

By 1974 Zero was calling himself Cipher. That year he sent a young agent, Paz, to bring Big Boss's private army under his control or else to blacken its name. She failed. In March 1975 Skull Face, who commanded Zero's own hidden unit XOF, destroyed that army's base without Zero's leave. Zero had the wounded Big Boss hidden in a hospital in Cyprus, with Ocelot to guard him.

The machines

Skull Face turned on Zero next. In 1976 he had him infected with a parasite, which began slowly to destroy his mind. Zero knew what was coming. He trusted no successor, so he had his authority handed over to computers that would run the Patriots by his rules when he no longer could. In 1977 he visited Big Boss's bedside for the last time, then dropped out of sight.

There were five computers in the end, known by initials: GW, TJ, AL, TR and their chief, JD. They did as he had taught them. Year by year they tightened their hold on America's elections, its money and, later, everything that passed along a wire.

The end

By 2014 Zero was about a hundred and five years old. He was alive only because machines breathed for him, with no knowledge of anything. That year the Patriots' computers were destroyed.

Afterwards Big Boss brought him in a wheelchair to The Boss's grave at Arlington. There he switched off the oxygen. He told Solid Snake that the hatred had gone out of him when he saw what his old friend had become.

pages.title: Margali Szardos
infobox: The Manouche, the Romani of France
The Winding Way, the witchcraft of the Szardos women
At home, by the women of her family
Fortune-teller to the Jahrmarkt, a travelling circus in Bavaria
Stefan Szardos (dead); Jimaine Szardos, who calls herself Amanda Sefton
Sorceress Supreme of the Winding Way
Beneath London, summer 1996; held afterwards in Limbo
pages.html:
Margali Szardos is a Romani witch, born in Paris to the Manouche, who walks the Winding Way, the craft that the women of her family hand down from mother to daughter. For years she told fortunes for a travelling circus in Bavaria. That is how she came to raise Kurt Wagner, the mutant later called Nightcrawler, with her own two children. She is one of the most powerful witches alive, and one of the least trustworthy.

The Winding Way

Margali was born in Paris, into a line of Romani women who had practised magic for longer than anybody could remember. She was taught at home, as the tribes teach their children, and she never went near a wizarding school. The craft of her family is called the Winding Way. It is wizarding magic, born in the blood, though it is taught in the family's own fashion. A witch who walks it climbs to heights of almost unlimited power, then falls into valleys where she has hardly any at all.

Protecting the Way, Margali says, is the duty of her blood. She styles herself the Sorceress Supreme, meaning the first of all who walk it. It is not the office that Stephen Strange holds, and he has never mistaken it for one.

The circus

In time Margali settled with the Jahrmarkt, a travelling circus in Bavaria, as its fortune-teller. Telling fortunes was the oldest disguise her people had. The Muggles who paid her to read their palms took her true sight for a fairground trick. There she had two children, Stefan and, about two years later, Jimaine.

About 1955 she found a baby with indigo fur and a tail, whom his mother had lost fleeing from a mob. She took him in and raised Kurt Wagner with her own two.

Jimaine she meant for the Way. When Jimaine, grown, wanted to leave the circus with Kurt, Margali put on the shape of the demon Belasco and killed the performer who had taken Jimaine's place in the act, so that her daughter would believe herself in danger. Jimaine stayed, and learnt her mother's craft.

Stefan

Stefan went bad. He left the circus, and in a village not far off he murdered children. Kurt tried to stop him without killing him, but Stefan died in the struggle. Margali blamed Kurt for her son's death, and she cursed him.

Revenge, 1980 to 1983

In 1980 she came for him. She drew Kurt into a world of her own making, built on Dante's Inferno, with several of the X-Men after him. Doctor Stephen Strange went in too. At the bottom of it Margali fought Strange, and the two of them were evenly matched. Then Strange turned the Eye of Agamotto on her. She was made to see what Stefan had become, and she forgave Kurt. Her daughter, it came out, had been beside Kurt the whole time, as his girlfriend, Amanda Sefton.

In 1983, low on the Way, she took power from a wand of doubtful origin. The wand had a will of its own. It set mother and daughter against Doctor Strange. He took it from them and sealed it away, which broke its hold on them both.

Cottbus and the Soulsword, 1994

In February 1994, at a low on the Way, Margali was taken prisoner at Cottbus, in eastern Germany, by D'Spayre, a demon that feeds on despair. He had come there to feed on the riots against the Romani. Kurt and Jimaine got her out. In the summer of 1994 she is climbing again.

That autumn she warned her daughter that the sorcerer Gravemoss meant to take the Soulsword, the blade of the dead Illyana Rasputina. Jimaine killed Gravemoss with the sword, then gave it to her mother, which was what Margali had wanted all along. With it Margali killed every witch and wizard who stood ahead of her on the Winding Way. She took a young body for herself.

London, 1996

In 1996 she joined the London Inner Circle of the Hellfire Club as its Red Queen. With Black Air she had Douglock's head joined to the demon that lies beneath London, meaning to drain its power through him. Instead it drained hers. Its power broke loose, and that summer London burnt. Kurt led the Excalibur team into Blackwall, Black Air's headquarters, while Jimaine sealed the demon away again. Margali faded to nothing in the fight.

Limbo

She had not quite gone. Belasco, the master of Limbo, caught what was left of her and tortured her there. Early in 1997 she slipped into her daughter's body to get away from him, and in it she left the Excalibur team, saying goodbye to nobody but Piotr Rasputin. In 1998 the two of them changed back in Limbo. With Kurt's help they beat Belasco, and Margali apologised to her daughter, then left at once. Jimaine stayed behind to rule Limbo.

pages.title: Maria of Silent Hill
infobox: A dancer from the club Heaven's Night
Three times by the Red Pyramid Thing; at last by James himself
pages.html:
Maria was a woman whom James Sunderland met in Silent Hill on 25 September 1994. She had his dead wife's face, her voice and none of her illness. She was not a living woman. The town made her out of what James wished for, as it made the Red Pyramid Thing out of what he thought he deserved.

Heaven's Night

Maria's first memory was of waking alone in Heaven's Night, a club in Silent Hill where girls danced for the customers. She had a dancer's clothes on, a revolver beside her and no idea how she had come there. The town outside was empty. She thought of shooting herself. She went to look for somebody instead.

She came to an old house, the Baldwin mansion, where a man spoke to her from behind a locked door. His name was Ernest Baldwin. He had lost a small daughter, Amy, years before, and wanted her back.
