Maria ran his errands through the house, fetching him a bottle of white oil that he needed. In return he gave her a warning. A man called James was looking for her. He was a bad man, said Ernest, and it was not her he was really looking for.

When she opened the door at last, the room behind it was empty. Maria went down to the park by the lake to wait for James.

With James

James Sunderland took her for his wife, then saw that she was not. She was bolder than his wife had been. She flirted with him and teased him. She said she had never heard of any Mary Sunderland. Yet she knew things that only his wife could have known, down to the tape he had left behind at the Lakeview Hotel.

She went with him as far as Brookhaven Hospital, where she was taken ill. He left her to rest in a room upstairs. When he found her again, in the basement, she was angry that he had gone. The Red Pyramid Thing came after them down a corridor. James reached the lift. Maria did not, and he watched her die through the closing doors.

He found her alive again under Toluca Prison, sitting in a cell with bars between them. She remembered nothing of the hospital. By the time he had found his way round to the door, she was lying dead on the bed. At the hotel two Red Pyramid Things killed her a third time, in front of him.

What she was

Maria was not a ghost, nor a woman under a spell. The Otherworld of Silent Hill takes its shapes from the mind it has fastened on, and in 1994 that mind was James's. He had killed a sick wife. What he wanted was that wife as she had been before the illness, warm, well and with no reproach for him. The town supplied her, dressed as a dancer from Heaven's Night.

The deaths were supplied by the same mind. Each time he began to lean on her, she was killed in front of him. He was made to watch his wife die over again until he remembered who had killed her.

The end

When James knew the truth, he had no more use for a copy. Maria met him at the top of the hotel wearing his wife's dress. She asked him to stay with her. He told her that she was not the one he wanted. She changed then into a thing in a cage of iron, hanging upside down, with his wife's face. He destroyed it. Nothing of Maria was left.

pages.title: Maria Renard
infobox: Akumajō Dracula X: Chi no Rondo (Rondo of Blood, PC Engine CD, 29 October 1993)
The Renards, distant kin of the Belmonts
The command of four sacred beasts
The dark priest Shaft; the servants of Dracula
pages.html:
Maria Renard was a distant relative of the Belmonts who fought beside Richter Belmont in Dracula's castle in 1792, when she was twelve years old. Five years later Richter vanished, and she went looking for him. It was Maria who gave Alucard the means to set him free.

Family and gift

Maria was born in about 1780, in the country near Dracula's castle. Her family, the Renards, were distant kin of the Belmonts. By 1792 she had lost both her parents.

She had a gift the Belmonts themselves did not have. She could call on the four guardian beasts of Chinese legend: the dragon, the tortoise, the tiger and the red bird. They came when she asked, and they fought for her. The wizarding world would have called her a witch, though nothing on record connects her with its schools or its ministries.

The castle of 1792

In 1792 the dark priest Shaft and his cult raised Dracula. The vampire's servants burnt the villages near the castle and carried off a number of young women. Maria was one of them. The others were Annette, whom Richter Belmont loved, a nun named Tera and Iris, the doctor's daughter.

Richter found Maria deep in the castle, where Shaft was working a spell on her, and set her free. He told the child to go home. She flatly refused, and went on refusing until he gave in.

From then on her beasts fought beside his whip. The two of them freed the other captives one by one and came at last to the top of the castle, where Richter destroyed Dracula. The castle fell into the sea behind them.

The search for Richter

Richter married Annette. In 1796 he disappeared without a word to anybody. A year went by. Then Maria, who was seventeen by now, set out to find him, and Dracula's castle came up out of the mist in front of her.

Inside it she met Alucard, Dracula's son, who had woken from his long sleep when the castle rose. She was wary of him at first. They agreed to share whatever they learnt.

Alucard told her that a man who called himself lord of the castle was sitting in its throne room, with Belmont blood in him. Maria did not want to believe it. When she had to, she was certain of one thing: that Richter was not acting by his own will. She begged Alucard not to harm him. She gave him a pair of holy glasses that show what is hidden.

Through them Alucard saw a green orb hanging over Richter, by which Shaft's spirit held him. He struck at the orb, not the man, and Richter came back to himself. Maria took Richter out of the castle while Alucard went up into the second castle that had appeared, upside down, in the sky. There he destroyed Shaft, then his father.

Alucard

By the time the castle fell, Maria had come to love Alucard. He told the two of them that his blood was cursed, and that he meant to go back to his sleep so that it could do the world no harm. Then he walked away. Richter, who had noticed more than she thought, told her to go after him. She went.

What passed between them is not recorded, nor is anything of her later life. Alucard did go back to his sleep.

pages.title: Mary Shepherd-Sunderland
infobox: Laura, an orphan she met in hospital
Room 312 of the Lakeview Hotel, Silent Hill
Smothered by her husband, at twenty-five
pages.html:
Mary Shepherd-Sunderland was the wife of James Sunderland. She fell ill with a disease that the doctors could not cure. She spent her last years between hospital and home. In the end her husband smothered her with a pillow. It was a letter in her name that brought James to Silent Hill in September 1994, and it was her last real letter that let him leave.

Silent Hill

Mary Shepherd married James Sunderland, a clerk, and joined his name to her own. The happiest days of the marriage were a holiday at Silent Hill. The two of them stayed in room 312 of the Lakeview Hotel, with a view across Toluca Lake, which they called their special place. James recorded her there with a video camera. On the tape she talks about how quiet the town is. She has heard that the whole place was once holy ground, she says, and she can understand why. She asks him to bring her back one day. She is already coughing.

The illness

The disease, when it came, was slow. The doctors gave Mary three years at the most. Between them the disease and the drugs spoilt her looks, so that she could not stand to be looked at. They spoilt her temper too. She threw James's flowers back at him and told him to get out. Then she called him back in tears. She knew what she was doing to him, which made it no easier to stop.

James believed afterwards that she had died three years before he went to Silent Hill. He was wrong about that, as he was wrong about how she died. She was alive, in hospital, only the year before.

Laura

In the last year of her life Mary made a friend, a patient in the same hospital. Laura was seven, an orphan. Mary had no children. The child came to love her as a mother. Mary talked to her about Silent Hill.

Mary would have liked to adopt her. She said so in a letter that she left with a nurse for Laura's eighth birthday. She asked her in the same letter not to be too hard on James, who was kinder than he seemed.

After Mary's death Laura took the letter and set off for Silent Hill to find her. She had turned eight the week before. She crossed the town from one end to the other in perfect safety. A child with nothing on her conscience sees nothing there but empty streets. She thought James a liar who had not loved his wife. When he told her the truth she screamed that she hated him. All the same, she left the town at his side.

The letters

The letter that James carried to Silent Hill said that Mary was waiting for him. She never wrote it. By the time he reached the hotel the page was blank, and soon afterwards there was no page at all.

The letter she did write was meant to be read after she was dead. In it she remembers the town in her dreams. She tells him she is sorry for the things the illness made her say. She says that he has given her everything he had, that he must now live for himself, and that he made her happy.

James heard the whole of it only at the very end, when the town had finished with him. A woman with Mary's face had walked beside him through Silent Hill for most of that time. She was no part of Mary. The town had made her out of what James wanted.

pages.title: Matt Cook
infobox: Angel Grove; Florida, from the summer of 1995
His parents, Mr Cook and Olivia Cook; his younger sister, Kira
Angel Grove High School, where he captains the football team
The Dragonzord, as Promethea rebuilt it
The Dragon Dagger; the Dragon Shield
In the summer of 1994, a pupil at Angel Grove High School
pages.html:
Matt Cook is a pupil at Angel Grove High School, the captain of its football team, who went out with Kimberly Hart in the summer of 1993. That August Rita Repulsa carried him off to the Moon, leaving a Putty in his place. He worked out for himself who the Power Rangers were, and he has kept their secret ever since. In December 1994 Grace Sterling gave him the mended Dragon Coin, which made him the second Green Ranger. He was the first Ranger to show the world his face. In February 1995, under Rita's spell, he killed the woman who had chosen him.

Angel Grove

Matt was born about 1977. He lives in Angel Grove with his parents, Mr Cook and Olivia Cook, together with his younger sister, Kira. As a boy he was the new arrival at school who got Zack Taylor out at dodgeball.

At Angel Grove High School he is the captain of the football team, its quarterback. When Bulk and Skull soaked Billy Cranston, Matt offered to have the team see to them, then gave Billy his own hat. Jason Lee Scott, Zack, Trini Kwan and Billy were all friends of his before any of them was a Ranger. Rocky DeSantos of Stone Canyon is a friend from his childhood.

Kimberly Hart

In July 1993 Matt took Kimberly Hart to the carnival, on their first date. She told him about her parents' divorce, then went down with food poisoning from the fried food. They agreed to try again. A few days later Rita Repulsa was set free on the Moon. On the day of her first attack on Angel Grove everybody else ran. Matt went looking for Kimberly.

He brought her into his circle of friends as his girlfriend. She could never tell him why she kept vanishing, since Zordon had forbidden his Rangers to tell anybody what they were.

The Putty in his place

In August 1993 Rita sent a spy into Angel Grove: the Putty Infiltrator, a Putty that could wear any human face, with the monster Flog to draw the Rangers out. Matt had begun to suspect that his friends were hiding something, so he would not let Kimberly out of his sight. When Flog attacked he put himself between it and her. It threw him into a building.

Kimberly had to fight. She handed him, badly hurt, to a passer-by who promised to get him to hospital. The passer-by was the Infiltrator. The boy who woke in the hospital bed with Matt's face was Rita's creature, while Matt himself was in chains in her palace on the Moon.

She kept him there for some weeks, drawing his memories out of him so that the copy could think as he did. The copy went to school in his place, sat with his friends, even saved Billy from Goldar.

In the end he worked his chains loose with a fork, then got out of the palace. On the night of the Homecoming dance, in September 1993, he stumbled on to the stage in front of the whole school, saying that aliens had abducted him. The copy, which had been on the point of confessing to Kimberly, was unmasked. Rita turned it into a false Megazord, which the Rangers destroyed.

For a while afterwards Matt barely spoke. He would not eat. There were gaps in his memory. He kept away from his friends, even from his family.

Late in September Goldar wrecked the juice bar, hunting for somebody worthy of the Dragon Coin. Matt helped to get people out, with Kimberly beside him. For a moment he accepted her as she was, secrets and all.

The secret

Matt went back to school convinced that Rita had taken him for a reason, which the Power Rangers would be able to explain. Early in October 1993 a strange Zord, the Gravezord, attacked the middle of the city. Matt ran towards the fight, where he was very nearly crushed.

The Gravezord belonged to the Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of Lord Drakkon's world, who had come back from a later day by mistake. Matt went by himself to the place where her Zord had come down. He left Kimberly a message to say that he loved her. Then he talked to the woman who climbed out of the wreck. She was older, harder, but she was Kimberly. After that the rest was easy to work out.

At the juice bar of the Youth Center he told his five friends that he knew they were the Power Rangers. He would keep the secret whatever they answered, but unless one of them told him the truth he would not speak to them again. Zordon's rule held. Nobody said a word, so Matt walked out.

That was the end of Matt Cook as Kimberly's sweetheart. She had already decided that he would be safer away from her, so she let him go. For three weeks he spoke to none of them.

He kept his word about the secret. Some weeks later each of them apologised to the other. He became the friend she could tell things to. He hoped for a while that they might begin again, but by then Tommy Oliver had come to Angel Grove. On the day in October 1994 when Tommy came back as the White Ranger, Matt watched her throw her arms round him at the juice bar. He told her afterwards that she could always talk to him.

The second Green Ranger

By the end of 1994 the Dragon Coin was a dead thing, drained first by Rita's green candle, then by Lord Zedd's crystal. Billy Cranston took it in secret to Grace Sterling, the head of Promethea, who had been Zordon's Red Ranger in 1969. She had kept the dagger of Psycho Green, the creature her team had fought that night. With its energy the two of them brought the coin back to life.

Billy wanted it to go to somebody the team could trust. Grace persuaded him to let Promethea choose. In the middle of December 1994 Lord Zedd turned his own servants into Dark Rangers, whose Terrorzords joined into a giant that began tearing Angel Grove apart. Matt was in the street below, with a wall coming down on top of him, when Grace's teleporter snatched him away to Promethea.

She asked him to be the Green Ranger, warning him that the mended coin might kill him the first time he used it. He used it. A Green Ranger whom nobody knew came down on Lord Zedd in the street, then smashed the crystal that powered the Dark Rangers. Matt was back in a laboratory at Promethea before the Rangers could speak to him. Grace promised him 'a mutually beneficial partnership'.

He thought afterwards that he had only been lucky. Grace talked him out of that, then offered him the place for good. He gave up the football team to train at Promethea, where her people were hard on him.

The suit was not quite the one Tommy had worn. It was a darker green, heavier, more like armour, with more gold about it, on the helmet most of all. He carried the Dragon Dagger, with the Dragon Shield across his chest. Promethea rebuilt the Dragonzord for him, so that it could join with the White Tigerzord or with the Thunderzords.

For about a fortnight nobody outside Promethea knew who he was: not Zordon, not the Rangers, not Kimberly. He would fight beside the team, then vanish when they asked him to join them. Billy coached him in secret. When one of Zedd's Chaos Putties knocked Matt senseless at a music festival, Billy ran to him in front of everybody. Aisha Campbell saw it, so Billy told her the truth. Zordon, once he knew where the new Ranger came from, had a furious quarrel with Grace about the coin.

The dome

Over Christmas 1994 Lord Zedd shut the whole of Angel Grove under a dome of green Chaos energy. Promethea pulled Matt out as it closed, against his will. He told Grace that the city could not be helped by people who hid from it. Then he went back in, with the Dragonzord.

From inside the dome he broke into every screen in the city. He told Angel Grove that he would not leave it. Then he took off his helmet. He was the first Power Ranger whose name the public ever knew.

What followed looked like treason. Inside the dome Zedd's Putties were mending the streets, his monsters were keeping order, so that a good many people seemed content. Zedd offered the city peace on those terms. Matt stood beside him, with Grace, telling the Rangers to stand down. He was under no spell, he said; he wanted what was best for Angel Grove. It was a feint. Grace told Zedd to his face that she had never changed sides, at which Matt brought the dome down with the Dragonzord.

For a few weeks Matt was famous. On Ranger Station, the programme that Bulk and Skull made about the Rangers, he promised to defend Angel Grove.

Tommy Oliver

Tommy mistrusted him from their first meeting. He accused Kimberly of having known all along. He told Matt to his face that Grace Sterling was using him as Rita had once used Tommy himself. Zartus of Eltar, who was then posing as the Rangers' ally, told Tommy that the Guardians could simply take the coin away.

The Eltarian War

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus smashed Zordon's tube, then loosed his three Empyreals on the Earth. They destroyed the Command Center, the Moon Palace and Promethea's headquarters. Matt dug Grace out of the ruins, with her scientists. When the Rangers struck back, he joined the Dragonzord to Tommy's White Tigerzord, in which the two of them destroyed one of the Empyreals. They apologised to each other afterwards.

While the others went into space to fetch a new Command Center, Matt stayed to guard the Power Chamber beneath the rubble of the old one. Zordon, who had not chosen him, gave him his blessing as a Ranger. Late that month he was one of the seven Rangers who went out against the Death Ranger.

Mistress Vile

At the beginning of February 1995 a call for help came from Lord Zedd. The Rangers found him beaten on the Moon. Over him stood Rita Repulsa, who now called herself Mistress Vile, with an army of Thralls behind her. Matt stayed to hold them off while the others got Zedd's people away in Serpentera. He was taken, the Dragonzord with him.

She went to work on the thing that troubled him most, which was that he would never be Tommy Oliver. She had forged the Sword of Darkness again, the blade that had once held her spell on Tommy. With it she bound Matt to her. He led her Putties against the Youth Center, where he wounded Jason Lee Scott, who by then had no powers of his own.

Aisha Campbell admitted, while he was Rita's prisoner, how much she cared for him. The Rangers trapped him inside the Dragon Thunderzord, then broke the sword, as Jason had once broken it to free Tommy. This time it did not work. Matt lost his armour, then vanished, still hers.

The death of Grace Sterling

Mistress Vile had taken the Zeo Crystal. She meant to use it at the Arch, an old gate into the Morphin Grid in the Bermuda Triangle, to bring Dark Specter through. She had Grace Sterling there as her prisoner. She had Matt there too, with the sword's spell still on him. At the Arch, by her will, he killed Grace.

He knew what he had done. He begged Tommy to kill him. Mistress Vile gave the Rangers a choice: they could save Matt or shut the gate. They saved Matt. Dark Specter came through.

With the spell off him at last, he was a broken young man. The silence that had followed his weeks on the Moon came back, with worse. Leading a mission to Safehaven, he was seized by a panic so complete that he could not go on; it was Aisha who talked him through it. When the Rangers went into the Grid to cleanse it, Matt was not with them.

The cleansing mended the world, for the second time in six months. Nobody in it remembered the dome, the Eltarian ships or the face of the Green Ranger. Matt remembered all of it, as did Terona Washington, Grace's oldest friend. Grace stayed dead. The mended world believed that she had been lost with a Promethea research ship in the Bermuda Triangle.

The end of the Green Ranger

At the end of February 1995 the Wizard of Deception, the sorcerer who had made Rita's green candle, came for the Dragon Coin. He took it from Matt to arm a copy of Tommy Oliver that he had made. When the copy was freed of the Wizard's spell he stayed in the Angel Grove of the 1700s, where the coin stayed with him, together with the Dragonzord.

Matt did not try to get it back. He had killed Grace with that coin on his chest, so he said that he was glad to see it go. He was close to Aisha Campbell that spring. In the summer of 1995 the Cooks moved to Florida. Matt kept the Rangers' secret.

pages.title: Maxim Kischine
infobox: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance (Game Boy Advance, June 2002)
A spirit born of the relics
pages.html:
Maxim Kischine was the closest friend of Juste Belmont, and his rival. In 1746 he went looking for the relics of Dracula's body, meaning to destroy them. They took possession of him instead. They raised a castle round him, and they very nearly cost him both his friends.

Juste's rival

Maxim grew up with Juste Belmont, the grandson of Simon Belmont, and trained as a hunter beside him. Lydie Erlanger had been the friend of both of them since they were children.

The two young men were well matched, but only one of them was a Belmont. The Vampire Killer went to Juste when he was sixteen. Maxim minded a good deal more than he admitted, even to himself.

The relics

In 1746 Maxim set out alone on what he called a journey of training. His real aim was to prove himself. Half a century earlier Simon Belmont had gathered the parts of Dracula's body, burnt them and broken the vampire's curse. Maxim meant to find what was left of those relics, then to destroy them for good.

He found all six. After that he remembered nothing. The relics woke an evil spirit in him, born of their own power together with the jealousy he had kept hidden. From then on two spirits shared his body, his own being one. The relics raised a castle to house them both.

The castle of 1748

The spirit of the relics drove Maxim to carry off Lydie. While he was still himself he hid her inside the castle, out of its reach. Then he went for Juste.

He reached Juste's door in 1748, badly hurt, with two years gone from his memory. He could say only that Lydie had been taken. He led Juste through the fog to a castle that stood on no map. He was too weak to go in.

Juste met him again and again inside. Sometimes Maxim was his friend, dazed, with his memory coming back in pieces. Sometimes he was something else, which set a monster on Juste and vanished. The castle itself stood in two layers on the same ground, each the mirror of the other, to hold the two spirits.

At last Maxim remembered everything. He told Juste the truth: the journey, the relics and who had carried Lydie off. He gave Juste his bracelet.

The last fight

Dracula's servant Death meant to use Lydie's blood to make the two castles one. That would have destroyed Maxim's own spirit, leaving his body to the other. Juste destroyed Death, but he was too late to keep Lydie from the possessed Maxim, who bit her.

Juste found them in the heart of the castle and had to fight his friend. In the middle of it Maxim saw his own bracelet on Juste's wrist. The sight gave him strength enough to throw the spirit off. Driven out of him, it took shape from the gathered relics as a revenant of Dracula. Maxim carried Lydie out of the castle while Juste destroyed the revenant.

The castle sank. The marks on Lydie's neck faded before she woke. The three of them went home together.

Afterwards

Nothing more is recorded of Maxim. Among the Kindred his story is told as a warning about the remains of an elder. He never drank Dracula's blood, and he was neither vampire nor ghoul. The relics alone were enough to master him.

pages.title: Maya Young
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
A city in the United States
Reporter; assistant in her aunt Grace's bookshop; later a writer
Kit Taylor; Trent Moseley; Lacey Sheridan
pages.html:
Maya Young is an American who, as a young reporter in 2008, found out about the Kamen Riders when one of them saved her life. She worked in her aunt's bookshop, wrote for a website about strange happenings, and wanted to know why people in her city kept vanishing. From December 2008 she was the closest friend that Kit Taylor and Len of Ventara had on Earth. For three weeks in 2009 she wore the armour of Siren herself. Afterwards she wrote the story down.

The reporter

Maya worked in the bookshop kept by her aunt Grace. Her friend Trent Moseley, who is clever with computers, worked there too. Her other great friend was Lacey Sheridan. In her own time Maya wrote for WayAboveTopSecret.com, a website given over to conspiracies, sightings and things that could not be explained.

The story she was chasing in 2008 was a run of disappearances. People were going missing all over the city. On the website the talk was of monsters seen in mirrors.

Through the glass

On 13 December 2008 mirror monsters came for Maya herself. A boy she did not know, Kit Taylor, tried to shield her. An armoured man, Len of Ventara, drove the monsters off. A month later she tracked Kit down, to offer him help in finding his missing father.

She kept her word. In February 2009 she and Trent Moseley slipped into a hospital, acting on a tip from an unseen source who signed himself JTC. There they found Frank Taylor lying drained in a bed. The same month a monster dragged her into Ventara. Len fetched her back, then told her the whole history of the Kamen Riders. She was able to warn Kit in time that Drew Lansing was working for Xaviax.

JTC turned out to be James Trademore, the Rider called Strike. He had been feeding her news for his master's purposes all along.

She did more than report. On 4 September, while Kit fought three Riders at once, she got his helpless father away from Strike.

Michelle Walsh

Early in 2009 Maya was taken on as assistant to a senior reporter, Michelle Walsh. It did her no good. In April Michelle Walsh had her dismissed from the website, on the charge that she had faked her evidence. She went on asking Maya what she knew.

Lacey Sheridan thought the whole business of armoured men was nonsense until 22 August, when Albert Cho put on his armour in the middle of the bookshop, in front of her and Trent Moseley. Soon afterwards Michelle Walsh tricked her into copying the files on Maya's computer. Lacey owned up to it at the end of September, and her friends forgave her. Maya wiped the files, but the No-Men already had them.

Michelle Walsh was no reporter. She was an agent of the No-Men, a secret office of the American government. In October the No-Men seized Kit. Maya went into their headquarters after him with Len and Kase. At the end of the month they took her as well, with Trent Moseley and Lacey Sheridan. On 7 November the two sides made common cause.

Siren

By the middle of November Kit and Kase had both been vented, so only one Rider was left. Eubulon, the Advent Master, altered the lock on Kase's Advent Deck so that it would open for Maya. On 14 November she became Kamen Rider Siren, with the swan Blancwing as her beast. Len trained her. She destroyed one of Xaviax's beacons the same day.

On 5 December, with Kase back from the Advent Void, Maya returned the deck to her.

The mirror

On 18 December 2009 Eubulon's Riders needed a way into Xaviax's stronghold. Maya went in with Trent Moseley, without armour, to open one through a mirror. The thirteen Riders came through it. Xaviax was destroyed that day.

Afterwards Maya wrote a book about the Kamen Riders, a story for children, which told what had become of them all. It was launched at her aunt's bookshop. Trent Moseley, who had been made to choose between prison and a post with the No-Men, stayed with the No-Men. Lacey Sheridan preferred to stay out of it.

pages.title: Mechagodzilla
infobox: A fighting machine in the shape of Godzilla
The people of the Third Planet of the Black Hole
1974, on Okinawa; rebuilt, then destroyed again in 1975
pages.html:
Mechagodzilla is a machine in the shape of Godzilla, built of space titanium by the people of the Third Planet of the Black Hole. They sent it against Japan in 1974 under a skin of false flesh. Godzilla destroyed it that year, then again in 1975.

The false Godzilla, 1974

In 1974 Nami Kunigami, a priestess of the old Azumi royal house of Okinawa, had a vision of a monster burning the cities. Soon afterwards Godzilla came out of the side of Mount Fuji. He was not behaving like himself. Anguirus, his oldest friend, attacked him on sight. Then the real Godzilla arrived. His breath burnt the skin off the other, showing steel underneath.

The machine belonged to invaders from the Third Planet of the Black Hole, who pass for men but have the faces of apes under their masks. Their leader on Earth, Kuronuma, ran it from a cave on Okinawa. It could fly. It had a rocket in every finger, a beam in each eye, with a wall of force round it that nothing could get through.

An old prophecy of the Azumi said that two monsters would save the people. One was Godzilla. The other was King Caesar, the guardian of Okinawa, a great beast like a temple lion that slept inside a cliff until Nami sang it awake.

The two fought Mechagodzilla on the shore. Godzilla made a magnet of his own body, dragged the machine out of the air, then twisted its head off. An Interpol agent called Nanbara blew up the invaders' cave with Kuronuma in it.

The second Mechagodzilla, 1975

A year later the invaders came back, under a commander called Mugal, to rebuild the wreck. They had help. Dr Shinzo Mafune was a biologist who had been driven out of his profession for claiming that a dinosaur lived in the sea, where he could control it. The dinosaur was real: Titanosaurus, a gentle creature when it was left alone. Mafune wanted revenge on the men who had laughed at him.

His daughter, Katsura, had been badly hurt in one of his experiments. The invaders had saved her life by rebuilding her as part machine. Now they put the controls of Mechagodzilla inside her body. The machine attacked Tokyo with Titanosaurus beside it, until the two had Godzilla buried in a ravine.

Interpol had found that Titanosaurus could not bear sound of a very high pitch, which it used to drive him off. Mafune was shot in the fighting. His dying cry brought Katsura back to herself, whereupon she shot herself to stop the machine. Godzilla threw it into the ravine, where it blew up.

In April 1975 Interpol asked the American industrialist Tony Stark to examine what was left of it. Iron Man was cutting samples of space titanium from the wreck when Godzilla came back up the valley for a last look. Iron Man shut off his weapons, then stood quite still until Godzilla had gone. What Stark learnt from the wreck went into Red Ronin three years later.

pages.title: Meggan
infobox: About 1963, in a blizzard near Fenborough, England
Romanichal travellers; her parents have never been found
Empathy; shape-changing; flight; command of the elements; she can take on other people's powers
Brian Braddock, Captain Britain; married in Otherworld, 19 August 1998
The Excalibur team (1987 to 1998), as a founder
pages.html:
Meggan is an English mutant whose body answers to the feelings of the people around her. Born to a family of Romanichal travellers who thought her a monster, she grew up hidden in a caravan, watching television, until Captain Britain found her. She loves him, and he loves her. She settled into the shape of a beautiful young woman with long golden hair because that was how he saw her. She was a founder of the Excalibur team in 1987, and in 1998 she married Brian in Otherworld.

A child in a caravan

Meggan was born about 1963, in a blizzard, near Fenborough station in England, to a family of Romanichal travellers. The cold made her grow fur at once, and her family were horrified. The more they feared her, the more monstrous she became, with webbed fingers, antennae, claws and wings of skin. An old fortress near Fenborough was said to be a place of dark magic, so the family took her for a cursed thing.

They hid her in their caravan, where she watched television from morning to night: Doctor Who, Quatermass and Gerry Anderson's puppets. It was all the schooling she ever had, and she grew up barely able to read.

Captain Britain, 1984 to 1987

In 1984 she met Captain Britain. She fought him at first, then made friends with him, then fell in love with him. With him she first met the Technet. A telepath named Alison Double told her that her soul looked as beautiful as a butterfly. Soon afterwards, in a fight, she settled into the shape that pleased Brian best, a shapely young woman with long golden hair. She has kept it ever since.

Brian fell in love with her in turn, though their courtship was long and stormy. In time they settled together in a lighthouse on the west coast of England, the Braddock Lighthouse.

The Excalibur team, 1987 to 1991

In December 1987, when Brian shut himself up with his grief for his sister, Meggan went to Muir Island for Kitty Pryde's advice. The Technet carried her off from there with Kitty. Freed in London, she sat by the campfire in the Highlands with the others and became a founder of the Excalibur team. In 1988 she set about turning the lighthouse into its headquarters.

Life with the team taught her a great deal. At first she did not know that Victor von Doom was anything to be afraid of. In Manhattan, over the winter of 1988 to 1989, the demons out of Limbo made her their Goblin Princess, and she enslaved Brian before Kitty set them both free. Ashamed, she ran off for a day among the young people of Coney Island, who comforted her without knowing who she was.

On the journey across the worlds her mind was linked for a time with Rachel Summers's. She saw worlds where other Meggans had become Captain Britain, or died. In 1990 a dark enchantment turned her for one night into a bat-winged creature that attacked her friends, until Doctor Strange drew it out of her. She thought of leaving the team afterwards.

Meggan has always been drawn to Kurt Wagner, and he to her. In 1991 the wraith of the Changeling took hold of her through it and made her turn on him. Gandalf, under the name of Myrd, helped her friends set her free. That summer it brought Kurt to blows with Brian.

Brian's loss, 1991 to 1994

In 1991 she and Rachel went across the Channel to look for her parents. In Germany a dying creature of an old race showed Meggan her true form. She chose to keep the face she had. In the autumn of 1992 Brian asked her to marry him, and she said yes.

In 1993 Brian was lost in the stream of time. Meggan, at Braddock Manor, would not eat or sleep. She melted into the waterfall in its grounds and stayed there. When the team moved to Muir Island, she went with them, hardly knowing where she was. Feron stayed beside her.

Early in 1994 her shape began to change, which was the first sign that Brian was coming home. She went into the stream of time with Rachel, and Brian came out of it. He came back cold and distant, calling himself Britanic. In the summer of 1994 she lives with him on Muir Island.

Powers

Meggan is an empath. She feels the moods of people, animals and even plants. She can see the auras about them too. Her body once changed with other people's feelings whether she liked it or not. She has learnt to hold her shape, and to send her own feelings out instead.

She can take almost any form, fly, become stronger than Captain Britain, copy the powers of other mutants and call on the elements. She can raise a gale, freeze the air or shake the ground. Her strength comes from the Earth itself, so she cannot use all of it without hurting the land.

Later years

Douglock, who joined the team in 1994, made himself her teacher. In later years she grew more sure of herself, took more of a lead in the team and wore a new costume. She used no more force than she needed, though she never minded frightening people.

In 1996 Brian came back to himself, and to the name of Captain Britain. In 1997 he went away again for a time. While he was gone, she and Piotr Rasputin fell for each other. Before the wedding she told Brian the truth herself.

She married Brian in Otherworld on 19 August 1998, with Roma of Otherworld presiding. The guests included the Captain Britain Corps, the Technet, the Crazy Gang and the Lightning Squad. Kitty Pryde caught her bouquet.

The Third World War

Meggan was sixty-three when the Third World War broke out in 2026. Her strength came from the Earth itself, and she had always held back from using all of it, for fear of hurting the land. In the war she used all of it at last, to shield a town from a storm of fire, and it killed her.

pages.title: Meryl Silverburgh
infobox: Roy Campbell; by repute his brother, Matt Campbell (died 1991)
pages.html:
Meryl Silverburgh is an American girl of about eight in the summer of 1994, the niece, as she believes, of Colonel Roy Campbell. She grew up wanting to be a soldier of FOXHOUND. In 2005 she was caught up in the Shadow Moses incident on her first posting, where she fought beside Solid Snake. In 2014 she led an Army team against the private armies of Liquid Ocelot.

Family

Meryl was born about 1986. The man she knew as her father, Matt Campbell, was killed in the Gulf War in 1991. She was brought up in a family of soldiers to admire her uncle Roy, with the unit he served in, FOXHOUND. She trained herself for the Army from girlhood.

She did not know that Roy Campbell was her real father.

Shadow Moses

She joined the Army straight from school. In 2005, at eighteen, she was sent as a last-minute replacement to Shadow Moses Island in Alaska. The soldiers there mutinied the day she arrived, led by the renegades of FOXHOUND. Meryl would not join them, so they locked her up.

She got out by knocking down a guard, Johnny Sasaki, whose uniform she took. Then she met Solid Snake, the soldier she had heard about all her life, who was not at all what she had expected. She had never shot at a living person. She learnt on the island.

The psychic Psycho Mantis, whose powers were quite real, took hold of her mind to turn her gun on Snake. Snake had to knock her senseless to free her. Later the sniper called Sniper Wolf shot her down, as bait for him.

Revolver Ocelot kept her alive as a lever against Snake while he tortured him. Snake did not give in. At the end the two of them escaped from the island together.

Rat Patrol

The two parted afterwards. Meryl stayed in the Army. By 2014 she commanded Rat Patrol Team 01 of its Criminal Investigation Command, which was sent to the Middle East to look into Liquid Ocelot's private armies. One of her men was the same Johnny Sasaki, known as Akiba. He had loved her since Shadow Moses without daring to say so.

That was the year she learnt who her father was. She would not speak to Roy Campbell, least of all after he appeared to have married a woman half his age. When Liquid Ocelot switched off every soldier whose blood carried the Patriots' nanomachines, her team went down with the rest. Johnny did not. He was afraid of needles, so he had never had the injections.

She fought her way through the warship Outer Haven beside Snake. Then she held a passage with Johnny against all comers while Snake went on. Johnny proposed to her there. They were married soon afterwards. Roy Campbell, forgiven, gave her away.

pages.title: Michael Kaufmann
infobox: Director of Alchemilla Hospital, Silent Hill
The drug PTV, made from White Claudia
The Order of Silent Hill, through Dahlia Gillespie
13 September 1983, dragged down by Lisa Garland
pages.html:
Dr Michael Kaufmann was the director of Alchemilla Hospital in Silent Hill, and the partner of the town's cult in a profitable trade in drugs. For seven years he kept the burnt child Alessa Gillespie alive in his basement as part of the bargain. He believed in very little. In September 1983 he was the man who forced the Order's god out into the open, where it could be killed. He did it out of spite, and it did not save him.

The hospital and the drug

Kaufmann was born about 1933, and by the 1970s he was running Alchemilla Hospital. He was a realist who did not believe in magic. He believed in money. The Order of Silent Hill grew White Claudia, a marsh plant whose seeds bring visions. Kaufmann had it made into a drug called PTV, which was sold for the most part to the summer visitors.

The Order asked for favours in return: death certificates that said what it wanted, drugs diverted from the dispensary, patients nobody was to ask about. Kaufmann obliged.

Alessa

The largest favour came in the summer of 1976, when Dahlia Gillespie brought him her daughter, burnt from head to foot in a rite that had gone wrong. Kaufmann signed the papers that declared the child dead in the fire. He put her in a room in the basement with a young nurse, Lisa Garland, to change the dressings. When the nurse wanted to leave, he saw to it that she needed his drug too badly to go.

What changed his mind about magic was the Order's enemies. The mayor who campaigned against PTV died suddenly. So did a narcotics officer, of a failed heart, with no history of heart trouble. The officer had been sending what he learnt about PTV to a federal narcotics agent, Hollis Tibbetts, who belonged to Delta Green. Kaufmann concluded that Dahlia could kill by ritual. He went on working with her, since it paid, but he took a precaution. He got hold of aglaophotis, the red liquid that drives out demons, and hid it where only he could find it.

1983

When the Otherworld swallowed Silent Hill on 12 September 1983, Kaufmann was caught in it like everybody else. Harry Mason found him in the hospital with a pistol in his hand, as bewildered as Harry was. He claimed to know nothing. Later Harry shot a creature off him in a bar by the lake, then turned up the flask of aglaophotis that the doctor had hidden at a motel. Kaufmann took it from him and went.

Dahlia had no more use for her partner once she had her daughter back, as he now understood. On the night of 13 September he walked in on the birth of the Order's god and threw his aglaophotis over it. The thing was driven out of the girl's body into a shape that Harry could kill.

Kaufmann ran for the way out behind Harry. He did not reach it. Lisa Garland rose up at his feet, covered in blood, and took hold of him. The two of them went down together.

A few days later Tibbetts came to Silent Hill and found the hospital's director gone. He carried off Kaufmann's ledgers of the drug trade. He read them, then burnt them.

pages.title: Minilla
pages.html:
Minilla is Godzilla's son, hatched on Sollgel Island in 1967. He is a round, snub-nosed creature, small for a monster, who blows rings of smoke where his father breathes fire. Godzilla did not father him, so far as anybody knows: he found him as a hatchling, then brought him up.

Sollgel Island

In 1967 a United Nations team under Dr Tsunezo Kusumi was on Sollgel Island, in the Pacific, trying to control the weather. If the weather could be made to order, the world could grow more food. The experiment went wrong. A balloon of radioactive material burst too soon, the island baked, then its praying mantises grew to a monstrous size. The team called them Kamacuras.

The mantises dug up an egg, which they broke open. A baby Godzilla was inside. It had been calling out before it hatched: something had been jamming the team's radios for days. Godzilla came ashore in answer, killed two of the Kamacuras, then stayed.

He was a strict father. Minilla could manage only smoke rings, so Godzilla trod on his tail, which produced a proper jet of fire. A reporter called Goro Maki watched the lessons from the trees. With him was Saeko Matsumiya, a girl who had grown up alone on the island. When the giant spider Kumonga caught Minilla in its web, father and son burnt it together.

To get away, the team ran the experiment again, which froze the island. The last they saw of the two monsters was Godzilla lying down in the snow with his arms round Minilla, to sleep until the thaw.

Later years

In 1969 a lonely schoolboy of Kawasaki, Ichiro Miki, dreamt night after night that he visited Monster Island. In his dreams Minilla was his own size, could talk, but was bullied by a monster called Gabara. Ichiro woke from them braver than he had been. He outwitted two bank robbers who had taken him hostage.

In August 1976 the Hulk was shipwrecked on Monster Island, where he fought Godzilla for a day. Minilla ended it by wandering between them. The Hulk looked at him, lowered his fists, then sat down, at which Minilla blew a smoke ring at him. Bruce Banner woke on the beach next morning with Minilla asleep beside him.

Minilla grows slowly. In 1999 he was still small, living on Monsterland with the others. At Mount Fuji he blew a smoke ring over one of King Ghidorah's dying heads.

pages.title: Mobile Task Force Upsilon-6
infobox: Silent Hill, Maine, and whatever comes out of it
Foundation staff who have never harmed anybody
A listening post on the Brahms road, got up as a highway depot
A security officer lent to it, 22 June 1994
pages.html:
Mobile Task Force Upsilon-6 is the unit of the SCP Foundation that keeps watch on Silent Hill, in Maine. It was formed in November 1983, after half of a team sent into the town's fog had failed to come back. Inside the Foundation its people are known as the Day Trippers, from their first rule: nobody stays in the town after dark. The second rule is stranger. Nobody may serve in it who has ever killed anybody.

The fog, October 1983

The Foundation had watched Silent Hill from a post on the Brahms road since 1976. On the night of 12 September 1983 the post logged every line out of the town going dead at once. By the time it had orders to do anything, the town was quiet again. The director of its hospital was missing, and nobody would say where he had gone.

In October 1983 a team from Mobile Task Force Zeta-9, the Mole Rats, went in by day. With them went their researcher, a botanist named Dr Agnes Pelletier, and three D-class on long lines. The town was empty, quiet and grey with fog. Near the lake the lines went slack one after another. When they were hauled in, the ends were rusted through.

Two of the Mole Rats went into the fog after the D-class. Neither came back. Three days later one of the D-class walked out on the Brahms road, raving of rust, sirens and the people he had killed, who he said had been waiting for him. He died within the week. The others were never found.

Dr Pelletier and the two men who came out with her had seen nothing but empty streets. She noticed what the five who were lost had in common. All five had killed. The two Mole Rats had served in Vietnam, and the D-class had come from death row. Her addendum to the file says that the anomaly 'appears to select its subjects by their histories'. The Foundation classed the town Keter. On her plan it formed a task force for Silent Hill alone.

The Day Trippers

Upsilon-6 is the least dangerous task force the Foundation has. Its people are surveyors, clerks, botanists and photographers, chosen because none of them has ever done anybody serious harm. It uses no D-class. It goes into Silent Hill only by daylight, never alone, and it always comes out before dark. A member who stays past sundown is to be counted lost. So far none has.

Between visits it watches from the post on the Brahms road. Its instruments log the fog, the weather and the traffic. Its analysts keep count of every visitor to the town who is reported missing. In the summer of 1984 it found the beds of White Claudia in the marsh burnt by persons unknown and growing again. It took seed into containment. The seed has never sprouted anywhere but at Toluca Lake, and it is classed Safe.

The morgue, 1994

In June 1994 Walter Sullivan, who had been raised in the orphanage of the Order of Silent Hill, killed ten people in ten days. He was arrested on 18 June. Early on 22 June he killed himself in his cell, and at about the same hour the post's instruments logged a disturbance in the town. Dr Pelletier went that afternoon to claim the body, with papers from the state medical examiner that the Foundation had written itself.

That night she found Delta Green at the morgue, come for the same thing. In a minute of darkness the security officer she had been made to bring was shot dead. When the lights came back the body was gone. The Silent Hill morgue incident is the only time the Foundation and Delta Green have come to blows over the town.

Room 302, 2002

The task force never stopped looking for the body. In 2001 a journalist who had been writing about the Sullivan murders, Joseph Schreiber, vanished from his flat in South Ashfield. The flat was Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, where Walter Sullivan had been born. In the spring of 2002, while it stood empty, two of the Day Trippers measured it twice, posing as surveyors for the building's insurers. Its walls added up. A D-class lent by another unit slept in it for a week and saw nothing. The Foundation closed its file on the flat that May.

The flat was let that summer to a young photographer, Henry Townshend. All the while Walter Sullivan's body had been hanging in a hidden room behind the wall of its store room, where the surveyors had not found it.

The last addendum, 2004

In June 2004 Henry Townshend found the body behind that wall, and put an end to the rite that Walter Sullivan had worked for ten years. A few days later two men who said they came from the state took the body from the coroner at South Ashfield. They were the Day Trippers, ten years late.

Dr Pelletier wrote the last addendum herself, before she retired that year. It reclassed Silent Hill as Euclid. The town, she wrote, contains itself better than the Foundation can. After 2004 Upsilon-6 went on watching the roads, sent nobody in who had ever killed and kept the public record quiet, which the town did very well without help.

pages.title: Moira MacTaggert
infobox: Moira Kinross, in Scotland, in the early 1930s
Joseph MacTaggert, a politician; killed in 1979
Kevin MacTaggert, called Proteus; died in 1979
Geneticist; head of the Mutant Research Centre on Muir Island
Muggle: neither a mutant nor a witch
Carries the Legacy Virus, which only Charles Xavier knows
Late in 2000, on Muir Island, in an attack by Mystique's Brotherhood
pages.html:
Moira MacTaggert is a Scottish geneticist, the world's leading authority on mutation and a winner of the Nobel Prize, who runs the mutant research centre on Muir Island, off the north-west coast of Scotland. She was once engaged to Charles Xavier and has been his closest ally for twenty years. Her son Kevin, the mutant called Proteus, died in 1979; her ward is Rahne Sinclair. Since the autumn of 1993 the Excalibur team has made its home on her island, with Moira as its doctor. In the summer of 1994 she is hunting for a cure for the Legacy Virus, and she has told nobody but Xavier that she has caught it.

Early life

Moira was born in Scotland in the early 1930s, the daughter of Lord Kinross. She went into genetics, and in time she became the world's foremost authority on mutation, with a Nobel Prize to show for it.

As a young woman she met Charles Xavier, a student of genetics like herself, and the two of them became engaged. Then she broke it off, without telling him why, and went home to Scotland.

There she married Joseph MacTaggert, an old flame who went on to a career in politics. He was a violent man. After one beating she lay a week in a coma, and when she left him she was expecting his child. She never told him about the boy. Joe would not give her a divorce, so she let people believe that she was a widow.

Her son, Kevin, was born a mutant of terrible power. He could bend the world about him as he pleased, but he could live only by wearing other people's bodies, which burnt out under him one after another. His mind was not sound. Moira kept him locked in a sealed room on Muir Island, where she built her research centre, and for years she told nobody that he existed.

In 1969, in Ullapool, she delivered a baby girl whose mother died at the birth. The Reverend Craig, a Presbyterian minister of the town, took the child in as a ward of his church. She was Rahne Sinclair, and nobody told her that the minister was her father.

Muir Island and the X-Men

In time Moira and Charles Xavier became friends again. When he gathered his new X-Men in 1975 she was at his mansion in Westchester, keeping house for the team while she worked beside him. Before them he had sent four young mutants she had been teaching to Krakoa, the living island, to rescue his first X-Men. Among them was Gabriel Summers, a younger brother of Scott Summers. They were believed dead, and Xavier hid the truth of it for more than thirty years.

In the 1970s Magneto, made a baby again by a being of his own making, was left in her care on Muir Island. While he was with her she quietly altered his genes to curb his violence. Other hands made him a man again, and she told nobody what she had done.

In the late 1970s she and Sean Cassidy, the Irish mutant who had served with the X-Men, became lovers. They have been together, on and off, ever since, though they have never married.

Proteus

In 1979 Kevin broke out of his room. Wearing one stolen body after another, he made his way to Edinburgh, where he took his father's body and burnt it out. By the time the X-Men caught up with him the streets themselves were bending round him. Piotr Rasputin, whose steel body Kevin could not twist, struck him down to save Moira's life, and Kevin died.

Moira had never been able to cure him or set him free, and she grieved for him all the same. She wanted to grow him again from his cells. Sean Cassidy talked her out of it, but she kept a full record of what Kevin had been made of.

The New Mutants and the Shadow King

In 1982 Rahne Sinclair's powers woke when she was thirteen, and the Reverend Craig led a mob to burn her for a devil. Moira got her away, made herself the girl's guardian and took her to Xavier's school. She had already talked Xavier into opening his doors to a younger class, the New Mutants, and Rahne was one of the first of them.

Late in 1986 Piotr Rasputin came to Muir Island to recover, paralysed after the massacre of the Morlocks. The next year the world saw the X-Men die in Dallas. They were alive, though nobody knew it. From 1989 Moira and Sean Cassidy kept a team of their own going on Muir Island in their place.

Something else had come to Muir Island by then: the Shadow King, a mind that lives by feeding on others, which had crept into the heads of many of the people there. In the summer of 1991 he took hold of David Haller, Xavier's son, the patient called Legion, then turned his powers on the island. The research centre was wrecked. Charles Xavier, who had come home from space only that year, lost the use of his legs again.

That autumn Magneto found out what she had done to him. He carried her off to Asteroid M, his fortress in orbit, then made her use her science against the X-Men. When it was over she could not face them. Early in 1992 she left Xavier's school in shame and went home to Scotland.

The Legacy Virus, 1993 to 1994

In the summer of 1993 Piotr Rasputin's little sister, Illyana, died of the Legacy Virus, the plague that Stryfe had let loose on the world's mutants. Moira went back to Muir Island determined to find a cure.

That September the Excalibur team came to the island. Kurt Wagner, Kitty Pryde and Rachel Summers caught Spoor, an escaped Acolyte who had killed more than a hundred people, then handed him over to her. They stayed at her asking, meaning to stop trouble before it grew into disaster, and Moira became one of the team herself.

The same month Kitty brought Piotr Rasputin to the island, where Moira mended the injury that had locked him in steel. In the autumn Siena Blaze, a mutant of the Upstarts, came after Kevin's records, and failed to get them. Dr Rory Campbell, a geneticist whom Xavier had sent to help, arrived half drowned after his boat went down.

In the spring of 1994 Charles Xavier left his school in Hank McCoy's charge and came to Muir Island to work beside her. That spring Moira found that the virus had changed, so that ordinary people could catch it. Early in the summer she found that she had caught it herself, from cells taken from Illyana's body. She told Xavier, and nobody else. In July the two of them spent a day in Paris among their old haunts, where Xavier made a waiter see her as the Princess of Wales.

In the summer of 1994 she is still hunting for a cure, with Xavier beside her. She looks a good deal younger than her sixty-odd years, which she owes to longevity medicine. The team who live on her island do not know that she is ill.

The Excalibur years, 1994 to 1998

At the end of 1994 Kurt Wagner worked out the truth, and she told him. In 1995 it came out that ordinary people could catch the virus, and Muir Island was besieged by the newspapers. That summer Rahne Sinclair came home to look after her. Moira lied to her about the virus, and for a while she drank to forget it.

In the summer of 1996, when Charles Xavier became Onslaught, she forbade the team to go to America. In the autumn the Mutant Liberation Front raided the island for Xavier's secret files on his X-Men, and she held them off behind a force field. That winter, in the snow, she wrote Xavier a long letter about Joe and Kevin, then deleted it.

In the autumn of 1997 she found that the virus could now pass through the air to any mutant. She sealed herself into quarantine in her laboratory, and Rahne leapt in after her as the doors closed. Sean Cassidy had flown over from his school in Massachusetts, at Rahne's call, to talk her out of it. In March 1998 Douglock broke the quarantine open to set Rahne free. In April Moira told Hank McCoy and Cecilia Reyes of the X-Men that she had the virus. Then she put her research aside for a while.

That August she helped Meggan choose a wedding dress in London, and on the 19th she saw her married to Brian Braddock in Otherworld.

Death

After the Excalibur team broke up, Rahne Sinclair and Douglock stayed on Muir Island with her. Late in 2000 Mystique's Brotherhood attacked the island, and Moira was killed. She had been close to a cure.

Her work was not lost. Working from it, Hank McCoy finished the cure, and in January 2001 Piotr Rasputin, the man who had killed her son to save her, gave his life to set it loose.

pages.title: Moloc
infobox: Molech, to whom the Canaanites burnt children
2004, killed by missiles sent from Earth
pages.html:
Moloc is a Goa'uld System Lord whom the Canaanites and Phoenicians knew as Molech, the god to whom children were burnt. He has not changed his habits since. On his worlds every Jaffa girl was burnt alive at birth, because Moloc held that only male Jaffa could win his wars. He was killed in 2004 by missiles sent through the Stargate from Earth.

Molech

In Canaan he was Molech, and children were passed through the fire to him. He came quietly, in defiance of Ra's ban, and he kept well away from the North.

The law of Moses forbade the Israelites to give any of their children to Molech, on pain of death. Some of them did it all the same.

The Ceremony of Fire

Moloc took the practice with him to the stars. He decreed that every girl born to the Jaffa of his worlds should be burnt alive, since only male Jaffa could win his wars for him. His priests called it the Ceremony of Fire.

Ishta, one of his high priestesses, was charged with the burnings. She began instead to smuggle the babies away. She took them to a hidden world called Hak'tyl, a word that means liberation, and raised them there as warriors.

The women of Hak'tyl lived by raiding Moloc's Jaffa for the symbiotes they needed to stay alive. In 2003 they found SG-1, and Earth gave them tretonin, the drug that frees a Jaffa from needing a symbiote at all. Teal'c and Ishta grew close.

Death

In 2004 Moloc's Imperial Guard fell on a gathering of Jaffa who meant to rise against him, on the new world of the Hak'tyl. Only Teal'c, Ishta and a Jaffa called Aron escaped.

Moloc came down himself. He took Ishta prisoner and tortured her with his hand device, calling himself her god while he did it.

Meanwhile two thousand Jaffa had gathered against his temple on Goranak. As Moloc made ready to deal with them, Earth opened the Stargate and sent missiles through. Aron guided them on to Moloc with a targeting beam, and they killed him along with his guard. Teal'c saved Ishta from Moloc's First Prime, Cha'ra, who later joined the rebellion himself.

Moloc's worlds did not go free. Ba'al took them, which made him stronger than ever.

pages.title: Mongul
infobox: Warworld; the destruction of Coast City, 1993
pages.html:
Mongul is the huge, yellow-skinned alien tyrant who once ruled Warworld, a battle station the size of a planet. In the summer of 1993 his forces destroyed Coast City and its seven million people on behalf of the Cyborg Superman. They built a great engine in its crater, and that August Hal Jordan beat him in the ruins.

Warworld

Mongul first troubled Earth in 1980. He was a conqueror of great strength and greater cruelty. He had been driven from his own world, and he wanted more.

For years he ruled Warworld, an artificial planet armed to destroy others. He gave it over to gladiatorial games, in which captured beings fought to the death for his entertainment.

In 1985 he came to the Fortress of Solitude on Superman's birthday, bringing a present. It was a Black Mercy, an alien plant that fastens on its victim and holds him in a dream of the life he most wants. Superman dreamt of a Krypton that had never exploded. Batman and Wonder Woman, who had come with birthday presents too, got him free. By the end of the day Mongul was caught in the plant himself.

In 1989, far from Earth, Superman was brought to Warworld as a captive and forced to fight in its arena. It was Mongul's mistake, and it cost him Warworld.

Coast City

In 1993 Mongul allied himself with the Cyborg Superman, Hank Henshaw, and knelt to him as the master of a new Warworld. In the summer of 1993 Mongul's warship destroyed Coast City with nearly everyone in it. Machinery sown in the crater built Engine City, the first of two engines meant to turn the whole Earth into a warworld.

That August Hal Jordan, whose home Coast City had been, fought his way into Engine City and beat Mongul unconscious. At the same time Superman, returned from the dead, defeated the Cyborg Superman.

In the saga

Nobody spoke Mongul's name on the news in August 1994, but his work was there to see. A man who had lost his family at Coast City told the cameras that there had been no city left, only ‘a hole, with a… with a machine in it’.

pages.title: Monster Island
infobox: The South Pacific; later Monsterland, in the Ogasawara Islands
Godzilla, Minilla, Anguirus, Rodan and others
pages.html:
Monster Island is the island in the South Pacific where Godzilla lives, with most of the other giant monsters of the Earth. By the end of the twentieth century they had been moved to Monsterland, in the Ogasawara Islands, where the United Nations could keep watch over them.

The island

By the end of the 1960s the monsters that troubled Japan had been gathered on one island in the South Pacific, where they could be watched. Godzilla has his home there. So have his son Minilla, Anguirus, Rodan, with a number of lesser creatures.

It was never much of a prison. In 1972 Godzilla left it with Anguirus to fight Gigan in Japan, then went back of his own accord.

In 1973 an underground bomb test on Asuka Island, in the Aleutians, sent a shock through the sea bed that split Monster Island open. Anguirus fell into the crack. The island has been a broken place ever since, which the monsters leave when they please.

The island has had one human castaway. In August 1976 a freighter went aground there with Bruce Banner among its crew, so that for a day the Hulk fought Godzilla from one end of the island to the other. A Japanese survey ship took Banner off.

Monsterland

In the years after 1994 the United Nations Science Committee made the monsters a new home on an island in the Ogasawara chain, south of Tokyo. It was called Monsterland. Each monster was kept to its own ground by barriers made to suit it. The staff lived in a control centre under the island.

By 1999 it held Godzilla, Minilla, a Mothra larva, Rodan, Anguirus, Kumonga, Gorosaurus, the burrowing Baragon, the gliding Varan, with Manda. Manda was a sea-dragon, once worshipped by the Mu Empire, a drowned kingdom of the Pacific. Captain Hachiro Jinguji's flying submarine Gotengo had destroyed that empire in 1963, when it declared war on the surface of the world. Nobody has ever called the Mu Empire Atlantis, which spared it one quarrel at least.

Mahoutokoro, Japan's school of magic, stands on Minami Iwo Jima, at the southern end of the same chain of islands. What the school thought of its new neighbours is not recorded.

The Kilaaks, 1999

In 1999 the Kilaaks, an alien people who showed themselves as women in silver hoods, filled Monsterland with gas. They took control of its staff with small devices set in the skull, then of its monsters. From a base on the Moon they turned the monsters loose on New York, Moscow, Beijing, London, Paris, then Tokyo.

The crew of the moon-ship Moonlight SY-3, under Captain Katsuo Yamabe, broke their control. The monsters destroyed the Kilaak stronghold at Mount Fuji, killed King Ghidorah there, then went home to Monsterland.

pages.title: Morrigan
infobox: The Morrigan, the Irish goddess of battle
P3X-289, at the Gate of Magh Mar
Surrendered to Ba'al by early 2005; afterwards unknown
pages.html:
Morrigan is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in Ireland as the Great Queen, a goddess of battle who goes about in the shape of a crow. Among the System Lords she is known for learning other people's secrets without their noticing. In 2002 she voted with the majority to take Anubis back among them. By early 2005 she had surrendered to Ba'al.

The Great Queen

Morrigan came quietly to Ireland, in defiance of Ra's ban, and kept to the western edge of the world, well away from the North. The Irish called her the Morrigan, which may mean the Great Queen or the Phantom Queen. She was a goddess of battle and strife, who chose which warriors would die. A man who saw her washing armour at a ford knew that the armour was his own. He did not live long afterwards.

Her worship reached further than Ireland. In 2003 SG-1 came to a walled city under a dome on the world called P3X-289. Its people knew their Stargate as the Gate of Magh Mar. According to their records it had been found 563 years before in the ruins of Danaan, and it was believed to have had some part in the worship of the goddess Morrigan. It stood in their national museum of history.

The council at Hasara

Morrigan was one of the seven System Lords at the council held under truce in the Hasara system in 2002. Each of them brought a single slave. Lord Yu warned his own to have nothing to do with hers.

His slave already knew why. Morrigan's servant would try to draw out strategic information in what sounded like idle conversation. Yu had learnt this the hard way: his previous slave had let slip the whereabouts of one of his secret bases, and had died in the surprise attack that followed.

When Osiris asked the council to take Anubis back among the System Lords, Morrigan nodded her agreement with the rest. Only Yu voted against.

Surrender

After Earth defeated Anubis in 2004, Ba'al turned Anubis's Kull warriors on the other System Lords, and their Jaffa were no match for them. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that Morrigan had capitulated. Two of her fellow lords, Bastet and Olokun, were already dead. What Ba'al did with her afterwards is not recorded. It was not an ending the Great Queen of the Irish stories would have recognised.

pages.title: Mother Hydra
infobox: One of the Great Old Ones; perhaps the eldest of the Deep Ones
The Deep Ones; the Esoteric Order of Dagon
pages.html:
Mother Hydra is the consort of Dagon, worshipped with him by the Deep Ones of the sea and by the Esoteric Order of Dagon at Innsmouth. Their oaths are sworn to Father Dagon and Mother Hydra together. Nobody knows whether she is a power of her own kind or only the eldest of the Deep Ones, grown vast with the centuries.

The mother of the Deep Ones

Her name is not found in Scripture, nor in what is left of the Philistines. It comes from the sea, where the Deep Ones have kept her worship beside Dagon's for longer than any record of men. She is said to be as vast as he is, and as old. Where she lies, and whether she ever sleeps, nobody on land can say.

The Deep Ones' marriages with men are made in her name as much as in Dagon's. Children born of them grow up human, or nearly, and in middle age begin to change, until at last they go down into the sea to join their elders in cities such as Y'ha-nthlei. The Deep Ones call that going home. Her worshippers call it the gathering of her children.

Innsmouth

At Innsmouth in Massachusetts the Esoteric Order of Dagon swore its members to Father Dagon and Mother Hydra. Through the nineteenth century the town's families married into the sea. A Christian town of New England lost its churches to the Order within a generation, and its children to the sea after that. The government's raid of 1928 ended it, or most of it.

Delta Green

Delta Green has met her children often since 1928, at Innsmouth, off Alaska and elsewhere. It has never met her. Some in Delta Green believe that the Deep Ones it has caught are only the smallest and youngest of their people. The eldest, they think, have grown to twenty feet or more, and Mother Hydra is one of those.

pages.title: Mothra
infobox: A giant moth, worshipped as a goddess
Infant Island, in the South Pacific
The Shobijin, twin women about a foot tall
Egg, caterpillar, moth; reborn from her own egg when she dies
pages.html:
Mothra is the giant moth whom the people of Infant Island worship as their goddess, though she is a mortal creature like any other. Of all the great monsters she is the one who has never done harm of her own will, except in somebody's defence. She speaks through the Shobijin, twin priestesses a foot high, who sing to call her. When she dies she is born again from her own egg.

Infant Island

Infant Island lies in the South Pacific, in waters where hydrogen bombs were tested in the 1950s. It was supposed to be uninhabited. In 1961 four sailors from a wrecked ship were found there alive, with no trace of radiation sickness. The islanders, they said, had given them a red juice to drink.

Behind the burnt shore of the island there is still jungle. A people live in it who worship Mothra. With them live the Shobijin, the Small Beauties: two women, twins, about a foot tall. They speak in unison. Mothra can hear their singing from the far side of an ocean.

The Shobijin stolen, 1961

A showman called Clark Nelson, of the country of Rolisica, came to the island with gunmen. He carried the Shobijin off, shooting the islanders who tried to stop him. In Tokyo he put the twins on the stage. Every night they sang; every night the audience clapped, never guessing that the song was a call for help.

On Infant Island an enormous egg hatched a caterpillar. It swam to Japan, sinking a liner on the way. Nothing the Self-Defence Forces had could stop it. It broke down Tokyo Tower, spun a cocoon in the wreckage, then came out as a moth whose wings raised a gale.

Nelson had fled home with the twins. Mothra followed him to New Kirk City, the chief city of Rolisica, which her wings blew to pieces. He died in a gunfight with the police. The linguist Shinichi Chujo, who had been to the island, noticed that the sign of Mothra looks very like a cross. He had one painted on an airfield runway to call her down. The Shobijin were given back to her there, whereupon she took them home.

Mothra and Godzilla

In April 1964 a typhoon carried Mothra's egg to the coast of Japan, where a company called Happy Enterprises bought it from the local fishermen for a sideshow. Its owners would not give it back. The Shobijin went home without it.

When Godzilla came up near Nagoya, three Japanese went to Infant Island to beg for help. The islanders were in no mood to give it: the bomb had burnt their home, then Japan had kept their egg. Mothra came anyway. She was old by then. She fought Godzilla over the egg, was burnt by his breath, then died with one wing spread across it.

The egg hatched twin larvae. They followed Godzilla to Iwa Island, where they bound him in silk until he fell into the sea. One of the two died not long afterwards. In January 1965 the survivor shamed Godzilla, with Rodan, into fighting King Ghidorah beside her. The Justice League was on the mountain that day, with the Avengers. It was the Wasp who saw what the larva was doing, so the heroes stood aside to let her do it.

By 1966 she was a full-grown moth. That year the Red Bamboo, a terrorist army, took people of Infant Island as slaves to Letchi Island. Mothra carried them home in a great net, moments before the island blew up.

Later years

By 1999 a new larva had hatched, which was kept on Monsterland with the other monsters. The Kilaaks sent her against Beijing. Once she was free she went with the rest to Mount Fuji, where she helped to bind King Ghidorah's body in silk.

pages.title: Muir Island
aliases: the Muir Island Mutant Research Centre
infobox: Off the north-west coast of Scotland, out beyond Ullapool
Laboratories and a medical wing; cells for dangerous mutants; the Proteus Room; a runway
The Excalibur team, from September 1993 to 1998
Charles Xavier works there beside Moira MacTaggert
pages.html:
Muir Island is a small, windswept island off the north-west coast of Scotland, where Moira MacTaggert built the world's foremost centre for the study of mutants. For years it was also a prison, for her son Kevin and for others too dangerous to be kept anywhere else. Since September 1993 it has been the home of the Excalibur team. In the summer of 1994 Charles Xavier is there too, working beside Moira on the Legacy Virus.

The island

Muir Island lies off the north-west coast, out beyond Ullapool. The boatmen of that coast do not like taking strangers across. The Royal Mail calls once a month. The X-Men's aircraft come and go from the runway.

Across the water lie the Kinross woods and the Chalk & Cheese, a pub that once belonged to Moira's father, Lord Kinross. The team goes there on its nights out.

The research centre

Moira built her Mutant Research Centre there in the years before 1977. For years its sealed room held her son, Kevin, the mutant called Proteus, until he broke out in 1979. Later its cells held other mutants who could not safely be kept anywhere else, among them Spoor, an Acolyte who had killed more than a hundred people.

It has laboratories and a medical wing, where Moira mended Piotr Rasputin's brain in 1993, then his spine in 1995. In the Proteus Room the mind can be taken into visions: in 1994 Captain Britain and his sister Psylocke used it to go into the mind of their brother Jamie, who lay in a coma. In 1997 the team set up a Cerebro there, Xavier's machine for finding mutants, which weighed thirty-five tons. A crypt under the centre held Xavier's secret files on how to stop each of his own X-Men.

History

Piotr Rasputin recovered there late in 1986, after the massacre of the Morlocks. After the X-Men were seen to die in Dallas in 1987, Moira and Sean Cassidy kept a team going there in their place. Over those years the Shadow King, a mind that feeds on others, crept into the island. In the summer of 1991 he turned David Haller, the patient called Legion, against it, and the research centre was wrecked.

It was rebuilt. In September 1993 the Excalibur team moved in at Moira's invitation, and in the autumn Siena Blaze attacked the island for the records of Kevin's powers. In the spring of 1994 Charles Xavier came to work there.

In the summer of 1994 the island is the team's home, and the hardest-working laboratory in the world on the Legacy Virus. Across Britain the Friends of Humanity hold meetings in church halls under the slogan KEEP BRITAIN HUMAN, and the island keeps an eye on them.

Later years

In 1996 Black Air's helicopters came over the water. That autumn the Mutant Liberation Front raided the island for Xavier's secret files, and Moira held them off behind a force field. In 1997 and 1998 she lived sealed in quarantine in her own laboratory, with Rahne Sinclair beside her.

After the Excalibur team broke up in 1998, Rahne and Douglock stayed on with Moira. Late in 2000 Mystique's Brotherhood attacked the island and destroyed the research centre. Moira was killed.

pages.title: Mums the mummy
infobox: Mummy; one of the undying of old Egypt
pages.html:
Mums is the mummy of Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville. He was a prince of Egypt some five thousand years ago, was buried as one and has not stayed buried. He is one of the undying of old Egypt, bandages and all.

A prince of Egypt

Mums was a prince in Egypt some five thousand years ago. He is one of the undying of that country, none the worse for the centuries. Unlike the Amenti who guard the tombs, he weighs nobody's heart. A stranger who walks in on Mums is more likely to be asked to stay for dinner, as the dinner.

Some years before 1996 two archaeologists woke him from his sleep, for which he laid a curse on them both. In April 1997 they came to Hillhurst to beg him to take it off. Vexor wanted the curse for his own use, so he sent a monster to get it.

Hillhurst

How Mums came from Egypt to a house in Charterville is not recorded. He was living there when three children let Flabber out of the pipe organ on 7 September 1996, having helped to chase them into it.

In October 1997 his mother, a mummy herself, came to visit, bringing a cursed ring. It turned Count Fangula into a monstrous bat. On Hallowe'en that year Mums lured a party of local children up to the house with supper in mind. The Beetleborgs saw every one of them home.

In November 1997, when both sides were hunting for the eight Astral Coins, the Firebug coin was found in his keeping. Jo McCormick used it to call up Fireborg, the second of the Astralborgs.

pages.title: Mutant Registration Act
pages.html:
The Mutant Registration Act is the American law, introduced in 1984 by Senator Robert Kelly, that requires mutants to register their identities and powers with the federal government. In the late 1980s it was enforced by a team of mutants in government service, Freedom Force. It has never been repealed, though by 1994 it is seldom heard of.

History
