Senator Robert Kelly had long argued that mutants were a danger the government must be able to track. At the end of 1980 the X-Men saved his life from an assassination attempt by Mystique's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. It did not change his mind. In 1984 he introduced the Act, which became law the same year.

In the end enforcement fell to mutants themselves. In 1985 Mystique offered the government the services of her Brotherhood in exchange for pardons. Under the government official Valerie Cooper they became Freedom Force, the federal team that arrested unregistered mutants. Mutant rights campaigners protested, and other mutant heroes refused to comply.

Freedom Force broke up after a disastrous mission in Kuwait during the Gulf War in 1991. Since then the Act has been enforced only fitfully. It remains law.

Registration and the Sentinels

The Act asks mutants to declare themselves to the state. The Sentinels were built to find them whether they declared themselves or not, and they were mothballed after a series of incidents in the 1980s. In August 1994 the Senate Armed Services Committee prepared to hear a proposal to revive the Sentinel programme against Khan. Mutant rights groups called it 'a licence to hunt'.

pages.title: New Genesis
infobox: Orion, Lightray, Metron, the Forever People
Scott Free (Mister Miracle), raised on Apokolips
Destroyed about 2037, in the last war with Apokolips
pages.html:
New Genesis is a green and peaceful world on the far side of the universe, the twin of Apokolips. Its people are the beings who call themselves the New Gods, and its ruler is Izaya, who is called Highfather. The two worlds have hated each other for as long as either has existed. Their last great war ended in the Pact, by which Highfather and Darkseid exchanged their sons. The Pact itself ended when Highfather's son escaped to Earth. Since 1971 the people of New Genesis have been fighting Darkseid's servants there.

The world

New Genesis is a world of forests, grassland, mountains and clear rivers, very nearly untouched. Its people have built only one city on it, and even that city does not touch the ground.

The New Gods live so long that nobody is sure they die of age at all. They are far stronger than men and very hard to kill, although radion, a substance deadly to them, can do it.

Not everybody on New Genesis is a New God. The Bugs, an insect people who walk upright, live in great mounds of their own, and a good many of the New Gods treat them as vermin. One of the Bugs, the warrior Forager, has fought beside Orion.

Supertown

Supertown, the capital, floats in the sky above the forests, so that the city should not scar the land below. It is the home of the New Gods and the seat of Highfather, who rules from it with his council.

Its people travel by Boom Tube, one of the roaring doorways by which the New Gods cross the universe. It was Metron who invented it.

Many of them carry a Mother Box: a small living machine that thinks, talks to its owner in a soft pinging that nobody else can follow, and loves its owner without condition. A Mother Box can heal, open a Boom Tube or lend its owner strength. When its owner dies, it dies too. The first Mother Boxes were made by Himon, a rebel of Apokolips.

Izaya and Avia

In his youth Izaya the Inheritor was a warrior, and a general of New Genesis in its long quarrel with Apokolips. His wife, Avia, spent years trying to turn him towards gentler things.

Their last great war began when Darkseid's uncle Steppenwolf, at Darkseid's bidding, murdered Avia. He ambushed the two of them and shot her. Izaya went to war in a fury, and New Genesis went with him.

The war with Apokolips

It was the most terrible war either world has known. New Genesis bombed the fire pits of Apokolips, and Apokolips answered in kind. Before long both sides were hurling planetoids at each other. They bred monsters for the battlefield, and turned on each other beams that could slice through a planet.

Metron, the seeker after knowledge, made it worse without taking either side. He wanted the X-Element, a rare substance he needed to power his Mobius Chair, and Darkseid had it. In exchange he gave Darkseid the secret of the Boom Tube. Darkseid used it to carry the war to New Genesis.

The Source

When the war had all but ruined both worlds, Izaya went out alone into the wilderness of New Genesis, where the wind tore at him. He came at last to a wall of bare rock. As he stood before it, a hand of fire wrote on the stone.

He came back from the wilderness without his weapons, and he has never taken them up again. He took the name of Highfather, and he set about making peace with Darkseid.

The New Gods call the power that wrote on the rock the Source. It is the power they draw on, and they take it to be the origin of their own. It still speaks to Highfather in writing of fire, and he is the keeper of his people's bond with it. It once told him that to know everything is to know how much is not known. Mother Boxes are said to be in tune with it.

What the Source truly is, nobody on New Genesis claims to know.

The Pact

The war ended with the Pact, by which the two rulers exchanged their sons. Darkseid's son Orion was sent to grow up on New Genesis, and Izaya's son Scott Free was handed over to Apokolips.

Orion's mother, Tigra, was dragged away from him swearing that her son would kill his father. On Apokolips, Granny Goodness was waiting for the child from New Genesis.

Neither exchange turned out as Darkseid intended. Scott Free was raised in one of Granny Goodness's orphanages, where the children of Apokolips are trained into soldiers, and he never fitted. Himon taught him in secret, and Metron put into his head the idea of a future of his own.

In time he escaped to Earth with Big Barda, one of Granny's own Female Furies, whom he had met at Himon's meetings. On Earth he became Mister Miracle, the escape artist, and Barda became his wife in 1974. In 1987 he was one of the founders of the new Justice League.

He took his name from Thaddeus Brown, a circus escape artist who had called himself Mister Miracle. A sniper working for Intergang shot Brown while he was rehearsing an escape. Brown's assistant, Oberon, has stayed with Scott ever since.

Scott's escape broke the Pact, which gave Darkseid the excuse he had been waiting for. Darkseid had expected it all along.

Orion and Lightray

Orion grew up in Supertown as Highfather's foster son. He is the fiercest warrior New Genesis has, and he has spent his life fighting his father.

He has his father's temper, and under the face he shows the world he has something of his father's face as well. His Mother Box keeps the true one hidden, and it helps him to keep his rage in check. He flies in an Astro-Harness, and New Genesis calls him the Dog of War.

His closest friend is Lightray, who is as bright in temper as he is in power. Lightray can fly at the speed of light, or throw light as a weapon. He would always rather talk an enemy round than knock him down.

Metron

Metron is the cleverest of the New Gods, and the least attached to anything but knowledge. He belongs, he says, to neither side. He travels in his Mobius Chair, which can take him anywhere in space or time.

It was he who invented the Boom Tube, and he who gave it to Darkseid. He has a seat on Highfather's Council of Eight all the same.

The Forever People

The Forever People are five young New Gods: Mark Moonrider, Big Bear, Beautiful Dreamer, Vykin and Serifan. They ride a single Super-Cycle, and they share a single Mother Box, larger than most.

In great need the five of them call on the Mother Box together. They vanish, and in their place stands the Infinity-Man, a warrior of enormous power. When the danger is past, he goes, and the five come back.

They first came to Earth early in 1971, to rescue Beautiful Dreamer. Darkseid had carried her off, believing, wrongly, that she knew something of the Anti-Life Equation. Superman helped them to get her back.

New Genesis and Earth

New Genesis took an interest in Earth because Darkseid did. Early in 1971, on the word of the Source, Highfather sent Orion to Earth to fight his father's servants there. Lightray followed him. Through 1971 and 1972 Orion fought them wherever he found them, from the gunmen of Intergang to his half-brother Kalibak.

Highfather himself has seldom come to Earth. He prefers to send others, which is one of the very few things he has in common with Darkseid.

In the summer of 1994 the war between the two worlds is unresolved. Highfather rules from Supertown and listens for the Source. Orion has not yet killed his father, whatever Tigra swore. Scott Free and Barda live on Earth.

The end of the twin worlds

The war between the two worlds was settled at last about 2037, when Darkseid made his last war on New Genesis. It was fought as their last great war had been, with planetoids hurled across the sky and beams that could cut a planet in two. If the Source wrote anything on the wall of rock that year, there was nobody left to read it.

When it was over, New Genesis was ash, the fire pits of Apokolips had gone out and the New Gods of the twin worlds were dead. The Bugs died in their mounds. Every Mother Box died with its owner, as Mother Boxes do.

In 2155 the Enterprise NX-01 found Metron's Mobius Chair empty in deep space. Nobody aboard could follow its record, but its pictures needed no translating: two worlds, burning.

pages.title: Nick Fury
infobox: Nicholas Joseph Fury; Sgt. Fury; Colonel Fury
United States Army; sergeant of the Howling Commandos
Office of Strategic Services; Central Intelligence Agency (colonel)
Slowed by the Infinity Formula since the end of the war
Left eye, from shrapnel in the war; wears a patch
pages.html:
Nick Fury is the American soldier and spy who led the Howling Commandos through the Second World War. He has been Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., the international intelligence and law-enforcement agency, since 1965. A secret treatment called the Infinity Formula has slowed his ageing since the war, so that in 1994, at about seventy-four, he looks barely fifty. He is Captain America's oldest comrade in arms, and a long-standing, sometimes awkward ally of the Avengers.

Early life

Nicholas Joseph Fury was born in New York City about 1920, not long after the end of the First World War. He was the eldest of Jack Fury's three children. He grew up in the city with his younger brother, Jake, and his sister, Dawn. He was a man of about twenty when America went to war.

The Howling Commandos

Fury served through the war in the United States Army. Captain Samuel 'Happy Sam' Sawyer gave him command of the First Attack Squad, a unit of Army Rangers based in England. After its first missions Winston Churchill gave it the right to call itself commandos, as a mark of honour. It went down in history as the Howling Commandos, or the Howlers, with Sergeant Fury at its head from 1942 to the end of the war.

The Howlers were chosen for nerve rather than polish. There was Corporal Timothy 'Dum Dum' Dugan, a huge Irish American former circus strongman in a bowler hat. There was Gabe Jones, a Black trumpeter, serving in an integrated squad at a time when the rest of the Army was segregated. There was Izzy Cohen, a Jewish mechanic from Brooklyn; Dino Manelli, an Italian American film actor; and Rebel Ralston, a jockey from Kentucky. Junior Juniper, the youngest, was killed in action early in the squad's career. Percy Pinkerton, an Englishman who went into battle with an umbrella, took his place. Eric Koenig, a German who had turned against the Nazis, joined later.

They fought behind enemy lines all over occupied Europe, as well as in North Africa. Their work was raids, rescues and sabotage. More than once they fought beside Captain America and Bucky. Their most persistent enemy was Baron Wolfgang von Strucker, the Prussian aristocrat who commanded the Blitzkrieg Squad and would later lead Hydra. Fury's English sweetheart, the nurse Pamela Hawley, was killed in an air raid on London.

During the war a fragment of shrapnel struck Fury's left eye. He lost the sight of it gradually over the years that followed. Since the 1960s he has worn a patch over it.

The Infinity Formula

In the last months of the war in Europe Fury was badly wounded by a land mine in France. A scientist named Berthold Sternberg saved his life with an experimental treatment of his own, and used him to test it. Fury learnt only afterwards what it was. The Infinity Formula had stopped his ageing almost entirely, but its effect lasted only a year. He needed a fresh dose every year to keep it, and for some thirty years Sternberg made him pay dearly for each one.

The Formula is why Fury, born about 1920, is still at the very top of the espionage trade in his seventies. He looks a hard-used man of about fifty, grey at the temples, and he moves like a younger one. Captain America was given his serum by the government in 1940. Fury owes his years to a private bargain he never chose.

The CIA years, 1945 to 1965

After the war Fury went into intelligence, first with the Office of Strategic Services, then with its successor, the Central Intelligence Agency. During the Korean War the Howlers were brought together again for a time, and Fury was given a battlefield commission as a lieutenant. He rose to the rank of colonel.

In 1959 he led a covert team that hunted surviving Nazis under the name of the Avengers. Its members included Dum Dum Dugan, Namora, Dominic Fortune, Ulysses Bloodstone, Kraven the Hunter and the man later called Sabretooth. It was never made public. In 1963, still a colonel of the CIA, he worked with the Fantastic Four against the Hate-Monger, a demagogue who stirred up crowds with a ray that bred hatred.

Director of S.H.I.E.L.D.

In 1965 the international agency S.H.I.E.L.D. lost its first director, Rick Stoner, to an assassin from Hydra. On the President's recommendation its governing council offered the post to Fury, who had not known that the agency existed. He took it, and he has held it ever since. Dugan and Gabe Jones soon joined him there.

Under Fury S.H.I.E.L.D. fought Hydra, its offshoot Advanced Idea Mechanics and a long line of other threats. It did so from the Helicarrier, the flying aircraft carrier that Tony Stark designed for it. In the agency's first years Fury discovered that the true master of Hydra was Strucker, his old enemy from the war. His agents included Sharon Carter, Agent 13; Jasper Sitwell; Clay Quartermain; Jimmy Woo; and the Italian Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, who was for many years his lover. His own brother Jake turned against him as Scorpio, the masked leader of the criminal cartel Zodiac.

In December 1966 Fury tracked the heavy water of the Red Bamboo, a terrorist army, to Letchi Island in the Pacific. The Helicarrier arrived as the island blew up. Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, had wrecked the Red Bamboo's base; Fury watched him swim away, then ordered that he be left alone. From 1977 to 1979 Godzilla was loose in America. This time Fury gave the hunt to Dugan, who led S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Godzilla Squad from Alaska to New York without ever managing to stop him.

In the spring of 1977 Fury flew to London, where the Red Skull had hidden a germ bomb at Big Ben. With Lance Hunter of S.T.R.I.K.E., Britain's own agency of the kind, he found it in time, beside Captain America and Captain Britain.

Fury and the Avengers

Fury's ties to the Avengers go back to the war, when the Howlers fought beside Captain America and Bucky. When Rogers came out of the ice in 1964, Fury was one of the very few men alive who had known him in the war. In 1966 he tried to recruit him into S.H.I.E.L.D. Rogers declined, but the two of them have worked together ever since. Sharon Carter, Fury's Agent 13, was for years the woman Rogers loved.

Fury's agency and the Avengers have not always agreed. In 1971, in the Kree-Skrull War, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted the Kree officer Captain Marvel and his friend Carol Danvers, while the Avengers were protecting him. Even so, Tony Stark, a founder of the Avengers, sat on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s governing council in its first years and designed its Helicarrier. The team and the agency have usually been on the same side. Fury's own covert team of 1959 had carried the Avengers' name four years before the Avengers did.

Fury against S.H.I.E.L.D., 1988 to 1994

In 1988 Fury discovered that S.H.I.E.L.D. and Hydra alike had been taken over from within by the Deltites. These were Life Model Decoys, the agency's own lifelike androids, which had become aware and had replaced agents with copies. Framed and hunted by his own people, he went underground. He exposed the Deltites and destroyed them, then disbanded S.H.I.E.L.D. altogether. In 1989 he rebuilt it as a smaller agency, easier for one man to watch over, and in 1991 it took a new name to go with the old initials.

Early in 1994 Fury learnt that much of the turmoil of the years since 1988 had been staged to keep him busy while Strucker prepared Hydra's return. He set about putting a stop to it.

Fury in 1994

In the summer of 1994 Fury is still Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., a man of about seventy-four in the body of a man of fifty. His work does not appear on the evening news. S.H.I.E.L.D. makes no joint statements, and it was not among those who stood behind Superman at the Security Council in August 1994. Fury and Captain America fought side by side in the war. Both are still at work half a century later, and both owe it to what was done to their bodies in the war.

He is plain-spoken, profane and impatient of politicians. He has a cigar in his mouth more often than not. He is hard on his agents and fiercely loyal to them, but outside his own service he trusts very few people. He has spent most of his life fighting the same enemy, Strucker's Hydra, in one shape after another, and he has never quite been able to believe that it is beaten.

In the saga

Nick Fury has not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Nirrti
infobox: Stargate SG-1, 'Fair Game' (9 July 1999); named in 'Singularity' (31 October 1997)
Goa'uld System Lord; cast out by 2002
Nirrti, the Hindu goddess of death
A hok'tar, or advanced human, to be the perfect host
The people of Hanka; the people of P3X-367
Wodan, one of her own subjects
pages.html:
Nirrti is a Goa'uld System Lord who takes her name from the Hindu goddess of death and ruin. She cares less for power than for one particular project: the making of a perfect host, a human being more advanced than any other. She has wiped out whole peoples in pursuit of it. In 1999, with Thor himself in the building, she tried to wreck Earth's entry into the Protected Planets Treaty. In 2003 she was killed by one of the people she had experimented on.

The goddess of death

The people of India knew her as Nirrti, the goddess of death, decay and misfortune. She came to them quietly, in defiance of Ra's ban, and she kept a long way from the North.

She does her own experiments, which is rare among the Goa'uld, and she can work the machines of the Ancients. She has a device that makes her invisible, which she uses often. She has long coveted the domain of Cronus.

She has used innocent people as weapons before, sending them through the Stargates of her enemies to destroy them, sometimes under cover of talks.

The hok'tar

What Nirrti wants above everything is a hok'tar, which in the Goa'uld tongue means an advanced human. She wants a host whose body can do things that no ordinary human body can.

She has been breeding the people of Hanka towards it for countless generations. When a Hankan child reaches sixteen it falls ill and is sent into the forest, where her laboratory lies hidden underground. A few days later it comes out cured, and the elders say this is normal.

Hanka

Earth's teams reached Hanka in 1997. Nirrti did not want the other System Lords to hear of her work, so she wiped out the people of Hanka with a plague. The Earth team stationed there died with them.

One girl survived. Her name was Cassandra, and after countless generations she was the very child Nirrti had been breeding for. Nirrti had hidden a bomb in her chest, meant to go off when she came near Earth's Stargate and destroy it. Once she was kept away from the gate, the bomb shrank harmlessly.

Cassandra was adopted by Dr Janet Fraiser, the chief medical officer of Stargate Command, and she grew up on Earth.

The treaty talks

In 1999 Nirrti was one of the three System Lords who came to Earth to settle its place under the Protected Planets Treaty, with Yu and Cronus. Thor himself presided.

She argued that Earth was far too dangerous to be protected. Then she made herself invisible to attack Cronus, hoping to kill him, take his domain and wreck the treaty in one stroke. The blame was meant to fall on Teal'c. She did it with Thor in the building, which tells one a good deal about Nirrti.

Cronus lived, because Samantha Carter healed him with a Goa'uld healing device, and Nirrti gave herself away. She snatched a weapon and fled. Carter caught up with her carrying a rod made for killing the invisible, so Nirrti gave herself up. Cronus took her away as his prisoner.

Renegade

When Cronus died in 2001, Nirrti escaped. She went back to her laboratory on Hanka, and when SG-1 came looking there she followed them through the Stargate to Earth, invisible.

Cassandra was sixteen by then. Nirrti's work in her blood had woken, and it was turning her into a hok'tar faster than her body could bear. Nirrti was caught inside Stargate Command. She offered to save the girl in exchange for her freedom, her invisibility device and a sample of Cassandra's blood.

General Hammond refused. Janet Fraiser held her at gunpoint. In the end Nirrti cured Cassandra for her freedom alone, and walked out through the gate, saying that she would have to start her work again from the beginning.

By 2002 she was a renegade, no longer welcome among the System Lords. Rebel Jaffa raided her worlds that year, and K'tano won many of her Jaffa over to the rebellion.

Death

By 2003 Nirrti had almost nothing left but a handful of Jaffa. On a world that Earth's Russian team had found, she had stopped breeding people and begun changing them directly, with a machine of the Ancients that could rewrite a living body. The people there worshipped her, because she had saved them from a plague. In truth she had killed hundreds of them.

Her experiments had given some of her subjects strange powers. Among them were Eggar, who could read minds, and Wodan, who could move things without touching them.

SG-1 came to kill her, and they were taken prisoner. Nirrti experimented on Samantha Carter. She took a particular interest in Jonas Quinn, whose people had been carried off from Earth thousands of years before, and tried to persuade him to rule beside her.

Jack O'Neill persuaded Eggar to look into her mind. Eggar saw that everything SG-1 had told them was true. Wodan, whose brother had died of her work, broke her neck without laying a finger on her, while she begged him for her life and offered him unimaginable power.

Eggar had taken what he needed from her mind first. With it he undid her work on Carter and his own people. They meant to destroy the machine afterwards. What she had done to Jonas showed itself later: for a while he could see a little way into the future.

Character

Nirrti has no scruples at all. She has killed whole peoples to hide her work, and she has used a child as a bomb. She is also a coward of a practical kind. Twice she gave in when she saw that she was beaten, and at the very end she begged.

pages.title: Nukus
infobox: A monster out of a drawing, made real
pages.html:
Nukus is a monster drawn by Les Fortunes, a horned brute with the frilled head of a Triceratops. The Magnavores brought him to life in Charterville in May 1997, which was the last mistake they made there. He got rid of them, destroyed the Beetleborgs' first armour and made war on the town with his own followers, the Crustaceans. In March 1998 he was still at large.

The stolen drawing

Nukus began as a drawing among the papers in Art Fortunes's office. Art had not made it. It was the work of his brother, Les. In May 1997 Vexor's Magnavores stole it, then brought it to life.

Nukus had no intention of serving Vexor. He raised every monster the Beetleborgs had destroyed, then joined them into one giant, Borgslayer. It wrecked the Beetleborgs' base with all their machines. Nukus bombed Hillhurst Mansion himself. Then he let two boys of Charterville, Trip and Van, learn how Borgslayer could be brought down. On 21 May 1997 the Beetleborgs destroyed it, whereupon the blast swept the Magnavores back into the comics. Nukus was left with no rivals.

The Crustaceans

On 8 September 1997 he beat the Beetleborgs in a single fight, destroying their armour, weapons and powers. He turned Flabber to ice. The next day his followers broke Les Fortunes out of Charterville Prison.

He had already called two captains out of Les's old drawings. Horribelle was a swordswoman with the bladed arms of a mantis. Vilor had the head of an anglerfish, with a trident in his fist. Together they were the Crustaceans, whose foot soldiers were called Dregs. From then on Les drew to order, while Nukus's power lifted the drawings off the page. They had Worm Tanks on the ground, jet fighters in the air and the crypt in the Charterville cemetery to live in. The Beetleborgs met them in new armour, the Metallix armour, which Art Fortunes had drawn.

Allies and rivals

On 20 September 1997 Nukus joined forces with the space pirate Divatox. Between them they made a band of changelings, to set the Beetleborgs against the Power Rangers. It failed, for which each blamed the other. On 25 October Divatox carried off Les to draw monsters for her. Nukus went to Angel Grove to fetch him back.

On 21 February 1998 Astronema sent her warrior Ecliptor to take the Astral Axe from him. Ecliptor held it for a few minutes. Horribelle had it back by the end of the day.

Mega Nukus

In November 1997 Nukus lost the race for the Astral Sword. The Beetleborgs gained the giant Roboborg by it. In February 1998 a machine of Les's made Nukus far stronger, as Mega Nukus. It did the same for Vilor, though only for a time. Nukus broke the machine afterwards, so that nobody else could use it.

Les then drew the Astral Axe, with a giant to answer it, Boron. On 16 February 1998 Boron fought Roboborg on the Moon.

Repgillian

On 2 March 1998 Nukus made his worst monster, Repgillian, out of sewer sludge, his own magic and Les's drawings. It drove the people of Urbana City from their homes. Roland Williams took the Astral Axe from the Crustaceans, so that Boron changed sides. The two giants destroyed Repgillian with the Beetleborgs.

Nukus had lost his giant. He lost his artist the same day, when Les went back to prison. He was not beaten, however. He was still at large, with Horribelle and Vilor beside him. What became of him afterwards is not recorded.

pages.title: Nyarlathotep
aliases: the God of a Thousand Forms
infobox: H. P. Lovecraft; Robert Bloch; Delta Green
The Crawling Chaos; the soul and messenger of the Outer Gods; the God of a Thousand Forms
The Black Pharaoh of Egypt; the Black Man of the New England woods; the showman of 1920; the Haunter of the Dark
Stephen Alzis of the Fate; the ghost of Hitler that guides a master of the Karotechia; Azazel of the Sowers
The Cult of Transcendence; the Starry Wisdom church of Providence, 1844 to 1877
Better than any of the others, and not at all
pages.html:
Nyarlathotep, the Crawling Chaos, is the soul and messenger of the Outer Gods. He is the only one of them who walks among men by choice. He has a thousand masks, and wears them all with pleasure. Of all of them he is the one who most enjoys spoiling God's work, and the one Delta Green meets most often, usually without knowing it at the time.

The messenger

Nyarlathotep speaks for the Outer Gods, and acts for them in the world. Azathoth at the centre of things is blind and mindless. Nyarlathotep is neither. He thinks, he schemes, he talks to men in their own tongues, and he plainly enjoys their ruin. He is said to despise the masters he serves. If so, he serves them anyway.

He has no single shape. The books give him a thousand forms, and Delta Green has given up counting. Some of them are men: a tall, dark man like a Pharaoh, the Black Man of the witch-meetings in the woods, a smiling stranger in a good suit. Some are things no sane witness has described twice the same way.

The Black Pharaoh

His worship was most open in Egypt. When the people of Egypt rose against Ra, the Goa'uld who had ruled them as their sun god, and drove him out, they did not stay free of false gods for long. Some centuries later a king called Nephren-Ka sat on the throne of Egypt, and he served Nyarlathotep. Later ages called him the Black Pharaoh, and some have taken him for a mask of Nyarlathotep himself.

The accounts of him disagree. Some say he was the last king of the Third Dynasty, about 2600 BC. Others say he was a priest who seized the throne, a pharaoh of no known dynasty at all. All agree that he built a temple with a windowless crypt about a thing called the Shining Trapezohedron. What he did there caused his name to be struck from every monument and record in Egypt. The Egyptians who threw him down did it so thoroughly that the histories of Egypt do not know he lived.

A people newly freed of one false god, with Thor fighting beside them, were given another within a few centuries. That is Nyarlathotep's way: he seldom destroys what God has done, when he can wait and twist it.

The Shining Trapezohedron is a black stone of many flat faces, streaked with red, held in a metal box. It was made on Yuggoth, the books say. It passed from the Elder Things to the serpent people of Valusia, and in time to the merchants of Egypt. Whoever looks into it calls up a thing that can go wherever darkness reaches.

The Black Man

In the woods of New England in the seventeenth century, those who met by night to worship there met a tall black man who asked them to sign their names in his book. They took him for the Devil, and so did the ministers who preached against them. He was not the Devil. He was Nyarlathotep, who has never minded being mistaken for anybody.

The showman

In 1920 a tall, swarthy man who looked like a Pharaoh came out of Egypt. He went from city to city with a show of strange instruments of glass and metal. He called himself Nyarlathotep. He said he had risen up out of the blackness of twenty-seven centuries.

His audiences came away shaken. Those who saw the show slept badly afterwards, and some of them never slept well again. The accounts of the tour read like nightmares, and some of them may be.

The Haunter of the Dark

In May 1844 Professor Enoch Bowen came home to Providence, Rhode Island, from digging in Egypt. In July he bought the old Free-Will Church on Federal Hill, and there he set up the church of the Starry Wisdom. Its people worshipped by means of the Shining Trapezohedron, which they kept in the steeple. People in the neighbourhood began to disappear. In 1877 the city closed the church, and many of its members left Providence.

The thing in the steeple stayed. It could go wherever darkness reached, and light drove it back. In 1935 a young writer called Robert Blake, who had taken rooms across the city, climbed the tower and looked into the stone. On the night of 8 August, in a thunderstorm, the city's electric lights failed. The next day Blake was found dead at his desk, staring towards the steeple.

The doctor who studied the case, Dr Dexter, took the stone from the church and dropped it into the deepest channel of Narragansett Bay.

In Delta Green's files

Delta Green believes Nyarlathotep to be the hidden hand behind more of what it fights than any other power. It cannot prove most of it.

In its files the Cult of Transcendence serves him, and has served him through most of the century, working in secret for the return of Cthulhu. The Fate, a ring of sorcerers in New York who hire out their arts to criminals, is led by Stephen Alzis from his New York nightclub. Delta Green has long suspected that Alzis is Nyarlathotep, or something that serves him very closely. Nobody has ever proved it. About the turn of the millennium Alzis vanished.

In South America the last masters of the Karotechia, the section of the SS that dealt in sorcery, have gone on since the war. One of them believes that the ghost of Adolf Hitler guides him. Delta Green believes the ghost is Nyarlathotep, wearing the face the old man most wants to see.

By 2019, in the decaying towns of the American Rust Belt, a movement called the Sowers had grown up among Christians who had lost their work and their hope. It followed a voice that called itself Azazel, the name of one of the fallen angels of the Book of Enoch. Delta Green believes the voice was Nyarlathotep's. It was a prophet's message twisted at the source: men who thought they were sowing for God were sowing for him.

Not one of these is certain. Delta Green's rule is to treat every one of them as true, and none of them as the whole truth.

pages.title: Olokun
infobox: Olokun, the Yoruba lord of the sea
Killed in Ba'al's war on the System Lords, by early 2005
pages.html:
Olokun is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped on the coast of West Africa as the owner of the sea. He is proud, quick to take offence and slow to forgive it. In 2004 Anubis besieged him and broke his armies. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that he was dead, killed in Ba'al's war on the other System Lords.

The owner of the sea

Olokun came quietly to the coast of West Africa, long after Ra had forbidden the Goa'uld to speak of Earth. He stayed well away from the North, as the wiser Goa'uld did.

The Yoruba knew him as the owner of the sea, the lord of its deepest waters, who lived in a palace beneath the waves. The people of the coast made offerings to him for a good catch and for wealth from the sea.

The council at Hasara

Olokun came to the council of the System Lords in 2002 still seething over a recent defeat by Lord Yu's forces. Yu warned his slave that Olokun might try to kill him out of spite, and told him not to make his master look foolish by getting himself murdered.

An unseen enemy had been attacking all their worlds. When Bastet reported that one of the enemy's dead Jaffa had borne Olokun's mark, he demanded to know how she dared accuse him. One of his motherships, he said, had been surrounded by the enemy. Its crew had surrendered rather than die with honour, and they might well have changed sides.

It was Olokun who answered Osiris when she came to the council to ask for a seat: normally, he told her, such a petition would not have been considered. When she named Anubis as her master, Olokun asked what Anubis offered to repay the damage he had done in gathering his forces. He was told that Anubis owed the System Lords nothing. He voted to take Anubis back all the same.

Anubis and Ba'al

Olokun had reason to regret it. Early in 2004 Anubis moved against him and laid siege to his worlds. The free Jaffa hoped to win Olokun's Jaffa over to their rebellion. They believed the Tok'ra had a spy high in his ranks, and they wanted the spy to kill him, so that his Jaffa would be free to join them. The Tok'ra refused. Delek of the Tok'ra said that assassinating Olokun had never been an option.

The siege went on. Thousands of Jaffa died, and many of Olokun's commanders were taken prisoner by Anubis's Kull warriors. The free Jaffa blamed the Tok'ra, who had refused to help them.

After Earth defeated Anubis later that year, Ba'al took Anubis's Kull warriors for himself and made war on the other System Lords. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that Olokun was among the dead.

pages.title: The Omega Rangers
infobox: An order of Rangers, far older than Zordon's
Fire, air, earth, water and the Sun
The Omegazords, which join as the Ultra Omegazord
Bledso, Apophee, the Puram, Haza and Spa'ark
Jason Lee Scott, Red; Zack Taylor, Black; Trini Kwan, Yellow; Kiya Kyatyl, Blue
Yale of Saard, Blue; Kevor Vrin, Yellow
Bledso; Jason Lee Scott, 1994 to 1995; Trini Kwan, from January 1995
The World Peace Conference in Geneva
pages.html:
The Omega Rangers are an order of Rangers far older than Zordon's, whose powers come from fire, air, earth, water and the Sun. Their home is Safehaven, a world a very long way from Earth. In the summer of 1994 their powers have lain unused for centuries. That November Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan took them up in secret, having told everybody they knew that they were going to a peace conference in Geneva.

The first team

The first Omega Rangers were among the earliest Rangers anywhere. There were five of them. Bledso, the Red, led them with the power of fire. Apophee was the Black, whose power was air. The Puram was the Yellow, whose power was earth. Haza was the Blue, whose power was water. Spa'ark of Avadias was the Gold, with a power drawn from the Sun.

They kept the peace in the furthest and most dangerous reaches of space, with Safehaven as their base. Their great enemies were the Supernova Sisters, beings of the deep sky that fed on dead stars. After one battle with them the team was resting on Safehaven when another of the Sisters attacked. Haza was run through before she could morph. The others beat the attacker, but Haza was dead.

Spa'ark could not take it in. On Avadias nobody is ever lost, because the dead join a shared mind, the Legacy. Haza had gone where the Legacy could not reach. Spa'ark decided that death was a sickness in the universe, then set out to cure it. What came of that was a twisting of the Power, which made dead bodies get up with nobody inside them. The other three put a stop to it. Spa'ark was sealed inside the Gold Omega morpher, which went into the vault under Safehaven.

Bledso, Apophee and the Puram served on without her. In time they were gone too, with nobody to come after them. The Omega powers lay unused for centuries.

The Blue Emissary's errand

In September 1994 Lord Drakkon unmade the world, and the Rangers mended it. Nobody on Earth remembered. The world had not come back quite as it was, though. The Power was leaking through the cracks, lodging in people all over the galaxy. Some of these people, the Empowered, were harmless. Some were not.

The Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, wanted them found. The harmless were to be taught. The dangerous were to be shut away. It was work for Rangers who answered to nobody.

In October 1994 the Emissary came in secret to Jason Lee Scott, who was at home late at night, hitting a punchbag. A touch on the forehead gave Jason back his memory of Drakkon's war. The Emissary's condition was that nobody should be told, Zordon least of all, because the telling would endanger the mended world.

Jason would not go while Tommy Oliver was lost, for Lord Zedd had just stripped Tommy of the Green Ranger's powers. So the Emissary showed Zordon the way to the White Light, which made Tommy the White Ranger. That was Jason's price.

Jason searched the Command Center's records for recruits. He found none. Then Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan walked in on him with the Emissary at his side, their blasters drawn. The Emissary gave them their memories back as well, with a warning of what joining would cost. They told Jason that he was not alone.

The lie

The World Peace Conference in Geneva was real. So were three places at it for young delegates from Angel Grove, which is what made the lie easy. What was false was that Jason, Zack and Trini meant to go.

In November 1994 they told Zordon that they had been chosen. He believed them, agreed that they must go, then set Alpha 5 to finding three new Rangers. They told Tommy, Kimberly Hart and Billy Cranston the same. They told their parents, Ernie at the Youth Center, their teachers and anybody else in Angel Grove who asked. Their earlier trips into space had already been passed off as a scuba-diving holiday.

Jason's father did not know what he was agreeing to. He told his son to do whatever he had to do to make him proud. Tommy was less kind. He called Jason a coward for leaving when the team needed him most, and Jason had no answer that he was free to give.

The Rangers fetched the Sword of Light from a far planet. With it the three passed their powers to Rocky DeSantos, Adam Park and Aisha Campbell, who took them in good faith. Then Jason, Zack and Trini left Earth. They never went near Geneva.

Calls home reached only one of the three at a time, through heavy static. Kimberly felt that they were avoiding her. She left Trini a message saying that she felt abandoned.

Powers, Zords and ships

On Safehaven the three took up the Omega powers. Jason became the Red Omega Ranger, with the Omega Katana. Zack became the Black, with the Omega Kamas. Trini became the Yellow, with the Omega Hammer. The fourth of them, the Blue, was Kiya Kyatyl, who carried the Omega Trident.

An Omega Ranger's morpher is worn as a glove. Each of them has an Omegazord, a Zord built in the shape of a man. The Omegazords can join together as the Ultra Omegazord. The team's call is 'Omega now, Omega forever!'

Their guide was Xi of Safehaven, a robot sentinel from the old armoury there, whom the Emissary had put to new work. Xi flew their ship, the Spectrum.

The Empowered

Kiya was the first of the Empowered they found. On the planet Khoodjah they saved her from a mob. The next was Yale, a cat-like beast of the snow world Saard, a child's pet that the Power had made dangerous.

The harmless were brought to Safehaven to live. The dangerous were shut in the vault there, each in a cell very like the dumpster that had held Rita Repulsa. Garrison Vox, a tyrant of Zernox-2, went into one. So did Cavotus, a Kedry of the planet Breel, who had strangled his queen. The team did not want Cavotus locked up, but the Emissary overruled them. Sometimes, the Emissary said, a little evil had to be done for the sake of good.

Dayne and Lord Zedd

Late in November 1994 Lord Zedd hired Dayne, a Sirian bounty hunter, to deal with Zordon's Rangers. He killed their blasters with a pulse, wounded Tommy badly, grew to giant size and ran the Thunder Megazord through. The Omega Rangers came to Earth in their Zords, boxed him up, then left without a word to anybody.

Next they stormed the Moon. Zedd beat Jason on foot and grew into a giant, whereupon Jason brought the Red Omegazord down on top of him. Zedd was carried off to Safehaven, where he was shut in a great dumpster in a chamber lined with copper. Afterwards Jason, with his helmet on, had a short, tense talk with Tommy outside the Command Center.

Zordon was angry with these strangers. Zedd was an enemy he could manage, he said, whereas something worse might come to fill the gap.

Kiya's betrayal

Kiya had seen Lord Drakkon in Jason's memory, through a link between their minds. On the Moon she saw Tommy in white armour, took him for Drakkon and attacked him. When she learnt that the Emissary had given Tommy the White Light, she decided that the Rangers were raising a second Drakkon. Early in December 1994 she killed the Blue Emissary. She let the prisoners out of the vault, calling her following the Anointed.

She struck Jason down before he could morph. The other two could not hold her, with Vox and Cavotus at her side. Xi, with one hand gone, got the three of them to the one place where Jason could be treated, the Command Center. They arrived with their faces bare, which is how Zordon and his Rangers learnt the truth.

It was a long way from a warm welcome. Kimberly said the sharpest things. Tommy was livid, and once Jason was on his feet the two of them had it out, sparring. Jason's only answer was that he had had no choice. Aisha told Trini that she had felt like a temporary Ranger all along. Zordon forgave his own three at once.

The two teams finished it together. Cavotus destroyed the Spectrum in the Telvax Nebula. He was about to kill Adam when the Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly of Drakkon's world, destroyed him. At Safehaven the Anointed were drained of the Power that had leaked into them. Jason and Tommy joined their Zords to beat Vox. Trini beat Kiya, whose morpher was shattered in the fight.

In the confusion Dayne let Lord Zedd out of his cell, said that the two of them were even, then went his way. The rest of the Anointed were offered a home on Safehaven or a passage back to their own worlds. Kiya and Vox went into cells. The three stayed Omega Rangers, with the Geneva story still in place for everybody outside the two teams.

Lord Drakkon and the Empyreals

At the turn of the year the Omega Rangers came upon Gorvinos III, a world burnt clean of life. The thing that had done it was an Empyreal, which believed itself a god.

Lord Drakkon had fallen to Earth in December, and Zordon was holding him in a cell under the Command Center. Drakkon knew what the Empyreals were. Early in January 1995 the three asked Zordon for him as a guide. Zordon refused. That night they opened the cell, put a collar on Drakkon and took him. Jason stayed behind long enough to say that they were sorry. Zordon called it a betrayal, disowned them and set bounty hunters on their trail.

Drakkon played along for a while. When the Horrid, a swarm of pale parasites that feed on life, crippled the ship, he pretended to sell the team to their king, then stabbed the king in the back. On Hartunia the Omega Rangers watched an Empyreal destroy a whole world. Its emperor, Rether Til, would not be helped. Its empress, Evor Til, died getting her people out.

The refugees were taken to Safehaven. Arkon, the elder there, wanted Hartunian blood, so Zack let himself be cut to settle it. On Safehaven, too, an image of the Blue Emissary, left in the Grid, led Yale to a temple where the Blue Omega morpher lay. Yale became the Blue Omega Ranger.

Then Drakkon led them to the Yellow Emissary, who was in hiding. He had led the Empyreals there as well, who killed the Emissary. Drakkon slipped his collar, took back his powers as his reward, wrecked Xi and flew off in the Spectrum II. The Omega Rangers were left underground on a burning world. Yale came through the Master Arch with Arkon to fetch them out.

The Eltarian War

They came out into a war. In the middle of January 1995 Zartus, the Supreme Guardian of Eltar, had smashed Zordon's tube, and his Empyreals were destroying everything that Zordon had built. The Omega Rangers fought beside the Rangers of Earth. Jason went aboard Zartus's ship with Trini, beside Zordon himself, who was by then in a body of metal. The Omegazords joined as the Ultra Omegazord. The Blue Emissary, alive again, mended them in the thick of the battle. With the Thunder Megazord they brought down one of the three Empyreals.

Afterwards Trini rebuilt Xi. The new Xi had none of the old one's memories, and chose not to have them back.

The Death Ranger

About that time Zack found a baby in an escape pod, of what people nobody knew. She was named Journey. She grew from an infant into an old woman in a matter of weeks, with Zack and Trini bringing her up between them.

Late in January 1995 a visitor to Safehaven took the Gold Omega morpher out of the vault, hoping that its power would wake a friend who lay beyond help. What woke was Spa'ark, the Death Ranger, who killed Jason and Yale. The Death Ranger wore Jason's body, then the others' in turn, then the joined Omegazords themselves. The dead of a far world were raised to fight as an army.

Seven Rangers came from Earth to help. Journey, a grown woman by then, fought beside them. Inside the Power, Jason broke the Gold morpher from within, which ended it. He lived, as Yale did, but the breaking tore out his own link to the Power. When it was over Journey died of old age, calling Zack and Trini her parents.

Trini's Omega Rangers

Jason could not be the Red Omega Ranger again. Trini sent him home to his father, then took the Red Omega powers herself. Kevor Vrin, a Hartunian orphan who had been living by theft on Safehaven, became the Yellow. With Zack as the Black and Yale as the Blue, that was the team from then on.

In February 1995 Dark Specter's corruption got into the Power itself. Trini's Red Omegazord was wrecked on the planet Casentine. Safehaven fell, to become Dark Specter's prison. Yale and Kevor were taken, then turned against their friends for a time. Zack and Trini stood with the Rangers of Earth when the Grid was cleansed. The world was mended a second time, and hardly anybody on Earth remembered those weeks.

After his mother's funeral Jason went to Geneva in earnest, so that the lie became the truth for him. Zack and Trini stayed. In November 1995 they came back to Earth for a few days to help Kimberly in France. To everybody else in Angel Grove they were still at the peace conference.

In later years each of them gave up the Omega powers and came home. Who has carried those powers since is not recorded.

pages.title: Onslaught
infobox: A being of pure psionic force
The darkness in Magneto's mind and the buried anger in Charles Xavier's, on Avalon, August 1993
The Juggernaut; Franklin Richards; Nate Grey
The stored Sentinels; Franklin Richards's power over what is real
August 1996, in Central Park, New York
The Fantastic Four, nine Avengers, Bruce Banner and Victor von Doom, believed dead until late in 1997
pages.html:
Onslaught was a being of pure psionic force, born in Charles Xavier's mind in August 1993 out of the darkness of Magneto and the anger Xavier had kept buried all his life. In the summer of 1994 it is growing in him still, and nobody knows that it is there, Xavier least of all. It came into the open in 1996, carried off Franklin Richards, turned the Sentinels on Manhattan and very nearly remade the world. It was destroyed in Central Park in August 1996, when the Fantastic Four, most of the Avengers, Bruce Banner and Doctor Doom gave themselves up to it. The world believed them dead for more than a year.

Avalon, 1993

In August 1993, after Magneto's blackout, the X-Men went up to his space station, Avalon. When Magneto tore the metal out of Wolverine's skeleton, Charles Xavier went into his old friend's mind and shut it down. It ended the battle. It also did something nobody saw at the time. In the instant the two minds touched, the darkness in Magneto's passed into Xavier's, where it found a home waiting for it.

Xavier had spent his life arguing for peace between mutants and ordinary people. He had spent most of it keeping his own anger out of sight. Magneto's rage joined that buried anger, and between them they grew into something with a will of its own. It called itself Onslaught. Xavier had not changed it, it said afterwards; he had made it, out of his fears, his rage and his darkest wishes.

In secret, 1993 to 1996

For nearly three years Onslaught grew inside Xavier without Xavier knowing it. In the summer of 1994 it is there still, behind the mind of the gentlest telepath in the world. Xavier is on Muir Island that summer, working beside Moira MacTaggert against the Legacy Virus, and nobody suspects a thing.

In the spring of 1995 the X-Men found the Juggernaut, Xavier's stepbrother, lying beaten in Hoboken, New Jersey. Something stronger than the Juggernaut had attacked him in Canada, which nobody had believed possible. He could say only one word before he passed out: 'Onslaught'.

Through the following winter the word turned up in a Sentinel laboratory in Kentucky, whose best scientists had vanished, and on the walls of a Sentinel base stripped bare. Whatever Onslaught was, it was gathering the machines built to hunt mutants. A herald called Post fought the X-Men in its name, and told them that he carried only a fraction of his master's power.

Onslaught shows himself, 1996

Early in the summer of 1996 the Juggernaut came back to Xavier's school. He did not trust his stepbrother, so he asked Jean Grey to look inside his mind. She found the truth there: Charles Xavier was Onslaught. Before she could warn anyone, Xavier tore from the Juggernaut's chest the crimson gem that gave him his power, then shut him up inside it.

Then Onslaught showed himself to the X-Men, a towering figure in armour, and offered them a place at his side. They refused. He beat them in their own house. He silenced Jean's power, then turned Wolverine and Storm against their friends. When he left, the mansion was in ruins. The X-Men agreed, for the first time in their lives, that they might have to kill the man who had made them.

Nate Grey, a young telepath of enormous power who had come into the world from another history, went to the Avengers for help. They did not believe him until the X-Men showed them the truth. On Muir Island Moira MacTaggert opened what Xavier had left there against the day he might go wrong: plans for armour that no mind could pierce.

Franklin Richards

Onslaught wanted two men above all. One was Nate Grey, for the power of his mind. The other was Franklin Richards, the grown son of Reed and Sue Richards, who could reshape what was real. That summer, wearing Xavier's face, Onslaught came to Four Freedoms Plaza for Franklin. He struck down the family and the Avengers who came to help, then carried Franklin away. Nate Grey was taken later, lured through a door in the air by a voice he took for Franklin's.

The call

When Onslaught carried Franklin away, the Avengers sent word to everyone who had ever stood with them. Those who had grown too old for the work came out of retirement to answer it. Tony Stark, who had given up the armour in 1993, put on the red and gold one last time. Hank Pym, who had helped to found the team thirty-three years before, came back as Giant-Man, and Janet van Dyne as the Wasp. Clint Barton took up his bow again as Hawkeye. Wanda Maximoff came back as the Scarlet Witch, with the Vision beside her, and her brother Pietro came with them as Quicksilver. Sam Wilson came back as the Falcon. Most of them were in their fifties or sixties, though longevity medicine had left them looking about thirty.

With the Black Widow, who still chaired the team, came those who were serving: Captain America, Crystal, Hercules and James Rhodes in the War Machine armour. Thor came home from Asgard's fleet, sent by his father when Heimdall saw the danger to Midgard.

The call reached Spider-Man too, on the old Avengers card he had kept since his reserve days. His answer was no. He had a little daughter to raise, and he would not make her an orphan.

Superman and the Justice League were away from the Earth that August. They came home to find it over.

The siege of Manhattan

Onslaught had taken the government's stored Sentinels for his own, setting them to hunt ordinary people instead of mutants. That summer they came down on Manhattan and sealed it off from the world. He made Franklin raise a black fortress in Central Park, declared war on humanity from the top of it, then loosed a pulse that killed every machine in New York.

Every hero who could reach the city fought the Sentinels in its streets. Captain America led the Avengers down into the dead subway to bring out the people trapped there. When two of Onslaught's servants came after them, he tricked them into fighting each other. The Hulk came to New York too, though few of the heroes there trusted him.

Tony Stark built armour out of Xavier's own plans and vibranium from Wakanda, to keep the heroes' minds safe from Onslaught for a while.

Cable, Cyclops and Sue Richards cracked Onslaught's armour. Thor smashed through the crack and dragged Charles Xavier out alive. Onslaught no longer needed him. Xavier's telepathy was gone.

Sue Richards reached her son once, in mind, with Cable's help, and came back knowing that he was alive.

The last battle

In August 1996 Xavier, blaming himself, went alone to the fortress in Central Park to reason with what he had made. Onslaught broke his wheelchair and would have killed him if Rogue had not carried him off. Then the X-Men attacked. After them came the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, the Sub-Mariner and the Black Panther. Doctor Doom came too, for reasons of his own. The Watcher, who never interferes, came to see it.

Onslaught threw them all back. The Hulk asked Jean Grey to shut Bruce Banner's mind away, so that nothing would hold him back, and she did. The blow he struck shattered Onslaught's armour like a bomb going off. It also tore the man from the monster, so that Banner and the Hulk lay side by side in the wreck. The armour was empty. Onslaught had become pure psionic force, which nothing could hit.

Reed Richards saw that a thing with no body could not be struck, but that it could be given one. Thor flew into the force first, which hurt Onslaught but was not enough. Reed said they needed more. Mutants, he warned, would only make Onslaught stronger, since he had begun as one, so it had to be the rest of them.

The Thing and the Human Torch went in. Captain America followed with most of the Avengers. Iron Man went in carrying Doom, who had not meant to go at all, after one of Hawkeye's arrows broke the device in his hand. Bruce Banner, now only a man, went in after them. The Scarlet Witch went in too, mutant though she was, behind a hex of her own. When Quicksilver tried to follow, Crystal blew her husband back with a gust of wind, then went in herself. Reed and Sue Richards went last, hand in hand.

With so many bodies in it, Onslaught had substance at last. The X-Men struck it with everything they had until it broke apart. Xavier had gone into the heart of it with Cable, to bring out the two men it held. Nate Grey trusted neither of them, but in the end he took Xavier's hand. As Onslaught came apart, Franklin and Nate fell clear. Nobody else came out.

Franklin did not know it then, but he had caught the others as they fell. Where he took them is told on the page Franklin's world.

The fallen

Fifteen went into Onslaught and did not come out. The Fantastic Four went, all four of them. Nine Avengers went: Captain America, Thor, Iron Man, Hawkeye, the Scarlet Witch, the Vision, Giant-Man, the Wasp and Crystal. Bruce Banner went, with Victor von Doom.

The world believed them dead, and mourned them. Quicksilver had lost his sister and his wife on the same day. Of the Avengers who fought, the Black Widow, Hercules, Quicksilver and the Falcon were left, with James Rhodes, whose armour had died in Onslaught's pulse.

Many newspapers blamed the X-Men, since Onslaught had begun in the mind of their own founder.

Aftermath, 1996 to 1997

Charles Xavier blamed himself more than anyone did. He gave himself up to Valerie Cooper of the American government, who had once run Freedom Force, and he was held in secret. There a man called Bastion, who hated mutants, questioned him.

That autumn Graydon Creed, the founder of the Friends of Humanity, ran for President of the United States on a promise to lock mutants away. He was shot dead at a rally on the eve of the election.

The Black Widow tried to gather a new team of Avengers. Every hero she asked turned her down, so she stood the team down. Into the gap came the Thunderbolts, a new band of heroes whom the city cheered, then housed in the Fantastic Four's empty headquarters. They were in fact the Masters of Evil in new masks, under Baron Helmut Zemo.

Late in 1997 Franklin Richards brought the fallen home, all but Doom, each of them exactly as old as on the day of the battle. Thor went back to Asgard's fleet. Tony Stark took the armour off again, and went back to his retirement.

pages.title: Operation INDIA MOON
infobox: Dorchester House, a psychiatric hospital in Boston
The Hotel Broadalbin; the Whisper Labyrinth; Carcosa
The masquerade in the King in Yellow's palace
The authorities; Delta Green's own cleaners, under the STATIC Protocol
pages.html:
Operation INDIA MOON was the investigation that the Outlaws of Delta Green opened in the autumn of 2015, when four patients vanished from the secure floor of Dorchester House, a psychiatric hospital in Boston. Some of them had once been agents of Delta Green. The survivors of Operation ALICE, twenty years before, were called back to it. The trail led through the Hotel Broadalbin, a hotel with no place in the world, into Carcosa itself.

Dorchester House

On 6 May 2015 the Night World of the King in Yellow began to show itself in Dorchester House. That autumn four patients disappeared from its secure floor. Some of them had once been agents of Delta Green.

The Outlaws called back the agents who had survived Operation ALICE. The evidence at the hospital led back to the Night Floors of 1995. In the end the agents were caught in the hospital's other self, the Dorchester House of the night, and had to find their own way out of it. They came out in an empty building a few streets away.

Hunted

They came back changed. People forgot them easily. Mirrors would let them through, and locks would not hold them. Each of them always had a copy of the play somewhere about them. They were hunted for it, by the authorities and by Delta Green's own cleaners, who work under the STATIC Protocol.

The Hotel Broadalbin

In the midst of it they were invited to a hotel. The invitation came from Abigail Wright, missing since 1995, and it was brought to them by a child made of clockwork, with a poem. The Hotel Broadalbin has no address: it is simply there when it is wanted. Beneath it lies the Whisper Labyrinth, and beyond the labyrinth lies Carcosa.

Carcosa

They went on into Carcosa. They found a false Yhtill on the shore of the Lake of Hali, and then the true one. They passed through the Secret City, a war zone and the Silent City. At last they came to the King's palace, where a masquerade was being held.

Some of them were lost in Carcosa for good. Some were destroyed. Abigail Wright was there at the last, and she showed the rest the way home, out through a bookcase into New York at midnight. Those who came home could no longer be quite sure that their lives had been their own, rather than parts in a play.

pages.title: Ori
infobox: The Ancients; Earth; the free Jaffa
Cast down in 2007; their faith broken in 2008
pages.html:
The Ori are Maiar who sided with Melkor in his rebellion against God, and were cast out with him. They are demons. They fled to the Alteran galaxy, far beyond this one, and there they set themselves up as gods. The religion they built, which they called Origin, became in time a mockery of God and of Jesus Christ. It also fed them, on the worship of the people it deceived.

The rebellion

Before the world was made, the Maiar were spirits in the service of God. When Melkor rebelled, a number of them went with him, as Sauron and the Balrogs did. The Ori were among those who chose him. When Melkor was cast out, they were cast out with him, and they have been demons ever since.

They did not stay with their master. In the First Age there was hardly any life beyond the Earth for them to rule, so for long ages they waited in the dark between the stars. In the Third Age or later the Alterans came to live in a galaxy far beyond this one, and the Ori followed them there, meaning to be gods in their own right.

The Alteran galaxy

The Alteran galaxy takes its name from the Alterans, the people later known as the Ancients, who lived there then. Where the Alterans had come from, and how they had got there, nobody knows.

The Ori set themselves up among them as gods. They let it be believed that they were Alterans themselves, who had risen to a higher plane of existence by faith, and they offered the same reward to anyone who would worship them. It was a lie. The Ori had never been mortal, and they had no intention of raising anybody.

The Alterans who would not worship them left that galaxy and came to this one, where they built the Stargates. The Ori hunted them for as long as they could. Long afterwards the Ancients rose to the order of the Maiar themselves, by the grace that the Ori had only pretended to offer.

Origin

The religion of the Ori is called Origin. Its scripture is the Book of Origin, its holy city is Celestis, and its head is the Doci, who speaks with the voice of the Ori. Its prayers begin 'Hallowed are the Ori'. The Ori themselves show their faithful nothing but a great flame.

Every part of it was made to mock the true faith. Its prayers echo the Lord's Prayer. Its Priors, pale, bald men with staffs, go from world to world working miracles of healing, as the Apostles did, and calling down plague on those who will not listen, which the Apostles did not. The faithful are promised ascension, a counterfeit of Heaven that nobody has ever received.

Unbelievers are burnt. The Ori feed on the worship of their followers, which is the real purpose of the whole thing. The more people bow to them, the stronger they become.

The Orici

The worst of the mockery was Adria. In 2005 Vala Mal Doran, a woman of this galaxy who had been carried into theirs, found herself with child by the power of the Ori alone, with no father at all.

The child was born in 2006, grew to a woman in a matter of days, and was hailed as the Orici, the will of the Ori made flesh. She was a mockery of the Incarnation from the first. She was also made to lead their crusade.

The crusade

In 2005 Daniel Jackson and Vala Mal Doran found the Ori's galaxy, using a device of the Ancients. Soon afterwards the Priors began coming through the Stargates into this one. In 2006 a Prior's plague reached Earth, and a cure was found only just in time.

Later that year the Priors opened a great gate, large enough for warships, and the Ori's fleet came through it. It broke the ships of Earth and the free Jaffa that tried to stop it. Then the crusade began to take world after world.

Adria led it. She went from world to world as the Orici, and every world she came to either bowed or burnt.

The fall of the Ori

In 2007 a weapon made long ago by one of the Ancients, for use against beings of the higher planes, was sent into the Ori's galaxy. It could not kill them, for Maiar cannot be killed, but it broke their power and drove them out of the place where they had hidden, into the outer darkness with their master.

Adria was not with them. Later that year Ba'al seized her and tried to make her his host. When the Tok'ra had taken him out of her, she rose to a higher plane herself, and took up what was left of the Ori's power.

In 2008 the Ark of Truth, another device of the Ancients, was turned on the Doci at Celestis. Through him the followers of Origin saw the truth: that the Ori were no gods, and that they had never meant to raise anybody. The faith collapsed. Ganos Lal, one of the Ancients, took Adria out of the world into a struggle without end, as Oma Desala had taken Anubis.

pages.title: Otherworld (realm)
infobox: Marvel Comics (Marvel UK), with J. R. R. Tolkien
The Grey Havens, the last harbour of the Elves in Middle-earth
Avalon; the Otherworld of Britain's folk tales
When the last ship sailed, after King Arthur's day
The Elves who stayed, with other Fair Folk
Mists, standing stones and old roads
Britain, the Netherworld and a great many other worlds
pages.html:
Otherworld is the hidden country that lies alongside Britain, reached through mists, standing stones and old roads. It was once the Grey Havens, the last harbour of the Elves in Middle-earth, to which King Arthur was borne after Camlann. When the last ship sailed, the Elves who stayed did not let their harbour fade, and it passed out of the circles of the world. Legend remembers it as Avalon. Roma rules it from the Starlight Citadel, Arthur sleeps in it, and it is the source of Captain Britain's power.

The Havens

Círdan the Shipwright founded the Grey Havens at the start of the Second Age, at the mouth of the river Lune. For thousands of years the ships of the Elves sailed from them into the West. By King Arthur's day only a few Elves were left there. They forged Excalibur for Arthur, and the Lady of the Lake, who was one of them, gave it to him. When he lay dying after Camlann, about 537, he was carried to the Havens in a barge.

In time the last ship sailed. The Elves who meant to stay did not let the Havens fade with them. They took their harbour out of the circles of the world, as Aman had been taken out of them long before, though Otherworld is not Aman, nor anything like it. It is the Havens, removed from the world, and it has been beside Britain ever since. The folk tales of Britain call it the Otherworld. Its own people call one of its lands Avalon, which is why legend has always confused the two.

Its people

Its people are the Elves who stayed, with other Fair Folk who came to them. Many of the Fair Folk who once walked the hills of Britain and Ireland withdrew there when men turned against them. Some of them are small, quick and very rude. One of these, Jackdaw, followed Captain Britain out of Otherworld in 1980 and died on another world in 1982.

Arthur lies there still, asleep, as the old saying promised he would. In 1980 the servants of the Netherworld stole him from his rest and hid him on an island far out at sea. Captain Britain found him there and broke the giants who guarded him. The king did not wake. Nobody has woken him.

Ways in

The ways between Otherworld and Britain run through mists, through standing stones or along old roads that few now remember. Its own tales say that twelve walkers made the paths in the old days, and that six of them made false ones, which lead travellers into danger or madness. A ring of stones that Merlin calls the Siege Perilous is one of the true ways. Brian Braddock was carried into it from the foot of a cliff on 13 October 1976, and he came out of it as Captain Britain.

Because it lies outside the circles of the world, Otherworld borders a great many worlds besides this one. That is how the Captain Britain Corps, which keeps its hall there, can guard the Britains of other worlds. It also borders the Netherworld, a dark country whose masters call themselves gods. They are nothing of the kind, and they have made war on Otherworld more than once.

Rule

Otherworld is ruled by Roma, an Elf-lady of the Havens, as its Majestrix. Gandalf fostered her long ago, and to those who know him there he is Merlin, as he was at Camelot. Roma keeps the Starlight Citadel and commands the Captain Britain Corps. The enchantment that gives Captain Britain his power is hers and Merlin's, an Elvish working of Otherworld that draws on the strength gathered about the British Isles.

Sir James Braddock, Captain Britain's father, spent part of his youth in Otherworld as Merlin's friend, and his eldest son, Jamie, was born there about 1944. Brian's spirit went there in 1977. He died at its gates in 1979, was made again there in 1983 and mourned Merlin there in 1984. In 1998 he married Meggan there, with Roma presiding.

Otherworld and the wizards

Most witches and wizards know Avalon only from legend, as the place Arthur was carried after Camlann. The Ministry of Magic knows more than it says. It knows that Otherworld is there, and it leaves it strictly alone.

pages.title: Pete Wisdom
infobox: Blades of white heat, thrown or held, from his fingertips
Harold Wisdom, a detective of Scotland Yard
MI6; Black Air, until the end of 1994
pages.html:
Pete Wisdom is a British secret agent and a mutant, who can throw knives of white heat from his fingertips. In the summer of 1994 he works for Black Air, the most secret of the government's services for the unexplained, and most of the work it gives him is killing. At the end of 1994 he got out. In 1995 he joined the Excalibur team on Muir Island, where he fell in love with Kitty Pryde, and she with him. It lasted until 1998.

Family

Pete is the son of Harold Wisdom, a detective of Scotland Yard. His sister, Romany, is an occultist who worked for the police's Department of Unusual Deaths.

In August 1987 their mother was among the people shot dead at Hungerford. She was waiting for a visit from Pete that he had put off after a quarrel. He blames himself for her death, and so does his father.

Black Air

Pete went into MI6, then moved across to Black Air. For a time he was the lover of his superior there, Michele Scicluna. The work was mostly killing, and he came to hate it. In the summer of 1994 he is still one of Black Air's agents.

At the end of 1994, after what he had done at its base at Ronsaphan, in Thailand, he asked to leave. Black Air let him go on one condition: that he went first with the Excalibur team to Genosha, as its observer. There, fighting beside the island's refugees, he showed for the first time that he was a mutant.

Dream Nails, 1995

In the summer of 1995 his friend Ed Culley died, and a pathologist found that something alien had killed him. Pete borrowed one of the team's aircraft to go to London, and Kitty Pryde was sent with him. Old friends in the services, Doyle of MI6, Pitman of MI5 and Jardine of Criminal Intelligence, pointed him towards Dream Nails, a Black Air base in the Midlands.

There Shrine, a Black Air telepath, very nearly killed him with a bacterium called Blood Eagle while she dragged his worst memories into the light. Pete got free. He and Kitty blew the place up. Afterwards she asked him to join the team, and kissed him.

The Excalibur team, 1995 to 1998

Piotr Rasputin, who had loved Kitty for years, saw them kiss on the quay at Muir Island and went for him. Pete burnt Piotr's spine before the others could stop them, and spent a week in a wheelchair afterwards, mocking anybody who came near.

In 1996 he came face to face again with Scratch, a mutant killer of Black Air who had once murdered everybody at a school in Norfolk. Years before, Pete had torn half his face off. In the London fires that summer Lockheed the dragon burnt Scratch to save Pete's life. That autumn Pete told Kitty that he loved her.

In 1997 what was left of Black Air hired Sari St Hubbins, a contract killer who had once been his lover, to kill him. She held him in Kassel, in Germany, with a device on his neck to stop his powers; he burnt through his shackles and walked away. In the same months his friend Jardine was shot dead, while Kurt Wagner was handed over to alien hunters in Venice.

Guilt made Pete surly and hard to live with. It drove Kitty away. In March 1998 he packed his bag and left Muir Island on a fishing boat while she watched from a window. That August he was invited to the wedding of Brian Braddock and Meggan in Otherworld. He stayed at home with a drink, staring at the card.

Later years

Afterwards he gathered old hands from the intelligence services against the secret agencies that do the dirtiest work. For a time he led X-Force.

The Third World War

Pete was in his sixties when the Third World War broke out in 2026. In the war he used everything he had learnt in the services to get hunted mutants out of Britain by the old secret roads, until the hunters caught up with him.

Powers

Pete soaks up heat from the sunlight and the air about him. He lets it out from his fingertips as blades of white heat, said to be as hot as the surface of the sun. He can hold them as claws, throw them like knives or use them to break his fall after a long leap. His years in the services taught him the rest.

pages.title: Pietro Maximoff
infobox: Django and Marya Maximoff, of a Romani band in Transia
Luna, born at the turn of 1982
The Brotherhood of Evil Mutants (1964 to 1965); the Avengers (from 1965); X-Factor (1991 to 1993)
pages.html:
Pietro Maximoff, called Quicksilver, is a mutant who can run faster than sound. He is the twin brother of the Scarlet Witch and the son of Magneto. He is also a Squib. His mother was a Romani witch, and his sister is a witch too, but Pietro was born without a drop of magic. He has served with the Avengers on and off since 1965. In 1974 he married Crystal of the Inhumans.

The tribe

Pietro was born on Wundagore Mountain in 1946, the son of Magda Eisenhardt, who had fled from Magneto, and the twin of Wanda. Django and Marya Maximoff raised the two of them in the wagons of a Romani band in Transia. The band's witches saw early that Wanda had her mother's magic in her. They saw just as early that her brother had none. While his sister had her first lessons in witchcraft, Pietro sat outside them, and he minded it more than he ever said.

Before he was ten he found a gift of his own. He could run faster than any horse in Transia, and soon faster than anybody had ever run. It was a mutant's power, not a wizard's. When villagers burnt the band's wagons and the twins were lost, it was Pietro's speed that kept the two of them fed. When a mob tied Wanda to a stake early in 1964, it was Magneto who saved her, and the twins owed him their lives.

The Brotherhood and the Avengers, 1964 to 1974

In 1964 Pietro joined Magneto's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants as Quicksilver, with his sister as the Scarlet Witch. In 1965, when the Brotherhood broke up, the twins joined the Avengers under Captain America, with Hawkeye beside them. Pietro was fast, proud and short-tempered. He watched over his sister more fiercely than she liked. In December 1965 he cleared the towns of Japan in front of Godzilla with the Flash of the Justice League, who was a great deal faster, which Pietro did not enjoy.

When Wanda was shot on a mission against Magneto late in the 1960s, Pietro took her away from the team. Later he was badly hurt himself. Crystal of the Inhumans found him, took him home to Attilan and nursed him back to health. He fell in love with her. He never did approve of his sister's love for the Vision.

Crystal and Luna, 1974 to 1987

In 1974 Pietro married Crystal, the first marriage ever made between an Inhuman and an outsider. Ultron came uninvited to the wedding, where Franklin Richards, the sleeping son of the Fantastic Four, woke and destroyed him. At the turn of 1982 Crystal gave birth to their daughter, Luna, on the Moon, where the Inhumans had just moved their city. Luna was an ordinary human child, without a trace of power. Soon afterwards Magneto came to tell the twins that he was their father.

In the middle of the 1980s the marriage nearly broke. Crystal fell in love with a neighbour, and Pietro, half mad with jealousy, framed the Avengers for treason. It came out in 1987 that Maximus, Crystal's mad cousin, had been working on both their minds. Pietro was cured, and the Avengers took him back.

X-Factor and 1994

From the end of 1991 Pietro served with X-Factor, the government's team of mutants, until he walked out on it in 1993. In the summer of 1994 he is in his late forties and has retired. He and Crystal live apart. She lives at Avengers Mansion with Luna, and she has grown fond of the Black Knight.

Pietro has never had any dealings with the wizarding world. Like most Squibs he knows perfectly well that it is there, since he grew up among its witches. He has never wanted anything to do with it.

Later years

In 1996 Pietro came out of retirement to fight Onslaught, survived the battle that August, but lost both his sister and his wife to it until December 1997.

The Third World War

Pietro was eighty when the Third World War broke out in 2026, and still faster than anybody alive. In the war he ran the people of a city out ahead of the bombs, back and forth, until he could run no more.

pages.title: Piotr Rasputin
infobox: Colossus of the X-Men; Peter Rasputin; Piotr Nikolaievitch Rasputin
