About 1956, on the Ust-Ordynsky Collective, near Lake Baikal in Siberia
Turns his whole body into living steel
Nikolai and Alexandra Rasputin, killed in 1993
Illyana, died of the Legacy Virus in 1993
The X-Men, 1975 to 1993; the Acolytes, 1993 to 1995; the Excalibur team, 1995 to 1998; the X-Men again, from 1998
The space station Avalon, among Magneto's Acolytes
January 2001, setting free the cure for the Legacy Virus; found alive in 2004
pages.html:
Piotr Rasputin is the Russian farm boy who can turn himself into living steel, the gentlest and strongest of the X-Men, who fought under the name Colossus. He would rather paint than fight, and he has never yet refused a fight that needed him. In 1993, with his parents murdered and his little sister dead of the Legacy Virus, he went over to Magneto. In the summer of 1994 he is on the space station Avalon among the Acolytes, Magneto's followers, trying to keep the gentler of them from the worst of Exodus. In 1995 he came to Muir Island, where he served with the Excalibur team until 1998.

The collective farm

Piotr was born about 1956 on the Ust-Ordynsky Collective, a farm near Lake Baikal in Siberia, the son of Nikolai and Alexandra Rasputin. His elder brother, Mikhail, became a cosmonaut and was given out as killed in an accident in space. The truth, which Piotr learnt many years later, was that Mikhail was a mutant, and that the state had hidden him away. Piotr's little sister, Illyana, was born after Mikhail had gone.

Piotr found his own power in his teens, when a runaway tractor bore down on Illyana. He turned to steel and stopped it. His father found the change hard to accept, and the family had to keep it quiet.

The X-Men, 1975 to 1984

In 1975 Charles Xavier came to the farm. He was gathering a new team to rescue his first X-Men from Krakoa, the living island, and Piotr went with him as Colossus. He was about nineteen, and a long way from home.

He fought the Shi'ar Imperial Guard at the M'Kraan Crystal in 1977. In 1979 the assassin Arcade got hold of him in Murderworld and turned his mind against his friends for a while. Later that year, in Edinburgh, he killed Kevin MacTaggert, the mutant called Proteus, to save Kevin's mother, Moira. Kevin could bend everything round him except metal. Piotr did what had to be done, and it troubled him for years.

Kitty Pryde came to the school at thirteen, at the start of 1980, and she adored him from the first. He was ten years older, and he was kind to her without letting it become anything more. In September 1983, in Japan, he cleared the harbour with Wolverine while Storm turned Godzilla out to sea.

In 1984 the Beyonder carried him off to Battleworld with the other heroes of the Secret Wars. There he fell in love with Zsaji, an alien healer, who gave her life to bring the fallen heroes back. He came home grieving for her. He told Kitty, who was nearly eighteen by then, that his heart had gone elsewhere. Then he went out and picked a fight with the Juggernaut in a bar.

Silence, 1986 to 1991

Late in 1986 Harpoon, one of the killers who massacred the Morlocks in the tunnels under New York, nearly killed Kitty Pryde. Piotr killed Riptide, another of them. Magneto, who was running Xavier's school by then, healed his wounds, but the healing left him paralysed for a time. He recovered on Muir Island in Moira MacTaggert's care.

In 1987 he died with the rest of the X-Men in Dallas, fighting the Adversary. Roma of Otherworld brought them back, and they went on in secret from a base in the Australian outback, while the world believed them dead.

In 1989 he passed through the Siege Perilous, Roma's gift to the X-Men, a gate that gives those who go through it a new life. He came out in New York with no memory of the old one. As Peter Nicholas he made a name for himself as a painter. In 1991 the Shadow King took hold of him through that new self, and Charles Xavier could free him only by wiping Peter Nicholas away. Piotr came back to himself and rejoined the X-Men.

Illyana, 1993

In another world beyond this one he found Mikhail alive, and lost him again when Mikhail, out of his mind, led the Morlocks into what looked like mass death. Early in 1993 agents of the Russian state killed his parents. Illyana came to live at the mansion in Westchester. In a fight with the X-Cutioner that year Piotr took a blow to the head which locked him in his steel form. He could no longer feel his sister's skin when he held her.

Illyana caught the Legacy Virus, and in the summer of 1993 she died of it. Piotr turned cold and silent. At her funeral in August Magneto came for the X-Men, and Piotr turned on his friends to let him go free. Then he went with him to Avalon.

Avalon, 1993 to 1995

Piotr was aboard Avalon when the X-Men came up after the blackout of August 1993. Xavier left Magneto in a coma. Piotr stayed with the Acolytes all the same, believing that the gentler part of Magneto's teaching was worth keeping alive. Most of them shunned him. A few, among them Amelia Voght and Scanner, came to respect him for standing up to Exodus, the zealot who leads them now.

In September 1993 Charles Xavier and the Excalibur team drew him down to Muir Island, with Kitty Pryde's help, to mend his injury. Moira MacTaggert repaired his brain, and he was flesh again. He spoke openly to Kitty for the first time since Illyana's death. Then he went back to Avalon.

In the summer of 1994 he is still there, an X-Man among the Acolytes.

In the summer of 1995 Avalon was wrecked and fell from the sky. Piotr got the helpless Magneto into an escape pod with him, which came down in Antarctica, where Magneto disappeared. Piotr had nowhere left to go but to Kitty.

Muir Island, 1995 to 1998

In September 1995, having crossed half the world, he reached Muir Island and saw Kitty kiss Pete Wisdom on the quay. He went for Pete. Pete burnt his spine with his knives of heat before Captain Britain and Meggan could stop the fight. Both men ended up in Moira's medical wing. Moira mended Piotr's spine and saved Pete. Piotr was ashamed of himself. They forgave him. He stayed on Muir Island to make amends, and by the spring of 1996 he was one of the team.

In 1996 he broke open the roof of Black Air's station in North Yorkshire, and fought through the summer that London burned. That winter the Acolytes, rebuilding Avalon from its wreckage, asked him to come back. He met two of them under the Australian outback and told them to think for themselves.

Early in 1997 he painted a portrait of Meggan as a wedding present for Brian Braddock. When Brian lost his powers that spring and went away to find himself, Piotr looked after her. In the summer a bomb brought down their aeroplane over the Swiss Alps, and he carried her through the snow to safety. They grew closer than either of them had meant.

When Brian came home in August 1998, Piotr told him that the fault was all his own, to shield Meggan. Meggan told Brian the truth herself, and Brian married her all the same. At the wedding Piotr walked down the aisle with Kitty. Afterwards he told his friends that he was going home to the X-Men with Kitty and Kurt Wagner. With that the Excalibur team came to an end.

Later years

Back in Westchester, Piotr found Mikhail again, and lost him in the end. In January 2001 Hank McCoy finished a cure for the Legacy Virus, working from Moira MacTaggert's research. It could spread only through the air, and it would kill the first mutant who carried it. Piotr did not want anybody else to die as Illyana had died. He injected himself with it, and the plague was gone. Kitty Pryde took his ashes home to Russia.

The body that was burnt had not been his. Ord, an alien of the Breakworld, had stolen him away to study the cure in his blood. In 2004 the X-Men found him alive, and he came home to them.

The Third World War

Piotr was seventy when the Third World War broke out in 2026, and still the strongest of the X-Men. In the 2030s, while Kitty Pryde walked the prisoners of the Sentinels' camps out through the walls, he held the gate behind her in his steel. Neither of them came out of the last camp.

Powers and gifts

Piotr can turn his whole body into a living steel, though never only part of it. In that form he stands seven feet seven inches tall, a foot taller than he does in the flesh, and weighs more than twice as much. He is enormously strong, bullets bounce off him, and he needs neither food, water nor air. Great heat followed by sudden cold can hurt him.

Scott Summers taught him judo, while Kurt Wagner taught him to fence. His truest gift is for painting, which he would rather do than anything else.

pages.title: PISCES
infobox: A secret section of British intelligence
In the First World War, as a section of psychics
By the insects from Shaggai, from 1968; its leadership theirs by 1988
pages.html:
PISCES is the secret section of British intelligence that deals with the unnatural, the nearest thing Britain has to Delta Green. It began in the First World War as a small section of psychics working for military intelligence, and took its present name in the Second, when its warnings to Winston Churchill earned it a place in the war. It fought the Karotechia beside Delta Green from 1942. Since 1968 it has been eaten away from within by the insects from Shaggai, and by 1988 they had its leadership.

The psychics

In the First World War British military intelligence set up a small section to make use of psychics. In the spring of 1925, when Cthulhu stirred in his sleep in the Pacific, its psychics broke down one after another, and the section very nearly died with them.

The war

In the Second World War the section's predictions for Winston Churchill saved it, and it was made over as PISCES. It fought the Karotechia in occupied Europe. Its first operation with Delta Green came in 1942, and the two fought the rest of the war as allies. Afterwards the friendship cooled, and in time it soured.

Goatswood

In 1968 PISCES raided Goatswood, a village of the Severn Valley in Gloucestershire, where the insects from Shaggai had long had their temple. The raid failed in the way that mattered most. The insects escaped it, and some of them went home inside the heads of PISCES's own agents.

The insects inside

From those few agents the insects spread through PISCES. By 1988 they had its leadership. In 1994 PISCES still looks like what it was, a hard-pressed British section doing difficult work in secret. Its masters are no longer British, or human.

Black Air

Since the early 1990s PISCES has shared its ground with Black Air, a secret unit that grew out of the Ministry of Defence to deal with superhumans and the unexplained. The two know of each other. Neither trusts the other any further than it trusts anybody else.

pages.title: Professor Horatio Hart
infobox: A laboratory in the hills outside Crossworld City, California
A mind kept alive in virtual reality since about 1984
A face on the laboratory's screens
pages.html:
Professor Horatio Hart is the scientist who, with his friend Tyler Steele, discovered the way into virtual reality. He has had no body since about 1984, when Grimlord all but killed him. His mind lives on in the machines of his laboratory outside Crossworld City, where he appears as a face on a screen. In September 1994 he called three young people to that laboratory, making them the VR Troopers.

The work with Tyler Steele

Horatio Hart was once a man like any other, a scientist of Crossworld City. Tyler Steele was his colleague, besides being his closest friend. Together, in secret, they found that virtual reality was a real world lying beside this one. They built a hidden laboratory in the hills, with the machines to reach it.

They found out what lived there too. Grimlord, the master of that world, meant to break through the reality barrier with an army. The two scientists designed the VR Troopers to stop him: armour, weapons and machines made in virtual reality for human beings to use. Professor Hart kept the old plans in a vault at Crossworld University.

The face on the screen

About 1984 Grimlord came for them both. He left Professor Hart with injuries no doctor could have mended. Tyler Steele saved his friend in the only way open to him, by sending his mind across into virtual reality. It has had to remain there ever since.

Then Tyler Steele was taken, so the Professor was alone. He cannot leave his machines. He can see through them, speak through them and work through them, with nothing left of the man but a face on a screen. For ten years he kept the laboratory running. He has never learnt who Grimlord is when he is not Grimlord.

Mentor of the Troopers

On 3 September 1994 he sent a message to the computer of Tyler Steele's son, Ryan. Ryan came to the laboratory with his friends Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese. The Professor told them the truth, played them the recording that he had made with Tyler Steele, then gave each of them a Virtualizer.

From then on he was their teacher as well as their armourer. He built their weapons, sent their machines to them, and kept watch on the barrier for the first sign of Grimlord's creatures coming through. When they asked him how to prepare for the next attack, he told them to keep up their karate.

He also mended what Grimlord broke. He turned Ryan's dog, Jeb, back into a dog when Grimlord had made a monster of him. He turned the three Troopers back into adults when a ray had made children of them. In November 1994 he gave the cyborg Dark Heart the memories of Ryan Steele, which woke Tyler Steele's mind inside him. In February 1995 he freed the mind of Amy, the girl inside the Red Python.

He had a Virtualizer of his own. In February 1995 he lent it to Ryan, who needed it to fight a copy of himself.

Later

Grimlord's aircraft bombed the laboratory in November 1994, while Ryan took his wounded father to a second, secret laboratory in the mountains. The Professor came through it. The Troopers were working from his laboratory again afterwards.

In October 1995 he joined the two halves of Kaitlin Star together after Grimlord's mirror machine had split her. The following month Knighttime put the three Troopers into a sleep full of false dreams. The Professor went in after them by way of a visor, to tell them that none of it was real.

When the record stops, in February 1996, he was still what he had been: a mind in a machine. His friend Tyler Steele was free again. His enemy was unbeaten. Nothing is recorded of him afterwards.

pages.title: Promethea
infobox: After 1969, by Grace Sterling and Terona Washington
Grace Sterling; Terona Washington, from February 1995
An island of its own in San Francisco Bay
A building that is also a ship
New sources of energy, among other things
Matt Cook, the second Green Ranger, December 1994 to February 1995
The designs of Terra Venture, which left Earth in 1999
pages.html:
Promethea is a technology company of California, one of the great firms of Silicon Valley, which Grace Sterling and Terona Washington founded after they came home from the Moon in 1969. It deals in new sources of energy, among other things. Its machines are far beyond anything a firm on Earth ought to be able to build, because they draw on the dagger of Psycho Green, the creature the two of them fought that night. In the summer of 1994 it is the Power Rangers' ally, which is not the same as telling them everything. From its designs came Terra Venture, the space colony that left Earth in 1999.

Founding

In July 1969 Zordon made Grace Sterling and Terona Washington Power Rangers for a single night. They came back from the Moon with three of their team dead. When Zordon took the powers back, the two of them left him in anger.

Grace resigned from NASA. With Terona she founded Promethea, to keep the promise that Nikolai Chukarin, the Blue Ranger, had asked of them before he died: to make sure that the world they had saved was worth saving. The company grew into one of the great firms of Silicon Valley, with an island of its own in San Francisco Bay. It has made Grace a billionaire, who gives a great deal of the money away. She runs it. Terona has been beside her from the start.

What it has

Grace kept Psycho Green's dagger. The energy in it is behind Promethea's machines, which Zordon himself thought more than human. Its headquarters is also a ship, which can fly. Its scientists, among them Andrea, work on things that no other firm has heard of. Its teleporters can snatch a man off a street in Angel Grove.

Promethea has soldiers of its own. It has relief crews, who go into cities after a monster has been through them. It has the Mechazord, a fighting giant like the Rangers' Megazord, which draws nothing from the Morphin Grid. Grace pilots it herself. Under one of its buildings, in the summer of 1994, is a cell that nobody outside the company has been told about.

Promethea and the Rangers

In August 1993 Promethea offered Billy Cranston, a schoolboy of Angel Grove who was also the Blue Ranger, an internship. His father thought it very important. Billy turned it down.

At the end of October 1993 Rita Repulsa turned the Rangers' own Zords on the cities of the world. Promethea's crews went into the cities that had been hit. A great many people were afraid of the Rangers after that. Grace went on television to defend them, at a time when few others would.

In the same weeks Promethea's soldiers found Lord Drakkon, the Tommy Oliver of another world, without his powers in the mountains. Grace locked him in the cell, in restraints of pure energy, without a word to Zordon or the Rangers.

That winter a Promethea aeroplane vanished over a village in the Carpathians that was on no map. The Rangers found Finster there, making monsters that could pass for people. Afterwards Grace told them who she was, then offered them an alliance. Promethea tracked the hidden monsters by the energy they gave off, while the Rangers dealt with them. Its methods wore on them. In the summer of 1994 it traced a monster to four streets of Vancouver, where its soldiers arrested everybody they found.

At the end of August 1994 Billy noticed that one of Promethea's buildings was drawing only half its power. He went to see why, which is how he found Drakkon in his cell. Jason Lee Scott, the Red Ranger, ended the alliance on the spot.

The ship

Days later Drakkon escaped to murder Tommy Oliver, then set out to rob every Ranger there had ever been. Jason sent for Grace after all. Promethea hardened the Rangers' morphers against him. Its headquarters rose into the air, carrying a company of Rangers to the Moon of Drakkon's world to free the Rangers he held.

When Drakkon unmade the world, Grace armoured the ship with the dagger's power. It was thrown clear, into a dark place where there was no Morphin Grid at all. Its crew were there for more than forty days, with Terona Washington, the Ranger Slayer and a handful of Rangers, before they found the way home. The Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of Drakkon's world, stayed in Promethea's service afterwards, patrolling space in her Gravezord.

The second Green Ranger

In November 1994 Lord Zedd sent a monster to dig into Promethea for the dagger. Grace fought it in the Mechazord, then blew the dagger to pieces before Goldar could carry it off. It was an illusion. The real dagger never left her keeping.

Billy Cranston saw through it. His price for keeping quiet was Promethea's help with the dead Dragon Coin, which the two of them woke with the dagger's energy. Grace persuaded him to let Promethea choose who should carry it. In the middle of December 1994, at a word from Billy, she set the plan going, which Promethea called the Green Protocol. Its Green Ranger was Matt Cook, a schoolboy of Angel Grove whom its teleporter had snatched from under a falling wall.

Matt trained at Promethea, answering to Grace alone. It rebuilt the Dragonzord for him. When Alpha 5 traced his teleport to Promethea, Zordon quarrelled bitterly with Grace about the coin.

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus of Eltar invaded the Earth. Eltarian troops closed in on Promethea, where the Rangers had fallen back. His Empyreals destroyed its headquarters, with Grace inside. Matt dug her out. Afterwards Promethea had the means of making Zordon a new tube. His tube stood at one of its bases until a new Command Center was brought home, while its soldiers guarded the Power Chamber.

The Arch

There is an old gate into the Morphin Grid in the Bermuda Triangle, the Arch. Grace had found it, then rebuilt it in secret. In February 1995 Mistress Vile, who had been Rita Repulsa, raided Promethea, carried Grace off to the Arch, then opened it with the Zeo Crystal to bring Dark Specter through. There Matt Cook, under her spell, killed Grace.

When the Rangers cleansed the Grid that month, the world was mended. Promethea's headquarters stood whole again. Nobody outside a handful of people remembered the weeks before. The world believed instead that Grace Sterling had been lost with a Promethea research ship in the Bermuda Triangle.

Terona Washington and Terra Venture

Promethea passed to Terona Washington, Grace's co-founder and the last of the 1969 Rangers. He closed its secret work. He kept its ships, then gave the rest of his life to the promise that Nikolai Chukarin had asked of them on the Moon.

Promethea's headquarters had always been a ship. From its designs came the colony ship built with the Global Space Alliance, which left Earth in 1999 as Terra Venture, the space colony that the Galaxy Rangers defended.

pages.title: Protected Planets Treaty
infobox: Asgard and the Goa'uld System Lords
Listed worlds are closed to Goa'uld attack and enslavement
pages.html:
The Protected Planets Treaty is the agreement between Asgard and the Goa'uld System Lords under which a list of inhabited worlds is closed to Goa'uld attack. Asgard enforces it. In 1994 Earth is not on the list.

Origins

The treaty was the end of a war that had begun in Egypt. Thor, the son of Odin, fought beside the Egyptians when they rose against Ra some five thousand years ago. For thousands of years afterwards he hunted the Goa'uld wherever they came near the North, killing Jaffa who surrendered and tearing symbiotes out of their hosts. In the 870s he followed Heru'ur to the world now called Cimmeria and freed the Northmen Heru'ur had taken there. Towards the end of the tenth century Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard. Thor destroyed two of the three.

The System Lords asked for terms soon afterwards. It is said in Asgard, and denied by the System Lords, that their first demand was that Thor should not be present when the treaty was signed. Earth was left off the list. Since the rising against Ra the Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of it, and a world that may not be named cannot very well be written into a treaty. It was also the one world in the galaxy where they could be surest of finding Thor.

Terms

Under the treaty the System Lords undertake not to attack, invade or enslave the people of the protected worlds. The list runs to some two dozen planets, most of them young human societies that Asgard has taken under its care. Asgard, for its part, may not use its own technology to advance the peoples it protects. A serious breach on one world could free the Goa'uld to attack all of them.

On some of the worlds in its care Asgard has also left defences of its own. On the planet Cimmeria, for instance, a device called Thor's Hammer traps any Goa'uld who comes through the gate.

The treaty holds because Asgard is stronger than any System Lord, and could destroy their fleets if they broke it. The System Lords dislike it, test it and look for ways round it. They keep it only so long as they believe Asgard can make them.

Asgard and the Replicator war

Asgard, the realm of Odin and Thor, has been at war for years with the Replicators, self-copying machines that devour technology. The war is fought in the Pegasus galaxy, far beyond this one, where Asgard has its worlds among the stars, and it has drawn Asgard's strength far away. Thor himself is absent from Earth because of it, and Eric Masterson carries the mace in his place as Thunderstrike. The more of Asgard's strength the Replicators consume, the less there is to hold the System Lords to the treaty.

The System Lords know nothing of the Replicators, or of Asgard's war with them. Asgard has made sure of it. The treaty now holds largely on a bluff: Asgard keeps up the appearance of its old strength over the protected worlds, and the System Lords, who do not know the bluff is false, dare not call it.

Earth

Earth is not a protected world in 1994.

In 1997 the Goa'uld came back to Earth for the first time in more than a thousand years. It was Apophis who came. Ra's death in 1994 had left the System Lords without a leader, and Apophis was making the most of it. He knew that the people of Earth had killed Ra, and he had heard that Thor seemed to be busy elsewhere, although he had no idea where or why.

Earth answered by sending its own teams out through the gate, and they killed Goa'uld. The System Lords came to look on Earth as fair game, and they have taken a close interest in it ever since. Earth's place under the treaty had to be negotiated afterwards, with Asgard as mediator.

In 1999 Thor himself opened the talks that put Earth under the treaty. Cronus, Nirrti and Lord Yu came through the Stargate for them. Nirrti tried to wreck the talks and failed. Cronus agreed to Earth's protection, as did Yu. None of the System Lords mentioned their old demand that Thor should stay away.

Later years

The bluff was never thinner than in the year after August 1996, when Thor fell in the battle with Onslaught and Asgard believed him dead. Asgard told the System Lords nothing. Apophis came to Earth in 1997 on the rumour that Thor was busy, never knowing that he was gone. The same year Thor's Hammer fell on Cimmeria. When Heru'ur came to take that world in 1998, it was Thor himself, home again, who answered.

The treaty bound Asgard as tightly as ever. In 2001 SG-1's own wormhole damaged the sun of K'Tau, a protected world whose people pray to Freyr. Freyr and the High Council would not mend it. To use Asgard's science there would have broken the treaty, leaving every protected world open to the Goa'uld. The sun cleared in the end, though nobody could say quite why.

In 2005 the rule of the System Lords collapsed, and the treaty had nobody left to bind. Asgard drew back from this galaxy afterwards. In 2007 it gave up its worlds among the stars altogether, leaving its knowledge to the people of Earth.

In the saga

The treaty has not been named in the saga. Its effects are on the Muggle news all the same. The hammer-bearing Avenger of Dudley's lunchbox has been replaced by a big blond man with a mace (Book Four, Chapter Three), because Thor is away at Asgard's war.

pages.title: Psylocke
infobox: Betsy Braddock; Elizabeth Braddock; Lady Mandarin
1953, in England, minutes before her twin brother
Sir James and Lady Elizabeth Braddock
Brian Braddock (Captain Britain), her twin; Jamie Braddock, her elder brother
Telepathy; a psychic blade; once precognition
Charter pilot; model; agent of S.T.R.I.K.E.'s Psi Division
Since 1989, that of Kwannon, an assassin of the Hand
Captain Britain, in 1985; Lady Mandarin, in 1989
pages.html:
Psylocke is Betsy Braddock, an English telepath, the twin sister of Captain Britain and a member of the X-Men since 1986. She has been a charter pilot, a model, a government psychic and, for a few weeks in 1985, Captain Britain herself, until Slaymaster tore out her eyes. Mojo gave her new ones and the name she is known by. In 1989 she came out of the Siege Perilous with no memory, and the Hand of Japan made her its assassin. Since then she has lived in the body of another woman, Kwannon, which was not her choice. She is a mutant, not a witch. In the summer of 1994 she is an X-Man at Professor Xavier's school in New York.

Early life

Betsy was born in England in 1953, a few minutes before her twin, Brian, which she has never let him forget. She grew up at Braddock Manor in Maldon, Essex. She was a tomboy who took after their elder brother, Jamie, more than after Brian: she liked speed, heights and anything her mother would rather she did not do. By her twenties she was a charter pilot with an aeroplane of her own.

Like Brian and Jamie, she is descended from King Arthur through a Squib branch of his house. None of them knows it. Her powers have nothing to do with that blood. She is a mutant.

Brian's secret, 1976 to 1977

In December 1976, after Jamie was nearly killed in a crash, Betsy flew Brian home to Maldon. On the way something reached into her mind. It was Lord Synne, who had made himself master of the villages round the Manor, and who set her on her brothers. Brian had to show himself as Captain Britain to stop her killing Jamie. When she came to herself she remembered very little of it.

In the first weeks of 1977 agents of the Red Skull took her hostage with Jamie, and Captain Britain freed them with Captain America. Brian took off his mask to prove to them who he was. That autumn Betsy began to model, and she found that she sometimes knew what was going to happen before it did. Not long afterwards she dyed her hair purple, which suited her.

The Psi Division

By the early 1980s she could read minds, a little. S.T.R.I.K.E., the British agency that worked beside S.H.I.E.L.D., recruited her into its Psi Division, a section of psychics, where she fell in love with another of them, Tom Lennox. The Psi Division had nothing to do with PISCES, the much older and far more secret section of British intelligence that also kept psychics. Each knew the other existed, and neither trusted the other.

The Vixen, a crime lord, had her people inside S.T.R.I.K.E., and in the spring of 1983 she hired the assassin Slaymaster to kill the Psi Division one by one. Betsy rang Brian, whom she had not seen in years. They met in a hamburger bar and did not at first know each other. Brian beat Slaymaster in Denmark Street. Only Betsy, Tom and their friend Alison Double were left alive, so all three went to live at Braddock Manor.

The warp, 1983 to 1985

Over the winter of 1983 to 1984 Sir James Jaspers bent Britain out of shape, and people with powers were rounded up into camps. Betsy's foresight kept her friends a step ahead of his men for a while. Then they were caught. Tom gave his life so that the others could get away, and Betsy, whose mind was open to his, felt him die. She was taken to a camp until the warp broke.

In 1985 Brian's double from another world, Kaptain Briton, came to the Manor in Brian's clothes. He tried to force himself on Betsy. She killed him with her mind. Later that year she let RCX, the government body that followed S.T.R.I.K.E., bring the Warpies to live at the Manor, children whom the warp had changed. Brian left in a fury.

Captain Britain, 1985

While Brian was away, RCX persuaded Betsy to take his place. Captain UK, Linda McQuillan, trained her, and in the autumn of 1985 she put on the uniform Kaptain Briton had left behind. In December the Vixen lured her into a trap with a party of kidnapped children. Betsy insulted her, which was a mistake. Slaymaster beat her senseless, then tore out her eyes. Brian came in time to kill him, though not in time to save her sight.

She turned down the cybernetic eyes RCX offered her. She went to the Swiss chateau of her friend Alison Double to recover, and she found she could still see the world through the eyes of the people about her.

Mojo

Early in 1986 she was carried off from the Alps by Mojo, a monstrous impresario from another world whose people live on broadcasts, and by his six-armed servant, Spiral. They gave her bright new eyes, renamed her Psylocke and made her the star of Mojo's broadcasts. Her new eyes were cameras. Everything she saw went back to Mojo's audience.

In the summer of 1986 the New Mutants, Professor Xavier's younger pupils, came to her rescue, and she went back with them to his school in Westchester. When she found out later what her eyes were for, she kept it to herself.

The X-Men, 1986 to 1989

That autumn hired killers butchered the Morlocks, the mutants who lived in the tunnels under New York, and the X-Men brought the wounded to the school. Sabretooth broke in after them. Betsy drew him away from the injured, kept him busy until Wolverine could take over, then took from his mind the name of the man who had sent him. Wolverine was impressed, and in October 1986 she joined the X-Men.

Early in 1987 she held Kitty Pryde's mind together while Kitty, unable to stop passing through solid things, came apart. In 1987 she fought the alien Horde beside her brother for the first time in years. Weeks later the X-Men died in Dallas, and Roma of Otherworld gave them back their lives. They let the world go on thinking them dead.

In 1988 they made their home in a base in the Australian outback, which they had taken from the cyborg Reavers. Betsy, who felt herself a liability in a fight, took to wearing armour. She grew close to Piotr Rasputin there, and sat for his drawings. In 1989, with half the team gone, she led what was left of it.

That autumn she foresaw the Reavers killing them all, with herself turned into one of them. She sent the last of the X-Men through the Siege Perilous, Roma's gate that judges those who pass and gives the worthy a new life. When Havok refused, she forced him through with her mind. Then she followed them as the Reavers came in.

Lady Mandarin, 1989 to 1991

Betsy came out of the Siege Perilous on an island in the South China Sea, naked and with no memory at all. The Hand, an old order of ninja, found her and took her to its leader, Matsu'o Tsurayaba. He wanted her telepathy to mend the mind of his lover, Kwannon, an assassin who lay brain-dead after a fall. He took both women to Spiral. Spiral did more than she was asked. She exchanged them, mind for body, and mixed what each of them was, so that most of Betsy woke in Kwannon's body believing herself Lady Mandarin, the Hand's chief assassin.

The Hand sent her against Wolverine late in 1989. Her psychic blade drew up his memories of her, and they broke the Hand's hold. She got away with Wolverine and his young companion, Jubilee. In the autumn of 1990 the three of them went to Genosha, where they helped to free the New Mutants. Back in Westchester, Betsy kept away from her brother for a while. Nobody, Forge included, could undo what had been done to her.

Revanche, 1991 to 1994

When the X-Men split into two teams in 1991, Betsy went to Cyclops's, where she flirted with him more than was wise. Jean Grey had it out with her in a battle of wills. In February 1993 another woman came to the school, calling herself Revanche, and took off her mask to show Betsy's own face. She said that she was the real Betsy Braddock. Neither Wolverine's senses nor Xavier's telepathy could tell them apart. For a year Betsy did not know who she was. Hank McCoy never doubted her, and they became firm friends.

Revanche was Kwannon, in Betsy's first body, with some of Betsy's memories in her. Early in 1994 the Legacy Virus took hold of her. As it burnt through her, her mind cleared, and she saw the truth. In March 1994, before she died, she gave back to Betsy what was hers, telepathy included.

In 1994

In the summer of 1994 Betsy is an X-Man at Professor Xavier's school in Westchester County, New York, and a stronger telepath than she has ever been. She is learning to use her full power with Jean Grey's help. She fights with a blade of pure thought that she can drive into a mind, and with what Kwannon's body knows of the Hand's arts. She has come to terms with the face in her mirror, more or less. In July 1994 she was among the X-Men taken prisoner at the school by the Phalanx, beings of living metal, and freed weeks later by friends who had escaped them.

That autumn she fell in love with Warren Worthington, Archangel, who knew as well as she did what it was to have a body changed by an enemy.

Later years

In the autumn of 1995 Sabretooth broke out of his cell at the school and gutted her. Warren, Wolverine and Stephen Strange fetched a draught from the dark realm of the Crimson Dawn that saved her life. It left her with a red mark over her left eye, a way of melting into shadows and a coldness that frightened her friends. In 1997 the master of the Crimson Dawn, Kuragari, tried to take her as his bride. Warren beat him, and paid for her freedom with some of his own life.

In the spring of 1998 the Shadow King, who feeds on minds, tricked her into a blow that silenced every telepath on Earth. She caught him in turn, at a cost: to keep him caged she could use her telepathy for nothing else.

The Third World War

Betsy was seventy-three when the Third World War broke out in 2026. She fell in it, defending a refuge of young mutants against the hunters, and she fought to the last. Of all the X-Men only Wolverine outlived the war.

pages.title: Qo'noS
infobox: Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'Sins of the Father' (19 March 1990); named as Kronos in Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country (6 December 1991)
The great hall, where the High Council meets
Praxis, the Empire's chief source of energy
The volcano of Kri'stak; the Lake of Lusor
pages.html:
Qo'noS is the homeworld of the Klingons, called Kronos by the people of Earth. Its capital is the First City, where the High Council of the Klingon Empire meets in the great hall.

The world

The oldest stories of Qo'noS belong to the volcano of Kri'stak, in whose molten rock Kahless the Unforgettable forged the first bat'leth in the ninth century, and to the Lake of Lusor, where he cooled it. It was on Qo'noS that he killed the tyrant Molor and founded the Klingon Empire.

In the fourteenth century the Hur'q came out of the stars to plunder it, carrying off its treasures. Emperors ruled from Qo'noS until the last of them died about 2069. After that the Chancellor ruled from the great hall of the First City with the High Council, whose members came from the great houses of the Empire. Boreth, the world of the monastery that waited for Kahless, lies elsewhere. So does Rura Penthe, the frozen prison world.

Visitors from Earth

The first ship from Earth to reach Qo'noS was the Enterprise NX-01, in April 2151. Captain Jonathan Archer brought home the wounded courier Klaang, whose blood held proof that the Suliban had been attacking Klingon houses. He delivered him to the Chancellor in the great hall.

pages.title: Rachel Summers
infobox: Rachel Grey; Rachel Anne Summers; Mother Askani
In a future that will now never happen
Scott Summers and Jean Grey, of that future
Telepathy; telekinesis; the power of the Phoenix Force
The X-Men (1984 to 1986); the Excalibur team (1987 to 1994)
Early in 1994, into the stream of time, in Brian Braddock's place
Gone; nobody in this time knows where
pages.html:
Rachel Summers is a mutant of great psychic power who comes from a future that will now never happen, the daughter Scott Summers and Jean Grey had in that other world. The Phoenix Force carried her into the present in 1984, and she has borne its power ever since. In 1987 it was she who gave the Excalibur team its name, for King Arthur's sword. Early in 1994 she went into the stream of time so that Brian Braddock could come home, and in the summer of that year she is gone.

The world she came from

In Rachel's world Jean Grey never died, and she married Scott Summers. Rachel was born to them with her mother's psychic gifts. In that world Senator Robert Kelly was murdered by mutants in 1980, the Mutant Registration Act followed, and in time the Sentinels took over North America.

Agents of a man called Ahab took Rachel as a girl, drugged her and broke her into a Hound, a telepath trained to hunt down other mutants. She felt every victim she found. In the end she turned on Ahab and scarred his face. For that she was sent to the camps, where she found friends among the last free mutants: Wolverine, Magneto, Storm, Kate Pryde and Franklin Richards, whom she loved.

It was Rachel who sent Kate Pryde's mind back to the year 1980, to save Senator Kelly. It did not save her world. Kate had gone into the past of another world, this one, so Rachel's own future went on unchanged. Not long afterwards the Phoenix Force tore Rachel out of her time and set her down in this one.

The X-Men, 1984 to 1986

She arrived in 1984, a young woman who had known the X-Men only as the dead and the hunted. Here they were alive. Her mother was believed dead in this world, and her father had married another woman, Madelyne Pryor. Rachel joined the X-Men. In 1985 she took the name Phoenix, and she found that the Phoenix Force was with her still.

She hated Selene, an ancient mutant who lives on other people's life, with a hatred she had brought from her own world. In 1986 she tried to kill her, and Wolverine stopped her with his claws. Hurt and ashamed, she fled. Spiral, the servant of Mojo, carried her off to Mojo's world, where she was made to perform for his audiences.

The Excalibur team, 1987 to 1991

At the end of 1987 she escaped from Mojo to Britain, with his Warwolves and the Technet on her trail. The X-Men were dead, as everyone believed. Four friends saved her instead: Kitty Pryde, Kurt Wagner, Captain Britain and Meggan. By the campfire in the Highlands she argued that Xavier's dream must not die with his students. She named the new team for Arthur's sword.

For the next few years she was the team's strongest member and its most troubled. She felt every death in London as it happened. In 1989 she called on Jean Grey, who had been found alive and was caring for Scott's baby son, Nathan. She was not made welcome. In the summer of 1990 an adult Franklin Richards from her own world appeared in New York, and she went to him. Over the Statue of Liberty she met her mother properly for the first time. Jean and Scott would not accept her as their daughter. She left them stung.

On the journey across the worlds she lived for a while on a farm with another world's Jean Grey, until slavers killed her. In another world she watched that world's Jean die in her arms.

Professor Alistaire Stuart of the Weird Happenings Organisation fell in love with her. In 1990 Galactus came to the lighthouse to destroy her body, with the Phoenix Force inside it. She resolved to give herself up for the Earth's sake, and he let her be. Over the winter of 1990 to 1991 she drove the creature D'spayre out of London with Commander Dai Thomas. It had stolen a child to feed on the grief of the city. Saturnyne, who had wanted her taken for years as a danger to every world, called off the hunt for her in 1991.

Necrom and the stars, 1992 to 1993

In the spring of 1992 Necrom came for the Phoenix Force. Rachel let him take all of it, more than he could hold, and it destroyed him. It left her all but dead, with her memories in pieces. That summer the Phoenix Force told Xavier, Jean and the team something of its own story. Then it carried her body away to the stars to mend her mind.

She came home early in 1993. That year she took the team into her own world, where she and Kate Pryde, linking their minds with the Sentinels' masters, set every Sentinel to protecting all life. Then she chose to come back. She had accepted that her past could not be changed.

Into the stream of time, 1994

In 1993 Brian Braddock was lost in the stream of time. Early in 1994 Rachel learnt that he could only come home if she went in his place, since the two of them could not share the same time. Kitty helped her face her years as a Hound one last time. Then she went into the stream, with Meggan and Amanda Sefton beside her. Brian came out of it. In the summer of 1994 her friends do not know where she is.

Mother Askani

She came out two thousand years ahead, in a world that Apocalypse ruled. There she gathered rebels and founded a sisterhood, the Askani. It was one of her people who fetched the infant Nathan forward to her time in 1991, when he was dying of the techno-organic virus, so that he could be cured. The Askani made a clone of the boy in case he died. Apocalypse's people stole it, and it grew up as Stryfe.

They wounded her so gravely that she lived on only through machines. Soon after Scott and Jean were married, she drew their minds two thousand years forward to raise Nathan. They came back moments after they had left, ten years older inside. She seemed to die then. In fact she had been flung still further ahead.

Nathan, who had come back to the present as Cable, found her there at last and brought her home. By 2004 she was back with the X-Men, as Marvel Girl, the name her mother had once worn. She took her mother's surname, Grey. Some years later the Shi'ar sent commandos to wipe out the Grey family, to rid the universe of the Phoenix's line. They killed everyone at a family gathering except Rachel, whom they marked to be hunted. She went into space after the men who had ordered it, and fought for a time with the Starjammers of her grandfather, Corsair.

The Third World War

Rachel came home from the stars before the Third World War. In the world she came from she had been made to hunt mutants for the Sentinels' masters. In this world's war she hid them instead, covering whole refuges from the Sentinels with her mind, until the machines found her.

Powers

Rachel is a telepath and a telekinetic of the first rank. She can reach minds at great distances, fly, and lift or crush almost anything. As the bearer of the Phoenix Force she has had, at times, power on a scale that frightens Galactus. She still bears the marks that Ahab's people tattooed on her face when she was a Hound.

pages.title: Rahne Sinclair
infobox: 1969, in Ullapool, in the north-west of Scotland
Changes into a wolf, or into a shape halfway between wolf and girl; the senses of a wolf
The Reverend Craig, a Presbyterian minister, though she did not know it until 1995
The New Mutants, 1982 to 1991; X-Factor, 1991 to 1995; the Excalibur team, 1995 to 1998
pages.html:
Rahne Sinclair is a Scottish mutant who can turn herself into a wolf, the shy, devout girl from Ullapool whom Moira MacTaggert saved from a mob and brought up as her own. She was one of the first New Mutants at Xavier's school. In the summer of 1994 she is twenty-five, serving with X-Factor, the American government's own team of mutants. In 1995 she came home to Muir Island to look after Moira, and she served with the Excalibur team until it broke up in 1998.

Ullapool

Rahne was born in Ullapool in 1969. Her mother died at the birth, and Moira MacTaggert, who delivered her, was there to see it. The Reverend Craig, a Presbyterian minister of the town, took the baby in as a ward of his church. He never told her that he was her father.

He brought her up hard. She was taught that her body was shameful and that anything strange was the Devil's work.

The New Mutants, 1982 to 1991

In 1982, when she was thirteen, her power woke, and she found that she could change into a wolf. The Reverend Craig called her a devil and led a mob after her to burn her. Moira MacTaggert got her away. She made herself the girl's guardian, took her to Charles Xavier's school in Westchester and saw her made one of the New Mutants, Xavier's younger class.

Rahne was painfully shy and quick to blame herself. Her best friend was Danielle Moonstar. In 1985 Loki carried the New Mutants off to Asgard, where Rahne fell for Hrimhari, a prince of the wolves of that country. She came home with her friends all the same.

Her first real love was Doug Ramsey, a boy who could understand any language, spoken, written or made by machines. At the end of 1987 he stepped in front of a bullet meant for her, and died.

In the autumn of 1990, on Genosha, she was taken and conditioned as a slave. Warlock, the alien who had been Doug's closest friend, was killed there, and at Rahne's asking his ashes were scattered over Doug's grave. She broke free by turning halfway into a wolf, but she could not take her human shape again without falling back under the conditioning. After Genosha's masters fell she stayed on the island for a while to help rebuild it.

X-Factor, 1991 to 1995

In 1991 she joined X-Factor, the team of mutants that works for the American government. At the end of 1993 the mutant Haven freed her at last from what Genosha had done to her mind, so that she could be a girl again without danger.

In the summer of 1994 she is in America with X-Factor, twenty-five years old and still uneasy in her own skin.

In August 1994, in the Alps, she climbed the Phalanx's Babel Spire with Douglock and Sam Guthrie. Douglock had Doug's face and Doug's memories. He knocked her down and seemed to go over to the Phalanx, then gave himself up to stop them. When he rose again afterwards she held on to him.

Muir Island, 1995 to 1998

In the summer of 1995 Rahne came to Muir Island on leave, and stayed. Moira lied to her about the Legacy Virus, but Rahne soon knew the truth, and that autumn she joined the Excalibur team to be near her.

In November 1995 a fire broke out in the Kinross woods across the water. A frightened young mutant, Bridgit Shane, had started it after the Reverend Craig drove her out. Rahne went to face him under his church spire, and learnt at last that he was her father.

She grew close to Douglock, who carried Doug Ramsey's memories without being Doug, and he fell in love with her. In 1996, when Kitty Pryde phased into Doug's grave at Salem Center, Rahne was with her, and saw that Doug's bones were still there. In 1997 she kissed Douglock before flying to New York for a reunion of the New Mutants.

In the autumn of 1997 Moira sealed herself into quarantine in her laboratory, and Rahne leapt in after her as the doors closed. The two of them quarrelled, then made it up. In March 1998 Douglock broke into the quarantine to free her. She was furious, and told him to get over his crush.

In August 1998 she helped Meggan choose her wedding dress in London, and she was a bridesmaid at the wedding in Otherworld. There she said sorry to Douglock.

Later years

After the Excalibur team broke up, Rahne stayed on Muir Island with Moira and Douglock. In 1999 Douglock turned out to be Warlock himself, and she stood by him. Late in 2000 Mystique's Brotherhood attacked the island. Mystique shot Rahne with a weapon that took her powers away, and Moira was killed.

In time she found her powers again. She went on to serve with X-Factor and X-Force. Her faith has stayed with her through all of it.

The Third World War

Rahne was fifty-seven when the Third World War broke out in 2026. In the war she guided hunted mutants over the hills by night, in her wolf's shape, ahead of the Sentinels. She was killed on the last of those crossings. Her faith stayed with her to the end.

pages.title: Raiden
infobox: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty (13 November 2001)
Jack the Ripper; the White Devil
pages.html:
Raiden, whose name is Jack, is a soldier born in Liberia. In the summer of 1994 he is a child of ten or a little more, fighting in his country's civil war for Solidus Snake, the man who killed his parents. He grew up to kill Solidus on the roof of Federal Hall in New York, in 2009. Later most of his body was replaced with machinery. He was still fighting in 2018.

Liberia

Jack was born in Liberia in the early 1980s. Civil war broke out there at the end of 1989. A foreign commander fighting in it killed the boy's parents, took him in, then gave him his name. The commander was Solidus Snake, the third clone of Big Boss, who called himself the child's godfather.

Solidus raised boys to kill, of whom Jack was the best. At barely ten he was the leader of the Small Boy Unit. The men he fought called him Jack the Ripper, or the White Devil.

After the war relief workers took the surviving children out of the country. Jack was sent to America. There the Patriots took charge of him, though he never knew it. He put Liberia out of his mind so thoroughly that he could not have said where he had grown up.

The Big Shell

He joined the United States Army. Nearly all his training was done in simulations, three hundred missions of them, without one day of real fighting. On 30 April 2007 he met a young woman called Rosemary outside Federal Hall in New York. She was an analyst for the Army. She had also been set to report on him to the Patriots, though she came to love him.

On 29 April 2009 he was sent alone into the Big Shell, an offshore plant in New York Bay that had been seized by terrorists. He believed that he belonged to FOXHOUND, which no longer existed. The colonel who spoke in his ear was not a man either. It was the Patriots' computer GW, using Roy Campbell's voice. The whole operation had been arranged to find out whether a soldier like Solid Snake could be produced to order, with Jack as the test.

He came through it with the help of Snake himself, who was there under a false name. At dawn on 30 April, two years to the day after he met Rosemary, he fought Solidus with swords on the roof of Federal Hall. He killed him. Rosemary was waiting in the street below, carrying their child.

The machine

Jack did not settle. Olga Gurlukovich had died protecting him on the Big Shell, because the Patriots held her baby. He went looking for the child. To learn where she was, he fetched Big Boss's body out of the Patriots' keeping for EVA. In 2011 he found the girl, Sunny, whom he left in the care of Solid Snake's friend Hal Emmerich.

In 2012 the Patriots caught him. At Area 51 they rebuilt him as a machine, with little of his own body left. EVA's people got him out.

In 2014 he fought beside Snake, mostly against Vamp, who had killed Emma Emmerich. Vamp was a living man kept alive by machines in his blood, never one of the Kindred, whatever his name suggested. Jack killed him at Shadow Moses. When it was all over Rosemary came to find him. She brought their son, John, who he had been told was never born.

2018

By 2018 Jack worked as a bodyguard for Maverick Security Consulting, while his wife lived safely in New Zealand with their son. That year the mercenaries of Desperado Enforcement murdered the African prime minister he was guarding. The Brazilian swordsman Samuel Rodrigues cut out his left eye, taking his left arm as well.

Rebuilt once more, he followed Desperado to Abkhazia. From there he went to a laboratory in Mexico, where the brains of orphaned children were being cut out to be trained as soldiers. He attacked the headquarters of Desperado's partners, World Marshal, in Denver.

In Pakistan he killed Rodrigues in a duel. Then he killed the man behind it all, Senator Steven Armstrong of Colorado, with Rodrigues's own sword. Afterwards he left Maverick to fight on alone.

pages.title: Raiga Saejima
infobox: Crow the Phantom Knight; the priestess Bikuu
pages.html:
Raiga Saejima was the only child of Kouga Saejima, the Golden Knight, by the painter Kaoru Mitsuki. He was the third Garo of his family in a row. He was born about 2014. His parents vanished when he was six. He was brought up by the family butler, trained by his father's friend Rei Suzumura, and held the title by 2040, when he destroyed the ancient Horror Eyrith.

The boy who was left

In about 2020 Raiga was out with his parents when a rift opened in the air. It dragged his mother in. His father went after her, stopping only to promise Raiga that he would come back. Raiga was six. He grew up taking both of them for dead.

Gonza Kurahashi, who had brought up Kouga, brought up Raiga too. When the boy was about ten he made up his mind to be Garo. Around then he met a priestess named Akari. He gave her a little bell, which he called a sound of light.

On the eve of his tenth birthday Rei Suzumura came for him, as Rei had promised Kouga he would. He took the boy on a night's hunt. Then he asked him what he wanted to do with his life. Raiga chose the sword. He became Rei's pupil. In time he became a knight.

The armour

When he went to the Tower of Heroic Spirits to claim his family's armour, the spirits of the dead Golden Knights turned him away. The armour had a holder. That was how he learnt that his father was alive, somewhere outside the world. Kouga gave the title up to him, with the ring Zaruba.

He was a different sort of knight from his father: easy, sociable, quick to smile, the kindest in the Order by Gonza's account. He fought with scabbard as well as sword. He drew a little, like his mother, with less talent.

Eyrith

In the spring of 2040 the knight Eiji Busujima broke into a museum, where he smashed an old stone slab. Sealed in it was Eyrith, a Horror whose flower was said to raise the dead, with nine lesser Horrors as the stones of her prison. Busujima wanted his dead lover back. She was Akari, who had died of an illness.

All ten got loose. Eyrith would hide inside the others, as a seed, until the last of them was caught. If she bloomed, the wall between the world of men and the Makai would come down. The Senate sent Raiga to hunt the nine. It gave him Crow the Phantom Knight, of the Shadowfolk, to help him. It also gave him Mayuri, a silent young woman, kept asleep between tasks, who could seal Horrors inside her own body.

The Senate called Mayuri a Madou tool. Raiga declined to. So did Gonza. Over that summer she learnt, slowly, to be a person. That same year Zaji, the gathered malice of every Horror the Golden Knights have killed, came for Raiga in his own house. Beating it won him the Madou Horse Gouten.

In September Eyrith took Crow's body, flew to a lake, and grew into a great tree. She told Raiga that it was she who had taken his mother. She could give his parents back, she said. He refused her. She burnt away his armour's time with a kiss, so that he became the Lost Soul Beast, turning on his friends. The sound of Akari's bell brought him back. He mastered the beast, then destroyed her.

Mayuri sealed what was left of Eyrith back into the slab. It nearly killed her. She slept for many days in the Saejima house. Then she woke, with her memory whole, smiling at him.

The black train

By 2045 Mayuri was growing flowers at the Saejima house. On a night of full moon a man in a white mask, Shiroku, took her. Raiga followed aboard a black train that ran towards the Makai. A boy called Baderu showed him the way through it.

Shiroku was the leftover evil of Kiba, the armour of Barago, who had murdered Raiga's grandfather. Baderu was that grandfather, Taiga. Kiba joined itself to the armour of a legendary knight. It had Raiga beaten when Kouga came through to stand over his son. Kaoru's thought reached Mayuri. Together the two women sent Raiga the golden armour, made clean.

Grandfather, father and son broke Kiba apart. Raiga struck the last blow. Afterwards it was found that Mayuri was carrying his child. Kouga went away again, promising, as he had once before, to come back.

pages.title: Red Ronin
infobox: Rob Takiguchi; Robert Takiguchi; Dr Yuriko Takiguchi
A giant fighting robot in the shape of a samurai
A little over a hundred feet
Dr Yuriko Takiguchi, with Tamara Hashioka
Stark International, at Detroit, for S.H.I.E.L.D.
A blade of burning hydrogen; a shield; magnetic cables
pages.html:
Red Ronin is a giant robot in the shape of a samurai, a hundred feet tall, built for S.H.I.E.L.D. in 1978 to fight Godzilla. Stark International made it. It answers to one pilot only: Rob Takiguchi, who was twelve when he stole it, and who was on Godzilla's side.

The machine

When Godzilla came ashore in America in 1977, Nick Fury of S.H.I.E.L.D. sent for Dr Yuriko Takiguchi, Japan's leading authority on the creature. Takiguchi joined the Godzilla Squad that Dum Dum Dugan led. He designed a fighting machine as big as Godzilla himself. His assistant Tamara Hashioka did the engineering, with technicians from Stark International, who built it at Detroit under the name SJ3RX. Tony Stark had examined the wreck of Mechagodzilla in 1975, which had taught his engineers a good deal.

It stands a little over a hundred feet tall. It flies on rockets in its legs. It carries a shield on one arm. Its chief weapon is a blade of burning hydrogen. It can also throw out a magnetic field, besides cables strong enough to hold Godzilla.

Rob Takiguchi

Dr Takiguchi's grandson, Rob, was twelve. He had come to America with his grandfather. He did not want Godzilla killed, having decided, on very little evidence, that Godzilla was not wicked. Early in 1978 he climbed into the new machine, put on the pilot's helmet, then took off. He called it Red Ronin, after the masterless samurai of old Japan.

The helmet took the print of his mind. After that the robot would not work for anybody else, which was awkward for S.H.I.E.L.D. Rob used it to turn Godzilla away from a missile base near San Diego. He fought him just hard enough to drive him off, then put the Helicarrier Behemoth out of action before it could finish the job.

In the Grand Canyon he helped Godzilla against Yetrigar, a giant of the Sasquatch kind, whom he buried under a rockslide. Near Salt Lake City the two of them faced three monsters sent by the Megans, an alien people. One of the three, Rhiahn, cut off Red Ronin's head with the blade on its tail. Rob was knocked senseless, though not badly hurt. Godzilla killed Rhiahn with its own blades.

New York, 1979

Rob had no robot when Godzilla came to New York. Godzilla had been shrunk by Henry Pym's gas, which was wearing off; at one point he was the height of a man. Rob hid him under a hat with a long coat, which deceived nobody.

In the summer of 1979 Godzilla stood at his full height on the Empire State Building, with the Avengers failing to move him. Rob called to him from the Behemoth. Godzilla took the boy in his hand. He let Rob guide him down to the harbour, where the water closed over his head.

Rob was born about 1966, so in the summer of 1994 he is a man of about twenty-eight.

pages.title: Red Talons
infobox: The last wildernesses of the north
Hatred of mankind's spread; longing for the Impergium
pages.html:
The Red Talons are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: a tribe of wolves, born only to wolves. They hold that mankind is the gravest wound ever dealt to Gaia, and they would gladly see the Impergium begin again.

Totem and ways

The Red Talons follow Griffin, a fierce hunting spirit of the high and lonely places. Every member of the tribe is lupus, born to a wolf and raised as one. They take human shape only when they must, and they dislike it. They speak little in human tongues, and they hardly ever use human tools. They keep their histories in the old way, by howl and by memory.

To the Talons, the Wyrm and mankind are hard to tell apart. They have watched the forests cut down, the rivers poisoned and the wolves shot out of one country after another. They hold that the Garou made a great mistake when they ended the culling of humanity at the Concord. Many of them would see it begin again tomorrow.

Homelands

Their Kinfolk are wolves, so the tribe lives where wolves still live. That means the last wildernesses of the north: the mountain forests of North America, the Russian taiga and the empty uplands of Europe. As the wolves have been driven back, so have the Red Talons. The tribe is smaller than it once was.

Place in the world

Other Garou respect the Talons for their purity and for their ferocity against the Wyrm. They fear their hatred of humans. The Talons despise the Glass Walkers and the Bone Gnawers for living among men. They scorn the Children of Gaia as soft, and they are wary even of homid Garou of other tribes. Vampires they regard with a particular loathing.

pages.title: Rei Suzumura
infobox: Zero the Silver Fanged Knight; Silver Fanged Knight Zero
Douji, a knight of the same line
A boy of seven in Douji's house
pages.html:
Rei Suzumura became Zero, the Silver Fanged Knight, the Makai Knight who came east in 2005 to kill Kouga Saejima. He ended as Kouga's closest friend. In the summer of 1994 he is a boy of seven called Ginga, a foundling being brought up by the old knight Douji beside a girl named Shizuka. Years later Barago murdered them both, in armour that the boy took for Garo's.

Ginga

Rei was born about 1987. He had no family, only the name Ginga. Douji, an ageing knight of the line of the Silver Fanged Knight, found the boy, took pity on him, and brought him up as his own son.

Douji had taken in a girl as well, Shizuka, another orphan. The two children grew up together. Douji taught the boy the sword. By the time Ginga was nearly grown he was promised to Shizuka, while the old man had become too ill to leave his bed.

One night a knight in armour came to the house. He wanted a potion Douji kept, which could change a man's face. Douji would not hand it over. The knight killed him, then Shizuka, then took what he had come for. Ginga saw only the armour, which he took for the golden armour of Garo.

He buried them himself. He gave up his name, called himself Rei, took up Douji's armour with the title of Zero, and went looking for the Golden Knight. Douji's Madou tool, the pendant Silva, went with him. She called him Zero, never Rei. For a long time she was the only company he kept.

The duel with Garo

In November 2005 he found Kouga Saejima in the eastern district. He was eighteen, quick, smiling, sweet-toothed, with two short swords where other knights carry one long one. He began by wounding Kouga with a poisoned dagger. Then he tried to kill Kaoru Mitsuki, the girl Kouga was protecting, on the grounds that the law required it. On 18 November the two knights fought each other in their armour through the middle of the city. Kouga won.

The three priestesses of the Eastern Watchdog encouraged his grudge, which suited plans of their own. For months he worked beside Kouga without trusting him. In January 2006 he saved Kaoru from a Horror, then told her his real name.

The truth

In March 2006 the knight who had killed Douji showed himself. He was Barago, who wore the black armour of Kiba. He had wanted the potion to hide a scar that Taiga Saejima had cut into his face. Rei had spent his hatred on the wrong man, whose own father the same murderer had killed.

He fought beside Kouga from then on. When Kouga lost himself in his armour, it was Rei who called him back. While Kouga went after Messiah, Rei faced Gulm, the body that the three priestesses had taken. Silva was broken taking a blow meant for him. Gonza Kurahashi, the Saejimas' butler, walked into the fight carrying a weapon of Soul Metal that he should not have been able to lift. It gave Rei the opening to run Gulm through.

The Order entered him formally in the line of the Silver Fanged Knights. It gave him the eastern district, which had been Kouga's. He mended Silva himself. From then on she rode on the back of his left glove.

Later battles

In December 2006 he was sent to Kantai to guard the rite of the Midnight Sun, where he fought the puppets of Legules beside Kouga Saejima and Tsubasa Yamagatana. In 2011 Sigma Fudou cut the Seal of Destruction into him, as into Kouga. He was with Kouga when Sigma was unmasked. In March 2012 he fought in the true Makai against the engine Idea.

When Kouga came back from the Promised Ground in 2013, the knights had been holding a contest whose winner might visit one of his dead. Rei had won it. Kouga challenged him to a duel on the spot. The spirit of Taiga Saejima took Rei's side.

The commune of Ring

In March 2014 Rei found something new: a Horror named Ring who kept a commune where Horrors lived beside human beings. The people were safe, on condition that one of them was handed over each month to be eaten. A blind priestess, Iyu, kept them calm with her singing. The Senate sent Rei to destroy the place. With him went a priest called Kain, with Iyu's own daughter, Yuna, who had thought her mother dead for ten years.

Ring believed in what he had built. Rei's answer was the Order's: a knight does not trade one life for others. At the end Iyu stopped singing for Ring, to save her daughter, so he ate her. Rei destroyed him while Yuna sang her mother's song.

The dragon

By 2017 Rei had been moved to another city. Between January and March of that year he was caught up in the last of an old wrong. Long ago a foundling named Edel had been brought up by a dragon. He had loved another dragon, Nova. Makai Priests of that day seized Nova for her power, which cost her her life. Edel slept for ages, woke hating mankind, and came for the one dragon egg left.

The egg had bonded with a photographer, Alice Hiromi, who thought no better of mankind than Edel did. When it hatched she named the dragon Loop. She flew on it to burn the city. Rei, fighting past his time, became a Lost Soul Beast. He wounded the dragon before the priestess Rekka could bring him back. Loop died. Alice, who was bound to him, died in Rei's arms, leaving a small egg behind.

Raiga

Before Kouga Saejima vanished, in about 2020, he had asked a promise of Rei: that if he did not come back, Rei would see to his son. Rei kept it. On the eve of the boy's tenth birthday, in about 2024, he came to the Saejima house. He took Raiga out on his first night's hunt, then let him choose for himself. Raiga chose the sword. Rei trained him until he was a knight.

He was believed to have gone into the rift himself afterwards, in search of Kouga and Kaoru.

pages.title: Rekka
infobox: Kengi, a Makai Knight (killed by the Horror Karma)
Fighting magic; a flute; the summoning of Makai dragons
Her own district, from 2010; the Senate, by 2017
pages.html:
Rekka is a Makai Priestess who wanted to be a Makai Knight, the daughter of the knight Kengi. Since no woman can lift Soul Metal she learnt the brush instead, dressed like a knight anyway, and hunted Horrors alone. In 2010 she fought beside Kouga Saejima against Karma, the Horror that had killed her father. In the summer of 1994 she is a child.

Kengi's daughter

Rekka's father, Kengi, was a Makai Knight, one of the teachers of the young Kouga Saejima. As a girl she wanted nothing but to follow him. It could not be done. She trained as a priestess under Akaza, an old priest who kept an antique shop, with a fellow pupil named Shiguto.

The Horror Karma killed Kengi. After that Rekka wore a knight's long coat. She spoke like a man. She went after Horrors by herself, sealing them with young Makai dragons that she called out of the air. She was reckless enough to get bystanders hurt.

Karma

In October 2010 the Order sent Kouga after Karma, one of the seven Apostle Horrors, who lived inside mirrors. Rekka wanted the kill for herself. She told him so, attacked him when he found fault with her guard, and lost. He passed on to her some of what his own father had taught him.

Karma's servants drew her into a trap with her father's likeness. Kouga was badly hurt getting her out, with his armour lost in Karma's mirror. Then Rekka found that the priest who had been hiding Karma was her own teacher. Akaza had done it for the sight of his dead wife with their daughter in the glass.

He paid for it. Rekka went into the mirror with Kouga. Akaza gave his life to carry her flute in after her. She played. The souls of everybody Karma had eaten came to the sound, her father's among them, and lent their strength to the golden armour. Kouga destroyed Karma.

Rekka stayed to keep Akaza's district with Shiguto. She gave Kouga a young Makai dragon, to send for her if he needed help. The dragon followed him into the Promised Ground in 2012, in the shape of a blue-skinned girl called Meru.

Later years

In February 2012 she hunted the Horror Sedinbale with Kouga, since it was after Kaoru Mitsuki. Shiguto was half won over by Sigma Fudou's talk of a world without knights, until Rekka reminded him of a promise they had both made to Kouga. In March she took Kaoru to where Kouga was held, went into Sigma's engine with the priestess Jabi, and stood with the priests at the mouth of the true Makai.

By 2017 she was a priestess of the Senate. That winter she worked with Rei Suzumura against Edel, the Dragon Knight, whom even her own dragons obeyed. When Rei lost himself in his armour, she brought him back.

In about 2042 the creature Zaji dragged her into a rift between worlds, meaning to end everybody bound to the line of Garo. There she met Rian, a Makai Priestess of another world. Kouga Saejima, long lost, came out of the dark, cut Zaji down, and vanished again. He left word that he would come back.

pages.title: Replicators
infobox: March 2005, by the weapon of the Ancients on Dakara
pages.html:
The Replicators are machines made of small interlocking blocks, which consume metal and technology in order to build more of themselves. They have spread from world to world. They are at war with Asgard, and it is that war which keeps Thor away from Earth in 1994.

Nature

A single Replicator block is a small grey piece of metal a few centimetres long. Thousands of them lock together to form a working machine, most often a scuttling, spider-like thing about the size of a dog, which can break apart and build itself again at will. They have one purpose, which is to copy themselves. Replicators strip whatever they find of its metal and its most advanced technology, then turn it all into more Replicators. A single block left alive aboard a ship can be enough to take it.

They learn as they go. Weapons that worked against them once soon stop working, because the swarm adapts to whatever is used against it. They are drawn above all to the most advanced technology in reach. That makes Asgard, the most advanced power they have met, their favourite prey.

Origin

The first Replicators were the toys of Reese, an android made in the likeness of a girl by an inventor on a distant world. She built them to protect herself and to keep her company. She could not control them. They destroyed the people who had made her, then went out into the stars.

Some years before 1993 an Asgard ship found Replicators on an isolated world whose people were dead. Not understanding what they were, its crew took some of them aboard to study. The Replicators took the ship instead. That was how the plague reached Asgard's worlds in the Pegasus galaxy.

In April 2002 SG-1 found Reese herself, alone on a dead world, and brought her to Earth. She had the mind of a child, and a child's temper. When she was crossed she set her Replicators loose in Stargate Command. Jack O'Neill shot her, and they fell still. Asgard later used what was left of her to lure the Replicators into its trap on Hala.

War with Asgard

Asgard has fought the Replicators for years in the Pegasus galaxy, far beyond this one, where it has its worlds among the stars. It is losing ground. Thor himself commands Asgard's fleet against them, and the war takes nearly all of Asgard's strength. That is why Thor, the god of thunder, is away from Earth, and why Eric Masterson carries the mace in the Avengers as Thunderstrike. It is also why Asgard has less to spare for enforcing the Protected Planets Treaty against the Goa'uld System Lords.

The war costs Asgard more than ships. The Aesir live for centuries but have children only seldom, so every Asgardian the Replicators kill is a loss that will take generations to make good. The Replicators, which can make a thousand more of themselves from the hull of a single ship, have no such difficulty.

The Goa'uld know nothing of it. Asgard has taken great care that they should not, since the System Lords keep the Protected Planets Treaty only because they believe Asgard could punish them for breaking it. Its ships still show themselves over the protected worlds as if nothing had changed. It is a bluff, and so far it has held.

Against the Tau'ri

In 2000 the Replicators took Thor's own ship, the Biliskner, and came with it to Earth. They meant to land, then devour whatever they found. SG-1 made the ship burn up as it fell into the Pacific. One Replicator lived through it and took a Russian submarine, which had to be destroyed with everything aboard. That summer, in the Pegasus galaxy, Samantha Carter's plan drew a great swarm into Asgard's newest warship, the O'Neill, which blew itself up with them inside.

In 2001 the Replicators met the Goa'uld for the first time, when the supernova at Vorash threw Apophis into another galaxy. They took his ship, then the one he took from SG-1 to get home, and it fell on Delmak with him aboard.

In 2003 they learnt a new shape. Asgard had shut them inside a field on Hala where time ran slow. They turned it round, so that time ran fast instead, and in the centuries it gave them they made themselves human bodies out of something like living cells, far too small to see. Their leaders took their names from the order in which they were made, First to Sixth. SG-1 shut them in again.

In 2004 Asgard crushed Hala's sun into a black hole, but some of them escaped to Orilla. The weapon that Jack O'Neill built there broke the bonds that hold a Replicator together. Fifth, the one SG-1 had left behind on Hala, got away with a Replicator he had made in Samantha Carter's likeness. Early in 2005 she destroyed him and led the Replicators herself.

She brought them into this galaxy. They tore through the fleets of the System Lords, and one of them, wearing her face, killed Lord Yu at the Hasara space station. In March 2005 the Tau'ri, with Ba'al's help, turned the weapon of the Ancients on Dakara against them, and every Replicator in the galaxy fell apart at once. The war was over.

In the saga

The Replicators have not been named in the saga. Their war is behind the change Harry noticed in the Avengers on the Muggle news of 20 August 1994 (Book Four, Chapter Three): the man with the hammer had been replaced by a big blond man with a mace.

pages.title: Revolver Ocelot
infobox: Liquid Ocelot; Major Ocelot; Shalashaska; Adamska
The GRU; the KGB; the CIA; Spetsnaz; FOXHOUND; the Patriots
pages.html:
Revolver Ocelot is a gunman, interrogator and spy who has worked for a great many masters. He has betrayed every one of them but one. He is the son of The Boss, born on the battlefield in Normandy in 1944, which makes him fifty in the summer of 1994. For half a century everything he did, however treacherous it looked, was done for Big Boss.

The Philosophers' child

He was born on 6 June 1944, the day of the Normandy landings, to The Boss of the Cobra Unit. His father was her comrade The Sorrow. The Philosophers took the baby from her at once. They brought him up as an agent of their own, under the name Adamska.

By 1964 he was a major in the Soviet GRU at the age of twenty. He commanded a unit of his own, the Ocelots, under Colonel Volgin.

Tselinoyarsk

He met Naked Snake in Tselinoyarsk in August 1964. Snake beat him more than once, each time leaving him a piece of advice. One was that a revolver would suit him better than an automatic. Ocelot took it. He has carried the Single Action Army ever since, with which he can hit a hidden man by bouncing the bullet off a wall.

It was Ocelot's pistol, going off in Volgin's torture cell, that cost Snake his right eye.

He had never been Volgin's man. He was reporting to the KGB, to the Philosophers and, under the codename ADAM, to the Director of Central Intelligence in Washington. When the operation was over he told the Americans that the record of the Legacy which EVA had carried off to China was a fake. The real one went to the CIA, with half the money.

Big Boss's man
