In 1970 he shot the head of the CIA dead at Langley, arranging it to look like suicide. He took the rest of the Legacy's records to Major Zero, with the names of the Philosophers. He agreed to join Zero's new organisation, the Patriots, on one condition: that Big Boss was part of it.

When Zero fell out with Big Boss, Ocelot stayed inside the Patriots while he served Big Boss in secret. From 1975 he watched over the hospital in Cyprus where Big Boss lay. In 1984 he brought the phantom, Venom Snake, out of the wreck of that hospital to the Seychelles. There he served as interrogator to Diamond Dogs.

He held the rank of major in the Spetsnaz. During the Soviet war in Afghanistan the guerrillas had a name for him, Shalashaska. In 1999 he was recruited into FOXHOUND under the codename Revolver Ocelot.

Shadow Moses

In 2005 he was one of the renegades who seized Shadow Moses Island with Liquid Snake. He tortured the head of DARPA, Donald Anderson, to death. Anderson had once been Sigint, a founder of the Patriots like himself. He tortured Solid Snake too. Gray Fox cut off his right hand with a sword.

He was the only renegade to leave the island alive. He took with him the test data for Metal Gear REX, which he sold all over the world. Afterwards he reported to the President, George Sears, who was Solidus Snake.

In Lyon a surgeon gave him the dead Liquid's right arm in place of his own. From then on Liquid's voice came out of him from time to time, with Liquid's manner.

The Tanker and the Big Shell

On 8 August 2007 he boarded a disguised Marine Corps tanker on the Hudson with the Russian mercenaries of his old comrade Sergei Gurlukovich. He shot Gurlukovich, stole the new Metal Gear RAY that the ship was carrying, then sank her.

On 29 April 2009 he was on the Big Shell beside Solidus Snake. There he shot President James Johnson. He killed Fortune of Dead Cell. Then he told Solidus that the whole affair had been arranged by the Patriots, whose agent he was.

Liquid Ocelot

By 2014 he called himself Liquid Ocelot. The grafted arm was gone by then, replaced with a machine. He had made himself into Liquid Snake's double by hypnosis, helped by the nanomachines in his blood, so thoroughly that the Patriots' computers were deceived.

Through a holding company called Outer Heaven he owned the five largest private armies in the world. That year he seized the system by which the Patriots controlled every soldier's weapon. It was a trap for them. He meant Solid Snake to destroy their computers for him, which Snake did.

He fought Snake with his fists on top of the warship Outer Haven until he could no longer stand. He died as himself. What killed him was a virus in Snake's blood, which the Patriots had made to be rid of their own founders. He was seventy. He had done all of it, with EVA's help, to set Big Boss free.

pages.title: Richard Jenkins
infobox: 17 May 2293, on Starbase Side 7, killed by Imperial stormtroopers
pages.html:
Richard Jenkins was a corporal of the Starfleet Marines, one of the three Marines posted to the USS Enterprise-A in 2293. He was killed on Starbase Side 7 in the first minutes of the Imperial Entanglement.

Service

Corporal Jenkins came from the colony of Eden Prime. He was young, eager to prove himself to Commander John Shepard, whom he admired. On 17 May 2293 he beamed aboard Side 7 with Shepard and Lieutenant Kaidan Alenko. He charged ahead of them into the first Imperial stormtroopers they met, who shot him dead. He was the first of the Federation's people to be killed by the Galactic Empire.

In the saga

Richard Jenkins has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Richie Preston
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Contract with the Dragon' (10 January 2009)
24 January 2009, by Len of Ventara; freed December 2009
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Richie Preston is an American, born about 1987, the spoilt son of a rich family. In January 2009 he was Kamen Rider Incisor, the first of the men of Earth whom Xaviax armed. He did it for money. He was also the first to be vented, by Len of Ventara, on 24 January 2009.

The offer

Richie had never had to earn anything. When he was about twenty-one his family lost patience, cut off his money and told him to find work.

A lawyer who gave his name as Walter Connors came to him with a simpler arrangement. Richie would be paid a million dollars for every armoured man he vented, beginning with the one called Wing Knight. The lawyer was Xaviax. He handed over the Advent Deck of Incisor, contracted to the crab Volcancer. It opened for Richie because he was the mirror twin of Ian, the Ventaran who first wore it.

Xaviax's wider plans did not interest Richie. He wanted the money.

Incisor

On 10 January 2009 Incisor ambushed Kit Taylor in Ventara, on the very day that Kit made his contract with the dragon. A week later he came after him again. When Len of Ventara joined in, Richie walked off. Two against one, he said, was not fair.

On 24 January his motorcycle was repossessed. The same day Len found out who was inside Incisor's armour. He challenged Richie to fight him alone, which Richie accepted. Len vented him.

Afterwards

Kit Taylor was so shaken by what Len had done that he tried to give up being a Rider. Richie lay in the Advent Void for nearly eleven months. In December 2009, with Xaviax dead, Eubulon brought him out, took away his memories of the war, then sent him home. Ian wears the armour of Incisor again.

pages.title: R'lyeh
infobox: The southern Pacific, about 47°9′ south, 126°43′ west
The spawn of Cthulhu, in the Third Age
From the end of February to 2 April 1925
Great blocks of green stone, at angles that are wrong
pages.html:
R'lyeh is the drowned city of Cthulhu, in the loneliest part of the southern Pacific. His spawn built it when they came to the Earth, and the Flood put it under the sea with him inside. It rose for a little over a month in the spring of 1925, long enough for one crew of sailors to land on it, and went down again in a storm.

The city

R'lyeh is built of great slimy blocks of green stone, carved with figures of Cthulhu and of things like him. Its geometry is wrong. Its angles do not behave as angles should: a sailor of the Emma was swallowed by one that was acute, but behaved as if it were obtuse. Men who look at it for long find that their eyes and their minds will not agree about what they see.

At its heart is a great carved door. Behind the door is the house where Cthulhu lies.

Where it lies

The Norwegian sailor who landed on it gave its place as 47°9′ south, 126°43′ west. That is in the emptiest stretch of ocean on the planet, as far from any land as the sea goes. Other charts put it a little to the south and west. Nobody who has gone looking for it has said where they looked.

The drowning

The spawn of Cthulhu built R'lyeh in the Third Age of the world, when they came down to the Earth from the stars, not long after the Elder Things. It stood above the water for long ages, with Cthulhu asleep in it.

The Flood that ended the Ice Age was God's judgement on the old world, and it drowned R'lyeh with the rest. The city did not break. It sank, whole, with Cthulhu inside it, and it lies there still. God's judgement fell on it, and did not finish the thing it held.

The spring of 1925

At the end of February 1925 an earthquake heaved part of R'lyeh up out of the sea. For a month the world's sensitive slept badly. On 23 March the crew of the Emma landed on it, and six of them died there. On 2 April a storm came up, and the city sank again. The freighter Vigilant passed over the place soon afterwards and found nothing but sea.

What has risen may sink, the man who put the pieces together wrote afterwards, and what has sunk may rise.

Since

No ship has reported R'lyeh since. Delta Green would very much like it to stay that way.

pages.title: Rodan
infobox: A giant flying reptile, a pteranodon
1956, in a coal mine in Kyushu
pages.html:
Rodan is a giant flying reptile, a pteranodon with a wingspan of a hundred and twenty metres, that hatched in a flooded coal mine in Kyushu in 1956. He flies faster than sound, so that the wind of his passing knocks buildings flat. He began as a terror to Japan, became Godzilla's rival, then his ally.

The mine, 1956

In 1956 miners began to die in a flooded pit in Kyushu, cut to pieces by something in the water. The killers were Meganulon, giant dragonfly larvae, left alive in a cavern under the workings since the age of the great reptiles.

An engineer at the mine, Shigeru Kawamura, was trapped in the cavern by a rockfall. He came out with his memory gone. It returned when he saw a bird's egg hatch. In the cavern he had watched a far bigger egg crack open, then seen the creature inside eat the Meganulon like grubs.

The palaeontologist Dr Kyuichiro Kashiwagi named the creature Rodan. He believed that the bomb tests had disturbed the earth enough to hatch it. There were two of them, a mated pair. Between them they destroyed the Saikai Bridge near Sasebo, then wrecked Fukuoka with the wind of their wings.

The Self-Defence Forces shelled their nest in the crater of Mount Aso until the volcano erupted. One Rodan fell into the lava. The other would not leave it, so they burnt together.

Godzilla's rival

In January 1965 a Rodan rose out of the crater of Mount Aso. Whether one of the pair had lived or a third egg had hatched, nobody knows. He fought Godzilla at the foot of Mount Fuji. Green Lantern, who had come to Japan with the Justice League, tried to wall the two of them apart with green light, which neither noticed. In the end the Mothra larva talked them both into turning on King Ghidorah.

That December the Xiliens of Planet X carried Rodan off with Godzilla, then sent the two of them back as weapons. The Justice League came back to Japan to hold them off; this time Green Lantern kept Rodan caged in green light for most of an hour. When the Xiliens' control was broken, the pair drove King Ghidorah away again. By 1973 Rodan was living on Monster Island.

Later years

In 1999 the Kilaaks sent him against Moscow. He was one of the ten monsters who met King Ghidorah at Mount Fuji that year, when the dragon was killed.

pages.title: Roland Williams
infobox: Green Hunter, 1996 to 1997; Titanium Silver, from September 1997; Mega Spectra, from February 1998
The Hunter Claw; the Metallix Grappler
pages.html:
Roland Williams is a boy of Charterville whose family keeps Zoom Comics, the town's comic shop. In the summer of 1994 he is about nine years old. In September 1996 a wish made him the Green Hunter Beetleborg, one of the three Beetleborgs. In 1997 he became the Titanium Silver Beetleborg. On 2 March 1998 it was Roland who took the Astral Axe from the Crustaceans, which brought the giant Boron over to the Beetleborgs' side.

Zoom Comics

Roland was born about 1985. His parents, Aaron and Abbie Williams, keep Zoom Comics in Charterville. He has grown up among the comics on its shelves. His best friends, Drew McCormick with his sister, Jo, spend most of their spare time there too.

His grandmother, whom everybody calls Nano, is a martial artist who rides a motorcycle, which makes her quite unlike anybody else's grandmother in the town. Some months after the wish his father went away on business. From then on his mother ran the shop.

It was at Zoom Comics, on 7 September 1996, that the brothers Trip and Van dared the three to go into Hillhurst Mansion.

The Green Hunter Beetleborg

Inside the house the three let Flabber out of the pipe organ, for which he granted them a wish. They wished to be the Beetleborgs. The comic they had in mind was one that Roland's family sold over the counter.

Roland became the Green Hunter Beetleborg, whose armour was modelled on the stag beetle. His weapon was the Hunter Claw, a great pincer that could be thrown like a boomerang. The wish left him a gift out of armour too. At a snap of his fingers he could run faster than the eye could follow.

Nano and the amulet

In September 1996 Nano found an amulet that made a slave of anybody who looked at it. Its holder could give orders even to the monsters of Hillhurst. The amulet had come out of the comics. So had its owner, a monster named LottaMuggs, who wanted it back.

Nano helped the three out of trouble more than once afterwards.

Titanium Silver

Roland fought Vexor's Magnavores beside Drew and Jo until 21 May 1997, when the three sent them back into the comics. On 8 September Nukus destroyed their armour, weapons and powers. The next day Art Fortunes drew the Metallix armour, which Flabber brought to life.

Roland became the Titanium Silver Beetleborg. His new weapon was the Metallix Grappler, which could seize an enemy as the Hunter Claw had. In November 1997 he hunted for the Astral Coins with the others. In February 1998 Roboborg gave all three the Mega Spectra armour.

The Astral Axe

In February 1998 Les Fortunes drew the Astral Axe for the Crustaceans. With it came Boron, a giant made to match Roboborg, who obeyed whoever held the Axe. For three weeks that was one or another of the Beetleborgs' enemies. On 16 February the two giants fought on the Moon.

On 2 March 1998 Nukus loosed his worst monster, Repgillian. The Crustaceans offered to give up the Axe if the three would hand over their Bonders. Roland took the Axe from them instead. Boron answered to him at once, then fought beside Roboborg, so that Repgillian was destroyed. Nukus had lost his best weapon to a schoolboy.

The Power Rangers

On 19 October 1996 the Machine Empire's Cogs came to Charterville with Klank, who carried his small companion, Orbus. Jara of the Magnavores tried to steal Orbus. Roland, the quickest of the three, took him from her while she was busy with the Cogs. Klank snatched him back a moment later.

On 3 May 1997 the Blue Turbo Ranger took off his helmet at Hillhurst, where he turned out to be Justin Stewart, twelve years old. Justin knew the Beetleborgs' comic almost as well as Roland did, which Roland took as a challenge. The two of them argued happily about it by post from then on.

It was Zoom Comics that Justin telephoned on 25 October 1997, when Nukus came to Angel Grove. Roland's mother called him to the telephone without the least idea who was ringing. On 21 February 1998 the Space Rangers helped to get the Astral Axe out of Ecliptor's hands in the Charterville cemetery. It went straight back to the Crustaceans. Nine days later Roland went to fetch it himself.

pages.title: Roma of Otherworld
aliases: the Lady of the Northern Skies
infobox: Marvel Comics (Marvel UK), with J. R. R. Tolkien and Arthurian legend
Excalibur to King Arthur, about 496; the Amulet of Right to Brian Braddock, 1976; the Siege Perilous to the X-Men, 1987
The Lady of the Lake; Nimue; Viviane
pages.html:
Roma is an Elf-lady of the Grey Havens who rules Otherworld as its Majestrix, from the Starlight Citadel. Gandalf fostered her long ago, so she calls him father, and the old stories make her Merlin's daughter. She was the Lady of the Lake who gave King Arthur Excalibur. In 1976 she helped Merlin choose Brian Braddock to be Captain Britain, and she commands the Captain Britain Corps, which guards the Britains of a great many worlds. She is stern, she plans a long way ahead and she is never cruel.

The Lady of the Lake

Roma was one of the last Elves at the Grey Havens in the days of King Arthur. Gandalf, who was Merlin at Arthur's court, had fostered her, and she calls him father still. About 496 he brought Arthur to a lake, where an arm clothed in white samite rose out of the water holding Excalibur, which the Elves of the Havens had forged for him. The arm was hers. At Camlann, about 537, Sir Bedivere threw the sword back, and she caught it. Then she saw Arthur carried to the Havens.

Legend has given her other names, among them Nimue and Viviane. It tells stories about her and Merlin that neither of them has troubled to correct. One of them, that she is Merlin's daughter, is nearly true.

Majestrix of Otherworld

When the Havens passed out of the circles of the world and became Otherworld, Roma stayed. She rules it as its Majestrix, from the Starlight Citadel. She can pass between the worlds that border it, read minds or mend a broken body. She sees a long way down the years. On Merlin's counsel she raised the Captain Britain Corps, which she commands.

Captain Britain

On 13 October 1976 she appeared with Merlin to Brian Braddock, as a great face of light over a ring of standing stones, calling herself the Lady of the Northern Skies. She offered him the Sword of Might or the Amulet of Right. He took the amulet. In 1977 he met her face to face in Otherworld. In 1982, after the Fury had destroyed him, she helped Merlin make him a new body. In June 1984 she brought him to Otherworld to mourn Merlin, who had fallen holding the world together, and she promised that Britain would mend.

In 1987 a being called the Adversary made her a prisoner in her own Citadel. The X-Men gave their lives in Dallas to bind him. Roma gave them back their lives, then gave them the Siege Perilous, a gate that judges those who pass through it and sends the worthy on to a new life.

The check on Brian

Roma had foreseen that the Excalibur team must hold together against Necrom, an old enemy of Otherworld, and that Brian would not stay with it of his own accord. So she laid a check on him: whenever he went off alone, things went wrong for him. In 1991 she sent Saturnyne to stop the Corps from putting him to death for breaking Kurt Wagner's leg. Merlin told Brian about the check soon afterwards. Brian went to the Citadel to tell her that the team should be asked, not handled. She lifted the check, and she did not argue. In 1992 the Excalibur team beat Necrom, as she had foreseen it would.

In 1993, when the Warpies of RCX left Brian for dead, she healed him. She also set right the fault between his uniform and his body that had been draining his power. In 1998 she presided at his wedding to Meggan in Otherworld.

pages.title: Romani witchcraft
infobox: Witches and wizards born into the Romani tribes
Wizarding magic, taught in the tribes' own ways
At home, by the tribe, never at a school
The Winding Way of the Szardos women; the curse-work of the Kalderash
Magda Eisenhardt; the Scarlet Witch; Margali Szardos; Amanda Sefton; Cynthia von Doom
pages.html:
Romani witchcraft is the magic of the witches and wizards born into the Romani tribes of Europe. It is wizarding magic like any other, in the blood from birth. The tribes teach it in their own ways, at home, and they never send their children to a school. It is best known in the wizarding world for its curses and bindings, the deepest of which no Ministry scholar has ever managed to reconstruct.

Teaching at home

A child of the tribes who shows magic is taught by the witches of the tribe, as a rule by the women of the child's own family. By long custom the wizarding schools of Europe do not write to the children of the tribes, and the tribes would not send them if they did. The teaching is spoken, not written. It passes from teacher to pupil within the family, which is why so little of it has ever found its way into wizarding books.

Each tribe, and sometimes each family, has its own ways. A Squib born into a tribe sits outside the lessons, as Pietro Maximoff did while his twin sister was taught.

The fortune-teller's booth

The tribes have always lived among Muggles, and they have always had to hide what they can do. The oldest disguise they have is the fortune-teller's booth. A Muggle who pays a Romani woman to read his palm takes her true sight for a fairground trick, which is the Statute of Secrecy kept in the plainest way there is. Margali Szardos told fortunes for a circus in Bavaria for years.

The Kalderash

The curse that the elders of the Kalderash laid on Angelus in 1898, giving him a new soul, was Romani witchcraft. Nobody outside the clan has ever been able to reconstruct it, since it was never written down.

The Szardos and the Winding Way

The Szardos women of the Manouche, the Romani of France, call their craft the Winding Way. It is handed down from mother to daughter. It rises and falls like a road through mountains: a witch who walks it has times of almost unlimited power, then times when she has hardly any. Margali Szardos walks it, and so does her daughter, Jimaine, who calls herself Amanda Sefton. Muggles who have seen Amanda at work with the Excalibur team take her for a mutant.

The Maximoffs and Magda

Magda Eisenhardt, Magneto's wife, was a Romani witch, taught by her own tribe. In 1946 she gave birth to twins on Wundagore Mountain in Transia, then vanished. The babies were raised by Django and Marya Maximoff, in the wagons of a Romani band in the foothills. Its witches saw that the girl, Wanda, had her mother's magic, while the boy, Pietro, had none. They began to teach her at home, until the twins were lost from the band as children.

Wanda grew up to be the Scarlet Witch, a mutant and a witch at once. Her teaching was finished in the 1970s by Agatha Harkness, an American witch of Ilvermorny.

Latveria

Cynthia von Doom was a Romani witch of Latveria. She sold her soul to Mephisto, one of the Devil's many faces, for power. She died when her son was small, and Victor von Doom was left without a teacher. He taught himself from her books, so that his magic, great as it is, owes nothing to any tribe's way of teaching. In 1989 he won her soul back from Mephisto, with Stephen Strange beside him.

The tribes and the wizarding world

The wizarding governments of Europe count the witches of the tribes as witches like any others, bound by the Statute of Secrecy. They have always left the tribes to teach their own. Some of the old pure-blood families look down on tribal witchcraft as fortune-telling, which nobody who has seen a Kalderash binding has ever done twice. The tribes, for their part, have never asked the ministries for anything.

The Ravnos, the vampire clan that came west with the Romani caravans about 1350, are careful of the tribes' old learning. Most Romani keep well away from them, and count a Ravnos as one of the dead.

Persecution

Muggles have persecuted the Romani for as long as there have been Romani in Europe, and the witches of the tribes have suffered with everybody else. The Nazis murdered a great many Romani in the camps. Magda Eisenhardt was one of those who survived. In February 1994 there were riots against the Romani at Cottbus, in eastern Germany, and D'Spayre, a demon that feeds on despair, came to feed on them.

pages.title: Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights
infobox: South Ashfield Heights; Joseph Schreiber; Frank Sunderland
South Ashfield Heights, South Ashfield, half a day's drive from Silent Hill
The parents of Walter Sullivan, 1970; Joseph Schreiber, to 2001; Henry Townshend, summer 2002 to June 2004
Room 303, the home of Eileen Galvin
Spring 2002, by the SCP Foundation, which found nothing
pages.html:
Room 302 is a flat on the third floor of South Ashfield Heights, an ordinary block in the city of South Ashfield. Walter Sullivan was born in it in 1970 and abandoned there as a newborn. He grew up believing that the room itself was his mother. In June 1994 he worked a rite of the Order of Silent Hill inside it. For the next ten years it was the door to a world of his own making, which cost two of its tenants very dear.

The birth

In 1970 a young couple were living in Room 302. One day they were gone. They had left a newborn baby behind them. The superintendent, Frank Sunderland, found the child and sent for an ambulance. The baby lived. He was called Walter Sullivan, and he was brought up in an orphanage near Silent Hill.

Sunderland found the baby's cord in the empty flat. He put it in a box and kept it. A few years later he began to notice a small boy who hung about the third floor, staring at the door of 302. He guessed who the boy was.

The man in the coat

In June 1994 Walter Sullivan murdered ten people. On the 22nd he killed himself in a cell. A few days later Frank Sunderland saw a long-haired man in a coat in the building. He was carrying a heavy tool, an old bowl and a bag with something dripping from it. Richard Braintree, of Room 207, saw him moving something heavy about in 302, which was standing empty. Days afterwards the neighbours heard noises through the wall.

There were signs that somebody had been in the flat. What had been done there was the Holy Assumption, a rite of the Order by which the one who works it puts off his flesh. From that time on, the noises from Room 302 never altogether stopped.

Joseph Schreiber

Joseph Schreiber was a journalist. About 1997 he wrote a long article for the magazine Concord about Wish House, the orphanage of the Order of Silent Hill, which he accused of taking children in to teach them its creed. Then he turned to the Sullivan murders. By 2001 he was the tenant of Room 302.

His diary for 2001 survives in scraps. On 4 April he was writing about ten murders seven years old. On 14 June he recorded a visit to Silent Hill, where he had found Walter Sullivan's grave empty. On 13 July he wrote that he had sealed off the back of his store room. At the end of that month he pieced together the story of the baby born in his own flat. He had headaches every day. He wrote, more than once, that he was afraid for the young woman next door.

By 2 August the walls of the flat were running with blood and rust, or he believed that they were. He could not get out. On 7 August, in his last dated entry, he set himself down as the fifteenth sacrament, whose name is Despair. His last pages were written for whoever took the flat after him. That person would be the twenty-first, he said, and he told him what he knew.

Joseph Schreiber was never seen again. He is reckoned to have died towards the end of 2001. His ghost stayed in the room. Wraiths are held to the world by what they cannot let go, and Joseph Schreiber could not let go of his story. In June 2004 he finished it, by telling Henry Townshend how Walter Sullivan could be killed.

Henry Townshend

In the spring of 2002, while the flat stood empty, two men measured it twice, saying that they were surveyors for the building's insurers. They were from the SCP Foundation, which had followed the Sullivan case since it lost Walter Sullivan's body in 1994. Joseph Schreiber's disappearance had brought it to the flat where Sullivan was born. Its walls added up. A man the Foundation left to sleep there for a week saw nothing. The Foundation closed its file on the flat that May.

Henry Townshend took the flat in the summer of 2002, six months after Schreiber vanished. Nothing troubled him for two years. Then, on 12 June 2004, he woke to find the front door chained from the inside. He was shut in for five days before a hole opened in the bathroom wall, on 17 June.

The holes led into Walter Sullivan's world: a railway station, the woods by Toluca Lake, a prison in the water, a maze of rooftops, a copy of the building itself. Four people died in those places in four days, while Henry watched. In the waking world the flat began to turn against him. The windows rattled. Faces showed in the walls. Things crawled out of the plaster. Holy candles drove them back for a while.

Behind the wall of the store room Henry found a second, hidden room. Walter Sullivan's body was in it, hung up on a frame. It had been there since 1994. In the last days of June 2004 the Foundation took it away from the coroner.

Frank Sunderland

Frank Sunderland has been superintendent of South Ashfield Heights since at least 1970. He is the father of James Sunderland, who went to Silent Hill in September 1994. He never heard from his son again. In 2004 he still supposed that James and his wife had both vanished there.

He kept Walter Sullivan's cord for thirty-four years without being able to say why. Lately it had begun to smell. Henry Townshend took it from the box in Sunderland's rooms, and used it to end the rite.

pages.title: Roy Campbell
infobox: The Marine Corps; the Green Berets; Delta Force; FOXHOUND
FOXHOUND, from 1995 until after Zanzibar Land
pages.html:
Roy Campbell is an American officer, in the summer of 1994 the second-in-command of FOXHOUND under Big Boss. He took over the unit after Outer Heaven. It was he who sent Solid Snake into Zanzibar Land in 1999, to Shadow Moses in 2005, then on his last mission in 2014. He is the father of Meryl Silverburgh, though she grew up believing him to be her uncle.

San Hieronymo

Campbell has been a Marine, a Green Beret and a member of Delta Force. In 1970, as a young Green Beret, he was sent with a team to look into an abandoned Soviet missile base on the San Hieronymo Peninsula in Colombia. The rebel FOX unit that held the place wiped the team out. Campbell alone lived. He was put in the cell next to Naked Snake's.

The two of them broke out together. Campbell had studied psychology. He talked the stranded Soviet garrison into joining Snake against FOX, which was how the rebellion was beaten.

FOXHOUND

He followed Big Boss into FOXHOUND as its second-in-command. In 1995, when Big Boss was found to be behind Outer Heaven, the command passed to him.

On Christmas Eve 1999 he called the retired Solid Snake back for Operation Intrude F014, the mission into Zanzibar Land, which he directed by radio. When Zanzibar Land had fallen he retired.

Shadow Moses

His younger brother, Matt, was killed in the Gulf War in 1991, leaving a wife with a small daughter, Meryl. Meryl was in truth Roy's child, by an affair with his brother's wife. She was brought up to call him uncle.

In 2005 Meryl was on Shadow Moses Island when the renegades of FOXHOUND seized it. The men who planned the answer used her safety to make Campbell take charge. He brought Snake out of retirement once more. He did not tell him all that he knew, which Snake held against him for a while.

The Secretary of Defence ordered the island bombed to bury the evidence, with Snake still on it. Campbell would not go along. He was removed from his post until the President stopped the bombing. Then he had Snake recorded as killed in action, to give him his freedom.

Later years

In 2009 a voice exactly like his directed the young soldier Raiden through the Big Shell. Campbell knew nothing about it. The voice belonged to GW, a computer of the Patriots.

By 2014 he was working for a body that advised the United Nations Security Council, keeping watch on the world's private armies. He learnt what Liquid Ocelot intended, so he asked Snake, by then an old man, to kill him.

That year too he was married to Rosemary, the wife of Raiden. The marriage was a pretence, meant to keep her small son out of the Patriots' sight. Meryl despised him for it until she was told why. He gave her away at her wedding.

pages.title: The RX-78-2 Gundam
infobox: A mobile suit: an armoured fighting machine in the shape of a man, with a pilot inside
Technology taken in secret from the Galactic Empire
pages.html:
The RX-78-2 Gundam was the Federation's first true mobile suit, finished at Starbase Side 7 in May 2293. It was built to answer the Klingon Zaku in the war that seemed to be coming. It fought the Galactic Empire instead.

The suit

The Klingons were the first power in the Milky Way to build mobile suits, the Zakus. The Federation's answer began with the Guntank. It ended with the Gundam, designed by Tem Ray. Both were built from technology that a few people in Starfleet had stolen in secret from the Galactic Empire, across a transporter bridge. The theft is what brought the Empire to the Milky Way.

The USS Enterprise-A was sent to collect the Gundam on 17 May 2293. The Empire attacked Side 7 that day to destroy it. Amuro Ray, the designer's fifteen-year-old son, took it into battle. It proved to be the only thing Starfleet had that could meet the Empire's small fighters on equal terms. It fought again in the Intergalactic War.

In the saga

The RX-78-2 Gundam has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Ryan Steele
infobox: The VR Troopers, as leader, from September 1994
Red and blue, to September 1995; blue, from 22 September 1995
The Turbo Cycle; later the Nitro Cycle, the Drill Tank, the Blue Hawk, the Troopertron
pages.html:
Ryan Steele is a young martial artist of Crossworld City, California, the son of the vanished scientist Tyler Steele. In September 1994 he became the leader of the VR Troopers, who fought Grimlord's armies on both sides of the barrier between this world and virtual reality. In the summer of 1994 he is eighteen years old, teaches karate at Tao's Dojo, and has not seen his father for about ten years. He found him in November 1994, lost him again within days, and brought him home at last in September 1995.

Boyhood

Ryan was born about 1976 and grew up in Crossworld City. His father, Tyler Steele, was a scientist who was also a martial artist, and he began to teach the boy when Ryan was very small. The lessons were given at a Buddhist temple. Ryan has never forgotten them. In a tight place it is still his father's voice he hears, telling him never to give up.

About 1984, when Ryan was about eight, his father disappeared. Nobody could tell the boy where he had gone, or whether he was alive. Ryan still had Jeb, the Redbone Coonhound who had been his since he was small.

He had Tao as well. Tao Chong, who keeps a karate school in the city, was an old friend of Tyler Steele's, so it was at Tao's Dojo that Ryan went on with his training. Nothing is recorded of Ryan's mother.

Tao's Dojo

By 1994 Ryan is an instructor at the dojo himself, teaching karate to the city's children alongside his friend J.B. Reese. Both are eighteen. Their friend Kaitlin Star, a reporter on the Underground Voice Daily, trains there too. Of the three Ryan is the most single-minded fighter, and the other two look to him to lead.

The first days

On 3 September 1994 a message appeared on Ryan's computer from a Professor Hart, who said that he had word from Ryan's father. Ryan went with Kaitlin and J.B. to the Professor's laboratory in the hills. He learnt there that his father had been taken by Grimlord, the master of the world called virtual reality. The armour of the VR Troopers was his father's work. Ryan agreed to wear it.

He nearly died on the first day. Grimlord's swordsman Decimator struck him down, and he was left lying senseless in a quarry. Lying there, he remembered his father teaching him never to give up. His friends found him on 10 September, and Professor Hart's machines mended him.

The same week a surge of power in the laboratory caught Jeb, who could talk from then on. Ryan made him promise not to do it in front of other people. On 15 September Ryan collided in mid-air with one of Grimlord's flying robots, Air Stryker, losing his memory altogether. Professor Hart tried to bring it back. In the end it was Jeb who did, simply by being glad to see him.

A fighter alone

In his first armour, half red, half blue, Ryan fought with his hands. His finishing blow was the Lightning Hand, a stroke with the open hand that cut like a sword. He rode the Turbo Cycle. More often than not he fought alone, while Kaitlin and J.B. were holding off Grimlord's aircraft somewhere else.

On 21 September 1994 J.B. was pulled bodily through a computer screen into Grimlord's dungeon. Ryan let himself be taken prisoner in order to get him out. In February 1995 Karl Ziktor grew a copy of Ryan from a lock of his hair, using notes of Tyler Steele's on the subject. The copy walked into Tao's Dojo as though it belonged there. Professor Hart lent Ryan his own Virtualizer for that fight, and the copy was beaten.

A few days later a stolen machine went off by accident, putting Ryan's mind into Jeb's body with Jeb's in his. Jeb fought that day as a Trooper. They were put right when the machine was destroyed.

Dark Heart

All this time Ryan was looking for his father. On 30 September 1994 Kaitlin photographed a prisoner in an abandoned building in the woods, a man with Tyler Steele's face. Ryan got there too late.

In November he met a warrior of Grimlord's called Dark Heart, a cyborg who was guarding a hole in the reality barrier. Ryan guessed who he might be. He beat Dark Heart, then refused to finish him, for which Grimlord condemned Dark Heart to death. On 15 November the truth came out: Dark Heart was Tyler Steele, with his memory wiped.

Professor Hart gave Tyler Steele back his mind by passing Ryan's own memories of their life together into him. His body stayed as it was. He chose to go back into virtual reality as Dark Heart, to fight Grimlord from inside. He was shot down by Grimlord's marksman, Renegade, then used as bait for his son.

Ryan rode into the trap on the Turbo Cycle, coming out again with his father behind him. Grimlord's aircraft were bombing the laboratory by then, so he took him to a second, secret laboratory in the mountains. On 17 November the two of them went into virtual reality together to face Grimlord. Grimlord blew up his own dungeon round them. Ryan fought Decimator in the wreck of it. Decimator wounded Dark Heart, who came back to his human shape. Before Ryan could get him away, Grimlord had taken him back.

For ten months after that Ryan had only scraps. The best of them came on 22 February 1995, when a film recovered from an old satellite showed that his father was still alive.

The rescue

On 12 September 1995 one of Ziktor's inventors, a Skug called Strickland, went back through time with a machine of his own making, to do away with Ryan as a boy. Ryan followed him. At the temple he fought Strickland's Skugs beside his own younger self, who forgot all about it afterwards. He saw his father there. He had to come away before he could speak to him.

Six days later Grimlord began draining Tyler Steele's knowledge into a prism, letting the Troopers watch. Ryan went into the dungeon after Jeb, who had gone in ahead as a spy, and Grimlord blew the place up with both of them inside. They walked out of it.

On 20 September Ryan fought his way through a cavern full of Grimlord's creatures to the place where his father was held. He brought him out. He brought out Kaitlin and J.B. as well, whom the Ultra Skugs had caught. Grimlord's lightning caught him as he went, melting his Virtualizer. When it was over he had his father back, with no armour left to defend him.

The second armour

Tyler Steele was very ill. Tao nursed him until he could stand, whereupon he went straight to the laboratory to build his son a new suit. Tao provided the crystal that powered it. Ryan first wore it on 22 September 1995, in a quarry outside the city, against the new army Grimlord had raised.

The second armour was blue, better armed than the first. With it came a pistol, a shoulder cannon, and a laser sabre with which Ryan finished his fights from then on. He had new machines too: the Nitro Cycle, the Drill Tank and the Blue Hawk. His father taught him the command that turned the Skybase into the Troopertron, a fighting robot.

On 11 October 1995 Tyler Steele left Crossworld City again, of his own choice this time, for secret work against Grimlord's world. Ryan saw him off. He had him home for Christmas.

Later battles

In November 1995 an archaeologist, Nebraska Smith, found an ancient doorway inside a pyramid, which held the secret of who Grimlord really was. Ryan worked out how to get in. Despera, Grimlord's new commander, met him there, but he drove her off. With the secret almost in his hand, he learnt that Kaitlin and J.B. were in danger. He went back for them. Oraclon sealed the doorway, so the secret stayed inside.

A few days later Ryan made friends with a girl called Alexis, who turned out to be a creature of Grimlord's. She led him into the Virtual Dark Fortress. There he fought the oracle Oraclon alone, found the weak place between its three eyes, and destroyed it with his laser sabre. Grimlord rebuilt it at once.

The strangest fight of his life came on 20 February 1996. Knighttime, an ally of Grimlord's, betrayed his master by stopping time over the whole Earth. For that one day Ryan fought with Grimlord beside him. Together they destroyed the machine, then went back to being enemies.

Where the record stops

The record of the VR Troopers ends on 21 February 1996, the day after, with a raid on the Virtual Dark Fortress. Ryan was about twenty. His father was free, though far away. Grimlord was still in his fortress, still unknown. Nothing is recorded of Ryan Steele after that.

pages.title: Ryuga Dougai
infobox: Aguri Kusugami; Takeru Jakuzure; the priestess Ryume; Souma Shirahane
pages.html:
Ryuga Dougai was the Golden Knight of another world: a Japan that lies beside this one, over the same Makai, with Horrors, Makai Knights and a golden armour of its own. In that world the armour of Garo had gone black long ago. Ryuga, who was no Saejima, took it up as a youth. In 2013 he won back its gold.

The island

Ryuga's mother, Hakana, was a Makai Priestess who could hear the thoughts left in an object by holding it to her ear. He had the same gift. As a girl she had stood in her world's Tower of Heroic Spirits before the armour of Garo, which had lost its light in some great battle of the past. She heard it ask to shine again. She gave her life to that. Her son promised her that he would be the one to wear it.

From the age of seven he trained on an empty island under her friend, the priest Burai, with a wolf-like Makai beast called Rago for a sparring partner. It lasted ten years. At the end Burai ordered him to kill Rago. He did it, kept one of its fangs, and was given the black armour. He was told that his mother had died.

He was a rough, loud, half-schooled young knight, with little respect for authority. He wandered Japan killing Horrors. Wherever he stopped he built a grave marker for his mother.

Vol City

In April 2013 he came to Vol City, a rich, shut-off town built round a volcano, which called itself a paradise. Burai was there before him. So were two knights: Aguri Kusugami, an archer, with Takeru Jakuzure, who liked girls. So was Burai's pupil Rian, a priestess who carried a gun.

The town was full of a kind of Horror that nobody could detect. Somebody was planting people with the seeds of Zedom, an ancient Horror whose head lay buried under the city. The planted ones kept their faces, their work and a twisted version of their natures. They ran the television station as well as the security force. They had Ryuga named on the news as a murderer.

Each time he killed one, a little gold came back to his armour, with a flash of somebody's memory. The memories were his mother's. Hakana was alive under the city. For years she had been forced to grow the seeds, growing younger with each one, singing all the while. The man who had done it to her was Tousei Kaneshiro, the cheerful owner of a steak house, the disowned son of the family that owned the town.

Tousei's man Sonshi, a knight he had planted years before, blinded Ryuga. In the dark the Madou Ring Zaruba, which had refused until then to say a word to him, at last made its contract with him. Hakana gave her own eyes to restore his. In September 2013 he cut Sonshi down. The armour blazed gold from head to foot. Hakana, who was turning into a Horror, had lived to see it. She asked him to kill her. He did.

Burai had already died trying to seal Zedom with his own body. It left a flaw in the Horror. A week later Ryuga, Aguri and Takeru killed Zedom through it. Rian took the memory of it all from the townspeople. She also finished Tousei, whom a Horror had taken at last.

Line City

Ryuga went on the road with Rian. By March 2015 the armour was so clogged with the malice of dead Horrors that it was turning on him. They went to Line City, where Ryume, an ageless priestess of the Dragon Tribe, could cleanse it. While she had it, a living Madou tool called Ago tried to wipe out the city's people as the surest way of ending the Horrors. Ryuga stopped him in a new, winged form of the armour.

The two of them stayed to guard the city for Ryume. That year the fallen knight Jinga came there to raise the flying fortress Radan. Ryuga destroyed him on 18 September 2015.

Later years

In January 2018 a grieving priestess, Banbi, stole the armours of Aguri, Takeru, then Ryuga, to raise her dead lover. A Horror had tricked her. What she raised was Jinga, with an ark meant to carry the Horrors to the Moon. The three knights won their armour back in time to break it.

Early in 2024 Ryuga came alone, an older, quieter man, to Crea City. Its knight, Godou Shirahane, who had once taught him a sword-art called the flash sword dance, had been missing for three years. Godou's son, Souma, a prickly young knight without a title, was holding the city with a novice priestess, Koyori. Their own mentor, the priestess Mutsugi, tricked them into opening the Gate of Destruction, which Godou had been holding shut with his own frozen body. She wanted a forbidden fruit that lay behind it. The thing that lived in the fruit made a Horror of her. Ryuga destroyed it, then sealed the gate again with Souma on 28 March 2024.

Rian

Rian had been Burai's only pupil. Her father died when she was a child, after which she trusted nobody for a long time. She ended as the one person Ryuga could not do without.

Once a rift in time brought her face to face with Rekka, a Makai Priestess of this world, in the dark between the two. Kouga Saejima saved them both there. It was from Rian that he heard of another Garo.

pages.title: Saba
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'White Light, Part 1' (17 October 1994)
The powers of the White Ranger
Keeper of the White Light, in the Tower of Light; Tommy Oliver's from October 1994
Made by that world's Zordon with Ninjor; in this world from November 1993
The Saba of the Coinless, September 1994, in Lord Drakkon's cell at Promethea
pages.html:
Saba is the talking sabre that goes with the powers of the White Ranger, a white blade with a tiger's head for a hilt. There have been two. The Saba of the World of the Coinless came into this world with Tommy Oliver in November 1993, and in the summer of 1994 he lives at the Command Center. In September 1994 Lord Drakkon killed him. This world's Saba keeps the White Light in the Tower of Light, on a far world, where he tested Tommy for it in October 1994.

The White Ranger's sabre

Saba is a sabre with a white blade and a tiger's head for a hilt, which speaks. He belongs with the White Ranger's coin. The White Ranger calls up the White Tigerzord with him. In the White Ranger's hand he is a weapon.

The Saba of the Coinless

In the World of the Coinless, Lord Drakkon conquered the Earth for Rita Repulsa. As a last hope that world's Zordon made the White Ranger's powers, with Ninjor's help, out of whatever good was left in the world: the White coin, the Tigerzord, the Falconzord, with Saba. They were meant for Jason. On the day they were to be given, Drakkon cut Jason down, then took the white light for himself. Saba was left behind in the chamber under the ruined Command Center.

Drakkon had stayed with Rita, Saba said, because his pride was too large for any team. He had also truly believed that the world would be better under her rule.

At the end of October 1993 this world's Zordon was cut adrift between the worlds. There he came upon that world's Zordon in his last hour, on the day its Rangers fell. Saba took hold of this world's Zordon, so that he would not fade. Zordon told Saba to trust the Tommy Oliver who was coming. He gave him a message for that world's Zack, on the strength of which Zack founded the Coinless.

Tommy and Billy

In November 1993, by this world's calendar, the wreck of the Black Dragon threw Tommy Oliver and Billy Cranston into that world. A voice led Tommy down under the ruined Command Center to Saba. Saba called up the White Tigerzord from the graveyard of Zords to draw off their hunters, then got the boys away in a salvaged Falconzord, which had to come down in Canada to recharge.

There Saba told them how it had all come about. Tommy was afraid that he might become such a man. The Coinless took them in. When Drakkon's army fell on their hiding place, Drakkon boarded the Falconzord himself to carry Saba off. When Drakkon fell, Saba came home with the Rangers to this world. He held Zordon fast until the Command Center was rebuilt.

At the Command Center

Saba stayed at the Command Center after that. When the Rangers caught Finster, Rita's maker of monsters, they kept him prisoner there. Saba offered him a new life, making art that would harm nobody. Finster declined. In the summer of 1994 Saba is still at the Command Center.

Death

At the end of August 1994 Billy found Drakkon in a secret cell at Promethea. In the first days of September Saba stole into the cell to kill him, but set him loose by accident. Drakkon struck off Saba's head, then worked what was left into one of Rita's incantations to open a way out. He took the headless blade with him. Soon afterwards he murdered this world's Tommy Oliver with it.

When the world was mended that September, Saba was not given back. He had died before the murder that broke the Grid, which was what the mending undid. Alone afterwards in the wreck of the world he had made, Drakkon talked to a Saba who was not there.

This world's Saba

How this world's Saba came to the Tower of Light, an old temple on a far world, is not recorded.

In October 1994, after Lord Zedd had drained the last of Tommy Oliver's Green powers, Zordon sent Tommy to the Tower. The Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, had shown Zordon the way. A creature like a white tiger led Tommy to the temple. Saba would give up the Light only to somebody who could beat him. Lord Zedd appeared, struck Saba down, then offered Tommy the Light if he would come back to evil. Tommy refused. It had been a test, so Saba gave him the White Light.

Tommy came back to Angel Grove as the White Ranger, with Saba in his hand.

Later years

Saba stayed with Tommy long after his days as the White Ranger. In 2014, on the day of the great battle against the Armada, Tommy used him to get a boy out of a wrecked car. Then he led the Rangers of every generation with Saba in his hand.

pages.title: Safehaven
infobox: A world a very long way from Earth, once the home of the Morphin Masters
The ruins of the Morphin Masters; the armoury of Eternity Point; the vault; the Master Arch
For the Empowered, from the autumn of 1994
Garrison Vox; Cavotus; Lord Zedd, late in 1994; Kiya Kyatyl
February 1995, to Dark Specter, who made it his prison
pages.html:
Safehaven is a world a very long way from Earth, where the Morphin Masters once lived and where the Omega Rangers have always had their home. Under its ground lie the Masters' ruins: an armoury called Eternity Point, a vault of cells for prisoners too dangerous to be loose, and the Master Arch, a gate into the Morphin Grid. In the autumn of 1994 it became a refuge for the Empowered. In February 1995 it fell for a time to Dark Specter, who made it his prison.

The world of the Masters

Safehaven was the home world of the Morphin Masters, the people who rose into the Grid long ago. What they left behind is under the ground. Eternity Point is an armoury, guarded in the old days by robot sentinels. Near it is the vault, a hall of cells, each of them very like the dumpster that once held Rita Repulsa. There is a temple that kept the Blue Omega morpher. There, too, stands the Master Arch, a gate through which the Grid itself can be reached, with other worlds beyond it.

The first Omega Rangers made Safehaven their base. It was there that Haza, their Blue Ranger, was killed by one of the Supernova Sisters. When Spa'ark, their Gold Ranger, tried to cure death by twisting the Power, the others sealed Spa'ark inside the Gold Omega morpher. The morpher went into the vault, where it lay for centuries.

The refuge

In the autumn of 1994 the Power began to leak into people all over the galaxy, the Empowered. The Blue Emissary made Safehaven their refuge. Those who meant no harm were brought there to live. The dangerous were locked in the vault. Arkon, a bird-man of Circina, was the elder of the place. The Emissary set one of the old sentinels of Eternity Point, Xi, to new work as the Omega Rangers' guide.

In November 1994 Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan took up the Omega powers on Safehaven, with Kiya Kyatyl of Khoodjah as their fourth. Garrison Vox, the tyrant of Zernox-2, went into the vault. So did Cavotus, a Kedry of Breel who had strangled his queen. Late that month Lord Zedd was brought there, a prisoner of the Omega Rangers, and shut in a great dumpster in a chamber lined with copper.

The Anointed

Early in December 1994 Kiya murdered the Blue Emissary on Safehaven, then emptied the vault. She called her following the Anointed. She meant to lead them through the Master Arch after the Morphin Masters. The bounty hunter Dayne let Lord Zedd out of his cell in the confusion.

The Rangers of both teams fought the Anointed at Safehaven. The Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of Lord Drakkon's world, went through the Master Arch. She came back with the Solarix, a piece of the Grid, which drained the Power out of every one of the Empowered. Three weeks later Jason offered the beaten Anointed a home on Safehaven or a passage back to their own worlds. Kiya and Vox went back into cells.

January 1995

Early in January 1995 refugees came to Safehaven from Hartunia, which an Empyreal had destroyed. Arkon demanded Hartunian blood. Zack let himself be cut to settle it. In the same days an image of the Blue Emissary, left in the Grid, led Yale, a cat-like beast of Saard, to the temple where the Blue Omega morpher lay. Yale became the Blue Omega Ranger.

When Lord Drakkon stranded the Omega Rangers on a burning world, Yale and Arkon went through the Master Arch to fetch them home. Soon afterwards, in the Eltarian War, the Empyreals destroyed the Command Center on Earth. The Rangers of both teams fell back on Safehaven with everybody they could save. Goldar, Squatt, Baboo and Finster, who believed their master dead, came with them. When the war was over they chose the Moon instead.

Late in January a visitor to Safehaven took the Gold Omega morpher out of the vault, hoping that its power would wake a friend who lay beyond help. What woke was Spa'ark, the Death Ranger.

Dark Specter's prison

At the beginning of February 1995 Lord Drakkon walked into the vault, let Kiya out and took her through the Master Arch to his own world. Days later Dark Specter came into this world through the other Arch, in the Bermuda Triangle. His corruption got into the Grid itself. Safehaven fell to him, and he made it his prison. When Matt Cook led a mission there, he was seized by a panic so complete that he could not go on.

The cleansing of the Grid threw Dark Specter back into the dark he had come from. Safehaven was free again, and the Omega Rangers went home to it.

pages.title: Saint Germain
infobox: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness (PlayStation 2 and Xbox, November 2005)
pages.html:
Saint Germain was a courteous stranger who crossed the path of the Devil Forgemaster Hector in 1479, the year Dracula's curse was broken. He could step through time. He knew a good deal more about what was coming than he was willing to say, and he was an enemy of Dracula's servant Death.

Wallachia, 1479

Hector was hunting his rival Isaac across Wallachia when Saint Germain first appeared to him, at Garibaldi Temple. He was polite, he was well informed, and he advised Hector to give up the chase. Hector refused.

Hector was being guided at the time by a priest who called himself Zead. Saint Germain warned him to keep clear of the man. In the Forest of Jigramunt Hector came upon the two of them quarrelling. Zead told Saint Germain that he had no business meddling with what was fated, then went for him with a blade. Saint Germain was no longer there when it landed. He had stepped out of the moment, as he could step out of any.

At the top of the Eneomaos Machine Tower he tried Hector's strength himself. Hector won. Saint Germain accepted the result with good grace, promised not to interfere again and told Hector that he must walk his road alone. He asked one favour, that Hector should give his regards to Zead. When Hector passed them on, in the Aiolon Ruins, Zead was badly shaken. He was Dracula's servant Death in a man's shape, as Saint Germain evidently knew.

The traveller

What Saint Germain wanted in 1479 he never fully explained. When Hector had destroyed the Dracula that rose in Isaac's body, he seemed satisfied that time was running in its proper course again. He left for the distant future, saying that he meant to see how the long war between mankind and Dracula would end.

That war ended in the Demon Castle War of 1999. Whether Saint Germain was there to see it is not recorded.

The wizards' Time-Turners carry a traveller back a few hours. Saint Germain crossed centuries, in either direction, by a means that has never been explained.

The name

A Count of Saint Germain was famous at the courts of Europe in the eighteenth century, three hundred years after Hector's time. He was a man of great learning who never seemed to grow any older, and he talked of the distant past as though he had been there. Whether the count and the traveller were one man is not recorded.

pages.title: Sarek
infobox: Astrophysicist; ambassador of Vulcan to the United Federation of Planets
Sybok, by a Vulcan princess; Spock, by his wife, Amanda Grayson of Earth
pages.html:
Sarek was a Vulcan astrophysicist who became his world's most famous ambassador, serving the United Federation of Planets for decades. He married a human, Amanda Grayson, and their son was Spock, with whom he did not speak as a father for eighteen years. In 2267 the two of them were reconciled, after Spock gave him the blood that saved his life.

Marriage and children

Sarek was born on Vulcan in 2165. Before his marriage he had a son, Sybok, by a Vulcan princess. Sybok grew up to reject logic and was banished from Vulcan.

Sarek then married Amanda Grayson, a teacher from Earth. Asked why, he said that it had seemed the logical thing to do, which Amanda found more annoying than anyone. Their son, Spock, was born in 2230.

He wanted Spock in the Vulcan Science Academy. When Spock joined Starfleet instead, about 2249, Sarek stopped speaking to him as a son.

The ambassador

In 2267 Sarek travelled on Spock's ship, the USS Enterprise, to the Babel conference, which was to decide whether Coridan should join the Federation. He argued for it. The Tellarite ambassador, Gav, quarrelled with him in public and was found murdered soon afterwards, killed in a Vulcan manner, so that Sarek was suspected. The killer was an Orion spy disguised as an Andorian. Sarek's heart failed on the voyage. Spock gave him the blood for the operation. Afterwards the two of them were reconciled, after eighteen years.

In 2285 Sarek came to Kirk to ask for his son's katra, which he believed Spock must have left in somebody's keeping, and the search for it led Kirk to steal the Enterprise. The next year Sarek spoke for Kirk and his officers before the Federation Council. Since 2273 he had also been at work on a treaty with the Legarans, a people so particular about their dealings with outsiders that the talks were still going on in 2287.

pages.title: Saturnyne
infobox: Majestrix of the Dimensional Development Court; later Roma's deputy among the worlds
Silver-white hair, pale skin, a cold blue gaze
pages.html:
Saturnyne is a woman of another world, a high officer of the Dimensional Development Court, which keeps order among the worlds that border Otherworld. She is beautiful, cold, clever and almost always sure that she is right. In 1982 she left Captain Britain to die on a world she had been sent to improve. In 1983 he saved her life anyway. Since 1984 she has served Roma of Otherworld, with a great deal of complaint.

The crooked world

Late in 1981 Brian Braddock came down on the Britain that the Captain Britain Corps numbers 238, a sour, frightened country whose government had hunted its heroes down. Saturnyne was there for the Court, with her agents, the Avant Guard, to hurry that world forward with a fluid that quickened all life. Her people caught Brian's companion Jackdaw, then shrank Brian himself to a creature like a monkey, until the fluid made him a man again, stronger than before. When he found out who she was, he decided that she was the lesser evil and threw in his lot with her.

The fluid worked. At the moment it took hold, Mad Jim Jaspers showed what he was, and that Britain began to come apart. The government sent out the Fury. Saturnyne took her people home, leaving Brian with Jackdaw behind. In 1982 the Fury killed them both.

The trial

The Court put Saturnyne on trial for her failure and replaced her with her rival, Mandragon. In the summer of 1983 the Special Executive, mercenaries of many worlds, carried Brian off to speak at her trial, since he was the only witness who could. He despised her for leaving him to the Fury, and he spoke for her all the same. Mandragon destroyed the crooked world before the court had finished with her. The Special Executive got Brian and Saturnyne away to this world.

In May 1984, as the Fury fought Jaspers in the ruins of the warp, she goaded Captain UK into facing her terror of it. Captain UK destroyed it. Saturnyne went with Brian to Otherworld to mourn Merlin. Then she went back to the Court, where she won back her place by means that nobody has cared to look into.

Roma's deputy

Since then Saturnyne has served Roma, keeping order among the Britains of the worlds that border Otherworld. In the Excalibur team's first years she set the Technet on Rachel Summers, then called them off. In 1991 Roma sent her to stop the Captain Britain Corps from putting Brian to death, which she did, with every sign of enjoying it.

She looks exactly like Courtney Ross, Brian's old love, once Courtney stopped dyeing her hair. On another world there is a Saturnyne who became a tyrant, Sat-yr-9, who killed Courtney and took her place. Brian has kept his distance from Saturnyne for that reason, among others.

pages.title: SaucerWatch
infobox: A society for the study of flying saucers
pages.html:
SaucerWatch is an American society for the study of flying saucers, better funded and more respectable than most. Now and then it stumbles on something that Majestic 12 would rather nobody found. It is led by Denton Schaeffer. In 2000 it collapsed under lawsuits and a criminal charge against Schaeffer that had been planted by NRO DELTA, Majestic 12's own arm for dirty work.

The society

SaucerWatch has money behind it, and it is taken more seriously than most saucer clubs. That has made it a nuisance to Majestic 12, whose business is keeping the truth about such things from coming out.

In 1994 SaucerWatch is still at work, and still respectable. Majestic 12 keeps a close watch on it, because the people of SaucerWatch have a way of asking the right questions in the right places.

Its end

In 2000 NRO DELTA brought SaucerWatch down. Lawsuits piled up against it, and a criminal charge was brought against Denton Schaeffer on evidence that NRO DELTA had planted. SaucerWatch did not survive the scandal.

pages.title: Scarlet Witch
infobox: Magneto, a mutant with no magic
Django and Marya Maximoff, of a Romani band in Transia
Pietro Maximoff, a mutant and a Squib
Hexes that turn chance against whatever she aims them at
Taught at home by her tribe as a child; then by Agatha Harkness, from 1974
The Brotherhood of Evil Mutants (1964 to 1965); the Avengers (from 1965); the West Coast Avengers (1987 to 1993)
The Vision, married 1975; they parted in 1990
In her late forties; off the active roster
Fell against Onslaught, August 1996; came home, December 1997
pages.html:
The Scarlet Witch is Wanda Maximoff, who is a witch and a mutant at once. She was born in 1946 in the small mountain country of Transia, to Magneto's wife, a Romani witch, and she was raised by a Romani band. She came to public notice in 1964 in Magneto's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants, joined the Avengers in 1965 and married the Vision in 1975. To the public her magic is simply part of her mutant power, which suits everybody, Wanda included.

Wundagore, 1946

Wanda's mother, Magda Eisenhardt, was a Romani witch who had survived the Nazi camps. After the war she married Max Eisenhardt, the man who became Magneto. When their daughter, Anya, died in a fire, his power broke loose and killed the mob that had held him back. Magda fled from him in horror. She was already carrying his children, and she never told him.

In 1946 she came to Wundagore Mountain in Transia, where a scientist called the High Evolutionary kept his Citadel of Science. There Bova, a cow he had made into a woman, delivered her of twins, a boy and a girl. At the moment the girl was born she glowed, and so did the peak of the mountain. Wundagore is one of the few places where Cthulhu, who has lain dead but dreaming in drowned R'lyeh since the Flood, can reach into the waking world, and the witch's blood in the baby had caught his eye. A few days later Magda left a note, saying that her husband must never find the children, then walked out into the snow for good.

Bova first told the Whizzer, Robert Frank, the wartime hero, that the babies were his. His wife, Madeline Joyce, once Miss America, had just died on the mountain in childbirth, and Frank was too lost in grief to take them. So the High Evolutionary carried the twins down to a Romani band camped in the foothills. There Django Maximoff and his wife, Marya, who had lately lost children of their own, took them in as theirs. They called them Pietro and Wanda.

The tribe, 1946 to 1964

The twins grew up as Romani children, in the wagons of Django's band as it moved about the mountains of Transia. Wanda was a witch from the start. The band's witches saw it in her long before her mutant power came, and they began to teach her at home, as the tribes have always taught their own. Pietro showed no magic at all. He was a Squib, though he would turn out to have a gift of another kind.

Their mutant powers came before they were ten. Pietro could outrun any horse in Transia. When Wanda pointed at a thing and wished it ill, a cart lost its wheel or a wall fell down. Those were her hexes, and they had nothing to do with what the tribe was teaching her.

The villagers of Transia had never loved the Romani, and the twins' powers gave them a reason. One hard winter Django stole bread to feed his family. The villagers came after him with torches and burnt the band's wagons. In the confusion the twins were lost, and Django believed them dead. Wanda's lessons stopped there, half finished.

For years the two of them lived as they could, wandering from village to village, and Pietro's speed fed them both. Once Wanda saved a child from harm with a hex, and the villagers who saw it called her a witch. They were right, though not in the way they meant. They tied her to a stake to burn her. Early in 1964 a man with a voice like iron tore the village apart and set her free. He was Magneto, and he took the twins for mutants, which they were.

The Brotherhood, 1964 to 1965

The twins owed Magneto their lives, and he did not let them forget it. In 1964 they joined his Brotherhood of Evil Mutants as Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch. Neither of them knew that he was their father, and he did not know it either. They fought the X-Men at his side, unwillingly.

In 1965 Magneto was carried off into space by a being from another world, and the Brotherhood fell apart. The twins went to New York and offered themselves to the Avengers, whose founders were stepping down. Captain America took them on, with Hawkeye, the circus archer: three newcomers with criminal records.

Wanda was the first witch ever to serve with the Avengers, thirteen years before Zatanna joined the Justice League. Nobody knew it, the Avengers included. In December 1965 she went to Japan with Captain America beside the Justice League, where her hexes tripped Godzilla twice, which nobody had managed in January.

The Vision and Agatha Harkness, 1965 to 1975

Late in the 1960s Wanda was shot on a mission against Magneto, and Pietro took her away from the team for a time. In 1970 the Avengers rescued Wanda from Arkon, a warlord of another world who had carried her off, and the twins came back to the team.

The Vision had joined the Avengers in 1968, an android built by Ultron to destroy them. The two of them fell in love by slow degrees, the android who was not sure that he could feel and the witch whom everybody took for a mutant. Their first kiss came in 1971, during the war between the Kree and the Skrulls. Pietro could not bear the match.

In 1974 Agatha Harkness, the old witch who was governess to the Richardses' son, Franklin, saw what the Avengers had not: there was a witch's magic in Wanda besides her hexes, half taught and never finished. Agatha took her as a pupil. Under her Wanda learnt true witchcraft, of a kind that no hex could give her.

That summer the Whizzer came forward to say that the twins were his children, and for a while Wanda called herself Wanda Frank. In 1975 she married the Vision. Immortus, a master of time, married them, for reasons of his own that came out only in 1990. Pietro objected, and so did a good many members of the public, who did not think that a woman ought to marry a machine.

Wundagore and Magneto, 1979 to 1983

In 1979 Django Maximoff, who had read of the Avengers' twins and known them for his own, took them home to Wundagore to learn where they had come from. There Bova told them of their mother, Magda. Then a sorcerer in Cthulhu's service led Wanda up the mountain, where Cthulhu's dreaming mind took her body.

Django had carved a wooden doll of Wanda when she was small. Between them, Pietro and the team drove Cthulhu out of her into it. Wanda buried the doll under an avalanche. Django's heart had failed in the struggle. The twins buried him in the forest he had loved.

In 1982 she and the Vision left the team to make a home in Leonia, New Jersey. There the Whizzer learnt that the twins were not his after all. He died soon afterwards defending them.

Late in 1982 Bova told Magneto about Magda, and he came to the twins to tell them that he was their father. They accepted it, uneasily. Neighbours who did not want a mutant and an android in their street burnt the house in Leonia down. The couple went back to Avengers Mansion.

New Salem and the boys, 1985 to 1987

In 1985 the witches of New Salem, the hidden town in Colorado that Agatha Harkness had once led, burnt her at the stake. They took Wanda and the Vision prisoner. Agatha's spirit came to Wanda all the same, and showed her how to draw the town's own power into herself. She came home with child.

In 1986 she gave birth to twin sons, Thomas and William. Doctor Stephen Strange was there to see them safely into the world. In 1987 the family moved to California, where Wanda and the Vision joined the West Coast Avengers.

The lost years, 1989 to 1990

Early in 1989 agents of several governments seized the Vision and took him apart. When he was rebuilt he had no feelings left. That same year Mephisto came for the boys. They had been made in part from shards of his own essence, and he took the shards back. Thomas and William were unmade.

Agatha Harkness had come back by then, alive, without ever explaining how. To save Wanda's reason she took away her memory of her sons. In 1990 Immortus worked on the grief that was left, until Wanda turned on the Avengers and went back for a while to Magneto. When the truth came out, Agatha gave back what she had taken. She and the Vision, who could no longer love her, agreed to part.

Witch and mutant

Wanda has two gifts, and they do not come from the same place. Her hexes are her mutant power, which turns chance against whatever she aims it at, while her witchcraft came from her mother. The two are tangled together in nearly everything she does, which is part of why her hexes are so strange.

To the public it is all one mutant power. Anybody who sees her cast a spell takes it for a hex, and nobody has ever thought to ask the difference. The Ministry of Magic, which has found mutants a useful cover story, likes it that way. So does MACUSA, which counts her a European witch living in America and has never troubled her.

Wanda never went to a wizarding school. The tribes teach their own, and by the age when a letter might have come she was living wild in the hills with no address to send it to. Magneto, who has no magic himself, took her for a mutant in 1964 like everybody else. He has never guessed that the name she took is the plain truth.

In 1994

The west coast branch of the Avengers was wound up at the end of 1993, and Wanda has been off the active roster since. In the summer of 1994 she is in her late forties, though longevity medicine leaves her looking little more than thirty. Her brother is still her brother, which with Pietro is not always restful.

Later years

In 1996 Wanda came out of retirement to fight Onslaught, fell with the Avengers that August, lived for a year in Franklin's world and came home in December 1997, exactly as old as on the day she fell.

Her sons were not lost for good. Their souls had passed into two baby boys born to other families, who grew up to find her in 2010.

The Third World War

Wanda was eighty when the Third World War broke out in 2026, though a witch of eighty is far from old. In the war she turned a wing of Sentinels away from a crowded city with a hex, and the effort killed her. Her twin brother fell in the same war.

pages.title: Secret Wars
infobox: Battleworld, a planet in a distant galaxy
Heroes and villains from across the world, and from beyond it
All but the Thing returned to Earth
pages.html:
The Secret Wars were the strange business of 1984 in which the Beyonder, a being of almost unlimited power from outside the universe, carried off heroes and villains from all over the world to a planet he had built for the purpose, Battleworld. There he set them to fight one another. He took the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, the X-Men, Spider-Man, heroes of the Justice League and the Jaffa master Bra'tac, among a good many others.

The taking

Early in 1984 a vast round structure appeared in the Sheep Meadow in Central Park. The heroes who went to look at it were carried away one after another, together with the Hulk, who had been drawn to it, and the structure went with them to the far side of the universe. There the Beyonder built a new world in front of them out of pieces of others, among them a suburb of Denver, people and all. He told the two sides, heroes and villains, that whoever destroyed their enemies should have whatever they desired.

The Beyonder cast his net wide. Besides the heroes of New York he took heroes of the Justice League. He also took Bra'tac of Chulak, a Jaffa master already more than a century old, who served the Goa'uld Apophis. On the villains' side he put Victor von Doom, Ultron, Kang the Conqueror, the Molecule Man, Doctor Octopus, the Absorbing Man, the Wrecking Crew and others. Magneto stood at first with the heroes, who did not much want him. Galactus came on his own account, hungry.

On Battleworld

Captain America led the heroes against the villains across Battleworld. Galactus tried to devour the planet. Doom built a machine to drain Galactus's power. With it he stole the power of the Beyonder himself and was for a time a god, until the Beyonder took it back.

An alien healer, Zsaji, gave her life to bring the fallen heroes back, and Colossus of the X-Men loved her. Spider-Man found what he took to be a new black costume, and brought it home with him. It was a living creature. Two women from the Denver suburb, Volcana and Titania, were given powers there by Doom, while a new Spider-Woman, Julia Carpenter, fought on the heroes' side.

When it was over, Reed Richards built a way home. Everyone came back except Ben Grimm, the Thing. He had found that on Battleworld he could turn back into a man whenever he liked, and he stayed on for a while to explore.

Afterwards

The Secret Wars changed several lives. The black costume later became Venom. She-Hulk took the Thing's place in the Fantastic Four. The Beyonder, having watched humanity at war, came to Earth himself in 1985 to try to understand it.

pages.title: Section 31
infobox: An idea, held in secret by a few people inside Starfleet
Article 14, Section 31, of the United Earth Starfleet Charter
That in times of extraordinary threat anything necessary to keep Earth safe was allowed
The heirs of Delta Green and the SCP Foundation
Never more than five people at any one time
None: no title, no ranks, no leaders
Active in times of danger; dormant between them
The lore of the Aesir, classified
pages.html:
Section 31 was less an organisation than an idea: the belief that Article 14, Section 31, of the United Earth Starfleet Charter, which allowed Starfleet to bend its own rules in times of extraordinary threat, was leave to do whatever was necessary to keep Earth safe. It had no title, no ranks and no leaders. At any one time it was a handful of people, never more than five, who held that belief and acted on it in secret. It woke when they judged Earth in danger and went dormant when the danger had passed. The idea came from the heirs of Delta Green and the SCP Foundation. Those who held it kept the lore of the Aesir classified.

The heirs of the secret keepers

Delta Green and the SCP Foundation did not outlive the Third World War. Both were destroyed by 2053, but a few of their people lived through the end, with what they could carry of their files. In the lawless decades of the post-atomic horror they kept to the shadows, as they always had. They taught their children their habits of secrecy, along with the old belief of both houses that some things must be kept from the world for its own good.

Among the things they kept was the lore of the Aesir, which had passed into the keeping of both organisations when the Stargate programme collapsed early in the war. They held it classified through the war and the years after it. In the ruins they let Zefram Cochrane study it, and only what touched warp flight ever became public.

When United Earth chartered its Starfleet to go out among the stars, their heirs read the charter closely. Its Article 14, Section 31, allowed Starfleet to bend its own rules in times of extraordinary threat. A few of them took it as leave for everything their forebears had done in the dark, and the idea that they shared took its name from that clause.

An idea, not an organisation

Section 31 was never an organisation in any ordinary sense. It had no title of its own, no ranks, no leaders, no headquarters and no budget anyone could trace. Nobody joined it. A person held the idea, or did not, and acted on it, or did not.

At any one time no more than five people held it and acted on it together. They knew one another, and when one of them died the others found the next. Almost nobody else knew that Section 31 existed, and none of those who held the idea ever admitted that it did.
