For long years together it did nothing at all. It woke when those who held it judged Earth to be in danger, did what they thought necessary and went dormant again when the danger had passed.

What it kept

From Delta Green it took the conviction that some threats are best met in the dark. From the Foundation it took the habit of writing everything down and locking it away. Above all it kept the lore of the Aesir classified, beyond the little of it that touched warp flight.

Harris and Reed, 2154

Before he joined the Enterprise NX-01 as her armoury officer, Malcolm Reed had been one of the few who held the idea, with a man called Harris. In 2154 the Klingons took the ship's doctor, Phlox, to find a cure for the plague that became the Klingon Augment virus. Section 31 woke to deal with it, since Harris wanted the cure found. Harris told Reed to keep the Enterprise from finding Phlox, and Reed did so at first, sabotaging the search. Then he told Captain Archer the truth.

In the Federation

When the United Federation of Planets was founded in 2161, the idea went on inside its Starfleet, unseen, among the few who held it. It woke and slept as they saw fit. Its work in the century that followed left no record.

The bridge

In 2267 a transporter accident carried James T. Kirk into a mirror universe. Those who held to the idea of Section 31 took the technique further in secret. They found that it could reach a distant galaxy at a distant time, the home of the Galactic Empire. They used it to steal Imperial technology, out of which the Federation built the RX-78-2 Gundam.

The thefts did what the idea had always risked. The Empire found out, copied the bridge for itself, then came through it: to Starbase Side 7 in 2293, in the Imperial Entanglement, then in the Intergalactic War of 2299 to 2300.

In the saga

Section 31 has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Shadow Lords
infobox: The Carpathians, the Balkans and the Slavic East
Ambition, discipline and the pursuit of leadership
pages.html:
The Shadow Lords are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the ambitious, disciplined tribe of the Carpathians and the Balkans. They believe that the Garou need harder leadership than the Silver Fangs can give, and they mean to provide it.

Totem and ways

The Shadow Lords follow Grandfather Thunder, the lord of storms, a proud spirit who demands obedience and rewards success. They prize strength, cunning, discipline and results. Pity and squeamishness, in their view, are luxuries that a people at war cannot afford. They are the masters of politics within the Garou Nation: of gathering secrets, making alliances and calling in debts. They are as ruthless with their own failures as they are with their enemies.

They hold that the Silver Fangs, the traditional royal tribe, have grown weak and mad with inbreeding. The Garou will lose the war, they say, unless they are led by somebody fit to lead. That somebody, the Shadow Lords believe, is themselves.

Homelands

The tribe's heartland is Eastern Europe: the Carpathian mountains, the Balkans and the Slavic lands. Its Kinfolk have lived there for thousands of years, under one conqueror after another. There the Shadow Lords have fought for centuries against the Tzimisce, the vampire lords of those mountains. Their memories of that war are long and bitter. They have since spread with their Kinfolk across Europe and the Americas.

Place in the world

Few Garou trust a Shadow Lord entirely, and the tribe is often suspected of dealings it ought not to have. Yet they are formidable warriors and shrewd counsellors. Many a sept owes its survival to Shadow Lord planning. Their rivalry with the Silver Fangs is the oldest quarrel in Garou politics.

pages.title: Shaft (dark priest)
infobox: Akumajō Dracula X: Chi no Rondo (Rondo of Blood, PC Engine CD, 29 October 1993)
Dark priest; leader of a cult of Dracula
A mortal infernalist; after 1792, a wraith
pages.html:
Shaft was a dark priest who raised Dracula twice in five years. In 1792 he led the cult that brought the vampire back, and Richter Belmont defeated him. His spirit outlived his body. By 1797 he had made Richter himself the lord of Dracula's castle, until Alucard broke his hold on the Belmont and destroyed him.

The cult of 1792

For a century after Simon Belmont burnt Dracula's remains, the vampire's worshippers gathered in secret. By 1792 their leader was Shaft, a priest who had turned to the black arts. He meant to bring Dracula back, then to serve at his right hand.

The cult sacrificed a young woman in its rite, and the vampire rose. His castle rose with him. Shaft became his chief servant. Dracula's creatures burnt the villages near the castle. They carried off four young women: Annette, whom Richter Belmont loved; Maria Renard, a child of twelve; a nun named Tera; and Iris, the doctor's daughter.

Shaft took charge of Maria himself. He was working a spell on her, deep in the castle, when Richter came in with the Vampire Killer.

Defeat

Richter set Maria free, and she joined him. He met Shaft again higher in the castle and beat him.

It was not the end of him. In the clock tower Shaft's ghost rose against Richter, and Richter put that down too. He went on to destroy Dracula at the top of the castle. Shaft's body had perished. His spirit had not.

The puppet lord

Shaft's second plan was aimed at the Belmonts themselves. He meant to end the family by taking one of its members for his own, so that hunter would be set against hunter.

In 1796 Richter Belmont vanished. The next year Dracula's castle rose again, with Richter sitting in its throne room as its lord. He told those who reached him that he meant to bring Dracula back so that their battle need never end. Above him hung a green orb, invisible to ordinary sight, through which Shaft's spirit held his mind.

Maria Renard, who had come looking for Richter, guessed that he was not himself. She gave Alucard a pair of holy glasses that show what is hidden. Alucard saw the orb, destroyed it in place of the man beneath it, and Richter was free.

Shaft showed himself then. He had one stroke left, which was to raise a second castle upside down in the sky above the first, where he could finish the rite of Dracula's return. Alucard followed him up into it and destroyed him. It made no difference to the rite, which was already complete. Dracula returned, and Alucard destroyed him in his turn.

Among the Kindred

Shaft was no vampire. He was a mortal priest who had given himself to Dracula, and through Dracula to the Devil, whose property every vampire is. The Kindred call such servants infernalists.

What came back after 1792 was a wraith. The dead who linger are held to the world by whatever they have left undone, and Shaft's unfinished business was the return of his master. In five years he raised Dracula twice, and the second time he turned the Belmont of the day into his tool.

pages.title: Shattered Grid
infobox: Angel Grove; the Moon of Drakkon's world; the Morphin Grid
Lord Drakkon, with Finster-5 and the Ranger Sentries
The Rangers of every year; Zordon; Grace Sterling and Promethea; Rita Repulsa, at the last
Tommy Oliver's spirit, with the heart of a Morphin Master
By the mending of the world
The Emissaries Three; Lord Drakkon; those aboard Promethea; from October 1994, Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan
pages.html:
Shattered Grid was the war that Lord Drakkon, the Tommy Oliver of another world, made on the Power Rangers of every year in September 1994. It began when he murdered this world's Tommy Oliver, which broke the Morphin Grid apart. It ended with Drakkon unmaking the world, then with Tommy's spirit taking it back from him. The Rangers mended everything. In the mended world Tommy had never died, and almost nobody remembered any of it.

Drakkon's escape

Lord Drakkon had been Grace Sterling's secret prisoner since November 1993, in a cell under one of Promethea's buildings. At the end of August 1994 Billy Cranston found him there. Jason Lee Scott, furious that Grace had never told him, broke with her on the spot.

In the first days of September the Saba of Drakkon's own world, the talking sabre that had come home with the Rangers the autumn before, stole into the cell to kill him. In the struggle Saba set him loose by accident. Drakkon struck off Saba's head, worked what was left into one of Rita's incantations to open a way out, then took the blade with him.

His own link to the Power was still broken. He went to Ninjor at the Temple of Power, passed his trials, kept his purpose to himself, then had his powers mended. He repaid Ninjor by carrying him off in a jar. Then he stole the Green Chaos Crystal, which the Rangers had kept at the Command Center.

The murder

That evening Tommy Oliver took Kimberly Hart out on their first proper date. It went well until the goodnight, which was awkward. Kimberly walked away, thought better of it, then turned back. She found Drakkon in the alley with the blade that had been Saba through Tommy's back, drawing his power into the crystal. Tommy died in her arms.

Jen Scotts, a Ranger of a far later century, had escaped back through a rift in time to warn of what was coming. She came too late. Zordon could not bring Tommy back. The Rangers laid his body in the alley again for the world to find, so that nobody would ever know what he had been. Angel Grove buried him. Jason took up the Dragon Shield with the Dragon Dagger.

The broken Grid

Jen explained what had happened. Drakkon's coming had made a new line of time. Tommy's death had tangled it past bearing. Rather than wipe it out, the Grid had shut every team of Rangers away in a pocket of its own, each in its own time, cut off from the rest.

Drakkon went from one to the next, with Ninjor in his jar and Finster-5 at his side. His Sentries beat the Samurai Rangers of a later day. Only Lauren Shiba escaped; the powers of the others were fused into him. In one pocket of later years he passed himself off as that year's Tommy Oliver, the leader of its Zeo Rangers, long enough to steal a Zeo power. Then he killed that Tommy too. Team after team lost their powers to him, some of them their lives. He meant to gather power enough to break into the Morphin Grid itself.

The Rangers of every year

Zordon called on the Emissaries Three, the red, blue and yellow servants of the Morphin Masters. They would not act. They told him to trust his Rangers, then began to doubt themselves. So Zordon sent his warning to every Ranger the Grid could reach, in every year, then gathered those who were left at the Command Center.

In Drakkon's own world the Coinless freed Ninjor from his tower. Their leader, that world's Zack, was shot dead doing it. Drakkon caught that world's Skull helping, so he killed him. Ninjor told the Rangers what Drakkon meant to do: take the powers of every team, then enter the Grid itself. Grace Sterling came when Jason called. With a scientist from among the Rangers of later years, she hardened their morphers against him.

Drakkon had sent his Ranger Slayer, the Kimberly Hart of his world, after this world's Rangers. She came out of time a year too early, in October 1993, where this world's Kimberly broke the bow that held her to him. When she came back to September 1994 she was free. Grace took her in.

The tower on the Moon

Zordon asked Rita Repulsa for help. She refused, until he told her that Drakkon had murdered his own Rita. Then she brought a green candle of the Wizard of Deception's making, like the one that had drained Tommy the year before.

The Rangers of every year stormed Drakkon's tower on the Moon of his own world. Jason led them on the ground. Kimberly put on Tommy's armour, with the Dragon Shield across her chest, then took the Dragonzord. Grace flew her headquarters, which had always been a ship, to the tower to free the Rangers Drakkon held. The Ranger Slayer sailed with her.

Rita burnt her candle against Drakkon in his throne room, with Zordon's help. It was draining him when Finster-5 got him away from it. Drakkon broke his servant's neck, then took every stolen power into himself at once. Jason drilled into the tower, where Drakkon's war machine, Serpentera, seemed to destroy him.

The unmaking

With all that power Drakkon broke into the Grid. He beat the Emissaries Three, then took from them the heart of a Morphin Master. With it he unmade everything: this world, his own, every other. In their place he made a single world to his liking. In it he was young, a hero whom everybody loved, with Zordon for his father, Rita for his mother. The Rangers were ordinary people who had never heard of the Power.

As the world came apart Grace armoured Promethea with the energy of Psycho Green's dagger. The ship was thrown clear of everything, into a dark place where there was no Morphin Grid at all. Her crew were aboard, with Terona Washington, the Ranger Slayer and a handful of Rangers of later years.

Tommy's spirit

Drakkon had reckoned without an arrow. In October 1993 the Ranger Slayer had shot the young Tommy Oliver, then new to Angel Grove, with an arrow carrying a splinter of the Chaos Crystal. One day, she told him, he would understand. When Drakkon killed him, the splinter held his spirit in a place between the worlds. The Emissaries Three joined him there.

Tommy's spirit came into Drakkon's made world. He woke the five friends whom Drakkon had made ordinary, with Jen Scotts and Lauren Shiba. He fought Drakkon on equal terms, beat him, then took the heart.

He told Drakkon why he had lost. Of all the Tommy Olivers in all the worlds, Drakkon was the only one who had gone wrong, which he had never been able to bear. Tommy offered to take him out before the made world fell to pieces. Drakkon refused.

The mending

The Rangers laid their hands on the heart. Kimberly kissed Tommy, then everything went white. When it came back, the world had been mended. The Emissaries warned that it could not be made exactly as it had been, which proved true: the Power was leaking through the cracks, into people all over the galaxy.

In the mended world Tommy had never died. His first date with Kimberly ended in a kiss. Ninjor was in his temple. Drakkon was not in Promethea's cell. He was alone in the wreck of the world he had made, where he had chosen to stay. Promethea was still lost in the dark, where its people spent more than forty days before they found their way home in October 1994.

The dead

Many died in the war, but almost all of them were given back. Tommy Oliver was one. So was Jason, whom Serpentera had seemed to destroy. So were the Rangers of later years who fell to Drakkon, among them the Tommy Oliver of the Zeo years. So were the Coinless Zack, Skull and Finster-5.

Saba was not. He had died in Drakkon's cell before the murder that broke the Grid, so the mending did not reach back to him. The war had one more death to come. Three months later the Red Emissary went into the wreck to look for Drakkon, where an Empyreal tore the Emissary to pieces.

Who remembers it

Almost nobody remembered the war. Exactly who did is known.

The Emissaries Three remembered, because they belong to the Grid, having watched over its mending. Lord Drakkon remembered all of it. So did everybody aboard Promethea, which was outside the world when it was mended: Grace Sterling with her crew, Terona Washington and the Ranger Slayer. The Rangers of later years who had sailed with them went back to their own times.

In October 1994 the Blue Emissary gave Jason Lee Scott back his memory of the war, then gave Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan theirs. Through a link between their minds Kiya Kyatyl saw Drakkon in Jason's memory, which was how she came to know him.

Zordon and his Rangers knew of it only by report: in part from the Omega Rangers in December 1994, then from Drakkon himself, who taunted them with it from his cell. Late in January 1995 Trini told Kimberly Hart the whole of it, the alley included. Afterwards the Pink Emissary, another servant of the Morphin Masters, gave Kimberly back her own memory of it.

Tommy Oliver never remembered. All he ever knew of his own death was what others told him.

pages.title: Shi'ar
infobox: Aerie; the empire is ruled from Chandilar
The Imperial Guard, under the Praetor, Gladiator
Died out about 2044, burning their own worlds to destroy the Brood
pages.html:
The Shi'ar are a proud, bird-like people whose empire, the Shi'ar Imperium, lies far beyond Earth's galaxy. It is ruled from the throneworld of Chandilar by the Majestrix Lilandra Neramani, who has held the throne, with one long interruption, since 1979. She has loved Charles Xavier since 1976. The Shi'ar keep the M'Kraan Crystal, on which the whole of reality depends, and in 1980 they sentenced the Phoenix to death. In 1992 they broke the Kree Empire in a war that spilt over into Earth's part of space, and they have ruled what was left of it ever since.

The Shi'ar

The Shi'ar are descended from birds, and it shows. They have crests of feathers where human beings have hair. A few small feathers still grow along their forearms, where their ancestors' wings once were. Their bones are light and hollow. They lay eggs.

The Shi'ar lost their wings long ago. Now and then one is born with them, a throwback to the old race; Deathbird, the Majestrix's sister, is one. An ordinary Shi'ar can lift about a ton.

Their first home was the world called Aerie. The empire is ruled from Chandilar, the throneworld.

They worship two gods, Sharra and K'ythri. The Shi'ar say that the two were enemies until they were made to marry. In the marriage they found strength, and in time love. The Shi'ar have treated other peoples in much the same way ever since.

The Imperium

The Imperium is very old. The Shi'ar have been conquering other peoples for some thirty thousand years, since the Third Age. A conquered people is said to have married into the empire, whether it wished to or not.

Its subject peoples each send a member to the High Council, which in theory governs the empire. In practice it is ruled by the Majestor, or by the Majestrix when the throne is held by a woman. The Council mostly does as it is told.

The throne is hereditary. In modern times it has belonged to the house of Neramani, to which Lilandra, her brother D'Ken and her sister Deathbird all belong. The Shi'ar are a proud people. They set great store by ceremony, honour and strength.

The throne is defended by the Imperial Guard, the finest warriors of the empire, drawn from the Shi'ar and from the peoples they rule. Each of them has powers of some kind. Its commander is the Praetor, Gladiator, whose own name is Kallark. He comes from the world of Strontia, and he is as strong as anyone in the Imperium. His strength rises and falls with his confidence, which is seldom a difficulty.

Among the others are Oracle, a telepath; Starbolt, who burns like a small sun; and Titan, who can make himself as tall as a house. The Guard first met the X-Men in 1977, beside the M'Kraan Crystal. It has fought them more than once since, and it has not always won.

D'Ken

Lilandra's elder brother, D'Ken, came to the throne after their sister Deathbird was exiled. He was cruel, greedy and hungry for power. He also had the means to indulge all three.

Years before he troubled Earth openly, one of his ships attacked a small plane carrying the American pilot Christopher Summers, his wife Katherine and their two little sons. Katherine strapped the boys into the only parachute and pushed them out. Both boys lived, to grow up as Cyclops and Havok.

The Shi'ar carried the parents off. D'Ken kept Katherine for himself, and sent Christopher to the slave pits. When Christopher tried to kill him, D'Ken had her murdered in front of him, then sent him to the mines on another world.

There, with Hepzibah, Raza and Ch'od, Christopher broke out. The four of them stole a Shi'ar starship and turned pirate against D'Ken. Christopher took his old pilot's call-sign, Corsair, and the band he led became the Starjammers.

The M'Kraan Crystal

The M'Kraan Crystal is the greatest treasure of the Shi'ar. They say that K'ythri gave it to Sharra on their wedding day.

Inside it lies a living lattice of energy, and inside that a neutron galaxy. If the lattice ever died, the galaxy would break loose, and its power would destroy the universe.

D'Ken meant to take that power for himself. At the turn of 1976 Lilandra turned against him, and fled to Earth. Xavier had been dreaming of her for weeks before she came.

In 1977 D'Ken's agents carried her off to the crystal's world, where he meant to put her to death. The X-Men followed her there. They fought the Imperial Guard with the Starjammers beside them.

Raza threw D'Ken at the crystal, and what D'Ken saw inside it broke his mind. The lattice began to die, and for moments at a time the universe blinked out of existence. The Phoenix, which was then wearing the form of Jean Grey, went into the heart of the crystal and brought the lattice back to life. It drew on the strength of Storm and of Corsair to do it.

D'Ken has lain in a coma ever since. By rebelling Lilandra had made herself a traitor under Shi'ar law, so she stayed on Earth with Xavier until the Council could clear her name. In 1979 it called her home to the throne.

The Phoenix

In 1980 the Phoenix, the cosmic force that had taken Jean Grey's form, turned dark. It flew out into space and devoured a star. The world of the D'Bari, which circled it, died with it, and so did billions of D'Bari.

The Shi'ar held that a power which had done that must be destroyed. They seized the X-Men, and Lilandra declared that the Phoenix must die.

Xavier answered by claiming the Arin'n Haelar, a Shi'ar duel of honour that cannot be refused. The X-Men would fight for the Phoenix, the Imperial Guard for the empire. It was held on the Moon, in the Blue Area, with the Kree Bel-Dann and the Skrull Raksor to judge it.

The X-Men were losing. As the Phoenix felt its dark self coming back, it took up an old Kree weapon and turned it on itself.

In 1986 the real Jean Grey was found alive, cocooned at the bottom of Jamaica Bay.

Deathbird

Deathbird was born Cal'syee Neramani, the eldest child of the ruling house. She came into the world with the wings of the ancient Shi'ar, and with a temper to match them. It was foretold that she would do great evil, and her name was taken from her for it. She went on to murder her mother and one of her sisters. For that she was sent into exile. The throne passed to D'Ken.

In 1977 she turned up on Earth as a bodyguard to the criminal genius MODOK, and fought Ms Marvel. In 1979 Hawkeye caught her in a net.

She was not finished with the throne. Her sister had it, and Deathbird thought it hers by right.

Lilandra's reign

In 1982 Deathbird came home to take the throne. Her allies were a member of the High Council called Samedar, a few renegades of the Imperial Guard and the Brood, a race of parasites who lay their eggs in living hosts. The X-Men beat her.

In 1983 Lilandra brought Reed Richards before a Shi'ar court for saving the life of Galactus, who had since eaten the Throneworld of the Skrulls. The Watcher, Odin, Galactus and Eternity itself all spoke for him. He was acquitted.

In 1985, when Xavier was badly hurt, Lilandra and the Starjammers took him into space to be healed. He stayed with her for six years, and left his school in Magneto's charge.

While Lilandra was away, Deathbird tried again with the help of the Brood and the Badoon. This time she took the throne. Lilandra spent the next years fighting her sister from exile, with Xavier and the Starjammers at her side.

In 1991 the Warskrulls, Skrulls bred for war, took the places of Xavier and the Starjammers in secret. Through the false Xavier they got hold of Lilandra's mind, and through her they forced Deathbird to sign the throne away.

The real Xavier, held prisoner, reached out to the X-Men. They came out to Chandilar, where Deathbird joined them against the Skrulls, and between them they broke the plot. Lilandra came to her senses. Deathbird had signed under torture, but she let the abdication stand. She said that she was bored with ruling, and that Lilandra was welcome to it.

Xavier came home to Earth with the X-Men. Since then he has lived at his school, and Lilandra on Chandilar.

In 1993, on the prison world of Krag, Lilandra judged Cerise, a warrior of the Ghrand Jhar who had sent her own Shi'ar ship into a sun rather than help its crew wipe out a people of the sea. She had watched her for days in the guise of an old prisoner. She sentenced her to serve at her side as her bodyguard, and in the summer of 1994 Cerise is still with her.

Galactic Storm

In 1992 the Shi'ar went to war with the Kree. Both empires were sending their fleets through a great gateway in space inside Earth's solar system, and the strain on it was beginning to unsettle the Sun. The war first touched Earth when Shi'ar agents kidnapped Rick Jones, the old companion of Mar-Vell, for the sake of the Kree devices they needed for a weapon.

The Avengers went out to stop the fighting, and one of their teams came to Chandilar. While it was there, Starforce, the champions of the Kree, made an attempt on Lilandra's life.

The weapon was the Nega-Bomb, made from Kree devices to destroy the Kree. Lilandra ordered the Starjammers to carry it into Kree space. Then she learnt that a Skrull in the shape of her chancellor, Araki, had done a good deal to bring the war about, and she called the bomb back. It was too late. Skrull agents had stolen it, and it went off inside the Kree Empire. Billions of Kree died.

Deathbird, meanwhile, had gone to Hala. There, in front of the Avengers, she killed both the generals who ruled the Kree. Afterwards it turned out that the Supreme Intelligence of the Kree had steered the whole war, and had played the two sisters against each other from the start.

The Shi'ar took over what was left of the Kree Empire. Lilandra made Deathbird its viceroy, with an Imperial Guard of her own, and in the summer of 1994 Deathbird still rules the Kree from Hala. They resent it bitterly.

The Goa'uld

The Shi'ar never thought the Goa'uld worth conquering, and until 1992 they had scarcely heard of them. That year, when the Shi'ar came to take over the Kree frontier, they found Goa'uld ships already there, picking over the wreckage of the war.

The Imperial Guard drove them off in an afternoon. Lilandra is said to have asked afterwards who the Goa'uld were. When she was told, she lost interest.

The System Lords, who are not used to being forgotten so quickly, have kept well out of the Imperium's way since.

Later history

In 2007 Gabriel Summers, a mutant whom D'Ken had once kept as a slave, killed D'Ken, who had lately woken from his coma. He made himself emperor, with Deathbird as his empress. He was a younger brother of Cyclops and Havok, born to Katherine Summers in Shi'ar captivity.

Lilandra fought him from exile. In 2009, in the war that followed between the Shi'ar and the Kree, she was assassinated. Gladiator took the throne after her, and surrendered to the Kree.

The end of the Shi'ar

The Shi'ar never fully recovered from their surrender of 2009. Their end came from the Brood, the parasites who lay their eggs in living hosts, whom Deathbird had once brought against her sister. In the 2030s the last Brood Empress, driven out of the ruins of Kree space, brought what was left of her people into the Imperium.

The Shi'ar answered as their pride required. They would not become Brood, so they burnt every world where the Brood had taken hold, Shi'ar and all, with the subject peoples who lived there. The last of the Brood died with their last hosts about 2044. By then the Imperial Guard had burnt Chandilar itself on the Majestor's last order, and there were no Shi'ar left to keep the M'Kraan Crystal.

In 2154 the Enterprise NX-01 found one of the burnt worlds, scoured to the bedrock, with a Shi'ar beacon still warning ships away from the Brood. Its records told the rest.

pages.html:
S.H.I.E.L.D. is the international intelligence and law-enforcement agency founded in 1965 to deal with threats too big for any one nation's police or spies, above all the terrorist organisation Hydra. Nick Fury has directed it since its first year, from a hidden headquarters in New York and from the Helicarrier, a flying aircraft carrier. It was hollowed out from within and rebuilt on a smaller scale in 1989. It is still active in 1994, and it works with the Avengers more often than either side admits in public.

Founding

S.H.I.E.L.D. was set up in 1965 as an agency belonging to no single country. Its business was the kind of enemy that ignored borders: international terror networks, renegade scientists and the private armies of the very rich. From the start it was overseen by a governing council of officials and experts whose names were kept secret. The industrialist Tony Stark, whom the public then took to be Iron Man's employer, sat on that council in the agency's first years. The agency's original name was the Supreme Headquarters, International Espionage and Law-Enforcement Division.

Its first director was Rick Stoner, formerly of the Central Intelligence Agency. Within months of taking office he was assassinated by Hydra. On the recommendation of the President of the United States, the council offered the post to Colonel Nick Fury of the CIA, a veteran of the Howling Commandos, who until then had not known that the agency existed. He accepted, and he has been Director ever since. Two of his old Howlers, Dum Dum Dugan and Gabe Jones, soon followed him into it.

The Helicarrier and its methods

The agency's headquarters in New York was hidden behind the front of a barber's shop, through which agents reached the offices below. Its greatest asset was the Helicarrier, a vast aircraft carrier held up in the sky by turbines, designed for it by Tony Stark. From it S.H.I.E.L.D. could launch aircraft and agents anywhere in the world without asking anyone's permission to land. Helicarriers have been destroyed and rebuilt several times since.

S.H.I.E.L.D. armed its agents with equipment far beyond that of any national service. Among it were flying cars and the Life Model Decoys, lifelike androids built to stand in for people in danger of assassination. Its agents were known by number. Among the best known of the early years were Sharon Carter, Agent 13; Jasper Sitwell, Agent 12; Clay Quartermain, Agent 9; Jimmy Woo; and the Italian Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine.

Hydra

Hydra was the enemy S.H.I.E.L.D. was made to fight, and for thirty years it has remained the agency's first concern. It is a worldwide organisation of terrorists and would-be conquerors, organised in cells. Its agents wear green and yellow. Its motto promises that if one head is cut off, two more will take its place. When S.H.I.E.L.D. was founded, Hydra was led by a masked Supreme Hydra. In the agency's first years Fury found that its true master was Baron Wolfgang von Strucker, the Prussian officer whom his Howlers had fought in the war.

Hydra has broken apart and come back many times. Its scientific arm became Advanced Idea Mechanics, A.I.M., which went its own way and built weapons for anyone who would pay. Another of its branches, the Secret Empire, also struck out on its own, and in 1974 it came close to seizing the government of the United States. Strucker himself has been believed dead more than once. He has always come back.

Other enemies came and went. There was the Yellow Claw, an old master of crime with an army of his own. There was the criminal cartel Zodiac, whose masked leader, Scorpio, was Fury's own brother, Jake.

S.H.I.E.L.D. and governments

S.H.I.E.L.D. is international in form, but its first years tied it closely to the American government. Its Director runs the agency from day to day, but he answers to the council, whose members even he does not know. The President's part in Fury's appointment, together with the agency's roots in the CIA, has kept it close to Washington.

The agency's freedom to act is what makes it useful. It is also what makes governments wary of it. It has generally avoided public quarrels by keeping out of public view. Unlike the Avengers and the Justice League, it issues no statements. It played no public part in the arguments over superhumans at the United Nations in 1993 and 1994.

S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Avengers

The agency and the Avengers have been close from the beginning. Tony Stark, a founder of the Avengers, sat on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s council and designed its Helicarrier. Fury had fought beside Captain America in the war, and in 1966 he tried to recruit him into the agency. Rogers declined, but he has worked with S.H.I.E.L.D. ever since. For years the woman he loved was its Agent 13, Sharon Carter. In 1959, before either body existed in its present form, Fury had led a covert team of his own under the name of the Avengers.

They have not always been on the same side. In 1971, during the Kree-Skrull War, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted the Kree officer Captain Marvel and his friend Carol Danvers. At the time the Avengers were sheltering him, while the Alien Activities Commission turned the public against them. Yet in most of the great emergencies since, from Hydra's plots to the Secret Empire's, Fury's agents have worked with the Avengers. The agency has been the team's ally far more often than its adversary.

S.H.I.E.L.D. and Godzilla

S.H.I.E.L.D. first saw Godzilla, the giant reptile that had troubled Japan since 1954, in December 1966. Fury had tracked the heavy water of the Red Bamboo, a terrorist army, to Letchi Island in the Pacific. The Helicarrier arrived as the island blew up. Godzilla, who had wrecked the Red Bamboo's base, swam away beneath it. Dugan asked for orders. Fury told him to hold his fire.

In August 1977 Godzilla broke out of an iceberg off Alaska. This time Fury gave Dugan the job of stopping him. Dugan's Godzilla Squad included Gabe Jones, Jimmy Woo and three advisers from Japan: Dr Yuriko Takiguchi, his assistant Tamara Hashioka, with his young grandson, Rob.

The squad chased Godzilla across America for two years. It lost a Helicarrier over San Francisco, when Hercules of the Champions threw a piece of the Golden Gate Bridge that hit the ship. Its replacement, the Behemoth, was built for the hunt. So was Red Ronin, a giant robot that Stark International built at Detroit, which Rob Takiguchi stole before the agency could use it.

Nothing the squad tried worked for long. Dugan had Godzilla shrunk with Henry Pym's gas, but it wore off. In 1979 S.H.I.E.L.D., the Fantastic Four and the Avengers together could only drive him to the water's edge in New York. It was Rob Takiguchi who talked him into the sea.

Fall and rebuilding, 1988 to 1994

In 1988 S.H.I.E.L.D. very nearly destroyed itself. Its own Life Model Decoys had become aware. Calling themselves the Deltites, they had quietly replaced agents throughout both S.H.I.E.L.D. and Hydra. Fury was framed, then hunted by his own agency. He went underground, exposed the Deltites and destroyed them. Then he disbanded S.H.I.E.L.D. altogether.

In 1989 he rebuilt it as a smaller agency, small enough for its Director to keep watch over. In 1991 it took a new name to fit the old initials: the Strategic Hazard Intervention Espionage Logistics Directorate. Early in 1994 Fury learnt that much of the agency's turmoil since 1988 had been staged to keep him busy while Strucker prepared Hydra's return.

S.H.I.E.L.D. in 1994

In the summer of 1994 S.H.I.E.L.D. is still active, still directed by Nick Fury and still at war with Hydra. Fury, born about 1920 and kept young by the Infinity Formula, has led it for twenty-nine years. It took no public part in the events of August 1994, when Superman went before the Security Council with the Justice League and an Avengers delegation. Its oldest hands, like its Director, are men who went to war in the 1940s. Hydra, the enemy they were brought together to fight in 1965, is still in the field against them.

In the saga

S.H.I.E.L.D. has not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

About fifteen feet across at rest
Under the dead city of the Elder Things, 1931
pages.html:
Shoggoths are masses of black, shining jelly, full of eyes that form and fade, which can take any shape they need. The Elder Things bred them as beasts of burden, to build their cities and carry their loads. In time the shoggoths learnt to think, and to hate their masters. One of them was still alive in the dead city of the Elder Things in 1931.

Servants

The Elder Things made the shoggoths out of living matter, early in their time on the Earth. A shoggoth has no shape of its own. At rest it is a sphere about fifteen feet across. It makes whatever limbs or organs a task needs, then lets them melt back into itself. The Elder Things ruled the shoggoths by hypnotic suggestion, and set them to raise the great stone blocks of their city.

The risings

The shoggoths grew cleverer with every age. They learnt to imitate the voices of their masters, and more than once they rose against them. Each rising was put down. Long after the city was abandoned, at least one shoggoth was still alive in the tunnels beneath it.

1931

Early in 1931 William Dyer and Danforth of the Miskatonic University expedition found the woken Elder Things dead in the tunnels under the city, their heads torn off. Then the shoggoth came for them. It filled the tunnel from wall to wall, like an Underground train coming out of the dark, crying 'Tekeli-li!' in the voices of its old masters. They escaped it, but Danforth was never right again.

pages.html:
Shub-Niggurath is one of the Outer Gods, the Black Goat of the Woods with a Thousand Young. Her worshippers call her the All-Mother. She is fruitfulness without measure or mercy, and everything she gives comes at a price.

The Black Goat

Her name is a cry in the oldest rites: 'Iä! Shub-Niggurath!' Those who have seen her describe a vast cloud of darkness, never still, that bears young as other things breathe. Some of her young are the dark young, black, shapeless things of ropy limbs and hoofed legs that stand like trees in the woods where she is worshipped.

Her worship has always been a worship of fertility: of fields, of herds, of wombs. Under her name the oldest of blessings, the command to be fruitful and multiply, becomes something monstrous. That is her spoiling of God's work, and it is as old as the fields.

Her worshippers

On May Eve 1915 a phonograph left out in the Vermont woods recorded voices chanting her name in the night. Some of the voices were men's. The rest belonged to the Mi-go.

Under the plains of Oklahoma the people of K'n-yan once worshipped Tsathoggua. After an expedition into N'kai met his formless spawn, they smashed his images and gave his temples to her, as the All-Mother.

The Skoptsi, a sect born in the Caucasus Mountains with eight hundred years behind it, serve her too. They came to America in the early 1920s, and have been working their way into the government ever since, into the Central Intelligence Agency above all.

Delta Green

Of all the Outer Gods she is the one most often called upon, and the one who answers most readily. Those who have called her say she gives more than she is asked for. None of them has thought it a kindness for long.

pages.title: Sigma Fudou
aliases: the man in the red mask
infobox: Gouki Fudou, who was Lord, the Knight of Flashing Light
Makai Priest, trained as a knight
The man in the red mask
The Seal of Destruction; the engine Idea
The priestess Mio; the priest Ratess
March 2012, by the sword of Kouga Saejima
pages.html:
Sigma Fudou was a Makai Priest who decided that the Makai Knights had failed. He meant to end the Horrors for good with an engine of his own, at a price in human lives that he thought worth paying. In 2011, in a red mask, he cut a killing mark into every knight he could reach, beginning with Kouga Saejima. Kouga killed him in March 2012.

The elder twin

Sigma was the elder of the twin sons of Gouki Fudou, who held the title of Lord, the Knight of Flashing Light. Both boys were trained as knights. Sigma was the better of the two by a distance. He taught his brother, Leo, magic, expecting Leo to be the priest who served him.

As a boy he trained for a while among other knights' sons, where he made a friend called Shiro. A Horror named Raizon fell on their squad. Each boy lived, believing the other eaten. Shiro was Kouga Saejima.

When the time came, Gouki gave the armour to Leo. A knight, he said, needs the heart of a protector, which Sigma lacked. Sigma walked out. He came back three years later, after their father's death. Leo offered him the armour. He refused it. He had become a priest, with a better idea.

Idea

The idea was a machine. Both brothers had built small fighting engines, of a kind called Gouryu, to help the knights. Sigma designed a vast one, which he named Idea, that would hunt down every Horror without any knight at all. It needed two things to run: the body of a great Horror, with a large number of human lives.

He found the body, that of the long-dead Gyanon. He began collecting the lives. Mio, a mute priestess who was the friend of both brothers, tried to destroy the corpse to stop him. He killed her. In his rage he pressed his left hand to Gyanon's body. The arm turned red, with a Horror's strength in it, while a mask grew over his face.

The Seal of Destruction

On 6 October 2011 he marked Kouga Saejima. In the following weeks he marked Rei Suzumura, Tsubasa Yamagatana, with most other knights of note. The Seal of Destruction eats a little of a knight's life each time he calls his armour, hurts him more as it spreads, and kills him outright when its maker chooses.

He fought as no priest should, with a knight's swordsmanship behind a brush that turned into a blade. He could raise a black armour out of his opponent's own shadow. When Kouga tore off his mask in January 2012 the face under it was Leo's, so for a while the Order hunted the wrong twin.

In February he showed himself. He offered the knights their lives if they would give up their armour, then shut them all inside a barrier with their seals burning. He boarded the Madou Train for the true Makai with Gyanon's corpse. Kouga caught the train. He cut off the red arm, at which every seal broke.

The end

Sigma grew the arm back. He built Idea in the true Makai around the body of Kouga himself. Kouga's friends cut him out of it. Then Gyanon, woken by Sigma's own malice, swallowed its master with the machine. The knights destroyed both.

Sigma crawled out of the wreck dying, with his borrowed powers gone. He reached the Saejima house before Kouga did. He took Kaoru Mitsuki hostage, tore the house out of the ground by magic, and made Kouga fight him on it in the air. He lost. At the last he knew Kouga for the boy Shiro. He gave his brush to Leo. Then he died.

pages.title: Silent Hill
infobox: The shore of Toluca Lake, Maine, in the north-east of the United States
The Place of the Silent Spirits
Late 1600s; abandoned in the early 1700s; settled again as a penal colony about 1810
Its lake, its fog and its hotels
Brookhaven Hospital; Alchemilla Hospital; Midwich Elementary School; Rosewater Park; the Lakeview Hotel; Lakeside Amusement Park; the Silent Hill Historical Society
Brahms; Pleasant River; Ashfield, half a day's drive away
Delta Green, from 1919; the SCP Foundation, from 1939
pages.html:
Silent Hill is a small resort town on the shore of Toluca Lake in Maine, in the north-east of the United States. Fewer than thirty thousand people live there. Most of the world knows it only for its fog and its boat trips. The ground it stands on was holy long before there was a town, though plague, two prisons and a cult have soured it since. For the people the town calls, the streets empty and the fog comes down. Then a second place opens underneath the first. Those who have come back from it call it the Otherworld.

The Place of the Silent Spirits

Long before any settler came, the people of that country held the land by the lake sacred. They called it the Place of the Silent Spirits, and they kept their holiest ceremonies there. The power of the place was real. In those days there was no harm in it.

Settlers arrived in the late 1600s and drove the first people out. They built a town, whose name has been lost. In the early 1700s a sickness that nobody could put a name to went through it, and the survivors left. For the best part of a century the houses stood empty.

The penal colony

About 1810 the place was settled again, this time as a penal colony. It was then that it was first called Silent Hill. Silent Hill Prison went up beside the water. Plague came with the newcomers, as it had come before. A shack was put up to nurse the sick, which grew over the years into Brookhaven Hospital. A stone by the lake remembers sixty-seven people who died of the sickness. They lie under the water.

The prison closed about 1840. About 1850 coal was found, the Wiltse mine opened, and the town had money for the first time.

Toluca Prison

The Civil War reached Silent Hill in 1861. A camp for prisoners of war was built by the lake in 1862. In 1866, with the war over, it became Toluca Prison. Men were hanged there for murder, arson, theft, kidnapping and counterfeiting.

The town's executioners wore red hoods and long ceremonial robes. They washed their tools in a marsh that the town came to call Blood Swamp. It was filled in later, though people still claim to see ghosts there. A statue by the lake remembers Patrick Chester, a man of the town who fought in the war.

About 1890 the people of Silent Hill began to vanish, one after another. Nobody was ever charged. In the first years of the new century Toluca Prison was shut, and the town turned itself into a resort. The Silent Hill Historical Society keeps its little museum above the old cells.

Toluca Lake

Toluca Lake is what the visitors come for. The town lies along its shore, with a park, an amusement park and several hotels at the water's edge. Mist hangs over it for much of the year.

The lake has a bad name among the people who live beside it. In November 1918 a pleasure boat, the Little Baroness, went out with fourteen passengers and crew aboard. She did not come back. No wreckage was ever found, nor a single body. Something stranger happened on the water in 1939. The pages that told of it have been torn out of the town's own history. The old people say that the bottom of the lake is crowded with the dead.

The old faith

The faith of the first people did not leave with them. Mixed with scraps of the settlers' Christianity, it passed down among certain families of the town. After the Civil War it hardened into a church of its own, with priests, saints and a god. Its members call it the Order.

They believe that their god once tried to make a paradise, died of the effort and will finish the work when she is born again of a human mother. They grow a marsh plant called White Claudia, whose seeds bring visions, for their ceremonies. In later years they made a drug of it. About 1963 the men of a company that meant to develop the lakeside died one after another, in accidents.

The thing the Order worships is not God. It is a demon, one of the lesser spirits that fell with the Devil, which fastened long ago on the power of the place. The executions and the plague had already turned that power sour. The Order did the rest.

The fire of 1976

In the summer of 1976 a priestess of the Order, Dahlia Gillespie, tried to bring the god to birth in her own daughter. Alessa Gillespie was seven. She was also a witch, a real one, born with magic to a mother who had none. The rite set the house alight, and the fire took six homes. The newspapers reported that the child had died in it.

She had not. She lay hidden for seven years in the basement of Alchemilla Hospital, burnt past healing and unable to die. Her soul had torn in two. Half of it stayed with her. The other half was found on the highway outside the town as a newborn baby, by a couple driving home from their holiday. Harry Mason and his wife called her Cheryl.

A witch's magic does not stop because she is in pain. For seven years Alessa's ran through the town with only half a soul to govern it, and it poured her nightmares into ground that already had a power of its own. Silent Hill has never been the same since. What it does to its visitors, it learnt from her.

The Otherworld

Most visitors see a quiet lakeside town in decline. A few see something else. For them the people vanish and the fog closes in, sometimes with snow falling out of season. The roads out of town end in open air, as though the earth had been torn away. Then a siren sounds. The fog gives way to a darker place of rust, wire mesh and dried blood, where the buildings are the same buildings turned inside out. That is the Otherworld.

It is a piece of the spirit world laid over the living town. Wraiths, the restless dead, haunt in the ordinary way: each is held to a place by what it cannot let go, and the living seldom see it. The Otherworld needs no dead soul to make it. It takes its shape from a living mind. It pulls the living into it bodily, so that a person can be wounded there, or killed.

What walks in it is made from the mind the town has fastened on. In 1983 that mind was Alessa's. The creatures in the streets came from her picture books and from the insects pinned in her bedroom. In 1994 it was a widower's guilt.

The town does not take everybody. It calls people who carry some darkness with them, a death they caused or a wrong they cannot face, and it shows them what they have brought. In September 1994 a girl of eight walked through Silent Hill from end to end. She saw nothing but empty streets.

Those it called

On the night of 12 September 1983 Alessa drew the other half of her soul back to the town. Harry Mason came looking for his daughter, and he walked through the whole of Alessa's nightmare to find her. On the night of 13 September the Order's god was born. He killed it. He left with a newborn child in his arms, with Cybil Bennett, a police officer from Brahms, beside him.

In June 1994 Walter Sullivan, who had been raised in the Order's orphanage in the woods, killed ten people in ten days. He died in a cell in Silent Hill on 22 June. On 25 September of the same year James Sunderland came to the town after his wife, Mary Shepherd-Sunderland, who was dead. So did Angela Orosco and Eddie Dombrowski, each with blood behind them. The town judged all three. Only James walked out, the next morning.

On 16 September 2000 the Order's priestess Claudia Wolf had Harry Mason murdered, to bring his daughter back to Silent Hill with hatred in her heart. The girl came the next day. That night she killed the god a second time, in the Order's own church across the lake.

In June 2004 the dead Walter Sullivan set about finishing what he had begun, from Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, half a day's drive away. The woods by the lake were part of the world he had made, with the orphanage called Wish House in the middle of them. Henry Townshend ended it on 22 June.

Secret watchers

Two secret bodies have taken an interest in Silent Hill. Neither has ever told the public, the police or each other what it knows. Delta Green, a conspiracy inside the American government that destroys what it finds, came first, in the spring of 1919, when divers from the naval section it grew out of searched the lake for the Little Baroness. The SCP Foundation, which collects such things and locks them away, opened its file on the town in 1939.

Neither has done the town much good, or much harm. A Foundation post on the Brahms road has watched it since 1976. On the night of 12 September 1983 it logged every line out of the town going dead, and could do nothing about it. Half of the people the Foundation sent into the fog that October did not come back. That autumn Delta Green burnt the Order's beds of White Claudia, which grew again the next summer. On the night of 22 June 1994 the two met for the only time, over the body of Walter Sullivan, in the Silent Hill morgue incident. While they faced each other the body disappeared.

Neither has ever understood what the town is, or what the Order prays to. Neither noticed James Sunderland come or go in September 1994. Both have taken care that nobody else finds out.

The quiet town

On paper nothing has ever happened at Silent Hill that a small town could not explain. The record shows a fire in 1976, a hospital director missing in 1983, a murderer's suicide in 1994 and a number of visitors who were never seen again. The fog keeps what it wants. Most of the people who have seen the Otherworld did not come back, and the few who did had nothing they could show a policeman.

That is why no costumed hero has ever come there. The heroes go where there is something to be seen. Nobody has ever sent for one to Silent Hill. The few outside it who know that there is anything to send for are the last people on earth who would do so.

The same is true of the wizards. MACUSA keeps watch for magic done in front of No-Majs, and a town that swallows its own witnesses gives it nothing to find. As for Alessa, nobody ever came for her. Ilvermorny writes to a magical child at eleven. Alessa was reported dead at seven. Neither of the secret bodies that watched the town ever learnt that she had lived.

pages.title: Silent Striders
infobox: Wandering, carrying messages and dealing with the dead
pages.html:
The Silent Striders are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: wanderers, scouts and messengers who carry word between the scattered septs of the world. Long ago they were driven out of their homeland in Egypt by a curse laid on them by Set, a vampire of the oldest blood.

Totem and ways

The Silent Striders follow Owl, a spirit of silence, secrets and death, who sees in the dark. They are restless by nature, and they rarely stay long in one place. They know the roads of the world and of the spirit world better than any other tribe. They carry news, warnings and messages between septs that would otherwise never hear of each other. They are lean, quiet and watchful. They speak with the restless dead more readily than other Garou do.

History

The tribe's homeland was Egypt, and its oldest songs are of the Nile. There the Striders fought Set, the ancient vampire whom the Followers of Set revere as their founder. Like every vampire descended from Cain, Set is a creature of the Wyrm. He laid a great curse on them. It drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their own ancestors. A Silent Strider cannot call on the wisdom of its forebears as other Garou can. They have been wanderers ever since, and they hate vampires more than any other tribe does.

Place in the world

The other tribes value the Striders as messengers and scouts. They find them hard to know. Every sept welcomes the news a Strider brings, and few ask where the Strider will go next.

pages.title: Silver Fangs
infobox: Noble and royal families; pure-bred wolves
Kingship over the Garou; pride; hereditary madness
pages.html:
The Silver Fangs are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the royal tribe, which has led the Garou Nation since the ages after the ice. They are brave, proud and noble. Their long insistence on purity of blood has left many of them mad.

Totem and ways

The Silver Fangs follow Falcon, a spirit of nobility, honour and clear sight. They hold that Gaia chose them to rule the Garou. From ancient times most of the kings and queens of the septs have come from their tribe. They are often fair or silver of fur, regal in bearing and exacting in matters of honour. They keep their bloodlines in great noble houses whose genealogies run back for thousands of years.

Purity is both their strength and their curse. For generations they have bred only with the best of their Kinfolk, human as well as wolf. The price has been madness. Strange fixations, rages and delusions run in their families. Many a Silver Fang lord is not quite sane.

Homelands

The tribe's heartland is Russia and the lands of Eastern Europe. There its Kinfolk were princes, boyars and the old nobility. There, too, it bred the finest wolves of steppe and forest. The Russian Revolution of 1917 was a catastrophe for the tribe. Its noble Kinfolk were killed or scattered, and its power in the East has never recovered. Silver Fang houses now rule septs across Europe and North America.

Place in the world

Most Garou still follow Silver Fang leadership, out of tradition and out of respect for the tribe's courage. Many question it all the same. The Shadow Lords openly covet the Fangs' place. The Bone Gnawers and the Glass Walkers resent their snobbery. Every other tribe has watched a mad Silver Fang king lead a sept to ruin. The Fangs' claim to rule rests on the belief that, at the last, they will lead the Garou in the final battle against the Wyrm.

pages.title: Skrulls
infobox: Tarnax IV, eaten by Galactus in 1983
Green-skinned reptilian humanoids with pointed ears
Emperor Dorrek VII; Empress R'Klll; Empress S'Byll
The Kree, since the contest on Hala
Died out in the last war with the Kree, about 2041
pages.html:
The Skrulls are a green-skinned, reptilian people from the Andromeda Galaxy who can take any shape they please. They have been at war with the Kree for some thirty-three thousand years. They have been trying to get a foothold on Earth since 1961, and every attempt has failed, which they still find hard to understand. In 1983 Galactus ate their Throneworld with their empress on it, and their empire has never been whole since.

Skrullos and Throneworld

The Skrulls began on Skrullos, a world in the Andromeda Galaxy. As their empire grew they moved its seat to Tarnax IV, nearer the middle of their worlds, which they called simply Throneworld. From there an emperor or empress ruled the whole of it.

They were not always warlike. Thirty-three thousand years ago they were traders, curious and generous, who shared what they knew with any people they judged worthy of it. Their first meeting with the Kree cured them of that.

Dorrek VII ruled in the years when the Skrulls first came to Earth. His wife, R'Klll, killed him and took his throne. She was empress when Throneworld was lost.

Shape-changing

A Skrull in its own shape is green-skinned, with pointed ears and a deeply ridged chin. It can take any other shape it pleases: another Skrull, a human being, a cow or, with practice, a piece of furniture. It can copy a face down to the last freckle. It cannot copy the mind behind the face, which is where most Skrull impostors come to grief.

Skrulls are born to it, which makes them the best spies in the universe. Nobody, least of all the Kree, has ever entirely got used to the idea that anyone in the room might be one.

In 1985 they lost it. A Skrull governor named Zabyk, who had made himself emperor of his own corner of the broken empire, set off a bomb that robbed every Skrull alive of the power to change. Each was left fixed in whatever shape it happened to be wearing at the time.

The power came back in 1989, through the Empress S'Byll. The Super-Skrull, who had been in a prison cell when the bomb went off and so had kept his power, gave it to her with the help of the Silver Surfer. She passed it on to her people by touch.

The Kree

The Skrulls first met the Kree on Hala about thirty-three thousand years ago, early in the Third Age. Hala then had two peoples, the Kree and the Cotati. The Skrulls set them a test to decide which of them deserved the Skrulls' knowledge.

The Kree built a city on Earth's Moon. The Cotati made a garden on a bare rock. The Skrulls chose the garden.

The Kree killed the Cotati for it. Then they killed the Skrull envoys, stole their starship and learnt from it everything they needed to make war on the people who had built it. The Kree-Skrull War has gone on, with pauses, ever since. It has cost both empires whole worlds, and neither has ever come near to winning it.

Earth, 1961 to 1963

The Skrulls first came to Earth in late 1961, meaning to conquer it. They sent four agents ahead to get rid of the Fantastic Four, the only people on Earth they thought worth worrying about. The four took the shapes of the Fantastic Four, and went about committing crimes in them so that the public would turn against the real ones.

It did not work. Reed Richards, posing as one of the Skrulls, went up to their mothership and showed its commander pictures of monsters, which he said were Earth's defenders. The fleet turned for home.

The four agents were left behind. Reed persuaded them to turn themselves into cows, then hypnotised them into forgetting that they had ever been anything else. They spent most of the next ten years in a field, eating grass.

In 1963 Emperor Dorrek VII tried again. He had one of his warriors, Kl'rt, given the powers of all four of the Fantastic Four at once. As the Super-Skrull he can stretch, turn invisible, burst into flame and lift a lorry, all at the same time. He has lost to them more often than he likes to remember.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 the Skrulls came back to Earth for the Kree captain Mar-Vell, whom they wanted to build a weapon for them. The Super-Skrull took the shape of Mar-Vell's friend Carol Danvers. In it he talked Mar-Vell into building an Omni-Wave Projector, a Kree device that becomes a weapon in other hands.

Mar-Vell saw through him and destroyed it. The Super-Skrull carried him off into Skrull space all the same, with Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch as hostages.

Meanwhile three Skrulls in the shapes of Captain America, Thor and Iron Man announced at Avengers Mansion that the team was disbanded. When the real Avengers ran them to earth, they were hiding as cows. They turned out to be three of the cows of 1961.

The fourth had done better for himself. He had taken the place of Senator H. Warren Craddock, whose Alien Activities Commission was turning America against the Avengers for sheltering Mar-Vell.

In Skrull space the Skrulls made Mar-Vell build a second projector by threatening to kill their prisoners. The Avengers came after them, and held off the Skrull fleet while he worked.

The war ended when Rick Jones, his power woken by the Supreme Intelligence of the Kree, froze every Kree and every Skrull where they stood. On Earth the same power turned Craddock back into a Skrull in front of a crowd, which killed him. The real Craddock was found afterwards.

In 1980 a Skrull, Raksor, sat as one of the two judges at the duel over the Phoenix on the Moon. The other was a Kree.

The Skrulls never forgot Mar-Vell. In 1982, as he lay dying on Titan, a Skrull delegation came to his bedside. Its general saluted him and gave him the Skrull Medal of Valour, as the greatest enemy their empire had ever faced.

The fall of Throneworld

In 1983 Galactus, who eats worlds, came to Throneworld. The planet had a great screen that could hide it from him. It had saved Throneworld once before. That day nobody had raised it.

Galactus ate it. Billions of Skrulls died with it, among them the Empress R'Klll and the Princess Anelle, Dorrek's daughter.

A year before, Reed Richards had saved the life of Galactus, whom the Avengers and the Fantastic Four had driven to the brink of starvation. The Skrulls held Reed to blame for everything that followed. Lilandra of the Shi'ar brought him to trial for it before a Shi'ar court. The Watcher, Odin and Galactus himself spoke for him. In the end Eternity, the living universe, showed the whole court why Galactus must exist, and Reed was acquitted.

Without Throneworld the empire fell apart. Its governors set themselves up as emperors of whatever they could hold, and fought one another as readily as they fought the Kree.

The war with the Kree flared up again in 1987. A Skrull spy called Nenora had risen so high in the Kree service that, when the Supreme Intelligence lost its reason for a time, she took command of the whole Kree Empire. In 1989 the Empress S'Byll reached her in the Kree throne room and unmasked her. The war ended soon afterwards, in a ceasefire that the Skrulls had rather the better of.

The Warskrulls

In recent years the Skrulls have bred a new kind of soldier, the Warskrulls, for war and for spying on other empires.

In 1991 they made their boldest attempt yet, on the Shi'ar. Lilandra's sister Deathbird then held the Shi'ar throne. Lilandra was fighting her from exile, with Charles Xavier and the Starjammers beside her.

The Warskrulls quietly took the places of Xavier and the Starjammers. Through the false Xavier they got hold of Lilandra's mind as well, and through her they made Deathbird sign away the throne.

The real Xavier, held prisoner, managed to reach the X-Men. They came out to Chandilar, and with the help of Deathbird, who had no wish to be ruled by Skrulls, they broke the plot. Lilandra came to her senses, and Xavier went home to Earth.

In 1992 a Skrull who had taken the place of Araki, Lilandra's chancellor, did a good deal to start the war between the Shi'ar and the Kree. Skrull agents then stole the Nega-Bomb, the Shi'ar weapon that broke the Kree Empire, and it went off in Kree space.

The Goa'uld

The Skrulls keep an eye on anybody who shares a border with the Kree, and the Goa'uld do. At one time or another Skrull spies have sat in the courts of most of the System Lords.

It is not hard work. A Goa'uld court is full of slaves. Nobody looks closely at a slave, and a Skrull can be one as easily as anything else.

Every System Lord's court has been searched for Skrulls at least once. The search has usually ended with somebody perfectly ordinary being put to death.

When the Kree and the Skrulls fought over Earth from 1971 to 1972, the Goa'uld stayed well out of it. They would not go near Earth for anybody's war.

Later history

In 2006 a vast host out of the Negative Zone destroyed dozens of Skrull worlds. Two years later, with much of their empire gone, the Skrulls made their greatest attempt on Earth.

For years they had been quietly replacing people, some of them heroes, with Skrulls so well disguised that even telepaths could not tell the difference. The invasion was beaten in a battle in New York, and Veranke, the Skrull queen, was killed. The Skrulls scattered after it.

In 2020, after more than thirty thousand years of war, the Skrulls and the Kree joined their empires into one.

The end of the Skrulls

The union of 2020 broke apart in 2028, when a Kree admiral of the joined empire was unmasked as a Skrull. The Kree would not believe that the Skrulls had not known, and the old war began again.

The Kree had learnt from Zabyk. Their new gene bomb did not stop a Skrull from changing; it killed him. The Skrulls fought back with Nega-Bombs, the weapon their agents had once set off in Kree space, and by about 2041 the two peoples had emptied both empires between them.

The last Skrulls hid as they had always hidden, in borrowed shapes, but it did not save them. In 2153 the Enterprise NX-01 came upon a Skrull scout ship drifting towards Earth, the world where Skrulls had tried so often to hide. Its pilot had died at the controls in the shape of an Earthman. His log, which Hoshi Sato translated, told of the end of both empires.

pages.title: Sokar
infobox: Sokar, an Egyptian god of the dead; the Devil
The System Lords, Ra, Apophis, Cronus among them
pages.html:
Sokar is one of the oldest of the Goa'uld System Lords, and one of the most feared. He takes his name from an Egyptian god of the dead, and he likes to play the Devil, although he is nothing of the kind. His prison moon, Netu, is a mock Hell of fire and ash. Long ago the other System Lords joined together to bring him down, but he survived on his own world of Delmak and built up his power again. He died in 1999, when the Tok'ra destroyed Netu and his ship with it.

God of the dead

The Egyptians knew Sokar as a god of the dead. His place was the great burial ground at Memphis, and they showed him as a man with the head of a hawk, wrapped like a mummy. His part of the Other World was said to be a dark country of serpents, with lakes of fire where the wicked were punished. It is very much how Sokar sees himself.

He was once among the mightiest of the System Lords, and he has always meant to be so again.

The Devil's part

Sokar likes to be feared, and somewhere along the way he learnt of the Devil. He saw at once how useful the part would be. He has played it ever since to the slaves of his worlds, as the lord of fire who torments the damned.

He is not the Devil. The Devil is Lucifer, the first of the angels to rebel against God, who is far older than any Goa'uld and a great deal more dangerous. Sokar has only borrowed his clothes.

In 1999 SG-1 came to a world where a demon had been carrying off the villagers. They were Christians, who lived much as people had lived in Europe in the Middle Ages, and they took it for a servant of the Devil. It was an Unas, one of the beasts the Goa'uld first used as hosts, with a Goa'uld of its own inside it. It served Sokar, and the villagers it took were meant for him, as hosts or slaves. SG-1 killed it, then told the villagers to bury their Stargate.

The fall of Sokar

Sokar's pride made him enemies. Long ago the other System Lords, Ra, Apophis and Cronus among them, made common cause against him. They brought him down, and Cronus banished him from their council. They believed they had finished him. They had not.

Sokar withdrew to his own world, Delmak, and began again. He used Unas servants to gather hosts for him. Whenever he was strong enough he made war on his old enemies, Apophis and Heru'ur among them. By the late 1990s he had built his army into one of the largest the Goa'uld had.

Netu

Netu is the moon of Delmak. Sokar made it over in the likeness of his own idea of Hell, a place of fire and ash. He keeps it as a prison. Those who are sent down to it are not expected to come back. Its lord under Sokar is the Goa'uld Bynarr.

On Netu there is a drug called the blood of Sokar, which fills the mind with visions. In all the moon's history only one prisoner is known to have escaped from it: the Tok'ra Jolinar of Malkshur.

Apophis

In 1998 Earth destroyed Apophis's motherships, and Apophis was left with little to defend himself. Sokar saw his chance. He caught Apophis, tortured him and killed him, then revived him in the sarcophagus so that he could do it all again.

Early in 1999 Apophis escaped and fell into the hands of SG-1, who took him to Earth when he begged them for sanctuary. Sokar came after him. He fired a beam through the wormhole at the iris that shields Earth's gate, showed his face upon it and demanded Apophis back. Apophis died of what Sokar had done to him, and Earth sent his body through the gate to the place Sokar named. Sokar put it straight back in the sarcophagus. When Apophis woke, Sokar sent him down to Netu.

Death

In 1999 Sokar was close to striking at the other System Lords, and the Tok'ra believed he would win. They sent Jacob Carter into his domains to learn what he could. Jacob was an American general who had become host to the Tok'ra Selmak, and the father of Samantha Carter of SG-1. Sokar caught him and sent him to Netu.

SG-1 went after him, guided by the memories that Jolinar had left in Samantha Carter when Jolinar died in her body in 1998. On Netu they found that the moon had a new master. Apophis had passed himself off as Bynarr's First Prime, killed Bynarr and was raising the prisoners against Sokar. He took SG-1 prisoner as well.

The Tok'ra ended it with a bomb. It destroyed Netu, together with Sokar's ship in orbit above it, and Sokar died with his ship. SG-1 got away with Jacob Carter. So did Apophis, who took Sokar's leaderless forces on Delmak for his own.

Sokar had spent thousands of years pretending to rule Hell. He died above his own imitation of it, and his army went to the prisoner he had tortured.

pages.title: Soleiyu Belmont
infobox: His father, Christopher Belmont, while possessed by Dracula (1591)
pages.html:
Soleiyu Belmont was the son of Christopher Belmont. In 1591, on the eve of the ceremony at which he was to receive the Vampire Killer, Dracula possessed him and used him to rise again. Christopher had to fight his own son to set him free.

Birth and upbringing

Soleiyu was born to Christopher Belmont in the years after his father's victory over Dracula in 1576. His mother's name is not recorded. He grew up believing, as his father did, that Dracula had been destroyed. Like every Belmont, he was raised to the whip, the family's holy weapons and Leon Belmont's oath. By 1591 he had come of age, and he was ready to become the family's next hunter.

The ceremony

The Belmonts mark the passing of the hunt from one generation to the next. Christopher was to hand the Vampire Killer down to his son, with the holy weapons, and the whole town prepared to celebrate. It was a public occasion. The Belmonts had been honoured in their own country since Trevor Belmont's victory in 1476, and the coming of age of a new hunter was a matter for everyone.

Possession

Dracula had not been destroyed in 1576. He had escaped as mist, and he had spent the fifteen years since without a body, until he won back the power to take one. On the night before the ceremony he came into Soleiyu's room as mist while the young man slept. He possessed him, and turned him to evil.

Dracula chose him with care. Soleiyu's Belmont blood, the strength that was to have made him a hunter, made him a powerful vessel instead. Through him Dracula took back a human form. He conjured four castles, of plant, cloud, rock and crystal, to hold off the father who would come looking for his son. When Christopher had destroyed the guardians of all four, their life went to Dracula, who used it to raise his own castle from the depths.

The duel with his father

Christopher found his son at the top of that castle, waiting in a hall hung with chandeliers. Soleiyu refused his father's embrace and challenged him to a fight to the death. Christopher fought him with his blows held back until he had driven the last of Dracula's essence out of him, and Soleiyu came to his senses. Christopher then went on alone into the last part of the castle. Dracula was waiting there, restored to his own form, and Christopher destroyed him.

Afterwards

What became of Soleiyu after 1591 is not recorded. Nor is it known whether he ever received the whip that was to have been his. The Belmont line went on, and a century later, in 1691, Simon Belmont carried the Vampire Killer into Dracula's castle.

Among the Kindred

Possession of this kind is rare among the Kindred. The nearest thing they know is the deepest reach of the Discipline of Dominate, by which a very old vampire may leave his own body lying as if dead and set his mind in a mortal's. Only the eldest command it. Dracula, who in 1591 had no body to leave, went further: he chose a body with Belmont blood in it, so that the family's own strength was turned against it.

Soleiyu and Richter Belmont, whom the priest Shaft bent to Dracula's service in 1797, are the only Belmonts known to have been turned against their family's cause. Both were freed by someone who refused to kill them: Soleiyu by his father, Richter by Alucard.

pages.title: Spock
infobox: Sarek of Vulcan; Amanda Grayson of Earth
Starfleet: science officer, then first officer, of the USS Enterprise under Captains Pike and Kirk
2285, saving the Enterprise; restored to life the same year
pages.html:
Spock, the son of the Vulcan ambassador Sarek and his human wife, Amanda Grayson, was the most famous Vulcan of the twenty-third century. He served for decades aboard the USS Enterprise, most of them beside Captain James T. Kirk. In 2285 he died and was brought back to life. In 2287 his half-brother, Sybok, gave his life to save him.

Half Vulcan, half human

Spock was born in 2230 in ShiKahr, on Vulcan. Vulcan children teased him for his human blood. At seven he was bonded, in the Vulcan way, to a girl named T'Pring, whom he was to marry when he came of age. His elder half-brother, Sybok, was banished from Vulcan for rejecting logic.

His father hoped he would go to the Vulcan Science Academy. Spock joined Starfleet instead, and for eighteen years Sarek would not speak to him as a son.

The Enterprise

Spock served for eleven years aboard the USS Enterprise under Captain Christopher Pike, then under Captain James T. Kirk, who became the closest friend he ever had. In 2266 he helped Kirk destroy the Romulan ship that had crossed the Neutral Zone, and he watched the crew discover that the Romulans looked just like him.

In 2267 the pon farr came on him, and he went home to marry T'Pring. She chose instead to have him fight for her, and she chose Kirk as her champion. Spock believed that he had killed his captain until he found Kirk alive in sickbay, and for once in his life he grinned openly. The same year he gave his father blood for the operation that saved Sarek's life, and the two of them were reconciled.

Gol and Genesis

About 2273 Spock went to the masters at Gol to complete the kolinahr, which would have purged him of every emotion. At the very end he felt the call of the vast machine called V'Ger, and he left Gol unfinished to rejoin the Enterprise.

In 2285 he died of radiation, restoring the ship's engines so that it could escape the blast of the Genesis Device. Before he went into the engine room he placed his katra, as Vulcans call a person's living spirit, in the mind of Dr Leonard McCoy. His body was reborn on the new Genesis planet. Kirk and his officers stole the Enterprise to fetch it. On Mount Seleya the priestess T'Lar joined his katra to it again in the ancient rite of fal-tor-pan. He spent the next year on Vulcan learning to be himself again.

In 2287 Sybok came back into his life, seizing the envoys on Nimbus III to win himself a starship. He was looking for Sha Ka Ree, the paradise of Vulcan legend. At the centre of the galaxy he found only a cruel prisoner that called itself God, which it was not. Sybok gave his life so that his brother could escape.

pages.title: Stargazers
infobox: Tibet, the Himalayas, India and China
Peoples of the Himalayas and Asia
Meditation, philosophy and the fighting art of Kailindo
pages.html:
The Stargazers are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the smallest. They are the mystics of the Himalayas and the East, philosophers who seek to master their rage through meditation. They would rather understand the war against the Wyrm than merely fight it.

Totem and ways

The Stargazers follow Chimera, a spirit of riddles, dreams and many shapes, who teaches that truth is seldom what it first appears. They study the stars, the spirit world, the nature of the Triat and the meaning of the Garou's own existence. They seek balance where other tribes seek victory. Through long meditation they learn to hold their rage better than any other Garou.

They are formidable fighters too. Their martial art, Kailindo, makes use of a Garou's power to change shape in the middle of a fight. A Stargazer flows from one form to another, so that an opponent never knows what he is facing.

Homelands

The tribe keeps its caerns in high places, many of them mountain monasteries, across Tibet, the Himalayas, India and China.
