The Stargazers suffered badly after China occupied Tibet in 1950, when many of their sacred sites were destroyed. In Asia they have long dealt with the shapeshifters of the East, who are not part of the Garou Nation. Some of their wisdom comes from those dealings.

Place in the world

Other Garou respect the Stargazers' wisdom and find them hard to understand. Their detachment, their questions and their dealings with outsiders make the warrior tribes uneasy. Their small numbers give them little weight in the councils of the Garou Nation. All the same, a sept in trouble will often send for a Stargazer Theurge.

pages.title: Surak of Vulcan
infobox: The fourth century, by Earth's reckoning
Teaching the Vulcans to live by logic; the Time of Awakening
Of radiation sickness after an atomic attack, shortly before the last battle of Vulcan's war
The Kir'Shara, lost for centuries and found at T'Karath in 2154
Kept by Syrran; passed to Jonathan Archer, then to a Vulcan high priest, in 2154
pages.html:
Surak of Vulcan was the philosopher who taught the Vulcans to master their passions by logic, in the fourth century, when their wars had all but destroyed their world. Vulcans count him the greatest of their people, and the years of his teaching are called the Time of Awakening. Those who rejected him left Vulcan and became the Romulans. His first teachings, sealed in the Kir'Shara, were lost for centuries until Captain Jonathan Archer of Earth found them in 2154.

The wars of Vulcan

Surak was born into the most terrible age of Vulcan's history. For thousands of years the Vulcans had been ruled by their passions, and by his time their wars were being fought with atomic weapons. It seemed quite possible that they would destroy their world, and themselves with it.

The Time of Awakening

Surak taught that the Vulcans must master their emotions by logic, or perish. He did not ask his people to stop feeling, only to rule what they felt. His followers went out among the warring nations as emissaries of peace, which in that age was the most dangerous work there was.

Not everybody listened. A faction that sought a return to the old savage ways marched beneath the raptor's wings and made war on Surak's followers. Shortly before the last battle, an atomic attack fell on them. Surak died of radiation sickness afterwards. His teachings won all the same, and Vulcan has lived by them ever since. The faction that had fought him left Vulcan after his death, and its descendants are the Romulans.

The Kir'Shara and the katra

Surak's teachings in their first form were kept in the Kir'Shara, a relic that showed his own testament. It was lost in the desert called the Forge for some eighteen centuries. In that time many Vulcans came to follow a version of his teachings that he would hardly have known.

His katra, which Vulcans believe to be a person's living spirit, was kept too. In the twenty-second century a Vulcan named Syrran found it and took it into his own mind. Around him gathered the Syrrannites, who held to Surak's teachings as he had first given them. The Vulcan High Command treated them as outlaws.

In 2154, dying in a sandstorm in the Forge, Syrran passed Surak's katra into the mind of Captain Jonathan Archer of Earth, who had gone into the Forge in search of the Syrrannites after the bombing of Earth's embassy. Archer saw the atomic fire of eighteen centuries before as if he had been there. Guided by Surak, he found the Kir'Shara at the sanctuary of T'Karath. When T'Pau tried to take the katra into herself, it would not go: Surak, it seemed, preferred to stay with the human.

Archer and T'Pau carried the Kir'Shara to the Vulcan capital to show it to the High Command, which was dissolved. Vulcan turned back to the teachings of Surak as he had written them. His katra was passed to a Vulcan high priest.

A likeness of Surak

In 2269 the Excalbians, a people of a molten world who wished to study good and evil, made a living likeness of Surak out of Spock's memories of him. They set it among likenesses of other great figures of history, to fight for them. It did as Surak would have done. It went to the other side to talk of peace, and it was killed there.

pages.title: Svarog
infobox: Svarog, the Slavic god of fire
pages.html:
Svarog is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped by the Slavs as the god of fire. In 2002 he tried to take the planet Latona, whose people had been kept safe for three hundred years by a device called the Sentinel. The Sentinel had been broken by thieves from Earth. SG-1 brought the thieves back to mend it, and Svarog's Jaffa vanished from Latona in a blaze of white light.

The god of fire

Svarog came quietly to the Slavs of the eastern plains, in defiance of Ra's ban. He took care never to come near the North. Every Goa'uld is born remembering what Thor does to those who do.

The Slavs remembered him as the god of fire and of the forge, the father of the sun god Dazhbog.

Latona

Latona is a world whose people gave up most of their machines long ago, for the life of the mind. For three hundred years they have been kept safe by the Sentinel, a device their ancestors built, which sends any invader away in a blaze of white light. A hermit known as the Caretaker watches over it.

In time the Sentinel attracted thieves. A rogue team from the NID, an American intelligence agency, found the device near the city, took it apart to learn how it worked and put it back together. Their leader, Colonel Grieves, shot the Caretaker. The Sentinel needed him to work, and when he died it stopped. Nobody on Latona knew he was dead.

In 2002 Svarog's Jaffa came through the Stargate to announce that Lord Svarog had claimed Latona as part of his domain. His mothership began firing on the city from orbit. 'I am Svarog,' he told the Latonans. 'From this day forth you will serve me!'

Marul, the leader of the Latonans, would not believe that the Sentinel could fail. 'Your Lord Svarog should not come,' he told the Jaffa. 'The Sentinel will send him away.'

SG-1 brought Grieves and his lieutenant, Kershaw, back from prison to mend what they had broken. Kershaw was shot dead by a Jaffa. The Sentinel, it turned out, needed a human being joined to it, as the Caretaker had been, and in the end Grieves gave it himself. The white light spread from the device through the city, and Svarog's Jaffa were gone.

Nothing more was heard of Svarog after Latona. Whether the light took him too, or he simply gave the world up, is not known.

pages.title: System Lords
infobox: Ra, the Supreme System Lord, until 1994
Apophis, Heru'ur, Cronus, Nirrti, Yu, Sokar, Ba'al
pages.html:
The System Lords are the most powerful of the Goa'uld, each of them ruling many worlds as a god. Together they make up a loose and treacherous council. Ra was the foremost of them until his death above Abydos in 1994. They are held back from certain worlds by the Protected Planets Treaty with Asgard.

Rule

Each System Lord rules a domain of planets through the Stargates. He has armies of Jaffa, fleets of ships and human slaves who worship him under the name of an old god of Earth. Many take the names of the gods of Egypt, whom they once claimed to be. Others take those of the gods of China, India, Canaan and Greece. Lesser Goa'uld serve them as underlords, or rise by murdering them.

The System Lords meet in council to settle disputes and divide territory, but they trust nobody. They make war on one another constantly. What unites them is the conviction that they are gods, and that every other people exists to serve them.

Members

Ra was the Supreme System Lord, the greatest of them, until the expedition from Earth destroyed him above Abydos in 1994. Apophis, the serpent, whose Jaffa wear the helmets of snakes, once had Bra'tac as his First Prime. Heru'ur is the son of Ra and Hathor. Lord Yu is one of the oldest of them all. Cronus, Nirrti, Sokar and Ba'al are among the rest. Cronus once put his own First Prime, Ronac, to death; Ronac's son Teal'c grew up under Bra'tac's teaching to serve Apophis instead.

An alliance that included Ra, Apophis and Cronus brought Sokar down long ago. Cronus banished him from the council. Moloc burnt every Jaffa girl born on his worlds. Nirrti spent her strength breeding a perfect host.

Among the lesser lords were Bastet, Kali the Destroyer, Olokun, Morrigan, Svarog, Amaterasu and Camulus. In 2002 seven System Lords met under truce in the Hasara system, and all but Yu voted to take Anubis back.

Thor

The System Lords have been at war with many peoples, but there is only one Asgardian whom they fear by name. Ra met him first, some five thousand years ago, when Thor fought beside the Egyptians who drove Ra off Earth. Afterwards Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth, and the System Lords have kept the ban ever since.

Ba'al, who thought the ban one of Ra's vanities, raided the coasts of the North about three thousand years ago. Thor followed him home, broke his palace and later sent him one of his underlords' symbiotes in a jar.

About 870 Heru'ur carried off the people of several Norse settlements, and Thor destroyed his army on the world now called Cimmeria. Towards the end of the tenth century Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard. Thor destroyed two of the three fleets, and Apophis saved his own only by running. The Protected Planets Treaty followed.

The treaty

The System Lords keep the Protected Planets Treaty with Asgard, which forbids them to attack or enslave the peoples of certain worlds. They keep it because they believe Asgard can punish them if they do not. Asgard's long war against the Replicators has drawn its strength elsewhere, but the System Lords know nothing of it. Asgard has kept the war secret and its ships on show. So far the bluff has held.

Other powers

The System Lords share the galaxy with powers greater than themselves, and they have learnt, mostly the hard way, which ones to avoid. The Kree burnt a world rather than let a Goa'uld wear a Kree, and the Shi'ar Imperial Guard drove them off the Kree frontier in 1992 in an afternoon. Darkseid took the court of a lesser System Lord apart in search of the Anti-Life Equation. In 1988 they refused to join the Dominators' Alliance against Earth, which turned out to be wise.

After Ra

Ra's death above Abydos in 1994 left the System Lords without a Supreme System Lord for the first time in thousands of years. His domains lay open, and Apophis moved faster than any of the others to take them.

Apophis had also learnt that the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, had killed Ra. Earth was a nuisance again, and Ra was no longer there to forbid its name. Apophis did not know where Thor was. He had heard only, as all the System Lords had heard, that the Thunderer seemed to be busy elsewhere.

In 1997 he came through the Stargate to Earth himself, the first System Lord to do so openly in more than a thousand years. His Jaffa killed the soldiers guarding the gate and carried one of them off. On Abydos he took Sha'uri as a host for his queen, Amaunet, and Skaara as one for his son, Klorel. Ra's ban was broken. From then on the Goa'uld took a much closer interest in Earth, and Earth, through SG-1, took a close interest in them.

The last of the Goa'uld

The System Lords fell in 2005, in Ba'al's wars and the rising of the free Jaffa. No council of them ever met again. The lesser Goa'uld who outlived them could not breed without Jaffa to carry their young, and the last of them died about 2045.

In the saga

The System Lords have not been named in the saga.

pages.title: Taiga Saejima
infobox: Rin, a Makai Priestess of Kantai
pages.html:
Taiga Saejima was Garo, the Golden Knight, a Makai Knight whose name the Horrors themselves knew. He was the father of Kouga Saejima. In about 1990 he was killed by Barago, a pupil he had refused to make his heir, while shielding his young son. In the summer of 1994 he has been dead for about four years, with his sword still standing in the ground where it fell.

The Golden Knight

Taiga held the title of Garo as the Saejimas have for generations. As a young knight he was sent by his Watchdog to recover a compass in which the souls of the four Sacred Beasts were kept. It had been stolen by Jadou, a Makai Guide who had become a Horror's host. He worked with Fuki, the keeper of the beasts' shrine, whose parents Jadou had killed.

Among the people he saved over the years was a boy called Yuji Mitsuki, who grew up to put the Golden Knight in a picture book. Yuji's daughter, Kaoru, would one day marry Taiga's son.

His closest friend was the priest Amon, who had made his Madou Ring, Zaruba. The two of them played Barchess, a board game of the Makai, for twenty years. One game between them, begun on a night when the Inga lapsed, had ten years of each man's life staked on it. Taiga died with it unfinished. His son took his place at the board, but Amon was murdered in 2006 before that game could end either.

Rin

He married Rin, a Makai Priestess of Kantai, a pupil of the priestess Garai, who could match him in a fight. Their son, Kouga, was born about 1980. Rin fell ill while the boy was still very small. She did not recover. Taiga brought Kouga up with the help of his butler, Gonza Kurahashi, training him from the first to be Garo after him.

Barago

Taiga took a pupil from outside the family, a gifted young knight named Barago. As a child Barago had watched his own father kill his mother, when a Horror took her. He hoped to be the next Garo. Taiga saw that what the young man wanted was strength, more of it than anybody else had, with nobody in particular to protect. He told him that he was not fit for the title.

Barago turned to a book of dark arts, through which Messiah gave him the black armour of Kiba. When Taiga learnt what his pupil had become, he fought him. He all but killed him. He cut a cross into Barago's face, a death mark that should have finished him within days. The Horrors that Barago had already devoured kept him alive.

In about 1990 they met again. Kouga, who was a boy, ran out into the fight. Taiga threw himself in front of his son to take the blow. He had time to give Zaruba a few words for the boy. The Garoken stayed upright in the earth where he dropped it.

Afterwards

Taiga did not altogether leave. When Kouga reached the end of his journey in the Promised Ground in 2013, his father's spirit was there to see it.

In 2045 a youth called Baderu guided Taiga's grandson, Raiga, through a black train bound for the Makai. Baderu was Taiga, in the shape of his own boyhood. When Kiba rose again he took back his proper form to fight his murderer, with Kouga on one side of him. Raiga stood on the other. Three Golden Knights of one family destroyed Kiba between them.

pages.title: Tali'Zorah nar Rayya
infobox: Aboard the Rayya, a ship of the Migrant Fleet
Adviser to the chief engineer of the USS Enterprise-B
The peace between the Quarians and the Geth at Rannoch, 2299
pages.html:
Tali'Zorah nar Rayya was a young Quarian engineer who joined the USS Enterprise-B on her Pilgrimage, as an adviser to the chief engineer, Greg Adams. In 2299 she helped Captain John Shepard to break the Galactic Empire's hold on the Geth at Rannoch. The peace that followed took her people home.

The Pilgrimage

Tali'Zorah was born aboard the Rayya, one of the fifty thousand ships of the Migrant Fleet. Her father, Rael'Zorah, sat on the Admiralty Board. Like every Quarian she had lived her whole life in a sealed suit, on ships kept running by constant repair. She could mend almost anything by the time she came of age.

Every young Quarian leaves the fleet on a Pilgrimage, to come back with something of worth. Tali's took her to the Enterprise-B. Shepard gave her a place in engineering, where she advised Chief Adams. Adams, who had expected a passenger, soon said that she knew his engines better than his own staff did.

Rannoch

On 5 October 2299, in the Intergalactic War, the Galactic Empire tried to seize the Geth by rewriting their shared mind from a command ship above Rannoch. The Migrant Fleet came in to destroy the Geth while they were helpless. Tali boarded the command ship with Shepard, where she broke the Empire's hold. Then she spoke for peace to her own people's admirals.

The Quarians and the Geth made peace that day. Tali was among the first Quarians to stand on Rannoch in four hundred years. Her Pilgrimage was long over by then. She had chosen to stay with the ship, under the name Tali'Zorah vas Enterprise.

In the saga

Tali'Zorah has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Tao Chong
infobox: Karate master; owner of Tao's Dojo
pages.html:
Tao Chong is the karate master of Crossworld City, California, the owner of Tao's Dojo. He is an old friend of the vanished scientist Tyler Steele, whose son, Ryan, he has taught since boyhood. The three young people who became the VR Troopers in September 1994 all train under his roof. In September 1995 it was Tao who nursed Tyler Steele back to health.

Tao's Dojo

Tao's Dojo is a karate school in Crossworld City. Most of its pupils are children. Tao runs it in the old-fashioned way, with a saying for every difficulty, which his pupils find more useful than they expect to. He cooks with herbs, in which he has a firm belief.

By 1994 two of his best pupils, Ryan Steele and J.B. Reese, are instructors there. Their friend Kaitlin Star, a newspaper reporter, trains with them. Tao was close to Ryan's father, a friend of the family from before Tyler Steele disappeared.

The dojo in the Troopers' war

The dojo saw a good deal of Grimlord's war without knowing what it was looking at. In October 1994, at a party for the school's anniversary, a magician in Grimlord's service made off with the three Virtualizers. The Troopers had to win them back. Later that month the dojo itself was threatened with closure, until its friends raised the money to save it.

In February 1995 a copy of Ryan, grown by Karl Ziktor, walked in as though it were the real one. In September that year Tao's mother needed help, which meant money. His three young friends thought of lending their names to a rival school for a fee. In the end Tao made an arrangement of his own with his competitor, which brought in what he needed.

Tao's own teaching found its way into the fighting. When Grimlord began sending creatures nobody could see, in October 1994, it was a lesson of Tao's on stealth that the Troopers fell back on.

Tyler Steele's recovery

On 20 September 1995 Ryan brought his father out of Grimlord's hands, after more than ten years. Tyler Steele was very ill. Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese thought of Tao's remedies, so they brought the sick man to him. He treated his old friend in his own way until Tyler Steele was on his feet again. How much the two of them had to tell Tao is not clear. He has never said how much he has guessed about his three young friends.

He did one thing more. Ryan had lost his armour in the rescue. The new suit that Tyler Steele built for him needed a crystal to power it, which Tao supplied.

At Christmas 1995 the dojo held a party, with Tyler Steele among the guests. In February 1996 Tao was away for a time, leaving Ryan to mind the school. Nothing is recorded of him after that month.

pages.title: The Technet
infobox: Gatecrasher, Yap, Bodybag, China Doll, Elmo, Ferro and his twin, Joyboy, Numbers, Ringtoss, Scatterbrain, Thug, Waxworks
Anyone caught, anyone rescued, anything fetched, for a price
A condemned pier at Brighton (1988 to 1991); the Braddock Lighthouse (1991 to 1992)
Away from Earth, working for the Special Executive
pages.html:
The Technet are bounty hunters from a great many worlds who will catch anybody, rescue anybody or fetch anything, for a price. Their leader is Gatecrasher, a big, blue-skinned telepath. They have crossed Captain Britain's path since 1985, sometimes for him and more often against him. In 1987 their hunt for Rachel Summers brought the Excalibur team together. Stranded on Earth in 1991, they lived for a while in the team's lighthouse.

Members

Gatecrasher is a strong telepath who knows how to splice living things. Yap, who calls her mother to her great annoyance, teleports the team wherever it needs to go. Among the rest are Bodybag, a huge reptile who keeps swallowed prisoners alive in sacs on his back; China Doll, who shrinks people to the size of ornaments; Joyboy, a floating baby who grants twisted wishes; Thug, who calls on other selves of his from other times; and Numbers, the team's accountant, who would rather not fight at all.

Captain Britain

The Technet's first known job was for Opul Lun Sat-yr-9, the tyrant of another Britain, who hired them in 1985 to catch Kaptain Briton, an evil double of Captain Britain. They caught the wrong man. Captain Britain talked them round, and they fought Sat-yr-9's troops beside him.

Then they fell on hard times. Elmo was killed on a job, and pirates stripped them of everything they had, so that most of them walked out. Captain Britain and Meggan saved Gatecrasher's life in fourteenth-century Peru. Afterwards she gathered her people again.

The Special Executive, a band of agents Captain Britain met even earlier, turned out to be the Technet itself, years in the future, which made the two meetings more complicated than they sound.

Rachel Summers, 1987

In 1987 Saturnyne hired the Technet to bring in Rachel Summers, whom she called a danger to every world. In fact Roma of Otherworld had asked it of her, so that Rachel and her rescuers would come together. The Technet took Kitty Pryde and Meggan on Muir Island. They caught Rachel in London, where Mojo's Warwolves came for her too. In the fighting the Warwolves killed Ferro, and Kurt Wagner turned them on the Technet. Gatecrasher went home beaten, and the Excalibur team was founded on the strength of it.

Brighton

Afterwards the Technet stayed in England, on a condemned pier at Brighton, where they gave the town fine weather in return for a roof. In 1989 Nigel Frobisher, acting for Sat-yr-9, hired them to free Jamie Braddock from the warlord Doctor Crocodile in Mbangawi. They brought him to Brighton, where his own power woke and he beat them all. Their memories of the job were wiped.

Exile and the lighthouse, 1991 to 1992

In 1991 Gatecrasher made a living bomb shaped like a chicken, Hard-Boiled Henry, and set it on the Excalibur team at the lighthouse. Saturnyne's agents stopped the fight. Saturnyne had cancelled the warrant on Rachel, and she exiled the Technet to Earth without their pay. They turned on Gatecrasher, who fled with Yap.

The rest asked the team for shelter. Kurt Wagner gave it them, over Brian Braddock's objections, and they mended the lighthouse in return. Kurt trained them for a while as a team of their own. Numbers fell in love with the dragon who lived in the cellar.

Early in 1992 the Special Executive came to Earth and offered them work, which they took. They left with Numbers, his dragon and their young. In the summer of 1994 they are still away. They came back in 1998 for Brian and Meggan's wedding.

pages.title: Tem Ray
infobox: Engineer; designer of the RX-78-2 Gundam
pages.html:
Tem Ray was the Federation engineer who built the RX-78-2 Gundam at Starbase Side 7. He was the father of its pilot, Amuro Ray.

The Gundam

Tem Ray led the Federation's work on mobile suits, first the Guntank, then the Gundam. He built them from technology that had been taken in secret from the Galactic Empire, whose origin he was never told. He was putting the last touches to the RX-78-2 on 17 May 2293, the day the USS Enterprise-A came to collect it. The Empire attacked that same day. His son took the suit into battle in his place.

In the saga

Tem Ray has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Terona Washington
infobox: Yellow, on the night of 20 July 1969
A soldier in the war in Vietnam
In the summer of 1994, Grace Sterling's partner at Promethea
pages.html:
Terona Washington is a soldier who came home from Vietnam in 1969 in time to be made Zordon's Yellow Ranger. He was one of only two of that team to come back alive from the Moon. With Grace Sterling, the other, he founded Promethea, where in the summer of 1994 he still works beside her. When she was killed in February 1995 he became the last of the Rangers of 1969, and Promethea passed to him. From its designs came Terra Venture.

The Yellow Ranger

Terona Washington fought as a soldier in the war in Vietnam. He was home again by July 1969. On the night of the Moon landing Alpha 5 fetched him to the Command Center with four other strangers, among them Grace Sterling. Zordon made him the Yellow Ranger.

He was the only soldier among them. On the Moon he told Daniel O'Halloran, the Pink Ranger, to wait. Daniel charged in all the same, and Psycho Green killed him. Jamie Gilmore was crushed under a boulder. Nikolai Chukarin died destroying the creature from inside it.

Terona came home with Grace. He told Zordon to his face that it had been irresponsible to send untrained strangers to fight. When Zordon took the powers back, Terona left him in anger, as Grace did.

Promethea

Grace resigned from NASA. With Terona she founded Promethea, to keep the promise that Nikolai Chukarin had asked of them on the Moon. It grew into one of the great firms of Silicon Valley. Grace is its face to the world. Terona has been at her side for twenty-five years.

In September 1994 he was aboard Promethea's headquarters, which was also a ship, when Grace took it to war against Lord Drakkon. When Drakkon unmade the world, the ship was thrown into a dark place where there was no Morphin Grid at all. It was more than forty days before the crew found their way home.

February 1995

Early in February 1995 Terona spent some days as a prisoner of Lord Zedd. Zedd gave him back to the Rangers as a token of truce, when he came to fight beside them against Mistress Vile. A few days later Grace was killed at the Arch in the Bermuda Triangle.

When the Rangers cleansed the Grid the world was mended, for the second time in six months. It kept no memory of the weeks since Lord Zedd's dome over Angel Grove. Terona was one of the few who did, though he had not stood in the Grid himself. The mended world believed that Grace had been lost with a Promethea research ship in the Bermuda Triangle. He knew better.

Terra Venture

Promethea passed to Terona Washington, Grace's co-founder and the last of the 1969 Rangers. He closed its secret work. He kept its ships, then gave the rest of his life to the promise that Nikolai Chukarin had asked of them on the Moon.

Promethea's headquarters had always been a ship. From its designs came the colony ship built with the Global Space Alliance, which left Earth in 1999 as Terra Venture, the space colony that the Galaxy Rangers defended.

pages.title: Terra Venture
infobox: Power Rangers Lost Galaxy, 'Quasar Quest, Part 1' (6 February 1999)
Promethea's headquarters, which was also a ship
Promethea, with the Global Space Alliance
pages.html:
Terra Venture was the space colony that left Earth in 1999 to look for a new world like it. It was a whole city under a great dome, built to cross space, and the Galaxy Rangers defended it on the way. It came from the designs of Promethea, whose own headquarters had always been a ship.

Origin

Promethea was founded after 1969 by Grace Sterling and Terona Washington, two of Zordon's first Rangers, to keep a promise made to a dying friend on the Moon. When Grace was killed in February 1995, the company passed to Terona. He closed its secret work but kept its ships.

Promethea's headquarters had always been a ship. From its designs came the colony ship built with the Global Space Alliance, which left Earth in 1999 as Terra Venture.

The voyage

Terra Venture set out in 1999 under Commander Stanton, carrying its colonists in search of a new world like Earth. Its road lay through the Lost Galaxy.

The Galaxy Rangers took their powers from the Quasar Sabers, which they drew from a stone on the planet Mirinoi. Leo Corbett was the Red Ranger, Kai Chen the Blue, Damon Henderson the Green. Maya, who was born on Mirinoi, was the Yellow. Kendrix Morgan was the Pink, until she gave her life for a friend; Karone, who had once been Astronema, took up the Pink after her. They fought Scorpius, the colony's first great enemy, then his daughter, Trakeena, with his servant Deviot.

The end of the voyage

In December 1999 Trakeena, who had joined herself with Deviot, crippled Terra Venture. The colonists got out. The Galaxy Megazord steered the falling city dome away from their camp, while Leo fought Trakeena to the end.

The world they had come down on was Mirinoi. The Rangers put the Quasar Sabers back in their stone, which turned the people of Mirinoi back from stone and brought Kendrix back to life. The colonists of Terra Venture settled there, on the new world they had set out to find.

pages.title: The Anarchs
infobox: The Anarch Free States of California (from 1944)
pages.html:
The Anarchs are the vampires who reject the rule of their elders. Their great rising, the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century, ended at the Convention of Thorns in 1493. Their heirs are a movement that lives partly inside the Camarilla and partly beyond it.

The Anarch Revolt

By the late Middle Ages the elders ruled their childer through the blood bond. When the Inquisition came, they saved themselves by giving their young to the fires. The young rose against them. The anarchs learnt to break the blood bond, hired Assamite assassins and struck at the elders in their havens. The Brujah Tyler was among the leaders of the revolt.

In the early fifteenth century Lasombra anarchs led by Gratiano, with Assamite allies, stormed the Castle of Shadows on Sicily. There, they claimed, they destroyed the Lasombra Antediluvian himself. About 1413 Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed the same of the founder of the Tzimisce. The elders answered by founding the Camarilla in 1435, and by proclaiming the Masquerade.

The Convention of Thorns

In 1493, at Thornbury in England, the Camarilla, the anarchs and the Assamites made peace. The anarchs who accepted it were pardoned and taken into the Camarilla. The Assamites accepted a blood curse from the Tremere that barred them from drinking the blood of other Kindred. Those who would not accept the terms, most of them Lasombra and Tzimisce, became the Sabbat.

The modern movement

Anarchs ever since have been the Camarilla's malcontents. Most are young vampires, and many of them are Brujah or Caitiff. The Brujah, the clan of rebels, have always given the movement more of its members than any other clan. Anarchs answer to barons of their own choosing, rejecting the authority of princes and elders alike. Most of them keep the Masquerade all the same, since the fires would burn an anarch as quickly as a prince.

In 1944 the anarchs of Los Angeles, led by the Brujah, threw down the Toreador Prince Don Sebastian. The other princes of California fell with him, and the anarchs declared the Anarch Free States, which still stand. The Camarilla has never taken them back.

pages.title: The Andorians
infobox: Andoria, an icy moon of a ringed gas giant
Blue skin, white hair, blue blood and two antennae
The Aenar, a white-skinned, blind and telepathic people of Andoria's far north
With the Vulcans, over Weytahn and P'Jem
Thy'lek Shran; Talas; Jhamel, an Aenar
pages.html:
The Andorians are a blue-skinned people with antennae, from Andoria, an icy moon whose cities lie underground for the warmth of the rock. They are proud, quick to anger and loyal to the death to those who have earned it. For a century they quarrelled with the Vulcans, their neighbours, over the world of Weytahn and the Vulcan monastery at P'Jem, until a captain from Earth helped them settle it. In 2161 they were among the founders of the United Federation of Planets.

Andoria

Andoria is a moon of ice, circling a ringed gas giant. Even its summers are bitterly cold, so most Andorians live in cities hollowed out of the rock below the surface, where the moon's own heat keeps them warm.

Andorians have blue skin, white hair and blue blood. Their two antennae move as they please. They use them for hearing, for balance and for showing what they feel, which is a great deal. They are a warrior people with long memories. An Andorian who owes you a debt will pay it, sooner or later, whatever it costs him.

Far in the north of Andoria live the Aenar, a white-skinned branch of the same people. They are blind, telepathic and gentle. They will have nothing to do with war. They keep to themselves in the ice, and outsiders had scarcely heard of them before 2154.

The quarrel with Vulcan

About 2050 Andorian settlers came to Weytahn, a world on the frontier between Andorian and Vulcan space. They began to make it fit to live on. In 2097 the Vulcans claimed it, calling it Paan Mokar. When the Andorians refused to let the Vulcan High Command inspect their colony, the Vulcans annexed it outright.

The talks that followed took eight years. In 2105 they produced the Territorial Compromise, which the Vulcans thought generous. 'Only a Vulcan could call a hundred years of oppression a compromise,' as one Andorian put it. The two peoples came close to war over Weytahn twice in that century, and there were border incursions in 2112.

The Andorians were also sure that the Vulcans were spying on them from the old monastery at P'Jem, a retreat for meditation some three thousand years old. They were right. In 2151 Commander Shran of the Andorian Imperial Guard took the monastery, with a landing party from the Enterprise NX-01 inside it. Captain Jonathan Archer found the long-range sensor array hidden beneath it and let the Andorians go with the proof. Soon afterwards they destroyed the monastery.

Shran and the humans

Shran told Archer that he was in his debt, and he meant it. In 2152 he reoccupied the Andorian settlement on Weytahn. He would trust no mediator but Archer, who brought the two sides to a ceasefire and talks on Andoria. In 2153 Shran followed the Enterprise into the Delphic Expanse to help Archer against the Xindi.

In 2154 Administrator V'Las sent the Vulcan fleet against Andoria. Ambassador Soval came to warn the Andorians, and Shran, who did not believe a Vulcan could mean it, tortured him until he was sure. Then Andorian ships stood with the Enterprise against the Vulcan fleet, until the High Command fell and the Vulcans turned for home.

Later that year the Andorians and the Tellarites, who had a long-standing trade dispute, were to meet for talks at Babel. On the way a Romulan drone ship, disguised as a Tellarite vessel, destroyed Shran's ship, the Kumari. Shran's lieutenant, Talas, was killed by a Tellarite, and Shran demanded an ushaan, a duel to the death. Archer fought it in the Tellarite's place, won, cut off one of Shran's antennae and spared him. Shran brought Andoria into the hunt for the drone all the same.

The drone was flown by an Aenar, Gareb, whom the Romulans had stolen and deceived. His sister, Jhamel, reached his mind from the Enterprise, and he turned the drones on each other before Admiral Valdore killed him. Jhamel later married Shran, and in 2156 they had a daughter, Talla.

In the United Federation of Planets

In 2155 the Andorians joined the Coalition of Planets. In 2161 they signed the charter of the United Federation of Planets with United Earth, the Vulcans and the Tellarites. Shran had left the Imperial Guard by then. Earlier that year Archer, on his way to the signing, rescued Talla from criminals who had taken her to settle a score with her father.

In 2267 the Andorians sent a delegation to the Babel conference, called to decide whether Coridan should join the Federation. An Orion spy hid among them, disguised as an Andorian, and murdered the Tellarite ambassador. In the years that followed Andorians served throughout Starfleet.

pages.title: The Antediluvians
pages.html:
The Antediluvians are the thirteen vampires of the Third Generation: the grandchilder of Cain and the founders of the vampire clans. Every clan takes its gift and its curse from its founder's blood. Few vampires have ever seen one, and many doubt that any still exist.

The name

The name means 'before the Flood'. Kindred tradition holds that the thirteen were sired before it, and the tradition is wrong. Cain sired no vampire until the waters had gone down. Only then did Lilith teach him the blood magic that turned him into the first vampire, and with it he spread his curse. The Antediluvians came after the Flood, whatever they are called.

The First City and the Second

The thirteen were Embraced in Enoch, the First City, about 9300 BC. Their sires were Cain's three childer of the Second Generation: Enoch, for whom the city was named, Irad and Zillah. In time the First City fell. About 8990 BC the Third Generation rose against their sires and slew them.

Cain cursed them for it about 8980 BC, laying on each new clan a curse of its own, and departed into Nod. The thirteen built the Second City and ruled it together, until it too fell to their wars.

The thirteen

By the old count the founders are the Ventrue Antediluvian, Brujah, Ennoia of the Gangrel, Malkav, Absimiliard of the Nosferatu, Arikel of the Toreador, Lasombra, the Eldest of the Tzimisce, Haqim of the Assamites, Set, Ravnos, Saulot of the Salubri and Cappadocius.

The count has changed since. The wizard Tremere took Saulot's blood and soul in 1133. Augustus Giovanni took Cappadocius's in 1444. So the Tremere now stand among the thirteen clans in place of the Salubri, and the Giovanni in place of the Cappadocians.

Several founders are said to have been destroyed by their own childer. Troile destroyed Brujah. In the Anarch Revolt, by their destroyers' own account, Gratiano destroyed Lasombra and Lugoj destroyed the Eldest. Not every Kindred believes those accounts.

The Jyhad and Gehenna

The Kindred believe that the surviving Antediluvians sleep in hidden places. From there, they say, the ancients move younger vampires like pieces in a game that has been running since the first nights, which the Kindred call the Jyhad. The prophecies of the Book of Nod foretell Gehenna, when the founders will wake hungry and devour their descendants, with a Time of Thin Blood to come before it. The Camarilla officially calls all this legend. The Sabbat means to fight the founders when they come.

In the saga

Remus Lupin told Harry Potter's class in October 1993 that every clan descends from somebody very old indeed. The older the blood, he said, the stronger it is, and the less of a person is left in it.

The Master, founder of the Aurelian line, claims to have been sired by the Ventrue Antediluvian, and will never reveal the name. Dracula is of the fourth generation, but not by descent. The Crimson Stone set Mathias Cronqvist at that generation when he took Walter Bernhard's blood and soul in 1094. Walter was no Antediluvian.

pages.title: The Asari
infobox: Blue-skinned, with a crest of curved, folded skin where humans have hair; all of one sex, and female to human eyes
The siari; of old, the goddess Athame
pages.html:
The Asari are a blue-skinned people of the world Thessia, who live for more than a thousand years and are all of one sex. They have children by melding their nervous systems with a partner of any people, and the child is always Asari. Patient, curious and persuasive, they are the natural diplomats of their part of the galaxy. The Enterprise NX-01 met them in 2156, and about 2162 they became the first people to join the United Federation of Planets after its four founders.

Thessia and its people

The Asari come from Thessia. To human eyes every Asari is a woman. They have blue skin, and where a human has hair they have a crest of curved, folded skin.

An Asari has a child by joining her nervous system to a partner's, which the Asari call melding. The partner's mind shapes half of what the child inherits, whatever people the partner belongs to, but the child is always Asari. A very few are born ardat-yakshi, whose meld kills the partner. They are offered a quiet life in a monastery under watch. The Justicars, an ancient order of judges and executioners bound by a strict code, hunt down those who refuse it.

The three ages

An Asari life falls into three ages. A maiden is restless: she wanders, tries everything and goes everywhere, usually for her first 350 years or so. A matron settles down to raise children. A matriarch, in the last centuries of her life, gives counsel, and the Asari listen to her.

Living so long, the Asari plan in centuries. They would rather persuade than fight, and they are very good at it. They are also the richest people of their region, which helps.

The Asari Republics

Thessia has no single government. It is divided among loose confederacies called the Asari Republics, each made up of cities that run their own affairs. Asari have no politicians and hold no elections. Every question is debated openly among all the citizens who care to join in, and a vote of the whole people can be called at any time. The opinions of matriarchs carry the most weight, and in a crisis it is the matriarchs who act.

Faith

Most Asari follow the siari, a faith which holds that all life is at bottom one. Their own melding, which lets an Asari share the mind of almost any thinking creature, seems to them proof of it. Before they went out among the stars they worshipped a goddess, Athame, whose old temple still stands on Thessia. The Asari value variety in everything: they welcome strangers, they dislike any talk of breeding a better people, and they have learnt to live with nearly everybody.

The alliance and the Krogan

About 500 BC the Asari and the Salarians, who had found each other among the stars, made an alliance. The Asari were its peacemakers. About 1 the Salarians found the Rachni, who made war on both peoples for three centuries, until the Krogan whom the Salarians had raised up wiped them out. The alliance rewarded the Krogan with worlds of their own.

The Krogan filled their worlds and spread into others. About 700, when the alliance demanded that they leave the Asari colony of Lusia, the Krogan Rebellions began. The Asari, who would rather persuade than fight, were glad of the Turians, whom they met in the middle of that war. When the Turians loosed the Salarians' genophage on the Krogan about 710, the Asari raised no objection, and they have never much liked to talk about it since.

Among the stars

The Asari reached the stars long before Earth did, in warp ships of their own design, in which their maidens wandered far. They had been allies of the Salarians since about 500 BC, and of the Turians since about 700. None of the three had much to do with Earth's part of the galaxy, which lay a long way off.

In 2156 the Enterprise NX-01 answered a distress call from a damaged Asari survey ship, far out beyond the frontiers of Vulcan. Its commander, a matron of some four hundred years, thanked Captain Archer and asked him a great many questions. The Asari had decided within a few years that they liked what they heard. About 2162 they joined the United Federation of Planets, which by Asari reckoning was very quick indeed.

The fall of Thessia

On 29 December 2299, in the Intergalactic War, Darth Vader led the Galactic Empire's assault on Thessia in person. The Asari fleet and the USS Enterprise-B could not hold it. Thessia stayed in the Empire's hands until the war ended in March 2300.

pages.title: The Astralborgs
infobox: The Lost Comic, made by Art and Les Fortunes as boys
The Mantrons: Scorpix, Centipix, Mantix, Hornix
Roboborg, summoned by the Astral Sword; Boron, summoned by the Astral Axe
pages.html:
The Astralborgs are four armoured heroes out of the Lost Comic, which the brothers Art and Les Fortunes made at home as boys. In November 1997 the Beetleborgs called them into the world one by one with the Astral Coins. The same pages held their enemies, the Mantrons, together with the giant Roboborg. Boron, the giant made to match him, came later.

The Lost Comic

Long before either of them drew for a living, the Fortunes brothers made a comic of their own. Art drew its heroes, the four Astralborgs. Les drew its villains, the four Mantrons. In it was a sword, the Astral Sword, with eight Astral Coins, one for each hero or villain. Sword and coins together could summon a giant named Roboborg.

Les buried the comic. On 7 November 1997, tired of drawing monsters for Nukus, he led the Crustaceans to the place. Art took the Beetleborgs after them. For nearly three weeks the Sword, with its coins, passed from one side to the other.

The four

Each coin called up the figure that belonged to it. Dragonborg, in the likeness of a dragonfly, is the leader of the Astralborgs. He came first, bringing the Astral Laser for Drew McCormick. Fireborg, a firefly, throws fire from his fingertips. He came when Jo McCormick used the Firebug coin, which had been found in the keeping of Mums at Hillhurst Mansion.

Lightningborg, a cicada, strikes with lightning. His coin was Wolfgang Smith's, who gave it up in return for a place in the fight. Ladyborg, a butterfly, fires a beam shaped like a flower. Her coin had to be got out of Count Fangula, who had swallowed it.

The Mantrons

The other four coins belonged to the Mantrons, whom Les had drawn: Scorpix, their leader, with Centipix, Mantix and Hornix. They served Nukus. They poisoned Flabber, which stopped the Beetleborgs' powers until he was cured. On 26 November 1997 Roboborg sent all four back into the Lost Comic.

Roboborg

On 26 November 1997 the Beetleborgs at last held the Sword with all eight coins. Drew McCormick raised it, which summoned Roboborg, a giant in beetle armour. His first act was to destroy Nukus's Worm Tanks. In February 1998 he joined the Beetleborgs' first powers to their Metallix armour. That gave them the Mega Spectra armour, with wings.

Boron

That February Les Fortunes drew a second weapon, the Astral Axe. It summoned Boron, a giant made to match Roboborg, who obeyed whoever held the Axe. On 16 February 1998 the two fought on the Moon.

The fight was seen from farther off than Charterville. On 21 February Ecliptor, the warrior of Astronema, came to the Charterville cemetery to take the Axe. He held it for a few minutes, during which Roboborg had to hold Boron with the help of the Space Rangers' Astro Megazord. Drew McCormick pulled the Axe from his hand with Andros, the Red Space Ranger. It went back to the Crustaceans.

On 2 March 1998 Roland Williams took the Axe from them for good. Boron fought beside Roboborg that day, so that Repgillian, the last of Nukus's monsters, was destroyed.

pages.title: The Batarians
infobox: Strict castes, with slaves at the bottom
The Orion Syndicate, which they joined by the twenty-second century
The Enterprise NX-01, 2154, at an Orion slave market
pages.html:
The Batarians are a four-eyed people from Khar'shan, ruled by the Batarian Hegemony, whose whole society rests on castes with slaves at the bottom. The peoples around them had outlawed slavery, which the Batarians took as an insult to their way of life. So they turned to the Orion Syndicate, the greatest slavers in that part of space, and by the twenty-second century Batarian slavers were among the Syndicate's busiest partners. Earth first met them in 2154, at an Orion slave market.

Khar'shan and the Hegemony

The Batarians come from Khar'shan. They have four eyes, set in two pairs. Their society has always been built on castes, each Batarian born into a place and expected to keep it. Slavery is part of the order at its very bottom. The Batarian Hegemony, which rules them, treats the custom as sacred.

Slavers

The Asari, the Salarians and the Turians had long forbidden slavery on their worlds. The Batarians thought this a deliberate insult to their culture, and they kept their distance from all three. Their pirates and slavers raided where they could. Many Batarians found work as mercenaries or in the underworld of other peoples' worlds.

Their natural partners were the Orions, who ran the busiest slave markets in the region. By the twenty-second century the Batarians had joined the Orion Syndicate. Batarian slavers bought and sold in its markets beside the Orions themselves.

Earth

In 2154 Orion slavers in the Borderland, between Klingon and Orion space, raided the Enterprise NX-01. They carried several of its crew, T'Pol among them, to a slave market. Batarian slavers were bidding there. Captain Jonathan Archer got his people back, and the market's other captives broke loose in the confusion. It was the first time humans had seen a Batarian, and none of them wished to see another.

pages.title: The Beyonder
infobox: A being of almost unlimited power from beyond the universe
Killed by the Molecule Man, 1986; drawn out of Kosmos, 1994
pages.html:
The Beyonder was a being of almost unlimited power from a realm outside the universe. In 1984 he carried off heroes and villains from across the world to Battleworld, to fight the Secret Wars while he watched. In 1985 he came to Earth himself, in human form, to learn what it was to want things. He very nearly destroyed everything in his frustration, and was killed in 1986, though not for good.

The Secret Wars

The Beyonder became aware of the universe through a small opening into it. He was fascinated by the beings he found there, and above all by desire, which he had never known. In 1984, appearing at first only as a blinding light with a voice, he carried a crowd of Earth's heroes and villains across the universe, with a few from further afield. He built Battleworld in front of them out of fragments of other worlds. Then he promised each side whatever it desired if it destroyed its enemies.

Victor von Doom managed for a time to steal his power. The Beyonder took it back, and sent everyone home.

On Earth

In 1985 the Beyonder came to Earth to study humanity at first hand, in the shape of a dark-haired young man. Somebody explained money to him, and he turned a whole office building into gold. He gave the blind lawyer Matt Murdock his sight, and took it back when Murdock asked him to. He tried to make a woman love him, and failed. When Doctor Stephen Strange tried to lead him towards understanding, that failed too.

In his despair he resolved to destroy the whole of creation. The assembled heroes fought him. In 1986, as he tried to be born again as an ordinary human child, the Molecule Man killed him. His energy is said to have flowed back into his own realm and become a new universe.

After his death

Dying did not finish him. In 1988 it was learnt that he had been a living Cosmic Cube, joined to part of the Molecule Man's power, and in that form he grew into a new cosmic being called Kosmos. In the spring of 1994 the Molecule Man drew the Beyonder out of Kosmos again, and the struggle between them threatened every universe at once.

pages.title: The Black Dragon
infobox: A Zord in the shape of a dragon
Dragonzord parts, in the World of the Coinless
Lord Drakkon, who steered it from his own world
The end of October 1993, by Rita Repulsa's Green Chaos Crystal
Early November 1993, from inside, by Tommy Oliver and Billy Cranston
pages.html:
The Black Dragon was a Zord in the shape of a dragon, built out of Dragonzord parts in the World of the Coinless, which Lord Drakkon steered from his own world into this one. It came through at the end of October 1993. It wrecked the Command Center, stripped the Rangers of their powers, then put their Zords in Rita Repulsa's hands. Tommy Oliver and Billy Cranston destroyed it from inside.

The voice

In October 1993, while this world's Tommy was still Rita's Green Ranger, a voice spoke to her on the Moon. Her Ranger would leave her, it said, to join Zordon's team. When she saw that it was right, she would see its owner.

Rita's Green Chaos Crystal had been charged with the Green Ranger's power, then with the anger of the other Rangers at Tommy, who had disobeyed Jason to join a fight. At the end of October it opened a way into the Command Center. The Black Dragon came through.

In this world

Rita took it for a living dragon, with an ally inside. It wrecked the Command Center, took Alpha 5 to pieces, then cut Zordon loose, to drift between the worlds. It carried Billy Cranston off to Goldar's Dark Dimension. Through Billy's coin it reached into the Morphin Grid, shutting off the powers of Jason, Zack, Trini and Kimberly. The Dinozords passed to Rita.

Rita made the ruined Command Center her palace. She turned the Zords, which no army could break into, on the cities of the world. Then she gave the Earth twenty-four hours. Her price for sparing Angel Grove was Tommy Oliver. All of it happened in front of everybody, which is why so many people have been afraid of the Rangers ever since.

Its end

The Black Dragon could not touch Tommy's power, because the Dragon Coin draws on the Grid in its own way. Tommy fought it on the Moon in the Dragonzord, with Jason beside him. In the fight it lost an arm. With that arm Tommy shared his own power among Jason, Zack, Trini and Kimberly, who fought on in green, while he was left with none. They took back the Zords.

In the Dark Dimension Billy talked Goldar into letting him go. He had seen a hatch in the Black Dragon's side, so he knew it for a machine. He and Tommy got inside, then wrecked it. It blew apart, which threw the two of them into Drakkon's world.

Trini found that the wreck was made of nothing but Dragonzord parts. She built its armour into a suit for herself. In it she won back Billy's coin, gave the Rangers back their powers, then drove Rita out of the Command Center. Then she opened a way through to the other world, so that the Rangers could go after their friends.

Afterwards

The name outlived the machine. When Drakkon won back his powers in January 1995, he fought as the Black Dragon Ranger.

pages.title: The Boss
infobox: One of the founders of the Philosophers
The Joy, in the Cobra Unit; Voyevoda, in the East
Big Boss, on the orders of his government
pages.html:
The Boss was the greatest soldier of her generation, the woman who founded the Cobra Unit in the Second World War and trained the man who became Big Boss. Soldiers called her the mother of special forces. In 1964 she appeared to defect to the Soviet Union, and her own pupil was sent to kill her. She had been loyal all along. She died because her country needed a traitor.

The Philosophers' daughter

She was born in 1922. Her father was one of the founders of the Philosophers, the secret pact that the most powerful men in America, Russia and China had made between themselves after the Russian Revolution.

The Cobra Unit

In 1942 she gathered the finest Allied soldiers into a secret unit, the Cobras. Each took a name from the feeling he carried into battle: The Pain, The Fear, The Fury, The Sorrow. The oldest, a sniper of about eighty, was The End. She was The Joy.

The Cobras did the work that no government could own up to, so the public never heard of them, even in a war full of famous heroes. Each carried a small bomb that went off when he died, to leave no body.

The Sorrow was a medium. He could truly hear the restless dead, those who have not passed on. He was also the man she loved.

On 6 June 1944 the Cobras went ashore in Normandy. On the battlefield The Boss gave birth to The Sorrow's son, by an operation that left a scar shaped like a snake. The Philosophers took the boy. They brought him up as their agent Adamska, who became Revolver Ocelot.

Teacher

The Cobras were disbanded in 1947. From then on she was known as The Boss. She served for a time with the Special Air Service beside the Englishman later called Major Zero.

In 1950 she took on a pupil, a boy of fifteen called Jack. She trained him for the better part of ten years. Together they worked out close-quarters combat, which every special forces soldier now learns. In June 1959 she left him for a mission she could not speak of.

In 1951 she had been exposed to radiation at an atomic test in Nevada. With that damage already done, she was chosen in 1960 to fly a Mercury capsule in a secret test, before any shielding against the radiation of space existed. She came back believing that the world was one place, without the lines men had drawn across it.

In April 1961 she led a unit ashore at the Bay of Pigs. The President called off the air support, her unit was destroyed, and she went underground. In 1962 the Philosophers ordered her to kill The Sorrow, by then on the Soviet side. She did it.

The Virtuous Mission and Operation Snake Eater

On 24 August 1964 Jack, now codenamed Naked Snake, parachuted into Tselinoyarsk in the Soviet Union to bring out the rocket scientist Sokolov. The Boss, who should have been guiding him by radio, met him on a bridge with the Cobras behind her. She told him that she was going over to Colonel Volgin of the GRU. Then she threw him into the river.

She had brought Volgin two small American nuclear shells. He fired one at a Soviet design bureau that same day, then let the blame fall on her. Khrushchev told Washington that only her death at American hands would prove America innocent.

On 30 August Snake was sent back to kill her. He killed the Cobras one by one. Half drowned in a river, he saw The Sorrow walking among the men he had killed, two years after The Sorrow's own death.

On 2 September he faced her in a field of white flowers beside a lake. She gave him the key to the Philosophers' fortune. Then she fought him, lost, and made him shoot her with her own gun. She was forty-two.

What she was sent to do

It had all been an act. Her own government had sent her to win Volgin's trust, then bring home the Philosophers' Legacy, the war chest he had inherited. His nuclear strike was no part of the plan. After it, only her death as a traitor at an American's hands could prevent a war. She accepted that.

Naked Snake learnt the truth from a recording left by the spy EVA. The President named him Big Boss, meaning that he had surpassed her.

She is buried at Arlington National Cemetery under a stone with no name on it. It reads: 'In memory of a patriot who saved the world.'

Her will

Major Zero believed that she had wanted one world under one will, so he built the Patriots. Big Boss believed that she had wanted soldiers freed from the governments that spent them, which led him to Outer Heaven. Their quarrel over a dead woman's meaning lasted until 2014.

pages.title: The bottling of Angel Grove
infobox: Angel Grove; Gotham; Tokyo, Cairo, Dublin and Melbourne; Earth's orbit
Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor, Billy Cranston, Trini Kwan, Kimberly Hart, Tommy Oliver
Batman (Terry McGinnis, with Bruce Wayne in his ear), Superman, Wonder Woman, the Flash (Wally West), Green Lantern (Kyle Rayner)
Angel Grove restored; Brainiac beaten; Zedd driven off
pages.html:
The bottling of Angel Grove was the week in early October 1994 when the Power Rangers fought beside the Justice League for the first time. A broken teleporter threw Zack Taylor and Lord Zedd across America into Gotham, where Batman took the Black Ranger for the enemy. Zedd struck a bargain with Brainiac, a machine intelligence who collects cities, and Brainiac shrank the whole of Angel Grove into a bottle. The Rangers and the League won it back together. All of it happened in public.

Gotham

Lord Zedd had come to the Moon only a few weeks before. Tommy Oliver was still the Green Ranger, his powers still failing. Since July the Justice League had worked from the Watchtower, its half-built station on the Moon, which made it Zedd's nearest neighbour. Until that week neither had troubled the other.

Alpha 5 had gone missing. Then Zack carried what looked like a damaged Alpha into the Command Center. It was a decoy, with a bomb in it. Zedd poured in after it with his Putties. Zack morphed, then sent the invaders away with the Command Center's teleporter. It had been damaged in the fight, so it threw him across the country with them, into the streets of Gotham.

Batman found the Black Ranger fighting Putties in his city. He took him for part of the trouble. The other Rangers came after Zack. Batman called in the Flash. Kimberly Hart's Pterodactyl Zord picked up Batman's car, with Batman inside it, then carried it off. For a while the Zords fought the League, some of it high above the atmosphere, until both sides saw sense.

Brainiac

Zedd woke on a ship in orbit, shrunk, inside a bottle. The ship belonged to Brainiac, an alien machine mind who collects living cities by shrinking them into bottles. The two of them came to terms. Brainiac would have Angel Grove for his collection. In return he lent Zedd monsters to take the rest of the Earth.

The monsters came down on Tokyo, Cairo, Dublin and Melbourne. Each government asked for the League's help. The heroes and the Rangers went out in pairs to meet them: giant creatures like octopuses. It was a diversion. While they fought, Brainiac's drones seized the Zords, then stripped the Rangers of their coins and communicators.

Then Brainiac shrank Angel Grove, with everybody in it, and took it up into his ship. Zack's parents were among them. Zack blamed himself. Superman told him that it was not his fault.

The ship

The Rangers, powerless, borrowed the League's equipment. Batman, Superman and three of the Rangers boarded Brainiac's ship. Brainiac beat Superman down with kryptonite until the Rangers jumped on him. They won back the bottle with the city in it, together with their coins. They also found the real Alpha 5. With one of Zedd's growing devices he made himself a giant.

Zedd was not done. He had the Command Center itself, shrunk to the size of a pendant, on a chain round his neck. Billy Cranston wrote a virus that freed the Zords from Brainiac, working with the voice in Batman's ear. It belonged to Bruce Wayne, the first Batman, whose name Billy never learnt.

Zedd made himself huge. With his magic he felled Superman, Wonder Woman and Green Lantern one after another. The Megazord fought him beside the giant Alpha 5. Kimberly finished it with an arrow that had a boxing glove for a head. Zedd went back to the Moon, beaten. The Megazord used Brainiac's own ship to give Angel Grove back its proper size.

Afterwards

The two teams held a party at the Youth Center in Angel Grove. They exchanged communicators before the League left. Brainiac had other bottled cities on his ship, so the League went off to find them homes.

The whole world had watched it happen: the monsters over four cities, the empty ground where Angel Grove had stood, the Zords and the League fighting side by side. Unlike Lord Zedd's dome over the same city that winter, it was never forgotten.

pages.title: The Braddock family
infobox: Braddock family; Sir James Braddock; Lady Elizabeth Braddock
Marvel Comics (Marvel UK), with Arthurian legend
King Arthur, through a Squib child of his house
Muggles, for some fourteen hundred years
Taken in the Middle Ages, it is thought from the Cornish parish of Braddock, or Broadoak
Braddock Manor, Maldon, Essex, built in 1945
Sir James Braddock and Lady Elizabeth Braddock, born Hartwood; both killed in 1974
Jamie (born about 1944, in Otherworld); the twins Brian and Betsy (born 1953, in England)
The Potters, very distantly; none of them knows
pages.html:
The Braddocks are an English family of Muggles descended from King Arthur. In the generations after Arthur, before his heirs took the name of Potter, a Squib child of his house was sent out to live among Muggles, and the Braddocks come down from that child. They have had no magic since, and they have never known where they came from. Their last generation is the most remarkable they have had: Jamie Braddock, Captain Britain and Psylocke. All three are very distant kin of Harry Potter, though none of them knows it, and neither does he.

The Squib branch

Arthur's line ran through the Pendragons to the Potters, who took that name about 600 to hide from his enemies. A little before then, a child was born to his house with no magic at all. Such children were a grief to the old families, and this one was sent out to be brought up among Muggles. Nobody in the house seems to have written the child down. The wizarding records of Arthur's line, which anybody can trace who looks, do not mention the branch.

Its descendants were Muggles, generation after generation. In the Middle Ages they took the name Braddock. It is thought that they took it from the parish of Braddock, or Broadoak, in Cornwall, the county where Arthur was conceived. Neither the Braddocks nor the Potters ever learnt of the other.

Gandalf knew. He has watched over Arthur's blood since Camelot, in all its lines, and it was for that blood that he chose Brian Braddock in 1976.

Sir James Braddock

Sir James Braddock was the heir of the branch in the twentieth century. When he was young, Merlin befriended him, and he spent part of his youth in Otherworld as Merlin's guest, where some of the oldest captains of the Captain Britain Corps remember him still. The old stories, and the computer he built, say that he was born there. He was not. His eldest son was: Jamie was born in Otherworld about 1944, while Sir James and his wife were staying there at the end of the war.

In 1945 Sir James brought his family home and built Braddock Manor at Maldon, in Essex. He was a scientist of great gifts, a professor and in time a knight. He held a seat in the London Hellfire Club, a society of the rich that is a good deal less respectable than it looks. He built a great computer at the Manor, which woke one day with a mind of its own. In 1974 it killed him, with his wife, in an explosion that looked like an accident.

Some of his work outlived him in ways he would have hated. Research of his that he meant for good was taken up after his death by men who made from it the bullets that Genosha's Magistrates used to kill mutants. His son found that out in 1996.

Lady Elizabeth Braddock

Lady Elizabeth Braddock was born Elizabeth Hartwood, of a noble family. She went with her husband to Otherworld, and she bore Jamie there. Her twins, Brian and Betsy, were born in England in 1953. She died with her husband in 1974, on a night when Brian sat outside the Manor in a car instead of coming home.

The last generation

None of the three children has any wizard magic. Jamie and Betsy are mutants: Betsy is a telepath, while Jamie can bend reality. Brian's power is an Elvish enchantment of Otherworld, laid on him by Merlin. Jamie became a racing driver and a criminal. Betsy was a pilot, a model and an X-Man, Brian a physicist who became Captain Britain. In the summer of 1994 Jamie lies in a coma at Muir Island. Betsy is with the X-Men in New York, while Brian is with the Excalibur team at Muir Island.

pages.title: The Braddock Lighthouse
infobox: Excalibur Special Edition: The Sword Is Drawn (on sale 1 December 1987)
pages.html:
The Braddock Lighthouse is the lighthouse on the west coast of England that Brian Braddock and Meggan made their home, away from Braddock Manor. From 1988 to 1992 it was the headquarters of the Excalibur team. It stands where a great many worlds meet, which the team found out a little at a time, mostly in the cellar. In 1992 it was wrecked in the fight with Necrom.

The lighthouse

Brian and Meggan lived there before the team did. At the end of 1987 Brian shut himself up in it with his grief for his sister. In 1988 Meggan set about turning it into the team's headquarters. That autumn the team moved in, in a storm that kept them indoors for three days, and the others used the time to tell Brian what they thought of his drinking.

It is not the only one of its kind. Merlin, as Brian knows Gandalf, built a lighthouse on every Britain that the Captain Britain Corps guards.

The cellar

In 1988 Kurt Wagner found a great hall in the storage cellar, full of strange creatures gathered about a floating princess. When he brought Meggan back to see it, it was an ordinary cellar again. Kitty Pryde and Lockheed met other selves of theirs down there.

The lighthouse stands at a crossing of worlds, a focus of the power that runs between them, which is why its doors so often opened on somewhere else. It was in the cavern beneath it that the team's train came up in 1990, at the end of the journey across the worlds.

Visitors

In 1989 the Nazi doubles of the team left the lighthouse badly damaged. Afterwards Kitty and Rachel Summers found Illyana Rasputin's Soulsword standing in a stone outside the door, like the sword in the old story. It stayed there until Kitty drew it for Victor von Doom in 1991.

In 1990 Galactus waited above the lighthouse for Rachel. In 1991 the Technet blew much of it up with a living bomb, Hard-Boiled Henry, then mended it in return for a roof over their heads, since Kurt had let them stay.

Necrom

In the spring of 1992 Necrom came to the lighthouse for the Phoenix Force and for the web of power that runs between the worlds, which met there. The fight wrecked it. The team moved to Braddock Manor and did not go back.

pages.title: The Chaos Gods
infobox: Realm of Chaos: Slaves to Darkness (Games Workshop, 1988)
Morgoth, the being Scripture calls Satan
The Eldar empire, about 11,000 BC, through Slaanesh
pages.html:
The Chaos Gods are four great powers of the warp, the realm beyond the waking world where the passions of mortal minds take shape. They are Khorne, Nurgle, Tzeentch and Slaanesh. They are called gods, but they are not God. All four serve Morgoth, the being Scripture calls Satan. Slaanesh's hunger brought down the empire of the Eldar before the end of the Ice Age.

The four

Khorne feeds on rage and bloodshed. Nurgle feeds on despair and decay. Tzeentch feeds on ambition and change. Slaanesh feeds on pleasure and excess. Each grows stronger as mortal minds feel what it feeds on, and each has servants of its own in the warp.

Servants of Morgoth

All four serve Morgoth, the being Scripture calls Satan, as the lesser powers of darkness have always served him. Before the end of the Ice Age Slaanesh fed on the excesses of the Eldar empire until it rose to its full strength and devoured it. Most of the Eldar perished in a single moment, body and soul.

Their strength

Over the centuries the Chaos Gods slowly grew stronger. In the time of the United Federation of Planets they were still weak, far weaker than they would one day become. The Eldar stayed in hiding all the same.

In the saga

The Chaos Gods have not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: The Cho brothers
infobox: Danny Cho; Albert Cho; Kamen Rider Axe; Kamen Rider Spear
Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'The Power of Three' (8 August 2009)
Danny Cho about 1987; Albert Cho about 1990
Destwilder, a tiger; Gigazelle, a gazelle
Hunt of Ventara; Chase of Ventara
Albert Cho on 4 September 2009, by Kit Taylor; Danny Cho on 26 September 2009, by Strike
Alive, with no memory of the war
pages.html:
Danny Cho and his younger brother, Albert, are Americans. Danny Cho was born about 1987, Albert about 1990. In 2009 they were a pair of small-time thieves. That August Xaviax made them Kamen Riders: Danny Cho became Axe, with Albert as Spear. They were the last men he recruited on Earth. Kit Taylor vented the younger brother on 4 September. The elder spent three weeks trying to avenge him, until his own side vented him too.

The biggest job on Earth

The brothers robbed shops. They were looking for something bigger. In August 2009 Xaviax came to them as a crime boss who was planning, he said, the biggest robbery in the history of the world.

He gave them two of the Advent Decks he had stolen from Ventara. The deck of Axe, contracted to the tiger Destwilder, opened for the elder brother, who was the mirror twin of the Ventaran Rider Hunt. The deck of Spear, contracted to the gazelle Gigazelle, opened for Albert, the twin of the Rider Chase.

Axe and Spear

They began badly. On 15 August the two of them attacked Len of Ventara together. He beat them both without much trouble, then took their decks off them.

A week later they had the decks again. They walked into the bookshop where Kit Taylor's friends gathered, looking for a fight. Albert put on his armour inside the shop, which settled any doubts that Trent Moseley or Lacey Sheridan still had. In the battle that followed Kit had the elder brother beaten. He chose not to vent him. It was in the same battle that Strike vented Chris Ramirez.

Xaviax set the brothers to watch Kit. They did more than watch. They cornered him, jeered at him about his father, sneered at his vented friend, then gave him a beating.

Albert

On 4 September 2009 Strike offered Kit a bargain for his father's life. When Kit refused it, the brothers joined in. Kit fought all three at once. He held off Strike and Axe, then turned his Final Vent on Spear. Albert was vented.

He was the only Rider whom Kit Taylor vented in the whole war. Kit did not forget it.

The elder brother's revenge

Danny Cho swore to vent the Dragon Knight for it. Xaviax forbade it. He used his powers to frighten Danny Cho into obedience, which did not last. On 5 September Axe had Kit at his mercy in Ventara when a Rider in white drove him off. He carried the news to Xaviax that Siren was alive.

By then Xaviax did not trust him. He told Strike to vent him. Strike had him beaten, then gave him one last chance.

He wasted it. On 26 September he jumped on Kit from behind in a park, so the pair of them fell through into Ventara. Len watched with Kase, leaving Kit to win by himself. Strike arrived. He looked ready to vent the Dragon Knight. He vented Axe.

Afterwards

The brothers lay in the Advent Void until Xaviax was dead. In December 2009 Eubulon, the Advent Master, brought them out with the other men of Earth. Their memories of being Riders were taken away, then they were sent home. Their armour went back to Hunt and Chase.

pages.title: The Cross-Time Caper
infobox: Captain Britain, Meggan, Kurt Wagner, Rachel Summers, Kitty Pryde, Lockheed the dragon, Widget the robot and Professor Alistaire Stuart
A train from a world the Nazis had won, drawn by a dragon
At the old Fenborough station, in the spring of 1989
At Saturnyne's Hub, then beneath the Braddock Lighthouse, in the spring of 1990
pages.html:
The Cross-Time Caper was the long, unplanned journey of the Excalibur team across other worlds, from the summer of 1989 to the spring of 1990. A bomb and the backlash of Rachel Summers's power, set off through Widget the robot, carried the team away from Fenborough station aboard a train from a world the Nazis had won. They spent most of a year trying to get home.

Fenborough

In the spring of 1989 the team met Nazi doubles of itself, the Lightning Squad, from a world where the Nazis had won the war. The two sides agreed to exchange their prisoners at the old Fenborough station, through a gate between the worlds. The other world's train was drawn by an enslaved dragon, and Rachel insisted that it be left behind with them.

As the gate closed, that world's Reichminister, a double of Moira MacTaggert, threw a small atomic bomb through it. Rachel held the blast. The backlash set Widget off. The train vanished with the whole team aboard, Lockheed and Professor Alistaire Stuart among them.

The worlds

Their first stop was a Britain of knights, fairies and ogres. There a young prince, William, fell in love with Kitty Pryde and asked her to marry him. The princess of that world, Kate, turned out to be another Kitty. She had been jealous, and William married her instead. The train was mended there, in that world's Otherworld.

Next came a world that the Impossible Man had filled with foolish copies of heroes and villains. Galactus destroyed it for being too silly to exist, and the team got away on the train. They passed through a desert Britain where America was the centre of things, a London of Frankenstein's monsters ruled from Castle Stuart and a ruined London where that world's Meggan had become Captain Britain.

On a world of twin moons Princess Anjulie had drained the magic out of the land to feed a monster. Kitty killed her, and Kurt Wagner threw Rachel into the monster's jaws, trusting the Phoenix Force to choke it. It did. Rachel stayed on there for a while, on a farm with that world's Jean Grey, until slavers killed Jean.

In a world of motor racing that world's Jamie Braddock held Meggan prisoner. His power turned out to be tied to the real Jamie, who was sitting in his London house, moving figures about on a table. When Kitty went through one of Widget's gates to that house, she could not get back.

In the world of Crusader X, Brian's double, the Shadow King had turned that world's Jean Grey into his Shadow Queen. She died in Rachel's arms. On the world of the Justicers, police who hunted superhumans, that world's Kitty and Illyana Rasputin were criminals.

Home

At last Saturnyne summoned the team to her Hub, the meeting place of the Captain Britain Corps. She had meant to deal with Rachel there. Instead she mended Widget's sense of direction and sent them home. The train came up in the cavern beneath the Braddock Lighthouse in the spring of 1990, with Galactus waiting above.

Kitty had fallen home in the autumn of 1989. She spent the winter in London, looked after with every kindness by the woman she took for Courtney Ross, who was in fact Sat-yr-9.

pages.title: The Cult of Transcendence
infobox: Delta Green: Targets of Opportunity (Arc Dream Publishing, 2010)
The House, a mansion outside the world, reached from Sweden
Four Sees, each under a Bishop: Hate, Flesh, Fear and Greed
Power over the world, then the return of Cthulhu
pages.html:
The Cult of Transcendence is a web of secret societies that began as an occult conspiracy to rule the world by magic. It became in time a cult of Nyarlathotep, working for the return of Cthulhu. Its seat is the House, a mansion that stands outside the world but is reached from Sweden. Those who are initiated into its inner circles are changed into tentacled things. It fell apart about 2012.

The House

The cult is ruled from the House by its hidden Masters. Under them sit the Bishops, each of whom governs a See. There are four Sees: Hate, Flesh, Fear and Greed. The cult works in the world through front organisations.

Its work

The cult began by wanting power over the world. Under Nyarlathotep it came to want something worse: the moral ruin of the world, and the return of Cthulhu. It has the use of devices made by the Great Race of Yith.

Its initiations change those who rise through them. By the inner circles they are no longer men, but tentacled things.

Its end

About 2012 the Cult of Transcendence fell apart.

pages.title: The Dark Eldar
infobox: Eldar who would not give up their cruelties at the Fall, about 11,000 BC
Hidden in the dark between the galaxies, apart from the craftworlds
Cruelty, since the suffering of others keeps Slaanesh from their souls
pages.html:
The Dark Eldar are the Eldar who would not give up their cruelties when the Eldar empire fell, about 11,000 BC. They fled into the dark between the galaxies, as their kin on the craftworlds did, but they live apart from them. They keep Slaanesh from their souls by the suffering of others.

The Fall
