When Slaanesh devoured the Eldar empire, a few of its cruellest people were hidden away from the worst of it. They had made Slaanesh what it was, and they did not repent. Afterwards they went into hiding in the dark between the galaxies, far from their kin.

Their way

Slaanesh hungers for every Eldar soul. The craftworld Eldar guard their souls with spirit stones and the discipline of the Path. The Dark Eldar keep their own from it by feeding on the pain of others, which renews them and holds off the thirst for a while.

In the saga

The Dark Eldar have not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: The Death Ranger
infobox: The Avadians, who have no sexes and no notion of death
The Gold Omega morpher, in the vault under Safehaven
Jason Lee Scott's link to the Power
February 1995, when the Grid was cleansed
pages.html:
The Death Ranger was Spa'ark of Avadias, the first Gold Omega Ranger, who set out long ago to cure death and was sealed inside the Gold Omega morpher for it. The morpher lay in the vault under Safehaven for centuries. In January 1995 somebody took it out, and the Death Ranger woke. Jason Lee Scott broke the morpher from within, at the cost of his own link to the Power.

Avadias

Spa'ark came from the planet Avadias. The people of Avadias are neither men nor women. They have no word for death, nor any custom of mourning, because none of them is ever lost. At the end of what an Avadian calls the Living Journey, the mind of the dying one joins the Legacy, a shared mind in which all their dead go on together. Nobody on Avadias has ever had cause to grieve.

The Gold Omega Ranger

Spa'ark was one of the first five Omega Rangers, the Gold, with a power drawn from the Sun. The Gold Ranger's call was 'Omega Sun Power!', the Zord the Gold Omegazord. The team's base was Safehaven.

The work kept Spa'ark far from Avadias for years on end, which was lonely. Haza, the Blue Omega Ranger, noticed. She made a point of keeping Spa'ark company.

Haza

The great enemies of the first Omega Rangers were the Supernova Sisters, beings of the deep sky that fed on dead stars. After a battle with one of them the team was resting on Safehaven. Haza had come to sit with Spa'ark when another of the Sisters attacked. Haza was run through before either of them could morph. The team beat the attacker, but Haza was dead.

Spa'ark waited to feel her in the Legacy. She was not there. She had died beyond its reach. The others grieved, which Spa'ark could not understand either.

The cure for death

Spa'ark concluded that the fault lay with the universe. Death was a sickness. It could be cured, so that every living thing might join the Legacy. Spa'ark went to work on the Power itself.

What came of it was no cure. Dead bodies got up, Haza's among them, with nobody inside them, doing whatever Spa'ark willed. Apophee, the Black Omega Ranger, had it out with Spa'ark. The Puram, the Yellow, tried reasoning. In the end the three who were left had to put a stop to it.

Spa'ark was sealed inside the Gold Omega morpher. Bledso, the Red Omega Ranger, put it away with the others' help in the vault under Safehaven. It stayed there for centuries. In that time Spa'ark changed. The lonely Ranger who had wanted to save everybody became something cold, patient and cunning, with one purpose: to end death by mastering it. That was the Death Ranger.

January 1995

Late in January 1995 a visitor to Safehaven took the Gold Omega morpher out of the vault. The visitor hoped that its power would wake a friend who lay beyond all help. What woke was Spa'ark.

The Death Ranger killed Jason Lee Scott, the Red Omega Ranger. Yale, the Blue, died the same way. The Death Ranger could pass from one body to another. Jason's came first, then Yale's, then Trini Kwan's, then Zack Taylor's. Last came the Omegazords themselves, joined as one machine, which the Death Ranger wore like a suit of armour. The dead of a far world were raised to fight as an army.

Seven Rangers came from Earth to help the Omega Rangers. A Dragon Thunderzord, which was the idea of Matt Cook, the Green Ranger, destroyed the Death Ranger's Zord.

Jason Lee Scott

Jason was not gone. He was held inside the Power. There he was offered what Spa'ark had always wanted to give the whole universe. He was shown his mother, alive. She had died only days before, at home in Angel Grove, while he was away under a lie.

Jason refused the vision. He broke the Gold morpher from within, which ended the Death Ranger's hold. Jason lived, as Yale did. The cost was his own link to the Power, which the breaking tore out. He could not be the Red Omega Ranger again, nor carry a Power Coin. Trini Kwan took the Red Omega powers in his place.

He had no powers of any kind until October 1996, when those of the Gold Ranger came to him. They were Triforia's, held in a staff, so they did not need the link that he had lost.

The end

Spa'ark was not destroyed with the morpher. In February 1995 Rita Repulsa, calling herself Mistress Vile, used the Death Ranger as a weapon in Dark Specter's war on the Rangers. Other Rangers' bodies were worn in that war as Jason's had been. When the Rangers cleansed the Grid, the Death Ranger was destroyed with the rest of the corruption in it.

pages.title: The Deep Ones
infobox: The Shadow over Innsmouth (Visionary Publishing Company, April 1936)
Grey-green and scaled, with gills, webbed hands and bulging eyes
They do not die of age
Father Dagon, Mother Hydra and Cthulhu
Children of Deep Ones and men, who bear the Innsmouth look
pages.html:
The Deep Ones are a scaled, grey-green people of the sea, with the eyes of fish and the wide mouths of frogs. They do not die of age, and they live in great cities on the sea floor. They worship Father Dagon, Mother Hydra and the sleeping Cthulhu. Where men by the sea will have them, they trade gold for sacrifices, then for brides. The children of those marriages go down into the sea in the end to join them. In 1928 the American government raided Innsmouth, Massachusetts, where they had been breeding with the townspeople for eighty years. Delta Green has been hunting them ever since.

Nature

A Deep One stands upright like a man, although it hops more often than it walks. Its skin is grey-green, with a pale belly, and its back is ridged with scales. It has gills at the sides of its neck, webbed hands, webbed feet and bulging eyes that never close. Its voice is a croaking, bleating sort of sound.

Deep Ones are very strong, and they are hard to kill. Unless they are killed, they do not die at all. Their cities lie far down on the sea floor, built of huge stone and hung about with gold. The best known to men is Y'ha-nthlei, beyond Devil Reef off the coast of Massachusetts.

Their gods

The Deep Ones worship Father Dagon and Mother Hydra. Above both they honour Cthulhu, who lies in drowned R'lyeh, and they wait for the day when he wakes.

Father Dagon is the Dagon of the Philistines, whose image fell on its face before the Ark of the Lord at Ashdod and was found broken on the threshold the next morning.

The bargain

Wherever men live by the sea, the Deep Ones can make them an offer. They drive fish into the nets and bring up gold from the sea floor. In return they ask first for sacrifices, then for husbands and wives. The children of those marriages look human when they are young. As they grow older they take on what the towns near Innsmouth called the Innsmouth look: a narrow head, a flat nose and wide, staring eyes that never seem to blink. In middle age they go down into the sea for good, as Deep Ones in full, and after that they never die.

It is how the Deep Ones lead a people astray. Innsmouth was a churchgoing town of New England before the bargain came to it. Within a generation its churches had lost their people to the Esoteric Order of Dagon. Old men of Innsmouth used to say there were enough Deep Ones in the sea to wipe out mankind, if they ever cared to.

Innsmouth

Captain Obed Marsh of Innsmouth found them in the South Seas, on an island of the Carolines near Ponape, in the first half of the nineteenth century. The islanders there gave them sacrifices in return for fish and gold. When the islanders of the neighbouring islands wiped that people out, Obed brought the bargain home. Before long Innsmouth was giving sacrifices at Devil Reef, and gold was coming up from the sea.

In 1846 the neighbouring towns grew suspicious, and Obed was jailed with several of his crew. That night the Deep Ones came up out of the sea. More than half the town died, and outside Innsmouth it was put down to a plague. Afterwards the Deep Ones lived among the survivors, married them and bred with them for eighty years.

The raid of 1928

In July 1927 a young man from Ohio, Robert Olmstead, got out of Innsmouth alive and went to the federal authorities with what he had seen. In February 1928 the Navy and the Bureau of Investigation raided the town. They burnt the waterfront and took a great many of the townspeople away to camps. A submarine fired torpedoes down into the deep water beyond Devil Reef, where Y'ha-nthlei lies. The city was damaged, but it was not destroyed. The story is told on the page The raid on Innsmouth.

Delta Green's war

P4, the section of the Office of Naval Intelligence that took over everything learnt at Innsmouth, went on hunting the Deep Ones and their hybrids round the world until 1941. In 1930 it took some five hundred prisoners on the island of Pedra Negra, in the Philippines. In the Second World War the Karotechia, the occult section of the SS, went looking for the Deep Ones as allies. In December 1942 Delta Green and Britain's PISCES wrecked a bargain that the Karotechia was striking with the Deep Ones off the coast of France.

In April 1963 the submarine Thresher was lost with all hands off New England. Delta Green linked the loss to Innsmouth, and that spring it bombed what was left of Y'ha-nthlei in Operation RIPTIDE.

Since the war most of the Deep Ones have drawn back from the coasts of men. A few of the old hybrid places remain. One is Black Cod Island, off the coast of British Columbia, where a people descended from the Deep Ones has lived for a very long time.

In the world

The public knows nothing of the Deep Ones. In 1928 the newspapers took the raid on Innsmouth for a strike against bootleggers. The two kingdoms under the sea that call themselves Atlantis are not known ever to have met them.

pages.title: The Drell
infobox: Rakhana, a desert world ruined by its own people
The Compact, their promise of service to the Hanar
Kepral's Syndrome, a disease of the lungs caught on damp Kahje
pages.html:
The Drell are a slender, reptilian people whose homeworld, Rakhana, was a desert that their own industry turned into a grave. Its people had grown to some eleven billion, and they had no ships to leave it. From about 1975 to 1985 the Hanar carried 375,000 of them to Kahje, and the rest died on Rakhana. The Drell have served the Hanar ever since under the Compact. The Enterprise NX-01 met them in 2156.

Rakhana

Rakhana was always dry. Its people's industry made it drier, then made it dead. By the time the Hanar found them the Drell had grown to some eleven billion, fighting over the last of the water and food, with no way of leaving. The Hanar spent ten years carrying away every Drell who was willing to go. The billions left behind died. Rakhana is a graveyard now, with a few thousand Drell living among its ruins and pilgrims coming to it from Kahje.

The Drell

Drell are slender and reptilian, with muscle much denser than a human's, which gives them a wiry strength. They give birth to live young, who can eat solid food from the start. A Drell lives about eighty-five years. Their throats can make sounds beyond the range of human hearing, and they are very hard to strangle.

Their ancestors lived in rocky deserts, and damp air does not suit them. On Kahje, a world of ocean, they live in domed cities where the air is kept dry. Even so, many die of Kepral's Syndrome, a slow sickness of the lungs that within a generation of the move had learnt to resist the Hanar's medicines.

The Compact

In gratitude the Drell made the Compact with the Hanar, a promise to serve them. Some outsiders, and some Hanar, look on the Drell as servants. In truth they have found a place in every part of Hanar society, and they are respected in it. Living among the Hanar has made them very good readers of other peoples' faces and bodies. Those Drell who leave Kahje tend to be adventurers, and they seldom come back.

Earth

The Enterprise NX-01 met the Drell in 2156, when it met the Hanar through the Asari. Its crew found the Drell easy company, which the Drell said was the result of a great deal of practice.

pages.title: The Elcor
infobox: Dekuuna, a world of heavy gravity and wide, flat plains
Massive, slow-moving creatures on four legs
Among themselves, by scent, small movements and sounds too low for humans to hear; with others, by naming the feeling first
pages.html:
The Elcor are a massive, four-legged people from Dekuuna, a world whose gravity is so strong that a fall can kill. They move slowly and think carefully. They are among the most conservative people in the galaxy. Since other peoples cannot read their feelings, an Elcor speaking to outsiders names the feeling before saying anything else. The Enterprise NX-01 met them in 2160.

Dekuuna

Dekuuna's gravity is so heavy that its mountains never rose, and most of the world is flat, open plain. The first Elcor wandered it in small family bands. On such a world a fall can be fatal, so the Elcor learnt to move slowly, on four strong legs, and never to hurry into anything. Their minds followed their bodies. An Elcor considers every choice at length and distrusts anything new until it has proved itself.

Speech

Among themselves the Elcor talk by scent, by slight movements of the body and by sounds pitched too low for human ears. Their spoken voices are slow and flat. Other peoples, who miss all the rest, cannot tell when an Elcor is amused, angry or being sarcastic, and so an Elcor speaking to outsiders says so first. 'Pleased,' an Elcor will begin, and then say what it has to say.

Among the stars

The Elcor had long been friends of the Asari, the Salarians and the Turians, though they never much liked space travel. They prefer an open sky over their heads, and long voyages make them restless. In 2160, soon after it met the Turians, the Enterprise NX-01 met an Elcor envoy. The talks were very long and very courteous. Nobody on either side lost patience.

pages.title: The Eldar
infobox: Noldor of the Exiles, who went out among the stars about 36,000 BC
Across the galaxy, for more than twenty thousand years
The craftworlds, hidden in the dark between the galaxies
The Vulcans, and through them the Romulans
On worlds across the galaxy, with dormant webway gates
pages.html:
The Eldar are a people of the Elves who left the world for the stars early in the Second Age. They built an empire there that lasted more than twenty thousand years, until their own excesses fed Slaanesh, the Chaos God of pleasure, who devoured them. Its fall came before the end of the Ice Age. The survivors are in hiding, on the vast ships called craftworlds in the dark between the galaxies. The ruins of their empire, and its dormant webway gates, lie on worlds across the galaxy. The Vulcans and the Romulans came of them, though neither people remembered it.

The Exiles who took to the stars

The Eldar came of the Noldor, the Elves who had left Valinor in rebellion in the First Age and lived in Middle-earth as exiles. When the First Age ended most of the Exiles were pardoned, and many of them took ship into the West. Early in the Second Age, about 36,000 BC, one great host of them would neither go back nor fade in Middle-earth. They built ships that could sail the sky, as Eärendil's had, and went out among the stars.

The empire among the stars

Out among the stars they kept the old name of their people, the Eldar. Their craft grew beyond anything the Elves of Middle-earth had known. Away from the world they were no longer deathless, though they lived a thousand years or more. Their minds were strong enough to see what others could not and to speak without words.

They spread across the galaxy and built an empire that lasted more than twenty thousand years. They crossed it by the webway, a labyrinth between the worlds, through gates that opened onto it from world to world.

The Fall

Their empire grew rich and idle. Its people gave themselves over to every pleasure and every cruelty they could imagine. All of it fed Slaanesh, the Chaos God of excess, who serves Morgoth as all the Chaos Gods do. About 11,000 BC, before the end of the Ice Age, Slaanesh rose to its full strength out of their excesses and devoured the empire. Most of the Eldar perished in a single moment, body and soul. The worlds at the heart of the empire were lost.

The survivors

A few lived. Some had seen the Fall coming and fled before it aboard the craftworlds, vast ships each carrying a whole people. Others, who would not give up their cruelties, fled too and became the Dark Eldar. Scattered bands came down on worlds at the edge of the empire, and one of them settled on Vulcan.

The craftworld Eldar are in hiding still, in the dark between the galaxies, far from any star. They live by the Path, a discipline in which each of them masters one calling at a time, so that no passion can ever rule them again. Each wears a spirit stone, which takes the soul at death and keeps it from Slaanesh.

In the time of the United Federation of Planets the Chaos Gods were weak, far weaker than they would one day become. The Eldar stayed in hiding all the same.

The ruins

The ruins of the Eldar empire lie on worlds across the galaxy. Among them are webway gates, long dormant, which once opened onto the webway. The peoples who found them in later ages could make little of them, and took them for the work of some vanished race. In the 2290s the Asari archaeologist Liara T'Soni was studying such ruins when John Shepard took her aboard the Enterprise-B.

The Vulcans

The Vulcans came of the band of survivors who settled on Vulcan after the Fall. They lost their ships there, with their craft, and in time their memory of what they had been. Neither the Vulcans nor the Romulans, who later left Vulcan, ever learnt where they came from.

In the saga

The Eldar have not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: The Elder Things
infobox: At the Mountains of Madness, Astounding Stories (February to April 1936)
A people from beyond the Earth
Early in the Third Age, about 32,900 BC
About six feet long, barrel-bodied, star-headed and winged
Far inland in Antarctica, beyond the Mountains of Madness
The star-spawn of Cthulhu; the Mi-go
pages.html:
The Elder Things were a people from beyond the Earth who came down early in the Third Age, about 32,900 BC, and built a great city in the far south, where the ice of Antarctica now lies. They were barrel-bodied, star-headed and winged, built on a pattern of fives. They bred the shoggoths to labour for them. They fought the star-spawn of Cthulhu, then the Mi-go, until at last the cold drove the last of them down into a dark sea beneath the ice. Early in 1931 the Miskatonic University expedition found their dead city, and some of the Elder Things it found frozen in the rock were not as dead as they looked.

From beyond the Earth

The Elder Things came down to the Earth from somewhere out among the stars. An Elder Thing was about six feet long, with a ridged body like a barrel and wings that folded away like fans. Its head was a five-pointed star, with an eye at each point. It could live in the deep sea as easily as on land, and it could fly between the worlds.

They built a great city of stone in the far south. For its labour they bred servants out of living matter, the shoggoths. The carvings on its walls boast that they made the life of the Earth as well. That was a lie, or a mistake. The Earth was full of life, the work of God, long before they came, and God had made them too.

Their wars

Not long after them came Cthulhu with his star-spawn, and the two peoples went to war. In the end they made a peace, and the star-spawn kept the lands that rose out of the Pacific. Later the Mi-go came down from Yuggoth and drove the Elder Things out of the northern lands.

Their own shoggoths rose against them more than once. Each rising was put down, but each time the shoggoths had learnt a little more.

The cold

In time the south grew cold. The Elder Things went down into a sunless sea that lay in great caverns beneath their city, and the city above them was left to the ice. Whether any of them still live down there, nobody knows.

The Miskatonic expedition

In the southern summer of 1930 to 1931 an expedition from Miskatonic University in Arkham, Massachusetts, went to Antarctica to drill for rock. Early in 1931 Professor Lake's party found frozen Elder Things in a cave in the mountains. Some of them woke. They destroyed Lake's camp, its men and its dogs.

William Dyer, the geologist who led the expedition, flew over the Mountains of Madness with a student called Danforth. On the plateau beyond they found the dead city, mile after mile of it. Its carvings told them the history of the Elder Things. Deep inside they found the woken Elder Things too, dead, their heads torn off. Then a shoggoth came after them, crying 'Tekeli-li!', and they ran.

Danforth looked back once, at something beyond the mountains, and it broke his mind. Dyer wrote his account afterwards, to try to stop another expedition from going.

Not the Ancients, not Atlantis

The city of the Elder Things has nothing to do with the star-faring city of the Ancients, which stood elsewhere on that land in another age, and nothing to do with Atlantis. Nor do the chronicles of the Sub-Mariner's kingdom under the Antarctic sea speak of the Elder Things. The sea where the last of them went lies far inland, under the ice of the continent itself.

pages.title: The Eltarian War
infobox: Eltar, under its Supreme Guardian, Zartus
Zordon's Rangers, the Omega Rangers and Promethea
Zordon's tube; the Command Center; Promethea's headquarters; the Moon Palace
The death of Zartus on the Moon, at Zordon's hands
By very few on Earth, after the mending of February 1995
pages.html:
The Eltarian War was the invasion of Earth by the armies of Eltar in January 1995, under Zartus, their Supreme Guardian. It lasted a matter of days. In that time Zordon's tube was smashed, the Command Center was destroyed, and three Empyreals were loosed on the world. It ended on the Moon, where Zordon killed Zartus with a piece of the Zeo Crystal.

The offer

Zartus had been Supreme Guardian of Eltar ever since Zordon was shut in his tube on Earth. He had long believed that order could be brought to the universe only through war. His weapons were the Empyreals, which burnt whole worlds clean. His watcher on Earth was the Guardian Zelya, who lived in Angel Grove as Candice Clark.

In the middle of January 1995 he came to the Command Center with soldiers. His elite, Sentry Force Four, came with him. He offered Zordon an alliance against Lord Zedd, then asked for the Power Coins. Zelya had learnt from Zedd whose creatures the Empyreals were. She exposed him. Zartus asked Zordon to come home to Eltar with him. Zordon chose Earth, telling him that the Rangers would stop him.

Zartus smashed the tube. He had Zelya seized. Then he claimed the Earth for Eltar, 'in the name of peace and justice'.

The fall of the Command Center

Billy Cranston had built a second vessel for Zordon in secret, against exactly such a day. He was working on it with Alpha 5 when Eltarian soldiers shot him in the back. They took the two of them prisoner. Sentry Force Four went after the Rangers, who fell back on Promethea. Eltarian troops closed in on it, blocking the Rangers' teleporters. Grace Sterling told them that Zordon was gone. She was in command now, she said.

The Omega Rangers had been stranded on a far world by Lord Drakkon. They were fetched out through the Master Arch in time to join the others. Zartus warned Lord Zedd to keep out of Eltar's business, which Zedd did not. Then Zartus sent in the Empyreals. They destroyed Promethea's headquarters. They destroyed the Moon Palace with Zedd inside it, as everybody supposed. They destroyed the Command Center.

The Rangers of both teams got away to Safehaven. Goldar, Squatt, Baboo and Finster, who believed their master dead, threw in their lot with them. On Earth Zartus announced that he ruled. His ships held the sky for a matter of days.

Zordon in a body of metal

Zartus believed that he had killed his old comrade. He had never known what Zordon was. A Maia cannot be killed, though he can lose the form he wears. What the tube had held was caught by Billy's second vessel. Zordon's mind had withdrawn deep into its own memories. Billy went in after him, guided by an image of the Blue Emissary that was left in the Grid, to bring him out.

He came out into a small tube that drove a body of metal. In that body Zordon went to war on his own feet for the first time in ten thousand years. He boarded Zartus's ship with Jason Lee Scott, Trini Kwan, Kimberly Hart and Finster, to free Zelya. Then he went to the Moon for the Zeo Crystal.

The Empyreals let loose

On Earth the Rangers fought Sentry Force Four, with Zedd's old servants for partners. Adam Park beat Zag with the help of Baboo. Rocky DeSantos beat Zeta with the help of Zelya. Goldar beat Zenith by himself. Billy beat Zero-Zero with the help of Squatt.

Zartus commanded the Empyreals through a crystal. Grace Sterling shattered it with the dagger she had kept since 1969. The Empyreals were free. They resolved to burn the Earth first, then everything else.

Tommy Oliver joined the White Tigerzord to Matt Cook's Dragonzord, which destroyed the Orange Empyreal. The Blue Emissary, killed a month before, rose out of it alive. The Emissary mended the Omegazords, which joined for the first time as the Ultra Omegazord. With the Thunder Megazord they destroyed the Green Empyreal. The Purple took the strength of the other two. Lord Drakkon, who had come back as master of the Horrid, threw his swarm at it. The Rangers finished it, with the Blue Emissary striking the last blow.

The Moon

Lord Zedd was alive in the ruins of his palace. Zordon found him there, so the two of them fought. Then Zordon laid down his weapon, telling Zedd to strike. Zedd did not. He saw that Zordon had never betrayed him, which meant that the Fire of Truth had been Zartus's doing.

Zartus had come to the caves beneath the palace for the power of the Zeo Crystal. The two old Guardians turned on him together. He was about to kill Zedd when Zordon drove a piece of the Crystal into his chest. Afterwards Zedd stood over Zordon, who was spent. He let Alpha 5 take him away.

Afterwards

Sentry Force Four surrendered, whereupon Eltar called its armies home. Zordon would not go back with them. He put Zelya's name forward as Supreme Guardian. The Blue Emissary went to look for the Morphin Masters. Zedd gathered his court in the ruins, then hid the palace from sight.

Zordon's body of metal was failing. The Rangers brought an empty Command Center home from the Lion Galaxy. Grace Sterling had the means of making a new tube, so Zordon went back into one. He made his peace with her. He made it with Billy too, whom he had barred from the Command Center a month before.

In February 1995 the world was mended for the second time in six months. Everything broken since Zedd's dome stood whole again. The world at large kept no memory of the Eltarian ships.

pages.title: The Emissaries Three
infobox: Emissaries Three; Red Emissary; Blue Emissary; Yellow Emissary
Mighty Morphin Power Rangers Free Comic Book Day Special (5 May 2018)
The Red Emissary; the Blue Emissary; the Yellow Emissary
Rangers, each of its own colour
Emissaries of other colours, among them the Pink
The Omega Rangers of 1994 (the Blue Emissary)
The Blue, early December 1994; the Red, later that December; the Yellow, January 1995
pages.html:
The Emissaries Three are the Red, Blue and Yellow Emissaries, the servants who speak for the Morphin Masters. Each appears as a Ranger of its own colour. In September 1994 they watched over the mending of the world after Lord Drakkon had unmade it, which is why they remembered a war that almost nobody else did. The Blue Emissary went on to make Jason Lee Scott, Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan the Omega Rangers. Within five months the Red and the Yellow were dead, while the Blue had died, then risen again.

Servants of the Masters

The Morphin Masters left their ruins under Safehaven, with the Master Arch, a gate into the Morphin Grid itself. In this age they keep apart from the world. Three servants speak for them: the Red Emissary, the Blue and the Yellow.

There are other Emissaries besides, of other colours, the Pink among them. When an Emissary dies an Empyreal rises from the death, through an ancient crystal, to serve Zartus of Eltar; three Empyreals together can remake the universe.

Shattered Grid

In September 1994, while Lord Drakkon made war on the Rangers of every year, Zordon called on the Emissaries for help. They would not act. They told him to trust his Rangers, then began to doubt themselves. In the end Drakkon broke into the Grid, beat all three, then took from them the heart of a Morphin Master, with which he unmade the world.

Tommy Oliver's spirit was waiting in a place between the worlds, where the Ranger Slayer's arrow had kept it. The Emissaries joined him there. When he had taken the heart back, they watched over the mending, warning that the world could not be made exactly as it had been. Since they belong to the Grid, they remembered the war afterwards.

The Blue Emissary's errand

The mending left cracks. The Power was leaking through them into people all over the galaxy, who were called the Empowered. The Blue Emissary wanted them found: the harmless taught, the dangerous shut away.

In October 1994 the Emissary came in secret to Jason Lee Scott, gave him back his memory of the war, then asked him to gather a team. Nobody was to be told, Zordon least of all, because the telling would endanger the mended world. Jason's price was help for Tommy. So the Emissary showed Zordon the way to the White Light. Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan walked in on Jason with the Emissary, their blasters drawn. They were given their memories too. In November 1994 the three took up the Omega powers on Safehaven, with Kiya Kyatyl as the fourth.

The Blue Emissary could be hard. The team did not want Cavotus, a Kedry who had strangled his queen, locked in the vault under Safehaven. The Emissary overruled them: sometimes a little evil had to be done for the sake of good.

The death of the Blue Emissary

Through a link between their minds Kiya had seen Drakkon in Jason's memory. When she saw this world's Tommy in white armour, she took him for Drakkon. The Emissary told her that Drakkon was the one Tommy Oliver, out of all of them, who had gone wrong. She was not comforted, for she learnt that the White Light had been the Emissary's own gift. Early in December 1994 she killed the Blue Emissary, then put on the Emissary's cloak.

The Red Emissary

Lord Drakkon was left alone in the wreck of his made world. In December 1994, soon after the Blue Emissary's death, the Red Emissary came into that ruin to look for him. An Empyreal tore the Emissary to pieces there. Early in January 1995 the Omega Rangers, with Drakkon as their guide, found the Red Emissary's body in the dead remains of that world.

The Yellow Emissary

Knowing what an Emissary's death would bring, the Yellow Emissary went into hiding. In January 1995 Drakkon led the Omega Rangers to the hiding place, where the Emissary told them why. Drakkon had led the Empyreals there as well, having bargained with them for his freedom. They killed the Yellow Emissary. The last of their number rose from that death.

The Blue Emissary's return

In January 1995 an image of the Blue Emissary, left in the Grid, led Yale of Saard to the Blue Omega morpher on Safehaven. The same image guided Billy Cranston into Zordon's memories to bring him out, after Zartus of Eltar had smashed Zordon's tube.

In the Eltarian War Tommy Oliver and Matt Cook destroyed the Empyreal that had risen from the Blue Emissary's death. The Emissary rose out of it alive. In the thick of the battle the Emissary mended the Omegazords, then struck the last blow against the last Empyreal. Afterwards the Blue Emissary went away to look for the Morphin Masters.

In February 1995 the world was mended a second time. The Red and Yellow Emissaries stayed dead.

pages.title: The Empyreals
infobox: World-burning giants, each born of the death of one of the Emissaries Three
Three: the Orange, the Green and the Purple
Zartus, Supreme Guardian of Eltar, who held them through a crystal
Gorvinos III; Hartunia; the world where the Yellow Emissary hid
pages.html:
The Empyreals were three giants that burnt whole worlds clean of life, so that those worlds could begin again on terms the Empyreals liked better. Each was born of the death of one of the Emissaries Three, the servants of the Morphin Masters. They rose in the winter of 1994 to 1995 and answered to Zartus of Eltar, who used them to clear away the peoples he judged unfit. All three were destroyed in the Eltarian War of January 1995.

Shadows of the Emissaries

The Emissaries Three, red, blue and yellow, speak for the Morphin Masters. Each of them has a shadow. When an Emissary dies, the shadow is born as an Empyreal through an ancient crystal. The new Empyreal goes straight to Zartus, who held that crystal.

One Empyreal was dangerous enough. Three together, it was said, could remake the universe. That was why the Yellow Emissary went into hiding once the other two had begun to die.

What they believed

An Empyreal did not think of what it did as destruction. It burnt a world bare of everything living, then meant to put life of its own making in the place of what had been. It called itself an instrument of change. The one that the Omega Rangers met on Gorvinos III told them that it had burnt the world clean so that it could begin again, in the name of its master.

Each of them believed itself a god. None of them was. There is one God, who made the world, and the Empyreals were not even among His great servants. Zordon of Eltar, who is a Maia and has known the true powers of creation since before the world began, was never impressed by them.

The three

The first to rise was the Orange. It was born in December 1994, when Kiya Kyatyl murdered the Blue Emissary on Safehaven. Soon afterwards the Red Emissary went into the wreck of the world that Lord Drakkon had made, looking for him. An Empyreal tore the Emissary to pieces there, and the second rose.

The Empyreals had a use for Drakkon. They offered him his freedom, with his powers to follow, if he would bring them to the Yellow Emissary. He agreed. They kept a hold in his mind afterwards, which punished him with pain whenever he disobeyed. In January 1995 he led them to the Emissary's hiding place, where they killed him. The last of the three, the Purple, rose from his death.

Gorvinos III and Hartunia

At the turn of the year the Omega Rangers came to Gorvinos III and found it burnt clean of life. The Empyreal that had done it was still there. They fought it, barely came away, then took the news to Zordon. It was to learn more about these creatures that they carried Lord Drakkon off from his cell under the Command Center.

Early in January 1995 the Orange Empyreal came to Hartunia. Its emperor, Rether Til, would not be helped. Its empress, Evor Til, died getting her people out. The Empyreal destroyed the planet, which was how the Omega Rangers learnt that it answered to Zartus. Not long afterwards the three Empyreals burnt the world where the Yellow Emissary had hidden, with the Omega Rangers sheltering underground on it.

The Eltarian War

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus smashed Zordon's tube, claimed the Earth for Eltar, then sent in the Empyreals. They destroyed Promethea's headquarters, Lord Zedd's palace on the Moon and the Command Center.

Grace Sterling of Promethea broke the crystal through which Zartus held them, using the dagger she had kept since 1969. They were his no longer. Free, they resolved to burn the Earth first, then everything else.

Tommy Oliver joined his White Tigerzord to Matt Cook's Dragonzord, and the two of them destroyed the Orange Empyreal. Out of it rose the Blue Emissary, alive. The Emissary mended the Omegazords in the thick of the fight. Joined as the Ultra Omegazord, they brought down the Green with the Thunder Megazord. The Purple took the strength of the other two. It refused Lord Drakkon's offer of a partnership, so he turned the Horrid, the life-eating swarm he now commanded, loose on it. The Blue Emissary struck the last blow.

In February 1995 the world was mended for the second time in six months. The world at large kept no memory of those weeks, so it does not remember the Empyreals either.

pages.title: The Esoteric Order of Dagon
infobox: Order of Dagon; Esoteric Order of Dagon
The Shadow over Innsmouth (Visionary Publishing Company, April 1936)
A cult of the Deep Ones
The old Masonic Hall on New Church Green, Innsmouth
Robes, and tall tiaras of a whitish gold
pages.html:
The Esoteric Order of Dagon is the religion that Captain Obed Marsh brought home to Innsmouth, Massachusetts, from the South Seas. Its members worship Father Dagon and Mother Hydra, the gods of the Deep Ones. They pay for the sea's gold with sacrifices, then with their own children. By the early twentieth century it was the only religion in the town that counted. The raid of 1928 broke it in Innsmouth, but not everywhere.

The Order in Innsmouth

Obed Marsh founded the Order after he brought the Deep Ones' bargain back from the Carolines. It took over the old Masonic Hall on New Church Green. The town's churches lost their congregations to it, one after another, and those who would not join it learnt to keep quiet.

Its priests wear robes and tall tiaras. The tiaras are of a whitish gold, worked in patterns of no known school. One of them found its way into the museum of the historical society at Newburyport.

The oaths

There are three oaths of Dagon, taken one after another. The first binds a member to secrecy. The deepest of them binds a member to the Deep Ones in marriage, and the children of such marriages have the Innsmouth look.

Its god

The Dagon of the Order is the Dagon of the Philistines, whose image fell on its face before the Ark of the Lord at Ashdod. The Order calls the Deep Ones' bargain a blessing. By that bargain a Christian town of New England was led away from its churches in a single generation.

After the raid

In February 1928 the federal raid on Innsmouth broke the Order there, and most of its members were taken away. It lived on in other places. Its best-known offshoot is the Exalted Circle, a wealthy branch in the cities, which in time broke away from the Order to go its own way.

pages.title: The Fate (New York)
infobox: A secret order of sorcerers and criminals
Broken by Delta Green in the 2000s
pages.html:
The Fate is a secret order of sorcerers and psychopaths at the heart of the occult underworld of New York. Its brain is Stephen Alzis, who is said to be able to talk a man's own shadow into betraying him. Its arm is the Network, a criminal syndicate that even the Mafia fears. It is whispered that Alzis is no man at all, but Nyarlathotep in one of his many masks.

The order

The Fate is ranked in three grades: the Lords at the top, then the Adepts, then the Neophytes. Its members are sorcerers, or would like to be, and many of them are murderers as well. Between them they hold a great store of occult books and objects.

The Network

The Network is the Fate's face to the criminal world. Through it the Fate takes contracts from the gangs of New York and sells them what its magic can do. Even the Mafia steps carefully round it.

Club Apocalypse

Stephen Alzis keeps his office in the basement of Club Apocalypse, a New York nightclub. Those who owe him favours are summoned there, and sooner or later he calls the favours in.

The fall of the Fate

In the 2000s Nyarlathotep stopped answering the Fate, and Stephen Alzis vanished. Delta Green moved in and killed most of the Lords. The survivors fled with what they could carry of the order's holdings. Club Apocalypse was bought by a company called Star Holding and Investment.

In the world

The public knows nothing of the Fate. None of the heroes of New York is known to have crossed its path.

pages.title: The feud of Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner
infobox: Aquaman, King of Aquaman's Atlantis; Namor, the Sub-Mariner, King of the Sub-Mariner's Atlantis
Which of their kingdoms is the true Atlantis
Iceland (1942); the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (1965); Rockall (1979); Godzilla's passage (1979); the United Nations (1981); the risen ruins (1987); the salvage war (1990); Superman's funeral (1992)
The Invaders; the All-Star Squadron; the Justice League; the Avengers; Captain America; Superman; the Martian Manhunter; Zatanna; the Black Widow
Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story, which was Númenor
pages.html:
The feud of Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner is the long, bitter and very petty quarrel between the two kings who each claim to rule the true Atlantis. It began over a U-boat off Iceland in 1942. It has since drawn in the Justice League and the Avengers more times than either team cares to count. Neither king is right. The Atlantis of the old story was Númenor, as Albus Dumbledore has tried to tell them both, several times, without the slightest success.

Two kings of one name

There are two kingdoms under the sea that call themselves Atlantis. The Sub-Mariner's empire lies under the Antarctic sea, a nation of blue-skinned people who breathe water and worship Neptune. Aquaman's kingdom of Poseidonis lies in the deeps of the Atlantic, a nation of pale people descended, by their own chronicles, from the islanders of a drowned city. Each says it is the only Atlantis. Neither has ever sent the other an ambassador.

Their histories cannot both be true, and each kingdom uses the other's against it. The empire says its people found the island of Kull's day, sunk in the Cataclysm about 18,000 BC, and inherited it. Poseidonis says its own island of Orin sank about 8000 BC, and that the blue folk simply moved into somebody else's ruins. The empire says a people that needed sorcery to breathe water was never a people of the sea. Poseidonis says an Atlantis at the bottom of the world, under the Antarctic ice, is a contradiction in terms.

They even quarrel over their god. Namor's kings carry the Trident of Neptune. Aquaman's keep the trident of Poseidon. Neptune and Poseidon are two names for one god, so the sea god's own trident cannot be in both places at once. Each king regards this as conclusive proof that the other's is a fake.

The two kingdoms are described on their own pages, The Sub-Mariner's Atlantis and Aquaman's Atlantis.

Two princes

Part of the trouble is that the two men are so alike. Both were born about 1920, within a year of each other, the half-human sons of Atlantean women and surface men who worked the sea: a sea captain in Namor's case, a lighthouse keeper in Aquaman's. Both came out of the water in the years before the war. Both breathe air as well as water. Both weaken if they stay too long out of the sea. Neither of them can bear to be reminded of any of this.

Where they differ, they each find something to resent. Namor came to public notice in 1939, two years first, and has never let Aquaman forget it. Namor can fly. Aquaman can call every creature in the sea to his side, which Namor dismisses as fish-herding. Namor's crown came to him by blood, Aquaman's by the vote of a council, and Namor regards an elected king as a sort of mayor. Aquaman, for his part, points out that the hereditary prince of Atlantis spent most of the 1950s sleeping in a doorway on the Bowery.

Their names for each other have not improved with the years. Namor calls Aquaman the fish-herder, the heir of Kordax or, in his gentler moods, the mayor of Poseidonis. Aquaman calls Namor the iceberg, or the gentleman in the bathing drawers.

The U-boat off Iceland, 1942

They first met in the spring of 1942, in the North Atlantic, off Iceland. A U-boat had been stalking an Allied convoy bound for Murmansk. Namor, with the Invaders, and Aquaman, of the All-Star Squadron, each went after it without knowing the other was there. They reached it at the same moment, from opposite sides.

Each claimed the kill. By the time they had finished arguing about it the argument had become a fight, and the U-boat's crew had abandoned the boat to row away in their lifeboats. The captain of a British destroyer on the convoy's screen recorded in his log that he had watched two gentlemen, one in green bathing drawers and one in an orange shirt, dispute possession of a German submarine in the water for the better part of an hour. The submarine sank while they were at it. Both of them still claim it.

The question of which of them had the right to call himself a prince of Atlantis came up within the first few minutes. It has never gone away since. For the rest of the war the Invaders and the All-Star Squadron took care to keep them on different oceans.

Dumbledore's first try, 1945

In the summer of 1945, after his duel with Greta Grindelwald, Albus Dumbledore sought out both princes in turn. He speaks Mermish and has friends in deep water. He told each of them the same thing: that the Atlantis of the old story was Númenor, which had gone down long before either of their kingdoms was founded, and that neither of them had the right to its name.

Namor told him that a wizard had no business telling a prince of Atlantis the history of his own people. Aquaman, more politely, said that his mother's city kept records older than Hogwarts, which was perfectly true and did not answer the point. Each later learnt that Dumbledore had spoken to the other. Each concluded that the other had put him up to it.

The Bowery years

Some time after 1946 Namor lost his memory and vanished. For the best part of fifteen years his empire had no prince, and the quarrel had only one party. Poseidonis made the most of it. Its people began to speak of their kingdom as the only Atlantis, and the surface world, which had forgotten the Sub-Mariner, mostly agreed.

Aquaman grew famous in those years. The newspapers took to calling him the King of the Seven Seas, though he was not yet king of anything. At the turn of 1960 he was one of the founders of the Justice League.

When Johnny Storm gave Namor back his memory in 1962, he went home to find his city wrecked by the surface world's nuclear tests and his people scattered. He then found out what Aquaman had been doing. It is generally agreed that he took the second discovery worse.

Two crowns, 1964 to 1966

In 1964 the council of Poseidonis asked Aquaman to be its king, and he was crowned King of Atlantis. Namor, who was still only a prince, learnt of it from a surface newspaper. Within months he set out to win the Trident of Neptune, the sign of his own kings, from its hiding place. He came home with it in 1966 and was crowned in his turn. He has always denied any connection between the two crowns. Nobody believes him.

Dumbledore wrote to both of them in the year of Aquaman's coronation. His letter to Aquaman congratulated him, then went on for several pages about Númenor. Aquaman thanked him warmly for the congratulations and said nothing about the rest. Namor burnt his.

The Mid-Atlantic Ridge, 1965

In 1965 an undersea survey found ruins on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Both kingdoms claimed them, and both sent warriors to hold them. Before long two armies faced each other across the ridge, with the shipping lanes of the North Atlantic above them, and the surface world began to notice.

The Justice League went down to restrain Aquaman, its own founding member. The Avengers went down to restrain Namor, whom they had been fighting on and off since 1964. Superman stood in the gap between the two armies for three days, with Captain America beside him. Captain America had brought Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch. Between them they talked the kings into going home. The ruins turned out to be a Portuguese fort that had slid into the sea in an earthquake in the 1700s. Both kings have since written to say that they knew this all along.

Grief, 1971 and 1977

Twice, grief came close to ending the feud. In 1971 Namor married the Lady Dorma, who had loved him all his life, and she was murdered on their wedding day by Llyra of Lemuria. Aquaman's wedding gift, a crown of black pearls, reached Atlantis the morning after. Namor sent it back unopened.

In 1977 Black Manta killed Aquaman's son, Arthur Curry junior, at twelve years old. Namor said nothing at all, in public or in private. For the whole of the following year, though, no ship of his empire crossed into the waters of Poseidonis, and none of his warriors spoke Aquaman's name. It is the only truce in the history of the feud. It ended in 1978, when Namor's court published a new map.

Rockall, 1979

In 1979 Dumbledore tried again, this time with both kings at once. Zatanna, who had joined the Justice League the year before, carried his invitation to Aquaman. She told the League nothing about who had sent it. The place he chose was Rockall, a lonely stump of granite in the North Atlantic, far from either kingdom.

Both kings came. Dumbledore set out the whole history of Númenor, with maps. The two of them agreed, for the first and only time in their lives, that he was wrong. They then fell out over which of them had said so first. By nightfall they had moved on to the question of who owned Rockall, which Britain, Ireland, Iceland and Denmark have argued about for years. Neither king has the faintest claim to it. Dumbledore left them to it.

Godzilla's passage, 1979

In July 1979 Godzilla, the great reptile of Japan, walked off the end of Manhattan into the Atlantic after two years in America. He was going home to the Pacific by way of Cape Horn, though nobody knew it at the time. His road ran the whole length of the ocean, past Poseidonis first, then through the waters of Namor's empire.

Aquaman met him on the sea bed with every whale he could call. He had read what became of Superman in 1954, so he made no attempt to stop him. The whales swam on either side to keep Godzilla clear of the domes of Poseidonis. They kept him company all the way south. At the edge of the Antarctic sea Aquaman turned back.

Namor took this as an act of war. The mayor of Poseidonis, he said, had driven a monster into his kingdom. Then he found out which monster it was. Namor had fought the same enemy as Godzilla in Suruga Bay in 1971, where he had decided that Godzilla was a fellow sufferer from the surface world's bombs. He declared Godzilla a guest of Atlantis. He went out to escort him past the city walls in person.

Aquaman's court replied that the iceberg was claiming the credit for a walk the whales had arranged. The letters went on until Christmas. Godzilla, who had walked from New York to the Pacific without once changing his pace, does not appear to have noticed either king.

The United Nations, 1981

In 1981 both kingdoms applied to the United Nations for recognition, each as the sole and true Atlantis. Their delegations arrived in New York on the same morning. Their bodyguards met in the lobby of the General Assembly building, with results that took the Justice League and the Avengers most of an afternoon to clear up.

The General Assembly referred both applications to a committee. They are there still. Each kingdom regards the other's application as the reason for the delay.

Two teams, 1985

In 1985 Aquaman left the Justice League, the Detroit League he had founded the year before. The same year Namor joined the Avengers. Namor's explanation, given to a reporter, was that he preferred a team whose headquarters were in New York rather than in a bunker in Detroit. Aquaman took this personally, as it was meant.

For the next three years the Avengers had to keep Namor well away from any business that touched the Justice League. Any case that involved the sea had to be checked first for Aquaman.

The risen ruins, 1987

In the autumn of 1987 an undersea earthquake lifted a stretch of drowned ruins out of the Atlantic, west of the Azores. For nine days they stood above the waves, streaming water, while the world's newspapers called them Atlantis.

Both kings arrived on the first morning to plant their flags. The new Justice League International sent the Martian Manhunter with a team to keep the peace. The Avengers sent theirs. The two kings fought across the ruins for most of a week regardless. On the ninth day the ground gave way beneath them, and the ruins went back into the sea, with both kings still on them.

Dumbledore studied the photographs. The stones, he said afterwards, were older than either kingdom. They belonged to neither of the islands that the two kings claimed.

The salvage war, 1990

In 1990 Namor's surface company, Oracle Incorporated, bought the salvage rights to a great stretch of the Atlantic seabed from three governments. Most of it lay in waters Aquaman counts as his own. When the company's ships arrived, Aquaman had every whale in the North Atlantic sit on their cables.

Both kings went to law. Both kings also went to the heroes. Members of both teams spent a long, cold fortnight at sea between the salvage fleet and an extremely large number of whales. The case is still before the courts, and the whales have gone home.

Superman's funeral, 1992

Superman died in Metropolis on 18 November 1992. Both kings came to his funeral, and the feud reached its lowest point there. Each insisted, as King of Atlantis, on taking precedence over the other in the procession. They argued in whispers at first, then not in whispers, while the coffin went by.

The Martian Manhunter, who had been Superman's friend for more than thirty years, took Aquaman by the arm. The Black Widow, who had chaired the Avengers since that year, took Namor by his. Neither of them said a word. The two kings walked in silence for the rest of the day, at opposite ends of the procession. When Superman came back to life in 1993, neither of them mentioned the funeral to him.

In 1992 Dumbledore wrote to them both for the last time, with a copy of his notes on the risen ruins of 1987. Namor's reply came from the lawyers of Oracle Incorporated. Aquaman's letter came back unopened, and wet.

The truth

Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story. Both are real, and both are old. But the great island empire that grew proud, made war on the powers of the West and was swallowed by the sea was Númenor. The Elves called it Atalantë, the Downfallen. It went down late in the Second Age, ages before Kull was born, long before either kingdom was founded. The island of Kull's day was a land of barbarian tribes, and the island of Orin was another place again. Myth has mixed into the story the memory of the star-faring city of the Ancients too.

No living man or woman knows the whole truth of it except Albus Dumbledore. He has told both kings, in person and in writing, four times in fifty years. Neither of them believes a word of it. Each of them is quite certain that the other put him up to it.

1994

In the summer of 1994, with crowds outside the United Nations demanding an end to superhumans, both kingdoms have drawn back into the deep. Neither king has been seen on the surface since the spring. The feud has gone back to letters, which neither king answers, and to maps, on which neither kingdom shows the other.

pages.title: The feud of Darkseid and Thanos
infobox: Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips; Thanos, the Mad Titan
The Cosmic Cube (1973); the Soul Gems (1977); the race for the Infinity Gems (1990); the Infinity Gauntlet (1991); Doomsday on Apokolips (1994)
The Avengers, the Justice League, Captain Mar-Vell, Adam Warlock, the Green Lantern Corps, the Silver Surfer, Superman
pages.html:
The feud of Darkseid and Thanos is the long enmity between the Lord of Apokolips and the Mad Titan. It began in 1973 over the Cosmic Cube, and it has dragged the heroes of Earth into one quarrel after another ever since. The two of them want very nearly opposite things. Thanos wants the universe dead, as a gift for the lady he loves; Darkseid wants it on its knees, and a dead universe cannot kneel.

Two tyrants

Darkseid had heard of Thanos long before they met, and Thanos of him. Each of them rules by fear, and each is used to being the most frightening thing in any room he enters. A room with both of them in it has never gone well.

Their quarrel is also about Death. Darkseid has no use for love, which he tried once, and he holds Thanos's devotion to Death of the Endless in open contempt. Thanos, for his part, thinks the Anti-Life Equation a coward's way of ending a universe, since it would leave everything alive and nothing living.

The Cosmic Cube, 1973

The feud began in 1973, when Thanos seized the Cosmic Cube, a device that could make any wish real. Darkseid saw in it the nearest thing to the Anti-Life Equation he had yet found, since a strong enough wish could make every mind in the universe obey. He sent his son Kalibak to take it, with an army of Parademons, through a Boom Tube: one of the roaring doorways by which the New Gods cross the universe.

The Parademons came out of the sky over the Pacific coast of America in their thousands. The Justice League came down from its satellite to fight them, while the Avengers and Captain Mar-Vell went into space after Thanos himself. For two days the two teams fought what amounted to the same war without ever meeting.

Thanos dealt with Kalibak personally. He broke his jaw and threw him back through his own Boom Tube, but the interruption cost him dearly. In the confusion Mar-Vell got to the Cube and broke its power. Thanos has blamed Darkseid for the loss of the Cube ever since, and Darkseid blames Thanos for losing it.

The Soul Gems, 1977

In 1977 Thanos gathered the Soul Gems, meaning to snuff out the stars of the universe one by one as an offering to Death. Earth's sun was to be among the first.

Darkseid does not save universes. He did, however, send DeSaad to the Justice League's satellite with the position of Thanos's ship, which was the nearest he has ever come to asking anybody for help. Superman did not trust the message, but he passed it on to the Avengers. The Guardians of the Universe, who had come to the same conclusion by other means, sent the Green Lantern Corps to stand guard over the stars Thanos had marked.

The Avengers went up with Captain Mar-Vell, the Thing, Spider-Man and Adam Warlock. They fought their way aboard Thanos's ship, and Warlock turned Thanos to stone.

That was the moment Darkseid had been waiting for. As the ship broke up, Parademons poured out of a Boom Tube to take the gems from the wreck. The Justice League, which had expected something of the kind, was waiting for them. In the scramble the gems were scattered across the universe, and Darkseid got none of them.

On Apokolips the news of Thanos's death was celebrated by order. The Lowlies were given a holiday, their first for some centuries, and told to enjoy it. Some years later Darkseid sent Kalibak to break the stone figure of Thanos into gravel. Kalibak hammered at it for most of a day and could not chip it.

The race for the Infinity Gems, 1990

At the end of 1989 Death brought Thanos back to life. He soon learnt that the gems he had once called the Soul Gems were the six Infinity Gems, and that whoever held all of them would hold the universe. By then each of them was in the keeping of one of the Elders of the Universe.

Darkseid wanted them as badly as Thanos did. All through 1990 the two of them raced each other for the gems, and Thanos won every race. He took them from the Elders one by one, by cunning, by force or at the gaming table. Granny Goodness's Female Furies reached the Collector a day after Thanos had left him.

The Silver Surfer, who had been following Thanos since his return, found the Furies instead. He sent them home.

The Infinity Gauntlet, 1991

In 1991 Thanos set all six gems in a single gauntlet and became master of the universe. Then, to please Death, he wiped out half of all living things with a gesture.

Half the Lowlies of Apokolips went with them, and half of Darkseid's Parademons. Thanos took particular care that Darkseid himself should not be among the vanished. He wanted him to watch.

For the first time in living memory, Darkseid came himself. He stood with the cosmic powers that rose against Thanos, while Captain America led what was left of Earth's heroes into space beside them: the Avengers, the Justice League, the Silver Surfer and Adam Warlock, who was back from the dead. Thanos killed the heroes. He turned Darkseid into a statue of glass, which he said was a fair exchange for the years he had spent as stone.

None of it lasted. Nebula, Thanos's granddaughter, seized the gauntlet from him and undid the day, so that almost nobody remembers it. Darkseid does. Of everything Thanos has ever done to him, the glass is the thing he minds most.

Thanos among the heroes

In 1992 and 1993 Thanos fought more than once on the side of Earth's heroes, against threats he liked even less than he liked them. Darkseid has let it be known that he finds this more contemptible than anything Thanos ever did before.

Doomsday, 1994

In the spring of 1994 Doomsday, the creature that had killed Superman, rose again far from Earth and fought its way across Apokolips. Superman went after it. For a few days the Lord of Apokolips had to put up with Superman on his own world, which neither of them enjoyed.

On Apokolips it is believed that Thanos showed Doomsday the way there. Nobody has ever proved it. Thanos has never troubled to deny it.

The feud and the heroes

The feud has done Earth's heroes very little good. The Avengers and the Justice League have both been caught between the two tyrants more than once, usually without knowing at first which of them they were fighting. Neither team has ever been thanked by either.

It has also brought the two teams together. Twice in the 1970s, in 1973 and 1977, the Avengers fought the same war as the Justice League. In 1991 they died together, on a day that was afterwards undone.

1994

In the summer of 1994 the feud is unresolved. Thanos lives quietly on a distant world, or says he does. Darkseid keeps the Cyborg Superman's life force in a small sphere and waits, as he always does. Neither of them has ever ended a quarrel in his life.

The end of the feud

The feud outlasted the twentieth century by a good many years. It ended about 2037, when Darkseid died with Apokolips in his last war on New Genesis. Thanos had no part in it. The quarrel was ended after all, though by neither of them.

pages.title: The Followers of Set
infobox: Set (Antediluvian), worshipped as a god in Egypt; said by his followers to sleep
Harmed by bright light, and burnt worse than other Kindred by the sun
The Serpents of the Light (Sabbat)
pages.html:
The Followers of Set are a clan and a religion: vampires who worship their founder, Set, as a god. They serve him by corrupting others through vice, addiction and temptation. The clan came out of Egypt, the heir of Stygia and of the dark craft Stygia kept. It stands outside both the Camarilla and the Sabbat. Other Kindred call them Setites, or the Serpents.

Set

Set was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, the Antediluvians, Embraced about 9300 BC by the childer of Cain in Enoch, the First City. His followers do not count him a vampire like other vampires. They worship him as a god who took the blood. They teach that he is the Old Serpent, whom Stygia worshipped in its black temples before the Flood, come again. The histories of the other clans count him only as one of the thirteen, Embraced long after the waters had gone down.

Like every vampire descended from Cain, Set belongs to the Devil. The Garou name him a creature of the Wyrm, which is the Devil by another name. Scripture calls the Devil himself that old serpent, and the Garou say the serpent of the Stygian temples stank of the Wyrm. Whichever story is true, the Setites' god is the Devil's creature either way.

No record tells where Set went after the fall of the First City, or after Cain cursed the clans and departed into Nod about 8980 BC. He is next known in Egypt. His followers believe that he lies sleeping now. One day, they say, he will rise to rule, and every soul they corrupt prepares the way for him.

Stygia and Egypt

Stygia was the kingdom beyond the River Styx in the Hyborian Age. It did not invent dark magic, but it kept, collected and practised the craft of Morgoth on a great scale. Most of the dark spells still in use derive in part from what it held. Its people worshipped a great serpent in black temples by the warm seas, and fed it; its sorcerers learnt their art in those temples. The Flood that ended the Ice Age drowned it.

About 3100 BC Egypt rose as Stygia's descendant, the heir to its dark craft. Everything the European wizarding tradition calls ancient and dark came through Egypt first. From there it passed to Greece, then to Rome, and so at last to Britain.

Into that inheritance came Set. By about 3000 BC he was worshipped in Egypt as a god: the lord of the desert, of storms and of foreign lands, whom the Egyptians also called Sutekh. He murdered his brother Osiris, then fought Horus, the son of Osiris, for the throne of Egypt. His cult, mortal and undead, endured in the temples of Egypt for thousands of years. From it the clan takes its rites, its priesthood and its serpent.

About 2900 BC Set laid a great curse on the Silent Striders, the Garou tribe of the Nile, who had fought him. It drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their ancestors. The Striders have hated vampires more than any other tribe has ever since.

Nature and Disciplines

Setites have Obfuscate and Presence. They also have Serpentis, the clan's own Discipline, which no other clan has learnt. With it a Setite can hold a victim still with his eyes, grow a serpent's forked tongue and fangs, harden his skin into scales, or take the shape of a great cobra. Its oldest masters can cut out their own hearts and hide them for safekeeping, so that a stake through the chest finds nothing to pin.

Their curse is light. They suffer more than other vampires in sunlight, which burns them worse and faster. Even bright lamps dazzle them, so they keep their temples and havens dim.

Faith and practice

Every Setite is a priest of Set. Most of the clan follow the Path of Typhon, a way of life that treats ordinary morals as chains and honours Set by breaking them. The clan teaches that to free a soul from its scruples, by offering it whatever it most wants, is to serve the god.

Setites Embrace those with a gift for persuasion, or a taste for the forbidden: priests, smugglers, dealers, courtesans, artists and criminals. For most of their history they were drawn from Egypt, Nubia and North Africa. They now Embrace across the world.

They keep temples hidden in the cities, each under its own priest. Around each temple lies a web of mortal servants, ghouls and debtors. They deal in drugs, flesh, money and secrets. They will sell their services, and their vices, to any Kindred who will buy. Other clans find them useful but do not trust them, and many princes of the Camarilla forbid them their cities.

From Egypt to the world

From Egypt the Setites spread along the trade roads of Africa and the Mediterranean, then across the world. They built temples in the cities of the Greek and Roman world, as well as in the kingdoms south of the Sahara. In the Middle Ages they sold their vices in Christian and Muslim lands alike. Their customers, mortal or Kindred, would never have admitted to buying.

They stayed out of the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century, were no party to the Convention of Thorns in 1493 and have remained independent since. A few, the Serpents of the Light, a line out of the Caribbean, have broken with the temples and gone over to the Sabbat.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Followers of Set keep temples in cities on every continent, many of them in Africa, the Caribbean and the Americas. They trade above all in drugs, which suit their faith as well as their purses. They are no party to the agreement the Camarilla made with the wizarding world in 1900, so nothing binds them to leave a witch or wizard alone.

Among the best known of them are Kemintiri, an ancient of the clan whom the Camarilla has long hunted, and Hesha Ruhadze, a scholar who deals in antiquities.

Enemies

The Setites have made enemies across the world. The Silent Striders have not forgiven Set's curse, and hunt his followers wherever they find them. The Camarilla distrusts the clan. The Sabbat, which means to fight the Antediluvians when they wake, despises a clan that worships one.

In Egypt their oldest enemies are the undying servants of Osiris and Ma'at. These are the risen dead who guard the tombs, weighing the hearts of those who enter uninvited.

In the saga

In the summer of 1993, in Egypt, Fred and George Weasley tried to shut Percy in a pyramid. One of those guardians, all bandages, sat up on its slab. It asked Percy whether he had lived with a true heart, what he had done with the years given him, and whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. Percy answered for about ten minutes, with examples, and it lay back down. Bill Weasley said afterwards that it does that to everyone who goes in uninvited.

pages.title: The forbidden books
infobox: Unaussprechlichen Kulten; De Vermis Mysteriis; Cultes des Goules; Liber Ivonis
H. P. Lovecraft; Robert E. Howard; Robert Bloch; Clark Ashton Smith; Delta Green
The Pnakotic Manuscripts; the Book of Eibon; De Vermis Mysteriis; Cultes des Goules; Unaussprechlichen Kulten
The Pnakotic Manuscripts, begun by no human hand
On the shelves of the Starry Wisdom church, Providence, 1935
Lock them away, or burn them
pages.html:
The forbidden books are the handful of volumes in which men have written down what they learnt of the Great Old Ones and the Outer Gods. The Necronomicon and the play called The King in Yellow are the most famous, with pages of their own. The rest are rarer, but no safer: the Pnakotic Manuscripts, the Book of Eibon, De Vermis Mysteriis, Cultes des Goules and Unaussprechlichen Kulten.

The Pnakotic Manuscripts

The Pnakotic Manuscripts are the oldest of them, and were not begun by men. Their first pages are said to have been written by the Great Race of Yith, and copied by men long afterwards. In the far north of the elder world, before the ice came down, the men of Lomar kept them.

What survives is in fragments, scattered through a few libraries. It tells of the Elder Things, of the Great Race and of gods older than any record.

The Book of Eibon

The Book of Eibon is the work of Eibon of Mhu Thulan, a wizard of the far north before the ice, who served Tsathoggua. It tells of his journeys, to places that are not on the Earth, and of his rites. It survives only in fragments, in Latin as the Liber Ivonis and in French.

De Vermis Mysteriis

De Vermis Mysteriis, the Mysteries of the Worm, is the book of Ludvig Prinn. He claimed to have been taken prisoner on the Ninth Crusade in 1271 and taught by the wizards of Syria. He was burnt at the stake in Brussels in the time of the witch trials, which, if his claim was true, made him very old indeed by then.

His book holds the spell for calling down a thing from the stars that drinks blood, and is unseen until it has drunk. It speaks of Father Yig, among others.

Cultes des Goules

Cultes des Goules is the work of the Comte d'Erlette, a French nobleman, on the cults of those who feed on the dead. In New Orleans the DeMonte family, which is not wholly human, has kept rites of that kind for generations, and Delta Green knows of them.

Unaussprechlichen Kulten

Unaussprechlichen Kulten, the Nameless Cults, is the work of Friedrich Wilhelm von Junzt, a German scholar who spent his life among the secret cults of the world. It was printed in Düsseldorf in 1839, in fewer than a thousand copies, and those who know it call it the Black Book. Von Junzt came to a gruesome end, and when word of it got about, most of the owners of the book burnt their copies.

A careless English translation was published in London in 1845 by Bridewall. A handsome but heavily cut edition came out in New York in 1909, which hardly anybody could afford. The book is full of keys: von Junzt uses the word time after time, for stones, temples and places, without ever saying what they open.

The King in Yellow

The King in Yellow is the youngest of the forbidden books, and the most widely read. It is a play in two acts, printed as a book, whose author nobody knows. When translated copies reached Paris in 1895 the French government seized them. It has been banned or burnt nearly everywhere since, and it still turns up on shelves where nobody remembers putting it.

Its first act is harmless. Its second breaks those who read it. Delta Green burns every copy it finds, under the STATIC Protocol of 1955. The play has a page of its own.

The shelves of the Starry Wisdom

In 1935 Robert Blake found most of these books together, rotting on the shelves of the old Starry Wisdom church on Federal Hill in Providence. There was a Latin Necronomicon, the Liber Ivonis, Cultes des Goules, Unaussprechlichen Kulten, De Vermis Mysteriis and the Pnakotic Manuscripts. Nobody had read them for nearly sixty years. Blake read them, and died that August.

Delta Green and the books

Delta Green treats every one of these books as dangerous. Its agents are taught to read as little of them as they can, and to lock away or burn whatever they find.

In the late 1990s the American Museum of Natural History in New York kept a hidden collection, the D Stacks, where Dr Jensen Wu catalogued what could not be catalogued. Delta Green had friends there. The library of Miskatonic University holds more of these books than any other in America.

pages.title: The Four Years War
infobox: The Four Years War, for Star Trek: The Role Playing Game (FASA, 1986); Axanar first named in Star Trek, 'Court Martial' (2 February 1967)
The United Federation of Planets and the Klingon Empire
The First Battle of Axanar, 29 August 2251
Garth of Izar, captain of the Xenophon
Axanar, twice; Andromeda; Lyclydun; Tini; Webirty; Zal Vhros; Alaris
The Axanar Peace Mission, late 2251, which failed
The talks at Axanar, from May 2255; the Treaty of Axanar, 13 June 2255
The border redrawn in the Federation's favour
The Battle of Donatu V, about 2245
The war of 2267 and the Organian Peace Treaty
pages.html:
The Four Years War was the first open war between the United Federation of Planets and the Klingon Empire, fought from 2251 to 2255. It began at Axanar, where the victories of Garth of Izar became required reading at Starfleet Academy. An early peace mission to Axanar failed, though a young cadet called James T. Kirk won a decoration on it. The war ended with the Treaty of Axanar of 13 June 2255, which moved the border in the Federation's favour. The peace it made was an uneasy one, and in 2267 the two powers went to war again.

Before the war

Relations between the Federation and the Klingons had been bitter since about 2223. About 2245 their fleets met at Donatu V, near Sherman's Planet, in a battle that settled nothing. By the 2250s the militant houses of the Empire had lost patience, and they pressed several members of the High Council to strike at the Federation.

Axanar, 2251

On 29 May 2251 Captain Garth of Izar, commanding the destroyer Xenophon, sighted a Klingon cruiser near Axanar, on the border. Following it, he found that a Klingon force had occupied the Axanar system. Its commander, Admiral Kkorhetza, would not leave.

On 29 August Garth's ships fought the Klingons at Axanar, in the first battle of the war. Garth offered Kkorhetza the choice of surrender or a withdrawal to the Klingon border under a Starfleet escort. Kkorhetza refused both. Instead he declared an alliance with the people of Axanar.

The Klingon High Council declared war that September. On 29 September, in the Second Battle of Axanar, Garth beat Kkorhetza's invasion fleet of seven warships and took the admiral's surrender. An eighth Klingon ship, an assault transport, was taken whole, and it was later put on show in Starfleet's Spaceflight Museum on the Moon.

The battle made Garth's name. Starfleet made him a fleet captain, with a squadron to hold the Axanar system for the rest of the war. His victories became required reading at Starfleet Academy, where cadets went on studying them for decades.

The Axanar Peace Mission

After the Second Battle of Axanar the Federation sent a peace mission to Axanar, hoping to end the war before it spread. Among the cadets who went with it was James T. Kirk, not long at Starfleet Academy. It was his first visit to Axanar, and he was given the Palm Leaf of the Axanar Peace Mission for his part in it. Garth, who had won the war's first victories there, had no patience with peace missions.

The mission failed. The militant houses of the Empire would not hear of peace while Kkorhetza's defeat went unavenged, and the war spread along the border.

The war, 2251 to 2255

Most of the fighting was along the border. After Axanar came the battles of Andromeda in October 2251, Lyclydun in April 2252, Tini in December 2252 and Webirty in December 2253. The Klingons fed their ground forces and forward bases with new cargo ships built for the purpose. Both powers came out of the war building their warships differently.

By 2254 the Empire was tiring of a war it could not win. That February the Klingons struck at Zal Vhros, an attack that showed how frustrated they had grown. The militant houses that had wanted the war now blamed the Chancellor for the caution with which he fought it. The last battle of the war was fought at Alaris, on 7 May 2255.

The Treaty of Axanar

Later in May 2255 envoys of the two powers met at Axanar, where the war had begun, and the fighting stopped. On 13 June their talks ended in the Treaty of Axanar, which redrew the border between the Empire and the Federation. Several worlds along it passed to the Federation. The Klingons living on them were moved to the Klingon side of the new border, which took until April 2256.

Afterwards

The treaty held, uneasily, for twelve years. In 2267 war broke out again, when Klingon forces under Kor occupied Organia, until the Organians stopped both fleets and imposed the Organian Peace Treaty.

Garth's own end was a sad one. After a terrible injury the people of Antos IV healed him, teaching him their art of changing shape. He repaid them by trying to destroy their world, for by then he had lost his reason.
