At first their subjects grew stronger and quicker. Then their ridges faded, their nerves began to fail, and they died in agony.

One of the subjects had the Levodian flu, a mild illness. The flu took up the Augment genes, becoming an airborne plague. It spread from Qu'Vat across the Empire. Fleet Admiral Krell was ready to destroy the colony from orbit to stop it.

The cure

The Klingons had Dr Phlox, the Denobulan doctor of the Enterprise, kidnapped from San Francisco. General K'Vagh, whose own son, Marab, had caught the plague, gave him five days to find a cure. Phlox would not help Antaak make stable Augments. He did help him find a way to stop the virus in its first stage, which saved lives but gave the Klingons none of the strength that K'Vagh wanted.

The cure needed human antibodies. Archer, who had followed Phlox to Qu'Vat, let himself be infected to supply them. When Krell came to destroy the colony, a canister of the virus was beamed aboard his flagship, so that Krell needed the cure as much as anybody. Krell stood down. The High Council sent the cure throughout the Empire.

Section 31, the idea held in secret by a few people inside Starfleet, wanted the cure found. Harris, one of the few, told Malcolm Reed of the Enterprise to keep the ship from finding Phlox, until Reed told Archer the truth.

The mark

The Klingons whom the cure saved lived, but they lost their ridges. The change passed to their children. Antaak, who lost his own ridges, said that a great many Klingons would have to live with it. Phlox told him that one day it might be undone.

It was. By the 2270s the change had been undone, though the Klingons do not discuss with outsiders how it was done.

pages.title: The Klingons
infobox: Kahless the Unforgettable, in the ninth century
Emperors until about 2069; then the Chancellor and the High Council
Sto-vo-kor and Gre'thor; the honour of the house
pages.html:
The Klingons are a warrior people from the planet Qo'noS, who have lived since the ninth century by the code of honour that Kahless the Unforgettable gave them. Their Empire first met the people of Earth in 2151, when a Klingon courier crashed in a cornfield in Oklahoma. From about 2223 onwards they were the bitterest enemies of the United Federation of Planets.

The old stories

The Klingons are a tall, strong people with ridged foreheads, built to go on fighting through wounds that would kill a man. They prize courage above every other virtue, and they count a death in battle the best death there is. When a warrior dies, those beside him roar at the sky, to warn the dead that a Klingon warrior is on his way.

Their oldest stories are about their gods, and they end badly for the gods. Klingon legend says that the gods forged the first Klingon heart in fire and steel. Because it beat alone, they forged a second heart to beat beside it. The two hearts together were too strong for their makers: they destroyed the gods who had made them, then turned the heavens to ashes. Another story names Kortar, the first Klingon, as the killer of the gods, condemned for it to ferry the dishonoured dead to Gre'thor in a barge. It is an old Klingon saying that their ancestors killed their gods long ago, finding them more trouble than they were worth.

These are the Klingons' own beliefs. So is Sto-vo-kor, where they believe the honoured dead go to feast with Kahless. So is Gre'thor, the place of the dishonoured, guarded by the Fek'lhr. A family can still win back the honour of one of its dead, which is one reason a Klingon's honour belongs to his whole house.

Kahless and the Empire

In the ninth century the Klingons lived under a tyrant called Molor. A warrior named Kahless killed him with a sword he had made himself, united the Klingon people, then founded the Klingon Empire, with himself as its first Emperor. He gave them the laws of honour by which they have lived ever since.

In the fourteenth century a people the Klingons call the Hur'q, a word meaning outsiders, came from far across the galaxy to plunder Qo'noS. They carried off many of its treasures, the Sword of Kahless among them.

The last of the emperors died about 2069, and no other took his place. The Empire was governed instead by the High Council, drawn from the great houses, under a Chancellor who held the first seat in the great hall of the First City. When a Chancellor died, a Rite of Succession settled the matter between the claimants, sometimes by combat.

A small power among great ones

For most of their history the Klingons were a small people among great ones. The masters of the stars in those centuries were the Kree, the Shi'ar and the System Lords of the Goa'uld. None of them took any notice of a few warlike worlds round Qo'noS.

The passing of the old powers came in the twenty-first century, when most of them died out. As they passed, the Klingons went out from Qo'noS to world after world. By 2151 theirs was one of the strongest empires in that region of space.

Earth, 2151 to 2154

In April 2151 a Klingon courier named Klaang crashed in a cornfield near Broken Bow, Oklahoma, where a farmer shot him. It was the first meeting between the Klingons and the people of Earth. Against the Vulcans' advice, Starfleet sent its new ship, the Enterprise NX-01, under Captain Jonathan Archer, to take him home. Written into Klaang's blood was proof that the Suliban Cabal had been behind attacks on Klingon houses.

Earth's dealings with the Empire stayed uneasy. About 2152 a Klingon tribunal sent Archer to Rura Penthe, the Empire's frozen prison world, for helping rebels against it. His advocate, the old lawyer Kolos, told him that Klingon courts had once been courts of law and honour, before the warriors came to believe that only victory mattered. In 2153 Archer destroyed the ship of Duras, a captain who had hunted him on the High Council's orders.

In 2154 Earth's oldest trouble reached the Empire. Augments raised by the geneticist Arik Soong, from embryos left over from the programme that had made Khan Noonien Singh, seized a Klingon Bird-of-Prey, then tried to start a war between Earth and the Klingons. From the wreck of their ship Klingon scientists took Augment embryos of their own, which led to the Klingon Augment virus. The cure saved the Empire, though it left those it saved with smooth foreheads, and their children after them.

Many of the Klingons who met Starfleet in the 2260s, Kor, Koloth and Kang among them, bore that mark. By the 2270s it had been undone, by means the Klingons do not discuss with outsiders.

Enmity with the Federation

Relations with the United Federation of Planets turned bitter about 2223, and they stayed bitter. About 2245 the two powers fought the Battle of Donatu V, near Sherman's Planet, which settled nothing. The worst of those years was the Four Years War of 2251 to 2255, the first open war between the two powers. It began with Garth of Izar's victories at Axanar and ended with the Treaty of Axanar, which moved the border in the Federation's favour.

War broke out again in 2267, when Klingon forces under Kor occupied the neutral planet Organia. The Organians, beings without bodies who had seemed to be simple villagers, stopped both fleets where they stood. They were not gods, but neither side could resist them. Both had to accept the Organian Peace Treaty.

After that the two powers fought by other means. Under the treaty a disputed world went to whichever side could develop it best, so in 2268 a Klingon agent poisoned the Federation's grain for Sherman's Planet. In 2285 Commander Kruge tried to steal the secret of a Federation device for remaking dead worlds. His men killed the son of James T. Kirk, before Kirk killed Kruge and took his ship.

Praxis and the Galactic Empire

By the 2290s the Klingons had begun to build mobile suits, the Zakus, armoured fighting machines in the shape of a man. Their best commander of them was Char of Aznable, a human raised among Klingons, called the Red Comet.

On 12 February 2293 the moon Praxis, the chief source of the Empire's energy, exploded. The Klingons suspected the Federation. Envoys of the Galactic Empire, a power from a distant galaxy, came to them in secret with an offer of alliance, which they took. On 17 May Char of Aznable led a Klingon force to Starbase Side 7 to help the Imperial fleet. There it came out that the Galactic Empire had destroyed Praxis itself. The Klingons turned on it at once, fighting beside James T. Kirk's Enterprise-A.

That battle did what a century of treaties had not. On 20 August 2293 the Klingons signed the Khitomer Accords with the Federation. In the Intergalactic War of 2299 to 2300 the Galactic Empire struck them first, at Morska. They fought through that war as the Federation's allies, with a Klingon fleet carrying the Krogan to the relief of Palaven. The two powers were never truly enemies again.

pages.title: The Krogan
infobox: Tuchanka, ruined by the Krogan's own atomic wars
Huge, hard-hided reptiles with a hump on the shoulders
Two or more of nearly every vital organ; very quick to breed, before the genophage
The Salarians, about 80, to fight the Rachni
The Rachni Wars; the Krogan Rebellions, about 700 to 800
Made by the Salarians and loosed by the Turians, about 710; one pregnancy in a thousand comes to term
Scattered and dwindling; many are mercenaries, some in the pay of the Orion Syndicate
pages.html:
The Krogan are a huge, hard-hided, quick-breeding people from Tuchanka, a world so savage that they grew a spare of nearly every organ to survive it. Having bombed themselves back into savagery with atomic weapons, they were raised up by the Salarians about 80 to fight the Rachni, and they won that war for everybody. Then they turned on the peoples who had armed them. The genophage, which the Salarians made and the Turians loosed about 710, broke them. By the twenty-second century they were a scattered, dwindling people, and Earth first met them in 2155 as mercenaries of the Orion Syndicate.

Tuchanka

On Tuchanka nearly everything that lived was trying to eat everything else, and the Krogan were what came out on top. Their eyes are set so wide apart that they can see almost all the way round. Their hide turns most blades, pain does not spoil their concentration, and they carry two or more of nearly every vital organ, so that losing one or two does not kill them. The hump on a Krogan's shoulders stores fat and water. A big one is the mark of a well-fed and successful Krogan, which is to say a dangerous one.

They bred fast and grew up quickly. Before they had guns, most Krogan died in the jaws of predators. Afterwards most of them died at the hands of other Krogan. In time they learnt to make atomic weapons. They used them on each other until Tuchanka lay in a nuclear winter and the Krogan were savages again, scrabbling to stay alive among the ruins.

The uplift and the Rachni Wars

About 80 the Salarians, who were losing the Rachni Wars, came upon the Krogan in their ruins. Here, they saw, was a people that could live on the poisonous worlds of the Rachni and breed faster than the Rachni could kill them. The Salarians taught them, armed them with disruptors and gave them warp ships, then sent them against the Rachni.

It worked better than anybody had hoped. The Krogan went down into the lairs beneath the ground where the hive queens lived, which nobody else had been able to reach, and drove the Rachni back to their homeworld. The Rachni would not surrender. By about 300 the Krogan had wiped them out.

The Krogan Rebellions

The grateful alliance of the Asari and the Salarians gave the Krogan worlds of their own. Within a few generations the Krogan had filled them, and they began to spread into the worlds of others. When the alliance demanded that they leave Lusia, an Asari colony, their leader, Overlord Kredak, walked out of the talks. About 700 the Krogan Rebellions began.

The Turians, met for the first time in the middle of it, declared war on the Krogan almost at once. The Krogan answered by dropping asteroids on Turian colonies, and three Turian worlds were left uninhabitable.

The genophage

The Salarians made a disease to end the war, which they meant as a threat. The Turians, who thought that naive, made it in quantity. About 710 they loosed it on Tuchanka, its colonies and every world the Krogan held. It did not take away the Krogan's fertility. It killed their children before they were born: only one Krogan pregnancy in a thousand came to term, and the curse passed from every parent to every child.

The rebellions dragged on for decades afterwards, as beaten warlords turned pirate, but by about 800 they were over. The Krogan have never forgiven the Turians. The Salarians prefer not to discuss it.

The Krogan since

The rebellions discredited every Krogan leader who survived them, and few of their chiefs command more than a thousand warriors. Krogan trust nobody, respect strength and take what they can, like people who expect to die tomorrow. The rare females who can carry children to term are guarded, traded and fought over. A Krogan battlemaster, it is said, is worth ten soldiers of any other people.

Many Krogan sell themselves as mercenaries, mostly for work that is against the law. By the twenty-second century a good many of them fought for the Orion Syndicate, often with Vorcha beside them.

Earth and the Krogan

Earth's first Krogan came after Captain Jonathan Archer in 2155: a mercenary crew hired by the Orion Syndicate, which wanted his head. The Enterprise NX-01 beat them off. Treating a wounded prisoner, Dr Phlox found an engineered disease in his blood that let almost none of his people's children be born. He was appalled. Later that year the Salarians told Archer where it had come from, though not how it was made.

The relief of Palaven

In the Intergalactic War the Krogan fought for the alliance that Captain John Shepard gathered against the Galactic Empire. On 19 January 2300 a Klingon fleet carried a Krogan army to Palaven, where it broke the Empire's siege beside the Turians who had once loosed the genophage on them.

pages.title: The Legacy Virus
infobox: X-Force #18 (January 1993), the end of the X-Cutioner's Song
A plague made to kill mutants
Stryfe, from a plague that Apocalypse designed in the far future
Sores, fever, weariness and a cough
Moira MacTaggert; Charles Xavier; Hank McCoy
The 2040s; killed every carrier of the X-gene
pages.html:
The Legacy Virus is a plague made to kill mutants. Stryfe left it behind him at the end of 1992, and it has been killing mutants ever since. In 1994 Moira MacTaggert found that it had changed, so that ordinary people could catch it too, and that she had caught it herself. In the summer of 1994 there is no cure. One was found in 2001, and Piotr Rasputin died setting it free.

Origins

Nearly two thousand years from now, in the age when Apocalypse rules the Earth, he designed a plague to kill the last people who were not mutants. He never perfected it. Stryfe, the clone of Cable whom Apocalypse raised as his heir, took it and turned it round, against the mutants themselves.

At the end of 1992 Stryfe gave Mister Sinister a sealed canister. When Stryfe seemed to have died, Gordon Lefferts, a scientist working for Sinister, opened it, and the virus got out.

The sickness

The virus stops the body making healthy cells. Its victims break out in sores, run fevers, cough and grow tired beyond any rest. Until 1994 it touched only mutants. In the summer of 1994 nobody is known to have recovered from it.

In the summer of 1993 it killed Illyana Rasputina, the little sister of Piotr Rasputin of the X-Men. Soon afterwards it killed the illusionist Jason Wyngarde, and others followed him. In the summer of 1994 few people outside the mutant world have heard of it.

The search for a cure

Moira MacTaggert took up the work on Muir Island after Illyana died. In the spring of 1994 Charles Xavier came to work beside her. That spring she found that the virus had changed, so that ordinary people could catch it. Early in the summer she found that she had caught it herself, from cells taken from Illyana's body. She told Xavier, and nobody else.

Zero, a machine that had served Stryfe, carried the virus's secrets inside him. When he died, in the early summer of 1994, he passed them to Douglock, who could not read them.

In 1995 it came out that ordinary people could catch it, and Muir Island was besieged. In the autumn of 1997 Moira found that it could now pass through the air to any mutant. She sealed herself into quarantine, with Rahne Sinclair beside her. That year Rory Campbell sold what he knew of it to Sebastian Shaw in exchange for an artificial leg.

The cure

Late in 2000 Moira was killed on Muir Island, close to a cure. Hank McCoy finished it from her work. It could spread only through the air, and it would kill the first mutant whose body carried it.

In January 2001 Piotr Rasputin injected himself with it in secret, so that nobody else would die as his sister had. It ended the plague at once, and cured everyone who had it.

The war strain

The cure of 2001 ended the plague, but not the knowledge of how it had been made. In the 2040s, during the Third World War, a new strain was made as a weapon and let loose. The old cure was useless against it.

The new strain killed anybody who carried the X-gene, whether or not their powers had ever shown. It did what Stryfe had meant the old one to do, and more: when it had run its course there was nobody left to pass the X-gene on, so no mutant was ever born again. Of all the mutants alive when it was let loose, only Wolverine, whose healing power kept him alive, came through it.

pages.title: The Makai Knights
infobox: Makai Knight; Makai Knights; Makai Order
Swords and armour of Soul Metal
The Senate, through the Watchdogs of the east, west, north and south
To protect people; never to raise a sword against a human being
Complete: the memories of witnesses are removed
pages.html:
The Makai Knights are an old Japanese order of swordsmen who hunt the Horrors, the demons that come up out of the Makai to feed on people. Each knight fights in a suit of armour made of Soul Metal, which he may wear for 99.9 seconds at a time. They are served by the Makai Priests, who make their tools, and governed by the Senate through houses called Watchdogs. They call themselves 'those who protect'. Almost nobody outside the Order knows that they exist.

The knights

A knight is born into the work. The sons of Makai families are trained from early childhood, first at home, then together in squads under a senior knight. Only a man can be a knight, because only a man trained to it can lift Soul Metal. A woman of a Makai family becomes a priestess. The one known exception came years later: a girl named Yuna, who by 2014 had a bone from her dead father's arm set into her own so that she could carry his sword. It hurt her every time she drew it.

Most knights have no title. They are called Hagane, which means steel, after the plain grey armour they are issued. Certain families hold named armours, which pass from father to son with a title. Garo the Golden Knight is one. Others are Zero the Silver Fanged Knight, Dan the Midnight Sun Knight, Baron the Thunder Knight and Lord, the Knight of Flashing Light.

Soul Metal and the armour

Soul Metal answers to the heart of whoever holds it. To a trained knight his sword weighs almost nothing. To anybody else it is too heavy to pick up. A blade of it will cut a Horror, which ordinary steel will not.

A knight calls his armour by cutting a circle in the air above his head. It comes down on him out of the Makai. He has 99.9 seconds. If he stays in it longer the armour begins to eat him, until he becomes the mindless thing the knights call a Lost Soul Beast. The limit does not hold inside the Makai itself.

A titled knight who has slain a hundred Horrors may win a Madou Horse, a steed of living metal.

Madou tools

A titled knight carries a Madou tool, made for him by a priest: a ring, a pendant, a bracelet or a brooch with a mind of its own. It senses Horrors, knows the old lore and gives advice whether asked or not. The Golden Knight's is the ring Zaruba. Zero's is the pendant Silva, whose name means 'family'. Dan's is the bracelet Goruba, one of the oldest of all.

A knight also carries a lighter that burns with Madou fire. Held up before a person's face, the flame shows in his eyes whether a Horror is hiding behind them.

The Watchdogs and the Senate

The country is divided into districts, each under a house of the Order called a Watchdog. There are four great ones, of the east, west, north and south. A knight takes his orders from his Watchdog. He brings his sword there to be cleansed of the Horrors it holds. He answers to it when he breaks the law.

Over the Watchdogs stands the Senate, which keeps knights of its own for the gravest work. In its walls lives Gajari, a power that the knights of long ago dreamed into being. Gajari will help a knight who makes a contract with it, at a price it names afterwards.

The Order's officers are not always sound. The Eastern Watchdog has been kept for centuries by three priestesses in the bodies of little girls, who were once a single woman. They want Messiah brought into the world. In later years they secretly helped the fallen knight Barago, until Rei Suzumura cut them down in March 2006.

The law

The first rule is that a knight protects people. He may not raise his sword against a human being, however wicked, which wicked men have sometimes used against him.

A person stained with a Horror's blood must be cut down at once. Kouga Saejima broke that rule in 2005 for Kaoru Mitsuki. The Order had no cause to regret it.

A knight who falls into darkness is hunted by his own side. The priests who do that work are called Darkness Slashers.

Secrecy

Heroes in bright costumes have been a public fact since 1938, but the Order has stayed hidden. A Horror feeds at night, behind a human face, on one or two people at a time. Afterwards the knight or his priest takes away the memories of anybody who saw. Neither Superman nor the Justice League has ever been given a reason to look.

The Makai Order is one of several old bodies of hunters in the world, with very little to do with the rest. The Belmonts of Wallachia hunt Dracula. The Society of Leopold hunts vampires for the Church, as the Watchers' Council in London trains the Slayer. The Order keeps to Japan, where its quarry is the Horror alone. Vampires it leaves to those whose business they are.

In 1999 priests of the Hakuba shrine in Japan worked the rite that shut Dracula's castle inside an eclipse of the sun. The Order watches every eclipse, since Legules first crossed into the world during one. It can hardly have missed that one, though no record says that it took any part.

What they honour

The knights honour their dead, whose spirits have more than once come back to stand beside the living. They keep their vows. They do not speak of God. The enemy they fight is His enemy all the same, though no knight has ever been told whose war he is in.

Knights of note

The Saejima family has held the title of Garo for generations: Taiga Saejima, his son Kouga, then Kouga's son Raiga. In the summer of 1994 the Order has no Golden Knight, since Taiga is dead with his heir only fourteen.

Rei Suzumura became Zero, the Silver Fanged Knight, taking the title from his murdered foster father, Douji. Tsubasa Yamagatana was Dan, the knight of Kantai. Wataru Shijima, who was Baron, taught a generation of young knights, Kouga Saejima among them. Leo Fudou held his family's title of Lord in secret while he served the Senate as a priest.

Barago, once the pupil of Taiga Saejima, became Kiba, a knight of darkness who ate Horrors, then knights. Bado the Storm Knight fought him many times before dying at his hands.

The Shadowfolk are knights who work unseen. By day they find gates of Inga, so as to destroy them before anything comes through. In 2040 their old commander, Eiji Busujima, turned against the Order. His pupil Crow, the Phantom Knight, helped to stop him.

pages.title: The Makai Priests
infobox: Makai Priest; Makai Priests; Makai Priestess; Makai Priestesses
The Makai Order, beside the Makai Knights
Kantai, in the north of Japan
Amon; Garai; Jabi; Akaza; Rekka; Leo Fudou; Sigma Fudou
pages.html:
The Makai Priests are the workers of magic in the Makai Order of Japan. Where a Makai Knight fights the Horrors with a sword, a priest works with a brush, drawing seals, wards or weapons out of the air. Priests make the knights' talking Madou tools, mend their gear and keep the lore. Many of them are women, since no woman can be a knight.

The art

A priest's art is learnt, over many years, from a master. Its chief tool is the Madou Brush, with which a trained priest can throw fire, bind a Horror, heal a wound or open a way into the Makai. Priests also call up the lesser creatures of that country, such as the young Makai dragons that carry messages.

It is no part of the wizarding world's magic. It is a tradition of its own, older than wands. Mahoutokoro, the school where Japan's witches and wizards are taught, has never taught it.

The priests are older than the knights. In the earliest days of the war there was nobody else to fight the Horrors. Soul Metal came later, since when the priests have stood behind the swordsmen. Not all of them have liked it.

Kantai

Kantai is a village of priests in the forests of the north, with a Makai Knight of its own to guard it. Children of Makai families are sent there to be taught. It keeps the Phosphorus Arrow. At the rite of the Midnight Sun the arrow is shot into an eclipse, to keep the worlds apart. In 2006 the village's elder was the priestess Garai, who had taught Kouga Saejima's mother.

Priests of note

Amon is the finest maker of Madou tools of his day. He made Zaruba, the Golden Knight's ring, was the friend of Taiga Saejima, and has brought up the orphan Jabi. He likes his sake. In the summer of 1994 Jabi, a girl in her teens, is still learning from him. He was murdered in February 2006.

Akaza kept an antique shop. In 2010 he betrayed his fellow priests to the Horror Karma for a sight of his dead wife with their daughter in her mirror. He gave his life to put it right. His pupils were Rekka, who would rather have been a knight, with Shiguto, who inherited his brush.

The twins Leo Fudou and Sigma Fudou were knights by training as well as priests. Leo built fighting machines for the Senate, while secretly holding his family's armour as Lord, the Knight of Flashing Light. Sigma tried to replace the knights altogether.

Priests whose work is to hunt knights or priests who have gone over to the dark are called Darkness Slashers. Bikuu, who worked with Raiga Saejima in 2040, was one.

The Makai Guides follow a kindred calling. Elda, who served the fallen knight Barago, read the future in cards.

pages.title: The Necronomicon
infobox: Dr John Dee, in the reign of Elizabeth I; never printed
The British Museum; the Bibliothèque nationale; the Widener Library at Harvard; the University of Buenos Aires; Miskatonic University
pages.html:
The Necronomicon is the most famous of the forbidden books, a compendium of what its author learnt of the Great Old Ones and the Outer Gods, with the means of calling them. Abdul Alhazred, a poet of the Yemen whom later ages called the mad Arab, wrote it in Damascus about 730 under the title Al Azif. It has been translated, burnt, banned and copied again ever since. It still turns up where it is least wanted.

Abdul Alhazred

Abdul Alhazred was a poet of Sanaa, in the Yemen, who flourished early in the eighth century. He wandered far. He saw the ruins of Babylon, and the hidden places under Memphis. He spent ten years alone in the great empty desert of southern Arabia, which the old Arabs believed haunted.

He came to worship Yog-Sothoth and Cthulhu. In his last years, at Damascus, he wrote down what he had learnt. He called the book Al Azif, after the sound that insects make at night, which the Arabs held to be the howling of demons.

In 738 he died in Damascus. The biographer Ebn Khallikan records that he was seized in broad daylight by an invisible monster and devoured before many witnesses.

The translations

In 950 Theodorus Philetas of Constantinople translated it into Greek, and gave it the name by which it is known: Necronomicon, the image of the law of the dead. Its readers tried terrible experiments with it. In 1050 the Patriarch Michael had the Greek burnt. By then the Arabic was already lost.

In 1228 Olaus Wormius made a Latin translation from the Greek. Pope Gregory IX forbade both the Latin and the Greek in 1232. Copies survived all the same. A Latin edition was printed in black-letter in Germany in the fifteenth century, and another in Spain in the seventeenth. The Greek was printed in Italy in the first half of the sixteenth century.

In the reign of Elizabeth I, Dr John Dee, her astrologer, made an English translation. It was never printed, and survives only in fragments. Old Whateley of Dunwich owned an imperfect copy of it, which is why his grandson went looking for a better one.

The last Greek copy anybody heard of went up in flames with a Salem man's library in 1692.

Where it is now

Five libraries are known to hold copies: the British Museum in London, the Bibliothèque nationale in Paris, the Widener Library of Harvard University, the University of Buenos Aires and the library of Miskatonic University at Arkham, Massachusetts. All five keep them locked away. There are others in private hands, whose owners seldom say so.

On the night of 3 August 1928 Wilbur Whateley of Dunwich broke into the Miskatonic library to steal its copy, and was killed by the watchdog. The Latin copy on the shelves of the Starry Wisdom church in Providence was still there when Robert Blake found it in 1935.

Its readers

The Necronomicon is not safe to read. Much of it is couched in double meanings, and the cults read it for the meaning they want. Its best-known couplet begins, 'That is not dead which can eternal lie', and the cult of Cthulhu takes it for a promise. Those who read it through come away knowing too much, and the knowledge does not stay quiet in them.

Delta Green's rule for it is its rule for every such book: lock it away, or burn it, and read as little of it as possible. Wizarding libraries are said to have heard of it, which is as near as most of them wish to come.

pages.title: The Night Floors
infobox: Storeys that are not there by day
Summer 1995, by Delta Green's Operation ALICE
The door to the roof, after dark
The King in Yellow, passed from tenant to tenant
pages.html:
The Night Floors are the storeys above the Macallistar Building in Manhattan that are not there by day. In the summer of 1995 a young painter, Abigail Wright, vanished from her flat in the building, where a copy of The King in Yellow had been going from tenant to tenant. Delta Green sent agents under the name Operation ALICE. After dark they found the Night Floors, and beyond them the Night World of the King in Yellow.

The Macallistar Building

The Macallistar Building is an old stone building in Manhattan, built to look like a castle, whose flats are let cheaply to artists. In 1995 Abigail Wright, a painter, lived there. That year a copy of The King in Yellow went from hand to hand among the tenants. Abigail Wright read it.

Operation ALICE

In the summer of 1995 she vanished. A friend of Delta Green noticed an occult symbol among her papers, and the case came to Delta Green. Its agents were sent, under the name Operation ALICE, to go through the flat. They were to record anything unnatural, and to destroy whatever they found.

Her flat was bare. The carpet had been torn up and the furniture was gone. Her walls were covered with hundreds of objects, glued fast one beside another, in a collage that must have taken her hundreds of hours.

Like the girl the operation was named after, the agents went down the rabbit hole.

Above the building

After dark the door to the roof opened on a smoking room of about 1900, and beyond it on floors that should not have been there. Rooms and passages repeated themselves. They went on further than the building could hold. A night manager kept them.

Beyond the Night Floors lay the Night World, the endless country about Carcosa, where anything the King has touched may be found. No hero came. Nobody but Delta Green knew there was anything to come to.

Afterwards

Abigail Wright was not found in 1995. In time A Cell came to suspect that the agents of ALICE had been tainted by what they found. Twenty years later the Night World broke into Dorchester House in Boston, and the survivors of ALICE were called back for Operation INDIA MOON. Abigail Wright was found at last, in Carcosa.

pages.title: The No-Men
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Kamen Rider Siren' (12 September 2009)
A secret office of the United States government
Visitors from other worlds; the sleeper Eubulon
Michelle Walsh; Agent Phillips; Trent Moseley, from November 2009
The Kamen Riders of Ventara, from November 2009
pages.html:
The No-Men are a secret office of the United States government, whose business is the unexplained. For more than forty years their chief charge has been one sleeping man: Eubulon, the Advent Master, who fell into the desert of New Mexico in 1947. In the summer of 1994 he is still asleep in their keeping. In 2009 the No-Men first hunted the Kamen Riders, then sheltered them. The last weeks of the war against Xaviax were fought from their headquarters.

The sleeper

In 1947 a wounded stranger came down near Roswell, in the New Mexico desert. He was Eubulon, struck down by Xaviax on Ventara, then thrown across to Earth. He could not be healed, so he was kept in a frozen sleep, sealed in a capsule.

The office that guarded him is known as the No-Men. They kept the capsule for sixty-two years.

It was a close secret. S.H.I.E.L.D., which was founded in 1965 to deal with such threats in the open, is not known to have been let into it. The American government has never been frank about what came down near Roswell. More than one thing did that summer, and the silence about the No-Men's stranger is their own doing.

Michelle Walsh

By 2008 people were vanishing from an American city, with talk of monsters in mirrors. The No-Men put an agent on it. Michelle Walsh passed herself off as a senior reporter. In January 2009 she took on a young writer named Maya Young as her assistant. Maya had been following the disappearances for a website.

She was not a kind employer. In April she had Maya dismissed from the website, on a charge of faking evidence. She went on pressing her for what she knew. Late in the summer she tricked Maya's friend Lacey Sheridan into copying the files on Maya's computer.

The files named Kit Taylor as the Dragon Knight. On 12 September 2009 Michelle Walsh laid them before her superior. Her orders were to bring the boy in.

The Dragon caged

On 3 October two agents took Kit as he left the hospital where his father lay. He was locked in a cell at the No-Men's headquarters. They let him out once, to fight a mirror monster while they studied his armour. Michelle Walsh questioned him about the Kamen Riders, Xaviax and Ventara.

Maya's friend Trent Moseley broke into the No-Men's records with the help of two friends, which told Len where Kit was. On 17 October Kit got out by himself. He spilt water on the floor of his cell, then left through the reflection. Len of Ventara, Kase and Maya, who had come to rescue him, had to fight their own way out.

The No-Men kept after them. A week later Michelle Walsh raided the bookshop where they had gathered. On 31 October her agents seized Maya, Trent Moseley and Lacey Sheridan.

The alliance

A week after that there was one Rider left. On 7 November 2009 Michelle Walsh came to Len, bringing her three prisoners with her. She showed him a photograph. The No-Men had the Advent Master.

On 14 November Len woke Eubulon at their headquarters. From then on the two sides worked as one. The Riders whom Eubulon brought out of the Advent Void made the No-Men's base their own. Trent Moseley, who had been offered a choice between a prison cell and a desk, took the desk. It was he who found Xaviax's transmitters, one after another. The agent who recruited him was called Phillips.

On 18 December 2009 Trent Moseley went into Xaviax's stronghold with Maya Young to open the way for the thirteen Riders. Xaviax was destroyed that day. Trent Moseley stayed with the No-Men afterwards.

pages.title: The Order of Silent Hill
infobox: Order of Silent Hill; Valtiel; Vincent Smith; Father Vincent
Silent Hill, Maine; its church stands across Toluca Lake from the town
A being it takes for the maker of paradise; in truth a demon
The Holy Mother; the women saints; Valtiel
Dahlia Gillespie, to September 1983; Vincent Smith and Claudia Wolf, about 1993 to September 2000
The Silent Hill Smile Support Society, which runs Wish House
White Claudia, sold as the drug PTV
pages.html:
The Order of Silent Hill is the cult of the town of Silent Hill, in Maine. Its members call it simply the Order. It grew out of the faith of the people who first held the lake sacred. It worships a god of its own, whom it means to bring to birth in the body of a human mother. The being is real, but it is not God. It is a demon. The Order tried to bring it into the world in 1976, in 1983 and again in 2000. Each attempt ended in fire or murder.

Origins

The first people of the lake held the ground of Silent Hill holy, kept their ceremonies there and honoured the spirits of the place. The settlers who drove them out took over more of that faith than they knew. It passed down in certain families of the town, mixed with scraps of the Christianity the settlers had brought with them.

After the Civil War it hardened into a church. It had priests, a scripture, three saints in time, and a chapel on the far shore of Toluca Lake. It has never been large. In a town of fewer than thirty thousand people it was a rumour, though a rumour with friends in the hospital and a seat on the council.

What the Order believes

The Order's story of the world is painted on the walls of its chapel. In the beginning, it says, people had nothing. They hated one another and fought without end, for nobody could die. A man offered a serpent to the sun. A woman offered a reed. From their prayers the god was born.

She gave the world time, dividing day from night, and she marked out the road to salvation. She made lesser gods to serve her, a red god called Xuchilbara and a yellow one called Lobsel Vith, with a host of angels. Then she set out to make paradise. Her strength gave out before it was finished. She died, promising to come back.

The faithful are told to wait. The Order's priests have seldom been content with that. They hold that the god must be born again of a human mother, whom they call the Holy Mother, and that the birth can be brought about by ritual. They also hold that she must be fed while she grows. What feeds her is suffering: pain, fear and above all hatred.

The Order's crest is the Halo of the Sun, a design of circles within circles. The three innermost stand for the present, the past and the future. The best known of its angels is Valtiel, the attendant, who watches over the mother of the god and turns the wheel of rebirth. The hooded executioners of the town's past were dressed in his likeness.

What it worships

God is real, and He is not what the Order worships. He made the world, and no prayer of a man with a serpent called Him into being.

The thing that answers the Order's rites is a demon. It is not the Devil himself. It is one of the lesser spirits that fell with him before the world was made, and it has lived on the power of the lake for longer than the town has stood there. It feeds on pain, which is why its worshippers have always been taught to supply it. Valtiel and the rest of the Order's angels are spirits of the same fallen kind.

The Order knows none of this. Its priests and its people believe, sincerely, that they serve the maker of paradise, which is why they have been willing to do what they have done.

Twice the thing has been born into flesh, and twice it has been killed within minutes of its birth. Flesh can be killed. A spirit of that kind cannot. Each time it lost its body, not its existence, and went back to what it had been before: a thing without flesh, waiting on the town.

The Order's magic

No priest of the Order has ever been a witch or a wizard. Its magic is the kind that No-Majs can do: learned, ritual and borrowed, written down in books such as the Crimson Ceremony. It works because the demon answers it. Men who crossed the Order have died of sudden heart failure with no history of illness. A mayor of Silent Hill who campaigned against its drug died that way, as did a narcotics officer after him.

The Order knows the things that work against it, too. Aglaophotis, a red liquid made from a desert herb, drives out demons. The Seal of Metatron, a magic square named after an angel, was believed by some of its priests to be able to stop the god altogether.

For years before 1976 the Order tried to get its god on a human mother. It never succeeded. Some of the young women who went missing from the town in those years are said to have been taken for the purpose.

Dahlia Gillespie

In the 1970s the Order's leading priestess was Dahlia Gillespie. Her daughter, Alessa Gillespie, had been born a witch, though nobody in Silent Hill knew the word in its true sense. Dahlia saw only that the child had power. In the summer of 1976 she burnt her in a rite of birth. The rite half worked: the god took root in the girl, but the girl's soul split, and the birth could not go forward.

For seven years the Order kept Alessa alive in the basement of Alchemilla Hospital. Its director, Dr Michael Kaufmann, was the Order's partner in the drug trade. On 13 September 1983 the two halves of the soul were joined, and the god was born. A writer named Harry Mason killed it. Dahlia died in the same minute, killed by what she had worshipped.

Father Vincent

With Dahlia dead, the Order went to ground for about ten years. It came back about 1993 under a very young priest, Vincent Smith, known as Father Vincent. He turned a secretive sect into a regular religion with a congregation and a collection plate. Within a few years it was larger than it had ever been.

Vincent believed in the Order's god. He had no wish at all to meet her. He liked the world as it was, with himself comfortable in it, and his flock complained that he spent the church's money on himself. His fellow priest Claudia Wolf wanted the birth more than anything on earth. The Order of the 1990s was their quarrel.

Wish House

The Order kept an orphanage, Wish House, in the woods outside the town. On paper it belonged to a charity, the Silent Hill Smile Support Society. The children in it were taught the Order's scripture. Those who would not learn were shut in a round concrete tower in the grounds.

Wish House was managed by the sect of the Holy Mother. A second sect was devoted to the women saints. A priest called Jimmy Stone founded a third, the sect of Valtiel, to keep the peace between the other two.

The orphanage's most famous child was Walter Sullivan. In June 1994 he murdered ten people, Jimmy Stone and his deputy George Rosten among them. He carried on after his own death with a rite from the Order's books, the 21 Sacraments. A few years later the journalist Joseph Schreiber wrote about the place in the magazine Concord.

The end of the Order

In September 2000 Claudia Wolf found the child Harry Mason had carried out of Silent Hill. She was seventeen by then, and went by the name Heather. On 16 September Claudia had Harry murdered, so that the girl would come to Silent Hill hating her. The god inside the girl would feed on that.

It ended the next night, 17 September 2000, in the chapel across the lake. Claudia stabbed Father Vincent to death when he tried to stop her. The girl rid herself of the god with a dose of aglaophotis that her father had given her. Claudia took it into her own body, gave birth to it, and died of the birth. The girl killed what was born.

With both its priests dead, the Order fell apart. On 8 April 2001 Joseph Schreiber could write in his diary that the cult was gone, though its spirit lived on.

The Order and the outside world

No hero ever moved against the Order, and the law never did. To the law it was a small-town sect with a charity attached. To MACUSA it was nothing, for there was no witch or wizard in it to break the Statute of Secrecy. The hunters of the Society of Leopold have their hands full with vampires an ocean away.

Two secret bodies took an interest in the town all the same. The narcotics officer who died in 1983 had been passing what he learnt about PTV to a federal agent who belonged to Delta Green. That October the agent burnt the Order's beds of White Claudia in the marsh. They grew back the next summer, and the SCP Foundation, which had been watching the town since 1939, took some of the seed into its keeping. Neither ever reached the Order's priests. Delta Green wondered whether the Order's god might be one of the powers it had fought since Innsmouth. The Foundation's file records it as an entity reported by the local religious group. Neither guessed the truth.

The Order did its worst in a place that kept its own secrets, which was enough.

pages.title: The Orion Syndicate
infobox: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'Honor Among Thieves' (23 February 1998)
A crime syndicate of the Orions, with partners from many peoples
Slavery, piracy, smuggling and murder for hire
Orion women, whose scent can bend men to their will
The Batarians; Krogan and Vorcha mercenaries
The Borderland, 2154; the Enterprise NX-01, 2155; Mindoir, 2268; Elysium, about 2277; Torfan, about 2279
pages.html:
The Orion Syndicate is the crime syndicate of the green-skinned Orions, who have been the slavers, pirates and smugglers of their part of space for as long as anybody can remember. Its men appear to run it, but its women rule it. By the twenty-second century the Batarians had joined it, and Krogan mercenaries fought for it. It tried to take the Enterprise NX-01 more than once.

The Orions

The Orions are a green-skinned people whose worlds lie beyond the Klingon frontier, across a lawless region called the Borderland. They have never been a great power in the ordinary way. They trade in goods and in people. Their slave markets have long been the busiest in that part of space. Orion women give off a scent that drives men to obey them, which is why the slave women of Orion are so much sought after, and why the men who think they own them so seldom do.

The Syndicate

The Orions' crime is organised in the Orion Syndicate, which deals in slaves, stolen goods, piracy and murder for hire. By the twenty-second century it had partners from many peoples. The Batarians, slavers themselves, joined it and sold their captives in its markets. Krogan mercenaries, with Vorcha among them, fought for whoever paid, and the Syndicate paid well.

The Enterprise NX-01

In 2154 Orion slavers raided the Enterprise NX-01 in the Borderland and carried off several of its crew to a slave market, where Batarians were bidding. Captain Jonathan Archer got them back, and the market's other captives escaped in the confusion. The Syndicate wanted his head for it.

Early in 2155 an Orion Syndicate captain, Harrad-Sar, offered Archer a share in a mining venture, with a gift of three Orion women, Navaar, D'Nesh and Maras. Their scent set the men of the Enterprise against one another, and the ship was very nearly taken. Harrad-Sar admitted afterwards that he was not their master. They were his. Later that year the Syndicate sent a Krogan mercenary crew after Archer, which he also beat off.

Later years

In 2267 an Orion agent, disguised as an Andorian, murdered the Tellarite ambassador on the way to the Babel conference, hoping to start a war in which the Orions could sell dilithium to both sides. In the years that followed Orion pirates went on raiding the Federation's shipping.

Mindoir, Elysium and Torfan

On 21 August 2268 slavers of the Syndicate raided the Federation colony of Mindoir. They tortured to death Hannah and Hank Shepard, former Starfleet officers who had fought them, with their ten-year-old daughter, Jane. They made the couple's son, John, watch. James T. Kirk's Enterprise saved the boy, who swore vengeance on the Syndicate to Kirk's face.

He kept the oath. On 14 June 2277 the Syndicate struck at Elysium in the Skyllian Verge, in the attack called the Skyllian Blitz, where Shepard held it off. On 27 October 2279 his Marines took its slavers' base under the moon Torfan, leaving none of the slavers alive. For twelve years after that he raided its markets and convoys.

pages.title: The passing of the old powers
infobox: Mostly 2026 to 2053, while the Third World War was fought on Earth

The Goa'uld; the Tok'ra; the Kree; the Skrulls; the Shi'ar; the Brood; the Badoon; the New Gods; the Guardians of the Universe; the Rannians; the Thanagarians; the Tamaraneans; the Daxamites; the Dominators; the Khunds; the Durlans; the Watchers
Krypton, before 1938; the Martians, long before that
The Jaffa, as men and women; the human peoples of the Stargate worlds
Asgard, gone home to the Realm Eternal in 2007; the Ancients; the Ori, cast out in 2007
The Vulcans, the Andorians, the Klingons and their neighbours
The mutants, all but Wolverine; the Inhumans
pages.html:
The passing of the old powers was the dying out of the Goa'uld and of every other alien people that had troubled the Earth in the twentieth century. Most of them perished from 2026 to 2053, while Earth was fighting the Third World War, and nobody on Earth noticed. Each end came out of the nature of the people it ended: the Kree died of their wars, the Shi'ar of their pride, the Goa'uld of the slaves who would no longer carry their young. The Enterprise NX-01 found out what had become of them a century later, when the stars round Earth belonged to the Vulcans, the Andorians and the Klingons.

The old powers

Through the twentieth century the Earth had more alien neighbours than it wanted. The Kree and the Skrulls fought over it in 1971. Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, hunted the Anti-Life Equation in human minds, and from 1997 the Goa'uld came through the Stargate. Most of these powers lay a very long way off, in other galaxies or on the far side of the universe.

In 2026 the Third World War broke out on Earth, and the Stargate programme was lost with much else. For decades nobody on Earth was watching the sky, and those of Earth's heroes who might once have gone out to look had a war of their own to fight. It was in those years that the old powers came to an end.

A few had gone already. Krypton had died before 1938, and the Martians long before that.

The Goa'uld

The Goa'uld never recovered from the fall of the System Lords in 2005. After the last of Ba'al's clones was taken out of its host in 2008, no Goa'uld ruled more than a handful of worlds.

Their own nature finished them. A Goa'uld could be born only of a queen, and its larva could grow only in a Jaffa. The free Jaffa, who lived on tretonin, the drug Earth had made for them, would carry no more larvae. The peoples of the Stargate worlds hid their sons from the raiders who came for hosts. The last lords kept their old hosts alive in sarcophagi, which ate away at their minds, and fought one another for what was left.

The last queen known to the Jaffa was killed about 2031. The last Goa'uld of all died about 2045, on a world whose name the Jaffa did not trouble to record.

The Tok'ra went with them. They had had no queen since Egeria, who first bore them, and once their war was won they took no more hosts. Each symbiote died with the man or woman whose life it had shared, the last of them about 2048.

The Jaffa lived on. Their children were never given a larva. Within two generations the Jaffa were simply men and women, of a proud warrior people.

The Kree and the Skrulls

In 2020, after more than thirty thousand years of war, the Kree and the Skrulls joined their empires into one. It did not last ten years. In 2028 a Kree admiral of the joined empire was unmasked as a Skrull, as Nenora had been in 1989. The Kree would not believe that the Skrulls had not known, and the old war began again inside the empire that had been meant to end it.

It was the last of their wars, and the worst. The Kree built a gene bomb on the pattern of Zabyk's, which had robbed every Skrull of the power to change in 1985; this one killed. The Skrulls answered with Nega-Bombs, the weapon that had killed nine in every ten Kree in 1992.

The Kree could not make good their losses. They had been at an evolutionary dead end for longer than their records went back, and every generation since 1992 had been smaller than the last. By about 2041 no living world was left in either empire. The last Skrulls died hiding in borrowed shapes. The last Kree died at their posts, which is how the Kree had always meant to die.

The Cotati, the thinking plants whom the Kree had tried to wipe out on Hala, died in the same bombs.

The Shi'ar, the Brood and the Badoon

The Shi'ar had never fully recovered from their surrender to the Kree in 2009. Their end came from the Brood, the parasites who lay their eggs in living hosts, who had been all but wiped out by the invaders from the Negative Zone in 2006. In the 2030s the last Brood Empress, driven out of the ruins of Kree space, brought what was left of them into the Imperium.

The Shi'ar answered as their pride required. Rather than become Brood, they burnt every world where the Brood had taken hold, Shi'ar and all, as the Kree had once burnt a world rather than leave a Goa'uld in a Kree. Most of the peoples they had married into their empire burnt with them. The last of the Brood died with their last hosts about 2044. By then the Imperial Guard had burnt Chandilar itself, on the Majestor's last order, and there were no Shi'ar left to keep the M'Kraan Crystal.

The Badoon, the reptilian conquerors who had helped Deathbird to her sister's throne, went more quietly. Their males and females had lived apart for ages: the Brotherhood ruled an empire among the stars, while the Sisterhood stayed at home on Lotiara, a swamp world of the star Capella. In the 2030s the Brotherhood went to one war too many, and its last ships never came home. Without them the Sisterhood had no children. The last of the Sisters died on Lotiara about 2050.

The Dominators and their allies

The Dominators had never forgiven the Daxamites, the kin of Krypton who turned on their Alliance under Earth's sun in 1988. Every Daxamite was fatally weak to lead. About 2033 the Dominators filled the air of Daxam with lead dust, and no Daxamite survived it.

The Dominators had always feared the metagene, the hidden seed of power in human beings, and they had always wanted it for themselves. In the 2030s they tried to give it to their own highest caste. The change ran wild in their blood, and by about 2039 it had killed them all. The Khunds, who lived for war, plundered the dying Dominion and carried the plague home.

The Durlans, the shape-changers of the old Alliance, had been few ever since the atomic war that gave them their power ruined their world in ancient days. By the 2040s the poison of that war had finished them.

Rann, Thanagar and the last Guardian

Three peoples who had dealings with Earth's heroes ended by sharing one world. Tamaran, which circled Vega, was destroyed by the Psions in 1995. In 2005 Rann was carried bodily into Thanagar's system, about the star Polaris; its coming knocked Thanagar out of its path, and Thanagar fell into its sun. Afterwards the Rannians, the Thanagarians and the Tamaranean refugees lived together on Rann, about as peacefully as might be expected.

About 2038 the old war of Rann and Thanagar broke out again on Rann itself. Ganthet, the last of the Guardians of the Universe, came to stop it. The Rannians, losing, tried to carry their world away with the zeta-beam that had brought it there. The beam failed, and Rann fell into Polaris with everyone on it.

The Guardians had had no children for longer than any record went back, so with Ganthet they came to an end. The Green Lantern Corps, finished since 1994, was never made again.

Apokolips and New Genesis

The twin worlds ended as they had always threatened to end. About 2037 Darkseid made his last war on New Genesis, fought as their last great war had been, with planetoids hurled across the sky. If the Source wrote anything on the wall of rock that year, there was nobody left to read it.

When it was over, New Genesis was ash, the fire pits of Apokolips had gone out and the New Gods of the twin worlds were dead, Darkseid among them. The Lowlies died with their masters, the Bugs in their mounds. Every Mother Box died with its owner, as Mother Boxes do.

The oldest peoples

The Watchers, the oldest of these peoples, kept their vow of non-interference to the last. They watched every one of these endings and did nothing. They had always been few, and they died out in the same years; the vow that kept them out of other peoples' endings kept them out of their own.

A great many lesser peoples had lived in the shadow of the old powers, as their subjects, their allies or their prey. None of them is known to have outlived the powers they had served or feared.

The mutants and the Inhumans

Two peoples of Earth, who were not aliens, went in the same years. Mutants grow old like anybody else. By 2026 the first X-Men, with most of the teams that followed them, had died of old age, so it was the younger generations that the war killed.

The great powers built Sentinels again to find each other's mutant soldiers, and the machines, which detect the mutant gene, could not tell one side's mutants from another's. By the 2030s the mutants of several countries were in camps, as in the world Rachel Summers came from. In the 2040s a new strain of the Legacy Virus, made for the war, killed anybody who carried the X-gene, whether or not their powers had ever shown. That is why no mutant was born after the war. Colonel Phillip Green's militia hunted down whoever was left, and the nuclear exchange of 2053 burnt the last refuges.

The mutant heroes who were still alive when the war began fell in it, every one of them, holding back the Sentinels and the purges or getting the hunted out. Among them were Kitty Pryde, Piotr Rasputin, Kurt Wagner, Storm, Psylocke, Rahne Sinclair, Rachel Summers, Meggan, Pete Wisdom, Franklin Richards, the Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver.

Of all the mutants, only one lived. Logan, called Wolverine, had outlived them all, because his healing power would not let him die. He went into hiding, and nobody knows where.

The Inhumans died with the Kree, who came to Attilan in their last war to take them as the soldiers they had first been made to be. The Royal Family held the city long enough to get many of their people away, and died holding it. Crystal, who had served with the Avengers, fell on Earth, fighting the fires of a burning city. The few Inhumans who lived on Earth, where the air had always made them ill, did not outlive the war. Attilan was left empty on the Moon, and the Terrigen Mists were never breathed again.

The findings of 2151 to 2161

When the Enterprise NX-01 left Earth in April 2151, under Captain Jonathan Archer, the old powers were a memory, and a disputed one.

She found the truth piece by piece. Late in 2151 a Kree Sentry, still guarding an empty outpost, challenged one of her landing parties; its last orders had come in 2041. In 2152 she found a Goa'uld mothership adrift, with the log of the free Jaffa who had taken it from the last of its lords, then reached the empty towns of the Badoon Sisterhood on Lotiara. In 2153 she came upon a Skrull scout ship bound for Earth, its pilot long dead in the shape of an Earthman.

In 2154 she charted a ring of green rubble round Rao, which was all that was left of Krypton, and found a Shi'ar beacon on a burnt world still warning ships away from the Brood. In 2155 Dr Phlox found the Dominators' plague in the dead crew of a drifting Khund warship. The records of a wrecked Thanagarian police cruiser told of Rann's fall. Last of all, the Mobius Chair of Metron was found empty in deep space, its memory full of two worlds burning.

Ensign Hoshi Sato, the ship's linguist, read most of the records. T'Pol, the Vulcan science officer, could add little, since the old powers had seldom come near the space the Vulcans knew. In 2161 Starfleet gathered the findings into a single report, the standard account of the passing of the old powers.

An open sky

Not every old power had died. Asgard had gone home to the Realm Eternal in 2007, the Ancients had risen beyond the world long before and the Ori had been cast into the outer darkness. The Jaffa lived on, as did the human peoples of the Stargate worlds.

Everyone else was gone. When Earth went out among the stars again, the space round it belonged to the Vulcans, the Andorians, the Tellarites and the Klingons, with the Romulans beyond them. Further off were the Asari, the Turians and the Salarians, whom the Enterprise would meet before 2161. The galaxy was theirs to share.

pages.title: The Patriots
infobox: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty (13 November 2001)
Secret organisation within the United States
The Philosophers, a pact of American, Russian and Chinese leaders
Major Zero, Big Boss, Revolver Ocelot, EVA, Para-Medic, Sigint
Five computers: GW, TJ, AL, TR and JD
pages.html:
The Patriots are the secret organisation that Major Zero founded in 1970 to make the world one, as he believed The Boss had wished. They grew out of an older conspiracy, the Philosophers. By the summer of 1994 they have a hand in much of what happens in the United States, through computers that their founder left to rule in his place. They were destroyed in 2014.

The Philosophers

After the Russian Revolution the most powerful men in America, Russia and China met in secret, where they signed a pact to steer the world between them. Twelve sat on its council, the Wisemen's Committee. They called themselves the Philosophers. By the 1930s the last founder was dead, though the pact went on.

In the Second World War the Philosophers pooled a fortune to beat the Axis. It paid for secret work on rockets, on the atomic bomb and on the Cobra Unit. This was the Philosophers' Legacy. When peace came the Soviet officer who had the laundering of it, a man named Volgin, hid the whole sum in banks round the world. His son, a colonel of the GRU, inherited it.

In 1964 the Americans sent The Boss to get the Legacy back from the younger Volgin, which cost her life. The records of the last of it followed in 1970, when Revolver Ocelot killed the Director of Central Intelligence, then took them to Major Zero.

Zero's Patriots

With the Legacy Zero made the American Philosophers over into something new, the Patriots. Its founders were the people who had been through 1964 with him: Big Boss, Ocelot, EVA, Para-Medic and Sigint. Big Boss was to be its figurehead.

In 1972 Zero had Big Boss cloned without his knowledge. The work was carried on the books of the Weapon programme as its third project, Les Enfants Terribles. Big Boss left. He spent the rest of his life at war with the thing he had helped to found.

In the 1970s Zero called the organisation Cipher. After 1976, with his mind failing, he had its authority given to computers, five in the end: GW, TJ, AL, TR and JD. Sigint, by then the head of DARPA, built them.

How they ruled

The Patriots worked through what was already there. They chose who stood for office, then saw to it that the right man won. They steered the money, the newspapers and the contracts for arms.

From the start of the new century until 2005 the President was their own creature: George Sears, who was Solidus Snake, the third clone of Big Boss. When he tried to act for himself they removed him.

Their wars were small ones, secret, fought by men who could be denied. Outer Heaven, Zanzibar Land, Shadow Moses: each was reported, if at all, as an earthquake, a border quarrel or an accident at a remote base. That is why no costumed hero was ever seen at any of them.

What they did not know

The Patriots believed that they ran America. They ran less of it than they thought. S.H.I.E.L.D. answered to an international council of its own, on which they never sat. MACUSA, the magical government of the country, was hidden from them by the Statute of Secrecy as it is from every No-Maj. The Kindred of the Camarilla kept their Masquerade in the Patriots' own cities. Nothing suggests that the Patriots ever learnt of either.

The S3 plan

By the 2000s the Patriots' computers were troubled by the flood of information that computers themselves had let loose. Their answer was the S3 plan, Selection for Societal Sanity. A new computer, GW, would sift everything on the world's networks, deciding what people would be allowed to find. It was housed in Arsenal Gear, a submersible fortress hidden beneath the Big Shell, a clean-up plant in New York Bay.

In April 2009 they tested the method. They arranged for Solidus Snake to seize the Big Shell. Then they sent a young soldier, Raiden, through a close copy of the Shadow Moses incident, to see whether events could be scripted to produce the man they wanted. GW was wrecked by a virus that day.

The war economy and the fall

After 2009 the Patriots made war itself the business that kept the world running. From about 2011 every soldier carried nanomachines tied to a system called Sons of the Patriots, which decided whether his gun would fire.

In 2014 Revolver Ocelot, calling himself Liquid Ocelot, seized that system. Solid Snake carried a virus into the heart of it aboard the warship Outer Haven. Dr Naomi Hunter had written the virus; a small girl, Sunny, had finished it. It destroyed JD with the other three, yet left the lights on. The Patriots ended there.

Of the six founders, Sigint had died in 2005 and Para-Medic two years before him. EVA, Ocelot, Zero and Big Boss all died in 2014.

pages.title: The Peverell family
infobox: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (16 July 2005)
The Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone, the Cloak of Invisibility
pages.html:
The Peverells were an ancient wizarding family. Antioch, Cadmus and Ignotus Peverell are the three brothers of the old tale who met Death on a lonely road. From the youngest, Ignotus, who was given the Cloak of Invisibility, descend the Pendragons, King Arthur among them, and from them the Potters. The Cloak in Harry Potter's trunk is the Peverell Cloak, come down the line intact.

The three brothers

In the Tale of the Three Brothers, which wizarding children are told at bedtime, three brothers came at twilight to a river too dangerous to cross, and made a bridge over it by magic. Death met them on the bridge. He was angry at being cheated of three victims, but he pretended to reward them for their cleverness.

The eldest, Antioch, asked for a wand more powerful than any in existence, and Death made him one from an elder tree. Antioch boasted of it, and was murdered in his sleep for it.

The second, Cadmus, asked for the power to recall others from death, and Death gave him a stone from the riverbank. With it he called back the girl he had hoped to marry. She came back cold and sorrowful. In the end he killed himself to join her.

The youngest, Ignotus, was the humblest of the three, and the wisest. He asked for something that would let him go from that place without Death following him, and Death, most unwillingly, handed over his own Cloak of Invisibility. Ignotus lived to a great age. When he was very old he gave the Cloak to his son, then greeted Death as an old friend and went with him gladly.

The Deathly Hallows

The three gifts are known together as the Deathly Hallows, and whoever holds all three is said to be the master of Death. The wand passed by murder and conquest through a long line of owners. The stone came down the line of Cadmus to the Gaunts, who set it in a ring bearing the Peverell arms and were proud to claim the descent. The Cloak went down the line of Ignotus.

Peverell, Pendragon, Potter

The Pendragons descend directly from Ignotus, the brother who received the Cloak, and the most famous of them was Arthur. After Arthur's time dark wizards aligned with Morgana persecuted his descendants. The family took the name Potter as camouflage. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what the name hid. The Cloak went down the line intact: Peverell, Pendragon, Potter.

The Potter line is documented. Anybody who pulls the genealogies in the right archive can trace it back through Arthur without difficulty; it is obscure only because almost nobody looks. Lucius Malfoy has looked. Harry does not know that he is a Peverell.

In the saga

James Potter used the Cloak at Hogwarts mainly for sneaking down to the kitchens for food. With Sirius Black and Peter Pettigrew he also used it to slip out every month to join Remus Lupin. Before he died he left it in Dumbledore's keeping.

At Christmas 1991 it came to Harry with an unsigned note: 'Your father left this in my keeping before he died. It's time it came back to you. Use it well.' Ron, Hermione, Hagrid and Dumbledore know that he has it. Very probably McGonagall does too. Dracina Malfoy does not.

In June 1994 Severus Snape followed Lupin to the Shrieking Shack under it, and afterwards Lupin gave it back to Harry. Dementors cannot be fooled by it.

pages.title: The Phalanx
infobox: Living machines that share a single mind
The transmode virus of Warlock's remains
Men who hated mutants, among them Cameron Hodge and Stephen Lang
pages.html:
The Phalanx are living machines that share a single mind. On Earth they began as men who hated mutants, who infected themselves with the transmode virus taken from Warlock's remains. They could swallow ordinary people into themselves but not mutants, so in the summer of 1994 they set out to destroy the mutants instead. They failed.

Nature

A Phalanx can change its shape, teleport and take living things into itself through the transmode virus. Each one keeps something of the person it was, but it cannot act against the will of the whole while it is joined to it.

Out among the stars the Phalanx are an old menace. Wherever they take hold, they drive their victims to build a tower, a Babel Spire, which calls down the Technarchy, Warlock's people, to eat the world.

On Earth the virus came from the remains of Warlock, whom Cameron Hodge had drained to ash on Genosha in 1990. Hodge was one of the men who took it into themselves. Stephen Lang, who had built Sentinels in the 1970s, was another.

1994

In the spring of 1994 one of them, made with the face and memories of Doug Ramsey, broke away. He called himself Douglock. In the summer the Phalanx took most of the X-Men prisoner. By then their single mind had begun to break apart. In August one faction built a Babel Spire in the Alps out of the villagers it had swallowed. Douglock climbed it with Rahne Sinclair and Sam Guthrie, then scrambled its beacon from within. The Phalanx there fell to pieces. The captured X-Men were rescued, and the Phalanx on Earth were broken.

In 1995 Black Air kept one of them prisoner at Dream Nails, a gift of the Hellfire Club.

pages.title: The Plateau of Leng
infobox: In Central Asia; in the Antarctic; in the country men reach in dreams
A monastery ruled by a masked high priest; a corpse-eating cult
pages.html:
The Plateau of Leng is a cold, high, desolate tableland that nobody can agree how to find. Some books put it in Central Asia, some in the Antarctic, and some in the country that men reach only in dreams. Wherever it lies, it is a place of evil repute, whose people are not quite men, and whose monastery is ruled by a high priest who wears a mask of yellow silk.

The cult of the hound

The Necronomicon speaks of Leng, and of the corpse-eating cult of the plateau, whose sign is a winged hound. Two young Englishmen who robbed graves for their own amusement once took a jade amulet of that cult from a grave in Holland, and both died of it. Something like a great hound tore the first of them apart. The second wrote down what had happened, meaning to shoot himself as soon as he had finished.

The men of Leng

The men of Leng have horns, which they hide under turbans when they go among other men to trade. They are slavers. Travellers in the lands of dreams have been carried off by them to their monastery, where the high priest who may not be described sits masked in yellow silk.

Who the masked priest is, the books do not say. Some have called him a mask of Nyarlathotep.

The Antarctic

In the southern summer of 1930 to 1931 an expedition of Miskatonic University found a range of mountains in the Antarctic higher than the Himalaya. The two men who flew over it took the high plateau beyond, where the city of the Elder Things lies under the ice, for Leng. That plateau is not the place where the Ancients once had their city, which lay elsewhere under the same ice and belonged to another people altogether.

pages.title: The Putty Infiltrator
infobox: A Putty that could wear any human face
pages.html:
The Putty Infiltrator was a spy of Rita Repulsa's, a Putty that could take on any human shape. In August 1993 it took the place of Matt Cook, a boy of Angel Grove, while Rita held him on the Moon. It lived his life for some weeks, until living it made it doubt what it was. Rita took it over, and the Rangers destroyed it.

In Matt Cook's place

In August 1993 Rita sent the Infiltrator into Angel Grove in human shape, to study the people there and to find the young people who were her Rangers. With it she sent a monster, Flog, to draw the Rangers out. When Flog attacked, Matt Cook threw himself in front of his girlfriend, Kimberly Hart, and was thrown into a building.

Kimberly had to fight. She handed Matt to a passer-by who promised to get him to hospital. The passer-by was the Infiltrator. Rita carried the real Matt off to her palace on the Moon, where she drew out his memories so that her creature could think as he did. The boy who woke in the hospital bed with Matt's face was the Infiltrator.

It went home as Matt, then back to school. Through it Rita learnt the Rangers' secrets. It told Jason Lee Scott that Trini Kwan was keen on him. It saved Billy Cranston from Goldar. Kimberly and Jason both felt that something was wrong. Zack Taylor saw it talking to Putties.

Doubt

The longer it lived Matt's life, the less sure it was what it was. On the night of the Homecoming dance, in September 1993, it was on the point of telling Kimberly the truth when the real Matt, escaped from the Moon, stumbled on to the stage. Jason stopped the false one, which turned back into the Putty it had been.

It copied each of the Rangers in turn and mocked their failings. It would not kill them. Instead it tried to reason with them. Rita took hold of it with one of Baboo's potions, then made it copy the Megazord. Billy had the Megazord split up into its five Dinozords, which the Infiltrator could not copy. Kimberly's Pterodactyl finished it.

pages.title: The Quarians
infobox: Rannoch, lost to the Geth in 1895; regained in 2299
The Migrant Fleet, about fifty thousand ships carrying some seventeen million Quarians
Slender humanoids, never seen by outsiders without their sealed suits
Built of mirror-image proteins, like the Turians; almost no immune system after generations in sterile ships
The Admiralty Board of five officers; the Conclave, in which every ship has a voice
About 2164 and about 2250; refused both times
pages.html:
The Quarians are a slender, wandering people who built the Geth and were driven from their own world, Rannoch, when the Geth rose against them in 1895. Ever since they have lived aboard the Migrant Fleet, some fifty thousand ships, sealed in suits against germs their bodies can no longer fight. The Enterprise NX-01 met a young Quarian on her Pilgrimage in 2152. The United Federation of Planets offered the Quarians aid and worlds to settle more than once, but they always refused, because the Federation would not help them take Rannoch back from the Geth.

Rannoch

The Quarians come from Rannoch. Like the Turians, they are built of proteins that are the mirror images of most other peoples', so that very little food in the galaxy is any good to them. They were always clever with machines. In ancient times they worshipped their ancestors, and later they kept the minds of their elders in computers, so that the dead could still give counsel to the living.

The Geth and the Morning War

About 1880 the Quarians built the Geth to labour and fight for them. They were android workers and soldiers whose computers were joined into one network. As the network grew, the Geth began to think for themselves. The Quarians took fright and tried to destroy them.

The Geth won. In the Morning War of 1895 they drove the Quarians from Rannoch and from every one of their colonies. They destroyed the stored minds of the Quarian ancestors as well. The survivors fled into space in whatever ships they could find. The alliance of the Asari, the Salarians and the Turians, whose friends they had been, would not let them settle any world that it claimed.

The Migrant Fleet

The Quarians have lived ever since in the Migrant Fleet, some fifty thousand ships carrying about seventeen million people, the greatest gathering of starships anywhere. Children are raised in sterile ships, so that the Quarians have almost no natural defence against disease. Among outsiders they never take off their sealed suits and masks, which has led to a great many stories that they are machines underneath.

A Quarian who comes of age leaves the ship of his or her birth on the Pilgrimage, and must bring back something of value to be taken on by another crew. It keeps the bloodlines of the fleet from growing too close. The fleet is governed by an Admiralty Board of five officers and by the Conclave, where every ship sends members according to the size of its crew. Many Quarians have gone back to the faiths of their ancestors. Many believe that the Geth were the price of their own pride.

Earth and the Federation

In 2152 the Enterprise NX-01 came upon a small Quarian ship with a failing engine and a young Quarian woman aboard, alone on her Pilgrimage. Commander Charles Tucker mended the engine. She took home, as her gift to the fleet, the Enterprise's charts of a region no Quarian had ever visited. It was from her that Earth first heard of Rannoch and the Geth.

After 2161 the United Federation of Planets offered the Quarians help twice. It offered medicine and a world to settle about 2164, then several worlds about 2250. Both times the Admiralty Board refused. The Quarians wanted only one thing: the help of the Federation's ships to take Rannoch back and destroy the Geth. The Federation would not give it. It would not make war on the Geth for them, nor help to destroy a people.

The return to Rannoch

In the Intergalactic War the Galactic Empire tried to seize control of the Geth.
