On 5 October 2299, while its agents were rewriting the Geth's shared mind from orbit, the Migrant Fleet came in to destroy them. Captain John Shepard of the USS Enterprise-B broke the Empire's hold with the help of Tali'Zorah nar Rayya, a Quarian of his own crew. Then he held the two fleets apart until they talked.

The Quarians and the Geth made peace. The Quarians went home to Rannoch after four hundred years in their ships, to live beside the people they had made. Both fleets fought in Shepard's alliance for the rest of the war. In 2350, fifty years after it, the Quarians and the Geth of Rannoch joined the United Federation of Planets together. Many Quarians entered Starfleet, where their engineers had a hand in the Galaxy-class starships of the next age.

pages.title: The Rachni
infobox: Insect-like beings of one mind, each hive ruled by a queen deep underground
Wiped out by the Krogan by about 300; believed extinct
pages.html:
The Rachni were an insect-like people who thought as one, each hive guided by a queen who lived deep beneath the ground of their poisonous homeworld, Suen. When Salarian explorers came upon them about 1, the Rachni made war on everybody they met. Since nobody could reach the queens to talk to them, the Rachni Wars went on for three centuries. The Krogan, whom the Salarians raised up for the purpose, wiped them out by about 300, and they are believed to be extinct.

The hives

The Rachni were workers, soldiers and warriors, all of them moved by the will of their queens. The queens never came to the surface. They lived in deep lairs beneath Suen, a world whose air would kill most other peoples, and from there they directed everything the Rachni did. The Rachni had ships of their own, and they spread across the worlds around Suen long before anybody else knew of them.

The Rachni Wars

About 1 a Salarian survey ship, exploring by warp, reached a system that nobody had visited before, and found the Rachni. The Rachni attacked at once. Within a few years they were overrunning the colonies of the Asari and the Salarians. The alliance of the two peoples was losing.

The war could not be ended by talking. Envoys could reach the Rachni soldiers, but the soldiers did not decide anything, and the queens who did were out of reach beneath the poisoned ground. Nobody ever made terms with a Rachni queen.

Extermination

About 80 the Salarians found the Krogan, a people who could live on poisonous worlds and breed faster than the Rachni could kill them. They armed them and sent them in. The Krogan went down into the queens' lairs, retook the alliance's lost worlds and drove the Rachni back to Suen, where the Rachni refused to surrender. By about 300 there were no Rachni left anywhere.

They are believed to be extinct. The Krogan, who were rewarded with worlds of their own for the work, became a far greater danger than the Rachni had ever been.

What Earth learnt

Earth heard of the Rachni only from the Salarians, who told Captain Jonathan Archer the story in 2155, when he asked them about the disease that Dr Phlox had found in a Krogan's blood. Nobody had seen a living Rachni for more than eighteen centuries.

pages.title: The raid on Innsmouth
infobox: The Shadow over Innsmouth (Visionary Publishing Company, April 1936)
Innsmouth, Massachusetts, and Devil Reef offshore
The Office of Naval Intelligence, with Marines, sailors, the Coast Guard and the Bureau of Investigation
The Deep Ones and the Esoteric Order of Dagon
The waterfront burnt; a great many townspeople held without trial; Y'ha-nthlei damaged
The work of P4, and in time Delta Green
pages.html:
The raid on Innsmouth was the secret action of the United States government against the town of Innsmouth, Massachusetts, in February 1928. The Navy and the Bureau of Investigation went in together, on President Coolidge's authority, under the code name Project COVENANT. They burnt the waterfront, took a great many townspeople away to camps and torpedoed the deep water beyond Devil Reef, where the Deep Ones have their city. To anyone outside, it looked like a strike against bootleggers. Delta Green grew out of it.

The young man from Ohio

In July 1927 a young man of twenty-one from Ohio, Robert Olmstead, was touring New England to look at old buildings and trace his family. At Newburyport he learnt that the cheapest way on to Arkham was by Joe Sargent's bus through Innsmouth, a decayed port that the towns round about avoided and would not talk about. He took the bus.

In Innsmouth he met Zadok Allen, a drunken old man of ninety-six, and paid him in whisky to talk. Zadok told him about Captain Obed Marsh's dealings with the Deep Ones, the sacrifices at Devil Reef and the night in 1846 when things came up out of the sea. That night the townspeople came for Olmstead at the Gilman House, where he had taken a room. He escaped through a window. Then he fled along the old railway line, while things that hopped and croaked went hunting for him in the dark.

He went to the federal authorities with what he had seen. Agents of the Treasury, which enforced Prohibition, began to look into the town. Through the winter of 1927 to 1928 a quiet census of Innsmouth was taken, house by house.

Project COVENANT

What the census found went up to President Calvin Coolidge, who gave his authority for a raid. It was planned by the Office of Naval Intelligence and given the code name Project COVENANT. Marines, sailors and men of the Coast Guard took part, with agents of the Bureau of Investigation under its young director, J. Edgar Hoover.

To anyone outside, it looked like one more strike against the liquor smugglers of the coast. Under Prohibition nobody thought that strange.

February 1928

The raid came in February 1928. Marines and federal agents went through Innsmouth from house to house. They made arrests on a scale that astonished the few reporters who heard of it. Along the abandoned waterfront an enormous number of crumbling, worm-eaten houses, supposedly empty, were burnt, then dynamited, under careful precautions.

Out at sea a submarine of the Navy fired torpedoes down into the deep water just beyond Devil Reef, a mile and a half out from the harbour. Beneath the reef lies Y'ha-nthlei, the city of the Deep Ones. The torpedoes damaged it, but they did not destroy it.

The camps

Those who were taken were never brought to trial, and no charges against them were ever made public. They were held in naval and military prisons, or in camps set apart for them. Many of them had the Innsmouth look: narrow heads, flat noses and staring eyes that never seemed to blink. Some, it was said, were far gone in the change.

Liberal organisations complained about the arrests, and about the secrecy. Their representatives were taken into long confidential talks, then on visits to certain of the camps. After that they said remarkably little.

What became of the prisoners was never made public. Innsmouth was left almost empty.

The tablets

Among the things taken from the town were stone tablets carved in no human script. In April 1928 they were handed to the Black Chamber, the government's codebreakers in New York. The work took a year and a half. The translation, which its makers called the Book of Dagon, was finished on 2 November 1929, a few days after the crash on Wall Street.

It came at a bad moment. President Herbert Hoover would have none of it. His Secretary of State, Henry Stimson, closed the Black Chamber down that autumn, and its staff passed to P4, the small section of the Office of Naval Intelligence to which everything learnt at Innsmouth had gone.

What came of it

P4 went on with the work. Until 1941 it hunted the Deep Ones and their hybrids wherever they could be found, from the coast of Central America to the Philippines. In 1930 it took some five hundred prisoners on the island of Pedra Negra. In the Second World War P4 became Delta Green.

The archives of the raid did not survive. In January 1955 Daniel Fraser, a cryptographer who had worked on the tablets for the Black Chamber, went mad. He destroyed the archives, the tablets with them.

Y'ha-nthlei did not die either. In April 1963 the submarine Thresher was lost with all hands off the coast of New England, and Delta Green came to believe that Innsmouth had something to do with it. That spring, in Operation RIPTIDE, it bombed what was left of the city under Devil Reef.

The newspapers of 1928 never learnt what the raid had really been for. Nor has anybody outside the government since.

pages.title: The Ranger Slayer
infobox: Kimberly Hart, of the World of the Coinless
The Bow of Darkness, which held Rita Repulsa's spell
Pink: as the Pink Solar Ranger, then as a Drakkon Ranger
Lord Drakkon; Grace Sterling, from September 1994
The World of the Coinless, from December 1994
Lord Drakkon, in February 1995, inside the Morphin Grid
pages.html:
The Ranger Slayer is the Kimberly Hart of the World of the Coinless, whom Lord Drakkon bound to him with Rita Repulsa's spell and made his hunter of Rangers. In September 1994 he sent her after this world's Rangers, but she came out of time a year too early. In October 1993 this world's Kimberly broke the bow that held her, which set her free. Before she left, she shot a new boy in Angel Grove, Tommy Oliver, with the arrow that later saved his life. In the end she ruled her own world in Drakkon's place, and it was her arrow that killed him.

Kimberly of the Coinless

In her world, as in this one, Kimberly Hart was a pupil at Angel Grove High School, and the Pink Ranger. Her world's Tommy Oliver stayed with Rita when the spell on him broke, then took the name of Lord Drakkon. When his armies came for Angel Grove, Kimberly led a party out of the school through his Mastodon Sentries. Bulk was with her, with a girl named Violet. So were the headmaster, Mr Caplan, and a teacher, Ms Appleby. Afterwards she fought on with Bulk for a long time.

Drakkon's regime killed Billy Cranston, who died shielding Trini. Matthew Cook, whom Kimberly loved, was wounded in a Sentry attack. She found him dying in a hospital. After that she went alone to kill Drakkon.

The Ranger Slayer

He did not kill her. He bound her instead with Rita's spell, which he had learnt from Rita before he murdered her. The spell was held in a bow, the Bow of Darkness, as Rita's spell on him had once been held in the Sword of Darkness. He made her his hunter of the Rangers who were left: the Ranger Slayer. Once he had her, he stood down the Pterodactyl Sentries, his marksmen. She had a Zord of her own, the Gravezord.

She served him for years. He found a use even for her life. That world's Jason, whom everybody believed dead, was kept in chains in Deadlock, Drakkon's prison tower. He never tried to escape, because Drakkon had told him that the Ranger Slayer was under orders to kill herself if he did.

The wrong year

In September 1994, in his war on the Rangers of every year, Drakkon sent her after this world's Rangers. She came out of time a year too early, in the first days of October 1993, in a railway yard in Angel Grove. She beat Goldar with his Putties single-handed, then turned on the Rangers, demanding Drakkon. Only then did she see that she had come to the wrong year. She let slip that she was a Kimberly Hart of a later day.

Rita Repulsa offered her help, then put new power into the Gravezord. It attacked the middle of the city to draw the Rangers off while the Ranger Slayer broke into the Command Center. Matt Cook, who had gone looking for the Rangers, ran towards the fight, where he was very nearly crushed.

The broken bow

At the Command Center Kimberly turned the power of its spires on the bow, which destroyed it. Drakkon's hold on the Ranger Slayer broke with it. Calling herself Sally, she spent an afternoon at the juice bar of the Youth Center with the girl she had once been. Drakkon spoke to her across the year that lay between them. He saw that she was free, so he said goodbye.

She was not entirely tame. She knocked Billy Cranston out, then went through Alpha 5's records. Matt went by himself to the place where the Gravezord had come down, where he found her waking it. They talked. When she had gone, Matt knew who his friends really were. Before she left, the Gravezord fought beside the Megazord against two of Rita's monsters.

The arrow

Her last errand in 1993 was in a school gym. Tommy Oliver had only just come to Angel Grove, and he was nobody's Ranger yet. She shot him with an arrow carrying a splinter of the Green Chaos Crystal. He would understand in time, she told him. Then she went back to her own day.

Eleven months later Drakkon murdered him. The splinter held his spirit between the worlds, which is how Tommy came to undo the war that followed.

In September 1994 Grace Sterling of Promethea took her in. She sailed in Grace's ship, Promethea, to Drakkon's tower on the Moon of her own world, to free the Rangers he held.

The lost ship

When Drakkon unmade everything, Grace armoured the ship with the energy of Psycho Green's dagger. It was thrown clear into a dark place where there was no Morphin Grid at all. The Ranger Slayer led the Rangers aboard, whose powers were guttering out.

After forty days a false call for help drew six of them away. While they were gone a hooded Ranger in purple raided the ship. She was Ellarien, called Ari, a scavenger who styled herself the Solar Ranger. With the Solarix, a piece of the Grid, she drew off one Ranger's powers, with the energy of Grace's dagger besides.

That place had a tyrant, the Praetor. The Praetor was one of the Morphin Masters, who had cut it off from the rest of creation, draining its Grid so that the Power could never be misused there. The Praetor's soldiers were the Crimson Raiders.

The castaways made common cause with Ari. Pieces of the Solarix made them Solar Rangers, the Ranger Slayer the Pink. Their Solar Megazord destroyed the Praetor, which joined that place to the Grid again. The way home was open. Ari stayed behind with Remi, a new Solar Ranger. Promethea came home in October 1994.

Grace Sterling's Ranger

After that she worked for Grace, patrolling space in the Gravezord. Early in December 1994 Grace sent her to help the Rangers against the Anointed. Cavotus had destroyed the Omega Rangers' ship. He was about to kill Adam Park when the Ranger Slayer destroyed him.

At Safehaven she went through the Master Arch. She came back with Ari, Remi and the Solarix, which drained the Power out of every one of the Empowered. When it was over she went home to her own world, to make amends.

Queen of the Coinless

She found her world believing Drakkon dead, with Scorpina commanding his Sentries. That world's Trini had raised Rita Repulsa from the dead with an old spell. An army of the dead followed the witch. The Sentries chose to follow Kimberly instead. Rita was sealed in her own staff, then Kimberly ruled in Drakkon's place.

She pulled down Deadlock. In it she found Jason alive. Then a signal from that world brought Eclipta, a herald of Dark Specter, who killed Adam Park. In the fighting every Power Coin was fed into a Diffuser at once. The coins burnt out, which was the end of the Sentries. Jason carried the dead coins off to the old fortress.

The Drakkon Rangers

By February 1995 Dark Specter's creatures of lava, which had once been people, were overrunning her world. Then Drakkon came back, bringing Kiya Kyatyl. Kimberly took him prisoner with the help of Trini, backed by Scorpina. He proposed that they should all become Rangers. Finster-5 made the suits, so that Kimberly became the Pink Drakkon Ranger.

Skull, who had become a monster, let the horde into their stronghold. Kimberly held the hatch so that the others could get away. They thought her lost.

The end in the Grid

She was not lost. Dark Specter had taken her. His corruption was in the Power itself by then, turning every Ranger it touched. When Drakkon went into the Grid alone, she was waiting for him in an image of their own world, his enemy now. He threw the Dragon Dagger at her with his White Tiger coin set in it. Its light burnt the corruption out of her. Her arrow, already loosed, went through his heart.

Dying, he gave her the coin. His last order was to find the Morphin Masters, then save the universe. She went looking for them with the Pink Emissary, another of the Masters' servants. They found the Masters withdrawn from the world, of no use to anyone. Drakkon's coin, joined with Tommy Oliver's own, let the Rangers morph in safety until the Grid was cleansed. What became of her afterwards is not recorded.

pages.title: The Rangers of 1969
infobox: Psycho Green, sent by Dark Specter
Terona Washington, a soldier home from Vietnam
Nikolai Chukarin, Jamie Gilmore, Daniel O'Halloran
pages.html:
The Rangers of 1969 were Zordon's first team of Power Rangers: five grown strangers of different nations, whom he chose in a hurry on the night of the Moon landing, 20 July 1969. They had one mission, which was to stop a creature called Psycho Green from breaking Rita Repulsa out of her dumpster on the Moon. They stopped him, but three of the five died doing it. The team never came to public notice, and for twenty-five years Zordon told nobody about it.

Psycho Green

In July 1969 Rita Repulsa had lain in her space dumpster on the Moon for some ten thousand years. Zordon had no Rangers. On the very day the Americans were to land there, Dark Specter sent a creature called Psycho Green to the same place, to break her out.

Psycho Green had once been a Ranger himself, on another world. Nothing more is known of where he came from. He carried a dagger, which was to matter a great deal later.

The five

Zordon had to choose at once. He had Alpha 5 fetch five grown strangers to the Command Center that evening. They were men and women of different nations who had never met, let alone fought side by side. Zordon told them what was coming, then gave each of them a Power Coin.

Grace Sterling ran the secretarial pool at NASA. She had wanted to be an astronaut herself, but NASA would not take a woman. She was on the roof with a colleague, Marcus, watching the Moon, when Alpha found her. Zordon made her the Red Ranger, with the command of the others.

Nikolai Chukarin, the Blue Ranger, was an agent of the Soviet KGB. Jamie Gilmore, the Black, was a British singer who wrote her own songs. Terona Washington, the Yellow, was a soldier, home from the war in Vietnam. Daniel O'Halloran, the Pink, was a student who marched against that war.

The night of 20 July 1969

They came down in the Aitken crater, on the far side of the Moon, while the world watched the astronauts of Apollo 11 on the near side. Grace wept for joy when she touched the ground.

They had never trained together, and it showed. They split up. Nikolai went ahead with Jamie Gilmore to scout. Psycho Green was waiting for them. He kicked Nikolai so hard that he would have flown off into space if Grace had not caught him. Then he threw a boulder, which crushed Jamie.

Terona told Daniel O'Halloran to wait. Daniel charged in all the same. Psycho Green broke the visor of his helmet, so that Daniel suffocated.

The three who were left put their weapons together into a single blaster. They fired it as Psycho Green reached Rita's dumpster. It did not destroy him. It fed him, so that he swelled into a monstrous giant.

They fell back on Rita's empty palace, where one of Zordon's old cannons still stood. It was failing. Nikolai took it all the same. 'We will save the earth today, Grace,' he said. 'Make sure it's worth saving.' Then he let Psycho Green swallow him whole, and he fired the cannon from inside. It destroyed them both.

Rita stayed in her dumpster. It was twenty-four years before anybody let her out.

Afterwards

Two came home, Grace Sterling and Terona Washington. Terona told Zordon that it had been irresponsible to send untrained strangers to fight. Zordon blamed himself, as it happened. All the same, he asked for the powers back, since the danger was over.

Grace wanted to keep them. With such power, she said, they could end the war in Vietnam, perhaps the Cold War itself. Zordon answered that it was not a Ranger's place to meddle in mankind's own affairs. He took back the coins. The two survivors left him in anger, which is how the team came to an end.

Grace had picked up one thing on the Moon: Psycho Green's dagger. Its energy lies behind the machines of Promethea, the company that she and Terona founded afterwards, to keep the promise Nikolai had asked of them.

Zordon never told the Rangers he chose in 1993 that there had been others before them. Early in 1994 Grace Sterling walked up to the door of the Command Center and told them herself. They watched the whole of that night on the viewing globe. Zordon's reasons for his silence did not satisfy them.

The promise outlived the Moon by a long way. Terona Washington, the last of the five, gave the rest of his life to it. Terra Venture, the space colony that left Earth in 1999, came of it in the end.

pages.title: The Red Pyramid Thing
infobox: The old executioners of Silent Hill
Maria of Silent Hill, three times
Killed itself when James no longer needed it
pages.html:
The Red Pyramid Thing was the creature that hunted James Sunderland through Silent Hill on 25 September 1994. It had the body of a big man in a butcher's stained smock. Where its head should have been it wore a great rusted pyramid of iron. James gave it its name, having no better one. Others have called it Pyramid Head. It was his executioner, made by the town out of his own wish to be punished.

Appearance

The creature stood taller than a man. It wore a filthy white smock that reached to its feet. The pyramid covered its head down to the shoulders, with one point jutting forward, and it had no face that anybody saw. It never spoke. It made a low groaning noise as it moved.

It carried the Great Knife, a blade as long as its own body, which it dragged along the floor behind it. The scrape of the knife gave warning of it. Later it carried a spear instead. James picked up the knife after the creature had laid it down. He could hardly lift it.

The executioner

James first saw it in a block of flats, standing quite still behind a barred gate. The next time, he surprised it at violence on two of the town's other creatures. He hid in a cupboard and fired at it through the slats of the door until it went away. It followed him after that. On a flooded stairway it would have killed him, but a siren sounded over the town and it walked down into the water.

Its chief business was with Maria of Silent Hill, the woman who had the face of James's dead wife. It ran her through with its spear in a corridor under Brookhaven Hospital. She was alive again by the time James reached the old prison, then dead again in her cell. In the lobby of the Lakeview Hotel there were two of the creatures. They had Maria hung up between them, and they killed her a third time while James watched.

What it was

The Otherworld of Silent Hill makes its creatures out of the mind it has fastened on. James Sunderland had smothered his sick wife. He had hidden the memory from himself. Some part of him knew. It wanted to be found out, judged and made to pay. The town gave that part of him a body.

It took the body's shape from its own past. For a century men were put to death at Silent Hill, first in the penal colony, later in Toluca Prison. The executioners wore red hoods with long ceremonial robes. The Order of Silent Hill had dressed them so, in the likeness of its angel Valtiel. James had seen a painting of them at the Silent Hill Historical Society, on the holiday he spent in the town with his wife. He remembered more of it than he knew.

That is why the creature killed Maria, over and over, in front of him. It was showing him a wife's death until he was ready to say whose doing it was.

The end

At the Lakeview Hotel James watched the tape that showed what he had done. When he met the two creatures in the lobby he was no longer afraid of them. He told them that he had been weak, that he had needed somebody to punish him, and that it was finished. He fought them to a standstill. Then each of them turned its spear on itself.

Nobody has reported such a creature at Silent Hill since. It belonged to one man.

pages.title: The Romulans
infobox: The Vulcans who rejected Surak, in the fourth century
The Eldar, through the Vulcans, unknown to either people
The Senate, with a Praetor and a Proconsul
pages.html:
The Romulans are the descendants of the Vulcans who would not follow Surak. They left Vulcan in the fourth century to build the Romulan Star Empire on Romulus and its sister world, Remus. Proud, passionate and secretive, they fought Earth from 2156 to 2160 without ever once showing their faces, then kept behind the Neutral Zone for more than a century. When one of their warships crossed it in 2266, the humans who crippled it saw a Romulan's face for the first time.

Those who marched beneath the raptor's wings

In the fourth century, while Surak was teaching his people logic, a faction of Vulcans sought a return to the old savage ways. They marched beneath the raptor's wings, the emblem that the Romulans carry still. It was they who made the atomic attack on Surak's followers that led to his death.

After Surak died, they would not live on a Vulcan that followed him. They left the planet for good, in the parting later called the Sundering. Their ships carried them far out into space to a pair of worlds in one system, which came to be called Romulus and Remus. There they settled, and there, over the centuries, they built an empire.

Through the Vulcans they came of the Eldar, though no Romulan ever knew it.

Romulus and Remus

The Romulan Star Empire is ruled from Romulus by a Senate, with a Praetor at its head and a Proconsul beneath him. Its secret police and intelligence service, the Tal Shiar, is feared inside the Empire as much as outside it. By the twenty-third century its warships carried cloaking devices that hid them from sight and sensors alike. The Romulans guarded the secret of the cloak jealously.

Remus is the harsher of the two worlds. The Remans who live there work its dilithium mines. The Empire has always treated them as a lower caste, fit only for the mines and for the front line in war. The Romulans prefer not to discuss them.

Romulans look like Vulcans, apart from a ridge on the brow that some of them have. They are not like Vulcans in anything else. They feel freely, plot patiently and trust almost nobody. A Romulan who tells you what he is thinking has usually decided that it no longer matters.

The war with Earth

Earth first met the Romulans in 2152, when the Enterprise NX-01 strayed into a cloaked minefield near a world they claimed, and two of their warships ordered it away. Nobody aboard saw a Romulan.

The Romulans watched the young alliance growing up around Earth with alarm. In 2154 their agent Talok worked with Administrator V'Las to push Vulcan into war with Andoria. The same year Admiral Valdore sent drone ships, able to disguise themselves as any vessel, to set the Andorians and the Tellarites at each other's throats. The drones were flown by Gareb, an Aenar of Andoria whom the Romulans had taken and deceived. Both plans failed. Between them they drew Earth, Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar closer together than they had ever been.

War came in 2156. It was fought with atomic weapons, by ships that gave no quarter and took no prisoners. In four years neither side ever saw the other's face. The Romulans never forgot their humiliating defeat at the Battle of Cheron. The war ended in 2160 with a treaty settled over subspace radio, which set a Neutral Zone between the two powers. For either side to enter it was an act of war.

The long silence

For a century the Romulans kept behind the Neutral Zone. In 2266 a Romulan bird-of-prey crossed it, cloaked, and destroyed the outposts along its edge. The USS Enterprise under Captain James T. Kirk crippled the ship, and its commander destroyed it rather than surrender. On the ship's viewscreen the humans saw a Romulan's face for the first time, and it looked like Spock's.

In 2267 the Empire joined the United Federation of Planets and the Klingons in founding a colony on Nimbus III, the Planet of Galactic Peace, which never lived up to its name. The Romulans had been trading with the Klingons, and by 2268 they were flying warships of Klingon design. That year Kirk and Spock stole a cloaking device from a Romulan flagship, whose commander had tried to win Spock over.

The Intergalactic War and Tomed

On 23 November 2299, in the Intergalactic War, a fleet of the Galactic Empire appeared over Romulus. A Federation and Klingon force relieved it. The USS Enterprise-B dropped her cloak among the Romulan warbirds to do it. The Romulans joined Captain John Shepard's alliance for the rest of the war.

They did not forgive the cloak, which the Federation had built from the device stolen from them in 2268. Their anger ended in the Tomed Incident of 2311, which cost thousands of Federation lives and destroyed the Enterprise-B. In the Treaty of Algeron, which followed, the Federation gave up cloaking devices altogether.

pages.title: The Salarians
infobox: Sur'Kesh, a world of tropical jungle
Very fast in body and mind; sleep about an hour a day; forget almost nothing
From eggs; about nine in ten Salarians are male
The Salarian Union, a web of clans ruled by the dalatrasses
pages.html:
The Salarians are a quick, slender, amphibian people from Sur'Kesh, who think, speak and move faster than anybody else. Few of them live past forty. They are the great scientists and the great spies of their part of the galaxy. Their Salarian Union is a web of clans ruled by their matriarchs, the dalatrasses. The Enterprise NX-01 found them in 2155, after they had been watching it for three days, and about 2163 they joined the United Federation of Planets.

Sur'Kesh and the Salarian body

The Salarians come from Sur'Kesh, a hot world of tropical jungle. They are warm-blooded amphibians, slender and large-eyed. Everything in them runs fast. They need about an hour's sleep a day. They think so quickly that other peoples seem slow and rather dim to them. They speak accordingly. They remember nearly everything they have ever seen or heard. The price of it is a short life: a Salarian of forty is old.

Salarians hatch from eggs. An egg left unfertilised becomes a male, and a fertilised one becomes a female. Each female lays a clutch of dozens once a year, but the clans allow very few to be fertilised, so that about nine Salarians in ten are men. The women are rare, honoured and kept apart on their home worlds. Salarians feel nothing that humans would call romantic love. They mate to have children, and the matches are arranged between clans, after months of bargaining, for the sake of alliances.

The Salarian Union

The Salarian Union is a web of bloodlines, joined by alliances of birth, which works rather like the noble houses of medieval Europe, with its fiefs, baronies, duchies, planets and marches. Each territory is ruled by a dalatrass, the matriarch of a great household, and the most powerful dalatrasses decide the Union's policy among themselves. Salarian men rise high in business, science and the forces, but they seldom have much say in politics.

Hatchlings imprint on the dalatrass of their clan, and they are loyal ever afterwards to those they knew when young. A Salarian's full name gives his homeworld, nation, city, district and clan before his own name. His first circle, of parents, brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts and cousins, may number a hundred.

Science and secrets

The Salarians are the great scientists of their region, and they trust their knowledge more than their arms. Their forces are small, quick and well informed. Their idea of war is to win it before it begins. They strike first without declaring war, and they see nothing wrong in it. Their Special Tasks Group works in small, separate cells, gathering intelligence, sabotaging and, when it must, killing.

Few Salarians of the modern age hold to any religion, though some believe in rebirth. Most of them would rather study a faith than follow one.

The Rachni and the Krogan

About 500 BC the Salarians made an alliance with the Asari. About 1 a Salarian survey ship found the Rachni, who made war on them both for three centuries. About 80, losing that war, the Salarians came upon the Krogan of Tuchanka, bombed back into savagery by their own atomic wars. The Salarians taught them, armed them with disruptors and gave them warp ships. The Krogan won the war for them.

Then the Krogan turned on the alliance. It was the Salarians who made the genophage, a disease that killed the Krogan's children before they were born, which they meant only as a threat. The Turians loosed it about 710. The Salarians have argued ever since about whether that made them less to blame, and they have never told anybody how the genophage was made.

Earth and the Federation

The Salarians had been allies of the Asari since about 500 BC, and of the Turians since about 700, before they ever heard of Earth. In 2155, far beyond the frontier of Tellar, the Enterprise NX-01 came upon a Salarian ship. The Salarians had been watching it for three days, and they had read every signal it sent, before they let it see them. Their captain then greeted Captain Archer by name.

Joining the United Federation of Planets took longer, because every dalatrass of consequence had to be satisfied. About 2163 the Union agreed the terms. Salarian scientists were soon at work in every great laboratory of the Federation.

pages.title: The serpent people
infobox: Robert E. Howard; Clark Ashton Smith; H. P. Lovecraft
A race with the bodies of men and the heads of snakes
Until kings of men cast them down, about 22,000 BC
Yig, of old; the Old Serpent, in Valusia
To wear the faces of men by sorcery
Kull of Atlantis, King of Valusia
pages.html:
The serpent people are an ancient race with the bodies of men and the heads of snakes. In the lost ages after the Fourth Age they ruled Valusia, on the Thurian continent, served the Old Serpent and practised his sorcery. Kings of men cast them down about 22,000 BC. They lingered in hiding, wearing the faces of men by their sorcery, until Kull of Atlantis found them out in his own court.

Yig and the Old Serpent

The oldest god of the serpent people was Yig, the father of serpents. By the days of Valusia most of them served another master, the Old Serpent, who is the Devil, and they practised the sorcery he taught. Their priests said that the two were one. They were wrong. Yig is not the Devil, and he does not serve him. The serpent people served both, and neither seems to have minded.

Valusia

Valusia was the eldest of the Seven Empires of the Thurian Age, and the serpent people ruled it before men did. About 22,000 BC kings of men overthrew them and took the land for their own.

The serpent people did not die out. They hid in the dark places of the kingdom, and by their sorcery they could wear the faces of men. A serpent man could sit at the king's council in the shape of one of his lords, and nobody would know. There was one thing he could not do in a man's shape. He could not say the old words 'Ka nama kaa lajerama', which his mouth had never been made to form.

Kull

About 18,578 BC Kull of Atlantis, the barbarian who had taken the throne of Valusia, was warned by Ka-nu, the Pictish ambassador, that serpent men were at his court. With the Pict Brule the Spear-slayer he found them out, wearing the faces of his own counsellors. He exposed them with the ancient words, then slew them.

After Valusia

The Cataclysm of about 18,000 BC broke Valusia. Whether any of the serpent people lived on into the Hyborian Age, under the temples of Stygia or anywhere else, no record tells.

One of them is remembered all the same. In the archives of the Great Race of Yith there was a mind from the reptile people of Valusia, borrowed from its own age to write down what it knew.

pages.title: The Silent Hill morgue incident
infobox: The morgue at Silent Hill, Maine
Hollis Tibbetts (Agent Homer) and the FBI agent called Hazel, of H Cell, with a friendly from the FBI
Dr Agnes Pelletier of Mobile Task Force Upsilon-6, three of her people and a security officer
The body and belongings of Walter Sullivan
The body vanished. It was found in Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights in June 2004
pages.html:
The Silent Hill morgue incident was the only time that Delta Green and the SCP Foundation came to blows over Silent Hill, in Maine. On the night of 22 June 1994 both came to the town's morgue to claim the body of Walter Sullivan, who had killed himself in his cell that morning. Each side took the other for something worse. In a minute of darkness a Foundation officer was shot dead and a Delta Green agent wounded. When the lights came back, the body was gone. Nobody outside the two parties has ever known that it happened.

Two claims

Walter Sullivan had been raised in Wish House, the orphanage of the Order of Silent Hill. In June 1994 he killed ten people in ten days, cutting out their hearts and carving numbers into the bodies. He was arrested on 18 June for the murders of two children of Silent Hill. Early on 22 June he was found dead in his cell, with a soup spoon in his neck.

Delta Green had two agents on the case. Hollis Tibbetts of the Drug Enforcement Administration, known in Delta Green as Agent Homer, had known the town since 1983. An FBI agent of his cell, known as Hazel, had got herself attached to the murder inquiry. They had meant to question Sullivan that day.

The Foundation had kept a file on the town since 1939. Its post on the Brahms road logged a disturbance in Silent Hill at about the hour Sullivan died. That afternoon Dr Agnes Pelletier of Mobile Task Force Upsilon-6 arrived at the morgue with papers from the state medical examiner, which the Foundation had written itself. She was told that the body could not be released before the evening, because the FBI had asked for it to be held.

The corridor

The Delta Green agents came at about nine that evening, with federal papers of their own and a young friendly from the FBI, who waited in the car. They found the Foundation's people in the corridor outside the cold room. There were five of them: Dr Pelletier, three of her task force and a security officer whom she had been made to bring. The night attendant looked at both sets of papers, found nothing wrong with either and went back to his desk.

Neither side had met the other before. Neither would say who it was. Tibbetts took the Foundation's people for the enforcers of Majestic 12, who had killed General Reginald Fairfield four months earlier. Dr Pelletier took the Delta Green agents for the Chaos Insurgency. For some hours the two parties stood on either side of the drawer that held the body, while Hazel and Dr Pelletier argued about jurisdiction. The men on both sides kept their hands near their guns. Dr Pelletier had never fired one in her life.

The dark

Some time after midnight the lights went out all over the building. They were out for less than a minute. In that time three shots were fired. When the emergency lights came on, the Foundation's security officer was lying dead with a bullet in his chest. Tibbetts was on the floor with a bullet in his hip. The drawer was open and empty. So was the box that had held Sullivan's clothes and belongings, a child's doll among them.

Nobody had heard the drawer open. Nobody had passed either party in the corridor. Each side's report blames the other for the shooting, and nobody has ever read both. Dr Pelletier added a note to her own report, which nobody above her took up. She wrote that the dead officer had killed men in the army, and she guessed that the wounded man had killed as well.

Afterwards

Both parties were gone before dawn. The Foundation took its dead with it and had the blood scrubbed from the floor. It gave amnestics to the night attendant, as it did to the duty officer at the police station who had signed the body over. The friendly from the FBI was told that there had been a misunderstanding with the state. Hazel drove Tibbetts to a doctor who asked no questions. Delta Green burnt its copies of the case file in a motel room in Pleasant River, as it burns most things.

On paper nothing had happened. On paper the body went from the morgue to a grave without a name near the lake, and a coffin was buried there. Nobody looked inside it until the journalist Joseph Schreiber opened the grave in June 2001. The coffin was empty, with 11/21 scratched on the lid. Neither agency's file says who scratched it.

The Foundation's officer was buried in his own town in another state, after a road accident that had never happened. The Foundation's file on Silent Hill now carries a note on the people at the morgue, whom it believes to have been Delta Green. A week after the incident Alphonse, at the head of Delta Green, ruled that they had been the Foundation, not Majestic. He closed Delta Green's file on Silent Hill, and forbade any agent to go back.

The body

Neither agency ever learnt where the body had gone. A few days after the incident a long-haired man in a long coat was seen about South Ashfield Heights, half a day's drive away, carrying a heavy tool, an old bowl and a bag that dripped. Nobody connected him with the morgue at Silent Hill.

Walter Sullivan's body hung for the next ten years in a hidden room at the back of Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, the flat where he had been born. Henry Townshend found it there in June 2004. A few days later the Foundation took it from the coroner at South Ashfield, ten years after it had lost it at Silent Hill.

pages.title: The Society of Leopold
infobox: Leopold of Murnau, a thirteenth-century inquisitor
The Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome
pages.html:
The Society of Leopold is the Inquisition as it survives in the modern age: a secret Catholic order of hunters sworn to destroy vampires and other supernatural beings. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries its hunters pursued Angelus across Europe, Daniel Holtz among them.

History

The Inquisition that hunted witches and heretics in medieval Europe hunted vampires as well. Its work against them did not stop when the Inquisition was said to have ended. Its successor takes its name from Leopold of Murnau, a leading inquisitor of the early thirteenth century, whose testament became the rule of the order. The Society is no longer an official part of the Catholic Church. It keeps the inquisitors' traditions all the same, and their aim of destroying every supernatural power that is not loyal to Christ. Its headquarters is the Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome.

After the Kindred established the Masquerade in 1435, vampires grew harder to find. For long periods the order dwindled, but it never disappeared. Its members have included Leo Allatius, the seventeenth-century Greek scholar who kept the Vatican Library and wrote on the vampires of Greece. Vampire blood has kept him alive ever since, and in 1999 he led the order. In the modern age the Society is once again the largest body of vampire hunters in the world, and the best informed. Several of its members hold true faith, which vampires cannot easily withstand.

The hunt for Angelus

Angelus and the rest of the Aurelian line flouted the Masquerade so openly that the Camarilla feared for every vampire in Europe. In secret, it often supported or manipulated the organisations that hunted him, the Society of Leopold among them. Hunters such as Daniel Holtz never knew whose money they were spending.

Holtz, a hunter from York, took up the chase in 1764, after Angelus and Darla had destroyed his family. He pursued the pair of them across Europe for nine years. All this was long before the Camarilla made its agreement with the wizarding world in 1900.

pages.title: The Sub-Mariner's Atlantis
infobox: Undersea empire of a blue-skinned people of the sea
The Atlanteans, a water-breathing branch of humankind
About 8000 BC, among drowned ruins its people say were Kull's island
pages.html:
The Sub-Mariner's Atlantis is the undersea empire of a blue-skinned people who breathe water, under the Antarctic sea. Namor rules it. Its people hold that they are the true Atlantis, heirs of the island that sank in the Cataclysm in the days of Kull. Aquaman's people deny it, and they have been saying so since 1942. Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story, which was Númenor.

The people

The Atlanteans of Namor's empire are a branch of humankind that took to the sea in the depths of time, so long ago that their own scholars cannot say how. Most of them have blue skin. They breathe water, not air, and a few minutes on land will suffocate them unless they wear helmets filled with water.

The sea has made them strong. They can bear the crushing weight of the deep and the cold of the southern ocean without harm. They live far longer than surface folk, often to a hundred and fifty. Their cousins in the Pacific, the people of Lemuria, have green skins. The two have been enemies for as long as either can remember.

They worship Neptune, the god of the sea. Atlantis has temples to him, and its kings swear by him. Its people have always been proud, warlike and suspicious of the world above, with some reason. For most of the twentieth century the surface world's ships and bombs did more harm to them than they ever did in return.

Origins

For a long age the Atlanteans lived as wanderers in the deep. Then, about 8000 BC, they found the ruins of a drowned island in the western ocean and built their first city among them. The island was the one that had gone down in the Cataclysm, some ten thousand years before, in the age of Kull. The wanderers took its name.

How they came by that name is the heart of the quarrel. The empire's historians hold that the drowned islanders were their own forefathers, changed by the sea into the people they became, so that Atlantis passed to them by right. Aquaman's people say it is nothing of the kind. In their account, the blue men of the deep moved into an empty house, then painted their name on the door.

In later ages the empire moved its capital south to the Antarctic sea, under the ice, taking the name with it. Aquaman's people have never tired of pointing out that their own kingdom lies in the ocean that bears the name of Atlantis, while the Sub-Mariner's lies at the bottom of the world.

The royal house

In 1919 the emperor was Thakorr. That year an American sea captain, Leonard McKenzie, brought an expedition to the Antarctic in his ship, the Oracle, and the explosives he used to break the ice did damage to the city below. Thakorr sent his daughter, the princess Fen, to spy on the strangers. She fell in love with the captain instead and married him. When Thakorr's warriors came for her, they killed most of the crew, and Fen went home to her father carrying McKenzie's child.

That child was Namor, born in 1920. He was half Atlantean, half human and a mutant besides. He had the strength of both races, with small wings at his ankles that let him fly. He was raised at Thakorr's court to see the surface world as the enemy that was poisoning and plundering the sea. Namor means the Avenging Son in the old tongue of Atlantis.

The court has never been short of rivals to the throne. Namor's cousin Byrrah has plotted against him. The warlords Krang and Attuma have each seized the city more than once. The Lady Dorma, a noblewoman of the court, loved Namor from his youth.

The surface wars

Namor took his grandfather's quarrel to the surface. He came to public notice in 1939. In 1940 he attacked New York, tearing up its streets and fighting the android Human Torch above the city. In 1941 he came back with the sea behind him and flooded it.

Once America was in the war, the empire turned on the Axis instead. Namor fought beside Captain America and the Human Torch in the Invaders until 1945. In 1946 he served in the All-Winners Squad. Some time after that he lost his memory and vanished from the world.

Atlantis was left without its prince. While he lived as a derelict on the Bowery, the surface world's nuclear tests wrecked the city, and its people scattered across the deep. When Johnny Storm of the Fantastic Four gave Namor back his memory in 1962, he went home to find his kingdom in ruins. He made war on the surface again almost at once.

The trident and the crown

Namor gathered his people again in the years after 1962. The Lady Dorma stood by him, though the warlord Krang seized the throne in 1965 while Namor was away. By ancient custom, only one who had won the Trident of Neptune from its hiding place could claim the throne by right, so Namor went to find it. He crossed the floor of the world's seas for it, fought the beasts that guarded it, then brought it home in 1966, when he was crowned king.

Two years before, in 1964, Aquaman had been made king of the other Atlantis. Namor has always denied that this had anything to do with his quest. Very few people believe him.

In 1971 Namor married Dorma at last. On their wedding day she was murdered by Llyra of Lemuria. In 1975 a poison left the people of Atlantis in a sleep like death. Namor went to Victor von Doom for help, a measure of how desperate he was. Doom woke them, then tried to make Namor his servant for it.

Later years

Namor has lost the throne and won it back more than once since. Attuma has held the city for a time, and so have worse. In 1985 Namor joined the Avengers, and in the early 1990s he ran a business empire on the surface. He named his company Oracle Incorporated, after his father's ship.

In the summer of 1994, with the surface world turning on everyone with powers, Atlantis has drawn back into the deep. Namor has kept away from the protests outside the United Nations. Some of the people protesting there are old enough to remember the day he flooded New York.

Atlantis and Aquaman

The empire calls Aquaman's kingdom Poseidonis and never Atlantis, as a matter of policy. Its maps do not show it at all. The empire's case against it is simple. By their own chronicles, Aquaman's people were men of the surface who drowned with their island, then needed sorcery to learn to breathe. To Namor that makes them a surface people who happen to live under the sea. He says so whenever he can.

The two kingdoms also quarrel over their god. Namor's people worship Neptune, and the Trident of Neptune is the sign of their kings. Aquaman's people keep what they call the trident of Poseidon, the same god by his Greek name, as the sign of theirs. Surface scholars have pointed out that this means one of the two tridents is false. Each king knows exactly which.

The whole history of the quarrel, from the U-boat off Iceland in 1942 to the funeral of Superman in 1992, is told on the page The feud of Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner.

The truth of it

Neither kingdom is the Atlantis of the old story. The island the empire's people found in the western ocean was real, and Kull was born on it, but in Kull's day it was a land of barbarian tribes. Nothing in it resembled the great kingdom the Greeks remembered. That kingdom, proud, mighty and swallowed by the sea for making war on the powers of the West, was Númenor, which the Elves called Atalantë, the Downfallen. Myth has also mixed into the story the memory of the star-faring city of the Ancients.

No living man or woman knows the whole truth of it except Albus Dumbledore. He has tried to tell Namor more than once, first in 1945. Namor does not believe him, and suspects Aquaman of putting him up to it.

pages.title: The Tcho-Tcho
infobox: August Derleth and Mark Schorer; Delta Green
A small, hairless people who pass for a hill tribe
The Plateau of Sung, in Burma
Villages in the hills of Vietnam and Cambodia
Lloigor and Zhar, with human sacrifice
Tiger Transit, an air freight company
pages.html:
The Tcho-Tcho are a small, hairless people of the hills of south-east Asia, who pass among strangers for one more mountain tribe. Whether they are wholly human has long been doubted. They worship the beings called Lloigor and Zhar with human sacrifice. Their oldest known home is the Plateau of Sung, in Burma. In November 1969 Delta Green suffered the worst defeat in its history against them, in Cambodia, and it cost Delta Green its official existence.

The Plateau of Sung

The Tcho-Tcho first come into the record as the people of the Plateau of Sung, high in the hills of Burma, where they served Lloigor and Zhar. Even the archives of the Great Race of Yith held the mind of one of them.

Indochina

By the 1960s there were Tcho-Tcho villages in the hills of Vietnam and Cambodia. In 1965 Delta Green warned the Central Intelligence Agency against arming the Tcho-Tcho as allies in the war in Vietnam. The warning was ignored.

Tiger Transit, an air freight company that the CIA used as a front in Indochina, came to be run by Tcho-Tcho.

Cambodia, 1969

On 23 November 1969, in Operation OBSIDIAN, Delta Green struck at a temple complex of the Tcho-Tcho behind the Cambodian border. It went disastrously wrong, and more than three hundred Marines died. Majestic 12 and Delta Green's other rivals in the government used the disaster against it. In July 1970 the Delta Green clearance was withdrawn.

The men who had held it did not forget. On Christmas Day 1971, in Operation BINGO, they diverted American bombers on to every village and holy place of the Tcho-Tcho that they knew of. It was the first operation of the Delta Green that went on without leave.

In later years

In later years the Tcho-Tcho of Tiger Transit came to America. In Chicago they set up an occult crime syndicate, the Tong Shukoran, which deals in strange drugs, Liao among them.

pages.title: The Tellarites
infobox: Stocky humanoids with broad, snouted faces
Argument, which they enjoy more than almost anything
pages.html:
The Tellarites are a stocky, snouted people from Tellar Prime who love an argument more than almost anything else in life. They speak bluntly and loudly. They think it a compliment to be answered in kind. In 2154 a Romulan plot nearly set them at war with the Andorians, their old rivals in trade. Seven years later they were among the four founders of the United Federation of Planets.

Tellar Prime and its people

The Tellarites come from Tellar Prime. They are short, heavily built and strong, with broad, snouted faces. They are not in the least sensitive about their looks.

Argument is the Tellarite art. A Tellarite who disagrees with you will say so, at length and at the top of his voice. He will think less of you if you are too polite to shout back. Outsiders often take this for rudeness. It is nothing of the kind: to a Tellarite a good quarrel is a sign of respect, and an insult well returned is the start of a friendship. Humans who learnt this got on with them well.

The Tellarites and the Andorians

The Tellarites and the Andorians had a long-standing quarrel over trade. In 2154 the two peoples agreed to talk it out at Babel, a neutral world, and the Enterprise NX-01 carried the Tellarite ambassador, Gral, to the meeting. The Romulans were determined that no agreement should come of it. Their drone ship, disguised as a Tellarite vessel, destroyed Shran's ship, the Kumari, then fired on the Enterprise in the shape of an Andorian.

It very nearly worked. Gral denied everything, Shran briefly took him prisoner, and a Tellarite delegate named Naarg shot Shran's lieutenant, Talas, who died of the wound. When Shran demanded a duel to the death with Naarg, Captain Archer fought in the Tellarite's place, and won without killing anybody. Gral then promised Tellar's ships to the hunt for the drone, beside those of Earth, Vulcan and Andoria. Afterwards the Tellarites and the Andorians began their talks early, which surprised everyone, the Tellarites included.

In the United Federation of Planets

In 2155 the Tellarites joined the Coalition of Planets. In 2161 they signed the charter of the United Federation of Planets with United Earth, the Vulcans and the Andorians.

They argued their way through its councils ever afterwards. In 2267 the Tellarite ambassador, Gav, quarrelled in public with Ambassador Sarek of Vulcan on the way to the Babel conference, over whether Coridan should join the Federation. Gav was found murdered soon afterwards. Sarek was suspected, but the killer was an Orion spy disguised as an Andorian, sent to start a war that Orion could profit from. Tellarites went on to serve in Starfleet.

pages.title: The Third World War
infobox: Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'Encounter at Farpoint' (28 September 1987)
pages.html:
The Third World War was fought on Earth from 2026 to 2053. It ended in an exchange of nuclear weapons that killed some six hundred million people and destroyed most of the world's great cities. The lawless decades that followed are called the post-atomic horror. Out of them, in 2063, came Zefram Cochrane's flight in the Phoenix.

The war

The war broke out in 2026, a generation after the Augment War had shown the world what one ambitious power could do. It was fought, in one form or another, for twenty-seven years. It ended in 2053, when the nuclear weapons that every great power had kept since the 1940s were used at last.

The war destroyed the secret organisations that had watched over the world's darker corners, among them Delta Green and the SCP Foundation. A few of their people lived through it, and from their heirs came Section 31, an idea held in secret by never more than five people at a time.

The post-atomic horror

Most of the world's governments fell with their cities. For years afterwards much of Earth was ruled by whoever had guns. Soldiers were kept fighting with drugs. Courts sat without law, and those who stood before them were judged guilty before they spoke.

Some things were kept through it all. Among them was the lore of the Aesir that Asgard had given the people of Earth in 2007. As the Stargate programme collapsed early in the war, copies of it passed into the keeping of Delta Green and the SCP Foundation. Their survivors guarded it through the war as their most precious possession. They kept it classified, and the world at large never learnt of it. The records of the Stargate programme did not survive, so by 2053 its keepers knew that the lore was the Aesir's but not how it had come to Earth.

The way out

On 5 April 2063 Zefram Cochrane flew the Phoenix at warp speed from a missile complex near Bozeman, Montana, drawing on that lore. A Vulcan ship saw the flight and came down to meet him. It was the first open meeting between the Vulcans and the people of Earth. It began the slow mending of the world.

pages.title: The Turians
infobox: Tall, with hard, metallic plates, mandibles and, in the men, swept-back crests
Built of proteins that are mirror images of other peoples', so that their food and others' cannot nourish each other
From fifteen to thirty, then the reserves
The spirits of peoples and places; no gods
pages.html:
The Turians are a tall, plated people from Palaven, a world whose weak magnetic field lets through a fierce sun, which is why their hides grew hard and metallic. They are a people of duty, discipline and service, governed by the Turian Hierarchy, in which every rank must be earned. The Enterprise NX-01 met a Turian patrol in 2160, and about 2165 the Turians joined the United Federation of Planets.

Palaven

Palaven has a core poor in metal, so its magnetic field is weak, and much more of its sun's radiation reaches the ground than reaches Earth's. Its living things grew metallic shells to bear it. The Turians' plates protect them from radiation, though not, as they are quick to point out, from weapons. Palaven has a moon, Menae.

Turians are tall and lean, with mandibles at the sides of their mouths. The men have swept-back crests. Their bodies are built of proteins that are the mirror images of most other peoples', so that human food does them no good at all, and some of it can kill them.

The Hierarchy

The Turian Hierarchy has twenty-seven tiers of citizenship. A Turian becomes a full citizen at the third, after basic training. He climbs the rest by the judgement of his superiors and his equals alike. When somebody is promoted too soon and fails, the shame falls on whoever promoted him. Corruption is rare.

Every Turian serves, from the age of fifteen until about thirty, then passes into the reserves. Police, firefighters and builders of colonies all work within the same military order. Each Primarch rules a cluster of colonies and leaves its people largely alone. The Primarchs vote together on matters that concern the whole Hierarchy. For all that, Turians have wide personal freedoms. A Turian may do very much as he likes, so long as he does his duty.

Character and faith

A Turian puts the group before himself and answers for what he has done. To lie about one's own actions is, to a Turian, the worst sin there is. Each Turian wears painted markings on the face that show which colony he comes from. A Turian without them is called barefaced, which means untrustworthy, and is also what Turians call politicians.

Turians have no gods of good or evil. Each Turian chooses for himself between selfishness and service. They believe that every people and every place has its own spirit, which can inspire the living but never meddles in their affairs. 'Spirits!' is the commonest Turian oath.

The legions

Early in their age of spaceflight, when the Turians had begun to settle other worlds by warp, the colonies farthest from Palaven drifted away under chieftains of their own and grew to hate outsiders. The Unification War that followed forced them back into the Hierarchy. The bitterness took decades to fade, and the colony markings date from that time.

Turian legions hold their ground, fall back in good order and lay ambushes. Each legion keeps a historian to record its honours, and a legion that is destroyed is raised again under the same name. It is said that you will only ever see a Turian's back once he is dead. In the centuries before Earth found them, the Turians had often kept the peace for the Asari and the Salarians, who were glad to have them.

The Krogan Rebellions

The Turians first met the Asari and the Salarians about 700, in the middle of the Krogan Rebellions. They declared war on the Krogan almost at once. The Krogan dropped asteroids on Turian colonies and left three Turian worlds uninhabitable. About 710 the Turians took the disease that the Salarians had made as a threat, made it in quantity and loosed it on every Krogan world. It was the genophage, and after it only one Krogan pregnancy in a thousand came to term.

By about 800 the last Krogan warlords were beaten. The Turians took their place beside the Asari and the Salarians as the alliance's soldiers. The Krogan have never forgiven them. The Turians, who answer for what they have done, do not pretend that it was anybody's doing but their own.

Earth and the Federation

In 2160, after the Earth-Romulan War, the Enterprise NX-01 met a Turian patrol on the far side of Andorian space. The Turians had heard of the war, and their officers wanted to know everything about how it had been fought. They decided that the humans had fought it well.

The Primarchs took longer than the Asari or the Salarians to make up their minds about the United Federation of Planets. About 2165 they voted to join it, and Turian officers soon began to serve in Starfleet.

The siege of Palaven

In the Intergalactic War the Galactic Empire laid siege to Palaven, from 28 April 2299. The legions held the planet for nine months. On 19 January 2300 a Klingon fleet broke the siege, carrying an army of Krogan, the Turians' old enemies, to fight beside them on the ground.

pages.title: The United Federation of Planets
infobox: United Earth; the Tellarites; the Vulcans; the Andorians
The Asari (about 2162); the Salarians (about 2163); the Turians (about 2165)
Paris, for the President; San Francisco, for Starfleet
pages.html:
The United Federation of Planets was founded in 2161 by United Earth, the Tellarites, the Vulcans and the Andorians, who signed its charter on Earth. Within a few years it was joined by the Asari, the Salarians and the Turians, three peoples whom the Enterprise NX-01 had found on its voyages.

Before the Federation

The Federation grew out of a decade of Earth's voyages. In 2151 Earth launched the Enterprise NX-01 under Captain Jonathan Archer. Within three years Archer had made himself useful, sometimes to his own surprise, to the Vulcans, the Andorians and the Tellarites alike. He brought the Vulcans and the Andorians to a ceasefire over Weytahn in 2152. In 2154 he gathered ships from all four worlds into one fleet to hunt a Romulan drone that was trying to set them against one another.

In 2155 the four, with other peoples, met on Earth to form the Coalition of Planets. John Frederick Paxton's movement, Terra Prime, seized an array on Mars and demanded that every alien leave Earth. Archer stopped him. Then he told the delegates that the peoples of the galaxy should explore its mysteries together, which was what most of them had come to hear.

From 2156 to 2160 Earth fought the Romulans, a war that ended in the Neutral Zone. It did a good deal to persuade the Coalition that its members would be safer in something stronger.

The founding

In 2161 United Earth, the Tellarites, the Vulcans and the Andorians signed the charter of the United Federation of Planets. Archer spoke at the signing. The Enterprise NX-01, which had done more than any other ship to bring it about, was retired that year after ten years of service.

The Federation was governed by a President, who sat in Paris, with a Council of delegates from its member worlds. Starfleet, its service for exploration and defence, had its headquarters in San Francisco, with its Academy.

The first to join

Three peoples whom the Enterprise NX-01 had found far beyond the frontiers of the four founders were the first to join them. The Asari of Thessia came first, about 2162. The Salarians of Sur'Kesh followed about 2163, once the dalatrasses of their great clans had agreed the terms. The Turians of Palaven joined about 2165, after the Primarchs of the Turian Hierarchy had voted for it.

None of the three had been a founder. All three had been watching the founders closely since the Enterprise first came among them, and once it existed they saw no reason to stay outside it. The Asari brought their diplomats, the Salarians their scientists and the Turians their soldiers. The Federation was never quite the same again.

The Federation also offered the Quarians of the Migrant Fleet medicine and worlds to settle, first about 2164, then again about 2250. Both times they refused, because the Federation would not help them take Rannoch back from the Geth. It would not make war on the Geth for them, nor help to destroy a people.

The Free Jaffa Nation

About 2270 the Free Jaffa Nation joined the Federation. The Jaffa were a warrior people of human stock whom the Goa'uld had once bred as soldiers, and Captain Kirk's Enterprise had found their worlds about 2268. Earth had long forgotten them, but the Jaffa remembered the Tau'ri, the people of Earth, whose warriors had helped to free their forefathers from the Goa'uld. They joined out of respect and thanks for them.

The Four Years War

From 2251 to 2255 the Federation fought its first open war with the Klingon Empire, the Four Years War. It began with Garth of Izar's victories at Axanar. It ended with the Treaty of Axanar of 2255, which moved the border in the Federation's favour and brought it several new worlds.

The Galactic Empire

In 2293 the Federation met the Galactic Empire, a human power from a distant galaxy, which attacked Starbase Side 7 in the Imperial Entanglement. That battle ended with the Klingons fighting beside the Federation, which led to the Khitomer Accords the same year.

The Empire came back in 2299 to conquer the Milky Way. In the Intergalactic War the Federation fought in an alliance with the Klingons, the Romulans, the Gorn, the Tholians, the Geth and the Quarians, gathered by Captain John Shepard of the USS Enterprise-B. The alliance threw the Empire out at the Battle of Earth in March 2300. In 2350 the Quarians and the Geth of Rannoch joined the Federation.

The great centuries

The Federation grew steadily. In 2267 the Babel conference decided whether Coridan, rich in dilithium, should join. The same year the Organians imposed a peace on the Federation and the Klingons.

pages.title: The Volus
infobox: Irune, far out from its star, kept warm by a thick, crushing atmosphere of ammonia
Short and stout; always in pressure suits among other peoples
The Turians, whose clients the Volus became centuries ago
pages.html:
The Volus are a short, stout people from Irune, a world whose crushing atmosphere of ammonia would kill a human, as Earth's thin air would kill a Volus. Among other peoples they always wear pressure suits. They are the traders and bankers of their part of the galaxy. Centuries ago they gave themselves to the protection of the Turians in return for managing their money. The Enterprise NX-01 met them in 2160, alongside the Turians.

Irune

Irune circles its star well outside the band where water would stay liquid. It is warm enough for life only because its heavy atmosphere traps the heat, and the life that grew up there is built on ammonia. Air of the kind most peoples breathe is poison to a Volus. At the low pressure most peoples live in, a Volus's flesh splits open, so that outside Irune a Volus never goes without a pressure suit and a breathing mask.

Trade

Volus society is made up of tribes, and from the start it was built on exchange. Tribes traded land, goods and even people for standing, which turned the Volus very early towards commerce. They became the bankers of their region. The laws by which the alliance's worlds lend, borrow and settle their accounts were written by Volus. Volus still keep them in balance.

Clients of the Turians

The Volus are not fighters. Centuries ago they joined the Turian Hierarchy of their own free will, as clients, putting their skill with money at the Turians' service in return for the protection of the Turian legions. The Turians, who are poor merchants, have done well out of the bargain. So have the Volus, who say so rather more often.

Earth

In 2160 the Enterprise NX-01 met the Volus soon after the Turians. A Volus trader aboard a Turian ship asked Captain Jonathan Archer, before anything else, what Earth used for money.

pages.title: The Vorcha
infobox: Small, scarred humanoids, part mammal and part reptile to look at
Their bodies remake themselves to suit wherever they are; they can eat and breathe almost anything
Mostly as mercenaries beside the Krogan
pages.html:
The Vorcha are a small, savage, short-lived people from Heshtok, whose bodies remake themselves to suit whatever world they find themselves on. They can eat and breathe almost anything. They fight one another constantly. Despised by most other peoples as vermin, they find work mostly beside the Krogan, as mercenaries. The Enterprise NX-01 met them in 2155, fighting for the Orion Syndicate.

Heshtok and the Vorcha body

A Vorcha's body is full of unformed cells, ready to become whatever it needs. When a Vorcha is hurt, the damaged part grows back tougher. A Vorcha struggling for breath in poor air grows lungs to suit it. One living under heavy gravity grows heavier bones and muscles. Their brains do not change, and a Vorcha seldom makes more than one great change in its life. It does not have long to make it: a Vorcha lives about twenty years.

Ways

Vorcha attack one another from their earliest days. The young who survive it grow stronger, cleverer and harder to kill. Giving and taking pain is, among Vorcha, an ordinary way of talking. Few of them study anything, which their short lives partly explain. Since they can live almost anywhere, they turn up almost everywhere, generally where nobody wants them.

Mercenaries

Most other peoples will not have Vorcha among them. The Krogan, who value toughness above everything, will, and most Vorcha who leave Heshtok end up in Krogan mercenary bands. In 2155 the Krogan crew that the Orion Syndicate sent after the Enterprise NX-01 had Vorcha in it, the first that humans had ever seen. They were very hard to stun.

pages.title: The Vulcans
infobox: Vulcan, about sixteen light years from Earth
ShiKahr; Mount Seleya; Gol; the desert called the Forge
Humanoid, with pointed ears and green blood
Stronger than humans; telepathic by touch; often live past two hundred
Survivors of the fall of the Eldar, about 11,000 BC, though the Vulcans never knew it
Logic, as Surak taught it in the fourth century
The Romulans, who left Vulcan after Surak's death
In secret, at Carbon Creek, Pennsylvania, 1957; openly, at Bozeman, Montana, 5 April 2063
Surak; T'Pau; T'Pol; Soval; Sarek; Spock
pages.html:
The Vulcans are the people of Vulcan, a hot, dry world about sixteen light years from Earth. They live by logic, as the philosopher Surak taught them in the fourth century, after wars that came close to destroying their planet. Those who would not follow him left Vulcan and became the Romulans. It was a Vulcan ship that came down at Bozeman on the night of Zefram Cochrane's flight, 5 April 2063, and in 2161 the Vulcans were among the founders of the United Federation of Planets.

Vulcan and its people

Vulcan is a desert world, hotter than Earth, with thin air that leaves a visitor gasping. It has no moon. Its people live in cities such as ShiKahr, and beyond them lies a great desert called the Forge. Among their holy places are the temples of Mount Seleya and the monastery at Gol, where the masters of the kolinahr teach.

Vulcans have pointed ears and upswept brows. Their blood is green, because it is built on copper rather than iron. They are a good deal stronger than humans, they live for two centuries or more, and they can share another person's thoughts by touch, in what they call the mind meld. Every seven years a Vulcan man passes through the pon farr, a fever of the blood that will kill him unless he takes a mate or burns it out of himself in combat. Vulcans do not discuss it with outsiders.

Vulcans feel as strongly as their ancestors did. What they have learnt is to master what they feel, and they are not always quite as good at it as they would have others believe.

Children of the Eldar

The Vulcans did not know it, but they came of the Eldar. When the Eldar empire fell, about 11,000 BC, a band of its survivors fled to Vulcan, a hot, harsh world on the edge of what had been their realm. They lost their ships there, with their craft, and in time their memory of what they had been. Their descendants became the Vulcans: long-lived, telepathic and pointed of ear, with passions they could barely rule. Neither the Vulcans nor the Romulans who later left them ever learnt where they came from.

The ancient Vulcans

Five thousand years ago the Vulcans were barbarians. Paranoia and murderous rage were common among them. Their feuds could last for generations. They worshipped gods of war, peace and death, whose images were carved on the Stone of Gol, a weapon that turned the violent thoughts of those it was used on against their own minds.

They were also clever, which made the rest a great deal worse. By the fourth century of Earth's reckoning their wars were being fought with atomic weapons, and the planet itself came close to being destroyed.

Surak and the Time of Awakening

In the worst of those wars the philosopher Surak taught that his people must master their passions by logic or perish. His followers went out among the warring nations as emissaries of peace. The years of his teaching are remembered as the Time of Awakening.

Without knowing it, Surak gave his people what the Path had given their kin among the Eldar: a discipline that kept their passions from ruling them.

Surak died of radiation sickness after an atomic attack on his followers, made by Vulcans who marched beneath the raptor's wings, shortly before the last battle of the war. His teachings won all the same. Rebuilding took a very long time: Ambassador Soval once admitted that his people had needed nearly a thousand years to recover from their last war, far longer than Earth needed after its own.

Vulcans hold Surak to be the greatest of their people. The story of his life is told on its own page, under Surak of Vulcan.

The Sundering

Not every Vulcan accepted Surak. After his death those who would not left Vulcan for good, in the parting later called the Sundering, and went far out into space. They settled the twin worlds that came to be called Romulus and Remus. There they became the Romulans. Humans did not know of the kinship until 2266, when they saw a Romulan's face for the first time.

Logic and belief

The discipline of logic is not the same for every Vulcan. Most master their feelings without denying that they have them. The masters of Gol go further, in the kolinahr, a long ordeal that purges every last emotion. Few complete it.

Vulcans believe that a person's katra, the living spirit, can be passed by a meld into another mind before death, to be carried home to Mount Seleya. In 2285 Spock's katra was carried there in the mind of a human friend and restored to his body, in the old rite of fal-tor-pan. Vulcans prize the saying of infinite diversity in infinite combinations, which they show in a symbol called the IDIC.

The watch on Earth

The Vulcans watched Earth for a long time before they spoke to it, and once, by accident, they lived on it. In the autumn of 1957 a Vulcan survey ship, sent to watch the launch of Earth's first satellite, crashed in the woods near Carbon Creek, a mining town in Pennsylvania. Its captain was killed. The three survivors, T'Mir, Mestral and Stron, waited weeks for a rescue that did not come, then went down into the town dressed as humans, with their ears hidden. For months they lived among the townspeople, and nobody guessed what they were. When an explosion trapped miners underground, Mestral cut them free with a phaser, and nobody in Carbon Creek ever learnt how. When a Vulcan ship came for them at last, Mestral chose to stay on Earth. T'Mir told the rescuers that he had died in the crash. She was the great-grandmother of T'Pol, who served aboard the Enterprise NX-01 nearly two centuries later.

The great star-faring powers of the twentieth century had little to do with Vulcan, which suited the Vulcans very well. They kept out of every war of that age and went on watching. Earth's few secret warships of the early 2000s, built from captured Goa'uld engines, did not change their minds. As the Vulcans saw it, a people that flew in borrowed engines had not yet learnt to fly.

On 5 April 2063 Zefram Cochrane took the Phoenix to warp speed from Bozeman, Montana, in an engine of Earth's own making. A Vulcan survey ship saw the trace of the flight. That night it came down outside the town, and its captain greeted Cochrane. It was the first open meeting between the Vulcans and the people of Earth.

In the decades that followed the Vulcans kept an embassy on Earth and helped its people mend their world. They were also careful about what they taught.
