They gave away their knowledge of warp engines so slowly that many on Earth came to resent them, Captain Jonathan Archer among them. By the time the Enterprise NX-01 was launched in April 2151, the old powers of the stars had gone, and the Vulcans were the strongest people within reach of Earth.

The Vulcan High Command

By the twenty-second century Vulcan was ruled by the Vulcan High Command, which controlled the fleet and most of the planet. It had drifted a long way from Surak. It treated the mind meld as a disgrace and persecuted those who practised it, blaming them for the Pa'nar Syndrome, a disease that a careless meld could spread. It hunted the Syrrannites, a sect who held to Surak's teachings as he had first given them.

Its quarrel with the Andorians, its neighbours, went back a century. In 2097 the Vulcans annexed Weytahn, an Andorian colony that they called Paan Mokar. Under the monastery at P'Jem they hid a long-range sensor array to spy on Andoria. In 2151 Captain Archer exposed it, and the Andorians destroyed the monastery. In 2152 Archer brought the two peoples to a ceasefire at Weytahn. It was the first great service that humans had ever done the Vulcans, and the High Command did not much enjoy owing it.

In 2154 a bomb wrecked the United Earth embassy on Vulcan, killing forty-three people, Vice-Admiral Maxwell Forrest among them. Administrator V'Las blamed the Syrrannites. In the Forge their leader, Syrran, died after passing to Archer what the Syrrannites held to be the katra of Surak. Guided by it, Archer found the Kir'Shara, Surak's own teachings, at the sanctuary of T'Karath. V'Las meanwhile sent the fleet against Andoria, on the pretext that the Andorians were building a weapon like the Xindi's.

Archer and T'Pau brought the Kir'Shara before the High Command. High Minister Kuvak ordered the fleet home, and the High Command was dissolved. Vulcan turned back to Surak's teachings as he had given them, the meld among them, and it stopped looking over Earth's shoulder. V'Las, it was afterwards learnt, had been working with a Romulan agent named Talok, who hoped to bring the two worlds back together under Romulus.

In the United Federation of Planets

In 2155 the Vulcans joined the Coalition of Planets. In 2161 they signed the charter of the United Federation of Planets with United Earth, the Andorians and the Tellarites. T'Pau became one of the most respected figures on Vulcan. In 2267 she presided over Spock's marriage rites. She was the only person ever to turn down a seat on the Federation Council.

Vulcans served the Federation as diplomats, scientists and officers. For decades Sarek was its most famous ambassador. In 2268 the USS Intrepid, crewed entirely by Vulcans, was lost with all four hundred of them.

pages.title: The Weaver
infobox: One of the three great powers of the Triat
Pattern Spiders and the spirits of cities and machines
pages.html:
The Weaver is one of the three great powers that the Garou believe work through creation: the power of order, pattern and form. Once it gave lasting shape to what the Wyld created. The Garou hold that it went mad, that it bound the Wyrm in its web, and that it now spins the whole world towards stillness.

In Garou belief

The Garou teach that creation is shaped by three powers, which they call the Triat. The Wyld brings forth new things. The Weaver gives them pattern and permanence. The Wyrm once ended whatever had served its time, so that the balance held. The Weaver is the maker of laws, structures and reasons. It is the power behind every wall, road, ledger and machine.

In the Garou telling, the Weaver grew obsessed with its own work. It spun ever more of the world into its web, until it caught the Wyrm itself and bound it there. The Wyrm went mad in the binding and became the Corruptor. The Weaver did not stop. Its madness, the Garou hold, shows in the spread of cities over the wild and in the spirit world hardening into fixed patterns. It shows, too, in a world grown so ordered that nothing new can grow.

The being the Garou call the Wyrm is the one Scripture calls Satan. The tale of his binding in the Weaver's web is told only by the Garou.

Servants and the Garou

The Weaver's spirits are the spirits of order, of cities, of electricity and of machines. Chief among them are the Pattern Spiders, which spin and mend the webs that bind the spirit world into shape. Most Garou see the Weaver as a lesser danger than the Wyrm, but a danger still, and they fight its works where they choke the wild. The Glass Walkers, the tribe of the cities, deal with its spirits and bargain with them. That is why the other tribes suspect them of leaning too far towards it.

pages.title: The Weird Happenings Organisation
infobox: A British government body for the paranormal
The twins Brigadier Alysande Stuart and Dr Alistaire Stuart
Black Air; from 1996, a new department under Alistaire Stuart
pages.html:
The Weird Happenings Organisation, W.H.O. for short, was the British government body that looked into the paranormal from the late 1980s until 1992. It was run by twins, Brigadier Alysande Stuart and her brother, Dr Alistaire Stuart, a physicist. It worked beside the Excalibur team, though it kept an eye on it too. When Alysande was murdered in 1992, the organisation was wound up, and in the summer of 1994 its work belongs to Black Air. Alistaire built it up again in 1997.

The twins

Alysande Stuart was a soldier, a brigadier, who ran W.H.O. Her twin, Alistaire, was its scientist. They set it up to look into weird happenings across Britain, work that the older RCX had done before them and resented losing. In 1989 Alistaire looked into a railway engine that had come from another Britain, one where the Reich had won the war.

Like every British service of its kind, W.H.O. was a Muggle body. Its masters may have known that a Ministry of Magic existed, but they had no dealings with it.

Working with the team

W.H.O. kept a base at Ruthymere. In 1991 it asked the Excalibur team for help when a scientist, Jonathan Cayre, built a machine in the likeness of Air-Walker, once a herald of Galactus. It also had the team's lighthouse bugged, until Lockheed the dragon frightened its agents off.

Alistaire was fond of Rachel Summers, and in 1991 he asked her to Ireland. Early in 1992 he led a survey at a prehistoric site in County Sligo, where Kitty Pryde mapped the foundations of a buried village for him. When the team's aircraft was stolen from the hangar at Ruthymere, the Brigadier lent them a captured one.

Alysande's death

In August 1992 Alysande Stuart was killed at the housewarming party at Braddock Manor by Jamie Braddock, Brian's elder brother, whom Sat-yr-9 had smuggled in among the guests. The RCX had framed her for crimes she had not committed, hoping to weaken W.H.O. Nick Fury of S.H.I.E.L.D. cleared her name, and she was buried at Dunoon nine days after her death.

W.H.O. did not survive her. It was wound up, and Alistaire found his contract handed over to the RCX. At the end of 1992 the RCX shut him away at Cloud Nine, its hidden home for some four hundred Warpies, the children whom the Jaspers warp had changed. The Excalibur team got him out in 1993.

Alistaire Stuart afterwards

In 1996 Black Air, which had taken over W.H.O.'s work, hunted Alistaire across England and shot down the aircraft that was carrying him to Muir Island. He lived. That summer, after the Excalibur team had broken Black Air in London, the government made him Director of a new department, which took in what was left of W.H.O. and Black Air. He offered Rory Campbell its work with mutants.

In 1997 he took Rory to Japan to be fitted with an artificial leg. Later that year he went home to England to build W.H.O. up again. In August 1998 he was at Brian Braddock's wedding in Otherworld, where he talked to Kitty Pryde about Rachel Summers, lost somewhere in the stream of time.

pages.title: The Wizard of Deception
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Return of the Green Ranger, Part 1' (20 February 1995)
The green candle, November 1993; a copy of Tommy Oliver, February 1995
The Dragon Coin, from Matt Cook, February 1995
End of February 1995, by Tommy Oliver, with the Wizard's own wand
pages.html:
The Wizard of Deception is the sorcerer who made Rita Repulsa her cursed green candle, which drained Tommy Oliver's powers in November 1993. At the end of February 1995 she called on him again. He made an evil copy of Tommy, armed it with the Dragon Coin that he took from Matt Cook, then trapped the other Rangers in the Angel Grove of the 1700s. Tommy destroyed him with the Wizard's own wand.

The green candle

In the autumn of 1993 Rita Repulsa lost the Black Dragon, the war machine that she had taken for an ally. Late that November she went to the Wizard of Deception for something subtler. He made her a green candle. When it had burnt down, the Green Ranger's powers would be gone.

Goldar took Tommy Oliver prisoner while it burnt. Jason Lee Scott went into the Dark Dimension to fetch it, but it burnt out before he could bring it back. Before the end Tommy gave his coin to Jason, so that Rita could never have it again.

The Wizard's craft had a second use. In September 1994, in the war that was afterwards undone, Rita burnt a green candle of his making against Lord Drakkon, at Zordon's own request.

The copy of Tommy Oliver

In February 1995 Rita was back on the Moon, married to Lord Zedd. She summoned the Wizard to get rid of the Rangers. The White Ranger, Tommy, was the obstacle.

The Wizard tried first to copy Tommy by way of Bulk and Skull, which failed. Then a Putty cut a lock of Tommy's hair, from which the Wizard made a copy of him. He bound it with a spell. It needed a Green Ranger's coin, so the Wizard came for the Dragon Coin, which he took from Matt Cook to arm it. The copy came to be called Tom, to tell him apart from Tommy.

Tommy fell ill. The copy lured the other Rangers to a meeting, at which the Wizard sent them back to the Angel Grove of the late 1700s, trapped and powerless. A girl of that town helped them to escape, while the Wizard loosed giant rats on it. In the present the copy fought the White Ranger to a standstill, until the Wizard stripped Tommy of his armour and ordered the copy to wake the Dragonzord against Angel Grove.

Tommy, barely able to stand, tricked the Wizard and the copy into giving away where his friends were held. The Rangers came home to fight the Dragonzord. Tommy took the Wizard's wand from him, which destroyed the Wizard and broke the spell on the copy.

The copy was sorry for what he had done. He laid the Dragonzord to rest for good, then chose to stay in the Angel Grove of the 1700s. The coin stayed with him, together with the Dragonzord. Matt did not try to get it back. He had killed Grace Sterling with that coin on his chest, and he said he was glad to see it go.

pages.title: The World of the Coinless
infobox: Drakkon's world; Ranger Sentries; Finster-5; Deadlock
Another world, lying beside this one
Rita Repulsa; Lord Drakkon; the Ranger Slayer, from December 1994
The Coinless, led by that world's Zack Taylor
By Dark Specter's creatures, early in 1995
pages.html:
The World of the Coinless is another world, lying beside this one, in which Tommy Oliver stayed with Rita Repulsa when her spell on him broke. As Lord Drakkon he conquered it, broke its Power Rangers, then ruled it through an army in Ranger armour. It takes its name from the Coinless, the old Rangers of that world, who fought on after their Power Coins had been taken from them. Its time does not keep step with this world's: when Tommy Oliver was thrown into it in the autumn of 1993, he found it some years further on.

How it came apart from this one

The two worlds had one history until the day Jason Lee Scott broke Rita Repulsa's spell on the Green Ranger. Each had a Zordon, an Angel Grove, five Rangers chosen from one school. In this world Tommy Oliver joined them. In the other he went back to Rita of his own free will, took the name of Lord Drakkon, then led her armies against the Earth.

The conquest took about two years, a city at a time, until governments stopped resisting. The Rangers held out longest. They lost on the day that world remembers as the day the Rangers fell. Drakkon broke into the Command Center, cut down Jason, took the new White Ranger's power for himself, then broke Zordon's tube. Ninjor died there with Alpha 5. Soon afterwards Drakkon murdered Rita. He ruled alone from then on.

Drakkon's Earth

What Tommy Oliver found in 1993 was a dark, hard, orderly place. Angel Grove had statues of the Green Ranger in it, beside statues of Rita. The Command Center was a ruin in the desert, with the wrecks of the Thunderzords lying next to it. Other dead Zords lay in a graveyard of their own, the White Tigerzord among them. Drakkon ruled from a throne by propaganda, fear and force. Later he had a tower on that world's Moon.

He believed that he had saved the place. Nothing from outside dared attack a world that his army guarded. He kept the Lord Zedd of that world, whom he had captured, as a war machine: a giant rebuilt in metal.

The Ranger Sentries

The army was made out of the Rangers' own power. Drakkon fed the captured Power Coins into a machine called the Diffuser, which shared the strength of each coin among a whole corps of soldiers. They wore Ranger armour. There were four kinds.

The Tyrannosaurus Sentries, in red, were the elite, armed with spears. The Mastodon Sentries, in black, were the foot soldiers, who carried blasters. The Sabre-tooth Sentries, in yellow, were the officers. The Pterodactyl Sentries, in pink, were marksmen. They were stood down once Drakkon had made that world's Kimberly his Ranger Slayer.

There were no blue Sentries. That world's Trini had hidden the Blue coin, which the Coinless called the Relic. A switch on Drakkon's throne could burn the power out of any Sentry who failed him. He used it on a Sabre-tooth officer who had failed him, while Tommy Oliver was loose in his world.

During the war of September 1994 he raised new kinds of Sentry, with powers stolen from the Rangers of later years. Those were undone with the rest of that war.

Drakkon's household

Finster, who had made Rita's monsters, stayed loyal to Drakkon after her death. Drakkon rebuilt him as Finster-5, part machine, with pieces of Alpha 5 in him. In the war of 1994 Finster-5 warned his master against taking too many powers at once. He saved him from Rita's candle, for which Drakkon broke his neck. The mending of the world gave him his life back. Scorpina commanded the Sentries, as she went on doing when Drakkon was believed dead.

Deadlock was the prison tower. Its most secret prisoner was Jason, that world's Red Ranger, whom everybody believed Drakkon had killed on the day the Rangers fell. He was kept alive for years as a trophy, chained in a suit of armour. He never tried to escape, because Drakkon had told him that the Ranger Slayer had orders to kill herself if he did.

The Coinless

The Coinless were the Rangers who were left, with the friends who stood by them. None of them had a Power Coin, which was the meaning of the name. They began with a message. On the day the Rangers fell, this world's Zordon, adrift between the two, came upon that world's Zordon in his last hour. He gave the sabre Saba a message for Zack. Zack founded the Coinless on the strength of it, then led them.

With Zack were Trini, Aisha Campbell and Bulk. Skull, Bulk's old friend, wore the armour of a Tyrannosaurus Sentry in Drakkon's army, where he was their spy. Katherine Hillard was with them for a time. Adam Park lived to see Drakkon gone. Their hiding place was in Canada. All of them were older than this world's Rangers, worn down, still fighting.

Their dead were many. Billy Cranston died shielding Trini; his photograph hung on their wall. Matthew Cook died in a hospital of wounds from a Sentry attack. Kimberly had led a party of pupils out of Angel Grove High School through the Mastodon Sentries, with two of their teachers, then fought on for a long time with Bulk beside her. After those two deaths she went to kill Drakkon by herself, which is how he came to take her.

At the end of October 1993 the wreck of the Black Dragon threw this world's Tommy Oliver among them, with Billy Cranston. The Coinless took the two boys in. With their help, with Saba's too, Drakkon was stripped of his powers for a time. In the war of September 1994 Zack was shot dead freeing Ninjor from Drakkon's tower. Skull was caught helping him, so Drakkon killed him. The mending gave both of them back.

After Drakkon

Drakkon was lost in the wreck of that war. His people believed him dead. In December 1994, by this world's reckoning, the Ranger Slayer came home, free of his spell, meaning to make amends. She found that Trini had raised Rita Repulsa from the dead with an old spell. An army of the dead followed the witch. The Sentries chose to follow Kimberly. Rita was sealed in her own staff, then Kimberly ruled in Drakkon's place.

She pulled Deadlock down. In it she found Jason alive. Then a signal sent out from that world brought an answer nobody had wanted: Eclipta, a herald of Dark Specter, who killed Adam Park. In the fighting every Power Coin was fed into a Diffuser at once. The coins burnt out. That was the end of the Sentries. Jason carried the dead coins off to the old fortress, where he went on living.

By February 1995 Dark Specter's creatures were overrunning what was left. They were things of lava that had once been people, Zack among them. Drakkon came back to this, bringing Kiya Kyatyl, an Omega Ranger who had turned on her team. Kimberly took him prisoner with the help of Trini, backed by Scorpina. He talked them round. Finster-5 made new armour, so that six of them became the Drakkon Rangers: Drakkon, Bulk, Trini, Scorpina, Kiya and Kimberly.

Skull, who had become a monster, let the horde into their stronghold. Kimberly was lost holding the hatch. The other five crossed into this world to carry the fight to Dark Specter, which is where Drakkon died. Nobody in this world can say whether the cleansing of the Grid reached that one.

pages.title: The Wyld
infobox: One of the three great powers of the Triat
pages.html:
The Wyld is one of the three great powers that the Garou believe work through creation. It is the power of raw creation, change and untamed life, from which all new things spring. The Garou hold that it is fading, starved by the Weaver's order and devoured by the Wyrm's corruption.

In Garou belief

In the Triat as the Garou teach it, the Wyld comes first. It is the endless, formless source of new things: the wildness in storms, forests, birth and growth. The Weaver gives its creations shape, and in time the Wyrm, in its proper place, would clear them away. Without the Wyld nothing new would ever be made. Its spirits are spirits of wild places, of chaos and of transformation. Many of them have no fixed form at all.

The Garou hold that the Wyld is the weakest of the three in this age. The Weaver has spun its webs over much of the world. The Wyrm's corruption devours what remains, and the truly wild places, where the Wyld is still strong, grow fewer every year. Its strength is greatest in the oldest caerns, in deep forests and on remote mountains. It is strong, too, in the places Minerva McGonagall warned Harry Potter to leave untouched: rings of stones, and springs in woods where the trees feel as though they are watching.

The Wyld and the Garou

The Garou count themselves defenders of the Wyld as well as enemies of the Wyrm, since Gaia's health depends on the balance being restored. The Black Furies, the Fianna and the Red Talons are closest to it. The Fianna keep old friendships with the Fair Folk, whom many hold to be children of the Wyld. Some Garou fear the Wyld as well, because untamed change can destroy as easily as it creates.

pages.title: The Yahg
infobox: Mass Effect 2, 'Lair of the Shadow Broker' (7 September 2010)
Parnack, forbidden to all visitors since 2125
Packs, ruled by whoever can master them
2125, by surveyors of the Asari, Salarian and Turian alliance
pages.html:
The Yahg are a people of huge predators from Parnack, who live in packs and will follow only a master. In 2125 envoys of the alliance of the Asari, the Salarians and the Turians came to them as equals. The Yahg took it for contempt and killed every one of them. Parnack has been forbidden to visitors ever since.

Packs

Yahg live and think in packs. A group of Yahg will not work together until one of them has made himself master of the rest, by cunning or by force. Once beaten, a Yahg bears no grudge and serves his new master loyally. Equality, to a Yahg, is an insult: it means that one has not been thought worth the trouble of mastering.

The envoys of 2125

Surveyors of the alliance found the Yahg in 2125, and envoys followed to open relations. They offered the Yahg the courtesy they would have offered anybody, as equals. The Yahg massacred the whole delegation. The alliance broke off all contact and declared Parnack forbidden, on the grounds that the Yahg could never live peaceably among other peoples.

In 2160 the Turians warned Captain Jonathan Archer of the Enterprise NX-01 to keep well away from Parnack. He did.

pages.title: The Yellow Sign
infobox: A symbol of no human script
A curious symbol or letter in gold
Inlaid in a clasp of black onyx, New York
The King in Yellow and Carcosa
It unhinges the mind of anyone who looks at it
pages.html:
The Yellow Sign is the mark of the King in Yellow: a curious symbol or letter in gold that belongs to no human script. Nobody is quite sure where it came from, except that it is very old. In Delta Green's files it unhinges the mind of anyone who looks at it, and seems to move when it is watched. In New York in 1895 a dead man came up the stairs for it.

The clasp

In March 1895 Tessie Reardon, an artist's model of New York, was coming back from the Aquarium at the Battery when she picked up a clasp of black onyx. Inlaid in it was a curious symbol or letter in gold. She advertised it, but nobody came to claim it. The same day she dreamt for the first time of a hearse passing under her window, with a driver who looked up at her.

She gave the clasp to the painter Scott, whose model she was, in his studio on Washington Square. Next door to the studio stood a church, whose night-watchman sat on its steps: a soft, white, puffy man with a face like a grave-worm. Before the end Scott had heard him ask, 'Have you found the Yellow Sign?'

When Scott and Tessie had read The King in Yellow she begged him to throw the clasp away. He would not. That night the hearse stopped outside. The watchman came up the stairs, tore the clasp from Scott's coat and struck him down. Tessie died. The doctor found the watchman lying beside her, and said that he must have been dead for months.

Castaigne's sign

In New York that same year Hildred Castaigne believed that the Yellow Sign marked the men of a great conspiracy. Mr Wilde of Bleecker Street had gathered them, he thought, to put him on a throne. He set the Sign on the orders he wrote out. There was no conspiracy and no throne. Castaigne had read the play, and the Sign meant everything to him.

Delta Green's files

Delta Green's files say that the Sign is old, so old that nobody is sure where it came from, and that it is bound up with Hastur. It seems to move when it is watched. It can unhinge the mind of anyone who looks at it.

With the play's many translations, the files count it as one of the two roads by which the King's influence travels from mind to mind. In 1995 a friend of Delta Green noticed an occult symbol among the papers of a missing painter in Manhattan. That was the beginning of Operation ALICE.

Where the accounts disagree

No account of 1895 sets down the Sign's shape. Nor do the accounts of 1895 bear out the files in every point. Tessie Reardon picked up the Sign in March 1895, and advertised it, without coming to harm. It harmed her only after she had read the play. Delta Green's files make the Sign dangerous to the eye by itself. This page gives both.

pages.title: Thor
infobox: Asgard; founding member of the Avengers
The Goa'uld, whom he fought from the rising against Ra to the Protected Planets Treaty
Away from Earth, commanding Asgard's fleet against the Replicators in the Pegasus galaxy
Supreme Commander of the Asgard fleet
The Biliskner (lost in 2000); the Daniel Jackson
pages.html:
Thor, son of Odin, is the Asgardian whom the Norsemen worshipped as the god of thunder, and one of the founders of the Avengers. For thirty years he was the man with the hammer in every picture of the team. By 1994 Asgard's war against the Replicators has called him away from Earth. Eric Masterson, as Thunderstrike, stands with the Avengers in his place.

Ra

Thor's war with the Goa'uld began in Egypt, some five thousand years ago. Ra, the greatest of the Goa'uld, ruled there as the sun god, and carried Egyptians away through his Stargate as slaves. When the people rose against him at last, Thor came down to fight beside them.

He came in a storm, which in that part of the world was a wonder in itself. While the rebels stormed the gate, he broke Ra's guards, the Jaffa who wore the masks of Horus and Anubis. As Ra's great ship rose from the desert, Thor struck it with lightning. Ra fled. The Egyptians buried his gate behind him, under cover stones declaring it sealed and buried for all time.

A slave rising was a shame no god could admit, and a god driven off by a thunderer from the North was worse. Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth again. The other System Lords, who had no wish to meet Thor either, kept the ban, and most of them have avoided Earth ever since. Every one of them remembers it, since a Goa'uld is born with the memories of its ancestors. None of them will mention it.

The raids on the North

About three thousand years ago Ba'al, who thought the ban one of Ra's vanities, sent his ships to the coasts of what is now Norway to carry off people as slaves and hosts. He had not reckoned on anybody in the North minding.

Thor met them on the shore. He killed every Jaffa who had set foot on the beach, and he brought one of the ships down into the sea with his lightning. Then he followed the rest back to the stars. On the world where Ba'al kept his palace he freed the captives, broke the palace open and killed every Goa'uld he could find in it. Ba'al himself escaped. He has kept Ra's ban ever since.

The Norsemen remembered it in their own way. In their stories Thor is forever cracking the skulls of giants who come to steal people away.

The Thunderer's war

For the next two thousand years, wherever the Goa'uld came near the North, Thor came after them. He did not take prisoners. Jaffa who threw down their weapons were killed with the rest. He pulled Goa'uld out of their hosts' necks with his bare hands, which killed the hosts as well, and he did not stop to ask whether they had wanted to be hosts. Once he sent the symbiote of one of Ba'al's underlords back to Ba'al in a jar.

Odin said afterwards that he had never seen his son so angry, and he had seen him angry a great deal. Thor laughed when he fought the Goa'uld. The Jaffa who lived to tell of it remembered the laughing more than the hammer.

Cimmeria

About the year 870, in the days of the Vikings, the System Lord Heru'ur took the people of several Norse settlements and carried them off to a cold world far from Earth to be his slaves. He was Ra's own son, and of all the Goa'uld he ought to have known better. Thor followed him there.

What he did on that world the Jaffa still tell their recruits, to frighten them. He came down in a storm that lasted three days. He killed Heru'ur's First Prime in front of his army, and then the army. He tore Heru'ur's ship out of the sky, and broke it on the mountains. Heru'ur got away in a cargo ship with a handful of guards, and left everyone else behind.

Thor did not bring the Northmen home. He judged it safer to leave them where they were, under his own protection, than to show the Goa'uld the way back to Earth. Their new home is the world now called Cimmeria. Thor left a device there, known as Thor's Hammer, which seizes any Goa'uld who comes through the gate and shuts it in the labyrinth under the mountain.

The war with the System Lords

Heru'ur went to the other System Lords. Towards the end of the tenth century they did a thing they have seldom done before or since: they made common cause. Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al brought their fleets together to strike at the worlds of Asgard, reasoning that Thor could not be everywhere at once.

Odin gave Thor command of Asgard's ships. He met the three fleets above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space, which the Jaffa still will not name. Of the three, only Apophis's fleet survived, and that only because Apophis turned it round before the end. Thor went down after the survivors of the others and finished them on the ground. It is still the worst defeat the Goa'uld have ever suffered.

The treaty

Soon afterwards the System Lords asked Asgard for terms, and the result was the Protected Planets Treaty. It closed a list of worlds to the Goa'uld, Cimmeria among them, with Asgard to enforce it. It is said in Asgard, and denied by the System Lords, that their first demand was that Thor should not be present when it was signed.

Earth was not on the list. The Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of it for four thousand years, and a world that may not be named cannot very well be written into a treaty. Besides, it was the one world in the galaxy where they could be surest of finding Thor. In 1994, with Thor away at the Replicator war, that is less true than it was.

The fear of Thor

The System Lords fear Asgard as a power. They fear Thor as a person. Because every Goa'uld is born remembering what its ancestors saw, every Goa'uld alive remembers him, including those who have never met him. A System Lord who hears thunder in a clear sky over a world he means to take has been known to turn his fleet round.

Odin was not pleased with his son. It was not the killing of Goa'uld that troubled him, but the pleasure Thor had taken in it. Many in Asgard count it among the reasons why, centuries later, Odin sent Thor to Earth as Donald Blake to learn humility.

On Earth

Thor is the son of Odin All-Father, the ruler of Asgard. The Norse knew him long before the modern world did, and the old tales of Thor the thunderer are memories of him. To teach his proud son humility, Odin sent him to Earth in the body of a lame American doctor, Donald Blake, with no memory of who he was.

In 1962, on holiday in Norway, Blake took shelter in a cave and found an old walking stick there. When he struck it on the ground it became Mjolnir, the hammer forged of the metal uru. It bears the promise that whoever holds it, if he be worthy, shall have the power of Thor. Blake became Thor.

He came to public notice that summer. The following year he helped to found the Avengers, when his adopted brother Loki tried to use the team's first battle against him. With Mjolnir he commands storm and lightning. He can fly with it, and open ways between the worlds.

He fought beside the Avengers for most of the next quarter of a century, against Loki, the Enchantress, the fire demon Surtur and a great many others. In 1984 he was among the heroes taken to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. That summer, back in New York, he was one of the heroes who fought the maddened Hulk through the streets.

In January 1965 he went to Japan with the Avengers, beside the Justice League, when three monsters were loose there at once. One was Godzilla, the great reptile of that country. Another was King Ghidorah, a three-headed golden dragon from the stars that breathed lightning. Thor met its lightning with his own. It was the first thing that had made the dragon give ground, though he could not bring it down. He stood aside with the rest when Godzilla drove it off. He met Godzilla again in New York in the summer of 1979, where he wrestled him on the side of the Empire State Building until the building began to crack. He did not win that time either.

Masterson and the fleet

From 1989 Thor's life was bound up with that of Eric Masterson, a New York architect whose life he had saved by merging with him. When Odin banished Thor himself at the end of 1991, Masterson served as Thor in his own right for more than a year. When Thor came back at the end of 1992, Odin gave Masterson an enchanted mace of his own.

Early in 1993 Thor left Earth again, and he has been away from it ever since. Asgard is at war with the Replicators, machines that devour technology to make more of themselves, and Thor is the supreme commander of Asgard's fleet in that war. The war is fought in the Pegasus galaxy, far beyond this one, where Asgard has its worlds among the stars. It is the same fleet that stands behind Asgard's Protected Planets Treaty with the Goa'uld System Lords, and the war is a heavy drain on it.

It is a war that Asgard can ill afford. The Aesir live for many centuries, but children are seldom born to them, so every Asgardian the Replicators kill is a loss that will take generations to make good. The Replicators have no such difficulty.

The Goa'uld do not know about the war. Asgard has kept it from them, and keeps its ships on show over the protected worlds as though nothing had changed. The System Lords have heard rumours that Thor is busy somewhere. They do not know where, or with what.

The warrior's madness

Through 1993 a madness grew in Thor. It had been a long time coming. For thirty years his life had been shared out: with Donald Blake, with Eric Masterson, with Beta Ray Bill, the alien warrior who had once lifted Mjolnir and been given a hammer of his own. Something in Thor gave way under it. He began to see a Valkyrie at his side whom nobody else could see. She told him that all of it was Odin's fault.

In the autumn of 1993 it broke out among the stars. Sif found him on a barren world with Beta Ray Bill. He fought them both. He fought the Silver Surfer next, then Adam Warlock's Infinity Watch, with Doctor Strange beside them, and beat them all. Then he came against Asgard itself, meaning to kill his father.

It took all of them to stop him, and Thanos, the Mad Titan, had a hand in it too, which Thor did not enjoy. At the last Odin went into his son's mind. He found Thor there in chains on a mountain, with the Valkyrie standing over him. She fought Odin, then Thor himself rose up against her. He destroyed her with Mjolnir, and the madness went with her.

Some in Asgard said that it had been the old fury of the Goa'uld wars, come back after a thousand years. Whatever it was, it did not come back again. The Thor who went back to the fleet at the end of 1993 was quieter than the one the Goa'uld remembered, and a good deal more patient.

The death of Thunderstrike

In the summer of 1995 Thor came home for the first time since he had gone to the war. Eric Masterson had taken up the Bloodaxe, the cursed axe of Skurge the Executioner, to stop a demon that threatened every life on Earth. The curse had taken him in turn, and he had beaten the Avengers when they came to stop him. Heimdall, who watches Midgard from the Rainbow Bridge, saw it all. Thor came down to face his friend.

They fought over New York while what was left of the Avengers looked on. Thor offered to take the fight to another world, where nobody else would be hurt. Masterson would not go. The end came inside Masterson's own mind, where the curse wore the face of Skurge himself. Skurge's own spirit came down from Valhalla to help him against it, and Masterson tore the mace Thunderstrike out of its grip. When the two weapons met, the blast destroyed both of them. It killed him too.

Thor carried his friend's spirit to Valhalla, but Masterson would not stay there. He was a man of Midgard, and Odin agreed that he should go where the souls of mortal men go. Thor asked his father to give him back his life. Odin would not, since Masterson had made his own choices and accepted what came of them.

At the grave Thor called down a storm. His lightning cut a new line into the headstone, beneath the words 'Beloved Father': 'The world still needs heroes.' Then he went back to the war.

Onslaught

In the summer of 1996 Heimdall saw a shadow fall over New York. It was Onslaught, the power that had grown out of the darkness in Charles Xavier's mind, and every hero who could reach the city was fighting it. Odin called Thor home from the Pegasus galaxy. He left the fleet to its captains and came down the Rainbow Bridge.

On the night before the last battle he worked among the wounded brought out of Manhattan, using what he had learnt in his years as Donald Blake, who had been a doctor. He found that he could no longer reach the berserk strength that had once multiplied his own, and he decided that he had never been meant to have it. Before dawn Hela, who rules the dead of Asgard, rose out of the Hudson to tell him that he would die the next day. He told her that he would not change a thing.

That summer Thor broke through Onslaught's armour to drag Charles Xavier out of it alive. In the last battle, in August, he was the first to fly into the force that was left, and he gave himself up with the others to destroy it. The world believed him dead, and mourned him. Hela had been wrong. Franklin Richards had caught him as he fell, with all the rest, and carried them into a world of his own making.

Asgard mourned him in private. To the Goa'uld it said nothing at all, since its bluff depended on the System Lords believing that the Thunderer was somewhere about. For more than a year the fleet fought on without him in the Pegasus galaxy, and it lost a great deal of ground. Ships went that could not be replaced. Worlds that Asgard had held for centuries fell to the Replicators, and Aesir died whose places would take generations to fill.

Meanwhile the Goa'uld stirred. In 1997 Apophis gambled on the rumour that Thor was busy, then came to Earth. The gamble was better than he knew, for Thor was not merely busy but gone. The same year, on Cimmeria, a team from Earth broke Thor's Hammer, and nobody came from Asgard to mend it.

Late in 1997 Franklin brought them home. On the way Thor stopped Victor von Doom from seizing Franklin's power, then put Doom off the ship before it crossed. Thor went straight back to his fleet. He found Asgard losing the war.

The Tau'ri

In the summer of 1998 Heru'ur came back to Cimmeria, the world where Thor had left the Northmen about 870, meaning to take it now that its Hammer was gone. SG-1, the team from Earth's Stargate that had broken the Hammer, came to help the Cimmerians fight him. Under the mountain, in the Hall of Thor's Might, Daniel Jackson and Samantha Carter passed the tests that Thor had left there. The hall called Asgard.

Thor answered it himself, in his own ship, the Biliskner. Carter and Jackson knew his face at once, as everybody on Earth did. They had not known that the Avenger of the evening news was the Thor of the Goa'uld's nightmares. His ship cleared Heru'ur's army off the planet, and Heru'ur ran for the gate. Thor was not pleased that people from Earth, of all places, had broken his Hammer. He left an Asgard teacher with the Cimmerians all the same.

Early in 1999 Jack O'Neill, whose head an Ancient repository had filled with more knowledge than any man could carry, built a device that took him through the Stargate to Othala, the chief of Asgard's worlds in the Pegasus galaxy. The Asgard took the knowledge out of his head. Thor told him that the people of Earth were on their way to becoming a fifth great race, fit one day to stand beside the four of an old alliance, of which Asgard was one.

That summer the System Lords resolved to destroy Earth for killing Hathor. Thor came to Earth himself to open the talks that put it under the Protected Planets Treaty, before he was called back to the war. He admitted to O'Neill that Asgard could not have gone to war for Earth. It had the Replicators to fight.

In 2000 the Replicators took the Biliskner. It reached Earth with Thor badly hurt aboard, and he brought O'Neill up to it. SG-1 could not save the ship, so they wired its engines to make it burn up as it fell, then escaped through a Stargate they had beamed aboard. It came down in the Pacific, off California. Thor lived.

One Replicator lived through the fall. It took a Russian submarine before it was destroyed. That summer Thor took Samantha Carter to the Pegasus galaxy, because Asgard's own minds had run out of answers and he hoped that a less sophisticated one might find another. She watched five Asgard ships lost in a single short battle. Her answer was to use Asgard's newest warship, the O'Neill, as bait. The Replicators swarmed into it, and it blew itself up with them inside. Thor promised that once the Replicators were beaten, Asgard would help Earth against the Goa'uld.

Anubis

In 2002 an Asgard scholar was trapped in a hidden laboratory on Adara II, one of the protected worlds, with a Goa'uld ship overhead. She had been at work there on the problem that troubles Asgard most, which is how seldom children are born to the Aesir. Thor went to drive the Goa'uld off. Soon afterwards Freyr of the High Council came to Earth to say that Thor was dead, and that Asgard had no ship to spare to save her.

Thor was not dead. Anubis, half-ascended through the Devil's trick, had taken him prisoner and put a device into his head to read his mind. Thor turned the link against him. Through it he let O'Neill and Teal'c out of their cell. SG-1 got him away. Three Asgard ships came, and Anubis withdrew. No other Goa'uld has ever laid hands on Thor.

The link had cost him dear. Thor lay senseless, with his mind still caught in the computer of Anubis's ship. A few weeks later that ship turned up above Earth, empty of Goa'uld, and fell into the northern Pacific. It was Thor's mind that had driven them out and brought it there. SG-1 carried the crystals that held it out of the sinking ship, and Asgard restored him to his body.

That August Thor came aboard Earth's first warship, the Prometheus, with bad news. The Replicators had overrun Othala.

Asgard's answer was a trap. Hala, the first world the Aesir settled in the Pegasus galaxy, had been emptied of its people after a great battle there. Asgard built a machine to wrap the planet in a field where time ran ten thousand times slower than outside, then lured every Replicator it could reach to Hala with what was left of Reese, the android who had made them. The field did not close. Early in 2003 Thor sent SG-1 in aboard the Prometheus, a ship too simple for the Replicators to want, to find out why. An Asgard ship carried it there, since its own engines could never have reached so far.

They found that the Replicators had turned the field round, so that time inside ran faster, and in the centuries that passed for them they had learnt to take human form. Their leaders called themselves by the order in which they were made, First to Sixth. SG-1 set the field to rights and escaped, leaving them shut inside it. One of them, Fifth, had helped SG-1. They had left him behind on purpose, and he did not forget it.

In February 2003 the Stargate was revealed to the governments of Britain, France and China. Thor appeared at the meeting in the Pentagon, to the astonishment of their envoys, and told them that Asgard wished the gate to stay where it was. It stayed there.

The end of the Replicators

In 2004 Asgard tried to finish the Replicators on Hala by crushing its sun into a black hole. Some of them escaped. They carried off Samantha Carter, then came to Orilla, the world in the Pegasus galaxy where the Aesir had made their new home, for the neutronium they needed to make more of their human kind.

Jack O'Neill had been lying frozen in an Ancient chamber in the Antarctic since he saved Earth from Anubis, with the Ancients' knowledge in his head for the second time. Thor woke him. With the knowledge O'Neill built a weapon that broke the bonds holding a Replicator together, before Thor took it out of him again. Thor built one large enough to sweep the whole of Orilla, and the Replicators there fell to pieces.

Fifth got away. Before he went he made a Replicator in Carter's likeness, and gave her everything he knew. Early in 2005 she came to the Tau'ri as a friend, made the Replicators proof against O'Neill's weapon, destroyed Fifth and took his place.

She led them into this galaxy. They tore through the fleets of the System Lords, who learnt at last what had been keeping Asgard so busy. Thor worked with the real Carter to answer her, but the Replicators changed faster than they could. They boarded his ship, the Daniel Jackson. He sent Carter home to Earth, then took the ship away with the Replicators aboard.

In March 2005 Carter, her father, Jacob, with Ba'al turned the weapon of the Ancients on Dakara against them, and every Replicator in the galaxy fell to pieces. Thor's ship was freed. The war that had kept him from Earth since 1993 was over. Asgard had won it, with a great deal of help from the Tau'ri.

The withdrawal from the stars

Asgard had won the war, but it had spent its people to do it. The Aesir among the stars were now so few that they could not go on, and at the rate children came to them they would be fewer still for centuries. In 2006 a single Asgard ship stood with the fleet of Earth and the free Jaffa at the Ori's great gate. The Ori destroyed it.

In 2007 the High Council gave up Asgard's worlds among the stars. Thor called the Tau'ri to Orilla. Asgard gave them what it had to give. It was not machines, for the Aesir have never handed their engines to a younger people. It was the lore of the Aesir: what Odin's people knew of the Nine Worlds, of the branches of Yggdrasil that join them, of the runes and of the Rainbow Bridge, which carries a traveller from world to world without crossing the space between. Thor set it down for them himself, aboard Earth's ship the Odyssey, and told them that they were the fifth race now, as he had once told O'Neill they would be.

The Ori's warships came while the work was being done. Asgard would not leave its lore for them to find, so it destroyed Orilla. The last of the Aesir among the stars went home to the Realm Eternal, Thor with them, where children might be born to them in peace, however slowly. The Odyssey got away from the Ori with everything that Thor had taught.

The Tau'ri kept what they had been given, and they kept it classified. It outlasted the Third World War and the dark years after it. In 2063 what it told of the Rainbow Bridge helped Zefram Cochrane to build the Phoenix, Earth's first warp ship, whose engine did in the body of a missile what Earth's battlecruisers had needed a whole hull to do. Only what touched warp flight ever became public knowledge. Section 31 kept the rest classified.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: watching the Avengers at the United Nations on the news of 20 August 1994, Harry notices that they look nothing like the Avengers on Dudley's old lunchbox. The man with the hammer has been replaced by a big blond man with a mace.

pages.html:
Tommy Oliver is the sixth of the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: the Green Ranger, the one with the gold shield across his chest. He came to Angel Grove in 1993, a new boy with a gift for martial arts. Rita Repulsa made him her Ranger under a spell, and he broke free to join Zordon's team. In the summer of 1994 his powers keep running out. In September 1994 his other self, Lord Drakkon, murdered him; the mending of the world gave him back his life, though he never remembered losing it. In October 1994 he became the White Ranger. In later years he led the Rangers in red, then taught a new team as the Black Dino Ranger. He is Dudley Dursley's idol.

Early life

Tommy was born about 1977. The foster system he grew up in failed him. Even when he was adopted, his new parents neglected him. It left him with a resentment that he had nowhere to put, so he poured it into martial arts. By the time he came to Angel Grove he was a black belt of the third degree, and very good indeed.

Rita's Ranger

In October 1993 Tommy started at Angel Grove High School as a new pupil. He sparred with Jason Lee Scott at a martial arts tournament, and the two became friends. Kimberly Hart liked him at once.

Rita Repulsa had been watching. Tommy was not a Ranger already, and to her he was a blank slate. She had lost a son of her own long before, and in Tommy she found something like a son. She worked his old resentment into the spell that twisted his mind, so that he was bound to her as a son is to his mother. Then she gave him the Dragon Coin, the Green Power Coin, with the Dragon Dagger that calls the Dragonzord up out of the sea.

As the Green Ranger he came closer to beating the Rangers than any monster had. He broke into the Command Center, wrecked it, put a virus into Alpha 5 and cut the Rangers off from Zordon. Rita's Sword of Darkness held her spell on him for as long as the sword lasted. Jason beat him in single combat and destroyed the sword. The spell broke. Zordon offered him a place on the team, and he took it.

The Black Dragon

In October 1993 a voice came to Rita on the Moon. Her Green Ranger would leave her, it said, to join Zordon's team; when she saw that it was right, she would see its owner. At the end of the month her Green Chaos Crystal let the Black Dragon into the Command Center. Rita took it for a dragon and an ally. It was a Zord, steered from another world.

It wrecked the Command Center, cut Zordon adrift, then stripped the other Rangers of their powers. Rita turned their Zords on the cities of the world, naming Tommy as her price for sparing Angel Grove. Many people have feared the Rangers ever since. In a fight on the Moon the Black Dragon lost an arm, with which Tommy shared his power among Jason, Zack Taylor, Trini Kwan and Kimberly Hart, so that they fought on in green. Then he got inside the machine with Billy Cranston to wreck it. It blew apart, throwing the two boys into its master's world.

Lord Drakkon

They came down in a dark Angel Grove, where soldiers in Ranger armour hunted them. Under the ruined Command Center a voice led Tommy to that world's Saba, the White Ranger's talking sword, who got the boys away. Then the master of that world took off his helmet in front of Tommy. He had Tommy's own face.

Lord Drakkon is the Tommy Oliver of that world. There Rita's spell broke too, but he chose to stay with her. Together they conquered his world, then broke its Rangers. When that world's Zordon made the powers of the White Ranger as a last hope, he meant them for Jason. Drakkon cut Jason down, then took them for himself, which is why his armour is part green, part white. Saba told the boys how it had all come about, which made Tommy afraid that he might become such a man.

The Coinless, the Rangers of that world, had lost their powers long before, but they were still fighting him, older and worn down. With Billy's help they struck the power out of Drakkon, with every soldier he had, as the other Rangers came through to fetch their friends. Drakkon told Tommy that a man can trust nobody but himself, then threw himself into a chasm. The Rangers' road home dragged him after them into this world, where Grace Sterling's people at Promethea took him prisoner without a word to the Rangers. Saba came home with them, to hold Zordon fast until the Command Center was rebuilt.

The green candle

Rita had lost her dragon, and she had never forgiven Tommy. Late in November 1993 she lit a cursed green candle to drain his powers. Goldar took him prisoner. Before the candle burnt out Tommy gave his coin to Jason, so that Rita could not have it.

Early in 1994 Zordon gave him back what power he could. It was not permanent. His powers depend on fresh boosts of Zordon's own energy, and in the summer of 1994 they keep running out, at the worst moments. The public has noticed.

Godzilla

In the spring of 1994 Zordon set Tommy to watch an old temple where a gem called the Multiversal Focus was kept. Rita Repulsa took it by force, so he went in after her by himself. The gem carried them both to Japan. There Tommy saw Godzilla for the first time, took him for one of Rita's monsters, then called up the Dragonzord. Godzilla knocked it down with one blow, then burnt it.

Goldar took Tommy prisoner. He was held on the saucer of Rita's allies, the Xiliens, where Rita tried to put him back under her spell. This time she failed. A Xilien guard who had lost his taste for the war let him go, giving him back his Power Coin. Tommy woke the wrecked Dragonzord in time to join the Megazord against King Ghidorah.

Shattered Grid

Early in September 1994 Drakkon escaped from Promethea, then had Ninjor mend his powers. That evening Tommy took Kimberly out on their first proper date. She walked away from an awkward goodnight, thought better of it, then turned back. She found Drakkon in the alley with a blade through Tommy's back. Tommy died in her arms. Angel Grove buried him.

His death broke the Power apart, which began the war remembered as Shattered Grid. It ended with Drakkon unmaking the world. But Tommy's spirit had been kept. A year before, a stranger had shot him with an arrow in a school gym, telling him that he would understand in time. She was the Ranger Slayer, Drakkon's own Kimberly. The splinter of the Chaos Crystal in its tip had held his spirit between the worlds.

That spirit came into the world Drakkon had made, woke his friends, beat Drakkon on equal terms, then took from him the heart of a Morphin Master. Tommy told him why he had lost: of all the Tommy Olivers in all the worlds, Drakkon was the only one who had gone wrong, which he could never bear. Drakkon refused to be saved. The Rangers mended the world, in which the date ended in a kiss. Tommy never remembered any of it.

The White Ranger

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon and went after Tommy first. With a green crystal he drained what was left of the Green Ranger's powers, and Tommy went away to his uncle's cabin by a lake. Zordon and Alpha 5 had been working in secret. The Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, had shown Zordon the way to the White Light.

In October 1994 Zordon sent Tommy to a far world, where a creature like a white tiger led him to an old temple, the Tower of Light. Its keeper, Saba, would give up the Light only to somebody who could beat him. Lord Zedd appeared, struck Saba down, then offered Tommy the Light if he would come back to evil. Tommy refused. It had been a test, so Saba gave him the Light.

Tommy came back as the White Ranger, with powers drawn from a light of goodness that Zedd could not steal. He had the White Tigerzord, with Saba, a sabre that talks. He took Jason's place as leader.

In November 1994 Jason, Zack and Trini left for a peace conference in Geneva, or so they said. Tommy called Jason a coward for leaving when the team needed him most, and Jason had no answer he could give. Rocky DeSantos, Adam Park and Aisha Campbell took their places.

Jason's secret

Late that month Dayne, a bounty hunter hired by Zedd, wounded Tommy badly. Strange Rangers boxed Dayne up, then left without a word. Their red one, his helmet on, later had a short, tense talk with Tommy outside the Command Center.

Early in December the strangers came to the Command Center with their faces bare, carrying their red one, who was badly hurt. They were Jason, Zack and Trini. Tommy was livid. Once Jason was on his feet the two of them had it out, sparring. Jason's only answer was that he had had no choice. They finished that fight side by side against the Anointed, joining their Zords. By the end they were friends again.

Drakkon's return

In the middle of December 1994 Drakkon fell out of the sky beside the Command Center, inside what looked like a meteor. Tommy knocked him senseless. Zordon locked him in a cell below, where he taunted the Rangers with a war they could not remember. Tommy would not go down to speak to him. Early in January 1995 the Omega Rangers took him away, against Zordon's orders.

Matt Cook

That December Grace Sterling made a new Green Ranger with Tommy's old coin, which Billy had brought back to life in secret. He was Matt Cook, who had once gone out with Kimberly. Tommy mistrusted him from the first. He accused Kimberly of having known all along. He told Matt to his face that Grace was using him as Rita had once used Tommy. When Zartus of Eltar invaded the Earth in January 1995, Tommy joined the White Tigerzord to Matt's Dragonzord, which destroyed one of Zartus's Empyreals. Afterwards the two of them apologised to each other.

The White coin

In February 1995 Dark Specter's corruption got into the Power itself, turning Ranger after Ranger. It could not turn Tommy, because the White light shielded him. He gave up his White coin, which was joined with Drakkon's so that his friends could morph in safety. When the Grid had been cleansed, the coin came back to him. Tommy had stood in the Grid, so he remembered those weeks, which the mended world did not.

In September 1995 Rito Revolto destroyed the Thunderzords. Ninjor gave Tommy a new coin, the Falcon, with the Falconzord, and he became the White Ninja Ranger. He broke Rita's spell on Katherine Hillard.

Kimberly

Kimberly Hart, the Pink Ranger, had liked Tommy from his first day, and in time the two became sweethearts. In November 1995 she left Angel Grove to train in Florida for the Pan Global Games, giving her coin to Katherine. For a while they kept it up across the distance. In May 1996 she wrote to tell him that she had met someone else. Afterwards Tommy began to go out with Katherine.

Zeo and Turbo

When Master Vile's Orb of Doom turned the Rangers back into children, Tommy went searching through time for a piece of the Zeo Crystal.

In April 1996 he became the Red Zeo Ranger, the leader of the Zeo Rangers. In May 1996 he found the brother he had never known, David Trueheart, whom Sam Trueheart had brought up. Tommy told David that he was a Ranger. In November 1996 Prince Gasket of the Machine Empire carried him off. Under Gasket's spell Tommy believed himself King of the Machine Empire, and the Rangers evil. Jason and Katherine brought him back to himself.

In March 1997 he and Katherine saved the wizard Lerigot from Divatox. Tommy became the Red Turbo Ranger. He took up stock-car racing. In September 1997, when he finished school, he handed the Red Turbo powers to T.J. Johnson.

On 19 October 1996 Tommy took the Zeo Megazord to the town of Charterville, where the Machine Empire had struck a bargain with a villain named Vexor. The Zeo Rangers fought there beside the town's own heroes, the Beetleborgs. Afterwards Tommy shook hands with their leader, the Blue Stinger Beetleborg, both of them in their helmets. On 3 May 1997 he led the Turbo Rangers back to Charterville on the trail of Divatox's Piranhatrons. That evening he learnt that the hand he had shaken belonged to Drew McCormick, a boy of twelve.

Doctor Oliver

In 2002 the last generals of the Machine Empire dug Lord Zedd's Serpentera out of the Moon. Tommy gathered the Red Rangers, ten in all, to stop them, and fought once more as the Red Zeo Ranger.

He went on to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and earned a doctorate in palaeontology. He worked with two other scientists, Anton Mercer and Terrence Smith. An accident in their laboratory turned Mercer into the creature Mesogog. Smith, who seemed to have died in it, came back as the cyborg Zeltrax.

Tommy hid the Dino Gems he had found and became a science teacher at Reefside High School. In 2004 three of his pupils found his laboratory, and the gems made them Rangers. Tommy became the Black Dino Ranger, with the Brachiozord, and he could make himself invisible. Once he was sealed in amber, and his gem shattered when he tried to change back. In his own mind he fought the Rangers he had once been, and they made it whole again. In the last battle the team gave up their powers to defeat Mesogog. Tommy went back to his classroom.

Later years

In 2014, in the great battle against the Armada, Tommy led the Rangers of every generation as the Green Ranger once more, with Saba in his hand.

In August 2018 Lord Draven, who was taking Rangers prisoner from world after world, put a robot in Tommy's place. Tommy escaped and fought him with the powers of all his old Ranger forms. He and Katherine had a son, J.J.

In 2023 Robo-Rita's creatures took him prisoner, with Jason and Kimberly. They were shut in a machine in the palace on the Moon, to power her plan to change the past. The other Rangers freed them, and they were taken to Aquitar to heal.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: in the summer of 1994 the news showed the Power Rangers nearly every morning. 'There were six of them now. The new one was green, with a gold shield across his chest, and Dudley thought he was the most wonderful thing that had ever lived.'

That summer Dudley took up karate, on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at the leisure centre. The club's leaflet said, in English under the Japanese, 'There is no first attack in karate'.

On the news of 20 August 1994 the Green Ranger stood on the roof of a multistorey car park in Angel Grove, his gold shield glinting in the sun. As Harry watched, he swayed, and put out a hand to a lamp post to steady himself. 'He's not well,' said Dudley darkly, through a mouthful of grapefruit. 'His powers keep running out. Everybody knows that.'

pages.html:
Trini Kwan is the Yellow Ranger of the Power Rangers, whose Power Coin draws on the Sabre-toothed Tiger. She is kind, quick-witted and a gifted student of kung fu, who uses no more force in a fight than she must. She is also the one who puts Billy Cranston's technical talk into plain English for the others. In November 1994 she told everybody that she was going to a peace conference in Geneva with Jason Lee Scott and Zack Taylor. In truth the three of them went into space as Omega Rangers. When Jason lost his powers in January 1995, Trini became the Red Omega Ranger in his place. Years later she came home to Angel Grove with a daughter, Minh. In 2022 she was killed by Robo-Rita, shielding Billy from a blast meant for him. A year later Minh took up her mother's powers as the Yellow Ranger.

Angel Grove

Trini was born about 1977 and grew up in Angel Grove, California, where she is a pupil at Angel Grove High School. She practises kung fu. Her style is all speed and high kicks. She tries to bring an enemy down with as little force as she can.

She is one of the team's thinkers. When Billy Cranston gets technical, she is usually the one who has to tell the others what he means.

Her uncle Howard is a professor, and Trini says he is a legend in the martial arts. In September 1993 he finished a potion of invisibility, and Rita Repulsa had him kidnapped for it. The Rangers got him back. Afterwards he used the potion himself to rough up Bulk and Skull without being seen.

Her cousin Sylvia was once turned into a cardboard cutout at a fair by Pineapple the Clown, one of Finster's monsters. Trini and Alpha 5 put her right.

The Yellow Ranger

Zordon chose Trini in 1993 for her compassion, her quick wits and her skill in the martial arts. She became the Yellow Ranger. Her Power Coin calls up the Sabre-toothed Tiger Dinozord, and her weapons are the Power Daggers.

On 30 July 1993 the Rangers came to public notice for the first time, when they fought a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham.

In September 1993 a Putty dragged Trini and Jason through one of Rita's portals to the planet Breel. There their minds were linked for a while, and the two of them began a short, secret romance. They ended it by agreement, since an enemy could have used it against them. Trini never trusted Alpha 1, an old robot of Zordon's who came back to help them in secret. She was right: within weeks he had turned on Zordon.

Late that year Tommy Oliver, as Rita's Green Ranger, shut Jason Lee Scott up in the Dark Dimension. Trini got him out with Billy and Alpha 5, seconds before Tommy would have killed him.

Weeks later the Black Dragon, Lord Drakkon's war machine, stripped the team of its powers and carried off Billy's coin. While Tommy and Billy were lost in Drakkon's world, Trini worked on the wreck. Out of the Black Dragon's own armour she made herself a suit. In it she took back Billy's coin, gave the team its powers again, drove Rita out of the ruined Command Center, then opened the way through to the other world.

In February 1994 she began to learn Praying Mantis Kung Fu from Master Li. Rita sent down a mantis monster to test her new skills.

In the spring of 1994 the team followed Tommy Oliver to Japan, where the Megazord fought Godzilla, then fought beside him. Trini trusted him less than the others did, since he had just tried to kill them.

The lie about Geneva

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon in Rita's place. His monsters outclassed Finster's, so Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords. Trini's became the Griffin Thunderzord.

That October Trini and Zack Taylor walked in on Jason in the Command Center with a stranger, the Blue Emissary. They drew their blasters. The Emissary gave them back their memories of a war the world had forgotten, then told them what joining would cost. They told Jason that he was not alone.

In November 1994 Trini, Jason and Zack were chosen as delegates to a peace conference in Geneva. Trini told Zordon that they ought not to leave in the middle of a crisis. He advised them to pass on their powers all the same. He did not know that they had no intention of going.

First the Rangers fetched the Sword of Light from a far planet. With it the powers of the three passed to three friends from Stone Canyon. Trini's went to Aisha Campbell, the new Yellow Ranger.

Geneva was not the whole story. The conference was also a cover. From Earth the three of them went out into space, to a world called Safehaven. There they took up the Omega powers, which had come down from some of the earliest Rangers in the universe. Trini became the Yellow Omega Ranger, whose power is earth, with the Omega Hammer. As the Omega Rangers they fought threats a long way from home.

Keeping up the story was hard on her. Calls home reached one of the three at a time, through static. Kimberly Hart, who felt that they were avoiding her, left Trini a message to say that she felt abandoned.

The Yellow Omega Ranger

Early in December 1994 Kiya Kyatyl, the Blue Omega Ranger, turned on the team and struck Jason down. The three came to the Command Center with their faces bare. Aisha told Trini that she had felt like a temporary Ranger all along. Zordon forgave them at once, reassuring Trini himself. When both teams met Kiya's following at Safehaven, it was Trini who beat Kiya, shattering her morpher.

In January 1995 the Omega Rangers carried Lord Drakkon off from his cell under the Command Center, against Zordon's orders, to guide them against the Empyreals. Trini came nearer to trusting him than anybody had in years. She told him that it was not too late. He asked whether he had 'Idiot' stamped on his forehead. She laughed, then told him that he need not be the man he had been. He betrayed them all the same. Afterwards he told her that he had left the wreck of Xi, their robot, where Safehaven would find it, so that they could be saved.

In the Eltarian War she went aboard Zartus's ship with Jason, beside Zordon in a body of metal, to free the Guardian Zelya. Afterwards she rebuilt Xi.

The Red Omega Ranger

About that time Zack found a baby in an escape pod, of a people nobody knew. She was named Journey. She grew from an infant into an old woman in a matter of weeks, with Trini and Zack bringing her up. Late in January 1995 the Death Ranger woke on Safehaven and wore Jason's body, then Trini's in turn. Journey fought beside them. When it was over she died of old age, calling the two of them her mother and father.

Breaking the Death Ranger's hold cost Jason his link to the Power. Trini sent him home to his father, then took the Red Omega powers herself. Kevor Vrin, a Hartunian orphan, became the Yellow in her place. From then on Trini led the Omega Rangers.

In February 1995, while Dark Specter's corruption was loose in the Grid, her Red Omegazord was wrecked on the planet Casentine. She stood with the Rangers of Earth when the Grid was cleansed. In November 1995 she and Zack came back to Earth for a few days to help Kimberly in France. To everybody in Angel Grove they were still in Geneva.

Minh

In later years Trini gave up the life of a Ranger. She came home to Angel Grove with a daughter, Minh.

In 2022 Billy Cranston tried to bring Zordon back. What came back instead was the evil that Zordon's light had driven out of Rita Repulsa, in a body of its own, Robo-Rita. Trini took up her old powers again and fought beside the rest of the old team.

Death

In the battle Robo-Rita fired a blast at Billy. Trini threw herself in front of it, and it killed her.

Minh blamed Billy. Zack Taylor gave up his seat in Congress to adopt her, and she came to look on him as something like a father.

Her daughter

A year later Robo-Rita came back. Minh tried to use her mother's morpher, but its power was too much for her. Then Robo-Rita took her prisoner. When Robo-Rita fired at Billy, Minh jumped in front of the blast, as her mother had done. That good deed bonded the Sabre-toothed Tiger coin to her, and she became the Yellow Ranger.

At the Moon Palace Minh pinned Robo-Rita down with her daggers. Zack destroyed her, saying Trini's name as he struck.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' news showed helicopter film of the fight in Birmingham the afternoon before. Five people in coloured suits and helmets ran in a line across a rooftop towards the creature. The one in yellow was Trini. Dudley, with a sausage halfway to his mouth, watched them leap off the roof as though he would like to be one of them.

Book Three, Chapter Four: Lucius Malfoy had been telling Harry that Muggles were not his people. Harry thought of the team in California, who fought monsters with no magic at all. 'There's a lot of them who help.'

Book Four, Chapter Three: by August 1994 the Rangers were on the Dursleys' news nearly every morning, and there were six of them now. Trini was still the Yellow Ranger, though Dudley's favourite was the newest, the green one.

pages.title: Tsathoggua
infobox: Clark Ashton Smith; Robert E. Howard; H. P. Lovecraft
A squat, furred, pot-bellied thing with the head of a toad
N'kai, a lightless gulf deep under the earth
Eibon of Mhu Thulan; the Voormis
pages.html:
Tsathoggua is one of the Great Old Ones, a squat, sleepy, pot-bellied thing with the head of a toad and a pelt like a bat's. He lives in N'kai, a lightless gulf deep under the earth, and waits there for his offerings to be brought to him. In the far north of the elder world, before the ice came down, the wizard Eibon served him, and wrote down what he learnt in the Book of Eibon.

The Sleeper of N'kai

Tsathoggua is said to have come to the Earth from another world, from the planet men call Saturn. He made his home first under a mountain of the far north, Voormithadreth, where the cave-dwelling Voormis worshipped him. When the ice took the north he went down into N'kai, deeper still, and there he lies.

He is slothful. He will not rise to hunt. He waits in his lightless gulf for the sacrifice, and it comes. Of all the Great Old Ones he is reckoned the least malign, which is not the same as saying he is harmless. His spoiling is the spoiling of patience: those who come to him for his secrets come of their own accord, and they do not go back to God.

The formless spawn

His servants are the formless spawn, shapeless things of black ooze that can pour through a crack the width of a hair, take any shape they please and are very hard to kill. They rest in basins in his temples.

The people of K'n-yan, under the plains of Oklahoma, once worshipped Tsathoggua, until an expedition of theirs into N'kai met the spawn. Afterwards K'n-yan smashed his images and gave his temples to Shub-Niggurath.

Eibon

Eibon of Mhu Thulan was a wizard of the far north of the elder world, before the ice came down. He served Tsathoggua, whom his people called Zhothaqquah. He left a book of his journeys and his rites, which has outlived his country by many thousands of years. Only fragments of it survive, in Latin as the Liber Ivonis and in French.

pages.title: Tsubasa Yamagatana
pages.html:
Tsubasa Yamagatana was Dan, the Midnight Sun Knight, the Makai Knight who guarded Kantai, the priests' village in the north of Japan. He fought with a spear. He was strict, correct, hard on himself, harder on everybody else. His one soft spot was his younger sister, Rin.

Kantai

Tsubasa's parents were Makai Priests, both killed by Horrors. He became a knight, brought up his sister Rin himself, and held that feelings only get in the way of duty. He dressed more like a priest than a knight. He worked some magic through an earring. His Madou tool was the bracelet Goruba, one of the oldest there is.

In December 2006 Rin slipped away to fetch Kouga Saejima, on the word of a dead priest. Tsubasa was not pleased with either of them. He barred Kouga's way into Kantai until the priestess Garai overruled him. When Kouga brought the priestess Jabi back alive out of a Makai Tree, Tsubasa called her undead.

Then Rin was stained with Horror's blood in a night attack. Jabi saved her. Tsubasa apologised. He told his sister, for once, that he was proud of her.

The Horror Legules had left a piece of himself hidden in Goruba. He used it to seize Rin with the Phosphorus Arrow, hoping to foul the rite of the Midnight Sun with innocent blood. Tsubasa went into the forest after her with Kouga, Rei Suzumura and Jabi. Kouga killed Legules.

The Seal of Destruction

In 2011 Sigma Fudou cut the Seal of Destruction into Tsubasa, as into many knights. His was the worst of them, since he had called his armour so often. In January 2012 the veteran knight Wataru Shijima, driven mad by the same seal, began attacking his own side. Tsubasa meant to kill him as a mercy. Kouga wanted to save him. Tsubasa let himself be persuaded. In the end he allowed himself to be run through with Wataru, which drove the evil out of the older man.

That March he fought in the true Makai against Sigma's machines.

Jabi

By 2016 he was hunting with Jabi, the priestess he had once called an abomination. The two of them were a couple. That spring he came down from Kantai to the city, where he had to cut down a man called Kazuma who had become a Horror.

pages.title: Tyler Steele
infobox: A cyborg warrior of Grimlord's, until November 1994
The armour of the VR Troopers; Ryan Steele's second armour; the Troopertron
pages.html:
Tyler Steele is the scientist of Crossworld City, California, who discovered the way into virtual reality with his friend Professor Horatio Hart. He is the father of Ryan Steele. About 1984 he vanished. In the summer of 1994 he has been Grimlord's prisoner for ten years, his memory gone, his body remade as a cyborg warrior called Dark Heart. His son found him that November, then freed him for good in September 1995.

The scientist

Tyler Steele worked in Crossworld City with Professor Horatio Hart. In secret the two of them found that virtual reality was a real world lying beside this one, then learnt how to reach it. When they understood that its master, Grimlord, meant to invade the Earth, they designed the VR Troopers to meet him: armour, weapons and machines for human fighters to call up out of virtual reality.

He was a martial artist too. His great friend outside the laboratory was Tao Chong, who keeps a karate school in the city. He taught his small son, Ryan, to fight at a Buddhist temple. Ryan remembers every lesson.

Lost

About 1984 Grimlord struck. Professor Hart was dying of his injuries when Tyler Steele saved him, by sending his friend's mind across into virtual reality. Tyler Steele himself was taken into the Virtual Dungeon.

In Crossworld City nobody knew what had become of him. His son, who was about eight, grew up without him.

Dark Heart

Grimlord did not kill his prisoner. He wiped his memory. Then he remade him as a cyborg, Dark Heart, who became one of his four chief warriors. Dark Heart remembered nothing of Tyler Steele. He fought for Grimlord as fiercely as any creature born on that side of the reality barrier.

The scientist's knowledge was put to use as well. Grimlord's servants drew on it for years.

Found and lost again, 1994

On 30 September 1994 Kaitlin Star photographed a prisoner in an abandoned building in the woods outside the city. He had Tyler Steele's face. He was moved before Ryan could reach him.

In November Dark Heart was guarding a hole in the reality barrier when the VR Troopers found him. Ryan beat him, then spared him. For losing, Grimlord condemned Dark Heart to death. On 15 November the Troopers learnt who he was. Professor Hart passed Ryan's memories of his father into the cyborg, which woke Tyler Steele's mind in Dark Heart's body.

He would not stay safe in the laboratory. He went back into virtual reality, as Dark Heart, to attack Grimlord in his own dungeon. Grimlord's marksman Renegade shot him down. Ryan rescued him. On 17 November father and son fought their way into the dungeon together, which Grimlord blew up round them. Wounded by the swordsman Decimator, Tyler Steele came back at last to his human shape. Grimlord took him away again before Ryan could get him home.

The prism

He was a prisoner for ten months more. On 22 February 1995 a film recovered from an old satellite gave his son proof that he was alive. That same month Grimlord's servants used his notes twice: to grow a copy of Ryan, then to build the Red Python, an armoured warrior modelled on the Troopers.

On 18 September 1995 Grimlord began draining everything Tyler Steele knew of virtual reality into a prism of green light. With it he made his Skugs stronger. He also built himself a new stronghold, the Virtual Dark Fortress.

Home

On 20 September 1995 Ryan brought his father out of a cavern where Grimlord was holding him. Tyler Steele was very ill. Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese took him to his old friend Tao, who nursed him back to health.

He went straight back to work. Ryan had lost his armour in the rescue, so his father built him a new suit, blue, stronger than the first. Ryan wore it on 22 September. Early in October Tyler Steele gave him the command that turned the Troopers' Skybase into the Troopertron, a fighting robot.

Afterwards

He did not stay. On 11 October 1995 he said goodbye to Ryan, leaving Crossworld City for secret government work on a way of destroying Grimlord's world for good. He was home for Christmas that year, when he joined his son at the party at Tao's Dojo.

Nothing is recorded of Tyler Steele after that. When the record of the VR Troopers stops, in February 1996, he was still away.

pages.title: Uktena
infobox: North America, and the Americas beyond
The native peoples of the Americas
Mysticism, secret lore and the binding of evil spirits
pages.html:
