The Uktena are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the Pure Ones, the tribes native to the Americas. They are mystics and keepers of secrets. They guard the evil spirits bound beneath the land, and they seek out hidden knowledge that other Garou would rather leave alone.

Totem and ways

The tribe follows Uktena, the great horned serpent of the waters and the underworld. It is a spirit of secrets, magic and patience. The Uktena know more than any other Garou about the lore of spirits and the binding of them. Their great duty is the watch over places where Wyrm spirits were bound in ancient times, beneath mountains, lakes and mounds, so that those spirits never wake.

The Uktena believe that a weapon is best understood before it is used. They gather knowledge of every kind, dark lore and the secrets of the Wyrm among it. The habit gives them power, and it makes them suspect.

Homelands

Their homelands are the forests, deserts, rivers and mountains of North America. Their Kinfolk are the native peoples of the continent. Over the centuries they have taken in Kinfolk from many other native peoples of the Americas. In later times they have also taken in Kinfolk from other peoples who have lost their own lands. With the Wendigo they are the Pure Ones, the tribes that were in the Americas before the European Garou came.

Place in the world

European settlers brought their own Garou with them, whom the Pure Ones call Wyrmcomers. Their coming cost the Uktena many caerns and many lives. The old grievance has not healed. Other tribes value the Uktena's knowledge and fear what they keep hidden. Some whisper that the tribe has studied the Wyrm so closely that it has been touched by it.

pages.title: Underground Voice Daily
infobox: The Underground Voice Daily; Woody Stocker; Percy Rooney; Percival Rooney
pages.html:
The Underground Voice Daily is the newspaper of Crossworld City, California. Its editor is Woody Stocker. Its reporters include Kaitlin Star, who from September 1994 was secretly one of the VR Troopers. Another is her rival, Percy Rooney, the mayor's nephew.

The paper

The Underground Voice Daily is the daily paper of Crossworld City. It covers the life of the town, from the mayor's office to the doings of its great man, Karl Ziktor. From September 1994 it had the VR Troopers to write about as well.

It has done some good in its time. In November 1994 a story of Kaitlin Star's kept the land of an animal sanctuary protected. In February 1996 her photographs of Karl Ziktor on a camping trip did real harm to his standing in the town. The paper never learnt that Ziktor was Grimlord, the Troopers' enemy. It never learnt that one of the Troopers was on its own staff either.

Woody Stocker

Woody Stocker is the editor in chief. He is a cheerful, scatterbrained man who wears a different hat every day, in an office full of toys. He likes to invent snacks. Some of them are good, his nachos among them. Others are not.

He is Kaitlin Star's employer, besides being Percy Rooney's. Percy is often in trouble with him.

Percy Rooney

Percival Rooney the Third, called Percy, is a reporter on the paper. He is the nephew of Abner Rooney, the mayor of Crossworld City. He is bookish and clumsy, forever trying to beat Kaitlin Star to a story. He is also badly allergic to animals, dogs above all. Ryan Steele's dog, Jeb, who can talk, takes shameless advantage of it.

Percy has a gift for being in the wrong place. In November 1994 Grimlord's creatures took him prisoner, so that he ended up in one of Grimlord's dungeons alongside two of the Troopers. They had to get him out without his finding out who they were. In November 1995 a love potion of Grimlord's set him on the way to marrying Kaitlin, until it was stopped.

pages.title: Urdnot Wrex
infobox: The USS Enterprise-B, in Captain John Shepard's pay
The Intergalactic War; the relief of Palaven, 2300
pages.html:
Urdnot Wrex was a Krogan mercenary whom Captain John Shepard paid to serve aboard the USS Enterprise-B. He was centuries old, a battlemaster of Clan Urdnot who had long since given up on his own people. In the Intergalactic War he went home to lead them.

Tuchanka

Wrex was born on Tuchanka after the genophage, when a Krogan child that lived was already a rare thing. As a young chief of Clan Urdnot he argued that the Krogan should stop fighting, to rebuild their numbers instead. His own father, Jarrod, wanted war. Jarrod called him to a meeting on sacred ground, then tried to murder him there. Wrex killed his father. He left Tuchanka afterwards.

He spent the next centuries as a mercenary and a hunter of men, selling his strength to whoever paid. He believed that his people were finished. He did not much care.

The Enterprise-B

Shepard hired him. Wrex was never a member of Starfleet, nor did he pretend to be one. He was paid, which he considered a more honest arrangement than an oath. He had fought for the Orion Syndicate's rivals often enough to know its ways, which made him useful to a captain who hated it. In time the two of them came to trust each other. Shepard later said that Wrex was the only one of his crew who had never once lied to him.

The war

When the Galactic Empire invaded in 2299, Wrex went back to Tuchanka. He took the leadership of Clan Urdnot, then brought the other clans behind it. On 19 January 2300 a Klingon fleet carried his army to Palaven. There the Krogan broke the Empire's siege, fighting beside the Turians who had loosed the genophage on them.

In the saga

Urdnot Wrex has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: USS Enterprise-B
infobox: 2311, in the Tomed Incident; her whole crew was saved
pages.html:
The USS Enterprise-B was the third Federation starship to bear the name, an Excelsior-class ship commanded for the whole of her life by Captain John Shepard. She carried a cloaking device in secret. She was the flagship of the alliance in the Intergalactic War, until she was destroyed at Tomed in 2311.

The maiden voyage

She left spacedock on 14 October 2293, unfinished, with James T. Kirk aboard as a guest. That day she went to the help of two transport ships caught in the Nexus. She saved forty-seven people. Kirk was lost when the ribbon tore open her hull.

The cloak

The Enterprise-B differed from the rest of her class in the swellings along her hull. They housed a cloaking device, built from the Romulan one that Kirk had stolen in 2268. With it she carried out the Federation's quieter business under Shepard, before the Intergalactic War, during it and afterwards.

War and loss

In the war of 2299 to 2300 she fought at Vega, Cestus III, Rannoch, Romulus, Thessia and Earth. The Romulans first saw her cloak at the relief of Romulus. Their anger at it ended in the Tomed Incident of 2311, in which she was destroyed. Captain Shepard held her together until every member of her crew had got away. He was the last to leave her, with Starfleet picking up all of them. The Treaty of Algeron, which followed, forbade the Federation to use cloaking devices again.

In the saga

The USS Enterprise-B has not appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Vampirism
pages.html:
Vampirism began with the curse God laid on Cain for the murder of his brother Abel. That curse left Cain deathless and soulless, but he was not yet a vampire. After the Flood, the blood magic Lilith taught him turned him into the first of them, and with it he passed his curse on. Every vampire descends from him. A vampire's soul is destroyed when it is sired, and the Beast fills the place where the soul was.

Origin

God's sentence on Cain had three parts. He would not die. The sun would repel him and burn him. He would wander for ever, without rest or home. Beneath all three it meant soullessness, which was the real sentence. It gave him no powers at all.

In that state he wandered through the ages of Middle-earth and the Hyborian Age. The Flood did not take him, since God does not revoke His own sentences: he could not drown.

After the Flood, Lilith came to him. She called herself Adam's first wife, which was a lie; she was in truth a servant of Morgoth. She led him into blood magic, and the magic turned him into the first vampire, of the First Generation. With it he sired others like himself. The bargain put Cain, and every vampire after him, under Morgoth's will.

Cain's three childer, Enoch, Irad and Zillah, were the Second Generation. They sired the thirteen Antediluvians of the Third, the founders of the clans, in Enoch, the First City. The older the blood, the stronger it is, and the less of a person is left in it.

Nature

A vampire is sired through the Embrace. Its sire drains a mortal of blood, then gives back a little of its own. The childe must drink blood to go on existing, and human blood is what it craves. Its blood carries powers called Disciplines, which differ from clan to clan.

A mortal who drinks a vampire's blood three times is bound to love it for life; this is the blood bond. A mortal kept on lesser draughts becomes a ghoul. A vampire that drinks another to the last drop, soul and all, takes its generation. The Kindred call this diablerie, and count it among their worst crimes.

Fire and sunlight destroy every vampire, though the very oldest can bear the sun for a few seconds. A stake through the heart paralyses a vampire rather than killing it. Garlic is mostly folklore. Running water and mirrors trouble some lines, but not others. No vampire may enter a home uninvited. A cross held by somebody who believes in Jesus Christ repels them, because the curse was God's and the sign is His.

Society

Vampires call themselves the Kindred, or Cainites. Since 1435 they have hidden from mortals under the Masquerade. Most clans belong to the Camarilla, or say they do. The Sabbat rejects it, and the Anarchs reject their elders. The Assamites, the Followers of Set, the Giovanni and the Ravnos stand apart from both sects. The clanless are called Caitiff. Dracula answers to nobody. Neither does the Aurelian line of the Master and Angelus.

In 1900 the wizarding governments of the world lent the Camarilla their concealment charms, in return for a promise that no Camarilla vampire would ever harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Children of the blood

Vampires cannot give life. Only the thin-blooded of the last generations, the fifteenth and after, the furthest from Cain, keep enough of the living body to father or bear a child. Their children are dhampirs: mortal at the last, but born with something of the vampire in them. The Kindred count those births among the signs of the Time of Thin Blood before Gehenna.

There are exceptions. Alucard, the son of Dracula, is a dhampir through the Crimson Stone. Blade is one because the vampire Deacon Frost fed on his mother while she was in labour. Connor, the son of Angel and Darla, was something else again. He was the one human child ever born to vampires, and a direct act of God.

In the saga

Hermione Granger took up vampires in September 1992 with Voyages with Vampires. In October 1993 Remus Lupin taught Harry Potter's class about the Masquerade, the sects, the clans, the Beast and the blood bond. He taught them a Fire-Making Charm, and a charm for a brief patch of sunlight. Then he made them repeat three times, 'Never ask one in.' He had never met a vampire, he said, that he would turn his back on.

pages.title: Ventara
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
A world beside Earth, reached through reflections
About 2007, by Xaviax, who carried its people off to Karsh
pages.html:
Ventara is a world on the other side of mirrors, a twin of Earth that can be reached through any surface that reflects. It is not a planet in the sky. It lies beside this world, as close as the back of a looking-glass, with its own people, its own cities and its own guardians, the Kamen Riders. In the summer of 1994 it is free. About 2007 the warlord Xaviax emptied it, carrying its whole people off to Karsh as slaves. They came home in December 2009.

The world behind the glass

Ventara looks very like Earth. A Rider who steps through a shop window in an American city comes out in a street much like the one he has left. The two worlds touch wherever there is a reflection: a mirror, a window, a car door, a puddle of spilt water.

Ordinary people do not cross by themselves. A Kamen Rider can, with his Advent Deck. So can the mirror monsters that serve Xaviax, which reach out of reflections to drag people in. Maya Young was pulled through by one in February 2009. Len of Ventara brought her back.

Ventara is one of the worlds that lie beside this one, not out among the stars. Another is the world that Tommy Oliver's double conquered as Lord Drakkon.

The enchanted mirrors of wizards are a different matter. The Mirror of Erised is a spell laid on a single glass. The way to Ventara lies behind every reflection, and it owes nothing to any wizard.

Mirror monsters

The creatures that serve Xaviax are called mirror monsters. They pass freely between the two worlds. They come out of reflections to seize people on Earth, whom they drag back through the glass. Xaviax has long used them as soldiers against the Kamen Riders. From about 2007 he used them as kidnappers too, to bring him the people of Earth one at a time.

A Kamen Rider can hear a way opening between the worlds. For Len of Ventara, in his first months on Earth, that sound was the only warning that somebody was about to vanish.

Mirror twins

A Ventaran may have a double on Earth: a person with the same face, the same voice, the same blood. The Riders call such a pair mirror twins. The twins need have nothing else in common. Adam of Ventara was a Kamen Rider. His twin, Kit Taylor, was a boy in foster care. Neither knew that the other existed.

The likeness goes deeper than looks. An Advent Deck, which is locked to the body of one Rider, will open for that Rider's twin. It was this that let Xaviax arm men of Earth with the decks he had stolen.

Eubulon and the twelve

Ventara's troubles came from Karsh, a world laid waste by its own wars. Its general, Xaviax, wanted slaves to rebuild it. His scientist Eubulon found the way into Ventara through reflections. Eubulon fell ill there. The people he had come to mark down for slavery nursed him, so he changed sides.

He made the armour of the Kamen Riders for twelve chosen Ventarans, who beat off Xaviax's first invasion. Eubulon himself was lost in 1947. After that his Riders guarded Ventara by turns. One kept watch for a year while the rest slept. In the summer of 1994 that watch is still being kept.

The empty world

About 2007 Xaviax came back by a trick. Calling himself Paragon, a friend of Eubulon, he persuaded the Dragon Knight, Adam of Ventara, to show him where the twelve slept. He vented them, took their Advent Decks, then sent the whole people of Ventara to Karsh. The traitor was shut up with Sarah, the woman he loved, in a false Ventara that Xaviax made to keep him quiet.

For the next two years the real Ventara stood empty. Nothing moved in its streets but Xaviax's monsters.

It became a battlefield. Through 2009 Riders of both sides fought most of their battles on the Ventaran side of the glass, in streets with nobody in them. Most of those who were vented that year were vented there.

Kit Taylor first saw Ventara on 13 December 2008, when a monster knocked him through a mirror. In October 2009 he escaped from a cell on Earth through a puddle of spilt water. A week later he fled through a mirror into Ventara with his friends, when the No-Men came to arrest them.

The restoration

Xaviax was destroyed on 18 December 2009. Afterwards the Ventarans came home from Karsh to the houses they had left. Eubulon brought the last of the vented Riders out of the Advent Void. Adam of Ventara laid down his deck to live quietly with Sarah.

The Riders took up their guard again, with one change. Kit Taylor of Earth now wore the Dragon Knight's armour, so the order watched over both worlds.

pages.title: Vexor
infobox: A villain out of a comic book, made real
A crypt in the Charterville cemetery
pages.html:
Vexor is the lord of the Magnavores, the villains of the comic book in which the Beetleborgs first appeared. When Flabber's wish made the heroes real, on 7 September 1996, Vexor came out of the same pages with three lieutenants. For eight months he made war on Charterville from a crypt in its cemetery. On 21 May 1997 the Beetleborgs sent him back into the comics for good.

Out of the comic

Vexor was drawn by Art Fortunes as the enemy of the Beetleborgs. He was ink on paper until three children of Charterville wished to be those heroes. The wish opened the comic in both directions, so that Vexor walked out.

He set up his court in a crypt in the Charterville cemetery. From there he could call other monsters out of the comics, a new one whenever the last was beaten. He had foot soldiers called Scabs, whom he seldom troubled to use, with a squadron of jet fighters shaped like wasps.

The Magnavores

Three lieutenants came out of the comic with him. Typhus is a brawler with a second mouth in the flat top of his head. Noxic is a machine in the shape of a man, who can take off his own head to master other machines, though he would sooner have a doughnut. Jara is a fighter in red with a white mask, who carries a whip.

Shadowborg

On 11 November 1996 Vexor made a Beetleborg of his own. He took a piece of the Blue Stinger's armour, from which he made Shadowborg, a black figure in the likeness of a longhorn beetle. Shadowborg drew his strength from Vexor's own source of power, the energy Axis. He beat the three Beetleborgs in their first fight, then took their powers.

Art Fortunes answered with a fourth Beetleborg, the White Blaster, worn by a boy named Josh Baldwin. Josh won the powers back. Drew McCormick stole the Axis itself, which gave him the Mega Blue armour.

Vexor offered a bargain. If the Beetleborgs could beat Shadowborg, he would take the Magnavores back into the comic. On 16 November Drew destroyed Shadowborg. Vexor broke his word, fought the Beetleborgs himself, then lost. He came back afterwards in a new body.

Bargains with strangers

Twice Vexor made common cause with an enemy of the Power Rangers. On 19 October 1996 he struck a bargain with Prince Sprocket of the Machine Empire. Vexor was to supply a monster, Scrapjaw, which the Empire's servant Klank would make into a giant. Vexor then tried to steal the means of doing it. He lost the monster, the bargain and the giant together.

On 3 May 1997 he helped the space pirate Divatox to carry off Flabber, by drawing the Beetleborgs away from Hillhurst Mansion. He gained nothing by that either.

Nukus

In May 1997 the Magnavores stole a drawing from Art Fortunes's office. They brought it to life as a new ally. It was Nukus, who was no ally of theirs. He built the giant Borgslayer out of every monster the Beetleborgs had destroyed, taking care that the children should learn how to bring it down. On 21 May 1997 they did. The blast swept Vexor, Typhus, Noxic and Jara back into the comics. They did not come out again.

pages.title: Virtual reality (Grimlord's world)
infobox: Grimlord's virtual world; Reality Barrier; Virtual Dungeon; Virtual Dark Fortress; Battle Grid
A world lying beside this one
Professor Hart's laboratory, outside Crossworld City
The Virtual Dungeon; the Virtual Dark Fortress, from September 1995
pages.html:
Virtual reality, as the scientists of Crossworld City use the words, is not a picture inside a computer. It is a real world lying beside this one, on the far side of what they call the reality barrier. Grimlord rules it. He means to break the barrier down, so that his armies can come through into the Earth. The VR Troopers, whose armour is made of the stuff of that world, were raised in September 1994 to stop him.

The name

In 1994 most people who say 'virtual reality' mean a scene drawn by a computer for somebody wearing a headset. Tyler Steele and Professor Horatio Hart, two scientists of Crossworld City in California, used the words for something else. Their experiments had led them to a place that was there already, with inhabitants of its own.

It is one more world beside this one. Nobody is known to have reached it except by the machines of Professor Hart's laboratory, or by Grimlord's own means.

The reality barrier

The two worlds are divided by the reality barrier. Whatever is made in virtual reality is real there. With the right machinery it can be brought across the barrier into this world, where it is just as real.

The barrier is not quite whole. There are holes in it, which Grimlord keeps guarded, so that a few of his creatures at a time can slip through to Crossworld City. What he cannot yet do is bring his whole army across. Breaking the barrier altogether is the aim of nearly everything he does. In September 1995 his scientist Colonel Icebot tried to warp it with two great electromagnets, one at the North Pole, the other beside the power station at Crossworld City. The Troopers destroyed both.

The inhabitants

Virtual reality is peopled by Grimlord's creatures: robots, cyborgs, beasts in armour. The Troopers call them mutants. The word is misleading, for they are nothing to do with the mutants born among mankind. Grimlord's are made, not born. His oracle Oraclon could turn out a new one to order.

His foot soldiers are the Skugs, who can pass for human beings on this side of the barrier. Not everything there serves Grimlord willingly. Knighttime, a prince from a savage part of that world, was his ally in 1995, then his betrayer in February 1996.

Human beings can live there. Tyler Steele was held in it for more than ten years. The mind of Professor Hart has been kept alive in it since about 1984.

Places

Grimlord's first seat was the Virtual Dungeon, where he sat enthroned among his creatures. He blew it up in November 1994 to kill Ryan Steele, then again in September 1995, after which he gave it up.

His second was the Virtual Dark Fortress, which he raised in September 1995 with knowledge drained from Tyler Steele. It is a stronghold in the shape of a great ship, hanging in space on the far side of the barrier. It ought not to be confused with the Dark Fortress of Astronema, a different vessel in a different war. The Troopers raided it on 21 February 1996, leaving it crippled.

The Battle Grid is an empty place in virtual reality. When Skugs appeared in the streets of Crossworld City, the Troopers would carry the fight there, where no bystander could be hurt.

The Troopers' own great machines were kept in virtual reality as well. The chief of them was the Skybase, a flying fortress, which from October 1995 could change into a fighting robot, the Troopertron.

Crossing over

A Trooper crossed the barrier by means of a Virtualizer, a pendant made in Professor Hart's laboratory. It clothed its wearer in armour from virtual reality. In the armour a Trooper could pass through at will. The laboratory never had more than a very few.

Grimlord crosses by another road. In this world he is the industrialist Karl Ziktor. An orb on Ziktor's desk carries him to his throne at a word.

Outside Crossworld City hardly anybody knows that this other world exists. When the record of the Troopers stops, in February 1996, the barrier was still holding.

pages.title: VR Troopers
infobox: Ryan Steele, Kaitlin Star, J.B. Reese
Professor Hart's laboratory, in the hills outside the city
The Skybase, later the Troopertron; the Turbo Cycle; a battle cruiser
pages.html:
The VR Troopers are three young martial artists of Crossworld City, California: Ryan Steele, Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese. From September 1994 they fought the armies of Grimlord, who rules the world called virtual reality, to keep him from breaking through into this one. Their armour came from the work of Ryan's lost father, Tyler Steele, by way of his friend Professor Horatio Hart. In the summer of 1994 none of it has happened yet, and the three spend their days at Tao's Dojo. The record of their war stops in February 1996, with Grimlord still undefeated.

Before the Troopers

Tyler Steele and Professor Horatio Hart were scientists of Crossworld City, colleagues who were also close friends. Working in secret, they found that what they called virtual reality was no picture inside a computer. It was a real world lying beside this one. They learnt how to cross into it, only to find it full of creatures who meant to cross the other way.

To meet that danger the two men designed the VR Troopers: armour, weapons and flying machines that exist in virtual reality, waiting to be called up by a human wearer. They never wore the armour themselves. About 1984 Grimlord, the master of that other world, struck at them both. Professor Hart was hurt so badly that his friend could save him only by sending his mind across into virtual reality, where it has had to stay. Tyler Steele was carried off to Grimlord's dungeon. To Crossworld City he had simply vanished.

Grimlord was a man of their own city, the industrialist Karl Ziktor, who had once worked with them both. Nobody on the laboratory's side has ever found that out.

The call, September 1994

On 3 September 1994 a message appeared on Ryan Steele's computer. It came from Professor Hart, who said that he had word from Ryan's father. Ryan took his two closest friends, Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese, to the Professor's laboratory in the hills on the edge of the city. There a face on a screen told them what Tyler Steele had been working on, who had taken him, and what Grimlord meant to do.

A recording left by the two scientists explained the Troopers. The Professor gave each of the three a Virtualizer, a pendant that calls the armour. Grimlord learnt of it almost at once, and he sent his army against them the same day. In that first fight his swordsman Decimator all but killed Ryan, who was left lying in a quarry.

On 10 September his friends found him there. They fought off the Skugs who were hunting him, then carried him back to the laboratory to be mended. Grimlord, meanwhile, was massing his creatures for an assault on the whole world. Kaitlin, out with her camera, saw them moving into position. The three transformed together, and they won. Afterwards they promised one another to keep Grimlord out of this world, and to find Ryan's father.

Armour and machines

To transform, the three held up their Virtualizers and called 'Trooper transform!', then 'We are VR!' The armour formed round each of them at once. Ryan's first armour was half red, half blue. Kaitlin's was red, while J.B.'s was black.

It was real armour, though made of the stuff of virtual reality. In it a Trooper could pass through the reality barrier at will. Ryan fought mostly with his hands. J.B. carried a laser sabre that opened out into a lance, while Kaitlin had a pistol. When Skugs appeared in the open street, the Troopers would draw them into the Battle Grid, an empty place on the far side of the barrier where a fight could hurt nobody else.

Their heavier machines waited in virtual reality until they were called. The Skybase was a flying fortress with a cockpit for all three. J.B. had a battle cruiser, a flying cycle, and a great bazooka for use against Grimlord's aircraft. Ryan rode the Turbo Cycle. Kaitlin's own small car was altered by Professor Hart until it could fly.

The search for Tyler Steele, 1994 to 1995

From the first the Troopers had two tasks: to hold the barrier, and to find Tyler Steele. On 30 September 1994 Kaitlin photographed a prisoner in an abandoned building in the woods outside the city. He looked like Ryan's father. By the time Ryan reached the place, the man had been moved. It was enough to show that Grimlord was holding Tyler Steele alive.

In between, Grimlord tried whatever he could think of. He hypnotised a hall full of dancers with music. He set a bomb at the city's dam. He loosed a sludge from virtual reality in the streets. A ray of his turned all three Troopers into children, who had to go on fighting as children until Professor Hart could turn them back.

In November 1994 the Troopers learnt that one of Grimlord's fiercest warriors, the cyborg Dark Heart, was partly human. Ryan fought him, beat him, then would not finish him. On 15 November Dark Heart was shown to be Tyler Steele himself, with his memory wiped clean. Professor Hart gave him back his mind by passing Ryan's memories of their life together into him. His body stayed as Grimlord had made it.

Over the next two days Ryan carried his wounded father out of a trap on the Turbo Cycle, while Grimlord's aircraft bombed the laboratory. Father and son went into virtual reality together to face Grimlord in his dungeon. Grimlord blew the dungeon up round them. Tyler Steele, wounded by Decimator, came back to his human shape, but Grimlord carried him off again before Ryan could get him away.

On 22 February 1995 Dr Monroe of the National Space Laboratory brought the Troopers a film recovered from an old satellite. It showed that Tyler Steele was still alive. Days later Grimlord sent out a Trooper of his own, the Red Python. Colonel Icebot had built it from Tyler Steele's stolen knowledge, but it needed a human being inside it. Skugs seized Amy, a friend of Kaitlin's who worked at an animal shelter, to be that human.

As the Red Python she nearly killed Kaitlin. Then the armour began to destroy itself. The Troopers got Amy out of it alive, and Professor Hart undid what had been done to her mind. She never learnt that the Troopers who saved her were her own friends.

The rescue, September 1995

On 18 September 1995 Grimlord began to drain Tyler Steele's knowledge of virtual reality into a prism of green light, taking care that the Troopers should watch him do it. The Troopers searched Professor Hart's old vault at Crossworld University for anything that might help. Ryan's dog, Jeb, volunteered to go into the dungeon as a spy, with Ryan close behind him. Grimlord blew up the dungeon for the second time. Both of them lived.

On 20 September the Troopers tracked Grimlord to a cavern where he was holding his prisoner. Ryan fought his way in. He brought his father out, along with Kaitlin and J.B., whom the Skugs had caught. It cost him everything he had: Grimlord's lightning melted his Virtualizer, so his armour was gone.

Tyler Steele was a free man for the first time in more than ten years, though a very sick one. Kaitlin and J.B. took him to Tao, who nursed him back to health. As soon as he could stand, he went to the laboratory to build his son a new suit of armour, more powerful than the first. Tao supplied the crystal that powered it. On 22 September Ryan put it on, and the three Troopers beat Grimlord's new army in a quarry outside the city.

The Virtual Dark Fortress, 1995 to 1996

Grimlord had gained as much as he had lost. With the prism he made himself stronger, gave up the ruins of his dungeon, and raised the Virtual Dark Fortress, a stronghold in the shape of a great ship. He made new commanders there: Despera, Doom Master and the oracle Oraclon. His Skugs became Ultra Skugs, which were a good deal harder to destroy.

The Troopers grew stronger too. In October 1995 Tyler Steele gave Ryan the command that turned the Skybase into the Troopertron, a fighting robot. That same month one of Grimlord's machines, a kind of mirror, split Kaitlin into two people. When Professor Hart had joined them again, she kept the power to become two Troopers whenever she needed to.

Then Tyler Steele went away again, this time of his own choice. On 11 October 1995 he said goodbye to his son, leaving Crossworld City for secret work on a way of destroying Grimlord's world. He was home for Christmas that year.

In November 1995 an archaeologist called Nebraska Smith found an ancient doorway inside a pyramid, which held the secret of who Grimlord really was. Ryan got as far as the place where it was kept. He could have stayed to learn it. He went back for Kaitlin and J.B. instead, who were in danger, so the Troopers never did find out.

Where the record stops

The last weeks of the record are a string of raids. On 7 February 1996 the Troopers destroyed Grimlord's Air Castle. On 20 February his ally Knighttime turned on him by stopping time over the whole Earth, so that for once Ryan Steele fought with Grimlord at his side, to break the machine that was doing it. On 21 February Grimlord's Skugs stole Galileo, a robot the Troopers had built to hold everything the laboratory knew. The Troopers followed it into the Virtual Dark Fortress, got it back, and left Oraclon's circuits burning behind them.

There the record ends. The fortress was crippled, not destroyed. Grimlord was still its master, Karl Ziktor was still the richest man in Crossworld City, and nobody had connected the two. Tyler Steele was away at his work. Professor Hart was still a face on a screen. Nothing is recorded of the VR Troopers after February 1996.

The Troopers and the wider world

The people of Crossworld City knew that three figures in armour appeared whenever Grimlord's creatures did, and their mayor spoke up for them. Beyond the city the Troopers were hardly known at all. Most of their fighting was done on the far side of the barrier, or else in quarries, woods and hills where there was nobody to film it.

California had a far more famous team in the same years, the Power Rangers of Angel Grove, who were on the news nearly every morning. No meeting between the two is recorded. Nor did Professor Hart ever ask the Justice League or the Avengers for help. Nobody on this side could cross the barrier without a Virtualizer, and the laboratory never had more than a very few.

pages.title: Vukodlak
infobox: A faction of the Sabbat; the Assamite assassin called Pink; smugglers of the Followers of Set
By the elders of the Tzimisce, in the 1140s
1999, in the Cathedral of Flesh in New York, by Christof Romuald
pages.html:
Vukodlak is a Methuselah of the Tzimisce, a voivode of the old Carpathian lords, who meant to rise above the Antediluvians themselves and make himself the equal of the clans' ancestors. Since the twelfth century he has slept beneath the castle of Vyšehrad above Prague, bound there by his own clan. His followers carried him to New York in 1999. He woke there in the Cathedral of Flesh, and Christof Romuald destroyed him.

The voivode

Vukodlak is among the oldest and most powerful of the Tzimisce, a voivode of the clan's old lords in the East. He is a master of Vicissitude, the clan's art of shaping flesh and bone. He took his name from the old Slavic word for a creature that is half wolf and half the walking dead.

His ambition is the greatest any Methuselah of his age is known to have held. He means to rise above the Antediluvians, the thirteen of the Third Generation from whom every clan descends, and to make himself their equal or their master.

Vyšehrad and Anezka

By the 1140s he lay asleep beneath Vyšehrad, the Tzimisce castle above Prague. In the war between the Tremere and the Tzimisce, his servants took a young nun, Anezka, to be his ghoul. When the crusader-turned-Brujah Christof Romuald came to Vyšehrad for her, she went to wake her master instead. Before she could, mortal forces stormed the castle and brought it down on them all, burying Christof in torpor.

The elders of Vukodlak's own clan feared him as much as anybody did. When the castle fell, they bound him in a sleep from which he was never meant to wake.

The long sleep

He slept for more than eight hundred years, and in all that time his followers never gave him up. Anezka stayed at his side as his ghoul, living on his blood. In secret, though, she worked against his waking, and undid what she could of their work.

By the end of the twentieth century a whole faction of the Sabbat served him. His followers took Vyšehrad back, and the Followers of Set smuggled the treasures of the castle to New York. An Assamite assassin called Pink, posing as a Brujah, worked for him. The Society of Leopold wanted him too. Its leader, Leo Allatius, meant to take Vukodlak's blood and use it to destroy every vampire in the world.

The Cathedral of Flesh

In 1999 his followers carried him to New York, where they hid him beneath the Cathedral of Flesh, a temple of shaped and living flesh. There he woke. Christof Romuald, woken himself in London that year, came looking for Anezka. Vukodlak offered her to him, since she now lived only by the Methuselah's blood, if Christof would serve him. Christof refused, and Vukodlak flung him into the tunnels beneath the Cathedral.

Christof came back up, and in the Cathedral of Flesh he destroyed Vukodlak. With the Methuselah gone, Christof Embraced Anezka so that she would not die.

pages.title: Wally West
infobox: The Flash; Kid Flash; Wallace West
pages.html:
Wally West is the third Flash. As a boy he ran beside Barry Allen as Kid Flash from 1959. After Barry died in the Crisis of 1985, Wally took up his name, his costume and his city. In August 1994, a man of about forty-five, he stood behind Superman at the United Nations Security Council.

Kid Flash

Wally West grew up in Blue Valley, Nebraska. In 1959, when he was about ten, he was visiting the laboratory of Barry Allen, who was courting his aunt Iris. Lightning struck the same rack of chemicals that had given Barry his speed, and it gave the same speed to Wally.

He became Kid Flash, Barry's partner, in a smaller copy of the red suit. Later he wore a yellow and red costume of his own.

In 1964 he was one of the founders of the Teen Titans, with Robin (Dick Grayson) and Aqualad. He grew up as a hero, working his way through his years in the Titans and through his own doubts. He was never far from his uncle.

The Flash

After Barry Allen's death in 1985 Wally West put on his uncle's costume and became the Flash. For some years he was markedly slower than Barry had been, and he had to learn the work of the name for himself. By the early 1990s he had grown faster than ever.

He has served with the Justice League in its various forms since the late 1980s, including its European branch. In 1994 he is one of its core members under Superman.

He is the first Flash to have grown up in the job, and his public career is now longer than his predecessor's. Unlike Barry, he has never hidden much about himself.

Early in October 1994 Batman called him to Gotham, where one of the Power Rangers had turned up in the middle of a fight with Lord Zedd's Putties. He fought beside the Rangers that week, when Brainiac shrank Angel Grove into a bottle.

In the saga

In the spring of 1994 Harry Potter remembered seeing a man in a red suit on the news from America, so fast that the cameras caught only a streak of light.

On 20 August 1994 the Flash stood with the League behind Superman at the United Nations, in red with a lightning flash on his chest. He was not the Flash of Dudley's annuals but the boy who used to run beside him, grown into a man of forty-five or so.

pages.title: Walter Sullivan
infobox: Silent Hill 4: The Room (17 June 2004); first named in Silent Hill 2 (25 September 2001)
None of his own: a No-Maj working a rite of the Order
The 21 Sacraments, for the Descent of the Holy Mother
Ten in June 1994; eight more after his death, from 1996 to 2004
22 June 1994, by his own hand, in a cell in Silent Hill
Vanished from the morgue at Silent Hill on the night of 22 June 1994; found in Room 302 in June 2004
pages.html:
Walter Sullivan was a murderer, born in 1970 in a flat in South Ashfield and raised by the Order of Silent Hill in its orphanage. He had no magic of his own. He had the Order's scripture, which taught him a rite of twenty-one murders called the 21 Sacraments, and he believed that it would give him back his mother. In June 1994 he killed ten people in ten days, then killed himself in a police cell. That was the eleventh sacrament, not the end. For ten years afterwards he went on killing from a world of his own on the far side of Room 302, until Henry Townshend put a stop to him on 22 June 2004.

Room 302

Walter was born in 1970 in Room 302 of South Ashfield Heights, a block of flats half a day's drive from Silent Hill. His parents, a young couple, walked out soon after his birth and were never seen again. The superintendent, Frank Sunderland, found the newborn there. He sent for an ambulance, which took the child to St Jerome's Hospital. He kept the baby's cord in a box, without quite knowing why.

The baby lived. Nobody claimed him, so he was sent to Wish House, an orphanage in the woods outside Silent Hill.

Wish House

Wish House belonged to the Order. Its children were taught the Order's scripture in the chapel. Those who learnt badly were beaten by the guard, Andrew DeSalvo, or shut in the round tower in the grounds. Walter kept a diary there in a child's handwriting. It records beatings, a friend called Bob who disappeared, and how hard he found the chapter on the 21 Sacraments.

On 16 October 1976, when he was six, important visitors came to the orphanage. One of them was Dahlia Gillespie. The next day she told him that his mother was asleep in Ashfield. If he learnt the 21 Sacraments properly, she said, he would be able to wake her. Walter was overjoyed. George Rosten, the priest who had the raising of him, wanted exactly that. He had picked the boy out to perform the rite one day. In the end he could not control what he had made.

From then on Walter made the long journey to South Ashfield Heights by train or bus, alone. By 17 March 1977 he had been four times. In time he went every week. He stood outside Room 302. There were always tenants in it, so he could not get in. He came to believe that the room was not where his mother lived. The room was his mother.

He was still making the journey as a youth. One day a very small girl felt sorry for the ragged young man and gave him her doll. Her name was Eileen Galvin. He kept the doll for the rest of his life, and afterwards.

The Ten Hearts

When he left Wish House, Walter moved to Pleasant River, a town near Silent Hill. In June 1994, aged twenty-four, he began.

He killed ten people in ten days, in Silent Hill, Pleasant River and Ashfield. He cut out each victim's heart and sewed up the chest. He carved a number into each body, from 01121 to 10121. The police took them for five-figure numbers. They were counts: one of twenty-one, two of twenty-one.

The first to die was Jimmy Stone, a priest of the Order, shot in the back of the head at Wish House. George Rosten was beaten to death at the altar underneath it. Two students, Bobby Randolph and Sein Martin, were strangled at Pleasant River. Four tradesmen of Ashfield were killed where they worked or lived: Steve Garland, who kept a pet shop; Rick Albert, who sold sports goods; William Gregory, a watchmaker; Eric Walsh, a barman. The seventh victim was a boy of Silent Hill called Billy Locane, the eighth his little sister, Miriam. Walter killed the two of them with an axe.

It was for the Locane children that he was arrested, on 18 June 1994. A former schoolmate said afterwards that Walter had babbled about somebody who was coming to punish him, whom he called the red devil. It had been Jimmy Stone's nickname. Early on 22 June he was found dead in his cell. He had stabbed himself in the neck with a soup spoon. That night the body vanished from its drawer in the town's morgue, while two parties of armed men who had come for it faced each other in the corridor outside: one from Delta Green, one from the SCP Foundation. Neither party ever learnt where it had gone. The coffin buried for him in a grave without a name, near the lake, went into the ground empty.

The Holy Assumption

A few days after his death the people of South Ashfield Heights saw a long-haired man in a long coat about the building. He was carrying a heavy tool, an old bowl and a bag that dripped. Room 302 was empty at the time. There were noises in it for some nights.

The rite Walter had learnt comes in stages. The ten hearts, with a cup of obsidian and a holy oil, were for the first of them, the Holy Assumption, by which the one who performs it puts off his flesh. His own death was the eleventh sacrament. It did not release him from the world. It tied him to Room 302, and it gave him a world of his own to rule. His body, which ought to have been in the grave by the lake, hung in a hidden room at the back of the flat. When the journalist Joseph Schreiber opened the grave by the lake in June 2001, the coffin was empty. Somebody had scratched 11/21 on the lid.

Walter was a No-Maj, with no more magic in him than his victims had. The 21 Sacraments is black magic of the Order's own tradition, taken from the scripture of a god that the Order itself believes to be dead. It worked for the same reason that all the Order's magic works. A demon answered it.

What came of the rite was two Walters. One was the man in the coat, who killed. The other was a small boy who only wanted to get into the room where his mother was.

The later sacraments

The killings began again about the end of 1996, two and a half years after his death. The twelfth victim, a schoolboy named Peter Walls, was beaten to death in a hotel room in South Ashfield. His body was found six months later, in the summer of 1997, with 12121 cut into it. As Walter Sullivan had been dead for three years, the police took it for the work of an imitator. They called it the Sullivan case, round two.

The thirteenth was Sharon Blake, who had gone into the woods near Wish House to look for relations lost to the Order. She was drowned there about the middle of 1997, though her body was not found until 2001. The fourteenth was Toby Archbolt, a priest of the Order's Holy Mother sect, who was pushed off a cliff in Mexico in the summer of 2001. The fifteenth was Joseph Schreiber himself, who was living in Room 302 by then. He died towards the end of that year, shut up in the flat. Unlike the first ten, these bodies kept their hearts. The rite gave each death a name: Void, Darkness, Gloom and Despair.

Four more died on four successive days in June 2004: Cynthia Velasquez on the 17th in a railway station under South Ashfield, Jasper Gein on the 18th in the woods by Wish House, Andrew DeSalvo on the 19th in the round tower, Richard Braintree on the 20th in his own flat. The rite called them Temptation, Source, Watchfulness and Chaos. Each of them had crossed his path at some time. Each died in a place that belonged to his own past, in the world on the other side of Room 302. Each was found dead in the waking world soon afterwards.

The end

Two sacraments were left. The twentieth, the Mother Reborn, was to be Eileen Galvin, now a grown woman living in Room 303. The twenty-first, the Receiver of Wisdom, was the tenant of Room 302, Henry Townshend, whom Walter had sealed into the flat with chains.

On the evening of 21 June Walter came for Eileen in her own flat and beat her nearly to death. The small boy stopped him from finishing it. She had been kind to him once.

Joseph Schreiber's ghost told Henry how the thing could be ended. Henry broke through the wall of his flat to find Walter's body hanging on a frame behind it. He took the cord that Frank Sunderland had kept in a box since 1970. With that, in the deepest part of Walter's world, he could wound the creature that the rite had put there in the mother's place. He drove eight spears into it. That made the man in the coat mortal again, and Henry killed him. It was 22 June 2004. Eileen lived, and the sacraments were never finished.

A few days later men who said they came from the state took his body away from the coroner at South Ashfield. They were from the SCP Foundation, which had lost it at Silent Hill ten years before.

pages.title: The Watchers' Council
infobox: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Welcome to the Hellmouth' (10 March 1997)
Finding, training and guiding the Slayer
The men who made the first Slayer after the Flood
pages.html:
The Watchers' Council is an old society of Muggle scholars and occultists, based in London. It finds, trains and guides the Slayer. It knows of the wizarding world and deals with it when it must. Like everything else it knows, it keeps that secret from the world at large. Witches and wizards who know of the Council at all look down on its members as pretenders: Muggles dabbling with dark forces they do not understand.

Origins

The Council descends from the men who made the first Slayer in the ages after the Flood, whom it remembers as the Shadow Men. It has kept watch over the line of Slayers ever since.

Each Slayer is given a Watcher, who finds her when she is called, trains her, advises her and records her deeds. The Council's library of the dark is among the greatest in the world, and it keeps its own counsel about what is in it.

Muggles and magic

Every member of the Council is a Muggle. What its members know of magic is occultism: learned, ritual and borrowed. It is the craft of men and women who have studied the darkness for centuries without being born to wield it, which makes it dangerous in their hands.

Some Watchers have meddled with it in their youth and paid for it. As a young man in London, Rupert Giles raised a demon called Eyghon with his friends, for their own amusement. Years afterwards it came back for them.

The Council and the wizarding world

The Council knows that the wizarding world exists. It deals with witches and wizards when it must. It keeps that knowledge as close as it keeps everything else, so that the general population knows nothing of either.

Witches and wizards think little of it. Those who have heard of the Council see Muggles playing with dark forces they do not understand, pretenders to a gift they were not born with. A great many wizards do not know it exists at all.

In the 1990s

In the 1990s the Council was led by Quentin Travers. In 1996 its Watcher Merrick found the newly called Slayer, Buffy Summers, in Los Angeles.

After Merrick's death her Watcher was Rupert Giles. From 1997 he kept watch over her in Sunnydale, California, as the librarian of her school.

Later years

The Council has an old test, the Cruciamentum, which every Slayer who reaches her eighteenth birthday must face without her powers. Buffy faced it in January 1999. Giles was dismissed for trying to protect her, and in the spring of that year Buffy broke with the Council altogether.

In the autumn of 2002 the Council's headquarters in London was blown up, and Quentin Travers died with most of the Watchers inside it.

pages.title: Wendigo
infobox: Wendigo, the spirit of the cold north wind
Canada, Alaska and the far north of America
The native peoples of the north
Ferocity, endurance and distrust of the European tribes
pages.html:
The Wendigo are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the Pure Ones native to the Americas. They are hard warriors of the northern forests and the frozen north. They have never forgiven the European Garou who came with the settlers.

Totem and ways

The tribe takes its name from its totem, Wendigo, the spirit of the cold north wind, of winter and of hunger. To its enemies it is a terrible spirit. The Wendigo are hunters and warriors, used to hardship. The long winters of the north are nothing to them. Keeping to the old ways of their Kinfolk, they guard the forests and lakes of the north. Wherever the Wyrm reaches into their lands, in mines, pipelines or poisoned rivers, they fight it.

Homelands

Their lands are the far north of America, from Alaska across Canada to the northern reaches of the United States, forest and tundra alike. Their Kinfolk are the native peoples of those lands. With the Uktena they are the Pure Ones, the tribes that were in the Americas before the European Garou came.

Place in the world

When Europeans crossed the Atlantic, their Garou came with them, seized caerns and made war on the native tribes. The Pure Ones call those Garou Wyrmcomers, and the Wendigo have neither forgotten nor forgiven. They work with the other tribes when the Wyrm leaves them no choice, but they trust few outsiders. They see what has befallen their Kinfolk as part of the same war.

pages.title: Widget the robot
infobox: A small robot, little more than a metal head, that opens gates between worlds
1988, at Loch Daemon, Scotland, by Tweedledope of the Crazy Gang
Kate Pryde, Kitty Pryde's older self from another future
Colin McKay, later Kylun; the Excalibur team
pages.html:
Widget is a small robot, little more than a metal head, that can open gates between worlds, though for years it could not choose where they led. It turned up in 1988 and carried the Excalibur team across a great many worlds. In 1993 it was found to hold the mind of Kate Pryde, Kitty Pryde's older self from Rachel Summers's future, who had fallen into it out of her own time.

Loch Daemon

In the summer of 1988, on a stormy night at Loch Daemon in Scotland, Tweedledope of the Crazy Gang threw together a gadget out of rubbish, odd chemicals and a transistor radio. Nothing seemed to happen, so he threw it away. Then the little thing opened its eyes.

It made friends with a boy called Colin McKay, who was hiding from the gangster Vixen's men. It opened a gate for him into another world, where he grew up as the warrior Kylun.

Gates

Widget's gates went off where they pleased. One of them carried off the train on which Moira MacTaggert and Callisto were travelling to London. Their Nazi doubles came back in their place. Another, in the Tower of London, turned a family of tourists into dinosaurs. Kitty Pryde phased through it in 1989 and shorted it out.

After that it worked for the Excalibur team, after a fashion. On the journey across the worlds it opened the way for the train, and at one stop it became a racing car. In 1990 Saturnyne mended its sense of direction. In 1991 her agents fitted it with a device to stop it jumping between worlds at all. That year Colin McKay, now grown, came through to the team and found his old friend again.

Kate Pryde

In 1993 Rachel Summers took the team into the future she had been born in. There it came out that Widget held the mind of Kate Pryde. Kate had escaped a Sentinel's collar by phasing out of it, then fallen through time into the little robot Tweedledope had made. With her memory back, she and Rachel set the Sentinels of her world to protecting all life. Kate stayed in her own time.

pages.title: Wish House
aliases: the Silent Hill Smile Support Society
infobox: Silent Hill 3 (23 May 2003), as Hope House; Silent Hill 4: The Room (17 June 2004)
The woods by Toluca Lake, on the edge of Silent Hill
The Silent Hill Smile Support Society, a charity of the Order of Silent Hill
The Order's sect of the Holy Mother
A round concrete tower, the Water Prison
pages.html:
Wish House is an orphanage in the woods on the edge of Silent Hill. On paper it belongs to a charity, the Silent Hill Smile Support Society, which takes in poor children with nowhere else to go. In fact it belongs to the Order of Silent Hill. The children are taught the Order's creed, and those who do not learn it are punished in a round tower in the grounds. Its best known pupil is Walter Sullivan.

The orphanage

The house stands by itself among the trees, a little way from Toluca Lake. The Silent Hill Smile Support Society, known as the 4S, presents it as a work of charity. The Order's sect of the Holy Mother manages it. Its priests hold their own rites at an altar under the floor.

The children have lessons in the chapel, where they read from the Order's scripture. A child who learns badly is beaten, or shut in the round tower in the grounds.

The Water Prison

The round tower in the grounds is called the Water Prison. It is built of concrete, three floors high, with the cells arranged in a ring on each floor. A watch room stands in the middle, from which a guard can look into every cell without being seen. A waterwheel drives its lights.

Children were shut up there as a punishment. The guard in Walter Sullivan's time was Andrew DeSalvo, who beat them. Walter's diary, written when he was six, mentions a boy named John who was kept in the round cell. It mentions another boy, Bob, who was gone one morning. The guards' own notes describe a hole dug under the cells, for the bodies.

Walter Sullivan

Walter Sullivan came to Wish House as a baby in 1970, abandoned by his parents. He learnt the Order's scripture there under the priest George Rosten. On 16 October 1976 the priestess Dahlia Gillespie visited the orphanage. The next day she told him that his mother was asleep in a flat in Ashfield, to be woken by the rite of the 21 Sacraments.

In June 1994 he began the rite at Wish House itself. The first of his victims was the priest Jimmy Stone, the founder of the Order's sect of Valtiel, whom he shot on the ground floor. Another was George Rosten, killed with an iron pipe at the altar underneath. Ten years later two more of his victims died there, in the world he had made out of his memories. Jasper Gein was burnt alive in the house on 18 June 2004. Andrew DeSalvo was drowned in his own prison the next day.

The article in Concord

About 1997 the journalist Joseph Schreiber wrote five pages about the place in the magazine Concord. He had not been allowed inside, or to take photographs. He had spoken to a neighbour, who had heard chanting at night with children crying. He had seen the round tower, which nobody would explain to him.

His conclusion was that the charity was a mask for a cult, that the cult was called the Order, and that it took children in to make believers of them. He promised to go on digging. A woman named Sharon Blake, whose family belonged to the Order, read about the ill-treatment of the children. She went into the woods to look for her relations. She was drowned there about the middle of 1997, the thirteenth of Walter Sullivan's sacraments.

Delta Green read the article, as it reads everything of the kind. One of its agents knew the name of Wish House from the Sullivan murders. He decided to leave Joseph Schreiber alone. A small magazine that nobody believed was, in his view, as good a silence as any.

pages.title: Wolfgang Smith
infobox: His mind is gone; more dog than wolf
pages.html:
Wolfgang Smith, called Wolfie, is the werewolf of Hillhurst Mansion, outside Charterville. He is a Garou whose mind is gone, more dog than wolf, whom the rest of the household keeps as its pet. He came to Charterville in September 1996. The following spring he changed Jo McCormick's face for good, by accident, with a spellbook.

A Garou astray

Wolfgang is a Garou, since there is no other kind of werewolf, but his mind is gone. He scratches at his fleas, chases whatever is thrown for him and talks in a growl that hardly anybody can follow. He keeps to one shaggy shape, never the war form, so no Delirium follows him. Everybody who meets Wolfgang remembers it afterwards.

Hillhurst

He turned up in Charterville in September 1996. Vexor's Magnavores tried to win him over to their side. He settled at Hillhurst instead, where the household took him in as the family dog.

Count Fangula, the vampire of the house, was his room-mate once. Vampires carry the scent of the Wyrm, which a Garou in his right mind cannot abide. Wolfgang is fond of this one. Fangula, for his part, is the only person who understands what Wolfgang says.

In March 1997 a pet of Wolfgang's own caused trouble in the house. That September a friend of his called at Hillhurst, a ghost who had sneezed his own head off at Wolfgang's fleas, hoping to get it back.

The spellbook

On 10 April 1997 Wolfgang got hold of Flabber's spellbook. The spell he set off changed the face of Jo McCormick, with her voice, for good. Flabber could only lay a second spell over it, so that the town went on seeing the girl it knew.

The next day he turned Jara of the Magnavores into a werewolf. The pair of them ran wild in Charterville until the Beetleborgs brought them in. A Garou can be made by the bite, which lasts for life. Jara's change did not last. She had walked out of a comic book, a thing of ink, in whom it found nothing to keep hold of.

Battles

On 3 May 1997 Elgar, the nephew of the space pirate Divatox, broke into Hillhurst with a crew of Piranhatrons to carry off Flabber. Wolfgang bit him.

In November 1997 both sides hunted for the eight Astral Coins. Wolfgang had one of them, the Lightning Bug coin. He would give it up only if he was allowed to join a battle himself, which he was. The coin called up Lightningborg, the third of the Astralborgs.

pages.title: X-Men
infobox: Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters, Salem Center, Westchester County, New York
Cyclops, Marvel Girl, the Beast, the Angel, Iceman
The Excalibur team (1987 to 1998), founded in Britain by Kitty Pryde and Kurt Wagner
Wolverine, the only mutant to outlive the Third World War
pages.html:
The X-Men are a team of mutants, founded in 1963 by the telepath Professor Charles Xavier and trained at his school in New York State. They use their powers to protect a world that fears and hates them. They first came to public notice fighting Magneto. They have been fighting him ever since, along with the Sentinels and the suspicion of ordinary people, the last of which has proved the hardest to beat.

The first X-Men

Xavier opened his School for Gifted Youngsters in the family mansion in Westchester County, as a cover for training young mutants. His first five pupils, all teenagers in 1963, were Scott Summers (Cyclops), Jean Grey (Marvel Girl), Hank McCoy (the Beast), Warren Worthington (the Angel) and Bobby Drake (Iceman). Their first public battle came that same year, against Magneto at the missile base at Cape Citadel. In 1965 they faced the Sentinels, the giant robots Dr Bolivar Trask had unveiled on live television that year.

The new X-Men

In 1975 the original team was captured on Krakoa, an island that turned out to be alive. Xavier gathered a new team from all over the world to rescue them, among them Storm, Colossus, Nightcrawler and the Canadian Wolverine. Most of the originals left afterwards, and the new X-Men became the most famous mutants in the world.

In 1977 the X-Men fought the Shi'ar Imperial Guard beside the Starjammers at the M'Kraan Crystal, where the Phoenix saved the universe.

In 1980 the cosmic force called the Phoenix, wearing Jean Grey's form, destroyed a star and then died on the Moon. In 1984 the X-Men were among the heroes carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. In 1986 the real Jean Grey was found alive, cocooned at the bottom of Jamaica Bay.

The Phoenix died in the Blue Area of the Moon, where the Inhumans have lived since 1982.

In September 1983 the X-Men were in Japan on business of Wolverine's when Godzilla, the great reptile of that country, came up off the coast. Storm went out over the water to meet him. She did not strike him. She raised a thunderstorm out at sea, then walked it slowly away from the land. Godzilla turned aside from the lightning, as he had once turned aside from the army's electric wires. Wolverine cleared the harbour behind her, with Colossus, while Nightcrawler fetched out the stragglers.

In 1986 the X-Men took in Betsy Braddock, an English telepath and the twin sister of Captain Britain, whom the New Mutants had rescued from Mojo. As Psylocke she joined the team that autumn, after the massacre of the Morlocks. In 1989 she sent the last of the X-Men through the Siege Perilous to save them from the Reavers. She came out of it in another woman's body, that of Kwannon, an assassin of the Hand. She has been an X-Man ever since.

Kitty Pryde, Dallas and the Excalibur team

Early in 1980 Kitty Pryde of Deerfield, Illinois, joined the X-Men at thirteen and a half, the youngest of them. In 1984 Rachel Summers came to them out of a future that will now never happen, the daughter that Jean Grey and Scott Summers had in that other world.

In the autumn of 1987 the X-Men died at Dallas, in front of the television cameras of the world, binding a demon called the Adversary. Roma of Otherworld drew their souls back before they had passed beyond the world and restored them to life. She also hid them from every camera on Earth. The X-Men let the world go on believing them dead, so that their enemies would leave the people they loved alone.

Kitty Pryde and Kurt Wagner, who were recovering on Muir Island, believed it with everyone else. In December 1987 they founded the Excalibur team in Britain with Rachel Summers, Captain Britain and Meggan. In 1991, knowing by then that the X-Men were alive, the team sent word to them. Kitty, Kurt and Piotr Rasputin came back to the X-Men in 1998, when the Excalibur team broke up.

The 1990s

By 1991 the team had grown so large that it split into two squads. In August 1993, after Magneto's global blackout, the X-Men went up to his space station, Avalon. Wolverine lost the metal from his skeleton there. Xavier ended the battle by shutting down Magneto's mind, and Wolverine left the team soon afterwards.

In 1991 Apocalypse infected Cyclops's small son Nathan with a techno-organic virus. The boy was taken into the future to be cured, and he came back as Cable.

The original five, who were teenagers in 1963, are now in their forties. In 1994 the X-Men stand between mutants and a frightened public, at a time when the Senate is weighing the revival of the Sentinel programme.

In the summer of 1993 the Legacy Virus killed Illyana Rasputina, the little sister of Piotr Rasputin. At her funeral that August Piotr turned on the X-Men to let Magneto go free, then went with him to Avalon. In the summer of 1994 he is still there, an X-Man among the Acolytes.

Since 1993 some of the X-Men's oldest friends have lived on Muir Island, off the north-west coast of Scotland, with Moira MacTaggert and the Excalibur team. In the spring of 1994 Charles Xavier left his school in Hank McCoy's charge to work there with Moira against the Legacy Virus.

In 1998, when the Excalibur team broke up, Kurt Wagner, Kitty Pryde and Piotr Rasputin came home to the X-Men.

The darkness that passed from Magneto into Charles Xavier on Avalon in August 1993 grew in secret into Onslaught. In the summer of 1996 he showed himself, wearing Xavier's face, beat the X-Men in their own house and left the mansion in ruins. The X-Men, who had loved Xavier all their lives, agreed that they might have to kill him.

That August they fought him in Central Park beside the Avengers and the Fantastic Four. Mutants could only make Onslaught stronger, so it was the heroes who were not mutants who gave themselves up to him, to give him a body. Then the X-Men struck it with everything they had, and Onslaught was destroyed. Many newspapers blamed the X-Men for the heroes who were lost.

Xavier, his telepathy gone, gave himself up to the government. The X-Men went home to the wreck of the school. Quicksilver went with them, who had lost his sister and his wife.

The end of the X-Men

The X-Men grew old, as everybody does. Longevity medicine kept many of them in their prime for years, but it could not carry anybody past a natural span. The first five, who had been teenagers in 1963, were nearly eighty by 2026, when the Third World War broke out. By then most of the old X-Men had died of old age, the founders among them. The last of the first five died about 2028.

Those who were left were growing old, but none of them died in bed. They fell in the war, heroes to the end: Storm, Kitty Pryde, Piotr Rasputin, Kurt Wagner, Psylocke, Rachel Summers, Rahne Sinclair, Cable and Hope Summers among them. They held back the Sentinels, broke open the camps and got the hunted out, until there was nobody left to get out.

The war killed the younger mutants too, the pupils of the X-Men's pupils. The Sentinels came back, then the camps, then a new strain of the Legacy Virus that killed everybody who carried the X-gene.

By the end of the war in 2053 the only X-Man left alive was Wolverine. His healing power, which had kept him from growing old since the nineteenth century, carried him through the war. He went into hiding.

In the saga

The X-Men have not been named in the saga. On Saturday 20 August 1994 the Muggle news Harry watched at Privet Drive showed old film from 1965, juddering, in black and white, of a bald man in a wheelchair arguing politely with a big, fierce man in a suit, until the Sentinels smashed through the studio wall. The same bulletin reported that the Senate Armed Services Committee would hear evidence the following week on reviving the Sentinels. Outside the United Nations a young nurse remembered the blackout of the August before: 'That was one mutant. One man, up in a space station, having a tantrum.'

pages.title: Xaviax
infobox: Kamen Rider: Dragon Knight, 'Search for the Dragon' (13 December 2008)
To rebuild Karsh with slaves taken from other worlds
He can wear any human face, drain the life from a living person and take over a body
Mirror monsters; the men he armed on Earth
Eubulon; the Kamen Riders of Ventara
pages.html:
Xaviax is a general of Karsh, a world ruined by its own wars, who means to rebuild it with slaves taken from other worlds. He can wear any face he likes. He was already at war with Ventara, the world behind mirrors, in the 1940s. About 2007 he emptied it. From then on he worked in secret to do the same to Earth, arming young men with stolen Advent Decks to clear the last Kamen Rider out of his way. Thirteen Riders destroyed him on 18 December 2009.

Karsh

Xaviax led Karsh through a long civil war, which left the planet in ruins. He did not mean to rebuild it with his own hands. He ordered his chief scientist, Eubulon, to find him other worlds, full of people who could be made to do the work. Eubulon built a teleport that worked through reflections. The first world it reached was Ventara.

None of the star-faring powers has ever met him. Xaviax does not cross space in ships. He steps from world to world through reflections, so the fleets of the Kree, the Skrulls, the Shi'ar and the Goa'uld have never seen him pass.

The first war for Ventara

Eubulon went over to the Ventarans. He armed twelve of them as Kamen Riders, who threw back Xaviax's army of mirror monsters. In 1947 Xaviax struck Eubulon down, hurling him out of Ventara altogether. Even so his Riders held their world. In the summer of 1994 they hold it still.

The taking of Ventara

Xaviax found his way round them about 2007. One Rider, Adam of Ventara, was in love and tired of his duty. Xaviax came to him as Paragon, a kindly man of Karsh who claimed to be Eubulon's old friend. He offered to free the young man from his Advent Deck. In return he asked only to be shown where the Kamen Riders slept.

The Riders were asleep when he reached them. He vented them where they lay, took their decks, then sent the whole people of Ventara to Karsh. Only Len escaped him, to Earth. A second Rider, Kase, had survived too, though Xaviax did not know it.

He left the traitor alive. He shut him up with Sarah, the woman he loved, in a false Ventara of Xaviax's own making, where the pair of them lived quietly.

The plan for Earth

Earth was next. Xaviax meant to take every human being on it. His monsters began by seizing people one at a time through mirrors, to build up a record of human blood that his machines could use. The missing were put down as ordinary disappearances. One of them, Frank Taylor, was found a year later in a hospital bed, alive but drained, in a sleep that nobody could break.

Len stood in his way, so Xaviax set out to have Len vented. The decks he had stolen would open only for the owners they were made for, or for those owners' mirror twins on Earth. He found the twins. To each he showed a different face.

He came to Richie Preston as a lawyer named Walter Connors, offering a fortune for every Rider vented. He came to Grant Staley as an officer hiring soldiers. Brad Barrett he blackmailed with a scandal of his own making. To Chris Ramirez he was a federal agent, recruiting for the defence of Earth. To the Cho brothers he was a crime boss. He promised Drew Lansing a share in ruling the world, once it was won. He got James Trademore out of the hands of the FBI. He sent Kit Taylor visions of a missing father.

Why nobody knew

All of it was done in secret. The Earth of 2008 was not short of heroes, but none of them ever learnt of Xaviax. His monsters took people singly, through reflections, leaving nothing behind. His Riders fought on the far side of the glass. The only people who spoke of monsters in mirrors were the kind that nobody believed, such as the readers of the website where Maya Young posted her reports.

It helped him that the world was looking elsewhere. That same year the Skrulls' great invasion was beaten in New York, in full view of everybody.

Wrath

In the autumn of 2009 Xaviax took the field himself. Vic Frasier, a building worker, had been hurt in an accident that Xaviax arranged, then drained as Frank Taylor had been. He was the mirror twin of Nolan, the Rider called Wrath. Xaviax entered his body, which let him wear Wrath's armour.

As Wrath he fought beside Strike through October. On 7 November he vented Kit Taylor. Wrath was vented in the same fight, with Vic Frasier inside the armour, but Xaviax slipped out of the body first. He kept the Dragon Knight's deck.

The transmitters

He took the deck to the false Ventara. Threatening Sarah, he made her lover put on the Dragon Knight's armour again as his spy. Meanwhile his servants were planting teleport beacons across the Earth, with a handful of great transmitters to drive them. At full power they would lift the whole human race to Karsh at once.

By then Len had woken Eubulon. The Advent Master made a virus to kill the transmitters, which his Riders carried to them one by one. Xaviax let them think that it was working. He shut a machine down for show, studied the virus, then set about making a cure for it. Once he put on Eubulon's own face, to bully his spy back into line.

The last transmitter stood in Australia. There, on 18 December, the spy's nerve failed, and he told Len the truth.

The end

The same day Maya Young and Trent Moseley crept into Xaviax's stronghold to open a way through a mirror. Through it came the Kamen Riders. Eubulon fought his old master in the control room while the rest cut their way to him through wave after wave of monsters. Then all thirteen used the Link Vent together. It destroyed Xaviax entirely.

The people of Ventara went home. Frank Taylor woke. The men whom Xaviax had tricked into armour came back out of the Advent Void, remembering nothing of him.

pages.title: Xi of Safehaven
infobox: Robot; once a sentinel of Eternity Point, on Safehaven
The Omega Rangers, as guide and pilot
pages.html:
Xi of Safehaven is the robot that guided the Omega Rangers and flew their ships. It was one of the old sentinels of Eternity Point, the armoury under Safehaven, until the Blue Emissary put it to new work in the autumn of 1994. It got the three Omega Rangers of Earth home to the Command Center when their secret came out, and it was wrecked by Lord Drakkon a month later.

The Emissary's robot

Xi was one of the robot sentinels of Eternity Point, the old armoury under Safehaven. When the Blue Emissary set about gathering a new team of Omega Rangers in the autumn of 1994, Xi was given to them as a guide. It flew the team's ship, the Spectrum, and called them to their work.

The night the secret came out

Early in December 1994 Kiya turned on the team. She killed the Blue Emissary and struck Jason down before he could morph. Xi came out of the fight badly damaged, with one hand gone. All the same it got the three to their ship, then to the one place where Jason could be treated, the Command Center on Earth. They arrived with their faces bare, which is how their friends learnt the truth.

Drakkon

In January 1995 the Omega Rangers carried Lord Drakkon off as their guide in the Spectrum II, the Spectrum having been destroyed in the Telvax Nebula. When he betrayed them he wrecked Xi, putting out its eye, then flew off in the ship. He said afterwards that he had left the wreck where Safehaven would find it, so that the three could be saved.

After the Eltarian War Trini rebuilt Xi. The new Xi had none of the old one's memories. It could have had them back, but it chose not to. In February 1995 Alpha 1, the robot that Edenoi had once built for Zordon, took Xi over in the service of Mistress Vile. What became of Xi after Dark Specter destroyed Alpha 1 is not recorded.

pages.title: Xiliens
aliases: the Supreme Controller of Planet X
infobox: Human, in grey uniforms with dark visors
King Ghidorah, Gigan, Megalon, Kumonga, Kamacuras
pages.html:
The Xiliens are the people of Planet X, a dark world hidden behind Jupiter. They look much like human beings, do nothing without asking their computers, and have been trying to take the Earth since 1965. Godzilla has stopped them every time. In the spring of 1994 he burnt the last of their expedition to Japan, their Supreme Controller with it.

Planet X

Planet X was found in 1965 by the World Space Authority. Its ship P-1 landed there with two astronauts, Kazuo Fuji of Japan, with an American called Glenn. It is a dry, sunless rock, so its people live underground.

They wear grey, with dark visors over their eyes. Their ruler is called the Controller. Their women all have the same face. Gold is as common on Planet X as gravel; water is what they lack.

Nothing is known on Earth of their history.

The loan of two monsters, 1965

The Controller told the astronauts that a monster was laying waste his world. He called it Monster Zero; the Earth knew it as King Ghidorah. He asked for the loan of Godzilla, with Rodan, to drive it off, offering a cure for cancer as payment. The Earth agreed. Xilien saucers lifted Godzilla out of a lake, then Rodan out of a mountainside, having known all along where each was sleeping.

The cure turned out to be a tape of the Controller's voice, demanding the Earth's surrender. The Xiliens had controlled King Ghidorah from the start. Now they controlled all three monsters, which they turned loose on Japan.

Japan asked for help, as it had in January, when King Ghidorah first came. On 19 December the Justice League came back, with the Avengers, to keep the three monsters out of Tokyo. They managed it for one night. The Martian Manhunter, who reads minds, could find nothing in Godzilla's but the Xiliens' machines. In January he had found a great deal of temper there, so the League knew that the monsters were not their own masters.

They were undone by a toy. An inventor called Tetsuo Torii had made a pocket alarm for women, the Lady Guard, which gave out a piercing shriek. A Xilien agent, Namikawa, bought it up to bury it, because that particular sound was agony to her people. She had also fallen in love with the astronaut Glenn. Her own side killed her for it. The note she left him gave the secret away.

The shriek was put out over every wireless in Japan. The Xiliens' control failed, then their saucers blew themselves up. Godzilla, with Rodan, threw King Ghidorah back into space.

It was the same month in which the sky caught fire over Manhattan, when Galactus came. The Earth was very nearly lost twice before Christmas.

Rita Repulsa, 1994

The Xiliens went on trying. By the spring of 1994 a new expedition under a Supreme Controller had a saucer over the coast of Japan.
