It had monsters to call on: Megalon first, then Gigan, Kumonga, Kamacuras. Godzilla killed Megalon. Then Rita Repulsa arrived. She boarded the saucer, overpowered its crew, then offered the Supreme Controller an alliance. He found her hard to refuse.

It did the Xiliens no good. Rita took over their ship. Against the Supreme Controller's advice she had King Ghidorah called down, which nobody could control; it turned on the saucer. One of the guards grew so sick of the war that he let her prisoner, Tommy Oliver, go free.

Godzilla burnt the saucer out of the sky. Afterwards he found the Supreme Controller in the wreckage, already planning his return. He burnt him with the rest.

pages.title: Y'ha-nthlei
infobox: The Shadow over Innsmouth (Visionary Publishing Company, April 1936)
A city of the Deep Ones
The sea floor beyond Devil Reef, off Innsmouth, Massachusetts
Huge stone, many-columned, hung with gold
February 1928, by a submarine's torpedoes; spring 1963, by Delta Green's bombs
Pth'thya-l'yi, the second wife of Obed Marsh
pages.html:
Y'ha-nthlei is a city of the Deep Ones on the sea floor just beyond Devil Reef, a mile and a half off the harbour of Innsmouth, Massachusetts. It is built of huge stone, many-columned, and hung with gold. A submarine's torpedoes damaged it in February 1928. Delta Green bombed what was left of it in 1963.

The city

Y'ha-nthlei lies in the black water beyond the reef. It has stood there for a very long time. Pth'thya-l'yi, the Deep One whom Captain Obed Marsh took as his second wife, lives there. So do many of the people of Innsmouth who went down into the sea, one generation after another, when the change in them was complete.

1928

In February 1928, during the federal raid on Innsmouth, a submarine of the Navy fired torpedoes down into the deep water beyond the reef. They damaged the city, but they did not destroy it.

Robert Olmstead

Robert Olmstead, the young man whose report had brought on the raid, was descended from Obed Marsh through Pth'thya-l'yi, although he did not know it in 1927. By 1930 he had begun to change. He dreamt of Y'ha-nthlei and of his great-great-grandmother, who told him that he would dwell there in glory for ever. He resolved to free his cousin Lawrence from the sanatorium at Canton and go down to the city with him.

1963

In April 1963 the submarine Thresher was lost off New England, and Delta Green linked the loss to Innsmouth. That spring, in Operation RIPTIDE, it bombed the remains of the city under Devil Reef. What is left of Y'ha-nthlei in 1994, nobody on land can say for certain.

pages.title: Yig
infobox: H. P. Lovecraft and Zealia Bishop
The Father of Serpents; Father Yig
A great serpent, or a man with a serpent's scales
Old peoples of the American plains; the serpent people, by some accounts
Avenging the killing of his children
The Old Serpent, who is the Devil
pages.html:
Yig is the Father of Serpents, one of the Great Old Ones. He is less hostile to men than most of his kind, so long as they leave his children alone. Those who harm a snake in his country may find that Yig harms them, or worse, that he gives them children of his own.

The Father of Serpents

Yig is a great serpent, or a man with a serpent's scales, and he is the father of every snake. On the southern plains of America the old peoples knew him, and knew better than to cross him. In autumn, when the snakes are hungry, his wrath is near. The old peoples beat drums through the autumn nights to keep him off.

The curse of Yig

In 1889 a settler called Walker Davis brought his wife, Audrey, to Oklahoma to take up land. On the way she killed a nest of young rattlesnakes. Her husband, who feared snakes more than anything, was horrified. Through the autumn he worked the rites the old peoples used to keep Yig away.

One night, frightened half out of her wits, Audrey took the shape at her bedside for Yig, and killed it. It was her husband. She was taken to the asylum at Guthrie, where she bore children who were not wholly human. She died there. One of them lived on in a locked room of the asylum for many years, and its doctor showed it to a visitor in 1925.

The serpent people

The serpent people of Valusia served the Old Serpent in the Thurian Age, and practised his sorcery. Some books say they had honoured Yig before that, as the father of their kind, and that a few of them later turned to Tsathoggua. Their priests said the two were one. They were wrong. Yig is not the Old Serpent, whom Scripture calls the Devil. He is a different thing, and he serves nobody.

Delta Green knows the serpent people as one of the more insidious of its enemies, for they can still wear the faces of men. Of Yig it knows only what the books say.

pages.title: Yog-Sothoth
infobox: The All-in-One and One-in-All; the gate and the key
Outside the world, touching every part of it
A heap of shifting, iridescent globes
Joseph Curwen of Providence; the Whateleys of Dunwich; Abdul Alhazred
The Whateley twins, born at Dunwich on 2 February 1913
pages.html:
Yog-Sothoth is one of the Outer Gods, the All-in-One, the gate and the key. It touches every moment and every place, yet it is locked outside the world, pressing on it from every side at once. Sorcerers who want to go where men cannot, or to bring in what should stay out, call on it. Some of them it answers.

The gate and the key

The Necronomicon says that Yog-Sothoth knows the gate, for it is the gate. It is the key and the guardian of the gate as well. Past, present and future are all one in it. Through it, the books say, the Great Old Ones came into the world, and through it they will return.

It shows itself, when it shows itself at all, as a great heap of iridescent globes, always shifting, always coming together and breaking apart. Those who have seen it describe it badly, and seldom more than once.

Abdul Alhazred worshipped it. So have most of the sorcerers since who wanted more than this world could give them.

Joseph Curwen

Joseph Curwen of Providence, a merchant who had come from Salem, called on Yog-Sothoth through most of the eighteenth century, and did not seem to age while he did it. In April 1771 a party of Providence men, the leading citizens of the town among them, raided his farm at Pawtuxet and killed him. They burnt his papers, struck his name from the town's records and never spoke of it again.

His descendant Charles Dexter Ward found his grave and raised him from his salts. Curwen killed Ward and took his place, until in 1928 Dr Marinus Bicknell Willett put him back into dust.

Dunwich

Dunwich is a decaying village in the hills of north central Massachusetts. On May Eve 1912 an old man there called Whateley worked a rite on Sentinel Hill with his daughter Lavinia. At five in the morning of Sunday, 2 February 1913, she bore twins.

It was Candlemas, the feast of the Presentation of Christ in the Temple. One of the children, Wilbur, looked nearly human, and grew at a terrible speed. The other looked more like its father, and was kept out of sight in the farmhouse. The Whateleys meant the twins to open the way for the Great Old Ones, who would clear the earth of men.

Wilbur needed a complete Necronomicon for the work. On the night of 3 August 1928 he broke into the library of Miskatonic University to steal its copy, and the watchdog killed him. What lay on the library floor afterwards was not human below the waist.

His brother broke loose from the farmhouse on 9 September. It went through the hills unseen, crushing houses with the families in them. Three men of Miskatonic went up Sentinel Hill after it: the librarian Dr Henry Armitage, Professor Warren Rice and Dr Francis Morgan. With a powder that made it visible for a moment and a formula from the Necronomicon itself, they destroyed it. At the end it cried out in English for its father.

Delta Green

To Delta Green Yog-Sothoth is a name in the books and in the mouths of sorcerers. Those who call on it want knowledge, of the past, of the future or of what lies outside. They usually get it, which is the trouble.

pages.title: Yoko Belnades
infobox: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (Game Boy Advance, May 2003)
The Belnades, the line of Sypha Belnades
Witch in the service of the Church
Genya Arikado, Julius Belmont, Soma Cruz
pages.html:
Yoko Belnades was a witch of the Belnades family, the line of Sypha Belnades, who served the Church in the twenty-first century. In 2035 the Church sent her into Dracula's sealed castle after the missionary Graham Jones, who very nearly killed her. In 2036 she worked with Julius Belmont against the cult of Celia Fortner.

The Belnades

Yoko was born in about 2011 into the family of Sypha Belnades, the sorceress who fought Dracula beside Trevor Belmont in 1476. The Belnades went on producing witches for centuries after her. Carrie Fernandez, who fought in 1852, was one of them.

Sypha had been a sorceress of the Church, and so was Yoko, more than five hundred years after her. The Belnades were in the Church's service long before the wizarding world went into hiding in 1692. Yoko took her orders from Rome. Nothing connects her with any Ministry of Magic.

The sealed castle

In 2035 the Church sent Yoko to Japan. She was twenty-four. A missionary named Graham Jones, who believed himself Dracula reborn, was on his way to the Hakuba shrine for the eclipse of that year, through which Dracula's sealed castle could be reached. Yoko was to stop him.

Inside the castle she met Soma Cruz, a student who had been drawn in by accident, as it then seemed. He had found that he could take the souls of monsters, and he was afraid of what that made him. Yoko told him that a dark power did not make its owner evil. She also warned him against Graham.

She found Graham herself soon afterwards, and told him to his face that he was a fraud. He stabbed her. Soma drove him off. Genya Arikado, whom she had worked with before, kept her alive, though she took no further part in what followed. Soma destroyed Graham, then the chaos at the heart of the castle.

The cult of 2036

A year later Yoko was at the gate of another castle, a copy of Dracula's in snowbound mountains. It was the stronghold of the cult called With Light. Julius Belmont was with her, for by then he was working with the Church. They told Soma to go home. He would not.

Julius went in alone. Yoko set herself up in the village outside the walls. From there she taught Soma the magic seals without which the great monsters of that castle could not be finished off. She also forged him weapons out of the souls he had taken.

Hammer, the former soldier who kept shop beside her, was plainly in love with her. Yoko took no notice. She was there with the others when Soma came out of the falling castle, having refused Dracula's inheritance a second time.

pages.title: Lord Yu
infobox: The Jade Emperor, Lord Yu-huang Shang Ti
Yu the Great, founder of China's first dynasty
The far side of Goa'uld space from Earth
A Replicator in the likeness of Samantha Carter
pages.html:
Lord Yu is the oldest of the Goa'uld System Lords, and the most sensible. He calls himself the Jade Emperor. In China, long ago, he ruled as Yu the Great, the founder of its first dynasty. His worlds lie on the far side of Goa'uld space from Earth, which has always made him readier than most to deal with it. He took part in the talks that brought Earth under the Protected Planets Treaty in 1999, fought Anubis from 2002 and was killed by a Replicator in 2005.

The Jade Emperor

Yu's full title is the Jade Emperor, the exalted Lord Yu-huang Shang Ti. Unlike most Goa'uld he did not set himself up on Earth as a god. In China he ruled as a man, an emperor, and he is remembered there as Yu the Great, who founded the first of its dynasties more than four thousand years ago.

That was long after Ra's ban. Yu came quietly, in defiance of it, and he kept to the far east of the world, as far from the North as a Goa'uld could get.

He is very old. He sat on the council that banished Anubis long ago. He took no part in the war of the 990s, when Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard.

Rule

Most of the other System Lords lie between Yu's domain and Earth. He is a practical ruler, more interested in keeping what he has than in conquering more. He believes in his own divinity, but he rarely troubles to insist on it.

He makes war on his neighbours as readily as any System Lord. In 2002 Olokun was still smarting from a defeat at his hands.

Earth found him, alone among the System Lords, a Goa'uld who kept his word. Twice he agreed to help Earth against another System Lord, and the only time he let Earth down was when his mind had begun to fail.

The treaty with Earth

In 1999 the System Lords meant to destroy Earth for killing Hathor. Thor offered Earth a place under the Protected Planets Treaty instead. Three System Lords came through the Stargate to settle the terms: Yu, Cronus and Nirrti.

Thor himself presided. The System Lords had once asked that he should not be present at the signing of the treaty. This time he was in the room, and none of the three looked at him more than they could help.

Yu favoured the treaty from the start, since Earth's survival would trouble his enemies a great deal more than it troubled him. The Goa'uld demanded Earth's Stargates as their price. Then Nirrti, invisible, struck down Cronus, and the blame fell on Teal'c. When she was found out, Yu flew at her in a rage, because she had put their peace with Asgard at risk.

Afterwards Yu and Cronus let Earth into the treaty without giving up its gates. Cronus warned that any of Earth's people caught on Goa'uld worlds would still be fair game.

The summit

By 2002 Apophis and Cronus were dead. The rest had worn themselves out fighting over what they left. They met in council on a space station to make peace. Yu believed that the slave who attended him there was his own lo'taur, Jarren. In fact it was Daniel Jackson, sent by the Tok'ra with a poison meant to kill every System Lord in the place, together with a drug that made Yu take him for Jarren.

Jackson never used the poison. Osiris arrived as the envoy of Anubis, and killing the System Lords would only have handed the galaxy to him. Yu was the only one of the seven System Lords there who voted against taking Anubis back. He alone was left of the council that had banished him.

Jackson also saw each of the System Lords eat a live symbiote from a tank, which horrified him more than anything else he saw there.

Yu came close to dying at the end of it. He caught Jackson trying to carry Osiris off in his cargo ship, and Osiris, thinking it Yu's doing, stabbed him with her dagger. Yu survived, and went to war with Anubis.

Teal'c and Ba'al

Later in 2002 K'tano, the leader of a band of rebel Jaffa, sent Teal'c to attack Yu, as a weak System Lord whose Jaffa were ripe for the taking. Teal'c was captured. Yu let him go, for reasons he kept to himself, and sent him back knowing enough to doubt K'tano. K'tano turned out to be Imhotep, a minor Goa'uld in disguise.

That year Earth asked for his help. Ba'al was holding Jack O'Neill at a fortress where he had been studying gravity in secret, and Yu had every reason to want it destroyed. Earth sent him its plans, asking only that he strike at its power first. He did, and O'Neill escaped.

The war against Anubis

Yu spent the next year rallying the System Lords against Anubis, and by 2003 he had persuaded them to act together. Their fleet met Anubis above Abydos, where Anubis had come for the Eye of Ra. Once he had it, he turned his new weapon on the fleet and destroyed most of it. Yu got away with the few ships that were left.

By then the sarcophagus had stopped working on Yu as it should. He spent most of his time in it. He could no longer take a new host, and his mind was going.

Later in 2003, just when his fleet was needed to destroy Anubis's ship, he sent it away to the far side of the galaxy. Teal'c, who argued, was put in a cell. Yu's First Prime, Oshu, began to doubt that his master was a god at all. He took command of Yu's armies to keep the domain from falling apart, leaving Yu on the throne. At Teal'c's urging he put the fleet under Ba'al, on condition that Ba'al used it to destroy Anubis.

Last years

In 2004, with Anubis beaten, Ba'al took Anubis's Kull warriors for himself. Yu went to Earth with his First Prime to ask for help against him. Camulus and Amaterasu went with them. The talks came to nothing, and while they were going on Ba'al destroyed the ship that had brought them.

Yu and Amaterasu fought on against Ba'al while the other System Lords fell, fled or surrendered. In 2005 Ba'al's envoy, Selkhet, met the last three System Lords of the High Council at the Hasara space station to offer them terms. A prisoner was brought in who looked like Samantha Carter. She was a Replicator. Her arm became a blade, and she ran it through Yu, who died at once.

He had outlived Ra, Apophis and Cronus. In the end it was a machine that killed him.

pages.title: Yuggoth
infobox: A world at the edge of the solar system
18 February 1930, at the Lowell Observatory, Flagstaff, Arizona
Windowless black towers; rivers of pitch; the making of the Shining Trapezohedron
pages.html:
Yuggoth is a world at the edge of the solar system, where the Mi-go keep an outpost. Astronomers found it in 1930 and named it Pluto, without the least idea of who uses it. It is a dark, cold place of great towers and black rivers of pitch.

The world

Yuggoth is too far from the Sun to be warmed by it. Its towers are windowless and black. Its rivers run with pitch under bridges built by a people older than the Mi-go, and the Mi-go use it as a way station on their journeys between the stars.

They are said to have carried the brains of men there, alive in metal cylinders, to see what they could see. The Shining Trapezohedron, the stone through which the Haunter of the Dark is called, was made there, the books say.

Pluto

On 18 February 1930 a young astronomer at the Lowell Observatory at Flagstaff, Arizona, Clyde Tombaugh, found a new planet on his photographic plates. It was announced on 13 March, and named Pluto. Albert Wilmarth of Miskatonic University, who had corresponded with a Vermont recluse about the Mi-go, was sure at once that it was Yuggoth.

Its visitors

The Mi-go come to the Earth from Yuggoth to mine in lonely hills, in Vermont above all. John Constantine knows at least one of them well enough to share a joke. In Delta Green's account the Greys, whom Majestic 12 deals with, are the Mi-go's creatures.

pages.title: Zack Taylor
infobox: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 'Day of the Dumpster' (28 August 1993)
The Mastodon Dinozord; the Lion Thunderzord, from the autumn of 1994
The Power Axe, which turns into a cannon; the Omega Kamas, as an Omega Ranger
Hip Hop Kido, his own invention
The Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, 1993 to 1994; the Omega Rangers, from 1994
Adam Park, as the Black Ranger
A member of Congress; guardian of Minh, Trini Kwan's daughter
The Black Omega Ranger, from 1994; the Black Ranger again, 2022 to 2023
pages.html:
Zack Taylor is the Black Ranger of the Power Rangers, whose Power Coin draws on the Mastodon. He is the joker of the team, a dancer as much as a fighter, who invented a fighting style of his own called Hip Hop Kido. Jason Lee Scott is his best friend. Before Rita Repulsa chose Tommy Oliver, she tried to make Zack her Green Ranger, and he turned her down. In November 1994 he told everybody that he was leaving for a peace conference in Geneva. In truth he went into space with Jason and Trini Kwan as the Black Omega Ranger. He stayed an Omega Ranger long after Jason had gone home. In later years he sat in Congress, then gave it up to bring up Trini's daughter, Minh. In 2023 he and Minh destroyed Robo-Rita.

Angel Grove

Zack was born about 1977 and grew up in Angel Grove, California, where he is a pupil at Angel Grove High School. He is quick, clever, energetic and very sure of himself. He loves a good joke. He is forever chasing a girl in his class called Angela.

Zack fights as he dances. He made up a style of his own, Hip Hop Kido, out of dance and the martial arts: fluid moves like a dancer's, finished off with fast, hard blows. He teaches it to a class in Angel Grove. He spars with Jason, and later with Tommy Oliver.

He has a horror of spiders, snakes and insects. The snakes worry him less than they did. He once frightened off Bulk and Skull with fake ones.

He met Jason in about 1988, on the day Ernie opened the Youth Center.

The Black Ranger

In 1993 Zordon chose Zack with four of his friends to fight Rita Repulsa. He became the Black Ranger. His Power Coin calls up the Mastodon Dinozord, and his weapon is the Power Axe, which turns into a cannon. In a fight he sometimes copies Billy Cranston's moves, so that the two of them strike at the same moment.

On 30 July 1993 the Rangers came to public notice for the first time, when they fought a giant starfish at the Bull Ring in Birmingham.

Rita's offer

A month before Tommy Oliver came to Angel Grove, Zack carried the team through a hard fight with one of Rita's giants in Italy. Rita noticed. Goldar and his Putty Patrollers seized him. They carried him off to her palace on the Moon, where she was all sympathy. It ought to be Zack leading the Rangers, she said, not Jason, and Zordon had not been entirely honest with him. Then she offered him the Dragon Coin, and the powers of the Green Ranger with it.

Zack saw through her and escaped to the Command Center. There he told Zordon and Alpha 5 the truth: he had felt the pull of it. They asked him to keep it from the others while they worked out what to do. Rita gave the coin to Tommy instead. For a long time afterwards Zack found it hard to trust the Green Ranger.

The Green Ranger

Late in 1993 Tommy joined the team, once Jason had broken Rita's spell on him.

Weeks later the Black Dragon, a war machine steered from another world by Lord Drakkon, Tommy's other self, took the powers of every Ranger but Tommy. Tommy shared out his own green power among the rest, so that for a while Zack fought as a Green Ranger. When Tommy and Billy Cranston were thrown into Drakkon's world, Zack crossed over with the others to bring them home.

Tommy and Zack became friends in time. Zack gave him advice about Kimberly Hart. Once, when a monster's acid had burnt Zack, Tommy lent him the Dragon Shield, whose power healed him.

In the spring of 1994 the team followed Tommy to Japan, where the Megazord fought Godzilla, then fought beside him. Zack complained that there was no way of telling a monster that size that they were on his side.

The lie about Geneva

In the autumn of 1994 Lord Zedd came to the Moon in Rita's place. His monsters outclassed Finster's, so Zordon and Alpha 5 made the Rangers' Zords over into the Thunderzords. Zack's became the Lion Thunderzord.

That October Zack and Trini Kwan walked into the Command Center to find Jason with a stranger, the Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters. They drew their blasters. Jason promised to explain. The Emissary gave them back their memories of a war that the world had forgotten, then warned them what joining would cost. They told Jason that he was not alone.

In November 1994 Zack, Jason and Trini were chosen as delegates to a peace conference in Geneva. The conference was real, but the three of them never meant to go. Zack told the story to Zordon, to his friends, to his parents and to everybody else in Angel Grove. Before they left, the Rangers fetched the Sword of Light from a far planet. With it the powers of the three passed to three friends from Stone Canyon. Zack's went to Adam Park, the new Black Ranger, who believed every word.

Geneva was a cover. The three of them went out into space, to a world called Safehaven, where they took up the Omega powers, handed down from some of the earliest Rangers in the universe. Zack became the Black Omega Ranger, whose power is air, with the Omega Kamas. As the Omega Rangers they fought a long way from Earth, where hardly anybody knew of it.

The Black Omega Ranger

Early in December 1994 the secret came out, when Kiya Kyatyl, the fourth of their team, turned on them and struck Jason down. The three arrived at the Command Center with their faces bare. Their old friends gave them a far from warm welcome. Zordon forgave them at once. Zack and Trini told him what had happened without telling him everything. He let it go at that.

While Jason healed, Zack and Trini took the three from Stone Canyon out into space after one of the Empowered. Cavotus, a prisoner whom Kiya had let loose, destroyed their ship and nearly killed Adam. Then both teams beat Kiya's following, the Anointed, at Safehaven.

In January 1995 refugees came to Safehaven from Hartunia, a world that one of the Empyreals had burnt. Arkon, the elder of Safehaven, demanded Hartunian blood. Zack let himself be cut to settle it. About that time he found a baby in an escape pod, of a people nobody knew. She was named Journey. She grew from an infant into an old woman in a matter of weeks, with Zack and Trini bringing her up between them. Late that month she fought beside them against the Death Ranger, who wore Zack's body in its turn. When it was over she died of old age, calling the two of them her mother and father.

The Death Ranger cost Jason his link to the Power. Trini took the Red Omega powers, Kevor Vrin the Yellow, while Zack stayed the Black. In February 1995 he stood with the Rangers of Earth when the Grid was cleansed. In November 1995 he and Trini came back to Earth for a few days to help Kimberly Hart in France. To everybody in Angel Grove they were still at the peace conference. In later years Zack gave up the Omega powers and came home.

Congress and Minh

In later years Zack went into politics and was elected to Congress.

In 2022 Billy Cranston tried to bring Zordon back. What came back instead was the evil that Zordon's light had driven out of Rita Repulsa, in a body of its own, Robo-Rita. Zack fought her with the rest of the old team, in the battle in which Trini was killed.

Afterwards he gave up his seat in Congress to adopt Trini's teenage daughter, Minh. He became her only guardian, and she came to look on him as something like a father. Minh blamed Billy for her mother's death.

Robo-Rita

A year later Robo-Rita took Jason, Tommy and Kimberly prisoner. With Billy, Katherine Hillard and Rocky DeSantos, Zack went after her. Minh wanted revenge. Zack told her, as Zordon would have, that a Ranger's power is for defending life, not for revenge.

Minh became the Yellow Ranger in the end, with her mother's coin. At the Moon Palace she pinned Robo-Rita down with her daggers, and Zack finished her with the cannon of his Power Axe. He said Trini's name as he struck.

Afterwards Zack, Billy and Minh sat together at the juice bar in Angel Grove. The two men told her stories of the old days.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' news showed helicopter film of the fight in Birmingham the afternoon before. Five people in coloured suits and helmets ran in a line across a rooftop towards the creature. The one in black was Zack. Dudley, with a sausage halfway to his mouth, watched them leap off the roof as though he would like to be one of them.

Book Three, Chapter Four: Harry told Lucius Malfoy about the team in California, who fought monsters to save people. 'And they've got no magic, Mr Malfoy. Not a drop.'

Book Four, Chapter Three: by August 1994 the Rangers were on the Dursleys' news nearly every morning, and there were six of them now. Zack was still the Black Ranger, though Dudley's favourite was the newest, the green one.

pages.title: Zartus
infobox: Silver Guardian; later Supreme Guardian of Eltar
Sentry Force Four: Zag, Zeta, Zenith and Zero-Zero
Zelya, who lived in Angel Grove as Candice Clark
January 1995, on the Moon, by Zordon
pages.html:
Zartus was the Silver Guardian of Eltar, who served beside Zordon under Zophram and rose to be Supreme Guardian after them both. It was Zartus who had the Zeo Crystal cursed. He made Lord Zedd out of what the curse left of Zophram, then raised the Empyreals to scour the worlds he thought unfit. In January 1995 he invaded Earth. Zordon killed him on the Moon with a piece of the Crystal that he had cursed.

The Silver Guardian

Zartus was a mortal Eltarian, though Eltarians live a very long time. He was one of the Guardians who keep Eltar under its Elders, as others of his family had been before him. He was the Silver Guardian, second to Zophram, the Gold. Zophram taught him. Zophram also taught the Bronze Guardian, a young spearman called Zordon, whom he had asked for himself.

Zartus never knew that Zordon was a Maia, one of the Istari. He took him for a soldier like any other. Once, on the planet Bivix, the two of them went about among the people in disguise, talking of why they had joined. Zordon said that he did not mean to be a Guardian for ever. What he wanted, he said, was to go home to Eltar when his service was done, to a farm, with a wife and children.

When the Guardians drove off an attack on the planet Artavias, the Elders made Zophram the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar. Zophram meant Zordon, not Zartus, to succeed him.

The Fire of Truth

On the moon of a young world the Guardians found the Zeo Crystal, in a palace kept by the Bandorian monks. The young world was Earth. In secret, Zartus had one of the monks lay a spell on the Crystal, the Fire of Truth, so that whoever touched it would die, or worse. He did not warn Zophram.

When Zophram went to take the Crystal, to end the war with Dark Specter at a stroke, the Fire of Truth flayed the skin from his body. It killed almost everything else on that moon. Zartus killed the few soldiers who were left. Then he carried Zophram off to his ship, where he kept him alive with tubes and a mask.

He told Zophram that he had been born again, stronger than before. He told him that Eltar believed him dead as a hero. He told him, too, that the Elders had called Zordon home to be Supreme Guardian in his place. Zophram came to believe that Zordon had betrayed him. He became Lord Zedd, sworn to the destruction of Eltar, which pleased Zartus very much.

Supreme Guardian

Zordon became Supreme Guardian after Zophram. Some ten thousand years ago Rita Repulsa's curse shut Zordon in a tube on Earth, outside time. The office passed to Zartus, who held it for the rest of his life.

Over those ages he came to believe that order could be brought to the universe only through war. Peoples he judged unfit were to be cleared away. For that he had the Empyreals, three vast beings that burnt whole worlds clean of life. He commanded them through a crystal. They destroyed Gorvinos III. They destroyed Hartunia, whose soldiers had once fought for Dark Specter. Through them he had a hold on Lord Drakkon as well, who served him to get his powers back.

Earth

Zartus kept a watch on Zordon. A Guardian called Zelya lived in Angel Grove as a girl named Candice Clark, who was going out with Skull, a boy at Angel Grove High School. She had been sent to watch Zordon, with a view to bringing Earth into Eltar's alliance. During Lord Zedd's dome, in December 1994, she showed herself for what she was. Zedd carried her off to the Moon. There he told her that he had once been Zophram, with the truth about the Empyreals for good measure. She took it to Zordon.

In the middle of January 1995 Zartus came to the Command Center himself, with soldiers. With him came his own elite, Sentry Force Four. Zag could step through doors that he made in the air. Zeta was a swordsman who seldom spoke. Zenith flew in a suit of her own, having not troubled to walk for years. Zero-Zero fought in an armoured suit that she had built herself.

He offered Zordon an alliance against Lord Zedd, then asked for the Power Coins. Zelya exposed him. He asked Zordon to come home to the council of Eltar at his side. Zordon chose Earth. Zartus smashed the tube that held him, believing that he had killed him. He had Zelya taken to his ship. Then he claimed the Earth for Eltar, 'in the name of peace and justice'.

The Moon

The war that followed lasted a matter of days. His Empyreals destroyed the Command Center, the headquarters of Promethea and Lord Zedd's palace on the Moon. Then Grace Sterling of Promethea shattered the crystal through which he commanded them. They were his no longer.

Zartus went to the Moon, to the caves under the ruined palace, for the power of the Zeo Crystal. Zordon was there before him, in a body of metal, fighting Lord Zedd. Zordon had laid down his weapon. Zedd had understood at last who had cursed the Crystal. The two of them turned on Zartus together.

He was about to kill Zedd when Zordon drove a piece of the Zeo Crystal into his chest. Zartus died there, more than ten thousand years after he had it cursed.

Afterwards

Sentry Force Four had been beaten one by one. Adam Park took Zag, with Baboo's help. Rocky DeSantos took Zeta, with Zelya's. Goldar took Zenith alone. Billy Cranston took Zero-Zero, with Squatt's. They surrendered, whereupon Eltar called its armies home. Zordon would not go back to be Supreme Guardian. He put Zelya's name forward instead. She said goodbye to Skull, told him the truth about herself and went home to Eltar.

In February 1995 the world was mended a second time. Lord Zedd kept no memory of the weeks before it. He never again knew what Zartus had done to him.

pages.title: Zaruba
infobox: Madou Ring: a Horror bound into a ring
Taiga Saejima; Kouga Saejima; Raiga Saejima
One day of the wearer's life at each new moon
2006, by the Western Watchdog, without its memories
On the hand of the boy Kouga Saejima
pages.html:
Zaruba is the Madou Ring of the Golden Knight: a ring with a skull's face, worn on the middle finger of the left hand, that talks. It is a Horror, bound into the metal by the priest Amon to serve the knights. It senses other Horrors, remembers the old lore, and says what it thinks of its wearer's decisions. In the summer of 1994 it belongs to Kouga Saejima, who is fourteen.

The contract

A Madou Ring does not serve for nothing. At each new moon Zaruba takes one day of its wearer's life. For that day the knight lies as if dead.

Its name means 'friend' in the old tongue of the Makai.

Taiga and Kouga

Zaruba was Taiga Saejima's ring first. When Barago cut Taiga down in about 1990, the dying knight gave the ring his last words for his son. It has been Kouga's ever since.

In 2005 Kouga gave the painter Kaoru Mitsuki a small ring to wear. It answered to Zaruba, so that he could always find her.

The first Zaruba

In March 2006 the empty armour of Kiba rose against Kouga. Zaruba spent everything it had to call the spirits of the dead Golden Knights to his side. The ring crumbled to dust on his finger.

The Western Watchdog remade it. The new ring had red eyes where the old one's were black, with no memory of anything that had gone before. Kouga gave it the old name.

Later years

In 2010 the priestess Rekka gave Kouga a young Makai dragon. Zaruba named it Kaoru, to annoy him. In January 2012 the ring sickened from stale water, so the priestess Jabi carried it to the Life-Circulating Waterfall to be cured. Sigma Fudou tried to steal it on the way, since he needed it to open the true Makai.

When Kouga went into the Promised Ground in 2012, Zaruba arrived there centuries before him by a slip of time. It forgot him. It became the guardian of the Temple of Wisdom, a giant that Kouga had to fight before it knew him again.

Kouga carried it into the rift in time in about 2020. Years later he sent it back to his son, Raiga, to help him claim the armour. It was on Raiga's hand in 2040.

In another world

Ryuga Dougai, the Golden Knight of another world, had a Zaruba too. That ring would not speak to him at all until 2013, when it judged him ready.

pages.title: Zatanna Zatara
infobox: Half-blood: her father a pure-blood wizard, her mother a No-Maj
The Justice League (from 1978; the Detroit League, 1984 to 1987)
Spells spoken backwards; a wand she seldom needs
pages.html:
Zatanna Zatara is an American witch, the daughter of the pure-blood stage magician Zatara and his No-Maj wife, Sindella, which makes her a half-blood. Like her father, she does real magic on stage in front of thousands of Muggles every week, by saying her spells backwards, and not one of them has ever believed it. She was schooled at Ilvermorny, searched America for her missing father in the 1960s, joined the Justice League in 1978, and lost her father for good in 1986, at a séance John Constantine had organised. She has not entirely forgiven him for it. She was, for a while, his lover.

Birth and schooling

Zatanna was born about 1944. Her parents' marriage was against the law at the time, since Rappaport's Law forbade any American wizard to marry a No-Maj. Zatanna grew up as the half-blood daughter of a couple most of wizarding America disapproved of. Her mother died when she was still small.

From 1955 to 1962 she was at Ilvermorny, where the Thunderbird carving beat its wings for her on her first evening, and she was sorted into the house of adventurers. She learnt the school's wand-work well enough. Her father taught her the family's own art at home: spells spoken backwards, which need no wand at all.

The search for Zatara

Her father vanished in the late 1950s. From 1964, already making her living as a stage magician, Zatanna went looking for him across America. Her search crossed the paths of one costumed hero after another: Hawkman, Hawkgirl, the Atom, Green Lantern, the Elongated Man and Batman. In 1967, with the Justice League beside her, she found him at last and broke the curse that had kept them apart.

The Justice League

Zatanna joined the Justice League in 1978, the first witch ever to do so, although the League took her for a sorceress of the stage like her father. When Aquaman broke up the old League in 1984 and moved it to Detroit, she was one of the few veterans who stayed. She served there until the Detroit League came to an end in 1987.

To Muggles she is a stage magician who also happens to fight crime, and they take every spell she casts for a trick they cannot quite see through. The hidden wizarding world behind her has never come out. MACUSA, which spent decades failing to catch her father, has left her alone since Rappaport's Law was repealed in 1965.

In 1979 she carried an invitation from Albus Dumbledore to Aquaman, asking him to meet the Sub-Mariner on Rockall. She told the League nothing about who had sent it.

Zatanna is the pattern for every witch or wizard who lives in public. The Scarlet Witch of the Avengers is a witch whom the public takes for a mutant. Doctor Stephen Strange, a No-Maj-born wizard, is taken for a showman with a stage name. Amanda Sefton of the Excalibur team passes for a mutant too. None of them has ever needed a Memory Charm to keep the secret, since nobody believes what is in front of them.

Constantine and the séance

In the 1980s Zatanna and John Constantine, the Liverpool occultist, were lovers for a time. In 1986 John gathered the most powerful magicians of the age for a séance, to guide the Swamp Thing against the darkness that had risen, and Zatanna came with her father. When the backlash of the darkness came at her, Zatara drew it into himself to save her. It killed him.

She has never entirely forgiven John, and he has never forgiven himself. She came to his fortieth birthday party in May 1993 all the same.

Later years

Zatanna has gone on performing, and on fighting beside the League whenever it needs a witch. In 2004, after a vote of the League, she used her magic to change the villain Doctor Light's mind and memories. When Batman found out, she did the same to him. It was a Memory Charm in all but name, and the most bitterly argued thing she has ever done.

pages.title: Zatara
pages.html:
Zatara was an American wizard of an old pure-blood family of Italian descent. From 1938 he worked in public as a stage magician in top hat and tails, doing real magic in front of packed theatres by speaking his spells backwards. He fought crime, served with the All-Star Squadron in the Second World War and broke Rappaport's Law every night for nearly thirty years. He married a No-Maj, Sindella, and was the father of Zatanna. He died in 1986 at John Constantine's séance against the darkness.

Life

Giovanni Zatara, always called John, was born about 1912 into a pure-blood family of Italian descent that had long been settled in America. He went to Ilvermorny in the 1920s. His family had an art of its own, which it had kept for generations: spells spoken backwards, which need no wand at all. He carried a wand on stage all the same, where everybody took it for a prop.

From 1938 he played the theatres of America as a stage magician. Off the stage he fought crime openly beside the first of the mystery men, and in the war he served with the All-Star Squadron.

Rappaport's Law

Rappaport's Law forbade American wizards any dealings with No-Majs, and every one of Zatara's performances broke it. So did his marriage, in the early 1940s, to Sindella, a No-Maj woman. MACUSA pursued him for years without ever convicting him. Not one No-Maj who saw his act believed the magic was real, and the Congress could hardly prove a breach of secrecy that nobody had noticed.

Their daughter, Zatanna, was born about 1944. Sindella died while the girl was still a child.

Disappearance and death

In the late 1950s Zatara vanished, kept from his daughter by a curse. From 1964 Zatanna searched for him across America, helped by one costumed hero after another. In 1967, with the Justice League beside her, she found him at last and broke the curse.

In 1986 John Constantine gathered the most powerful magicians of the age for a séance, to guide the Swamp Thing against the darkness that had risen, and Zatara was among them. When the backlash of that darkness came at Zatanna, he drew it into himself to save her, and it killed him. The sorcerer Sargon died with him.

pages.title: Zefram Cochrane
infobox: The classified lore of the Aesir, given to the Tau'ri in 2007
A missile complex near Bozeman, Montana
pages.html:
Zefram Cochrane is the man who made Earth's first warp flight. On 5 April 2063, from an old missile complex near Bozeman in Montana, he took the Phoenix to warp speed, with an engine small enough to fit inside an old missile. He built it in the ruins left by the Third World War, drawing on the classified lore of the Aesir that Asgard had given the people of Earth in 2007. The flight was seen by a passing Vulcan ship, which landed that night.

The war years

Cochrane was born in 2030, four years after the Third World War began, and he grew up while it was still being fought. He was a young man of twenty-three when it ended in 2053, in the exchange of nuclear weapons that killed some six hundred million people. The years after it, which came to be called the post-atomic horror, were the years in which he did his work.

The lore of the Aesir

In 2007, when Asgard gave up its worlds among the stars, it gave the people of Earth the lore of the Aesir. It gave them none of its machines. The Aesir teach younger peoples, and leave them to build for themselves.

That lore was kept through the war, classified, by the survivors of Delta Green and the SCP Foundation, who understood what it was worth. They let Cochrane study it in the ruins. Most of it told of the Nine Worlds and the branches of Yggdrasil that join them. What mattered to him was the Rainbow Bridge, which carries a traveller from world to world without crossing the space between. It did not hand him a warp engine. It showed him that space could be folded, which of his own ideas were right and where to look, so that the engine he built was his own. Only what touched warp flight ever became public knowledge, as part of Cochrane's own work. The rest of the lore stayed classified. In later years the few who held the idea called Section 31 kept it, and almost nobody else knew that it existed at all.

The Phoenix

Cochrane built his ship near Bozeman, out of the body of an old nuclear missile left in its silo from before the war. He named it the Phoenix, for the bird that rises from its own ashes, which was what he hoped Earth might do.

On 5 April 2063 he flew it. The Phoenix went up from the silo, cleared the atmosphere and went to warp for a few minutes before it came home. It was the first warp flight by a ship from Earth.

Earth had flown between the stars before, in the warships its Stargate programme built from 2002 to 2007, the Prometheus, the Odyssey and the rest of Earth's first starships. They were crude and ruinously expensive. Their engines filled their hulls, failed often and never carried them far without Asgard's help. None of them outlasted the war. Cochrane's engine did what theirs had done, better, in the body of a missile.

The Vulcans

A Vulcan survey ship, passing the solar system, saw the trace of the warp flight. Its people had been watching Earth for some time, and had thought it not yet ready to be met. The flight changed their minds. That night the ship came down near Bozeman, and its captain greeted Cochrane in front of the people of the town. It was the first open meeting between the Vulcans and the people of Earth.

The man

Cochrane was never the solemn hero that schoolbooks later made of him. He drank too much, he liked his old rock records played loud and he said more than once that he had built the Phoenix for money. He was also brilliant, and in the end he told the truth about where his ideas had come from, which was more than most great men do.

In 2117, at the age of eighty seven, he set off alone into deep space. He was never heard of on Earth again.

Gamma Canaris N

In 2267 Captain James T. Kirk found him alive on Gamma Canaris N. A being of energy that Cochrane called the Companion had found him there in 2117, as he was dying, and kept him young ever since. Cochrane chose to stay with the Companion. Kirk promised to keep his secret, so Earth never heard of him again.

pages.title: Zero Hour
infobox: The Atom (Al Pratt); Hourman (Rex Tyler); Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider)
Time slips across the world; the dead, and people of other eras, walking the streets
Early August 1994, when time was begun again
pages.html:
Zero Hour, sometimes called the Crisis in Time, was the breakdown of time itself in July and early August 1994. For some weeks history came apart. The past leaked into the present, heroes of other eras walked the streets, and a wave of nothingness rolled back from the end of time, wiping out the ages in front of it. The Justice Society made its last stand against the time-mad Extant and was broken. The power behind the whole catastrophe turned out to be Hal Jordan, the lost Green Lantern, who now called himself Parallax. Time was begun again early in August, and most people remember those weeks only as a strange dream.

Time begins to fail

In July 1994 time began to go wrong all over the world. Clocks disagreed with one another. Whole districts of cities slipped into other years for an hour at a time, and people met the dead in the street, or their own younger selves. Heroes from other eras, some of them from histories that had never happened at all, appeared and vanished again.

Behind it all a wave of entropy was rolling back from the end of time, and the ages of the far future were going out ahead of it one after another, like lamps. The heroes of every nation gathered against it, Superman among the first. With them stood the Linear Men, who keep watch over history from Vanishing Point, a citadel beyond the end of time.

Extant and the Justice Society

The first face the enemy showed was Extant's. He had once been Hank Hall, the hero Hawk, and he had taken the powers of time for himself. At Vanishing Point the Justice Society, the oldest heroes in the world, stood against him.

Ever since the war the Society's members had been kept young by the temporal energies of the sorcerer Ian Karkull, and Extant simply took those stolen years back. The Atom (Al Pratt), Hourman (Rex Tyler) and Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider) died of it. The others were aged to their true years in a matter of moments: the Flash (Jay Garrick), Starman (Ted Knight), the Sandman (Wesley Dodds), Johnny Thunder and Wildcat (Ted Grant). Wildcat had a heart attack under the strain. Kent Nelson and his wife, Inza, were torn from the power of Fate as well as aged to their true years. The helmet, cloak and amulet of Nabu were scattered. Hawkman (Carter Hall) and Hawkgirl (Shiera Hall) were merged into a single being. Only Alan Scott, the first Green Lantern, came through unchanged, because his ring's power held.

When it was over the survivors, old now in body as well as in years, agreed that the Society's day was done. They disbanded it.

Parallax

Extant was not working alone. The power behind the catastrophe was Hal Jordan, Green Lantern for thirty-four years, who had vanished at the turn of 1994 after destroying the Green Lantern Corps. He called himself Parallax now. He meant to unmake history and build it again, this time without the destruction of Coast City, with its seven million people, or any of the other wrongs he could not forgive.

The heroes would not let him. At the beginning of time they stood against him, his own successor Kyle Rayner among them. It was Connor Hawke, the young son of Oliver Queen, the first Green Arrow, who shot him through the heart. Hal Jordan survived even that. He vanished again, and nobody knows where he is.

Time begins again

Parallax was stopped before he could remake the universe to his own design. By then, though, there was too little of time left to save. The young hero called Damage, whose power was the energy of a new beginning, let it go at the dawn of all things. Time was begun again from it, with the heroes shaping what came after. Early in August 1994 the world simply went on, as though time had never broken.

What is remembered

Almost nobody outside the heroes' own circles remembers Zero Hour clearly. Most people recall a few strange weeks that summer and are not sure which parts of them were real. Those who were there agree that history came back very nearly as it had been. Not quite, though: a few small things are said to be different, and nobody can say for certain what they are.

By the middle of August the news was full of the Augment War again, and Zero Hour was hardly mentioned. What stayed were the deaths of the Atom, Hourman and Doctor Mid-Nite, together with the end of the Justice Society.

pages.title: Ziktor Industries
pages.html:
Ziktor Industries is the company of the billionaire Karl Ziktor, with its headquarters in the middle of Crossworld City, California. Its owner is the richest man in the town. He is also Grimlord, the master of virtual reality, though nobody outside his private office knows it.

The company

Ziktor Industries has interests in oil, timber and scientific research. In Crossworld City it gets its own way. The mayor, Abner Rooney, rarely stands up to its owner. It is a modest affair all the same beside LexCorp of Metropolis or Stark Enterprises, with nothing like the age of the Wayne fortune in Gotham: one rich man's company in one Californian town.

Karl Ziktor runs it from his own office. On his desk stood, until September 1995, the orb that carried him across the reality barrier to become Grimlord. His secretaries are Skugs, soldiers of Grimlord's in human shape. So is Strickland, the company's inventor.

The company in Grimlord's war

The business of the company is hard to tell apart from the business of its owner. In September 1994 Ziktor tried to get hold of an inventor's plans for a clean engine, which would have hurt his trade in oil. That October he set about felling a stretch of old forest. The VR Troopers stopped him both times, without learning that the businessman they had thwarted was Grimlord.

Strickland's inventions were made for Grimlord's use. One turned the three Troopers into children. Another turned J.B. Reese into one of Grimlord's creatures. In September 1995 Strickland built a machine for travelling in time, then went back with it to attack Ryan Steele as a boy. Later that year he made a box of chocolates with a love potion in them.

In February 1996 Ziktor announced that a forest would be cleared for a new research station. The Troopers, as three ordinary young people, pressed him into coming on a camping trip there with a reporter from the Underground Voice Daily. Her photographs did his public standing no good. That is the last the record says of the company.
