pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl Who Noticed Him
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl Who Noticed Him

Book One of the Malfoid Saga · 1991 to 1992 · Complete

Read Book OneFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1The Girl Who Noticed

Hagrid had slipped off to the Leaky Cauldron to recover from the Gringotts cart ride, so Harry Potter went into Madam Malkin's Robes for All Occasions in Diagon Alley on his own, still wearing Dudley's cast-off clothes. He was put on a stool beside a girl with waist-length silver-blonde hair. She had silver eyes, said she was Dracina Malfoy and held out her hand to be kissed. Harry, who knew nothing of the custom, asked her quite seriously whether she was a princess, which made her blush. Then she talked about racing brooms, about Quidditch and about how certain she was of being sorted into Slytherin. Harry was strongly reminded of Dudley. When Hagrid appeared at the window with two ice-creams, she dismissed him as a drunken servant, and Harry coldly defended him. On learning that Harry's parents were dead, she asked whether they had been 'our sort' and said that Muggle-borns should not be let into Hogwarts. Harry left without telling her his surname. He did not see her watch him all the way to the door, or go on gazing after him once he had gone. He ate his ice-cream in silence, unable to make the two halves of her fit together.

Chapter 2The Wrong Sort

On the Hogwarts Express Harry shared a compartment with Ron Weasley, who told him about his five older brothers and his rat, Scabbers. Ron admitted that his family could not afford an owl. Harry bought a heap of sweets from the trolley and swapped pasties for Ron's corned beef sandwiches; his first Chocolate Frog card showed Albus Dumbledore. Neville Longbottom came looking for his lost toad. Hermione Granger watched Ron fail to turn Scabbers yellow with a dud rhyme he had got from George. Then Dracina Malfoy arrived with Crabbe and Goyle, having heard that Harry Potter was on the train. She was rude about the Weasleys and offered Harry her hand, along with her guidance on 'the wrong sort'. Harry refused both. Dracina warned him that he would end up like his parents. When Goyle grabbed at the Chocolate Frogs, Scabbers bit him on the knuckle, and the three of them fled. Dracina's eyes stayed on Harry as she went, like someone who had already decided to have a thing she had seen in a shop window. Ron told Harry afterwards that the Malfoys had claimed to have been bewitched after You-Know-Who's fall. His father did not believe a word of it.

Chapter 3Silver Eyes

Hagrid took the first-years across the lake by boat to Hogwarts, where Professor McGonagall told them about the four houses and the House Cup. While they waited, a crowd of ghosts frightened them all. Dracina screamed and clutched Harry's arm, then shoved him away as though he had bumped into her. The Sorting Hat sang its song and the Sorting began. Dracina was in Slytherin almost before the hat had touched her head. Harry begged the hat, 'Not Slytherin'. It remarked on his courage, his talent and 'so much pain' for one so young, then put him in Gryffindor. Dracina looked disappointed when he was sorted, then turned her back. At the feast Harry met Nearly Headless Nick and learnt that Slytherin had won the House Cup six years running. Seamus and Neville described their families. When Professor Snape looked at him past Quirrell's turban, Harry's scar burned. Dumbledore warned the school that the forest was out of bounds, and so was the right-hand corridor on the third floor. Then everybody sang the school song. Percy led the Gryffindors past Peeves to their tower. That night Harry dreamed that Quirrell's turban was urging him to go into Slytherin, and that Malfoy was laughing at him. When he woke, all he could remember was a pair of cruel silver eyes.

Chapter 4The Old Hogwarts Try

Harry's first week at Hogwarts was a struggle against moving staircases, Peeves and a school that would not stop staring at him. In Astronomy Hermione lectured him on astrology. In History of Magic Professor Binns read out pure-blood marriage lists, which set Ron and Hermione explaining wizarding ideas of blood. Hermione told Harry about the Norman wizarding families who had won the Conquest for William with dark magic. Dracina claimed that the Malfoys had been in Britain before Britain existed. When Hermione corrected her, Dracina mocked her hair, nose and teeth, then called her a Mudblood. Ron rebuked her for using such a filthy word. With Harry, Dracina was softer. She urged him to side with his own kind, the old pure families like his, but he told her she was not the sort of girl he wanted as a friend. All she could find to say back was 'pottyhead', which made him laugh. Charms, Transfiguration and a Defence lesson with the stammering, garlic-reeking Quirrell went little better. On Friday Hedwig brought Hagrid's invitation to tea. In double Potions Snape mocked Harry's fame, quizzed him on things he could not possibly know and took two points from Gryffindor. He praised Dracina's work. Neville, meanwhile, melted Seamus's cauldron and came out in boils.

Chapter 5The Seeker

Flying lessons with the Slytherins began in Harry's second week. At breakfast Dracina snatched Neville's new Remembrall, until Professor McGonagall stepped in. In the lesson Neville took off too early, fell and broke his wrist. While Madam Hooch was taking him away, Dracina found the Remembrall and flew off with it. Harry went after her on the first flight of his life. He charged at her, saw her for a moment as a frightened little girl, and caught the Remembrall she threw at the end of a fifty-foot dive. Professor McGonagall marched him off. Instead of expelling him, she introduced him to Oliver Wood as Gryffindor's new Seeker, the youngest house player in about a century. She told him that his father had been a fine Quidditch player. Dracina challenged Harry to a wizard's duel at midnight in the trophy room, with Ron and Crabbe as seconds. Hermione, who had been locked out of the tower, came along, and so did Neville, who had forgotten the password. Dracina never turned up. Filch did. Running from Peeves, the four of them opened a locked door with Hermione's Alohomora, and found a three-headed dog in the forbidden corridor on the third floor. Hermione noticed that it was standing on a trapdoor. Harry realised that it was guarding the package Hagrid had taken from vault seven hundred and thirteen at Gringotts.

Chapter 6The Yearning

The morning after the duel that never happened, Dracina came in to breakfast looking forlorn. She brightened when she saw Harry, then remembered to be angry that he had not been expelled. A week later Harry received a Nimbus Two Thousand from Professor McGonagall. Dracina tried to get him into trouble over it, but Professor Flitwick already knew of the special circumstances. Harry thanked her for getting him on to the team, and said he owed her a favour. It left her blushing, silently repeating the word to herself. That evening Oliver Wood taught Harry the rules of Quidditch on the pitch. Afterwards Harry found that Dracina had been watching from the stands. Their quarrel grew worse until Harry exploded. He shouted about Dudley hanging him off the school roof, and about Aunt Petunia's frying pan, then stopped, ashamed of having frightened her. Dracina's eyes shimmered and she began to speak, but Wood sent her off. Her whispered apology never reached Harry. On Hallowe'en Ron's cruelty sent Hermione crying into the girls' toilets. When Quirrell announced that there was a troll in the dungeons, Harry and Ron went to warn her. By accident they locked the troll in, with Hermione and Dracina still inside. Then they fought it. Harry jammed his wand up its nose, and Ron knocked it out with its own club. Both girls lied to the teachers to protect the boys, and each lost five points for her house. From then on Hermione was Harry and Ron's friend. Dracina watched the three of them from the shadows, seething with jealousy, thinking of her brave knight.

Chapter 7Secret Weapon

As November turned frosty, Harry got ready for his first Quidditch match, against Slytherin; Oliver Wood was keeping him hidden as Gryffindor's secret weapon. Hermione, grateful after the troll, began doing all of Harry's homework, and she was especially warm to him whenever Dracina was watching. Dracina repaid her with hostility. Harry noticed that Dracina never threw back at him any of the things he had shouted at her on the pitch, the ones that would really have hurt; she stuck to 'Pottyhead'. Snape, who was limping, confiscated Harry's library copy of Quidditch Through the Ages. When Harry went to ask for it back, he saw Snape's bloodied leg and heard him complain about watching three heads at once. That convinced him Snape had let the troll in to get past the dog. At the match Dracina watched Harry with plain worry. After Marcus Flint fouled him, Harry's broom began to buck so violently that he was left hanging from it by one hand. Hermione checked on Dracina first and found her white with fear. Then she spotted Snape muttering and set his robes alight, knocking Quirrell over on the way. Harry recovered, caught the Snitch in his mouth and won the match 170 to 60, while Dracina cheered in the Slytherin stand. Over tea Hagrid let slip that the three-headed dog was his, that it was called Fluffy, and that he had lent it to Dumbledore. Worse, he let slip that whatever it guarded was a matter for Dumbledore and Nicolas Flamel.

Chapter 8Desire Behind Glass

In snowbound December Dracina grabbed Harry's shoulder in a corridor, which brought back a flash of Dudley. She had come to give him her mother's invitation to spend Christmas at Malfoy Manor. Harry laughed, taking it for a prank, and she told him he was too stupid to see a good thing. In Potions she went on taunting him about having nowhere to go, dropping hints about the invitation. She goaded Ron into grabbing her robes, and Snape took five points from Gryffindor. In the decorated Great Hall Harry saw Dracina standing alone, staring at the mistletoe; she and Hermione glared at each other across the room. In the library, where Harry, Ron and Hermione were hunting for Nicolas Flamel, Dracina offered to help Harry by the Restricted Section, until Hermione towed him away. Harry stayed at Hogwarts for Christmas with the Weasleys. He received the first presents of his life, among them a Weasley jumper, a fifty-pence piece from the Dursleys and, from somebody who did not sign the note, his father's Invisibility Cloak. Under the Cloak he fled from a screaming book in the Restricted Section, then from Filch and Snape. While he was hiding from them he found a mirror. In it he saw his parents, two sets of grandparents, a little brother and a little sister. Ron saw himself as Head Boy and Quidditch captain. Harry, resentful, shoved him. On the third night Dumbledore found Harry at the mirror. He told him it was the Mirror of Erised, and that it showed the deepest desire of a person's heart. Harry's wish, he said, was for love and a family. Then he apologised to Harry, and asked him not to go looking for the mirror again.

Chapter 9Five Minutes

Harry did as Dumbledore asked and stayed away from the mirror. Instead he began to have nightmares of green light, with a woman screaming. When term began again, Dracina sat down beside him at breakfast while he was alone. She stayed until Ron and Hermione arrived, then retreated with an insult. Wood drove the team hard before the Hufflepuff match, which Snape, unexpectedly, was to referee. Harry made up his mind to play, whatever his friends feared. Dracina hit Neville with the Leg-Locker Curse, saying that she had been looking for someone in particular to practise on. Harry cheered him up with a Chocolate Frog, and its Dumbledore card gave them Nicolas Flamel's name; Hermione's library book showed that Flamel was the only known maker of the Philosopher's Stone. In Potions Dracina corrected Harry's stirring, which stopped his potion exploding. At the match, which Dumbledore came to watch, Dean Thomas led the Gryffindor stand in football chants. Dracina, sitting behind Ron, taunted him and Neville until Ron went for her. Neville fought Crabbe and Goyle single-handed. When nobody came to her rescue, Dracina mauled Ron. She bit his ear, screaming about Harry and the company he kept. Harry caught the Snitch in about five minutes, which put Gryffindor top of the House Championship, and Dumbledore quietly praised him. That evening Harry followed Snape into the Forbidden Forest on his broom. He overheard Snape pressing Quirrell about getting past Fluffy, and about Quirrell's 'hocus-pocus' protecting the Philosopher's Stone.

Chapter 10The Egg in the Fire

With Quirrell apparently still holding out against Snape, Harry, Ron and Hermione kept checking that Fluffy was still on guard. Hermione drew up revision timetables ten weeks before the exams, and seemed always to know where Harry was. Dracina put it about that Ron was a violent animal. When they spotted Hagrid in the library with books on dragons, the three of them went down to his sweltering hut. There Hagrid, coaxed by Hermione, listed the teachers who had set enchantments round the Stone, Snape among them. He also showed them a Norwegian Ridgeback egg, which he had won at cards from a stranger in the village. Dracina overheard that the egg was hatching, and spied on the newborn dragon through Hagrid's curtains. Harry tackled her on the lawn, but she got away by crying assault. Hagrid named the dragon Norbert, and Harry suggested sending him to Charlie Weasley in Romania. Norbert bit Ron's hand with his poisonous fangs. In the hospital wing Dracina threatened to tell what had bitten Ron unless he stopped being Harry's friend. She went off with a book that had Charlie's reply inside it. On Saturday night Harry and Hermione carried Norbert's crate to the tallest tower under the Invisibility Cloak. On the way they passed Professor McGonagall, who was giving Dracina a detention for being out of bed and would not hear a word about Harry having a dragon. Charlie's friends took Norbert away. Harry and Hermione, though, left the Cloak behind on the tower. Filch caught them at the foot of the stairs.

Chapter 11The Death of Beauty

Filch left Harry and Hermione in Professor McGonagall's study. She came in with Neville trailing behind her. Harry and Ron, she announced, had lured Dracina out of bed with a ridiculous story about a dragon. She rebuked Hermione for calling Dracina an evil harpy. Then she took fifty points each from Harry, Hermione and Neville. Alone with Harry, she produced Charlie's letter, the one Dracina had taken. She gave him the advice she had once given his father: that one is only punished for what one is caught doing. Afterwards Harry realised that she had covered for him. Gryffindor fell to last place, and Harry became the most hated boy in the school, with only Ron standing by him. A week before the exams Harry overheard Quirrell apparently giving in to someone, and decided not to meddle. Quirrell supervised the detention, which Dracina was serving too. He took them into the Forbidden Forest, supposedly to collect mushrooms along a silver trail. Quirrell, whose stutter vanished whenever he grew irritated, suddenly screamed and bolted into the trees with his lamp. Harry lost the others in the dark. Dracina found him there, holding the only lamp left in the Forest, and demanded that he escort her, reminding him of the favour he owed her. She clung to his hand, overjoyed that her knight was protecting her. A shimmering unicorn came up and let Dracina touch it. Then a hooded figure killed it with green light and began to drink its blood. Harry's scar blazed and Dracina fled. The centaur Firenze rescued Harry, defying Bane to do it, and hinted that Voldemort was drinking unicorn blood while he waited for the Stone. Back in the tower Harry found his Invisibility Cloak returned to him, with a note that read 'Just in case'.

Chapter 12Seven Bottles

Quirrell was found at dawn at the edge of the Forest, cut about and howling. The school blamed centaurs, but Harry was still suspicious of his lies and his vanishing stutter. Through the sweltering exams of June 1992 Harry suffered from pains in his scar and nightmares about the hooded figure. Dracina showed off in Potions. After the last exam she called Hermione a violent Mudblood, and Harry comforted Hermione. Then Harry realised that Hagrid's hooded card partner had learnt from him that music sent Fluffy to sleep. He tried to reach Dumbledore, but Professor McGonagall said the headmaster had been called to London by the Ministry, and insisted that the Stone was safe. Snape warned the three of them off. McGonagall caught Harry and Ron near the third-floor corridor. Harry made up his mind to go through the trapdoor that night. Ron and Hermione insisted on coming too. Dracina, who had been given the password by Neville, was waiting in the Gryffindor common room, apparently to apologise to Harry. Hermione, calling her Snape's spy, petrified her with the Body-Bind. Harry accepted Dracina's apology, apologised for Hermione and promised to come back for her. He saw a twinkle in her eyes that he would remember for years. Harry got rid of Peeves by pretending to be the Bloody Baron, and lulled Fluffy to sleep with Hagrid's flute. Hermione's fire freed the three of them from the Devil's Snare. Harry caught the winged key, and Ron sacrificed himself in a giant game of chess so that Harry could checkmate the king. They passed a stunned troll. Then Harry and Hermione solved Snape's logic puzzle of the seven bottles. Harry sent Hermione back for help and walked through the black flames into the final chamber. There he found neither Snape nor Voldemort.

Chapter 13Rage Against Evil

In the final chamber Harry found Quirrell, calm and without a trace of his stutter, standing in front of the Mirror of Erised. Quirrell told him that it was he, not Snape, who had jinxed Harry's broom; Snape had been muttering a counter-curse. Quirrell had let the troll in himself, and Lucius Malfoy had arranged for Dumbledore to be away in London. Quirrell had also used the students in detention as bait for the unicorn, which would never have come near a man like him. He bound Harry in conjured chains and confessed that he served Lord Voldemort, who had punished him for failing to steal the Stone from Gringotts. When Harry looked into the Mirror, his reflection put the blood-red Stone in its pocket, and the Stone dropped into Harry's real one. Harry lied about what he saw. Quirrell unwrapped his turban. On the back of his head was Voldemort's chalk-white, red-eyed face. Voldemort taunted Harry about his parents' deaths and demanded the Stone. But wherever Quirrell touched Harry's skin, his own hands and face blistered. Harry clung on through pain and hatred until he blacked out, seeing his parents in the Mirror, proud of him. He woke three days later in the hospital wing. Dumbledore explained that he had pulled Quirrell off him, and that the Stone had been destroyed with Flamel's agreement. Lily's love had left a protection in Harry's skin, he said. Lily might also descend from a very powerful magical line, and James had once saved Snape's life. Hagrid, in tears, gave Harry an album of photographs of his parents. Neville confessed that Dracina had been kind to him, and that was how she had got the password. At the end-of-year feast Dumbledore's last-minute awards to Ron, Hermione and Harry drew Gryffindor level with Slytherin. Then he took a hundred points from Slytherin for Dracina's trespass, and the House Cup went to Gryffindor. On the platform at King's Cross Dracina warned Harry, almost anxiously, to watch out next year. Harry left with the Dursleys, certain now that he could endure them.

How it differs from the original

  • The book opens at Madam Malkin's; there are no Privet Drive or Dursley chapters, no Hagrid letter-delivery scene, no Gringotts, Ollivander's, Leaky Cauldron or Diagon Alley tour on the page.
  • The platform departure happens offstage; Chapter 2 opens with the train already moving.
  • Draco Malfoy is Dracina Malfoy, a girl infatuated with Harry from first sight, so her antagonism plays as thwarted courtship and the Gryffindor boys repeatedly debate whether boys may hit girls.
  • Harry asks Dracina 'Are you a princess?' at Madam Malkin's, and she teaches him that a witch's hand is to be kissed.
  • Dracina watches Harry's first solo practice, and Harry shouts his abuse history at her; she begins an apology only Wood hears.
  • Dracina is in the girls' toilets with Hermione on Hallowe'en and is the troll's first target; Harry saves both girls, and Dracina lies to McGonagall to cover for Harry and Ron.
  • Narcissa invites Harry to Malfoy Manor for Christmas and Harry laughs it off as a prank.
  • Dean Thomas writes football terrace chants, and a brawl breaks out in the stands in which Neville beats Crabbe and Goyle and Dracina savages Ron.
  • The detention is not with Hagrid: Quirrell takes Harry, Hermione, Neville and Dracina into the Forest on a fake mushroom hunt and abandons them as bait for unicorns.
  • Dracina touches the dying unicorn, and Harry sees it killed by a green-light curse; Dracina runs.
  • On the final night Dracina gets the password from Neville to apologise, and Hermione Body-Binds her, not Neville.
  • Dumbledore docks Slytherin one hundred points for Dracina's trespass, which decides the House Cup; final points are Ron 50, Hermione 50, Harry 60, and Neville gets nothing.
  • Snape takes one point, not five, for Harry's impertinence, and Harry's answer is a sincere suggestion to ask Hermione.
  • Hermione's friendship becomes an obsessive, jealous attachment: she does all Harry's homework.
  • Gryffindor's second match is against Hufflepuff, won in five minutes, and they lose the third to Ravenclaw while Harry is in hospital.
  • Dracina, not Draco, is caught on the dragon night, and McGonagall knowingly calls the truth a lie to protect Harry.
  • McGonagall has a hidden military past: mujahideen, Kosovo, Kandahar and Zanzibar Land.
  • Harry's final fight is a mauling fuelled by hatred, and he senses Voldemort's fear.
  • Dumbledore reveals Lily descended from an unnamed, very powerful line of magic.
  • The Mirror of Erised shows Harry two sets of grandparents, a little brother and a little sister.
  • The Sorting Hat song, the seven-bottles riddle and Dumbledore's opening words are all new, and the password changes from Caput Draconis to Pig snout.
  • Dracina warns Harry at King's Cross, in a worried tone, to watch out next year.
  • Draco Malfoy is a girl here: Dracina Malfoy.
  • Dracina offers her hand to be kissed, not shaken, and Harry asks whether she is a princess.
  • The chapter closes on Dracina watching Harry go, a sign of her interest in him from their very first meeting.
  • Dracina again holds out her hand palm down, and Harry orders her out before Ron can finish his insult.
  • Ron's rhyme for turning the rat yellow is 'Buttercup, custard, morning sun'.
  • Dracina's long, possessive look at Harry as she leaves is new.
  • Dracina screams at the ghosts and grabs Harry's arm, then pushes him away.
  • The Sorting Hat remarks on Harry's pain as well as on his courage and talent.
  • Dracina is plainly disappointed when Harry is sorted into Gryffindor.
  • Harry's dream ends with Dracina's silver eyes, which stay with him after he wakes.
  • Hermione gives a history of the Norman dark wizarding families who won the Conquest, and says that William granted Armand Malfoy his land in Wiltshire.
  • When Dracina taunts Hermione about her looks, Harry remembers Aunt Petunia's prejudice. He starts to ask whether she means the Jews, before she says 'Mudbloods'.
  • Dracina urges Harry to side with the Malfoys because the Potters are an ancient, pure family. Her comeback, 'pottyhead', becomes a running joke.
  • Ron says that Charlie learnt a Shield Charm in his first year.
  • Ron keeps threatening to hit Dracina, girl or not. Hermione and Harry tell him off for it. Ron admits that he does not actually hit girls.
  • Harry sees Dracina for a moment as a frightened little girl in the air. There is also something in her voice when she speaks to him that an eleven-year-old would not notice.
  • Harry compares Crabbe and Goyle to Tolkien's Uruk-hai.
  • Dracina is in the girls' toilets with Hermione when the troll arrives, and the troll goes for her first.
  • Losing his temper, Harry blurts out to Dracina the details of Dudley's bullying and of the Dursleys' abuse.
  • Dracina whispers an apology to Harry that he never hears.
  • Hermione lies to McGonagall to protect Harry and Ron. So does Dracina, and Snape takes five points from Slytherin.
  • A rivalry over Harry between Hermione and Dracina is hinted at. Only Ron notices it.
  • Hermione writes the whole of Harry's homework for him. She is protective of him, believing that he will keep her safe.
  • Dracina is plainly worried for Harry during the match, and cheers when he beats her own house.
  • Dean wears a West Ham scarf, and Hagrid covers it with a Gryffindor one.
  • Hagrid bought Fluffy from a man with a caravan whom he took to be Greek; Harry doubts that he was Greek.
  • Quidditch Through the Ages describes an 1877 duel between the English and French managers that killed two hundred people.
  • Narcissa Malfoy invites Harry to Malfoy Manor for Christmas through Dracina, and Harry laughs it off.
  • When he is grabbed from behind, Harry has a flashback to Dudley's bullying.
  • In the mirror Harry sees a little brother and a little sister, as well as his parents with both sets of grandparents.
  • Harry's resentment of Ron's family and the voice of the Dursleys in his head are explored at length.
  • Dumbledore apologises to Harry and speaks of people like the two of them being burdened by destiny.
  • Dracina, not Draco, uses the Leg-Locker Curse on Neville, saying that she meant it for someone in particular.
  • Dracina helps Harry with his potion in class.
  • Dean Thomas leads football chants against Hufflepuff, among them 'Five minutes!' and 'Can we play you every week?'.
  • Ron fights Dracina instead of Draco, and comes off worse. She scratches him, bites him and pulls his hair, screaming about Harry the whole time.
  • Flamel lives in Devon with Perenelle.
  • Dracina, in Draco's role, spies on Norbert's hatching; Harry tackles her, and she escapes by crying assault.
  • Dracina's price for keeping quiet is that Ron must stop being Harry's friend.
  • Hermione seems always to know where Harry is, and she coaxes Hagrid with a smile that reminds Harry of Dracina.
  • Ron regrets fighting Dracina, saying his mum was right that you should not hit girls.
  • In public McGonagall treats Dracina's dragon report as a lie, but in private she shows Harry that she knows the truth. She advises him only to avoid being caught, as she once advised James.
  • McGonagall hints at a past involving feral mujahideen.
  • Quirrell, not Hagrid, leads the detention. He lies that the unicorn blood is a mushroom secretion, and runs off theatrically.
  • Dracina, not Draco, is paired with Harry in the Forest. She holds his hand. The unicorn comes up to her and lets her touch it.
  • Hermione calls Dracina an evil harpy, and hisses at her whenever she comes near Harry.
  • McGonagall alludes to a holiday in Kosovo, to a night spent warding a camp outside Kandahar, and to an old friend from Zanzibar Land who taught her to move silently.
  • Harry calls the man who sold Fluffy to Hagrid a Pikey, meaning that he was not Greek.
  • Dracina, not Neville, confronts the trio in the common room, where she is trying to apologise to Harry. Hermione petrifies her instead of Neville.
  • Harry pretends to be the Bloody Baron to get rid of Peeves.
  • Harry catches the winged key by spotting its crushed wing, overcoming the voice of the Dursleys in his head.
  • Quirrell says that Lucius Malfoy made sure Dumbledore was in London, and that he used the students in detention as bait because unicorns will not come to him.
  • Quirrell says that James Potter was a few years ahead of him at school, and meddled in 'our business'.
  • Dumbledore tells Harry that Lily, though Muggle-born, may descend from a very powerful magical line. The protection, he says, came from several things together, among them her dying spell and whatever anchors Voldemort to this plane.
  • Neville receives no points. Instead Dumbledore takes a hundred points from Slytherin because Dracina entered the Gryffindor common room, and that wins Gryffindor the Cup.
  • Dumbledore says that Snape and James loathed each other. He compares their loathing with what Harry believes lies between him and Dracina.
  • At King's Cross Dracina warns Harry to watch out next year, and on the train Hermione holds Harry's hand.

Characters introduced

  • Albus Dumbledore
  • Argus Filch
  • Arthur Weasley
  • Bill Weasley
  • Charlie Weasley
  • Dean Thomas
  • Dracina Malfoy
  • Dudley Dursley
  • Filius Flitwick
  • Firenze
  • Fred Weasley
  • George Weasley
  • Ginny Weasley
  • Gregory Goyle
  • Harry Potter
  • Hedwig
  • Hermione Granger
  • Justin Finch-Fletchley
  • Lord Voldemort
  • Lucius Malfoy
  • Minerva McGonagall
  • Molly Weasley
  • Mrs Norris
  • Narcissa Malfoy
  • Nearly Headless Nick
  • Neville Longbottom
  • Oliver Wood
  • Pansy Parkinson
  • Percy Weasley

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary

Book Two of the Malfoid Saga · 1992 to 1993 · Complete

Read Book TwoFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1Making No Noise

On 31 July 1992, Harry Potter's twelfth birthday, Vernon Dursley shouted at him over Hedwig's hooting. Breakfast turned to uproar when Harry said 'the magic word' by accident, then called the family malignant on purpose. He had come home from his first year at Hogwarts with a defiant streak, and had taken to goading the Dursleys. They had padlocked his school things in the cupboard under the stairs, and Hedwig in her cage. The Dursleys forgot his birthday entirely. Instead they rehearsed for a dinner party at which Vernon hoped to sell drills to a wealthy builder, Mr Mason, and his wife. Harry was ordered to stay in his room making no noise. Alone in the garden, he brooded. Not a single letter had come from Ron or Hermione, and an inner voice kept telling him that nobody had ever liked him. He caught himself missing Dracina Malfoy, and the twinkle in her silver eyes. Then he noticed two enormous green eyes watching him from the hedge. When Dudley jeered that he had no friends, Harry pretended to be turning the hedge into an Ent. Aunt Petunia swung a frying pan at him and kept him working in the garden until evening. All he was given to eat was bread and cheese. He went upstairs as the Masons arrived, and found somebody already sitting on his bed.

Chapter 2DMD: Dobby Must Die

The creature on Harry's bed was Dobby, a house-elf dressed in a pillowcase. He wept loudly at being treated as an equal, and battered his own head whenever he came close to betraying the wizarding family he served. Dobby warned Harry that a plot would make terrible things happen at Hogwarts that year, and that he must not go back. His Mistress, he added, had been very clear that Harry should be told. He gave Harry to understand that the danger did not come from He Who Must Not Be Named, and hinted at powers that no decent wizard used. Then Dobby admitted that he had been stopping Harry's letters from Ron, Hermione and Hagrid, in the hope that Harry would think himself friendless. He offered them back only if Harry promised not to return. When Harry refused, Dobby ran to the kitchen, levitated Aunt Petunia's pudding, dropped it on the floor and vanished with a crack. An owl then brought a Ministry warning from Mafalda Hopkirk about the Hover Charm. It dropped the letter on Mrs Mason, who was terrified of birds, and that was the end of the deal. Once Vernon learnt that Harry was not allowed to use magic outside school, he locked him in his room. He had bars fitted to the window, put a cat-flap in the door and fed him almost nothing. After three days of it Harry dreamed that he was in a cage at a zoo while Dracina laughed at him. He woke to find Ron Weasley outside his window.

Chapter 3Touchdown

Ron, Fred and George had come for him in their father's enchanted flying Ford Anglia. They ripped the bars from the window. The twins picked the lock on Harry's door with a piece of wire and fetched his trunk from the cupboard. As Harry escaped, Uncle Vernon seized his ankle; Harry clawed himself free, shouting that he hated him and would never come back. In the car Harry wept with relief and told the Weasleys about Dobby. The twins thought that someone with a grudge must have sent the elf. Harry and Ron named Dracina Malfoy at once. Fred and George described Lucius Malfoy as a former supporter of You-Know-Who, from a family of Dark wizards going back to the Norman Conquest. Harry remembered Dracina mentioning a house-elf in their first year. On the flight Ron told Harry about Errol, and about Percy's owl, Hermes. He explained that Percy had been behaving oddly ever since their mother took away a statue Charlie had given him. He told Harry, too, about his father's job in the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office. At dawn they landed at the Burrow, outside Ottery St Catchpole, where Molly Weasley confronted her sons in the yard. Overcome by exhaustion and guilt, Harry apologised to her, then fainted.

Chapter 4As Long As You Want

Harry woke on the Weasleys' sofa. Ron told his mother about the bars, the lock and the empty soup bowl. Molly Weasley had already seen the bruises Vernon's grip had left on Harry's ankle, and she asked him gently whether he had been hit. Harry could not lie to her. He let slip the frying pan first. Then out came the whole history of the beatings and the cupboard. He broke down sobbing. He said Ron was the best person he knew, and thanked her for the Christmas jumper. Molly held him and promised to make everything better, though inside she was growing furious with the Dursleys. She told him he could stay at the Burrow for as long as he wanted. Harry took in the Weasleys' cosy kitchen and met a painfully shy Ginny. He ate an enormous breakfast, then helped to de-gnome the garden once Molly had consulted Gilderoy Lockhart's Guide to Household Pests. Arthur Weasley came home from a night of Ministry raids, and Molly confronted him over the enchanted car. He admitted that he had written a loophole into the law himself. Ron showed Harry his orange bedroom, which was covered in Chudley Cannons posters. Harry declared the Burrow the best house he had ever been in.

Chapter 5The Wrong Grate

At the Burrow Harry got his strength back. He explained Muggle devices to Arthur, and noticed Molly's hints about Professor McGonagall's Muggle connections. The Hogwarts letters arrived with a booklist made up of Lockhart's titles. Molly firmly refused Harry's offers to pay for the Weasleys' books, and Hermione wrote to suggest meeting in Diagon Alley. On his first journey by Floo powder Harry came out in Borgin and Burkes in Knockturn Alley, and hid in a cabinet. From inside it he overheard Lucius Malfoy selling dangerous possessions ahead of the Ministry raids. Dracina complained about Harry, and was warned not to seem obsessed with him. Hagrid found Harry and took him back to Diagon Alley. At Gringotts, where Harry was reunited with Hermione and the Weasleys, he saw how little there was in the Weasleys' vault. At Flourish and Blotts, Gilderoy Lockhart pulled Harry into a photograph and announced that he would be teaching Defence Against the Dark Arts. Harry gave his free books to Ginny. Dracina was about to tell Harry something when Ginny stood up for him. Dracina turned and bullied Ginny instead. While Arthur and Lucius brawled, Ginny hurled books at her. Hagrid pulled the fathers apart. Dracina gathered up the spilt books, a small black one among them. She pressed one on Ginny, kept the rest and hissed at Ginny as the Malfoys left.

Chapter 6Due North

Harry spent the rest of the summer at the Burrow, where Molly kept telling him that he need never leave. She had written to Dumbledore to say where Harry would be living from now on, and to condemn him for leaving Harry with the Dursleys for eleven years. On 1 September 1992 Arthur proudly explained the Ford Anglia's many charms. The family was held up by forgotten fireworks, a broom and Ginny's diary. Molly forbade Arthur to fly to London. At King's Cross the barrier sealed itself against Harry and Ron. Harry blamed Dobby and Dracina. He spoke of revenge so violent that it alarmed Ron. Ron flew them to Hogwarts in the car, following the Hogwarts Express due north. But the engine died over the lake. They crashed into the Whomping Willow, and Ron's wand snapped. Harry thought Ron had been crushed, until Ron knocked him clear of a falling branch. The battered car threw out their luggage and fled into the Forbidden Forest. Snape caught them and showed them a Daily Prophet report that Muggles had seen the car. He fetched McGonagall and Dumbledore. They chose not to expel the boys, but they warned them and wrote to their families. McGonagall took no house points, though she gave both boys detentions. They learnt that Ginny had been sorted into Gryffindor. Then the house greeted them as heroes.

Chapter 7Freshly Caught

At breakfast on 2 September 1992 Hermione was full of the vampire lore in Voyages with Vampires: Angelus, William the Bloody, Dracula and the Belmont family. Then Ron received a Howler from his mother, which revealed that Arthur was facing an inquiry at work. Dracina Malfoy came over to Harry as if to tell him something. But when Ginny came near him, Dracina called him an idiot and told him to enjoy his girlfriend. Then she stormed off to berate Crabbe and Goyle. In Herbology, after Lockhart had lectured Harry on seeking publicity, Professor Sprout taught the class to repot Mandrakes, and they met Justin Finch-Fletchley. In Transfiguration Professor McGonagall remembered turning a vault of gold into beetles for a Scottish Muggle colleague, and Ron's damaged wand misfired. In the courtyard Colin Creevey asked Harry for a photograph. Dracina mocked Harry for giving out signed pictures, and Lockhart seized the moment for a double portrait. In Defence Against the Dark Arts Lockhart set a quiz about himself, then let loose Cornish pixies he could not control. Harry beat four of them off Dracina. Lockhart left Harry, Ron and Hermione to clear up. Afterwards Dracina sat alone in the wrecked classroom, writing in a small black book.

Chapter 8Some Pretty Thing

Over the next few days Harry dodged Lockhart and was followed everywhere by Colin Creevey, whom he came to like. Ron's wand struck Professor Flitwick and raised a boil. On Saturday Oliver Wood woke Harry at dawn for practice. But the Slytherin team arrived with a note from Snape, and their new Seeker turned out to be Dracina Malfoy. Her father had given the team seven Nimbus Two Thousand and Ones. When Harry asked whether 'some pretty thing' could make up for talent, Dracina blushed and asked whether he thought she was pretty. He said he had meant the brooms, and she thumped him. Hermione stepped in. Dracina called her a Mudblood, and the two girls fought until Harry pulled Dracina away. Ron's attempt to curse Dracina backfired, and he began belching slugs. At Hagrid's hut Ron explained the insult, and the idea of Squibs. Harry urged that all witches and wizards should stand together, whatever their blood. Hermione pledged herself to him, while Hagrid and Ron quietly understood that there was a rivalry over Harry. McGonagall gave out the detentions: Ron would polish trophies with Filch, and Harry would answer Lockhart's fan mail. During his detention Harry heard a cold voice threatening to rip, tear and kill, which Lockhart could not hear.

Chapter 9Black Candles and Horses

October 1992 brought a cold that went round the castle, and Percy forced Pepperup Potion on a peaky Ginny. Harry noticed that Dracina Malfoy looked pale and sleepless. She was writing in a small black book, and seemed to be reading replies. A few days before Hallowe'en, Nearly Headless Nick told Harry that he had been refused entry to the Headless Hunt yet again, and that Dracina had offered him mocking condolences. Filch caught Harry dripping mud and took him to his office, where Harry saw a Kwikspell correspondence course. Then Nick arranged for Peeves to crash a cabinet overhead as a distraction, and Harry got away unpunished. In gratitude Harry agreed to come to Nick's five hundredth Deathday Party, to Hermione's delight and Ron's dismay. On Hallowe'en evening Harry glimpsed Dracina running alone up the marble staircase. At the party the three of them met Brother Aldric, Moaning Myrtle and Peeves. Harry defended Nick in front of everyone against Sir Patrick Delaney-Podmore. As they were leaving, Harry heard the murderous voice again and followed it to the second floor. There they found a message announcing that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened, with Mrs Norris hanging stiff beneath it. Dracina pushed to the front of the gathering crowd and taunted Hermione. Nobody noticed the red stain on her finger. When Harry shielded Hermione, Dracina left muttering under her breath. The only word Harry caught was the last one, 'Mine'.

Chapter 10The Horror Within a Fairy Tale

On Hallowe'en night 1992 Argus Filch found his cat, Mrs Norris, Petrified beneath a message announcing that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened. He accused Harry Potter of killing her. In Gilderoy Lockhart's office Dumbledore examined the cat while Lockhart boasted of curses, African language parasites and a Transylvanian vampire cult. One by one, Professor McGonagall quietly exposed the boasts as lies. She shared a knowing look with Harry, and a wink. Dumbledore declared that Mrs Norris was Petrified, not dead. He took twenty points from Gryffindor after Harry mocked Filch's parentage, refused Snape's suggestion that Harry be dropped from the Quidditch team, and promised a Mandrake cure. Dracina Malfoy waited alone on the stairs to ask whether Harry was hurt. She told him off for standing in front of Hermione as though Dracina were a dragon. Over the following days Ginny Weasley grew distraught, and Justin Finch-Fletchley began avoiding Harry. Dracina tormented Hermione in Potions, then wrote in a small black book and read its reply. Hermione explained to Harry the warring magical cultures of early medieval Britain. She also persuaded Professor Binns to recount the legend of Slytherin's Chamber and its monster. Investigating the corridor, the three of them found scorch marks, fleeing spiders and Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. Percy Weasley took five points from Ron for being there. That night Hermione, convinced that Dracina was the Heir of Slytherin, proposed brewing Polyjuice Potion so that they could question her in the Slytherin common room. Harry guessed which teacher would sign for the recipe.

Chapter 11Rather Like a Princess

After Lockhart had let Cornish pixies loose on his class, Professor McGonagall forbade him in public to bring any creature into a classroom without her written permission. So he turned his lessons into re-enactments of his own exploits, with Harry as his prop. Hermione punctured his story of fighting the vampire called the Master: the Master, she pointed out, had been sealed beneath a Californian town since 1937. Her faith in Lockhart began to fail, though she still flattered him into signing a note for Moste Potente Potions. Dracina confronted Hermione in the library, and went white when Hermione claimed Harry as her own. The three of them studied the Polyjuice recipe in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. McGonagall privately taught Harry the truth about werewolves, the Garou and the Delirium. At the Gryffindor match against Slytherin, Dean Thomas led a mocking terrace chant. A rogue Bludger hunted Harry. Dracina, by turns taunting, jealous of Hermione and tender, threw her broom in front of the Bludger to shield him. With his right elbow broken, Harry caught the Snitch from just above Dracina's head and crashed into the mud. Then Lockhart removed every bone from his arm. While Madam Pomfrey regrew them with Skele-Gro, a girl who gave no name left sugared violets and a note. Harry assumed they came from Ginny. In the night Dobby came. He admitted that he had sealed the barrier at King's Cross and bewitched the Bludger. He also let slip that the Chamber had been opened before. Then Dumbledore and McGonagall brought in the Petrified Colin Creevey, whose camera had melted inside. Dumbledore declared that the Chamber had been opened once more.

Chapter 12I'll Make You See

Leaving the hospital wing, Harry found Dracina waiting for him, haggard and ink-stained, to see whether his arm had healed. She muttered that someone had said, wrongly, that he would never fly again. Ron and Hermione had begun brewing the Polyjuice Potion in Myrtle's bathroom. Harry told them about Dobby's visit and Colin's Petrification. As panic spread, Dracina asked Ginny, 'Do you love him?', without saying whom she meant. She talked to an invisible Tom at dinner, and signed up to stay at Hogwarts for Christmas, telling McGonagall that she had the most wonderful dreams. In Potions she stirred Harry's Swelling Solution for him while Hermione growled. Harry's firework in Goyle's cauldron covered Hermione's theft of Boomslang skin and Bicorn horn from Snape's stores. At the new Duelling Club Snape paired Harry with Dracina. Their duel went far beyond disarming, until Dracina, exhausted and desperate, conjured a snake with Serpensortia. When Lockhart's bungling sent the snake at Justin Finch-Fletchley, Harry ordered it away in Parseltongue. Dracina gazed at him in rapture, whispering that it was him and always had been. Ron and Hermione explained that Parseltongue was Slytherin's famous gift. The school concluded that Harry was the Heir. The next day Ernie Macmillan accused him in the library. Then Harry, after hearing a girl singing a lullaby in a dark corridor, found Justin and Nearly Headless Nick Petrified. Peeves raised the alarm, and McGonagall took Harry to Dumbledore's office.

Chapter 13Interlude: Precisely When He Means To

On the night of the Duelling Club an old man in grey, who went at present by the name of Ambrose Greyhame, walked up from Hogsmeade with the first snow. He carried a long package wrapped in oilcloth. He remembered helping four quarrelsome young people to found Hogwarts more than a thousand years before. Long before that, he had been sent by the One beyond the golden gates to teach magic to the first frightened families after a great meltwater flood. Unseen, he watched Harry and Dracina duel. In Harry he saw the look of an old friend; in Dracina, the eyes of a prince of the forest folk. He sensed, too, a cold, whispering thing fastened over Dracina's heart, made in the same way as a gold ring he had once known. Peeves fled from him, and the Grey Lady recognised him from her mother's house. He waited all night in Dumbledore's office while Dumbledore was at the Ministry with Cornelius Fudge. The next morning the two old friends talked of the six summers Ambrose had spent teaching the young Albus staff magic, and of Greta Grindelwald, whom Dumbledore still loved. Ambrose handed over the package, a thing once used by Godric that had been broken and remade long ago. Dumbledore confessed his guilt over leaving Harry with the Dursleys. Ambrose insisted that the protection Harry's mother had given him must hold. He warned that Tom Riddle was only a leaf on a far older tree, planted by an ancient enemy. Then he vanished, leaving a smoke-ring ship sailing west. Dumbledore hid the package inside the Sorting Hat just as Justin's attack was discovered and Harry was brought upstairs.

Chapter 14A Yearning for Polyjuice

Left alone in Dumbledore's office, Harry noticed a Muggle portrait of a bald, blue-skinned man in golden armour. Then he put on the Sorting Hat. It told him that Salazar Slytherin had never been evil, and that Harry's mind reminded it most of Slytherin's. Fawkes burst into flame and was reborn. Hagrid stormed in to protest Harry's innocence. Dumbledore said he did not believe Harry guilty, though Harry kept back everything he knew. Panic sent most students home for Christmas. Fred and George mocked the idea of Harry as Heir. Dracina told the school, then Harry himself, that she knew he was the Heir and was on his side. Hermione grew pale and fixated. She muttered in her sleep. After a snowball fight on Christmas Eve, watched from a high window by a lonely fair-haired girl, Harry opened his presents, and Hermione declared the potion ready. That evening the boys drugged Crabbe and Goyle with cakes full of Sleeping Draught. Then Harry, as Goyle, and Ron, as Crabbe, followed Dracina into the Slytherin common room. Hermione had to stay behind, because the hair she had used turned out to be a cat's. Dracina, gravely ill, confided her lost hours, the red on her hands and the comfort of Tom in her diary. She told them of the Ministry raid on Malfoy Manor, and of her father's hints about the last opening of the Chamber, fifty years before. When Pansy mocked Harry, Dracina broke down sobbing, babbling of bars on a window and a house-elf who had misread her order to warn him. Harry took the abandoned diary. It was blank but for a faded name beginning with T and a date fifty years old. He resisted an urge to write in it, and locked it in his trunk.

Chapter 15What's Underneath

On Boxing Day 1992 Madam Pomfrey turned Harry and Ron away from the hospital wing, where Hermione was recovering from her cat-hair Polyjuice transformation. Harry, meanwhile, found himself constantly drawn to Tom Riddle's diary, which he had hidden in his trunk. Without the diary, Dracina Malfoy ransacked the Slytherin dungeon. Then she burst into the Great Hall barefoot, raving that a thief had taken her 'precious'. She scratched a Hufflepuff prefect and beat Harry with her fists. At last Dumbledore calmed her with a touch, and announced that she had Morrigan's Fever. Harry wrote in the diary. It answered him, knew his name and asked whether he had noticed 'what's underneath' Dracina's hostility. When Harry visited Dracina in the hospital wing, she taunted him that the Dursleys starved him. Ron found him afterwards on the Astronomy Tower, and promised that he would spend the summer at the Burrow. Hermione, recovering, admitted that the Polyjuice plan had become a personal crusade against Dracina. She resolved to be 'less a lot', and turned against Lockhart. Moaning Myrtle told them that a posh girl had searched her bathroom at night and whispered at the sinks. Ron caught Harry with the diary and recognised Riddle's name from a trophy. He urged Harry to give it to Dumbledore, which Harry silently decided not to do. After Hermione came back in February, spells failed to reveal what was in the diary, but the three of them found Riddle's name among the Head Boys. On Valentine's Day Lockhart's dwarfs sang Harry two Valentines on the stairs. Dracina briefly got hold of the fallen diary before Percy returned it to Harry. She then savaged Ginny for writing the second song. That night the diary drew Harry into Riddle's memory of 13 June 1943. In it the sixteen-year-old Riddle confronted the young Hagrid over a monster in a box. Harry concluded that Hagrid had opened the Chamber fifty years before.

Chapter 16Whoever Took It

Harry, Ron and Hermione argued over whether Hagrid could be the heir of Slytherin. Harry felt that only Tom Riddle could understand his life with the Dursleys, but he resisted the urge to confide in the diary. Months passed without an attack, while Dracina sickened, grey and silent. At Easter the second-years chose their subjects for the third year. On the eve of the Hufflepuff match Harry's dormitory was ransacked. The diary had been stolen, along with his match scarf. Neville behaved guiltily. Harry realised that his craving for the diary had not been wholly his own. The next morning Dracina appeared radiant and healthy. A pale, ink-stained Ginny tried to tell Harry that she had seen somebody the night before, until Percy interrupted. Harry heard the voice in the walls again, and Hermione ran off to the library. McGonagall then cancelled the match. Hermione and the Ravenclaw prefect Penelope Clearwater, she told them, had been Petrified near the library, with a mirror beside them. Dracina appeared at the door of the hospital wing to offer flat condolences. Harry, sure that she was guilty, punched a wall. Under the strict new rules, Harry and Ron went under the Invisibility Cloak to Hagrid's hut. There Cornelius Fudge took Hagrid off to Azkaban, and Lucius Malfoy delivered an Order of Suspension removing Dumbledore. Dumbledore declared that he would not truly be gone while anyone kept faith with him. Hagrid told the hidden boys to follow the spiders and to feed Fang. Harry's fury set off a burst of accidental magic, until Ron talked him down.

Chapter 17Total Spider Death

With Dumbledore and Hagrid gone, fear settled over Hogwarts. Dracina strutted about the castle, taunting Harry that being locked in and counted must feel like home. Ron reassured Harry that he belonged at the Burrow. Dracina pointedly thanked Neville for being 'such a help'. Percy caught Ginny alone on the second floor, where she claimed to have been 'following' something. In Potions, nearly a month after Dumbledore's suspension, Snape rebuked Dracina in front of the class, in a low, cold voice, for speaking of McGonagall without respect. Later in the lesson Dracina said it was a pity Hermione had not been killed, and Ron held Harry back. When she went on to mock Ginny, Ron had to be held back himself. In Herbology Ernie Macmillan apologised to Harry. Asked whether Dracina was the heir, Harry could only answer 'Maybe'. A line of spiders was seen heading for the Forbidden Forest. That night Harry and Ron took Fang into the Forest. There they met Mr Weasley's Ford Anglia, which had gone feral, before giant spiders carried them off to the hollow of the blind Aragog. Aragog told them that he had never been the monster of the Chamber, and that the girl killed fifty years earlier had been found in a bathroom. Spiders feared the creature too much to name it, he said. Then he gave the boys to his children for food. The car crashed into the hollow and rescued them. Back in bed, Harry realised that the dead girl might still be in her bathroom, as Moaning Myrtle.

Chapter 18Faith Managed

McGonagall announced that the exams would begin on 1 June 1993, with an allusion to friends of hers who had been eaten by Nephilim when she was young. Three days before the exams she announced that the Mandrakes were ready. Ginny again tried to confide in Harry and Ron, but Percy interrupted her. Caught slipping away towards Myrtle's bathroom, Harry disarmed McGonagall's anger with sarcasm. She let him visit Hermione. She also warned him never to go after the creature alone, citing her own encounters with Garou, Wraiths and William the Bloody. In Hermione's fist Harry found a page on the Basilisk with the word 'Pipes' written on it. From it he worked out how the monster moved about, and why its victims had survived. Hidden in a wardrobe in the staff room, he and Ron heard that Ginny had been taken into the Chamber. A Slytherin girl was missing too. The teachers sent Lockhart to face the monster. Finding Lockhart packing to run away, Harry disarmed him. Myrtle described her death, and Harry opened the entrance in the sink with Parseltongue. In the tunnel Lockhart's Memory Charm backfired through Ron's broken wand and brought down the roof. Harry went on alone. In the Chamber he found Dracina collapsing in his stolen scarf, Ginny bleeding, and Tom Riddle's memory taking solid form. Riddle explained Lucius Malfoy's plot, how he had possessed Dracina, and his own plans, then revealed himself as Lord Voldemort. Harry refused Riddle's offer of revenge on the Dursleys, and called him a fraud like Lockhart. The Basilisk was set on him, and its fang caught his arm. But a warm presence and a fatherly voice saved him. Fawkes brought the Sorting Hat, and from it Harry drew an ancient sword. Harry withstood the Basilisk's stare, beheaded it while he stood over Dracina, and destroyed the diary. Then the venom took hold again. He collapsed in Dracina's arms, while a man in white watched him with pride.

Chapter 19The Sign of the Cross

Harry woke unharmed, with his head in Dracina's lap. She healed Ginny's cut. Fawkes carried them up the pipe, with Ron and the memoryless Lockhart. The Weasleys were waiting in McGonagall's office, and so was Dumbledore, who had returned. Harry told the story but left out Dracina's part in it. Dumbledore and Ginny both shielded her. When Dracina broke down and confessed, Harry's hand on her shoulder silenced her. Dumbledore cleared both girls of blame. He awarded Harry and Ron Special Awards for Services to the School, with two hundred points each. He told Harry that his Parseltongue came from Voldemort, that choices define a person, and that the sword was an ancient blade once called the Sword of Gryffindor. Lucius Malfoy arrived with Dobby, and Dumbledore exposed his plot. Harry tricked Lucius into freeing Dobby with a sock. In a private exchange Lucius admitted that he had been 'instructed'. He laughed at Harry's mockery of Voldemort, and said that he was beginning to see what Dracina saw in Harry. In the hospital wing Harry and Dracina agreed to be friends. They found that both of them had seen the man in white; Harry wondered whether he might be Jesus Christ. Molly Weasley warned Dracina never to break Harry's heart. At the feast Hermione was revived. She privately resolved to be Harry's best friend until the time came to deal with Dracina. Hagrid came back, Gryffindor won the House Cup and the exams were cancelled. At the end of term Dumbledore told Harry that he must go back to Privet Drive. Lily Potter's protection, the magic of Elves and of Númenor, lived on in his aunt's blood. Dumbledore had also seen to it in person that the Dursleys would never harm Harry again. On the train Ginny revealed that Percy was secretly going out with Penelope Clearwater. At King's Cross Harry made the sign of the Cross for the first time.

How it differs from the original

  • Lucius always meant the diary for Ginny, but Dracina swept it into her own bag at Flourish and Blotts in a temper, and he did not know his daughter had it.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is possessed by Riddle; she opens the Chamber, sets the Basilisk on Muggle-borns and writes on the walls without remembering.
  • Riddle petrifies Hermione deliberately as a gift to Dracina.
  • Both Dracina and Ginny are taken into the Chamber; Riddle drains Ginny instead of Dracina.
  • The diary passes from Dracina to Harry, who steals it while Polyjuiced as Goyle, and back to Dracina when Neville lets her into Gryffindor Tower.
  • Dracina is never punished; Dumbledore covers her breakdown as Morrigan's Fever, and Ginny covers for her.
  • Dracina sent Dobby to warn Harry, and Dobby told her about the bars, cupboard and bread.
  • Harry is rescued from Privet Drive in a far worse state, starved behind bars, and collapses at the Burrow; Molly takes him in and writes to Dumbledore condemning him.
  • The Burrow clock has one hand and no numbers, and the Weasleys keep a ghoul fed on gnomes.
  • Hermione is obsessed with vampire lore from Lockhart's books and catches him out over the Master.
  • Dracina sends Harry anonymous sugared violets in the hospital wing, and he assumes Ginny sent them.
  • Harry receives two singing Valentines, Dracina's and Ginny's, and Lockhart winks at Harry and Dracina.
  • Harry's detention is Lockhart's fan mail and Ron's the trophy room.
  • A wholly new Interlude has Ambrose Greyhame, implied to be Gandalf and Merlin, visit Dumbledore.
  • The sword from the Hat is not Gryffindor's by origin, but an older blade broken and reforged.
  • Harry is bitten, dies briefly, and is healed by a voice in the dark before Fawkes arrives; a man in white, Jesus Christ, watches by a pillar and Dracina sees him too.
  • Lucius ends the book half-liking Harry.
  • Dumbledore personally visits Privet Drive and threatens the Dursleys.
  • Hermione and Dracina each resolve to deal with the other, and Molly threatens to kill Dracina slowly if she hurts Harry.
  • Harry makes the sign of the Cross on the last page.
  • Harry baits the Dursleys on purpose, and calls them 'malignant'.
  • Harry keeps thinking about Dracina Malfoy, and the twinkle in her eyes.
  • Harry threatens to turn the hedge into an Ent, instead of setting it on fire.
  • Dobby says his Mistress wanted Harry to be warned.
  • Harry calls Dobby 'mate' and threatens him. He vows to kill Dobby.
  • Dracina appears in Harry's dream of the zoo.
  • Harry fights Vernon off in a rage, and hurls insults at him as they fly away.
  • Ron learns that Harry was starved, and Harry hints at the cupboard.
  • Percy's odd behaviour is tied to a statue Charlie gave him, which Molly confiscated.
  • The cursed tea set once belonged to a French nobleman who had himself been under a curse, and to his peasant wife.
  • A wholly new chapter, in which Harry tells Molly Weasley about his abuse and she comforts him.
  • Molly invites Harry to stay for as long as he wants.
  • Dracina and Lucius appear in Borgin and Burkes, not Draco. Lucius warns her about seeming obsessed with Harry, and mutters about 'Cissy'.
  • Ginny stands up to Dracina, and the two girls fight over the books.
  • Dracina, not Lucius, handles the books, and keeps a small black book for herself.
  • Hermione is jealous at the idea of Dracina talking about Harry.
  • Molly writes to Dumbledore to tell him, in terms that leave no room for argument, where Harry will live from now on. She also condemns his decision to leave Harry with the Dursleys.
  • Ginny has a diary of her own, which she leaves on her bed.
  • Ron now distrusts Dumbledore, while Harry reveres him.
  • The fight with the Whomping Willow is longer, and Ron saves Harry.
  • Hermione's book describes vampires and vampire hunters who never appear in the original.
  • McGonagall hints at past work alongside a Scottish Muggle agent.
  • Harry rescues Dracina from the pixies, and she writes in a small black book.
  • Dracina is the Slytherin Seeker, and the 'pretty thing' exchange is new.
  • Hermione and Dracina come to blows on the pitch.
  • Harry makes a speech about wizarding unity, and Hermione pledges herself to him.
  • Dracina shows signs of the black book's influence, and it is implied that she painted the message.
  • Harry openly tells Sir Patrick to leave, and defends Nick.
  • Hermione interviews ghosts such as Brother Aldric, and clings to Harry at the scene.
  • Dracina whispers, 'Mine.'
  • McGonagall openly catches Lockhart in one lie after another during the inquiry over Mrs Norris.
  • Harry, not Ron, makes the cutting remark about Filch's birth. He loses twenty points and apologises.
  • Dracina carries the black diary and writes in it. She waits on the stairs to make sure that Harry is unhurt.
  • Hermione writes Harry's essays for him, and pushes the Polyjuice plan out of personal animosity towards Dracina.
  • Hogwarts is dated to 990, and Hermione describes four rival magical cultures of early medieval Britain.
  • McGonagall bans Lockhart from bringing creatures into lessons after the business with the pixies.
  • Lockhart's anecdotes take in vampires, the Master, Angelus and the Slayer. Hermione exposes him in class.
  • McGonagall teaches Harry practical werewolf lore, and warns him about the Garou.
  • Dean Thomas leads football chants from the Gryffindor stand.
  • Dracina blocks the Bludger on purpose to protect Harry, and secretly leaves him sugared violets.
  • Dobby says that his mistress gave him an order, then punished him over the barrier.
  • Dracina, plainly under the diary's influence, holds the place that Ginny holds in the original.
  • Snape pairs Harry with Dracina. She casts Serpensortia after a far more violent duel.
  • Snape turns grey with recognition as he watches Dracina, and mutters about a foolish girl.
  • Dracina asks Ginny whether she loves him, without saying whom she means, and records it in the diary.
  • Harry hears a girl singing a lullaby just before he finds Justin and Nick.
  • A wholly original chapter, in which Gandalf visits Hogwarts as Ambrose Greyhame.
  • Gandalf is revealed as the guide who brought the four founders together. He also taught Dumbledore and Grindelwald staff magic.
  • Grindelwald is a woman, Greta, whom Dumbledore loved.
  • Gryffindor's sword is brought to Hogwarts from outside and hidden in the Sorting Hat.
  • A portrait, implied to be of Zordon, hangs in Dumbledore's office.
  • The Sorting Hat defends Salazar Slytherin at length.
  • Dracina believes Harry is the Heir. She is sick and losing time because of the diary.
  • Harry takes the diary from the Slytherin common room, instead of finding it in Myrtle's bathroom.
  • Dracina's order to Dobby was to warn Harry, and Dobby misread it.
  • Dracina Malfoy, not Ginny Weasley, has been writing in the diary. Her withdrawal from it brings on a public breakdown, which Dumbledore covers up as 'Morrigan's Fever'.
  • The diary talks to Harry about Dracina, and urges him to be kinder to her.
  • Hermione comes out of her Polyjuice mishap humbled, and resolves to change her ways.
  • The first singing Valentine is implied to be Dracina's. Percy, not Harry, gets the diary back from her.
  • The diary is stolen back by Dracina, with Neville's help, not by Ginny.
  • Ginny is shown trying to warn Harry about what she has seen, not confessing her own guilt.
  • Harry's rage in Hagrid's hut sets off accidental magic.
  • Snape publicly rebukes Dracina for disrespecting McGonagall.
  • Dracina thanks Neville, which hints at his part in the theft.
  • The narration states that God brightened the moon for Harry at the moment of his realisation.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is the possessed girl lying in the Chamber; Ginny was taken after tracking her.
  • McGonagall reveals a past spent fighting Garou, Wraiths and William the Bloody.
  • Riddle speaks of a 'union' between the bloodlines of Potter and Malfoy. He speaks too of Lily Potter's ancient lineage.
  • The sword is neither jewelled nor named, and bursts into white fire. Harry is saved by a divine presence, not by phoenix tears.
  • A man in white, later suggested to be Jesus Christ, appears in the Chamber.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is the one cleared and comforted. Harry and Dracina become friends.
  • Lucius Malfoy reveals that he was coerced, laughs at Harry, and leaves with grudging respect.
  • Dumbledore puts Lily Potter's protection down to the magic of Elves and Númenor. He has also confronted the Dursleys himself.
  • Harry is sent back to Privet Drive in spite of the Weasleys' offer, and the book ends with him making the sign of the Cross.

Characters introduced

  • Aragog
  • Colin Creevey
  • Cornelius Fudge
  • Dobby
  • Fawkes
  • Gandalf
  • Gilderoy Lockhart
  • God
  • Jesus Christ
  • Marjorie Dursley
  • Moaning Myrtle

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl

Book Three of the Malfoid Saga · 1993 to 1994 · Complete

Read Book ThreeFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

InterludeThe Morgoth in the Details

On a rainy night in the summer of 1993, the night Harry Potter fled Privet Drive, John Constantine flagged down the Knight Bus in Liverpool. In a Tesco carrier bag he had a D'ni linking book marked Myst. The conductor, Stan Shunpike, kept stopping him from smoking. Constantine thought back to 1985, when he had stolen Dumbledore's Deluminator to defeat a demon that fed on light. Dumbledore was still livid about it. Now a letter had come from him in green ink, demanding that Constantine fetch the book from Ephraim Shacklewell in New Mexico. In memory he went back over his years at Hogwarts. They began in 1964, when he made friends with a stammering Lucius Malfoy before both of them were sorted into Slytherin. As a Muggle-born he was bullied relentlessly. He took clever revenges, he cheated, and he watched Lucius drift towards the future Death Eaters. It all ended in their seventh year, in a duel and then a fistfight over a Ravenclaw girl. He remembered burgling Shacklewell House without his wand. He had used salt, chalk, the seal of Andromalius, a backwards Lord's Prayer and a Hand of Glory. When the book fell open he had nearly been drawn into it. He had bluffed the sleepless Shacklewell with an enchanted library card, along with a receipt signed J. Lennon. On the bus he watched a boy get on at Magnolia Crescent who claimed to be Neville Longbottom. Constantine recognised the signs of abuse in him. He saw the Minister for Magic meet the boy at the Leaky Cauldron. There the boy, who was Harry Potter, called himself Barry Trotter. At a nearly empty Hogwarts Hagrid greeted Constantine joyfully, and the password Acid Pop let him into Dumbledore's office. Dumbledore had been expecting him. He lost his temper and began to echo Greta Grindelwald's words about the greater good. Then he stopped, horrified, and confessed his own regrets. He explained that the book belonged to a very old acquaintance, who had written it. A second small leather book led from that writer's island back to this world. As for the burglary, Dumbledore called it a kindness.

Chapter 1The Man Outside the Church

By late July 1993, five weeks into the summer after his second year, Harry Potter had noticed that the Dursleys had stopped hitting him. Every evening, after a strange twitch that seized both of them at once, they set a plate for him at dinner. It was the work of a visit Albus Dumbledore had paid to Privet Drive, though nobody had explained it to Harry. Harry brooded over the Chamber of Secrets. A voice there had told him that his work was not yet done, and he had seen a man in a white robe by a fallen pillar. Dracina Malfoy had seen the man too, and Harry was almost sure he had been Jesus Christ. Dumbledore had said that his mother's protection was the magic of Elves and of Númenor, so Harry was reading Dudley's unwanted copy of The Lord of the Rings. Ron had telephoned early in the holidays and been bellowed at by Uncle Vernon; nobody had written since. On his fourth visit to St Michael's Church in Magnolia Crescent, Harry met a very tall old man on the bench by the lych-gate, who had been counting his visits. The old man told him the door was open. When Harry looked back, he was gone. At midnight on 31 July Harry turned thirteen, and four owls arrived. Hedwig brought Hermione's present from Brittany, a Broomstick Servicing Kit. Errol brought Ron's Pocket Sneakoscope, with a cutting from the Daily Prophet about the Weasleys winning seven hundred Galleons and going to Egypt. A school owl brought Hagrid's present, a Monster Book of Monsters that bit, along with the Hogsmeade permission form. Last came Ganymede, Narcissa Malfoy's eagle owl, carrying a scented letter from Dracina tied with a green ribbon. The letter denied any affection whatever and promised Harry a present in person. It let slip that Lucius had forbidden her to have anything to do with him, and that Narcissa had helped her all the same. It also offered, should Uncle Vernon have been mistreating Harry, to try a few items from her father's cellar collection on him. Harry kept the ribbon in his pyjama pocket. For the first time in his life, he was glad it was his birthday.

Chapter 2Blood of Elves, Rage of Man

On the morning of 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' new kitchen television carried the news of Sirius Black's escape. It also reported that New Delhi had fallen to Khan Noonien Singh, the genetically engineered warlord. Neither the Avengers nor the Justice League would intervene without a mandate from the United Nations. Uncle Vernon announced that his sister Marge was coming to stay for a week, and that Harry was to pretend he attended St Brutus's Secure Centre for Incurably Criminal Boys. Then a British National Party membership card fell out of Uncle Vernon's wallet. Harry blackmailed him with it, threatening to reveal it unless Vernon agreed to sign his Hogsmeade form. Vernon agreed, visibly choking back his rage, and muttered about Dumbledore's threats. Harry sent Hedwig off to Egypt with Errol. Dudley, meanwhile, watched the Power Rangers fight a giant creature in Birmingham with rapt admiration. Aunt Marge arrived ranting about immigrants. Harry played the part of a dull-witted boy who said 'nuffink'. On the second night he overheard Vernon and Petunia whispering. Dumbledore, it seemed, had sat on their sofa and promised that he would know the moment they used a hand or a word against Harry. When Marge compared Lily to a defective bitch in dog breeding, Harry's anger made her wineglass explode. On the last evening she called James an unemployed drunk who had died in a car crash, and Harry's rage inflated her until she floated up against the ceiling. Harry grabbed his things. He held Uncle Vernon off at wandpoint, while Aunt Petunia begged her husband not to move. Then he walked out of the house, hating Muggles.

Chapter 3The Dog in the Dark

Harry dragged his trunk as far as Magnolia Crescent, furious with the Dursleys, with Marge, with Muggles and with himself. Then it came to him that the Ministry would snap his wand, and he panicked. He was searching for his Invisibility Cloak, meaning to fly to London, when he sensed that something was there. He lit his wand. An enormous black dog was standing in a gap between a garage and a fence. Harry fell backwards into the gutter, and the Knight Bus very nearly ran him over. He gave the conductor, Stan Shunpike, the name Neville Longbottom. All night he rode through the dark, past a dishevelled Liverpudlian in a raincoat who was guarding a glowing book in a carrier bag. In the Daily Prophet he read that twelve years earlier Sirius Black had killed thirteen people with a single curse. At the Leaky Cauldron Cornelius Fudge was waiting for him. Over tea and crumpets the Minister told him that Marge had been punctured. Her memory had been modified, and Harry, Fudge insisted, would not be punished. He gave Harry room eleven, on condition that he stayed in Diagon Alley and was back indoors before dark. Harry flattered him with a technique he had copied from Hermione, but it did him no good: Fudge refused to sign his Hogsmeade form. Harry realised afterwards that he had been expertly handled. Hedwig was waiting in his room. She had arrived only minutes after he had.

Chapter 4Two Parts of Himself

Harry spent the rest of August at the Leaky Cauldron, wrestling all the while with a growing anger at Muggles. In the end he decided that there were two of him: an angry boy from the cupboard and a boy from the Chamber who wanted to protect good things. Tom the landlord warned him that grudges weigh on the one who carries them. Florean Fortescue told him that most witch-burners had simply been frightened people. Harry admired the new Firebolt without buying it, and Madam Malkin measured him for robes. A black dog on the cover of a book of death omens chilled him. Near Knockturn Alley he met Lucius Malfoy, who complained that Dracina talked about Harry incessantly. When Lucius heard what Marge had said of Lily, his anger turned to cold menace. It turned out that he had never heard of Khan, Superman or Spider-Man. This convinced Harry that the wizarding world had no idea superhumans existed. Lucius urged him to stop living as though he were a Muggle, and Harry found himself nodding. Then he argued back that Muggle heroes saved people, just as he had gone down the pipe for Dracina. Lucius flared with anger. After that, fear crossed his face, followed by a sly grin. Harry had begun to doubt his vision of Christ. Then he found The Lord of the Rings lying in his trunk in a ray of sunlight, and began to read it properly. On 31 August he was reunited with Ron and Hermione. Hermione bought Crookshanks, and the Weasleys arrived. That night Harry overheard Arthur Weasley telling his wife that Sirius Black had escaped to kill him.

Chapter 5A Long, Slow Breath

On 1 September 1993 Ministry cars drove the Weasleys, Harry and Hermione to King's Cross. There Mr Weasley made Harry promise not to go looking for Sirius Black. Harry, Ron and Hermione shared a compartment with a sleeping Professor R. J. Lupin, whose presence unsettled Crookshanks. Dracina Malfoy turned up with Crabbe and Goyle behind her. She insulted Ron for form's sake, then signalled silently to Harry that it was all an act. In private she relished their secret and burned with jealousy of Hermione. She meant to arrange matters, one careful step at a time, until Harry looked up one day to find that what he wanted had been beside him all along. When a Dementor boarded the stopped train, Harry collapsed, hearing screams. Hermione held him. Lupin drove the creature off and handed round chocolate. At the carriages Dracina pressed a box into Harry's hands, and Lupin noticed her with interest. Professor McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey looked Harry over in an office that held a horrible stuffed creature. Hermione had a private word with McGonagall about her timetable. At the feast Dumbledore announced that Dementors were stationed at every entrance to the grounds. He also announced two appointments: Lupin to teach Defence Against the Dark Arts, and Hagrid to teach Care of Magical Creatures. Ron sat silently resenting Dumbledore for sending Harry back to the Dursleys. In bed Harry opened Dracina's box. Inside were a dozen chocolate violets, decorated by hand, with a card that read 'Not from Ginny'.

Chapter 6The Knight and the Hippogriff

At breakfast on 2 September 1993 Dracina mocked Harry's faint for the benefit of the Slytherins, but the joke went out of her the moment she saw him. Fred and George then told Harry that she had burst into their compartment during the Dementor attack, demanding that somebody fetch him. She went on to mimic Hermione, and implied that Hermione's people had stolen their magic. Sir Cadogan, after a comic exchange with Harry, guided the three of them to Professor Trelawney's tower. There Harry asked whether signs could be sent by somebody, and was mocked for his Muggle superstition. Hermione defended him. Then Trelawney saw the Grim in his teacup. McGonagall waved away Trelawney's annual death predictions. Ron and Hermione quarrelled over Grims, then over Arithmancy. In Care of Magical Creatures, Dracina's hair ribbons had mysteriously turned Gryffindor scarlet and gold. Harry bowed to the hippogriff Buckbeak and rode him over the lake. Buckbeak slashed Dracina's arm when she insulted him. Harry caught her. At her demand he nearly drew his wand on Buckbeak, until Hagrid stopped him.
