That evening Hermione explained why the wizarding world hated Christianity. The three of them found Hagrid drunk and despairing. Lupin watched them as they walked back up to the castle. Harry sneaked off to the hospital wing to rebuke Dracina for her cruelty. The rebuke provoked a furious, tearful outburst about Hermione and his indifference. Madam Pomfrey threw him out. Afterwards Dracina resolved to have her father ruin Hagrid and Buckbeak.

Chapter 7It Came Out of the Wardrobe

Dracina Malfoy spent a week in the hospital wing after Buckbeak's attack. Harry hovered outside the door, unable to decide how to apologise. She came back for double Potions on a Thursday, with her arm in a black silk sling, and sat down beside him. She had Harry prepare her Shrinking Solution, passing on potion tricks wrapped in insults, until he snapped that they could not be friends while she abused his friends. Their quarrel boiled both cauldrons over. Snape quelled them, docked both houses ten points and warned them that friendships had ended over a single word. Dracina apologised. She said she had decided not to send a four-page complaint to her father after all. When Seamus reported a Muggle sighting of Sirius Black, Dracina urged Harry to hunt Black down himself. After the lesson her heirloom serpent brooch went missing. For a short while nobody knew where Hermione was. When she reappeared she smelt of dittany. Then she dropped something silver and green. The brooch turned up on Peeves's bow tie, where it stayed until Lupin's Waddiwasi sent it flying into a fire bucket. In the staffroom Lupin introduced the class to a boggart. Neville dressed the boggart Snape in his grandmother's clothes. Dracina's boggart was her father, telling her that she was always second and not a real Malfoy. It made her weep, before she defied it and turned it into a drunken tramp. Lupin kept the boggart away from Harry. When it came back at Lupin himself, as a vast, blood-soaked werewolf that seemed to know him, he faced it and shrank its legs. Afterwards Hermione and Dracina each seized one of Harry's arms, growling at each other. Harry was left baffled. Ron resolved to keep an eye on both girls.

Chapter 8The Lady Who Wasn't There

Lupin's lessons on Red Caps, kappas and vampires quickly became the most popular in the school. The one on vampires covered the Masquerade, the Sabbat, the clans and the blood bond. It also covered the Camarilla's agreement with the Ministry and the world's other wizarding governments, made in 1900. Dracina began a campaign of public kindness. She helped Neville. She even greeted Ron and Hermione civilly, though Ron noticed that it only ever happened when Harry was looking. Hermione would have none of it. Oliver Wood held a desperate team meeting before his last season, and the first Hogsmeade visit was announced for Halloween. Crookshanks went for Ron's bag to get at Scabbers, which soured things between Ron and Hermione. Hermione also tactlessly questioned Lavender's belief that Professor Trelawney had foretold the death of her rabbit, Binky, on 16 October. In Transfiguration McGonagall described parasites that possess a host along the spine. She revealed that she had once killed one herself, with the help of a man she did not name. Then she refused Harry permission to go to Hogsmeade. On Halloween Dracina silenced Pansy and Daphne's taunts. She told Harry about a quill shop she had meant to show him. Over tea in his office, Lupin learnt that what Harry feared most was the Dementors, and drank a smoking potion that Snape brought him. At the feast Lupin flinched at a moon, nearly full, in the enchanted ceiling. Afterwards Hermione promised Harry that she would try to be nicer to Dracina. When the students got back to Gryffindor Tower, they found the Fat Lady's portrait slashed. Peeves told Dumbledore that Sirius Black had done it. Lupin, meanwhile, stood breathing in the air, as though he recognised a scent.

Chapter 9A Soft Answer

On Halloween night the whole school slept in the Great Hall. Dracina and Hermione bedded down on either side of Harry. Dracina told him that everybody in the castle slept better that night because Dumbledore was awake, while nobody had ever been awake for Harry. She admitted that her own childhood had been pampered. She had begun to confess something about the diary when Percy interrupted. Harry overheard Snape suggest to Dumbledore that Black had had help from inside the castle. Sir Cadogan took the Fat Lady's place. Percy and the staff shadowed Harry. Aunt Petunia wrote to him for the first time in his life, to forbid him to come home for Christmas. In a disused corridor on the fourth floor Harry met a painted man at a smouldering altar, who resented his brother's accepted offering. The painted man told Harry to mind the door-sill. McGonagall restricted Harry's movements but kept his Quidditch practices going under supervision. Hermione began a dogged campaign of courtesy towards Dracina, and Dracina stepped up her own in return. Slytherin pulled out of the opening match, citing Dracina's arm, so Gryffindor had to play Hufflepuff in a storm. On the path Dracina cowed her own team when they hissed at her for laughing with Harry. Hermione told Harry and Ron the history of the vampire Angelus. Snape, covering for Lupin, lectured the class on the Garou and humiliated Hermione. Harry would have had it out with him, but the Fat Friar's story of a shepherd turned aside from vengeance by a soft answer stopped him. At the match Harry glimpsed a huge black dog in the stands. Then more than a hundred Dementors flooded on to the pitch. Harry heard his mother pleading, and fell fifty feet. Dumbledore slowed his fall and drove the Dementors off. Cedric Diggory caught the Snitch. The Whomping Willow smashed Harry's Nimbus. After hours Dracina came to the ward. She had written to her father about the Dementors, she said, and nobody was permitted to kill Harry.

Chapter 10Rain Coming

Harry was kept in the hospital wing, where he refused to give up the splinters of his Nimbus. Hagrid, Ginny and the Quidditch team came to see him. Dracina paid a formal call with her entourage. Throughout it Pansy stared at the bedside table where Dracina's four-page letter had once lain, for it was Pansy herself who had taken the letter to the Owlery. That night Harry dreamt of revenge on the Dursleys. The painted man from the fourth-floor corridor watched him, until a beam of light burnt the watcher away. Back in lessons, Dracina, without her sling now, mimicked a Dementor and Harry's fall in Potions. Ron threw a crocodile heart into her face. Lupin returned. He cancelled Snape's essay, and agreed to teach Harry a defence against the Dementors after the holidays. When Harry described his dream, Lupin nearly lost control of himself. He told Harry to seek God, or at least a priest. Gryffindor's hopes revived when Ravenclaw beat Hufflepuff. Wood drove the team hard, telling Harry that he would be captain one day. Hermione and Dracina both took to watching practices, trading barbs. On the last Hogsmeade weekend before Christmas Fred and George gave Harry the Marauder's Map. He reached Honeydukes by the passage behind the one-eyed witch. In the Three Broomsticks Hermione told him she believed Dracina's attachment to him was possessive, and admitted her own jealousy. Then, hidden behind a Christmas tree, Harry heard McGonagall, Flitwick, Hagrid, Fudge and Madam Rosmerta talking. Sirius Black, they said, had been his father's best friend, his best man and Harry's own godfather. He had betrayed the Potters as their Secret-Keeper. He had handed Hagrid the motorbike that carried Harry away, then killed Peter Pettigrew in a street full of Muggles.

Chapter 11The Best Man

Harry went back to the castle in a daze. He found his parents' wedding photograph, and recognised Sirius Black as the laughing best man. In the dark he resolved to make Black pay. On the last morning of term Ron and Hermione begged him not to go after Black. Ron insisted that the Weasleys were his family, but Harry would not have it, because the blood protection tied him to Privet Drive. He shouted in Dumbledore's defence. Then he broke down, weeping about his childhood, while Hermione held him. When they went down to Hagrid's, they found him distraught over a letter from the Ministry. Lucius Malfoy's complaint had been upheld. Buckbeak was to face the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures on 20 April. Harry concluded that Dracina had lied about dropping her complaint. He threw himself into legal research for Buckbeak's defence. On Christmas morning he received a Weasley jumper and an anonymous Firebolt. Crookshanks went for Scabbers, which set off the Pocket Sneakoscope. At Christmas lunch Trelawney fretted about sitting down thirteen at table. Dumbledore said that Lupin was unwell, though he seemed worried by his absence. McGonagall told the story of a mission in Siberia in 1966, and of the rules taught her by her partner, whom she did not name. Above all, she said, the hard part was learning to put a weapon down. Afterwards Hermione reported the Firebolt to McGonagall, who confiscated it so that it could be tested for jinxes. Hermione told Ron that she believed Sirius Black had sent it.

Chapter 12A Single Happy Thing

Harry refused to speak to Hermione over the confiscated Firebolt. He apologised to Oliver Wood for losing it, and Wood told him that he did not have to carry the whole team on his back. When term began again in January 1994, Lupin started teaching Harry the Patronus Charm in the History of Magic classroom. He used a boggart that turned into a Dementor. The charm, Lupin explained, ran on light derived from God meeting a good soul. Harry privately doubted that he was good. He collapsed twice, hearing first his mother die and then, for the first time, his father. In the end he produced a large silver shield, though it had no shape. Lupin admitted that he had been James's friend and had known Sirius Black. He told Harry that Lily had believed in Christ with all her heart. Prompted by Mrs Weasley's letters, the Weasleys quietly organised themselves to keep watch over Harry. Slytherin beat Ravenclaw, with Dracina as Seeker. A Ministry letter had convinced Harry that she had lied about not sending a complaint about Buckbeak. Four times he tried to confront her, and four times he was stopped by something to do with faith, proof or forgiveness. A Hufflepuff fell through the ice on the lake. Two first-years tested a healed wound. Flitwick shamed Hobday over two Sickles, having secretly paid Hobday's own nine-Galleon debt. A Ravenclaw tested a fleece twice. Harry accepted Dracina's spare broom, a Nimbus Two Thousand and One. Lupin explained the Dementor's Kiss, which the Ministry had licensed for use on Black. Harry said Black deserved it. Lupin urged him to remember that nobody was beyond forgiveness. McGonagall gave back the Firebolt. Harry hugged her, then sent Dracina's broom back to her. He and Ron resolved to make peace with Hermione. Then Ron found that Scabbers had gone. There was blood on his bedsheet, with ginger hairs in it.

Chapter 13What the Hood Was Hiding

Ron and Hermione fell out bitterly over Scabbers. Isolated and overworked, Hermione began to frighten Harry with a cold, patient menace towards anyone who crossed her. At practice Madam Hooch admired the Firebolt. Wood warned them that Ravenclaw's Seeker was Cho Chang. Afterwards Ron had a go on the broom, and Harry mistook Crookshanks's eyes in a tree for the black dog. At breakfast Cedric Diggory apologised for his win in November. Percy let slip a ten-Galleon bet with Penelope Clearwater. Dracina taunted Harry in public, though Harry could see that she was privately frightened for him. In the match in early March Gryffindor were trailing 40 to 10 when Wood called a time-out. In the huddle Harry gave the tactical orders that turned the game round. When three hooded figures appeared below him, he cast a solid Patronus without a moment's hesitation, then caught the Snitch for a win of 230 to 70. The figures were Dracina, Crabbe, Goyle and Marcus Flint, in rigged robes. McGonagall gave them detention, taking fifty points from Slytherin besides. Harry felt betrayed. He turned his back on Dracina, who was plainly guilty. Lupin told him afterwards that his Patronus had been 'bright'. He also said that he recognised Harry's habit of hiding his feelings behind a blank face. At the victory party Harry told Hermione that she had been right about Dracina. Then a careless remark of Ron's sent her away in tears. That night Ron woke to find Sirius Black slashing his bed curtains with a knife, and punched him in the face. Sir Cadogan revealed that he had let Black in because Black had a written list of the week's passwords. Neville had lost it.

Chapter 14What She Deserved

After Black's escape the castle tightened its defences. Sir Cadogan was sacked. The Fat Lady, mended, came back under the guard of security trolls. Neville was banned from Hogsmeade for the rest of his schooling, and his grandmother sent him a Howler. A letter from Lucius Malfoy distressed Dracina. She spent the following week trying to make Harry listen to her, while he ignored her and burnt her notes unread. Hagrid revealed that Buckbeak's hearing had been brought forward at Lucius Malfoy's urging. He reproached Harry and Ron for neglecting Hermione. In his Thursday lesson Harry produced a Patronus that moved, and Lupin told him the teaching about forgiving seventy times seven. Afterwards Dracina ambushed Harry in a dark corridor, until Lupin interrupted. On the next Hogsmeade Saturday Harry went under the Invisibility Cloak. By the Shrieking Shack he pelted Dracina, Crabbe and Goyle with mud. Then the Cloak slipped, and he was seen. Frightened for his safety, Dracina ran to Snape. There she confessed everything. Her team had pressured her into the fake-Dementor stunt, and she had stood ready to catch Harry with Arresto Momentum. She had written the letter about Buckbeak but never sent it. She believed she deserved the mud. Snape told her that she still had a chance to do something, rather than merely say something. Then he interrogated Harry, mocking James Potter. He confiscated the Marauder's Map, which insulted him. Lupin, summoned by Floo, covered for Harry, though he was visibly fighting something bestial in himself. Afterwards he reproached Harry for gambling with his parents' sacrifice. Hermione met them with the news that Hagrid had lost. Buckbeak was to be executed.

Chapter 15Seventy Times Seven

Ron forgave Hermione first, and she apologised for Scabbers. It set Harry thinking about letting go of a grievance, even when he was in the right. After Care of Magical Creatures, Dracina accused Hermione of stealing her letter. When Dracina began a slur implying that Hermione was Jewish, Hermione punched her. The two of them fought on the castle steps until Harry and Ron pulled them apart. Dracina begged Harry to believe her. Remembering Lupin's teaching, Harry chose to embrace her and accept her account. She vowed to put everything right. Hermione denied any wrongdoing. She missed Charms for no reason anyone could see, and later walked out of Divination for good after Harry challenged Professor Trelawney's contempt for Christianity. On Hermione's advice Harry sought out the Fat Friar. The Friar told him that wizards and the Church had once lived in harmony. He told how the witch-hunts had grown, and spoke of an old man who had taught the early students of Hogwarts that magic was a gift from God. When Harry told him about seeing Jesus in the Chamber of Secrets, the Friar said that he believed him. Over the Easter holidays Dracina secretly borrowed books on hippogriffs, practised bowing to a suit of armour and gave Harry an Easter egg she had made by hand. Hermione grew more possessive of him. The night before the final Harry saw the black dog walking with Crookshanks. The final against Slytherin was vicious. Harry caught the Snitch, winning Gryffindor the Quidditch Cup. Only afterwards did he realise that Dracina had let him win on purpose, as an apology.

Chapter 16An Act of God

As the exams drew near, Ron told Harry about Percy's plans for a regulated 'fair and orderly society'. Harry remarked that a Minister was not what was needed to put things right. Many years later, when half the wizarding world had learnt to do as Harry told them, he would remember that conversation. Hermione's impossible timetable ended in a breakdown at two in the morning. Ron looked after her with evident, growing feeling. Twice Hermione was tempted to use the small golden object on her chain against Dracina. During a last flare-up of the house feud Harry hid the Invisibility Cloak down the one-eyed witch's chute. From then on Snape guarded the chute. Hagrid's appeal was fixed for the last day of the exams. Dracina avoided Harry, though she secretly helped him in the Potions exam. She also studied the ground between Hagrid's cabin and the Forest. In the Defence Against the Dark Arts exam Hermione's boggart was McGonagall, telling her she had failed. It led to a bitter exchange with Dracina, which Lupin broke up. On the front steps Harry flattered Cornelius Fudge. He also saw the executioner, Walden Macnair. At the sight of him Dracina fled. At the end of Harry's Divination exam Professor Trelawney fell into a trance. She prophesied that the Dark Lord's servant would break free that night. Hagrid lost the appeal. Hermione fetched the Cloak, and the three of them went down to see Hagrid. They found Scabbers alive in a milk jug, then left. At sunset the axe fell. But Buckbeak had broken loose, and he flew off into the Forest carrying a hooded rider, who waved to the castle. Hagrid cheered. Harry called it an act of God.

Chapter 17Wrath

After Buckbeak's escape Harry, Ron and Hermione stayed hidden under the Invisibility Cloak. They watched Walden Macnair rage in Hagrid's pumpkin patch, until Hagrid threw him into the pumpkins for insulting his giant mother. Hermione quietly remarked that Dracina Malfoy had not been at dinner. Scabbers broke free of Ron's pocket as Crookshanks stalked them. A huge black dog knocked Harry down, then dragged Ron by the arm under the Whomping Willow, snapping his leg on a root. Crookshanks froze the Willow by pressing a knot on its trunk. Harry and Hermione followed the tunnel to the Shrieking Shack, where old claw marks were gouged through the plaster to the brick. Upstairs Ron warned them that the dog was an Animagus. Then Sirius Black disarmed them. Harry went for Black with his bare hands, screaming about the cupboard under the stairs and about his parents. Black wore a crude wooden cross. He never struck back, only muttered that it was his fault. When Black's hand closed on Harry's throat, Hermione attacked him savagely. Harry got his wand back, but he could not bring himself to kill Black while Crookshanks lay across Black's chest. Remus Lupin burst in, disarmed them all and embraced Black. Then he admitted that he was a Garou, as Hermione had worked out from Snape's essay. He was also Moony, one of the makers of the Marauder's Map. The map, he said, had shown Peter Pettigrew with them. Black and Lupin declared that Scabbers was the Animagus Peter Pettigrew.

Chapter 18The Doorkeeper

Lupin and Black set out to prove that Scabbers was Pettigrew. All the while Lupin was fighting down his Garou war form, maddened by the Wyrm-reek of the rat, and Black steadied him by calling him Moony. Lupin told them how he had been bitten as a small boy. The Wolfsbane Potion now suppressed his compulsion to transform. Dumbledore had let him into Hogwarts, with the Whomping Willow planted and the Shrieking Shack built for his monthly transformations. James, Sirius and Peter had become illegal Animagi. They were known as Prongs, Padfoot and Wormtail. Snape had seen the Marauder's Map in Lupin's office, then followed them under Harry's Cloak. He bound Lupin, told Black 'You failed her!' and resolved to hand both men over to the Dementors. Harry blocked the door. He had been wrong about Dracina Malfoy, he said, which proved that things were complicated. He taunted Snape. Then Harry, Ron and Hermione disarmed Snape together, so forcefully that he was knocked out. Black explained that he had recognised Pettigrew in a photograph in the Daily Prophet, which Fudge had given him. Crookshanks had helped him. It was Black, too, who had persuaded the Potters to make Pettigrew their Secret-Keeper. Lupin and Black forced Pettigrew back into human form. Lupin nearly transformed. Black calmed him by quoting 'Be ye angry, and sin not', a verse Lily had kept on her wall. Black described how he had found true faith in Azkaban through Bible passages printed in The Quibbler. After that the Dementors had stopped coming to him. In the end he had escaped as a dog. Harry stopped Black and Lupin from killing Pettigrew, so that he could be handed over as evidence. Hermione listed four lethal curses with alarming relish. Then they set off. Pettigrew was shackled to Lupin by one wrist and to Ron by the other, while Snape floated along unconscious.

Chapter 19Fear No Evil

On the way out of the Shack Ron swore at the stairs and bantered with Black. Black said that Ron reminded him of himself, and that James would have liked him. Ron admitted he had been thinking about God ever since he saw Harry's Patronus. Once he had come to believe Sirius a murderer, Lupin said, he had spent years with a pack in the hills of mid-Wales. Most of the pack were of the Fianna tribe. He called himself a coward. He promised to tell Harry about James and the Black sisters. In the tunnel Black asked Harry to come and live with him. Harry joyfully agreed, before he remembered the blood ward that bound him to his aunt's house. Black revealed that he had watched Harry leave Magnolia Crescent the summer before. He asked whether all was well with the Dursleys, but Lupin interrupted before Harry could answer. On the lawn the two men said the evening collect together. Then the clouds parted to show the full moon. Lupin had missed his Wolfsbane Potion. He began the Lord's Prayer, and changed into a nine-foot Garou. His cross flew off, and Harry pocketed it. The creature called Harry 'Wyrm'. It hurled Black aside. Then it hunted Harry, clawing his arm and leg. It shrugged off every spell until a silver Sickle burnt its muzzle. Harry's Shield Charm held it for a moment. Black, praying Psalm 23, changed into the dog and fought it. Pettigrew seized Lupin's wand. He struck down Ron and Crookshanks, then escaped as a rat. The creature fled into the Forest as a giant wolf. By the lake about a hundred Dementors closed in on Sirius, Harry and Hermione. Harry's faith faltered, and his Patronus failed. A Dementor was about to give him the Kiss when a silver animal drove them back. Across the lake Harry glimpsed a figure he almost seemed to know.

Chapter 20The Ending Has Not Yet Been Written.

Harry woke in the hospital wing to hear Snape telling Fudge that the three of them had been Confunded. Black, he said, was locked in Professor Flitwick's office, awaiting the Dementor's Kiss. Harry flattered the Minister, then mocked him, until Madam Pomfrey silenced him with chocolate. Dumbledore heard Harry and Hermione out. He promised to believe them, then hinted that what they needed was more time. He named the thirteenth window from the right of the West Tower, and handed Harry a small leather book that was not to be opened. Hermione revealed her Time-Turner, a gift from McGonagall, and took them back three hours. Harry concluded that they must rescue Buckbeak. Before they could, a cloaked figure lured the hippogriff away with a dead ferret, then flew off on him as Macnair's axe fell. The figure was Dracina Malfoy. In the Forest Hermione accused Dracina of using Harry. She described Dracina's cruelty in the girls' toilets in their first year. When Harry brought up Dracina's missing brooch and ribbons, Hermione stormed off. The werewolf found Harry in the Forest. Dracina dived to his rescue on Buckbeak. Hermione whispered a confession, and her forgiveness, before she was hurled into a tree. Kneeling in a stream in front of Dracina, Harry cast a Shield Charm. It turned white as the moon came out, swept through the creature and restored Lupin to human form. Dracina sobbed her apologies. Harry carried her out of the stream and forgave her. At the lake he realised that the rescuer he had seen was himself. He cast a stag Patronus that scattered the Dementors, and an arrow of white light from the sky destroyed the last of them. Hermione and Dracina apologised to each other. Hermione admitted to the brooch and the ribbons, though not to the letter. The three of them flew Buckbeak to Flitwick's office. Sirius had vanished, leaving behind a book marked MYST with grey fingermarks on it. As Aurors opened the door, Hermione identified it as a D'ni linking book. All three of them linked to Myst Island.

Chapter 21Find The Red Pages

Harry, Hermione and Dracina Malfoy came through a D'ni linking book on to the rotting dock of a deserted island, in a grey, empty sea. Dracina mocked Hermione's explanation. Hermione accused her of never once having been kind, and very nearly said 'my Harry'. Dracina broke down. She told them about her lonely, gilded life at Malfoy Manor and her hopeless longing for her father's approval. In Harry's head the old voice of the cupboard silenced him, so that he heard none of what followed. Hermione hugged Dracina and confessed that she had been friendless as a child herself. She forgave Dracina properly, then offered her friendship. The two girls agreed to be friends and rivals for Harry. Hermione explained what was known of the D'ni, the Art, the linking books and Anna's journal. Then she realised that the small book Dumbledore had given Harry would take them home. They followed footprints to a ruined library, where they found Sirius Black. He had been keeping company with a woman who had since vanished. They linked back one at a time to Professor Flitwick's office. After they had gone, the woman reappeared. She took the little book her father had written and said 'Shorah'. Dracina whistled Buckbeak up to the window. Before Sirius flew away he told Harry that James was proud of him, and that Lily would want him to sort things out with Christ. Holding Dracina's hand at the window, Harry resolved that the wizarding world must be made to change. A brilliant white star shone out in the west. On the stairs they overheard Snape covering for Dumbledore with Fudge, and losing his Order of Merlin for it. They reached the hospital wing just as Dumbledore came to lock the door. He praised Dracina and sent her down to the dungeons. Then he walked away, thinking of Greta Grindelwald. Harry lay awake thinking about God, Númenor and the white arrow until Ron woke up.

Chapter 22The Greater Good

The next day Harry, Ron and Hermione found the castle almost empty, now that the Dementors had been driven off. On the front steps Pansy Parkinson confessed that it was she who had sent Dracina's letter about Buckbeak to Lucius Malfoy. Dracina flew at her, but Ron calmly talked her out of her rage. From then on Pansy looked at Ron with obvious interest. The Fat Friar told Harry that his Patronus had killed Dementors because he had touched God and stopped doubting, like Peter walking on the water. He asked Harry to go into the church near his home, just once. Lupin, exposed as a werewolf by Snape, resigned. He told Harry that Christianity was a gift given to everyone. He gave back the Invisibility Cloak and the Marauder's Map. Then he gave Harry his own little wooden cross. Dumbledore told Harry that saving Pettigrew had created a bond, and that his father lived on in him. Then he saw Greta Grindelwald's anger in Harry's eyes. The anger, he said, never completely went away. Harry resolved to use his for the greater good. Hermione and Dracina each wrote Molly Weasley a long letter about the Dursleys. They sent them together, by the same owl. Mrs Weasley read them and smiled. On the train Dracina secretly passed Harry a note about her owl, Juniper. Then a tiny owl brought a letter from Sirius, confessing that it was he who had sent the Firebolt. With it came a Hogsmeade permission form, and the owl itself was a gift for Ron. A week after he got back to Privet Drive, having finished The Lord of the Rings, Harry went into St Michael's for Evensong. The vicar turned out to be the old man from the bench by the lych-gate. He preached on holy anger.

How it differs from the original

  • The book opens with Harry visiting St Michael's church, where an old man on the lych-gate bench speaks to him.
  • The Dursleys no longer dare mistreat Harry after Dumbledore's visit, and Harry blackmails Vernon with a BNP membership card.
  • Muggle news reports Khan Noonien Singh's Augment War, the Avengers and Justice League, the Power Rangers in Birmingham, Superman's death and Spider-Man's retirement; wizards know nothing of them.
  • A dodgy Muggle-dressed man with a glowing book in a carrier bag rides the Knight Bus.
  • Lucius Malfoy meets Harry in Diagon Alley, defends Lily's standing as a witch against Marge, and shows fear of Harry.
  • Harry reads The Lord of the Rings, bookmarked with Dracina's green ribbon of favour.
  • Dracina sends Harry a birthday letter and hand-made chocolate violets, and conducts a secret friendship with him.
  • Buckbeak slashes Dracina's right arm; she writes a letter to Lucius but decides not to send it, and Pansy sends it.
  • Werewolves are the Garou, who change at will rather than by the moon; Lupin is heavily implied to be one, and his own boggart is a Garou war-form.
  • Lupin's lessons cover vampire clans, the Masquerade, the Camarilla and the Sabbat, and Snape lectures on the Garou.
  • Lupin is a Christian, tells Harry Lily believed in Christ, and teaches the Patronus as light from God.
  • Harry meets a painting of Cain and dreams of him; the Fat Friar turns Harry from attacking Snape with the story of David and Abigail.
  • McGonagall's previous career includes a 1966 Siberian mission and a kept parasite in her office.
  • Dracina's boggart is her disappointed father.
  • Harry breaks down before Ron and Hermione at the end of the autumn term.
  • Dracina lends Harry a Nimbus Two Thousand and One before McGonagall returns the Firebolt.
  • Harry casts his first corporeal Patronus at the Ravenclaw match, against Dracina and her teammates dressed as Dementors.
  • Ron strikes Sirius Black in the face during the dormitory break-in.
  • Buckbeak's hearing is brought forward from April to March on the strength of Dracina's letter.
  • Dracina reports Harry to Snape after the mud to make him come back to safety, and confides in Snape.
  • Dumbledore calls at Privet Drive in person and frightens the Dursleys out of ever striking or starving Harry again.
  • Harry believes he saw Jesus Christ in the Chamber of Secrets. He finds himself drawn to St Michael's Church, where a mysterious old man speaks to him.
  • Dumbledore has linked Lily's protection to the Elves and Númenor, so Harry reads The Lord of the Rings in search of his own ancestry.
  • Dracina Malfoy sends a birthday letter tied with a green ribbon, a token of her favour that Narcissa arranged.
  • Harry gets Uncle Vernon's promise to sign the form by blackmailing him over a British National Party membership card.
  • The television news covers Khan Noonien Singh's conquest in India, the Avengers, the Justice League and the Power Rangers in Birmingham.
  • Fear of Dumbledore visibly holds Vernon and Petunia back. As Marge inflates, Petunia watches Harry, not Marge.
  • Harry's rage is sharpened by what Dumbledore told him: that his mother was descended from Elves.
  • A man strongly hinted to be John Constantine rides the Knight Bus, with a glowing book in a Tesco carrier bag.
  • According to Ern, the cover story for Black's massacre was a mutant attack.
  • Harry jokingly introduces himself to Fudge as Barry Trotter, then manipulates him with flattery.
  • Fudge mentions the strange blood ward Dumbledore described to him, and admits that he saw the Dursleys himself.
  • Lucius Malfoy meets Harry in Diagon Alley, walks with him a while, and tries to win him over to blood purism.
  • Wizards turn out to know nothing at all of superhumans or of Muggle wars.
  • Harry reads The Lord of the Rings and is moved by the Elves of Rivendell.
  • Mr Weasley asks Harry privately whether the Dursleys hurt him, and puts him down on the Ministry car list under the name Weasley.
  • Fred and George tried to shut Percy in an Egyptian tomb, whose guardian questioned him about the weighing of his heart.
  • Lupin shows hints of animal senses: flaring nostrils, a dog-like growl and eyes that catch the light.
  • Dracina only pretends to bully Harry's friends, and secretly gives him chocolate violets she has made herself.
  • Hermione cradles Harry after his collapse and grows jealous of Dracina.
  • McGonagall's office contains a stuffed, eyeless creature with a four-way mouth.
  • Harry makes a friend of Sir Cadogan by joking with him on the way to Divination.
  • Harry asks Trelawney about signs from God and is mocked for it. Hermione defends him, then later explains why the wizarding world is hostile to Christianity.
  • Dracina's ribbons are turned to Gryffindor colours and her Potions essay is inked over; both are hinted to be Hermione's doing.
  • Harry catches the injured Dracina, and she begs him to kill Buckbeak.
  • Harry visits Dracina in the hospital wing, and she screams at him about Hermione.
  • Dracina, not Draco, faces the boggart. It becomes her disapproving father, Lucius, and she completes the Riddikulus herself.
  • Lupin faces the boggart himself. It becomes a nine-foot, blood-soaked werewolf that recognises him, not a full moon.
  • There is a new subplot about a brooch: Hermione is hinted to have taken Dracina's heirloom and left it for Peeves.
  • Snape gives Harry and Dracina private advice about friendships ending over a single word.
  • Dracina apologises and claims to have dropped her complaint about Buckbeak.
  • Vampires are taught in terms of the Masquerade, the Camarilla, the Sabbat and the clans, such as the Ventrue or the Malkavians.
  • McGonagall teaches about spinal parasites and keeps a dead one in her office.
  • Lupin's growling is shown openly, along with the way his body reacts to Snape or to the moon.
  • Dracina defends Harry from Pansy and Daphne on Halloween morning.
  • Harry tells Lupin that he would have turned a boggart Voldemort into a screaming baby.
  • Slytherin's excuse for pulling out is Dracina's arm, which turns out to be a prop she uses for theatre.
  • Snape's substitute lesson is on the Garou, with their five forms, moon signs and tribes, instead of textbook werewolves.
  • New scenes include the painting of two brothers at their altars, the Fat Friar's story and Hermione's account of Angelus.
  • Dean leads a football-style chant, which Hufflepuff answer.
  • Harry feels an unexplained stillness in the storm. In the hospital wing he makes the sign of the cross.
  • Pansy, not Dracina, sent the letter that led to Lucius Malfoy's complaint.
  • Harry's revenge dream ends with the watching figure burnt away by light, and Lupin advises him to seek God.
  • Hermione gives Harry a frank opinion of Dracina in the Three Broomsticks.
  • Flitwick privately recalls a long feud between the sisters Bellatrix and Narcissa in his Charms classes.
  • Fudge speaks of 'parasite creatures' and 'Nephilim'. McGonagall mentions her 'previous career'.
  • Harry's grief and rage are explored at length. Ron makes a speech about the Weasleys being Harry's family, and Harry breaks down.
  • The blood protection is the stated reason why Harry cannot live with the Weasleys.
  • Harry blames Dracina for the Buckbeak complaint, although it was Pansy who posted the letter.
  • At Christmas lunch McGonagall tells the story of a mission in Siberia.
  • Lupin's absence at Christmas is hinted to involve a pack and a fight against a corruption, not simple illness.
  • Lupin frames the Patronus as light derived from God and tells Harry that Lily was a devout Christian.
  • Dracina is the Slytherin Seeker who beats Ravenclaw. She lends Harry her spare Nimbus Two Thousand and One.
  • On Mrs Weasley's instructions, the Weasley family deliberately organise themselves to watch over Harry.
  • Four new scenes deal with trust and forgiveness. They show the boy on the lake ice, the Hufflepuff girls in the library, Flitwick with Hobday and the Ravenclaw with the fleece.
  • Harry's early Patronus has no shape at all, only a mass of silver light.
  • Harry takes command during a time-out and gives the team its tactics against Ravenclaw.
  • The fake Dementors are Dracina, Crabbe, Goyle and Marcus Flint, with Dracina on Goyle's shoulders.
  • Ron punches Sirius Black in the face during the break-in at the dormitory.
  • Lupin speaks to Harry about the trick of hiding his face, which he says he shares.
  • Dracina confesses privately to Snape, revealing that she was coerced into the fake-Dementor stunt and never sent the letter about Buckbeak.
  • Harry's mud lands on Dracina's carefully styled hair, and she refuses to have it mended because she thinks she deserved it.
  • In Snape's office Lupin shows signs of a struggle with something bestial. He smells Snape's left arm, and prays afterwards.
  • Lupin teaches Harry the saying about forgiving seventy times seven.
  • Hermione punches Dracina over a slur and the two girls fight on the steps, instead of Hermione slapping Draco.
  • Harry forgives Dracina and believes her account of the letter.
  • The Fat Friar gives Harry a long account of wizards, the medieval Church and the witch-hunts. He also believes Harry's account of seeing Jesus.
  • Dracina throws the final so that Gryffindor wins the Cup, and gives Harry an Easter egg she has made by hand.
  • Buckbeak escapes during the execution itself, flying off with a hooded rider who is hinted to be Dracina.
  • Hermione is tempted to use her Time-Turner against Dracina, and she grows possessive of Harry.
  • Dracina secretly coaches Harry through the Potions exam.
  • A look ahead shows Harry's future rule over much of the wizarding world.
  • The Fat Lady flirts with the security trolls.
  • Lupin is a Garou rather than a classic werewolf. He struggles to hold back a war form, and he smells dark magic as the reek of the Wyrm.
  • Sirius wears a home-made wooden cross from Azkaban and keeps saying 'my fault'.
  • Harry physically beats Sirius at length, and Hermione attacks him even more savagely.
  • Hermione learnt Lupin's secret from Snape's essay, and she calls him a Garou.
  • Sirius's faith, with Psalm 84 at its heart, runs right through the scene in the Shack. So does Lupin's struggle with a war form that hates the Wyrm.
  • Lupin can smell dark magic on Pettigrew and on Snape's left arm.
  • Harry taunts Snape about having no friends, and mentions Dracina Malfoy as a lesson learnt.
  • Hermione describes several killing curses in gruesome detail.
  • Lupin changes into a Garou war form, described in great physical detail, and it calls Harry 'Wyrm'.
  • Harry burns the creature with a silver Sickle and holds it off with a Shield Charm.
  • Sirius and Lupin pray together. Harry's failure with the Patronus is tied to a crisis of faith.
  • Sirius offers Harry a home, but it is Harry himself who remembers the blood ward.
  • Dracina Malfoy, not Harry and Hermione, rescues Buckbeak. She later joins the time-travelling rescue.
  • Harry's Shield Charm turns white and forces Lupin back into human form.
  • An arrow of white light falls from the sky to destroy the last Dementor.
  • Sirius escapes, apparently by a D'ni linking book. Instead of freeing him on Buckbeak, Harry, Hermione and Dracina link to Myst Island.
  • Hermione confesses to persecuting Dracina all year.
  • John Constantine is a Muggle-born Slytherin who was at Hogwarts with Lucius Malfoy, and he rides the Knight Bus with Harry.
  • Grindelwald is a woman, Greta Grindelwald. Dumbledore owns a Deluminator that Constantine once stole.
  • The D'ni of Myst really existed, in a cavern under New Mexico, and their linking books circulate in the wizarding world.
  • The Headmaster's password is Acid Pop.
  • Sirius escapes from Flitwick's office to Myst Island through a D'ni linking book, rather than being freed directly on Buckbeak.
  • Dracina Malfoy is with Harry and Hermione throughout the rescue.
  • Dracina and Hermione are reconciled. They become friends and rivals for Harry.
  • Snape covers for Dumbledore in front of Fudge, and Fudge withdraws the Order of Merlin in person.
  • Sirius is a Christian, and he urges Harry to see the Fat Friar.
  • Harry makes up his mind that the wizarding world must change.
  • Pansy Parkinson, not Hermione, turns out to have sent the Buckbeak letter, and Ron makes peace on the castle steps.
  • Harry goes to the Fat Friar about God and his Patronus.
  • Lupin gives Harry his wooden cross and urges him to go to church.
  • Dumbledore admits that the anger never completely stops, and Harry takes up the phrase 'the greater good'.
  • Hermione and Dracina write to Molly Weasley about the Dursleys.
  • The last chapter ends with Harry at Evensong in St Michael's.

Characters introduced

  • Buckbeak
  • Cain
  • Cedric Diggory
  • Crookshanks
  • Ephraim Shacklewell
  • John Constantine
  • Peter Pettigrew
  • Remus Lupin
  • Sirius Black
  • Stan Shunpike
  • Sybill Trelawney
  • Walden Macnair

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl of Fire
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl of Fire

Book Four of the Malfoid Saga · 1994 to 1995 · In progress

Read Book FourFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1The House on the Hill

Harry dreamt that he was walking down a Privet Drive that lay sunk at the bottom of a valley. He passed number four, which was an orphanage kept by Aunt Petunia, where his mother had died after giving birth to him. He passed Mrs Figg at her knitting, then went through a leafless wood to a shack with a dead boa constrictor nailed to its door. Inside he found a filthy Uncle Vernon. The two of them spoke to each other in hisses. Harry put Vernon to sleep and took his wand, along with a gold ring set with a black stone. He climbed on past the Leaky Cauldron, and past a small boy weeding by moonlight, to the big house on the hill. There his father, James, sat at dinner with Harry's grandparents, Fleamont and Euphemia. Aunt Marge was serving them. James claimed that Lily had tricked him, and that he had abandoned her when the spell wore off. Harry tortured all three of them with the Cruciatus Curse until they apologised. Then he killed them with the Killing Curse, and felt wonderful. Dracina appeared in a scaled blue dress and embraced him. Then she slipped away through the curtains into a rainy circus. There she turned into a long blue snake, and slid off into the dark. Harry screamed that he loved her, begging her not to forget him. A flash of green light woke him. He was in his bedroom at Privet Drive, clutching Lupin's cross, with his scar burning.

Chapter 2The Scar

Harry woke at Privet Drive on a Saturday morning in August 1994 with his scar burning. He tried to make sense of his dream. In it he had murdered his own father and grandparents, then lost Dracina to a snake. Thinking of Dracina, he admitted to himself that he was in love with her. He read her birthday letter again. It offered help against his relatives, and reported that her father kept asking after Harry. Her mother, it said, was helpfully covering for her. It also described Pansy's sudden passion for the Chudley Cannons. The last line, 'Don't forget me', made his scar sear. He wondered whom he could tell. He remembered St Michael's, where he had been to Evensong every Sunday since July, and the elderly vicar, who took an odd interest in his soul. Then he read Hermione's letter again. A Muggle computer game called Myst, she wrote, showed their island exactly. She told the story of Atrus and his sons. There were Muggles online, she reported, who felt called towards New Mexico. Harry thought back over his summer of hard study. There had been a night when moonlight lit his book, and two cheerful letters from Sirius, brought by tropical birds. There had also been a prank in which the Dursleys' fridge was filled with bleeding rats. He wrote to Sirius about his scar, leaving out the dream. Then he heard a scream from downstairs.

Chapter 3Fear and Anger

Harry ran downstairs to find the Dursleys' kitchen coated in pond mud, which had erupted from the plughole. Uncle Vernon realised who was behind it. He thrust at Harry a letter from Mrs Weasley, so heavily stamped that there was hardly room for the address, inviting Harry to the final of the Quidditch World Cup. It ended 'P.S. Actions have consequences.' Dudley was on a strict diet. He had lately become devoted to the Green Ranger, and to karate. He made room for Harry on the sofa, and they watched the news together. The bulletin described the Augment War. Khan Noonien Singh's forces were near Belgrade, and a commander called Joaquin was overrunning the Balkans. Then it showed Superman, alive again, asking the Security Council of the United Nations to let the Justice League and the Avengers intervene. It showed angry protests against superhumans outside the United Nations. Among the protesters were grieving victims of the Hulk, of Coast City, of the Sub-Mariner and of a mutant's blackout. There was a report, too, of a proposal to revive the Sentinel robots. The last item was the death of the Egyptologist Daniel Jackson in a shaft collapse at Giza, with a tribute from Dr Richard Watson in New Mexico. Harry realised how small the wizarding world was beside the Muggle one, and how ignorant. He felt ashamed of his plans to remake it. Upstairs Ron's tiny owl, Pig, brought word that Mr Weasley had got the tickets. They would come and fetch Harry at five on Sunday. Harry sent Hedwig off to Sirius. Then he fished a large slab of birthday cake out from under the loose floorboard and ate it, perfectly content.

Chapter 4In All Matters

On Sunday 21 August 1994 Harry packed his trunk at Privet Drive, missing Evensong for the first time since July, while the Dursleys waited in dread for the Weasleys; the kitchen sink gurgled whenever Aunt Petunia drew breath to snap at him, and Dudley seemed quieter and more grown up. In the afternoon Harry glimpsed a figure in shimmering air beside the lamp post across the road, and noticed a new HUMANS FIRST sticker in Mr Prentice's car. The Weasleys arrived by Floo after half past five, found the fireplace boarded up, and Mr Weasley blasted it open, deliberately making as much mess as he could. He faced Uncle Vernon down, made the Dursleys say goodbye to Harry, and secretly set a house gnome loose under their sideboard while Dudley choked on one of Fred's Ton-Tongue Toffees. At the Burrow Harry met Bill and Charlie, was hugged by Mrs Weasley, and heard about Fred and George's joke business, Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, and Percy's report on cauldron thickness for Mr Crouch. Hermione questioned Harry closely about his diet and wrote it down in a notebook headed Privet Drive, while Mrs Weasley denied that the mud had been more than a nudge and pocketed a letter in green ink. At dinner in the garden the Weasleys discussed Bertha Jorkins's disappearance, Muggle attacks on wizards and the World Cup; Harry tried to explain the Augment War, mutants and metahumans and found that not even Mr Weasley knew of them, and Mrs Weasley described house gnomes, which feed on spite. In Mr Weasley's shed Harry told Ron and Hermione about the bleeding rats and offered to buy the Weasleys a computer, and Hermione set out her theory that a few D'ni survived the fall of 1788 and that their descendants were the Muggles feeling a calling to New Mexico. Walking back up the garden, Harry saw a hooded figure holding a small book on the hill beyond the hedge. That night Ron sent Pig north with a three-page letter to a pen pal, headed OPERATION GET IT OVER WITH, about Harry and Dracina.

Chapter 5One Quiet Year

Mrs Weasley woke Harry Potter at the Burrow before dawn on Monday 22 August 1994, and he found an emerald jumper on his trunk and his old jeans taken in overnight, with Dracina's letter still in the pocket. In the scullery Harry joked bitterly about Khan's conquests in the Balkans, and Hermione told him that three hundred thousand people were now protesting against superhumans outside the United Nations and that her own parents went to Friends of Humanity meetings. Upstairs Ron read Pansy Parkinson's reply to his three-page plan: they would bring Harry and Dracina to a lantern-lit clearing in the wood after the match and leave them alone together. At breakfast Mr Weasley talked about splinching and blamed Britain's troubles on foreigners, Mrs Weasley Summoned the twins' hidden Ton-Tongue Toffees, and at the gate she told Harry he deserved some peace while he fought back tears. With Amos and Cedric Diggory the party took a Portkey, a mouldy old boot, from the top of Stoatshead Hill and landed on a misty moor at seven minutes past five. At the campsite the Muggle manager, Mr Roberts, was Obliviated just as he began to say 'Mutie', which made Harry furious with the wizards' complacency. The party pitched Perkins's enlarged tent, passed the Malfoys' silk palace with its white peacocks, and met Seamus Finnigan, Oliver Wood and Cho Chang while fetching water, as an unseen smoker left cigarette ends near the trees. At lunch Ludo Bagman took the twins' bet on the final, while Mr Crouch warned that the Muggles were organised against people born with powers and that the Statute must be protected on British soil; Bagman nearly let slip a secret about Hogwarts, and Harry prayed for one quiet year. In the afternoon Ron slipped away to meet Pansy, and at dusk Harry bought three pairs of Omnioculars and glimpsed Lucius Malfoy. Then a gong sounded, and the party set off up the lantern path, followed by something in the darkness between the trees that smelt of cigarettes.

Chapter 6Just Right for Her

On the night of Monday 22 August 1994 Arthur Weasley led his party through the wood to the vast golden stadium of the Quidditch World Cup final and up to the Top Box, where Harry met Winky, Barty Crouch's house-elf, who disapproved of Dobby's wish to be paid. Harry deliberately charmed Cornelius Fudge, then unsettled him by talking about the Muggle campsite manager, mutants, Magneto, Khan's Augments and the American Sentinels, until Fudge fled to deal with the Bulgarians. Lucius Malfoy took Harry aside to thank him for saving Dracina from the werewolf, admired his handling of Fudge and admitted that the Ministry was frightened, but broke off in fury on glimpsing an old enemy on the stairs. Narcissa Malfoy introduced herself, called Harry Dracina's knight, revealed that she and her twin sister Bellatrix had fought over James Potter, and hinted that Lily Evans had done something to Bellatrix in their last year that drove her to Voldemort. Dracina, watching through her Omnioculars, realised that Pansy Parkinson, sitting below in Chudley Cannons orange, was in love with Ron. Ludo Bagman opened the final, the Bulgarian veela and the Irish leprechauns performed, and Ireland's Chasers built a huge lead while Fred and George quietly steered the game with the leprechauns, broom polish on the Bulgarian Keeper's broom and a fake whistle. Viktor Krum, his nose broken by a Bludger, caught the Snitch with Ireland 160 points ahead, so Ireland won 170 to 160, exactly as the twins had bet. After the Cup was presented, Winky's shriek exposed John Constantine, who had been trailing Harry all day, and Lucius chased him out of the stadium with jinxes while Narcissa urged him on. Pansy then took Dracina into the wood on the pretext of a lost earring while Ron, armed with a comb and Sleekeazy's, steered Harry towards the forked pine, beginning Plan A.

How it differs from the original

  • In the original, the first chapter follows Frank Bryce at the Riddle House. Here it is Harry's dream instead, in which he murders his own father and grandparents in a house on a hill.
  • Harry admits to himself that he is in love with Dracina Malfoy.
  • Letters from Dracina and Hermione replace the letters in the original chapter. Hermione's is about the Myst game and the D'ni.
  • Harry goes to Evensong every week and is reading a Bible from the vicar.
  • The prank with the bleeding rats in the Dursleys' fridge is new.
  • Mrs Weasley's invitation comes by Muggle post, covered in stamps, as in the original, but here it arrives with a magical mud attack on the kitchen and a threatening postscript.
  • Dudley is a Power Rangers fan who is learning karate, and he shows signs of a gentler nature.
  • The Muggle news of the Augment War, Superman, the Justice League, the Avengers, the Sentinels and Daniel Jackson's death is entirely new.
  • Ron's letter comes by the tiny owl Pig, as in the original, but here it adds Mrs Weasley's warning that the Dursleys had better say yes, for their own sake.
  • Harry goes to Evensong every Sunday and will miss it for the first time since July; he quotes Gandalf to Uncle Vernon.
  • Dudley shows signs of growing up: he practises karate alone, has stopped bullying Harry and stays silent when his father calls for 'freaks' to be rounded up.
  • Mr Weasley makes as much mess as he can on purpose, faces down Uncle Vernon at his full height, refuses to mend the wall and secretly plants a house gnome in the Dursleys' house.
  • Mrs Weasley, Hermione and Dracina are secretly working together against the Dursleys: Mrs Weasley cackles, pockets a letter in green ink and lies about the mud, and Hermione keeps a list headed Privet Drive.
  • House gnomes, which feed on spite, are a new creature.
  • Hermione's attachment to Harry is possessive: she measures his wrist, bristles at Dracina's name and watches Ginny like a cat watching a rat.
  • The Daily Prophet reports Muggle attacks on wizards by men in Friends of Humanity T-shirts, and none of the Weasleys has heard of the Augment War, mutants or metahumans.
  • Percy screams that he hates Indians and their shoddy cauldrons, and Harry approves; Harry plans to make use of Percy.
  • Bill reports American soldiers at Giza, Charlie reports Muggle aeroplanes and refugees near the dragon reserve, and the Bulgarians want their Portkey allowance doubled.
  • Charlie blames England's defeat by Transylvania partly on rumours about Dracula.
  • The meeting in Mr Weasley's shed, Hermione's D'ni theory and Harry's offer to buy the Weasleys a computer are new.
  • Ron has a secret pen pal and a plan to bring Harry and Dracina together; a shimmering hooded figure watches Harry twice.
  • Harry and Hermione's scullery talk about Khan, the protests outside the United Nations and her parents' membership of Friends of Humanity is entirely new.
  • Ron receives a letter from Pansy Parkinson setting out a plan to leave Harry and Dracina alone together after the match.
  • Mrs Weasley keeps Dracina's letters under her bed and has privately decided that Dracina would make Harry a wonderful wife.
  • Mrs Weasley, Hermione and Mr Weasley share private amusement about the plumbers at the Dursleys' and the house gnomes breeding there.
  • Hermione keeps a red notebook of curses headed 'For anyone who hurts my Harry', and snarls when Harry waves at Cho Chang.
  • Harry lands from the Portkey swearing, with vocabulary learnt from John Constantine on the Knight Bus, and introduces himself to Amos Diggory as 'Barry Trotter'.
  • Mr Roberts is Obliviated as he starts to say 'Mutie', and Harry protests to the Obliviator.
  • Mr Crouch speaks at length about the organised Muggle danger to people with powers, the American machines and a British register, and approves Harry's remark about brooms.
  • Oliver Wood is going into RAF training rather than professional Quidditch.
  • Cedric introduces himself to everyone as 'Diggory, Cedric Diggory', in the manner of a spy film.
  • An unseen smoker in a pale raincoat shadows the Weasley party through the campsite.
  • The chapter ends at the gong and the lantern path, before the stadium, with Harry's prayer for one quiet year.
  • Narcissa Malfoy is warm towards Harry, calls him Dracina's knight and reveals that she and Bellatrix are twins who fought over James Potter until Lily came.
  • Narcissa hints that Lily Evans did something to Bellatrix in their last year that broke her and sent her to Voldemort.
  • Lucius Malfoy privately thanks Harry for saving his daughter, admires his handling of Fudge and admits the Ministry is frightened of Muggle events.
  • Harry deliberately flatters Fudge and then unsettles him with talk of mutants, Magneto, Augments and Sentinels.
  • Fred and George do not merely bet on the result: they secretly fix the match with the leprechauns, broom polish and a fake whistle.
  • John Constantine is exposed in the Top Box and chased through the stadium by Lucius Malfoy.
  • Hermione and Dracina compete to look after Harry during the match, and Dracina sees Cho Chang watching the Top Box.
  • Pansy Parkinson attends in Chudley Cannons robes, Dracina discovers that Pansy loves Ron, and Ron and Pansy begin their plan to bring Harry and Dracina together in the wood.

Events in these years

  1. c. 1994
    Percy passes his Apparition testB4 Ch5
    Percy Weasley passed his Apparition test about two weeks before the World Cup final.
  2. c. 1994
    Cheaper-ticket holders arrive at the World CupB4 Ch5
    World Cup visitors with cheaper tickets had to arrive at the site two weeks before the final.
  3. c. 1994
    Death of Manfred WörnerB4 Ch3
    Nato's Secretary-General Manfred Wörner died the weekend before 20 August 1994, and an acting Secretary-General took over.
  4. 14 August 1994
    Harry tells the vicar he may leaveB4 Ch4
    Harry slipped late into the back pew at St Michael's and afterwards told the vicar his friends might send for him; the vicar nodded as though he knew the very day.
  5. c. 1994
    Arthur writes to Ali BashirB4 Ch5
    Arthur Weasley sent Ali Bashir an owl about the embargo on flying carpets, the week before the World Cup.
  6. August 1994
    Parallax is stopped at the beginning of time
    Hal Jordan, the lost Green Lantern, now calling himself Parallax, was revealed as the power behind Zero Hour, trying to remake history so that Coast City had never fallen. The heroes stopped him, and Connor Hawke, son of the first Green Arrow, shot him through the heart; he survived and vanished again.
  7. August 1994
    Time begins again
    Early in August 1994 the young hero Damage released the energy of a new beginning at the dawn of all things, and time was started again from it. History came back very nearly as it had been, and most people remember the weeks of Zero Hour only as a strange dream.
  8. August 1994
    The Justice Society disbands
    After Zero Hour the surviving members of the Justice Society, old now in body as well as in years, agreed that the Society's day was done, and disbanded it.
  9. August 1994
    Douglock at the Babel Spire
    In the Alps the Phalanx built a tower, the Babel Spire, out of the people of the villages it had swallowed, to call the Technarchy down on the Earth. Douglock climbed it with Rahne Sinclair of X-Factor and Sam Guthrie of X-Force, then scrambled its beacon from within. The Phalanx there fell to pieces, and Douglock rose again afterwards.
  10. August 1994
    Daniel Jackson declared deadB4 Ch3
    The Egyptologist Daniel Jackson, twenty-nine, was declared dead after a shaft collapsed beneath the Giza plateau.
  11. August 1994
    Senate hearing on the Sentinel programmeB4 Ch3
    The Senate Armed Services Committee was to hear evidence on reviving the Sentinels against Khan.
  12. August 1994
    Wilfred Thimble attacked in StockportB4 Ch4
    A gang of young Muggles dragged the retired wizard Wilfred Thimble off his ladder as he mended his guttering by wand on a Sunday morning, shouting 'mutie'; it was the third such attack that month, and Obliviators were sent in.
  13. August 1994
    Attacks in Godalming and on Mrs FenwickB4 Ch4
    A witch in Godalming had her windows put in twice, and Muggles painted a fist and HUMANS FIRST on Mrs Fenwick's front door.
  14. August 1994
    Khan holds half of YugoslaviaB4 Ch5
    By late August Khan Noonien Singh's forces held half of Yugoslavia.
  15. c. 1994
    Two wizards fined for splinchingB4 Ch5
    The Department of Magical Transportation heavily fined two wizards who had splinched themselves while Apparating without a licence.
  16. August 1994
    Plumbers called to the Dursleys' sinkB4 Ch5
    Trouble at the Dursleys' sink struck twice in one night, and the second plumber would not set foot in the kitchen.
  17. c. 1994
    Lucius Malfoy donates to St Mungo'sB4 Ch6
    Lucius Malfoy made a very generous contribution to St Mungo's Hospital, earning a seat in the Top Box as Fudge's guest.
  18. 18 August 1994
    Bleeding rats in the Dursleys' fridgeB4 Ch2
    On Thursday morning Aunt Petunia found the fridge crammed with bleeding rats; Harry suspected Sirius.
  19. 18 August 1994
    The Prime Minister returns from holidayB4 Ch3
    The British Prime Minister returned early from his holiday because of the Augment War.
  20. 18 August 1994
    Dracina writes to Hermione about the Malfoy tentB4 Ch5
    On Thursday Dracina wrote to Hermione that the Malfoys' World Cup tent had a fountain inside, which she called vulgar.
  21. 19 August 1994
    Superman addresses the Security CouncilB4 Ch3
    Superman asked the UN Security Council to let the Justice League and the Avengers act against the Augments; the Council adjourned without a vote.
  22. 19 August 1994
    Twenty thousand protest at the United NationsB4 Ch4
    On the Friday night, Harry said, twenty thousand people gathered outside the United Nations shouting 'No more capes', on the day Superman spoke to the Security Council.
  23. 20 August 1994
    Harry's dream of the house on the hillB4 Ch1
    Harry dreamt of murdering his father and grandparents in a house on a hill and of Dracina turning into a snake, and woke with his scar burning.
  24. 20 August 1994
    Harry writes to Sirius about his scarB4 Ch2
    At dawn Harry wrote to Sirius that his scar had hurt, leaving out the dream.
  25. 20 August 1994
    Mud from the Dursleys' plugholeB4 Ch3
    Pond mud erupted from the Dursleys' kitchen plughole, and Vernon gave Harry Molly Weasley's letter inviting him to the World Cup final.
  26. 20 August 1994
    Augment forces near BelgradeB4 Ch3
    The news reported Augment forces within forty miles of Belgrade after the collapse of the rump Yugoslav army.
  27. 20 August 1994
    Pig brings Ron's letterB4 Ch3
    Pig brought Ron's letter about the World Cup tickets; Harry replied and sent Hedwig to Sirius.
  28. c. 1994
    HUMANS FIRST sticker in Privet DriveB4 Ch4
    Mr Prentice put a new HUMANS FIRST sticker in the back window of his car.
  29. 20 August 1994
    Pansy finds the clearingB4 Ch5
    On Saturday Pansy Parkinson found a clearing past the forked pine at the World Cup campsite and hung it with fairy lanterns.
  30. 20 August 1994
    Petrol bomb in OhioB4 Ch5
    On Saturday night a petrol bomb was thrown through the window of an Ohio electrician whose lights flickered; he was not a metahuman.
  31. c. 1994
    The Weasleys book their tentsB4 Ch5
    Arthur Weasley booked two tents with Mr Roberts a couple of days before the World Cup final.
  32. 21 August 1994
    The Weasleys to collect HarryB4 Ch3
    The Weasleys planned to fetch Harry from Privet Drive at five o'clock on Sunday.
  33. 21 August 1994
    Harry packs his trunkB4 Ch4
    By noon Harry had packed his trunk at Privet Drive and cleared out his hiding place, missing Evensong that evening for the first time since July.
  34. 21 August 1994
    A shimmering figure in Privet DriveB4 Ch4
    In the middle of the afternoon a figure in shimmering air stood beside the lamp post outside number five, looking up at Harry's window, then vanished.
  35. 21 August 1994
    The Weasleys blast open the Dursleys' fireplaceB4 Ch4
    After half past five Arthur, Fred, George and Ron Weasley arrived by Floo, found the fireplace boarded up, and Arthur blew it open, leaving the living room in ruins.
  36. 21 August 1994
    Dudley eats a Ton-Tongue ToffeeB4 Ch4
    Dudley ate a Ton-Tongue Toffee that Fred had dropped, and his tongue grew to four feet before Arthur shrank it.
  37. 21 August 1994
    Arthur Weasley plants a house gnomeB4 Ch4
    While the Dursleys were busy with Dudley, Arthur Weasley set a house gnome loose in their living room, and it hid under the sideboard.
  38. 21 August 1994
    Harry arrives at the BurrowB4 Ch4
    Harry Flooed to the Burrow, met Bill and Charlie Weasley for the first time and was hugged by Mrs Weasley.
  39. 21 August 1994
    Dinner in the Burrow gardenB4 Ch4
    At seven o'clock the Weasleys, Harry and Hermione dined in the garden; Harry tried to explain the Augment War and the metahumans, and Mrs Weasley described house gnomes.
  40. 21 August 1994
    The meeting in Mr Weasley's shedB4 Ch4
    In Mr Weasley's shed Harry told Ron and Hermione about the bleeding rats, offered to buy the Weasleys a computer, and heard Hermione's theory of the D'ni survivors.
  41. 21 August 1994
    The figure on the hillB4 Ch4
    Walking back from the shed, Harry saw a hooded figure holding a small book in shimmering air on the hill beyond the Burrow's hedge.
  42. 21 August 1994
    Ron writes to his pen palB4 Ch4
    Ron sent Pig north with a three-page letter to his pen pal headed OPERATION GET IT OVER WITH, about Harry and Dracina.
  43. 21 August 1994
    Ron sends his plan to PansyB4 Ch5
    Ron sent his three-page plan to Pansy by Pig; it reached her at half past eleven at night.
  44. 21 August 1994
    Percy dismisses the Security CouncilB4 Ch5
    Percy Weasley called the United Nations Security Council a Muggle committee of no consequence.
  45. 21 August 1994
    Mr Roberts says 'Mutie'B4 Ch5
    The Muggle site manager Mr Roberts used the word 'Mutie' to one of Mr Crouch's people before being Obliviated.
  46. 22 August 1994
    Quidditch World Cup finalB4 Ch3
    The 1994 Quidditch World Cup final, Ireland against Bulgaria, was set for Monday night.
  47. 22 August 1994
    Ron reads Pansy's letterB4 Ch5
    Before dawn Ron read Pansy Parkinson's reply setting out Plan A to leave Harry and Dracina alone together after the match.
  48. 22 August 1994
    Hermione's scullery talk with HarryB4 Ch5
    In the Burrow's scullery before dawn Hermione told Harry about the growing protests and her parents' Friends of Humanity meetings, and hugged him.
  49. 22 August 1994
    Ton-Tongue Toffees confiscatedB4 Ch5
    At about half past four in the morning Mrs Weasley Summoned the twins' hidden Ton-Tongue Toffees and binned them; the twins left without a word to her.
  50. 22 August 1994
    Molly Weasley's farewell at the gateB4 Ch5
    At the gate of the Burrow Mrs Weasley asked why Harry could not have one quiet year and told him he deserved peace.
  51. 22 August 1994
    Portkey from Stoatshead HillB4 Ch5
    The Weasley party and the Diggorys took a Portkey, an old boot, from Stoatshead Hill, landing on the moor at seven minutes past five.
  52. 22 August 1994
    Black Forest party dueB4 Ch5
    A big party of wizards from the Black Forest was due at the World Cup Portkey arrival point at five fifteen.
  53. 22 August 1994
    Mr Roberts ObliviatedB4 Ch5
    At about half past five in the morning a Ministry wizard Obliviated Mr Roberts as he began to say 'Mutie', and Harry protested.
  54. 22 August 1994
    The Weasleys pitch their tentsB4 Ch5
    Harry and Hermione put up the Weasleys' two tents by hand at the top of the field, and Arthur lit a cooking fire with Hermione's help.
  55. 22 August 1994
    Bill, Charlie and Percy arriveB4 Ch5
    Around midday Bill, Charlie and Percy Weasley Apparated into the wood and joined the party for lunch.
  56. 22 August 1994
    Bagman and Crouch at the Weasley fireB4 Ch5
    At lunch Ludo Bagman took the twins' bet on the final, and Mr Crouch warned of the organised Muggle danger to people with powers before cutting off Bagman's hint about Hogwarts.
  57. 22 August 1994
    Harry's prayer for one quiet yearB4 Ch5
    Harry prayed under his breath for one quiet year without something trying to kill him.
  58. 22 August 1994
    Ron meets Pansy at the forked pineB4 Ch5
    In the afternoon Ron slipped away for nearly half an hour to meet Pansy under the forked pine, where she pressed something into his hand.
  59. 22 August 1994
    Harry glimpses Lucius MalfoyB4 Ch5
    At dusk Harry saw Lucius Malfoy across the crowd of souvenir sellers, while a figure in a pale raincoat moved sharply away.
  60. 22 August 1994
    Harry buys three pairs of OmniocularsB4 Ch5
    Harry bought Omnioculars at ten Galleons a pair for himself, Ron and Hermione.
  61. 22 August 1994
    The gong sounds for the finalB4 Ch5
    At dusk a deep gong sounded beyond the wood, lanterns lit the path to the stadium, and the Weasley party set off, followed by something in the dark that smelt of cigarettes.
  62. c. 1994
    Three hundred thousand outside the United NationsB4 Ch5
    By Monday the crowd protesting against superhumans outside the United Nations had grown to three hundred thousand, arriving by coach from all over America.
  63. 22 August 1994
    The Weasley party's Portkey arrivesB4 Ch6
    The Weasley party's Portkey reached the World Cup site at seven minutes past five in the morning.
  64. 22 August 1994
    Mr Roberts Obliviated mid-wordB4 Ch6
    In the morning Obliviators caught Mr Roberts halfway through saying 'mutie', in front of Harry.
  65. 22 August 1994
    Fred and George prepare the fixB4 Ch6
    At lunchtime Fred made a rude sign at Percy, and in the afternoon the twins went to 'look at the pitch', returning smelling of broom polish.
  66. 22 August 1994
    Constantine trails HarryB4 Ch6
    All day John Constantine followed Harry around the World Cup site, leaving cigarette smoke and glimpses of his raincoat.
  67. 22 August 1994
    Harry meets WinkyB4 Ch6
    In the Top Box Harry met Winky, Barty Crouch's house-elf, who was saving her master a seat and disapproved of Dobby's freedom.
  68. 22 August 1994
    Harry handles FudgeB4 Ch6
    Harry flattered Fudge and then unsettled him with talk of mutants, Magneto, Augments and Sentinels, until Fudge fled.
  69. 22 August 1994
    Lucius Malfoy thanks HarryB4 Ch6
    Lucius Malfoy thanked Harry privately for saving Dracina from the werewolf, then broke off on glimpsing Constantine on the stairs.
  70. 22 August 1994
    Narcissa Malfoy meets HarryB4 Ch6
    Narcissa Malfoy called Harry Dracina's knight, told him of her and her twin's rivalry over James, and hinted at what Lily did to Bellatrix.
  71. 22 August 1994
    Dracina sees that Pansy loves RonB4 Ch6
    Watching Pansy Parkinson through her Omnioculars, Dracina realised that Pansy was in love with Ron Weasley.
  72. 22 August 1994
    The 422nd World Cup final beginsB4 Ch6
    Ludo Bagman opened the final of the 422nd Quidditch World Cup, and the Bulgarian veela and Irish leprechauns performed.
  73. 22 August 1994
    Krum's Wronski FeintB4 Ch6
    Viktor Krum drew Aidan Lynch into the ground with a Wronski Feint and hunted the Snitch during Lynch's time out.
  74. 22 August 1994
    The fake whistleB4 Ch6
    With Ireland 130 to 10 up, George Weasley's fake whistle stopped the Bulgarian Chasers and Troy scored.
  75. 22 August 1994
    Mostafa tries to send off the veelaB4 Ch6
    Entranced by the veela, Mostafa had to be kicked awake, tried to send off the mascots and gave Ireland two penalties.
  76. 22 August 1994
    The veela attack the leprechaunsB4 Ch6
    Provoked by a rude leprechaun hand sign, the veela turned bird-headed and hurled fire at the leprechauns.
  77. 22 August 1994
    Quigley breaks Krum's noseB4 Ch6
    An Irish Bludger broke Krum's nose, and he played on.
  78. 22 August 1994
    Ireland win the 1994 World CupB4 Ch6
    Krum caught the Snitch with Ireland 170 to 10 up, and Ireland won 170 to 160.
  79. 22 August 1994
    The Bulgarian Minister speaks EnglishB4 Ch6
    After the match the Bulgarian Minister for Magic revealed he spoke English, having let Fudge mime to him all day.
  80. 22 August 1994
    The World Cup presentedB4 Ch6
    The World Cup was carried into the lit Top Box, the teams came up, and Troy and Quigley lifted the Cup.
  81. 22 August 1994
    Fred and George are paidB4 Ch6
    Ludo Bagman paid Fred and George in full for their bet.
  82. 22 August 1994
    Constantine exposed in the Top BoxB4 Ch6
    John Constantine trod on Winky, whose shriek exposed him to Lucius Malfoy in the Top Box.
  83. 22 August 1994
    Lucius chases ConstantineB4 Ch6
    Lucius Malfoy jinxed and chased Constantine through the stadium until Constantine escaped over the last barrier and leprechauns swarmed Lucius.
  84. 22 August 1994
    Plan A beginsB4 Ch6
    Pansy took Dracina into the wood on the pretext of a lost earring while Ron led Harry towards the forked pine.
  85. 23 August 1994
    Security Council to meet againB4 Ch3
    The UN Security Council was due to meet again on Tuesday, and the protest was to continue until then.
  86. August 1994
    Billy Cranston finds Lord Drakkon at Promethea
    Puzzled that a Promethea building drew only half its power, Billy Cranston found Lord Drakkon in a secret cell beneath it, where Grace Sterling had held him since the autumn before. Jason Lee Scott ended the Rangers' alliance with her.
  87. 1 September 1994
    Mrs Weasley to take the children to King's CrossB4 Ch5
    Mrs Weasley planned to take the children to King's Cross for the Hogwarts Express the week after the World Cup.
  88. 3 September 1994
    Professor Hart calls the VR Troopers
    A message from Professor Hart brought Ryan Steele, Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese to his laboratory outside Crossworld City, where each was given a Virtualizer. Grimlord attacked the same day, and his swordsman Decimator left Ryan for dead in a quarry.
  89. 10 September 1994
    The Troopers turn back Grimlord's first assault
    Kaitlin Star and J.B. Reese brought Ryan Steele back from the quarry to be mended. The three then fought together for the first time, turning back the army Grimlord had massed against the Earth. In the laboratory that week a surge of power left Ryan's dog, Jeb, able to talk.
  90. September 1994
    Saba dies in Lord Drakkon's cell
    The Saba of Drakkon's world went to Drakkon's cell at Promethea to kill him, but set him loose by accident. Drakkon struck off Saba's head, then worked what was left into one of Rita's incantations to open a way out, taking the blade with him.
  91. c. 1994
    Oliver Wood to begin RAF trainingB4 Ch5
    Oliver Wood was soon to begin an RAF Basic Recruit Training Course, following his father.
  92. September 1994
    Ninjor mends Lord Drakkon's powers
    Lord Drakkon passed Ninjor's trials at the Temple of Power, keeping his purpose to himself. Ninjor mended his link to the Power. Drakkon carried him off in a jar, then stole the Green Chaos Crystal from the Command Center.
  93. September 1994
    The murder of Tommy Oliver
    On the night of Tommy Oliver's first proper date with Kimberly Hart, Lord Drakkon ran him through from behind in an alley with the blade that had been Saba, drawing off his power. Tommy died in Kimberly's arms. Angel Grove buried him.
  94. September 1994
    Drakkon makes war on the Rangers of every year
    Tommy Oliver's murder broke the Power apart, shutting each team of Rangers of later years away in a time of its own. Lord Drakkon went from one to the next, taking their powers into himself. Zordon called on the Emissaries Three, who would not act, then warned every Ranger the Power could reach.
  95. September 1994
    The storming of Drakkon's tower
    The Rangers of every year stormed Lord Drakkon's tower on the Moon of his own world. Grace Sterling flew Promethea in to free his prisoners. Rita Repulsa burnt a green candle against him. Drakkon killed Finster-5, then took every stolen power into himself at once.
  96. September 1994
    Lord Drakkon unmakes the world
    Lord Drakkon broke into the Morphin Grid, beat the Emissaries Three, then used the heart of a Morphin Master to unmake everything. In its place he made one world, with himself as its hero. Promethea, armoured with Psycho Green's dagger, was thrown clear into a dark place without the Power.
  97. September 1994
    The world is mended
    Tommy Oliver's spirit, held between the worlds by the Ranger Slayer's arrow, beat Lord Drakkon in his made world, then took the heart from him. The Rangers mended everything with it. Tommy was alive, his first date with Kimberly Hart ended in a kiss, and nobody on Earth remembered. Drakkon chose to stay in the wreck.
  98. Autumn 1994
    Lord Zedd comes to the Moon
    Lord Zedd came to Rita Repulsa's palace on the Moon, angry at her long failure, and banished her into space in a dumpster.
  99. 25 September 1994
    James Sunderland comes to Silent Hill
    James Sunderland came to Silent Hill after a letter from his dead wife, Mary Shepherd-Sunderland. The town set the Red Pyramid Thing on him, with Maria of Silent Hill, who wore his wife's face. Angela Orosco walked into a fire there, and James killed Eddie Dombrowski under Toluca Prison.
  100. 26 September 1994
    James Sunderland leaves Silent Hill
    In the night, at the Lakeview Hotel, James Sunderland remembered that he had smothered his sick wife himself. He read her last letter. In the morning he walked out of Silent Hill with Laura, an orphan of eight who had been her friend.
  101. 30 September 1994
    Kaitlin Star photographs Grimlord's prisoner
    In the woods outside Crossworld City Kaitlin Star photographed a prisoner who looked like Tyler Steele. He had been moved by the time Ryan Steele reached the place, but the Troopers now knew that Grimlord held him alive.
  102. October 1994
    The bottling of Angel Grove
    Lord Zedd made a bargain with Brainiac, an alien machine mind who collects cities, and Brainiac shrank Angel Grove into a bottle. The Power Rangers fought beside the Justice League for the first time to win it back, in full view of the world.
  103. October 1994
    The Blue Emissary comes to Jason
    The Blue Emissary, a servant of the Morphin Masters, came in secret to Jason Lee Scott and gave him back his memory of Lord Drakkon's war. At Jason's price the Emissary showed Zordon the way to the White Light. Zack Taylor and Trini Kwan, who walked in on them, joined too.
  104. Autumn 1994
    Kitty Pryde draws the Soulsword
    On Muir Island Kitty Pryde drew the Soulsword out of her own body, where it had lain since Illyana Rasputina's death. The sorcerer Gravemoss came for it wearing Kurt Wagner's body, until Kitty drove him out and Amanda Sefton killed him with the sword.
  105. October 1994
    Lord Zedd tries to make Kimberly Hart his queen
