    Early in the Third Age the Elder Things, a winged, star-headed people from beyond the Earth, came down in the far south. They built a great city where the ice of Antarctica now lies, and bred the shoggoths to labour for them.
  6. c. 32,759 BC
    Arwen is born
    In the year 241 Arwen Undómiel, the Evenstar, was born to Elrond and Celebrían, daughter of Galadriel; she was said to bear the likeness of Lúthien.
  7. c. 32,001 BC
    The Valar choose the Istari
    The Valar met in council to send messengers to Middle-earth against Sauron; Olórin said that he feared Sauron and was too weak, and Manwë answered that this was the more reason why he should go.
  8. c. 32,000 BC
    The Istari come over the Sea
    About the year 1000 of the Third Age five Istari, Maiar sent on commission in the likeness of old men, landed at the Grey Havens to unite all who would resist Sauron; Saruman the White came first, and they were forbidden to match his power with power or to dominate the minds of those they came to help.
  9. c. 32,000 BC
    Círdan gives Narya to Gandalf
    Gandalf came last of the five, seeming the least of them, and Círdan at the Grey Havens gave him Narya, the Ring of Fire, set with a red stone; Radagast the Brown went to the borders of the Greenwood.
  10. c. 32,000 BC
    Bertron makes Doomsday on Krypton
    Some thirty-four thousand years ago, early in the Third Age, the alien scientist Bertron bred Doomsday on Krypton, then still a savage world, by cloning a creature over and over from its own remains.
  11. c. 31,998 BC
    The Blue Wizards go east
    The two Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, went into the far East with Saruman and never returned, and the record of them goes vague, never settling what became of them.
  12. c. 31,995 BC
    Zordon is sent to Eltar
    One of the two Blue Wizards went further than anyone was keeping records of, off the world altogether to Eltar; he became Zordon of Eltar, Gandalf's equal and colleague of the same commission, while Gandalf's charge was the Earth.
  13. c. 31,900 BC
    The Necromancer of Dol Guldur
    About the year 1100 the Wise discovered that an evil power had made a stronghold at Dol Guldur in southern Mirkwood; they thought it one of the Nazgûl, but it was Sauron taking shape again.
  14. c. 31,700 BC
    The Witch-king rises in Angmar
    About the year 1300 the Nazgûl stirred again, and their chief came north and founded the realm of Angmar, where he was called the Witch-king, and made war on the divided kingdoms of Arnor.
  15. c. 31,563 BC
    The Kin-strife
    In the year 1437, in the Kin-strife of Gondor, Castamir the Usurper drove out King Eldacar, Osgiliath was burned and its Seeing-stone lost in the river; Eldacar returned in 1447 and slew Castamir.
  16. c. 31,399 BC
    The Shire founded
    In the year 1601 the hobbit brothers Marcho and Blanco crossed the Brandywine with leave of the King at Fornost, and the Shire was founded.
  17. c. 31,025 BC
    The end of the North-kingdom
    In the year 1974 the Witch-king took Fornost, and in 1975 King Arvedui was drowned in the Ice Bay of Forochel and the kingdom of Arnor came to an end; the heirs of Isildur became the hidden Rangers of the North.
  18. c. 31,025 BC
    The Battle of Fornost
    In the year 1975 Eärnur of Gondor and Glorfindel of Rivendell overthrew the Witch-king at the Battle of Fornost, and Glorfindel foretold that he would not fall by the hand of man.
  19. c. 31,020 BC
    Durin's Bane wakes in Moria
    In the year 1980 the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm delved too deep and woke a Balrog, which slew King Durin VI, and Moria was soon abandoned; the same year the Witch-king came to Mordor and gathered the Nazgûl.
  20. c. 31,000 BC
    The Great Race of Yith comes to the Earth
    Fleeing the death of their own world, the minds of the Great Race of Yith crossed to the Earth and took the bodies of a people of great cones. Their city of archives, Pnakotus, stood in what is now the Great Sandy Desert of Australia.
  21. c. 30,950 BC
    Eärnur rides to Minas Morgul
    In the year 2050 Eärnur, last King of Gondor, accepted the Witch-king's challenge, rode to Minas Morgul, the Tower of Sorcery that had once been Minas Ithil, and was never seen again; Mardil began the rule of the Stewards.
  22. c. 30,937 BC
    The Watchful Peace
    In the year 2063 Gandalf went to Dol Guldur and Sauron withdrew into the East, and the Watchful Peace began; it ended in 2460, when Sauron returned to Dol Guldur.
  23. c. 30,537 BC
    Sméagol murders Déagol
    About the year 2463, when the White Council was formed, the river-hobbit Déagol found the One Ring in the Anduin near the Gladden Fields. His friend Sméagol strangled him for it on his own birthday. About 2470 Sméagol, now Gollum, hid under the Misty Mountains with the Ring, which lengthened his life and wore it thin.
  24. c. 30,490 BC
    Eorl and the founding of Rohan
    In the year 2510 Eorl the Young rode from the north to the Field of Celebrant and saved Gondor, and Cirion the Steward gave his people Calenardhon, which became Rohan; the same year Celebrían, wounded by Orcs, passed over the Sea.
  25. c. 30,230 BC
    Smaug takes Erebor
    In the year 2770 the dragon Smaug descended on the Lonely Mountain, drove out the Dwarves of Erebor and destroyed the town of Dale.
  26. c. 30,155 BC
    Thráin loses the last of the Seven
    In the year 2845 Thráin, King of Durin's Folk, was taken prisoner in Dol Guldur, where the last of the Seven Rings was taken from him.
  27. c. 30,150 BC
    Gandalf in Dol Guldur
    In the year 2850 Gandalf entered Dol Guldur in secret. He discovered that its master was Sauron, who was gathering the Rings and seeking news of the One. In the dungeons he found Thráin dying. Thráin, robbed of the last of the Seven, gave him a map and a key.
  28. c. 30,069 BC
    Aragorn is born
    On 1 March in the year 2931 Aragorn son of Arathorn, the heir of Isildur, was born, the last of the line whose ancestors had come out of drowned Númenor.
  29. c. 30,067 BC
    Aragorn raised as Estel
    In the year 2933 Arathorn was slain, and his widow Gilraen took the boy to Rivendell, where Elrond fostered him under the name Estel, Hope.
  30. c. 30,059 BC
    Gandalf sends Bilbo to Erebor
    In April of the year 2941 Gandalf sent Bilbo Baggins out of the Shire as burglar to Thorin Oakenshield and twelve Dwarves, to win back the Lonely Mountain from Smaug.
  31. c. 30,059 BC
    Bilbo finds the Ring
    In July of the year 2941 Bilbo, lost in the goblin tunnels under the Misty Mountains, found a ring on the floor. He won a game of riddles with Gollum, then slipped past him invisible to escape. The Ring had left Gollum, wanting to be found.
  32. c. 30,059 BC
    The Battle of Five Armies
    In the autumn of 2941 Bard the Bowman shot down Smaug over Lake-town, and Elves, Men, Dwarves and Eagles defeated the Goblins and Wargs before the Lonely Mountain; Thorin died of his wounds.
  33. c. 30,058 BC
    Bilbo comes home with the Ring
    In the year 2942 Bilbo returned to Bag End with the Ring, and Sauron secretly returned to Mordor.
  34. c. 30,056 BC
    Gollum leaves the mountains
    In the year 2944 Gollum left the Misty Mountains to hunt for the thief who had taken his precious.
  35. c. 30,049 BC
    Aragorn learns his lineage and meets Arwen
    In the year 2951 Elrond told Estel his true name and ancestry and gave him the shards of Narsil, and the next day, in the woods of Rivendell, Aragorn met Arwen and loved her.
  36. c. 30,047 BC
    Saruman takes Isengard
    In the year 2953 the White Council met for the last time, and Saruman withdrew to Isengard, coveting the One Ring for himself.
  37. c. 30,044 BC
    Aragorn meets Gandalf
    In the year 2956 Aragorn met Gandalf, and their long friendship began.
  38. c. 30,043 BC
    Aragorn's errantries
    From the year 2957 Aragorn went on great journeys, serving in disguise as Thorongil under Thengel of Rohan and Ecthelion of Gondor, and as a Ranger of the North he guarded Eriador unthanked; to the folk of Bree he was Strider.
  39. c. 30,020 BC
    Troth plighted on Cerin Amroth
    In the year 2980 Aragorn met Arwen again in Lothlórien and gave her the ring of Barahir, and they plighted their troth on the hill of Cerin Amroth; Elrond would not let them wed until Aragorn was king of both Gondor and Arnor.
  40. c. 29,999 BC
    Bilbo's farewell party
    On 22 September 3001 Bilbo held his farewell party and left the Shire, leaving the Ring to Frodo Baggins. Gandalf first suspected that it was the One.
  41. c. 29,983 BC
    Gollum is caught in Mordor
    Hunting for the Ring, Gollum came into Mordor, where Sauron's servants caught him. Under torment he gave Sauron two words, Shire and Baggins. In the year 3017 he was let go.
  42. c. 29,983 BC
    Gandalf reads the scroll of Isildur
    In the year 3017 Gandalf read at Minas Tirith the scroll in which Isildur had written of the Ring. It had been 'hot as a glede' when he took it, Isildur wrote, and the letters on it had faded as it cooled.
  43. c. 29,982 BC
    The fire at Bag End
    In April of the year 3018, in a little round room with a fire in the grate at Bag End, Gandalf threw Frodo's ring on the fire. Letters of fire rose on it, 'One Ring to rule them all', and he knew it for the One.
  44. c. 29,982 BC
    Frodo leaves Bag End
    On 23 September 3018, at nightfall, Frodo left Bag End with the Ring, on the day the Black Riders entered the Shire.
  45. c. 29,982 BC
    Gandalf imprisoned in Orthanc
    In July 3018 Saruman revealed his treachery and imprisoned Gandalf on the pinnacle of Orthanc, whence Gwaihir the eagle bore him away in September.
  46. c. 29,982 BC
    Strider at the Prancing Pony
    On 29 September 3018 Frodo, fleeing the Black Riders, came to the Prancing Pony at Bree, where a weather-stained ranger called Strider sat hooded in a dark corner; it was Aragorn, who guided the hobbits towards Rivendell.
  47. c. 29,982 BC
    Frodo wounded on Weathertop
    On 6 October 3018 the Witch-king and four other Ringwraiths attacked on Weathertop and wounded Frodo with a Morgul knife, and on 20 October Frodo escaped them over the Ford of Bruinen.
  48. c. 29,982 BC
    The Council of Elrond
    On 25 October 3018 the Council of Elrond at Rivendell resolved to destroy the Ring in the fire where it was made, and Frodo took the task upon himself.
  49. c. 29,982 BC
    Narsil reforged as Andúril
    Before the Fellowship set out, the Elven smiths of Rivendell reforged the shards of Narsil for Aragorn, and he named it Andúril, Flame of the West; its blade was traced with seven stars between a crescent moon and a rayed sun.
  50. c. 29,982 BC
    The Fellowship sets out
    On 25 December 3018 the Fellowship of the Ring set out from Rivendell: Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin, Gandalf, Aragorn, Boromir, Legolas and Gimli.
  51. c. 29,981 BC
    Gandalf falls in Moria
    On 15 January 3019 Gandalf held the Bridge of Khazad-dûm against Durin's Bane, the Balrog of Moria, and fell with it into the abyss.
  52. c. 29,981 BC
    Gandalf the White
    Gandalf pursued the Balrog to the peak of Zirakzigil and threw it down on 25 January 3019, and died; he was sent back on 14 February as Gandalf the White.
  53. c. 29,981 BC
    The Breaking of the Fellowship
    On 26 February 3019 the Fellowship was broken at Parth Galen: Boromir fell defending Merry and Pippin, and Frodo and Sam went on alone towards Mordor.
  54. c. 29,981 BC
    Helm's Deep
    On 3 March 3019 the Rohirrim under Théoden, with Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli, held the Hornburg at Helm's Deep against the host of Saruman, and at dawn the host was destroyed.
  55. c. 29,981 BC
    Saruman's staff broken
    On 5 March 3019 Gandalf cast Saruman out of the order of the Istari and broke his staff on the stair of Orthanc.
  56. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn wrestles Sauron in the palantír
    On 6 March 3019 Aragorn looked into the palantír of Orthanc and wrestled with Sauron himself through it, showing him the reforged sword, and from then on he stopped doubting that he would be king.
  57. c. 29,981 BC
    The Paths of the Dead
    On 8 March 3019 Aragorn took the Paths of the Dead under the White Mountains, which everybody told him led only to death, came out at the other end, and summoned the Oathbreakers to the Stone of Erech.
  58. c. 29,981 BC
    The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
    On 15 March 3019 the Witch-king was slain by Éowyn and Merry on the Pelennor Fields before Minas Tirith, and Aragorn came up the Anduin on the black ships with a star on his brow, Arwen's standard unfurled and Andúril drawn, and turned the battle.
  59. c. 29,981 BC
    The hands of the king
    That night in the Houses of Healing Aragorn laid his hands on Faramir, Éowyn and Merry and they woke, and the old woman Ioreth said that the hands of the king are the hands of a healer.
  60. c. 29,981 BC
    The One Ring destroyed
    On 25 March 3019, at the Crack of Doom in the Sammath Naur, the Ring was too strong for Frodo, and he claimed it for his own. Gollum bit off his finger with the Ring on it, then fell with it into the fire. So the One Ring, the first Horcrux, was unmade where it was made. Barad-dûr fell, and Sauron's power ended for ever.
  61. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn crowned
    On 1 May 3019 Gandalf set the crown on Aragorn's head before the gates of Minas Tirith, and he became King Elessar of Gondor and Arnor.
  62. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn weds Arwen
    At Midsummer of the year 3019 Aragorn wedded Arwen in Minas Tirith; she chose the mortality of Men, and from their line, which carried the Elves and Númenor together, would come Godric Gryffindor, the Pevensies and Harry Potter.
  63. c. 29,981 BC
    The Battle of Bywater
    On 3 November 3019 the hobbits drove Saruman's ruffians out of the Shire at the Battle of Bywater, and Saruman was killed by Gríma Wormtongue at Bag End.

The Fourth Age and the forgotten ages

  1. c. 29,979 BC
    The Ring-bearers sail West
    On 29 September 3021 Frodo and Bilbo sailed from the Grey Havens into the West with Elrond, Galadriel and Gandalf, who bore Narya openly at last; it was the end of the Third Age.
  2. c. 29,919 BC
    Samwise sails
    In the year 61 of the Fourth Age, after the death of his wife Rose, Samwise Gamgee rode to the Grey Havens and sailed into the West, the last of the Ring-bearers.
  3. c. 29,860 BC
    King Elessar dies
    On 1 March in the year 120 of the Fourth Age King Elessar laid down his life at the age of two hundred and ten, after a reign of a hundred and twenty years, and his son Eldarion took the throne.
  4. c. 29,860 BC
    Andúril passes to Eldarion
    Andúril passed to Eldarion and went on down the line of Aragorn and Arwen, carried by a series of brave men through the ages.
  5. c. 29,860 BC
    Legolas and Gimli sail
    After Elessar's death Legolas built a grey ship in Ithilien and sailed down the Anduin and over the Sea, taking Gimli the Dwarf with him, and the last of the Fellowship passed out of Middle-earth.
  6. c. 29,859 BC
    Arwen dies on Cerin Amroth
    Arwen went alone to Lórien, empty by then, and in the year 121 of the Fourth Age, when the mallorn leaves were falling, she laid herself to rest on the hill of Cerin Amroth.
  7. c. 29,000 BC
    Most of the Elves pass out of the world
    Through the Fourth Age, the Dominion of Men, most of the Elves took ship into the West or faded. Their craftsmanship went with them, and so did the last of the ring-lore that Sauron had taught in Eregion. A remnant stayed on with Círdan at the Grey Havens, where some were still to be found in the days of King Arthur.
  8. c. 29,000 BC
    The Clone Wars begin on Krypton
    Nyra's clone bride for her son Kan-Z set off a thousand-year war, which ended when Black Zero's Destroyer wiped out Kandor.
  9. c. 28,000 BC
    Cain walks through the Middle-earth ages
    Through the Third and Fourth Ages and the forgotten ages after them Cain still wandered, older than the Istari and the Rings, unseen by the Wise, a cursed man who could not die and had no powers.
  10. c. 27,000 BC
    The heirs of Elessar endure
    In the lost ages after the Fourth Age the line of Aragorn and Arwen went on unrecognised among Men, carrying the blood of the Elves and of Númenor.
  11. c. 27,000 BC
    The Mi-go come to the Earth
    The Mi-go came to the Earth from Yuggoth, at the edge of the solar system, to mine its hills. They drove the Elder Things out of the northern lands.
  12. c. 25,000 BC
    The Great Race flees into the future
    When the flying polyps that the Great Race had shut away under the earth broke out, the minds of the Great Race fled forward in time into a people of beetles that will come after mankind.

The Thurian Age

  1. c. 24,000 BC
    The serpent men rule Valusia
    In the lost ages after the Fourth Age the serpent men, an ancient race who served the Old Serpent and practised his sorcery, ruled the land of Valusia on the Thurian continent.
  2. c. 22,000 BC
    Men cast down the serpent men
    Kings of men overthrew the serpent men and took Valusia for their own, but the serpent men lingered in hiding, able by their sorcery to wear the faces of men.
  3. c. 21,000 BC
    The Seven Empires of the Thurian Age
    Valusia, eldest and greatest of the Seven Empires, flourished with Kamelia, Verulia, Grondar, Thule and Commoria on the Thurian continent, while barbarian Atlantis lay in the ocean to the west, the Pictish Isles beyond it, and the isles of Lemuria in the east.
  4. c. 20,000 BC
    Atlanteans and Picts at war
    The barbarian Atlanteans and the Picts of the western isles waged long wars on one another, and Valusia kept the Picts as allies.
  5. c. 18,620 BC
    Kull is born in Atlantis
    Kull was born in Atlantis, a foundling who grew up wild in the Tiger Valley until the Sea-mountain tribe took him in.
  6. c. 18,602 BC
    Kull exiled from Atlantis
    As a youth Kull broke the law of his tribe by killing a girl condemned to the stake so that she would not suffer the fire, and fled Atlantis an exile.
  7. c. 18,595 BC
    Kull's wandering years
    Kull was in turn a pirate, a galley slave of the Lemurians, an outlaw, a gladiator and a soldier of the Valusian armies, in which he rose to high command.
  8. c. 18,580 BC
    Kull takes the throne of Valusia
    Kull slew the tyrant Borna and took the throne of Valusia, an Atlantean barbarian on the seat of the oldest kingdom of men.
  9. c. 18,578 BC
    The Shadow Kingdom
    Warned by Ka-nu, the Pictish ambassador, Kull and the Pict Brule the Spear-slayer uncovered serpent men wearing the faces of his own court, exposed them with the ancient words 'Ka nama kaa lajerama' and slew them.
  10. c. 18,575 BC
    The Mirrors of Tuzun Thune
    The wizard Tuzun Thune lured Kull into gazing into his enchanted mirrors until he nearly passed into them, and Brule saved the king by running the wizard through.
  11. c. 18,570 BC
    By this axe I rule
    When Ardyon and a band of conspirators fell on him in his chamber, Kull fought them off, then broke with his axe the ancient tablet of law so that the girl Lala-ah could marry Seno val Dor, the man she loved, crying 'By this axe I rule!'
  12. c. 18,565 BC
    Kull and Thulsa Doom
    Kull thwarted the plotting of the skull-faced necromancer Thulsa Doom, a sorcerer of the old dark craft who fled from him rather than be destroyed.

The Hyborian Age

  1. c. 18,000 BC
    The Cataclysm
    The Thurian Age ended in the Cataclysm: Atlantis and Lemuria sank beneath the sea, the Pictish Isles were heaved up to become the peaks of a new continent, and Valusia and the Seven Empires were broken by earthquake, fire and flood.
  2. c. 17,800 BC
    The survivors of the Cataclysm
    The Atlanteans of a colony on the mainland survived the Cataclysm and fell back into ape-like savagery, the Picts sank to the Stone Age, and a remnant of the Thurian folk, the Zhemri, endured in the eastern hills.
  3. c. 17,000 BC
    The Lemurians enslaved
    Survivors of Lemuria who reached the eastern shores were enslaved by an ancient race that dwelt there.
  4. c. 16,500 BC
    The Hyborians appear in the north
    In the north a tribe descended from Thurian survivors grew into a nation of hunters named after their chief Bori, who was later worshipped as a god; these were the Hyborians.
  5. c. 16,000 BC
    The founding of Stygia
    The Lemurians rose and threw off their masters, and the ancient race, driven westward, conquered the land south of the river Styx and founded Stygia, the serpent kingdom.
  6. c. 15,500 BC
    Hyperborea founded
    The Hyborians drifted south and built their first kingdom, Hyperborea, with fortresses of uncut stone.
  7. c. 15,000 BC
    Set worshipped in Stygia
    The Stygians worshipped Set, the Old Serpent, who was the being once called Morgoth, in black temples where a great serpent was kept and fed, and their sorcerers learned their art from the thing in those temples and paid dearly for it.
  8. c. 14,800 BC
    Stygia becomes the library of dark magic
    Stygia did not invent dark magic, but there Morgoth's craft was kept, collected, systematised and practised at scale, and most dark spells still in use derive at least in part from what Stygia held.
  9. c. 14,500 BC
    Acheron rises
    Acheron, an empire of sorcerers whose capital was purple-towered Python, rose in the lands that would later be Aquilonia, Nemedia and Argos.
  10. c. 14,000 BC
    The Cimmerians emerge
    Over long ages the descendants of the Atlanteans climbed back out of savagery and became the Cimmerians, a grim people of the dark northern hills.
  11. c. 13,050 BC
    Xaltotun of Python
    Xaltotun of Python, a priest of Set and the greatest sorcerer of Acheron, wielded the Heart of Ahriman, a jewel that burned like living fire.
  12. c. 13,040 BC
    The fall of Acheron
    The barbarian Hyborians overthrew Acheron three thousand years before Conan's reign; Xaltotun's body was hidden away and the Heart of Ahriman taken from him, and Acheron's surviving sorcerers fled into Stygia with their craft.
  13. c. 12,500 BC
    The Hyborian kingdoms
    In the centuries after Acheron's fall the Hyborians founded Nemedia, Koth, Ophir, Argos, Corinthia and the Border Kingdom, and in the west Aquilonia, which became the mightiest of them.
  14. c. 12,000 BC
    Cain wanders the Hyborian world
    Through the Hyborian Age Cain walked unnoticed among its kingdoms and sorcerers, older than Stygia and still no vampire, only a cursed man who could not die.
  15. c. 11,550 BC
    Epemitreus the Sage
    Epemitreus the Sage, who had fought Set and his servants all his life, died and was laid in a crypt beneath Mount Golamira in Aquilonia, fifteen hundred years before Conan's reign.
  16. c. 11,000 BC
    Turan founded
    The Hyrkanians, descendants of the Lemurians, came out of the east round the inland Vilayet Sea and founded the kingdom of Turan on its western shore.
  17. c. 11,000 BC
    The Fall of the Eldar
    The Eldar empire, given over to every excess, fed Slaanesh, the Chaos God of pleasure, until Slaanesh rose and devoured it. Most of the Eldar perished in a moment, body and soul. The survivors fled into hiding.
  18. c. 11,000 BC
    Eldar survivors settle on Vulcan
    A band of Eldar fleeing the Fall came down on Vulcan. In time they forgot what they had been, and their descendants became the Vulcans.
  19. c. 10,400 BC
    The Nephilim are born
    In the days before the Flood the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and their children were the Nephilim, giants in the earth, mighty men of old, men of renown; the Book of Enoch tells that their fathers were the Watchers, angels who had left their place.
  20. c. 10,350 BC
    Noah is born
    Noah was born to Lamech, a descendant of Seth son of Adam, who named him saying that this son would comfort them concerning their work and the toil of their hands on the ground which the Lord had cursed.
  21. c. 10,200 BC
    The giants devour men
    The Nephilim consumed all that men could grow and then turned to devouring men themselves, and the earth was filled with violence.
  22. c. 10,090 BC
    Conan is born in Cimmeria
    Conan was born in Cimmeria, among the dark hills of the north, of a ritual in which a circle of the elder world's sorcerers gave their lives so that their power would be reborn together in a single child.
  23. c. 10,075 BC
    The sack of Venarium
    At fifteen Conan was among the Cimmerian warriors who stormed and burned Venarium, the Aquilonian fort on their southern border.
  24. c. 10,073 BC
    The Frost-Giant's Daughter
    Fighting beside the Æsir against the Vanir in the snows of Nordheim, Conan pursued Atali, daughter of Ymir the frost-giant, across the ice.
  25. c. 10,070 BC
    Thoth-Amon of the Black Ring
    In Stygia Thoth-Amon, mightiest sorcerer of the Black Ring, drew his power from the Serpent Ring of Set and kept the dark craft of the serpent kingdom.
  26. c. 10,070 BC
    The Tower of the Elephant
    As a young thief in Zamora Conan climbed the Tower of the Elephant to steal its jewel and found Yag-Kosha, a blinded being from the stars, enslaved by the sorcerer Yara; at his bidding Conan used the Heart of the Elephant to destroy Yara and his tower.
  27. c. 10,069 BC
    The God in the Bowl
    In the temple of Kallian Publico in Numalia in Nemedia, Conan, accused of murder, faced a serpent thing out of Stygia that had been sent there sealed in a bowl.
  28. c. 10,065 BC
    Conan and Bêlit
    Conan joined Bêlit, the pirate queen of the Black Coast, on her ship the Tigress, and her black corsairs called him Amra, the Lion.
  29. c. 10,063 BC
    The death of Bêlit
    In a ruined city on the river Zarkheba Bêlit was killed by a winged demon like an ape; Conan laid her on the Tigress and sent her burning out to sea.
  30. c. 10,062 BC
    Black Colossus
    Made general of Khoraja's armies by Princess Yasmela, Conan destroyed Natohk the Veiled One, the sorcerer Thugra Khotan, who had woken from three thousand years' sleep in ruined Kuthchemes.
  31. c. 10,061 BC
    A Witch Shall Be Born
    In Khauran the witch Salome usurped the throne of her twin sister Queen Taramis and had Conan, captain of the guard, crucified in the desert; he survived and returned to overthrow her.
  32. c. 10,060 BC
    The People of the Black Circle
    As chief of the Afghuli hillmen of the Himelian Mountains, Conan carried off Yasmina, the Devi of Vendhya, and with her broke the Black Seers of Mount Yimsha.
  33. c. 10,058 BC
    Red Nails
    With Valeria of the Red Brotherhood, Conan came upon the walled city of Xuchotl in the southern jungles and ended both its long feud between the Tecuhltli and the Xotalanc and the witch Tascela.
  34. c. 10,056 BC
    Beyond the Black River
    Serving as a scout at Fort Tuscelan on the Pictish frontier of Aquilonia, Conan fought the Pictish wizard Zogar Sag, whose swamp devils and painted warriors destroyed the fort.
  35. c. 10,053 BC
    Thoth-Amon loses the Serpent Ring
    Thoth-Amon lost the Serpent Ring of Set to a thief, fled Stygia, and fell into slavery to the outlaw Ascalante.
  36. c. 10,050 BC
    Conan seizes Aquilonia's throne
    As general of Aquilonia's armies on the western frontier, Conan led a rebellion against the mad king Numedides and strangled him on his own throne, taking the crown of Aquilonia with his own hand at about forty years of age.
  37. c. 10,049 BC
    The Phoenix on the Sword
    Ascalante and his Rebel Four plotted to murder King Conan; the shade of Epemitreus marked Conan's sword with a phoenix in a dream, and Thoth-Amon, his ring regained, sent a demon out of Set's darkness that slew Ascalante and was slain by Conan with the marked sword.
  38. c. 10,048 BC
    The Scarlet Citadel
    Betrayed by Strabonus of Koth and Amalrus of Ophir, Conan was cast into the dungeons beneath the Scarlet Citadel of Khorshemish by the wizard Tsotha-lanti, freed the imprisoned sorcerer Pelias, and returned to save his throne.
  39. c. 10,045 BC
    The Hour of the Dragon
    The priest Orastes raised Xaltotun from his three-thousand-year sleep with the Heart of Ahriman; by his sorcery Tarascus of Nemedia and the pretender Valerius overthrew Conan at Valkia, and Conan escaped the pits of Belverus with the help of the girl Zenobia.
  40. c. 10,044 BC
    Conan in Khemi
    Pursuing the stolen Heart of Ahriman, Conan went into Stygia, to the black city of Khemi and the dark places of Set, and won the jewel back.
  41. c. 10,044 BC
    Conan regains his throne
    With the Heart of Ahriman Conan destroyed Xaltotun and won back the throne of Aquilonia, and made Zenobia his queen.
  42. c. 10,025 BC
    Conan lays down his crown
    Conan gave the crown of Aquilonia to his son Conn and sailed west into the unknown lands beyond the ocean. In the years that followed he understood that he was not growing old, and could not die.
  43. c. 9980 BC
    The Hyrkanians press west
    In the generations after Conan the Hyrkanians pressed in from the east and the Hyborian kingdoms began to fall apart in war.
  44. c. 9960 BC
    The ice begins to come down
    The ice began to come down out of the north, until it lay a mile thick on the mountains, and drove the Nordic peoples, the Æsir and the Vanir, south against the failing Hyborian kingdoms.
  45. c. 9950 BC
    Arus and Gorm
    A Nemedian priest named Arus went among the Picts to teach them the gentle worship of Mitra, but their chief Gorm learned from him and his kind the arts of war and iron, and united the Pictish clans.
  46. c. 9930 BC
    The Picts overrun Aquilonia
    Under Gorm the Picts broke over the Black River and overran Aquilonia, and the Hyborian kingdoms fell to Picts, Hyrkanians and Nordic invaders.
  47. c. 9900 BC
    The second great cataclysm
    A second great cataclysm shook the west of the world: lands sank and seas broke in, the dominion of the Picts was thrown down, and the wrecks of the Hyborian kingdoms were scattered under the ice, though Stygia's black towers still stood by the warm seas.
  48. c. 9850 BC
    Shem, Ham and Japheth are born
    When Noah was five hundred years old he begat Shem, Ham and Japheth.

Noah's Flood and the end of the Ice Age

  1. c. 9820 BC
    God's warning to Noah
    God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth and resolved to destroy all flesh; but Noah found grace in His eyes, and God told him that the end of all flesh was come and commanded him to build an ark.
  2. c. 9800 BC
    Noah builds the ark
    At God's command Noah built an ark of gopher wood, three hundred cubits long, fifty broad and thirty high, pitched within and without, with rooms, a window and a door in its side; Noah did all that God commanded him.
  3. c. 9750 BC
    Noah enters the ark
    When Noah was six hundred years old he went into the ark with his wife, his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth and their wives, and the beasts of the earth went in with him two by two, and the Lord shut him in.
  4. c. 9750 BC
    Noah's Flood ends the Ice Age
    The ice that had lain a mile thick on the mountains of the north went back at last, groaning and cracking, and its meltwater came down over the old world. That was the Flood of Genesis, the forty days of rain and the waters that rose above the mountains, God's judgement on the old world. Noah, who had built the ark at God's command, was saved in it with his family and the animals while everything else drowned.
  5. c. 9750 BC
    The rains and the rising waters
    The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened, and it rained forty days and forty nights; the waters increased and bore up the ark, and it went upon the face of the waters.
  6. c. 9740 BC
    The waters at their height
    The waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, fifteen cubits above the highest mountains, and every living thing outside the ark perished; the Nephilim, who were under no sentence of immortality, drowned with the rest.
  7. c. 9740 BC
    Stygia and the Hyborian world drowned
    The Flood drowned whole countries: the black towers of Stygia by the warm seas, the temples where men had worshipped a great serpent and fed it, and the sorcerers who had learned their craft from the thing in those temples.
  8. c. 9740 BC
    Knowledge of the elder ages drowned
    Nearly all knowledge of the ages of Middle-earth and of the Hyborian Age went under the water, so that they would reach later times only as story, and a wizard digging for the origins of his craft would find Egypt, then Stygia, then nothing.
  9. c. 9740 BC
    Cain survives the Flood
    Cain came through the Flood because he could not die: God had already sentenced him to live, and God does not revoke His own sentences, so he went into the water a cursed man and came out of it a cursed man, still no vampire.
  10. c. 9740 BC
    The line of Aragorn survives the Flood
    The line of Aragorn and Arwen survived the Flood and the forgetting of the old ages, carrying the magic of Elves and of Númenor in its blood towards Godric Gryffindor, the Pevensies and Harry Potter.
  11. c. 9740 BC
    Morgoth's craft scattered, not drowned
    The dark craft that Stygia had kept was scattered rather than drowned: one Stygian sorcerer lived through the water carrying its broken remnants, the man history would later miscall Herpo the Foul.
  12. c. 9740 BC
    R'lyeh goes down in the Flood
    The Flood that ended the Ice Age, God's judgement on a world filled with violence, drowned R'lyeh in the southern ocean with Cthulhu asleep inside it. The water did not kill him; it has held him dead but dreaming ever since.
  13. c. 9720 BC
    The ark rests on Ararat
    In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, as the waters went down, the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat.
  14. c. 9715 BC
    The raven and the dove
    Noah sent out a raven, and then a dove, which came back the second time with an olive leaf plucked off in her mouth, and the third time did not return.
  15. c. 9705 BC
    Noah leaves the ark
    When the face of the ground was dry, Noah came out of the ark with his household and the beasts, built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings on it.
  16. c. 9700 BC
    The covenant of the rainbow
    God blessed Noah and his sons and made His covenant with them and with every living creature, that the waters would never again become a flood to destroy all flesh, and He set His bow in the cloud as its token.

After the Flood: Cain, the First City and the first vampires

  1. c. 9600 BC
    God sends Gandalf to teach light magic
    After the Flood that ended the Ice Age, God sent the Maia Gandalf to the few frightened families of men left on the cold new shores, to teach them light magic as a counterweight to Morgoth. By their fires he taught them how to call a flame, ask the rain to wait, heal a cut and know that a voice from the dark offering power is never a friend's.
  2. c. 9598 BC
    Gandalf teaches the first Patronus Charm
    Among the first spells Gandalf gave the earliest wizards of men after the ice went back was the Patronus Charm, a defence against Morgoth's works and the only spell that has no dark version. The hands that passed it down were afterwards forgotten.
  3. c. 9595 BC
    Noah plants a vineyard
    In the years after the Flood Noah became a husbandman and planted a vineyard. Every man living after the Flood descends from him and his three sons.
  4. c. 9590 BC
    Cain meets Lilith
    Shortly after the Flood the cursed, deathless wanderer Cain met Lilith, a powerful immortal servant of Morgoth, who lied to him that she was Adam's first wife, the woman made before Eve who would not bow. He believed her.
  5. c. 9585 BC
    Cain learns blood magic and becomes the first vampire
    Lilith showed Cain the power in his own cursed blood and taught him blood magic, and he drank and became a vampire as the Kindred know them, with the Beast, the thirst and the Disciplines: the First Generation. He thought he was being given relief from his sentence; the bargain put him and every vampire after him under Morgoth's will.
  6. c. 9550 BC
    A Stygian survivor invents the modern Horcrux
    A Stygian sorcerer who lived on after the Flood, the man history calls Herpo the Foul and wrongly makes a Greek, gathered the broken remnants of Morgoth's craft and filled the gaps by guesswork. The result was the modern Horcrux, the One Ring reverse-engineered at the price of the maker's torn soul.
  7. c. 9500 BC
    Cain Embraces Enoch, Irad and Zillah
    After a time alone with his blood in the land of Nod, Cain Embraced three childer, Enoch, Irad and Zillah, who became the Second Generation of vampires.
  8. c. 9450 BC
    Enoch, the First City, is built
    With his three childer and the mortals who gathered to them, Cain built a city and named it Enoch after his eldest childe. It was the First City, and its vampires ruled it openly as gods.
  9. c. 9400 BC
    The Garou begin the Impergium
    In the age after the ice, fearing mankind's numbers and its growing works, the Garou began to hold humanity down by culling it. They call this age, which lasted some three thousand years, the Impergium, and many hold that the Delirium is its memory.
  10. c. 9400 BC
    Noah dies
    Noah died three hundred and fifty years after the Flood, at the age of nine hundred and fifty.
  11. c. 9300 BC
    The Antediluvians are Embraced; Cain forbids more
    The Second Generation Embraced thirteen childer of their own, the Third Generation or Antediluvians, founders of the thirteen clans: Brujah, Ennoia of the Gangrel, Malkav, Absimiliard of the Nosferatu, Arikel of the Toreador, the Ventrue founder, Lasombra, the Eldest of the Tzimisce, Haqim of the Assamites, Set, Ravnos, Saulot of the Salubri and Cappadocius. Seeing what the blood was becoming, Cain forbade any more Embraces.
  12. c. 9200 BC
    The Garou divide into tribes
    The Garou, once a single people, grew apart into tribes in the ages after the ice, each following its own totem spirit and its own Kinfolk across the world. The Silver Fangs led the Garou Nation from those ages onwards.
  13. c. 9000 BC
    The First City falls
    In time Enoch, the First City of Cain and his childer, fell.
  14. c. 9000 BC
    The first Slayer is made
    In the ages after the Flood, as the childer of Cain spread across the world, the men the Watchers remember as the Shadow Men worked a ritual that drew on the dwindling power of the Solar Exalted and bound it into a girl, the first Slayer, a guardian of the people where she lived.
  15. c. 8990 BC
    The Third Generation slays the Second
    The thirteen Antediluvians of the Third Generation rose against their sires and slew Enoch, Irad and Zillah of the Second.
  16. c. 8980 BC
    Cain curses the clans and departs into Nod
    Cain cursed the clans for the slaying, laying on each its own weakness, so that Absimiliard, once the most beautiful of the Third Generation, and all his Nosferatu line were made to wear their cruelty on their faces. Then Cain departed into the wilderness of Nod and has not ruled his get since.
  17. c. 8700 BC
    Zordon joins the Guardians of Eltar
    In the likeness of an Eltarian, Zordon rose from spearman to Bronze Guardian under Zophram, the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar.
  18. c. 8500 BC
    The Garou wage the War of Rage
    In the same ages as the Impergium the Garou made war on the other shapeshifting peoples, among them the bear-folk, cat-folk and raven-folk, and destroyed several of them outright. They count the War of Rage among their great shames.
  19. c. 8500 BC
    Zophram becomes Lord Zedd
    The Fire of Truth on the Zeo Crystal flayed Zophram, the first Supreme Guardian of Eltar. Zartus's lies turned him against Zordon, and Lord Zedd was born. Zordon became Supreme Guardian.
  20. c. 8000 BC
    The D'ni come to the cavern under New Mexico
    Ri'neref led the D'ni, descendants of the Ronay of the Age of Garternay, through a linking book into an enormous cavern deep beneath what is now the New Mexico desert. They gave the cavern, the city they raised round its underground lake and themselves the one name, D'ni.
  21. c. 8000 BC
    Zordon's war with Rita Repulsa
    Some ten thousand years ago Rita Repulsa, Lord Zedd's commander, made war on Zordon on Earth and on Eltar. At false peace talks she caught him in a time warp, and her curse put him in a tube outside time. His fail-safe sealed her with her servants in a space dumpster.
  22. c. 8000 BC
    The drowning of Aquaman's Atlantis
    By the chronicles of Poseidonis, the island city of Atlantis broke apart and sank about 8000 BC. King Orin's domes kept the people of Poseidonis and Tritonis alive under the sea.
  23. c. 8000 BC
    The Sub-Mariner's people settle a drowned island
    A wandering people of the deep, blue-skinned and water-breathing, found the ruins of the island that sank in the Cataclysm. They built their first city among them, taking its name of Atlantis.
  24. c. 7990 BC
    The D'ni enslave the Bahro
    The D'ni took the cavern from its original inhabitants, the Bahro, and enslaved them, binding them by a stone Tablet whose holder could command them; there are signs the Bahro were once hunted for sport.
  25. c. 7500 BC
    The Warders of Men watch over the first towns
    In the earliest towns the Garou who lived among humans and watched over them were called the Warders of Men, the forerunners of the Glass Walkers, while the Bone Gnawers followed people into the towns and scavenged at their edges.
  26. c. 7000 BC
    The Kree experiment on Earth
    In the thousands of years after the Flood the Kree took a tribe of hunters and altered them, hoping to make soldiers, then lost interest and left. Their descendants are the Inhumans.
  27. c. 6400 BC
    The Concord ends the Impergium
    The Impergium ended at a great gathering of the Garou tribes called the Concord, where the Children of Gaia were foremost in calling for its end. The Garou agreed to hide among men rather than rule them by fear, and took the Litany as their common law.
  28. c. 5000 BC
    Attilan is built
    The Inhumans built Attilan on an island far out in the North Atlantic.
  29. c. 3100 BC
    Egypt inherits Stygia's dark craft
    Ancient Egypt rose as Stygia's descendant and heir, and everything the European wizarding tradition calls ancient and dark came through Egypt first.

Antiquity and the first ages of magic

  1. c. 3000 BC
    Set is worshipped as a god in Egypt
    The Antediluvian Set was worshipped as a god in ancient Egypt, where he murdered Osiris and fought Horus. His childer, the Followers of Set, revere him as a god who sleeps and will rise to rule.
  2. c. 3000 BC
    Egypt rises against Ra
    Thousands of years ago the people of Egypt rose against Ra, the Goa'uld who ruled them as sun god and carried Egyptians through the Stargate as slaves to Abydos. Thor, the son of Odin, came down in a storm to fight beside them. Ra fled, and they buried his gate at Giza under cover stones declaring it sealed for all time.
  3. c. 3000 BC
    Ra forbids the Goa'uld to speak of Earth
    After the rising in Egypt, in which Thor fought beside the rebels, Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth again. The other System Lords kept the ban, and most of them avoided Earth from then on.
  4. c. 3000 BC
    En Sabah Nur is born at Akkaba
    Abandoned for his grey skin, the first of the mutants was raised by Baal of the Sandstormers in the years after the rising against Ra.
  5. c. 3000 BC
    The barbarian age of Vulcan
    About 3000 BC the Vulcans were still barbarians, ruled by their passions. Paranoia and murderous rage were common among them. They worshipped gods of war, peace and death.
  6. c. 2900 BC
    Set drives the Silent Striders from Egypt
    Set laid a great curse on the Silent Striders, the Garou tribe of the Nile who had fought him, which drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their ancestors.
  7. c. 2600 BC
    The Black Pharaoh reigns in Egypt
    Some centuries after the rising against Ra, a king called Nephren-Ka sat on the throne of Egypt and served Nyarlathotep, building a temple with a windowless crypt about the Shining Trapezohedron. What he did there caused his name to be struck from every monument and record.
  8. c. 2070 BC
    Yu rules China
    The Goa'uld Yu, defying Ra's ban, ruled China as Yu the Great and founded its first dynasty.
  9. c. 1440 BC
    Moses's spies see the sons of Anak
    The spies Moses sent into Canaan reported seeing the sons of Anak, who came of the giants, beside whom they were as grasshoppers.
  10. c. 1070 BC
    Samson pulls down the house of Dagon
    At Gaza the lords of the Philistines gathered in the house of Dagon to give thanks for the capture of Samson. Blinded and in chains, Samson asked the Lord for his strength once more, then pulled down the pillars. He killed more Philistines at his death than in his life.
  11. c. 1050 BC
    Dagon falls before the Ark
    The Philistines carried the captured Ark of the Lord into the house of Dagon at Ashdod. On two mornings running Dagon's image was found fallen on its face before it; the second time its head and hands lay broken on the threshold. After seven months of plague the Philistines sent the Ark home to Israel.
  12. c. 1000 BC
    Ba'al raids the North
    About three thousand years ago Ba'al, defying Ra's ban, sent ships to the coasts of the North to take slaves and hosts. Thor killed every Jaffa on the shore, brought one ship down into the sea and followed the rest to Ba'al's palace, which he broke open. Ba'al escaped.
  13. c. 850 BC
    The monastery at P'Jem is built
    Vulcan monks built a monastery on the world of P'Jem, a retreat for meditation that would stand for some three thousand years.
  14. c. 600 BC
    The dark inheritance passes to Greece
    The dark craft descended from Stygia passed from Egypt into Greece, where the wizarding record later picked up the Stygian it remembers as Herpo the Foul.
  15. c. 500 BC
    The Asari and the Salarians make an alliance
    The Asari and the Salarians, who had found each other among the stars, made an alliance that would last for more than two thousand years. The Asari were its peacemakers, the Salarians its scientists and spies.
  16. c. 450 BC
    The Toreador flourish in Athens
    The Toreador, the clan of artists and lovers of beauty, flourished in Athens and afterwards in Rome.
  17. c. 147 BC
    Jonathan burns the house of Dagon
    Jonathan, the brother of Judas Maccabeus, beat the army of Apollonius near Azotus, which is Ashdod. He burnt the temple of Dagon over the heads of the men who had fled into it.
  18. 146 BC
    Rome destroys Brujah Carthage
    Rome, guided by the Ventrue, destroyed Carthage, where the Brujah ruled and Kindred and mortals were said to have lived openly together. The Brujah have never forgiven the Ventrue for it.
  19. c. 4 BC
    Jesus Christ is born in Bethlehem
    Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was born in Bethlehem of the Virgin Mary in the reign of the emperor Augustus, and grew up in Nazareth.
  20. c. 1
    The Rachni Wars begin
    A Salarian survey ship found the Rachni, an insect-like people of one mind whose hive queens lived deep beneath their poisonous homeworld, Suen. The Rachni attacked at once. Since nobody could reach the queens to talk peace, the war went on for three centuries.
  21. c. 27
    Christ is baptised and tempted in the wilderness
    Jesus was baptised by John in the Jordan, and was tempted by Satan for forty days in the wilderness and refused him.
  22. c. 28
    Christ calls Simon Peter
    Simon, son of Jonah, was fishing on the lake of Galilee with his brother Andrew when Jesus called them to follow him and become fishers of men, and gave Simon the name Peter, the rock.
  23. c. 29
    Peter walks on the water
    One night in a storm Christ came to his disciples walking on the lake of Galilee, and Peter climbed out of the boat and walked towards him until he looked at the wind and the waves and began to sink. Christ caught him by the hand: 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?'
  24. c. 29
    Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ
    Peter was the first to confess Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and when he asked how often he must forgive his brother, Christ answered, until seventy times seven.
  25. c. 30
    Christ drives the money changers from the Temple
    In Jerusalem Christ found the Temple turned into a market, made a whip of cords and drove out the money changers, overturning their tables.
  26. c. 30
    Peter denies Christ three times
    On the night Christ was betrayed, Peter denied him three times before the cock crowed, and wept bitterly.
  27. c. 30
    Christ is crucified under Pontius Pilate
    Jesus was betrayed, condemned under Pontius Pilate and crucified at Jerusalem.
  28. c. 30
    Christ rises from the dead
    Christ rose from the dead on the third day and showed his wounds to his disciples, and Thomas believed. He asked Peter three times whether he loved him, and told him to feed his sheep.
  29. c. 30
    Peter leads the apostles after Pentecost
    After Pentecost Peter led the apostles in spreading the faith of Christ.
  30. c. 43
    The dark inheritance reaches Britain through Rome
    From Greece the dark craft passed to Rome, and with Rome it came to England and the rest of Europe, where Celtic, Norse and Druidic blood rites carried downstream fragments of the same source.
  31. c. 64
    Saint Peter is crucified at Rome
    By tradition Peter was crucified at Rome under the emperor Nero, head downwards at his own request.
  32. c. 80
    The Salarians raise up the Krogan
    Losing the war, the Salarians came upon the Krogan of Tuchanka, a people bombed back into savagery by their own atomic wars. The Salarians taught them, armed them with disruptors and gave them warp ships to fight the Rachni.
  33. c. 95
    The Revelation warns of the Mark of the Beast
    In the Revelation given to John, a beast rising out of the earth causes all to receive a mark on the right hand or the forehead, the number six hundred threescore and six, without which none may buy or sell; the power behind the beasts is the dragon, Satan.
  34. c. 300
    The Peverell brothers meet Death
    Antioch, Cadmus and Ignotus Peverell made a bridge by magic over a dangerous river at twilight and met Death on it, who gave them the Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone and his own Cloak of Invisibility: the Deathly Hallows.
  35. c. 300
    The Krogan end the Rachni Wars
    The Krogan went down into the lairs of the Rachni queens, retook the alliance's lost worlds and wiped the Rachni out. The grateful alliance gave the Krogan worlds of their own.
  36. c. 301
    Antioch Peverell is murdered for the Elder Wand
    The eldest brother, Antioch, boasted of his unbeatable wand and was murdered in his sleep for it; the wand passed on by murder and conquest through a long line of owners.
  37. c. 302
    Cadmus Peverell takes his own life
    The second brother, Cadmus, called back the girl he had hoped to marry with the Resurrection Stone, found her cold and sorrowful, and killed himself to join her. The stone came down his line to the Gaunts.
  38. c. 320
    Surak teaches logic on Vulcan
    With Vulcan's wars now fought with atomic weapons and the planet close to destruction, the philosopher Surak taught that his people must master their passions by logic or perish. His followers went out among the warring nations as emissaries of peace. The years of his teaching were remembered as the Time of Awakening.
  39. c. 350
    Death of Surak
    Shortly before the last battle of Vulcan's war, Vulcans who marched beneath the raptor's wings made an atomic attack on Surak's followers. Surak died of radiation sickness afterwards, but his teachings won. What Vulcans believe was his katra was kept in an urn, while his first teachings were sealed in the Kir'Shara, and both were lost for centuries.
  40. c. 360
    Ignotus Peverell greets Death as an old friend
    The youngest brother, Ignotus, lived to a great age, gave the Cloak of Invisibility to his son and greeted Death as an old friend. From his line came the Pendragons.
  41. c. 370
    The Sundering: the Romulans leave Vulcan
    After Surak's death the Vulcans who would not accept his teachings left Vulcan for good. Their ships carried them far out into space to a pair of worlds that came to be called Romulus and Remus. There they became the Romulans, and in time they built the Romulan Star Empire.
  42. c. 400
    The White Howlers dance the Black Spiral
    In the days when the Picts held the north, the White Howlers, the Garou of Scotland, went down into the caverns beneath their land to carry the war to the Wyrm and danced the Black Spiral. It turned their minds inside out, and they came back up as the Black Spiral Dancers, the fourteenth tribe, which serves the Wyrm.
  43. c. 480
    Arthur Pendragon is conceived at Tintagel
    Arthur, son of Uther Pendragon, King of the Britons, and Igraine of Cornwall, was conceived at Tintagel through Merlin's art and raised in secret away from the court. Merlin was Gandalf, who advised him through the whole long, strange stretch of his years.
  44. c. 495
    Arthur draws the sword from the stone
    Arthur proved his right to the throne of the Britons by drawing a sword from a stone.
  45. c. 496
    The Lady of the Lake gives Arthur Excalibur
    From the Lady of the Lake, the Elf-lady Roma, Arthur received Excalibur, which the Elves of the Grey Havens had forged for him. Its scabbard kept its bearer from bleeding.
  46. c. 500
    Arthur founds the Round Table and marries Guinevere
    At Camelot Arthur gathered the knights of the Round Table, at which no seat stood higher than another, and married Guinevere.
  47. c. 500
    Wizards and the Church begin their long conflictB3 Ch6
    About fifteen hundred years before 1993, Christian missionaries reached Britain; early monks were often wizards, but the Church later turned against magic.
  48. c. 510
    Arthur defeats the Saxons
    King Arthur and his knights defeated the Saxons.
  49. c. 520
    Arthur's knights seek the Holy Grail
    Arthur sent the knights of the Round Table on the quest for the Holy Grail.
  50. c. 525
    Morgana steals the scabbard of Excalibur
    Morgana, Arthur's half-sister, a dark sorceress learned in healing and the dark arts, stole the scabbard of Excalibur and threw it into a lake, and sent enchantments to Camelot to expose Queen Guinevere.
  51. c. 537
    Arthur falls at Camlann and is borne to Avalon
    Arthur's reign was broken by Lancelot's love for Guinevere and Mordred's treachery. At Camlann he killed Mordred but was mortally wounded. He was carried in a barge to Avalon, which was the Grey Havens of the Elves. He sleeps there still.
  52. c. 550
    The Havens pass out of the world
    When the time came for the last ship to sail from the Grey Havens, the Elves who meant to stay did not let their harbour fade. They took it out of the circles of the world, and it became the hidden country beside Britain that the folk tales call the Otherworld. King Arthur sleeps there.
  53. c. 580
    A Squib child of Arthur's house goes among Muggles
    In the generations after King Arthur, before his house took the name Potter, a child was born to it without magic and sent out to be brought up among Muggles. The child's descendants, Muggles ever after, became the Braddocks.
  54. c. 600
    Arthur's heirs take the name Potter
    Attacked by Arthur's ancient enemies, dark wizards aligned with Morgana among them, his descendants the Pendragons changed their name to Potter as camouflage, long before the Norman Conquest. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what the name hid. The Peverell Cloak came down the line intact.
  55. c. 600
    Wizard monks bring Christianity into British magic
    When the missionaries came to Britain many of the early monks were wizards; half the healing charms still in use came from monasteries, and some monasteries were all but magical schools. For a long while wizards and the Church lived in harmony there.
  56. 664
    Synod of WhitbyB3 Ch15
    The Synod of Whitby was held; Hermione Granger later questioned the Fat Friar about it.
  57. c. 700
    The Krogan Rebellions begin
    The Krogan, who bred far faster than anybody else, spread from their own worlds into the worlds of others. When the alliance demanded that they leave the Asari colony of Lusia, Overlord Kredak walked out of the talks, and the Krogan Rebellions began.
  58. c. 700
    The Turians join the alliance
    In the middle of the rebellions the Asari and the Salarians met the Turians, who declared war on the Krogan almost at once. The Krogan dropped asteroids on Turian colonies, leaving three Turian worlds uninhabitable.
  59. c. 710
    The Turians loose the genophage
    The Salarians made a disease to end the rebellions, meant only as a threat. The Turians made it in quantity and loosed it on every Krogan world. After it only one Krogan pregnancy in a thousand came to term.
  60. c. 730
    Abdul Alhazred writes Al Azif
    In Damascus the poet Abdul Alhazred of Sanaa, who worshipped Yog-Sothoth and Cthulhu, wrote down what he had learnt of the Great Old Ones in a book he called Al Azif. Later ages called it the Necronomicon.
  61. 738
    Death of Abdul Alhazred
    Abdul Alhazred died in Damascus. The biographer Ebn Khallikan records that he was seized in broad daylight by an invisible monster and devoured before many witnesses.
  62. c. 795
    Viking raids begin the Fenris and Fianna feud
    The Get of Fenris came raiding with the Norse across the North Sea into Britain and Ireland, and the Viking raids began the long feud between them and the Fianna, still sung on both sides.
  63. c. 800
    The last Krogan warlords are beaten
    Decades after the genophage the last Krogan warlords, long since turned pirate, were beaten. The Turians took their place beside the Asari and the Salarians as the alliance's soldiers.
  64. c. 870
    Thor frees the Northmen on Cimmeria
    The Goa'uld Heru'ur, son of Ra, carried off the people of several Norse settlements to a cold world far from Earth. Thor followed, destroyed his army in a storm that lasted three days and left the Northmen on Cimmeria under his protection, with the device called Thor's Hammer to guard its gate.
  65. c. 870
    Kahless kills Molor and founds the Empire
    Kahless forged the first bat'leth from a lock of his own hair, in the molten rock of the volcano of Kri'stak. With it he killed the tyrant Molor, then united the Klingons as the first Emperor of the Klingon Empire.
  66. c. 870
    Kahless and Lukara hold Qam-Chee
    When five hundred warriors stormed the great hall at Qam-Chee, its garrison fled. Only the Emperor Kahless stood his ground, with the Lady Lukara beside him. She became his mate.
  67. c. 870
    Kahless promises to return
    Before he left his people, Kahless pointed to a star in the sky over Qo'noS, promising to return there one day. Klingons later settled Boreth, the world that circles that star, where clerics waited for him.
  68. 950
    Theodorus Philetas translates the Necronomicon
    Theodorus Philetas of Constantinople translated Al Azif into Greek under the title Necronomicon. Its readers tried terrible experiments with it.
  69. c. 950
    The beard-gold feud beginsB3 Ch4
    In the 900s a ritual failed to turn the dwarfs' beards to gold, starting a feud with a party of warlocks.
  70. 954
    Anglo-Saxons take JorvikB1 Ch12
    The wizarding war between the Norse völvas of Jorvik and the last Hellenic sorcerers out of London ended with the Anglo-Saxons taking Jorvik.
  71. c. 979
    Gandalf gathers the four founders on the crag
    Gandalf rounded up the four most quarrelsome young wizards of the isle, Rowena Ravenclaw, Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff and Salazar Slytherin, and stood them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake. It took him eleven years and two broken staffs to get them to sit at one table.
  72. 980s
    Gandalf gives Andúril to Godric Gryffindor
    When he gathered the four founders of Hogwarts, Gandalf placed Andúril in the hands of Godric Gryffindor, Aragorn's heir. Millennia had worn the blade down, and Godric took it to the goblin smith Ragnuk the First to be repaired, the work on which the goblins later built their claim to have forged it.
  73. 990
    Hogwarts is founded
    Hogwarts was founded by Ravenclaw, Gryffindor, Hufflepuff and Slytherin, whom Gandalf had brought together after eleven years of argument. Gandalf had placed in Godric Gryffindor's hands Andúril, which was his by blood as an heir of Aragorn.
  74. c. 990
    Gandalf brings the founders to one tableB2 Ch13
    Over eleven years Gandalf, who goes by Ambrose Greyhame in the twentieth century, brought the four quarrelling founders to the same table and made them build a hall of grey stone on a crag above a lake, breaking two staffs on the table along the way.
  75. c. 991
    Gandalf speaks to the first Hogwarts pupils
    When the hall at Hogwarts had half a roof, Gandalf came up out of the valley in the snow and told the muddy first-years by the kitchen fire, the boy who became the Fat Friar among them, that magic was a gift from Somebody who had never given up on them. The young school used the Patronus Charm against all sorts of nasty things.
  76. c. 993
    Hogwarts shuts out the old roadsB3 Interlude
    About a thousand years before 1993, the Hogwarts castle saw to it that none of the old crossroads routes ran within twenty miles of it.
  77. 990s
    Helga Hufflepuff teaches the first pupils
    Helga Hufflepuff taught at Hogwarts in its first years, brought house-elves into the castle kitchens where they could work in safety, and boxed the ears of the boy who became the Fat Friar for turning the porridge into frogspawn.
  78. 990s
    The founders enchant the Sorting Hat
    The four founders of Hogwarts put something of their own minds into a hat that had belonged to Godric Gryffindor, so that it could go on choosing their students after them; it still speaks of Godric, Helga and Salazar by their first names.
  79. 990s
    Thor destroys the fleets of the System Lords
    Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets to strike at Asgard. Thor, given command of Asgard's ships by Odin, destroyed two of the three above a dead world the Jaffa will not name; Apophis saved his own by running.

The Middle Ages to the sixteen hundreds

  1. c. 1000
    Gandalf wins an argument with Rowena Ravenclaw
    When her daughter Helena was very small, Gandalf came to Rowena Ravenclaw's house and argued with her by the fire all night, and in the morning she said he was the only man who had ever won an argument with her.
  2. c. 1000
    Hogwarts closes the midnight roads
    About a thousand years before 1994 the castle of Hogwarts saw to it that none of the old midnight roads, which run from crossroads to crossroads across the world, came within twenty miles of it.
  3. c. 1000
    The Protected Planets Treaty is signed
    Soon after their defeat by Thor the Goa'uld System Lords asked Asgard for terms, and the Protected Planets Treaty closed a list of worlds to them, Cimmeria among them. Earth, which the Goa'uld were forbidden to name, was left off it.
  4. 1000s
    Slytherin leaves Hogwarts
    After a bitter quarrel with Godric Gryffindor over admitting children of non-magical parents, Salazar Slytherin left Hogwarts, breaking Helga Hufflepuff's heart, and before he went built the Chamber of Secrets deep beneath the castle, sealed so that only his true heir could loose its Basilisk.
  5. 1000s
    Quidditch first played at Queerditch Marsh
    Quidditch was first played at Queerditch Marsh in the eleventh century and took its name from the place.
  6. 1000s
    The Tzimisce fight the Tremere
    From the eleventh century the Tzimisce voivodes of Transylvania fought the Tremere, newly become vampires, for the Carpathians.
  7. c. 1006
    The Makai Priests seal Legules
    About a thousand years before his return in 2006, the Horror Legules crossed into the world of men during a solar eclipse. The Makai Priests of Japan sealed him with the Phosphorus Arrow.
  8. c. 1020
    Death of Helena Ravenclaw
    Helena Ravenclaw stole her mother Rowena's diadem and fled to Albania; the dying Rowena sent the Baron to bring her home, and when she refused him he stabbed her to death in an Albanian forest and killed himself, returning with her to Hogwarts as the Bloody Baron and the Grey Lady, while the diadem lay hidden in a hollow tree.
  9. c. 1020
    Death of the Fat Friar
    The Fat Friar, a pupil of Helga Hufflepuff who became a Benedictine monk at a priory on the Wash that was in effect a school of magic, died about two centuries before the first friars reached England, and haunted his priory for a few hundred years.
  10. 1022
    The Tremere become vampires
    House Tremere, a house of wizards of the Order of Hermes, sought immortality as their magic waned, and Tremere's pupil Goratrix found it in the blood of captured vampires. Tremere and his inner council drank it and became vampires, and turned their magic into Thaumaturgy.
  11. c. 1030
    Gandalf takes back Gryffindor's sword from the goblins
    After Godric Gryffindor died, the goblins named his sword the Sword of Gryffindor and claimed to have forged it, meaning to take it for themselves. Gandalf stole it back first and kept it hidden for a later heir of Aragorn, and the histories record only that the sword vanished.
  12. c. 1050
    Gandalf hides the sword of Gryffindor
    After Godric Gryffindor's death the goblins put about the name 'the Sword of Gryffindor' for Andúril and claimed to have forged it, as grounds for taking it; before they could, Gandalf stole the sword back and hid it for the day another of Aragorn's heirs would need it.
  13. 1050
    The Patriarch Michael burns the Necronomicon
    The Patriarch Michael of Constantinople had the Greek Necronomicon burnt. The Arabic original was already lost.
  14. 1066
    Armand Malfoy is granted land in Wiltshire
    The Malfoys came over from Normandy with William the Conqueror, who granted Armand Malfoy the land in Wiltshire where Malfoy Manor stands and the family has lived ever since.
  15. 1066
    Norman ConquestB1 Ch4
    Norman wizarding families won the Conquest for William the Conqueror mostly with dark magic; Armand Malfoy received land in Wiltshire.
  16. 1066
    Malfoys arrive in EnglandB2 Ch3
    The Malfoy family came to England at the Norman conquest and, according to Fred Weasley, have been Dark wizards ever since.
  17. 1093
    Elisabetha Cronqvist dies
    While the knight and strategist Mathias Cronqvist was away on campaign in the Church's wars, his wife Elisabetha fell ill and died. Mathias took it as a betrayal by God, withdrew from the Church's service and resolved to live for ever to curse Heaven.
  18. 1094
    Walter Bernhard carries off Sara Trantoul
    The Tzimisce vampire Walter Bernhard, lord of a castle in a forest of eternal night kept dark by the Ebony Stone, carried off Sara Trantoul, betrothed of the knight Leon Belmont. Leon, refused leave by the Church, gave up his title and went after her alone.
  19. 1094
    Rinaldo Gandolfi arms Leon Belmont
    At the edge of the Forest of Eternal Night Leon Belmont met the alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi, whose daughter Walter Bernhard had killed. Rinaldo gave him a whip of alchemy in place of his surrendered sword, then enchanted his gauntlet so that it could draw in the magic of his enemies.
  20. 1094
    Leon Belmont defeats Walter's five guardians
    To reach Walter Bernhard's throne Leon Belmont had to defeat five guardians: a golem, the Medusa, a succubus, an undead parasite and the vampire Joachim Armster, whom Walter kept prisoner. From Joachim he learnt of the Ebony Stone, which kept the forest in endless night.
  21. 1094
    The Vampire Killer is made
    Leon Belmont brought Sara Trantoul out of the castle, but she had been bitten and was already turning. At her own wish he struck her down, so that her soul passed into Rinaldo Gandolfi's whip, which became the Vampire Killer.
  22. 1094
    Leon Belmont destroys Walter Bernhard
    With the newly made Vampire Killer Leon Belmont destroyed Walter Bernhard in his castle, the whip's first victim.
  23. 1094
    Mathias Cronqvist rises as a vampire
    At the moment of Walter's destruction Mathias Cronqvist, who had set the whole affair in motion, took Walter's blood and soul into the Crimson Stone and rose as a vampire. The Stone broke the rules of diablerie, setting him at the fourth generation and in Walter's clan, the Tzimisce.
  24. 1094
    Leon Belmont swears the Belmont oath
    Leon refused Mathias's offer of eternity at his side. He fought Dracula's servant Death, which had begun to serve Mathias, while Mathias withdrew. Then he swore that his descendants would hunt the night for ever, so the war between the Belmonts and the vampire who became Dracula began.
  25. 1094
    Mathias Cronqvist goes into hiding
    Mathias Cronqvist left for foreign lands, where he went on cursing God. Centuries passed before a Belmont met him again, under the name of Dracula.
  26. c. 1099
    The Assamites fight the Crusaders
    From their mountain fortress of Alamut in Persia, the Assamites fought the Crusaders and the Kindred who came east with them.
  27. 1133
    Tremere usurps the blood of Saulot
    Tremere drank the blood and soul of Saulot, the Antediluvian of the Salubri, and took his place among the Third Generation; the Tremere then hunted the Salubri almost to nothing and are called the Usurpers.
  28. 1140s
    The fall of Vyšehrad buries Christof
    Mortal forces stormed the Tzimisce castle of Vyšehrad above Prague and brought it down, burying Christof Romuald in torpor; the Tzimisce elders bound the Methuselah Vukodlak in a sleep of their own.
  29. 1141
    Christof Romuald is Embraced in Prague
    After killing a Tzimisce monster in a silver mine near Prague, the French crusader Christof Romuald was Embraced into Clan Brujah by Ecaterina the Wise.
  30. c. 1150
    The Tremere and Tzimisce war over Transylvania
    For generations the Tremere fought the Tzimisce for the mountains of Transylvania from their first fortress, Ceoris, and made gargoyles from captured Tzimisce, Gangrel and Nosferatu to fight for them.
  31. c. 1170
    The Toreador preside over the Courts of Love
    In the Middle Ages the Toreador presided over the Courts of Love of France and the courts of Spain and Italy, while the Ventrue ruled Europe's Kindred as feudal princes.
  32. c. 1190
    The four peoples of Hogwarts intermarryB2 Ch10
    About two hundred years after Hogwarts was founded, the four magical peoples of Britain at last began to marry one another.
  33. c. 1200
    The Squib branch takes the name Braddock
    In the Middle Ages the Muggle descendants of the Squib child of Arthur's house took the name Braddock, it is thought from the parish of Braddock, or Broadoak, in Cornwall. They never knew where they came from.
  34. c. 1220
    Leopold of Murnau leaves his testament
    Leopold of Murnau, a leading inquisitor of the early thirteenth century, left a testament that became the rule of the Society of Leopold, the secret Catholic order that carried the Inquisition's war on vampires into the modern age.
  35. 1228
    Olaus Wormius's Latin Necronomicon
    Olaus Wormius translated the Necronomicon from Greek into Latin.
  36. 1232
    Pope Gregory IX forbids the Necronomicon
    Pope Gregory IX banned both the Latin and the Greek texts of the Necronomicon. Copies survived all the same.
  37. 1289
    International Warlock Convention of 1289B2 Ch10
    The International Warlock Convention met, with a sub-committee of Sardinian sorcerers sitting that September.
  38. 1296
    Manticore clearedB3 Ch11
    A manticore was cleared of savaging a woodcutter, only because the Committee could find nobody willing to fetch it in.
  39. c. 1300
    Medieval witch-burningsB3 Ch1
    Thousands were burned between 1300 and 1400.
  40. 1346
    Welsh knight killed at CrécyB2 Ch9
    A Welsh knight was killed by a crossbow bolt through his visor at the Battle of Crécy and became a ghost.
  41. c. 1350
    The Ravnos come west with the Romani
    The Ravnos, a clan of tricksters out of India, came west into Europe with the Romani caravans, from whom they Embraced many of their childer.
  42. c. 1350
    Fourteenth-century witch burningsB3 Ch1
    Between 1300 and 1400 many thousands were burned, nearly all without magic; Wendelin the Weird was burned forty-seven times.
  43. c. 1370
    The Hur'q plunder Qo'noS
    A people from far across the galaxy, whom the Klingons called the Hur'q, or outsiders, invaded Qo'noS. They carried off many of its treasures, the Sword of Kahless among them.
  44. 1392
    The Wailing Widow drownsB2 Ch9
    A woman of Kent drowned herself in a well when her husband did not return from the Crusades; he returned a week later, and she became the Wailing Widow.
  45. c. 1400
    The Anarch Revolt breaks out
    As the Inquisition burned vampires across Europe and the elders saved themselves by giving their young to the fires, the young Kindred rose against their sires, learned to break the blood bond and hired Assamite assassins. The Brujah Tyler was among the revolt's leaders.
  46. 1400s
    The first Quidditch World Cup
    The Quidditch World Cup began to be played in the fifteenth century.
  47. 1400s
    Lugoj claims the Eldest's blood
    In the Anarch Revolt of the early fifteenth century the anarch Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed to have drunk the blood and soul of the Eldest, the Antediluvian founder of Clan Tzimisce, though many Tzimisce doubt it.
  48. c. 1405
    Gratiano storms the Castle of Shadows
    Lasombra anarchs led by Gratiano, the Antediluvian's youngest childe, stormed the Castle of Shadows on Sicily with Assamite allies, and Gratiano claimed to have drunk the blood and soul of Lasombra himself. No witness has ever confirmed it.
  49. c. 1413
    Lugoj claims to destroy the Tzimisce founder
    In the Anarch Revolt Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed to have destroyed the Eldest, the Antediluvian founder of the Tzimisce.
  50. c. 1430
    Alucard is born to Dracula and Lisa
    Dracula's son Adrian, the dhampir later called Alucard, was born to the vampire's second wife, Lisa, a witch who healed the sick. From his father he took long life with great strength, from his mother a conscience.
  51. 1430s
    Nider's book about antsB3 Ch15
    The Dominican Johannes Nider wrote a long book about ants in which he described witches as an organised army with the Devil for its bishop.
  52. 1435
    The elders found the Camarilla
    With the Inquisition burning and the Anarch Revolt raging, the Ventrue Hardestadt called a convocation of elders of several clans, among them the Toreador Rafael de Corazón, from which the Camarilla grew.
  53. 1435
    The Masquerade is proclaimed
    The convocation of elders agreed that the Kindred must vanish from mortal sight and become a legend, and the Masquerade became the first of the Camarilla's Six Traditions. After it vampires grew harder to find, and the Society of Leopold dwindled for long periods.
  54. 1435
    The vampire Masquerade beginsB3 Ch8
    The Masquerade, the vampires' own law of secrecy, came into force for vampires.
  55. c. 1437
    Johannes Nider calls witches a secret church
    The Dominican Johannes Nider wrote in a book about ants that witches were an army, a secret church with the Devil for its bishop.
  56. 1444
    Augustus Giovanni usurps the blood of Cappadocius
    Augustus Giovanni, a Venetian merchant prince Embraced into the line of Cappadocius, drank the blood and soul of Cappadocius himself and took his place in the Third Generation. The Giovanni then hunted down the rest of the Cappadocians.
  57. 1450
    Sonia Belmont meets Alucard
    On her seventeenth birthday Sonia Belmont met Alucard, the dhampir son of Dracula, who had turned against his father. The two became lovers, though he tried to keep her out of the war he saw coming.
  58. c. 1450
    Kaluu falls at Kamar-Taj
    In Kamar-Taj, a hidden valley of wizards high in the Himalayas, the young wizard later called the Ancient One overthrew his friend Kaluu, who had made its people his slaves. The old village was destroyed in the fighting. On its ruins the victor founded a school of wizards.
  59. c. 1450
    A blood-boiling curse kills a Muggle-baiterB3 Ch18
    A fifteenth-century curse that boils the blood from the feet up, recorded in a footnote in Moste Potente Potions, took nine hours to kill a Muggle-baiter in Shropshire.
  60. 1450
    Dracula's creatures kill Sonia Belmont's grandfather
    Dracula's castle rose in Transylvania, and his monsters attacked the house where Sonia Belmont had grown up. Her grandfather, who had trained her, was mortally wounded, so she took up his whip, the Vampire Killer.
  61. 1450
    Alucard tests Sonia Belmont
    In Dracula's castle Alucard challenged Sonia Belmont, to see whether she was strong enough for what lay ahead, and she beat him. He left the fight to her, sealed away his own power and withdrew to rest.
  62. 1450
    Sonia Belmont destroys Dracula
    Sonia Belmont, in her seventeenth year, destroyed Dracula on his throne, the first of her family to face him under that name. As he fell he swore to rise again for as long as evil remained in the world.
  63. c. 1451
    Trevor Belmont is born
    Sonia Belmont bore a son, Trevor. The Belmont chronicles hold that his father was Alucard, though Trevor was a mortal man in every respect.
  64. c. 1470
    The Wallachians drive out the Belmonts
    After Sonia Belmont's victory the people of Wallachia grew afraid of what the Belmonts could do. The townsfolk of Warakiya asked the family to leave, so Trevor Belmont grew up in exile.
  65. 1473
    Every Quidditch foul in one matchB1 Ch7
    All seven hundred recognised ways of committing a Quidditch foul were committed in a single World Cup match.
  66. c. 1474
    Hector leaves Dracula's service
    Hector, a Devil Forgemaster who forged demonic Innocent Devils for Dracula's armies, turned against his master, gave up his powers and lived quietly among mortals.
  67. c. 1475
    Lisa is put to death as a witch
    Dracula's wife Lisa was put to death as a witch; her last wish to their son was that he should not hate mankind for it. Dracula answered her death with war on the human race, and Alucard took the opposite side.
  68. 1476
    Trevor Belmont destroys Dracula
    Trevor Belmont, Sypha Belnades, Grant DaNasty and Alucard fought their way up through the clock tower of Dracula's castle, past his servant Death, to the keep. There the four of them destroyed Dracula together. The reported death of the Wallachian prince Vlad Tepes, which was Dracula, fell at the end of the same year.
  69. 1476
    Dracula looses his armies on Wallachia
    After the death of his wife, Lisa, Dracula raised armies of the dead to destroy mankind. Towns burnt across Wallachia, and the forces the Church sent against him were destroyed.
  70. 1476
