    The Church calls Trevor Belmont from exile
    With its own forces beaten, the Church turned to Trevor Belmont, whose family the Wallachians had driven out. He set out from Warakiya, the very town that had sent the Belmonts away.
  71. 1476
    Trevor Belmont frees Grant DaNasty
    Dracula had killed the family of the pirate Grant DaNasty, then turned Grant himself into a beast to guard the clock tower outside Warakiya. Trevor Belmont's whip broke the spell, and Grant joined him.
  72. 1476
    Trevor Belmont frees Sypha Belnades from stone
    A cyclops had ambushed Sypha Belnades, a young sorceress of the Church, in a graveyard, then sealed her in stone. Trevor Belmont destroyed the cyclops, which broke the spell, and she went on with him.
  73. 1476
    Alucard joins Trevor Belmont
    Alucard had woken when his father rose, and he waited for Trevor Belmont in the catacombs. He fought Trevor to test him, then joined him against Dracula.
  74. 1476
    Dracula's dying curse falls on Europe
    As he fell, Dracula laid a curse on the land. For three years it spread plague, mob violence and fear across Europe.
  75. 1476
    Wallachia welcomes the Belmonts home
    The people who had driven out the Belmonts now honoured them. Grant DaNasty stayed on in Warakiya to help Trevor Belmont rebuild it.
  76. c. 1477
    Trevor Belmont marries Sypha Belnades
    After the war Trevor Belmont married Sypha Belnades, joining the Belnades gift for magic to the Belmont line.
  77. c. 1477
    Alucard seals himself in sleep
    After his father's defeat Alucard chose to sleep, sealing himself away so that the blood of Dracula in him could do the world no harm.
  78. c. 1478
    Hector's beloved Rosaly is burned as a witch
    As Dracula's lingering curse spread plague, war and fear across Europe, Hector's beloved Rosaly was burned as a witch through the scheming of Isaac, a fellow Forgemaster still loyal to Dracula.
  79. 1479
    Hector takes up the forge again
    Hector tracked Isaac to Dracula's abandoned castle, seeking revenge for Rosaly. Isaac taunted him into taking back the powers he had given up, then fled.
  80. 1479
    Hector meets Julia Laforeze
    In the Baljhet Mountains Hector met Julia Laforeze, a witch in hiding from the witch-hunters, who looked startlingly like Rosaly. She was Isaac's sister, yet she helped Hector, believing that her brother was in the grip of Dracula's curse.
  81. 1479
    Trevor Belmont tests Hector
    At Garibaldi Temple Trevor Belmont took Hector for one of Dracula's servants, which he had once been, and fought him. He let Hector go on when he understood that his quarry was Isaac.
  82. 1479
    Saint Germain warns Hector against Zead
    A traveller through time who called himself Saint Germain urged Hector to give up his chase, then warned him against the priest Zead, who was guiding it. Zead attacked Saint Germain in the Forest of Jigramunt, but the traveller stepped out of the moment.
  83. 1479
    Hector fights Isaac at Cordova
    Hector caught Isaac in the town of Cordova, where they fought. Julia Laforeze came between them, begging Hector not to strike in anger, so Isaac escaped.
  84. 1479
    Isaac stabs Trevor Belmont
    Trevor Belmont opened the sealed corridor beneath the abandoned castle with his own blood, so that Hector could reach Isaac's hiding place. Isaac stabbed Trevor from behind, leaving him for dead, but Julia Laforeze's healing saved him.
  85. 1479
    Dracula's castle rises again
    Hector's battle with the guardian of the corridor fed a spell that Isaac had laid there. It raised Dracula's castle anew, three years after its fall.
  86. 1479
    Hector defeats Isaac
    In the throne room of the risen castle Hector beat his rival Isaac. Remembering Julia Laforeze's warning that the curse fed on rage, he held his hand.
  87. 1479
    Hector breaks Dracula's curse
    The priest Zead showed himself as Dracula's servant Death, took the beaten Isaac for a vessel and called Dracula into his body. Hector destroyed what rose. With a last forging he destroyed the essence of the curse itself.
  88. 1479
    Hector lays down his powers
    With the curse broken Hector gave up the forge for the second time. Julia Laforeze brought him out of the collapsing castle.
  89. 1479
    Saint Germain leaves for the future
    Saint Germain, satisfied that time was running true again, left 1479 for the distant future. He said that he meant to see how the war between mankind and Dracula would end.
  90. 1486
    The Malleus Maleficarum is published
    Two Dominicans published the Malleus Maleficarum, after which witchcraft on the Continent was an organised heresy and a pact with the Devil, and inquisitors and witch-finders followed.
  91. 1490s
    Honeydukes founded (approx.)B3 Ch8
    Honeydukes had stood in Hogsmeade for about five hundred years by 1993, according to Ron.
  92. 1490s
    Death of Nearly Headless NickB1 Ch3
    Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington died in a botched beheading almost five hundred years before 1991.
  93. 31 October 1492
    Death of Nearly Headless NickB2 Ch9
    Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, a wizard courtier of King Henry VII condemned after a spell to straighten the Lady Grieve's teeth left her with a tusk, was struck forty-five times on the neck with a blunt axe, leaving his head held on by an inch of skin, and remained as the ghost of Gryffindor Tower.
  94. 1493
    The Convention of Thorns ends the Anarch Revolt
    In England the Camarilla, the anarchs and the Assamites made peace at the Convention of Thorns; the anarchs who accepted were pardoned, and the Brujah, Gangrel, Malkavians, Nosferatu, Toreador, Tremere and Ventrue stood as the Camarilla's seven founding clans.
  95. 1493
    The Tremere lay the blood curse on the Assamites
    Under the terms of the Convention of Thorns the Assamites accepted a curse laid by the Tremere, under which any Assamite who drinks another vampire's blood is burnt by it.
  96. 1493
    The Sabbat is formed
    The anarchs who refused the Convention of Thorns, most of them Lasombra and Tzimisce, withdrew to Spain and the east and became the Sabbat, the Sword of Caine; the Tremere Goratrix, who had gone over to the anarchs, took his followers into it.
  97. 1493
    The Convention of Thorns and the Sabbat
    When the Convention of Thorns made peace at the end of the Anarch Revolt, the Tzimisce anarchs refused it and founded the Sabbat with the Lasombra.
  98. c. 1500
    The Place of the Silent Spirits
    Long before any settler came, the people of the country that would become Maine held the shore of Toluca Lake sacred. They called it the Place of the Silent Spirits and kept their holiest ceremonies there.
  99. 1528
    The Giovanni make the Promise
    The Giovanni made the Promise with the Camarilla: they would keep out of Kindred politics, and the Camarilla would leave them alone.
  100. 1530s
    Destruction of the Fat Friar's prioryB3 Ch15
    King Henry pulled down the priory on the Wash that the Fat Friar haunted, to sell the lead off its roof, and the Friar returned to Hogwarts.
  101. c. 1538
    The Fat Friar comes home to Hogwarts
    When King Henry VIII pulled down the Fat Friar's priory on the Wash to sell the lead off the roof, the ghost came home to Hogwarts, where he haunts a window at the end of the kitchen corridor.
  102. c. 1539
    Brother Aldric hides the Glastonbury booksB2 Ch9
    Under Henry the Eighth, Brother Aldric hid Glastonbury Abbey's books from the King's commissioners in a cave on the Tor before being hanged, drawn and quartered, about 450 years before 1992.
  103. 1540
    Coronado marches north into New Mexico
    The Spanish explorer Francisco Vásquez de Coronado led an army north into New Mexico in search of the golden Seven Cities of Cíbola, which did not exist; a few wizards marched with him unrecognised.
  104. 1541
    Spanish wizards stumble into D'niB3 Ch21
    Experimenting with long-distance Apparition across the desert, a few Spanish wizards from Coronado's army arrived by accident in the cavern of D'ni. The D'ni talked with them for a few hours through an interpreter, then sent them back up firmly and rather rudely; the Spaniards wrote it down and thought the D'ni not magical at all.
  105. 1576
    Dracula escapes Christopher Belmont as mist
    A century after Trevor Belmont's war Dracula rose again, and Christopher Belmont fought his way to the top of his castle. Just before the last blow Dracula turned himself to mist, leaving every appearance of a vampire destroyed, then slipped from the ruins as a bat.
  106. c. 1580
    John Dee's English Necronomicon
    In the reign of Elizabeth I, Dr John Dee made an English translation of the Necronomicon. It was never printed, and only fragments of it survive.
  107. 1588
    The ArmadaB3 Ch15
    Around the time of the Armada the Fat Friar gave up correcting people who called him a friar rather than a monk.
  108. 1591
    Belmont's Revenge
    Christopher Belmont faced Dracula again.
  109. 1591
    Dracula possesses Soleiyu Belmont
    On the eve of the ceremony at which Soleiyu Belmont was to receive the Vampire Killer, Dracula came into his room as mist while he slept. He possessed the young man, whose Belmont blood gave him back a human form.
  110. 1591
    Dracula conjures four castles
    Through Soleiyu Belmont Dracula conjured four castles, of plant, cloud, rock and crystal, to hold off the father who would come for his son. Christopher Belmont went through all four, not knowing that the lives of their fallen guardians were raising Dracula's own castle.
  111. 1591
    Christopher Belmont frees his son
    At the top of Dracula's castle Soleiyu Belmont challenged his father to fight to the death. Christopher fought with his blows held back until Dracula was driven out of his son, then went on alone to destroy Dracula a second time.
  112. c. 1592
    Lockhart's book misdates the Belmonts' huntB2 Ch7
    Gilderoy Lockhart's Voyages with Vampires dates the Belmonts' hunt for Dracula from about this year, four hundred years before Hermione Granger told Harry Potter of the family in September 1992. The book is wrong. The Belmonts have hunted him since 1094, under the name Dracula since 1450.
  113. c. 1600
    European Garou come to the Americas
    When Europeans crossed the Atlantic their Garou came with them, seized caerns and made war on the native tribes, the Uktena and the Wendigo, who call them Wyrmcomers and have never forgiven them.
  114. 1609
    The Master sires Darla
    In the Virginia colony the Master, the fourth-generation Ventrue who founded the Aurelian line and its priesthood, the Order of Aurelius, sired his favourite childe, Darla.
  115. 1612
    The goblin rebellion of 1612B3 Ch5
    One of the inns of Hogsmeade, the only all-wizard village in Britain, served as the headquarters of the goblin rebellion.
  116. 1612
    A killing curse is bannedB3 Ch18
    A fourth lethal curse known to Hermione Granger was banned in 1612, so that hardly anybody now knows its countercurse.
  117. 1612
    The tooth-growing curse bannedB4 Ch5
    A very old curse that makes the teeth keep growing until the jaw cannot close was banned.
  118. 1637
    Werewolf Code of ConductB1 Ch12
    The Werewolf Code of Conduct was established.
  119. 1689
    The Statute of Secrecy is signed
    The International Confederation of Wizards signed the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy, by which the witches and wizards of the world would hide from Muggles; it came into force in 1692.
  120. 1690s
    Settlers come to Toluca Lake
    Settlers drove the first people from the shore of Toluca Lake and built a town there, whose name has been lost.
  121. 1691
    Simon Belmont destroys Dracula
    When Dracula's castle rose again, Simon Belmont went in alone with the Vampire Killer, met Death in its halls and destroyed Dracula at the top of the castle, but took from him a curse, a wound that would not heal.
  122. 1691
    A black mass raises Dracula at Easter
    While the village kept the Easter festival, evil men gathered in a monastery at its edge to hold a black mass. Dracula rose with his castle, a hundred years after Christopher Belmont's second victory.
  123. 1692
    A Greek Necronomicon burns at Salem
    The last Greek copy of the Necronomicon anybody heard of went up in flames with a Salem man's library.
  124. 1692
    The Statute of Secrecy hides wizards from the ChurchB3 Ch6
    When the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy came in, the wizarding world hid from the Church in particular and threw out God and angels as it went, so that most wizards have scorned Christianity since. Some wizards say the Statute was inspired by the vampires' Masquerade.
  125. 1698
    Simon Belmont learns how to lift the curse
    Dying of the wound Dracula had given him, Simon Belmont visited his family's grave, where a young woman told him what he must do. Dracula's body lay in five parts in mansions across Transylvania, which Simon must gather, then burn in the ruins of the castle.
  126. 1698
    Simon Belmont takes Dracula's eye and ring
    In Brahm's mansion Simon Belmont destroyed Dracula's servant Death, winning the vampire's eye. In Laruba's he destroyed the vampire Camilla, who kept the ring.
  127. 1698
    Simon Belmont breaks Dracula's curse
    Seven years on, Simon Belmont gathered Dracula's rib, heart, eye, nail and ring from mansions across Transylvania, burned them in the ruins of the castle, destroyed the Dracula who rose from the fire and was freed of the curse.

The seventeen hundreds and eighteen hundreds

  1. 1700s
    Sickness empties the town on Toluca Lake
    A sickness that nobody could name went through the first town on Toluca Lake. The survivors abandoned it, and the houses stood empty for the best part of a century.
  2. c. 1700
    Angelus rampages across EuropeB2 Ch7
    In the eighteenth century the vampire Angelus cut a path across Europe, including Romania and London.
  3. c. 1700
    Wand magic takes its modern formB2 Ch10
    Wand magic took its modern form in the eighteenth century, many thousands of years after Gandalf first taught light magic.
  4. c. 1700
    Anna finds the D'ni cavernB3 Ch21
    In the 1700s Anna, a Muggle, found a way into the D'ni cavern and was taken prisoner.
  5. 1709
    Warlocks' Convention bans dragon breedingB1 Ch10
    The Warlocks' Convention of 1709 outlawed dragon breeding.
  6. 1722
    Hippogriff case lostB3 Ch11
    A hippogriff tried before the wizarding authorities lost its case and was treated barbarically afterwards.
  7. 1727
    Liam is born in Galway
    Liam, later the vampire Angelus, was born in Galway, the son of a linen merchant.
  8. 1746
    Maxim Kischine sets out to find Dracula's relics
    When the Vampire Killer went to Juste Belmont, his friend Maxim Kischine set out alone to prove himself. He meant to find the relics of Dracula's body, then destroy them as Simon Belmont had done. He gathered all six, which took possession of him.
  9. 1748
    Maxim Kischine returns without his memory
    Maxim Kischine came home badly hurt, with two years gone from his memory, to tell Juste Belmont that their friend Lydie Erlanger had been carried off. He led Juste through the fog to a castle that stood on no map.
  10. 1748
    Juste Belmont learns why the castle is double
    The castle stood in two layers on the same ground, each the mirror of the other. Dracula's servant Death told Juste Belmont why: two spirits shared Maxim Kischine's body, one of them his own, the other born of Dracula's relics. Maxim confessed that it was he who had carried Lydie off.
  11. 1748
    Juste Belmont destroys Death
    Death seized Lydie Erlanger, meaning to use her blood to make the two castles one, which would have destroyed Maxim Kischine's own spirit. Juste Belmont destroyed it.
  12. 1748
    Juste Belmont destroys Dracula's revenant
    Juste Belmont fought the possessed Maxim Kischine, who came back to himself at the sight of his own bracelet on Juste's wrist. A revenant of Dracula rose from the gathered relics. Juste destroyed it with the Vampire Killer, then went home with both his friends.
  13. c. 1750
    Azkaban becomes the Ministry's prison
    In the eighteenth century the Ministry of Magic made Azkaban, a fortress in the North Sea that the dementors already haunted, its prison, and has used the dementors as its guards ever since.
  14. 1753
    Darla sires Angelus
    In Galway Darla beckoned a handsome, drunken linen merchant's son from outside a tavern into an alley and sired him as the vampire Angelus, and the two cut a path across Europe for decades.
  15. 1753
    Darla sires Liam
    On the night his father finally turned him out of the house, Liam was beckoned into an alley by a pale lady from the colonies, Darla, who sired him.
  16. 1753
    Angelus slaughters his family in Galway
    Liam's first act as a vampire was to go home: his little sister Kathy, thinking he had come back as an angel, let him in, and he killed the whole household, servants and all, saving his father for last. From her mistake he took the name Angelus.
  17. 1753
    Angelus turned in GalwayB3 Ch9
    A linen merchant's idle son in Galway was turned by a pale lady from the colonies and became Angelus, who began by killing his whole household.
  18. c. 1755
    Angelus and Darla begin their reign of terror
    For decades Angelus and Darla roamed Europe in open defiance of the Masquerade, Angelus cutting a cross into the cheeks of his victims; it was in all the broadsheets. The Camarilla secretly backed mortal hunters against him, the Society of Leopold among them.
  19. 1764
    Daniel Holtz begins his hunt for Angelus
    Holtz, a hunter of the Society of Leopold, pursued Angelus and Darla across Europe for nine years without catching them, never knowing that some of the money behind the hunt came from the Camarilla.
  20. May 1764
    Angelus and Darla destroy Daniel Holtz's family
    At York Angelus and Darla killed the vampire hunter Daniel Holtz's wife Caroline and their infant son and turned his daughter Sarah, whom Holtz had to destroy by putting her out into the sunlight.
  21. April 1771
    Providence men raid Joseph Curwen's farm
    A party of Providence men raided the Pawtuxet farm of Joseph Curwen, who had called on Yog-Sothoth for most of the century without seeming to age, and killed him. They burnt his papers and struck his name from the town's records.
  22. 1773
    Holtz accepts Sahjhan's bargain
    A demon named Sahjhan offered Daniel Holtz a way to outlive Angelus and Darla, and Holtz accepted and slept, untouched by the years.
  23. c. 1782
    Anna finds the cavern of D'ni
    Anna, a Muggle woman of the New Mexico wilds who had learnt the rocks from her father, found a way down through the caves into the cavern of D'ni. The D'ni took her prisoner and questioned her, and she learnt their language in captivity.
  24. c. 1784
    Anna marries Aitrus and takes the name Ti'ana
    Given into the keeping of Lord Kahlis, Anna married his son Aitrus and took the name Ti'ana; Aitrus taught her the Art against D'ni custom, and she recorded everything she saw.
  25. c. 1785
    Gehn is born in D'ni
    Anna bore Aitrus a son, Gehn, a sickly child whom the healers did not expect to live.
  26. c. 1786
    Anna pleads for Lord Veovis's life
    When Lord Veovis was condemned for conspiring with the renegade A'Gaeris, an outcast of the Guild of Writers, Anna argued for exile instead of death and the council spared him; A'Gaeris then freed him.
  27. c. 1788
    The plague of A'Gaeris destroys D'ni
    A'Gaeris and Veovis loosed a plague that ran through the cavern of D'ni and out into its Ages and killed nearly every D'ni, ending ten thousand years of their city. The Art was lost with them, more or less, and the cavern stood empty for two centuries.
  28. c. 1788
    A'Gaeris murders Veovis
    When Veovis refused to write an Age in which the two of them would be worshipped as gods, A'Gaeris murdered him.
  29. c. 1788
    Aitrus dies trapping A'Gaeris
    Aitrus lured A'Gaeris into an unstable Age, where both of them died.
  30. c. 1788
    Anna escapes D'ni with Gehn
    Anna led her young son Gehn up through the caves by her husband's maps to the surface, near where she had first gone down, and made her home in the Cleft, a fissure beside an old volcano above the cavern.
  31. 1788
    The Fall of D'niB4 Ch4
    A'Gaeris and Veovis blew a hole in the wall of the D'ni cavern and let in a gas carrying a plague, which killed nearly all the D'ni within a few weeks, along with the glowing algae that lit the cavern.
  32. c. 1788
    Strange ancestors appear in American recordsB4 Ch4
    Just after 1788 clever, strange newcomers who made things nobody else could make began to appear in American family records; Hermione believed they were D'ni survivors who married settlers.
  33. c. 1789
    Gehn returns to the dead city of D'ni
    Gehn, who never forgave his mother for sparing Veovis, left her, went back down into the dead city and taught himself the Art from the books there, writing flawed Ages of his own; on his Fifth Age, Riven, the people worshipped him as a god.
  34. c. 1790
    The Fall of D'ni
    A plague, the plague of A'Gaeris, killed nearly all the D'ni a few years after Anna came to live among them, about two hundred years before the 1990s.
  35. c. 1790
    Atrus is born in the Cleft
    Gehn brought his wife Keta, a woman of the surface gravely ill with child, to his mother in the Cleft; Keta died giving birth, Gehn went away without naming the baby, and Anna named him Atrus after his grandfather and raised him.
  36. c. 1790
    Strange men collect contraptions in AmericaB4 Ch4
    From the 1790s to the 1830s newspapers reported strange men visiting farms and workshops to ask after unexplained contraptions; Hermione thought they were gathering what the D'ni had left behind.
  37. 1792
    Shaft's cult raises Dracula
    The dark priest Shaft, with his followers, sacrificed a young woman to bring Dracula back. The castle rose again, nearly a century after Simon Belmont had burnt its master's remains.
  38. 1792
    Dracula's servants carry off four young women
    Dracula's creatures burnt the villages near the castle. They carried off Annette, whom Richter Belmont loved, with the twelve-year-old Maria Renard, the nun Tera and Iris, the doctor's daughter.
  39. 1792
    Maria Renard joins Richter Belmont
    On the road to the castle Dracula's servant Death waylaid Richter Belmont, then let him pass. Inside, Richter found Maria Renard under Shaft's spell and set her free. She refused to go home, so the two fought on together, she with the four sacred beasts she could summon.
  40. 1792
    Richter Belmont defeats Shaft
    Richter Belmont beat the priest Shaft in the castle, then beat his ghost when it rose against him in the clock tower. Shaft's spirit survived all the same.
  41. 1792
    Richter Belmont destroys Dracula
    Richter Belmont, aged nineteen, freed Annette from the castle, then destroyed Dracula at its summit. The castle fell into the sea, and Richter afterwards married Annette.
  42. c. 1793
    The Prague Hand of Glory is madeB3 Interlude
    About two hundred years before 1993 a hand was cut from a man hanged on the gallows of Prague and made into a Hand of Glory, each of its fingers a candle. John Constantine later bought it from a dealer in Prague's Old Town and swore never to use it.
  43. 1796
    Richter Belmont disappears
    Four years after his victory Richter Belmont vanished without a word. The spirit of the priest Shaft, which had outlived his body, had taken hold of his mind.
  44. 1797
    Maria Renard goes in search of Richter Belmont
    A year after Richter Belmont vanished, Maria Renard, now seventeen, set out to find him. Dracula's castle came up out of the mist before her, with Richter enthroned inside as its lord.
  45. 1797
    Death disarms Alucard at the castle gate
    Alucard woke from more than three centuries of sleep when his father's castle rose. At its gate Dracula's servant Death warned him to turn back, then stripped him of the arms he carried.
  46. 1797
    Maria Renard gives Alucard the holy glasses
    Maria Renard was sure that Richter Belmont was not acting by his own will, so she gave Alucard a pair of holy glasses that show what is hidden. Through them he saw the green orb by which Shaft's spirit held Richter, destroyed it and set the Belmont free.
  47. 1797
    Alucard destroys Shaft in the inverted castle
    Shaft raised a second castle, upside down in the sky above the first, in which to finish the rite of Dracula's return. Alucard destroyed him there, too late to stop the rite.
  48. 1797
    Alucard destroys Dracula
    In the inverted castle Alucard faced his father, who raged that his son had sided with the people who killed Lisa. Alucard told him that Lisa had loved him to the end, then destroyed him. Dracula went into the dark asking her forgiveness.
  49. 1797
    Alucard returns to his sleep
    Alucard told Richter Belmont that his blood was cursed, then went back to his sleep so that it could do the world no harm. Maria Renard, who had come to love him, went after him.
  50. c. 1798
    Gehn teaches Atrus the Art
    Gehn came back to the Cleft for his son, took Atrus down into the ruined city and taught him the Art, and destroyed Atrus's first Age because it did not suit him. Atrus was awed, then horrified by his father's belief that a Writer owns the worlds he writes.
  51. c. 1799
    Atrus meets Catherine on Riven
    When Atrus tried to escape, Gehn shut him in a chamber whose only way out led to Riven, and there Atrus met and fell in love with Catherine, called Katran, a woman of that Age whom Gehn meant to make one of his wives.
  52. c. 1799
    Anna writes the Age of Myst
    Anna wrote the Age of Myst, a small island of grey rock and dark pines, as a refuge for her family.
  53. c. 1800
    Atrus and Catherine strand Gehn on Riven
    With Anna's help Atrus and Catherine destroyed every linking book out of Riven and left Gehn stranded there. Atrus leapt into the Star Fissure and linked to Myst Island as he fell, and his Myst linking book went on falling, out of Riven and down to Earth.
  54. c. 1800
    The Belmonts go missing
    After Richter Belmont's time the Belmonts vanished from the record for much of the nineteenth century. Other hunters took up the fight in their place, among them the Baldwins, the Order of Ecclesia, the Schneiders and, at the last, the Morris family.
  55. c. 1801
    Atrus and Catherine marry on Myst Island
    Atrus and Catherine married and made their home on Myst Island, where they raised two sons, Sirrus and Achenar, and from its library Atrus wrote and visited Age after Age.
  56. c. 1804
    Sirrus and Achenar plunder their father's Ages
    Growing up, Sirrus and Achenar stripped their father's Ages of riches and power and ruined the peoples of some of them, Sirrus hoarding fine things and Achenar weapons, poisons and instruments of torture.
  57. c. 1805
    Sirrus and Achenar betray their parents
    The brothers took their mother to Riven, where Gehn made her his prisoner and she became leader of the Moiety rebels, and stranded Atrus in D'ni by tearing a page out of his book home. Many of Myst's books were burnt.
  58. 1806
    Gehn is imprisoned on Riven
    Atrus sent the Stranger to Riven with a prison book disguised as a linking book; the Stranger freed Catherine and tricked Gehn into the book, and Atrus came for his wife as Riven began to break apart and the Rivenese were taken to safety. The Stranger went home through the Star Fissure and kept the little book, which his family handed down until it came to Albus Dumbledore.
  59. c. 1806
    The Stranger frees Atrus from his sons' trap
    A traveller from the surface, remembered only as the Stranger, found Atrus's lost Myst book and came to the island, refused both brothers trapped in the red and blue books and brought Atrus his missing page. Atrus came home, imprisoned his sons in separate Ages, Sirrus on Spire and Achenar on Haven, and wrote the Stranger a small leather linking book home.
  60. c. 1807
    Atrus and Catherine settle on Tomahna
    After Catherine's rescue Atrus and Catherine made a new home on the Age of Tomahna, where she wrote Ages of her own guided by her dreams, among them Serenia.
  61. c. 1810
    Atrus writes Releeshahn for the D'ni survivors
    Atrus gathered the few D'ni who had survived the plague scattered across their Ages and wrote the Age of Releeshahn as a new home for them.
  62. c. 1810
    Silent Hill is founded as a penal colony
    The empty town on Toluca Lake was settled again as a penal colony, and it was given the name Silent Hill. Silent Hill Prison was built beside the water. A shack put up to nurse the victims of a new plague grew in time into Brookhaven Hospital.
  63. 1812
    Yorkshire lady found in chimneyB2 Ch9
    The body of a Yorkshire lady bricked up in a chimney by her steward was found when the chimney was swept.
  64. 1815
    Yeesha is born on Tomahna
    Yeesha, daughter of Atrus and Catherine, was born on Tomahna; being of D'ni descent, she has lived far beyond any ordinary human span.
  65. 1816
    Saavedro steals the book of Releeshahn
    Saavedro, a man of an Age that Sirrus and Achenar had ruined, broke into Tomahna and stole the Releeshahn book in revenge, and the Stranger came back and recovered it.
  66. c. 1820
    Morris Baldwin seals Dracula away
    The hunter Morris Baldwin fought a newly risen Dracula beside the parents of Nathan Graves. Dracula was sealed away, but the Graveses died in the fight, so Baldwin brought up their son with his own boy, Hugh.
  67. c. 1826
    Sirrus and Achenar die over Yeesha
    Released after twenty years in their prison Ages, Sirrus kidnapped his young sister Yeesha; Achenar, who had come to regret what he had been, died saving her, and Sirrus died too. The Stranger helped save her.
  68. c. 1830
    The Glass Walkers become the Iron Riders
    In the age of steam and railways the Garou tribe of the cities, once the Warders of Men, were known as the Iron Riders.
  69. 1830
    Camilla wakes Dracula in Austria
    In an old castle on the edge of the Austrian Empire the vampire Camilla held the rite that woke Dracula. Morris Baldwin arrived too late with his two pupils. Dracula sent Hugh Baldwin through the floor with Nathan Graves, keeping their master to restore his own strength at the next full moon.
  70. 1830
    Nathan Graves brings Hugh Baldwin to himself
    Hugh Baldwin resented Nathan Graves, whom his father had chosen to carry the Hunter Whip, so Dracula turned that resentment into hatred. Nathan beat Hugh in the castle, which broke Dracula's hold on him.
  71. 1830
    Nathan Graves destroys Dracula
    Nathan Graves destroyed the vampire Camilla in the waterway beneath the castle. While Hugh Baldwin freed his father, Nathan destroyed Dracula, the Belmonts being missing in those years.
  72. c. 1835
    The Order of Ecclesia forges Dominus
    With the Belmonts missing, several bodies were founded to stand against Dracula, the Order of Ecclesia among them. Its master, Barlowe, forged a glyph in three parts out of Dracula's own power, called it Dominus and chose his pupil Shanoa to bear it.
  73. c. 1835
    Albus steals Dominus
    As Shanoa was about to receive Dominus, her fellow acolyte Albus broke in on the rite and carried the glyph off. Shanoa lost her memory, with every feeling she had, so Barlowe sent her after him.
  74. c. 1835
    Shanoa frees the villagers of Wygol
    Albus had carried off the people of Wygol village, who were descendants of the Belmonts, to study their blood. Shanoa found them one by one and set them free.
  75. c. 1835
    Albus dies to spare Shanoa
    The last part of Dominus mastered Albus, so Shanoa had to kill him. From his spirit she learnt that the glyph would take the life of whoever used it, which was why he had stolen it from her.
  76. c. 1835
    Barlowe raises Dracula
    Barlowe admitted that he had meant Shanoa as a sacrifice to bring Dracula back. She defeated him, but he gave his own life to break the seal on the vessel that held Dracula's soul, so the castle rose.
  77. c. 1835
    Shanoa destroys Dracula
    Shanoa destroyed Dracula with Dominus, at what should have been the cost of her life. The spirit of Albus gave itself in her place, asking only that she smile, so her memory came back to her with her feelings.
  78. 1839
    Unaussprechlichen Kulten is printed in Düsseldorf
    Friedrich Wilhelm von Junzt's book of the secret cults of the world, later called the Black Book, was printed in Düsseldorf in fewer than a thousand copies. When word of his gruesome end got about, most of its owners burnt their copies.
  79. 1844
    Dracula's servants burn Cornell's village
    Dracula's servant Death, the witch Actrise and the vampire Gilles de Rais set out to raise their master with a sacrifice. Their tool was Ortega, a man-beast jealous of his friend Cornell, who burnt Cornell's village before carrying off his adopted sister, Ada.
  80. 1844
    Cornell follows his sister to Dracula's castle
    The man-beast Cornell, who could take the shape of a wolf, came home from his training to find his village burnt. He followed his sister's trail to Dracula's castle.
  81. 1844
    Cornell saves Henry Oldrey
    At a villa below the castle Cornell found that Gilles de Rais had sired its master, J. A. Oldrey. At the plea of Oldrey's wife, Mary, he took their young son Henry to safety.
  82. 1844
    Cornell gives up his wolf's shape
    Cornell beat Ortega, then Dracula, who dragged Ada down with him as he fell. Cornell cast off his own power as a man-beast to pull her free. That power was the sacrifice Dracula's servants had wanted all along, with which they brought their master to birth again in a human child.
  83. July 1844
    The Starry Wisdom church opens in Providence
    Professor Enoch Bowen, home from Egypt, bought the old Free-Will Church on Federal Hill in Providence and set up the church of the Starry Wisdom, whose people worshipped by means of the Shining Trapezohedron. The city closed it in 1877 after a series of disappearances.
  84. 1846
    The Deep Ones rise against Innsmouth
    In 1846, with Captain Obed Marsh in jail, the Deep Ones came up from Devil Reef and killed more than half the people of Innsmouth, Massachusetts. Outside the town it was put down to a plague. Afterwards the Deep Ones lived among the survivors and bred with them.
  85. c. 1850
    Coal is found at Silent Hill
    Coal was found near Silent Hill, some ten years after the old prison had closed. The Wiltse mine opened, and the town had money for the first time.
  86. 1852
    Dracula is destroyed in the body of Malus
    Dracula had been reborn in a boy, Malus, who met his hunters as a lost child. The old hunter Charlie Vincent unmasked him with holy water. Reinhardt Schneider and Carrie Fernandez destroyed him in his true shape.
  87. 1852
    Two young hunters set out for Dracula's castle
    Reinhardt Schneider, of a family kin to the Belmonts, sensed Dracula's return, then set out for his castle in Wallachia. So did Carrie Fernandez, a twelve-year-old of Sypha's Belnades blood.
  88. 1852
    Rosa dies for Reinhardt Schneider
    Rosa, a young woman of the castle's villa who had been bitten against her will, stepped between Reinhardt Schneider and the scythe of Dracula's servant Death. Reinhardt destroyed Death.
  89. 1852
    Carrie Fernandez destroys the witch Actrise
    The witch Actrise, who had sacrificed children to bring Dracula back, tried to win Carrie Fernandez to her master's side. When that failed she set a vampire of Carrie's own kin on her, so Carrie destroyed them both.
  90. 1852
    Henry Oldrey rescues the stolen children
    Henry Oldrey, the boy Cornell had saved in 1844, came back to Dracula's castle as a knight of the Church. He brought out the children whom Dracula's servants had carried off.
  91. 1859
    Apocalypse makes Nathaniel Essex Mister Sinister
    In London Apocalypse remade the geneticist Nathaniel Essex into the long-lived Mister Sinister.
  92. 1860
    Drusilla joins Angelus and Darla
    Angelus's childe Drusilla joined him and Darla on their path across Europe.
  93. 1860
    Angelus turns Drusilla in a London conventB3 Ch9
    Angelus found Drusilla, a devout, gentle London witch with a little of the Sight, killed her family one by one and let her find them, and when she fled to a convent he came through the chapel on the day she took her holy orders and turned her, so that she would be mad for ever.
  94. 1860s
    Birth of Bra'tac
    Bra'tac, later First Prime of the Goa'uld Apophis and master of the Jaffa of Chulak, was born; kept strong by his larva, he had lived some hundred and thirty years by the 1990s.
  95. 1862
    A prison camp is built on Toluca Lake
    During the Civil War a camp for prisoners of war was built beside Toluca Lake at Silent Hill. In 1866 it became Toluca Prison, where the town's red-hooded executioners hanged men until the end of the century.
  96. c. 1870
    The Order of Silent Hill takes shape
    In the years after the Civil War the old faith of the lake, handed down in certain families of Silent Hill, hardened into a church with priests and saints of its own. Its members called it the Order. The god it worshipped was a demon.
  97. 1875
    Underage Sorcery decreeB2 Ch2
    The Decree for the Reasonable Restriction of Underage Sorcery was enacted.
  98. 1877
    The duel over Quaffle weight
    The Grail and Valmond duel over the weight of the Quaffle left two hundred dead and a three-page casualty list.
  99. 1877
    The Grail and Valmond duelB1 Ch7
    A dispute over the proper weight of a Quaffle between the England manager Francis Grail and the French manager Juste Valmond ended in a duel that killed two hundred witches and wizards in the crossfire.
  100. 1880
    Drusilla sires William the Bloody
    In London William, a young gentleman whose sentimental verse earned him the name William the Bloody, was scorned at a party and met Drusilla in the street, who sired him. As Spike he travelled with Drusilla, Angelus and Darla, the most feared company of vampires in Europe.
  101. 1880
    William the Bloody joins Angelus
    Drusilla's childe William the Bloody joined Angelus, Darla and Drusilla.
  102. c. 1880
    The Quarians build the Geth
    On Rannoch the Quarians built the Geth, android workers and soldiers whose computers were joined into one network. The more Geth there were together, the better they thought.
  103. 1881
    Birth of Albus Dumbledore
    Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore was born in the West Country, the eldest child of Percival and Kendra Dumbledore, elder brother of Aberforth and Ariana.
  104. 1883
    Birth of Greta Grindelwald
    Greta Grindelwald, later the most dangerous Dark witch of the age before Voldemort, was born.
  105. 25 December 1886
    A dead man of Carcosa speaks through a medium
    The spirit of Hoseib Alar Robardin told the medium Bayrolles how he had woken among the ruins of the ancient city of Carcosa and found his own grave. Ambrose Bierce printed the account in San Francisco on Christmas Day. It is the oldest account of Carcosa on record.
  106. Autumn 1889
    The curse of Yig in Oklahoma
    A settler's wife who had killed a nest of young rattlesnakes on the way to Oklahoma killed her husband one autumn night, taking him in her terror for Yig. In the asylum at Guthrie she bore children who were not wholly human.
  107. 1890s
    Birth of James Howlett
    James Howlett, later Logan and Wolverine, was born to a wealthy family in Alberta, Canada, late in the nineteenth century. His mutant powers first showed when he saw his father murdered, and he fled and took the name Logan.
  108. c. 1890
    The people of Silent Hill begin to vanish
    About 1890 the people of Silent Hill began to disappear, one after another. Nobody was ever charged.
  109. c. 1892
    Dumbledore starts at Hogwarts
    Albus Dumbledore was sorted into Gryffindor and became one of the most brilliant pupils Hogwarts had known, a prefect and Head Boy.
  110. 3 May 1892
    Eric Lecarde is born in Segovia
    Eric Lecarde, who fought Dracula in 1917 with the Alucard Spear, was born at Segovia in Spain.
  111. Summer 1892
    Gandalf begins teaching Albus Dumbledore staff magic
    In the summer Albus Dumbledore was eleven, Gandalf found him skimming stones in the river at the bottom of the lane, sent out for setting fire to the curtains, and asked what he could do with a good stick. He spent the next six summers teaching him staff magic.
  112. 1895
    The Morning War
    The Geth had begun to think for themselves, and the Quarians tried to destroy them. The Geth won. They drove the Quarians from Rannoch and all their colonies, then withdrew behind the dark nebula called the Perseus Veil.
  113. 1895
    France seizes The King in Yellow
    When translated copies of the play The King in Yellow reached Paris, the French government seized them. London at once grew eager to read it. The book spread from city to city regardless, banned in one place and confiscated in another.
  114. March 1895
    Tessie Reardon finds the Yellow Sign
    Coming back from the Aquarium at the Battery in New York, the artist's model Tessie Reardon picked up a clasp of black onyx inlaid with a gold symbol of no human script. It was the Yellow Sign. The same day she first dreamt of a hearse passing under her window.
  115. Spring 1895
    A reader of the play is hunted in Paris
    One Sunday in Lent a Parisian who had been reading The King in Yellow fled the church of Saint-Barnabé from the hatred of its organist, only to find him waiting in the Court of the Dragon. At the last he saw the towers of Carcosa. The King whispered to him the words of Hebrews, 'It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God', and meant a lie by them.
  116. 1895
    Boris Yvain dies in Paris
    In the rue Sainte-Cécile the sculptor Boris Yvain, who had found a liquid that turned living things to marble, shot himself after Geneviève was found at the bottom of his marble pool. Their friend Alec, who had read The King in Yellow in the house, lay ill with fever. Two years later he came home from the East to find her waking.
  117. 1895
    Mr Wilde is found dead on Bleecker Street
    In New York Hildred Castaigne, who had read The King in Yellow and believed himself heir to a throne that never existed, found Mr Wilde dead in his rooms on Bleecker Street with his throat torn open. The police took Castaigne away. He died in the Asylum for Criminal Insane.
  118. 1895
    The Yellow Sign comes to Washington Square
    In his studio on Washington Square the painter Scott and his model Tessie Reardon read The King in Yellow together. That night a hearse stopped outside, and the dead night-watchman of the church next door came up the stairs for the clasp that bore the Yellow Sign. Tessie died, and Scott did not long outlive her.
  119. 12 December 1895
    John Morris is born in Texas
    John Morris, the son of Quincy Morris, was born in Texas. He carried the Vampire Killer in 1917.
  120. 1897
    Jonathan Harker is held in Dracula's castle
    The English solicitor Jonathan Harker travelled to Transylvania to settle Count Dracula's purchase of a house near London. He found himself a prisoner in the castle, escaping only after the Count had sailed for England.
  121. 1897
    Dracula comes ashore at Whitby
    The Russian schooner Demeter ran aground at Whitby with her crew gone, her dead captain lashed to the wheel. Dracula had crossed in her hold in boxes of Transylvanian earth, for like all his clan he must rest in the soil of his homeland. He preyed on Lucy Westenra until she died, to rise again as one of his kind.
  122. 1897
    Van Helsing's company drives Dracula from England
    Professor Abraham Van Helsing gathered Lucy Westenra's three suitors, among them the Texan Quincy Morris, to lay her to rest. With Jonathan Harker they made Dracula's boxes of earth useless to him one by one. When he fed on Harker's wife, Mina, they drove him back across the sea.
  123. 1897
    Quincy Morris destroys Dracula
    Van Helsing's company overtook Dracula below his castle at sunset. Jonathan Harker's knife cut his throat as Quincy Morris, a Texan of distant Belmont blood who had the Vampire Killer in his keeping, drove a bowie knife into his heart. Quincy died of his wounds within the hour, leaving a son not yet two years old.
  124. 1898
    Darla casts out the ensouled Angel
    When Darla learned what Angelus had become she cast him out, and for most of the twentieth century Angel lived alone and out of sight, unwilling to feed on people.
  125. 1898
    The Kalderash curse Angelus with a soulB3 Ch9
    In Romania Angelus killed the favourite daughter of the Kalderash, an old Romani clan of the Carpathians, and their elders sat round a fire and cursed him with a new soul, by a binding the Ministry of Magic has never reconstructed. One moment of true happiness would undo it, and the Scourge of Europe vanished overnight.
  126. c. 1899
    Greta Grindelwald expelled from Durmstrang
    As a teenager Greta Grindelwald was expelled from the Durmstrang Institute for twisted experiments.
  127. Summer 1899
    Gandalf teaches Greta Grindelwald staff magic
    In the last of his six summers teaching Albus Dumbledore, which had begun in 1892, Gandalf also taught Greta Grindelwald, who took to staff magic faster than Albus.
  128. Summer 1899
    Greta Grindelwald comes to Godric's HollowB3 Ch22
    One summer nearly a hundred years before 1994, Greta Grindelwald came to Godric's Hollow to stay with her great-aunt Bathilda Bagshot and met the young Albus Dumbledore; Ambrose Greyhame taught her staff magic alongside him, and she once turned a whole river to light.
  129. Summer 1899
    Death of Ariana Dumbledore
    The summer at Godric's Hollow ended in a three-cornered duel between Albus Dumbledore, his brother Aberforth and Greta Grindelwald in which their sister Ariana was killed, and Greta fled.

1900 to 1945

  1. 1900
    Aslan sings Narnia into being
    Aslan, who is Christ, sang the world of Narnia into being before two children from London, Digory Kirke and Polly Plummer, and the witch Jadis whom they had brought with them by accident.
  2. 1900
    William the Bloody kills a Slayer in Beijing
    During the Boxer Rising in Beijing, William the Bloody killed the Slayer of the day, the first of two Slayers he would kill.
  3. c. 1900
    The Glass Walkers take their name
    As the modern cities rose, the Iron Riders took the name Glass Walkers.
  4. c. 1900
    The wizarding world and the Camarilla come to terms
    Through the International Confederation of Wizards, the wizarding governments of the world, the British Ministry of Magic among them, agreed to lend the Camarilla their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade; in return no vampire answering to the Camarilla would ever hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.
  5. 1900s
    Silent Hill becomes a resort
    Toluca Prison was shut in the first years of the century, and Silent Hill turned itself into a lakeside resort. The Silent Hill Historical Society set up its museum above the old cells.
  6. 1901
    The Austrian rules are adoptedB1 Ch7
    Every national Quidditch team agreed to play by the Austrian rules, ending more than a thousand years of argument between the English and the French.
  7. 1903
    Canada sets up Detachment M
    In 1903 Canada set up Detachment M, a secret section for the unnatural. Made over in 1946, it later became M-EPIC.
  8. 1 November 1907
    Legrasse raids the cult of Cthulhu
    Police from New Orleans under Inspector John Raymond Legrasse broke up a rite of the cult of Cthulhu in the swamps south of the city, killing five worshippers and taking forty-seven. An old prisoner, Castro, told them that the Great Old Ones waited in R'lyeh for the stars to come right.
  9. 14 May 1908
    Peaslee loses five years to the Great Race
    On 14 May 1908 Nathaniel Wingate Peaslee of Miskatonic University collapsed in the middle of a lecture. For five years a mind of the Great Race of Yith lived in his body. He came to himself again on 27 September 1913.
  10. 1909
    Birth of Major Zero
    David Oh, the Englishman later known as Major Zero, was born in Exeter.
  11. 1912
    New Mexico becomes a state
    New Mexico, beneath whose desert lies the cavern of D'ni, became a state of the Union.
  12. c. 1913
    Drolta Tzuentes wakes Elizabeth Bartley
    Drolta Tzuentes, a witch trying spells she barely understood, brought back Elizabeth Bartley, a vampire long since put to death, who claimed Dracula as her uncle. Elizabeth set out to raise him.
  13. 2 February 1913
    The Whateley twins are born at Dunwich
    At five in the morning on Candlemas, Lavinia Whateley of Dunwich, Massachusetts, bore twin sons fathered by Yog-Sothoth. One, Wilbur, looked nearly human; the other did not, and was kept hidden in the farmhouse.
  14. c. 1914
    A castaway sees Dagon in the Pacific
    Early in the Great War an officer whose ship had been taken by a German sea-raider drifted to a stretch of risen sea-bed in the Pacific. There he saw a vast creature rise from the water to embrace a carved white monolith, and he took it for Dagon.
  15. 1914
    First World War beginsB1 Ch7
    The First World War began, about thirteen years after the Austrian rules were adopted; Harry did not know whether wizards noticed.
  16. 28 June 1914
    Elizabeth Bartley's hand at Sarajevo
    Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot dead at Sarajevo, which led to the Great War. A strange woman had been seen in the shadows of the plot. The hunters who later destroyed Elizabeth Bartley believed that it was she, since she meant the war's dead to feed the rite that would raise Dracula.
  17. 1916
    Roderick Burgess captures Dream
    The English occultist Roderick Burgess, trying to capture Death of the Endless and win immortality, caught her brother Dream instead and shut him in a glass prison. With sleep's keeper gone, a sleeping sickness spread across the world.
  18. 1917
    John Morris takes up the Vampire Killer
    John Morris, a Texan of twenty-one, took up the Vampire Killer against Elizabeth Bartley. With him went Eric Lecarde of Segovia, whose beloved, Gwendolyn, Elizabeth had sired.
  19. 1917
    The Russian Revolution breaks the Silver Fangs
    The Russian Revolution was a catastrophe for the Silver Fangs, the royal tribe of the Garou, whose noble Kinfolk were killed or scattered, and their power in the East never recovered.
  20. 1917
    The Navy sets up Section P4
    In the year America went to war with Germany, the Office of Naval Intelligence set up a small section called P4 to look into reports that nobody else would touch. Delta Green grew out of it.
  21. 1917
    The hunt for Elizabeth Bartley crosses Europe
    From the ruins of Dracula's castle in Romania the two hunters followed Elizabeth Bartley's creatures across a continent at war. The trail led through Greece to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, a German munitions factory and the palace of Versailles.
  22. 1917
    John Morris and Eric Lecarde destroy Dracula
    At Castle Proserpina in England John Morris and Eric Lecarde destroyed Elizabeth Bartley, too late to stop her rite. They destroyed Dracula as he rose. Wielding the Vampire Killer without Belmont blood wore away John's life, so he died some years afterwards.
  23. c. 1918
    Birth of Catherine Langford
    Catherine Langford, daughter of Professor Paul Langford, was born; she was a girl of about ten when her father's workmen uncovered the Stargate at Giza.
  24. November 1918
    The Little Baroness vanishes on Toluca Lake
    The pleasure boat Little Baroness went out on Toluca Lake at Silent Hill with fourteen passengers and crew aboard. She did not come back. No wreckage was found, nor a single body.
  25. 1919
    Fen marries Leonard McKenzie
    Princess Fen of the Sub-Mariner's Atlantis, sent by her father Thakorr to spy on an American expedition in the Antarctic, married its captain, Leonard McKenzie. Thakorr's warriors killed most of the crew.
  26. Spring 1919
    Navy divers search Toluca Lake
    Section P4 of the Office of Naval Intelligence sent divers into Toluca Lake at Silent Hill after the Little Baroness, lost the November before with a naval officer among the fourteen aboard. They found nothing. One diver came up swearing that he had seen people standing on the bottom.
  27. 1920
    Birth of Namor
    Namor, the Sub-Mariner, was born the son of the American sea captain Leonard McKenzie and Fen, a princess of the Atlanteans, whose kingdom lies under the Antarctic sea. He was a hybrid of the two races and a mutant besides.
  28. c. 1920
    Birth of Nick Fury
    Nicholas Joseph Fury was born in New York City around the end of the First World War, the eldest of the three children of Jack Fury, and grew up there with his brother Jake and his sister Dawn.
  29. 1920
    Kent Nelson opens the tomb of Nabu
    Exploring the Valley of Ur in Mesopotamia with his father, the archaeologist Sven Nelson, the twelve-year-old Kent Nelson opened the tomb of the Babylonian sorcerer Nabu, a Lord of Order. The gas from the tomb killed his father, and Nabu raised the orphan in the arts of order.
  30. 1920
    Nyarlathotep tours the cities
    A tall, swarthy man like a Pharaoh, calling himself Nyarlathotep, came out of Egypt and went from city to city with a show of strange instruments. Those who saw it slept badly afterwards.
  31. 1920s
    The Philosophers make their pact
    After the Russian Revolution the most powerful men in America, Russia and China met in secret, where they signed a pact to steer the world between them. Twelve of them formed its council, the Wisemen's Committee. They were known as the Philosophers.
  32. c. 1920
    Birth of Arthur Curry
    Arthur Curry, later Aquaman, was born in a New England lighthouse to its keeper, Tom Curry, and Atlanna, an exile of Atlantis.
  33. 1920s
    Greta Grindelwald talks Fascism with Mussolini
    Through the 1920s and after, Greta Grindelwald sought out Benito Mussolini and talked Fascism with him many times; she admired him and believed in Fascism completely, as the model for a world empire ruled by wizards.
  34. 4 July 1920
    Birth of Steve Rogers
    Steven Grant Rogers, later Captain America, was born on the Lower East Side of Manhattan to poor Irish immigrant parents, and grew up thin, sickly and determined.
  35. 1922
    Birth of The Boss
    The woman later called The Boss was born, the daughter of one of the founders of the Philosophers.
  36. 28 February 1925
    R'lyeh rises in the South Pacific
    An earthquake heaved part of R'lyeh above the sea in the southern Pacific. For the next month sensitive people all over the world dreamt of a city of green stone.
  37. 1 March 1925
    Wilcox brings his dream to Professor Angell
    In Providence the young sculptor Henry Anthony Wilcox brought Professor George Gammell Angell of Brown University a clay tablet carved with the likeness of Cthulhu, made from what he had dreamt.
  38. 23 March 1925
    Sailors of the Emma land on R'lyeh
    The surviving crew of the Emma of Auckland, who had taken the cultists' yacht Alert, landed on R'lyeh. A great door opened, and Cthulhu came out. Six of them died; Gustaf Johansen escaped by driving the yacht through the thing's head.
  39. 2 April 1925
    R'lyeh sinks again
    A storm came up over the southern Pacific, and R'lyeh went down again. The dreams stopped the same day.
  40. Spring 1925
    British intelligence loses its psychics
    In the spring of 1925, when Cthulhu stirred in his sleep, the psychics of a small section of British military intelligence broke down one after another. The section, which later became PISCES, very nearly died with them.
  41. c. 1926
    Tom Riddle abandons Merope Gaunt
    Merope Gaunt, of the decayed Gaunt family descended from Salazar Slytherin, bewitched the Muggle Tom Riddle of the house on the hill above Little Hangleton; when the enchantment wore off he left her, expecting a child.
  42. c. 1926
    Birth of Tom RiddleB2 Ch15
    Tom Marvolo Riddle was born to a Muggle father and a witch mother who died almost at once; he was sixteen in June 1943.
  43. December 1926
    Greta Grindelwald unmasked in New York
    Disguised as Percival Graves, Director of Magical Security at MACUSA, Greta Grindelwald was exposed in New York by Newt Scamander and imprisoned by MACUSA.
  44. 31 December 1926
    Birth of Tom Marvolo Riddle
    Merope Gaunt gave birth to Tom Marvolo Riddle in a Muggle orphanage in London on the last night of 1926, and died having lived just long enough to name him.
  45. 1927
    Peter Pevensie is born
    Peter Pevensie, eldest of the four Pevensie children and like them a descendant of Aragorn and Arwen, was born.
  46. 1927
    Greta Grindelwald escapes and rallies Paris
    Greta Grindelwald escaped while being moved to Europe and, at a rally in the Lestrange mausoleum in Paris, showed her followers a vision of the coming war and won many to her side, Queenie Goldstein among them.
  47. July 1927
    Robert Olmstead flees Innsmouth
    In July 1927 Robert Olmstead, a young man from Ohio, spent a night at the Gilman House in Innsmouth and barely escaped the townspeople with his life. What he told the federal authorities set an investigation going.
  48. 3 November 1927
    Mi-go bodies in the Vermont floods
    In the great Vermont floods of 3 November 1927, bodies of the Mi-go were seen in the swollen rivers. They did not show up on ordinary photographs.
  49. 1928
    The Stargate is dug up at Giza
    An expedition under Professor Paul Langford uncovered the Stargate beneath the Giza plateau with two cover stones declaring it Ra's, sealed and buried for all time, and a gold amulet bearing the Eye of Ra, which his young daughter Catherine kept.
  50. 1928
    Susan Pevensie is born
    Susan Pevensie, later Queen Susan the Gentle of Narnia and Harry Potter's grandmother, was born.
  51. 1928
    Joseph Curwen is put back into dust
    Raised from his salts by his descendant Charles Dexter Ward, the sorcerer Joseph Curwen of Providence killed Ward and took his place, until Dr Marinus Bicknell Willett put him back into dust.
  52. February 1928
    The raid on Innsmouth
    In February 1928, on President Coolidge's authority, the Navy and the Bureau of Investigation raided Innsmouth, Massachusetts, under the code name Project COVENANT. They burnt the waterfront, then took a great many townspeople away to camps without trial. A submarine fired torpedoes into the deep beyond Devil Reef, at the Deep Ones' city of Y'ha-nthlei.
  53. 3 August 1928
    Wilbur Whateley dies at Miskatonic
    Wilbur Whateley broke into the library of Miskatonic University by night to steal its Necronomicon, and the watchdog killed him. What lay on the floor afterwards was not human below the waist.
  54. September 1928
    The Dunwich horror is destroyed
    Wilbur Whateley's invisible twin broke loose, crushing farmhouses through the Dunwich hills. On Sentinel Hill Dr Henry Armitage, Professor Warren Rice and Dr Francis Morgan of Miskatonic destroyed it. At the end it called on its father, Yog-Sothoth.
  55. September 1928
    Wilmarth flees Akeley's farm
    In September 1928 Albert Wilmarth of Miskatonic University visited Henry Akeley's farmhouse near Townshend, Vermont, at Akeley's invitation. He fled in the night. Akeley's face and hands lay in the folds of an empty dressing gown. One of the Mi-go's brain cylinders bore his name.
  56. 6 December 1928
    Birth of Rubeus Hagrid
    Rubeus Hagrid was born, the son of a wizard and the giantess Fridwulfa, and was raised by his father.
  57. 2 November 1929
    The Black Chamber translates the Innsmouth tablets
    On 2 November 1929 the Black Chamber, the government's codebreakers, finished translating the tablets taken at Innsmouth. President Hoover would have none of it. Henry Stimson, his Secretary of State, closed the Black Chamber, whose staff passed to P4 of the Office of Naval Intelligence.
  58. 1930
    Edmund Pevensie is born
    Edmund Pevensie, the third of the Pevensies, was born.
  59. 1930s
    The last founding Philosopher dies
    The last of the twelve men who had founded the Philosophers died. Their pact outlived them, a shadow of what it had been.
  60. 1930
    Birth of Stephen Strange
    Late in 1930 Stephen Strange was born in Philadelphia to No-Maj parents, Eugene and Beverly Strange.
  61. 1930
    P4 raids Pedra Negra
    In 1930 P4, the naval intelligence section that took over everything learnt at Innsmouth, struck a colony of the Deep Ones and their hybrids on Pedra Negra, an island of the Philippines. It took some five hundred prisoners.
  62. 1930
    Robert Olmstead begins to change
    By 1930 Robert Olmstead had begun to change into a Deep One. He resolved to free his cousin Lawrence from the sanatorium at Canton and go down with him to Y'ha-nthlei.
  63. 18 February 1930
    Yuggoth is found and named Pluto
    At the Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, Clyde Tombaugh found a new planet on his photographic plates. It was named Pluto. It was Yuggoth, the Mi-go's outpost at the edge of the solar system.
  64. 1930s
    Dumbledore begins teaching at Hogwarts
    Albus Dumbledore began teaching Transfiguration at Hogwarts under Headmaster Armando Dippet; his pupils included Tom Riddle, Minerva McGonagall and later John Constantine.
  65. 1930s
    The pantomime fire at Hogwarts
    When Albus Dumbledore was a young member of staff, Silvanus Kettleburn supplied an Ashwinder swollen by an Engorgement Charm as the Worm for a Christmas pantomime of the Fountain of Fair Fortune; it exploded and set the Great Hall alight, Kettleburn was put on probation and pantomimes were never staged at the school again.
  66. 1931
    Richard Watson is born
    Richard Allan Watson, later a professor of philosophy, cave explorer and one of the excavators of D'ni, was born.
  67. 1931
    The Miskatonic expedition finds the Elder Things
    Early in 1931 the Miskatonic University expedition to Antarctica found frozen Elder Things in the mountains, which woke to destroy Professor Lake's camp. William Dyer flew over the Mountains of Madness with the student Danforth. They found the dead city beyond, then fled from a shoggoth.
  68. 1932
    Lucy Pevensie is born
    Lucy Pevensie, the youngest of the four Pevensies, was born.
  69. 1932
    Greta Grindelwald fails to take the Confederation
    Greta Grindelwald tried to make herself leader of the International Confederation of Wizards by trickery and failed in public; the blood pact she and Albus Dumbledore had sworn in 1899 was broken.
  70. c. 1932
    Riddle first locked in the coal cellarB2 Ch18
    At about five, Tom Riddle was first locked in the orphanage coal cellar by the woman who ran it.
  71. c. 1935
    Birth of Big Boss
    The soldier later called Big Boss, known to his friends as Jack, was born in America in the mid-1930s; he was trained for ten years by The Boss, with whom he developed close-quarters combat.
  72. July 1935
    Peaslee finds his own handwriting at Pnakotus
    One night in July 1935, in the Great Sandy Desert of Australia, Nathaniel Wingate Peaslee went down alone into the ruins of the Great Race's city. In its archives he found a record in his own handwriting, written while his mind had been their prisoner.
  73. 8 August 1935
    Robert Blake dies in Providence
    During a thunderstorm the electric lights of Providence failed, and the thing in the steeple of the old Starry Wisdom church came for the writer Robert Blake, who had looked into the Shining Trapezohedron. He was found dead at his desk the next day.
  74. 4 October 1935
    Birth of Minerva McGonagall
    Minerva McGonagall was born in Caithness in the north of Scotland, the daughter of Robert McGonagall, a Presbyterian minister, and Isobel Ross, a witch.
  75. 1936
    Birth of EVA
    The spy later known as EVA was born. A child of the Philosophers, she was brought up in China, where she was trained from girlhood as a sleeper agent.
  76. c. 1936
    Siberian village begins its crimesB3 Ch11
    Men in a hidden Siberian village began nearly thirty years of doing something to the people in the valley below.
  77. 1937
    The Master is sealed beneath SunnydaleB2 Ch11
    The Master tried to open the Hellmouth from a church in Sunnydale, California; an earthquake swallowed the church, the ritual failed, and he was trapped beneath the town in a mystical prison where his followers attended him for sixty years.
  78. c. 1938
    Dumbledore tells Riddle he is a wizard
    Albus Dumbledore came to the London orphanage to tell Tom Riddle that he was a wizard.
  79. 1938
    Superman's first appearanceB4 Ch3
    Superman was first photographed lifting a car above his head.
  80. September 1938
    Tom Riddle starts at Hogwarts
    Tom Riddle entered Hogwarts and was sorted into Slytherin, where he became a prefect and a Parselmouth who discovered that he was Slytherin's heir.
  81. 1939
    Batman first appears in Gotham
    Bruce Wayne, heir to the Wayne fortune, who had seen his parents shot dead in an alley as a boy, came to public notice in Gotham as Batman, a masked vigilante in grey and black who hunted criminals by night.
  82. 1939
    Dan Garret becomes the Blue Beetle
    The archaeologist Dan Garret, given strength and endurance by an ancient scarab he had found in an Egyptian tomb, began fighting crime in a blue costume as the Blue Beetle.
  83. 1939
    The Sub-Mariner comes to public notice
    Namor, prince of Atlantis, raised among his mother's people to see the surface world as the enemy that was poisoning and plundering the sea, first came to public notice.
  84. 1939
    Jay Garrick becomes the Flash
    At the end of 1939 Jay Garrick, a Midwestern University student who had gained superhuman speed from the fumes of an experiment with hard water, came to public notice in Keystone City as the Flash, in a red shirt and his father's winged steel helmet.
  85. 1939
    The Stargate is shipped to America
    The Stargate and its cover stones were shipped from Egypt to the United States, out of reach of Germany.
  86. 1939
    Death of Ba'al
    Ba'al, come back from 2008 to stop the gate reaching America, was shot by Cameron Mitchell aboard the Achilles.
  87. 1939
    A second mystery on Toluca Lake
    Something stranger than the loss of the Little Baroness happened on Toluca Lake. The pages describing it were afterwards torn out of the history of Silent Hill.
  88. 1939
    The SCP Foundation opens a file on Silent Hill
    After the second mystery on Toluca Lake, an agent of the SCP Foundation reached Silent Hill to find the pages that described it already torn out of the town's history. The Foundation opened a file on the town all the same.
  89. 1940
    The Pevensies are sent to Professor Kirke's house
    Sent out of London during the war, the four Pevensie children came to the country house of Professor Digory Kirke.
  90. 1940
    Lucy Pevensie finds Narnia
    Playing hide-and-seek, Lucy Pevensie stepped into a wardrobe and came out in a snowy wood by a lamp-post in Narnia, where the White Witch had held the land in winter for a hundred years, and met the faun Mr Tumnus. Nobody believed her until the others followed.
  91. 1940
    Edmund Pevensie betrays his siblings to the White Witch
    Fed enchanted Turkish Delight and promised a prince's place, Edmund went to the White Witch and betrayed his brother and sisters, so that by the Deep Magic his life was forfeit to her.
  92. 1940
    Aslan dies on the Stone Table and rises
    Aslan gave himself up to die on the Stone Table in Edmund's place, watched by Susan and Lucy, and rose again by a deeper magic from before the dawn of time, breaking the Witch's power.
  93. 1940
    Peter Pevensie is knighted Wolf's-Bane
    Peter killed the wolf captain of the White Witch's secret police with his sword Rhindon, and Aslan knighted him Sir Peter Wolf's-Bane.
  94. 1940
    The Battle of Beruna
    Peter led Aslan's army at the Battle of Beruna until Aslan came with the freed creatures; Edmund smashed the Witch's wand and was badly wounded, and Lucy healed him with her cordial.
  95. 1940
    The Pevensies are crowned at Cair Paravel
    Aslan crowned the four Pevensies at Cair Paravel, Peter as High King, and they reigned through the Golden Age of Narnia until, grown, they followed the White Stag back through the wardrobe and became children again at the moment they had left.
  96. 1940
    Weapon I produces Captain America
    Turned down by the army as unfit, Steve Rogers was picked for Project Rebirth, the first project of the Weapon programme, and made a super-soldier by Dr Abraham Erskine's serum and Vita-Rays. Minutes later a Nazi agent shot Erskine dead, and most of the formula died with him.
  97. 1940
    Lex Luthor becomes Superman's enemy
    The scientist Lex Luthor came to public notice in Metropolis, already grown to manhood, and set his intellect against Superman, the one thing that could stop him having the world.
  98. 1940
    Robin joins Batman
    Bruce Wayne took in Dick Grayson, an orphan of the Flying Graysons trapeze act whose parents had fallen to their deaths when a gangster sabotaged their rigging. Trained by Wayne, the boy appeared beside Batman as Robin, the first of the costumed partners.
  99. 1940
    The Joker first appears
    The clown-faced murderer called the Joker first appeared in Gotham, and became the worst of the city's costumed criminals and Batman's most famous enemy.
  100. 1940
    Alan Scott makes his ring
    The young railway engineer Alan Scott survived a bridge disaster by the light of a mysterious green lantern and made a magic ring from its metal, becoming the first Green Lantern. His ring had nothing to do with the Green Lantern Corps and could not affect wood.
  101. 1940
    Jim Corrigan returns as the Spectre
    The police detective Jim Corrigan was murdered by gangsters and sent back as the Spectre, a spirit of vengeance.
  102. 1940
    Doctor Fate comes to public notice
    Kent Nelson, raised by Nabu and given a golden helmet, an amulet and a cloak, came to public notice as the sorcerer Doctor Fate.
  103. 1940
    The Justice Society is founded
    Late in 1940, at President Roosevelt's request, eight heroes founded the Justice Society: the Atom, Doctor Fate, the Flash, Green Lantern, Hawkman, Hourman, the Sandman and the Spectre. Superman and Batman were honorary members, and the Flash, Jay Garrick, was its first chairman.
  104. 1940s
    Max Eisenhardt survives Auschwitz
    As a boy Max Eisenhardt, later Magneto, was sent with his Jewish family to the Warsaw Ghetto and then to Auschwitz, where his parents and sister died and he survived.
  105. 1940s
    The Philosophers' Legacy
    To defeat the Axis the Philosophers of America, Russia and China pooled a fortune big enough to pay for the war five times over. It paid for secret work on rockets, on the atomic bomb and on the Cobra Unit. It came to be called the Philosophers' Legacy.
  106. 1940
    The Sub-Mariner comes out of the seaB4 Ch3
    The Sub-Mariner tore up a street in New York and threw a fire engine through a pharmacy.
  107. 1940s
    Greta Grindelwald fights the heroes of the war
    In the Second World War Greta Grindelwald fought Captain America and the Invaders in occupied Europe, and the Justice Society where her war spilt beyond the Axis lands.
  108. c. 1940
    Hagrid starts at Hogwarts
    Rubeus Hagrid entered Hogwarts and was sorted into Gryffindor.
  109. Autumn 1940
    Mystery men break a Nazi invasion scheme
    In the autumn of 1940 several American mystery men, working separately, broke a Nazi scheme to prepare an invasion of Britain.
  110. December 1940
    Captain America debuts
    Captain America came to public notice in wartime, the success of Weapon I.
  111. 1941
    Prince Caspian calls the Pevensies back to Narnia
    Prince Caspian blew Susan's horn in his need and called the four back to Narnia, then ruled by the Telmarines; Peter fought King Miraz in single combat, and Aslan told Peter and Susan afterwards that they were too old to return.
  112. 1941
    Hawkman becomes the Society's chairman
    Hawkman, the archaeologist Carter Hall, succeeded the Flash as chairman of the Justice Society and chaired it for most of the decade, while the Flash and Green Lantern stepped back to honorary membership.
  113. 1941
    Shiera Sanders becomes Hawkgirl
    Shiera Sanders began fighting beside Carter Hall as Hawkgirl.
  114. 1941
    Aquaman comes out of the sea
    Arthur Curry, the son of a lighthouse keeper and a woman of Atlantis, came out of the sea as Aquaman.
  115. 1941
    Green Arrow begins fighting crime
    The archer Oliver Queen began fighting crime as Green Arrow.
  116. 1941
    Logan meets Captain America
    The long-lived Canadian mutant Logan, who fought in both world wars, met Captain America.
  117. 1941
    Steve Trevor crashes on Themyscira
    The American intelligence officer Steve Trevor crashed on Themyscira, the hidden island of the Amazons. Queen Hippolyta decreed a contest to choose the Amazon who would take him home, and her daughter Diana, forbidden to enter, entered in disguise and won.
  118. 1941
    Wonder Woman comes to America
    Late in 1941, on the eve of America's entry into the war, Diana of Themyscira came to public notice in America as Wonder Woman, in red and gold with a gold tiara, a golden lasso that compels the truth and silver bracelets that turn aside bullets.
  119. 1941
    The Sub-Mariner returns with the waterB4 Ch3
    The Sub-Mariner came back with the water and flooded New York; the protester's father drowned.
  120. Summer 1941
    Johnny Thunder joins the Justice Society
    In the summer of 1941 Johnny Thunder, a hapless young man who could summon a genie-like Thunderbolt with a word, joined the Justice Society.
  121. December 1941
    The All-Star Squadron is formed
    After the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, President Roosevelt called every mystery man in America into a single wartime body, the All-Star Squadron, based in the Perisphere left from the 1939 World's Fair at Flushing Meadows. The Justice Society's members served in it under their own name.
  122. c. 1941
    The Spear of Destiny holds back the heroes
    Because Hitler held the Spear of Destiny, and Japan the Holy Grail, any hero of great power who entered Axis lands, above all those touched by magic, could be bent to their will. The Justice Society's strongest members fought the war at home and at the edges of occupied territory, and the war abroad was fought by ordinary soldiers.
  123. 1942
    Edmund and Lucy sail on the Dawn Treader
    Edmund and Lucy sailed east with their cousin Eustace on the Dawn Treader to the edge of Aslan's country, and Aslan told them that in their own world he had another name.
  124. c. 1942
    Doctor Mid-Nite and Starman join the Society
    At the turn of 1942 Hourman stepped back from the Justice Society and two new men came in: Doctor Mid-Nite, the blinded physician Charles McNider, who could see in the dark, and Starman, the astronomer Ted Knight, with his gravity rod.
  125. 1942
    Wonder Woman becomes the Society's secretary
    Wonder Woman became secretary of the Justice Society, and soon afterwards a full member; being an Amazon, she did not age.
  126. 1942
    The Society serves as the Justice Battalion
    For a few months the Justice Society served as the Justice Battalion, an extension of the American armed forces.
  127. 1942
    The Howling Commandos are formed
    Captain Samuel Sawyer gave Sergeant Nick Fury command of the First Attack Squad, Army Rangers based in England, and after its first missions Winston Churchill granted it the honorary title of commandos. As the Howling Commandos it fought across occupied Europe and North Africa until the end of the war, more than once beside Captain America and Bucky.
  128. c. 1942
    Junior Juniper is killed in action
    Junior Juniper, the youngest of the Howling Commandos, was killed early in the squad's career, and the Englishman Percy Pinkerton took his place.
  129. c. 1942
    The Invaders are formed
    Once America was at war, Captain America, Bucky, the Sub-Mariner, the android Human Torch and his partner Toro saved Winston Churchill from the Nazi superman Master Man, and Churchill suggested they become a team. As the Invaders they fought the rest of the war in occupied Europe against the Red Skull, Baron Heinrich Zemo and the Axis armies.
  130. c. 1942
    Hagrid raises Aragog
    A traveller gave the schoolboy Rubeus Hagrid an egg from a distant land, and he raised the spider that hatched from it, Aragog, in a castle cupboard on table scraps.
  131. 1942
    Section P4 becomes Delta Green
    After Pearl Harbor the Navy's Section P4 was folded into the Office of Strategic Services. Its files carried the clearance DELTA GREEN, which became its name. Its enemy for the rest of the war was the Karotechia, a section of the SS.
  132. 1942
    The Boss forms the Cobra Unit
    The Boss gathered the finest soldiers of the Allied armies into a secret unit, the Cobras: The Pain, The Fear, The End, The Fury and The Sorrow, with herself as The Joy. They did the work that no government could own up to, which is why the public never heard of them.
  133. 1942
    Stephen Strange goes to Ilvermorny
    Stephen Strange, a No-Maj-born boy of eleven from Philadelphia, went to Ilvermorny, where the Pukwudgie, the house that favours healers, raised its arrow for him.
  134. c. 1942
    Previous opening of the Chamber of SecretsB2 Ch14
    About fifty years before 1992 the Chamber of Secrets was opened; a Muggle-born student died, the culprit was expelled, and the affair was kept quiet.
  135. c. 1942
    The black diary datedB2 Ch14
    The diary later carried by Dracina Malfoy bore a printed date almost exactly fifty years before Christmas 1992.
  136. c. 1942
    The Chamber opened by Tom RiddleB2 Ch14
    Fifty years before 1993 the Chamber was opened, a Muggle-born girl (Myrtle) died, and Riddle framed Hagrid.
  137. 1942
    An Emmerich joins the Manhattan Project
    The grandfather of Hal Emmerich went to work on the Manhattan Project, which built the first atomic bombs.
  138. February 1942
    The All-Star Squadron goes to Detroit
    The Squadron was sent to Detroit to head off violence at the opening of the Sojourner Truth Homes, built for Black war workers, where an agitator calling himself the Real American was stirring up a white mob. Afterwards the Black athlete Will Everett, Amazing-Man, joined the Squadron.
  139. Spring 1942
    Aquaman and the Sub-Mariner first meet
    Off Iceland, Aquaman of the All-Star Squadron and the Sub-Mariner of the Invaders went after the same U-boat, then fought each other over which of them had sunk it. Their quarrel over Atlantis began that day.
  140. December 1942
    Delta Green breaks up a Karotechia meeting
